author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of traffic snarl from Pakistan dating back to 2021 falsely shared on social media as recent incident from India
content: New Delhi, Jan 1 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ) : A video is being circulated on social media depicting a long traffic snarl with users claiming that it depicted congestion in Uttarakhand owing to the new year. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk, in its investigation found that an old video from Kaghan valley in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province of Pakistan resurfaced on social media with a false claim. Claim An Instagram user, named, 'Nitesh Talks' shared a post on December 30 2024 claiming that the roads in Uttarakhand were jam packed due to traffic due to the new year, and had garnered 15,089 likes. The video which was shared with a Hindi message read: "Traffic jam in Uttarakhand on new year" Here is the link and archive link and below is the screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk first ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across another social media post, which carried the same video with users claiming it to be from Himachal Pradesh. The link of the post can be viewed here and here and their archive link can be found here and here . On further scanning the search results we came across an Instagram post by 'Pakistani Journal' put out on July 25, 2021, whose caption read: "Situation right now at Balakot-Naran road as tourists head towards northern areas after Eid." Here is the link and archive link and below is the screenshot the same. Below is a combination image, highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the May 2021 Facebook post. Taking cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword research on Google to find relevant material to substantiate the investigation. We came across a news bulletin on YouTube by Pakistani media outlet 'ARY News', uploaded on July 26, 2021. The title of the report read: "Roads blocked, hotels full, tourist stuck on roads towards kaghan". It featured a similar video of the one making rounds on social media claiming it to be from India. Here is the link and below is the screenshot of the same. The video report mentioned that in Naran, hundreds of thousands of cars were stuck in a traffic jam, with the vehicles' line stretching as far as the eye could see. Another customised keyword search on Google led the Desk to an article published by Pakistani newspaper Daily Times on July 26, 2021, that featured the same image of the jam as seen in the viral video. Here is the link and below is the screenshot of the same. The report mentioned: "Tourists have flocked to the Kaghan valley of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's Mansehra district in record numbers this Eidul Azha, with hundreds of thousands of vehicles choking the roads and causing traffic jams in the scenic tourist site, a private TV channel reported on Sunday." Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the viral video to that of the photo featured in the Pakistani news report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was from Pakistan and not India.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Harbhajan Singh's daughter falsely identified as Virat Kohli's child, 2017 photo shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, Jan 1 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ) : A picture of Indian cricketer Virat Kohli with a girl child on his lap was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that he was with his daughter in the picture. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found that the girl child was not Virat Kohli's daughter, but that of former cricketer Harbhajan Singh. The photo was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user named 'Crico' shared a photo on December 25 claiming that it showed Virat Kohli with his daughter. Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the photo through Google Lens and found that another user had shared the same photo with a similar caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post. On further scanning the search results, we came across a news report published by News 18 in May 2017, whose headline read: "Virat Kohli is in Awe of Harbhajan Singh's Daughter". It carried an Instagram post by Kohli, shared on May 2, 2017. Here is the link to the report. The caption of the post read: "Baby hinaya looking for something in my beard. And i am surprised how can someone be so beautiful and cuteee. What a blessing to @harbhajan3 @geetabasra . God bless you all" Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. We then looked for pictures of Virat and Anuskha's daughter Vamika to substantiate the investigation and found an article by News 18, whose headline read: "Twitter Reaction: First picture of Anushka Sharma-Virat Kohli's daughter Vamika surfaced, people are praising her cuteness" Here is the link to the article and below is the screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the girl child with Virat Kohli in the viral photo was Harbhajan Singh's daughter.

title: PTI Fact Check: Fake news report screenshot shared on social media to falsely allege molestation of South Korean YouTuber by two men in Mumbai; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 1 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A purported screenshot of a news report, that featured a photo of a woman with two men was shared on social media. The headline in the screenshot claimed that the woman was a South Korean YouTuber, who was sexually assaulted by the two men seen in it, who had earlier saved her from being harassed on the streets in Mumbai. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a fake screenshot was attributed to Times of India and was shared on social media with a false claim. The Times of India never published such a report. It is pertinent to note that a South Korean YouTuber was allegedly harassed in Mumbai while she was live streaming earlier in December. Two men identified as Aditya and Atharva had back then rescued her from the situation. However, a photo of the YouTuber having lunch with the two men was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on December 19 a post containing screenshot of a purported news report by Times of India, that featured a photo of two men with a woman. The user claimed that the woman in the photo – a South Korean YouTuber – was sexually assaulted by the two men, who had earlier saved her from being harassed on the streets of Mumbai. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk carried out a customised keyword search on Google but could not find any such news report published by the Times of India. However, the search results led us to a Times Now report published on December 2, 2022. The headline read: "[WATCH] South Korean YouTuber, harassed in Mumbai, meets two 'Indian heroes' who rescued her; shares video." Here's the link to the news report, and below is the screenshot of the same. Going through the investigation, the Desk compared the viral article with the Times Now report and found multiple indications of the viral report to be digitally altered. While the headline of the Times Now article reads, "[WATCH] South Korean YouTuber, harassed in Mumbai, meets two 'Indian heroes' who rescued her; shares video." In the viral report, the same has been altered to, "WATCH: South Korean YouTuber, harassed in Mumbai, meets two 'Indian heroes' who rescue her only to end up getting raped by them." Clearly, the part "only to end up getting raped by them" was falsely included in the headline. Further, a similar change has also been made to the lead. The phrase "bid in Mumbai" was replaced with "ended up getting brutally raped by the two who are yet to be apprehended by the Mumbai police." Below is the screenshot of the comparison indicated. Further, taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search on Google and came across a social media post by South Korean YouTuber herself, who, as a gesture of gratitude, invited Aditya and Atharva for lunch. In a post on X (formerly Twitter), YouTuber Hyojeong Park thanked the two Indian men who helped her to post the video and saved her on the street. Below is the link and screenshot of the social media post by Park. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the screenshot shared on social media in the name of Times of India was fake.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: DigiYatra data to be used for catching tax evaders? Income tax department, DigiYatra, civil aviation ministry deny media report as inaccurate
content: New Delhi, Jan 2 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ) : Multiple social media user recently cited a media report to claim that the Income Tax Department will tap DigiYatra data to crack down on tax evaders. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the claims made on social media were false. The report, which initially quoted sources to make the claim and lacked evidence, was later updated with DigiYatra's response, which refuted the claim as 'false'. The Income Tax Department also rubbished the claim. Even the Ministry of Civil Aviation clarified that the media report was based on "unfounded and inaccurate claims". The DigiYatra app uses Facial Recognition Technology (FRT) to provide contactless and seamless passenger processing at airport checkpoints, enhancing the travel experience. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a post on December 30, claiming that the tax department will tap DigiYatra data. The post carried the link to a report by The New Indian Express, whose headline read: "Tax department to tap Digi Yatra data to go after evaders." The caption of the post read: "Tax dept to tap Digi yatra data. Misuse of data by the Income tax department . One more reason why people will hesitate to use Digi Yatra. People have no faith in this gov, as any gov department may start using DigiYatra data." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: https://x.com/digiyatraoffice/status/1873691979910971593?s=46 https://ghostarchive.org/archive/JXbto Investigation The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google, which led us to an X post by the Income Tax Department, shared on December 30, 2024, where it refuted the claim made in the news report. "It is seen that news articles have appeared stating that Digiyatra data will be used to crack down on tax evaders. In this connection it is clarified that as on date there is no such move by the @IncomeTaxIndiadepartment," it read. Here is the link and archive link to the X post, and below is a screenshot of the same. The Ministry of Civil Aviation had also shared an X post on the same day, stating that the media report was based on "unfounded and inaccurate claims". "The Ministry of Civil Aviation hereby clarifies that the recent media report concerning Digi Yatra is based on unfounded and inaccurate claims. There is no sharing of Digi Yatra passengers data with Indian tax authorities. The Digi Yatra app follows the Self-Sovereign Identity (SSI) model, where Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and travel credentials are stored exclusively on the user's device, not on any central repository. Furthermore, if a user uninstalls the Digi Yatra app, the data is deleted entirely. Additionally, airport systems automatically purge passenger data within 24 hours of the flight's departure. It is also important to note that Digi Yatra is designed solely for domestic passengers and does not apply to international travelers," the post read. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Digi Yatra CEO Suresh Khadakabhavi also responded to claims made in The New Indian Express report and said that "no central storage of biometric, or personal data stays on users' phones, and facial authentication is decentralized." Here is the link to an X post by DigiYatra, quoting its CEO, and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of investigation, the Desk found the LinkedIn post by Khadakabhavi, whose screenshot was carried in the X post by DigiYatra. Here is the link to the LinkedIn post and below is a screenshot of the same. "These are unfounded claims by The NEW Indian Express about the misuse of Digi Yatra data based on unknown sources. It is crucial to clarify that Digi Yatra operates without storing any Personally Identifiable Information (PII) in any central repository. This ensures there is no database to breach, share, lose, or leak, safeguarding user privacy," read a section of the post. "The claim that "financial records of frequent international travelers could be subjected to scrutiny" is also incorrect. Digi Yatra is not yet available for international travel. Furthermore, with no central repository, scrutiny and corelation of records is not feasible. Digi Yatra's Privacy-Preserving ecosystem aligns with the Self-Sovereign Identity (SSI) framework, ensuring unmatched data security, privacy and global scalability," read another section of the post. In the next part of investigation, the Desk read the report by The New Indian Express. While it was updated with the response by DigiYatra in the later part, its heading and subheading still made the same claim. Here is the link and archive link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: As can be seen in the two screenshots below, the article made the claims based on "sources". It also mentioned that "questions sent to the tax department and Digi Yatra on the issue remained unanswered till the time of filing of this report." Towards the end, the report mentioned the response by DigiYatra. Below is a screenshot of the same: However, while searching for more details we found a PDF with the details of the DigiYatra personal data guidlines released by the Ministry of Civil Aviation. Here is the link and below is the screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claims made in the media report lacked evidence, and were refuted by the concerned authorities. Disclaimer: The copy has been updated to add the personal data guidelines PDF issued by the Ministry of Civil Aviation regarding the DigiYatra Biometric boarding system and personal data guidelines .

title: PTI Fact Check: Old video from inside Algerian flight before its emergency landing shared on social media, falsely linking it to Azerbaijan plan crash
content: New Delhi, Jan 2 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Days after Azerbaijan Airlines flight 8243 crashed in Kazakhstan, a video was recently shared on social media with users claiming it showed visuals from inside the doomed aircraft just before it crash-landed. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk, in its investigation, found the claim to be false. The video actually showed an Air Algérie flight that made an emergency landing due to a technical fault in September 2024. The old and unrelated video was shared with on social media as recent, falsely linking it to the Azerbaijan plane crash. On December 25, Azerbaijan Airlines' Embraer 190 was flying from Azerbaijan's capital of Baku to the Russian city of Grozny in the North Caucasus when it was diverted for reasons still unclear and crashed while making an attempt to land in Aktau in Kazakhstan after flying east across the Caspian Sea. The crash killed 38 people and left all 29 survivors injured. Azerbaijan's President Ilham Aliyev has alleged that the Azerbaijani airliner was shot down by Russia, albeit unintentionally, and criticised Moscow for trying to "hush up" the issue for days. Claim An Instagram user on December 26 shared a video claiming it showed passengers inside the Azerbaijan Airlines flight 8243 chanting "Allahu Akbar", moments before it crashed in Kazakhstan on December 25. Here's the link , archive link and screenshot of the post. Investigation The Desk ran the viral clip through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, and found that several other users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a Facebook post published by a local Algerian news portal, '3ish radio,' on September 23. The post carried the same video as shared on social media. Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of the post. According to the details published by the Algerian channel, the video was shot as the Air Algerie plane returned to Houari Boumediene Airport after facing a technical malfunction earlier in September. Below is also a combination image, which shows that the video shared on social media was the same as the one shared by the Algeria-based media house in September 2024. To further corroborate the details, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a YouTube Shorts video, published by Al-Jazeera in September. In the video, (which was shot from a different angle), the passengers inside the Air Algerie flight could be seen chanting Allahu Akbar as the pilot made an emergency landing. Below is the link and screenshot of the post. The Desk also found a news report published by Algerian news portal Dzair Tube, which stated the Air Algerie flight departed from Houari Boumediene Airport at 11:02 PM on September 22, 2024; however, it was turned back after one hour in the air owing to some technical glitch. Below is the link and screenshot of the news report published by Dzair Tube. The article mentioned, "The decision to turn back was made by the flight commander after one hour in the air, prioritizing the safety of passengers and crew. Air Algérie reassured the public and its valued customers that all necessary measures were taken to ensure the well-being of those on board." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old and unrelated video from Algeria was shared on social media as recent, falsely linking it to the plane crash in Kazakhstan.

title: PTI Fact Check: News clips dating back to 2022 shared on social media as recent to falsely claim that Nitish Kumar resigned as Bihar CM and quit NDA
content: New Delhi, Jan 3 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Amid speculations of another political realignment in Bihar ahead of the Assembly polls in the state, scheduled to be held later this year, several news clips related to Nitish Kumar have been doing rounds on social media, with some users claiming that he had resigned as the Bihar CM and moved out of the ruling NDA in Bihar. The social media posts also claimed that Kumar had once again joined the RJD-led grand alliance. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found that news reports dating back to August 2022, when Kumar had moved out of the NDA, accusing the BJP of trying to "split and finish" off his party Janata Dal (United). The videos were shared on social media as recent with false claims. Notably, Kumar has aligned with the RJD twice in the last decade, most recently as part of the 'Mahagathbandhan' before switching sides to rejoin the BJP-led NDA in January 2024. The Desk cross-checked the veracity of four such social media posts. Here's what we found: Claim 1: A user shared an Aaj Tak report claiming that Nitish Kumar had resigned as the Chief Minister of Bihar and broke the alliance with the BJP. Here's the link and archive link of the post. The Desk analyzed the video using InVid Tool Search and extracted several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found a YouTube video published by Aaj Tak on August 9, 2022. The content in the YouTube video matched the viral clip. The video dated back to when Kumar had severed ties with the BJP and stepped down as CM in August 2022, and later joined the RJD-led grand alliance to form government. Here's the link and screenshot of the post: Below is a combination image, which shows that the content in the viral video is the same as that of the YouTube channel. Claim 2: A social media user shares a news report by Republic Bharat about Nitish Kumar's exit from NDA Here's the link and archive link of the post. The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a YouTube video uploaded by Republic on August 9, 2022. Upon review, it was found that the viral clip was taken from this 3-minute video. Here's the link and screenshot of the news report published. Below is a combination image attached, which shows that the content in the viral video is the same as that of the YouTube channel. Claim 3: A Facebook user shared a News18 report claiming Nitish Kumar had once again broken ties with the BJP. Here's the link and archive link to the post. The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and extracted keyframes. By running these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk discovered a YouTube video uploaded on the official channel of News 18 India on August 9, 2022. Here's the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same. The video featured visuals same as that of the viral clip, which made it clear that it was from the time when Kumar had quit the NDA and joined hands with the RJD in August 2022. Below is a combination image, highlighting the same: Claim 4: A social media user shared a TV9 Bharatvarsh report, claiming that Nitish Kumar had severed ties with the BJP and stepped down as the Bihar CM. Here's the link and archive link to the post. The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by TV9 Bharatvarsh, on August 9, 2022. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that a part of this was the same as the clip shared on social media. Below is a combination image highlighting the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral clips of Kumar claiming that he resigned as Bihar CM and quit the NDA, dated back to August 2022.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: 2019 video of man entering lion's enclosure in a zoo falsely shared as a recent incident
content: New Delhi, Jan 3 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ) : A video recently shared on social media showed a man at a distance confronting a lion in what looked like an animal enclosure in a zoo. The users shared the video, claiming that it was a recent incident that took place in the 'National Zoo of India'. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a five-year-video of an incident that happened in Delhi Zoo was falsely shared on social media as a recent incident. Claim A Facebook user named 'Rowmari Press club' shared on December 24, a video claiming that a visitor entered the lion's cage in a zoo two days ago. The caption, originally in Bengali, translated to: "Visitors in the lion's cage at the zoo. Brave effort continues to save lives. The incident took place in the National Zoo of India two days ago." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk first ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across an X post carrying the same video, shot from a different angle. The caption of the post, shared on September 10, read: "An old video resurfaced of a man supposedly drunk trying to tame a lion either due to his inebriated state, a dare, or saving his life inspired by Life of Pie(types). " Here is the link and archive link to the tweet and below is the screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image, which makes it clear that the viral video is the same as shared in an X post in September 2024. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across an extended version of the viral video, which was uploaded by Hindustan Times on its YouTube channel on October 17, 2019. The title of the video read: "Watch: Man enters lion's enclosure in Delhi Zoo, rescued safely" Here is the link and below is a screenshot of the same. "A 21-year-old man climbed into a lion enclosure in the Delhi zoo but was rescued without any injuries by the authorities. The man, who police said is mentally disturbed, was seem seen sitting, squatting & then tumbling in front of the lion. Police said that the man belongs to Seelampur in North-East Delhi and has been sent for medical examination. Police also said that the man gained entry into the enclosure by scaling the iron grill that serves as a fence around the enclosure," read the description of the video. The search results further led us to an X post by Times of India, posted on October 27, 2019, whose caption read: "A man jumps into Lion's fence in #Delhi zoo, survives." Here is the link and below is the screenshot of the same. The New Indian Express also shared the same video on YouTube on October 17, 2019, with the title, "WATCH | Mentally disturbed man falls into lion's enclosure at Delhi Zoo". Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the post: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that video of a man entering the lion's enclosure,shared on social media as a recent event, was actually five years old.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Social media posts claiming Pakistani boy married his mother are false and baseless; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 3 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ) : A video recently was shared on social media with the claim that it showed a Pakistani boy marrying his mother as he turned 18. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found that the boy had got his mother married for the second time. The text plate on the video, which read, "son marries off his mother", was misinterpreted and the clip was shared on social media with a false claim. For the unversed, 'marries off' is a phrasal verb which means to find a spouse for someone. In this case, it means the son getting his mother married, and not what has been claimed on social media. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on December 30 a post claiming that a Pakistani boy married his mother as he turned 18. The tweet, that garnered 69.9k views, read: "In Muslim Pakistan a Son marries his Mother. The societal degradation had reached on melting point. Although its Pakistan so anything can happen !" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk first ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across several other social media posts, which carried the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archive links can be found here and here , respectively. In the subsequent part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across an article by 'Bloom Pakistan', published on December 31, 2024. The title of the article read: "She sacrificed her whole life for us', son gets mother married after 18 years, video goes viral." Here is the link to the article and below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a December 30 report by Hindustan Times, whose headline read: "Pakistani man wins hearts by arranging his mother's second marriage: 'Queen raised a king'" Here is the link and below is the screenshot of the same. The news article also carried an Instagram post by 'Abdul Ahad', shared on December 28, featuring his mother with a video message. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the Instagram post. In the video, Ahad thanked his mother for the hardships she faced for her children, and stated that he made the decision to marry off her after 18 years. Taking a cue from this, the Desk then went through Abdul Ahad's Instagram profile and came across another post by him. Here is the link and below is a screenshot of the post. Several other news reports also covered the incident. Two such articles can be found here and here . Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the Pakistani boy got his mother married again, and did not marry her as claimed on social media.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: 2022 video of stone pelting on a church near Bethlehem shared on social media as recent with false claim; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 4 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ) : A video of several men pelting stones on a church-like structure was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that it showed a Muslim mob attacking a church in Beit Sahour, a town near the Palestinian city of Bethlehem, the biblical birthplace of Jesus Christ on Christmas 2024.However, the PTI Fact Check Desk, in its investigation found that video dates back to October 2022 and is not related to the Christmas celebration that took place in 2024. The viral video was shared with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on December 25, 2024, a post claiming that muslim men targeted the holy site of Bethlehem during Christmas. The caption, originally in Hindi, translates to: "Attack of heretics on Bethlehem Church: Muslims targeted the holy site with stones and bullets during Christmas. Hundreds of Christians were injured" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk first ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across several other social media posts, which carried the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here , and their archived versions can be found here , here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, we came across an X (formerly Twitter) post by a user named Avi Kaner, shared on October 31, 2022. The caption of the post read: "Christians were attacked in Bethlehem by a Palestinian mob while they were rehearsing for Christmas in a church." Here is the link and below is a screenshot of the same: The video posted on X in 2022 had a striking resemblance with the viral video. Below is a combining image highlighting the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across an article by All Arab News, on October 2022, whose headline read: "Church attacked by Muslims in Christian town near Bethlehem" A section of the article mentioned: "It is very unfortunate and enraging to watch what happened last night in the attack on the Greek Orthodox Church of The Forefathers in Beit Sahour by a group of thugs, following a quarrel between some young men," the report quoted Wadie Abunassar, spokesman for the Catholic Bishops of the Holy Land, saying in a Facebook post. Here is the link and below is the screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image, comparing the visuals of the viral video to that of the photo featured in the news report. Another report was published by The Jerusalem Post in October 2022, whose headline read: "Christian leaders condemn attack on church near Bethlehem" Here is the link to the article. Taking a cue from the report, the Desk located The Holy Forefathers Greek Orthodox Church on Google Maps. Here is the link to Google Street view of the church and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was the same location as seen in the viral video. Below is a combination image, highlighting the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that while the attack took place on a church near Bethlehem, the video dated back to 2022, and was not recent.

title: PTI Fact Check: Dancing video of Hemant Soren's lookalike falsely attributed to Jharkhand CM; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 5 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of a man dancing, falsely claimed to be Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren during New Year celebrations, was widely shared on social media. However, the individual in the video has been identified as Jasbir James Lakra, a lookalike of the CM. The social media post sharing the dancing video in name of Jharkhand CM was misleading. Claim A Facebook user shared on January 1 a purported clip, claiming that it showed Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren dancing during New Year celebrations. The user shared the clip with the caption, "Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren dances at the New Year party." Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of the post. Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across several other social media posts, carrying the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , respectively, and their archive links can be found here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X (formerly Twitter) post published by a local Jharkhand news portal 'The Followup', on December 31. The post carried the same video as shared on social media. Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of the post. The caption of the X post stated that the person dancing in the video was not Chief Minister Hemant Soren, but his lookalike. Below is a combination image, which shows that the video shared on social media was the same as the one shared by 'The Followup' channel on December 31, 2024. In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by News18 on January 1, 2025. The article stated that the person captured in the video was the JMM chief's lookalike. Here's the link and screenshot of the news article. Additionally, during the investigation, the Desk also found a social media post by Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren, in which he shared some pictures with his lookalike Munna Lohra on September 25, 2024. Here's the link and screenshot of the post. The Desk compared the person seen in the viral video with Munna Lohra, but found their faces to be completely different. Below is a screenshot of comparison of pictures. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search on Google and found a video uploaded on the YouTube channel 'Student fighter' on December 31, 2024. Here's the link and screenshot of the YouTube video. According to the description, the video featured Jasbir James Lakra, another lookalike of Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren. On careful examination, the Desk observed that the face and clothes of the person in the YouTube video matched exactly with the person seen in the viral video. Below is a combination image, highlighting the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the person seen in the viral video was not Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren, but his lookalike Jasbir James Lakra.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: 2017 photo of Allu Arjun's temple visit with his family shared on social media as recent with false claims; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 6 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ) : A photo of actor Allu Arjun with his wife and children was recently shared on social media with users claiming that he recently visited Shiv temple with his family following the box office success of 'Pushpa 2: The Rule'. Sharing the photo, users also claimed that Arjun rejected an endorsement offer of Rs 10 crore from a famous liquor brand. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found that the photo dated back to 2017, which was being shared on social media as recent. Further, we found that the claim of rejecting an endorsement offer was related to a 2023 report when he turned down a brand placement deal for his film 'Pushpa 2'. The social media posts were shared with false claims. Claim A Facebook user shared on December 26 a post claiming Allu Arjun rejected an endorsement offer of Rs 10 crore from a liquor brand and that he visited Shiv temple with his family after the success of Pushpa 2. Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the photo through Google Lens and found that another user had shared the same photo with a similar caption. Here is the link and archive link of the same. The Desk categorically investigated the claims made in the viral social media posts, and here's what it found: Claim 1: Allu Arjun rejects Rs 10 crore offer from a famous liquor brand after the success of Pushpa 2. To verify the claim, we conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by Hindustan Times from December 2023, whose headline read: "Allu Arjun turns down liquor and pan brand placements for Pushpa The Rule: Report" "The report in Gulte states that a popular liquor and pan brand approached the makers of Pushpa, offering them a fat sum for a brand placement. Whenever the hero drinks, smokes or chews on-screen, the brand wants their logo to be visible in the frame. What's more, they even offered a sum of ₹10 crore for the same, state reports. However, Allu turned down the offer as he wasn't comfortable with promoting such brands. He is said to have said no because he doesn't want to encourage fans to smoke or drink in reality," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. We found another report by News18 published in December 2023, which mentioned: "...The Telugu star has turned down a liquor and pan brand offer which wanted its logo to be displayed on screen each time 'Pushpa' smokes or chews in the movie. As reported by Gulte, the brand had offered a huge sum of Rs 10 crore to the makers of the film but Allu Arjun rejected it saying he wasn't "comfortable" with the promotion of such brands." Here is the link to the article. The offer was regarding brand placement, which was made in 2023, when 'Pushpa 2' was in the making, and not after its success. Claim 2: Allu Arjun visited a Shiv temple with his family after the success of Pushpa 2 To investigate this claim, we conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a video on YouTube by United Andhra posted in the year 2017. The title of the video read: "Allu Arjun With His Family Visits Tirumala Venkateswara Temple |Allu Arjun, | Sneha | Ayaan |Arha" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same. The visuals of the YouTube video had striking similarity with the photo shared on social media. Below is a combination image, highlighting the same: The search results also led us to a report by International Business Times, published in February 2017, whose headline read: "Allu Arjun visits Tirupati with his family - Sneha, Ayaan and Arha". Here is the link to the article and below is a combination image, which shows that a photo in the article was the same as the viral image. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claims made on social media were false; neither Arjun's photo with his family is recent, nor is the report regarding him rejecting an endorsement offer.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: 2020 report of US White House unfollowing PM Modi misleadingly shared as recent on social media
content: New Delhi, Jan 6 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ) : Multiple social media users have recently shared a screenshot of a purported X (formerly Twitter) post by Hindi news channel Aaj Tak, claiming that the White House unfollowed PM Modi on the platform. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk revealed that a five-year-old news report was misleadingly circulated as recent by some of the users on social media. In 2020, during then-US President Donald Trump's visit to India, the White House briefly followed PM Modi and other Indian officials on X. The White House's "following" list frequently changes based on current events and diplomatic engagements. The social media post featuring the Aaj Tak screenshot was therefore misleading. The social media claims emerged amid speculations on whether PM Modi will receive an invitation from the White House for US President-elect Donald Trump's inauguration ceremony at the US Capitol on January 20, 2025. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on January 2 a screenshot of a purported X post by Aaj Tak, which stated that the White House had unfollowed PM Modi on the social media platform. The X post, that garnered 1137 views, originally in Hindi, read: "White House unfollows PM Modi" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran a customised keyword search on Google and found that several other users had made the same claim across social media platforms. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. Below are the screenshots of the two posts: We first checked the White House's X account and found that it follows only six US officials at the moment. Below is a screenshot of the people that White House follows: The Desk then ran the viral screenshot through Google Lens and found that the same post was shared by Aaj Tak on April 9, 2020. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. In the next part of investigation, the Desk found that the several reports had covered the news back then. Two such reports can be found here and here . Amid speculation about why the White House made such a decision, the administration explained that its X handle typically follows accounts of officials from host countries on a temporary basis during presidential visits. A report by PTI was carried by India Today, whose headline read: "After White House unfollows PM Modi, Trump office says that's the norm for presidential visit" A section of the report read: "The White House Wednesday explained that its Twitter handle typically 'follows' the accounts of officials from host countries for a brief period during a presidential trip to retweet their messages in support of the visit. During President Donald Trump's visit to India in the last week of February, the official Twitter handle of the White House -- @WhiteHouse -- had started 'following' the accounts of President Ram Nath Kovind, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the Prime Minister's office, the Indian Embassy in the US, the US Embassy in India and the US Ambassador to India, Ken Juster." Here is the link to the report and below is the screenshot of the same Subsequently, the Desk concluded thata five-year-old news was shared on social media as recent.

author: Pratyush Ranjan/Kaushiki Goel
title: PTI Fact Check: Social media posts claiming a Tamil Nadu pani puri vendor received income tax/GST notice for accepting Rs 40 lakh payment are baseless; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 6 (Pratyush Ranjan / Kaushiki Goel, PTI Fact Check ): A social media user shared a screenshot of a Facebook post with PTI Fact Check on its WhatsApp number (+91-8130503759) and requested it to verify a claim in the social media post saying a pani puri street vendor from Tamil Nadu received an income tax notice for accepting online payments totalling over ₹40 lakhs during the financial year 2023-24. The PTI Fact Check Desk, in its investigation, found no evidence to support the claim made in the social media post. No such notice was issued by the GST or the income tax departments to any pani puri vendor in Tamil Nadu for accepting payments of more than Rs 40 lakh in the financial year 2023-24. A Commercial Taxes Department (Tamil Nadu) official clarified to PTI that the notice in the widely shared screenshots was issued to a hotel owner in Kanyakumari, not a street vendor selling pani puri. The social media claims were determined to be false and baseless. Claim An X user shared a screenshot of a purported notice claiming that a pani puri seller made Rs 40 lakh per year and received a notice from the Income Tax department. Below is a screenshot of the message PTI Fact Desk's WhatsApp number received and the link and archive link to the post. Investigation The Desk started the investigation by carefully examining the notice shared in the social media post. While the caption claimed the pani puri vendor received an Income Tax notice, the screenshot indicated the notice pertained to violating Goods and Services Tax (GST) clauses. The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found reports referencing the same claim. Reports from the NDTV and Times of India websites noted that the claim originated from an X post shared by a user named Jagdish Chaturvedi. NDTV: https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/gst-notice-issued-to-tamil-nadu-pani-puri-seller-over-rs-40-lakh-earnings-7403011 Times of India: https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/life-style/food-news/panipuri-seller-from-tamil-nadu-receives-gst-notice-after-earning-rs-40-lakh-through-online-payments/articleshow/116937510.cms The caption in the X post, published on January 2 and used in reports by NDTV and TOI, read: "Pani puri wala makes 40L per year and gets an income tax notice (Sic)." This post garnered significant engagement, including 995,000 views, 1,500 reposts, 9,400 likes, and 574 comments. The Desk used Google Lens to analyse the photo in the post and found that multiple users shared the same image with similar captions on Facebook. Also, below is the screenshot, link and archive link to the X post- To learn more about the claim, the Desk ran the photo through Google Lens and found multiple other users shared the same picture with a similar caption on Facebook. Two such posts can be viewed here and here , and their archive links can be found here and here . While scanning the screenshot, the Desk noticed the recipient's name and address were blank, with the handwritten text "Notice to Panipuri vendor" added to the document. In the subsequent part of the investigation, the Desk searched Google to know what the GST or income-tax policies for street vendors are in India and here's what we found- The tax regime in India is divided into two broad categories: direct taxes and indirect taxes. A direct tax is levied directly on an individual's income, whereas indirect taxes are levied on their consumption of goods and services. Income tax, governed by the Income Tax Act 1961, is a part of the direct tax system in India. On the other hand, the Goods and Services Tax (GST) is an indirect taxation system governed by the Goods and Services Act 2017. It was formed by subsuming all other indirect taxes, i.e. VAT, service tax, central excise duty, etc. Below is a screenshot of a table explaining the difference between GST and Income Tax. Here is the link to the post. In India, street vendors are generally exempt from GST unless their turnover exceeds a certain threshold. The GST threshold is currently set at Rs 40 lakh, meaning vendors who operate at a small scale and have limited digital transactions may be exempt from GST. The notice, as per the screenshot, was sent on December 17 for an alleged violation under Section 70 of the Tamil Nadu Goods and Services Tax Act and the Central GST Act. PTI contacted the state's Commercial Taxes official, who denied that the department had sent any GST notice to any pani puri vendor. However, he confirmed that a notice was sent to a hotel in Kanniyakumari (a town in Tamil Nadu) asking the enterprise to register under the GST. "The notice circulating in social media was sent to a hotel vendor in Kanniyakumari in December last year. The 'to address' was found to be handwritten, and the remaining content was typed out," the Commercial Taxes Department official told PTI. The official further added that the notice had been misrepresented and some users had altered the 'to' address. "It was only to inform the vendor to get his registration certificate, come under the GST purview and acquire a GST number to which the vendor also agreed. This was the primary agenda. But, some users had altered the 'to address'," the official said. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the GST department had issued a notice to a hotel owner in Kanniyakumari, and the 'to address' part was edited to include the 'pani puri vendor'.

title: PTI Fact Check: Man in viral video slapped outside court is Munawar Faruqui's friend Sadaqat Khan; 4-yr-old old clip shared in name of stand-up comedian
content: New Delhi, Jan 7 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video circulating on social media claims to show stand-up comedian Munawar Faruqui being slapped by a bystander while being escorted by policemen on a motorcycle. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk has found this claim to be false. The man in the video was Sadaqat Khan, a friend of Faruqui, who was arrested alongside him in 2021 for allegedly hurting religious sentiments during a show in Indore. The four-year-old video has been misleadingly shared on social media with the false claim that it features Faruqui. Sadaqat Khan, an engineer, was arrested on January 2, 2021, a day after Faruqui and four others were detained. He was taken into custody when he visited the district court in Indore, where the others were being produced. Claim A Facebook user shared on January 4 a video and claimed that it showed standup comedian Munawar Faruqui being arrested and taken on a motorcycle by policemen. "Comedian Munawar Faruqui, who used abusive language against the gods and goddesses, was first thrashed by the general public. After that, a lawyer stopped him and slapped him three times," read the caption of the post. Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of the post. Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across several other social media posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archive links can be found here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video published by NDTV on February 11, 2021. The news channel carried the same video as shared on social media. Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of the post: According to the details published by the channel, the person in the viral video was Sadaqat Khan, who was arrested along with Munawar Faruqui in connection with a case linked to "insulting Hindu Gods and Goddesses" during a stand-up event in Indore in 2021. Below is also a combination image showing that the video shared on social media was the same as the one shared by NDTV in February 2021. The video also made it clear that the man in the video was not Munawar Faruqui. In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found a report published by Bar and Bench on February 10, 2021. The feature image of the report matched with the visuals of the viral video. Here's the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the person arrested and beaten up in the viral video was not Munawar Faruqui, but his friend Sadaqat Khan.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old earthquake videos from Taiwan and Nepal falsely shared in name of January 7 quake in Tibet; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 7 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A 6.8-magnitude earthquake rocked the region of Tibet on January 7, whose tremors were felt in several parts of Nepal, India and Bhutan. Soon after, two video were shared on social media, with users claiming that they showed the impact of the earthquake. One of them showed building swaying and half-tilted due to tremors while the second one showed people running towards the street for safety. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found that old and unrelated clips were shared on social media, falsely linking them to the January 7 earthquake in Tibet. On the morning of January 7, a 6.8-magnitude earthquake struck Tibet's Dingri County, near the Nepal border, claiming several lives and leaving behind a trail of destructions, including collapsed buildings and uprooted trees, bringing the normal life in the region to a standstill. Earlier the earthquake was reported to be 7.1 on richter scale, however, reports later stated that the magnitude of the earthquake was 6.8. The Desk cross-checked the veracity of the social media posts. Here's what we found: Claim 1: A social media user shared a video of a damaged building, claiming it to be from the aftermath of the earthquake that hit Tibet. "#BREAKING: A magnitude 7.2 #earthquake just hit China, Taiwan, Nepal, and India," read the caption of the post. Here's the link and archive link of the post: The Desk analysed the video using InVid Tool Search and extracted several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found a YouTube video published by Sky News on April 3, 2024. The content in the YouTube video matched the viral clip. However, the description stated that the video of the tilted building was from Hualien in Taiwan, where a 7.4-magnitude earthquake earlier last year, causing massive destruction. Here's the link and screenshot of the YouTube video: Below is a combination image, which shows that the content in the viral video is the same as that of the YouTube channel. According to the details published by Sky News, at least nine people died and more than 1,000 were injured after 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck the island in April 2024. The video published by the channel showed the quake causing thrashing waves in a swimming pool, while another video captured a 10-storeyed structure called the 'Uranus Building' in Hualien, being thrown dramatically off-kilter by the quake and appearing to be on the verge of collapse. Claim 2: Another user shared a video, claiming that it showed the aftermath of tremors hitting a roundabout in Nepal, in which people can be seen rushing towards the street in panic. Here's the link and archive link of the post: The Desk ran the video through the InVid Tool Search and extracted keyframes. By running these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk discovered a YouTube video uploaded on the official channel of the Nepal Daily, Setopati, on April 30, 2015. Here's the link and screenshot of the post: The video featured visuals identical to the viral clip, which made it clear that it was from the April 2015 earthquake in Nepal that killed thousands of people. Below is a combination image highlighting the same: To corroborate the details, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a news report by The Guardian, published on April 30, 2015. The feature image of the report matched with the visuals of the viral video, and it stated that it showed the moment when earthquake hit the Tripureshwor district of southwest Kathmandu, where the powerful tremors brought down a brick structure on a busy roundabout. Here's the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that both the videos were old and unrelated, and were falsely linked to the January 7 earthquake.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Photo of Gandhi family dining at Delhi restaurant shared on social media with false claims; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 8 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A photo of Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi, Sonia Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, along with Priyanka's husband Robert Vadra and his mother Maureen Vadra seemingly at a restaurant was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that they were spotted in Vietnam, just days after the demise of former PM Dr Manmohan Singh. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found the claim to be false. The photo was from their visit to Delhi's iconic Kwality Restaurant on December 22 last year, which predated Singh's demise on December 26. Claim A Facebook user shared on January 3 a photo of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, Sonia Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, along with Priyanka's husband Robert Vadra and his mother, seemingly at a restaurant. Sharing the photo, the user claimed that the photo was from Vietnam, after the demise of former PM Dr Manmohan Singh. "Antonio's family mourning the demise of former PM Manmohan Singh in Vietnam," read the caption of the post. Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of the post. Investigation The Desk ran the photo through Google Lens and found that another user had shared the same photo with a similar caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post. On further scanning the search results, we came across a report by NDTV, published on December 22, 2024. The feature image of the report was the same as the viral image, and the caption stated that it was from the family's outing at Delhi's iconic Kwality Restaurant. Here's the link and screenshot of the report. On further scanning the search results, the Desk found that the same photo, along with several other, was shared by Rahul Gandhi on his Instagram handle on December 22, 2024. "Family lunch at the iconic Kwality Restaurant. Try the Chole Bhature if you go," read the caption of the post. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across several media reports, which stated that Dr Manmohan Singh passed away on the night of December 26 at AIIMS, Delhi. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the photo predated the Singh's demise and was shared on social media with a false claim.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Scripted video of girl confessing to marrying her brother shared on social media with false claim and communal spin
content: New Delhi, Jan 8 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media claimed to show an 18-year-old Hindu woman confessing to marrying her 20-year-old brother. In the video, the woman stated she married her brother and was now pregnant with his child. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was scripted and falsely presented as a real incident with a communal narrative. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on January 4 a video, claiming it showed an 18-year-old Hindu girl confessing to have married her 20-year-old brother. In the video, the girl could be seen stating that she married her brother as they were in love and that she was now pregnant with his child. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across several other social media posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archive links can be found here and here , respectively: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the viral video and found it carried a disclaimer at 9-second timestamp, which read that the video was made for "entertainment purposes only." Here is the screenshot of the disclaimer posted in the video: "This video is purely made for entertainment purposes only. This video has no intention to disrespect or defame based on race, color, ancestry, national origin, ethnic group identification, age, religion, marital or parental status, physical or mental disability, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity or expression," read the disclaimer, with further mentioned a name 'Kanhaiya Singh'. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search, which led us to a YouTube channel with 94.7k subscribers and 235 videos. The description on the user's profile read: "Content Creator | Helping and Expose Prank Videos." Here's the link and the screenshot of the profile: The Desk scanned the YouTube channel and found that the same girl, as seen in the viral video, had featured in other videos too, which looked scripted. Below is a combination image highlighting the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was scripted and was shared as a real incident with a false communal narrative.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Social media posts claiming RBI to release Rs 5,000 currency note are fake; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 9 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ) : A photo was recently shared on social media with users claiming that it showed the 5000-rupee currency note that the Reserve Bank of India was about to release. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found the claim to be fake and baseless. No such announcement has been made by the RBI or the Ministry of Finance. Claim A Facebook user named 'Pathsala Vision' shared a photo on January 6, claiming that it showed the₹ 5000 currency note, that the RBI was set to launch. The caption of the post, originally in Hindi, read: "New note of five thousand rupees to be released very soon; RBI gave information" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran a customised keyword search on Google and found that several other users had shared the same photo with similar claims across social media platforms. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. Below are the screenshots of the two posts: The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google but did not find any report supporting the claim made in social media posts. In the next part of investigation, the Desk scanned the official website of Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and found the list of denominations in circulation, which had no mention of 5000-rupee note. Here is the link to the website and below is a screenshot of the same. Moreover, the Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) section clearly stated that banknotes in circulation were of ₹10, ₹20, ₹50, ₹100, ₹200, ₹500, and ₹2000. Here is the link to the FAQ section and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral posts claiming that the RBI was releasing Rs 5000 currency notes are fake.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: 2024 earthquake video from Japan falsely shared in name of January 7 quake in Tibet; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 9 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video claiming it showed a terrifying scene from Nepal, which experienced powerful tremors after a 6.8-magnitude earthquake struck the nearby Tibet region on January 7. The video showed a cyclist panicking and running for safety after he found himself caught in the midst of a powerful tremor that collapsed one building and violently shook another. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old and unrelated clip from Japan was shared on social media, falsely linking it to the January 7 earthquake in Tibet. On the morning of January 7, a 6.8-magnitude earthquake struck Tibet's Dingri County, near the Nepal border, claiming 126 lives and leaving behind a trail of destruction, including collapsed buildings and uprooted trees, bringing normal life in the region to a standstill. The earthquake was initially reported to be 7.1 on the Richter scale; however, later reports stated that its magnitude was 6.8. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video on January 7, claiming it showed terrifying scene from Nepal, which experienced powerful tremors after a 6.8-magnitude earthquake struck the Tibet region on January 7. The video showed a cyclist running for safety after he found himself caught in the midst of a powerful tremor that collapsed one building and violently shook another. The post garnered 41.6k views. Here are the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across several other social media posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , respectively, and their archive links can be found here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a news report published by Japanese daily 'The Mainichi' on February 8, 2024. The news report carried the same video as shared on social media. Here's the link to the post, and below is the screenshot of the same. It is pertinent to note that the news report carried a range of visuals, capturing the damages caused in the aftermath of the January 1, 2024, Noto Peninsula earthquake. Below is a combination image, which shows that the video shared on social media was the same as the one shared by the Japanese daily. Taking a cue from this, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a YouTube video published by Japan's All-Nippon News on February 2, 2024. The description (translated into English) stated that the video showed horrifying scenes of the ground rolling, houses getting damaged during the January 1, 2024, Noto Peninsula earthquake in Japan. Here's the link to the post, and below is the screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of the cyclist panicking dated back to January 2024 and was from Japan.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of Odisha govt official disrespecting national flag falsely shared on social media as recent in the name of Andhra Pradesh; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 9 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of a man allegedly wiping a table in his office with the national flag. The users claimed that he was the Deputy Registrar of Anantapur, Andhra Pradesh and demanded action against him. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found the claim to be false. The video was of an incident that happened in Odisha's Puri in October 2022. The person in the video was a government official who was detained after a video of him cleaning office furniture with the flag went viral on social media. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on January 2 a video, claiming that it showed an Andhra Pradesh government official cleaning his official furniture with the national flag. "This is Anantapur Deputy Registrar... Share it till his arrogance subsides, see how he is insulting the national flag. This Anantapur is probably from Andhra Pradesh. Such insult of the national flag by an officer is worrying," read an English translation of the caption, originally in Hindi. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk first ran the video through the InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across several other social media posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be found here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a report by Times of India on incident, published on January 13, 2023. The news report mentioned that the person in question in the video was an employee of the Odisha government and was identified as Prasant Kumar Swain. Here's the link , and below is the screenshot of the same: According to the news report, the incident occurred at the Simili Gram Panchayat office under the Konark police area in October 2022. "A meeting was scheduled to be held in the Panchayat office. Just before the start of the meeting, the PEO found dust on the chairs and tables. He brought the national flag from the Panchayat office and started wiping the furniture with it. A ward member had shot the video," a police official had said at that time. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by Odisha local daily 'Odisha Bytes', published on January 12, 2023. The feature image of the report was the same as the viral image, and the description stated that the incident occurred in Odisha's Puri, where a Panchayat executive officer (EO) used the Indian tricolour to clean office furniture. Here's the link and screenshot of the report: The search result further led the Desk to a news report published by Odisha TV on January 12, 2023. According to the report, Prashant Kumar Swain, the Odisha government official, had apologised for disrespecting the Indian national flag. Here's the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of a man cleaning his office furniture with the national flag was from Odisha's Puri, and not Anantpur in Andhra Pradesh. The video was from an incident dating back to October 2022.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Did Narayan Murthy advocate 'limited interaction between boys and girls'? No, viral screenshot of news report is fake
content: New Delhi, Jan 10 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ) : Multiple social media users shared a screenshot of a purported medias report, claiming that Infosys founder NR Narayana Murthy recently argued for limiting interaction between young boys and females. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found that the screenshot was fake and no such article was published by Hindustan Times. Also, no such remark was made by Murthy. The social media posts were shared with a false claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on January 7 a screenshot of a purported article by Hindustan Times, which stated that Infosys founder Narayan Murthy advocated limited interaction between young boys and girls for success. The caption of the post read: "One more Statement of Mr. Murthy. Is Narayana Murthy okay? does not seem to be so." Here is the link and archive link to the X post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran a customised keyword search on Google and found that several other users had shared the same photo with similar claims across social media platforms. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google, but could not find any such article published by Hindustan Times. We, however, came across another report on Narayan Murthy, published by Hindustan Times, on December 16, 2024. The headline of the report read: "Narayan Murthy defends 70-hour workweek idea 'Indians have a lot to do'." Notably, the feature image of this report was the same as that of the viral screenshot, except one discrepancy. The former has a timestamp just above the subhead, whereas the former lacks one. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same: In the next part of investigation, the Desk reached out to Infosys Global PR Team via e-mail. The article will be updated as and when a response is received. In the next part of the investigation, we conducted a customised keyword search on Google, but did not find any report supporting the claim made in social media posts. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post by Hindustan Times where it categorically termed the screenshot as "photoshopped". It also stated that their legal team was actively addressing the matter, and "appropriate legal action would be taken against those responsible for creating and spreading this misinformation". Here is the link of the X post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral screenshot was fake and no such statement was made by Narayan Murthy.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: 2020 video of PM Modi announcing COVID-19 lockdown falsely shared on social media as recent amid HMPV outbreak
content: New Delhi, Jan 11 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ) : Amid some cases of Human Metapneumovirus (HMPV) reported in India, a video was shared on social media with users claiming that PM Modi has announced a 21-day lockdown to curb the spread of the virus. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found that the video dated back to 2020 when PM Modi had announced nationwide lockdown during the COVID-19 outbreak in the country. The five-year-old video was shared on social media as recent with a false claim. In India, at least eight HMPV cases have been detected. Several state governments have heightened their surveillance amid rising cases of respiratory illnesses, especially those due to Human Metapneumovirus (HMPV). Health Minister JP Nadda earlier said that HMPV is not a new virus and asked people not to worry about it. Claim A Facebook user shared a post on January 8, featuring a video message by PM Modi, claiming that he announced a 21-day lockdown amid the Human Metapneumovirus (HMPV) cases reported in the country. Here is the link and archive link of the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk first ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across several other social media posts, which carried the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here , and their archived versions can be found here , here and here , respectively. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google but did not find any report supporting the claim made in social media posts. A statement of this importance would have grabbed the headlines across the country and even worldwide. The Desk then ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across a video of PM Modi from March 2020 announcing 21 days lockdown in wake of the COVID-19 outbreak. It was aired live on the official YouTube channel of PMO India on March 24, 2020. The title of the video read: "PM Modi addresses the Nation on vital aspects relating to the menace of COVID-19" At 9:23 minutes, PM Modi said: "In view of the current situation, the lockdown shall be enforced for 21 days…Which means the next 21 days will be very crucial for us…" Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk found that this was the viral video was extracted from this original video, dating back to March 2020. Below is a combination image, highlighting the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video of PM Modi announcing a 21-day lockdown following the COVID-19 outbreak, dating back to March 2020, was falsely shared as recent in wake of HMPV cases reported in India earlier this month.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Unrelated videos from China and US falsely shared in the name of Maha Kumbh 2025; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 11 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ) : Two videos were recently shared on social media, with users claiming them to be from the Maha Kumbh, which is being held in Prayagraj. One of them showed a fire pot act while the other once displayed a drone show. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found that the two videos were not related to the event. Maha Kumbh2025 is taking place at Prayagraj in UP from January 13 to February 26. The Desk categorically cross-checked the veracity of two social media posts and here's what it found: Claim 1: A social media user shared a video of a fire pot act, claiming it was performed at the Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj. The caption, originally in Hindi, translates to: "This time Kumbh in Prayagraj is historic. So try to participate in this Maha kumbh and cherish some unique memories." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we came across a Facebook post that carried a video from a different angle, which had striking resemblance to the visuals of the viral video. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. The caption on the post read: "Shocking fire pot performance, praise for Chinese intangible heritage" Below is a combination image, which shows that the content in the viral video is the same as that of the Facebook post. Furthermore, on closely examining the viral video we found a text in Mandarin. Below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran one of the keyframes of the viral video along with customised keyword search, which led us to the same video posted on X (formerly Twitter) in September 2024, with the caption stating that it was from China. Here's the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video has been available online at least since September 2024, which makes it clear that it is not related to the Maha Kumbh Mela. Claim 2: Another user shared a video, claiming that it showed preparations of the drone show to be held at Prayagraj Maha Kumbh. The caption of the X (formerly Twitter) post, originally in Hindi, read: "Preparations for the grand drone show to be held at Prayagraj Maha Kumbh" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same. The video shows thousands of drones making different designs in the sky. At 21-second timestamp, it showed a figure seemingly Santa Claus and at 28-second timestamp, it showed two Reindeers. Below is a screenshot of the two figures in the viral video. The Desk first ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across a video uploaded on a channel named 'FOX 4 Dallas-Fort Worth's' (owned by the Fox network) on December 17, 2024. The title of the post read: "Texas holiday drone show breaks record". Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. On further scanning the search results, the Desk found that the video was originally shared by a US-based drone company 'Sky Elements Drones' on its Instagram account on December 6, 2024. Here is the link to the video. We found that this video had striking similarities to the one shared on social media. Below are the combination images showing the same. Hence, the Desk concluded that an unrelated video from Texas was shared in the name of Maha Kumbh.

title: PTI Fact Check: Fake video of people celebrating Justin Trudeau's resignation as Canadian PM shared on social media as real clip; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 12 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video claiming it showed celebrations erupting after Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau announced his resignation on January 6. The users shared a video that showed a huge crowd, seemingly at a club, bursting into celebration as they saw Trudeau's resignation announcement on the screen there.
