In its investigation, however, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video shared on social media was fake. The video was created using a popular meme template and shared on social media as real with a false claim. Meanwhile, it is pertinent to note that, citing 'internal battles within party lines,' Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau announced his decision to step down from the top post on January 6. Trudeau stated that he would continue serving in his office until his Liberal Party could choose a new leader and that parliament would be prorogued—or suspended—until March 24. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on January 7 a video claiming it showed celebrations erupting after Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau announced his resignation. The video showed a crowd of people, seemingly at a club, celebrating after seeing Trudeau's address (specifically announcing his resignation) on a large screen. Here's the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through the InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across several other social media posts, which carried videos holding striking similarities with the viral clip. Those videos, however, did not show Justin Trudeau's resignation announcement, but other global leaders, with the crowd seen cheering in a similar manner. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archive versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a video published by the YouTube channel of UK radio station 'Heart News West Country' on June 17, 2016. The channel carried the same video as shared on social media, with its caption reading, "Fans at Ashton Gate Stadium, Bristol, celebrate England winner against Wales at Euro 2016." Here's link to the post and below is the screenshot of the same. Below, a combination image has been attached, showing that the video shared on social media was the same as the 2016 video by Heart West Country (R). Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by a UK-based news portal 'Bristol Post' on December 5, 2020. "The Bar Goes Wild meme - the real story behind that Ashton Gate Sports Bar video," read the headline of the article. Here's link to the post and below is the screenshot of the same. The report mentioned details about how the Ashton Gate Sports Bar video turned into a meme format, which has been used in different contexts over the years. Further, the search result also led to a YouTube video that taught people how to edit and use the meme template according to their own requirements. Here's link to the post, and below is the screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of people celebrating while watching Justin Trudeau's resignation announcement at a bar was fake.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated photos of Shah Rukh Khan with wife Gauri shared on social media to falsely claim latter converted to Islam in Mecca; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 12 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ) : Multiple social media users shared photos of Bollywood actor Shah Rukh Khan with his wife Gauri Khan, claiming that it was from their visit to Mecca, the holiest place in Islam. Some users also claimed that Gauri had accepted Islam after 33 years of marriage. In its investigation, the Desk found that AI-generated photos were shared on social media with false claims. Neither Khan and his wife visited Mecca in the recent times, nor Gauri convert to Islam. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user, named Ayudhika, on December 31 shared two pictures of superstar Shah Rukh Khan along with his wife Gauri Khan at the holy site of Mecca. The users claimed that the latter had converted as non-muslim's are not allowed for Umrah. The post that garnered 34k views, read: "I thought Gauri hadn't converted. Non - Muslims aren't allowed for Umrah. What am I missing? Why this sudden change of Shahrukh Khan's heart after this?" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk used Google Lens to analyse the photo and found that multiple users shared similar photos. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here , respectively. Below is a screenshot of one of the posts: The Desk closely watched the viral images and noticed that their quality was extremely smooth and texture free, with blurred backgrounds, giving a strong suggestion that they may be fake or AI-generated. Below is a photo highlighting the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the photos through Site Engine, an AI detection tool, which suggested a substantial presence of AI-generated or deepfake content. Below are the screenshots of the results: The Desk ran the viral photos through Hive Moderation, another AI detection website, which suggested substantial presence of AI content. Below are screenshots of the results: The Desk then moved to the second claim made in social media posts, that Gauri Khan had converted to Islam. We ran a customised keyword search on Google, and came across an article by Indian Express, dated October 8, 2024, whose headline read: "When Gauri Khan said she respects Shah Rukh Khan's religion but wouldn't convert: 'My relatives wondered if SRK will change my faith'" Here is the link to the article. "In the first season of Koffee With Karan, Gauri spoke about her decision not to convert. She said, "There is a balance. I respect Shah Rukh's religion, but that doesn't mean I would convert. I believe everyone should follow their own faith, and there should be mutual respect. Shah Rukh would never disrespect my religion either."," read a section of the report. We further scanned the search results, but could not find any substantial report, confirming the claim. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that AI-generated photos of Shah Rukh Khan and Gauri Khan were shared on social media with fake claims.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: This photo of PM Modi wearing wristwatch is AI-generated; shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, Jan 12 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A photo purportedly showing Prime Minister Narendra Modi wearing a wristwatch was shared on social media, accompanied by claims that it was an expensive watch and that he owns a collection of such watches in his residence. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk revealed that the image used in the social media post was AI-generated and falsely circulated as genuine. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a post on January 8, claiming it showed PM Modi trying an expensive wrist watch at his residence. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and found that it shared by several other social media users with the same claim. Two such posts can be viewed here and here , and their archive versions can be found here and here , respectively. The Desk also noticed several users commenting that it was an AI-generated photo. Below are screenshots of two such comments: In the next part of investigation, the Desk examined the photo carefully and noticed several discrepancies, strongly suggesting that it was AI-generated. For instance, the fingers of PM Modi look abnormal, along with the blurred background and a watermark at the bottom right corner of the photo. Below is a photo highlighting the same. PTI Fact Check Desk carefully looked at the viral picture and found Grok written on the lower right hand side of the picture. We then asked Grok for photographs of PM Modi in black coat. Below is a screenshot of the result: We then asked Grok for a picture of the Prime Minister Modi in a black coat with a watch in his hand, below is the result: In the next part, we asked Grok to give a picture with a pen and a watch in his pocket. Below is the screenshot of the result: In the subsequent part of the investigation the Desk using customised keyword asked Grok to create a luxurious showroom in the background of PM Modi's picture. It yielded us the following result. Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the photo through Hive Media, an AI detection tool, which suggested a substantial presence of AI-generated or deepfake content. Below is a screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the photo of PM Modi shared on social media was fake.

title: PTI Fact Check: BJP's Ramesh Bidhuri denies remarks against UP, Bihar people; old and unverified newspaper clipping shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, Jan 13 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Amid rising political temperature in the national capital ahead of the Delhi Assembly polls, a screenshot of an alleged Hindi newspaper report surfaced on social media. The report purportedly quoted BJP leader Ramesh Bidhuri as saying that people from Uttar Pradesh and Bihar should be driven out of Delhi. However, an investigation by PTI Fact Check revealed that the screenshot of the news report was fabricated and was shared on social media with a false claim. Notably, the screenshot has been going viral since 2018. Back then too, Bidhuri had refuted the claim, stating that the statement was falsely attributed to him. Bidhuri is contesting from Kalkaji assembly seat, and faces a three-way contest from Delhi Chief Minister and AAP candidate Atishi, and Congress leader Alka Lamba. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user going by the name 'Ravish Kumar Parody' shared on January 10 a purported screenshot of a news report claiming that BJP candidate from Kalkaji constituency, Ramesh Bidhuri, said the people from Uttar Pradesh and Bihar should be driven out of Delhi. The post gained more than 20k views so far. Here is the link and an archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation: The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found that similar claims were shared by several other social media users. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and its archive versions can be found here and here , respectively. On further investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google but didn't find any news report, substantiating the viral claim. However, the search results led us to an X post by Bidhuri, dated October 13, 2018, in which he clarified that the alleged remarks against the people of UP and Bihar were falsely attributed to him. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Back then, the Delhi BJP unit had also shared an X post on October 13, 2018, stating that the statement attributed to Bidhuri was entirely false and baseless. "The statement is being spread by those who want to divide society for their politics as part of a well-planned conspiracy. It has no connection with BJP or any of its leaders," the BJP Delhi unit said. Here is a link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk contacted Bidhuri for his response on the viral claim, who refuted the screenshot as "fake". "This is fake news spread by the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) on social media. The same news clip was used by AAP leaders in previous elections to malign my image. However, I am in direct touch with the people of my constituency, and they know it's fake," the BJP leader told PTI Fact Check Desk. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral screenshot was fake.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: 2023 video of PM Modi visiting school in Varanasi falsely shared as recent in name of Delhi; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 13 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video was shared on social media with users claiming that PM Modi visited a school in Delhi built by former CM Arvind Kejriwal. The video showed the PM interacting with children in a classroom. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk in its investigation found the video dated back to 2023 from PM Modi's Varanasi visit. The two-year-old-video was shared on social media as recent with a false claim. The viral posts come amid heightened poll campaign by political parties in Delhi, which goes to polls on February 5. The Arvind Kejriwal-led Aam Aadmi Party has put its education model in focus in its campaign, claiming to have built world-class schools in the national capital. Claim A Facebook user shared on January 10 a video, claiming that it showed PM Modi visiting a school in Delhi built by former CM Arvind Kejriwal. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we came across an X post which shared the same video with a similar claim. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is the screenshot of the X post. On further scanning the results, the Desk came across a video on the official YouTube channel of Narendra Modi posted a year ago.The video had a lot of similarities with the viral clip. The title of the video read: "PM Modi interacts with tiny tots during a school visit in Varanasi" Here is the link to the YouTube video, and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk found that the viral video was extracted from this original video, dating back to 2023. Below is a combination image, highlighting the same: Taking a cue from this, we conducted another keyword search on Google and came acrossa report by Republic World, published on December 18, 2023. The report carried the same video as the one viral on social media. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was from PM Modi's visit to Varanasi in December 2023.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Photo of Sheikh Zayed Road in Dubai falsely shared in the name of Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 13 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A photo was recently shared on social media with users claiming that it showed an aerial view of the Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway, which is scheduled to be operational from this year. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found the claim to be false since the photo actually showed Dubai's popular Sheikh Zayed Road, and not the Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a photo on January 10, claiming that it showed an aerial view of the Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway, which is reportedly set to open to the public this year. The user shared the image with the caption: "A view of Kanpur Highway, Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh. New 'Uttar Pradesh' continuously leading on the path of development." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and came across a report by Dubai-based media outlet 'Zawya,' published on May 23, 2023. The article's feature image was the same as the one seen in the viral post. Here's lin k to the article, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting striking similarities between the viral photo and the original image of Sheikh Zayed Road in Dubai. In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a video published by Dubai-based daily Khaleej Times on video-sharing platform Daily Motion. The viral image matched the visuals of a video posted by the channel in 2021, titled "Bird's-eye view of Sheikh Zayed Road." Here's link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image, which shows that the viral video is indeed that of the Sheikh Zayed Road in Dubai. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral image is not from Uttar Pradesh but is of Sheikh Zayed Road in Dubai.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video shared on social media as real visuals of Los Angeles wildfires; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 13 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ) : A video was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that it showed the wildfires across the Los Angeles area. However, an investigation by PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was AI-generated, which was shared on social media as real with a false claim. Wildfires that have ignited across the Los Angeles area have left a trail of destruction, killing at least 24 people and destroying thousands of structures. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video on Jan 12, claiming that it showed the Los Angeles wildfires. "Fire on Los Angeles," read the caption of the post with over 348K views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk first ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across several other social media posts, which carried the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here , and their archived versions can be found here , here and here , respectively. On further analysis of the viral video, the Desk found that the video was created by combining several clips from different angles. We then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found credible news reports featuring the same or similar images. The Desk also noticed several users commenting that it was an AI-generated photo. Below are screenshots of three such comments: Taking cue from this the desk ran some keyframes of the viral video through Wasitai an AI detection tool, which suggested a substantial presence of AI-generated or deepfake content. Below is the screenshot of the results: The Desk ran the other keyframes through Hive Moderation, another AI detection website, which suggested substantial presence of AI content. Below are screenshots of the results: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was AI-generated.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Clipped video of skit performed at Lucknow school in 2022 shared as recent incident from Delhi with false communal claim; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 13 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video of a skit performed by schoolchildren was circulated on social media, with users claiming it was from a school in Delhi CM Atishi's constituency, Kalkaji (South). The users alleged that the video showed a girl dressed as 'Bharat Mata' being forced to recite the 'Kalma' (Islamic prayer) while the crown on her forehead was replaced with a white cloth. Upon investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video dates back to 2022 and is from a school in Lucknow. The video was clipped and shared on social media with a false communal narrative as if it were a recent incident from a Delhi school. The original video depicted children performing a play on social harmony, showcasing the manner of worship across various religions, not just Islamic customs. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) usershared on January 8, 2025 a video, claiming that it showed a girl depicting Mother India, whose crown was replaced with a white cloth to make her recite 'Kalma', an Islamic prayer. The caption of the post, originally in Hindi, translates to: "If you still want a free bus ticket after seeing this, then you should also recite Kalma. This is happening in government schools of Delhi!! Kalma is taught by removing the crown from the head of Bharat Mata and placing a white cloth on it. This school is in Atishi area, this is the Kejriwal model of Delhi schools" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk first ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across a 2022 X post by Sudarshan News. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same Below is a combination image, which shows that the content in the viral video is the same as the one shared by the news channel in 2022. On further scanning the search results, we came across an extended 2.18-minute version of the viral video, which was shared by the official X handle of Lucknow Police on August 15, 2022. The caption of the post, originally in Hindi, read: "The entire video of the play presented by small children for communal harmony has been propagated in a wrong manner by some anti-social elements and a criminal act has been committed to spread communal hatred. Strict legal action will be taken against such people." Below is a screenshot of the X post. In another X post the Lucknow Police released a statement, it mentioned: "Video going viral on social media regarding a programme being conducted by children in a school under Police Station Bazarkhala area." This made it clear that the video was from a school in Lucknow, not Delhi. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was a clipped version of a video from a school play in Lucknow, which dated back to 2022.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: 2021 video of jewellery recovered in Vellore robbery case falsely shared as recent seizure from Tirupati priest's residence; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 14 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ) : A video was shared on social media with users claiming that it showed a huge recovery of gold jewellery from the residence of a Tirupati temple priest. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation found that the video dated back to 2021 and showed ornaments recovered by the police, that was stolen in a burglary case at a jewellery showroom in Vellore, dating back to December 2021. The three-year-old video was shared on social media as a recent incident with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on January 8 a post claiming that around 128 kg of gold was recovered from a priest's residence in Tirupati. The caption, originally in Hindi, read: "128 kg gold caught at priest's house in Tirupati.150 crore cash. 70 kg diamonds. Now think about those who give money and jewellery in the temple. If any brother has money, get a girl from a poor family married. Instead of donating in the temple, it is better to do Kanyadaan, get a girl from a poor family married. Do not give money in the temple, the priests eat it up" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is the screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we came across several posts, carrying the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, we came across a video posted by 'Jaya Plus' on their official YouTube channel in December 2021. The post carried similar visuals to the viral video. The English text in the title of the video read: "...Vellore | 15 kg Gold Stolen From Jewellery Store" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking cue from the title, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant news publications and came across an article by The Indian Express posted in December 2021. The headline of the article read: "Tamil Nadu: Burglary at Vellore's Jos Alukkas cracked, jewellery worth Rs 8 crore recovered" Here is the link to the article. "With an arrest on Monday, police claimed to have cracked a December 15 burglary at a popular jewellery showroom in Vellore and recovered 15.9 kg of stolen gold and diamonds worth Rs 8 crore from a burial ground in Odukathur. The police said they had analysed 200 pieces of footage from the streets near the Jos Alukkas showroom in Thottapalayam and found the accused, V Teekaraman, loitering around on a couple of occasions," read a part of the article. Furthermore, the feature image of the news report was similar to the visuals of the viral video circulated on social media. Below is a combining image, highlighting the same. The Desk also came across an X post, shared by Tamil Nadu Police on December 21, 2021. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. "15.9 kg of gold jewellery worth Rs 10 crore looted at Vellore Jose Alukkas jewelery shop was found by Vellore district special forces within 5 days of the incident, Tamil Nadu Director General of Police/Commissioner Mr. C.Sailendra Babu E.K.P., was highly praised by him," read a rough translation of the post, originally in Tamil. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was from Vellore, dating back to December 2021.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Mock drill video falsely shared as real fire incident in Maha Kumbh area of Prayagraj; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 14 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video was recently shared on social media with users claiming that a massive fire broke out at a hospital in Maha Kumbh mela area in Prayagaraj, resulting in eight casualties. The video showed police personnel seemingly carrying out firefighting operations with hi-tech equipment. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found the claim to be false. The video actually showed a mock drill in the Maha Kumbh area, as part of the department's preparedness for the Kumbh, which was shared on social media as a real incident with a false claim. The Maha Kumbh 2025 began in Prayagraj on January 13 amid chants of bhajans and slogans. The inaugural day of the Mela was marked by the Paush Purnima bathing festival, during which millions of devotees converged at the sacred Sangam for a holy dip. The event will conclude on February 26. Reports suggest that over 60 lakh devotees visited the Maha Kumbh area on the first day of the Mela. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on January 12 a video of officials engaged in a firefighting operation at Maha Kumbh Nagar in Prayagraj. The user claimed that a massive fire broke out at a hospital situated in the Maha Kumbh Nagar premises, and the firefighting operation was being carried out in response to the incident. The text plate running on the video also claimed eight casualties in the incident. Here is a link , archive link to the post, and below is the screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that the same the same video was shared by several other users with the same claim. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archive versions can be found here and here , respectively. On further investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google, but didn't find any news report substantiating the viral claim. However, the search results led to an X post by the official handle of 'Kumbh Mela Police UP 2025,' which was in response to a now-deleted X post, which carried the same video. The authorities clarified that the video was of a mock drill conducted by Uttar Pradesh Fire Service Department earlier, ahead of the commencement of the Maha Kumbh 2025. Here is a link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk also found an X post by the Fire & Emergency Services, Uttar Pradesh Police, which stated that the video was of a mock drill conducted on December 27, 2024. "Do not spread rumors based on misleading facts," it added. Here is a link to the post and below is the screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim circulated with the viral video was fake. The video was of a mock drill conducted by the Fire & Emergency Services, Uttar Pradesh Police, on December 27, 2024.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Edited video shared on social media to falsely claim AAP's Awadh Ojha made remark against Manish Sisodia; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 14 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): Amid the rising poll temperature in Delhi ahead of the Assembly polls, a video of AAP leader Awadh Ojha was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that he called former Delhi Deputy Chief Minister Manish Sisodia "a coward". Users shared the video, claiming that Ojha, the AAP candidate from Patparganj Assembly segment, made the remark in response to a media query on why Sisodia was not contesting from the seat, despite his previous winning record. However, an investigation by PTI Fact Check Desk found that an edited video was shared on social media with a false claim. Two different portions of Ojha's conversation with NDTV were combined to create the viral video. Delhi will go to polls on February 5, and the counting of votes will be taken up on February 8. The Aam Aadmi Party has announced Awadh Ojha as its candidate from Patparganj seat, while Manish Sisodia will be contesting from Jangpura assembly segment. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on January 12 a video of AAP's Patparganj candidate, Awadh Ojha, and claimed that it showed making remarks against former Delhi Deputy Chief Minister Manish Sisodia. "AAP-DA candidate from Patparganj, Avadh Ojha, says that liquor minister Manish Sisodia, who was jailed in the liquor scam, ran away from Jangpura because he is coward and did not fulfill his promises. Well Awadh Ojha is right. After coming out of jail, Sisodia's face has also lost colour," read a rough translation of the caption, originally in Hindi. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google but didn't find any news report substantiating the viral claim. However, the search results led to an X post by NDTV, dated January 8, 2025, wherein the news channel published the full interview of Ojha. Here is the link to the post, and below is the screenshot of the same. In the video published by NDTV, at the 53-second mark, Ojha recited an idiom (loosely translated as): "Those who have not faced battles in their lives are either unfortunate, have broken their vows, or have fled from the battlefield." The remark by Ojha was in response to a query on his political entry and now contesting the upcoming Delhi Assembly polls, and not on Manish Sisodia, as claimed in the viral posts. The Desk further watched the video and noticed that at 1:46-minute, the reporter posed the question on Sisodia to Ojha, which was there in the viral video. To the question, Ojha replied: "He did not leave the seat, he gave it to me because he was also connection to the field of education and I also wanted to work on the same direction. So, I requested him to give the seat to me (to let me contest from that seat)." In the next part of investigation, the Desk reached out Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) for its response on the edited video, shared on social media. "Our Patparganj candidate Awadh Ojha's morphed video reflects their (BJP's) sheer desperation—they cannot compete in the politics of work, so they stoop to such tactics. The people of Patparganj know that even after Manish Sisodia's arrest, not a single task for them came to a halt. From jail, he ensured the construction of roads, badminton courts, streetlights, and met the needs of the area's residents," the party told PTI. "People from across India and the world now look up to Delhi's government schools for inspiration and Patparganj, the cradle of Delhi's education revolution, has always stood resolutely with Manish Sisodia through every adversity. It is now witnessing the baton pass to one of India's finest educators," the party added. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an edited video was shared on social media to falsely claim that Awadh Ojha made remarks against his party colleague Manish Sisodia.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Social media posts claiming 'Indian Hindu' arrested for trying to start blaze in Los Angeles neighbourhood are fake; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 15 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video was recently shared on social media with users claiming that it showed an Indian Hindu named Bhuvesh Patel being arrested for allegedly trying to start a fire in Woodland Hills, a neighbourhood in Los Angeles which is already reeling under the wildfires, with the intention of looting the blaze-hit areas. An investigation by PTI Fact Check Desk, however, found that the person arrested was a Mexican national and he was held on a felony probation violation. The video was shared on social media with false claims. According to reports, Juan Manuel Sierra-Leyva, a Mexican national residing in the US illegally, was arrested last week after being chased by local residents in Woodland Hills. These residents reportedly saw him using a blowtorch to ignite old Christmas trees and debris shortly after the wildfires began spreading on Thursday (January 9). Sierra-Leyva, who is being held on a felony probation violation, has not had his prior conviction details publicly disclosed by the Los Angeles Police Department (LAPD). Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on January 11 a video, claiming that it showed the Los Angeles Police Department (LAPD) officials apprehending an Indian Hindu, named Bhuvesh Patel, for trying to start a fire in the Woodland Hills area of Los Angeles. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found that similar claims were shared by several other social media users. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archive versions can be found here and here , respectively. In the next part of investigation, the Desk ran the video through the InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across a Times Now news report published on January 13. Here is the link to the news report, and below is a screenshot of the same. According to the news report, the suspect identified in connection with the Woodland Hills incident was Juan Manuel Sierra-Leyva, an illegal immigrant from Mexico. "He is currently in custody on a probation violation and has not been charged with arson yet," the report added. Further, the search result also led the Desk to a news report by Fox News, published on January 13. The report identified the accused as an illegal immigrant from Mexico, Juan Manuel Sierra-Leyva. Here is the link to the news report, and below is a screenshot of the same. The news report stated, "Los Angeles police took the man into custody after a group of local residents grabbed him near the Kenneth Fire, allegedly carrying a blowtorch, according to video from Fox 11 Los Angeles. He is shown holding a torch head and a yellow fuel tank before being tackled to the ground by at least five residents." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the man arrested in Woodland Hills was a Mexican national, and not an Indian Hindu.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: 2022 video from Karachi falsely shared as Muslims performing 'call to prayer' during Los Angeles wildfires; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 15 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video was recently shared on social media with users claiming that it showed a group of Muslims in Californiaperforming'Azaan' (Islamic call to prayer) during the Los Angeles wildfires. However, an investigation by PTI Fact Check Desk revealed that the video dated back to 2022 and was related to a fire that broke out in a supermarket in Karachi, Pakistan. The old and unrelated video was shared on social media as recent with a false claim. Wildfires that have ignited across the Los Angeles area have left a trail of destruction, killing at least 24 people and destroying thousands of structures. Claim A Facebook user shared on January 12 a post claiming that a group of Muslims in Californiaperformed'Azaan' during the ongoing Los Angeles wildfires. "America is making every possible effort to deal with the uncontrollable fire in the US state of California and the new technology seems to be failing and helpless. In such a situation, the Muslims there are praying to their Lord "Allah" to get rid of this disaster!! The residents there are raising the voice of Azaan," read a rough translation of the caption, originally in Hindi. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we came across an X (formerly twitter) post, dating back to June 3, 2022. The caption of the post read: "In Karachi yesterday, a supermarket near Jail Chowrangi, was on fire. An experiment was carried out to extinguish fire by group Azan. It didn't work." Here is the link and archive link to the X post and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk noticed that this was the video carried in the 2022 post was the same as the viral clip. Below is a combination image, highlighting the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by Dawn, dating back to June 1, 2022. The headline of the report read: "Fire at departmental store's basement near Karachi's Jail Chowrangi leaves 1 dead, 3 unconscious." Here is the link to the report. "A person died and three fell unconscious from inhaling of smoke after a fire broke out in the basement of a well-known departmental store near Jail Chowrangi in Karachi on Wednesday, police said," read a section of the report. Furthermore, a video report by UNewsTV also featured the same visuals as the viral clip, stating that the fire incident occurred at Jail Chowrangi in Pakistan's Karachi. Here is the link and below is a screenshot of the same. On further scanning the search results, we came across a video posted by Pak Exclusive TV on their YouTube in 2022, whose title read: "Fire in Karachi I Fire broke out in the warehouse of a superstore near Jail Chowrangi | Chase Up" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk noticed similarities between the visuals of the report and the viral clip, which have been highlighted in the combination image below: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dated back to 2022 and is from Karachi, Pakistan.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: 2023 photo of house that survived Lahaina fire falsely shared in the name of Los Angeles wildfires; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 16 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A photo was recently shared on social media with users claiming that it showed a house that was saved from wildfires in Los Angeles, while its neighbourhood was completely destroyed, because it had the holy Quran inside it. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found that the photo dated back to 2023 and showed a house that had survived the fire that broke out in Lahaina, Hawaii back then. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a post on January 13, claiming that it showed a house survived the wildfires in Los Angeles since it had the holy Quran inside it,while the entire neighbourhood was destroyed. The post, originally in Hindi, read: "Surely, Allah is the Almighty and the Ever-Living!. Look at this photo and say Subhanallah. According to Al Jazeera, a Muslim in Los Angeles had a sacred Quran in his home. So Allah saved him from a great disaster. While all the houses around him were burnt down." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through Google Lens and found that several other users had shared the same photo with a similar claim. Two such posts can be viewed here and here and their archived versions can be found here and here , respectively. In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a BBC report, dated August 22, 2023, whose headline read: "Hawaii wildfires: The red Lahaina house that survived Maui fires". Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. We found that the feature image of the report was similar to the viral photo. Below is a combination image highlighting the same. "Mr Millikin and his wife learnt that the whole neighbourhood had been caught in the blaze and would likely burn down. But the next morning, aerial footage showed their house was intact…Mr Millikin and his wife said they are unsure exactly what saved their home. Two years ago, the couple purchased the 100-year-old property that used to be a bookkeeper's house for employees of a sugar plantation," read a part of the report. On further scanning the search results, we came across a video report by CBC News,dated August 24, 2023, whose title read: "How a nearly 100-year-old "miracle house" survived the Lahaina wildfire." Here is the link to the video report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Another report by Honolulu Civil Beat mentioned what saved the miracle house from the Lahaina wildfire. The report mentioned: "During renovations, Millikin installed a commercial-grade steel roof, something that definitely would have provided better protection from flying embers than shingles. At first, Millikin thought this might have made the biggest difference in why his home was spared. But Michael Wara, the director of the Climate and Energy Policy Program at the Stanford Wood Institute for the Environment, said it was likely the Millikins' decision to dig out the existing landscaping directly surrounding the house and replace it with river stones that made the biggest difference." Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral photo dated back to August 2023, and was falsely shared in the name of Los Angeles wildfires.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: 2024 video of firefighter plane crashing in Chile falsely shared as recent in the name of Los Angeles wildfires; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 16 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video was recently shared on social media with users claiming that it showed a firefighter plane crashing on a highway and burstinginto flames, while tackling theLos Angeles wildfires. However, an investigation by PTI Fact Check Desk revealed that the video dated back to 2024 and showed a firefighter plane that exploded after hitting an overhead cable while tackling a blaze in Chile. The old and unrelated video was shared on social media as recent with a false claim. Wildfires that have ignited across the Los Angeles area, have left a trail of destruction, claiming at least 25 lives and destroying thousands of structures. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a post on Jan 11, claiming that a firefighter plane crashed while battling the wildfires in Los Angeles, California. The post, which garnered 937 views, read: "Terrifying: Watch the haunting moment firefighting planes crash in the fiery apocalypse of Los Angeles amidst the relentless California fires." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we came across several posts, carrying the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be viewed here and here and their archived versions can be found here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a video by Al Jazeera posted on their official Instagram account on January 16, 2024. The caption of the post read: "Video from Chile shows a small plane exploding as it crashed onto a highway.⁠ The crash claimed the life of the pilot and at least four people were injured." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk noticed that this was the same video as the one shared on social media, but with a mirrored one. Below is a combination image, highlighting the same: In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by Daily Mail, published on January 16, 2024. "This is the horrifying moment a firefighter plane explodes after hitting an overhead cable while tackling a blaze in Chile. Spaniard Fernando Solans Robles, 58, was killed as he and a colleague were mobilised to deal with a blaze near an aerodrome in Talca in central Chile. Footage of the tragedy showed the plane exploding into a ball of flames and coming down beside a busy motorway after hitting the power cables," read a portion of the article. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video dated back to January 2024, and was falsely shared in the name of Los Angeles wildfire.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Social media posts falsely identify 'IITian Baba from Maha Kumbh' as ex-Brahmos engineer convicted for espionage; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 16 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A photo of a man was recently shared on social media with some users claiming that he was Nishant Agarwal, an alumnus of IIT Ropar and aerospace engineer at Brahmos, who was sentenced to life in prison for becoming a spy for the Pakistan's Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI). However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Dek found was the person in the photo was Abhey Singh, a self-styled holy man who claims to be a former aerospace engineer from IIT Bombay, and is now popular as 'IITian Baba'. Singh as wrongly identified as ex-BrahMos Aerospace engineer Nishant Agarwal, who was sentenced to life imprisonment in June 2024, for spying for Pakistani's spy agency ISI. The photo was shared on social media with a false claim. The social media claims emerged soon after news channels interviewed the 'IITian Baba' at the ongoing Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj, where he claimed that he had done aerospace engineering from IIT Bombay. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on January 13 a photo of a man claiming that he was Nishant Agarwal, a former engineer at Brahmos, who was sentenced to life imprisonment on charges of spying for Pakistan's ISI. Here is the link and archive link to the post with over 120k views, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the photo through Google Lens and found a similar claim made by a Facebook user. Here is the link and archive link to the post. On further scanning the search results, we found the original video published by News18 on January 12, 2025, from which the viral screengrab was taken. "Mahakumbh 2025: लाखों का पैकेज छोड़ बने संन्यासी, IIT वाले बाबा के जादू करते ही Reporter हुआ..!|N18K," read the title of the video report. Here is the link to the YouTube video, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk watched the video in which the man identified himself as Abhey Singh and claimed that he completed aerospace engineering from IIT Bombay, later went into photography and then left everything for spirituality. Singh revealed that he was born in Haryana and spent four years studying aerospace engineering at IIT Bombay. After that, he went into the "arts side" and pursued a Masters in Design. In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find out Nishant Agarwal, as mentioned in the viral social media posts. The search results led the Desk to a report by Hindustan Times on June 3, 2024, which stated that Nishant Agarwal, working as a BrahMos Aerospace engineer, had been sentenced to life imprisonment on charges of spying for Pakistan's ISI. The report also mentioned that he had studied at National Institute of Technology, Kurukshetra, and was not an IIT-Ropar graduate, as mentioned in the viral claim. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk also compared the image of the viral 'IITian Baba' with that of Nishant Agarwal. The comparison confirmed that the two were different individuals. During the investigation, the Desk found another post by the same X user on January 14, a day after he shared the viral post. In this post, the user clarified that the earlier post was a response to a tweet validating godmen by stating that even IITians become godmen. "It's meant to highlight that IITians become ISI agents too," the user added, along with the link to a Hindustan Times report on Nishant being sentenced to life imprisonment. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk reached out to the public relations department of IIT Bombay to verify the claim made by "IITian Baba" about his graduation from the institute. Falguni Banerjee, Public Relations Officer of IIT Bombay, confirmed that Abhey Singh, popularly known as "IITian Baba" following his visit to the Mahakumbh, is indeed an IIT Bombay graduate. She also verified that Singh pursued aerospace engineering at the institute from 2008 to 2012. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Abhey Singh, aka 'IITian Baba', was falsely identified as ex-Brahmos engineer Nishant Agarwal.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of foreign tourist falsely shared to claim Bill Gates visited Varanasi's Kashi Vishwanath temple recently; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 16 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video was recently shared on social media with users claiming that it showed Microsoft co-founder and former CEO Bill Gates visiting the Kashi Vishwanath Temple in Varanasi. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the person in the video, claimed to be Gates, was actually a foreign tourist. The social media posts were shared with a false claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on January 14 a video claiming it showed Microsoft co-founder and former CEO Bill Gates visiting the Kashi Vishwanath Temple in Varanasi. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through the InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that the same video was shared by several other users with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archive versions can be found here and here , respectively. Some users had also shared the video (viral since December 2024), claiming it to be from Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj. Here is a link to one such post. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google but didn't find any substantial report, corroborating the viral claim. Had gates visited India, the news would have grabbed the headlines. The Desk also scanned the social media handles of the former Microsoft CEO, but did not find anything about him visiting India recently. The last time Gates posted anything about his visit to India was in March 2024. On his website 'Gates Notes', he wrote a blog dated March 5, 2024, detailing about his experience of visit to India. Here is the link to the blog and below is a screenshot of the same: To further corroborate the claim made on social media, the Desk contacted the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, which termed the claim as false. "This claim is false," the Media Relations Department of Gates Foundation told PTI Fact Check in an email response. During the investigation, the Desk geolocated a keyframe of the viral video and found that it was from Manikarnika Ghat in Varanasi. Here is the link to the Google Maps location, and below is the screenshot of the same. The combination image below highlights that the viral video was also from Varanasi's Manikarnika Ghat. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the person seen in the viral video was falsely identified as former Microsoft CEO Bill Gates.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Photo of Prayagraj civic body display board at Maha Kumbh reading 'PDA' falsely shared linking it to Samajwadi Party's slogan; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 16 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A photo of a display board, with "P.D.A. Mahakumbh Prayagraj 2025" written on it, was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that the government promoted the opposition's narrative by writing 'PDA'. The photo was shared to insinuate that the 'PDA' written on the board promoted Sajawadi Party's slogan. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found that the PDA written on the display board actually meant 'Prayagraj Development Authority'. The photo was shared on social media with a fake claim. For the unversed, 'PDA' is an acronym tossed by Akhilesh Yadav for 'Picchde, Dalit, Alpsankhyak' (backwards, Dalits and minorities) in 2023. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on January 11 a photo of a display board with 'PDA Mahakumbh Prayagraj' written on it and claimedthat the BJP-led UP government was promoting the opposition's (Samajwadi Party's) slogan of PDA, which stands for 'Picchde, Dalit, Alpsankhyak'. The post that garnered 28.2k views, originally in Hindi, read: "For the first time I saw that the government is promoting the opposition's issue...This is called Ganga Jamuni Tehzeeb" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and found that another user had also shared the same photo with a similar claim. The link of the post can be found here and its archive link can be viewed here. On further scanning the search results, we came across a post by an X handle named'Prayagraj Development Authority', shared on December 10, 2024. The post carried the same photo as the one shared on social media. The caption of the post read: "To welcome millions of devotees in the upcoming divine, grand, new Maha Kumbh, the PDA is engaged on a war footing to decorate the roads, parks and squares of the city, for which 33 projects have been completed, the remaining work will also be completed before the PM's visit to Prayagraj on December 13." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. On analysing the viral photo carefully, we found 'Prayagraj Vikas Pradhikaran' logo on the top left corner. The same has been highlighted in the image below: We then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across its website. The Desk found that the logo on the banner was the same as on the official website of Prayagraj Development Authority. Here is the link to the website and below is a screenshot of the same. In the subsequent part of the investigation, the Desk contacted the office of the District Magistrate of Prayagraj, seeking a response on the viral claim. DM's OSD Narendra Kumar told PTI Fact Check that 'PDA' mentioned on the board meant Prayagraj Development Authority. "P.D.A means Prayagraj Development Authority, it has nothing to do with any government, if you zoom in on the picture, our logo is on the left side, on which Prayagraj Vikas Pradhikaran is clearly written along with the logo," he told PTI Fact Check. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the photo of the banner was shared on social media with a false claim.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: 2021 clip of police raid at Andheri bar raid falsely shared as recent, linking it to Aaditya Thackeray; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 17 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video was recently surfaced on social media, with users claiming that a cafe owned by Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray in Mumbai's Andheri was raided. The video showed women coming out of what appears to be a secret basement while covering their faces. Upon investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video dated back to December 2021 and was falsely shared as recent with fabricated claims linking it to Aaditya Thackeray. The video actually pertained to a raid at a bar in Mumbai's Andheri and had no connection to Aaditya Thackeray. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video on January 8, claiming that a raid was conducted at a café owned by Aaditya Thackeray in Mumbai's Andheri. The video showed several women coming out of a secret basement. "Raid in Udhav Thackeray son Aditya Thackeray's Cafe in Andheri Mumbai found large underground Treasure," read the caption of the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we came across another similar post, carrying the same video. The post can be viewed here and its archive version can be found here . The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a PTI report carried by The Print. The headline of the report read: "Sena (UBT) leader files police complaint over video 'defaming' Aaditya Thackeray" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. "Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Vinayak Raut on Friday filed a police complaint alleging that a video of a raid at a dance bar is being falsely linked to party colleague Aaditya Thackeray, an official said. According to the official, the purported video was shot at a dance bar in Mumbai's area. It shows a few women emerging from a cavity created inside the premises after police action. However, the text superimposed on the visual claims that the place is a "cafe" owned by Aaditya Thackeray, Raut said in his complaint," read a part of the report. Another report by NDTV stated that 17 women were rescued during a raid at Deepa Bar in Mumbai's Andheri in December 21. Here is the link to the report titled, "17 Women Rescued From Secret Basement Of Mumbai Dance Bar: Police". Below is a screenshot of the report. India Today also reported the incident on Dec 13, 2021. The headline of the report read: "Cops rescue 17 women hidden in secret room at Mumbai bar during late-night raid" Here is the link to the report. "The social service branch officials of Mumbai Police were shocked to find 17 women hiding in a secret room at a bar in Andheri, Mumbai, during a recent raid on a bar. Initially, nobody could be found. However, after 15 hours, the police found the secret room adjacent to a green room, where the women were hiding. The secret room had AC and ventilation and was stocked with food, water, and cold drinks for the girls to survive long hours. The cops rescued the girls and filed FIR against 20 people," read a portion of the report. On further scanning the search results the Desk found a video by News Tak posted on their official YouTube page in 2021, whose title read: "Mumbai Bar Raid: Raid in the secret basement, even the police team was surprised to see, this is how the business used to run." The Desk similarities between the 3-year-old video and the viral clip. Below are some combination images highlighting the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk accessed the FIR copy of the case, filed at Andheri Police Station. We scanned the entire copy, but did not find any mention of Aaditya Thackeray in it. Below are screenshots of the FIR: The Desk used Google Lens to translate the entire complaint in the FIR, which was in Marathi, but there too, did not find any mention of Aaditya Thackeray. It mentioned the names of 28 people, including 17 women found during the raid. In the next part of the investigation,the Desk checked Aaditya Thackeray's election affidavit, whichmade it clear that he did not own any commercial property in Andheri. Below is a screenshot of the affidavit. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dated back to 2021 and had no connection to Aaditya Thackeray.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: PUMA changed brand signage to 'PVMA' to onboard PV Sindhu as brand ambassador; social media posts falsely link it to Virat Kohli
content: New Delhi, Jan 17 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): Social media was recently abuzz with reports of sports brand PUMA India changing its the spelling of its brand signage in various stores to 'PVMA'. Meanwhile, some users shared a video in which a man explained that the company made the move as a gesture in honour of Indian cricketer Virat Kohli. The video also featured a photo in the bottom which showed a PUMA store with the changed name spelling. An investigation by PTI Fact Check Desk found that the company rebranded its signage to 'PVMA' in honour of its latest collaboration with badminton star and two-time Olympic medallist PV Sindhu. The social media posts were shared with a false claim. Notably, PUMA India expanded its sporting portfolio by partnering with Sindhu in a multi-year collaboration. Also, it is important to mention here that Virat Kohli is also a prominent ambassador of the brand in India. Claim A Facebook user shared on January 14 a video, in which a man claimedthat PUMA India changed its name spelling to'PVMA'in honour of Indian cricketer Virat Kohli. The caption of the post read: "Puma Changed Their Name From U To V It's Dedicate To Their Brand Ambassador Virat Kohli" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we came across several posts, carrying the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. In the next part of investigation, the Desk scanned the social media handles of PUMA and came across a post on PUMA India's Instagram page, which featured PV Sindhu, along with the hashtag 'PVMA'. The caption of the post mentioned 'PVMA' as their hashtag, it read: "Smash? Harder. Soar? Higher. Roar? Louder. Greatness? UNLEASHED. Welcome to the PUMA fam, @pvsindhu1. #PVMA #PUMAxPVSindhu" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. In another Instagram post by PUMA, PV Sindhu was seen wearing an athleisure with 'PVMA' written on it. The link and archive link of the post can be found here and below is the screenshot of the same. In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a News18, published on January 14. "Why Has Puma Changed Its Spelling To 'PVMA' On Store Boards?" read the headline of the report. "In a striking move, Puma has announced renowned badminton player PV Sindhu as its brand ambassador. To commemorate this partnership and honour PV Sindhu, the company temporarily replaced the 'Puma' signage with 'PVMA' at numerous stores," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. We also came across another report by Times of India, whose headline read: "Why did PUMA rebrand itself as PVMA ?" "Ahead of announcing the partnership, PUMA India initiated a unique campaign by temporarily altering its iconic signage at select stores across the country. For nearly a week, "PUMA" transformed into "PVMA," symbolising the brand's dedication to Sindhu and the sport she has elevated on the global stage. This bold gesture sparked widespread excitement online, amplifying anticipation for the partnership." Here is the link to the report. In the next part of investigation, the Desk reached out to the Corporate Communications Team of PUMA India, which confirmed that the move was made in honour of PV Sindhu, with whom the brand signed a multi-year collaboration. "We have launched badminton icon PV Sindhu as our brand ambassador and the temporary signage change was a tribute to her, as part of her launch," Puma India told PTI Fact Check in an email response. They also shared with the Desk the press release which was issued on January 13 which mentioned that the brand changed its signage at several of its stores for nearly a week as a gesture to celebrate the legendary PV Sindhu. "Ahead of the announcement, PUMA India launched a never-done-before activation wherein the sports brand made a serious move by changing its brand signage at several of its stores across the country for close to a week. The brand name 'PUMA' was changed to 'PVMA', as a massive gesture to celebrate the legendary Sindhu. This big move created ample buzz on the internet over the last few days," read a section of the press release. Below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Puma India temporarily changed its name spelling to 'PVMA' at several stores in India in honour of its collaboration with Sindhu.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Is 'Enrog Egg' real? No; hoax product, launched by parody company, shared on social media as new tech revolution
content: New Delhi, Jan 18 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): Social media was recently abuzz with reports of American energy company 'Enron' launching the 'Enron Egg', a white egg-shaped tabletop device touted as a micronuclear reactor that can power a home for 10 years. Meanwhile, the PTI Fact Check recently received a social media post link on WhatsApp with the request to verify its veracity. The post featured a video of Enron 'CEO' Connor Gaydos announcing the launch of 'Enron Egg' and detailing its features. In its investigation, the Desk found that the claims made in the social media post to be fake. After Enron went bankrupt, its name and logo were purchased by a content creator who specialises in satire in the year 2020. The parody company "launched" a hoax product, which was shared as genuine on social media. Claim The PTI Fact Check received on its WhatsApp Number +91-8130503759 an X (formerly Twitter) post, which featuredthe viral video claiming that the 'Enron Egg' will power homes for up to ten years. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the video through the InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that the same video was shared by several other users with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archive versions can be found here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, we came across an X post by Enron on their official page, dated January 7, 2025. The video posted on their X handle elaborated about 'Enron Egg', featuring the company's new 'CEO' Connor Gaydos, who claimed that the Egg was the world's first micronuclear reactor for residential suburban use. In the five-minute video, Gaydos, playing the Enron CEO, claimed the Enron egg was going to revolutionise the power industry Here is the link to the X post and below is a screenshot of the same. We also came across the link to the company's website, which was mentioned in the thread of another X post by the company. The 'Terms of Use and Conditions of Sale' section of the website mentioned that the website is 'First Amendment protected parody' and is for 'entertainment' purposes only. "The information on the website about Enron is First Amendment protected parody, represents performance art, and is for entertainment purposes only," read a portion of the 'Terms of Use and Conditions of Sale' section. Here is the link to the 'Terms of Use and Conditions of Sale' section and below is a screenshot of the same. Moreover, 'The Enron Egg' section on the website mentioned the option of 'prebooking', for which the user was required to give his email ID. Here is the link to the page and below is a screenshot of the same: On following the process, the Desk received a reply on email which read: "Hi, there! We understand that trust is earned, not given. Together we can move on from the past and into the future. That's why we're committed to an open and authentic path forward. We are focused on developing breakthrough solutions tailored to your needs, powered by a revitalized Enron dedicated to elevating standards in the industry." Below is a screenshot of the email response received by the Desk: On clicking the video screenshot mentioned, it redirected us to the Instagram page of the company – with 15 posts and 195k followers. However, no price was mentioned anywhere. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google that yielded us several reports terming the 'Enron Egg'as "totally fake". The headline of one such report by Forbes, published on January 7, 2025, read: "Meet The 'Enron Egg,' An At-Home Nuclear Reactor That's Totally Fake" Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. "As CES product launches flood the internet faster than you can say consumer tech, you may have come across the "Enron Egg," a micro nuclear reactor that promises to power your home for 10 years straight. But don't cut ties with your electric company just yet. Enron, the company infamous for its massive accounting scandal and eventual collapse, hasn't made a comeback. The Enron Egg is a hoax from a parody company of the same name," read a section of the report. Another headline of an article by Gulf Business read: "April Fool's comes early as fake Enron Egg grabs attention" "The Enron Egg, described in over-the-top detail, allegedly featured heat-resistant casing designed to withstand "extreme temperatures," a "closed-loop cooling system," and an integrated chip for "24/7 monitoring by Enron's nuclear management facility. The parody extended to a CES-style product launch video, complete with a charismatic fake CEO, Connor Gaydos, pacing on stage in front of a massive screen displaying the oversized egg," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the article. In the next part of investigation, the Desk tried to find details about the company's background and why it went bankrupt. We came across a January 7 report by Daily Mail, whose headline read: "Is the Enron egg real? Mini nuclear reactor that claims to power houses for years explained." The latter part of the report mentioned that Enron, once a leading energy company of the United States, filed for bankruptcy in December 2001 after news of widespread internal fraud was made public on October of that year. "Some of the company's top executives were sent to prison, and the event was the largest bankruptcy reorganization in US history at that time. Today, Enron's infamous downfall is known as the 'Enron scandal," read a section of the report. "Publicly available documents show that an Akansas-based LLC called The College Company, co-owned by Gaydos, bought the Enron trademark for $275 in 2020. Gaydos then launched Enron.com December 2, 2024, 23rd anniversary of the company's bankruptcy filing, along with a press release and a promotional video. Though the website and launch materials appeared legitimate at first, closer inspection reveals their unserious nature. Gaydos unveiled himself as the 'new CEO' on December 9, 2024, and has featured in a series of parody videos since then," it added. Here is the link to the report: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a hoax product, launched by a parody company, was mistaken as a real technological revolution on social media.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Photos of Akhilesh Yadav taking dip in Ganga in Haridwar falsely shared as from Maha Kumbh 2025; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 18 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A collage of three photos of Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, immersed in a waterbody at night, was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that he participated in the ongoing Maha Kumbh Mela and took a holy dip in the sacred Sangam. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found that the photos were from Yadav's visit to Haridwar, Uttarakhand, on the occasion of Makar Sankranti on January 14 this year. The photos were shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) sharedon Jan 15 a collage of three photos of Akhilesh Yadav half immersed in a waterbody at night, and claimed that he took a holy dip in Sangam at the Maha Kumbh Mela 2025. "He may have come to the Kumbh Mela in the dark to atone for his sins. Did you think that if you come to the Kumbh Mela like a thief when no one is there, you wouldn't know," read a rough translation of the post, originally in Kannada. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk first ran the collage through Google Lens and found that another user had shared it with a similar claim. Here is the link and archive link to theFacebook post. On further analysing the search results, we came across an X post by Akhilesh Yadav on Jan 14, 2025, which carried the same three photos as shared in the social media posts. In the post,Yadav mentioned that he took the blessings of Ganga on the festival of Makar Sankranti. The caption of the post, originally in Hindi, read: "Took blessings of Mother Ganga on the sacred festival of Makar Sankranti." Here is the link to the X post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant news reports and came across a PTI report carried by NDTV on Jan 14, whose headline read: "Akhilesh Yadav Takes Holy Dip In Ganga On Makar Sankranti" Here is the link of the report and below is a screenshot of the same. "Samajwadi party chief Akhilesh Yadav took a dip in the Ganga river in Haridwar on the occasion of Makar Sankranti on Tuesday…Though the former Uttar Pradesh chief minister did not disclose the location, party sources said he took the dip in Haridwar," read a section of the report. In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find out whether Yadav visited the Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj, and came across a report by ABP News published on January 17, whose headline read: "महाकुंभछोड़करअखिलेशयादवनेहरिद्वारमेंक्योंकियागंगास्नान? सपासांसदनेबताईवजह (Why did Akhilesh Yadav leave Mahakumbh and take bath in Ganga in Haridwar? SP MP gave the reason)." Here is the link to the report. The report quoted Samajwadi Party SP MP Afzal Ansari saying that after the Ganga flows from Haridwar, garbage gets mixed in it, hence instead of Kumbh, Akhilesh Yadav took bath in the Ganga in Haridwar. Another report by Dainik Bhaskar quoted Yadav saying that he would visit Sangam when Mother Ganga calls him. Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Akhilesh Yadav's photos from his Haridwar visitwere shared in the name of Maha Kumbh.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video falsely claims Virat Kohli performed kirtan in this social media post; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 19 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video circulating on social media recently claimed to show Indian cricketer Virat Kohli performing kirtan. The video depicted Kohli playing a harmonium while others in the background appeared involved in recitation. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk revealed that the video was AI-generated and shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video on January 17, claiming that it showed star Indian cricketer Virat Kohli performing kirtan. The user shared the video with the caption (loosely translated into English): "After marrying Anushka Sharma, brother (Virat Kohli) has forgotten his real game (cricket) and started doing all this—engaged in performing bhajan and kirtan." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google but didn't find any substantial report corroborating the viral claim. Had such a video been real, the news would have grabbed headlines. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk examined the video carefully and noticed several discrepancies, strongly suggesting that it was AI-generated. For instance, the fingers of the former Indian cricket team captain look abnormal, and the background appears blurred. Below is a photo highlighting the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the video through the InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Wasitai (an AI detection tool), the Desk found substantial evidence of AI-generated or deepfake content in the video. Below is the screenshot of the results: The Desk also ran the keyframes through 'Sightengine,' another AI detection website, which similarly suggested substantial evidence of AI content. Below are screenshots of the results: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was AI-generated.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated photo of Saif Ali Khan with Kareena Kapoor Khan shared on social media with false claim; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 19 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported image of Bollywood actor Saif Ali Khan with his wife and fellow actor Kareena Kapoor Khan, seemingly at a hospital bed, was shared on social media. The post insinuated that the two were clicked at Mumbai's Lilavati Hospital, where Saif is currently admitted for injuries sustained after being stabbed multiple times at his residence earlier. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk, however, found that the photo shared on social media was fake. An AI-generated image was shared on social media as real with a false claim. It is pertinent to note that Bollywood actor Saif Ali Khan sustained multiple injuries after an intruder attacked him with a knife during an alleged burglary attempt at his residence in Mumbai in the early hours of January 16. Khan, 54, was taken to Lilavati Hospital, where he underwent surgery and is currently recovering. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a purported photo of Saif Ali Khan and Kareena Kapoor Khan on January 19, with a claim that they were clicked in a hospital where Saif is currently recuperating from the injuries he sustained after being stabbed multiple times at his residence in Mumbai. The user shared the image with the caption, "Get well soon, Saif Ali Khan." Here is a link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through Google Lens and found that the same image was shared by veteran Bollywood actor-turned-politician Shatrughan Sinha. In an X post, the Lok Sabha MP from Asansol, while sharing the image, appealed to the masses to stop the "blame game" and let the law take its own course as things are moving in the right direction.
