"We certainly appreciate our CM & HM, Maharashtra Devendra Fadnavis, for his concern & remedial measures. Let's not complicate the matter further," he added. Here is a link to the post, along with a screenshot of the same: On further analysis of Sinha's post, the Desk noticed several users commented that the image shared along with it was AI-generated. Below are screenshots of two such comments: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk examined the photo carefully and noticed several discrepancies, strongly suggesting that it was AI-generated. For instance, the background in the image is blurred, and a Grok (an AI-generative artificial intelligence chatbot) logo was also seen placed at the bottom right corner of the photo, confirming that the image is AI-generated. Below is a photo highlighting the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the image through 'Sightengine,' another AI detection website, which also suggested the substantial presence of AI content. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the photo of Saif Ali Khan and Kareena Kapoor Khan shared on social media was fake.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: 2024 video of stone pelting on train falsely shared as recent incident of attack on Prayagraj-bound train; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 19 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video was recently shared on social media with users claiming that it showed a train which was allegedly attacked with stones while it was on its way to the ongoing Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj. However, an investigation by PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video dated back to July 2024 and showed a stone pelting incident on the Bhusawal-Nandurbar passenger train in Maharashtra's Jalgaon. The old and unrelated video was shared on social media as recent with a false claim. The video was shared on social media following a recent stone pelting incident on the Tapti Ganga Express carrying Maha Kumbh devotees while it was passing through Jalgaon. Claim A Facebook user shared on January 14 a video, claiming that it showed stone pelting on Tapti Ganga Express carrying devotees to Maha Kumbh Mela in 2025. The caption of the post, originally in Hindi, read: "Passengers of Tapti Ganga Express going to Maha Kumbh were attacked. Windowpanes of AC coaches were broken" Here is the link and archive link of the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we came across another similar post, carrying the same video. One such post can be found here and its archived version can be viewed here . On further scanning the search results, we came across a report by Free Press Journal, published on July 13, 2024, whose headline read: "Maharashtra Viral Video: Stones Pelted AtBhusaval-Nandurbar Passenger Train By Unidentified Miscreants In Jalgaon" Here is the link to the article and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk noticed that the feature image of the news report matched the visuals of the viral clip. Below is a combination image, highlighting the same. A section of the report read: "Tensions prevailed in Jalgaon district of Maharashtra as an unidentified group of miscreants pelted stones at Bhusaval-Nandurbar passenger train. Reports said that the mob gathered at the railway tracks and began pelting stones at the train, due to which a state of panic struck among the minds of the passengers." In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search that yielded a report by TV9 Marathi. The title of the report originally in Marathi, translates to: "Incident of stone pelting on express in Amalner of Jalgaon" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. We also found an X post by Divisional Railway Manager- Mumbai Division of Western Railway, shared on July 13, 2024, regarding the incident. "Railway is committed to ensuring the safety and security of passengers. In the said incident, the RPF in-charge of Amalner started an inquiry by registering AN CR 473/2024 against an unknown person under Railway Act 154. Amalner GRP has also been informed about the incident for necessary legal action," read the post. Here is the link to the post and below is the screenshot of the same. We also found a report by Hindustan Times, dated January 14, whose headline read: "Stone pelted at train carrying people for Mahakumbh, passenger shows damaged windowpanes". Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. "A video of a passenger showing damaged windowpanes caused by stone pelting surfaced on social media. According to the passenger, an unknown person threw stones at the train, causing significant damage to the windowpane of the Tapti Ganga Express from Surat, which was headed for Mahakumbh in Uttar Pradesh's Prayagraj," read a section of the report. Another report by NDTV, dated January 12, 2025, quoted the Chief Public Relations Officer of Central Railway saying that a stone was thrown on the train coming from Surat Udhan, near Jalgaon. "A stone was thrown on this train, coming from Surat Udhna, near Jalgaon. In this case, immediate action was taken by the Railway Protection Force and four teams were deployed on the train. A complaint has also been lodged," said Swapnil Neela, Chief Public Relations Officer of Central Railway. The title of the report read: "Stones Thrown At Train Headed To Prayagraj In UP For Maha Kumbh" Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a video dating back to July 2024 was shared on social media as recent, falsely mentioning it as a recent stone pelting incident on a train in Jalgaon.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: 2023 video of man blowing conch shell at Gang Aarti in Varanasi falsely shared in the name of Maha Kumbh Mela 2025; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 19 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ) : A video of a saint blowing conch shell ('shankh') was recently shared on social media with users claiming that it was from the inauguration of the ongoing Maha Kumbh Mela 2025 in UP's Prayagraj, where the 'shankh' was blown for a record 2:49 minutes. The video also showed President Droupadi Murmu and UP Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath in attendance at the event. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video dated back to 2023 and showed the start of Ganga Aarti in Varanasi. The two-year-old video was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on January 16 a video, claiming that conch shell was blown for a record 2:49 minutes at the inauguration of Maha Kumbh Mela 2025 in Prayagraj. The caption of the post read: "At Kumbhmela's inaugural function, the shankh was blown non-stop for 2 minutes 49 seconds - this is perhaps a world record. Modern science will tell you how powerful is this exercise for our lungs & the wave of positivity with this Shankhanad. This is the power of Sanatan" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through the InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found that the same video was shared by several other users with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archive versions can be found here and here , respectively. On further analysing the viral video, we found a watermark on the top right corner of the video which mentioned 'VK News' on it. President Droupadi Murmu and UP CM Yogi Adityanath and President Murmu were also visible in it. Below is a screenshot highlighting the above mentioned findings. Taking a cue from this, the Desk scanned the YouTube channel of VK News and found that the original video was posted in Feb 2023. The title of the video, originally in Hindi, read: "A devotee blew such a conch at the Ganga Ghat. President Murmu also kept watching." Here is the link to the original video and below is the screenshot of the same. Below are two screenshots, which shows that this was the same as the viral video. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and found the external version of video uploaded on the official YouTube channel of the President of India on February 13, 2023. "President Droupadi Murmu attends Ganga Aarti at Varanasi," read the title of the video. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same. We also found a report by Hindustan Times, dated February 13, 2023, whose headline read: "President Droupadi Murmu visits Varanasi, offers prayers at Kal Bhairav, Kashi Vishwanath temples, witnesses Ganga aarti." Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. "Soon after offering prayers at Kashi Vishwanath temple, the President, accompanied by the Governor and the chief minister, also inspected the entire Kashi Vishwanath Corridor till the Ganga banks," read a section of the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video was from Varanasi, dating back to February 2023.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: No, RBI has not banned cheques written in black ink; fake claim shared in name of media report
content: New Delhi, Jan 20 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a purported news report by a leading English daily claiming that the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) had announced that cheques written in black ink would not be accepted starting January 1, 2025. The alleged report suggested that the move was aimed at "enhancing security features" and "preventing fraudulent activities." However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the news report screenshot was fabricated, and no such story was published by the English daily. The social media posts were shared with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on January 16 a text, claimed to a be a report by Times of India published on January 14, 2025. It claimed that the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) had issued a guideline stating that cheques written in black ink would not be accepted from January 1, 2025. Here are the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found that similar claims were shared by several other social media users. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archive versions can be found here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google but did not find any such report published by the Times of India. Further, through the search results, the Desk also tried finding an official announcement on the RBI's website regarding the alleged new rule, but no official communique was found either. Moreover, as part of the investigation, the Desk also reviewed the FAQ section of the RBI website and found a question under the section "Cheque Truncation System." The question detailed what care customers should take while writing cheques. In response, the bank stated, "The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has not prescribed specific ink colours to be used for writing cheques." Below is a screenshot of the response provided by the bank for the above query: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a text with false claims was falsely attributed to Times of India. No such guideline was issued by the Reserve Bank of India.

title: PTI Fact Check: Social media posts claiming Sandhya Marawi is India's first woman porter are false; details inside
content: Delhi, Jan 21 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A photo of a woman carrying heavy luggage on her head was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that she was the first lady coolie of India. The users shared the post identifying the woman as 31-year-old Sandhya Marawi, who took up her husband's job after his death in 2016. However, an investigation by PTI Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false as Marawi is not the first woman porter. Another woman named Manju Devi took up reportedly the job of porter at Jaipur Railway Station in 2013, four years before Sandhya started working as a porter at Katni Railway Station. Claim A Facebook user shared on January 8 a photo of a woman, claiming that she was the first woman coolie of India. The user identified the woman as 31-year-old Sandhya Marawi, who took up her husband's job in 2016 after his death. "Salute to women power. 31-year-old lady coolie Sandhya Marawi, badge no 36. Her husband died in 2016, so she took up her husband's job, who used to work as a coolie, to feed her three small kids and her mother-in-law! She works at Katni Railway Station in Jabalpur. She is the first lady coolie," the user shared the photo with the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the photo through Google Lens and found a similar claim made by a Facebook user. Here is a link and an archive link to the post. On further scanning the search results, the Desk also found that similar posts with the same claims have been making rounds on social media platforms over the years. Two such posts can be seen here and here , with their archive versions available here and here . In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found multiple media reports which identified the woman in the frame above as Sandhya Marawi, who took up the job as a coolie after the death of her husband in 2016. A report by The Better India news portal on May 28, 2018, identified Marawi as a native of Kundam village in Madhya Pradesh who travels over 40 km daily to get to her work "station." Notably, the report mentioned that Marawi was neither the first woman coolie nor the only one presently working in the male-dominated job, "but her determination to help her family is indeed inspirational." Further, the search results about the first female coolie also led the Desk to reports covering Manju Devi. A report by The Indian Express on May 28, 2018, stated, "Manju Devi acquired her deceased husband Mahadev's porter license no. 15 and took to the demanding task of hauling luggage of passengers at the Jaipur Railway Station in 2013." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. During the investigation, we also came across a YouTube video posted on a channel named Context, run by the Thomson Reuters Foundation. The video, published on June 5, 2013, depicted the story of Manju Devi, who, after her husband's death, entered into the occupation of a coolie to support her family. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk also found a YouTube video by NDTV posted on Mar 20, 2013, reporting about Manju Devi. The video's headline read: "Manju, Rajasthan's first woman coolie (porter)." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: While it cannot be claimed that Manju Devi was India's first woman porter (coolie), but it was confirmed that she started working as a woman porter in 2013, way before Sandhya took up the job of porter in 2017. The Desk subsequently concluded that Sandhya Marawi could not be termed India's first woman porter. The social media posts were shared with a false claim. We found during the investigation that this claim has been time and again shared on social media over the past several years. PTI Fact Check has debunked this claim earlier too, back in January 2023. Click here to read the report.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Photo of video content creator falsely linked to Kota student death incident and shared in social media post with false claim
content: New Delhi, Jan 21 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A photo of a woman was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that she was a 17-year-old IIT-JEE aspirant who recently died by suicide after jumping from a five-storey building in Kota, Rajasthan. The users shared the post two days after media reports surfaced about the death of a 16-year-old who died of suicide in Kota on January 17. This present incident marked the fourth such incident in Kota this year. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found the social media claims to be false. The photo shared in the social media post was of a video content creator named Jyoti Thakur. She also posted a video on social media denying the claim. Also, the student who died in Kota on Jan 17 this year was a male student, not a female, as claimed in the social media post. Claim: An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a photo on January 19, claiming that a 17-year-old IIT-JEE aspirant died by suicide after jumping from a five-story building in Kota, Rajasthan. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the image through Google Lens and found multiple users shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here . Archive links can be found here and here , respectively. Further scanning the results, we found the same photo shared from an Instagram handle with the username Jyoti Thakur. Here is the link to the profile, and below are the screenshots of the same: As seen in the screenshot above, Thakur shared the photo on December 14, 2024, which was recently shared in the name of Kriti Tripathi. Also, the Desk noticed that Jyoti had posted her latest Instagram post on the night of January 20, 2025 (till the time of writing this article), whereas the claim was shared on social media on January 19, thereby making it false. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google about the recent suicide incident in Kota and came across a PTI report carried by Deccan Herald on January 18, 2025. According to the report, the deceased who reportedly took his life of suicide is a 16-year-old male student hailing from Rajasthan's Bundi. While, the viral post purportedly claims the deceased to be a female. Here is a link to the report and below is the screenshot of the same. Further, to corroborate the details about if any female student identified as Kriti Tripathi had died of suicide in Kota, the Desk again conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by Hindustan Times on May 10, 2016. Here is a link to the report, and below is the screenshot. According to the report, the deceased Kriti died of suicide after jumping from a five-storey building in Kota on April 28, 2016. She also left a suicide note behind, wherein she urged the Government of India and the Human Resource Development (HRD) Ministry to shut coaching institutes as soon as possible. Moreover, during the investigation, the Desk also came across a video posted by Thakur on her X handle. In the video, she vehemently rejected her association with the viral claim and stated that she has never ever been to Kota and is a native of Himachal Pradesh. Here is a link to the post, and below is the screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Jyoti Thakur, a popular content creator, was falsely identified as Kriti Tripathi, a 17-year-old student who died by suicide in 2016.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Speech video of PM Modi referring to annual vehicle sales in India shared on social media with false claim; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 22 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's speech at the inaugural ceremony of the Bharat Mobility Global Expo 2025 was recently shared on social media, with users claiming he stated that India sells over 2.5 crore cars annually, which exceeds the population of many countries across the world. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk revealed that PM Modi's speech, delivered in Hindi, was misrepresented to falsely claim he referred only to car sales. In his speech, the Prime Minister referred to the sale of all types of vehicles, not just cars. The claim shared with his speech video in the social media post was false and baseless. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a post on January 17, claiming PM Modi stated that India sells over 2.5 crore cars annually, more than the population of most countries. The caption of the post that garnered 41.1k views, read: "India sells over 2.5 crore cars annually—more than the population of many countries! A testament to rising aspirations and strong economic growth." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through the InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found that the same video was shared by several other users with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archive versions can be found here and here , respectively. In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found the original and extended part of the video, uploaded on the official YouTube channel of 'Narendra Modi'. "PM Modi's speech at Bharat Mobility Global Expo 2025," read the title of the video. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. At 4:58 minutes, PM Modi said: "Following the mantra of Make in India, Make for the World, exports are also increasing now. The population of many countries of the world is not as much as the number of vehicles being sold in India every year. Nearly 2.5 crore vehicles being sold in a year shows how the demand is constantly increasing in India. This shows why India is being looked up with so much hope when it comes to the future of mobility." In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search which yielded us a PIB report, dated January 17, which carried a transcription of the PM's speech at Bharat Mobility Global Expo. A section of the release mentioned: "Today's India is full of aspirations, full of youthful energy. We see these aspirations in India's automotive industry. In the past year, India's auto industry has grown by around 12 percent. Following the mantra of Make in India, Make for the World, exports are also increasing now. The population of many countries of the world is not as much as the number of vehicles being sold in India every year. Nearly 2.5 crore vehicles being sold in a year shows how the demand is constantly increasing in India. This shows why India is being looked up with so much hope when it comes to the future of mobility." Here is the link to the PIB release and below is a screenshot of the same: We also found a report by the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM), which highlighted India's growing vehicle demand trend from 2018-19 to 2023-24. The data showed that the country's automobile domestic sales trend in 2023-24 was 2,38,53,463, which included sales of passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, three wheelers, two wheelers, and quadricycles. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. Seeking further confirmation, the Desk spoke to the National Business Editor & Chief of Economic Bureau at PTI, Ammar Zaidi, who said that PM's reference was regarding the sale of all types of vehicles, and not just cars. "PM Modi, in his speech at the Bharat Mobility Global Expo, referred to the sale of all types of vehicles and not just cars," said Zaidi. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that PM Modi's speech was taken out of context and shared on social media with a false claim.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Social media post claiming EAM Jaishankar was 'asked to leave' Donald Trump's inaugural ceremony is baseless; clipped video shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, Jan 22 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video from the inauguration ceremony of US President Donald Trump was recently shared on social media, claiming it showed External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar was asked to leave the event. The video depicted a US administration official approaching the EAM and allegedly requesting him to exit the ceremony. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found this claim absolutely baseless and false. The alleged direction by the US official was, in reality, intended for a cameraperson standing near Dr. Jaishankar during the ceremony. The clipped video was shared on social media with a false claim. It is also noteworthy that Donald Trump was sworn in as the 47th President of the United States on January 20, 2025. Dr. Jaishankar attended the inaugural function as Prime Minister Narendra Modi's special envoy. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video on January 21, claiming it showed External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar being asked by a US authority official to leave from the inaugural ceremony of Donald Trump, as he took oath as the 47th President of the United States. The user shared the post with the caption: "What a shame! Authorities demanding S. Jaishankar to leave the show." Here is the link and archive to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google but did not find any substantial reports corroborating the viral claim. Had the incident actually happened, it would have made headlines. In the next part of investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found multiple keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found a video posted by the official YouTube channel of White House on January 21, 2025. This video showed the complete coverage of President Trump's swearing-in ceremony held on January 20, 2025. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Analysing the video at 34:34-minute timestamp, the Desk found the same visuals that have been shared on social media. The footage showed a female cameraperson standing nearby (or possibly in front of) Dr S Jaishankar to capture the event. Below is a screenshot from the video where the hand of the female cameraperson standing near Jaishankar is clearly visible. As the video progressed, the Desk captured multiple movements of the cameraperson, as well as a lady from the US administration approaching her. The visuals then showed the lady from the US administration seemingly speaking to the cameraperson and requesting her to record the event from behind, as can be assumed from the former's hand gesture. The same sequence of events has been highlighted in the screenshot below: At 35:10-minute timestamp, just after the lady from the US administration left, the female cameraperson could be seen leaving the area near Jaishankar. Below is a screenshot of the cameraperson exiting the scene: The Desk continued to watch the video and found that Jaishankar attended the entire event. Below is a screenshot showing him at the event after Trump concluded his inaugural address. In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found a video from the event, uploaded on the official YouTube channel of Hindustan Times, which showed Jaishankar sitting in the first row as Trump delivered the speech. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from the title of the video, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search on Google and came across a PTI report carried by The Tribune on January 20. The headline of the report read: "'Privileged' to represent India at Trump's swearing-in ceremony: EAM Jaishankar." Here is the link to the report: In the next part of investigation, the Desk checked the official X handle of Jaishankar and found several posts from the event. "A great honour to represent India at the inauguration ceremony of @POTUS President Donald J Trump and @VP Vice President JD Vance in Washington DC today," read the post from after the inaugural ceremony. He also shared several others posts carrying photos of him meeting global leaders at the event. Two such posts can be seen here and here, and below are their screenshots. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a clipped video was shared on social media to falsely claim that EAM Dr S Jaishankar was asked by a US administration official to leave from the US President Donald Trump's inaugural ceremony.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: 2024 video of woman crying after chain snatching in Hardoi falsely shared on social media in name of Maha Kumbh; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 22 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video of a woman crying was recently shared on social media with users claiming that her gold necklace worth ₹ 1.5 lakh was snatched during the Maha Kumbh Mela 2025. However, an investigation by PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video dated back to 2024 from a mass marriage ceremony held in Hardoi, Uttar Pradesh. The woman later gave a written application to the police, informing about the necklace being found at her home. The old and unrelated video was falsely shared in the name of Maha Kumbh Mela. Claim A Facebook user shared a post on January 20 claiming that it showed a woman crying after her gold necklace worth ₹1.5 lakh was stolen during the Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj. The caption of the post, originally in Hindi, read: "This woman's gold necklace worth ₹ 1.5 lakh was stolen in the Kumbh Mela. Now the thing to think about is why did the woman come wearing a gold necklace?" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through the InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found that the same video was shared by several other users with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archive versions can be found here and here , respectively. On further analysing the search results, we came across a video posted by Live Hindustan in 2024. The video featured the same woman as the viral clip. The title of the video read: "Hardoi SamuhikVivah loot: Loot during the CM marriage scheme amidst heavy police force creates stir | Hardoi Police" Here is the link to the video report and below is a screenshot of the same. Below are two combination images which show that the woman in the news report was the same as the one in viral clip. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found a report by News 18, published on Dec 15, 2024. The report's cover image featured the woman's photo as seen in the viral video. The report mentioned: "A robbery was committed with a woman during the MukhyamantriVivah Yojana program in Hardoi." Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. Further, we came across a news report by Uttar Pradesh Times, dated Dec 16, 2024. A section of the report mentioned: "Lakshmi Srivastava, a resident of Barwan village of Lonar police station area, who had come to CSN PG College for her brother-in-law's wedding ceremony, had informed the police that she was going to eat, when an unknown person snatched her gold necklace and fled after pushing her. Based on this information, the police immediately registered a case of robbery and started investigating the incident." Here is the link to the report. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search on Google and found an X (formerly Twitter) post by Hardoi Police, shared on December 15, 2024. The post confirmed that the woman found her necklace at her home. The tweet mentioned: "Regarding the news circulated on certain social media platforms, it is to be informed that on 4.2.2024, the applicant Smt. Laxmi Srivastava, wife of Shivam Srivastava, came to attend the wedding of her brother-in-law in a mass marriage program organized at CSN College under Kotwali City area. While eating food, due to the large crowd, the applicant fell down due to a push. After which the applicant found that the gold necklace was missing from her neck. On receiving the information, the local police inspected the spot and on the basis of the complaint of the applicant Smt. Laxmi Kamal Srivastava, FIR No. 837/24 under Section 303(7) was registered against an unknown person at Kotwali City. In the same sequence, today on 45.2.2024, the applicant Smt. Laxmi Srivastava wife of Shivam Srivastava informed Kotwali City, Hardoi that when the applicant returned to her home from the mass marriage program, she saw that the necklace was at her home, while going to the mass marriage program, the applicant left the house in a hurry without wearing the necklace. A written application has been given by the applicant Smt. Laxmi Srivastava to Kotwali City, District Hardoi regarding the necklace being found at her home and not taking any further action in the above case." Here is the link to the X post and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to 2024 from Hardoi, and was falsely shared in the name of Maha Kumbh Mela 2025.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Social media post claiming Parthiv Patel made remarks on Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma is fake; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 22 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A recent social media post quoted former Indian cricketer Parthiv Patel stating that Virat Kohli didn't want Rohit Sharma to play Test cricketer in his captaincy, fearing that the latter would break his record. However, an investigation by PTI Fact Check Desk found that Patel did not make any such remark, and the social media post was shared with a fake claim. Virat Kohli served as the captain of the Indian Test cricket team from 2014 to 2022, after MS Dhoni retired from Test cricket. He first took on the role during the Border-Gavaskar Trophy against Australia on December 9, 2014. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on January 17 a post, quoting former Indian cricketer Parthiv Patel stating that Virat Kohli did not want Rohit Sharma to play Test cricket under his captaincy. According to the post, Patel stated, "Virat Kohli didn't want Rohit to play Tests under his captaincy because Rohit was equal to Virat in ODIs and T20Is — 3 double hundreds, 11 hundreds in World Cups, and 5 hundreds in T20Is. Virat was ahead of Rohit only in Tests. He was afraid Rohit would be equal to him in all formats." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by a media portal named Cricket Addictor, published on January 18, 2025. The report mentioned that the former Indian wicketkeeper had disassociated himself from the viral claim, stating it to be false. He clarified that the quote regarding Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma was fake and urged people to verify their sources. Here is a link to the report, and below is the screenshot of the same. The Desk also found a social media post by Parthiv Patel. In a statement on X (formerly Twitter), the former Indian cricketer said, "I haven't said this. And this isn't true either. Please check your sources, because they're feeding you very false info." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. In the next part of the investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk also reached out to Patel for his remarks and the copy will be updated as soon as we get his response. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the post bearing a quote from Parthiv Patel is fake.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: 2022 video of Canadian MP Chandra Arya speaking in Kannada in Canadian Parliament shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, Jan 23 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video of Canadian MP Chandra Arya speaking in Kannada in the Canadian Parliament was recently shared on social media with users claiming that he spoke in his first language after filing nominations for the post of Canadian Prime Minister. However, an investigation by PTI Fact Check Desk found that the viral video dated back to May 2022, when he first spoke in Kannada mother tongue in the Canadian Parliament. The old video wasshared on social media as recent with a false claim. Chandra Arya, an Indian-origin Liberal Party MP from Nepean, Ottawa, recently announced his candidacy to become the Prime Minister of Canada following Justin Trudeau's resignation. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a post on January 18, claiming that it showed Canadian MP Chandra Arya speaking in Kannada after filing his nominations for the Canadian PM post. The caption of the post,which has garnered 450.9k views so far, read: "Kannada in Canada!! Canadian MP Chandra Arya officially enters the race to become Canada's next Prime Minister and speaks in Kannada after filing his nomination." Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk conducted a customised keyword search and found that several users had shared the same video with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. We conducted another set of customised keyword searches on Google, but did not find any report corroborating the viral claim. On further scanning the search results, we found Canadian MP Chandra Arya's X post, dated May 20, 2022, where he spoke his first language Kannada in Canadian parliament. The caption of the post read: "I spoke in my mother tongue (first language) Kannada in Canadian parliament. This beautiful language has long history and is spoken by about 50 million people. This is the first time Kannada is spoken in any parliament in the world outside of India." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. This was the same video as the one shared on social media. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same: We also found a PTI report carried by Times of India on May 20, 2022, whose headline read: "Canadian MP Chandra Arya's speech in Kannada in Parliament earns him praise" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to 2022 when Chandra Arya spoke in Kannada in the Canadian Parliament.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: 2024 video of stampede-like situation at Ganga Ghat in Bhagalpur falsely shared as recent in the name of Maha Kumbh Mela 2025
content: New Delhi, Jan 23 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video of a huge crowd, seemingly devotees, immersed in a waterbody was recently shared on social media with users claiming that a stampede-like situation had occurred on the Ganga Ghat in Prayagraj during the ongoing Maha Kumbh Mela. However, a PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found that the video dated back to 2024 and was from Bhagalpur, Bihar. The massive crowd gathered at the Ganga Ghat on the occasion of fourth Monday of the Sawan month. The old and unrelated video was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user on January 15 shared a video, claiming it showed a stampede-like situation on Ganga Ghat in Prayagraj in the ongoing Maha Kumbh Mela. The caption of the post read: "Breaking news.... Stampede at Ganga Ghat...More than 50 devotees escaped drowning...Who is responsible....? Where is the government....?" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we came across an X post by AajTak, dated August 12, 2024, which mentioned that there was a stampede at the Ganga Ghat as devotees in large numbers gathered on the occasion of the fourth Monday of Sawan in Bhagalpur, Bihar. The caption of the post, originally in Hindi, read: "There was a stampede during bathing at the Ganga Ghat on the occasion of the fourth Monday of Sawan in Bhagalpur, Bihar. Due to this, the barricading in the river broke and many women and children started drowning due to reaching deep water. Fortunately, the SDRF team was deployed on the spot and saved everyone's life by jumping into the water in time." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. The visuals of the video report were the same as the clip shared on social media recently. Below are two combination images highlighting the same: On conducting a customised keyword search on Google, we found a report by Dainik Bhaskar, dated August 12, 2024, whose headline read: "Stampede at Ganga Ghat, 50 women rescued: Devotees broke barricades in Bhagalpur and moved ahead; chaos prevailed for 30 minutes" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. On further scanning the search results, we came across another report by Bihar Tak, where the video was uploaded on their YouTube Channel in August 2024. The title of the video read: "After Jehanabad, there was a stampede in Bhagalpur, more than 50 people fell into the river | Bihar Tak" Here is the link and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video dated back to August 2024 and was falsely shared in the name of Maha Kumbh Mela 2025.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Pakistani man, arrested in Japan for molesting a girl, falsely identified as Indian national in social media posts; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 23 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A photo of a person, seemingly in police custody, was recently shared on social media with some users claiming that he was Pramod Rathore, a resident of Haryana, who was arrested in Japan for molesting a girl. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the man in the photo was a Pakistani national named Afzal Muhammad. He was arrested in September 2024for allegedly sexually assaulting a female high school student on a local train in Japan. The photo was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user on January 20, a post allegedly containing an image of an Indian man named Pramod Rathore who was arrested for molesting a high-school girl in Japan. Here is a link and an archive link to the post, and below is the screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to check whetherany Indian national was arrested in Japan in the recent times. However, no credible report was found, reporting any such development. In the next part of investigation, the Desk ran the photo of the accused through Google Lens and found a report published by a media portal named Hindu Post on September 16, 2024. The feature image of the report was the same as the one shared on social media recently. However, the report identified the person as a Pakistani national, who was arrested for molesting a high school girl in train. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Further, the search result also led the Desk to a report by MSN, which also confirmed the accused to be a Pakistani national – 31-year-old Afzal Muhammad. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. According to the report, the accused forced the victim off the train at the last stop, took her into the bushes near the station and sexually assaulted her. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the person in the viral photo was a Pakistani national, and not a Haryana-based individual.

title: PTI Fact Check: Clipped video of Arvind Kejriwal shared on social media to falsely claim he criticised Delhi CM Atishi; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 23 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of Aam Aadmi Party convenor Arvind Kejriwal was recently shared on social media, with users claiming it showed him criticising Delhi Chief Minister Atishi. The video showed Kejriwal allegedly slamming Atishi for not doing any work in his absence (referring to the time when he was in prison). However, the PTI Fact Check Desk, in its investigation, found that a clipped video was shared on social media with a false claim. In the original video, Kejriwal criticised BJP's Vishwas Nagar MLA Om Prakash Sharma, stating that he had not done any work in his constituency in the past ten years. The video has been shared amid the heightened social media campaigns run by the political parties ahead of Assembly polls in the national capital, scheduled to be held on February 5. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on January 20 a video claiming it showed Arvind Kejriwal criticising Delhi Chief Minister Atishi for not doing any work in his absence. A user shared the video with the caption, "That means Kejriwal is clearly saying that in my absence, Chief Minister Atishi Marlena did not do any work. Atishi Marlena is useless; the entire government of Delhi is useless. When Kejriwal himself is admitting that Aam Aadmi Party cannot work, then the people of Delhi should not vote for Aam Aadmi Party." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through the InVid tool search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across a video posted by the Aam Aadmi Party on its official YouTube channel on January 20, 2025. The title of the video read, "Arvind Kejriwal's public meeting in Vishwas Nagar | Delhi Elections 2025 | AAP Delhi." Below is the link and screenshot of the YouTube video. The Desk noticed that this was an extended version of the video shared on social media, as can also be seen in the comparison below: In the next part of investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the video. At 25:50 timestamp, it found the same clip that was shared on social media. The clipping showed Kejriwal stating, "I just came to know, there is a water problem in every colony...is it or not? There is a sewer problem in every colony...is it or not? The roads are broken...is it or not? There is filth all around...isn't it?" However, going through the extended part of the video, it became clearly evident that the dig by Kejriwal was directed towards BJP's sitting MLA from Vishwas Nagar constituency, Om Prakash Sharma. Prior to making the above statement, Kejriwal was giving a reference of Sharma, where he stated, "Sharma fought a lot with us for ten years but did not do any work. Am I wrong?" The same part can be seen at the 25:28-second timestamp. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a selected portion of Arvind Kejriwal's address at a public rally in Delhi's Vishwas Nagar area was clipped and shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2016 video of Kuwait househelp mixing urine in employer's breakfast shared in the name of India with false communal narrative
content: New Delhi, Jan 24 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video, claiming it showed a woman house help allegedly contaminating her employer's food with urine. The users claimed that the house help was a Muslim woman, who worked at a Samajwadi Party leader's home, and was caught mixing her urine in fruit juice before serving it to the latter's family. However, in its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false. The video dated back to 2016 and was actually from Kuwait, where a house help was caught on camera pouring urine into the family's juice before serving it. The nine-year-old clip was shared on social media as recent, with a false communal narrative. Claim An X user shared on January 19 a video, claiming that it showed a house help allegedly contaminating her employer's food with urine. The user shared the video with the caption, "Maid Farida Khatoon was caught on camera mixing her URINE in fruit juice before serving it to her Hindu house owner. The house owner is allegedly a Samajwadi Party leader. When will Hindus realise we are all kaafir to them, our caste, state, language or political ideology don't make any difference." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through the InVidTool search and found multiple keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that the same video was shared by several other users with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archive links can be found here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a report by Metro, a British freesheet tabloid, dated April 26, 2016. The report contained the same video, with its title mentioned as: "Maid is caught on camera sloshing loads of urine into her boss's orange juice." Here is a link to the report, and below is the screenshot of the same. "A Kuwaiti householder got suspicious of what his maid was up to when preparing his breakfast – and captured one of the most vomit-inducing videos ever. The woman calmly pours about AN INCH of fresh, foamy urine into the family's orange juice before bringing it through to be served," read a section of the report. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across multiple reports by Indian media outlets covering the development. Zee News, in its report published on April 27, 2016, also stated that the incident occurred in Kuwait, where a maid was caught on camera adding urine into the family's orange juice just before serving it for their breakfast. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a nine-year-old video, originally from Kuwait, was falsely shared on social media in the name of India.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of vandalism at toll plaza in Dhaka falsely shared on social media in the name of India; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 24 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it showed a group of Muslim men vandalising a toll plaza in India. However, the PTI Fact Check, in its investigation, found that the video was from an incident that occurred in Bangladesh in September 2024.The video was shared on social media, falsely linking it to India. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on January 21 a video, claiming that it showed a group of Muslim men aboard a pickup van engaging in a scuffle with toll plaza officials and later vandalising it. The user shared the video with the caption, "Muslims have opened the toll gate today, tomorrow the gate of your house will be opened like this. There's still time. Congress, which nurtured them along with indie parties, treats these Jihadis too." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through the InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that the same video was shared by several other users as well, with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archive versions can be found here and here , respectively. The search results also led the Desk to a few posts dating back to September 2024, which carried the same video. Here is a link and an archive link to one such post. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google, which led to a report by Dhaka Tribune, published on September 18, 2024. The title of the report read: "Elevated Expressway's Kuril toll plaza vandalized centring pickup van crossing." Here is the link to the report. The feature image of the report matched the visuals of the video shared on social media. The same can be seen in the screenshot below. According to the report, the incident occurred at the Kuril Toll Plaza on the Dhaka Elevated Expressway, where an altercation broke out after a pickup van, carrying 30-40 people, was stopped by toll plaza officials since it was a prohibited vehicle. The brawl escalated further leading to one individual breaking the barrier and another one assaulting the staff. On further scanning the search results, the Desk conducted another keyword search and found a YouTube video uploaded by a local Bangladeshi channel, Channel 24, on September 19, 2024. The video showed a statement from a Bangladesh Highway Authority official who stated that the altercation occurred after the group of men was denied entry despite paying the toll, as access was restricted for safety reasons. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of a group of men vandalising a toll plaza is from Bangladesh, not India.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Rahul Gandhi clicked with his wife and children? No, 2022 photo of him meeting Congress worker's children shared with false claims
content: New Delhi, Jan 24 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A photo of Congress leader and Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi, along with a woman and three children, was recently shared on social media with users claiming that they were his wife and children, and the picture was clicked during a trip. The users also identified the woman as one Jonita Vinci and two of the kids as Nohak and Minak. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found that the photo dated back to 2022, and the individuals accompanying Gandhi were children of Priyanka Nandwana, president of Mahila Congress in Rajasthan's Baran district. Gandhi, during his Bharat Jodo Yatra, met them after Kamakshi – the eldest daughter of Priyanka – expressed her desire to meet him, and also took them on a helicopter ride. The three-year-old old photo was shared on social media as recent with false claims. Claim A Facebook user shared on January 7 a photo claiming that it showed Congress leader Rahul Gandhi with his wife and children, while on a trip. The caption of the post read: "Raul Vinci on tour with his wife Jonita Vinci, son Nohak Vinci, daughter Minak Vinci? This same Rahul Vinci calls Hindus violent animals and the foolish people of India want him to become the Prime Minister. Lies are spread in the whole country. I am a young bachelor leader but he has connections with foreign countries. His wife's father is a drug dealer." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk conducted a ran the image through Google Lens and found that the same photo with a similar claim was shared in August 2024. One such post can be found here and its archived version can be viewed here . Below is a screenshot of the same. On further scanning the search results, we came across a report by Rajasthan Tak which mentioned that Rahul Gandhi met these children from the Nandwana family in Bundi, Rajasthan, and gave them a helicopter ride. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. The viral photo had a striking similarity to the pictures shared in the news report. Below is a combination image highlighting the same. The report carried other photos from the meeting, which can be seen in the collage below: The third photo shows Priyanka Nandwana. Taking cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found a report by ABP Live, dated December 9, 2022. The headline of the report read: "Rajasthan News: Rahul Gandhi fulfilled the promise made to three girl students in 10 days, know here". Additionally, the cover picture of the report was similar the viral photo being shared on social media. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. A section of the report mentioned: "Rahul Gandhi fulfilled the promise made to three students of MP during Bharat Jodo Yatra in just 10 days. Former Congress national president Rahul Gandhi is currently in Rajasthan for his Bharat Jodo Yatra. The yatra entered Bundi district on Thursday. After completing the yatra in Kota, Rahul Gandhi directly reached the helipad built in Gudli, Bundi. Three students from Ujjain, MP were waiting for him there. They had come to take a helicopter ride with Rahul Gandhi." Furthermore, a video report by First Khaber, dated December 9, 2022, stated that Gandhi was enroute from Nainani Farm in Bundi to Sawai Madhopur to celebrate his mother Sonia's birthday, when he learned about Kamakshi's desire to meet him. As Kamakshi was celebrating her 14th birthday, Gandhi fulfilled her dream and also met other children of the family. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the photo dating back 2022 was shared on social media as recent with false claims.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Donald Trump's executive order to end US birthright citizenship doesn't specifically target Indians; posts shared on social media are misleading
content: New Delhi, Jan 24 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): Shortly after his swearing-in as the United States President, Donald Trump signed an Executive Order cancelling the provision of 'citizenship by birth'. Soon after, several social media users claimed that the executive order specifically targeted Indians, and "children born to Indian couples will not be eligible for automatic USA's citizenship". However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found the posts to be misleading. The executive order to end birthright citizenship in the US is intended for immigrants, irrespective of the country, and not Indians in particular. Trump signed an executive order curbing multiple immigration laws, including birthright citizenship that provides automatic American citizenship to anyone born in the country, which stands contrary to the 14th amendment of the US Constitution. The executive order signed by Trump states that a child born in the country will only be granted US citizenship if at least one parent is a US citizen, a green card holder or a member of the US military. Within hours of him signing the executive order to end birthright citizenship for children whose parents lack legal status, he was sued by immigrant and civil rights advocates, including the American Civil Liberties Union. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user on January 21 shared a post, claiming that children born to Indian couples in the United States will not be eligible for automatic American citizenship. The caption of the post, which has garnered 629k views so far, read: "Children born to Indian couples will not be eligible for automatic USA's citizenship. Donald Trump. NRIs should come back to India in protest & contribute in Amritkaal." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk conducted a keyword search on Google and found that several other users had shared the same claim. Two such posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be found here and here , respectively. In the next part of investigation, the Desk reviewed the executive order signed by President Donald Trump regarding the end of birthright citizenship. "Among the categories of individuals born in the United States and not subject to the jurisdiction thereof, the privilege of United States citizenship does not automatically extend to persons born in the United States: (1) when that person's mother was unlawfully present in the United States and the father was not a United States citizen or lawful permanent resident at the time of said person's birth, or (2) when that person's mother's presence in the United States at the time of said person's birth was lawful but temporary (such as, but not limited to, visiting the United States under the auspices of the Visa Waiver Program or visiting on a student, work, or tourist visa) and the father was not a United States citizen or lawful permanent resident at the time of said person's birth," the order read. Here is the link to the document and below is a screenshot of the same. The document also mentioned: "Subsection (a) of this section shall apply only to persons who are born within the United States after 30 days from the date of this order." Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. On further conducting another set of customised keyword search of Google for relevant media reports, the Desk came across a report by CBS News, dated January 20, whose headline read: "Trump signs flurry of executive actions and memos on Day 1" A section of the report mentioned: "Trump also moved to dismantle the longstanding interpretation of the 14th Amendment, signing an order to federal agencies to deny birthright citizenship to children of parents who are unauthorized immigrants or temporary visa holders. The U.S. government has long interpreted the 14th Amendment of the Constitution as granting a right of citizenship for those born on American soil, regardless of their parents' immigration status." Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. Another report by The Indian Express dated January 22, whose headline read: "Trump signs executive order to end US birthright citizenship. Can he do it?" This report discussed the number of immigrants and children who could be impacted by the order. "According to 2024 data by the Pew Research Center, the US foreign-born population reached a record 47.8 million in 2023, an increase of 1.6 million from the previous year. This is the largest annual increase in more than 20 years, since 2000. In 2022, Mexico was the top country of birth for immigrants who arrived in the last year, with about 150,000 people. India (about 145,000) and China (about 90,000) were the next largest sources of immigrants. Venezuela, Cuba, Brazil and Canada each had about 50,000 to 60,000 new immigrant arrivals," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the executive order to end birthright citizenship in the US was meant for illegal immigrants, and not Indians in particular.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of new year celebrations in China falsely shared on social media in the name of Maha Kumbh Mela 2025; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 25 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video of a huge crowd releasing balloons in the sky was recently shared on social media, claiming it to be from the ongoing Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj. However, an investigation by PTI's Fact Check Desk revealed that the video showed New Year celebrations in China. The viral video was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A user named Satyendar Sharma shared on January 16 a YouTube Shorts video, claiming that it showed a huge crowd of Hindus releasing balloons in the sky during the Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj. The text written on the post, which garnered 558 views, originally in Hindi, read: "Jai Shri Ram, crores of Hindus of India together released balloons in the sky". Whereas the caption of the post mentioned that the video was from Kumbh Prayagraj. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through the InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found that the same video was shared by several other users with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archive versions can be found here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports, but did not find any reports that mentioned about any such event taking place at the ongoing Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj. Furthermore, on closely examining the viral video we found a text in Mandarin. Below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword on Google and found a similar video shared on Instagram on January 1, 2025, by a user named 'Sharing Delicacy', with 1 million followers. The caption of the post read: "Happy New Year! 2025" Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same.On further checking the account, we found that the user was based in China. Below is a screenshot of the same. On further checking the account, we found that the user was based in China. Below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image, which shows that the content in the viral video is the same as that of the Instagram post. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted another set of customised keyword search which yielded us several videos, mentioning that the incident happened in China's Nanchang. Below is a screenshot of the same. Also, it is pertinent to note that the Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj officially started on January 13, and will conclude on February 26, while this video dates back to January 1, 2025. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video showed new year celebrations, reportedly in China's Nanchang.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Old and unrelated photos related to Balasore train mishap and Israel-Palestine conflict falsely shared in the name of Jan 23 train mishap in Jalgaon
content: New Delhi, Jan 25 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): Three photos recently circulated on social media, with users claiming they showed the aftermath of the recent train mishap in Maharashtra's Jalgaon, which has claimed 12 lives so far. Two of the photos showed the derailed and crushed bogies of the train while the third one showed multiple bodies, allegedly of those who died in the accident. However, an investigation by PTI Fact Check Desk found that the first two photos were of the Balasore train tragedy, that happened in June 2023 while the third one showed bodies of Palestinians killed in Israeli strikes in December 2023. The old and unrelated photos were shared on social media as recent, falsely in the name of the train mishap in Jalgaon. On January 23, some passengers of the 12533 Mumbai-bound Pushpak Express got off the train after an alarm chain-pulling incident and were run over by the Karnataka Express on the adjacent tracks in Maharashtra's Jalgaon district. Claim A Facebook user named Anshu Baghel shared three photos on January 23, 2025, claiming that they were from the train mishap in Jalgaon that occurred on the same day. "Details of those who died in the train accident in Jalgaon, Maharashtra have been received till now. 1. Radheshyam Bhaiya (Nepal) 2. Nandram BK (Vinayak Achham) 3. Kamala Naveen Bhandari (Solta Kailali) 4. Himu Nandram BK (Vinayak Achham) 5. Jaikala Bhatte Jaigadhi (Kambazar Achham) 6. Mysara Bk (Vinayak Achham) 7. Lachhiram Kannu Paswan (Nepal) 8..... more details...yet to be given," read the caption of the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk categorically investigated the three photos shared in the post. Here's what we found: Photo 1 The Desk ran the image through Google Lens and found that another user had shared the similar pictures with the same claim. One such post can be found here and its archived version can be viewed here . On furthre scanning the search results we found a PTI report carried by The Telegraph Online, dated June 2023, which carried the same photo. The headline of the report read: "Odisha triple train accident death toll rises to 291 as one more victim succumbs." Here is the link to the report, and below is a combination image showing that the viral image was the same as featured in the news report. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a news report by Hindustan, dated June 2023, whose feature image was the same as the viral one. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. Photo 2 The Desk ran the image through Google Lens and found a PTI report carried by NDTV in June 2023, which carried the same photo as the one shared in the social media post. The headline of the report read: "Opposition Condoles Loss Of Lives, Blames Signalling System Failure For Odisha Train Crash" Here is the link to the report and below is a combination image, which shows that the viral image is actually related to the Balasore train tragedy. On further scanning the search results, the Desk found another PTI report carried by Economic Times, whose feature image was similar to the photo in the viral post. The headline of the June 2023 report read: "52 bodies of train accident victims await identification; BMC cremates 2 bodies" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. Photo 3 The Desk ran the image through Google Lens and found the same photo in a report by Reuters, dated December 7, 2023. The report mentioned: "Bodies of Palestinians killed in Israeli strikes on houses lie on the ground at Abu Yousef al-Najjar hospital in Rafah in the southern Gaza Strip, December 7." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the first two pictures in the viral post were related to the Balasore train accident, that happened in June 2023, whereas the third photo was of Palestinians killed in Gaza in an attack by Israel in December 2023.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of MP Police finding woman's body in fridge shared on social media with false communal claim; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 26 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently shared on social media showed several police personnel entering a room where a body was lying near a fridge. The users claimed that a Muslim woman was killed by her Hindu live-in partner and her body was stuffed inside a refrigerator. However, an investigation by PTI Fact Check Desk found that the viral video was of an incident reported in Madhya Pradesh's Dewas, where a Hindu woman was killed her live-in partner, of the same religion. The video was shared on social media with a false communal claim. Claim An Instagram user named Akhtar Naqshbandi on January 24 shared a video, claiming it showed the body of a Muslim woman, who was killed by her Hindu live-in partner, and her body was stuffed inside a fridge. The caption of the post, originally in Hindi, read: "My sisters, if you leave Islam, you will have to lose both your life and faith." The text plate running on the video, originally in Hindi, read: "Sanjay and Gulnaz eloped and got married, they lived in a rented house which was locked for the last four days. When people broke the door and checked everything, they found Gulnaz's body cut into pieces and kept in the fridge." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found that several other users had shared the same claim. One such post can be viewed here and its archived versions can be found here : On further scanning the search results, we came across a report by India Times News, dated January 11, whose headline read: "MP man kills live-in partner, hides body in refrigerator for 10 months, arrested" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. The report also carried some pictures which were similar to the viral video. Below is a combination image highlighting the same. The Desk also found an X (formerly Twitter) post by news agency IANS, dated January 10, whose caption read: "Dewas, Madhya Pradesh: A woman's dead body was found in a house in Vrindavan Dham Colony. The body was found inside a fridge in a locked room. Police are investigating the matter" Here is the link to the post and below is the screenshot. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by Times of India, dated Jan 11, whose headline read: "Decomposed body of woman found 'stuffed' inside refrigerator in locked room in Madhya Pradesh" "For over six months, the body of a murdered woman remained decomposing inside a refrigerator in a rented room in Dewas, Madhya Pradesh, while a family lived just a few feet away, completely unaware of the horror just a few feet away," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. Another section of the report mentioned: "When the neighbors alerted the police about the foul smell, the police arrived at the scene, opened the refrigerator, and found the decomposed body of Pinky alias Pratibha Prajapati, Sanjay Patidar's live-in partner, wrapped in a bedsheet…Police said Pratibha was killed in March 2024. Patidar strangled her during an argument over her insistence on marriage, despite knowing he was already married with children…Police arrested Patidar hours after the body was found…" In the next part of investigation, the Desk contacted Dewas Superintendent of Police (SP) Puneet Gehlot who confirmed that there was no communal angle in the incident. "The deceased is a Hindu, her name is Pratibha Prajapati. There is no communal angle in this entire matter," Gehlot told PTI. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the victim was a Hindu and so was the accused, and there was no communal angle to it.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Fictional advertisement in newspaper claiming govt will ban paper currency from Feb 1 shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 26 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a Malayalam newspaper clipping, claiming it stated that the government will permanently ban paper currency and only digital currency will be allowed from Feb 1, 2025. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found that claim to be fake. The newspaper clipping shared on social media was actually a marketing feature, and the RBI made no such announcement. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user on January 24, shared a post claiming that the government will be banning paper currency and only digital currency will be allowed from Feb 1. The caption of the post which garnered 2414 views, read: "Malayalam Media is filled with news that govt is banning "currency" from Feb 1 and only digital currency will be allowed" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk conducted a reverse image search on Google and found that several users had shared the same post with a similar claim. One such post can be viewed here and its archived version can be found here . On further scanning the search results we found an Instagram post by Asianet News, a Malayalam news broadcaster. "'Good bye note, now digital currency' This is not news, it is advertisement. #advertisement," read the Malayalam translation of the post. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. In the next part of the investigation the Desk Google translated the news report and found that some of the names named in the newspaper clippings called into question the veracity of the assertions. It named Dr Aravind Kumar as RBI governor, Rajeev Singh as Union finance minister, and Dr Anjali Mehra as opposition leader—none of them currently hold the roles mentioned.The article mentioned Nobel laureate Dr Rin Patel lobbying for cryptocurrency; however we discovered that this name was made up. Below is a screenshot of the Google translate result. The Desk also conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found a report by The News Mint, dated January 24, whose headline read: "Kerala dailies print 'news' on end to paper currency, readers fooled by ad" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and found the first page January 24 edition of Mathrubhumi, shared on Kerala sub Reddit. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: "So, I opened today's Mathrubhumi, and it's wild. One article is about an interplanetary football match on Mars—Earth apparently won despite the gravity. Another one celebrates the first anniversary of Kerala's robot minister. And then there's India ditching paper notes for cryptocurrency.I kept looking for a "this is satire" disclaimer or something, but nope. Did I miss a memo, or did Mathrubhumi accidentally time travel? Someone tell me you saw this too," the post read. We then searched for the epaper version of Mathrubhumi, and found a note in the top-right corner stating that the articles were marketing features. The page also carried a disclaimer that read, "Notice: The front-page news presented in the newspaper is fictional, created as part of the promotional campaign for 'The Summit of Future 20205'," hosted by Jain-Deemed-to-be University in Kochi. Below is a screenshot of the same: "This is an imaginative depiction of what the front page of newspaper might look like in 2050. Any resemblance to real events or reports is purely coincidental. The opinions expressed here do not reflect the views of Jain Deemed-to-be University or its affiliated institutions," it added. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the newspaper clipping shared on social media was a fake advertisement.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2021 photo of actor Kunal Kemmu with wife Soha Ali Khan performing puja shared with false claim after recent attack on Saif Ali Khan; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 27 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A photo of Bollywood actors and couple Kunal Kemmu and Soha Ali Khan was recently shared on social media with users claiming that it showing them praying for the well-being of latter's brother and actor Saif Ali Khan, who was recently injured in a stabbing incident. The photo was shared on social media after Khan was discharged from Mumbai's Lilavati Hospital. However, an investigation by PTI Fact Check Desk found that the photo dated back to November 2021 and showed Kunal praying with his family on Diwali. The old and unrelated photo was shared on social media as recent with a false claim. The 54-year-old actor suffered stab injuries in the attack last week and had to undergo emergency surgery at Lilavati Hospital. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared an photo on January 24, claiming it showed Bollywood actor Kunal Kemmu, along with his wife and fellow actor Soha Ali Khan, praying for Saif Ali Khan's well-being after the latter was discharged from the hospital following a stabbing incident. The user shared the image with the caption, "Taimur, Jahangir's uncle and Saif Ali Khan's brother-in-law, Kunal Kemmu, is thanking God for his brother-in-law's safe return from the hospital. Soha Ali Khan is also seen with folded hands beside him." Here is a link and an archive link to the post, and below is the screenshot of the same.
