Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and found it was shared by several other users with a similar claim. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archive versions can be found here and here , respectively. The search results further led us to a report by ABP News dated November 4, 2021. The report contained numerous images of the Bollywood couple, including the viral one, with the caption stating, "Soha Ali Khan's Diwali celebration, performs puja with husband Kunal and daughter Inaaya." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across an Instagram post by Kunal Kemmu dated November 4, 2021. In this post, Kemmu shared the same image seen in the viral claim, stating that it was from their Diwali celebrations in 2021. "To love, light, happiness, and health... Happy Diwali," the caption of the post read. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the image of Kemmu praying along with his wife and daughter was from their Diwali celebrations, dating back to 2021.

title: PTI Fact Check: Photos of Shah Rukh Khan's daughter with cricketer Rinku Singh shared in this social media post not real; AI generated images used as real with false claim
content: New Delhi, Jan 27 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple photos of Bollywood actor Suhana Khan with Indian cricketer Rinku Singh were recently shared on social media, with some users claiming it showed them in a hotel room in the United Kingdom, insinuating that they are in a relationship. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the photos shared on social media were fake. AI-generated pictures were shared on social media as real with a false claim. Significantly, Suhana Khan is a daughter of Bollywood superstar Shah Rukh Khan. Claim A Facebook user shared on January 23 purported pictures of Bollywood actor Suhana Khan with Indian cricketer Rinku Singh, claiming that they were in a UK hotel room. "Rinku Singh & Suhana Khan in UK Hotel Room," the caption of the post read. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral images through Google Lens and found that it was shared by several other users with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archive versions can be found here and here respectively: On further analysis of the posts, the Desk noticed several users commenting that the images were AI-generated. Below are screenshots of two such comments: Taking a cue from this, the Desk examined the photos carefully and noticed several discrepancies, suggesting that it was AI-generated. For instance, the background in the images was blurred. Also, a Grok (an AI-generative artificial intelligence chatbot) logo was visible at the bottom right corner of the photo, confirming that the image is AI-generated. Below is a photo highlighting the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the images through Wasitai (an AI detection tool), which also suggested the substantial presence of AI content. Below is a screenshot of the result: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk also ran the images through Hive Moderation, another AI detection website, which suggested substantial presence of AI content. author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Photo of Karnataka tableau featuring Tipu Sultan in 2014 Republic Day parade falsely shared on social media as recent; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 28 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A photo was recently shared on social media with users claiming that it showed the Karnataka tableau in this year's Republic Day parade, featuring 18th century Mysuru ruler, Tipu Sultan. However, an investigation by PTI Fact Check Desk revealed that the viral photo showed the state's tableau in the 2014 Republic Day Parade. The old photo was shared on social media as recent with a false claim. Karnataka's this year's tableau in the 76th Republic Day parade depicted the exquisite and artistic temples of the historic city of Lakkundi. Claim A Facebook user shared on January 26 a post claiming that itshowed Karnataka's tableau in this year's Republic Day Parade,featuring Tipu Sultan. The caption of the post read: "Most powerful and most iconic movment of Republic day parade. Tipu Sultan. #26January2025" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and found that it was shared by several other users with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archive versions can be found here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, we came across a report dated Jan 27, 2014, whose headline read: "Tipu Sultan tableau on Republic Day sparks war on Twitter". The feature image of the report was similar to the photo shared on social media. Here is the link to the report and below is a combination image showing that the viral image was the same as featured in the news report. A section of the report mentioned: "Tipu Sultan has become a hotly debated topic on social media after Karnataka's tableau for Sunday's Republic Day parade glorified the 18th century ruler with a complex legacy. Moments after a giant bust of Tipu Sultan brandishing a sword glided down Rajpath on Sunday, with the commentary describing him as a hero who died fighting the British, a war of words erupted on Twitter. Many critics argued on the micro-blogging site that it was wrong to pay tribute to a "tyrant" responsible for killing thousands." Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google that yielded us the live streaming uploaded on Doordarshan's official YouTube channel of Republic Day Parade 2014. The title of the video read: "The 65th Republic Day Parade - 26th January 2014 - Live". At a timestamp of 1:59:31, Karnataka's tableau can be seen featuring Tipu Sultan. Here is the link to the YouTube video and below is a screenshot of the same. In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted another set of customised keyword search to look for this year's Karnataka tableau at the Republic Day parade. The results led us to Sansad TV's official YouTube channel that posted a video of the tableau that depicted the temples of Lakkundi, a city renowned as the 'Cradle of Stone Craft'. Here is the link to the YouTube video and below is a screenshot of the same. Moreover, the Desk came across several media reports regarding the Republic Day Parade 2025 which mentioned that Karnataka's tableau in the 76th Republic-Day parade here on Sunday depicted the exquisite and artistic temples of the historic city of Lakkundi. One such report by PTI was carried by Hindustan Times, dated Jan 26, 2025. The headline of the report read: "Karnataka's Republic Day tableau depicts artistic temples of Lakkundi" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral photo showed Karnataka's tableau in 2014 Republic Day parade.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of collision between two trams in France falsely shared as Delhi Metro accident; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 29 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently shared on social media claimed to show a collision between two Delhi Metro trains. The text plate on the video also stated that the accident occurred in Delhi on January 25, 2025. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk revealed that the video was actually from France, where two trams collided at Strasbourg Central Station on January 10. The video was falsely shared as an incident from Delhi, India. Claim An Instagram user named Omprakash Kumar shared on January 26 a video, claiming that it showed a collision between two metro trains in Delhi. The text on the viral video, originally in Hindi, read: "Delhi Metro. Namo Bharat Metro. Two metro trains collided creating a havoc among the people" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found that several other users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be found here and here , respectively. On further analysis of posts, the Desk noticed several users commenting that the video was not from India. Below are screenshots of two such comments: On further analysis of the search results, we found a Facebook post by FirstPost, which carried the same video.It stated that several people were injured when two trams collided in Strasbourg, France. The caption of the post read: "At least 65 people were injured when two trams collided in Strasbourg. On Saturday afternoon, a stationary tram at the main railway station's underground stop was struck by another tram, which began to move backwards for unknown reasons. The collision occurred near Strasbourg's main train station, one of France's busiest outside Paris." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image showing that the video shared by FirstPost was from the same incident. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google that yielded us a report dated Jan 12, 2025 by NDTV whose headline read: "Rare Collision Of Trams In Tunnel Leaves Dozens Injured In France" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. A section of the report mentioned: "Two trams collided in a tunnel in a rare accident in the eastern French city of Strasbourg on Saturday, injuring dozens of people, authorities said. The collision occurred near Strasbourg's main train station, one of the busiest in France outside Paris. Minister of Transport Philippe Tabarot said "probably around 36" people were injured in the accident, while firefighters put that figure at around 50. A video posted by a witness on social media showed a chaotic scene with the two trams significantly damaged in a tunnel near the station. One of the trams appeared to have derailed as a result of the impact, whose cause has yet to be established." The incident was also reported by BBC on Jan 12, 2025. "More than 60 injured after Strasbourg trams collide," read the headline of the report. Here is the link to the report. "A spokesman for the prefecture said an investigation into the cause of the accident has been opened and no fatalities have been confirmed. Prosecutors said the collision was not deliberate," the report mentioned. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was from France, and not Delhi.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Delhi minister Saurabh Bharadwaj's on-stage interaction with Siri 'exposed' AAP? No, video shared on social media is edited
content: New Delhi, Jan 30 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that Delhi's ruling Aam Aadmi Party was exposed in an on-stage interaction of party leader and Delhi minister Saurabh Bharadwaj with Apple's digital voice assistant 'Siri' over a query on Yamuna cleaning promise. However, an investigation by PTI Fact Check Desk found that a digitally altered video was shared on social media with a false claim. Originally, the question posed to 'Siri' was regarding who coined the term 'guarantee' in Indian politics. The video was shared on social media amid the heightened poll campaigns by the parties ahead of Assembly polls in the national capital, scheduled to be held on February 5. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on January 27 a video, claiming that AAP leader Saurabh Bhardwaj interacted with Siri which exposed the party for failing to fulfill its promise to clean Yamuna river. In the video Saurabh Bhardwaj can be heard saying: "Hey Siri. Who used the word 'Yamuna 5 saal me saafkardengey?' Please use Chat GPT while you answer." Responding to the same, Siri allegedly says, "The term '5 saal me Yamuna saafkardengey' was used by Kejriwal in 2015." Furthermore, the caption of the post that garnered 5598 views, read: "Even SIRI knows the reality of @ArvindKejriwal...Guys pls listen to this...." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found that several other users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be found here and here , respectively. The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by Economic Times, dated January 27, 2025. The headline of the report read: "Hey Siri! Who said 'guarantee' first in Indian politics? AAP's Saurabh Bharadwaj takes a dig at BJP; Watch video" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. "Hey, Siri? Who used the word guarantee first in Indian politics? asked Bharadwaj. Arvind Kejriwal used the word Guarantee first time for Indian politics, was the reply by the voice assistant on the politician's phone," read a section of the report. While we found several media reports on this interaction between Bharadwaj and 'Siri' over the term 'guarantee', nowhere did we find anything related to Siri responding to a query on Yamuna cleaning. In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted another set of customised keyword search which yielded us a video uploaded on AAP leader Saurabh Bhardwaj's X handle on January 27. In the 1:23 minute video, Bhardwaj asks 'Siri': "Who used the word 'guarantee' in Indian politics for the first time? Please use Chat GPT while you answer." In response, Siri says, "The term 'guarantee' was first prominently used in Indian politics by Tam (Aam) Aadmi Party AP during the 2020 Delhi assembly elections. Journalist Rajdeep Sardesai noted that AP's use of 'guarantee' was a pioneering move, which was later adopted by the other parties in subsequent elections." Here is the link to the X post and below is a screenshot of the same. The caption of the post, originally in Hindi, read: "Today asked Siri who first used the word guarantee in Indian politics. So listen to what Siri replied." Below are two combination images showing that the video shared by the AAP leader was the same as the one shared on social media. Furthermore, on closely monitoring the viral video, the Desk found 'Sarcasam Politics' written at the bottom right corner of the viral video. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a Google search and found the X account with the same username. The bio section of the account mentioned 'political memes', with the user having shared several political memes. The AAP leader addressed the gathering during the manifesto launch of the party, a video of which could be found on the official YouTube channel of Aam Aadmi Party, uploaded on Jan 25. The title of the report read: "Arvind Kejriwal 15 Guarantees | AAP Manifesto Launch" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. At 56 seconds timestamp, Saurabh Bhardwaj said: "When the Aam Aadmi Party launches its manifesto, we don't call it a 'manifesto', we call it 'Kejriwal's guarantee.' Arvind Kejriwal was the first to use the word 'guarantee', and multiple leaders used this word…" The Desk listened to the entire address, but did not find any such interaction of Bharadwaj with 'Siri' that made a mention of Yamuna cleaning. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral clip of 'Siri' responding to a query on Yamuna pollution in Delhi was digitally altered.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: 2024 video of man dressed as 'Krrish'at a Gujarat event falsely shared in the name of Maha Kumbh 2025; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 30 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video of a man entering an event wearing a long coat and mask resembling Hrithik Roshan from this film 'Krrish' was recently shared on social media. Sharing the video, users claimed that it showing 'Krrish' arriving at the Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the viral video dated back to 2024 from a fair that was organised in Ankleshwar, Gujarat. The video was shared on social media as recent with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user on January 21 shared a video, claiming that it showed a man dressed as Hrithik Roshan-starrer 'Krrish', arriving at the Maha Kumbh Mela 2025. The caption of the post originally in Hindi, read: "Krrish reached Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj' Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found that several other users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be found here and here , respectively. On closely monitoring the viral video, the Desk found 'JCI Ankleshwar' written on the back screen. Ankleshwar is located in Gujarat. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google which yielded us a video shared by an Instagram page named 'My City Ankleshwar' on December 29, 2024. The caption of the post read: "Krrish at Jci Fun fair Ankleshwar" Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk found that this was the same video as the one shared on Instagram. Below is a combination image highlighting the same. Several videos of the fair were also posted on the official Instagram page of 'JCI Ankleshwar'. Here is the link to one such video. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was from a fair that was held in Gujarat in 2024, and not from the Maha Kumbh Mela 2025.

title: PTI Fact Check: 1938 photo of Jawaharlal Nehru after immersing his mother's ashes in Prayagraj falsely shared as him taking holy dip in Maha Kumbh
content: New Delhi, Jan 30 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A purported photo of India's first Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru was recently shared on social media, with some users claiming it showed him taking a dip in the holy Ganga River during the Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj (then Allahabad) in 1938. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the viral photo showed Nehru when he immersed the ashes of his mother in Allahabad in 1938. The photo was shared on social media, falsely in the name of Maha Kumbh Mela. Notably, the 1938 Maha Kumbh was held in Haridwar, not Allahabad, and it was marred by a fire and a cholera outbreak. Nehru's photo was shared on social media amid the recent row over Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge's remark targeting Union Home Minister over the latter's visit to Maha Kumbh. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user on January 28 shared a photo claiming it showed late PM Jawaharlal Nehru taking a holy dip during the 1938 Maha Kumbh Mela in Allahabad. " Pt.Nehru while taking a dip in the Holy Sangam during 1938 Kumbh was trying to eradicate poverty from the nation ! The photo is available in Anand Bhavan, Prayagraj ! " the user captioned the image. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and found that several other users had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be found here and here respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the now-viral posts and found users commenting that the photo dated back to 1938 when the former Prime Minister visited Prayagraj to immerse his mother's ashes. Below is a screenshot of one such comment: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found an India Today report, dated March 6, 2006. The report contained some unseen images of Nehru from his childhood to his later years. It also included the viral image, with its caption stating it was from the ritual where Nehru immersed his mother's ashes in Allahabad. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: "ENDURING TRAGEDY: Jawaharlal Nehru immersing his mother's ashes in Allahabad," read the caption of the photo. Further, the search results led the Desk to a report by Reckontalk.com titled, "15 Rare & Old Photos of 'Place of Sacrifice' Allahabad | Part II." The report featured a list of images, including the viral one. The photo caption read, "Nehru after immersing his mother's ashes at Allahabad." Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: During its investigation, the Desk also found that the 1938 Kumbh Mela was held in Hardiwar, and not Allahabad. Reports mention that back then, a fire broke out at a slum along Ganga and there was a cholera outbreak at the mela premises. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the 1938 photo of Nehru was falsely circulated on social media in the name of Maha Kumbh.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of stone pelting ritual at a religious event in Uttarakhand falsely shared in the name of Maha Kumbh 2025; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 30 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of several men dancing while pelting stones was recently shared on social media, with users claiming it to be from the ongoing Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj. The video showed several of those men dressed in saffron outfits, throwing stones at each other near a temple premises while seemingly dancing. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video dated back to August 2024 and was actually from an annual ritual in Uttarakhand. The clip showed participants of the Devidhura Bagwal Mela throwing stones at each other as part of a traditional practice during the month of Shravan. The video was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An Instagram user on January 27 shared a video, claiming that it showed men pelting stones in the ongoing Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool search and extracted multiple keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that the video had been shared by other users with a similar claim. Two such posts can be seen here and here , with their archived versions can be found here and here . The search results further led the Desk to a video published by a YouTube channel named 'Gaurangi Dholgai' on August 20, 2024. The channel featured the same video. However, its title mentioned it to be from the Devidhura Bagwal Mela held in Uttarakhand in August 2024. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found multiple reports confirming that the unique stone-pelting tradition was followed at the Devidhura Bagwal Mela, which is held every year during the month of Shravan. The fair features a stone-pelting event at the Varahi Devi Temple in Devidhura, located in the Champawat district of Uttarakhand. An ETV Bharat report, sharing the details about the 2024 Bagwal Fair, stated that the 10-day long event was inaugurated on August 16, 2024, by Union Minister of State for Road Transport and Highways Ajay Tamta. "A grand procession was taken out by local women and school children in traditional attire till the temple premises," the report added. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. On further scanning the search results, we came across another YouTube video by a a channel named Devbahuguna Garhwali, uploaded on August 23, 2024. The headline of the video read: "Bagwal Mela 2024 || Devidhura ll जिसमें होती है पत्थरों से लड़ाई" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was the same location as seen in the viral clip. Below is a combination image, highlighting the same: Furthermore, the customized keyword search about the incident also led the Desk to detailed information about the Bagwal Fair, shared by the Ministry of Tourism. "Every year, during the festive preparations for Rakshabandhan, the Champawat district of Uttarakhand is filled with the colors of love and joy due to the Bagwal Mela, which is organized in the month of Shravan. The Devidhura Temple of Goddess Barahi is situated in Devidhura village, located 75 km from Champawat. The term 'Bagwal,' meaning 'fight with stones,' hints at the fair's main event," the information mentioned on the Ministry's website reads. Here is the link to the post, followed by a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of people engaged in stone-pelting was part of a religious event from Uttarakhand.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated photo of Prakash Raj shared on social media to falsely claim he took the holy dip at Maha Kumbh 2025; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 31 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A photo of actor Prakash Raj immersed in a water body with folded hands was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that he visited the Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the viral photo was AI generated, which was shared by users thinking it to be real. Claim A Facebook user shared on January 29 a photo of actor Prakash Raj, claiming it showed him taking a dip in the Sangam at the ongoing Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj. The user shared the photo, which showed the actor taking a dip in the Ganga River. "Hindu hater Prakash Raj, who doesn't believe in God, has gone to Kumbh Mela to pollute it! Now I understand what they mean by pollution," the user wrote in the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the image through Google Lens and found that it was shared by other users with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archive versions can be found here and here respectively. Upon further analysis, the Desk noticed several users commenting that the image was AI-generated. Below are screenshots of two such comments: Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the image through Hive Moderation, an AI detection tool, which suggested a substantial presence of AI-generated content. Below is a screenshot of the result: In The next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across an X post shared by the actor in which he vehemently called out the image as fake. "FAKE NEWS ALERT - The last resort of bigots and the coward army of 'Feku Maharaj' is to stoop down and spread FAKE NEWS... even during their holy ceremony. What a SHAME! A complaint has been filed against the jokers... face the consequences," the actor stated. Here is a link to the post, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the photo of Prakash Raj taking a dip in Sangam at the Maha Kumbh Mela was AI-generated.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: 2022 video of Dimple Yadav taking dip in Ganga at Haridwar falsely shared in name of Maha Kumbh 2025; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 31 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video of Samajwadi Party MP Dimple Yadav was recently shared on social media, with some users claiming it showed her taking a holy dip in Sangam, Prayagraj during the ongoing Maha Kumbh. However, an investigation by PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video dated back to October 2022 when Dimple Yadav, along with her husband and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, had visited Haridwar to immerse the ashes of party founder Mulayam Singh Yadav in Ganga. The old and unrelated video was shared on social media as recent, falsely linking it to the ongoing Maha Kumbh Mela. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video on January 30, claiming it showed Samajwadi Party MP Dimple Yadav taking a holy dip in Sangam, Prayagraj during the ongoing Maha Kumbh Mela. "Dimple Bhabhi is also taking a dip in the Kumbh to reduce her sins to an extent," the user captioned the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that the video had been shared by several other users with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archive versions can be found here and here respectively. Further, the search results led the Desk to a YouTube video uploaded on October 18, 2022. The video showed Dimple Yadav taking a dip in the river, matching the visuals in the viral post. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image, establishing that this video was the same as the viral clip. Upon careful analysis of the video, the Desk found that Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav was also present with Dimple Yadav. The description of the YouTube video confirmed that it was from a ritual where the couple immersed the ashes of late Samajwadi Party supremo Mulayam Singh Yadav in the Ganga River in Haridwar. Below a screenshot has been attached highlighting the same. In the next part of investigation, taking cue from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found a report published by Amar Ujala on October 20, 2022. The feature image of the report matched the visuals in the viral video. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: According to the report, the video was from Haridwar, where Akhilesh Yadav, accompanied by wife Dimple, immersed the ashes of Mulayam Singh Yadav in the Ganga River. The couple also took a dip in the holy river following the ritual. Additionally, the keyword search led the Desk to a video report by News18, uploaded on YouTube on October 17, 2022. The video provided a detailed report on Akhilesh Yadav and Dimple Yadav's visit to Haridwar. The report also showed the duo taking a dip in the Ganga River, matching the content in the viral video. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that video shared on social media as a recent incident, actually dated back to 2022.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of accused assaulted by lawyers in Raipur falsely linked to Amritsar statue vandalism case; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 31 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently shared on social media claimed to show a man, accused of vandalising Dr BR Ambedkar's statue in Amritsar, being assaulted by a group of lawyers, before being presented before the court. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk revealed that an unrelated video from Chhattisgarh was shared on social media, falsely linking it to the recent incident in Amritsar. The January 17 video actually showed a group of lawyers in Raipur hitting a man accused of assaulting a senior advocate. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user on January 29 shared a post claiming that a person accused of vandalising Dr BR Ambedkar's statue in Amritsar was beaten by lawyers ahead of court appearance. The caption of the post, originally in Hindi, read: "In Amritsar, the person who broke the statue of Baba Saheb was beaten up during his court appearance." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found that several other users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be found here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a Dainik Bhaskar report published on January 13, 2025, whose headline read: "Chaos in Raipur court..Lawyers beat up a young man; VIDEO: Police had come to court with a man in the case of murderous attack on a lawyer; He even had a scuffle with an IPS officer" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. The video uploaded with the report was similar to the viral video being circulated on social media. Below is a combination image highlighting the same. Furthermore, a report by Zee News, published on January 17, 2025, mentioned: "There was a ruckus in the court in Raipur, the capital of Chhattisgarh, on Friday, when an accused beat up a lawyer in the court premises. After this, there was an atmosphere of tension in the court premises. After the assault on the lawyer, all the lawyers present in the court premises gathered. As soon as the accused returned from inside the court after appearing in court, the lawyers present outside pounced on him. The lawyers beat up the accused fiercely. In this ruckus, many policemen including IPS were also pushed and shoved." Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. According to the report the accused named Ajay Singh had attacked a lawyer Dirghesh Sharma who was fighting a case against him. Following this, a case was registered against the accused. "After this incident, lawyers created a ruckus in Khamtarai police station. After the ruckus created by the lawyers, the police arrested the accused. A case was registered against the accused for assault, abuse and murderous attack. After registering an FIR against the accused, the police brought the accused to the court to present him in the court…As soon as the police brought the accused out after presenting him in the court, the lawyers got furious after seeing the accused. The lawyers pulled the accused by his hair and dragged him and beat him up," a section of the report read. Taking a cue from this, the Desk accessed the FIR copy of the case, filed at Khamtarai Police Station on January 16, 2025. We scanned the copy and it mentioned that Ajay hit Dirghesh Kumar Sharma on his left cheek with a stone in his hand with the intention of killing him, due to which Dirghesh Kumar Sharma's facewas injured. Below is a screenshot of the FIR copy. In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a cutomised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports regarding the accused who allegedly vandalised DR BR Ambedkar's statue in Amritsar. The search yielded us a PTI report carried by The New Indian Express, dated January 27, 2025. Clearly, the original video predated the Amritsar incident of statue vandalisation. The headline of the report read: "Attempt to vandalise Ambedkar statue in Amritsar; Punjab CM Mann, opposition leaders condemn incident" Here is the link to the report. "Police on Sunday arrested a man hailing from Moga district of Punjab, who allegedly attempted to damage the statue of Ambedkar at the Town Hall on Heritage Street that leads to the Golden Temple. The Amritsar Police Commissionerate arrested the accused after registering an FIR," read a section of the report. Another report on the incident was published by The Indian Express on January 29, whose headline read: "'He never met us after returning from Dubai, committed grave mistake': Mother of man arrested for trying to vandalise Ambedkar statue in Amritsar" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. The report mentioned: "On Republic Day, Akashdeep Singh, 24, a resident of Dharamkot in the Moga district of Punjab, climbed up a ladder placed near the Ambedkar statue with a hammer in an alleged attempt to vandalise it. He also allegedly tried to damage a sculpture depicting the Constitution placed beneath the statue. The Kotwali police arrested Akashdeep and recorded his statement." A combination image below clearly shows that the accused in the Raipur and Amritsar incidents are different. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was of an incident that happened in Raipur, which predated the statue vandalisation event in Amritsar.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Photo of woman's body killed in Punjab shared on social media with false communal claim; details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 31 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A photo recently circulated on social media, with users claiming it showed the body of a woman named Neelam, allegedly stuffed in a suitcase and dumped in a canal in Rajasthan by a Muslim man named Abid. It was also claimed that Abid and Neelam had married five months ago. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the accused was actually Yuvraj Singh, a police officer. Singh, who was already married, was in a relationship with the victim. Reports suggest he killed the woman to get rid of her before his wife returned to India from abroad. Additionally, it was confirmed that the body was dumped in a canal in Punjab, not Rajasthan. The photo was shared on social media with false claims and a communal spin. Claim An Instagram user on January 24, shared a post claiming that a Muslim man named Abid killed his wife Neelam and disposed of her body in a suitcase at a canal in Rajasthan. The caption of the post, originally in Hindi, read: "Abid packed Neelam in a suitcase and threw him into the canal, he was married 5 months ago. #Rajasthan" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. (The image of the deceased has been blurred owing to the sensitivity of the matter). Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and found that it was shared by several other users with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archive versions can be found here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a report by Dainik Bhaskar, published earlier this week. The feature image of the report matched with the picture of the deceased that is being shared on social media. The headline of the report read: "Policeman murders girlfriend in Punjab: body thrown in canal; hails from Himachal, was taking air hostess coaching in Chandigarh" Here is the link to the report. A section of the report mentioned: "A 22-year-old girl from Himachal Pradesh, who was undergoing training to be an airhostess in Chandigarh, has been murdered. Her body was found in the Bhakra canal in Patiala. Her boyfriend is accused of her murder. He is a policeman by profession and is posted in Mohali." The Desk found another report by The Indian Express, published on January 24, whose headline read: "'Cop' allegedly kills woman friend by pushing her into canal, held" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. A section of the report read: "The accused, identified as Yuvraj Singh was produced in the district court, which remanded him in five-day police custody. The preliminary investigation indicated that the accused is married and was in a relationship with the victim. The accused wanted to get rid of the victim as his wife was returning to India from abroad." In the next part of investigation, the Desk accessed the FIR copy of the case, wherein the accused has been identified as Yuvraj Singh and the victim as 22-year-old Nisha Soni. Below is a screenshot of the translated FIR copy. In the next part of investigation, we contacted Rupnagar Police for their comment on the viral claim. The fact-check report will be updated as and when a response is received. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that there was no communal angle in the incident, since both the victim the accused were of the same religion.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: 2024 video of Sant Siyaram Baba shared to falsely claim 154-year-old monk visited this year's Maha Kumbh Mela; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 1 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently went viral on social media, with users claiming that a 154-year-old monk from the Himalayas participated in the Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj. However, a PTI Fact Check investigation found that the video actually dates back to 2024. Furthermore, the monk, Sant Siyaram Baba, passed away in December last year at the reported age of 94. The viral video was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user on January 27 shared a video claiming that it showed a 154-year-old monk, who came from the Himalayas to participate in the Maha Kumbh Mela. The caption of the post, that garnered 3497 views, read: "A 154-year-old monk who came from the Himalayan mountains to participate in the Maha Kumbh Mela" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found that several other users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be found here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a similar video uploaded by a user, named Dilip Kumar Singh on December 15, 2024. The caption of the X post, originally in Hindi, read: "154 years old Saint Siyaram Baba is still alive and serving God." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk found that this was the same video as the viral clip. Below is a combination image highlighting the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and found a report by Live Mint, published on December 11, 2024. The headline of the report read: "Who is Siyaram Baba? Madhya Pradesh's revered saint passes away at 94" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. The Live Mint report, published on December 11, 2024, quoted another report by Times of India, stating that Sant Siyaram Baba passed away at the Bhattyan village Ashram near the Narmada coast at the age of 94. Another report dated December 11, 2024 by Economic Times mentioned: "Siyaram Baba, a revered spiritual figure known for his devotion to Lord Hanuman and the Narmada River, passed away on Wednesday at the age of 95" Here is the link to the report. "Siyaram Baba, a revered spiritual figure known for his devotion to Lord Hanuman and the Narmada River, passed away on Wednesday at the age of 95. His demise occurred on the auspicious day of Mokshada Ekadashi and Gita Jayanti, drawing an outpouring of grief from devotees nationwide," read a section of the report. On December 11, 2024, News18 India also published a video report on Siyaram Baba, and mentioned that he passed away at the age of 94. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video dated back to 2024, and was not related to the ongoing Maha Kumbh Mela. Also, the social media posts falsely mentioned Baba's age as 154.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Edited video shared on social media to falsely claim British pilot made in-flight announcement on Maha Kumbh Mela; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 1 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that a British pilot made an in-flight announcement, praising the Maha Kumbh Mela 2025 before the Prayagraj-bound flight made a landing. However, an investigation by PTI Fact Check Desk found a video was digitally altered by overlaying a different audio and was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on January 27 a video claiming that a British pilot made an announcement in an international flight, praising the Maha Kumbh Mela before landing in Prayagraj. The caption of the post read: "The historic announcement made by British pilot Roger Blades regarding Mahakumbh while landing at Prayagraj from an international flight should make us Hindus proud of our Sanatani Culture ....!!" Here is the link and archive link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. In the video, the pilot was heard saying: "Good evening ladies and gentlemen. This is your captain speaking, check your windows we are about to land in Prayagraj to the Maha Kumbh 'Nagri'. Flying over the spiritual Sangam ghat where the holy Ganga, Yamuna and Saraswati rivers meet offering blessings to all. My co-pilot Mr Anvesh Patel just shared an exciting fact that the Purna Maha Kumbh is happening after 144 years. So, what's the plan after landing? Of course a holy dip for all of us. Let's be part of history before we become history. It's a once in a lifetime blessing…" Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found that several other users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be found here and here , respectively. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google, but did notfind any relevant report, substantiating the viral claim. In the video shared in one of the viral posts, the Desk noticed 'Anveshgraphy' written with an Instagram logo. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk searched for 'Anveshgraphy' on Instagram, and found that the account was of one 'Anvesh Patel',who mentioned 'Photography and videography' mentioned in the bio section. Below is a screenshot of the same. We found that the same video was uploaded by the user on January 23, 2025. The caption of the post read: "This voiceover is human original and fully copyrighted. Any use of this audio without my permission is strictly prohibited" Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the Instagram post. We also realised that the user had shared several similar videos from different parts of the country accompanied by an audio of a pilot making somewhat similar announcements. Here is the link to one such post. The Desk also reached out to Patel for his comments on the viral claim. The fact-check report will be updated as and when a response is received. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video shared on social media was digitally altered using a different audio clip.

title: PTI Fact Check: Photo in social media post claiming Dhirendra Shastri's letter predicted January 29 stampede at Maha Kumbh is AI-generated; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 2 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check): A photo of a purported letter was shared on social media, with users claiming that it was written by Dhirendra Shastri, the Peethadhishwar of Bageshwar Dham, predicting the recent Maha Kumbh stampede, that happened on January 29. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an AI-generated photo was shared on social media with a false claim. Thirty people were killed and 60 others were injured during a stampede in the Maha Kumbh on January 29. Claim A Facebook user shared on January 29 a photo of an alleged letter written, claiming that it was written by Bageshwar Dham head priest Dhirendra Shastri, predicting the Maha Kumbh stampede. The caption of the post, originally in Hindi, read: "Found this page from Ghat. In which yesterday evening itself, Pt. Dhirendra Krishna Shastri ji had written in advance about the incident that happened in the night after seeing it with his trinity. But it had become wet while bathing, so he could not give it to the administration." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the post. Investigation The Desk ran the image through Google Lens and found that it was shared by another user with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived version can be viewed here and here , respectively. On watching the photo closely, the Desk found several discrepancies, suggesting that it was AI-generated. The background of the image was blurred and the language seemed unrecognisable. Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the images through Wasitai, an AI detection tool, which also suggested the substantial presence of AI content. Below is a screenshot of the result: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk ran the image through Hive Moderation, another AI detection website, which suggested similar presence of AI content. Below isa screenshot of the result: In the next part of investigation, we contacted Dhirendra Shastri's team via e-mail for their comment on the viral claim. The fact-check report will be updated as and when a response is received. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an AI-generated image was falsely as letter written by Dhirendra Shastri, predicting the Maha Kumbh stampede.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: 2019 video of TTE taking money from elderly passenger falsely shared as recent incident involving a devotee traveling to Maha Kumbh 2025
content: New Delhi, Feb 2 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video was recently shared on social media with users claiming that it showed a Travelling Ticket Examiner (TTE) forcibly taking money from an elderly passenger, who was travelling to Prayagraj for the ongoing Maha Kumbh Mela. However, an investigation by PTI Fact Desk revealed that the video was from Uttar Pradesh's Chandauli, dating back to 2019. The clip was shared on social media as recent, falsely linking it to the Maha Kumbh Mela. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user on January 31shared a video, claiming that it showed a TTE forcibly taking money from an elderly passenger going to Prayagraj to attend the Maha Kumbh Mela. The caption of the post, originally in Hindi, read: "Don't know the location of the incident but this is not acceptable. Make this viral so that this can be detected and action can be taken against this person because this TTE swindled all the money from a poor passenger going to Prayagraj Maha Kumbh." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found that the same video was shared by several other users with the same claim. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. We also found that the similar video was shared on social media back in 2019. One such post can be viewed here and its archived version can be found here . Below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post by the official handle of DRM Pt. Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Division, dated July 23, 2019, which mentioned that the concerned employee was suspended back then. The caption of the post, originally in Hindi, read: "An explanation was sought from the concerned employee regarding the video clip. The incident took place 3-4 months ago. The employee said that he was taking money from the passenger for making the ticket and he had made the ticket. The concerned employee has been suspended for detailed investigation." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report, dated July 25, 2019, by Patrika, whose headline read: "TTE suspended for snatching money from an old man in a moving train, video went viral very fast." Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. Another report by Amar Ujala reported the incident on July 25, 2019. An English translation of the report read: "Chandauli: TTE snatched money from an old man in a train, suspended after the video went viral" Here is the link to the report. "As soon as the matter came to light, Divisional Railway Manager Mughalsarai suspended the accused TTE and formed a team to investigate the matter. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of TTE taking money from an elderly passenger dated back to 2019.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: This Delhi election opinion poll details shared in name of ABP news channel is fake; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 3 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): Just days ahead of the Assembly polls in Delhi, a purported opinion poll by ABP News went viral on social media, which predicted a victory for the BJP. However, an investigation by PTI Fact Check Desk found that the alleged opinion poll was fake. A digitally altered video was shared on social media, falsely attributing it to the news channel. For the February 5 polls, Delhi is witnessing a triangular contest between AAP, BJP and Congress. While the AAP eyes at retaining power for a third straight term, its rivals aim at wresting power from the hands of Arvind Kejriwal-led party. The counting of votes will be taken up on February 8. Claim An X user shared on January 30 an alleged video report by ABP News – an opinion poll on Delhi Assembly polls – predicting a victory for the BJP. The survey predicted 47 seats for the BJP in the 70-member Assembly, 17 seats for the AAP and just six seats for the Congress. "Based on the latest figures, BJP Delhi can get 41-46, AAP 17-22, Congress 1-2. The margin of defeat of AAP stalwarts will be like this – Arvind Kejriwal (8,000-12,000), Manish Sisodia (10,000-13,000), and Atishi (8,000-11,000)," the user shared the video with this caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through the InVid Tool and found several keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across multiple posts shared with a similar claim. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archive versions can be found here and here , respectively: The search results also led the Desk to media posts dated December 2024. At that time, a similar video was shared on social media in the name of ABP News opinion polls, which had predicted victory for the BJP, but the seat margin was different. Back then, the media house had released a statement calling the video fake, and urging social media users to avoid misinformation and rely only on official sources. Here are links to two such posts ( Link 1 , Link 2), along with a statement published by ABP News on December 17, 2024, on its official handle. Also, find the screenshots of the same. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google but did not find any substantial report regarding any such opinion poll published by ABP News. The Desk thoroughly scanned ABP News' official YouTube channel and social media handles, but did not find anything on any such opinion poll regarding Delhi Assembly elections. Next, as a part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the viral video, and found the format to be different from the standard ABP News broadcast format. For instance, the standard ABP News broadcast format features a "Breaking News" banner at the top of the screen, appearing briefly at the bottom with a red and white colour scheme. However, in the viral video, the "Breaking News" banner is placed at the bottom of the screen throughout, with yellow text on a red background, deviating from the standard format. Below is a comparison image highlighting the discrepancies between the viral video and a video posted by ABP News in November 2024. Also, the channel typically collaborates with polling agencies such as IANS-Matrize and mentions it prominently in its opinion poll, which is presented in an analysis form. However, the viral clips don't follow any such format. Below is a combination image, comparing an original opinion poll by the channel to the viral clip. Furthermore, as part of the investigation, the Desk reached out to an official from ABP News, seeking comment regarding the viral claim. In a telephonic conversation with the Desk, the senior official from the ABP News said, "The viral video is false." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video claiming to show ABP News' opinion poll predicting BJP's victory in the upcoming Delhi Assembly Elections 2025 was fake.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of scuffle between locals and cops in Rajkot falsely shared as incident from Delhi
content: New Delhi, Feb 3 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a group of men clashing with police personnel was recently shared on social media, falsely claiming that the incident took place in the national capital on January 27. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk revealed that the video was from an incident that occurred in Gujarat's Rajkot, and was misleadingly shared on social media as an event from Delhi. Claim An Instagram user shared a video on January 27, showing a group of men clashing with police personnel on a street in broad daylight, claiming it to be from Delhi. "The biggest accident happened in Delhi this morning, 27/1/2025," the user shared the video with this caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk discovered that several other users had shared the same video with similar claims. One such post can be viewed here , and its archived version can be found here : In the next phase of investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the viral video and found a watermark of '@samnagujarat' placed on it. Upon further investigation, we found an Instagram account with the same name. Here is a link to the handle, along with a screenshot of the same: As a part of the investigation, the Desk carefully examined the Instagram account and came across a post made on January 6, 2025. The post featured the same viral video, but the caption stated that the incident occurred in Gujarat's Rajkot. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image, showing this is the same video as the one shared on social media recently. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found multiple news articles, reporting the incident. According to a report published by Jagran's Gujarati edition on January 6, 2025, the altercation took place between police officials and locals from Vinchhiya village in Jasdan Taluka of Rajkot district, after the police refused to publicly parade six murder suspects through the village. "Around 50 people have been detained in connection with the incident," said Superintendent of Police (Rajkot Rural) Himkar Singh as quoted in the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same: Additionally, the search also led the Desk to a report by The Indian Express, published on January 7, 2025. The report also confirmed that the incident occurred in Gujarat's Rajkot, and not Delhi, as claimed in the viral post. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video of clashes between a group of men and police personnel is from Gujarat's Rajkot, not Delhi.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: 2024 video of Ganpati celebration in Mumbai shared on social media with fake claim about Salman Khan; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 4 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video featuring Salman Khan's photo recently circulated on social media, falsely claiming to show thousands of people mourning on the streets after the Bollywood actor's alleged killing by jailed gangster Lawrence Bishnoi. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video is unrelated and actually shows a Ganpati celebration in Mumbai, which was shared with a fake claim. The video surfaced amid repeated death threats to Khan from the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, prompting authorities to beef up security at his Galaxy Apartments residence in Mumbai. Claim An Instagram user shared a video on February 2, featuring Bollywood superstar Salman Khan's image, claiming that it showed thousands of people gathering on the street after the news of Salman Khan getting killed by jailed gangster Lawrence Bishnoi. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and found multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that same video with identical claim was shared on YouTube as well. Two such videos can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can viewed here and here , respectively. In the next part of investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the viral video and found a watermark of 'Mumbai cha Ganpati' placed on it. We found an Instagram account with the same name. Here is the link to the handle, along with a screenshot of the same: As the Desk scanned through the Instagram posts, it found the same video shared on August 31, 2024. The video showed a large crowd gathered on the streets; however, the caption clearly stated that it was from Ganpati celebrations in Mumbai. Notably, in the video posted by the Instagram handle, an idol of Lord Ganpati being carried was also visible. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot of the same: Below is a comparison image showing that the content in the viral video matches that of the Instagram post. Furthermore, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google but did not find any substantial evidence backing the claim made regarding Khan. The search led us to multiple news reports on the alleged feud between Salman Khan and jailed gangster Lawrence Bishnoi over the blackbuck poaching case. The latest report we could find around the development was by Economic Times, published on January 6, 2025. The headline of the report read, "Salman Khan's Mumbai Galaxy Apartment home gets bulletproof balcony amid rising threats." Here is the link to the report. "More than eight months after a shocking firing incident outside Salman Khan's residence at Galaxy Apartments in Bandra, Mumbai, the Bollywood actor has implemented substantial security enhancements. The measures include bulletproof windows, a high-tech security system, and high-resolution CCTV cameras to monitor any suspicious activity. Additionally, bulletproof glass has been installed to fortify the balcony from which Khan greets his fans. The actor lives in a one-bedroom flat on the ground floor of the building, while his parents reside on the first floor," read a section of the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that claim made on social media was fake and baseless.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: 2021 video of foreign saint who walked from Switzerland to Haridwar shared in the name of Maha Kumbh Mela 2025; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 4 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video – an interview of a man – claiming that it showed a man who walked from Switzerland to India for four years to attend the ongoing Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj. However, an investigation by PTI Fact Check Desk found that the dated back to 2021 Kumbh, that was held in Haridwar. The four-year-old video was shared on social media as recent, falsely linking it to the Maha Kumbh Mela 2025. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user on January 29 shared a video, claiming that it showed a man who walked for four years to reach India from Switzerland, to attend the Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj. The caption of the post, that has garnered 33.1k views, originally in Hindi, read: "This person reached India from Switzerland for Prayagraj Maha Kumbh by walking continuously for 4 years" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found that the same video was shared by several other users with the same claim. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. On listening to the viral video carefully, the Desk noticed that the interviewer asked the man how many days did it take him to reach Haridwar from Himachal Pradesh. At 1:26-minute timestamp, the interviewer asked: "When did you start from Himachal Pradesh to reach Haridwar? (Himachal se kabchale the Haridwar aanekeliye)." To this, the man replied: "It took me 25 days. (25 din lage)". Furthermore, on analysing the video completely, the Desk found a text written on the video, which was visible at 3:46-minute timestamp. The text read: "...Kumbh 2021…" Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword on Google and came across a YouTube video uploaded on March 22, 2021. The title of the report read: "Haridwar Kumbh 2021॥ Switzerland BEN BABA reached Maha Kumbh Mela after walking for 4 consecutive years." Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. The Description of the YouTube post mentioned: "You all are aware that the world's biggest fair Mahakumbh is being organized in Haridwar in which we are introducing you to the discussions and dialogues of the sages. In this series we will introduce you to Bel Baba of Switzerland who reached India in 4 years after passing through 18 countries." Below is a combination image, showing that the person in the YouTube video was the same as the one in recent social media posts. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a report by Life Beyond Numbers, published on May 3, 2021, whose headline read: "This Techie Walked All The Way From Switzerland To India To Attain Spirituality." A section of the report highlighted: "Baba remains barefoot not just while walking, but all the time. He reached Haridwar for Kumbh Mela after 25-days of walking from Kangra, Himachal." Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a four-year-old video was falsely shared on social media in the name of Maha Kumbh Mela 2025.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of cops baton charging angry mob in Dhanbad falsely shared in name of Prayagraj Maha Kumbh
content: New Delhi, Feb 4 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video of policemen thrashing people on the streets was recently shared on social media with users claiming that it showed the treatment meted out to the devotees visiting Prayagraj for the Maha Kumbh Mela 2025. However, an investigation by PTI Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false. The video actually showed an unrelated incident that took place in Jharkhand's Dhanbad. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on January 28 a video, claiming that Uttar Pradesh Police thrashed devotees who had come to take a holy dip at the Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj. The caption of the post, originally in Hindi, read: "This is how the Uttar Pradesh Police welcomes the bathers in the Mahakumbh bath. This is the Mahakumbh arrangement of the Uttar Pradesh government 'Gundaraj'" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found that the same video was shared by several other users with the same claim. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results the Desk found an X post by BJP leader Deepak Prajash, dated January 2, 2025. The caption of the post, originally in Hindi, read: "See, what you get when you demand justice in Jharkhand!" Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk noticed striking similarities in the viral video and the one shared on X by the BJP leader. Below are three combination images highlighting the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report dated January 1, 2025, published by 'The Jharkhand Story'. The headline of the report read: "Jharkhand News: Police lathi-charge angry mob in Dhanbad" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. "Police had to resort to a mild lathi charge on an angry mob that had surrounded the Bank More police station and blocked the main road, demanding the handover of a murder accused on Wednesday afternoon," read a section of the report. The two feature images of the report were similar to the visuals seen in the viral video. Below are two combination images highlighting the same. Another report by ETV Bharat also reported the incident on January 1, 2025, whose headline, originally in Hindi, read: "Chaos over the death of a youth, arson near the police station on the charge of murder, police lathicharge - DEAD BODY FOUND" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was related to an incident from Dhanbad, and had no relation to Prayagraj or Maha Kumbh Mela 2025.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: No, Tata Trusts did not propose to organise any event for jailed Baramulla MP in Delhi; social media posts shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, February 5 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A purported video news report, along with a news article clipping, was recently shared on social media to claim that jailed Baramulla MP Sheikh Abdul Rashid, also popularly known as Engineer Rashid, was invited as the guest of honour at the India Visionary Leaders' Summit 2025, where he was to be bestowed with the Ratan Tata National Icon Award 2025. Users also claimed that the event was sponsored by Tata Trusts, along with Delhi Today Group. However, an investigation by PTI Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false. Tata Trusts, in an official statement, categorically denied any association with the event or the award or its organisers. Meanwhile, it is pertinent to note that MP Engineer Rashid remains lodged in Delhi's Tihar Jail in connection with a 2017 terror funding case. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on January 30 a clipping of a news report which claimed that MP Engineer Rashid, who is currently lodged in Tihar Jail, will receive the Ratan Tata National Icon Award 2025, at the India Visionary Leaders' Summit 2025. The user shared the post claiming that the event was sponsored by Tata Trusts. "Terrorist funding accused Engineer Rashid, who is currently in jail under UAPA, has been selected to receive the Ratan Tata National Icon Award 2025. He has also been invited as a guest of honor at the India Visionary Leaders' Summit, which is funded by Tata Group (Tata Companies and Tata Motors)," the user shared the post with the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through the InVid Tool search and found multiple keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived links can be found here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to learn more about the 'India Visionary Leaders Summit 2025'. The search result led the Desk to a report by the Hindustan Times published on January 28, 2025. The report mentioned that Engineer Rashid has been invited as a guest of honour at the India Visionary Leaders Summit 2025 (by Dr Rajat Shrivastava, founder of the Delhi Today Group) and was also said to be bestowed with the Ratan Tata National Icon Award 2025 at the event, set to be held on February 10, 2025. However, the report nowhere mentioned that the program would be supported by Tata Trusts. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. The search result also led the Desk to a statement issued by Tata Trusts dissociating itself from the summit and the award (the Ratan Tata National Icon Award 2025) set to be bestowed on the participants during the event. "It has been brought to our notice that the 'India Visionary Leaders Summit 2025' and the 'Ratan Tata National Icon Award 2025' are being organized in February 2025, and claims are being made that the event(s) are supported by Tata Trusts. The Tata Trusts would like to categorically state that we have no association with either the event(s) or the award or its organizers in any form whatsoever," the Tata Group said in a statement. "The Tata Trusts have, in fact, served a legal notice on December 13, 2024, to Dr. Rajat Shrivastava, Founder of Delhi Today Group, asking him to cease and desist from using the Tata Trusts brand name and/or the name of our late Chairman, Shri Ratan N Tata, for these events. Refusal to do so shall result in appropriate legal action as per due process of law," it added. Here is the link to the statement published on the Tata Trusts website, along with a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the event inviting Engineer Rashid as guest of honour had no links to the Tata Group.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Video from West Bengal falsely shared as UP Police action against miscreants who pelted stones on Prayagraj-bound train carrying Maha Kumbh devotees
content: New Delhi, Feb 5 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video was recently shared on social media, with some users claiming that it showed Uttar Pradesh Police personnel thrashing a miscreant who pelted stones at a train carrying devotees to Prayagraj for the Maha Kumbh Mela. However, in its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the viral video was unrelated to Maha Kumbh Mela 2025. The video was from an incident that took place in Suri town in West Bengal's Birbhum district. The unrelated clip was shared on social media, falsely linking it to Maha Kumbh Mela 2025. It is pertinent to note that two incidents of stone pelting on train en route to Prayagraj have been reported recently. Stones were hurled at the Tapti Ganga Express near Jalgaon Railway Station in Maharashtra earlier in January, and a case was also registered in the matter. In another incident, passengers waiting for the Maha Kumbh special train at Harpalpur railway station pelted stones at the train, allegedly after finding the doors of bogies locked. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video on February 2, claiming it showed Uttar Pradesh Police personnel thrashing with batons a miscreant who pelted stones at a Prayagraj-bound train. The video showed the police chasing the man, thrashing him with lathis, and forcibly taking him into custody. "UP Police serving the stone pelters who pelted stones at the train going to Maha Kumbh by evicting them from their homes," the user shared the video with the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool search and found multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived links can be found here and here , respectively. The search results also led the Desk to a local Bangla YouTube channel that had uploaded the same video on January 28, 2025. The video's description mentioned that the incident was reported in Suri town, in West Bengal's Birbhum district. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image, showing that the content in the viral video matches that of the YouTube video. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found multiple news reports covering detailed aspects of the incident. According to a PTI report published by The Print on January 29, 2025, the incident occurred in Suri town in West Bengal's Birbhum district, where 20 people were arrested following a clash between two factions of the ruling party over a land dispute near the district headquarters. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: According to the details published in the report, "A gang entered Mallikpur village near Suri, the district headquarters town, and as they threatened locals, a clash ensued. Police personnel went to the area and arrested one person for brandishing a firearm to terrorize the villagers. Soon after, other members of the group manhandled an officer of the local police station and tried to snatch the arrested man. Other villagers present at the spot tied up the men who manhandled the police officer as reinforcements arrived and brought the situation under control." Additionally, the customised keyword search also led the Desk to a video published by the official YouTube channel of Republic Bangla on January 28, 2025. The YouTube channel posted the same video seen in the viral post, mentioning that the incident happened in Suri town in West Bengal's Birbhum district. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video had no link to the incidents of stone pelting on Prayagraj-bound trains.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Fake opinion poll on Delhi Assembly polls shared on social media in the name of Aaj Tak; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 4 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A purported opinion poll by Aaj Tak recently circulated on social media, which predicted a sweeping victory for the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP). However, an investigation by PTI Fact Check Desk found that the alleged opinion poll was fake. A digitally altered video was shared on social media, falsely attributing it to the news channel. For the February 5 polls, Delhi is witnessing a triangular contest between AAP, BJP and Congress. While the AAP eyes at retaining power for a third straight term, its rivals aim at wresting power from the hands of the Arvind Kejriwal-led party. The counting of votes will be taken up on February 8. It is pertinent to note here that all opinion polls have been barred till voting concludes in the national capital.
