Claim A Facebook user shared on February 2 an alleged video report by Aaj Tak News – an opinion poll on Delhi Assembly polls – predicting a victory for the AAP. The survey predicted 56 to 58 seats for the ruling party in the Delhi Assembly elections. "Biggest opinion poll, AAP is going to create history for the fourth time," the user wrote in the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through the InVid Tool and found several keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across another post shared with a similar claim. The link to two such posts can be found here and here and their archived versions can be viewed here and here respectively. In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google but did not find any substantial report regarding any such opinion poll published by Aaj Tak. The Desk thoroughly scanned Aaj Tak's official YouTube channel and social media handles, but did not find anything regarding any such opinion poll. Next, as a part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the viral video, and found several discrepancies in the text plate running in the video. Below are three screenshots highlighting the same. Moreover, India Today also released a clarification on February 3, stating that fake polls attributed to Aaj Tak and India Today, were being circulated, adding that the TV Today Group has not conducted any exit poll for Delhi so far. The caption of the X post by India Today read: "Fake polls, falsely attributed to Aaj Tak and India Today, are currently being circulated ahead of the Delhi Elections 2025. The India Today Group has not conducted any exit polls for Delhi" Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video claiming to show Aaj Tak's opinion poll predicting AAP's victory in the Delhi Assembly Elections 2025 was fake.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of stone pelting on train carrying Maha Kumbh devotees to Prayagraj shared on social media with false communal angle; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 5 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video, claiming that it showed a group of 'jihadis' pelting stones at a special train carrying Maha Kumbh devotees from Jhansi to Prayagraj. The incident was claimed to have happened at Harpalpur Railway Station. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false since there was no communal spin to the entire incident. and a passenger at the station threw stones as the doors to the compartments were locked. The viral video was shared with a false communal angle on social media. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on January 28 a video, claiming that some 'jihadis' pelted stones at a train carrying devotees from Jhansi to Prayagraj for the Maha Kumbh Mela. "Breaking Alerts. Bharat 🇮🇳. Some suspicious people attacked the train going to Mahakumbh in Prayagraj. These rioters and Jihadis pelted stones at the passengers. There is only one treatment for them…" read the caption of the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found that the same video was shared by several other users with the same claim. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. The Desk further conducted a customised keyword search and came across a NDTV report dated January 28, 2025, whose headline read: "Passengers Throw Stones AtMahakumbh Special Train On Finding Doors Locked" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. "A special train travelling from Jhansi to Prayaraj was pelted with stones at HarpalpurStation after passengers waiting on the platform found the doors of the compartments locked. Videos circulating on social media show the attackers throwing stones at the train and shattering its windows as the passengers scream in fear," read a section of the report. The Desk noticed that the video carried by NDTV was similar to the viral video being shared on social media. Below is a combination image highlighting the same. We found another report by India Today, published on January 28, 2025, whose headline read: "Video: Doors locked, angry passengers throw stones at Maha Kumbh-bound train." Here is the link to the report. A section of the report mentioned: "The matter was immediately brought to our attention, and security personnel from RPF and GRP took swift action to control the situation. The train was safely dispatched to its destination, said Public Relations Officer (PRO) of the Jhansi Railway Division, Manoj Kumar." Furthermore, as part of the investigation, the Desk reached out to Harpalpur police station in-charge Pushpak Sharma, regarding the claim. In a telephonic conversation with the Desk, the official clarified that there was no communal angle to the incident. "The claim is false. It was not that a group of people pelted a stone but only a person who was a passenger at the station broke the window, as the train doors were closed from inside. The train was about to depart. Further, swift action was taken and the matter was resolved," Sharma told PTI. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that there was no communal angle to the incident.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: 2024 video of bus accident in Pakistan falsely shared in name of Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 6 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that it showed the accident in which a Prayagraj-bound bus, carrying devotees going to Maha Kumbh 2025, fell into a drain, claiming 10 lives. However, an investigation by PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video showed an accident that happened in Pakistan's Raiwind town in November 2024. The old and unrelated clip was shared on social media, falsely linking it to the ongoing Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj. Claim A Facebook user shared a video on February 1, claiming that it showed a Prayagraj-bound bus that fell into a drain, leaving 10 Maha Kumbh devotees dead. Here is the link and archive link to the post, followed by a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral clip through the InVid Tool Search and found multiple keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , with their archive links found here and here , respectively. |The search results also led the Desk to a video posted by Facebook page named 'Hangu and Orakzai Fans' on November 3, 2024. This was the same clip as shared on social media recently. However, the description along with it identified it to be from Raiwind town in Lahore. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image, showing that this was the same video as the one shared on social media recently. In the next part of investigation, the Desk scanned the details of the above-mentioned Facebook page and found it to be handled from Pakistan. The page had been sharing posts regarding developments reported in Pakistan. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a video posted by the official channel of Pakistan-based media outlet 'Aaj TV' on November 3, 2024. The channel confirmed that the incident of the bus falling into the open drainage was from Pakistan's Raiwind town. "The bus returning from the Raiwind gathering fell into the drain," the title of the video read. Here is the link to the post, followed by a screenshot of the same: The customised keyword search also led the Desk to a report by Pakistani news outlet Dawn, published on November 4, 2024. "Up to 29 participants returning from the Raiwind congregation were injured, 16 of them seriously, when a bus overturned in Lahore," it mentioned. Here is the link to the report. Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a video from Pakistan was falsely shared in the name of Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of overcrowded lane in Barsana falsely shared in name of Maha Kumbh Mela 2025; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 6 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of a narrow, overcrowded lane was recently shared on social media to claim that such were the arrangements at the Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj, where devotees were not even able to move. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found that the video actually showed a lane leading to Radha Rani Temple in Barsana, where devotees had gathered for darshan on the first day of this year. The video was falsely shared in the name of Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video on February 3, showing hundreds of people stuck in a narrow lane. Users shared the video, claiming it showed the lapses in arrangements for devotees at the Maha Kumbh Mela 2025 in Prayagraj. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool search and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. The search results further led the Desk to a video published on a YouTube channel named 'Vrindavan Devotee: Journey to Divine Bliss'. This video – uploaded on January 2 – was the same as the one shared on social media recently. It predates the Maha Kumbh Mela, which began with the first 'Amrit Snan' on January 13. Also, the caption of the clip stated that it was from the Radha Rani Temple in Barsana, where devotees had gathered for darshan on the first day of the new year. Here is the link to the video, followed by a screenshot of the same. A combination image below shows that this was the same video as the one posted on social media in the name of Prayagraj. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across an official Instagram handle of Shyam Sundar Goswami, who introduces himself as a spiritual and motivational speaker. Here is the link to the handle, followed by a screenshot of the same. After carefully scanning through the Instagram handle, the Desk found the user had posted the same viral video on January 1. He had captioned the same as- "See what is happening in Barsana on January 1? Why do people come in crowds?" Here is the link to the post, followed by a screenshot of the same. The Desk also found another video shot at the same location, but from a different angle, posted on the user's account. The caption confirmed that the video was from Barsana town in Uttar Pradesh's Mathura district. Here is the link to the post: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a video from Barsana was falsely shared in the name of Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered video shared on social media to falsely claim Samay Raina joked about Rekha during Kaun Banega Crorepati episode
content: New Delhi, Feb 7 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video, claiming it showed comedy sensation Samay Raina and Bollywood megastar Amitabh Bachchan bursting into laughter after the former joked about actress Rekha on the sets of Kaun Banega Crorepati Season 16. However, an investigation by PTI Fact Check Desk found that a clip was digitally altered using AI-generated audio and shared on social media with a false claim. Samay, along with Tanmay Bhat, Bhuvan Bam and Kamiya Jani, was recently invited for an influencers' special episode of Sony TV's popular quiz show. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user on February 3 shared a clip from the latest episode of the popular TV show Kaun Banega Crorepati, hosted by veteran Bollywood actor Amitabh Bachchan. The clip showed comedian Samay Raina allegedly cracking a joke mentioning veteran actress Rekha, leaving Bachchan in splits. Here is the link and archive link to the post, followed by a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid Tool Search and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , with their archive links found here and here , respectively. In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across the original video of the episode on Sony LIV's official app, uploaded on January 31, 2025. Here is the link to the episode: The Desk watched the entire episode but found no instance of Raina making a joke about veteran Bollywood actress Rekha. Meanwhile, the Desk went through the comment sections of the viral post and noticed several users mentioning that it was AI-generated. Below are screenshots of two such comments. Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the viral video through the AI detection platform Hive Moderation, which suggested a strong presence of AI-generated or deepfake content. Below is a screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was created by digitally altering a clip and overlaying it with AI-generated audio.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Clipped video of PM Modi's Lok Sabha speech shared on social media to falsely claim he said India will become independent in 2047
content: New Delhi, Feb 7 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): Amid the ongoing Budget Session, a video of Prime Minister Narendra Modi speaking in the Parliament went viral on social media, with users claiming he said that "when the country will gain independence in 2047…" The PTI Fact Check Desk, in its investigation, found that a selected portion of PM's speech was taken out of context and shared on social media with a false claim. In his reply to the Motion of Thanks on President's address in the Lok Sabha, the PM was actually reiterating his push for 'Viksit Bharat' by 2047, when the country will complete 100 years of its independence. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user on February 4 shared a10-second clip of PM Modi speaking in the Parliament, in which he was heard saying "the country will gain independence in 2047…". "Modi ji, this country became independent in 1947 itself. Despite the apologies and reports from your ancestors...Congress has given freedom to India by making sacrifices.This is true, no matter how much you try to hide it, it will keep reminding you!" read a rough translation of the caption, originally in Hindi. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk first ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across several other social media posts, which carried the same video with similar claims. The link to two such posts can be found here and here and its archived versions can be found here and here , respectively. The clip was was shared by Congress leader Supriya Shrinate on her official X handle. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search which yielded PM Modi's original address in Lok Sabha during the ongoing Budget Session of the Parliament. A video of PM Modi's reply on the motion of thanks on the President's Address in Lok Sabha was uploaded on Sansad TV's official YouTube. At 1:32:56 seconds timestamp, he said that we (India) have the demography, democracy and demand and we are moving forward with the dream (of Viksit Bharat) and when the country completes its 100 years of independence in 2047 we will become Viksit Bharat. PM Modi said: "The country is moving forward to fulfill the dreams of Viksit Bharat…We have demography, democracy, and demand, why can't we do it? We have to move forward with this belief and we are also moving forward with the dream of 2047, when the country will become independent, when it will be 100 years of independence, when we will become a developed India." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same. The viral clip was taken from 1:33:06 to 1:33:10 timestamp. The Desk noticed that PM Modi inadvertently said "when the country will get independence", and the very next second, he said, "when it will complete 100 years of independence". The first part was clipped out and shared on social media. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a selected portion of PM's speech was shared on social media to falsely claim he made the alleged remark.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: 2021 video of Priyanka Gandhi Vadra taking dip in Sangam falsely shared in name of Maha Kumbh Mela 2025; details inside
content: New Delhi, February 8 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's recent remark on Maha Kumbh Mela 2025, in which he said that "dip in Ganga won't eradicate poverty" was recently shared by some social media users. The clip was combined with another video of Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, in which she was seen taking dip in a waterbody, to suggest that she recently visited the ongoing Maha Kumbh Mela. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a four-year-old clip of Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, when she took a holy dip in Sangam, was shared on social media as recent with a false claim. The video was shared to insinuate that in contrast with Kharge's remarks on Maha Kumbh, Vadra took a holy dip in the Triveni Sangam during the ongoing religious congregation. Claim An Instagram user shared on January 30 a video, claiming it showed Congress leader and Wayanad MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra taking a holy dip in Triveni Sangam, Prayagraj, at the ongoing Maha Kumbh Mela. "Priyanka Gandhi punyasnana at Mahakumbh Mela! Congress President, aren't the noble pillars of your party listening to you?" read a rough translation of the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot of the same: Investigation We first ran the clip showing Priyanka Gandhi through InVid Tool Search and found multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, it found that several other users had shared the same clip with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , with their archive versions available here and here , respectively. The search result also led the Desk to a PTI report carried by The Indian Express on February 11, 2021. The feature image of the report matched one of the keyframes from the viral clip. It mentioned that the image was from Priyanka Gandhi Vadra's visit to Sangam in Prayagraj on the occasion of Mauni Amavasya in 2021. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image establishing that the feature image in the report was the same as the keyframe from the viral video. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across an X post shared from the official X handle of Congress on February 11, 2021. The party's official handle posted two pictures of Priyanka Gandhi Vadra (including one used in the viral video) from her visit to Sangam in Prayagraj on the occasion of Mauni Amavasya in February 2021. "Congress General Secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra took a bath in the Ganga on the auspicious occasion of Mauni Amavasya at the Sangam and offered holy water to the Sun, praying for the prosperity and progress of the country," the party shared in the post. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of Priyanka Gandhi Vadra shared in the name of Maha Kumbh Mela 2025, actually dated back to 2021. In the next part, the Desk ran the visuals of Kharge from the viral clip on Google Lens and came across a video report by India Today, published on Jan 27, 2025. Here is the link to the report: This was the same video as share in the viral posts, which can be seen in the combination image below: Kharge made the remark while addressing the party's 'Jai Bapu, Jai Bhim, Jai Samvidhan' rally in Madhya Pradesh's Mhow district on January 27.

title: PTI Fact Check: Scripted video from Bangladesh falsely shared as real robbery incident on Indian street; details inside
content: New Delhi, February 8 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video purportedly showing a masked person looting a passerby using a hypnosis technique was recently shared on social media, with users claiming it happened in India. The video claimed to showed a motorcycle rider being stopped by a masked person on the street. The latter then gives the rider a paper, which was sprayed with a certain chemical, which hypnotised them, as claimed by the voiceover in the video. the rider can then be seen handing over all his belongings to the masked man. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a scripted video made a Bangladeshi content creator was shared on social media as a real incident, falsely linking it to India. Claim An Instagram user shared a video on January 29, claiming that it showed a robbery on an Indian street through hypnosis. Here is the link and archive link to the post, followed by a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through InVid Tool search and found multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, it found that several users had shared the video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , with their archive links available here and here , respectively. In the next part of investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the viral video and found a watermark of 'The Jim Ahmed' placed on it. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a Facebook handle with the same name. The user of the handle, in the bio, introduced himself as a digital content creator from Bangladesh. Here is the link to the handle, along with a screenshot of the same. The Desk scanned the page and found the same video shared on January 25, 2025. The video included the extended part of the viral video, where the masked man as The Jim Ahmed, a content creator, introduced himself towards the end of the video. Here is the link to the post, followed by a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image showing that the content in the viral video matches that of the Facebook video. Below is another screengrab from the video, where the person identifies himself as a "funny content creator". Further, scanning through the account, the Desk also came across another video posted on the user's handle on January 24, 2025. In reference to the viral video (originally posted on January 23), he mentioned that it was created for entertainment purposes only. Here is the link to the video. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video shared as a robbery incident on an Indian street was actually a scripted video created by a Bangladeshi content creator.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of Cong leaders celebrating party's theme song launch ahead of Delhi elections shared on social media with false claim after poll results
content: New Delhi, Feb 10 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video, claiming to show Congress leaders celebrating BJP's victory in the recently held Delhi Assembly elections. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk revealed that the viral video dated backto January 2025 when the party had launched its theme song for the elections, which the leaders were seen celebrating. The video was shared with a false claim on social media. The counting of votes for the Delhi Assembly polls – held on February 5 – was taken up on February 8. The BJP registered a landslide victory, bagging 48 seats in the 70-member Assembly, marking its return to power in the national capital after 27 years. The Aam Aadmi Party won the remaining 22 seats, whereas the Congress once again failed to open its account. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user named Tarsem Lal shared on February 8 a video, claiming that Congress leaders celebrated BJP's victory in the Delhi Assembly elections. The caption of the post, originally in Hindi, read: "On BJP's victory in Delhi #INDIA head of the alliance. Bhangra dance in Congress office Khushiyan @ArvindKejriwal Team keep this tweet safe. We have been saying this for a long time that the BJP and Congress are together." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found that the same video was shared by several other users with the same claim. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a video report by India Today, dated January 23, 2025 uploaded on their Facebook page. The caption of the post read: "Congress launches a theme song '#DelhiCongressAnthem' for the upcoming Delhi Assembly elections." Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. In the next part of the investigation the Desk found another report by Aaj Tak, dated January 23, 2025, whose headline, originally in Hindi, read: "Leaders danced to the theme song of Congress in Delhi, see VIDEO" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the news report. A video was uploaded by News 24 on their official X handle on January 23, whose caption, originally in Hindi, read: "Delhi Congress launched theme song, leaders danced". This was the same video as the one shared on social media. Here is the link to the X post. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video predated the Delhi Assembly poll results. It shows Congress leaders celebrating the launch of party's theme song during the run-up to the polls.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: 2020 video of fire from Egypt falsely shared as recent in the Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj
content: New Delhi, Feb 10 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of vehicles engulfed in flames, claiming that the incident occurred due to a massive fire that broke out recently at a bus stand near the ongoing Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the viral video was from Egypt and dated back to 2020. The clip actually showed several cars set ablaze from a massive fire in a pipeline. The viral video was shared on social media as recent, falsely linking it to Prayagraj, India. Claim An Instagram user on February 9 shared a video, claiming it showed vehicles engulfed in fire after a massive fire broke out at a bus stand in Maha Kumbh. The text plate running on the video, originally in Hindi, read: "Fire in Maha Kumbh for the third time. Fire broke out in Mahakumbh bus stand. 40 to 50 vehicles burnt to ashes. The fire has not yet been doused off" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found that the same video was shared by several other users with the same claim. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video by Global News uploaded on July 15, 2020, whose title read: "Cars set ablaze after massive fire breaks out along pipeline in Egypt" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image, which shows this is the same video as the one shared on social media. Furthermore, the Desk came across another video showing the same scene from a different angle was uploaded to YouTube on July 14, 2020. A rough translation of the title in English read: "Underground gas pipeline explosion on Cairo-Ismailia desert road" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google that yielded us a report by Reuters dated July 15, 2020. The headline of the report read: "Egyptian oil pipeline fire injures 17" Here is the link to the report. "A major fire broke out after a leak of oil from the Shuqair-Mostorod pipeline next to a busy highway in a Cairo suburb on Tuesday and 17 people were injured, authorities said. The pipeline runs along a motorway on the outskirts of the capital and a spark caused by passing cars ignited crude that was leaking from the pipe, the petroleum ministry said," read a section of the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video shared in the name of Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj, India was is actually from Egypt and dates back to 2020.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Social media post claiming UP cops checked voters' ID cards at polling booth during Milkipur by-election is misleading; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 10 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a photo, claiming that police officials were checking the ID cards of the voters at a polling booth during the Milkipur by-elections. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk revealed that the viral photo was of police officials checking the ID of a booth agent of a political party candidate in Milkipur. The viral photograph was shared with a false claim on social media. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) won the by-elections on Milkipur Assembly seat on Saturday, with its candidate Chandrabhanu Paswan trumping his Samajwadi Party (SP) rival Ajit Prasad by 61,710 votes. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video on February 5 claiming that senior police officials were checking voters' ID cards during the Milkipur by-elections. The caption of the post, originally in Hindi, read: "The Election Commission should immediately take cognisance of the pictures related to the news that the police of Ayodhya is checking the ID cards of voters in Milkipur, in which senior police officers are also involved. This is a democratic crime of indirectly influencing voting by creating fear among the voters." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk conducted a Reverse Image Search on the photo and found several other users shared the same image with a similar claim on social media platforms. Two such posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be found here and here . Notably, Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav also shared the photo on his X handle on February 5. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Upon further analysis of the above X post, the Desk found that Ayodhya Police had shared an X post, which denied the claim and clarified the entire incident. The police said the person seen in the photo was a booth agent, and verification was being done after checking his identity card. "The above photo is of a booth agent's identity card; the person seen in the photo is a booth agent of a candidate, verified by seeing his identity card. Please do not make misleading tweets," shared Ayodhya Police on their official X handle. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Taking a cue from this, the Desk analysed the official X handle of Ayodhya Police and found a video statement by Senior Superintendent of Police, District Ayodhya, Raj Karan Nayyar. "I want to say this very clearly that any police officer is checking no voter IDs at any polling booths. A photo that has come to my notice is being shared with a false claim, as the person seen in the photo is a booth agent of a particular candidate…," said Ayodhya SP Raj Karan Nayyar. Here is the link , and below is a screenshot. On further scanning the search results, the Desk found a combination image uploaded by Ayodhya Police clarifying the entire incident. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant news reports and found a report published by The Mint on February 5. The headline of the report read: "Milkipur by-polls: Ayodhya Police debunks Akhilesh Yadav's claim of 'officials checking IDs of voters', 'Do not make…'" Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral photo was of police officials checking the IDs of a booth agent for a particular candidate in Milkipur.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: 2024 train accident video from Chile falsely shared as recent collision in Lucknow, India; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 10 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video, claiming that it showed a recent incident of collision between a Vande Bharat Express and another train in Lucknow. However, an investigation by PTI Fact Check Desk found that an unrelated video from Chile, dating back to June 2024, was shared on social media as recent, falsely in the name of Lucknow, India. Claim An Instagram user shared on February 4 a video, claiming it showed a recent collision between a Vande Bharat Express and another train in Lucknow. The text overwritten on the video, originally in Hindi, read: "Vande Bharat express accident at 2:00 am, in Lucknow" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across several other social media posts, which carried the same video with similar claims. The link to two such posts can be found here and here and its archived versions can be found here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a report by The Hindu dated June 20, 2024, whose headline read: "Train collision in Chile kills at least 2 people and injures several others" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. The feature image of the report was similar to the visuals of the viral video. Below is a combination image highlighting the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google, which yielded a report by Associated Press, dated June 20, 2024, that featured the similar video as the one seen in the viral clip. The title of the report read: "Chile train collision kills at least 2 people, injures several others" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the YouTube video and viral video being shared on social media. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video was from Chile, and not Lucknow, India.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: 2024 remark by AAP's Sanjay Singh on Arvind Kejriwal's health falsely shared on social media as recent after party's poll debacle in Delhi
content: New Delhi, Feb 11 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): Just days after the BJP won the Delhi Assembly polls, an alleged screenshot of a news report went viral on social media, which quoted AAP MP Sanjay Singh stating that party's national convenor Arvind Kejriwal may slip into coma. However, an investigation by PTI Fact Check Desk found that the alleged statement was made by Singh in July 2024, when Kejriwal was lodged in Tihar Jail in connection with the Delhi excise policy case. A screenshot of the news report from back then was shared on social media with a false claim. The counting of votes for the Delhi Assembly polls – held on February 5 – was taken up on February 8. The BJP registered a landslide victory, bagging 48 seats in the 70-member Assembly, marking its return to power in the national capital after 27 years. The Aam Aadmi Party won the remaining 22 seats, whereas the Congress once again failed to open its account. Claim An Instagram user shared on February 9 a screenshot of an alleged news report by News 24, which quoted AAP MP Sanjay Singh saying that party convenor Arvind Kejriwal could slip into coma. The text in the screenshot from the news report, originally in Hindi, read: "Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal can go into coma: Sanjay Singh" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk conducted a Reverse Image Search on the photo and found that several other users shared the same screenshot with similar claims on social media. Two such posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be found here and here , respectively. Meanwhile, the Desk noticed that the alleged statement by Singh referred to Kejriwal as 'Chief Minister', the post from which he had resigned in September 2024. After him stepping down, Atishi took charge as Delhi CM while Kejriwal remained lodged in jail. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant news reports, and came across a report by India Today, dated July 15, 2024, whose headline read: "Arvind Kejriwal may slip into coma, says AAP, shreds Tihar Jail report". "A team of AIIMS doctors has been examining Arvind Kejriwal's health, and they have found out that Kejriwal is losing weight fast and is suffering from hypoglycemia. His blood sugar level dropped below 50 mg/dL five times, which could have caused him to slip into a coma or even resulted in his death, Sanjay Singh claimed," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. On further scanning the search results, the Desk also found the original X (formerly Twitter) post of News 24, which was uploaded on July 15, 2024. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old and unrelated statement by Sanjay Singh was shared on social media as recent with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered videos falsely shared in name of bead seller Monalisa from Maha Kumbh; details inside
content: New Delhi, February 11 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Two videos were recently shared on social media, with users claiming they featured Monalisa Bhosale, a bead seller from Madhya Pradesh who became an internet sensation after being photographed during the ongoing Maha Kumbh 2025. The videos allegedly showed her in modern outfits, suggesting that her appearance had changed after gaining popularity. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the clips shared on social media were digitally altered using Artificial Intelligence tools. The original videos actually featured social media influencer Tanu Rawat and Bollywood actor Wamiqa Gabbi. Claim Social media users shared two videos of Monalisa Bhosale, a 16-year-old garland seller from Madhya Pradesh who became an internet sensation during the ongoing Maha Kumbh 2025. While the first video purportedly showed her dancing in a modern outfit, the second one showed her interacting with media persons. Investigation The Desk cross-checked the veracity of the two viral videos and here's what we found: Claim 1: Video shows Monalisa dancing in a red outfit to the famous Bollywood song Sharara Here is the link and archive link to the post: The Desk ran the viral video through InVid Tool Search and extracted keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that multiple users had shared the video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archive links can be viewed here and here , respectively. In the next part of investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the viral video and found a watermark of 'NI8.OUT9' placed on it. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across an Instagram handle with the same name. The user, on January 28, had shared the same video as seen in the viral post. However, in the caption, it was clearly mentioned that this video was created using face-swap technology for entertainment purposes only. "The images and likenesses of actors shown here are digitally altered and do not reflect the real appearances, endorsements, or opinions of the individuals depicted. No intention to deceive or mislead; all content is meant solely for fun and creative expression. Viewer discretion is advised," the disclaimer in the post stated. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image showing that the content in the viral video matches that of the Instagram video. Further, the search results also led the Desk to an Instagram handle of a user named Tanu Rawat. Scanning through the handle, the Desk found that the user had shared the original video of herself dancing to the Bollywood song on December 11, 2024. Here is the link to the post: Below is a combination image clearly highlighting that the video was digitally altered. Claim 2: Video of Monalisa in a black dress waving to the media Here is the link and archive link to the post: The Desk ran the video through the InVid tool search and extracted keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archive links can be viewed here and here , respectively. The search results led the Desk to a report published by Bollywood Hungama. The feature image of the report matched the description of the person seen in the viral video. However, a close analysis of the image revealed that it was actually Bollywood actor Wamiqa Gabbi. The viral video, on the other hand, featured internet sensation Monalisa. Below is a combination image highlighting the same. Next, the Desk scanned through the viral posts and found several users commenting that the video of internet sensation Monalisa Bhosale was AI-generated. Below are two such comments highlighting the same: Taking a cue from the above information, the Desk ran the keyframe featuring Monalisa through WasItAI (an AI detection tool), which suggested a substantial presence of AI content. Below is a screenshot of the result: The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search and came across the original video of Wamiqa Gabbi waving to the media on the Instagram page of Bollywood Chronicle on January 16. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the videos shared on social media were digitally altered, where the faces of an influencer and an actress were swapped with that of Monalisa Bhosale.

title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated photo of Sonakshi Sinha wearing hijab shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, Feb 11 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A purported photo of Bollywood actor Sonakshi Sinha wearing hijab and standing alongside her husband and fellow actor Zaheer Iqbal, who wore a skull cap, was recently shared on social media. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an AI-generated photo was shared on social media as real with a false claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a photo on February 10 claiming it showed Bollywood actress Sonakshi Sinha wearing hijab, along with her husband and fellow actor Zaheer Iqbal in a skull cap. "Sonakshi Sinha used to post very few photos earlier. But ever since she got married to Zaheer Iqbal, she keeps sparking the fans' excitement and posts photos every day! Today she posted a photo in a burqa with Zaheer Iqbal. I don't know how the crab will feel now," the user shared in the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and found that it was shared by several other users with a similar claim. Two such posts can be seen here and here , with their archive versions available here and here , respectively. On further analysis of the posts, the Desk noticed several users commenting that the image was AI-generated. Below are screenshots of two such comments: Taking a cue from this, the Desk carefully examined the image and noticed several discrepancies, suggesting that it was AI-generated. For instance, the background in the image was blurred. Additionally, the faces of the two in the viral image appeared to be forcefully added. Below is a photo highlighting the same: In the next part of investigation, the Desk ran the image through WasItAI (an AI detection tool), that suggested a substantial presence of AI content. Below is a screenshot of the result: Further, the Desk also ran the image through Hive Moderation, another AI detection tool, which confirmed a significant presence of AI-generated content. Below is a screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the photo of Sonakshi Sinha and Zaheer Iqbal shared on social media was AI-generated.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Scripted video shared on social media with false claim of showing police parading Maha Kumbh stampede accused; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 12 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing policemen parading three men in prisoners' uniforms was recently shared on social media, with users claiming they were arrested in connection with the recent stampede at the Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was actually part of an awareness campaign, in which the three men portrayed freedom fighters Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, and Sukhdev. The unrelated video was falsely linked to the Maha Kumbh stampede incident and circulated on social media. Claim A video shared on YouTube on February 4 claimed to show UP Police personnel parading the three accused arrested in connection with the stampede incident that occurred during the Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj on January 29, 2025. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through InVid Tool Search and found multiple keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , with their archive links available here and here , respectively. The search results further led the Desk to a video published on a YouTube channel named 'Dicky Bari.' The video featured the three people wearing the same costume as seen in the viral post. However, in this video, they mentioned that they were portraying the characters of Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, and Sukhdev to bring awareness among the youth regarding the freedom fighters' contribution to the nation's struggle for independence. "We are walking on the banks of the Ganga at Maha Kumbh to remind people of the sacrifices of Rajguru, Bhagat Singh, and Sukhdev," ​one of the person potraying the character said. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image which shows that the people seen in the viral video were the same as those in the YouTube video. The search result also led the Desk to two other videos posted by the YouTube channel covering the same development. In these videos too, the three stated that they were dressed as Rajguru, Bhagat Singh, and Sukhdev to remind people of the formers' contributions to India's independence. The two videos can be seen here and here . In the next part of investigation, the Desk carefully scanned through the above mentioned three videos published by the YouTube channel. It was found that the videos were published on January 21, January 22, and January 24, all predating the day the stampede incident happened. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a scripted video – part of an awareness campaign – was falsely linked to the Maha Kumbh Mela stampede incident.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Social media posts claiming hike in Delhi Metro fares by 50% after BJP's victory in assembly polls are fake and baseless
content: New Delhi, Feb 12 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A post claiming a rise in Delhi Metro fares was recently shared on social media. Users alleged that metro ticket prices had increased by up to 50% and that this hike was implemented immediately after the BJP was elected to power in Delhi in the recently concluded Assembly polls. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found this claim to be false. The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) did not announce any such fare hike. Notably, it was the Bengaluru Metro Rail Corporation Limited that announced an increase in ticket prices, raising the maximum fare by 50 per cent. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a post on February 11, claiming that the Delhi Metro authorities had announced a fare hike by 50 per cent. The user alleged that this came immediately after the BJP won in the recently concluded Delhi Assembly polls. "As soon as the Modi government entered Delhi, it gave a gift to the people of the country by increasing metro fares by 50% from Sunday. The Modi government has given good news to the people of Delhi," the user wrote in the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, followed by a screenshot: Investigation The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found that several users had shared similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , along with their archive links ( Link 1 , Link 2 ) found here respectively. One such post claimed that Delhi Metro fares had increased from ₹60 to ₹90. Here is the link and archive link to the post, followed by a screenshot: In the next part of investigation, the Desk scanned the official website and social media handles of the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation. However, no details regarding a fare hike were found. The search results, however, led the Desk to multiple media reports stating that the Bengaluru Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) had recently increased metro fares. According to a Hindustan Times report, BMRCL announced a fare increase of about 50% on February 8. The maximum fare has risen from ₹60 to ₹90. Here is the link to the report, followed by a screenshot: Additionally, few media reports also indicated that fares for the Rapid Metro operating on Golf Course Road in Cyber City, Gurugram, will also increase. Currently, the minimum fare for the Gurugram Rapid Metro is ₹20, and the maximum fare is ₹35. After the hike, they will become ₹25 and ₹40, respectively. Here is the link to the report shared by News 24, followed by a screenshot: In the next part of investigation, the Desk reached out to an official from the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation, who denied any such proposal linked to an increase in Delhi Metro fares. "This is in reference to some social media posts claiming that Delhi Metro fares have been revised. Delhi Metro's fares can only be revised by an independent Fare Fixation Committee, which is nominated by the Government. Presently, there is no such proposal for the constitution of any Fare Fixation Committee," said Anuj Dayal, Principal Executive Director. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral claim about a fare hike in the Delhi Metro was fake and baseless.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Poll campaign video of AIMIM's Mustafabad candidate Tahir Hussain falsely shared as him holding rally after his defeat in Delhi elections
content: New Delhi, Feb 12 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that it showed AIMIM candidate from Mustafabad constituency, Tahir Hussain, holding a large public rally after his defeat in the recently concluded Delhi Assembly elections. However, an investigation by PTI Fact Check Desk found that the viral video showed Hussain campaigning during the run-up to the Assembly polls. The viral video was shared on social media with a false claim. Hussain contested from the Mustafabad constituency, bagged 33,474 votes to secure the third position after BJP's Mohan Singh Bisht and AAP's Adeel Ahmad Khan. Bisht won by securing 85,215 votes. Hussain was suspended from AAP in 2020, after being named as an accused in a case linked to the death of Intelligence Bureau staffer Ankit Sharma during the riots in Northeast Delhi in February 2020, which left 53 people dead. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on February 8 a video of AIMIM leader Tahir Hussain, claiming that he took out a huge procession after his defeat in the Delhi Assembly elections. The caption of the post, originally in Hindi, read: "Procession of Tahir Hussain after defeat. What did you understand by seeing this crowd?" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across several other social media posts, which carried the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be found here and here , respectively. Initially, the Desk conducted customised keyword research on Google and found several news reports which mentioned that he was granted six-day in-custodial parole from January 29, 2025 to February 3, 2025 for canvassing for 12 hours daily. Here is the link to a report published by Hindustan Times on January 30, 2025. The headline of the report read: "After 12 hours of canvassing, Tahir Hussain back in jail" Here is the link to the report. "On Tuesday, the Supreme Court granted Hussain a six-day custodial parole to campaign for 12 hours daily till February 3. He left Tihar around 6am and hit the streets of Mustafabad by 8am. Addressing a gathering at 25 Futa Road, he credited "the people's love" for his candidacy," read a section of the report. On further scanning the search results, the Desk found a reel uploaded on Tahir Hussain's official Facebook page on February 3, 2025. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the Facebook video shared by Tahir Hussain. Notably, he was granted parole for campaigning till February 3, whereas the counting of votes was taken up on February 8. On further scanning the search results, we came across a video uploaded on the X handle of AIMIM Delhi State President Dr. Shoaib Jamai on February 3, 2025. "Before the end of the election campaign, a huge rally was held in Mustafabad today and the support of thousands of people in support of Tahir Hussain will, Insha Allah, be converted into votes. Thanks to Hyderabad MLA Majid Hussain sahab. Today the people of Mustafabad have chosen their leader," read the caption of the post, originally in Hindi. Here is the link to the post. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of AIMIM leader Tahir Hussain holding a rally was from the run-up to Delhi Assembly polls, and not after his poll defeat.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Social media posts claiming French President Emmanuel Macron 'ignored' PM Modi at AI Action Summit are misleading; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 12 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video of French President Emmanuel Macron was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that he 'ignored' Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the Paris AI Action Summit and did not shake hands with him. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a selected video was shared on social media to falsely create the impression of Macron "ignoring" the Indian PM, whereas in reality, the two leaders shook hands and even hugged several times during PM Modi's visit to Paris and Marseille. In fact, Macron showed special gesture as he received PM Modi from the airport and escorted him back as the latter flew to the United States. On the invitation of Macron, PM Modi was in France from February 10 to 12, during which he co-chaired the AI Action Summit, held bilateral talks with Macron, jointly inaugurated the Consulate General of India in Marseille, visit the Mazargues War Cemetery and the ITER facility. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user named Veena Jain shared a video of French President Emmanuel Macron, claiming that he 'ignored' shaking hands withPM Modi at the Paris AI Action Summit. The caption of the post, that has garnered 59.9k views so far, read: "Emmanuel Macron shouldn't have done this. World Number 1 leader Narendra Modi G tried three times to shake hands with him, but he intentionally ignored. Sh@me on you Macron" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk conducted a Reverse Image Search on the photo and found that several other users shared the same screenshot with similar claims on social media. Two such posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be found here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an extended version of the viral video on X. The 1:13-minute-long video showed PM Modi and French President Emmanuel Macron entering together at the conference hall, where the AI Action Sumit was held. Here is the link to the X post shared on February 11, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below are two combination images highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the full video shared on social media. We then documented PM's visit to France and the various instances when the two leaders were seen together. We scanned PM Modi's X handle and found that the two leaders met several times. A February 11 post carried photos of the two leaders hugging each other when Macron received PM Modi at the airport. Here is the link to the X post, and below is a screenshot of the same: In another post, PM Modi shared glimpses from the AI Action Summit in Paris. The caption of the post read: "The AI Action Summit in Paris is a commendable effort to bring together world leaders, policy makers, thinkers, innovators and youngsters to have meaningful conversations around AI." Here is the link to the X post and below are two screenshots. In another post on X, PM Modi stressed that India-France CEO Forum plays a key role in strengthening economic ties and fostering innovation. "The India-France CEO Forum plays a key role in strengthening economic ties and fostering innovation. It is gladdening to see business leaders from both nations collaborate and create new opportunities across key sectors. This drives growth, investment and ensures a better future for the coming generations," read the X post. Here is the link to the post and below is the screenshot. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk scanned the YouTube handle of Narendra Modi and found a 2:53-minute-long video, whose title read: "India-France partnership stronger than ever! PM Modi's Paris visit recap" While analysing the entire video, we found several clips where the French President and PM Modi could be seen shaking hands. Here is the link to the video and below are a few screengrabs where the two can be seen shaking hands. PM Modi also shared a picture of the two leaders when they reached Marseille. The caption of the post read: "President Macron and I reached Marseille a short while ago. This visit will witness important programmes aimed at further connecting India and France. The Indian consulate which is being inaugurated will deepen people-to-people linkages. I will also pay homage to the Indian soldiers martyred in First and Second World Wars." Here is the link to the X post and below is a screenshot. In another X post, PM Modi shared the photo of him and Macron raising their hands in unity after the inauguration of Indian consulate in Marseille on February 12. Here is the link to the post and below is the photo shared in it. At the Mazargues War Cemetery, President Macron and PM Modi paid homage to the soldiers who fought in the world wars. A report was publised on YouTube by News 9 Live. Here is the link to the report and below is screenshot. We also found an X post by PTI which carried the video of Macron escorting PM Modi to the airport, from where he flew for United States. Here is the link to the X post and below is a screenshot of the same. Another X post by PTI read: "In yet another special gesture, President Macron comes to the Marseille airport to see off PM Modi as he emplanes for Washington" Here is the link to the post and below is the screenshot. While the clip shared on social media was not edited, it selected a particular incident to falsely claim that Macron ignored the PM at the Summit. In reality, the two leaders arrived together at the event. Also, the entire visit of PM Modi included several such instances where the two leaders shook hands and hugged each other, displaying a strong bonhomie between the two.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: 2021 video of corpses floating in Ganga during COVID-19 pandemic falsely shared in name of Maha Kumbh Mela 2025 in Prayagraj
content: New Delhi, Feb 13 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video – an alleged news report – claiming it showed bodies of devotees floating in the Ganga in Uttar Pradesh's Ghazipur amidst the celebration of the Maha Kumbh Mela 2025 in Prayagraj. However, an investigation by PTI Fact Check Desk revealed that the video dated back to 2021 and showed a journalist reporting on the bodies lying on the banks of Ganga in Ghazipur during the COVID-19 pandemic. The four-year-old unrelated video was shared on social media as recent, falsely linking it to the Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on February 6a purported news report that claimed to show bodies lying on the banks of Ganga in UP's Ghazipur during the ongoing Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj. The caption of the post, originally in Hindi, read: "This video exposes Modi and Yogi in Ghazipur, UP. Hundreds of corpses are floating in the Ganges. On one side the drum of #महाकुंभ_प्रयागराज is being blown and on the other side corpses are being thrown in the same Ganges. A government of liars, fraudsters and shameless people is running in the country and the state." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across several other social media posts, which carried the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be found here and here , respectively. In the next part of investigation, The Desk conducted a customised keyword search and found a 23:42-minute-long video uploaded on YouTube on May 17, 2021 by one BrajbhushanMarkandey. The title of the video, originally in Hindi, read: "When CM Yogi was called; People with weak hearts should not watch! Dogs were tearing them apart! They were not worth counting!" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same. This was an extended version of the video shared on social media recently, as can be seen in the combination image below: The description of the video stated that the reporter witnessed over two dozen dead bodies on the banks of the Ganga near Har Balam Pur village in Ghazipur, Uttar Pradesh, on 17 May 2021. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports and came across a report by India Today uploaded on their YouTube on May 14, 2021. The title of the report read: "Bihar: More Dead Bodies Found Floating In Ganga River In Ghazipur & Buxar| India Today Ground Report" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. Another report published by BBC on May 19, 2021, mentioned that hundreds of corpses have been floating in the river or buried in the sand of its banks, adding that the bodies were suspected to be COVID-19 victims. The title of the report read: "Covid-19: India's holiest river is swollen with bodies" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. "Hundreds of corpses have been found floating in the river or buried in the sand of its banks. Those who live close to where they have washed up, in the northern state of Uttar Pradesh, fear they are Covid-19 victims," mentioned a section of the report. The Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find if such an incident had happened during the Maha Kumbh Mela, but the search did not yield us any report substantiating the viral claim. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dated back to 2021 and allegedly showed bodies lying on the banks of Ganga in UP's Ghazipur during the COVID-19 pandemic.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of clashes at Pushpa-2 event in Patna falsely shared as Maha Kumbh 2025 incident; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 13 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video was recently circulated on social media, with some users claiming it showed an unruly crowd clashing with security officials. The video was shared with the claim that it was from Prayagraj, where a crowd gathered for the Maha Kumbh allegedly threw slippers at army officers attempting to maintain security. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found this claim false. The investigation revealed that the video is from the trailer launch event of Pushpa-2, held at Gandhi Maidan in Patna in November 2024. It has no connection to the ongoing Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video on February 12, claiming it showed an unruly crowd from Maha Kumbh throwing slippers at army officials present there. "At Kumbh, nationalist and Sanatani people threw slippers at army men. Had they been Muslims, this would have been the news on all government media channels today, but perhaps all this is allowed for people of this religion," the user shared the video with the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several users shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen [ here ] and [ here ], and their archive links can be found [ here ] and [ here ], respectively. The search results also led the Desk to a post shared by a media portal named Now India on its official Instagram account on November 18, 2024. The post contained image similar to the visuals from the viral video. However, its caption stated it to be from Patna's Gandhi Maidan, where the filmmakers of Pushpa-2 had organised a trailer launch. However, there a stampede like situation occurred as over 200,000 people gathered for the event. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. A combination of images was also attached, showing that the content seen in the viral post matches that of the Instagram post. In the next part of the investigation, taking cue from the above generated input, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google. It came across a video posted by News18 Bihar/Jharkhand on its official YouTube handle on November 17, 2024. The video showed scenes from Gandhi Maidan in Patna, where a large crowd gathered to meet their favourite stars from Pushpa-2. However, as the situation turned violent, police resorted to a lathi charge. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. In the subsequent part of the investigation, the customised keyword search led the Desk to a report published by Zee News covering the incident on November 17, 2024. According to the report, actors Allu Arjun and Rashmika Mandanna had reached Gandhi Maidan in Patna for the trailer launch event of Pushpa-2. A massive crowd gathered to see them, and fans went out of control, trying to catch a glimpse of them. The situation became so chaotic that the police had to resort to a lathi charge, leading to angry people throwing slippers at the stage and breaking barricades. Here is the link to the report: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video is not from the ongoing Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj but from the trailer launch event of Pushpa-2, held last year at Gandhi Maidan in Patna. The police and security forces struggled to control the massive crowd. Users share old and unrelated videos with false claims, linking them to Maha Kumbh 2025.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of Diljit Dosanjh praising UP govt for his concert arrangements last year falsely shared as praise for Maha Kumbh arrangements
content: New Delhi, Feb 13 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media, with some users claiming it showed popular Indian singer and actor Diljit Dosanjh praising the Yogi Adityanath-led Uttar Pradesh government for its arrangements during the ongoing Maha Kumbh 2025. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found the video clipped and shared with a misleading claim. In the original video, Dosanjh praised the state authorities for the arrangements made during his concert in Lucknow in 2024, not for the Maha Kumbh. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a February 11 video showing popular Indian singer and actor Diljit Dosanjh lauding the Yogi Adityanath-led Uttar Pradesh government for its arrangements during the ongoing Maha Kumbh 2025. The user shared the video with the caption, "What happened to Diljit? Now he's praising CM Yogi ji for Mahakumbh arrangements. " Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid Tool Search and found multiple keyframes. By running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several users shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found [ here ] and [ here ], with their archived links viewed [ here ] and [ here ] respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to corroborate the claims made in the viral post. It came across Diljit Dosanjh's official Instagram handle, which has around 25.4 million followers. Here is the link to the handle, along with a screenshot: While scanning through his account, the Desk found a live video posted on February 9, 2025. The video contained the clipped portion that had been shared in the viral post; however, Dosanjh was not heard praising the UP government for its arrangements during the ongoing Maha Kumbh. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image showing that the visuals in the viral video match those in the Instagram video. Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk carefully watched the 40-minute video shared by Diljit Dosanjh on his official handle. At the 18:00 timestamp, Dosanjh thanked everyone for supporting him during his India tour. At around the 18:09 timestamp, he was seen responding to a comment about his visit to Lucknow for a concert, confirming that he had already performed there. However, at the 18:28 timestamp, the segment from the viral clip appeared, where Dosanjh thanked the UP government for the preparations made during his Dil-Luminati India Tour. "I want to say a special thanks to the UP government for their special arrangements," Dosanjh said, which matches his statement in the viral video. However, as the video progressed, it became evident that Dosanjh immediately praised Ludhiana after mentioning UP for the best arrangements made during his concert. This reference to Ludhiana was omitted in the viral video, making it appear that he was only talking about UP. Meanwhile, to learn more about the Indian singer's concert in Lucknow, the Desk again conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found a social media post by Dosanjh on November 23, 2024. In the post, the singer thanked the Uttar Pradesh Police for the arrangements made during his Dil-Luminati India Tour. "Thank you so much. We received the best arrangements from UP. I am their fan now. Very respectful host," Dosanjh wrote. Here is the link to the X post, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that popular Indian singer and actor Diljit Dosanjh praised the UP administration for his concert arrangements, not for the preparations made during Maha Kumbh 2025.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: 10-year-old video of Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati facing police action in Varanasi falsely shared on social media as a recent incident
content: New Delhi, Feb 13 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video was recently shared on social media with users claiming it showed Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati of the Jyotish Peeth in Uttarakhand being chased and beaten by police forces. The video was shared with the claim that the incident happened recently. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk, in its investigation, found the claim to be false. The video dated back to 2015 and depicted police action on Hindu seers, including Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati, who were staging a sit-in protest in Varanasi to demand immersion of Lord Ganesha idols in river Ganga. The decade-old video was shared on social media as recent with a false claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video on February 11, claiming it showed Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati of the Jyotish Peeth in Uttarakhand being thrashed and beaten up by police. Users shared the video, alleging that the incident occurred recently. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid Tool search and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, it found that several users had shared the video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , with their archive links available here and here , respectively. In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by India Today on September 23, 2015. The report mentioned about a crackdown (lathicharge) in Varanasi by authorities against some Hindu seers, including Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati, who were holding a sit-in protest demanding the immersion of Ganesha idols in the Ganga. Over two dozen people, including Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati, suffered injuries in the lathicharge ordered by the Akhilesh Yadav-led SP regime in the state, the report added. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot of the same: Further, the search result also led the Desk to a video published on the official YouTube channel of First India News on September 23, 2015. The video showed an extended version of the visuals seen in the viral post, where police lathicharged seers, including Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati, amid their protest over immersing Lord Ganesha's idols in the Ganga. The video's description stated: "The conflict started over the immersion of a Ganesha idol in the Ganga river. Protesters threw stones at the police, leading to chaos. Over 15 people were injured in the baton charge. The police and the PAC initially warned people to vacate the intersection. However, the protesters continued shouting slogans in defiance. Police arrested around 25 people from the spot." Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image showing that the viral video content matches the YouTube footage. Additionally, during the investigation, the Desk conducted a further keyword search on Google and came across a report published by Daily Pioneer on April 13, 2021. The report mentioned that Samajwadi Party President Akhilesh Yadav apologised to the late Shankaracharya Swami Swaroopanand and his disciple, Swami Avimukteshwaranand (who is now the Shankaracharya of the Jyotish Peeth in Uttarakhand), for the 2015 lathicharge in Varanasi. It is pertinent to note that at the time of the incident, Akhilesh Yadav was the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video shared on social media dates back to 2015 from Varanasi, when there was Samajwadi Party government in the state.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Podcaster Ranveer Allahbadia's 3-year-old video from COVID times falsely shared as recent after India's Got Latent controversy; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 13 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of podcaster Ranveer Allahbadia crying inconsolably and speaking about his work being impacted was recently shared on social media. Users claimed it was his reaction to the recent controversy over his remarks on comedian Samay Raina's YouTube show, India's Got Latent. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found this claim to be false. The investigation revealed that the video was originally from April 2021, when Allahbadia had tested positive for COVID-19, leading to a temporary halt in his team's work. Despite this, social media users shared the nearly three-year-old video with a false claim, presenting it as recent. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video on February 12 showing podcaster and content creator Ranveer Allahbadia (also popularly known as BeerBiceps) getting emotional on camera. Users shared the video, claiming it was Allahbadia's reaction (where he was crying inconsolably and talking about his work being impacted) over a recent controversy surrounding his statement on comedian Samay Raina's show India's Got Latent.
