Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool search and found multiple keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be found here and here . In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find details about Allahbadia's reaction to the controversy surrounding his statement. The search results led the Desk to a video posted on his official X handle on February 10, in which Allahbadia apologised to the public for his comment. However, this video does not match the one seen in the viral post. Here is the original link to the video of Allahbadia apologising to the public for his controversial statement. Below is also a screenshot of the same: Additionally, to find details about when the viral video of Allahbadia crying inconsolably was originally shot, the Desk ran keyframes of it through Google Lens and came across a video uploaded on his official YouTube channel on April 7, 2021. The video contained the clipped portion shared in the viral post; however, the timeline and description confirmed it was from the COVID-19 period. The video was titled "This Is NOT Clickbait—My COVID-19 Experience." Further, as the Desk carefully watched the video, it heard Ranveer say that his COVID test came back positive, so he had to stay in quarantine for 14 days. He further states that he is feeling bad because all the work has stopped because of him. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot: Below, a combination image has been attached, showing that the content seen in the viral video matches that of the YouTube video. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video's origins date back to April 2021, when Ranveer Allahbadia tested positive for COVID-19. Users are sharing a nearly three-year-old video with a false claim, calling it recent.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of Kannada actor Tukali Santhosh and his wife falsely linked to traffic condition in Prayagraj amid Maha Kumbh Mela 2025
content: New Delhi, Feb 13 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video, claiming that it showed a couple crying after their vehicle was stuck in a traffic jam in Prayagraj during the ongoing Maha Kumbh Mela in the city. The video showed people surrounding a car and shouting on the couple inside, that was seemingly crying. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the couple in the car was Kannada Bigg Boss fame Tukali Santhosh and his wife Manasa Santu after attending Bigg Boss Kannada Season 11 finale in Bengaluru. The unrelated video was falsely linked to the Maha Kumbh Mela 2025 in Prayagraj. Amid the unprecedented influx of devotees to Prayagraj for the Maha Kumbh mela, the roads and highways leading to the city have been jam-packed over the past several days, with traffic jams stretching to several kilometres. Reports claimed that several people struggled to find drinking water and other essentials as they remained stuck in traffic jam for several hours. Claim An Instagram user shared on February 1 a video of people surrounding a car, claiming that those stuck in traffic in Prayagraj could be seen crying. The caption of the post read: "Mahakumbh Prayagraj2025 mai fase log Royce" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found that the same video was shared by several other users with the same claim. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. On analysing the viral video closely, we found Suman TV Kannada's watermark and logo on the video. Taking a cue from this, the Desk found the video on their official Instagram account uploaded on January 27, 2025. The caption mentioned hashtag "#thukalisantosh". Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. On further scanning the search results, the Desk found that a similar video was uploaded by Tv19 Kannada on their Instagram account on January 27, 2025. The caption of the post read: "Fans betrayed Tukali Manasa" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and Instagram video. In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search that led us to a report by Asianet News. "No one was harmed, don't make it viral by mistake; Tukali Santosh apologizes to people – Manasa," read a translation of the title, originally in Kannada. A section of the report read: "It was around 2.30 am when the finale of Bigg Boss Season 11 ended and the contestants and others who were present came out. However, fans were still waiting to take selfies. At this time, fans were crowding around each car coming out of the main gate, asking for selfies. The situation was such that it was not possible to open the car window or door to take selfies. Since it was late at night, everyone was tired. At this time, people were crowding around the car of Tukali Santosh and Manasa." Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video of Kannada Bigg Boss fame Tukali Santhosh and his wife Manasa Santhosh, surrounded by a crowd, was falsely linked to Maha Kumbh 2025.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of Bollywood actors Akshay Kumar and Tiger Shroff visiting Abu Dhabi's Hindu temple falsely shared in name of Maha Kumbh; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 14 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media, with users claiming it showed Bollywood actors Akshay Kumar and Tiger Shroff arriving in Prayagraj to attend the ongoing Maha Kumbh 2025. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found this claim to be false. The viral video dates back to April 9, 2024, when the actors visited Abu Dhabi's BAPS Hindu Mandir before the release of their highly anticipated film, Bade Miyan Chote Miyan. The old and unrelated video was falsely shared on social media as recent, misleadingly linking it to the Maha Kumbh Mela. Claim A Facebook user shared a video on February 4, claiming it showed popular Bollywood actors Akshay Kumar and Tiger Shroff arrived in Prayagraj to attend the ongoing Maha Kumbh 2025. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and found multiple keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen ( here ) and ( here ), and their archived versions can be found ( here ) and ( here ), respectively. The search result also led the Desk to a report published by a media portal named Spotboye on April 10, 2024. The report's feature image matches a keyframe the Desk extracted from the viral video. However, the report's title confirmed it to be from Abu Dhabi's BAPS Hindu Mandir, where Akshay Kumar and Tiger Shroff visited ahead of their Bade Miyan Chote Miyan movie release. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot of the same. Below, a combination image has been attached, showing that the content seen in the viral video matches that of the feature image in the news report. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above findings, the desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google. It came across a video posted by Akshay Kumar on his official Instagram account on April 9, 2024. The video included the extended part of the viral post, showing Akshay Kumar and Tiger Shroff's visit to Abu Dhabi's BAPS Hindu Mandir in April 2024. "Got the opportunity to visit the BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi; it was an absolutely divine experience," Kumar shared in the post caption. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of Akshay Kumar and Tiger Shroff shared as their trip to Prayagraj for Maha Kumbh was originally from their visit to Abu Dhabi's BAPS Hindu Mandir in April 2024 ahead of their movie release.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, Zepto did not offer full-scale delivery of Skoda cars; campaign designed to create curiosity around test drives shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, Feb 14 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Social media users recently shared posts claiming the quick-commerce company Zepto has offered to deliver Skoda cars within 10 minutes following its partnership with Skoda India. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found this claim false. Zepto confirmed to the Desk that it launched a campaign to generate curiosity around the Skoda Kushaq test drives. The campaign was not about full-scale vehicle delivery service. Claim On February 6, an X (formerly Twitter) user shared a post claiming that Zepto will deliver cars to your doorstep within 10 minutes after it partners with Skoda India Cars. The post's caption, read: "Big news! Skoda and Zepto are partnering to deliver cars in just 10 minutes." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and found several other users shared it with a similar claim. Two such posts can be seen here and here , with their archive versions available here and here respectively. We first scanned Zepto's official handle and found an Instagram post dated February 4. The caption read: "Humare pass mixer hai, phone hai, tablet hai, aur abb…Coming soon on 8th Feb! #SkodaIndia #SkodaIndiaNewEra #LetsExplore." Skoda India shared the post on its official Instagram account. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports. It came across a report by HT Auto, dated February 6, whose headline read: "Test drive delivered in 10 minutes: Zepto to bring Skoda Kylaq straight to your doorstep." Here is the link to the report, as well as a screenshot. Another report was also published by Outlook startup on February 10, whose headline read: "Zepto's 10-Min Skoda Test-Drive Delivery: Can Q-Commerce Deliver Products Like Cars?" Here is the link to the report. The Desk also came across a LinkedIn post by Aadit Palicha, Co-Founder and CEO of Zepto, dated February 6, 2025. The post mentioned that they are not delivering cars in 10 minutes yet. "No, We're Not Delivering Cars in 10 Minutes… yet. We've seen the headlines—Skoda & Zepto delivering cars in 10 minutes?! We love the energy, but let's clear things up: you won't be ordering a Škoda Kylaq from the Zepto app (as tempting as that sounds). What you can get in 10 minutes? A test drive of the Škoda Kylaq for now :) But… who knows what the future holds?" wrote the CEO. Here is the link , and below is a screenshot. Further, the Desk emailed the Zepto PR team, who clarified that the teaser was meant to generate curiosity around a test drive of the Skoda Kylaq for now, not a full-scale vehicle delivery. "Regarding your query on the latest Zepto X Skoda teaser campaign. To clarify, as Aadit Palicha, Co-founder & CEO of Zepto, shared on LinkedIn, Zepto is not delivering cars in 10 minutes. The teaser was meant to generate curiosity about a test drive of the Skoda Kylaq for now, not a full-scale delivery of vehicles," read the email response from the team. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Zepto would give a test drive from Skoda Kylaq and not deliver cars in 10 minutes.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video of fire at Dubai's Burj Khalifa falsely shared as real on social media; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 15 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ) : A video recently circulated on social media, with users claiming it showed Dubai's Burj Khalifa engulfed in flames as people ran in panic. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found this claim to be false. The video was AI-generated and falsely shared on social media as a real incident. Claim A Facebook user shared a video on February 12, claiming it showed visuals of a massive fire that broke out at Burj Khalifa on February 11. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. In the next investigation stage, the Desk carefully scanned through the comment section of the viral video and found several users commenting that the video was fake and AI-generated. Below are screenshots of two such comments: The Desk also carefully scanned the viral post and found several discrepancies in the video, indicating it was AI-generated. For instance, the background in the video appeared unnaturally blurred, and the usual trees were spotted surrounding the pathway toward Burj Khalifa. Below is a screenshot highlighting these inconsistencies: In the final part of the investigation, taking cues from the previous findings, the Desk ran multiple extracted keyframes from the viral video through Hive Moderation, an AI detection tool. The results indicated a substantial presence of AI-generated content. Below are screenshots of the results: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of Burj Khalifa engulfed in a thick blanket of fire was AI-generated. It would have been major news if such an incident had actually occurred at Dubai's Burj Khalifa skyscraper.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2021 Japan earthquake video falsely shared in name of Feb 17 tremors in Delhi-NCR; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 17 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Hours after a 4.0-magnitude earthquake was felt in Delhi-NCR, several videos showing water splashing out of a bathtub were shared on social media, with users claiming it was caused by the tremors that jolted the national capital and its adjoining areas. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral video actually dates back to 2021, when tremors were felt in Japan. The video was shared with a false claim unrelated to the February 17 earthquake in the Delhi-NCR region. A 4.0-magnitude earthquake struck Delhi early Monday morning, and mild tremors were felt across north India. According to an update from the National Centre for Seismology, the nodal agency that monitors earthquake activity, the quake occurred at a depth of approximately 5 km in Delhi. Claim On February 17, an X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video of water spilling out of a bathtub, claiming that a severe earthquake had jolted the national capital. The caption of the post, which garnered 196.6k views, read: "It was as bad as this in Delhi NCR #earthquake" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a video uploaded on YouTube by Jukin Media on February 16, 2021. The video's title read: "Water Spills Out of Bathtub as it Shakes Rigorously During Earthquake in Japan." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Below are the combination images highlighting the similarities between the viral and YouTube videos shared in 2021. Taking a cue, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports. It came across a video uploaded on The Weather Channel on February 23, 2021. The report mentioned that a 7.1 magnitude earthquake on the Richter scale hit Japan's Chiba. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. The Desk came across another report by Al Jazeera dated February 13, 2021, whose headline read: "Blackouts, injuries as quake hits off Japan's Fukushima coast." A section of the report read: "A magnitude 7.3 earthquake has struck off Japan's east coast, rattling a region hit by a powerful 2011 quake, tsunami, and nuclear meltdown just weeks before the disaster's 10th anniversary. The earthquake on Saturday produced powerful shaking along the coast and was felt strongly in the capital, Tokyo, but triggered no tsunami alert." Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to the 2021 Japan earthquake and is unrelated to the recent tremors in Delhi.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old earthquake video falsely shared in name of February 17 quake in Delhi-NCR; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 17 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A CCTV footage captured outside a house was recently circulated on social media, with some users claiming it showed the impact of the earthquake that struck the Delhi-NCR region in the early hours of Monday (February 17). The video, purportedly showing disturbing visuals, depicted the surroundings shaking violently, accompanied by a loud thundering sound in the background as the earthquake hit. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found this claim to be false. Many users previously shared the video in the name of an earthquake that occurred in Pakistan's Islamabad on February 15. The unrelated footage, possibly from Pakistan (the source of the video couldn't be verified), was falsely shared with a claim that it captured the impact of the Feb 17 tremors in the Delhi-NCR region. The National Centre for Seismology reported a 4.0-magnitude earthquake early Monday in the Delhi-NCR region. While there were no immediate reports of damage or injuries, a loud sound was heard as the earthquake struck. An official speaking to PTI confirmed that the epicenter was near Durgabai Deshmukh College of Special Education in Dhaula Kuan, New Delhi. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on February 17 a video claiming it had been shot outside his house and showing the exact moment when the 4.0-magnitude earthquake hit the Delhi-NCR region in the early hours of Monday. The video showed the house's surroundings shaking terribly, with a thundering sound in the background. "Just look at the blast and wave. It was something else. I'm still thinking about it." The user shared " my home CCTV video #earthquake #Delhi" with the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search results also led the Desk to an X post shared with a video by a handle named Muhammad Abdullah Hashmi on February 16. The user claimed the video captured terrifying scenes outside his house in Islamabad during an earthquake that had struck the region. "Just look at the blast and wave. It was something else. Still thinking about it. My home CCTV video #earthquake #Islamabad," the user shared the video with the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below, a combination image has been attached, showing that the content seen in the viral video matches that of the video shared in an X post. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk carefully scanned through the viral video and found a timestamp of February 15 written on it. This predates the Delhi earthquake (which occurred in the early hours of today), but it falls in line with the earthquake that struck Pakistan on February 15. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Additionally, to find details about the earthquake that struck Pakistan, the Desk conducted a keyword search on Google. It came across a report by a Pakistani daily, The News, on February 15. The report confirmed that a 4.8 magnitude earthquake jolted Islamabad, Rawalpindi, and its adjoining areas on Saturday (February 15) night. However, no casualties or damage were reported. "The tremors were also felt in Murree and some parts of the Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) region, including Balouch, Dhirkot, and its adjoining areas. The quake's magnitude was recorded at 4.8," the report added. Here is the link to the report: However, the Desk couldn't find the source of the video clip to establish that it was from Islamabad, Pakistan. But, it was confirmed that the video shared in the social media post had no connection to the early morning earthquake that struck Delhi-NCR on February 17.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, Waqf (Amendment) Bill 2024 was not passed in Rajya Sabha; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 17 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Two videos of the Parliamentary proceedings—Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha—were recently posted on social media, with users claiming that the Waqf (Amendment) Bill 2024 was presented and passed in the Rajya Sabha amid heavy uproar. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the JPC report on the Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024, was tabled in the Rajya Sabha. As of February 14, the Parliament had not passed the bill, as the session had been adjourned until March 10. The social media post was shared with a false claim. Claim On February 13, an X (formerly Twitter) user named Namami Bharatam shared two videos of the proceedings of the Upper House and Lower House, claiming that the Waqf (Amendment) Bill was presented and passed in the Rajya Sabha. In the Lok Sabha, Jagdambika Pal, chairman of the joint parliamentary committee on the Waqf (Amendment) Bill 2024, tabled the bill in Parliament. In another video, Rajya Sabha Chairman Jagdeep Dhankar was seen pacifying a protest that erupted against the JPC report on the Waqf (Amendment) Bill. The post's caption, which garnered 7741 views, read: "#WaqfAmendmentBill presented and passed in Rajya Sabha. Opposition leaders started shouting against it, and BJP leaders started slogans such as Bharat Mata ki Jai. Those who had created Waqf to give our lands to Muslims through the Waqf Board are in too much pain." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant news reports and came across a report published by Hindustan Times on February 13, 2025. The title of the report read: "JPC report on Waqf bill tabled in Parliament amid uproar from Opposition: 'Biased, one-sided'" "The Joint Committee of Parliament (JPC) report on the Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024, was tabled in Parliament on Thursday amid uproar. The report on the Waqf (Amendment) Bill was tabled by BJP member Medha Vishram Kulkarni, a member of the panel, in Rajya Sabha. JPC chairman and BJP MP Jagadambika Pal tabled the bill in the Lok Sabha after it was adjourned till 2 pm amid Opposition sloganeering against the report," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Another report by The Indian Express mentioned that the report's tabling led to disruptions and chaos in both Houses of Parliament. The Opposition alleges that its dissent notes have been deleted, and the government rejects the charge. The report, published on February 13, was titled "Waqf report: Oppn protests dissent redaction, corrigendum restores notes." Here is the link to the report. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted another set of customised keyword searches on Google, which yielded a February 13 report published by The New Indian Express. The report headline read: "Lok Sabha adjourned till March 10 after uproar over JPC report on Waqf Bill." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. The report mentioned: "Lok Sabha proceedings were adjourned till March 10, bringing the first part of the Budget Session to a close on Thursday. The day saw massive uproar in both Houses after the Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) tabled its Waqf (Amendment) Bill report, with Opposition members accusing the government of removing their dissenting notes. Earlier in the day, Rajya Sabha proceedings were also disrupted by protests as the JPC report was tabled in the Upper House. LoP Mallikarjun Kharge called the report "anti-democratic", citing the alleged rejection of the Opposition's dissent." Furthermore, the Parliament has been adjourned until March 10th, marking the end of the first phase of the Budget Session, and will then reconvene and continue until April 4th. Another news report, Business Standard, dated February 14, mentioned that the Rajya Sabha also adjourned and will resume its session alongside the Lok Sabha on March 10th. The report's title read: "Parliament adjourns until March 10th after the productive first session." Here is the link to the report. A portion of the article highlighted: "A key development during this period was the tabling of the Joint Committee's report on the Waqf (Amendment) Bill 2024. The Rajya Sabha has been adjourned and will resume its session alongside the Lok Sabha on March 10th. The Budget Session's initial phase began on January 31st." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the Waqf (Amendment) Bill 2024 has been tabled in the Rajya Sabha, and as of February 14, the Parliament has not passed it.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2024 video of Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra meeting Wayanad landslide survivors falsely shared in name of recent New Delhi Railway station stampede
content: New Delhi, Feb 18 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Days after the tragedy at New Delhi Railway Station that claimed the lives of 18 people, multiple social media users shared a video of Congress leader and Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi and party leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, claiming that they met the victims of the New Delhi Railway Station stampede after the tragic incident. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found this claim to be false. The viral video dates back to August 2024 and shows Congress MP Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra meeting survivors of the Wayanad landslide. The unrelated video was falsely linked to the recent New Delhi Railway Station stampede. At least 18 people were killed and several others injured in a stampede that broke out at the New Delhi Railway Station on February 15, 2025. The tragedy was reportedly triggered by a sudden surge of passengers waiting to board trains to Prayagraj, where the Maha Kumbh Mela is underway. Claim On February 17, an X (formerly Twitter) user named Rukmanand Swami shared a video of Congress leader and Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi and party leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, claiming that the two leaders met with those affected by the stampede at New Delhi Railway station. The post's caption, originally in Hindi, read: "Who is responsible for the deaths in the stampede at Delhi Railway Station? The opposition? The country's Prime Minister and Railway Minister should resign as soon as possible. Respected Shri Rahul Gandhi ji stands with the people of the country and the families of those who died in the Delhi accident." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users sharing the same video with similar claims. One such post can be found here , and its archived version can be viewed here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post by Ankit Mayank dated August 2, 2024. The post's caption read: "This is so painful to watch. Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi met the landslide victim families in a hospital in Wayanad. Seeing their pain, RaGa and PGV couldn't hold their tears. Look how they are hugging their Wayanad family, so painful…" Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Below are the combination images highlighting the similarities between the viral video and X post shared in 2024 Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a video report by Hindustan Times uploaded on their YouTube handle on August 2, 2024. The report's title read: "Wayanad Landslides: Rahul Gandhi Gets Emotional After Meeting Victims, Promises To Build 100+ Houses." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. On further analysing the search results, we also found an X post by the All India Congress Committee's national secretary on August 2, 2024. The caption of the post read: "Prayers for Wayanad." Here is the link , and below is a screenshot. Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra shared on her official X handle on August 1, 2024, that the depth of suffering experienced by survivors of the landslides in Wayanad is unimaginable. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. She can be seen wearing similar clothes in the viral video shared on social media. Below is a combination image highlighting the same. A report published by India Today on August 1, 2024, mentioned that Congress MP Rahul Gandhi and party leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra visited the landslide site at Chooralmala in Kerala's Wayanad. The Congress leaders assessed the situation in the area and met the affected people. The title of the report read: "Rahul Gandhi meets Wayanad landslides victims: How I felt when my father died." Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to August 2024 when Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi and Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra met survivors of the Wayanad landslide.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2015 building collapse photo falsely shared in name of Feb 17 earthquake in Delhi-NCR region
content: New Delhi, Feb 18 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Following a strong earthquake of magnitude 4.0 that hit Delhi-NCR on Monday (February 17), a photo of a partially collapsed building was circulated on social media, with users claiming that it showed the after-effects of the recent tremors that were felt in the national capital and its adjoining areas. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral photo dates back to 2015, after the tremors were felt in Delhi, and was unrelated to the recent February 17 earthquake in the Delhi-NCR region. A 4.0-magnitude earthquake struck Delhi early Monday morning, and mild tremors were felt across north India. According to an update from the National Centre for Seismology, the nodal agency that monitors earthquake activity, the quake occurred at a depth of approximately 5 km in Delhi. Claim On February 17, a Thread user shared a post of a partially collapsed building, claiming that it showed the after-effects of the recent earthquake that struck Delhi-NCR. The text written on the picture read: "Earthquake in Delhi-NCR. Strong tremors of an earthquake of 4.0 magnitude were felt across Delhi-NCR at around 5:30 am and then in Bihar at 8 am." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the image through Google's Reverse Image Search and found that several users had shared the same post with a similar claim. Here is the link and archive link to one of the posts. On further scanning the search results, the Desk found that a similar photo was shared on Instagram in 2024. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google for relevant media reports and came across a report by the Hindustan Times dated November 9, 2015, whose headline read: "Quake-hit building collapses, triggers scare in south Delhi." A report section mentioned: "A four-storey building partially collapsed at an unauthorised colony in Safdarjung Enclave, triggering fear of a domino effect on the adjoining buildings on Sunday." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. The Desk noticed that the report's cover image was similar to the viral photo being circulated on social media. Below is a combination image highlighting the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral photo dates back to 2015 and has been falsely linked to the recent earthquake in Delhi and its adjoining areas.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Pakistan Cricket Board denies claims shared by Pak social media users about PCB removing Indian flag from cricket stadium ahead of Champions Trophy; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 18 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media, with some users claiming it showed the absence of the Indian Tricolour from the roof of the National Stadium in Karachi, just days ahead of the ICC Champions Trophy in Pakistan. Users alleged that while the flags of all other participating nations were displayed, the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) deliberately removed the Indian flag after India refused to play tournament matches in Pakistan. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found this claim false. A PCB source, speaking to PTI, confirmed that there was no controversy regarding the flags on the stadium's roof. As per ICC guidelines, only four flags will be hoisted on match days during the Champions Trophy 2025 (CT25)—those of the ICC (Event Authority), the PCB (Event Host), and the two participating countries playing on that day. The source also clarified that the viral picture was taken before the CT25 Support Period had even started. It is important to note that India will play all its Champions Trophy matches in Dubai after the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) refused to play in Pakistan due to security concerns. Both the PCB and the BCCI have agreed that India and Pakistan will play their matches at a neutral venue during tournaments hosted by each other. Claim On November 16, an X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video claiming it showed the Indian flag absent from the roof of the National Stadium in Karachi. The flags of all other nations participating in the ICC Champions Trophy and India's were present. Users claimed that the Pakistan Cricket Board had carried out the purported move after India refused to play tournament matches in Pakistan. "No Indian flag in Karachi: As only the Indian team faced security issues in Pakistan and refused to play Champions Trophy matches in Pakistan. The PCB removed the Indian flag from Karachi stadium while keeping the flags of the other guest-playing nations. Absolute Cinema, well done, Mohsin Naqvi," the user shared the video with the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, to corroborate the claims made in the viral video, the Desk spoke to a PCB source, who dismissed the speculations surrounding the alleged controversy. "There is nothing controversial about the flags on the roof of the stadium because, as per ICC guidelines, only four flags will be hoisted on match days during CT25—ICC (Event Authority), PCB (Event Host), and the two participating countries on that day," a PCB source said. He added that the picture circulating on social media was from before the CT25 Support Period started. "At that time, on February 11, the PCB was hosting a three-nation event, and the CT Support Period began on February 12," the PCB source remarked. Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the viral video and found a watermark of 'Mr_Hamxay_3' on it. Upon further investigation, we found an Instagram account with the same name. Here is the link to the handle, along with a screenshot of the same: As the Desk carefully examined the Instagram account, it came across a post made on February 14, 2025. The post featured the same viral video and shared a similar claim that the PCB had not included the Indian flag because the country refused to play in Pakistan during the upcoming Champions Trophy. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image showing that the video seen in the viral post is the same as the one shared by the Instagram handle. Moreover, going further with the investigation, to corroborate whether the video was from the period before the CT25 Support Period began (as claimed by the PCB), the Desk contacted the user of the Instagram handle to verify if it was shot before February 12 or not. The story will be updated as and when a response is received. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim regarding the absence of the Indian flag at Karachi Stadium was false.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2024 video of Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann getting emotional shared with false claim after AAP's defeat in Delhi polls
content: New Delhi, Feb 18 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): After the Bharatiya Janata Party's (BJP) victory in the recently held Delhi Assembly elections, a video of Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann was shared on social media, with users alleging that he became emotional after Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) convener Arvind Kejriwal's defeat in the polls. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral video actually dates back to 2024, when the Punjab CM broke down while speaking about the AAP convener, who was detained in connection with the Delhi liquor policy case. The BJP registered a landslide victory, defeating AAP and securing 48 seats in the 70-member Assembly, marking its return to power in the national capital after 27 years. Kejriwal's party won the remaining 22 seats, while Congress failed to open its account once again. Claim On February 9, a Facebook user shared a video of Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann getting emotional while he delivered a speech, claiming that he got emotional after AAP convener Arvind Kejriwal's defeat in the recently held Delhi Assembly Elections. The post's caption, originally in Punjabi, read: "Bhagwant Mann started crying after Kejriwal's defeat." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. In the 46-second video, Mann could be heard saying: "Where should we go? Should we go to the Supreme Court? Tell us, where should we go? Which lawyer should we hire? What was our fault? We built schools...we built hospitals...we made electricity free, what was our fault?..." Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post by Punjab Tak, dated July 30, 2024. At 3:12 seconds, Punjab CM said: "This is too much, friend… where should we go then, should we go to the Supreme Court...which court is there...which lawyer should we hire...what was our fault...we built schools...we built hospitals...we made electricity free, what was our fault? This is too much, friend (wiping tears), this is too much. CBI backtracked, ED backtracked, Sanjay Bhai remained in jail for six months; what did ED say when he got bail, 'Sorry sir, we do not have any proof'." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. The Desk noticed Punjab CM wearing similar clothes as seen in the viral video shared on social media. Below is a combination image highlighting the same. We also scanned the official YouTube handle of Aam Aadmi Party (AAP). We found a video uploaded on July 30, 2024, whose title read: "CM Bhagwant Mann became emotional after taking the name of CM Kejriwal | India Alliance Jantar Mantar Protest." At 7:50 seconds, the CM can be heard saying similar things as claimed in the viral video. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google, which yielded a video report by Live Hindustan uploaded on their YouTube channel on July 30, 2024. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to 2024, when Bhagwant Mann became emotional while talking about Arvind Kejriwal's health when he was detained in Tihar Jail in the Delhi liquor policy case.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2023 video of AAP MLA Amanatullah Khan shared with false claim that he was dragged by cops recently after Delhi polls
content: New Delhi, Feb 19 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of Aam Aadmi Party MLA Amanatullah Khan claiming that police officers dragged him during his recent questioning by Delhi Police. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video dates back to 2023 when several AAP leaders, including Amanatullah Khan, protested against the CBI summons to then-Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal in the new excise policy case. The viral video was falsely linked to his recent questioning by the police on 13 February, 2025. Notably, a Delhi court on February 13 granted interim relief to Amanatullah Khan, protecting him from arrest till February 24 in connection with a case involving alleged obstruction of police officers. According to reports, the court directed Amanatullah Khan to cooperate with the investigation and instructed the police to interrogate CCTV surveillance. Claim On February 13, an X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video of Aam Aadmi Party MLA Amanatullah Khan claiming that police officers were dragging him during this recent questioning. The post's caption, which garnered 29.7K views, was originally in Hindi and read: "Kejriwal's right-hand newly elected MLA should not have been dragged away like a pig. Don't abuse me, sir, even if you slap me a couple of times." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. Upon further scanning the search results, the Desk found a similar video uploaded on MLA Amanatullah Khan's official Facebook on April 16, 2023. The caption of the post, originally in Hindi, read: "Whenever the oppressor commits atrocities from the corridors of power, every inch of the land will reverberate with the slogan of revolution. Protest against the failed attempt of CBI and ED to intimidate Delhi's popular Chief Minister Shri @ArvindKejriwal ji. We will keep raising our voice against the dictatorship of the BJP government." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the Facebook post. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google for relevant news reports and came across a report by The Hindu dated April 17, 2023, whose headline read: "AAP comes all out to protest Kejriwal's questioning by CBI; over 1,000 detained." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. The report mentioned: "The rank and file of the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), from Delhi and Punjab, hit the streets of the national capital in protest against the questioning of AAP national convener and Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal in connection with the alleged liquor scam at the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) headquarters on Sunday." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to 2023, when several AAP leaders, including Amanatullah Khan, protested against the CBI summons to then-Delhi CM Arvind Kejriwal in the excise policy case.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Viral video claiming DM was slapped during Maha Kumbh 2025 in Prayagraj was scripted; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 19 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media, with users claiming it showed an altercation between a top government official and a reporter over the entitlement of VVIP culture during the Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj. The video begins with a reporter questioning a car driver navigating a crowded street. When asked for an explanation, the driver responded that VIPs were seated in the back. However, as the reporter questioned the need for VIP treatment at a religious gathering, a man—who identified himself as the District Magistrate—suddenly exited the car and confronted him. The situation escalated, with the reporter allegedly slapping the official as well. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found this claim to be false. The video was discovered to be scripted and falsely presented as a real incident. Claim A Facebook user shared a February 17 video alleging an altercation between a reporter and a District Magistrate during the ongoing Maha Kumbh 2025. The video allegedly showed the reporter reprimanding the District Magistrate over the entitlement of VVIP culture during the Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj. He was also seen allegedly slapping the official. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search results also led the Desk to a YouTube video shared by a channel named Harsh Rajput on February 12. The YouTube video (which contained the content seen in the viral post at the 4:01 timestamp) included a dramatic depiction of multiple instances that went viral on social media during the ongoing Maha Kumbh 2025. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot. In the next part of the investigation, as the Desk carefully scanned the video, it found a disclaimer at the 5-second timestamp stating that the video was a scripted sketch made for entertainment. Here is a screenshot highlighting the same. Further, to verify whether the viral video was shot in Prayagraj during the Maha Kumbh, the Desk also conducted a customised keyword search on Google Maps for the gate named Ram Dwar, seen in the background. The search result found it situated at Ghantaghar Ramlila Ground in Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh. Here is a street view of Shri Ram Dwar's location. https://www.google.com/maps/uv?pb=!1s0x390cf1cc3d3426ed%3A0xaac858f9c179a57!3m1!7e115!4s%2Fmaps%2Fplace%2Fram%2Bdwar%2Bghaziabad%2F%4028.6589568%2C77.4293577%2C3a%2C75y%2C352.54h%2C90t%2Fdata%3D*213m4*211e1*213m2*211scrg2rLLpgAGwHMEIJg32mA*212e0*214m2*213m1*211s0x390cf1cc3d3426ed%3A0xaac858f9c179a57%3Fsa%3DX%26ved%3D2ahUKEwie8OnApM2LAxWVTWcHHRsJJtsQpx96BAglEAA!5sram%20dwar%20ghaziabad%20-%20Google%20Search!15sCgIgAQ&imagekey=!1e2!2scrg2rLLpgAGwHMEIJg32mA&cr=le_a7&hl=en&ved=1t%3A206134&ictx=111 Below is a combination image highlighting that the visuals of Ram Dwar seen in the viral video match that of the Ram Dwar situated at Ghantaghar Ramlila Ground in Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was scripted and not an actual incident from Maha Kumbh 2025.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2022 Bangladesh train fire incident falsely linked to recent Prayagraj Maha Kumbh; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 19 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of a train engulfed in fire was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that the train was en route to Prayagraj Maha Kumbh and around 300 people died due to the fire. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the viral video dates back to 2022, when the Parabat Express train from Bangladesh caught fire. The incident was falsely linked to Prayagraj Maha Kumbh, and the video was shared on social media with a false claim Claim: On February 15, a Thread user shared a video of a burning train, claiming that the train going to Prayagraj Maha Kumbh caught fire killing 300 people. The text written on the post, originally in Hindi, read: "Accident happened in Allahabad on 14/02/2025, 300 people died" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. On analysing the video closely, the Desk noticed that the colour of the train bogies was different from what is typically used in the Indian Railways. Taking this as a cue, the Desk further scanned the search results and found a video uploaded on United News of Bangladesh (UNB) on June 11, 2022. "Parabat train | Terrible fire in the coach of the intercity Parabat Express train running in Moulvibazar Shamsernagar | UNB," read the report's title, originally in Bengali. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combination of images highlighting the similarities between the viral and YouTube videos. The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant news reports and came across a report by BSS News dated June 11, 2022, whose headline read: "Dhaka-Sylhet rail link halted as train catches fire in Moulvibazar" The report mentioned: "A fire broke out on 'Parabat Express' train in Chowk Kabiraji area under Kamalganj upazila of the district this afternoon, halting rail communication on the Dhaka-Sylhet route." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a 2022 video of a train fire in Bangladesh was shared as a recent incident from Prayagraj during the Kumbh Mela.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, Prayagraj Junction railway station has not been closed; viral post shared with a false claim.
content: New Delhi, Feb 20 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a post claiming that Prayagraj Junction railway station had been shut down due to an overwhelming number of passengers travelling to the Maha Kumbh. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found this claim to be false. Only Prayagraj Sangam railway station has been temporarily closed, while eight other stations, including Prayagraj Junction, continue to operate as usual. According to railway officials familiar with the matter, in response to the surge in crowds traveling to Maha Kumbh, the Indian Railways has decided to shut down Prayagraj Sangam railway station until February 28. The decision was made following a request from the Prayagraj administration to prevent overcrowding and ensure better crowd management while minimising the risk of any untoward incidents. Claim On February 17, a Facebook user shared a post claiming that Praygraj Junction has also been closed. The text in the post, originally in Hindi, read: "Prayagraj Junction has been closed" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through Google Reverse Image Search and found several other users shared the same post with a similar caption. One such post can be found here , and its archived version can be viewed here . The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports and came across a report by the Hindustan Times dated February 18. The report headline read: "Mahakumbh: Prayagraj Sangam rly station to remain shut till Feb 28." The report mentioned that only Prayagraj Sangam railway station has been closed while eight other stations—of which Prayagraj Junction is one—will continue to function. "Out of Prayagraj's total nine railway stations, only Prayagraj Sangam railway station has been closed because it is near the Mahakumbh Nagar area. The remaining eight railway stations will, however, continue to function. They are: Prayagraj Junction, Prayagraj Chheoki, Naini, Subedarganj, Prayag, Phaphamau, Jhunsi and Prayagraj Rambagh," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Another report was published by Samachar Plus 24/7, which contained a letter by DM Prayagraj written to the divisional railway manager, Northern Railway Lucknow, regarding the closure of Prayagraj Sangam Railway Station, given the heavy crowd. Here is the link to the report and a screenshot of the letter. On further analysing the search results, the Desk found an X (formerly Twitter) post by Lucknow Division, Northern Railway, dated February 17, 2025, which mentioned that the Prayagraj Sangam station will remain closed for passengers till February 28. The caption of the post, originally in Hindi, read: "All concerned are informed that as per the order of Prayagraj District Administration, #प्रयागराज_संगम station of Northern Railway Lucknow Division will remain closed for passenger traffic from 17th February to 28th February midnight. #MahaKumbhMela2025 #KumbhRailSeva2025." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Furthermore, Northern Central Railways clarified X, stating that train operations at Prayagraj Junction are normal and passengers should not heed rumours. "Important information for all passengers. Railways clarify that train operations at Prayagraj Junction are completely normal. Passengers are requested not to pay heed to any rumours and get information only from official sources," read the post, originally in Hindi. Here is the link to the post. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the original notice mentioned the closure of Prayagraj Sangam station, which was falsely linked to the closure of Prayagraj Junction station.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated photos of Ranveer Allahbadia, Samay Raina shared as real with false claim on social media.
content: New Delhi, Feb 20 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Following the YouTube show 'India's Got Latent' controversy, multiple social media users shared a photo of YouTuber Ranveer Allahbadia and comedian Samay Raina wearing BJP sash insinuating that the two have joined the party as this was their last option. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an AI-generated photo was shared on social media as real with a false claim. Claim On February 17, an X (formerly Twitter) user shared a picture of YouTuber Ranveer Allahbadia and comedian Samay Raina wearing Bharatiya Janata Party's (BJP) sash, claiming the matter was solved. The post's caption, which garnered 10.5k views, read: "This is the last option left…" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and found several other users shared it with a similar claim. Two such posts can be seen here and here , with their archive versions found here and here , respectively. The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports, but it yielded no credible results. The Desk then carefully analysed the viral image and noticed several discrepancies, suggesting it was AI-generated. For instance, the image was severely edited, and the colours in the background were distorted. Additionally, the faces of the two in the viral image appeared to be forcefully added. Below is a photo highlighting the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk ran the image through Hive Moderation, another AI detection tool, which confirmed a significant presence of AI-generated content. Below is a screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the photo of Ranveer Allahbadia and Samay Raina shared on social media was AI-generated.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Scripted video claiming cop stopped MLA's car with black tinted window falsely shared as real incident; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 20 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video claiming it showed a policeman stopping an MLA's car with black-tinted windows. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigation revealed that the video was scripted and falsely shared as a real incident on social media. Claim On February 13, an X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video of a policeman stopping a car allegedly of an MLA, claiming that he was stopped due to dark-tinted glass in his car. The post's caption, originally in Hindi, reads, "The country needs such police, whether it is an MP or an MLA. No one will listen. If you want to suspend, do it. If you want a resignation, take it right now. Salute Sir Ji." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. In the video, in a telephonic conversation with allegedly a DSP, the policeman can be heard saying: "The MLA's car has been fully covered in dark films…Was I appointed to the police force by the MLA? I got in on my merit. If you ask me to resign, I will tender my resignation immediately. I will not betray my position. What will the common man think? That we are listening to an MLA. If you want to suspend me, I won't mind, but I will not betray my position." Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users sharing the same video with similar claims. One such post can be viewed here , and its archived version can be found here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an extended version of the viral video uploaded on YouTube by a user named Monty Deepak Sharma on February 6, 2025. The video's title read: "During checking, police found weapons in MLA's black car, and then there was chaos." Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot. On scanning the video closely, the Desk found that at 00:16 seconds, a slate mentions a disclaimer stating that the video is just for entertainment. It read: "Disclaimer: This video is presented by Monty Deepak Sharma. This video is a work of fiction. The video does not insult any stream, field, or people from different occupations. This video is just for entertainment purposes." Below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk also analysed Monty Deepak Sharma's Instagram handle and found similar videos featuring similar people. We also noticed that 'Video Creator' was written in the Bio section of the handle. Here is the link and a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a scripted video was falsely shared as an actual incident.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Pakistan accident video falsely shared in name of another stampede-like situation in Prayagraj Maha Kumbh
content: New Delhi, Feb 20 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of a massive crowd in chaos, claiming that another stampede-like situation had occurred at the Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the viral video is actually from Ambiri Kalla Chowk in Pakistan, where an accident on January 11 resulted in the deaths of 12 people. This incident took place before the Maha Kumbh began in Prayagraj in India. Therefore, the viral video was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim On January 31, a Facebook user shared a video of a massive crowd going amok, claiming that another stampede-like situation had happened in Prayagraj, Maha Kumbh. The video's text, originally in Hindi, read: "After serving your parents, your sins will be washed away. While washing away your sins, you will lose your life here." The hashtags in the video were those of Maha Kumbh and Prayagraj. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be viewed here and here , and archived versions, can be seen here and here . On further analysing the search results, the Desk came across a similar video shot from a different angle that was uploaded on Facebook on January 11. The video mentioned that an accident had happened in Ambiri Kala Karak. We then looked for the place's location and found that Ambiri Kala Karak is a village in Karak District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the Facebook post. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports and came across a video report by ETV 247 URDU, dated January 11. The report's title read: "Live: Unbelievable Traffic incident at Indus Highway | KPK Karak Incident - Pakistan Live News." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. The Desk found striking similarities between the viral video's visuals and the news report. Below is a combination image highlighting these similarities. Furthermore, news reports by The News International also mentioned an accident that occurred near Ambiri Kalla Chowk, which killed 12 people. The title of the report read: "12 killed, 25 injured in Karak accident" Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was of an accident in Pakistan and was falsely linked to a stampede-like situation in Prayagraj.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of Rohit Sharma's visit to Maharashtra falsely shared as him travelling to Pakistan for the ICC Champions Trophy
content: New Delhi, Feb 20 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media claiming to show Indian cricket team captain Rohit Sharma arriving in Pakistan for the ICC Champions Trophy. The footage depicted him receiving a warm welcome at the airport by Pakistani authorities. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video was originally from Sharma's visit to Rashin village in Maharashtra in October 2024. An old and unrelated video was falsely shared as recent. It is important to note that India will play all its Champions Trophy matches in Dubai after the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) refused to play in Pakistan due to security concerns. The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) and the BCCI have agreed that India and Pakistan will play their matches at a neutral venue during tournaments hosted by either country. Claim A Facebook user shared a video on February 19 claiming it showed Indian cricket team captain Rohit Sharma arriving in Pakistan for the ICC Champions Trophy. The video depicted Sharma receiving a warm welcome upon his arrival. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid Tool Search and extracted keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users shared the video with similar captions. Two such posts can be seen here and here , with their archive links available here and here respectively. The search results also led the Desk to an X post that Rohit Pawar (Maharashtra Cricket Association president) shared on October 3, 2024. The post features the same video of Rohit Sharma seen in the viral claim. However, the caption stated that it was from Sharma's visit to Rashin village in Maharashtra to launch his new cricket academy. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image showing that the content in the viral video matches that of the X post. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google. It came across a report published by India TV on October 4, 2024. The report detailed Sharma's visit to Rashin village in Karjat town in the Ahmednagar district of Maharashtra on October 3, 2024. There, he launched his new cricket academy and addressed the gathering. MLA from Karjat-Jamkhed and Maharashtra Cricket Association president Rohit Pawar were also at the location. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Additionally, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google regarding the Indian team's schedule for the Champions Trophy 2025, which commenced in Pakistan today. The search results led the Desk to a report published by ESPN Cricinfo on December 24, 2024. The report elaborated that all matches involving India in the tournament will be played in Dubai, as the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) refused to travel to Pakistan due to security concerns. The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) and BCCI agreed that India and Pakistan would play their matches at a neutral venue during tournaments hosted by either country. Here is the link to the report: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video claiming to show Rohit Sharma's arrival in Pakistan for the ICC Champions Trophy 2025 was actually from his visit to Maharashtra. An old and unrelated video of Sharma was falsely shared in the context of his visit to Pakistan.

title: PTI Fact Check: Two-year-old video of in-flight brawl among passengers shared with false communal narrative
content: New Delhi, Feb 20 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media, with some users claiming it showed a Hindu passenger being assaulted by a group of five Muslim men inside an aircraft. The video depicted two individuals—one purportedly from the Hindu community and the other from the Muslim community—engaged in a heated altercation. As the situation escalated, a few other Muslim men allegedly joined in, collectively attacking the Hindu passenger. Users shared the video with the caption: "When one Muslim started fighting with a Hindu and began hitting him, other Muslims joined in and also started attacking the Hindu. However, no other Hindu came forward to support him." However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found the claim to be false. The incident occurred on a flight from Bangkok to Kolkata on December 26, 2022. The two passengers involved in the altercation were identified as Ahmed Mohammed Hussain and Shaikh Azharuddin. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video on February 15, claiming it showed a purported attack on a Hindu passenger by a group of five Muslim men inside an aircraft. The footage showed an alleged altercation between two individuals (one purportedly from the Hindu community and the other from the Muslim community). However, as the fight escalated, a few other members of the Muslim community joined in, and together, they started thrashing the Hindu passengers. "Oh, Foolish Hindus, When Will You Change? There were five Muslims on a flight, while the rest were mostly Hindus and people of other religions. When one Muslim started fighting with a Hindu and began hitting him, the other Muslims joined in and also started attacking the Hindu. However, no other Hindus came forward to support him. The main reasons for this were: The Hindus did not see it as an attack by Muslims on a Hindu, they lacked awareness of their own identity as Hindus, they were unsure about what to do in such a situation, they viewed religion as something irrelevant or untouchable, and they did not have any sense of religious pride," the user shared with the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search results also led the Desk to a report published by News18 on December 29, 2022, wherein its feature image matched keyframes from the viral video. The report stated that the incident occurred on December 26, 2022, before the take-off of an A320 plane from Bangkok. "The scuffle started sometime after a passenger refused to return his reclining seat to the straight position despite requests from the cabin crew, saying he had back pain. The crew also told the male passenger that in case of an evacuation, a reclining seat would block passengers behind him from moving and that he would be unable to perform the bracing position properly. While the passenger refused to follow the instruction, another passenger intervened, and the fight started," the report added. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the content seen in the viral video, matched to the feature image of the news report. Additionally, to ascertain the identity of the two individuals involved in the fight, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found the first information report (FIR) filed by the BCAS regional director at Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose International Airport (NSCBI) Police Station on December 29, 2022. The FIR identified the passengers involved as Ahmed Mohammed Hussain and Shaikh Azharuddin. Below is a link to the FIR, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video showed a three-year-old in-flight brawl from a THAI Smile aircraft and was shared with a false communal narrative.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered video falsely claims Ukrainian President Zelenskyy performed as belly dancer; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 20 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media falsely claims to show Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy dancing in a room. The footage depicts a man wearing a form-fitting red costume and performing a belly dance routine. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found the claim false in its investigation. The original video featured an unidentified man dancing, but digital techniques were used to swap his face with Zelenskyy's. The altered video was then shared on social media as if it were real. Claim On February 18, an X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video allegedly showing Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy dancing inappropriately. The video showed Zelenskyy wearing a form-fitting red costume and performing a belly dance choreography. "This man is the President of Ukraine. It succumbed to the Biden administration's influence to become a member of NATO, thereby throwing its prosperous country into a war against a superpower like Russia. Biden lost, and now Trump has made it clear that we will not take Ukraine into NATO. Currently, Russia and America are holding a meeting to decide the fate of Ukraine, in which Ukraine itself is not included. A joker should not be allowed anywhere near power; running a government requires a lot of maturity. And yes, Chanakya once said that a child born to a foreign woman can never be a patriot," the user shared the video with the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users had shared the same video with similar captions. Two such posts can be seen here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search results also led the Desk to a video published on a YouTube channel named Boboycha on December 1, 2020. The background in the video matches the viral video's settings; also, a man was spotted performing belly dancing. However, the person could not be identified as Ukrainian President Zelenskyy but originally shows an unidentified man performing. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below, a combination image shows striking similarities between the background settings in the viral and YouTube videos. However, the only difference between the two is that the viral video features Ukrainian President Zelenskyy, whereas the YouTube video shows an unidentified man dancing. Thus, it is pointed out that the video is digitally altered. Additionally, the Desk made multiple attempts to find the origin of the video; however, it could not be independently ascertained. The Desk, however, confirmed its existence as early as 2020, underscoring that it does not feature President Zelenskyy. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video shared on social media was digitally altered, where an unidentified man's face was swapped with that of the Ukrainian President.

title: PTI Fact Check: Photo of local politician from Lucknow falsely shared in name of father of KIIT suicide case accused
content: New Delhi, Feb 21 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A post recently circulated on social media, with users claiming it showed an image of Manoj Srivastava, the father of Advik Srivastava, who was arrested in connection with the suicide case of Nepali student Prakriti Lamsal at the Kalinga Institute of Industrial Technology (KIIT), Odisha. The post alleged that Manoj Srivastava was a BJP leader in Lucknow and suggested that this connection would prevent the victim from getting justice. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found this claim to be false. The image actually featured a local politician from Lucknow named Manoj K. Srivastava, who was falsely identified as the father of the accused student in the KIIT suicide case. It is important to note that Prakriti Lamsal, a third-year B.Tech student at KIIT, allegedly died by suicide in her hostel on February 16. The incident sparked tensions on campus, leading Nepalese students to protest and demand justice for Prakriti. They also called for the arrest of 21-year-old Advik Srivastava, who had emerged as the prime accused in the case. Following a complaint, Odisha Police arrested Advik Srivastava on February 17 and charged him with abetment of suicide. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user on February 18 shared a social media post claiming that the image featured Manoj Srivastava, the father of Advik Srivastava, the accused arrested in connection with the suicide case of Nepali student Prakriti Lamsal at the Kalinga Institute of Industrial Technology (KIIT), Odisha. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the image through Google Lens and found several other users who had shared the post with similar claim. Two such posts can be seen here and here , with their archived versions available here and here . In the next part of the investigation, to corroborate the claim made in the viral post, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search for the name Manoj K Srivastava, who had been identified in the social media post as the father of Advik Srivastava, the accused in the KIIT suicide case. The search results led the Desk to a Facebook profile of the same person whose image and name were being circulated in the social media post. According to the details mentioned on his profile, the person identified as Manoj K Srivastava is a local politician from Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, and is presently serving as the National President of the Bharatiya Kesariya Vahini outfit. Here is the link to his social media handle, along with a screenshot of the same: Upon carefully analysing the social media profile, the Desk came across a video he shared on February 18, 2025. In the video, Srivastava could be seen vehemently dismissing any association between him and the accused, Advik Srivastava. He stated: "Advik Srivastava, caught on suspicion in the student's death in Odisha, is being misrepresented by the media as my son, which is absolutely wrong. This is a failed attempt to tarnish my name and years of social reputation. Those using my name and photo under a misunderstanding should immediately deny and remove them." Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot of the same: Additionally, to ascertain the identity of the accused Advik's father, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by Hindustan Times published on February 19, 2025. The report identified the accused Advik's father as a civil engineer in Lucknow; however, no name was mentioned. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot of the same: While the Desk was unable to independently verify the details of the accused Advik's father, it confirmed that Manoj Srivastava in the viral photo is not related to the accused. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral photo featured a local politician from Lucknow named Manoj K Srivastava, who had been falsely identified as the father of the accused student in the KIIT Nepal student suicide case.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video from Ram Mandir inauguration falsely shared as Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Jayanti celebration in Ayodhya; details inside
