content: New Delhi, Feb 21 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media, with some users claiming it showed celebrations at Ayodhya's Shri Ram Janmbhoomi Mandir on the occasion of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Jayanti, observed on February 19. The video featured a troupe of drummers, likely from Maharashtra, captivating spectators with their energetic performance during the alleged celebrations in Ayodhya. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found the claim false. The video actually dates back to January 2024, when the Shriram Pathak drummers troupe from Pune, Maharashtra, performed at the inauguration of the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya. An old and unrelated video was falsely shared as recent, linking it to Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Jayanti celebrations. Claim An X user shared a video on February 19 claiming to show celebrations held outside Shri Ram Janmbhoomi Mandir in Ayodhya on the occasion of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Jayanti. The user captioned the video, "Goosebumps! Jai Shivaji Jai Bhavani slogans and performance in Ayodhya Ram Mandir on the occasion of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Jayanti today. " Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively: The search also led the Desk to a video published on an Instagram handle named 'kattar_hindutva.ist'. The video matched the visuals seen in the viral post; however, the posting date of January 26, 2024, confirmed it was from the time of the consecration of the Ram Lalla idol in Ayodhya. The video was shared with the caption, "The enthusiasm of devotees from Maharashtra who came to Ramlala's court." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image highlighting the content seen in the viral video, matched with the Instagram video posted on January 26, 2024. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google. It came across a video posted by Republic World on its official YouTube channel on January 25, 2024. The video contained extended footage of the visuals seen in the viral post. It was shared with details that a group of dhol artists from Maharashtra performed outside the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya on January 25. Here is the link to the post along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dated back to January 2024, during the consecration of the Ram Lalla idol in Ayodhya. The famous drummer's troupe from Pune, Shriram Pathak, performed at the inauguration ceremony of the Ram Mandir.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, free bus travel scheme for women will not be discontinued in Delhi; social media post shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, Feb 21 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Days after the Bharatiya Janata Party was elected to power in the national capital, a viral social media post claimed that the former AAP government's 'Pink Ticket' scheme, which allows women to travel for free on Delhi's buses, had been discontinued. Users alleged that the decision was made following the BJP's landslide victory in the Assembly elections on February 5. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found this claim to be false. An official from the Delhi Transport Corporation dismissed the misinformation, and newly sworn-in Delhi Transport Minister Pankaj Kumar Singh confirmed to PTI that the free bus travel scheme for women would continue. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a post on February 15, purportedly claiming that the former AAP government-led 'Pink Ticket' scheme, which allows women to travel for free on Delhi's buses, had been stopped. "It is heard that after the BJP government came to power in Delhi, the free bus service provided by the Aam Aadmi Party for women is being stopped," the user shared in the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found several other users who shared the same image with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be viewed here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, to corroborate the claim made in the post, the Desk scanned the Delhi Transport Corporation (DTC) 's social media handles and official website but found no credible reports or announcements regarding the scheme's discontinuation. Next, it (the Desk) contacted Navneet Chaudhary, the Public Relations Officer at the DTC, who, in a statement issued, vehemently rejected the false news surrounding the scheme. He clarified that women could continue to take advantage of free bus travel. Additionally, as a part of the investigation, the Desk again made a customised keyword search on Google. This time, I came across a statement by Delhi Transport Minister Pankaj Kumar Singh given to PTI regarding the free bus service scheme implemented by the erstwhile AAP government. He said, "It will continue... Public transport will be free, the facility will continue, and we will bring better facilities. We are committed to providing better facilities for women." Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the free bus travel facility for female passengers in Delhi has not been stopped. A false claim was shared on social media, suggesting the scheme had been discontinued.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of Jamia students protesting against University admin falsely shared claiming they protested against Waqf (Amendment) Bill
content: New Delhi, Feb 22 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of heavy police deployment, claiming that students of Jamia Millia Islamia University protested against the Waqf (Amendment) Bill and were later detained by the police. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found this claim to be false. The Jamia students protested against the University administration over demands unrelated to the Waqf (Amendment) Bill. They were demonstrating against show-cause notices issued to participants of a December 2024 protest marking the anniversary of the CAA demonstrations and alleged police brutality on campus in 2019. Claim On February 13, an X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video of heavy police deployment, claiming that students of Jamia protesting against the Waqf (Amendment) Bill were held. The caption of the post, which garnered 93.5k views, originally in Hindi, read: "For several days in Jamia, some anarchists were starting drama on the Waqf Bill, just like CAA. Delhi Police has picked them up, and force is deployed in Jamia. That thug is no longer in Delhi. If there is anarchy, then you will be caught." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users sharing the same video with similar claims. One such post can be viewed here , and its archived version can be seen here . On further scanning of the search results, the Desk came across an extended version of the video, uploaded by IANS on their official X on February 13. The caption of the 00:38 seconds video read: "Delhi: Heavy deployment of paramilitary forces has been made outside Jamia Millia Islamia University. Student organisations have been protesting for several days over their demands. Today, several students were detained by the authorities." The caption makes it clear that the students were protesting over their demands and not against the Waqf (Amendment) Bill. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports and found a report by News 18, dated February 13. The headline of the report read: "Jamia Students Detained For Protesting Over Disciplinary Action, University Call It An 'Unlawful Gathering'" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. "The protest is taking place at the Central Canteen of Jamia Millia Islamia. The issue began on December 17, 2024, when the university's disciplinary committee issued notices to two PhD scholars for allegedly organising a demonstration in 2023. The disciplinary measures are linked to "Jamia Resistance Day" on December 15, 2024, an annual event marking the 2019 protests against the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA). That year, Delhi Police allegedly entered the campus and used batons on students inside the library, leading to widespread outrage across the country," read a portion of the report. Furthermore, another report by Zee Salam, dated February 15, discussed an advisory from the Office of Chief Proctor, Jamia Millia Islamia, stating that campus studies were being disrupted due to student protests. The report's title read: "JMI News: Jamia administration is scared of student protest; is defaming its female students!" Here is the link to the report, as well as a screenshot of the advisory. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the Jamia students were protesting against the administration regarding their demands unrelated to the Waqf (Amendment) Bill.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video shared in social media posts claiming 'ghosts' took dip at Maha Kumbh is absolutely false and imaginary; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 23 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media, with some users claiming it showed ghosts taking dip in the Sangam during the ongoing Maha Kumbh 2025 in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh. The footage, captured at night from a helicopter, shows multiple orange-colored figures near a water body, some appearing to be in the water. It was shared with claims that these figures were 'ghosts' bathing during the Maha Kumbh. However, PTI Fact Check found this claim to be false. The video was actually filmed during the Verão Maior Paraná event in Brazil. The orange-colored figures are humans detected through thermal imaging, not ghosts. The footage was falsely linked to the Maha Kumbh 2025 in Prayagraj.\ Claim A Facebook user named Chandan Chitra shared a video claiming that ghosts attended the ongoing Maha Kumbh 2025 ceremonies and took a holy dip in the river Ganga. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively: The search results also led the Desk to a video published on an Instagram handle named bpmoa.pmpr on January 19, 2025. This handle shared the exact same video seen in the viral post; however, the caption stated that the visuals were captured from the Falcão Project aircraft (a remotely piloted aircraft developed for Brazil's military and civilian use) during nighttime monitoring after events on the beach, in coordination with the state's remotely piloted aircraft. The post read: "Falcão Project aircraft with its technology, acting in night-time monitoring after events on the beach, in coordination with the State's remotely piloted aircraft. Worth guidance for summer goers regarding the risk of entering the water at night with low visibility. In these conditions, the risks of rip currents are present and can surprise swimmers. Especially avoid entering the water under the influence of alcohol. Don't put your life at risk. The Paraná Military Police and Fire Brigade teams are ready to act, but your safety starts with you and your attitudes." Here is the link and archive link to the video, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting the content seen in the viral video, matched with the Instagram video posted on January 19, 2025. In the next part of the investigation, to corroborate the claim made in the viral post, the Desk scanned through the same Instagram handle and found another video published on January 19, 2025. The video showed a similar setting seen in the earlier viral post and was shared with the caption: "Police patrol at the Verão Maior Paraná events." Further, it is important to note that, as the video progressed, a still frame on the screen revealed about large hoardings displaying information about the Verão Maior Paraná 2025 event which is being held in Brazil. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Additionally, to learn more about the orange figures visible on the helicopter's dashboard screen, the Desk conducted a customized keyword search on Google and found that this technique is called thermographic inspection. While researching this technique, the Desk came across a report published on a website called SATIR. The report highlighted how thermal imaging technology is used in Search and Rescue (SAR) operations. Regarding its use in sea rescue operations, the report mentioned: "Sea rescue operations are one of the search and rescue missions that would benefit greatly from the use of thermal imaging equipment. This is because thermal imaging cameras work by measuring heat/temperature radiated from everything and everyone. In sea rescue operations, the temperature difference between the sea and the human body helps locate people more easily." Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral claim linking the video to ghosts bathing during the Maha Kumbh 2025 in Prayagraj is false. The video actually shows footage from a night-time patrol during the Verão Maior Paraná events in Brazil, with humans detected using thermal imaging technology.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Claim in social media post that PM Modi watched child crying and complaining about back-to-back exams is false; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 23 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video claiming that Prime Minister Narendra Modi watched a child on a television screen as he complained about the pressure of back-to-back exams. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigation found that the viral video was digitally edited. In the original footage, PM Modi was watching the live broadcast of the Chandrayaan-2 launch in 2019. The claim in the social media post that PM Modi watched the child crying on the TV screen was false. Claim On February 22, an Instagram user shared a video of Prime Minister Narendra Modi claiming to watch a child on a television screen, complaining about the pressure of exams. The child in the video says: "Even we want to live a life. But there are multiple exams one after the other. When I become the Prime Minister, I will ban exams." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be viewed here and here , and its archived version can be seen here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk found an X (formerly Twitter) post by Times of India dated July 22, 2019, whose caption mentioned that PM Modi was watching the launch of Chandrayaan 2. The post's caption read: "#GSLVMkIII #ISRO #IndiaMoonMission. Efforts such as #Chandrayaan2 will further encourage our bright youngsters towards science, top-quality research and innovation: PM @narendramodi." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. The Desk found several similarities between the viral video and the X post; below is a combination image highlighting the same. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports and came across an India Today report dated July 22, 2019. The title of the report read: "PM Modi Watching Live Telecast Of Chandrayaan-2 Launch" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the news report. The post's description read: "Prime Minister Narendra Modi watched the live telecast of Chandrayaan-2 launch by ISRO. ISRO Moon Mission, Chandrayaan 2, successfully launched from the Sriharikota space station. After a tense countdown at the Isro space centre, the Chandrayaan 2 launch occurred at exactly 2:43 on Monday. The much-anticipated launch on Monday afternoon after the initial attempt on July 15 was watched by a billion population after it was abandoned due to a technical snag. Chandrayaan 2 took off aboard the most powerful GSLV-Mk-III rocket, "Baahubali." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video had been digitally edited, as PM Modi watched the live telecast of the Chandrayaan 2 launch 2019.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Hardik Pandya's diving catch in 2024 T20I match against Bangladesh falsely shared as recent from 2025 ICC Champions Trophy match; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 24 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): India began its 2025 ICC Champions Trophy campaign with a six-wicket victory over Bangladesh. Following this, multiple social media users shared a video of all-rounder Hardik Pandya's diving catch, claiming it occurred during the recent ICC Champions Trophy match against Bangladesh. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral video actually dates back to October 2024. It showed Hardik Pandya displaying his athletic brilliance to dismiss Bangladeshi cricketer Rishad Hossain in a T20I match during spinner Varun Chakravarthy's over when Hossain had scored just nine runs. India secured an 86-run victory in that match, restricting Bangladesh to 135/9 with a dominant bowling performance. This win marked India's most significant T20I victory against Bangladesh and sealed a 2-0 triumph in the three-match series. Claim On February 21, a Facebook user shared a video of star all-rounder Hardik Pandya's diving catch, claiming that it happened during the 2025 ICC Champions Trophy match against Bangladesh. The caption of the post read: "There's a reason they call him Kung Fu Pandya. #IndvsBan | #ChampionsTrophy2025" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. On further analysing the search results, the Desk came across an X (formerly Twitter) post from a user named 'Cricadium CRICKET', dated October 10, 2024. The caption of the post read: Hardik Pandya with an incredible diving catch! A stunning display of athleticism and skill. What a moment! #HardikPandya #indvsban #cricket #t20cricket #pandya." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. The October 2024 video features the same clip as seen in the viral video, confirming that it is not from the 2025 ICC Champions Trophy match against Bangladesh. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the X post. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports and came across a report by India Today dated October 10, 2024, whose headline read: "Watch: Hardik Pandya races 25m to take a stunning catch in Delhi T20I vs Bangladesh" "The all-rounder pulled off one of the most memorable moments of the match, sprinting 25 meters from deep midwicket to dismiss Bangladesh's Rishad Hossain. The extraordinary catch occurred during Varun Chakravarty's over, as Rishad, who had accumulated nine runs, aimed for a boundary. However, Pandya's quick movement and remarkable athleticism allowed him to cover the ground, dive horizontally, and secure the catch," the report mentioned. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. On further scanning the search results, we found a similar video from a different angle on the official Instagram handle of the Indian cricket team, dated October 9, 2024, when India's second T20I match was played against Bangladesh. "Athleticism at its best! An outstanding running catch from Hardik Pandya #TeamIndia | #INDvBAN | @hardikpandya93 | @idfcfirstbank" Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video of Hardik Pandya's catch dates back to 2024, from the second T20I against Bangladesh.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Social media post claiming BJP's Rekha Gupta bought 50-lakh car after taking oath as Delhi CM is false; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 24 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): After the Bharatiya Janata Party's (BJP) victory in the recently held Delhi Assembly elections, a viral video circulating on social media claimed that Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta purchased a car worth Rs 50 lakh after assuming office. The post also alleged that AAP convenor Arvind Kejriwal used a car worth Rs 20 lakh, making it a political issue raised by the BJP. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found the claim to be false. The car seen in the viral video is a government vehicle that Arvind Kejriwal officially used during his tenure as Chief Minister. Following protocol, it was later handed over to the new CM, Rekha Gupta, during the oath ceremony. Claim On February 22, an X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video claiming that Delhi CM Rekha Gupta bought a car worth Rs 50 lakh after assuming charge. The caption of the post, which garnered 66.9k views and was originally in Hindi, read: "Kejriwal vs Rekha Gupta. As soon as #RekhaGupta became the Chief Minister of Delhi, She first bought a Car worth ₹50 lakh for herself. Arvind Kejriwal has a Car worth ₹20 lakhs. 𝐀𝐧𝐝 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐇𝐲𝐩𝐨𝐜𝐫𝐚𝐜𝐲 #Kejriwal's ₹20 lakh car was one of the #BJP's issues in the #DelhiElections2025. #DelhiCM #MechanicalElephants #GetOutModi #TVKForTN" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users sharing the same video with similar claims. One such post can be viewed here , and its archived version can be seen here . On further analysing the search results, the Desk came across a video report by ET Now dated February 20, 2025, which mentioned that Rekha Gupta rode Arvind Kejriwal's former official car for the oath ceremony. The title of the report read: "Rekha Gupta Rides Arvind Kejriwal's Former Official Car For The Oath Ceremony" Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Arvind Kejriwal officially owned this car during his tenure as the CM, and it was later handed over to the new CM, Rekha Gupta, during the oath ceremony. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find relevant media reports and came across a report by the National Herald dated July 10, 2022. The report's headline read: "Delhi govt has spent Rs 1.44 crore on 'Aam Aadmi' CM Kejriwal's cars, reveals RTI reply." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. The Desk conducted another set of customised keyword searches and found a report by Social News XYZ dated November 2, 2024, in which Arvind Kejriwal is seen using the same car as in the viral video. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the news report. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk checked the car's details through CarInfo and found that the vehicle's registration date was April 22, 2022. Here is the link and a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the car seen in the viral video is a government car previously used by Arvind Kejriwal.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2024 Yamuna cleanliness drive by volunteer group falsely shared as recent after BJP govt formation in Delhi; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 24 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Days after the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) swept the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) out of power in Delhi, a video showing a group of people cleaning a water body was shared on social media. Users claimed that efforts to clean the Yamuna River had begun following the BJP's government formation in the national capital. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found the claim to be false. The viral video dates back to 2024, before the BJP government was formed in Delhi, and the cleanliness drive was conducted by a volunteer group named Earth Warriors, not by any political party. Pollution in the Yamuna River was a significant issue during the 2025 Delhi Assembly elections, with the Arvind Kejriwal-led AAP facing widespread criticism for failing to fulfil its long-standing promise to clean the river. Claim On February 22, an X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video of a group of men and women cleaning a water body, claiming that efforts to clean the Yamuna River have commenced after the formation of the BJP government in Delhi. The video's text read, "Yamuna cleaning drive," while the post's caption, originally in Hindi, read, "Cleaning of Yamuna Maiyya. Thank you, Modi Ji, Thank you, Rekha Gupta Ji." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be viewed here and here , and its archived version can be seen here and here . On further analysing the search results, the Desk came across a comment on X by 'Earth Warrior' on one of the viral videos, in which they mentioned that the video dated back to 2024 and the team is not affiliated with any political party. The comment, originally in Hindi, read: "This video of our team is from 2024, and we have no connection with any political party. We have been cleaning and driving Kalindi Kunj Ghat in Delhi for the last five years!" Here is the link to the comment, and below is a screenshot. Taking a cue from this, the Desk scanned Earth Warrior's social media handles and found several such cleanliness drive videos uploaded to its account. Furthermore, we also came across the video uploaded to their Instagram handle on December 29, 2024. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot. This clarifies that the video predates the formation of the BJP government in Delhi. Below is a combination of images highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the Instagram post. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports. It came across a report by ETV Bharat dated December 9, 2024. The report headline read: "Delhi's 'Oxygen Man' Pankaj Kumar Leads Cleanup Drive At Kalindi Kunj Ghat To Protect Yamuna River." "Pankaj Kumar, popularly known as Delhi's "Oxygen Man," continues his unwavering commitment to environmental conservation. Recently, he led his Earth Warrior Volunteer Group in a cleanup drive at Kalindi Kunj Ghat, a bustling area along the Yamuna River," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Another part of the report read: "The cleanup drive, focused on restoring the area's natural beauty, is part of the Earth Warrior Volunteer Group's broader mission to inspire Delhi residents to care for and maintain the Kalindi Kunj Ghat." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video of the Yamuna cleaning drive dates back to 2024 and was conducted by Earth Warriors, not by any political party

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of Kannada film star Yash spotted with family in Mumbai falsely linked to Maha Kumbh 2025; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 24 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media claimed to show Kannada film star Yash, along with his family, arriving in Prayagraj to participate in the ongoing Maha Kumbh 2025. The video depicted Yash walking through the streets of Prayagraj, accompanied by his wife and two children. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video actually dates back to November 2024 and was shot in Mumbai. In it, Yash was seen spending time with his wife, Radhika Pandit, and their children. The old and unrelated video was falsely shared on social media as recent, misleadingly linking it to the ongoing Maha Kumbh Mela. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video on February 23, claiming it showed Kannada film star Yash and his family arriving in Prayagraj to participate in the ongoing Maha Kumbh 2025. "Yash reaches Maha Kumbh with family. Congressis, not only general public but celebrities from South too are visiting Maha Kumbh. Keep howling now," the user shared the post with the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively: The search result also led the Desk to a video shared by the official Facebook page of News18. The handle carried the same video seen in the viral post; however, the origin of the video dates back to November 25, 2024, which predates the Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj, which began on January 13, 2025. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting the content seen in the viral video, matched with the Instagram video posted on November 25, 2024. Additionally, the Desk also scanned through multiple social media handles of the Kannada movie star to corroborate whether he had visited the Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj. However, no such information or posts were found. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of Kannada movie star Yash spotted along with his family was shot in Mumbai in November 2024. The old video was misattributed and falsely linked to the ongoing Maha Kumbh Mela.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2023 video of woman complaining about passengers misbehaving falsely shared as recent incident on social media; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 24 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video of a woman raising concerns about passenger safety on trains. She claimed that while traveling from Jaipur to Sri Ganganagar, some individuals created disturbances and misbehaved under the influence of alcohol. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the incident did not occur recently. The viral video dates back to 2023, and the accused passengers were arrested after the incident was reported. Claim On February 22, a Facebook user shared a video of a woman raising questions about the safety of passengers on trains, claiming that some people created problems after drinking alcohol on the train. The woman in the 1:47 second video says: "It is 1:00 am, and I am travelling from Jaipur to Sri Ganganagar in second class AC. Three people sitting in the next compartment are drinking alcohol and have been abusing. I tried to warn them, but nothing changed…What is surprising is that there is not a single police officer on the train…" Here is the link and archive link to the video, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be viewed here and here , and its archived version can be seen here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across the viral video uploaded on X by Gayatri Bishnoi, President of the AAP Rajasthan State Women Wing, on November 20, 2023. The caption of the post read: "Not only women, no passenger is safe in @IRCTCofficial.It is a matter of great surprise that at 1 o'clock in the night, some miscreants are openly consuming drugs and harassing passengers by using foul language. When I tried to complain, I found that not a single RPF / JRPF was deployed in the entire train. When my TT complained, the police came after 1 hour. Meanwhile, the miscreants kept threatening me. With the help of fellow passengers, I stood firm in the whole matter till the police came. But if any accident had happened during this 1 hour, who would have been responsible for it?" Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. We scanned the post and found a comment on the video by North Western Railway on November 1, 2023. The comment read: "On 20.11.2023, information was received about some persons creating a nuisance in coach number HA-1 of train number 22997 Shri Ganganagar Express. On reaching the next station, Resub Degana attended the complaint, took immediate action, caught 03 persons causing a nuisance in the said coach, and took legal action." Here is the link to the comment, and below is a screenshot. On further analysing Gayatri Bishnoi's X handle, we found another X post by her dated November 20, 2023, in which she shared a photo that mentioned the action taken by RPF regarding the entire incident. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Furthermore, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports and came across a report by Times of India, dated November 21, 2023, whose headline read: "3 Held For Drinking In Train After Aap Leader's Tweet" A section of the report read: "Three train passengers were arrested in Nagaur district on Monday for allegedly consuming alcohol and misbehaving with passengers after a leader of Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) travelling in the train tweeted about the incident." Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was not recent, but dates back to 2023.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Viral video falsely linked celebrations from two unrelated cricket events to India's win against Pakistan in ICC Champions Trophy 2025
content: New Delhi, Feb 25 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media, with some users claiming it showed Indian cricket fans chanting the Ganesh Aarti at a stadium after India's emphatic victory against arch-rival Pakistan in their ICC Champions Trophy 2025 Group A match at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium on Sunday. The video featured a massive crowd enthusiastically chanting the Ganesh Aarti amid grand celebrations at the stadium. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigation found the claim false. The Desk determined that the viral video was a compilation of unrelated footage from two previous events, falsely shared as a recent celebration following India's win against Pakistan in the ICC Champions Trophy 2025. Claim An Instagram user shared a video on February 24, claiming that Indian cricket lovers started chanting Ganesh Aarti at a stadium after India registered a thumping victory against arch-rival Pakistan in their ICC Champions Trophy 2025 Group A match held at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium on Sunday. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively: The search results also led the Desk to a video published on an Instagram handle named Sanchit Desai on January 19, 2025. The Desk found that the first sixteen seconds and the last six seconds of the visuals seen in the viral post matched the video posted on the Instagram handle, which was shared along with a caption stating it had been shot at the Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai during the 50th-anniversary celebrations of the stadium held last month on January 19. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting the content (the first sixteen seconds and the last six seconds of the video) seen in the viral video matched to that of the Instagram handle shared on January 19, 2025. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found multiple reports confirming that on January 19 this year, a grand ceremony was hosted to commemorate the 50th anniversary of Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai. Here is the link to the report by Hindustan Times published on January 20, which elaborated on the events held on the grand occasion: Additionally, to find details about another video segment (seen between the timestamps of 17 seconds to 26 seconds) clubbed in the viral post along with the celebrations from Wankhede Stadium, the Desk scanned through that particular part and observed multiple banners of specific brands displayed, along with a scoreboard showing England's score at 175/8 after 30.5 overs. Also, the two batters present at the crease at that time were Mark Wood and Gus Atkinson. Below is a screenshot of the same: Taking cues from this, the Desk ran the keyframe through Google Lens and came across a report by Indian Express published on February 13, 2025. The report's cover image matched the viral post's background setting. It confirmed that it was from the Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad, where India beat England by 142 runs in the third match of the three-match T20I series to complete a 3-0 clean sweep. Here is the link to the report: Below is a combination image highlighting the background setting in the viral video that matches the cover image from the report: Moreover, regarding the scoreboard displaying England's score at 175/8, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search on Google and found a highlight video of India vs England 3rd ODI match posted by the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) on February 12, 2025. The Desk found that the scoreboard displayed in the viral video matched the team score shown in the BCCI highlight video. At 30.3 overs, England stood at 175/8, with Wood and Atkinson batting. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was falsely linked to the ICC Champions Trophy 2025 match against Pakistan and was, in fact, a compilation of unrelated footage from previous events.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Social media post falsely claimed Delhi CM Rekha Gupta posted a comment on X against Arvind Kejriwal after India's victory against Pak in Champions Trophy match
content: New Delhi, Feb 25 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Following India's spectacular six-wicket victory over arch-rival Pakistan in the highly anticipated Champions Trophy match—powered by Virat Kohli's unbeaten century—a purported screenshot of an X post began circulating on social media. The post, allegedly from Delhi CM Rekha Gupta, appeared to contain an objectionable comment about AAP convenor Arvind Kejriwal after the India-Pakistan clash. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigation revealed that the viral post originated from a parody account. Despite this, users widely shared it on social media under the false assumption that the X post was real. Claim On February 24, a Facebook user shared a screenshot of a purported X post claiming to be that of Delhi CM Rekha Gupta, who allegedly made an objectionable comment on AAP convener Arvind Kejriwal after yesterday's India-Pakistan Champions Trophy match. The purported tweet, allegedly by Delhi CM, read: "The firecrackers that Kejriwal ji had kept to burst on Pakistan's victory went in vain" Meanwhile, the post with the caption read: "Of course, she became the Chief Minister, but the cheapness of her thinking did not go away." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through Google Reverse Image and came across a similar post by another user. The link to one of the posts can be found here , and its archived version can be viewed here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across the X handle that initially shared the post. The user name of the handle is 'Rekha Gupta Delhi'. The bio section of the handle mentioned, 'Not affiliated with anyone. ' The desk noticed no BJP leaders or senior ministers followed the handle. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. In the next part of the investigation, the desk searched the official 'X' handle of Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta. The handle's user name is 'gupta_rekha'. The Desk noticed that PMO India and other senior officials followed the account. Further scanning the handle, we found no post, as the viral screenshot was being shared on social media. Here is the link to the official X handle, and below is a screenshot. Moreover, after India's victory, the Delhi CM posted on X on February 23, congratulating the team and wishing for the winning streak to continue. The post's caption, originally in Hindi, read: "Glorious victory. The Indian cricket team registered another historic victory by defeating Pakistan in the Champions Trophy with its strong performance. This is not just a match but a victory of the enthusiasm and passion of every Indian. The hard work, teamwork and fighting spirit of the players are commendable. Hearty congratulations to the entire Indian cricket team! May this winning streak continue." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. At first glance, the user's profile looks similar to Delhi CM Rekha Gupta's real profile. However, a closer look at the profile bio reveals that it is a parody account. Below is a combination image highlighting the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta did not make any such comment about Kejriwal after the Indian team's victory. The viral post was shared from a parody account, which users are sharing with false claims, assuming it to be real.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Image claiming to show Hyderabad's Outer Ring Road found to be AI-generated; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 25 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared an image claiming it showed an aerial view of Hyderabad's popular Nehru Outer Ring Road (ORR). Users shared the image, marveling at the road's impressive construction and describing it as the largest ring road in India. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the photos shared on social media were fake. AI-generated pictures were shared on social media as real with a false claim. Claim An Instagram user shared on February 19 an image purportedly showing an aerial view of Hyderabad's popular Nehru Outer Ring Road (ORR). "Hyderabad, India, has a 156-kilometer-long road, which is the largest ring road in the country," read the information shared with the image. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users had shared the same video with similar claims. One such posts can be found here , with its archived versions available here respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customized keyword search on Google to find more information about the ring road expressway encircling Hyderabad, the capital city of Telangana state. The search led the Desk to information published on the official website of IRB Infrastructure, the company awarded the Nehru Outer Ring Road (ORR) project in Hyderabad on a Toll, Operate, and Transfer (TOT) basis for 30 years. As the Desk carefully scanned through the website, it found multiple images of the expressway (specifically aerial views) published by IRB Infrastructure. The Desk compared the images from the viral post with those released by the company and found no similarities. Additionally, to find more matching visuals of Hyderabad's popular Nehru Outer Ring Road (ORR), the Desk conducted a customized keyword search on YouTube and came across a video published by a media portal named HYBIZTV HD on April 23, 2019. The visuals seen in the video matched those of the expressway images released by the company, unlike the image shared on social media. Here is the link to the video. Below is a combination image highlighting the visuals from the video that matched the images released by the company. In the subsequent part of the investigation, as the Desk carefully analyzed the viral image, it found multiple discrepancies, indicating that the image was AI-generated. For instance, the background in the image appeared unnaturally made. Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the image through Hive Moderation (an AI detection tool), which suggested a substantial presence of AI content. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the image claiming to show an aerial view of Hyderabad's popular Nehru Outer Ring Road (ORR) was AI-generated.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2024 J&K earthquake video falsely shared on social media in name of Feb 25 Kolkata tremors; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 26 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Hours after a 5.1-magnitude earthquake hit the Bay of Bengal, with tremors felt in Kolkata and several parts of West Bengal, several videos showing a trembling fan were shared on social media, with users claiming it was caused by the tremors that jolted the Kolkata. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral video dates back to 2024, when tremors were felt in Jammu and Kashmir. The video was shared with a false claim unrelated to the February 25 earthquake in Kolkata and parts of West Bengal. An earthquake of magnitude 5.1 hit the Bay of Bengal on Tuesday morning, with tremors felt in Kolkata and several parts of West Bengal. The National Center for Seismology (NCS) reported that the quake occurred at 6:10 am. Claim On February 25, an X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video of a trembling fan, claiming that the incident happened due to recent earthquake tremors felt in Kolkata. The post's caption, originally in Hindi, read: "Strong earthquake tremors were felt in Kolkata on Tuesday morning. The magnitude of the earthquake was measured at 5.1 on the Richter scale. The earthquake's epicentre was in the Bay of Bengal at a depth of 91 kilometres. Earthquake tremors were also felt in Jharkhand's capital Ranchi." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post by DD India, dated August 20, 2024, featuring the same video as seen in the viral video. The post's caption read: "#WATCH | An #earthquake of magnitude 4.9 on the Richter Scale struck Jammu and Kashmir." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the X post by DD India. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports and came across a video report by ABP dated August 20, 2024. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Furthermore, another X post by Zee Delhi-NCR Haryana, dated August 20, 2024, featured the same video. The caption of the post read: "Earthquake of 4.9 magnitude on Richter scale in Jammu and Kashmir". Here is the link to the X post. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk checked the National Center for Seismology's (NCS) website for official data on the earthquake that struck Jammu and Kashmir. It reported that on August 20, 2024, two moderate-magnitude earthquakes were recorded in the Baramulla district of Jammu and Kashmir. Here is the link to the official release, which is available on the NCS website. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to the 2024 Jammu and Kashmir earthquake and is unrelated to the recent tremors in Kolkata.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video of US President Donald Trump shared with false claim that he made derogatory remarks about India
content: New Delhi, Feb 26 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media, with some users claiming it showed US President Donald Trump making nasty comments about Indians. In a one-minute and 47-second video shared by the users, President Trump first discussed an executive order banning the hiring of Indian customer service representatives in the US. He was then allegedly heard saying that "Indians should get jobs to clean up trash in their country." "This is in every square mile of India, and they don't care. They even dump loads of plastic and trash into their rivers," he added. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found the claim false in its investigation. The video was originally taken from a YouTube channel that posts conservative political satire content. Regarding the viral video, the channel stated that it contains a voice-over by a Trump impersonator and that AI was used to alter the visuals. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video on February 22 purportedly showing US President Donald Trump making nasty comments about Indians. In the one-minute and 47-second video, President Trump first spoke about an executive order calling for a ban on hiring Indian customer service representatives in the US. As the video progressed, he was also allegedly heard saying, "Indians should get jobs to clean up trash in their country." "This is in every square mile of India, and they don't care. They even dump loads of plastic and trash into their rivers," he added. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , along with their archived versions viewed here and here : As the Desk carefully examined the viral video of President Trump announcing the executive order, it found multiple discrepancies suggesting the video was a satirical version. While scanning through the video, the Desk noticed it was shared under the banner of 'Faux News'—which reportedly is a satirical play on words of the US-based news channel Fox News. Additionally, the Desk found the text mentioned, 'Sobering Satire,' just above the ticker. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same: As the Desk held a customised keyword search for the word 'Sobering Satire,' it discovered a YouTube channel with the same name. The channel description states it focuses on political satire: "Sobering Satire – Part Comedy, part Commentary, all Conservative. A group of veteran talent goes OFF-Script to produce unique satire, audio & video for Conservatives and American Patriots." Here is the link to the channel, along with a screenshot: As the Desk continued its investigation, it scanned the YouTube channel and found the same video from the viral post, published by the channel on January 25, 2025. The video description explicitly labelled it as satire: "Trump Impression & Performance by Clive. A.I. did NOT Write, Speak, or Perform this video. It only masked Clive's face/performance." Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot: Below is a comparison image highlighting that the video seen in the viral post matches the one shared by the YouTube channel in January 2025: The Desk also mentioned a website (www.michaelclive.com) in the video's description, corresponding to the term Clive, credited above for Trump's voice impression. Upon scanning the website, the Desk found it linked to Michael Clive, a voice actor and comedian credited with impersonating President Trump's voice multiple times. Several other videos on his website also featured him impersonating Trump. Although the Desk could not independently verify whether the audio in the viral video was directly linked to Michael Clive, the details published on the YouTube channel strongly suggest this connection. The satirical video digitally altered the visuals and included a fake voice-over. In the subsequent part of the investigation, to verify whether the visuals of Trump in the viral video had been digitally altered, the Desk ran keyframes through Google Lens. It found the original footage used in the satirical video was shared by Hindustan Times earlier last month. The original event occurred during a press conference held by Trump at a dinner for GOP governors at Mar-a-Lago. During this press conference, Trump did not mention Indians or discuss any executive order related to a "new customer service bill." Here is the link to the video by Hindustan Times that matches the visuals from the viral post: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video originated from a satirical YouTube channel, Sobering Satire, which specialises in conservative political satire. The video explicitly states that it contains a voice-over by a Trump impersonator and that AI was used to alter the visuals digitally.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated image falsely claims Bollywood actress Preity Zinta visited Maha Kumbh with Australian cricketer Glenn Maxwell; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 26 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): An image recently circulated on social media claimed to show Bollywood actress Preity Zinta visited the ongoing Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj with Australian cricketer Glenn Maxwell. The users shared the image, which showed the celebrity duo dressed in white attire standing aboard a boat in Prayagraj. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk, in its investigation, found the image shared on social media was fake. An AI-generated picture was shared on social media as real with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared an image on February 17, purportedly showing Bollywood actress Preity Zinta visiting the ongoing Maha Kumbh 2025 in Prayagraj with Australian cricketer Glenn Maxwell. "Glenn Maxwell and Preity Zinta. Lovely picture in Maha Kumbh 2025," the user shared the image with the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and found multiple users had shared the same post with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analyzed the viral image and found multiple discrepancies suggesting it was AI-generated. For instance, the viral image showed the Bollywood actress with six fingers, and the background of the image appeared to be quite blurred. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Taking cue from the above generated inputs, the Desk then ran the image through Hive Moderation (an AI detection tool), which also predicted a substantial presence of AI content. Below is a screenshot of the result. Additionally, the Desk also scanned through the social media handles of the celebrities to find out if either of them had visited Prayagraj separately for the Maha Kumbh 2025. While the Australian cricketer's handle bore no such posts or information, it was found that Preity Zinta had recently made her third visit to Prayagraj to participate in the Maha Kumbh. In a video post on her X (formerly Twitter) handle, visuals from her visit to Maha Kumbh along with her loved ones were captured. However, no authentic post or information mentioned Glenn Maxwell accompanying her on the trip. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the image showing Bollywood actress Preity Zinta visiting the ongoing Maha Kumbh 2025 in Prayagraj with Australian cricketer Glenn Maxwell was AI-generated.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Social media post claiming singer Shreya Ghoshal leaked any confidential information about country's economy is false and baseless
content: New Delhi, Feb 27 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a screenshot of a purported article by a leading English news publication, claiming that Singer Shreya Ghoshal leaked confidential information that could harm the country's economy, during an interview. In its investigation, the Desk found that the viral screenshot was fake and that the English Daily had published no such article. The social media posts were shared with a false claim. Claim On February 24, an X (formerly Twitter) shared a screenshot of a purported article by The Indian Express, stating that fans advocated for Shreya Ghoshal's release after a controversial interview. The caption of the X post, which garnered 12.5k views, read: "The Nation Reacts – How Do You Feel About It?" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral screenshot through a Google Reverse Image search and found several other users had shared the same post with a similar claim. One such post can be found here , and its archived version can be viewed here . Initially, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google but could not find any such report by The Indian Express. However, on clicking the link in the viral post, we found several discrepancies- the article did not have a date of publication, and the other hyperlinks, when clicked, led us to Immediate Fastx™- a platform that features a user-friendly interface and free registration for all new sign-ups, and the main link had 'https://innews.fixedsight.mom/' written. Below is the screenshot highlighting the same. The article mentioned that fans expressed their outrage as charges were brought against Shreya Ghoshal for leaking confidential information that could harm the country's economy. "The incident occurred during the broadcast of the program "Mirchi Plus" during which Shreya Ghoshal accidentally revealed an additional source of income. Although this income is legal, authorities are concerned that disclosing this information could lead to mass layoffs by exposing income disparities," read a section of the report. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk skimmed through the entire interview featured on Mirchi Plus's official YouTube channel; however, it did not find any such conversation. Here is the link to the entire interview. In the next part of the investigation, we contacted The Indian Express team for clarification. In its response, the team told us that these ake web pages are designed to look identical to that of The Indian Express and have been designed to mislead, adding that they have been warning readers. "We have been warning readers for two years. Characters and links keep changing," the team responded. Here is the link to the article The Indian Express published warning readers to beware of fake web pages. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral screenshot was fake and that Shreya Ghoshal did not make such a statement.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of social media user dancing to Bollywood song falsely shared in name of Delhi CM Rekha Gupta; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 27 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video, claiming it showed Delhi's newly elected Chief Minister Rekha Gupta dancing to a famous Bollywood number. However, in its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false. The viral video does not feature the Delhi CM but a social media user whose video (dated back to January 19) was now shared with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared a video on February 22, claiming that the woman dancing in it is Delhi's newly elected Chief Minister Rekha Gupta. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found [ here ] and [ here ], with their archived versions available [ here ] and [ here ], respectively. The search results also led the Desk to a video published on an Instagram handle named 'boldmeeraaswag' on January 12, 2025. Here is the link and archive link to the post: The post contained the same video seen in the viral post. However, the Desk's investigation revealed that the video did not feature the Delhi Chief Minister but a woman running the Instagram handle under the name 'boldmeeraaswag'. It is important to note that the Desk reached this conclusion after carefully comparing an image of the Delhi Chief Minister with the woman in the video; however, no similarities were found. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk scanned other videos the user posted on her handle. Videos shot in a similar setting as the viral one were published on the user's handle on a similar date, further confirming that the viral video does not feature the Delhi CM. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video claiming to feature Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta was originally posted by a social media user on January 12, 2025.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of 2020 India-Bangladesh post-match altercation shared as recent incident after ICC Champions Trophy match; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 27 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Days after the Indian cricket squad defeated Bangladesh in its first match in the 2025 Champions Trophy, multiple social media users shared a video of Bangladesh cricket players getting into an altercation with Indian players, claiming that it happened after the recently held India vs Bangladesh ICC Champions Trophy. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found out that the viral video dates back to 2020, when the players of the two teams got involved in an ugly fight after the U19 World Cup final. According to reports, a tense India U19 vs Bangladesh U19 ICC U19 World Cup final turned ugly after players from both sides got physical as soon as Bangladesh hit the winning runs to claim their maiden ICC tournament. Claim On February 20, an Instagram user shared a video of Bangladesh cricket players getting into an altercation with Indian players, claiming that it happened after the recently held India vs Bangladesh ICC Champions Trophy. The text on the video read: "India vs Bangladesh…20/2/2025" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral screenshot through a Google Reverse Image search and found several other users had shared the same post with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , and its archived version can be viewed here and here . The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports and found a report by the Times of India dated February 10, 2020, whose headline read: "Under 19 World Cup Final: India, Bangladesh players clash after the match" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. The report featured the extended version of the viral video, below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the news report. The Quint published another report on February 11, 2020, whose headline read: "ICC Pulls Up 5 Players For Fight After India-B'desh U-19 Final." "Two Indians -- Akash Singh and Ravi Bishnoi -- and three Bangladeshi players have been charged by the ICC for their involvement in the on-field fight that broke out just after Sunday's U-19 World Cup summit clash in Potchefstroom, South Africa: Akash and Bishnoi and three Bangladeshi players -- Md. Towhid Hridoy, Shamim Hossain, and Rakibul Hasan -- were found guilty of breaching ICC Code of Conduct after a few players from both sides nearly came to blows after Bangladesh beat India by three wickets to win their maiden U-19 World Cup title," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to 2020 from the U-19 World Cup, which was shared as a recent incident after the ICC Champions Trophy match between India and Bangladesh.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2022 video of miscreants wreaking havoc in Pune falsely shared as recent incident from Uttar Pradesh giving false communal twist; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 27 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of miscreants wreaking havoc on local shops and stalls; eventually, police can be seen catching the miscreants. The users sharing the video claimed that the Uttar Pradesh police rightly took action against the 'Jihadis' who were responsible for the vandalism in the area. However, the PTI Fact Check investigated and found that the viral video dates back to 2022 from Maharashtra's Pune—not Uttar Pradesh. Further, there is no communal angle to the entire incident, and the accused were caught by the Police. Claim On February 20, an X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video of miscreants wreaking havoc on local shops and stalls, claiming that the Uttar Pradesh Police rightly took action against the 'Jihadis'. The caption of the post, originally in Hindi, read: "Wow, Yogi ji's police made Jihadi's biryani" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , along with their archived versions, which can be viewed here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a report by Mirror Now dated December 29, 2022, whose cover image was similar to the clips in the viral video. The report also carried the viral video. The headline of the report read: "Goons go on a rampage, vandalise shops and terrorise people in Pune, video goes viral." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. "In a shocking incident reported from the Pune district of Maharashtra, a group of goons went on a rampage and vandalised several shops. The goons who were armed also terrorised people in the area. The incident took place near Sinhgad College of Engineering. Later, police reached the spot and arrested the accused and allegedly thrashed them publicly," read a section of the report. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the news report. After analysing the viral video further, the Desk found that a shop's banner contained material written in the Marathi language. Below is a screenshot highlighting this. In the next part of the investigation, we looked for street view images, and below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the street view. Here is the link to the street view. The Desk conducted customised keyword searches on Google to find relevant media reports and came across a report by Policenama, a website that covers crime news from Pune. The report mentioned the names of the individuals involved, and their names indicate that they are not Muslims. Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to 2022 from Maharashtra's Pune, and there is no communal angle to the incident.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, this aerial acrobat was not performed at Maha Kumbh 2025; old and unrelated image shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, Feb 27 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared an image claiming it showed the aerial acrobatics performed by the Indian Air Force on the last day of the Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj, which also coincided with Mahashivratri celebrations in the country. The image depicted three Sukhoi aircraft forming the shape of a Trishul in the sky over Prayagraj. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found the claim false in its investigation. The viral image has been shared with different claims over the years (at least since March 2019), making it clear that it was not taken during the aerial show at the Maha Kumbh 2025. An old image was shared as recent with a false claim linking it to Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared an image on February 26, claiming it showed three Sukhoi aircraft creating the formation of Lord Shiva's Trishul in the sky over Prayagraj on the occasion of Mahashivratri. "What a view! Sarvam Shivamayam! In Prayagraj Mahakumbh Mela, the Indian Air Force mesmerised the crowd on the eve of MahaShivaratri with a spectacular Air Show. Three Sukhoi fighter jets formed Lord Shiva's Trishul, making the MahaKumbh even more unforgettable," the user shared the image with the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and found that multiple other users had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , along with their archived versions viewed here and here respectively: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google. It came across various videos published by media outlets covering the air show performed by the Indian Air Force on the last day of Maha Kumbh 2025, which also fell on the occasion of the Mahashivratri. While the Desk carefully scanned through those videos, it found no visuals from yesterday's event that could match the viral post. Here is the link to the video posted on the official Instagram handle of Doordarshan News on February 26, which further confirmed that no such aerial acrobat was performed by the Indian Air Force on the occasion of Mahashivratri. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Additionally, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search on Google to find more information about Trishul formations performed by the Indian Air Force over the years. The search results led us to multiple images of the Trishul formation made by the Indian Air Force over the years; however, none matched the viral photo. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Moreover, as a part of the investigation, to determine when the viral image was taken initially, the Desk ran it through Google Lens again and found an X post shared by a user named Purushottam Vyas. The image shared by the user exactly matched the viral post; however, it was found that the post was shared on March 6, 2019, predating the Maha Kumbh Mela 2025 in Prayagraj. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral image was not captured during the air show conducted in Prayagraj on February 26, 2025, the last day of the Maha Kumbh Mela.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of Dev Deepawali celebrations in Varanasi falsely shared in name of Maha Kumbh 2025; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 28 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media, with users claiming it showed spectacular fireworks and a mesmerising laser show at the ghats of the River Ganga in Prayagraj on the last day of 'Maha Kumbh 2025.' The video featured people capturing the breathtaking display on their devices. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found the claim to be false. The viral video captured initially celebrations held during Dev Deepawali in Varanasi, where grand fireworks illuminated the sky over the ghats of the River Ganga. An old video from Varanasi was falsely shared on social media, misattributing it to Maha Kumbh 2025. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video on February 27 showing fireworks and a laser show held at the ghats of the River Ganga in Prayagraj on the last day of Maha Kumbh 2025. "This is the last video from Maha Kumbh for this generation, and it is giving me goosebumps. The next Maha Kumbh will occur in the next century," the user captioned the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple other users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search results also led the Desk to a video published on an Instagram handle named official_kunal_070. The handle posted a video matching the settings in the viral post. However, further details revealed it was first posted on November 16, 2024, which predates the 45-day celebrations of Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting that the content seen in the viral video matched that of the video posted by the Instagram user on November 16, 2024. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search about the celebrations held at the ghats of the River Ganga in Varanasi on Dev Deepawali in November 2024. The search results led to multiple news reports confirming the celebrations. Here is the link to a video released by Zee Business's official YouTube channel on November 15, 2024. It shows a laser show similar to the one seen in the viral post, organized on the occasion of Dev Deepawali in Varanasi. Additionally, as part of the investigation, the desk was scanned through official handles linked to the Maha Kumbh. However, no official details confirmed that fireworks were held on the last day of the 45-day religious congregation. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video showing grand fireworks at the river's ghats was from Varanasi and dated back to November 2024.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: One-year-old video of Rahul Gandhi's visit to Mahakaleshwar temple in Ujjain shared as recent with false claim; details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 28 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media, with users claiming it showed Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and senior Congress leader Rahul Gandhi visiting the Shri Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga temple in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh, on the occasion of Mahashivratri. Users shared the video, which purportedly showed the Congress leader arriving at the temple for this year's Mahashivratri celebrations, accompanied by former Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Kamal Nath. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found the claim to be false. The viral video of Rahul Gandhi at the Ujjain temple actually dates back to his visit in March 2024. An old video with a misleading claim was recently shared on social media. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video on February 26, claiming it showed Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi visiting Shri Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga temple in Ujjain on the occasion of Mahashivratri. "Rahul Gandhi offered prayers at the Mahakaleshwar temple in Ujjain. Rahul Gandhi, a devotee of Mahadev, will be the country's next Prime Minister," the user captioned the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with the screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the same video with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively: The search results also led the Desk to a video published on the official X handle of ANI. The handle posted a video that matched the settings in the viral post. However, further details revealed that it was first posted on March 5, 2024, which predates the February 26 Mahashivratri celebrations held in the country this year. Here is the link to the post: Below is a combination image highlighting that the visuals seen in the viral post matched those of the original video posted on March 5, 2024. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google regarding Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's visit to Ujjain in March 2024. The search results led to multiple news reports confirming his visit. Here is the link and a screenshot of a report by ABP News, which elaborated on Rahul Gandhi's visit to Ujjain along with former Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Kamal Nath in March 2024: Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk scanned the social media handles of the Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha but found no details regarding his schedule on Mahashivratri.
