However, a post was found on his X handle in which he extended greetings to the countrymen on the occasion. "Heartiest greetings to everyone on the holy festival of Maha Shivratri! May the blessings of Shiv Shakti always remain on you. Har Har Mahadev," Congress leader Rahul Gandhi posted. Here is the link to his post, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video of Rahul Gandhi's visit to Mahakaleshwar temple in Ujjain from March 2024 was shared on social media as recent with a false claim.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of road caving in Turkiye falsely shared in name of Jaipur incident; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 1 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media, with users claiming it showed a major portion of a road caving in outside a tunnel in Jaipur on February 21, 2025. However, in its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was initially linked to a road caving-in incident in Ordu city, Turkiye, back in July 2023. An old video was recently shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An Instagram user shared a video on February 21, 2025, claiming it showed a road caving in near a tunnel in Jaipur, Rajasthan. "How the road ahead of Jaipur tunnel is breaking down 21/2/2025," the user captioned the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across a video posted by Russia's state-owned news agency, Sputnik. The handle posted the same video as the viral post; however, its first publication was confirmed in July 2023, and the video's origin was linked to Ordu city in Turkiye. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting that the content seen in the viral post matched that of the video published by the Russian state-owned news agency. Additionally, the Desk carefully scanned through other details mentioned alongside the post and came across a report published by Sputnik regarding the development on July 11, 2023. The report mentioned, "Due to the heavy rain that continued for three days in Ordu, the road at the tunnel exit on the Black Sea-Mediterranean Highway in the Mesudiye district collapsed." "Landslides occurred yesterday due to heavy rain on the Ordu leg of the Black Sea-Mediterranean Highway, which indirectly concerns approximately 50 provinces," it added. Here is the link to the report along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video from July 2023 from Ordu, Turkey, was shared on social media as recent with a false claim.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Satire post claiming ABVP attacked Zoo for serving non-veg to tigers on Maha Shivratri shared as real incident
content: New Delhi, March 3 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared screenshots of a purported news clip with a headline claiming that ABVP attacked a zoo for serving non-vegetarian food to tigers on Maha Shivratri. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found the claim to be false. The viral screenshot is from a satirical post shared by a parody account and was misleadingly circulated as real news. Claim On March 1, an X (formerly Twitter) user shared a screenshot of a purported news clip, whose headline claimed that ABVP attacks Zoo for serving non-veg to tigers on Maha Shivratri. The post's caption, originally in Hindi and garnering 365.8K views, read: "You won't find such a group of foolish people anywhere else." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Reverse Image search and found several other users shared the same screenshot. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. Initially, the Desk carefully analysed the purported screenshot shared by the users and found 'This Might be Satire' written in the top right corner. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Taking the investigation ahead, the Desk did a Google search for 'The Savala Vada' and came across their Instagram account. The bio section mentioned 'Satire/parody' and regularly posts satire content for entertainment. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. The purported news clip was shared on February 28. The second slide in this post featured another parody news story suggesting that South Asian University had been renamed Akhand Bharat University. The page regularly features political satirical posts. We scanned the comments sections of the post and found that users mentioned it as satire. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google to check the veracity of the post, but it did not yield any relevant results or news. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral screenshot of the news clip is a satire posted by a parody account and is being misleadingly shared as real news.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI generated image falsely claimed students staged protest against Tamil Nadu CM MK Stalin with posters of #Getoutstalin
content: New Delhi, March 3 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid the ongoing language row in Tamil Nadu, multiple social media users shared an image purportedly showing school students protesting against Tamil Nadu Chief Minister MK Stalin with posters that read "Get Out Stalin." The image surfaced amid a social media war that erupted after Tamil Nadu's Deputy Chief Minister Udhayanidhi Stalin criticised Prime Minister Narendra Modi, demanding the release of the state's share of funds. In response, BJP state chief K. Annamalai launched the #GetOutStalin campaign, asserting that the online anti-Stalin sentiments would translate into real votes in the 2026 Assembly elections, leading to Stalin's removal from power. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found the image to be fake. The viral picture was AI-generated and falsely shared as real on social media. Claim On February 22, an X (formerly Twitter) user shared a photograph of students with a banner, claiming they staged a protest against Tamil Nadu CM MK Stalin. The quote written on the banner read: "All Indians are brothers and sisters. Stop North vs South Divide. #GetOutStalin." The user shared the post with the caption, "Share and comment if you resonate with these kids' thoughts! #GetOutStalin. " Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through a Google Reverse Image search and found several other users shared the same post with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports. However, the search did not yield any results claiming that school students staged a protest against the Tamil Nadu CM. However, we did find a report by One India, dated February 21, which mentioned that Tamil Nadu's Deputy Chief Minister, Udhayanidhi Stalin, criticised Prime Minister Narendra Modi and demanded that the Union government release the state's share of funds. He warned that if the funds were not provided, the DMK would intensify its rhetoric from 'Go Back Modi' to 'Get Out Modi.' Tamil Nadu BJP chief K Annamalai challenged the DMK IT wing to a hashtag face-off on X. Annamalai dared them to tweet 'Get Out Modi' all night, vowing to begin his 'Get Out Stalin' trend at 6 a.m., claiming it would prove which slogan gained more traction on the social media platform. He further claimed that these anti-Stalin sentiments on social media would translate into real votes in the 2026 Assembly elections, leading to Chief Minister Stalin's removal from power. Here is the link to the report. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the viral image and found multiple discrepancies suggesting it was AI-generated. For instance, the viral image showed one of the school girls with six fingers, the eyes looked distorted, and the background of the image appeared to be quite glossy. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. After careful analysis of the photo, we also noticed 'Grok', a generative AI tool designed to create art and visuals from text inputs, written on the bottom. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Taking a cue from the above-generated inputs, the Desk then ran the image through Hive Moderation (an AI detection tool), which also predicted a substantial presence of AI content. Below is a screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral claim is false, as the image is AI-generated.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video of US President Trump falsely shared claiming he criticised Ukranian Prez Zelenskyy's outfit during White House meeting
content: New Delhi, March 3 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): After US President Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's meeting at the Oval Office, several questions were raised about Zelenskyy's attire. Multiple social media users shared a video claiming that Trump had criticised Zelenskyy's outfit during the visit. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found the claim to be false. The viral video originated from an "AI Parody" account that creates AI-generated voiceovers. During the meeting, a reporter interrupted Trump and asked Zelenskyy why he wasn't wearing a suit. The question left Trump and Vice President JD Vance in splits, but Trump responded positively, saying, "I do like your clothing." Claim On March 1, an X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video, purportedly showing US President Donald Trump criticising Ukraine President Zelenskyy's outfit that he wore during his visit to the White House. In the 00:56 second video Trump can be heard saying: "President Zelenskyy showed up to the White House wearing an outfit from Temu and I found that very disrespectful. I have to be honest, I will start calling him Temu Zelenskyy from now on. Someone get this guy a suit for god's sake. Sleepy Joe (Biden) gave him 500 billion dollars, but he can't even afford a 1000-dollar suit. What a cheap guy he was. He spent all that money from US taxpayers on the Temu app. He should use Amazon so taxpayers' money does not go to China. Temu has awful quality…Either way, you cannot show up like that to the White House…" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users had shared the same video with similar claims. One such post can be found here , and their archived versions can be viewed here . Initially, the Desk carefully watched the viral video and found a 'Dangerous AI' remark on the video with a link to YouTube. We then searched the YouTube handle, which mentioned 'AI Parody Content' in the About section. "Everything said in my videos is the original script I wrote; it's not real quotes or opinions of those people in the videos. I use AI to create the voiceovers in my videos. They are not the real voices of the video characters," read the Disclaimer. It makes it clear that the viral video does not feature Donald Trump's real voice. Below is a screenshot highlighting this. Further, the Desk found the video uploaded on March 1. In the top left corner of the video, 'Altered or synthetic content' was mentioned. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot. In the subsequent part of the investigation, to verify whether the visuals of Trump in the viral video had been digitally altered, the Desk ran keyframes through Google Lens. It found the original footage in the AI parody video was shared by News 9 Live on February 27. The original event was a press conference by Trump. The title of the report read: "President Donald Trump's Remarks During Cabinet Meeting I USA I DOGE I Elon Musk | News9" Here is the link to the report. The Desk noticed that the viral video was a mirror image of the original video. Below is a combination image highlighting this. Subsequently, the Desk concluded the viral video originated from an 'AI Parody' account, which uses AI to create the voiceovers. The footage was falsely shared as real.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of former US President Joe Biden with PM Modi resurfaced with false claim; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 3 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared an old video of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and former US President Joe Biden, claiming that Biden mocked the Indian PM during his 2023 visit to the United States while Modi laughed without understanding what was being said. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that a selectively edited portion of the original video was shared with a false claim. The video actually dates back to the 2023 State Dinner hosted at the White House. In the original footage, Biden shared an anecdote about his grandfather, and both leaders shared a moment of camaraderie as Biden mentioned that neither of them drinks alcohol. Claim On March 1, an X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video of PM Modi and former US President Joe Biden, claiming that the latter mocked the Prime Minister, while the PM laughed without even understanding what he was saying. In the 00:16-second video, Joe Biden discusses how to raise a toast without alcohol in the glass. The post's caption, which garnered 225k views, read: "PROPAGANDA ❗ : Modi is great diplomat and Rahul Gandhi will defame India. REALITY ⚡ : When Joe Biden said, "He thinks I am kidding, but I am not," Modi laughed without even understanding what he was saying. INDIA NEEDS AN EDUCATED PM LIKE RAHUL GANDHI IN 2029." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and found that the same video with a similar claim was also shared in 2023. The link to one such post can be viewed here , and its archived version can be found here . As the Desk continued its investigation, the Desk found a video on the official YouTube handle of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, dated June 23, 2023. This was during the State Dinner hosted at the White House. The title read: "PM Modi, President Biden raise the toast at the State Dinner hosted at the White House" At 6:37 seconds in the video, a man can be seen offering a glass of water to former US President Biden and a glass of ginger ale to PM Modi. At 6:40 seconds, Biden says, "Mr Prime Minister, I had a grandfather…and he used to say when give a toast and you do not have any alcohol in your glass, you should do it with your left hand." He added, "You think I am kidding, I am not…Toast to our partnership, the people, the possibilities ahead, two great friends, two great nations, and two great powers. Cheers!" Here is the link to the video and below a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral and YouTube videos. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports. It came across a report by Business Today dated June 23, 2023. The title of the report read: "'Good news, we both don't drink': Biden's joke on alcohol at state dinner leaves PM Modi laughing" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. The report mentioned: "'The good news for both of us is we both don't drink,' President Biden said, as both raised their glasses." It further added: You think I'm kidding, I'm not, President Biden said" Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a selected portion of the video was shared on social media to insinuate that former President Biden mocked PM Modi. In the original video, Biden shared an anecdote about his grandfather, and the two shared a moment of bonhomie at the state dinner as Biden revealed that they do not drink alcohol.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2017 video of Virat Kohli's advertisement for ethnic-wear clothing brand shared with false claim ahead of Ramadan
content: New Delhi, March 3 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): With the start of the holy month of Ramadan, several social media users shared a video of Indian cricketer Virat Kohli celebrating Eid, claiming that he had extended his wishes for Ramadan ahead of the start of the month-long festival. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigation found the claim false. The viral video dates back to 2017 and is an edited clip from a Manyavar advertisement shoot. Additionally, the background music has been altered and manipulated. Manyavar, a renowned Indian clothing brand, specialises in elegant traditional wear and ethnic attire, including sherwanis, kurtas, and jackets. Ramadan has begun worldwide, marking a period during which those observing the fast refrain from eating and drinking from dawn to dusk for 29 or 30 days. Fasting durations vary from 12 to 16 hours, depending on location. Claim On March 2, an X (formerly Twitter) shared a video of Indian cricketer Virat Kohli celebrating Eid, claiming that Kohli shared his wishes for Ramadan. The caption of the post, which garnered 244.5k views, originally in Hindi, read: "Virat Kohli is a King" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the same video with similar claims. One such post can be found here , along with its archived versions, can be found here . After further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a video uploaded to YouTube by 'Manyavar' on March 10, 2017. In the 00:54 seconds advertisement, Cricketer Virat Kohli says: "During Holi, the flying gulal colors every heart, be it Mahesh or Michael. On Eid, we eat sevai made by Khan Chachi more often than Firoz. During Diwali, lights brighten everything. Everyone, not just Christians, can hear the sound of Christmas bells. On Gurupurab, langar food fills everyone's stomach. In India, every festival belongs to everyone." This makes it clear that he was talking about the diverse festivals celebrated in India, not just Eid. Here is the link to the advertisement, and below is a screenshot. Below are a few combination images highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the original YouTube video. On further analysing the Manyavar advertisement, we found that the original video had a different background music to the one shared in the viral post. Taking a cue from this, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search to find the music in the viral video. While searching, we found the music in the viral clip to actually be Noor e Ramazan. Here is the link to the video. Also, the Desk scanned Kohli's social media handles and found that no such message has been posted yet. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was actually from a Manyavar advertisement shot in 2017, which has been edited and the background music altered.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: UP video of group of people being attacked by another shared with false communal angle; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 3 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of a group of people being attacked by another group of people claiming that it depicted a religious hate crime against a Muslim family in Amroha, Uttar Pradesh. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral video was shared with a false communal angle. The incident occurred in Bagarpur Kalan village, under the jurisdiction of Amroha Dehat police station, due to a personal dispute between the children of the two families. Moreover, both the accused and the victims belong to the same community. Claim On February 25, an X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video of a group attacking another group with sticks, claiming that it depicts a religious hate crime against a Muslim family in Amroha, Uttar Pradesh. The post's caption, which garnered 42.9k views, originally in Hindi, read: "Look at the fury of UP. Posts should not stop until arrest. Goons are brutally beating a Muslim family after entering their house. The viral video is being reported from Bagdpur Kala of Amroha's rural police station area." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the same video with similar claims. One such post can be found here , along with their archived versions, which can be viewed here . Initially, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find relevant media reports and came across a report by Hindustan, dated February 26, 2025. The headline of the report read: "Attacked after entering the house, video of beating with sticks went viral" The report mentioned that the incident took place in Bagarpur Kalan village under the jurisdiction of Amroha Dehat police station due to a personal dispute between the children of the two families. After the video went viral on social media, the Police swung into action and registered a case against the accused. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. On further analysing the search results, the Desk found another report by Dainik Bhaskar, dated February 25, whose headline read: "Attack by goons in Amroha: Entered the house and attacked the family, three accused arrested" The report also included a video that has been widely shared on social media. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the video in the news report. Here is the link to the report. "According to the Rural Police Station in charge, Balendra Singh, the police identified the accused using the video. Three accused have been arrested in the case. The police are taking legal action," the report mentioned. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that it was a personal dispute between the two families. Both the accused and the victims belong to the same community. The viral video was shared with a false communal angle.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Afghan cricketer Ibrahim Zadran's celebratory gestures after victory in CT 2025 match falsely linked to Maha Shivratri; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 3 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming that Afghan cricketer Ibrahim Zadran's celebratory hand gestures after scoring a century against England in the ICC Champions Trophy 2025 were linked to a claim that he offered prayers to Lord Shiva, as the match coincided with Maha Shivratri. Users alleged that his distinctive gestures mimicked the playing of the damru (Lord Shiva's drum) and included folded hands as a mark of prayer. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found that Zadran's gestures, which gained widespread attention, were his way of thanking Rashid Khan. The two had a pre-match conversation that seemingly inspired his performance. The viral video was shared on social media with a false claim, misleadingly linking it to Maha Shivratri. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video on February 27, claiming Afghan cricket player Ibrahim Zadran's distinctive hand gesture after registering his century win against England in the ICC Champions Trophy match was linked to him offering prayers to Lord Shiva, as the match took place on the occasion of Maha Shivratri. The users claimed the cricketer's distinctive hand gestures were actually him mimicking the playing of the damru, Lord Shiva's instrument, and offering prayers with folded hands. "Afghanistan's Ibrahim scored a century yesterday and saw his reaction. He played the damru and offered prayers to Bholenath during Mahashivaratri. Seeing this, the whole of Pakistan was burning with rage," the user shared the video with the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customized keyword search on Google to find more information about Zadran's distinctive hand gestures, which grabbed headlines among cricket fans after his winning century in the ICC Champions Trophy Afghanistan vs. England match held on February 26, 2025. The search result led us to a report published by a website named Cricket Times on February 27, 2025. The report elaborated on the reason behind Zadran's distinctive hand gesture (where he mimicked bowling a leg-spin and then folded his hands). The report mentioned that this was a tribute by Zadran to his teammate Rashid Khan, with whom he had a pre-match conversation that seemed to inspire his performance. Here is the link and archive link to the report, along with a screenshot. The search results also led the Desk to a video published on February 26 by the International Cricket Council's official Instagram handle. The video includes a statement by Zadran himself explaining that special gesture. He asserted, "Before the game, I chatted with Rashid. Whenever I chat with Rashid, I get a score. That's why I thanked Rashid when I got to my century." Here is the link and archive link to the Instagram post by the ICC, along with a screenshot. ​Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of Ibrahim Zadran making celebratory gestures after his historic century in the ICC Champions Trophy match against England on February 26 was not linked to Maha Shivratri celebrations.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of woman's corpse found inside suitcase in Kolkata shared with false and communal narrative; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 4 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Days after a woman's body was found stuffed inside a blue suitcase in Kolkata, a video allegedly linked to the incident began circulating on social media. Users claimed that the woman was a Hindu who had been murdered by her Muslim partner, Akram, after being lured into a relationship under the pretext of marriage. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigation found the claim false. Multiple news reports confirmed that the deceased, identified as Sumita Ghosh, was allegedly murdered due to a family dispute by her relatives, Arati Ghosh and Falguni Ghosh. There was no communal angle to the incident. The viral video was misleadingly shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared, on February 26, a video showing a woman's corpse found stuffed inside a suitcase in Kolkata. The user claimed that the victim was a Hindu woman allegedly murdered by her Muslim partner named Akram. "In Bengal, Akram killed a girl on the pretext of marriage and packed her body in a suitcase. Love Jihad causes the murder, rape, and robbery of a thousand Hindu girls every day. Despite knowing this, Hindu girls are reaching such a fate," the user shared the video with the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and found multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search result also led the Desk to a video published on the official YouTube channel of Crime Tak on February 26, 2025. The video matched the keyframes the Desk used for the investigation; however, it further revealed that the incident occurred in Kolkata and that the body of the woman found inside the suitcase was that of Sumita Ghosh, who was allegedly murdered by her relatives (Arati Ghosh and Falguni Ghosh) after a heated altercation. The video also reported that the accused stuffed the woman's body inside a blue suitcase but were apprehended while attempting to dump it near the Ganga River in Kolkata. Here is the link and archive link to the video, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the content seen in the viral post matches that of the video posted by the YouTube channel. Additionally, in the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find more details about the gruesome incident in Kolkata. It came across a report by India Today, published on February 25, 2025. The report confirmed that the alleged murder of Sumita Ghosh, whose body was found inside the suitcase, was committed during a family discord, and there was no communal angle to the incident. Here is the link and archive link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing the woman's corpse found stuffed inside a suitcase in Kolkata does not have any communal angle. The deceased was identified as Sumita Ghosh, who her relatives murdered following a family dispute.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old, unrelated video from Chhattisgarh falsely shared claiming Sheikh Hasina recently taken to Prayagraj from Delhi under high security
content: New Delhi, March 4 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Following former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's recent statement that she would return to her country, multiple social media users shared a video of a convoy of vehicles, claiming that the Indian government had evacuated Bangladesh's former Prime Minister from Delhi to Allahabad (now Prayagraj). However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found the claim to be false. The viral video is old and unrelated; it shows a convoy of a Chhattisgarh government official. It was falsely shared on social media with the claim that the Indian government recently provided high security to Hasina for her travel from Delhi to Prayagraj. Claim On February 27, an X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video of a convoy of vehicles, claiming that the Indian government evacuated Bangladesh's former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina from Delhi to Allahabad. The English translation of the post's caption, which garnered 25.6k views, read: "Bangladesh Awami League President to Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. The Indian government has evacuated them back to Delhi and Allahabad under maximum security." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , along with their archived versions, which can be viewed here and here . The Desk initially conducted a customised keyword search to find relevant media reports, but the search did not yield any authentic or verifiable results. However, a report by NDTV cited Hasina who vowed to return to Bangladesh. In response, the country's interim government, led by Muhammad Yunus, is prioritizing the former prime minister's extradition from India to Bangladesh. Here is the link to the report. However, there are no reports of Hasina being shifted under heavy security from Delhi to Prayagraj. The Desk carefully analysed the video and found that all the cars in the convoy had registration plates of Chhattisgarh. Below is a screenshot highlighting this. In the subsequent part of the investigation, the Desk ran keyframes through Google Lens to verify the visuals. It found the same video in the viral YouTube clip dated March 7, 2023. This post only provided the date and added no context about the video. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot. Below is a set of combination images highlighting the similarities between the viral and YouTube videos. On further analysing the search results, the Desk came across another YouTube video on May 14, 2023. The user claimed that this video showed a convoy of the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) and Sub Divisional Magistrate (SDM). Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot. The Desk then carefully scanned the viral video and found a statue of Lal Bahadur Shastri in the background displaying the text "छ ग." This strongly suggests that the video was likely recorded in Chhattisgarh. However, we could not find the exact date and time the viral video was filmed. However, the video has been available since 2023, predating the Bangladesh protests that started in 2024. Subsequently, an old and unrelated video of a Chhattisgarh government official's convoy falsely claimed that the Indian government provided high security for Hasina's travel from Delhi to Prayagraj.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered video of FM Nirmala Sitharaman falsely shared claiming she endorsed investment scheme
content: New Delhi, March 4 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of a news report by a leading English news broadcaster was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that in the video Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman had endorsed a government investment scheme. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found this claim to be false. The minister did not endorse the scheme, and the video was digitally altered to promote fraudulent investments. Claim shared in the social media post was false. Claim A Facebook user recently shared a video of an alleged CNN-News18 report claiming that Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has endorsed a government investment scheme. In the video, Sitharaman can be heard saying, "I am here to tell you about an automotive system we have been developing over the past two years, which is already generating additional income for many Indians. I am not promising you millions in a single day but earning Rs 50,000 a day is completely realistic, to the math yourself…You have to register and invest Rs 21,000 in the account, after that you will see your money grow almost daily…" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found users had shared the same video but cited that scammers misused a Sitharaman video and dubbed it with AI to promote illegal schemes. One such user, name V.C. Sajjanar, IPS, shared the video on X (formerly Twitter), the caption read: "Look how scamsters have misused a video of our Hon'ble Union Finance Minister @nsitharaman is dubbing it with an AI-generated voice to promote their illegal schemes. No one can profit from network marketing without others bearing the loss — that's the harsh truth. Since the start of my career, I've been relentlessly fighting against MLM companies, and the misuse of AI has only strengthened my resolve to protect innocent people from falling into such traps. Don't trust everything you see online!" Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Taking the investigation ahead and to verify, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find reports that mentioned that the Union Minister advocated about the investment platform, but it did not yield any report. The Desk then ran a reverse image search of the keyframe featuring Sitharaman. It came across a live stream by DD News dated February 1, 2025, of Sitharaman's press conference after presenting the Union Budget. We heard the entire 49:44 press conference but Sitharaman did not mention any investment or trading platform. It only indicates that the viral video was digitally altered. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot. In the next part of the investigation, we used an AI tool, Resemble Detect, to check the authenticity of Nirmala Sitharaman's voice. The viral audio has been edited according to the results obtained after scanning. Here is the link and below is a screenshot of the result. We used another detector tool, elevenlabs, and according to the results found there, the viral audio was edited 97%. Below is a screenshot of the results and here is the link . Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Union Minister Nirmala Sitharaman's video has been digitally altered as she has not endorsed any government investment scheme.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Five-year-old silambam athlete from Tamil Nadu wrongly identified as RSS functionary in Kerala; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 4 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of a young boy performing martial arts was recently shared on social media, with many users claiming that he was a five-year-old named Karthik, who had been elected as the head teacher of the RSS Baal Shakha in Kannur, Kerala. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found this claim false. The viral video features Aarav, a trained Silambam athlete from Tamil Nadu. An unrelated video was misleadingly shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a February 23 video showing a school-aged boy performing martial arts. The user claimed that his name was Karthik and that he was appointed as the head teacher of the RSS Baal Shakha in Kannur, Kerala. The user shared the video with the caption, "He is Karthik, age 5, head teacher of RSS Bal Shakha, Kannur, Kerala. " Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found various users shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here . In the next part of the investigation, the Desk carefully examined the viral video and found it comprised of three different clips of the five-year-old boy performing martial arts moves. To gather more details about the clips mentioned, the Desk ran keyframes (generated via the InVid tool) of them through Google Lens and came across an Instagram handle with the username "aarav_aj_official." The Desk found that the user of this handle was the same boy seen in the viral post. However, his name was mentioned as Aarav AJ, an athlete, and not Karthik. Here is the link to the Instagram handle, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting that the boy seen in the viral video was the same as the user of the Instagram handle. Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk scanned through the Instagram handle and found the exact three videos (which were clubbed together in the viral post) published at different times. For instance, the first video (from timestamp 00:01 to 00:29) was posted on January 13. The second video (from timestamp 00:30 to 01:21) was posted on January 20, and the third video (from timestamp 01:22 to 02:11) was posted on January 17. Additionally, the Desk observed that in all three clips, Aarav performed Silambam, an ancient Indian martial art originating in Tamil Nadu. Here are separate links to the videos ( Link 1 , Link 2 and Link 3 ) seen clubbed together in the viral post: Furthermore, while scanning through Aarav's Instagram handle, the Desk found that some of his posts collaborated with another Instagram page named "stickman_silambam_academy." Upon checking this page, the Desk found it is affiliated with a Silambam training academy in Tamil Nadu. Here is the link to the Instagram page: As part of the investigation, the Desk contacted the number on the same Instagram page and spoke to a person associated with the academy. The individual confirmed that Aarav was currently training at the academy in Tamil Nadu and that the viral claim about him was false. In the subsequent part of the investigation, the Desk also contacted the media vertical of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), which confirmed that Aarav was not affiliated as a Swayamsevak in Tamil Nadu. At the time of reporting, a response regarding his alleged affiliation with Kerala was awaited. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a video of Silambam athlete Aarav from Tamil Nadu was falsely shared as that of a five-year-old boy named Karthik, who was allegedly elected as the head teacher of RSS Baal Shakha in Kannur, Kerala.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of anti-terror mock drill at VIT Vellore shared on social media with false claim; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 4 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it showed a group of armed, masked men carrying out explosions on the Vellore Institute of Technology (VIT) campus, a private deemed university in Vellore, Tamil Nadu. The video depicted these armed men running through the campus premises, setting off explosions, and entering a main building. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found this claim to be false. The video shows a mock drill conducted by the National Security Guard (NSG) on the VIT campus on March 2, 2025, as part of a security and rescue operation exercise in case of a potential threat. Despite this, the video was shared on social media with a misleading claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video on March 2, showing a group of armed men allegedly carrying out sudden blasts at the university campus of Vellore Institute of Technology (VIT). The video showed the armed masked men running through the campus premises and carrying out blasts before entering a main building. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. The search result also led the Desk to a video posted on a YouTube channel named 'Shraddha - The Frustrated Human' on March 3, 2025. The video included visuals from the viral post. Still, it was shared with a caption clarifying that it was a mock drill conducted by the National Security Guard (NSG) at the VIT Vellore campus. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting that the content in the viral video matches that of the YouTube video posted on March 3, 2025. In the next part of the investigation, taking cue from the above generated inputs, the Desk conducted a customized keyword search on Google. It came across a report published by The Hindu on March 2, 2025. While the report's feature image matched the keyframes the Desk used for the investigation, the report's details revealed that the video was of a mock drill carried out by the National Security Guard (NSG) on the spacious campus of VIT Vellore to rehearse security and rescue operations in case of a threat. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of the anti-terror mock drill at VIT Vellore campus was shared on social media without proper context to mislead people.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: Scripted video of man injecting chemicals in watermelons shared as real with a false communal spin
content: New Delhi, March 4 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of a man injecting chemicals into watermelons, claiming that he was a Hindu man selling chemically adulterated watermelons during Ramadan. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found this claim to be false. The original video was scripted and created to spread awareness about watermelon adulteration. Despite this, it was misleadingly shared as real with a false communal angle. Claim On March 2, an X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video of a man injecting some chemicals in watermelons, claiming that he was a Hindu man and was selling chemically injected watermelons during Ramadan. "Ramadan starts today. Keep these things in mind and send this video to your friends and family. Do not buy anything from people like Ayush Verma," the voiceover in the video said. The post's caption, originally in Hindi and garnering 81.2k views, read: "Save the lives of Muslims in Ramadan. Earn goodness by sharing this video!! While shopping for Iftaar in Ramadan, one mistake of yours can result in everyone's loss." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , along with their archived versions, which can be viewed here and here . On further scanning the search results, we came across a report by India Today about artificial food colour and sweeteners being injected in watermelons. The report's title read: "Is your watermelon safe to eat? Find out if it's chemically injected like that viral video" The report carried a similar video as the viral video uploaded to YouTube by The Social Junction. According to the report, the video posted as a part of a social experiment demonstrates adulteration practice. Here is the link to the report. Next, we scanned the video uploaded on The Social Junction's YouTube and found that it was uploaded on March 9, 2024. The man and background of the video were similar to those circulated on social media, except that there was no voice-over. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral and YouTube videos. While analysing the YouTube video, the Desk found that at 00:28 seconds in, a disclaimer pops up on the screen. The Disclaimer reads: "The video is complete fiction. All the events in the video are scripted and made for awareness purposes only. This does not promote any activity or defame any kind of rituals…" Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. The channel's About section mentions that the videos on this page are for entertainment and social experimentation purposes only. Below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a scripted video to spread awareness was shared as real with a false communal angle.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Images showing Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma playing holi are AI-generated; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 5 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Three purported images of Indian cricketer Virat Kohli along with his wife and Bollywood actress Anushka Sharma were recently shared on social media. Users claimed that these images were from their Holi celebrations this year. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the photos shared on social media were fake. AI-generated pictures were shared on social media as real with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user going by the name "Cric News" shared multiple images on March 2, featuring Indian cricketer Virat Kohli along with his wife and Bollywood actress Anushka Sharma. The images allegedly showed the celebrity duo playing Holi. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation: The Desk ran all three images shared in the social media post through Google Lens; however, the search results did not lead to any credible report that could corroborate the authenticity or origin of the images. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analyzed the images and found multiple discrepancies suggesting that they were digitally altered or AI-generated. For instance, the background in all three images appeared visibly blurred, and the hands of the duo seen in the first and third images looked distorted. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Next, taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk ran the images one by one through Hive Moderation, an AI detection tool, which suggested a substantial presence of AI-generated or deepfake content in all three images. Below, a combination image has been attached highlighting the results of the AI detection in the images. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the images of Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma from their Holi celebrations this year are AI-generated.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old and clipped video of Mulayam Singh Yadav's speech shared claiming he made anti-Hindu remarks in Parliament
content: New Delhi, March 5 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of former Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Mulayam Singh Yadav, purportedly from Parliament, was shared on social media. Those sharing the video claimed that Yadav made anti-Hindu remarks during his address in Parliament. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was old and shared with a false claim. The original video was clipped, and his speech was misinterpreted. In reality, Yadav was responding to BJP leader Virendra Singh, who had objected to his accusations regarding the anti-copying law imposed in the state at that time. Claim On February 27, an X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video of Samajwadi Party founder Mulayam Singh Yadav, claiming that he passed anti-Hindu statements in Parliament. In the 0:39 seconds video, he can be heard saying: "We are enemies of Hindus and friends of Muslims, and we proudly say this. Everywhere—on TV, in magazines—they say Mulayam Singh is a criminal. I am a criminal" The caption of the post which garnered 1531 views, originally in Hindi, read: "Even after watching this video of Mulayam Yadav, one can only express regret over the mentality of those Yadav brothers who support the Samajwadi Party" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , along with their archived versions, which can be viewed here and here . Mulayam Singh Yadav was elected as a Member of Parliament (MP) to the Lok Sabha only, and not the Rajya Sabha, starting in 1996. The video appeared to be from Parliament, taking a cue from all this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on YouTube to find the original video of Mulayam Singh Yadav speaking in the Parliament. The search resulted in a video uploaded by the Digital Sansad – Parliament of India YouTube channel. The title of the video read: "Shri Mulayam Singh Yadav on 27.03.1998 - Discussion on Confidence Motion". On carefully scanning the entire video, we found that at 27:57 seconds time stamp, Yadav can be heard saying: "...Hamari toh magazines mein apradhiyo ki party hai he. (In every magazine we are branded as a party of criminals). But you claim to be a person of clean image. Tell us about yourself; what are you?. Everywhere—on TV, in magazines—they say Mulayam Singh is a criminal…Hamare baarein mein toh na jaane apne kya kya bol dia hai (You've said all sorts of things against us)- Hum toh Hinduo ke khilaf hai aur musalmano ke sath hai (that we are against the Hindus and support the Muslims)..." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking the investigation forward, the Desk conducted another set of cutomised keyword searches for the English transcript of this speech and found it in the Parliament Library. Here is the link to the transcript and below is a screenshot of the same. It read: " I said so because our party is branded as a party of the criminals. In every magazine and on television it is shown that there are the criminals belonging to Mulayam Singh party. We are nothing but criminals ...... (interruptions) but you claim to be a person of the clean image. Tell us about yourself what you are. Much is said about us that we are enemies of the Hindus and friends of the Muslims. We can say with pride that…" According to reports, Mulayam Singh Yadav criticised the then Uttar Pradesh BJP government's anti-copying law in Uttar Pradesh. His response was after Virendra Singh of the BJP interrupted, objecting to the accusation. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video of Mulayam Singh Yadav had been clipped, with his speech edited and misinterpreted.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Photo of Istanbul Airport falsely shared with report on airports in Uttar Pradesh; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 6 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a photo of an airport, claiming that it is from Uttar Pradesh, the first state in India to have 21 airports. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found this claim to be false. The viral photo actually depicts Istanbul Airport in Turkey and has no connection to Uttar Pradesh. Claim On March 4, an X (formerly Twitter) user shared a picture of an airport, claiming that it is from Uttar Pradesh, the first state in India to have 21 airports. The post's caption, originally in Hindi and garnering 138.7 K views, read: "Uttar Pradesh created history, becoming the first state in India to have 21 airports." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Reverse Image search and found several other users shared the same screenshot. Two such posts can be found here and here, and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. On further analysing the search results, the Desk came across a report published by Condé Nast Traveller, a luxury travel magazine. The cover photo was similar to the viral one circulated on social media. The title of the report read: "iGA Istanbul Airport Was Named World's Best International Hub—Here's Why" Here is the link and below is a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral photo and the cover image. We also found a Blog written on April 27, 2020, whose title read: "Istanbul Airport opens new runway in June." The blog's cover image consisted of a picture similar to the one making rounds on social media. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Additionally, Uttar Pradesh has over 14 operational airports, while others are under construction or in the proposal stage. Here a Times of India report link : "At 14, Uttar Pradesh has the highest number of airports that will get regular commercial flights this summer." Another report was published by the same English Daily, dated February 28, 2024, whose headline read: "Uttar Pradesh to have 21 airports: CM Yogi Adityanath soon" Here is the link to the report. While Adityanath stated that the state will "soon" have 21 airports, the claim that it already has that many is false. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral photograph is of Istanbul Airport and has no connection with Uttar Pradesh.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2021 video of Aussie fan chanting 'Bharat Mata Ki Jai' after India's win at Gabba falsely shared as India's recent win in ICC Champions Trophy 2025 semi-finals
content: New Delhi, March 6 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): After India's four-wicket victory over Australia in the first semi-final of the ICC Champions Trophy on Tuesday, March 4, 2025, multiple social media users shared a video of an Australian fan chanting "Bharat Mata Ki Jai" and "Vande Mataram". Users claimed that he was cheering for India even after Australia lost in the semi-finals. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found this claim to be false. The viral video actually dates back to 2021, when India secured a historic victory at the Gabba in Brisbane, and is unrelated to the ICC Champions Trophy 2025 semi-finals. With this win, India has booked a spot in Sunday's final in Dubai, where they will face New Zealand. Claim On March 4, an Instagram user shared a video of a man dressed in an Australian cricket jersey chanting 'Bharat Mata Ki Jai' and 'Vande Mataram', claiming that he was cheering for India even after Australia lost to India in the ICC Champions Trophy 2025 semifinals. The caption of the post read: "An Australian fan after they lost the semifinal against India in the Champions Trophy 2025" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , along with their archived versions, which can be viewed here and here . Initially, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports. It came across a report by India Today, dated January 21, 2021, whose headline read: "India vs Australia Gabba Test Series: Australian Fan Chants 'Vande Mataram'!" "An Australian fan was heard shouting slogans of 'Bharat Mata ki Jai' and 'Vande Mataram' after team India defeated Australia in the final match of the Border-Gavaskar Trophy. In the video, the fan was heard rooting for Team India, as he was followed by Indian fans singing after him. The video, which was taken on Day 4 of the Gabba Test, showed the lone Australian fan shouting at the top of his voice," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. The report also carried the video which is being circulated on social media. Below is a combination image highlighting the same. Furthermore, another report was published by India Times dated January 20, 2021, with the headline: "Australian Fan Chanting 'Bharat Mata Ki Jai' During India's Big Win At Gabba, Is What Cricket Is All About" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. The Indian cricket team had scripted history in Brisbane to retain the Border-Gavaskar Trophy with a three-wicket win against Australia in the fourth Test match. India registered the win at the Gabba – which has been Australia's fortress for the last 32 years. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to 2021 when India recorded a historic victory at the Gabba in Brisbane, and is not related to Australia's loss in the ICC Champions Trophy 2025 semifinals.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated photo of Australian cricketer Travis Head with his wife shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, March 6 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Social media has been abuzz following India's victory over Australia in the ICC Champions Trophy 2025 semi-final. In the aftermath, several social media users shared a collage of two pictures featuring Australian cricketer Travis Head with his wife, claiming that he hugged her and broke down after Australia's defeat to India. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigation found that the viral images were AI-generated and falsely shared on social media as real. Claim On March 5, an Instagram user shared a collage of two pictures featuring Australian cricketer Travis Head and his wife, claiming that the cricketer hugged and broke down in front of his wife after their defeat in the Champions Trophy 2025 semifinals against India. "Travis Head hugged his wife & started crying after losing the match to India. But 16 months ago, 145 crore cried when we lost at Ahmedabad in the Final (Sic)," the user shared the post with this caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral images through the Reverse Image Search and found several users shared the same collage with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be found here and here , respectively. The Desk first looked for relevant data, however, the search results did not lead to any credible report that could corroborate the authenticity or origin of the images. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the entire post and found that several users in the comment section had written 'AI'. Below is a screenshot of two such comments. Taking a cue from this, the Desk carefully examined the image and noticed several discrepancies, suggesting that it was AI-generated or digitally altered. For instance, the two pictures showed the cricketer in different jerseys, with blurry backgrounds, and glossy textures. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk ran the image through WasItAI (an AI detection tool), which suggested a substantial presence of AI content. Below is a screenshot of the result: Further, the Desk also ran the image through Hive Moderation, another AI detection tool, which confirmed a significant presence of AI-generated content. Below is a screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the viral photos allegedly showing Travis Head breaking down after Australia lost are AI-generated.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of fireworks display at Kuwaiti stadium falsely shared as celebrations for India after their ICC Champions Trophy semifinal victory; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 6 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media, with some users claiming it showed a dazzling fireworks display inside Dubai International Cricket Stadium after India's historic four-wicket victory over Australia, securing their place in the ICC Champions Trophy 2025 final. The video purportedly captured fireworks lighting up the sky in Dubai following India's grand triumph. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found this claim to be false. The video features a fireworks display at Jaber Al-Ahmad International Stadium in Kuwait during the 26th Arabian Gulf Cup tournament. An old, unrelated video was falsely shared on social media with a misleading claim. Claim An X user shared a video on March 4, claiming it showed a fireworks display inside Dubai International Cricket Stadium after India's massive triumph against Australia in the ICC Champions Trophy semi-finals held on March 4, 2025. The Indian team beat Australia by four wickets to enter the finals of the ICC Champions Trophy in a match held at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to learn more about the architectural design of Dubai International Cricket Stadium, also known as the "Ring of Fire." The search led the Desk to a video posted on the stadium's official Instagram page on September 15, 2022. The footage showed the stadium's circular structure, whereas the stadium seen in the viral post had a double-curved, saddle-shaped surface, indicating that the two differed. Below is a combination image highlighting the stark differences. In the subsequent part of the investigation, to identify the stadium featured in the viral video, the Desk ran the above extracted keyframes of the viral video through Google Lens. It came across a video posted by an Instagram handle named Rishad Madhathil on December 23, 2024. The handle had posted a video that matched the settings seen in the viral post but was shot from a different angle. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image, highlighting that the video posted on the Instagram handle matched the visuals seen in the viral post. Further scanning through the video, the Desk noticed that the description mentioned, along with it, stated that it was from Jaber Al-Ahmad International Stadium in Kuwait. It also noted that the video was shot during the 26th Arabian Gulf Cup tournament, held in Kuwait from December 21, 2024, to January 4, 2025. Additionally, taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk conducted a customized keyword search on Google and came across a video posted by Prime Minister Narendra Modi's official YouTube channel on December 21, 2024. The channel posted a video of PM Modi's visit to Jaber Al-Ahmad International Stadium in Kuwait, where he witnessed the opening ceremony of the Gulf Cup. The video also included visuals identical to those seen in the viral post, making it clear that the fireworks display was not from Dubai but from Kuwait. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting that the video posted on the YouTube channel matched the visuals seen in the viral post. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of the dazzling fireworks display inside a stadium was from Kuwait's Jaber Al-Ahmad International Stadium during the 26th Arabian Gulf Cup tournament held in December 2024.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of man being thrashed and hung upside down falsely shared in name of religious hate crimes against Hindus in Bangladesh; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 6 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a man being mercilessly thrashed by an angry mob while hanging upside down from a foot overbridge was recently shared on social media. Users claimed that the incident was the latest in a series of religious hate crimes against Hindus in Bangladesh. The viral post alleged that on February 25, 2025, a Hindu man was brutally attacked by a Muslim mob in Bangladesh. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found this claim false. The incident took place in Uttara, Dhaka, where two individuals, identified as Nazim and Bokul, were beaten and hung upside down from a foot overbridge on charges of robbery. An unrelated video was misleadingly shared on social media with a communal spin. Claim An X user shared on March 4 a video showing a man getting thrashed while being hung upside down from a foot over bridge in Bangladesh. The user claimed that the man, allegedly a Hindu, was subjected to brutal hate crimes by Muslims in Bangladesh. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search result also led the Desk to a video posted on an Instagram handle named 'amarbanglaremati' on February 25, 2025. The video shared by the handle contains visuals from the viral post; however, the description stated that the incident occurred in Dhaka's Uttara neighborhood, where the public caught a person suspected of theft and later hung by his feet on a foot over bridge. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting that the content in the viral video matches that of the video posted on the Instagram handle. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above input, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google. It came across a news report published by The Business Standard, a Bangladesh daily newspaper, on February 25, 2025. The feature image of the report matched one of the keyframes the Desk used for the investigation. However, a careful analysis of the report revealed that the incident involved two persons who were allegedly beaten and hung upside down from a foot over bridge by an angry mob on charges of theft. The report confirmed the identities of the two individuals (said to be injured in the incident) as Bokul (40) and Nazim (35), thus indicating that the incident was in no way related to religious hate crimes against Hindus in Bangladesh, as mentioned in the claim. Moreover, further investigation into the case is underway. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a man being thrashed mercilessly while being hung upside down from a foot overbridge does not link to a religious hate crime against Hindus in Bangladesh. An unrelated video was falsely shared with a communal spin.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Skipper Rohit Sharma's 'no more Australia' quote from 2024 T20 World Cup falsely shared after India's win against Australia in ICC Champions Trophy semi-finals
content: New Delhi, March 6 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a photo of Indian men's cricket captain Rohit Sharma at a press conference following India's victory in the ICC Champions Trophy 2025 semi-finals. The post claimed that when asked about his biggest takeaway from the win against Australia, Sharma took a playful dig at the team, saying the victory meant "there was no more Australian cricket team in the competition." However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found this claim to be false. The viral photo, along with Rohit Sharma's quote, dates back to the 2024 T20 World Cup and is unrelated to the ICC Champions Trophy 2025. The press conference was held before India's semi-final clash against England at the Providence Stadium in Guyana during the 2024 ICC T20 World Cup. Rohit remarked Australia's exit from the tournament when a reporter asked him about his biggest takeaway from their Super 8 match against the Aussies. Claim On March 5, an X (formerly Twitter) user shared a photo of Indian men's cricket captain Rohit Sharma in a press conference after the victory in the ICC Champions Trophy semi-finals. When asked what was his biggest takeaway from the win against Australia, Sharma took a playful dig at Australia and said that the victory meant there was no more Australian cricket team in the competition. The overlying text on the photo read: "What's the biggest takeaway from the win vs Australia? That there is no more Australian cricket team in the competition" "India ends Australia's run! One step closer to glory! 🇮🇳 #ChampionsTrophy #ChampionsTrophy2025 #INDvAUS #RohitSharma #TeamIndia #IndianCricketTeam," the user shared it with this caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through Reverse Image Search and found several other users shared the same post with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , and the archived version can be viewed here and here , respectively. After carefully analysing the viral photo, the Desk noticed that the sponsors' board in the background of the press conference read, "ICC Men's T20 World Cup West Indies & USA 2024." Below is a screenshot highlighting this. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search, found credible reports and came across a video consisting of the entire exchange between the reporter and Sharma uploaded by ICC on their official Instagram, on June 27, 2024. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same, Below is a combination image highlighting the similarity between the viral photo and the report by ICC. Furthermore, the Desk then conducted another set of customised keyword search to find relevant media reports for corroborating details, and came across a report by the sports desk of Times Now, dated June 27, 2024, whose headline read: "There Is No More...: Rohit Sharma's Witty Remark On Australia's Exit From T20 World Cup Goes Viral - Watch" Here is the link to the report. "Indian captain Rohit Sharma did not hide his relief at the Australian cricket team being knocked out of the 2024 T20 World Cup ahead of the Men in Blue's all-important semi-final against England on Thursday (June 27) at the Providence Stadium in Guyana," the report read. Another report was published by The New Indian Express, whose headline read: "Familiar foes stand between India and Champions Trophy final" A portion of the report read: "At that press conference, Sharma was asked about the one big takeaway from the win against Australia. In his typical way, he paused, let out a wry laugh before saying: "That there is no more Australian cricket team in this competition." It led to laughter." Here is the link to the report. The Rohit-led outfit had come into the summit clash unbeaten in the tournament with 10 wins in a row, but could not cross the final hurdle then. India's last global title was the 2013 Champions Trophy, while they have not won the T20 World Cup since their triumph in the inaugural edition under MS Dhoni's captaincy in 2007. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral photo with Rohit Sharma's quote dates back to the 2024 T20 World Cup, not after India's victory over Australia in the 2025 Champions Trophy semi-finals.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Image of bleeding cow in Kota shared with false communal narrative; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 6 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): An image showing a cow in visible distress was recently shared on social media. Users claimed that the injuries seen in the post were the result of an attack allegedly carried out by Muslim jihadis at an illegal shrine in Charanchowki, near Kota's Kaithun police station area. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found this claim false. According to a statement issued by the Kota Rural Police, the cow sustained deep cuts from wires used to fence fields, not from an attack by Muslims. A false claim was misleadingly shared on social media with a communal spin. Claim An X user shared a social media post on March 3 bearing an image of an injured cow. The user claimed that the injuries inflicted upon the animal were the result of an attack allegedly carried out by Muslim 'Jihadis'. "Jihadis sitting at an illegal shrine in Charanchowki, in the Kaithun police station area, attacked a cow with a sharp object. In the absence of strict action against the illegal shrine, the morale of the Jihadis is rising," the user shared the post with the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the above image through Google Lens and came across a social media handle sharing the same post with similar claims. Here is the link and archive link to the post: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk carefully scanned through the comment section of the posts sharing the claims related to the alleged attack on the cow. The search result led the Desk to a response from the Kota Rural Police on their official X handle about the incident, in which they claimed that the cow was hurt due to wires used to fence fields. "There was no evidence of anyone deliberately hurting the cow," the Kota Police added. The police also shared a video showing the wires in the field, which hurt the bovine. Here is the link to the post shared by the Kota Rural Police, along with a screenshot: Additionally, taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk contacted Rajesh Dhaka, DYSP Kota Rural Police, who confirmed that the cow got injured by wires used to fence fields. He stated that even the veterinarian treating the bovine confirmed that the injuries resulted from a wire-like cut. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the injuries reported on the cow occurred as it tried to enter a field covered with wire fencing. A false post was shared on social media with a communal spin.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2021 news bulletin discussing lockdown restrictions in Uttar Pradesh shared with false as recent announcement
content: New Delhi, March 7 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported video clip of a news bulletin wherein the anchor discussed the lockdown restrictions was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that lockdown will be imposed in Uttar Pradesh from March 4, 2025. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral video dates back to 2021, when lockdown restrictions were imposed in Uttar Pradesh for a week due to COVID-19. A false claim was shared on social media. Claim On February 21, a YouTube user shared a purported clip of a news bulletin claiming that Uttar Pradesh would be on lockdown for a week starting March 4, 2025. The text written on the video read: "Lockdown will start from March 4, share this clip as much as possible so that people can buy all necessary items on time" Meanwhile, the news bulletin presenter can be heard saying, "Let us tell you that if you live in Uttar Pradesh, what will be open and what will not be open…" Here is the link and archive link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the same video with similar claims. One such post can be found here , along with its archived versions, which can be viewed here . At first, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find relevant information corroborating the claims made in the viral post. However, it did not yield credible reports or official announcements about any upcoming lockdown in Uttar Pradesh. Further, if such a major decision had been made, mainstream news media would have covered it widely.
