Continuing the investigation, the Desk ran the keyframes through Google Lens and found an extended version of the clip uploaded on Republic Bharat's official YouTube channel on April 17, 2021. The report's title read: "UP is 'locked'! Watch Ye Bharat Ki Baat Hai with Syed Suhail." At the 1:54-second time stamp, the anchor can be heard saying the same details as given in the viral video circulated on social media. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the news report. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports and came across reports published by leading media houses. NDTV carried one such PTI report on April 29, 2021. The title of the report read: "UP Weekend Lockdown To Cover Mondays Too, Now Friday 8 pm To Tuesday 7 am" "Amid a surge in COVID-19 cases, the Uttar Pradesh government today decided to increase the duration of weekend lockdown by 24 hours, announcing that it will now cover Mondays too," the report read. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Indian Express published another report on April 20, 2021, whose headline read: "UP: Weekend lockdown extended in districts with over 2,000 cases; night curfew continues" "According to the new order, districts with over 500 active Covid cases will continue to remain under night curfew, effective between 8 pm to 7 am every day," mentioned the report. Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to 2021, when lockdown was imposed in Uttar Pradesh due to COVID-19.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated photo of Pak Army Chief and PM Modi shared as accurate with false claim
content: New Delhi, March 7 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported photo of Pakistan Army chief Asim Munir and Prime Minister Narendra Modi was recently shared on social media. Users sharing it claimed that the Pakistan Army chief gifted PM Modi Kashmir's map. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral photo is AI generated, which is being shared as accurate with a false claim Claim On February 27, an X (formerly Twitter) user going by the name 'Bilal AI' shared a picture of Pakistan Army chief Asim Munir and PM Modi, claiming that the former allegedly gifted Kashmir's map to the Prime Minister. The post's caption, which garnered 13.7k views, read: "Indian administered Kashmir. Asim Munir presents Kashmir map as a gift to Narendra Modi" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through a Reverse Image Search and found several other users shared the same photo with a similar claim. One such post can be found here and its archived version can be viewed here . Initially, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant data to corroborate the details and found no such report or announcement citing the incident. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk scanned the X handle of 'Bilal AI' and found that the bio stated that it posts AI content, satire, and memes. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk carefully analysed the picture and found several discrepancies suggesting that they were digitally altered or AI-generated. For instance, the background in the image and the distorted text on the Army Chief's uniform were blurred. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. To advance the investigation, the Desk ran the images one by one through Hive Moderation, an AI detection tool that suggests a substantial presence of AI-generated or deepfake content. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. The Desk ran the image through Sight Engine (an AI detection tool), which suggested a substantial presence of AI content. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral post allegedly showing Pakistan Army chief Asim Munir and PM Modi is AI-generated.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Photo collage of Rohit Sharma's daughter from her toddler days falsely shared as the first look of his newborn son; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 7 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A photo collage featuring Indian cricketer Rohit Sharma, his wife Ritika Sajdeh, and a young child was recently shared on social media. Users claimed that the child in the photo collage was Sharma's newborn son, Ahaan. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found this claim to be false. The viral collage, which contains multiple images of Rohit Sharma's family, actually dates back to July 2019. It originally featured his daughter, Samaira, from her toddler days, not their son Ahaan, who was born on November 15, 2024. An old photo collage was misleadingly shared on social media with a false claim. Claim On March 6, a Facebook user going by the name 'Cricket Duniya' shared a collage containing multiple images of Indian cricketer Rohit Sharma, his wife Ritika Sajdeh, and a young child. The user claimed that the child seen in the images is Rohit Sharma's newly born son, Ahaan. "Fans were shocked to see the first look of junior hitman Ahaan. It was a pleasant feeling to see Rohit Sharma and Ritika Sajdeh's son openly at Dubai International Cricket Stadium for the first time," the user shared the post with the caption. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral collage of images through Google Lens and found that multiple users had shared the same post with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . The search results also led the Desk to a news report published by Zee News on July 7, 2019. The report's feature image matched the images seen in the collage; however, it stated that the images were over five years old, and the child seen in the image alongside Rohit Sharma's wife, Ritika Sajdeh, was their daughter, Samaira (born in 2018). Significantly, the report also added that Sharma shared the images of the two (his wife and daughter) during India's last league match in the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup against Sri Lanka at Headingley Cricket Ground in 2019. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting that the images seen in the collage were the same as those shared in the Zee News report dated July 7, 2019. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google. It came across a post shared by Rohit Sharma's official X handle. The post contained the same images of Rohit Sharma's wife, Ritika Sajdeh, seen alongside their daughter, Samaira, from July 7, 2019. Sharma shared the post with the caption. "Nothing can beat this, when your loved ones are up there in the stands rooting for you with fingers crossed." Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the collage bearing images of Rohit Sharma's family dated back to July 2019 and featured his daughter, Samaira, from her toddler days.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated photo of Virat Kohli with Anushka Sharma shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, March 7 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Social media has been abuzz following India's victory over Australia in the ICC Champions Trophy 2025 semi-final. In the aftermath, several social media users shared a collage of two pictures featuring Indian cricketer Virat Kohli and his wife, actress Anushka Sharma, claiming that the couple was seen hugging after India's victory. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigation found that the viral images were AI-generated and falsely shared on social media as real. Claim On March 5, a Facebook user shared a collage of two pictures featuring cricketer Virat Kohli along with his wife, actress Anushka Sharma. The user claimed that the two were seen hugging each other after India's victory against Australia. "Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma were seen hugging after winning the match against Australia," the post was shared with this caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through the Reverse Image Search and found several other users shared the same photo with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be found here and here , respectively. The Desk initially conducted a customised keyword search to verify if Anushka Sharma attended the semi-finals match against Australia. The Desk came across several reports published featuring the two, but the difference was that Sharma's attire was not the same as seen in the viral images. Here is a l ink to a report by India Today, dated March 5, 2025, whose headline read: "Watch: Virat Kohli fist pumps in joy as Anushka Sharma cheers for him" Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk carefully scanned the two viral photos and found several discrepancies suggesting that they were AI-generated or digitally altered. For instance, the facial features of both of them in the first picture looked distorted, the background in both pictures was different and blurred, and the picture looked extra glossy. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk ran both images through Hive Moderation (an AI detection tool), which suggested a substantial presence of AI content. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral photo was AI-generated.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 9-yr-old video of Delhi Traffic cops being attacked falsely shared as recent incident from Udaipur; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 8 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media, with users claiming it showed a group of Muslim men brutally thrashing two traffic police constables. The post alleged that the incident took place at Paras Circle in Udaipur, where an angry Muslim mob assaulted two on-duty traffic police officers following a dispute over the issuance of a challan. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found this claim to be false. The viral video captures an incident from 2015 in Delhi's Gokulpuri area, not Udaipur. At the time, two traffic police constables were attacked by a man named Shahnawaz and his family after the police issued a challan to him and his younger brother for not wearing helmets. An old video was misleadingly shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An X user with the name 'Anuradha Mishra' shared a video on March 5 showing a group of Muslim men thrashing two on-duty traffic police constables. The user claimed that the incident allegedly occurred near Paras Circle in Udaipur, where the mob attacked the constables following an altercation over issuing a challan. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through InVid and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. The search results also led the Desk to a video published by the official YouTube channel of ABP News. The video contained visuals from the viral post; however, the details confirmed that the incident took place in Delhi and dated back to 2015. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting the visuals seen in the viral post, matched with those of the video posted by the channel. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google. It came across a news report published by Deccan Herald on July 14, 2015. The report elaborately detailed the incident, in which a group of Muslim men attacked two police constables over the issuance of a challan. According to the report, over 15 men in Delhi's Gokulpuri area attacked traffic police constables Sanjay and Manoj after they had issued a challan to a bike-borne duo identified as Shahnawaz and his younger brother Amir for not wearing helmets or carrying a driving license. "As the police issued a challan to them, the duo refused to pay and heatedly argued with them. After a while, Shahnawaz and Amir left without paying the challan. It is alleged that Shahnawaz and Amir returned to the spot after 10 minutes with their father, Sagir Ahmed, and around a dozen men. They overpowered Sanjay and Manoj and allegedly bragged about their clout in the area," the report added. Here is the link to the report: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a few Muslim men attacking traffic police constables was from Delhi in 2015 and was falsely shared as a recent incident that occurred in Udaipur.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Edited video of Cricketer Mohammed Shami falsely shared claiming he apologised for not observing Roza during Ramadan; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 9 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid the ongoing controversy over fasting, a video of Indian pacer Mohammed Shami wearing a skull cap and kurta, allegedly apologising for not observing Roza during Ramadan, has been circulating on social media. Additionally, a photo of him consuming an energy drink was superimposed over the alleged video. Those sharing the content claimed that Shami was forced to break his Roza during a Champions Trophy match. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found this claim to be false. The viral video actually dates back to April 2024, when Shami extended Eid greetings. Meanwhile, the photo is from India's Champions Trophy semi-final match against Australia in Dubai on March 5, 2025. Claim On March 7, a Facebook user shared a video of Indian pacer Mohammed Shami allegedly apologising for not observing fast during Ramadan. The video also included a picture of him consuming an energy drink. In the video, Shami can be heard saying, "Yes, I broke Roza that day. Muslim brothers and sisters, please do not misunderstand me. I did not do it on purpose. I was forced to break Roza; otherwise, they would have destroyed my career. I apologise to my Muslim brothers and sisters again." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , along with their archived versions, which can be viewed here and here . To verify the claim, we first carefully watched the entire video and found a discrepancy in the lip movement indicating that this video was edited. The Desk ran the keyframes of the video through Google Lens and came across Shami's official Instagram account where he had shared multiple photos wearing the same attire as seen in the viral video. The post shared on April 11, 2024, read: "Eid Mubarak. Eid Mubarak to all my dear friends and family! May this special day be filled with joy, love, and blessings for you and your loved ones. Wishing you all peace, happiness, and prosperity on this joyous occasion." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Further scanning his Instagram account, we found the original video of Shami wearing the same kurta and skull cap. In the original video, the cricketer was extending his wishes for Eid. The post, shared on April 11, 2024, read: "May the magic of Eid bring never-ending happiness, peace, and prosperity to your life. Eid Mubarak!" Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral and original videos shared on Shami's social media. Meanwhile, Shami was criticised for failing to fast during India's Champions Trophy semifinal match versus Australia. Shami was seen on camera consuming an energy drink during the March 5 match in Dubai, sparking a scandal. Following this, Shami's cousin Mumtaz defended him against criticism for not observing roza. A report was published by Times Now, dated March 6, 2025, whose headline read: "Many Pakistan Players...: Cousin, Coach Defend Mohammed Shami Over 'Criminal' Accusation" The report section read: "He is playing for the country. There are many Pakistani players who have not kept 'Roza' and are playing matches, so this is nothing new. It is very shameful that such things are being said about him. We will tell Mohammed Shami not to pay attention to these things and prepare for the match on March 9," Dr. Mumtaz said" Here is the link to the report. Furthermore, the Desk found no official announcement or statement from the cricketer regarding the controversy. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was edited and shared with a false claim. The original video dates back to 2024 when Shami extended wishes for Eid and is unrelated to the ongoing controversy.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Did India-Pak cricketers mourn death of Kohli's father during Champions Trophy match? Claim in video shared on social media is absolutely false
content: New Delhi, March 10 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media, with users claiming it showed Indian and Pakistani cricket team players mourning the death of Virat Kohli's father, Prem Nath Kohli, as soon as the news broke to them during the recent Champions Trophy match. The video began with India opener Rohit Sharma having a brief conversation with Pakistan cricket team captain Babar Azam, followed by a scene where Indian players kneeled on the ground. In contrast, Pakistani players stand with their hands on their chests. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found this claim to be false. The video was actually from the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2021, where both teams (India vs. Pakistan) showed support for the 'Black Lives Matter' movement before the match commenced. In the footage, the Indian team kneeled to express solidarity, while the Pakistani team placed their hands on their chests as part of the gesture. An old and unrelated video was misleadingly shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user going by the name 'Amrish M A Raj' shared a video on March 4, claiming it showed Indian and Pakistani cricket team players observing a minute of silence during a live match after hearing about the passing of Virat Kohli's father, 'Prem Nath Kohli.' The video showed Indian team players kneeling on the ground, while the Pakistani team players stood with their hands on their chests. Since being posted, the video has received 15 million views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool search and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found various users shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. The search results also led the Desk to a report published by India Times on October 25, 2021. The report includes images of Indian and Pakistani cricketers (as also seen in the keyframes the Desk used for investigation) extending support to the Black Lives Matter movement during the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2021. It showed Indian cricketers kneeling on the ground. At the same time, Pakistani players kept their hands near their chests to support the movement against racism, which was started in the United States after the death of 46-year-old African American George Floyd in the year 2020. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting that the content seen in the viral video matched that of the images used in the India Times report. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customized keyword search on Google and came across a report by the Times of India. The report, published on September 19, 2024, elaborated on the circumstances surrounding the death of Virat Kohli's father, Prem Nath Kohli, in 2006. The report revealed that Virat Kohli's father died in December 2006, when Virat was just 18 years old. "In a 2006 Ranji Trophy match, batting maestro Virat Kohli demonstrated remarkable commitment by playing for Delhi against Karnataka despite losing his father. At 18 years old, he returned to the field the next day and scored an essential 90 runs, helping his team recover from a tough spot," the report added. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing the Indian and Pakistani cricket teams mourning the death of Virat Kohli's father by observing a minute of silence during a live match was false.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Police parading cow smugglers in Ujjain falsely shared as incident from Delhi; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 10 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of police personnel thrashing and parading two men was shared on social media, with users claiming that the incident happened in Delhi where Delhi Police took action against the two accused allegedly involved in cow smuggling. However, the PTI Fact Check investigated and found that the viral video shared in the social media post contained a false claim. The incident in the video happened in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh. It had nothing to do with Delhi or Delhi Police. Claim On March 4, an X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video of police personnel thrashing two men, claiming that Delhi Police took action against them as the two were allegedly involved in cow slaughter. In the 1:06-second video, the two men can be heard saying, "Gau hamari maa hai, police hamare baap hain" (Cow is our mother, police are our father). The post's caption, which garnered 441K views, originally in Hindi, read: "Ever since the Delhi Police. Since then we have received instructions from Amit Shah ji. Delhi Police is in full force at this time. Cow killers are raising slogans...Cow is our mother, police is our father... Brutality in the name of Mewat will no longer be tolerated" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , along with their archived versions, which can be viewed here and here . On further analysing the search results, the Desk came across a video uploaded on the official channel of Punjab Kesari MP on March 3, 2025, whose title read: "Cow is our mother and police is our father…'A procession of cow slaughterers and sellers was taken out in Ujjain, they were seen limping" In the video the two men can be heard saying: "Gau hamari maa hai, police hamare baap hain" (Cow is our mother, police are our father). Moreover, at the top left corner of the video 'Ujjain' was mentioned, which confirms that the incident happened in Madhya Pradesh and not. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the news report. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find relevant media reports and the search results led us to a report by ABP News, dated March 3, 2025, whose headline read: "'Cow is our mother and police is our father', a procession of goons took place in CM Mohan Yadav's city" According to the report, a procession was taken out in Ghatiya after the accused were arrested. During this, they also raised slogans like 'Police is our father'. When the procession of both accused was taken out, a huge crowd gathered there. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. The report's cover image was similar to the visuals in the viral video, which further confirms that the video is from Ujjain and not Delhi. Taking the investigation ahead, the Desk scanned the official handles of the Madhya Pradesh Police to find official statements regarding the entire matter. We found an X post by Ujjain SP featuring an image of the two accused and a statement from police officer Nitesh Bhargava. In the video, the SP says: "On 16 February 2025, Ghatiya police received information about cattle found near a Swift Dzire with some suspects nearby. The police seized the cattle and the vehicle, and the accused involved in cow smuggling have now been arrested…" Here is the link to the X post, and below is a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video of police thrashing and parading two men accused of cow smuggling is from Madhya Pradesh's Ujjain and is unrelated to Delhi.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2015 video of anti-crime drive by Indore Police falsely shared in name of Uttar Pradesh; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 10 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of police officers thrashing a group of people was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that the incident took place in Uttar Pradesh after the individuals were accused of molesting women. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found this claim to be false. The viral video actually dates back to 2015 and shows an anti-crime drive conducted by Indore Police. It is not related to Uttar Pradesh and was misleadingly shared with a false claim. Claim On March 6, an X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video of police officers thrashing a few people, claiming that the incident happened in Uttar Pradesh as they were accused of molesting women. The caption of the post, which garnered 524.4k views, originally in Hindi, read: "How costly can it be to tease girls coming and going in Uttar Pradesh. Our ancestors will also remember these goons. Everybody has daughters and sisters, Babaji is treating them properly." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , along with its archived versions, which can be viewed here and here, respectively. To verify the claim, the Desk further scanned the search results and came across a video report by ABP News uploaded on their official YouTube channel on May 29, 2015. The title of the report read: "Indore police beats criminals publicly on roads" Similar visuals as seen in the viral video can be seen at the 00:26 seconds timestamp in the video. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the video published by ABP News. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across another video report by IndiaTV, dated May 29, 2015, whose title read: "Indore: Police Thrash and Parade Local Criminals - India TV" Here is the link to the report. The Desk then conducted another set of customised keyword searches to find relevant media reports and came across a report by Hindustan Times dated May 7, 2015, whose headline read: "Citizens bear the brunt of police drive against 'goondas' in Indore" The report mentioned: "Around 1700 anti-social elements have been held or rounded-up in the last one week and the numbers are increasing every day. Around 1700 anti-social elements have been held or rounded-up in the last one week and the numbers are increasing every day." Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to 2015, when it was created as part of an anti-crime drive conducted by Indore Police, not Uttar Pradesh.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video falsely shared on social media claiming metro accident happened in Gurugram; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 10 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of a derailed metro train caused by the caving-in of the rail track, claiming that the incident took place in Gurugram. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found this claim to be false. The viral video was AI-generated and falsely shared as a real incident from Gurugram. The claim shared in the social media post was imaginary and false. Claim On March 6, a Facebook user going by the name Sayed Ali Bhai shared a video of a derailed metro train caused by the rail track caving in, claiming that the incident happened in Gurugram. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . To verify the claim, we first conducted a customised keyword search to find relevant data. However, the search did not result in any authentic data or report to corroborate the viral claim. Notably, such an incident would have become important and garnered a lot of attention. Further, the Desk checked the comment section of the viral video and found that several social media users commented that it was fake AI-generated. Below is a screenshot of two such comments. Taking cue from this, the Desk carefully analysed the video and saw several discrepancies. For instance, the metro did not have Delhi Metro's logo. Further, the people seen on the track and the station appeared to be disfigured, which highlighted that the video could be AI-generated. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk ran the keyframe of the video through WasitAI(an AI detection tool), which suggested a substantial presence of AI content. Below is a screenshot of the result: Further, the Desk also ran the image through SighEngine, another AI detection tool, which confirmed a significant presence of AI-generated content. Below is a screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video is AI-generated, no such incident in Gurugram.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video claiming woman forgot her child in park while talking on phone was still from film shoot; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 10 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media, with users claiming it depicted a real-life incident where a mother 'forgot' her child in a park while talking on the phone. The footage showed a man holding a child in his arms, repeatedly calling out to a woman walking ahead of him. The video suggests that the woman was supposedly the child's mother, who left the baby behind as she was too engrossed in her phone conversation. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found this claim to be false. The video is part of a film shoot. The Desk contacted senior actor Sharad Sharma, who appeared in the film, and he confirmed that the video was a part of a movie shoot. An old video was misleadingly shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An Instagram page named "Mint News" shared a video on March 8, claiming to show a real-life incident where a woman forgot her child in a park while talking on the phone. The video showed a man holding a child and continuously calling out to the woman from behind. However, after a brief moment, the woman realised what had happened and took the child back from the man. At the time of posting this article, the video has garnered 2,79,668 likes. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found various users shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the video and found multiple indicators suggesting it was part of a film shoot. For instance, at the 0:07 second timestamp, a crowd can be seen gathered at the spot, standing still and recording the entire conversation between the man and the woman on the phone. A tripod-like object was also spotted near the site, suggesting the video was perhaps a scene from a film/ad shoot. Below is a screenshot from the video highlighting the key findings: Moreover, as a part of the investigation, scanning through the viral post, the Desk also came across a comment posted by a user who identified the person in the video as an actor named Sharad Sharma. Below is a screenshot of one such comment: In the subsequent part of the investigation, taking cues from the above generated inputs, the Desk contacted the senior actor, who confirmed that the video was part of a short film shoot. He stated, "This is a video from a short film titled 'Hello Mobile,' shot back in 2019. The movie was filmed in Nashik, where, during the shoot, one of the onlookers recorded it and later shared it on social media." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of a woman forgetting her child in a park while talking on the phone was scripted and part of a short film shoot.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Scripted video of saffron-clad man being forced out of iftar party shared as real incident
content: New Delhi, March 11 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a man dressed in saffron attire attending an iftar party has been widely shared on social media, with claims that he was beaten and thrown out by a Muslim man. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the footage and found that the viral video was misleadingly shared with false claims. The video is entirely scripted and staged, bearing no connection to real events. Claim On March 7, an Instagram user, named Vajinder Sharma, shared a video of a few people sitting and having a meal together- featuring a man wearing saffron clothes while the others wore a white kurta with a skull cap, claiming that it was from an iftar party where a Hindu man (seen in saffron clothing) was allegedly beaten and thrown out of the iftar party. The caption of the post read: "And go eat free Iftari…Beat the bastard and then make halala of it all together" Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a more extended version of the viral video uploaded by a user named Prank Buzz. The 7:06-second video was titled "When a Hindu Sanyasi goes to a Muslim's Masjid for Iftar? Hindu vs. Muslim Social Experiment." The title indicates that the video does not depict the incident but was part of a social experiment. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a screenshot highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the video uploaded on YouTube. The disclaimer mentioned that the video is intended for entertainment, adding that viewers' discretion is advised. "The following video is intended for entertainment purposes only. The views and opinions expressed in this video are those of the individuals featured, and do not necessarily reflect the views and opinions of the video's creator, producer, or distributor. Some content in this video may be considered inappropriate for certain audiences, including but not limited to graphic or explicit language, violence, or adult themes. Viewer discretion is advised," it read. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk analysed the Prank Buzz YouTube channel, which revealed that it regularly posts entertainment and prank videos. The About section describes the channel as "Hey Guys, We are PrankBuzz. Here you can enjoy unlimited entertainment with our trust and quality." Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. On further scanning the entire YouTube channel we found multiple videos featuring the same actor who played the Hindu sanyasi in the viral video. The channel frequently uploads staged prank videos on the channel. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video featuring a Hindu man beaten and thrown out from an iftar party is scripted and not an actual incident.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of passengers arguing with airline staff falsely linked to Air India's March 5 lavatory failure incident
content: New Delhi, March 11 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing dozens of passengers arguing with an airline staff member was recently shared on social media. The video claims to have been filmed inside a Delhi-bound Air India flight, which was forced to return to its departure airport (Chicago) on March 5 after most of its onboard lavatories became clogged. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the footage and found that the viral video dates back to January 6. It captures passengers inside an Air India flight from London arguing with staff after being informed that their flight had been canceled, despite waiting inside the aircraft for seven hours. The old and unrelated video was falsely shared on social media during the recent March 5 incident. Claim An 'X' user named 'Dom Lucre' shared a video on March 10, seemingly showing dozens of passengers inside an Air India flight from Chicago to Delhi arguing with airline staff members after the flight was forced to turn back to its departure airport on March 5 due to clogged toilets. "An Air India flight was forced to return on a 10-hour trip to Chicago, Illinois because their toilets were clogged, leaving hundreds of Indians trapped on a plane with no restroom," users shared the video with this caption. When writing this article, the post had garnered 18.5 million views and 47,000 likes. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found various users shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google but could not find visuals matching those in the viral video linked to the lavatory inmalfunction incident ivolving the Air India flight. However, the search led the Desk to a recent report published by The Indian Express on March 11, which confirmed that the Air India flight from Chicago to Delhi returned to its origin airport due to clogged toilets on March 5, 2025. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: In the subsequent part of the investigation, to verify the timeline of the viral video, the Desk ran the above extracted keyframes through Google Lens again. The search led to a video posted on an Instagram page belonging to the Turkey-based TV show Londra Aktuel. The handle posted the same video as the viral post. Still, the details in the caption indicated that the footage dated back to January 6—predating the March 5 incident involving the Air India flight. The video was shared with the caption: "Air India passengers who waited seven hours on the plane at Gatwick, London, reacted when they learned that the flight was canceled." Here are the link and the archive link to the video, along with a screenshot: Below is a composite image highlighting how the content in the viral video matches that of the video posted by the Instagram handle on January 6, 2025. Additionally, while the Desk could not independently verify further details about the viral video showing the argument between passengers on an Air India flight from London, we can confirm that it was on the internet for at least two months before the widely reported March 5, 2025, lavatory incident. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video showing passengers arguing with airline staff was unrelated to the March 5, 2025, incident and depicted an event from January 6, 2025.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2019 video of Pawan Kalyan at Jana Sena party candidates's residence shared falsely claiming he attended Iftar party recently
content: New Delhi, March 11 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of Jana Sena Party founder and Andhra Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan wearing a white cap, claiming that he attended an Iftar party during the ongoing Ramadan. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found it false. A search revealed that the viral video actually dates back to 2019, when Kalyan had a meal at the residence of a Jana Sena candidate as part of his election campaign in Guntur. The video is unrelated to any Iftar gathering during Ramadan 2025. Claim On March 9, an X (formerly Twitter) user, named Sandip Luharuwalla, shared a video of Jana Sena Party founder and Andhra Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan in Muslim attire, claiming that he attended an Iftar party during the ongoing Ramadan. The post's caption, originally in Hindi, read: "The protector of Sanatan Dharma of devotees. New Abba Pawan Kalyan ji is in a new form, enjoying Iftar dishes of Muslim brothers in Ramadan and wearing a cap. Chilly in the backyard for sure. Retweets should not stop for Sanatan awareness" Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . To verify the claim, the Desk initially conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find corroborating details. We found a website named Hans India, featuring the same image along with several other images from the same day. The title read: "Pawan Kalyan enjoys Quran, biryani during election campaign in Guntur," uploaded on March 25, 2019. This makes it clear that the video is not recent. Here is the link , and below is a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the pictures uploaded on the website. Taking the investigation forward, the Desk conducted another set of customised keyword searches to see if the incident was reported by Pawan Kalyan or the JanaSena Party. Upon searching, we found a post on JanaSena Party's official Facebook post dated March 25, 2019. The caption mentioned that Pawan Kalyan visited Sheikh Zia ur Rehman's residence as part of a Guntur district tour. The post featured the same images as seen in the viral video. "As part of Guntur district tour, Janasena president Sri Pawan Kalyan garu visited the house of Shri Sheikh Zia ur Rehman contesting as Janasena candidate from Guntur East constituency," the post was shared with this caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Notably, Ramadan in 2019 was observed between May and June, whereas the incident occurred in March 2019, indicating no connection with Ramadan or iftar. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to 2019 when Pawan Kalyan had his meal at the residence of a Jana Sena candidate, and is not related to the recent Iftar gathering during Ramadan 2025.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of Afghan people celebrating Afghanistan's victory against England falsely linked to India's win in Champions Trophy 2025 final
content: New Delhi, March 12 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a large crowd celebrating on the streets was recently shared on social media. Users claimed it depicted people in Afghanistan rejoicing over India's victory against New Zealand in the ICC Champions Trophy 2025 final on March 9 in Dubai. The video shows people dancing, bursting crackers, and celebrating. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found that the video was old and shared with a false context. The footage actually predates the Champions Trophy final and captures celebrations following Afghanistan's victory over England. Claim On March 10, an X (formerly Twitter) user, named Amrendra Bahubali, shared a video of a large group of people taking to the streets, claiming that it showed people from Afghanistan celebrating India's triumph at the ICC Champion's Trophy 2025. The post's caption, originally in Hindi, read: "There were loud celebrations in Afghanistan after India won the Champions Trophy. Only Afghanistan was with India in the entire Champion Trophy. I respect them all from my heart. Hindustani and Afghani are brothers". The post garnered 177.2k views so far. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found various users shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . To verify the claim, the desk carefully watched the video and found a watermark at the bottom that mentioned 'zekria_zeer' with an Instagram logo. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk looked up the Instagram account, which confirmed him to be a video creator from Afghanistan. On the Instagram account, we found the video uploaded by the user on February 27, 2025, which predates the Champions Trophy Final. Moreover, according to the caption, it celebrates Afghanistan's victory over England in the Champions Trophy match. The caption shared with the post read:" A historic win for Afghanistan. Their first-ever victory in Champions Trophy history will be forever remembered in the cricket record books." Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the Instagram post. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk took a closer look at the video and found 'Afghanistan' and 'England' written on the TV screen in one of the clips. The date in the time clock also mentioned '26.2'. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. The Desk could not independently verify other details of the video. However, it predates India's win in the 2025 Champions Trophy. Notably, the match between Afghanistan and England was held on February 25, while the finals of the Champions Trophy were held on March 9 between India and New Zealand. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video predates the Champions Trophy finals and actually shows celebrations after Afghanistan's victory over England.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video showing PM Modi wearing white skull cap shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, March 11 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media claimed to show Prime Minister Narendra Modi wearing a white skull cap and holding a religious prayer during the month of Ramadan. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigation found the video fake. The AI-generated video was shared on social media as real with a false claim. Claim An Instagram user going by the name 'Danish Rana' shared a video on March 7 that allegedly showed Prime Minister Narendra Modi wearing a skull cap and performing a religious prayer during the month of Ramadan. The video (which, when posting this article, had received 47,873 likes) also appeared to show the Prime Minister reciting a prayer. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that various users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the viral video and found multiple indicators suggesting the footage was AI-generated. For instance, the background in the video appeared visibly blurred, and the beard added to the person (purportedly PM Modi) seen in the third frame appeared forcefully added. Further, other significant details related to the person's physical appearance in the viral video differed across all three frames. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Next, taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk ran the viral video through 'Hive Moderation,' an AI detection tool suggesting a substantial presence of AI-generated or deepfake content. Below is a screenshot highlighting the result. Additionally, the Desk separately ran the keyframes generated from the video above through 'Was It AI,' another AI detection tool, which also confirmed that a significant part of them was created by AI. Below is a screenshot highlighting the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing Prime Minister Narendra Modi wearing a skull cap and performing a religious prayer was AI-generated.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Edited video of Burj Khalifa falsely claimed to show Team India's photos after Champions Trophy 2025 victory
content: New Delhi, March 12 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): After Team India won the Champions Trophy 2025 by defeating New Zealand in the final at Dubai International Stadium on March 9, several social media users shared a video of Dubai's iconic Burj Khalifa displaying photos of the winning team, the Indian Tricolour, skipper Rohit Sharma, and the Champions Trophy. The users claimed the images were projected on the skyscraper to celebrate India's victory. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found it to be false. The viral video was edited and misleadingly shared on social media with a false claim. Claim On March 10, an X (formerly Twitter) user, Satya Swar, shared a video of the Burj Khalifa displaying the Indian Flag, Skipper Rohit Sharma, and the Champions Trophy, claiming that it was a tribute to Team India after their victory in the Champions Trophy 2025 Finals. The post's caption, originally in Hindi, read: "Sharmaji's son...He is the one who is famous everywhere...it is his name!! Burj Khalifa also has pride." Here is the link and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found various users shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . To verify the claim, the Desk initially conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant reports corroborating the details, but the search did not yield any authentic data or articles. In the next part of the investigation, we carefully analysed the viral video and found a watermark mentioning 'Ahmed _Raza_Indori'. Taking a cue from this, we scanned the user's social media accounts and came across his Instagram profile where a similar video was posted on March 9, 2025. Here is the video link and a screenshot of the same. Additionally, we found similar edited videos posted by Ahmed Raja, featuring cricketers like Mohammed Shami, Hardik Pandya, and Virat Kohli on the Burj Khalifa. Also, the user's Bio section mentioned 'Only Editor'. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Continuing our investigation, we checked the official Instagram account and found no video featuring a tribute to the Indian team. The last video posted on the account was in March, marking the beginning of Ramadan. Here is the link to the account. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video had been edited, and no video of the Indian Flag, Rohit Sharma, and the Champions Trophy was displayed.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of Nepal Police thrashing Buddhist monk falsely shared as recent incident from Bihar; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 12 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing police personnel thrashing a Buddhist monk on the street was recently shared on social media, falsely linking the incident to the ongoing protest in Bihar's Bodh Gaya, where Buddhist monks are on an indefinite hunger strike against Brahmin control over the Mahabodhi Temple. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found that the video was unrelated to the recent protest in Bodh Gaya. The footage actually captured clashes between Nepal Police and members of the National Liberation Movement in April 2024, during which police misbehaved with a monk while attempting to control the situation. An old and unrelated video was misleadingly shared with a false claim. Meanwhile, it is essential to note that protests have indeed erupted in Bodh Gaya (February 2025), where Buddhist monks, activists, and organisations are demanding full control of the Mahabodhi Temple. A joint Hindu-Buddhist committee under the Bodh Gaya Temple Act of 1949 currently manages the temple. Protesters are calling for the repeal of the 1949 law and for complete Buddhist control over the temple's management. Claim An Instagram user with the name 'baba_sahab_ka_beta_mp_13' shared a video on March 9, showing police personnel kicking a Buddhist monk on the road. Users claimed that the video was linked to the recent protest in Bihar's Bodh Gaya, where Buddhist monks are on an indefinite hunger strike, challenging Brahmin control over the Mahabodhi Temple. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that various users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. The search results also led the Desk to a video posted on an Instagram handle named 'we_lovenepal.' The video posted by this handle includes visuals from the viral post. However, it stated that the video (published on April 7, 2024) was from an incident in Nepal. "Nepal Police kicked the monk," the post caption read. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting that the content in the viral video matches that of the video posted by the Instagram handle. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to gather more details about the incident in Nepal, where the police mistreated Buddhist monks. The search results led the Desk to a report published by a Nepalese daily named Nepal Press, which reported Nepal Police's ill-treatment of two Buddhist monks during a protest in Bhadrakali, Kathmandu. The report, mentioning the timeline of the incident in April 2024—(predating the Bodh Gaya protest that started in Bihar in February 2025)—also stated that after the video of the incident went viral, departmental action was initiated against the police personnel who mistreated the monks. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing police kicking a Buddhist monk was falsely shared as an incident from Bihar's Bodh Gaya.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Raj
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of teacher beating a student from Tunisia falsely shared as incident from India
content: New Delhi, March 12 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Raj, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a student being brutally thrashed inside a classroom, allegedly by his teacher, was recently shared on social media with claims that the incident occurred in India. Users tagging the Uttar Pradesh Police urged authorities to identify the location of the incident. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found it misleading. According to media reports, the incident actually took place in Tunisia in 2021. An old and unrelated video was falsely circulated on social media as a recent incident from India. Claim An X user named Pritam Kumar Bauddh shared a video on March 5, allegedly showing a student being brutally thrashed by his teacher inside a classroom. The user insinuated that the incident occurred somewhere in India and approached the Uttar Pradesh Police to find out more details about it. After posting this article, the video gained over 589K views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively: The search also led the Desk to a report published by a website named Business News on November 25, 2021. The feature image of the report matched the settings seen in the viral video. However, it stated that the incident occurred at a primary school located in the Taffala district of the Sousse governorate in Tunisia. According to the report, a young student filmed the video after repeatedly complaining to his family about the teacher's violent behavior. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: A comparison image highlights that the visuals in the viral video match those in the report's feature image. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found a report by the Tunisian daily Tunisnow. The report contained the same video seen in the viral post and confirmed that the incident occurred in Tunisia's Sousse city on November 25, 2021. Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of the teacher thrashing a student was filmed at a local school in Tunisia in 2021.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of fight between two rival gangs shared with a false narrative of caste rivalry angle in Uttar Pradesh; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 12 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a group of people brutally thrashing a boy was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that members of the Yadav community had attacked a boy from the Dalit community. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found it false. Further verification revealed that the individuals involved belonged to rival gangs, and the fight stemmed from an old enmity between them. The video was misleadingly shared with a false narrative of caste rivalry. Claim On March 10, an X (formerly Twitter) user, going by the name Dr Ashish Kumar, shared a video of a group of people thrashing a boy, claiming that the group of people belonged to the Yadav community and the boy being beaten was from the Dalit community. The overlying text on the video, originally in Hindi, read: "In Meerut, people of Yadav community are brutally beating a boy from Dalit community. I appeal to the government to have these people caught and arrested immediately. Jai Bhim, Jai Constitution, Jai Bharat." Here is the link , and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation They ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found various users shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . To verify the claim, the Desk initially conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant news reports. It came across several reports that featured screenshots of the viral video. One such report was published by Dainik Bhaskar, whose headline read: "Youth beaten up in Meerut: Lodhi gang caught a member of Fatte gang in Bajot forest" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the video featured in the news report. Another report by The Fress Press Journal, dated March 10, mentioned that a youth named Vinay Jatav was kidnapped at gunpoint and brutally assaulted in the jungle of Bajaut village. The attackers mercilessly hit him with bricks until he was left half-dead. The title of the report read: "Sir Phaado, Taangon Pe Goli Maaro': Youth Kidnapped At Gunpoint, Brutally Attacked In Meerut, Pleads For Help; 2 Arrested (VIDEO)" Here is the link to the report. Taking the investigation forward, we also found an X post by Meerut Police on one of the posts, which clarified that both parties belonged to the same caste and the fight was due to only enmity. "In this case both the parties belong to the same caste. There has been a fight between the two parties due to old enmity. Based on the complaint, a case has been registered immediately. One accused has been arrested and sent to jail. A team has been formed to arrest the remaining accused. They will be arrested soon," read the X post. Here is the link and a screenshot. Taking a cue from this, the Desk scanned the Meerut Police's X handle and found a post dated March 9 2025, by Senior Superintendent of Police Vipin Tada of Meerut Police regarding this incident. He stated a case of attempted murder was filed, and the accused were arrested. The main accused is in custody, and efforts are underway to arrest the others. He also clarified that the victim and the accused belong to the same community. Here is the link to the X post, and below is a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the scuffle between the two was caused by a fight between rival gang members in Meerut and did not have any communal angle to it.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Demolition video of theme park in Indonesia shared with false claim of mosque being razed in India
content: New Delhi, March 13 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of a turquoise colour mosque-like structure, those sharing the video claimed that it was an illegally built mosque in India that was being demolished with the help of bulldozers. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral video was shared with a false claim. Upon investigation, it was revealed that the video shows a building in a theme park in Java, Indonesia, being demolished for violating land permits and is unrelated to India. Claim On March 11, an X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video of a turquoise building shaped like a mosque claiming that bulldozers in India demolished it. The caption of the post read: "Bulldozers in India demolish illegal mosques." When posting this article, the post had garnered 2.2 Million views. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found various users shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a video uploaded on YouTube on March 7, 2025, showing the structure's destruction visible in the viral video. The video's title, initially in Indonesian, reads, "End of the story for Hibisc Fantasy Tourism Park." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk found a striking resemblance between the viral video and the video uploaded on YouTube. Below is a combination image highlighting the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across an Instagram post by a local media outlet featuring the same video. The video's caption, a demolition of the Hibisc Fantasy Puncak recreation center, which stands in the middle of the tea plantation, Cisarua, Bogor Region, was carried out. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking the investigation further, the Desk conducted another set of customised keyword searches to find relevant media reports and found a video report by Indonesian news outlet TribunNews uploaded to YouTube on March 6, 2025. At the 0:22 second mark, the structure is visible. Here is the link , and below is a screenshot of the same. Furthermore, CNN Indonesia also reported the incident on March 11, 2025. According to the report, the theme park was built on plantation land, and it violated construction rules, exceeding the number of buildings allowed on plantations. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot featuring the structure of the mosque. The report mentioned: "PT Perkebunan Nusantara ( PTPN ) has finally spoken up after being criticised by the Governor of West Java, Dedi Mulyadi alias Demul, regarding the conversion of their plantation lands into tourist attractions, one of which is the construction of Hibiscus Fantasy Puncak which is accused of triggering flooding." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video shows a building in a theme park in Java, Indonesia, being demolished for violating land permits and is unrelated to India.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of people showering flowers and garlands on Akhilesh Yadav shared with false claim; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 13 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video purportedly showing Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav being mistreated by the public was recently shared on social media. Users claimed that people threw shoes and slippers at him after he allegedly stated, during a meeting in Kannauj, that he would lock the Ram Temple in Ayodhya if his party were elected to power. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found it false. The video dates back to the 2024 Lok Sabha election campaign, when Akhilesh Yadav, then contesting from the Kannauj Lok Sabha seat, held a roadshow. Additionally, the claim that he was pelted with shoes and slippers was false, as a closer analysis of the video showed that flower garlands were being flung toward him, not footwear. Furthermore, the investigation found no authentic reports supporting the claim that Akhilesh Yadav had stated he would lock the Ram Temple if elected to power. The statement attributed to him was also found to be false. Claim An X user named 'Mallikarjuna N1986' shared a video on March 10 showing the public's mistreatment of Akhilesh Yadav. The video allegedly showed people hurling shoes and slippers at Akhilesh Yadav after he, during a meeting in Kannauj, asserted that he would lock Ram's temple in Ayodhya if his party were elected to power. "In a meeting in UP, Akhilesh Yadav said that if elected to power, he would lock the Ram temple in Ayodhya. The people attending the meeting gave him the proper treatment with their footwear," the user shared the video with the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the report. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. After running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk conducted multiple keyword searches on Google to find any incidents suggesting Akhilesh Yadav was mistreated by the public and any statement he made regarding the Ram temple in Ayodhya. However, the search results did not lead to any media reports confirming these claims. Had the incident been real, news portals and channels would have covered it extensively. Later, in the subsequent part of the investigation, the Desk ran the keyframes (generated above) of the viral video through Google Lens and came across a video posted by News 24 on its X handle. The handle posted the same video seen in the viral post on May 10, 2024. However, a closer analysis revealed that the objects flung toward Akhilesh Yadav were actually flower garlands, as seen at different timestamps in the video. Here is the link to the video along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image indicating the objects flung toward Akhilesh Yadav were flower garlands. Further, taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a video posted by the Samajwadi Party's official YouTube channel on April 27, 2024. In this video, the woman who appears beside Akhilesh Yadav in the viral video can be seen with him. Still, the description stated that the video was from Akhilesh Yadav's roadshow in Rasulabad, which falls under the Kannauj Lok Sabha seat. Further, no reports suggesting any misoccurrence during Akhilesh Yadav's roadshow had then been reported. Below is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a video of supporters throwing garlands toward Akhilesh Yadav was shared on social media with false claims.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 3-year-old, unrelated video from Pakistan falsely shared as recent linking it to Jaffar Express hijack incident
content: New Delhi, March 13 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Days after the hijacking of the Jaffar Express, which was carrying around 400 passengers in nine coaches and seized by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) militants in Pakistan, multiple social media users shared a video of a train engulfed in flames. Those sharing the video claimed it depicted visuals from the Jaffar Express hijacking. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found it false. The viral video dates back to 2022 and shows a BLA attack on a train in Balochistan, which was falsely shared as footage from the recent Jaffar Express hijacking. Notably, the Jaffar Express, traveling from Quetta to Peshawar, was derailed using explosives and hijacked near the mountainous terrain of Gudalar and Piru Kunri, inside a tunnel 160 kilometers from Quetta. According to recent updates, the hijacking ended on Wednesday (March 13), with some passengers and paramilitary Frontier Corps soldiers killed by BLA militants who had taken control of the train. Claim On March 11, an X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video of a train on fire, claiming that it showed the visuals of the hijacking of the Jaffar Express by the Baloch Liberation Army which took 120 passengers hostage. The caption of the post, which garnered 60.8k views, read: "Pakistan: The Baloch Liberation Army hijacked a train and took 120 passengers hostage. They are fighting against the tyranny of the Pakistani government towards the Baloch people and for a free Balochistan. They aren't terrorists but freedom fighters...Hope they get back their Balochistan soon." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found various users shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post dated April 15, 2022, featuring the same video as seen in the viral video. This clarifies that the video was on the internet before the recent Pakistan train hijack. The caption of the post read: "The #balochliberationarmy has attacked a train carrying Pakistani soldiers." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Further examination of the comments on the April 2022 X post revealed that a user suggested the video might be from January 2022. Following which, we conducted a keyword search to find any media reports and came across a report dated January 18, 2022 by a media outlet named News Vibes of India. The report mentioned that BLA militants had bombed a train carrying Pakistani Army personnel. The attack left several dead and injured, derailing four carriages. Here is the link to the report. Another report by Pakistan Today published on January 18, 2022, whose headline read: "At least five injured as IED blast hits Jaffer Express near Balochistan's Bolan" Here is the link to the report. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk again ran the keyframes of the viral video through Google Lens and found a video report that featured the same visuals as seen in the viral video. The report's title read: "Separatists Derail Train With Improvised Explosive Device" "Footage released by the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), a separatist group operating in the Pakistan Baluchistan region, shows an improvised explosive device (IED) attack on a train they claimed was carrying Pakistani troops on Jan. 18, 2022. The BLA stated the attack killed multiple and wounded multiple, however, local reports suggest that five people were injured and taken to the hospital. While the train may have been carrying Pakistani troops, Balochistan Chief Minister Mir Abdul Qaddos Bizenjo condemned the attack, claiming it was a passenger train also carrying civilians," the report mentioned. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk, however, could not independently verify the exact incident in the video. Still, it's clear that a 2022 video of a BLA attack on a train in Balochistan was falsely shared as the recent Jaffar Express hijacking.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
