author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of Indians in China celebrating Chinese New Year shared in India with false claim
content: New Delhi, March 14 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of Indians allegedly playing Holi in China was recently shared on social media. Users shared the video, which showed a long line of firecrackers bursting on a street, leading to colors erupting in the air. In the video, several people could watch the celebrations from their balconies, while others were spotted standing on the roads. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found the video linked to the Chinese New Year celebrations held between January 29 and February 12 this year. An old and unrelated video with a false claim was recently shared on social media. Claim An X user named 'Hindustan Mere Jaan' shared a video on March 13, claiming that it showed Indians celebrating Holi in China. Users shared the video, which depicted a long line of firecrackers being burst on a street, leading to colors erupting in the air. "This is how Hindus in China celebrate Holi," users shared the video with this caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. After running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search results led the Desk to a video published on an Instagram page named 'itschina.baby'. The video (posted by the channel) included visuals from the viral post. However, further details revealed that it was first posted on February 16, predating the Holi celebrations held across India. The caption of the video stated, "The sixteenth day of the first lunar month." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting that the content seen in the viral video matches that of the original video. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google. It came across a video posted by a Facebook page named 'The JRE Companion'. The Facebook page posted the same video seen in the viral post on February 19, 2025, along with a description mentioning the significance of the 16th day of the first lunar month. The video's description stated: "China gets it done!! It is the 16th day of the first lunar month. This date follows the Lantern Festival on February 12, 2025, which marks the culmination of the Chinese New Year celebrations. While the 16th day is not a major national festival, it holds cultural significance in certain regions and communities across China." Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. While the Desk could not independently verify the location where the viral video was shot, based on the above findings, it became clear that the viral video was unrelated to the Holi celebrations. Meanwhile, as part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find more information about this year's Chinese New Year festivities. According to a report published by Hindustan Times on January 28, "In 2025, Chinese New Year will begin on Wednesday, January 29, and celebrations will span 15 days, concluding with the Lantern Festival on Wednesday, February 12. Public holidays for the festival will run from January 28 to February 4, 2025, as per the China Public Holiday List." Here is the link to the report: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of Indians celebrating Holi in China was actually from Chinese New Year celebrations and was shared on social media with a false claim.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, PM Modi was not welcomed with song on inflation in Mauritius; digitally altered video shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 17 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check): A video of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and a group of performers is widely circulated on social media.Those sharing the video claim that the performers sang the 'Mehngai Dayain' song from the Bollywood movie Peepli Live during PM Modi's two-day visit to Mauritius. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found the viral video to be edited and digitally altered. In the original video, PM Modi received a traditional Bihari welcome in Mauritius with 'Geet Gawai'. Notably, Geet Gawai is a traditional Bhojpuri musical ensemble that embodies the rich cultural heritage brought to Mauritius by women from the Bhojpuri belt of India. Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Mauritius for a two-day state visit (from 11 to 12 March), marking his second trip to the island nation since 2015. He was the chief guest at Mauritius' National Day celebrations on March 12, highlighting the strong ties between the two nations. Claim On March 12, an X (formerly Twitter) user, Ashish Prasher Himachal, shared a video of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and a group of performers allegedly singing the 'Mehngai Dayain' song, claiming that the song was sung during the PM's Mauritius visit. The post's caption, originally in Hindi, read: "He doesn't understand the difference between respect and disrespect. The people of Mauritius did it right." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. After running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here, with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Desk first conducted a customised keyword search on Google to verify the claim and find relevant media reports. However, the search results did not yield credible results corroborating the details mentioned in the viral video. Furthermore, the Desk then conducted another set of customised keyword searches regarding PM Modi's Mauritius visit and came across a PTI report carried by the Hindustan Times dated March 11, 2025. The report mentioned that PM Modi received a warm welcome from the Indian diaspora in Mauritius, with the women from the community honouring him through a traditional Bihari cultural performance known as Geet Gawai. The headline of the report read: "PM Modi receives traditional Bihari welcome in Mauritius with 'Geet Gawai'" Here is the link to the report; below is a screenshot of it. Taking a cue from this, the Desk carefully scanned Prime Minister Modi's official social media handles and found the same video as seen in the viral video on PMO India's official YouTube handle. The videos showed the PM in the exact location and featured the same performers. However, the performers did not sing any songs to highlight inflation. The clips' audio was different, indicating that a song highlighting inflation had been digitally overlaid on the original clip of Geet Gawai's performance. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the video uploaded on YouTube. Similar videos were also shared on the official YouTube channel of Narendra Modi and an X post by Sansad TV on March 11, 2025. The original video uploaded on the official YouTube channel mentioned: "Geet Gawain is a traditional Bhojpuri musical ensemble that embodies the rich cultural heritage brought to Mauritius by women from the Bhojpuri belt of India." Here is the link to the YouTube post and here is the link to the X post. Continuing the investigation, the Desk also found a watermark, 'NETAFLIX,' on the top right corner of the viral video. The Desk scanned the X handle named 'NETAFLIX' and found it a parody account. Below is a screenshot highlighting both. The Desk then skimmed through the profile and found the video shared on March 11, 2025. Replying to a comment, the user clarified that it was an edited video. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Therefore, it makes it clear that no such song on inflation was sung by the performers for PM Modi. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video showing people singing a song on inflation is edited and digitally altered.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Rajasthan youth murder incident captured on CCTV video shared with false and communal angle; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 18 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A CCTV footage showing a ruckus inside a library was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that a Muslim man was lynched by Hindu men after he refused to play Holi, in Rajasthan. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral video was shared with a false communal angle. Upon further search it was revealed that the victim and the accused both belonged to the same community and the three accused have been arrested by the Police. The viral video was shared with a false claim on social media. Claim On March 14, an X (formerly Twitter) user, going by the name 'Mohammed Ullah', shared a video showing a ruckus inside a library, claiming that a Muslim man was lynched by Hindu men after he refused to play Holi, in Rajasthan. The caption of the post read: "Hindus are the most dirtiest creatures on earth. With their fucking hindutva! A Muslim man was lynched inside a library by Hindutva men in Rajasthan, India, because he refused to play Holi." Here is the link and archive link to the story and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. After running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here, with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. To verify the claim, the Desk again ran the keyframes of the viral video through Reverse Image Search and found a report by NDTV Rajasthan, dated March 13, 2025. The report mentioned that the student was beaten to death in Ralawas village's library, located in the Ramgarh Pachwara police station area in Dausa district, Rajasthan, after refusing to be smeared with colours. Adding that the deceased has been identified as 25-year-old Hansraj, who was preparing for competitive exams. The title of the report read: "Dausa Student Murder Case: रंग लगाने से किया इनकार तो Library में कर दी हत्या | Rajasthan Holi 2025" Here is the link and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports. We found multiple reports that reported the incident, one such article by The Indian Express, dated March 15, 2025 highlighted that s per the CCTV footage, there was an issue over applying of colours on the now deceased Hansraj Meena — who was preparing for patwari (revenue officer) exams — in the local library. Which makes it clear that the deceased was also a Hindu. The title of the report read: "25-year-old killed in Rajasthan's Dausa for refusing Holi colours" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot. Furthermore, Additional Superintendent of Police (ASP) Dinesh Agarwal told PTI that as Hansraj refused to be smeared with colours, the trio kicked him and thrashed him with belts, before one of them strangled him to death. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was shared with a false communal angle as the deceased was a Hindu.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2022 video of Ukrainian marines surrendering in Mariupol falsely shared as recent incident from Kursk region of Russia
content: New Delhi, March 18 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video featuring people in military uniforms walking on a landscape with their hands in the air was recently shared on social media. Those sharing the video claimed that the Ukrainian army surrendered in the Kursk region of Russia. However, the PTI Fact Check investigated and found that the viral video dates back to 2022 when the Ukrainian marines surrendered in Mariupol and is unrelated to the ongoing conflict in the Kursk region. Claim On March 11, an X (formerly Twitter) user, going by the name Concerned Citizen, recently shared a video featuring people in military uniforms, claiming that the Ukrainian army surrendered in the Kursk region of Russia. The post's caption, which has garnered 147.2k views, read: "Reports Ukrainians are surrendering in huge numbers in the Kursk region. Hopefully, they will be treated well & be able to return to their families alive once this Deep State proxy war is ended." Here is the link , and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. After running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . To verify the claim, the Desk again ran the keyframes of the viral video through Reverse Image Search and came across a video published on YouTube by a channel called Serge Antoine on April 7, 2022. The video's title, originally in Russian, translates to: "Mariupol Ukrainian marines 268 people of the 501 battalion of the Armed forces of Ukraine surrendered to DPR fighters in Mariupol." People walking in military uniforms, similar to those in the viral video, were also seen in the post. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral and YouTube videos. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and found a news report published by Belarus Today on April 5, 2022. The report featured the same video as the one seen in the viral post. The report read: "The video shows captured Ukrainian Navy marines in Mariupol. Two hundred sixty-seven soldiers and officers surrendered voluntarily. They chose life. These are the remnants of the 503rd separate marine battalion." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Furthermore, another report by Reuters published on April 14, 2022, mentioned that according to Russia, some 1000 Ukrainian marines surrendered in Mariupol. Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to 2022, when the Ukrainian marines surrendered in Mariupol, and is unrelated to the ongoing conflict in the Kursk region.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2024 video of aircraft emergency landing in Oslo Torp Sandefjord Airport falsely shared as recent incident happened in UP's Bareilly
content: New Delhi, March 19 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of an aircraft veering off the runway was recently shared on social media with users claiming that it was the KLM Airlines that made an emergency landing near Bareilly International Airport. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral video was shared with a false claim on social media as Bareilly does not have an international airport. Upon further investigation, it was found that the viral video dates back to 2024 when KLM Airlines veered off the right side of runway 18 after landing at Oslo Torp Sandefjord Airport. Claim On March 13, an Instagram user named 'ASLI BAREILLY' shared a video of an airplane, claiming that a KLM aircraft faced a terrifying emergency landing near Bareilly International Airport late last night. The overlying text on the video read: "Airplane crashed near Bareilly International Airport" However, the caption of the post mentioned: "A KLM aircraft faced a terrifying emergency landing near Bareilly International Airport late last night. The plane, carrying passengers on board, veered off the runway and landed in a rough terrain area. Emergency services responded swiftly, evacuating all passengers safely. While some minor injuries were reported, no fatalities have been confirmed…" Here is the link and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation To verify, the Desk first carefully analysed the claim made in a viral post and found 'Bareilly International Airport' written, however, Bareilly does not have an international airport. Bareilly Airport is also known as Bareilly Air Force Station or Trishul Air Base. The Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find if such an incident had taken place at Bareilly Airport, but it did not yield any relevant reports corroborating the details. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk ran the keyframes of the viral video through Reverse Image search and came across a Facebook post dated December 29, 2024. The video featured similar visuals as seen in the viral video. The translation of the caption mentioned that a KLM flight was involved in an incident when it ran off the runway after landing at Torp Sandefjord Airport in Oslo, Norway. "Airport authorities confirmed that, despite the incident, no injuries were reported among passengers or crew," it read. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a screenshot highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the Facebook post. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and found an X (formerly Twitter) by Aviation Safety Network (ASN) dated December 29, 2024. The caption of the post read: "KLM flight #KL1204, a Boeing 737-800, veered off the right side of runway 18 after landing at Oslo Torp Sandefjord Airport. The flight had diverted there shortly after takeoff from Oslo Airport (OSL)." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to 2024, when KLM Airlines veered off the right side of runway 18 after landing at Oslo Torp Sandefjord Airport and not at Bareilly International Airport.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated photo of astronauts Sunita Williams and Butch Wilmore, along with US Prez Trump and Elon Musk, falsely shared as accurate; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 20 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): After a successful homecoming of astronauts Sunita Williams and Butch Wilmore, several social media users shared a photo of the astronauts with US President Donald Trump and SpaceX founder Elon Musk claiming that it was after they returned to Earth. Though several reports mentioned about Sunita Williams and Butch Wilmore's return to Earth after spending over nine months at the International Space Station (ISS) due to unexpected delays. For instance, both individuals' facial features appeared distorted, and the images had an overly glossy appearance. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the viral images through Hive Moderation (an AI detection tool), which indicated a substantial presence of AI-generated content. author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2024 video of protest against attacks on Hindus in Bangladesh falsely shared as recent violence in Nagpur
content: New Delhi, March 21 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Violence erupted in Nagpur's Chitnis Park on Monday (March 17) following clashes over rumours during the right-wing agitation in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, after which several social media users shared a video of a massive crowd gathering with saffron flags and chanting slogans praising Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj—those sharing the video claim that a rally was organised in Nagpur after the recent communal tension. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral video was shared with a false claim. Upon further investigation, the Desk found that the video dates back to December 2024 when a protest was organised by Sakal Hindu Samaj against the atrocities on religious minorities in Bangladesh, in Nagpur. Claim On March 18, an X (formerly Twitter) user named 'Chrom09' shared a video of a massive crowd gathering with saffron flags, claiming that a rally was organised in Nagpur after the recent communal tension. The caption of the post read: "Power of Hindu. Don't tease me or else I'll bury you in the dust. #NagpurViolence #Nagpur #Hindu" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. After running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . To verify the claim, the Desk carefully analysed the viral clip and found a watermark '@vedantcreation__' at the bottom of the video. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. We then looked for the social media handles and found the same video on the Instagram profile uploaded on December 10, 2024. The user also posted the video on his Instagram story 16 hours ago. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk found several similarities between the viral video and the Instagram post. Below is a combination image highlighting the same. We also noticed the 'Sakal Hindu Samaj' banner in the viral video; taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find relevant media reports and came across a report by ABP Majha dated December 10, 2024. The report consisted of similar visuals as seen in the viral post. The visuals can be seen at the 1:21-second time stamp. The title of the report read: "Nagpur Sakal Hindu Samaj Morcha: Dharna protest in Nagpur against atrocities on Hindus in Bangladesh" Here is the link to the report; below is a screenshot of the same. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk also came across a report by the Times of India dated December 10, 2024, in which they published several pictures of the protest organised in Nagpur. The report read: "People take part in a protest organised by Sakal Hindu Samaj against the atrocities on religious minorities in Bangladesh, in Nagpur, on December 10, 2024. The Sakal Hindu Samaj (All India Hindu community ) in Nagpur strongly condemned the atrocities being committed against Hindus, Buddhists, Sikhs, Jains and other minorities in Bangladesh by radical Muslims with a jihadi mentality." Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to December 2024 when a protest was organised by Sakal Hindu Samaj against the atrocities on religious minorities in Bangladesh, in Nagpur.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2022 video from Madhya Pradesh falsely shared as recent incident of communal violence in Nagpur, Maharashtra
content: New Delhi, March 21 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Violent mobs went on a rampage after a right-wing call to remove Aurangzeb's tomb, leading to widespread clashes, after which several social media users shared a video of police personnel beating two people. Those sharing the video claim that they were students coming out of a Masjid after offering Namaz and were beaten by the Nagpur police during the recent violence in the state. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral video was shared with a false claim as the viral video dates back to 2022 when the communal clashes broke out in Madhya Pradesh's Khargone following the Ram Navami celebrations. The video is unrelated to the recent violence in Nagpur. Claim On March 19, an X (formerly Twitter) user, going by the name 'Thanos_Pandit', shared a video of police personnel thrashing two people, claiming that they were students coming out of a Masjid after offering Namaz, who Nagpur Police beat. The caption of the post, which garnered 31.2k views, read: "Students coming out of Masjid after offering namaz were beaten by police in Nagpur on Monday" Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. After running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. One such post can be found here. https://x.com/AmitRan18326848/status/1902593347279319114 On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post by 'MaktoobMedia' on April 13, 2022. The post mentioned that the incident happened in Madhya Pradesh's Khargone after the Ram Navami celebrations The caption of the post read: "Visuals of police personnel attacking Muslims have been shared with @MaktoobMedia from Madhya Pradesh's Khargone. Critics complain that police are torturing Muslims following Ram Navami celebrations that turned violent." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the X post. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports and came across a report by MP Tak, dated April 15, 2022. The media outlet also interviewed one of the men seen in the video, who said that he had gone out to buy milk when the incident happened. The title of the report read: "After Khargone violence, the video of police brutality went viral, the victim said he had gone to get milk" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Further, several media reports carried the news of communal violence that broke out during the Ram Navami celebrations in Khargone, Madhya Pradesh, in April 2022. The Hindu carried out one such report of PTI on April 13, 2022. The headline of the report read: "Khargone violence: M.P. govt. sets up claims tribunal to recover damages from rioters" Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to 2022 from Khargone of Madhya Pradesh and is unrelated to the recent violence in Nagpur, Maharashtra.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of bus explosion in Turbat, Balochistan, shared as recent BLA attack on Pakistani military convoy
content: New Delhi, March 21 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid heightened tensions in Balochistan, a video of what looked like CCTV footage of an explosion of a vehicle on the road was shared on social media. Those sharing the video claimed that it was Baluchistan's BLA that blew up Pakistani buses in which 90 Pakistani soldiers were killed in Noshki, in Pakistan. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral video was shared with a false claim. The video is actually from January 2025 and shows a bus explosion in Turbat, Balochistan. It was misinterpreted as the recent attack on a Pakistani military convoy in Noshki, Balochistan. The viral video was misleadingly shared with a false claim on social media. This comes days after the BLA hijacked the Jaffar Express, taking over 450 passengers hostage before Pakistani forces claimed to have neutralised the attackers. Claim On March 16, an X (formerly Twitter) user, going by the name 'Yati Sharma', shared a video of an explosion of a vehicle on the road, claiming that Baluchistan's BLA blew up Pakistani buses in which 90 Pakistani soldiers were killed. The caption of the post, originally in Hindi, with around 9,672 views, read: "Baluchistanis have turned Pakistan into a mess. Video surfaced today in which Baluchistan's BLA blew up Pakistani buses in which 90 Pakistani soldiers were killed" Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. After running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . To verify the claim, the Desk again ran the keyframes of the viral video through Google Lens and found that PM News, a media outlet based in Lakki Marwat in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, shared a similar video on Facebook on January 5, 2025. The caption of the post, originally in Urdu, read: "Balochistan: Explosion near pilgrims' bus in Turbat, 4 killed, 32 injured. Security sources." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the news report. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports and found the same visuals published by Geo TV on January 4, 2025. The report mentioned that at least four people were killed while 32 others sustained injuries after a blast rocked Balochistan's city of Turbat on Saturday, police said. The headline of the report read: "Four killed, 32 injured as blast rocks Balochistan's Turbat." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Furthermore, according to a report by Dwan, the bus detonated while travelling from Karachi to Turbat in the New Bahman area. Zuhaib Muhsin, Senior Superintendent of Police Serious Crime Wing in Quetta, and his family, who were passing by at the time of the explosion, were injured. According to the article, the Balochistan Liberation Army has claimed responsibility for the attack. Here is the link to the article. The Desk, during its search, also found that Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif condemned the bombing and expressed his condolences to the families of those "martyred in the bomb explosion". Here is the link to the report carrying his statement. Additionally, while the Desk could not independently verify further details about the viral video showing an explosion of vehicles, we can confirm that it was on the internet since January 2025, which pre-dates the recent attack on a Pakistani military convoy in Noshki, Balochistan. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was from January 2025, which showed a bus explosion in Turbat, Balochistan. It was misinterpreted as an attack by the Balochistan Liberation Army on a Pakistani military convoy in Noshki.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Social media post falsely claims Shirdi Sai Trust donated Rs 35 crore for Hajj; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 21 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media post containing a screenshot of a Google search page was widely shared online. The screenshot featured a post by a user named 'kavita_tewari,' who claimed that the Shirdi Sai Trust had donated Rs 35 crore for Hajj. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found this claim to be false. The Desk contacted Goraksha Gadilkar, Chief Executive Officer of the Shree Saibaba Sansthan Trust (Shirdi), who vehemently rejected the claim, stating that the Trust had never made such a donation. Claim An X user named 'Patriotic Parav' shared a social media post on March 19, claiming that the Shirdi Sai Temple Trust had gifted ₹35,00,00,000 to Muslims for their Hajj pilgrimage. The user attached a screenshot of a Google search page mentioning the alleged donation linked to the Shirdi Sai Trust. "Shirdi Sai Temple Trust has gifted ₹35,00,00,000 to Muslims for their Hajj pilgrimage! Our Hindus' donated money is being given to Muslims for their Hajj journey. There is still time, please understand these systems, please do not donate any money at Sai's shrine," the user wrote in the post caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found multiple social media posts making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively: In the next step of the investigation, the Desk conducted another customized keyword search on Google but could not find any authentic reports substantiating the viral claim. If such an incident had actually occurred, it would have been widely covered by news outlets. The search results also led to reports indicating that the same claim and a similar screenshot had gone viral in 2023. A report by ETV Bharat, published on April 24, 2023, quoted then-CEO of the Sai Baba Sansthan, Rahul Jadhav, stating: "There is no provision in the constitution of Sai Sansthan to provide such funds. No one has even demanded it. Therefore, there is no question of giving or denying funds to anyone. Regarding this misinformation, we will take legal action against those who defame us as well as social media platforms like YouTube, Twitter, and Facebook." Here is the link and archive link to the report, along with a screenshot: Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk also contacted Goraksha Gadilkar, Chief Executive Officer of the Shree Saibaba Sansthan Trust (Shirdi), for further clarification. He vehemently rejected the claim and termed it false. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral claim regarding the Shirdi Sai Trust donating ₹35 crore for Hajj is entirely false.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of scripted bike theft incident falsely shared as real incident happened in broad daylight; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 22 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media claimed to show two individuals who had just returned from playing Holi attempting to steal two bikes. The footage showed the individuals making several attempts before finally breaking open the lock systems of the bikes and fleeing from the location. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the footage and found that the viral video was misleadingly shared with a false claim. The video is entirely scripted and staged, not connected to a real event. Claim An X user shared a video on March 17 allegedly showing two individuals stealing bikes parked on a roadside. The video depicted the individuals making several attempts before finally breaking open the bikes' lock systems and fleeing from the location. "Thieves have become so clever these days that they have made a mockery of the law. Two bikes were stolen in broad daylight right in front of a policeman's eye," the user captioned the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively: The search results also led the Desk to a video posted on an Instagram handle named 'official_rajthakur_' on March 15, 2025. The video posted on this handle shows visuals from the viral post, but it includes a disclaimer stating: "This video is totally scripted, not real. All content is just for entertainment purposes and awareness and is not hate speech." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the visuals from the original post. Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk also examined other social media handles associated with Raj Thakur, which feature many similar scripted videos. Upon scanning the user's Facebook page, the Desk found the full version of the viral video posted on March 14. Here too, the caption clarified that it is a scripted video created solely for entertainment and awareness purposes. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing the individuals stealing bikes parked alongside the road on Holi is scripted and not an actual incident.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Delhi's murder case video falsely shared claiming Nagpur residents boycotted Muslims after recent incident of communal violence
content: New Delhi, March 22 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Following the communal tension in Nagpur, Maharashtra, several social media users shared a video of a man addressing a huge gathering, claiming that Hindus in Nagpur have decided to boycott people belonging to the Muslim community after the recent violence in Nagpur. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral video was shared with a false claim. The footage actually predates the March 17 clash in Nagpur, relates to a murder case in Delhi's Ghazipur, and is unrelated to the incidents that have occurred in Nagpur recently. Claim On March 19, an X (formerly Twitter) user, going by the name S.C.Rana, shared a video of a man addressing a huge gathering, claiming that Hindus in Nagpur have decided to boycott people belonging to the Muslim community after the recent violence in Nagpur. In the video, which garnered 114.3k views, the man can be heard saying: "Take a pledge…if you befriend them, no one will support you; if anyone does business with them…no one will support you…that Muslim is friends with him. Someone is doing business with him. If this continues, the same situation will prevail". Moreover, the overlying text on the video read: "Decision by Hindus in Nagpur" Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. After running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . To verify the claim, we first carefully analysed the entire viral video, and at 1:34 seconds, another man says that a Mahapanchayat will be organised at Ghazipur in Delhi. Further, in the video 2:30 seconds time stamp, another person says that the main motive is to get justice in the murder case of Rohit Gurjar. Here is the link from the timestamp mentioned, and below is a screenshot of the same. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk ran the keyframes of the viral video through Reverse Image Search and came across a Facebook post by a user named Sanjeev Bhatia on March 16, 2025, which predates the violence that broke out in Nagpur on March 17. Moreover, the caption refers to the murder of a person named Rohit Gurjar in Delhi. The caption of the post read: "Rohit Gurjar was murdered in Delhi on 09 March 2025 by Jihadis living in Ghazipur Dairy Farm, in which the police still has a lax attitude. And the 4 main accused are out of police custody. Please, all my 36 communities, come forward to get justice for my brother Rohit. Place - Ghazipur village Time - noon. Date - 23 March Day - Sunday" Here is the link , and below is a screenshot. Below is a screenshot highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the Facebook post. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports. It came across a PTI report from Print, dated March 10, 2025. According to DCP (East) Abhishek Dhania, eyewitness Akash Chaudhary, who had accompanied Rohit, stated they were returning from a dumping yard on a scooter after refuelling with diesel when a car carrying three people intercepted them and opened fire. The accused have been arrested. The section of the report read: "The accused have been identified as Nazim (40), previously allegedly involved in six criminal cases, and Talib alias Tariq (24), both residents of Ghazipur Dairy Farm, he said, adding that the reason behind the murder was an ongoing monetary dispute between the victim and the accused." Here is the link to the report However, the Desk could not independently verify the further details about the viral video; we can confirm that it was on the internet since March 16, which predates the recent Nagour violence. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video pre dates the recent Nagpur violence and is from Delhi regarding a Mahapanchayat being organised following the killing of a youth in Ghazipur Dairy Farm.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old photo of RSS leader Indresh Kumar shared with false claim after recent Nagpur violence; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 22 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Two purported images showing RSS leader Indresh Kumar attending an Iftar party were shared online with a claim that he attended the event hours after communal violence broke out in Maharashtra's Nagpur on March 17, 2025. However, in its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the images showing the RSS leader attending an Iftar Party predate the incident of the violence in Nagpur that broke over the removal of the tomb of the Mughal ruler Aurangzeb. A false claim was shared on social media as real. Meanwhile, it is pertinent to note that large-scale stone pelting and arson were reported in several parts of Nagpur on Monday evening after rumors began circulating about a 'chadar' with holy inscriptions being burnt during protests led by the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) seeking the removal of Aurangzeb's tomb. Claim A Facebook user going by the name T Ranjeet Singh posted on March 20 two purported images of National Executive member (RSS) Indresh Kumar attending the Iftar party. The user claimed that the RSS leader attended the event hours after communal violence broke out in Nagpur on March 17, 2025. "The so-called organizations are making a Muslim National Forum with Hindus' money and dealing with the killing of Hindus. The night in Nagpur, the houses and vehicles of Hindus were being marked and burnt, RSS's Indresh Kumar was licking the false dates of Muslims," the user shared the post with the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral images through Google Lens and found multiple users had shared the same post with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . In the next part of the investigation, to corroborate the claims made in the viral post, the Desk conducted a customized keyword search on Google and came across several media reports that covered the development. According to a video released by News18 India (which also includes visuals from the viral post), RSS leader Indresh Kumar attended the Iftar party organized by the Community Centre in Delhi on March 15, i.e., two days before the violence broke out in Nagpur over the removal of the tomb of the Mughal ruler Aurangzeb. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. Below is the combination image highlighting that the images seen in the viral post match the visuals from the News18 India news channel video. Additionally, the Desk also scanned through the Facebook handle of Indresh Kumar, National Executive member (RSS), and on March 16 found a post made by him regarding his attendance at an Iftar Party organized at the Community Centre, Nizamuddin West, New Delhi, on March 15. Kumar also posted several images (matching the images seen in the viral post) from the event, which was also attended by Iqbal Singh Lalpura (Chairman, National Commission for Minorities), Dr. Shahid Akhtar (Acting Chairman, NCMEI), among other religious and social leaders. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the images showing RSS leader Indresh Kumar attending an Iftar Party predate the incident of the violence in Nagpur over the removal of the tomb of the Mughal ruler Aurangzeb.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2018 video of BJP councillor thrashing a police constable shared as recent with false claim
content: New Delhi, March 22 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of a man beating a police officer was recently shared on social media, with users identifying the attacker as West Bengal MLA Mansoor Mohammad Dimir. The footage allegedly showed the TMC MLA thrashing a West Bengal police official in a restaurant-like structure while others tried to intervene. However, in its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false. The video originally dates back to October 20, 2018, when Munish Chaudhary, a BJP councillor and owner of a local restaurant in Meerut, attacked a UP Police constable and a woman lawyer who had arrived at his restaurant following an altercation over a delay in serving meals. An old video was recently shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An X user named Nazia Elahi Khan shared a video on March 22, claiming it showed West Bengal MLA Mansoor Mohammad Dimir thrashing a police official. The video depicted a TMC MLA publicly assaulting the officer while others tried to intervene. "Look at Bengal MLA Mansoor Mohammad Dimir. When this is the condition of the police on duty in uniform, what will be the condition of the voters of Bengal...! Share this video so much that it is seen all over India. TMC MLA Mohammad Dimir beat up Bengal Police in uniform," the user captioned the video. Here is the link , along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . The search results also led the Desk to multiple news reports covering the incident. According to a report by The Times of India, whose feature image matched visuals from the viral video, the incident occurred on October 20, 2018. A sub-inspector, accompanied by a female lawyer friend, visited a local restaurant in Meerut, where they were thrashed by the owner, Munish Chaudhary, who was also a BJP councillor. The altercation occurred over a delay in serving meals. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting that the viral video's content matches the report's feature image. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customized keyword search on G. It came across a video released by the official YouTube channel of NDTV on October 20, 2018. The video posted by the news outlet showed the exact same visuals as the viral video and confirmed that the incident took place in Meerut, with the individual attacking the police constable identified as BJP councillor Munish Chaudhary. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of an individual attacking a police constable was from October 2018 and featured BJP councillor Munish Chaudhary, not TMC MLA Mansoor Mohammad Dimir.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Social media video shared with false claim that Hindu devotees attacked in Sambhal
content: New Delhi, March 23 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it showed an alleged attack on Hindu devotees by a group of jihadists in Uttar Pradesh's Sambhal. The users claimed the altercation between the two communities broke out over bhajans playing in a bus carrying the Hindu devotees. It was on its way to Purnagiri Temple in Uttarakhand. However, a violent altercation ensued as the bus stopped for a short break during the journey. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false. According to a statement released by the Sambhal Police, the video actually shows a fight between two Hindu community members over the purchase of fruits. The police stated that preventive action has been taken against six people from both parties, and further legal proceedings are underway. A video was shared on social media with a false claim linking it to communal violence. Claim An X user with the handle '@TriShool_Achuk' shared a video on March 22 showing a group of people engaged in a physical altercation. The user claimed that it depicted an alleged attack on Hindu devotees by jihadists over the playing of bhajans in their bus. "The bus carrying Maa Purnagiri devotees was attacked in Sambhal. Bhajans were playing in the bus that had stopped for food and drinks, which the Jihadis were adamant about stopping...! The devotees of the goddess were beaten to death... the cowardly Sanatanis standing nearby became mute spectators. Hopefully, Sambhal police will give a strong reply," the user wrote in the caption while sharing the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that multiple users had shared the same video with similar captions. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively: In the next phase of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customized keyword search on Google and came across multiple news reports covering the incident. According to a report published by Republic, whose featured image matched visuals from the viral video, the violence in Sambhal erupted over the price of fruits. It stated that a group of devotees traveling to Purnagiri Temple was beaten up by fruit vendors on the roadside in Sambhal after a dispute over fruit prices. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting that the viral video's content matches the report's feature image. Additionally, the search results led the Desk to a statement released by Sambhal Police regarding the incident. In response to a now-deleted X post by an unidentified user, which contained the same video, the Sambhal Police stated: "There was a fight between two parties while buying fruits; both parties belong to the same community (Hindu). The local police station has taken preventive action against a total of six people from both sides, and further legal action is underway." Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Moreover, as part of the investigation, the Desk also contacted a senior official from the Sambhal Police for an official statement regarding the incident. The story will be updated as soon as a response is received. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video falsely claims to depict a communal attack in Sambhal.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of LLB examination at Barabanki Law College falsely shared claiming mass cheating happened during UPSC examination
content: New Delhi, March 23 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video allegedly showing mass cheating inside an examination centre during a UPSC (Union Public Service Commission) exam was recently shared on social media. The footage depicted a person recording a large number of students openly using guides and cheat sheets to solve their papers. The video was shared with the caption: "IAS Exam centres of UP, Bihar, Jharkhand!! The future of Indian governance." However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation revealed that the video was actually from a law college in Barabanki, Uttar Pradesh, where students appearing for the LLB examination in February 2024 were caught engaging in mass cheating. After the video went viral, authorities took strict action and subsequently declared the exam null and void. Claim An X user named '@Mahaveer_VJ' shared a video on March 21 allegedly showing mass cheating inside an examination centre conducting the UPSC (Union Public Service Commission) examination. The footage showed a person capturing visuals inside the centre, where many students were openly using guides and cheat sheets to solve their papers. The user shared the video with the caption, "IAS Exam centres of UP, Bihar, Jharkhand!! The future of Indian governance. " Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analyzed the viral video and, at the 00:04-second timestamp, found a mention of City Law College, Barabanki, by the person shooting the video. Taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk conducted a customized keyword search on Google and came across several news reports covering the development. Upon scanning through a report released by Zee News, whose feature image matched that of the visuals in the viral video, the Desk found that the incident occurred at Barabanki's City Law College on February 27, 2024, where students could be seen cheating en masse during the LLB examination, even in full view of the invigilators. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting that the viral video's content matches the report's feature image. Additionally, the Desk conducted another customized keyword search on Google and found a detailed report by Dainik Bhaskar covering the development. The report identified Shivam Singh as the person recording the video inside the examination centre. Singh had live-streamed the mass cheating that took place during the first shift of the examination on February 27, 2024. Further, as the incident went public, the authorities took stringent action. They ordered that City Law College would not be considered an examination centre for the next six years and imposed a fine of Rs 2 lakh on the institution. Additionally, the exam held at the centre was declared null and void. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video showing mass cheating inside an examination centre was from Barabanki and depicted students appearing for the LLB examination. The claim that the incident took place during a UPSC examination in Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, or Jharkhand is false.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Viral video of father pleading with daughter is scripted; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 23 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of a middle-aged man pleading with a couple was recently shared on social media. The video claims to depict a real-life incident of a helpless father from Tamil Nadu desperately trying to stop his daughter from eloping with her alleged lover. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the footage and found that the viral video was misleadingly shared with a false claim. The video is entirely scripted and staged, without connection to real-life events. Claim An X user with the handle '@KajjoKajal' shared a video on March 22 showing a middle-aged man pleading with a young couple. The user claimed that the man was the father of the girl and was begging her not to elope with her lover. "Look at the pain of a father of a daughter... and understand more... A father, overwhelmed with joy at the birth of his daughter, raises her like his Mahalakshmi (Goddess)! He works tirelessly, ensuring that no hardship ever touches her shadow, raising her with utmost care and love. But then, she falls in love with a worthless man and forgets the love and sacrifice of the father who raised her. What do we say about such daughters? The father's struggle will begin again when the lover fulfils his needs and leaves her tomorrow. Because a father can never abandon his part under any circumstances... With a heavy heart, the father requests his daughter: 'Don't go with a man who can't fulfil his own needs, so how can he fulfil yours?' A heart-wrenching incident from Tamil Nadu... It disturbs the mind... An unfortunate situation," the user shared the video with this caption. Here is the link and archive link to the video, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search results also led the Desk to a video posted by a content creator named Sai Vijay on his YouTube channel. The video, posted on his handle on March 19, showed an extended version of the viral clip but included a disclaimer clearly stating: "This video is for entertainment purposes only, and it is made/uploaded with the permission of the people concerned." Here is the link and archive link to the video, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting that the content in the viral video matches that of the video originally posted by the creator. Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk carefully scanned through the other videos posted by the content creator and found a seven-episode entertainment series (as of the time of publishing this article) covering the alleged love story of the couple mentioned above. Here is the link to the channel. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a couple walking away on a road while a distressed man chases after them is scripted, not an actual incident.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2019 video of protest against CAA in UP's Gorakhpur falsely shared as recent incident of lathi charge on Waqf Bill protesters
content: New Delhi, March 24 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Days after the protest by the All India Muslim Personal Law Board (AIMPLB) against the Waqf (Amendment) Bill 2024 at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi multiple social media users shared a video showing a massive crowd being charged by the police. Those sharing the video claimed it depicted people from a particular community protesting against the Waqf Amendment Bill in Uttar Pradesh. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral video dates back to the 2019 anti-CAA protest in Uttar Pradesh's Gorakhpur. It was falsely shared as a recent incident during the Waqf Bill protest. The viral video was misleadingly shared with a false claim on social media. Claim On March 20, an X (formerly Twitter) user, going by the name Ankit Valmiki, shared a video of a massive crowd who were charged by Police, claiming they were people from a particular community who were protesting against the Waqf Amendment Bill, in Uttar Pradesh. The post's caption, which garnered 1,011 views, originally in Hindi read: "People of a particular community gathered against the Waqf Bill in Uttar Pradesh! Treatment was done immediately! For instant relief from chronic back pain, waist pain, leg pain••••Famous Vaidya: Yogi Adityanath Ji Maharaj!!" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. To verify the claim, the Desk first conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports, but the search did not yield any results for protests against Waqf Bill protesters in Uttar Pradesh, as mentioned in the viral video. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk again ran the keyframes of the viral video through Reverse Image Search. The search led us to a Facebook post dated January 25, 2020, featuring the same viral video. According to the post, the protest was held against the CAA (Citizenship Amendment Act) protests in Uttar Pradesh. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Taking a cue, the Desk conducted another set of customised keyword searches to find media reports citing the incident. It came across a report by Live Hindustan dated December 20, 2019. As per the report, the police cracked down on demonstrators who threw stones at them during anti-CAA demonstrations at Nakhass Chowk in Gorakhpur on December 20, 2019. The report featured the same video but from a different angle. The title of the report read: "Gorakhpur: Two injured in stone pelting, lathi charge during a protest against CAA" Here is the link , and below is a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarity in the location between the viral video and the news report. Another report, published by News Nation on December 20, 2019, mentioned that a clash broke out between Police and protesters in Gorakhpur. The title of the report read: "Anti-CAA Protests: Clashes Between Police In Gorakhpur." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to the 2019 anti-CAA protest video from Uttar Pradesh's Gorakhpur, which was falsely shared as a recent incident during the Waqf Bill protest.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2023 photos of SP Chief Akhilesh Yadav attending Iftar party falsely shared as recent; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 24 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A collage of two purported photos featuring Samajwadi Party (SP) Chief Akhilesh Yadav along with a few people wearing skull caps was shared on social media. The users claimed that the SP chief recently attended an Iftar party. However, the PTI Fact Check investigated and found that the viral photos were old and misleadingly shared as recent. The photographs from the Iftar party date back to April 2023 from Lucknow and are not recent. Claim On March 12, an X (formerly Twitter) user, Janardan Mishra, shared a collage of two photos featuring Samajwadi Party (SP) Chief Akhilesh Yadav, claiming that he recently attended an Iftar party. The post's caption, originally in Hindi, read: "The water of Ganga is not clean but dirty. Ramadan's meat is sacred." Here is the link and archive link to the post; below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran a viral photo through a Reverse Image Search and found several other users shared the same picture with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk found similar photos and even more in a report published on April 9, 2023. The report's title read: "Lucknow: Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav during 'Iftar' #Gallery." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral post and the news report. Taking a cue from this, the Desk scanned the official handles of the SP Chief and came across an X post by Akhilesh Yadav featuring the same photos as seen in the viral post. The X post was dated April 9, 2023, whose caption read: "During Iftar today, Lucknow." Here is the link , and below is a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the photos from the Iftar party in Lucknow date back to April 2023 and are not recent photographs.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video claiming fire incident happened at Mumbai Airport was AI-generated; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 24 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing thick smoke billowing from inside an airport was recently shared on social media with the claim that it was from Mumbai Airport, where a fire erupted on March 18, killing at least 1,300 people and causing property damage worth Rs 47,000 crores. The video depicted a large plume of smoke continuously rising from the tarmac. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video was AI-generated, and the claim associated with it was false. Social media users had shared the AI-generated video along with the misleading claim. Claim An Instagram user with the handle 'life_is_very_important001' shared a video on March 18, claiming it showed a massive fire erupting at Mumbai Airport, which killed 1,300 people and caused property damage worth Rs 47,000 crores. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here . In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google but could not find any authentic reports substantiating the viral claim that the fire erupted at Mumbai airport. If such an incident had actually occurred, it would have been widely covered by news outlets. Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk closely examined the video and observed several inconsistencies that indicated it was not real footage. The flames and smoke in the video had an unnatural appearance, unlike those seen in actual fires. Instead, the visuals appeared overly smooth and uniform, resembling computer-generated effects. Below is a screenshot highlighting the points. Taking cues from the above findings, the Desk ran the keyframes of the video generated above through 'Wasitai,' an AI detection tool, which confidently stated that a significant part of it was AI-generated. Below is a screenshot highlighting the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a fire at Mumbai Airport was AI-generated.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Social media user falsely claimed Karnataka govt's decision to impart self-defence training was only for Muslim girls; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 25 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Days after a 22-year-old girl, Swati Byadgi, was found murdered, reportedly by her former partner, Niyaz Bennigere, in Karnataka's Haveri district, a social media post linking the crime to the Karnataka government's decision to impart self-defence training to 25,000 girls in the state has been recently shared online. In the post, however, the users attempting to insinuate communal disharmony stated that while a Hindu girl was brutally murdered in Karnataka by a culprit from another faith, the irony is that in the state budget, Karnataka CM Siddaramaiah announced self-defence training only for girls from the Muslim community. The PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found that the initiative was intended for girls from various minority communities, not just Muslims. A factually incorrect claim was shared on social media by the user. Claim An X user identified with the handle '@ssaratht' shared a social media post on March 18 featuring images of Karnataka CM Siddaramaiah and a young girl posing with a cow. The post included text reading: "Hindu girl Swati brutally murdered in Karnataka. One culprit, Nayaz, was arrested by police (sic)." "However, the irony is that in his budget, Karnataka CM Siddaramaiah has announced self-defence training only for girls from the Muslim community!!" Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral post through Google Lens and found multiple users shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google regarding the Karnataka government's initiative launched for girls in its recently presented state budget. The search results led the Desk to a report published by The New Indian Express, titled "Train 'em young: Self-defense for 25k girls in 169 educational institutes in Karnataka." According to the report, on March 8, 2025, the Karnataka Chief Minister announced in the recently presented state budget that self-defence skill training would be imparted to 25,000 girl students studying in 169 residential schools and colleges run by the Directorate of Minorities. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: The customised keyword search also led the Desk to a government document detailing the Karnataka State budget for 2025-2026. Under it, Point 221 in the Minorities Welfare section stated: "Self-defense skills training will be provided to 25,000 girl students studying in 169 residential schools/colleges run by the Directorate of Minorities." Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Furthermore, in the subsequent part of the investigation, to identify how many communities have been included in the minority section of the state, the Desk scanned the website of the Directorate of Minorities in Karnataka, which mentioned that Muslims, Christians, Jains, Buddhists, Sikhs, and Parsis fall under the category of minorities. "The Directorate of Minorities was carved out of the Directorate of Backward Classes and created in the year 1999-2000 to ensure a more focused approach toward issues relating to the notified Minority communities, namely Muslims, Christians, Jains, Buddhists, Sikhs, and Parsis," the website stated. Below is a screenshot highlighting the findings: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the social media post claiming that the Karnataka government announced self-defence skill training only for Muslim girls was false. The initiative is intended for girls from various minority communities.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Scripted video showing child-lifting incident at Delhi's Rajiv Chowk Metro station shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 25 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video from Delhi's Rajiv Chowk metro station was shared on social media with a claim that it allegedly captured a child-lifting incident that occurred there. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the footage and found that the viral video was misleadingly shared with a false claim. The video was entirely scripted and staged, without connecting to real-life events. Claim A Facebook user named Bhavin Patil shared a video on March 25, allegedly capturing a child-lifting incident that occurred at Delhi's Rajiv Chowk metro station. "A child was kidnapped from Rajiv Chowk metro station in broad daylight," the user shared the video with the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search results from Google Lens also led the Desk to a video published on a YouTube channel named 'Raj Thakurrrr' on March 24, 2025. Upon carefully scanning through it, the Desk found that the handle had posted the same video as seen in the viral post. However, it had been uploaded with a description stating: "The video is totally scripted and not real. All content is just for entertainment purposes and awareness, not hate speech." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the content seen in the viral video, which matched that of the video posted by the YouTube channel. As part of the investigation, the Desk also carefully scanned the social media handles of the same user 'Raj Thakurrrr'. In his social media profiles, he identified himself as a 'video creator' who consistently posts scripted videos for viewers. A description of the content is also seen in most of his videos, specifying whether or not the content is scripted. Here is the link to his YouTube channel: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a child-lifting incident at Delhi's Rajiv Chowk metro station is scripted.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered photo of person carrying placard with offensive text shared with false claim related to Aurangzeb controversy
content: New Delhi, March 25 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): An image of a man carrying a placard displaying an offensive message against Mughal ruler Aurangzeb and those who preached to him was recently shared on social media. The image showed him standing in a crowded stadium, sporting a black Batman-like mask and holding a placard containing the offensive text. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the image was digitally altered. The original image showed a person displaying a message for Indian cricketer Mahendra Singh Dhoni, but it was digitally manipulated to mislead viewers. Claim An X user identified with the handle 'Voice of Hindus' shared, on March 24, an image of a man displaying an offensive message against Mughal ruler Aurangzeb and those who preached to him. The picture showed him standing in a crowded stadium, sporting a black Batman-like mask and holding a placard containing the offensive message. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and found multiple users had shared it with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk carefully scanned the viral image and found a watermark at the bottom left corner. The watermark suggested that the image was AI-generated. Below is a screenshot highlighting the findings: Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk ran the image through Hive Moderation, an AI detection tool, which confirmed that the image contained AI-generated or deepfake content. Additionally, to identify the real message initially displayed on the placard but purportedly replaced with offensive text, the Desk scanned the comments under the viral post. One of the comments by a user named Parthik Patel, posted on March 24, led the Desk to a social media handle of a user identified as Rathna Kumar. The Desk found that on March 23, this user had posted an image that matched the viral one in terms of settings; however, the message displayed by the man holding the placard read: "The Man. The Myth. The Mahi!!" Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the image depicting offensive comments against Mughal ruler Aurangzeb was digitally altered.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of 2019 train collision near Hyderabad's Kacheguda Railway Station shared as recent Assam-bound train accident in Ajmer
content: New Delhi, March 25 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared CCTV footage of two trains colliding. Those sharing the video claim that it was a train travelling from Ajmer to Assam that collided with another train on the same track, which led to several casualties and injuries. However, the PTI Fact Check investigated and found that the viral video dates back to 2019, when a local train collided with another train near Kacheguda railway station in Hyderabad. The incident is unrelated to the collision of two trains from Ajmer to Assam. The viral video was shared with a false claim on social media. Claim On March 18, an Instagram user, going by the name 'majisa_jawelrsh_kumpliya', shared a video of a train colliding with another. The user claimed that it was an Assam-bound train from Ajmer that claimed seven lives while 50 others were injured. The overlying text on the video read: "This morning at 9:00, a train going from Ajmer to Assam collided with another train on the way in which seven died, and 50 people were injured" Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . The Desk first conducted a customised keyword search on Google to verify the claim to find relevant media reports citing the train collision on the Assam-Ajmer route. However, the search yielded no credible results; such an incident would have received wide media coverage. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk again ran the keyframes of the viral video through Reverse Image Search. It came across a report by Outlook Magazine dated November 12, 2019, which featured similar visuals as seen in the viral video. The report mentioned that two trains collided at Hyderabad's Kacheguda Railway Station. The report's title read: "Moment When Two Trains Collided At Hyderabad's Kacheguda Railway Station." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the news report. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted another set of customised keyword searches on Google to find relevant media reports and came across a report by NDTV dated November 12, 2019. The report mentioned that hours after two trains collided near Hyderabad's Kacheguda Railway Station on Monday morning, footage from a nearby CCTV camera gave a frame-by-frame account of the accident that reportedly occurred due to manual error. The title of the report read: "Hyderabad Head-On Collision Caught On Camera, Train Lifted Off Tracks" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to 2019, when two trains collided near Hyderabad's Kacheguda Railway Station, not an Assam-bound train from Ajmer.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Edited video of hippopotamus with a human face falsely shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 25 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video claiming to show a hippopotamus with a human face while the people in the video can be seen sitting inside a car and trying to feed the hippopotamus. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video was edited and digitally altered, as the original video does not show a hippo with a human face. The viral video was shared with a false claim on social media. Claim On March 17, an Instagram user named 'i_am__devil_780' shared a purported video from Thailand featuring a hippopotamus with a human face. The video's overlying text read: "A hippopotamus the size of a man was seen on the road in Thailand." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes.
