Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . To verify the claim, the Desk carefully analysed the video and found discrepancies that hinted that it was edited or digitally altered. For instance, when the hippo takes something from the passenger sitting in the car, their hands appear to merge. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk again ran the keyframes of the viral video through Reverse Image search. It came across an Instagram post by a user named 'hippolivelove', where the video was uploaded on March 17, 2025. The video featured a hippopotamus, but the face was not that of a human. The video in the Instagram post closely resembles the viral video. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search and came across an article by Taman Safari in Bali, Indonesia, about Hippo Feeding Near the T-Savo Lion Restaurant. According to the article, feeding hippos near the T-Savo Lion restaurant is one of the most enjoyable activities. This activity provides a unique and unforgettable experience, allowing visitors to get up close and personal with one of Africa's iconic animals. Here is the link to the article, and below is a screenshot. ​ Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was edited, and the original video did not show a hippo with a human face.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated photo shared to falsely claim KL Rahul, Athiya Shetty posted photo of their newborn daughter
content: New Delhi, March 26 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A photo collage featuring two purported images of Indian cricketer KL Rahul with his wife and a kid was recently shared on social media. In the first image, KL Rahul was seen alongside his wife, Bollywood actress Athiya Shetty, and a newborn child. The second image only featured him caressing the baby. Users sharing the collage claimed it was the Indian cricketer's original family photo following the birth of his daughter on March 24. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigation found that the photo collage was AI-generated. The social media user shared the AI-generated collage with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user named Jeney Debbarma shared a collage on March 25, showing images of Indian cricketer KL Rahul. The first image featured KL Rahul with his wife and a newborn child, while the second image showed him holding and caressing the baby. The user claimed that these were the first official pictures of KL Rahul's family after the birth of their daughter on March 24. The user wrote in the caption, "KL Rahul and Athiya Shetty have been blessed with a baby girl. Many congratulations to both of them. " Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the image through Google Lens and found that multiple users had shared it with a similar claim. Two such posts were found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analyzed the viral collage containing images of KL Rahul and his family. The Desk discovered multiple inconsistencies, indicating that it might be AI-generated or digitally altered. For instance, subtle distortions in the facial features of KL Rahul and Athiya Shetty and the baby's appearance irregularities were noticeable. Additionally, the images in the collage had an excessively glossy finish, a common characteristic of AI-generated visuals. Below is a screenshot highlighting these key findings: Next, taking cues from the above generated inputs, the Desk neatly cropped the two images included in the collage and separately ran them through 'Was It AI', an AI detection tool. The tool detected a substantial presence of AI-generated elements in both images. Below are the screenshots of the results. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the collage depicting images of KL Rahul, Athiya Shetty, and their newborn child was AI-generated and not real.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2013 video of astronaut Sunita Williams mentioning Bhagavad Gita in press conference falsely shared as recent after her return to Earth; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 26 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): After Indian-origin NASA astronaut Sunita Williams returned to Earth following an extended nine-month mission in space, several social media users shared a video of a press conference featuring her. Those sharing the video claimed she credited the Bhagavad Gita and Upanishads for her safe return after nine months. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found that the viral video actually dates back to 2013, when Williams was interacting with students at the National Science Centre in Delhi. It is unrelated to her recent return to Earth from her nine-month mission. Excerpts from the original video were edited together and misleadingly shared with a false claim. Claim On March 23, an X (formerly Twitter) user, going by the name 'Dr Krishn Singh', shared a 40-minute clip from a press conference by NASA astronaut Sunita Williams, claiming that she credited Bhagavad Gita & Upanishads for her safe return after nine months. In the video, Sunita Williams says, "I appreciate my Indian heritage and was glad I could bring part of it with me to space. (Lord) Ganesh has been in my house, everywhere I have lived…He had to come with us to space. Indian food, you can never get enough of Indian food…I had samosas in space with me. Bhagavad Gita. I brought a small copy. Interpretations of Upanishads…" The post's caption read: "Sunita Williams credits Bhagwad Gita & Upanishads for her safe return. She stayed in space for 9 months" Here is the link , and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . To verify the claim, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find relevant media reports regarding William's press conference on returning to Earth. However, the search did not yield credible results, citing a press conference. Furthermore, after carefully analysing the viral video, the Desk found the 'Williams In Delhi' band popping up at a 00.08-second time stamp, referring to the press conference not following her return on March 18. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across a report by NDTV dated April 2, 2013, whose headline read: "I had samosas in space with me, says astronaut Sunita Williams". Williams was seen wearing the same attire as in the viral video. Listening to the press conference, the viral excerpts edited together can be heard from the 00:39-00:46 mark, 00:56-01:11 mark, 01:17-01:24 mark, and the 01:42-01:52 mark. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and found a report by News18, dated March 19, 2025, whose headline read: "When Sunita Williams, A Samosa Lover, Talked About Her Connection To Indian Culture" A report section read: "Amid all the buzz about his much-awaited return, an old video of Williams has gone viral on social media. The clip showed the veteran astronaut proudly embracing her Indian roots while admitting the influence of Lord Ganesha and the Bhagavad Gita in her life. She also expressed her love for Indian food and shared that she had samosas at the International Space Station (ISS)." Here is the link to the post. Further, another report was published by Hindustan Times in April 2013, which mentioned that she was interacting with students at the National Science Centre in Delhi, where she highlighted that she takes a tiny part of India every time she goes to space. "Indian-American astronaut Sunita Williams takes a little part of India whenever she goes to space. The 47-year-old, who holds the record for the longest spacewalk by a woman astronaut, told students that "space feels like home now," read the report section. Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video of Sunita Williams talking about the Bhagavad Gita and Upanishads dates back to 2013 when she interacted with students at the National Science Centre in Delhi.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Claim shared in video that Pakistan's Army Headquarters engulfed in flames is false; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 26 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media, claiming to show a massive blast at Pakistan's Army Headquarters. The footage depicted thick smoke billowing as a fiery explosion engulfed the building. People near the scene were seen running in panic to save their lives. Social media users claimed that 20 Pakistani soldiers had lost their lives in the incident. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk revealed that the incident was unrelated to Pakistan. The video shows a blast in Syria, where a fuel tanker exploded in the city of Douma, located in the Damascus countryside. Claim An X user, identified as Dr. Anita Vladivoski, shared a video on March 23, allegedly showing a massive blast at Pakistan's Army Headquarters. The user claimed that a total of 20 Pakistani soldiers had lost their lives in the incident. Here is the link and archive link to the video, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be viewed here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search results via Google Lens also led the Desk to a video posted on an X handle named Rojava Network. The handle, which describes itself as a network of independent journalists covering reports from Syria, Kurdistan, and Turkey, shared the same video on March 18. However, instead of the now-viral claim about a blast in Pakistan, the Rojava Network described the incident as a fuel tanker explosion in the city of Douma, Syria. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting that the content in the viral video matches the video posted by Rojava Network. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to verify the incident in Syria. The search results led the Desk to a video report published by Al Jazeera on March 18, 2025. Al Jazeera also published the same video seen in the viral post but provided additional details that the blast occurred in Syria due to a fuel tanker explosion near the Misraba Bridge in Douma, Damascus countryside. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a second customised keyword search on Google to check if a similar blast had occurred in Pakistan. However, the search yielded no reports confirming such an incident. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a massive blast was from Syria's city of Douma.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered image falsely shared to claim Tamil Nadu BJP chief leader K Annamalai protested against xAI chatbot Grok
content: New Delhi, March 26 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Days after media reports surfaced about the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology's concerns over the recent controversy over xAI chatbot Grok using Hindi slang and abusive language in its responses, a social media post featuring an image of Tamil Nadu BJP chief K Annamalai began circulating online. The image appeared to show him holding a placard that read "Go Back Grok," allegedly as part of a protest against the chatbot. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigation revealed that the image had been digitally altered. The original photo showed K. Annamalai protesting against Tamil Nadu Chief Minister MK Stalin, holding a placard that read, "Shame on you, Stalin." The digitally manipulated version was shared on social media to mislead viewers. Claim An X user with the handle '@AskAatukutti' shared an image on March 17, allegedly showing Tamil Nadu BJP chief K. Annamalai holding a demonstration against AI chatbot Grok after it used Hindi slang and abuses while responding to users. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the image through Google Lens and found multiple users had shared it with a similar claim linked to K Annamalai holding a demonstration against AI chatbot. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search results via Google Lens also led the Desk to an image posted by the BJP Tamil Nadu chief on his official X handle on December 26, 2024. The photo he posted was the same as in the viral post. However, in the original post, his placard displayed the message '#ShameOnYouStalin', whereas it read 'Go Back Grok' in the altered version. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a comparison image highlighting that the image seen in the viral posts matches the one shared by K. Annamalai on his official X handle, except for the message displayed on the placard. Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google regarding the Tamil Nadu BJP chief's demonstration against Chief Minister MK Stalin. The search results led the Desk to a report published by The New Indian Express on December 26, 2024. While the feature image in the report matched the one posted by K. Annamalai on his official social media handles, the report further stated that Annamalai had intensified his attack on the DMK government, with him accusing the state police of exposing the identity of a sexual assault victim from Anna University by disclosing FIR details. Here is the link to the report: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the image of Annamalai holding a placard was digitally altered.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2024 video of Pope Francis' visit to East Timor falsely shared in name of recent protest against Waqf (Amendment) Bill 2024 from Delhi
content: New Delhi, March 26 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of a large group of people taking out a procession, claiming that they were Muslims protesting against the Waqf (Amendment) Bill 2024 in Delhi. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral video dates back to 2024 during Pope Francis' three-day visit to East Timor in September 2024 and is unrelated to the recent protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi. The viral video was shared with a false claim on social media. Claim On March 19, a user named 'ilahi official' shared a video on YouTube of a large group of people taking out a procession, claiming that they were Muslims protesting against the Waqf (Amendment) Bill 2024 in Delhi. The overlying text on the video read: "Indian Muslims only want peace. Don't make the mistake of considering them weak even by mistake. 17 March Jantar Mantar" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a Facebook post dated September 12, 2024, featuring the same video as the viral post. The post's caption, originally in Vietnamese, read: "More than 600,000 people attended the Mass presided over by Pope Francis in Taci Tolu, Timor-Leste, on the afternoon of 10 September 2024." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the news report. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by Reuters published on YouTube on September 10, 2024. The report mentioned that hundreds of thousands of Catholics in East Timor braved the scorching heat to join a Mass with Pope Francis. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. We also compared the posters seen in the viral video and the news report, and below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the two. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to 2024 from East Timor and is unrelated to the recent protest against the Waqf (Amendment) Bill 2024 in Delhi.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2021 video of youth attacking police vehicle in France falsely shared as recent incident following release of Bollywood movie Chhava
content: New Delhi, March 26 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Following tensions that escalated in Nagpur when protesters demanded the demolition of Mughal emperor Aurangzeb's tomb, multiple social media users shared a video of people pelting stones and attacking a police vehicle. Those sharing the video claimed that they were Muslims who were protesting in Paris after the release of the 'Chhava' movie. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral video dates back to January 2021. It shows youths attacking a police vehicle during a video shoot in Pantin, France. It was an old video that had nothing to do with the release of the Bollywood film Chhava in France. Claim On March 21, an X (formerly Twitter) user going by the name 'ocean jain' shared a video of people pelting stones and attacking a police vehicle, claiming that they were Muslims in Paris protesting the release of the 'Chhava' movie. The caption of the post, which garnered 40.9k views, originally in Hindi, read: "In the French capital Paris too, Muslims are rioting since last night after the release of the film 'Chhava'" Here is the link , and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post by the official account of the Independent Union of Police Commissioners (SICP) dated January 25, 2021. The post featured the same video as seen in the viral video. The post's caption, originally in French, read: "Yesterday, in Ville de Pantin, in the city of #courtillières, a crew of #Police was besieged by #individus. The # police were violently attacked, under the amused and filmed gaze of thugs! The #République must not move backward!" Here is the link , and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the news report. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by Le Parisien, a local media outlet in France, dated January 25, 2021. The title of the report read: "Seine-Saint-Denis: Police officers stoned during rap video shoot" A portion of the report read: "Four police officers were violently attacked in Pantin, in the Courtillières district, by a gang of youths filming a rap music video. Two suspects were arrested." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to 2021, when people in France attacked a police vehicle during the filming of a music video in Pantin, and is unrelated to the protest against the 'Chhava' movie.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, Hardik Pandya didn't discuss Yuzvendra Chahal and Dhanashree Verma's divorce; digitally altered video falsely shared as real
content: New Delhi, March 27 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported video of Indian cricketer Hardik Pandya was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that he was allegedly talking about his former teammate Yuzvendra Chahal and his ex-wife Dhanashree Verma's divorce. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the original video is from a Gujarat Titans podcast uploaded on 20 April 2023. In the podcast, Pandya talks about his journey to joining the Gujarat Titans. Further, he does not comment on Chahal's divorce in the entire episode. Notably, the Bandra Family Court granted Yuzvendra Chahal and his estranged wife, Dhanashree Verma, a divorce on March 20, 2025. Claim On March 22, an Instagram user named 'dailycricketposts' shared a video of cricketer Hardik Pandya claiming that he allegedly talked about Chahal's separation from Dhanashree Verma. In the video, Pandya can be heard saying: "...I did get a call from someone the other day asking about Yuzi. People see him as a fun, light-hearted guy. But what he went through after his divorce was tough. It's never easy when a relationship ends. For someone like him, carrying that pain inside must have been harder. I saw him struggle, so it was very important where I was in my stage…" Here is the link , and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. One such post can be found here . We first conducted a customised keyword search on Google to verify the claim. Still, we found no credible reports citing cricketer Hardik Pandya as having commented on Yuzvendra Chahal and Dhanashree Verma's divorce. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk checked the viral post and found that several users commented that it was either fake or AI-generated. Below is a screenshot highlighting this. Further, the Desk noticed Pandya wearing the IPL team Gujarat Titans jersey, and the setup looked like a podcast. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across the extended video uploaded on the Gujarat Titans' official YouTube channel on April 20, 2023. The title of the video read: "Gujarat Titans | GK meets GT Podcast | Episode 2 (Part 1)" At the 5:23 timestamp, Hardik Pandya can be heard talking about the Gujarat Titans and other new franchises that had offered him a spot. The Desk carefully heard the entire podcast, and he did not discuss Chahal and Dhanashree Verma's divorce. Here is the link to the podcast, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Hardik Pandya's video had been manipulated, as in the original video, where he was discussing his journey to join the Gujarat Titans.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated photo of Bollywood actors Kareena Kapoor, Sonakshi Sinha wearing hijabs falsely shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 27 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a collage of two photos, claiming to show Bollywood actors Kareena Kapoor and Sonakshi Sinha wearing hijabs. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk revealed that the images were AI-generated and falsely presented as real on social media. Claim On March 24, an X (formerly Twitter) user, going by the name 'ShatruGhan Sinha' shared a set of two photos, claiming that Bollywood actors Kareena Kapoor and Sonakshi Sinha wore hijabs. The post's caption, which garnered 618.7k views, originally in Hindi, read: "Daughters look lovely in culture, why friends? happy ramadan" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through Reverse Image Search and found several other users shared the same photo with a similar claim. Two such posts can be viewed here and here . To verify the claim, the Desk checked the account where the photo was shared and found that it was shared by a 'Stan' (a person who is fan of a particular celebrity) account. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the photo and found several discrepancies, indicating that it might be AI-generated or digitally altered—for instance, subtle distortions in the facial features. Additionally, the images in the collage had an excessively glossy finish, a common characteristic of AI-generated visuals. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the photo through 'Was It AI', an AI detection tool. The tool detected a substantial presence of AI-generated elements in both images. Below are the screenshots of the results. The Desk ran the viral photo through Sightengine, another AI detection tool, indicating a substantial presence of AI-generated content. Below is a screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral photo was AI-generated.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Two-year-old video of man beating woman in Malaysia falsely shared as recent incident from India; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 27 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of a long-haired man mercilessly thrashing a woman (believed to be his wife) was recently circulated on social media. The video claimed that the incident was reported from India, where a man verbally and physically abused his wife by dragging her by the hair and kicking her in the face. However, in its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video originated from Malaysia and dated back to November 2022, not India. An old and unrelated video was recently shared on social media as recent with a false claim. Claim An X user, identified as Adv. Nazneen Akhtar shared a video on March 26 showing a man mercilessly thrashing a woman. The user claimed the incident took place in India. "Now it seems that there is a trend in India to kill people so that these criminals can become headlines in newspapers. By the way, Savdhaan India has been banned on TV. The live show of Savdhaan India can be seen in real life every day. The cameraman plays the biggest role. He should get an award," the user shared the video with this caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (WARNING: The video contains sensitive visuals) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search results via Google Lens also led the Desk to a report published by the Malaysia-based news portal Alhijrah. While the featured image of the report matched the keyframes used in the investigation, further analysis revealed that the incident was reported from the Malaysian town of Batu 9 Cheras on November 19, 2022. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting that the report's featured image matched the visuals from the viral post. Next, taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk conducted a customized keyword search on Google and came across a report covering the incident published by another Malaysia-based news portal, Says. According to this report, the man seen in the video was identified as Reduan Mahmood, 58, who was charged under Section 323 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt to Adrina Mohd Ariff, 45, by hitting and kicking her at their home in Batu 9, Cheras, on November 14, 2022. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a man mercilessly thrashing a woman was from Malaysia.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Social media post claiming PhonePe offered cashbacks during ongoing IPL season is fake; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 27 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a post claiming that PhonePe was offering a ₹696 cashback during the Indian Premier League season. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the post was fake. PhonePe had not announced any such cashback offer, and the links in the post led to fraudulent, non-functional pages. Claim On March 22, a Facebook user going by the name 'Ipl-Hub' shared a post about PhonePe claiming that it is offering a cashback of Rs 696 this IPL season. The post also shared a link where the user had to register to avail of the cashback. The text in the post, which garnered 979 likes, originally in Hindi, read: "This IPL PhonePe is giving ₹696 free cashback." Here is the link , and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral post through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be viewed here and here To verify the claim, the Desk checked the link to the viral post that read Get.Offer.com, which does not carry the company's name. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. In the next part of the investigation, after the Desk linked on the given link, it led us to a website called 'Summers Gift', which was inaccessible at the time of writing this report. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. The Desk then checked PhonePe's actual domain registration, which showed that the company's website was registered in 2015, through the domain registration website GoDaddy. Here is the link to the website, and below is a screenshot of the same. For further verification, we scanned all of PhonePe's social media handles to check whether they had launched any such cashback scheme, but the search did not yield any results mentioning the claim made in the viral post. Conducting a customised keyword search, the Desk came across a blog on PhonePe's official website, whose headline read: "Stay alert from Cashback frauds!" The blog mentioned that these links and social media pages are cleverly designed to resemble PhonePe's official Website and logo to trick you into believing that the offer is genuine. It added that PhonePe does not offer Cashback or rewards over phone calls or links. "No additional action is needed from you to claim or accept Cashback. PhonePe does not offer Cashback or rewards for phone calls or links. Any URLs, social media posts or phone calls promising Cashback are misleading," the blog read. Here is the link , and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that PhonePe had not launched any cashback offer for the ongoing IPL season.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: This video of Uday Kotak promoting financial platform is digitally altered; false claim shared on social media as real
content: New Delhi, March 28 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Several social media users shared a video featuring Founder and Director of Kotak Mahindra Bank Uday Kotak, claiming that he allegedly promoted an AI-based financial platform developed with the government's support. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral video was manipulated and AI-generated. He did not announce a financial platform. The viral video was shared with a false claim on social media. Claim On March 26, a Facebook user going by the name 'Afterdark' shared a video featuring Uday Kotak, claiming that he allegedly promoted an AI-based financial platform developed with the government's support. In the purported video, he can be heard saying: "With a small investment of ₹21,000, you can earn more than ₹400,000 per week…" The post garnered 3.5k views at the time of writing this article. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation To verify the claim, the Desk first conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports citing the information mentioned by Uday Kotak. However, the search did not yield any credible results. In the next part of the investigation, after carefully analysing the entire video, the Desk at the very start, such as the lip movement, appeared to be distorted and blurred in several frames, indicating that the video was likely manipulated using Artificial Intelligence. Below is the screenshot highlighting the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the video through Hive Moderation, an AI-detecting tool that denoted that it contained deepfake or AI-generated content. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool search and came across a YouTube video by Kotak Mahindra Bank dated May 14, 2014. The title read: "Uday Kotak's views on Young & Digital." After listening to the entire report, the Desk noticed that nowhere in the 15:13-second video did he mention any investment platform or investment opportunities. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk noticed that the attire worn by Uday Kotak and the background in the YouTube video were similar to those in the viral video. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral and YouTube videos. Furthermore, the Desk ran the viral video Resemble.ai to check if the audio was AI-generated. Below is a screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video featuring Uday Kotak promoting the investment platform is AI-generated, and he did not make such an announcement.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of fire incident in Ghana falsely shared as Hindu colony burning in Bangladesh; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 28 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media, claiming to show a Hindu colony being burnt down in Bangladesh. The footage depicted a massive fire engulfing a large area, destroying multiple structures. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video does not show a Hindu colony burning in Bangladesh. The footage is actually from a fire incident at Kantamanto Market, located in the central business district of Accra, Ghana. An old and unrelated video was misleadingly shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An Instagram user identified as 'pappu_yadav_8601' shared on March 24 a video allegedly showing a Hindu colony being burnt down in Bangladesh. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search results via Google Lens also led the Desk to a video posted on an X handle named Yung Bull on January 2, 2025. The user shared the same video as seen in the viral post, but the caption described it as a fire incident at the Kantamanto Market in Accra, Ghana. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting the content in the viral video matches that of the video posted by the user on X earlier in January. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the findings above, the Desk conducted a customized keyword search on Google regarding the massive fire that erupted at the Kantamanto Market in Ghana. The search led to a report published by the Anker Research Institute. The report included an image matching the keyframe used in the Desk's investigation. A detailed analysis mentioned that a catastrophe unfolded in Ghana, where a fire decimated the secondhand clothing market of Kantamanto in Accra. "Though the reasons for how the fire started and who or what was responsible for triggering the blaze are still unclear, it seems quite apparent that thousands of people working as retailers and traders have lost their livelihoods. Families have been affected and are now without income," the report stated. Here is the link to the report along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of a fire engulfing a large area does not depict a Hindu colony being burnt down in Bangladesh. Instead, it shows a fire outbreak at the Kantamanto Market in Accra, Ghana, earlier this year.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Photos of brutally assaulted boy in Yemen falsely shared linking it to Rajasthan incident where Dalit man thrashed for touching water pot
content: New Delhi, March 28 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A screenshot of a news report and two purported images of an individual covered in bruises were recently circulated on social media. Users claimed that the photos depicted the same person—a Dalit man—who was brutally thrashed by a brick kiln owner in Rajasthan for touching a pot, as mentioned in the news report. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found this claim false. The images of the bruised boy were actually of a 14-year-old who was assaulted by his father in Al-Mahwit, Yemen, in October 2020, and were not related to India. Meanwhile, the screenshot of the news report referred to a separate incident from January 2025, in which a brick kiln owner in Rajasthan allegedly thrashed a Dalit man for touching a water pot. Old and unrelated images were falsely circulated on social media, misleadingly linking them to the Rajasthan incident. Claim An X user, identified as Naeem Ahmed, shared on March 21 a screenshot of a news report along with two purported images of an individual covered in bruises. The user claimed that the photos were of the same individual belonging to the Dalit community, who was brutally thrashed by a brick kiln owner in Rajasthan for touching a pot, as mentioned in the news report. "Aurangzeb was cruel, but who are these people...? He had just taken water to drink! He was beaten to death! And now they are asking for 1.5 lakh rupees from his family to let him go," the user shared the post with this caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the images attached to the post through Google Lens and found multiple users shared them with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with archived versions viewed here and here respectively. The search results via Google Lens also led the Desk to a report published on a Yemen-based news portal on October 5, 2020. The news report carried multiple images, some of which matched the pictures of the boy (covered in bruises) that the Desk analysed. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. According to the details mentioned in the report, it spoke of an incident from Yemen, where a 40-year-old man named Rashid Muhammad Al-Qahili was arrested for torturing his 14-year-old son, Shamikh Rashid Al-Qahili. A police official, speaking about the incident, confirmed that on October 3, the accused tied the child up with ropes, tortured him, and violently beat him with wires and whips, causing severe injuries to various parts of his body. The images attached to the report (including the ones analysed by the Desk) showed the boy who was severely covered in bruises after the incident. Below is a combination image highlighting the images attached to the news report, which matched those from the viral post. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google regarding an incident in which a Dalit tractor driver was brutally beaten up by a brick kiln owner for touching a water pot in Rajasthan's Jhunjhunu on January 21, 2025. Police officials said that the incident took place at a brick kiln under the Pacheri Kalan police station area. The victim was taken to Rewari in Haryana by car, where he was beaten up with a belt. Further, the report added that cash worth Rs 1.5 lakh was also demanded from the victim's family for his release. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the images showing an individual covered in bruises were not those of the Dalit man who was thrashed by a brick kiln owner for touching a water pot in Rajasthan. The images of the individual in bruises were of a Yemeni boy who his father thrashed, and the incident dated back to October 2020. Meanwhile, the incident of a Dalit man being beaten by a brick kiln owner for touching a water pot in Rajasthan took place in January 2025.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video falsely claimed bridge collapse in Rajasthan's Sikar; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 28 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A recently circulated social media video claimed to show a flyover bridge in Rajasthan's Sikar collapsing. Users claimed the incident occurred at 9 AM on March 9, when the flyover bridge suddenly crashed. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was digitally altered and shared on social media to mislead viewers. Claim A Facebook user identified as 'Saroj Saini' shared a video on March 11, allegedly showing a flyover bridge in Rajasthan's Sikar collapsing. The user claimed the incident occurred on March 9, 2025, at 9 a.m. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found numerous users shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . In the next stage of the investigation, the Desk carefully examined the viral video and noticed it displayed strange or implausible characteristics. These included objects disappearing into thin air, fire erupting and suddenly being extinguished before reigniting, and two individuals who appeared to be part of the construction team vanishing abruptly. Next, taking cues from the above findings, the Desk ran one of the extracted keyframes of the video through 'Sight Engine,' an AI detection tool. However, the result did not conclusively confirm that the video was AI-generated. Below is a screenshot highlighting the result: Additionally, to verify the above findings, the Desk, through search results, again examined a video posted by an Instagram user named 'ridar3200' on March 12. The video he posted matched the visuals seen in the viral post; however, he did not specify the location of the incident. Next, the Desk ran this video through the InVid tool, extracted multiple keyframes, and analysed one using Sight Engine again. This time, the AI detection confidence was measured at 95%. Below is a screenshot of the result: Similarly, the Desk again analyzed another video posted by a user named 'shazia_wani_07' on March 8. The visuals of the video she posted also matched the viral post, and the AI detection confidence for the extracted keyframes in this case was found to be 99%. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, based on the above findings, the Desk concluded that the video showing a flyover bridge collapse in Rajasthan's Sikar was AI-generated.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Water spilling from rooftop pool in China's hotel falsely shared as recent from Bangkok after massive earthquake jolted Thailand
content: New Delhi, March 31 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Following the massive 7.7-magnitude earthquake that struck northwest of Sagaing in central Myanmar, which was followed by a 6.7-magnitude aftershock minutes later, multiple social media users shared a video showing people running in panic as a massive surge of water poured over them. Those sharing the video claimed that the water had washed away a crowd in Bangkok due to the earthquake. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral video was shared with a false claim on social media platforms. Upon further verification, it was confirmed that the footage actually depicted the effects of an earthquake in China, not Bangkok. Notably, a strong 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck central Myanmar on March 28. The ruling junta reported on March 29 that the death toll had surpassed 1600. Claim On March 28, an X (formerly Twitter) user 'Ian Collins' shared a video featuring people running amok as a massive amount of water poured on them, claiming that water washed away the crowd in Bangkok following the earthquake. The caption of the post, which garnered 11.2k views, read: "Water from rooftop pool spills after #earthquake, washes away crowd in #Bangkok #bangkokearthquake #Thailand #Thailand #Myanmar #Myanmarquake" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a report by MSN News dated March 28, whose headline read: "Debris falls from 31-storey building sending residents fleeing as earthquake hits China." The report featured similar visuals to those seen in the viral video. "At 2:20 p.m. Beijing time on March 28, a 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck Myanmar, causing strong tremors in Ruili City, Dehong Dai and Jingpo Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan Province, near the China-Myanmar border," the report read. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the news report. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk ran a customised keyword search to find relevant media reports and came across a report by The World Watch, dated March 29, whose headline read: "Rooftop Pool Water Explodes Onto Streets of People After Quake" "A chilling video has surfaced from China's Yunnan province following a powerful earthquake that struck Myanmar on Friday. The 7.7-magnitude quake sent shockwaves across the region, reaching neighboring countries, including Thailand and China. In Yunnan, the tremors triggered the collapse of a rooftop pool from a high-rise building, sending a massive wave of water falling to the streets below. The footage shows people frantically running for their lives as the pool's water consumes the area, sweeping some off their feet," read the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk carefully scanned the viral video and found some hoardings with text written in Chinese, confirming that the video is from China. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video showed the effects of the earthquake in China and not Bangkok.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2023 riot video from Bangladesh falsely shared in name of recent unrest in West Bengal's Malda
content: New Delhi, March 31 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid reports of violence between two communities in West Bengal's Malda, a video showing an unruly mob vandalising vehicles and setting them ablaze was recently shared on social media, claiming to be linked to the same incident. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk revealed that the video was unrelated to India. Instead, it depicted a violent protest in Bangladesh's Sylhet district in November 2023 during a demonstration by the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). An old and unrelated video was misleadingly shared on social media with a false claim. Meanwhile, according to local sources, it is important to note that unrest in West Bengal's Malda began on March 27 after a religious procession passed by a place of worship in Mothabari on Wednesday evening. The violence led to incidents of arson, vandalism, and physical attacks, resulting in the arrest of 50 people in connection with the clashes. Claim An X user named 'Islamist Cannibal' shared a video on March 28, allegedly showing an unruly mob setting fire to vehicles parked on the streets. The user claimed the video depicted an incident in West Bengal's Malda, where people from a particular faith attacked Hindus with stones and set their vehicles on fire. "Islamist mayhem continues in Malda, West Bengal. A mob of Muslims set fire to Hindus' vehicles and attacked them with stones. Are Hindus in India so helpless that they cannot even retaliate?" the user wrote in the caption while sharing the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that multiple users had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. Additionally, the search results via Google Lens led the Desk to a YouTube video published by the Bangladesh-based news channel Prothom Alo on November 26, 2023. The video, an extended version of the one in the viral post, was shared with the description: "Torchlight procession and vehicle vandalism in support of the blockade in Sylhet." Here is the link and archive link to the video, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting that the visuals seen in the YouTube video match one of the keyframes the Desk used for investigation. In the next phase of the investigation, taking cues from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google about the arson reported in Sylhet in November 2023. The search results led the Desk to a report published by the Bangladesh-based news portal The Daily Sylhet Mirror on November 26, 2023. The feature image in the report matched one of the keyframes used in the Desk's investigation. A detailed analysis of the report confirmed that widespread vandalism and arson were reported during a 48-hour blockade in Sylhet. The BNP and its allies had called the blockade against the then-Sheikh Hasina-led Awami League government, during which mobs torched vehicles in Sylhet's Subid Bazar. Here is the link to the report and a screenshot: Additionally, the Desk's customised keyword search about the Sylhet incident led to a post from the official X handle of the West Bengal Police on March 28, 2025. The post confirmed: "The attached video of arson and vandalism is being circulated on social media from certain quarters as an incident in the Malda district. This claim is completely FAKE. This video captures events from November 2023 in the Sylhet region of Bangladesh and has no connection whatsoever with yesterday's incident in Malda." Here is the link to the post and a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing large-scale arson on the streets by an unruly mob was unrelated to India. The video originally depicted violence that erupted in Bangladesh's Sylhet district during a 48-hour blockade. The BNP and its allies had called the embargo against the then-Sheikh Hasina-led government.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered image falsely shared to claim shopkeeper showcased placard against PM Modi
content: New Delhi, April 1 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media post recently shared an image allegedly depicting a disrespectful statement against Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The image showed a poster displayed in front of a small shop, highlighting a message for its visitors that 'until Modiji starts speaking the truth, nothing would be given on credit'. In its investigation, however, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the image was digitally altered. The original image showed a message displayed on a poster outside a shop that read, "Kindly do not ask for things on credit; we, too, have taken a loan." A digitally altered image was shared on social media to mislead viewers. Claim A Facebook page identified as 'Love me India' shared an image on March 29, allegedly depicting a disrespectful statement against Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The image showed a poster hooked outside a shop with a message that read: "Till the time Modiji will not start speaking the truth, nothing will be given on credit." Since being posted on social media platforms, the post received around 5.8K shares and 46K reactions (when this article was published). Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the image through Google Lens and found that another user, '@BappiLaher08001,' had shared it with similar claims. The post can be viewed here , with its archived version available here . The search result via Google Lens also led the Desk to multiple posts, confirming that the same image had been shared in the past by different users as well. Here are links to two such posts ( Link 1 , Link 2 ), along with their archived versions ( Link 1 , Link 2 ): A comparison of these posts made it clear that the viral picture was old. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk again ran the image seen in the viral post through Google Lens. The search led the Desk to a picture uploaded 2018 on a Facebook page named Nagina, District-Bijnor - UP. While the picture posted by the page matched the setting of the image in the viral post, the only difference spotted was the line written on the poster outside the shop. In the Facebook post, the text read: "Kindly do not ask for things on credit; we too have taken a loan." Nowhere was there any mention of PM Modi on the pamphlet. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting that the image in the viral post was altered, as the original image on social media displayed a different message. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the image depicting a disrespectful statement against PM Modi was digitally altered.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2021 news bulletin on Covid lockdown restrictions in Delhi shared with false claim as recent announcement
content: New Delhi, April 1 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported video clip of a news bulletin wherein the anchor discussed the lockdown restrictions was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that the lockdown will be imposed in Delhi till April 25, 2025. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral video dates back to 2021, when lockdown restrictions were imposed in Delhi for a week due to COVID-19. A false claim was shared on social media. Claim On March 30, a Thread user named deepak_sahin shared a clip of a news bulletin claiming that a six-day lockdown would be imposed in Delhi. In the viral clip, the presenter allegedly says: "Luckdown will be imposed till April 25 from 10 pm. Chandni Chowk has been closed…" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk first conducted a customised keyword search on Google to verify the claim and find relevant media reports. However, it did not yield credible reports or official announcements about any upcoming lockdown in Delhi. Further, if such a major decision had been made, mainstream news media would have covered it widely. Continuing the investigation, the Desk ran the keyframes through Google Lens and found an extended version of the clip uploaded on Republic Bharat's official Facebook channel on April 19, 2021. The report's title read: "Lockdown returns in Delhi, strict restrictions announced from 10 pm tonight till 5 am next Monday". This makes it clear that the mention was about the lockdown to manage COVID-19 in Delhi back then. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted another set of customised keyword searches to find media reports and came across a report by India TV, dated April 19, 2021. According to the report, the restrictions will remain in place from 10 PM tonight till 5 AM next Monday. Kejriwal said that the city's health system is under stress, adding that hospitals are facing a shortage of oxygen and ICU beds. "Amid an exponential rise in Covid-19 cases, Delhi has been placed under lockdown till next Monday morning (April 26), Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal announced on Monday. The restrictions will remain in place from 10 PM tonight till 5 AM next Monday. Kejriwal said that city's health system is under stress, adding that hospitals are facing shortage of oxygen and ICU beds." Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to 2021, when a lockdown was imposed in Delhi due to COVID-19.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of 2024 protest near Rajasthan's Chief Minister's residence falsely shared as recent incident of Mahabodhi Mukti Andolan in Bihar
content: New Delhi, April 1 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of a massive crowd in a scuffle with police officers, claiming that the protestors were demanding justice for the Mahabodhi Mukti movement. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral video dates back to December 2024, when a protest was held near Rajasthan's Chief Minister's residence. Notably, a group of Buddhist monks, leaders, and followers entered the 14th day (March 25) of an indefinite hunger strike at the Mahabodhi Temple in Bodh Gaya, Bihar, in central India, demanding full administrative control of the site, considered the most sacred by Buddhists. The protest challenges the existing management structure established under the Bodh Gaya Temple Act of 1949, which grants a majority in the temple's management to Hindu committee members despite its centrality to Buddhism. Claim On March 26, an X (formerly Twitter) user named 'Rani Boudh - ASP' shared a video of a massive crowd in a scuffle with police officers, claiming that the protestors were demanding justice for the Mahabodhi Mahabihar Mukti movement. The caption of the post, which garnered 8,737 views, originally in Hindi, read: "India is the country of Buddha. We have been knocking the doors of the system for a long time, demanding justice for the Mahabodhi Mahabihar Mukti movement and are getting nothing. Now the time has come to break those doors. Shame on the Bihar government and the Central government." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. On carefully analysing the viral video the Desk noticed Indian National Congress flags, hinting that this video may not be from the Buddhist monks' protest in Bihar's Bodh Gaya. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk again ran the keyframes of the viral video through a Reverse Image Search and found the same video uploaded on Facebook by the official account of the Indian Youth Congress on December 21, 2024. According to the post, a protest was held by the Youth Congress near the Rajasthan Chief Minister's residence in Jaipur against insulting comments made about Dr B.R. Ambedkar in Parliament and the issue of unemployment in Rajasthan. The caption of the post read: "CM House Gherao, Jaipur. Rajasthan Youth Congress workers led by IYC President Shri Uday Bhanu Chib held a strong protest against the insult of Baba Saheb Ambedkar in Parliament and rising unemployment in the state!" Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and Facebook post. On further scanning the search results, the Desk found the same video with the same caption uploaded on the official YouTube channel of Jharkhand Youth Congress. Here is the link , and below is a screenshot of the same. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find relevant media reports and came across a report by ABP Live dated December 21, 2024, whose headline read: "Jaipur: Youth Congress Workers Lathicharged, Water Cannons Deployed Amid Bid To Gherao Rajasthan CM Residence" "A score of youth Congress workers on Saturday gathered to stage protest against the BJP-led state government in Rajasthan against the issue of unemployment, drug addiction, and MSP. The Congress workers had planned to gherao CM Bhajanlal Sharma's residence in Jaipur over the issue. The demonstration was named 'Naukri Do, Nasha Nahi' campaign," read the portion of the report. Here is the link to the report. Another report was published by Patrika on December 21, 2024, whose headline read: "Rajasthan Politics: Youth Congress's strong protest in Jaipur, police lathicharged workers; sprayed water on them" The report mentioned: "Hundreds of Youth Congress workers in Jaipur protested against the Bhajanlal government on Saturday over unemployment. During this, Sachin Pilot and Govind Singh Dotasara gave speeches at the Shahid Smarak. After which Congress workers proceeded to surround the CM residence. But the police chased away all the workers at the Shahid Smarak itself." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to December 2024, when a protest was held near Rajasthan's Chief Minister's residence

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video showing violent clash between two cousins in Bangladesh shared as recent incident of religious hate crime against Hindus
content: New Delhi, April 1 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media claimed to show another incident of religious hate crimes against Hindus in Bangladesh. The video allegedly showed radical Islamists brutally attacking three Hindus in Bangladesh with an axe for cutting water hyacinths from the river. However, in its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was unrelated to any religious hate crime incident. Instead, it depicted a violent clash that erupted over a property dispute between two cousins (belonging to the same community) in Bangladesh's Kaliganj area. An unrelated video was shared on social media to mislead viewers regarding religious hate crimes in Bangladesh. Claim An X user identified as '@HinduVoice_in' shared a video on March 31, allegedly showing another incident of a religious hate crime against Hindus in Bangladesh. The video depicted an alleged incident from Bangladesh's Gazipur district, where Islamists attacked three Hindu people with an axe for cutting water hyacinths from the river. All three victims were said to be in critical condition, fighting for their lives. At the time of posting this article, the viral video had been viewed by 24.1K people. Here is the link and archive link to the video, along with a screenshot. (Warning: The video contains sensitive visuals) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, to corroborate the claims made in the viral post, the Desk conducted a customized keyword search on Google and came across a report published by the Bangladesh-based Bengali-language newspaper, Dainik Desh Rupantor. The report, published on March 31, 2025, provided extensive details of the incident, stating that it occurred due to a long-standing property dispute between two cousins named Ramcharan and Narayan in Bangladesh's Kaliganj area. "On Sunday (March 30), Ramcharan and his son Jhantu Das attacked their cousins Narayan, Giribala, and Haradhan Chandra Das with axes in Kaliganj due to previous enmity over a land dispute," the report mentioned. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing the attack against individuals with an axe does not depict an incident of religious hate crime against Hindus in Bangladesh.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Social media post claiming govt providing jobs to all unemployed youth under One Family, One Job scheme is baseless; details inside
content: New Delhi, April 1 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Several social media users shared a post with users claiming that the Government is providing jobs to all unemployed youth under the One Family, One Job scheme. However, the PTI Fact Check investigated and found that the viral post was shared with a false claim. Upon further search, it was found that the central government does not have any scheme named 'One Family One Job scheme' to provide jobs to unemployed youth. Claim On March 24, a Facebook user, going by the name 'Govt Jobs & Gov.t News Daily', shared a post claiming that the government is providing jobs to all unemployed youth under the One Family, One Job scheme. The post's caption, originally in Hindi, read: "One Family One Job Scheme: Government gives employment to all unemployed youth. Know how?" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation To verify the claim, the Desk checked the hyperlink with the viral post and found it led to https://ytsave.online/ek-parivar-ek-naukri-yojana/ . The Desk further investigated to see that the domain was registered on 13 July 2024. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find relevant media reports regarding the claim made in the viral post. However, it did not yield credible reports or official job announcements for all unemployed youths. Further, if such a major decision had been made, mainstream news media would have covered it widely. Taking the investigation ahead, the Desk scanned the official website of the Ministry of Labour and Employment and looked for details about this scheme. However, we did not find any information regarding any such scheme. Here is the link to the website, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the central government is not providing jobs to all unemployed youth under the One Family One Job scheme.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Viral video of hospital staff protecting patient during earthquake falsely shared in name of Myanmar; details inside
content: New Delhi, April 2 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media claimed to depict scenes from a hospital in Myanmar on Friday (March 28), when a massive earthquake, measuring 7.7 on the Richter scale, struck the nation. The video showed hospital staff running towards a patient to save his life while they experienced massive tremors caused by the earthquake. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was unrelated to Myanmar. Instead, it depicted scenes from Ruili People's Hospital in southwestern China's Yunnan Province, where a surgeon and a medical team risked their safety to protect a patient amid tremors from the Myanmar earthquake that were felt across the region. It is pertinent to note that more than 2,700 people have been killed and thousands injured in Myanmar following a 7.7-magnitude earthquake, with tremors also felt in neighboring countries. The head of Myanmar's military government, Senior General Min Aung Hlaing, stated that so far, 2,719 people have been confirmed dead, 4,521 injured, and 441 missing. Claim On March 31, an X user '@IPSinghSp' shared a video claiming it depicted scenes from a hospital in Myanmar on Friday (March 28), when a massive 7.7 magnitude earthquake struck the nation. The footage showed hospital staff running towards a patient to save his life while experiencing massive tremors caused by the earthquake. "This is a great example of humanity. The doctor and nurse did not abandon their patient but ran towards the bed to save him. #MyanmarEarthquake," the user shared the video with the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively: The search via Google Lens also led the Desk to a video posted on an Instagram handle run by China Central Television, a national television broadcaster of China. The handle posted the video on March 31, 2025, which exactly matches the visuals from the viral post but was shared with a caption stating that the video was shot at China's Ruili People's Hospital and not in Myanmar. "When the earthquake hit, the surgeon and medical team at Ruili People's Hospital in southwest China's Yunnan Province stayed calm, risking their safety to protect the patient. In that moment, their devotion to life outshone all fear," the post reads. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting that the content seen in the viral video matches that of the video posted by the China-based news portal. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video originally depicted scenes from Ruili People's Hospital in southwestern China's Yunnan Province, where a surgeon and a medical team risked their safety to protect a patient as tremors from the Myanmar earthquake were felt across the Chinese region.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Bus fire video from Jharkhand's Dumka falsely shared in name of fire incident happened in Rajasthan's Barmer; details inside
content: New Delhi, April 2 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it showed buses stationed at the Barmer bus stop in Rajasthan erupting flames. The users claimed the incident occurred on March 30, when six buses stationed at the stand were gutted by fire, killing at least three people. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found the video to be unrelated to that of the Barmer bus stand. The video originally showed five buses parked in a field near Basukinath bus stand in Jharkhand's Dumka catching fire. No reports of any casualties were noted in the incident, which occurred on March 29. A video from Jharkhand's Dumka was shared on social media with a misleading claim. Claim An Instagram user 'itz_pk_royal__5k' shared a video on April 1 allegedly showing buses stationed at Barmer bus stand in Rajasthan catching fire. The user claimed the incident occurred on March 30, and three lives were lost, while seven buses erupted in flames. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search results via Google Lens also led the Desk to a video published by News18 Jharkhand on its official X (formerly Twitter) handle on March 29. The video showed a setting similar to the viral clip, confirming it was from Dumka. The caption along with it reads, "In Dumka, fire rages at Basukinath bus stand, five buses burnt to ashes." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the content seen in the viral social media video, which matches the video published by the news portal, confirming it to be from Jharkhand's Dumka. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google regarding the Dumka bus fire incident. The search result led the Desk to a report published by Navbharat Times on March 29, which stated that five buses parked in a field near Basukinath bus stand in Jharkhand's Dumka caught fire. "In the fire that broke out in Basukinath, two buses of Ajit Roadways and three other buses of Pagal Baba Company were burnt to ashes," the report added. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Additionally, the Desk conducted another customized keyword search on Google to determine whether any such incident or a related incident had occurred in Rajasthan's Barmer. However, the search did not yield any reports confirming such an incident. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing several buses gutted in fire was from Jharkhand's Dumka, not Barmer, Rajasthan.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 9-year-old video shared to falsely claim audience gave good reviews for Salman Khan-starrer Sikandar; details inside
content: New Delhi, April 2 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Following the release of Salman Khan's Sikandar, several social media users shared a video of a large crowd exiting a theater, claiming it showed audience reactions to the film. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk revealed that the viral video actually depicted public reviews of the 2014 movie Kick, not Salman Khan's latest release, Sikandar. The video was misleadingly shared on social media, with a false claim. Notably, Sikandar marks Salman Khan and Rashmika Mandanna's first on-screen collaboration and also serves as Salman Khan's first project with director AR Murugadoss. Claim On March 30, an X (formerly Twitter) user, going by the name Imtiyaz Ali, shared a video of viewers' positive reviews claiming to be of Salman Khan's movie Sikandar. The caption of the post, which garnered 1712 views, read: "Sikandar first public movie review ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ #SalmanKhan #Sikandar #SikandarReview" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared it with similar claims. One such post can be found here . To verify the claim, the Desk carefully analysed the viral video and found a ticker that read: "bollywoodhungama.com exclusive" at the start of the video. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Further examining the video, we found the viewers mentioning 'Jackline' (Fernandez) and her performance in the movie at a 1:06-second time stamp. Taking a cue from all the finds, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across the same video uploaded on Bollywood Hungama's official YouTube channel on July 25, 2014. The title of the video read: "First Day First Show | Kick" Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a screenshot highlighting the similarities between the viral and YouTube videos. The Desk also noticed that clips showing the audience talking about the movie Kick were removed from the viral video to insinuate that the audience was praising Salman Khan's recent release, Sikander. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to 2014 after the audience watched Kick and not the recent release of Salman Khan's Sikander.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of nurses protecting infants during China quake falsely shared as from Myanmar; details inside
content: New Delhi, April 2 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ) : A CCTV video recently circulated on social media, claiming to show a hospital in Myanmar during the 7.7-magnitude earthquake that struck the country on March 28. The footage depicted nurses shielding infants as the hospital shook. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk revealed that the video was actually recorded in China's Yunnan province. It showed nurses ensuring patients' safety as tremors from the Myanmar earthquake were felt in the region. The viral claim is misleading. Claim On March 31, an X (formerly Twitter) user named Intrigue Archive shared a video of nurses trying to protect newborn babies, claiming that the incident occurred during the earthquake jolted Bangkok, Thailand. The post's caption read: "Nurses protect and shield newborns as Myanmar earthquake tremors rock hospital. This is why I admire and respect nurses so much.' Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively: On further scanning the search results, the Desk found the same video on China Global Television Network's (CGTN) official YouTube handle. The title of the report, dated March 20, 2025, read: "Nurses in SW China protect newborn babies during earthquake in Myanmar" According to the report, the incident occurred on 28 March and identified the location as Ruili City, China. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the news report. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find relevant media reports and came across a report by the Indian Express dated March 31, 2025.
