According to the report, CCTV footage from the Jingcheng Hospital's maternity center shows the nurses in a ward filled with cradles when the tremors began. The report's title read: "Does This Video Show Nurses Protecting Babies in Bangkok During Earthquake? No!" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video showed the incident in China's Yunnan province.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated photo of Mahendra Singh Dhoni with PM Modi shared on social media with false claim; details
content: New Delhi, April 3 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): An image purportedly showing Prime Minister Narendra Modi standing alongside former Indian cricket team captain Mahendra Singh Dhoni was recently shared on social media. Users claimed Dhoni had joined the Bharatiya Janata Party and thus both wore the party's sash in the image. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the image was AI-generated and was shared on social media as accurate with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user, 'K Shankar,' shared an image on April 1 showing Prime Minister Narendra Modi standing alongside former Indian cricket team captain Mahendra Singh Dhoni. The user claimed that Dhoni had joined the Bharatiya Janata Party and thus the two were seen wearing the party's sash in the image. "MS Dhoni joins the BJP. Nightmare for opposition," the user captioned the post. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the image through Google Lens and found multiple other users who shared it on social media with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customized keyword search on Google regarding the claim that the former Indian cricket team captain had joined the BJP in the presence of PM Modi. The search did not yield the Desk to any news reports that could verify the claim. Had such a development occurred, the media would have covered it extensively. Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analyzed the viral image to identify any key findings that could potentially help verify the claim. Upon doing so, the Desk found multiple inconsistencies in the image, indicating that it might be AI-generated or digitally altered. For instance, subtle distortions in PM Modi's facial features were noticeable. Additionally, the image had a glossy finish, a common characteristic of AI-generated visuals. Below is a screenshot highlighting these key findings: In the subsequent part of the investigation, taking cues from the above findings, the Desk ran the image through Hive Moderation, an AI detection tool. The tool detected a substantial presence of AI-generated elements in the image. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the image showing PM Modi standing alongside former Indian cricket team captain Mahendra Singh Dhoni was AI-generated and shared on social media with a false claim.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2013 video of Maharashtra cop slapping NCP leader shared as recent with false claim; details inside
content: New Delhi, April 3 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of a police official slapping a man was recently circulated on social media. Users claimed that the official in the video was DySP Ganesh Gawande, who allegedly slapped NCP (then undivided party) leader Pramod Mohod after the latter misbehaved with police officials and tried to obstruct their work during a raid in Chandrapur. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found the claim to be false. The video dates back to 2013 and shows police official Ganesh Gawande slapping Mohod. Mohod had reportedly misbehaved with policemen during a protest over the dismissal of coal mine workers in Chandrapur. An old video with a false claim was recently shared on social media . Claim A Facebook user 'satyendranath74' shared a video on March 18, allegedly showing a police official slapping a man during a confrontation. The video claimed that DySP Ganesh Gawande slapped NCP (then undivided party) leader Pramod Mohod after the latter misbehaved and obstructed the police team's work during a raid in Chandrapur. "DySP Ganesh Gawande slapped Chandrapur NCP leader Pramod Mohod. The leader saw stars in the daytime. He was misbehaving with the police to stop the raid. DySP slapped him," read the text inscribed on the video frames. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found various users had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , respectively. The search results via Google Lens also led the Desk to a video published by TV9 Marathi on the video-sharing platform Dailymotion. The video, posted by the channel, matched the visuals in the viral post. However, further analysis revealed that it was first uploaded in 2013, with a caption reading, "Chandrapur DySP Ganesh Gawande badly beats NCP leader." Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the video published by the channel: In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from these findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google regarding a police official slapping an NCP leader in 2013. The search led to a video published on the YouTube channel Maharashtra Bhumi on February 16, 2025. The video explained the context of the 2013 incident that led to the police official taking action against the NCP leader. According to the details in the video, several coal mine workers had been dismissed suddenly. The workers alleged that the company was removing local employees and hiring outsiders. They staged a protest, which NCP leaders and workers joined. During the rally, Pramod Mohod and others demanded entry into the factory and misbehaved with the police officers. As Mohod's misbehavior escalated, Ganesh Gawande slapped him. Following this incident, Gawande was transferred. Here is the link to the video: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video of a police official slapping then NCP leader dates back to 2013. The altercation did not start because the leader obstructed a police raid, as claimed. Instead, it happened during a protest over coal mine worker dismissals, where Pramod Mohod misbehaved with police officers, leading to DySP Ganesh Gawande slapping him. An old video was falsely shared as a recent incident with misleading claims.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Did upset audiences attack Salman Khan's residence after watching Sikandar? Video from Syria shared on social media with fake claim
content: New Delhi, April 3 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video claiming to show an attack on Bollywood actor Salman Khan's residence in Mumbai was recently shared on social media. The post alleged that a disgruntled group stormed Khan's home on March 30, supposedly upset after watching his recent film Sikandar. It further claimed that an investigation was underway while Salman Khan and his family were safe. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk revealed that the video originated from Syria. The footage depicts fighters loyal to Syria's ousted leader, Bashar al-Assad, launching a deadly attack on government forces, killing at least 13 security personnel on March 6. An unrelated video was misleadingly shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An Instagram page 'gwalior.say' shared a video on April 1, alleging that unidentified attackers fired at Salman Khan's residence in Mumbai. The post claimed that the assailants were angry after watching his film Sikander and thus opened fire at his Galaxy Apartments home in Bandra, Mumbai. "Bollywood superstar Salman Khan's upcoming film Sikander is generating tremendous excitement among fans. However, shocking news has emerged. Reports suggest that unknown attackers opened fire at Salman Khan's Galaxy Apartment in Bandra late on Sunday night. This incident has sent shockwaves through Bollywood and among his fans. Sources indicate that a disgruntled group may be behind the attack, allegedly angry about Sikander. The police are investigating, but no suspects have been identified yet. Salman Khan and his family are reportedly safe, though the incident has raised deep concerns," the post read. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation To verify the claim, the PTI Fact Check Desk conducted a keyword search on Google but found no credible news reports confirming an attack on Salman Khan's residence. Had such an incident occurred, the media would have covered it extensively. Next, the Desk analysed the viral video using the InVid tool to extract keyframes. A Google Lens search on these frames led to multiple news reports confirming that the video did not depict an attack in Mumbai. Instead, it originated from Syria and showed an assault against government forces by fighters loyal to Bashar al-Assad. A March 7, 2025, report by Reuters confirmed that the viral video actually showed a targeted attack by Assad-linked fighters against security forces in Syria's Jableh region, resulting in at least 13 casualties. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting keyframes used by the Desk in the investigation, matched with those from the video attached to the Reuters report. The video does not depict an attack on Salman Khan's residence but an incident in Syria. Additionally, the Google Lens search also led the Desk to a report by NBC News, which, like Reuters, confirmed that the video shared on social media was related to an attack by Bashar al-Assad-led fighters in the coastal region of Jableh, Syria, on March 6. Here is the link to the report: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim that Salman Khan's residence was attacked in Mumbai was false. The viral video actually originates from Syria and depicts an attack by fighters loyal to Bashar al-Assad against government forces.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2021 video of Rahul Gandhi visiting Mata Vaishno Devi temple falsely shared as a recent visit during Chaitra Navratri
content: New Delhi, April 4 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users have shared a video featuring the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, claiming that he visited Mata Vaishno Devi on the second day of Chaitra Navratri 2025. However, PTI Fact Check investigated and found that the viral video actually dates back to 2021, when Rahul Gandhi visited the Mata Vaishno Devi temple. The video is unrelated to Chaitra Navratri 2025 and has been shared on social media with a false claim. Claim On March 31, a Facebook user shared a video featuring Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, claiming that he visited Mata Vaishno Devi on the second day of Chaitra Navratri. The post's caption, originally in Hindi, read: "Congress MP Rahul Gandhi and Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi reached to visit Mata Vaishno Devi on the second day of Chaitra Navratri. Earlier, last year, Rahul Gandhi had also reached out to visit Mata Vaishno Devi." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . To verify the claim, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find relevant data to corroborate the viral post's claim. However, we found no credible reports confirming that Rahul Gandhi visited Mata Vaishno Devi during Chaitra Navratri 2025. Furthermore, the Desk found an X (formerly Twitter) by Rahul Gandhi dated 30 March 2025, in which he wished everyone a happy Chaitra Navratri. The post's caption read: "Best wishes to everyone celebrating Gudi Padwa, Chaitra Navratri, Ugadi, Cheiraoba, Cheti Chand, and Sajibu! May this auspicious occasion bring joy and happiness into your lives and fill your homes with peace and prosperity." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk ran the keyframes of the viral video through Reverse Image Search and found the same video on Rahul Gandhi's official YouTube channel on September 10, 2021. The title of the video read: "Darshan of Shri Mata Vaishno Devi" Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. At the 1:46-second timestamp, the Desk found the same visuals as in the viral video. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the YouTube post. The Desk came across several videos uploaded on Congress's official social media handles in September 2021 from his visit to Mata Vaishno Devi. Here is the link , and below is a screenshot of the same. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across a report dated September 9, 2021, by AAJ Tak, whose headline read: "Rahul Gandhi visited Mata Vaishno Devi temple, also participated in Aarti; said- I will not speak on political issues" The report states, "Former Congress President Rahul Gandhi arrived in Jammu on Thursday on a two-day visit. Here he visited Shri Mata Vaishno Devi. Rahul Gandhi also participated in the Aarti. Rahul Gandhi reached the temple on foot from Katra. Earlier, Rahul Gandhi told the journalists that he had visited his mother, so he would not speak on any political issue." Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to 2021 when Rahul Gandhi visited the Mata Vaishno Devi temple and is unrelated to Chaitra Navratri 2025.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2024 video of Asaduddin Owaisi falsely shared as recent claiming he cried during Waqf (Amendment) Bill debate in Lok Sabha
content: New Delhi, April 4 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported video from the Parliament featuring AIMIM Chief Asaduddin Owaisi was recently shared on social media. Those sharing the claim that the AIMIM chief broke down over the Waqf Amendment Bill, which was passed in the Lok Sabha on Thursday. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral video was misleadingly shared with a false claim on social media. The viral video dates back to 2024, wherein Owaisi was merely rubbing his eyes during the Parliament session and not crying. The video is unrelated to the recent session. Parliament approved the Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2025, in the early hours of Friday, following an extensive discussion in the Rajya Sabha. The amended Waqf Bill reduces the mandatory contribution of Waqf institutions to boards from 7 percent to 5 percent, whilst implementing mandatory audits by state-appointed auditors for institutions earning above Rs 1 lakh. Claim On April 3, an X (formerly Twitter) user, Syed Hasan Imam Zaidi, shared a purported video from the Parliament featuring AIMIM Chief Asaduddin Owaisi claiming he allegedly broke down over the Waqf Amendment Bill, which was passed in the Lok Sabha on Thursday. The post's caption garnered 238 views and read: "Saw Asaduddin Owaisi crying in Parliament today. My heart shattered into pieces. His tears carried the pain of millions, a scream for justice that echoes in my soul. #WaqfBoard #WaqfBillAmendment. #Owaisi #WaqfBill" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. To verify the claim, the Desk carefully watched the entire video and encountered several other leaders, including Prime Minister Narendra Modi. However, PM Modi arrived in Thailand on Thursday (April 3) for a two-day visit to attend the sixth BIMSTEC Summit, which makes it clear that the video is not recent. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk looked up Sanad TV's Lok Sabha Session from Thursday and found that Owaisi was wearing a white attire during the session; however, in the viral video, he can be seen wearing a blue coloured attire. Below is a combination image highlighting the same. Further, the Desk also noticed the 'AIMIM RR District' watermark on the top of the viral video. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk looked for the Instagram handle and skimmed through it; we then found the video uploaded on August 7, 2024. Here is the link , and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk again ran the keyframes of the viral video through Reverse Image Search and came across the Live Streaming of the Lok Sabha session of August 7, 2024, shared on YouTube by OdishaLIVE. At 4:46:56 timestamp, it is visible that Owaisi is just rubbing his eyes and not crying. Here is the link , and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded the viral video dates back to 2024 and was shared with a false claim that Owaisi was crying in the Parliament over the Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2025.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2020 video of woman self-immolating in Lucknow falsely shared as recent incident; details inside
content: New Delhi, April 4 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media claiming to show a recent incident in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, where a woman attempted self-immolation outside Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's office. The video showed the woman taking the drastic step before being stopped by local police, who later took her to the hospital in serious condition. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video was from 2020. The victim, identified as Anjali Tiwari, also known as Ayesha, set herself on fire near Gate No. 2 of the BJP headquarters on Vidhan Sabha Marg in Hazratganj. She had reportedly complained of domestic abuse by her in-laws. Police officials immediately took her to the hospital, but she later succumbed to her injuries. Despite being an old video, it was recently shared on social media with a misleading claim. Claim An X user named Adv Deepak Babu shared, on April 3, a sensitive video in which a woman was seen self-immolating on the road. The user claimed the incident occurred recently in Uttar Pradesh's Lucknow, where the victim took the drastic step outside Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's office after getting tired of not getting justice. "In UP, a woman set herself on fire outside Yogi ji's office in Lucknow to get justice. The victim woman made several rounds to the police station as well as to the SP office, but no hearing took place. UP Police is working only for BJP leaders and influential people," the user stated as the alleged reason behind the woman's action. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (WARNING: The video contains sensitive visuals.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search results via Google Lens also led the Desk to a report published by Amar Ujala on October 14, 2020. The report detailed the incident and why the 35-year-old Anjali Tiwari alias Ayesha (seen in the viral video) took the extreme step of self-immolation. According to the report, Anjali alias Ayesha (who later died while being treated for injuries) set herself on fire in front of the legislative assembly in Lucknow on October 13, 2020, after complaining of domestic violence. "The woman said that after her relationship with her first husband ended, she changed her name and religion and was living in a separate house with a young man named Asif Raza. When Asif went to Saudi Arabia, she went to his house to live, but his family refused to keep her. The woman complained to the police but did not get any help. She came to Lucknow to meet the Chief Minister. But she did not succeed. After this, on Tuesday, she set herself on fire," the report added. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting the visuals in the viral video, matched with the feature image of the report. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk held a customised keyword search on Google about the incident. The search results led the Desk to a social media post by the Lucknow Police, who, replying to the viral video, confirmed it to be from the incident that occurred in 2020 and mentioned that action had also been taken against those responsible. "The above video is from the year 2020, in which the Hazratganj police station has taken action," the Lucknow Police mentioned. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of the woman self-immolating was from an incident that occurred in Lucknow in 2020. The woman had also reportedly died in the incident.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2021 video of SP leader beaten over abusive remark against Yogi Adityanath shared as recent with false claim; details inside
content: New Delhi, April 4 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media claims to show members of the Karni Sena allegedly attacking Samajwadi Party (SP) leader Mahendra Yadav. Users claimed the incident occurred in Uttar Pradesh's Mau, where Yadav allegedly misbehaved with members of the Karni Sena and the Vishwa Hindu Parishad, who were holding a protest in honour of Rajput ruler Rana Sanga. The video gained attention amid widespread protests across Uttar Pradesh following a controversial statement by SP leader and Rajya Sabha member Ramji Lal Suman. Suman called Rana Sanga a "traitor," alleging that the Rajput ruler had invited Mughal emperor Babur to India to defeat Ibrahim Lodi, the last Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate. However, a PTI Fact Check investigation revealed that the viral video is unrelated to the current Rana Sanga row. The video is from 2021 and shows SP leader Mahendra Chauhan, not Mahendra Yadav, being assaulted over his allegedly derogatory remarks against Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. Thus, an old video was falsely shared on social media as a recent incident. Claim An X user, Madan Singh Gaur Kshatriy, shared the video on March 29, claiming it showed members of the Karni Sena thrashing SP leader Mahendra Yadav. According to the user, the incident occurred during a protest by the Vishwa Hindu Parishad and Karni Sena in honour of Rajput warrior Rana Sanga. The user alleged that Yadav misbehaved with the protestors and was then beaten up by Karni Sena members. The video, at the time of publishing the article, received 19.8k views. Here is the link and archive link to the video, along with a screenshot. Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk used the InVid tool to extract keyframes from the viral video. One of these frames was reverse-searched on Google Lens, revealing multiple other posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts are found here and here , with archived links available here and here . The search result via Google Lens also led the Desk to a post by the Samajwadi Party's official X handle. The party shared a video dated February 1, 2021, that matched the visuals from the viral clip and featured SP leader Mahendra Chauhan. "The assault on SP leader Mahendra Chauhan in the Collectorate premises by ruling party goons in the presence of police in Mau is a result of jungle raj prevailing in the state — highly condemnable," read the caption accompanying the video. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting that the viral clip is identical to the one posted by the Samajwadi Party in 2021. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above generated inputs, the Desk conducted a keyword-based search on Google, which led to several news reports covering the 2021 incident. According to a Dainik Jagran report dated February 1, 2021, members of the Karni Sena allegedly assaulted SP's backward class state secretary Mahendra Chauhan after he reportedly used abusive language against Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. "Karni Sena members alleged that Chauhan abused Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath during a conversation. Enraged by this, they attacked him. Though some people tried to shield Chauhan, the Sena members continued to chase and beat him. On the other hand, Chauhan claimed that the Sena members had previously gone viral with a video showing them beating a poster of Cabinet Minister Dara Singh Chauhan with shoes," the report said. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video was shared on social media falsely linking it to a recent controversy.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2024 video of Manipur torch rally shared as recent to falsely claim people protested and demanded independence from India
content: New Delhi, April 7 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a large group of people has been shared on social media with the claim that it depicts protesters in Manipur demanding independence from India. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the viral video was shared with a false claim. Upon investigation, it was revealed that the footage dates back to 2024, when a torch rally was organised to protest the government's inaction in resolving the conflict in Manipur. The conflict in Manipur escalated in May 2023 due to long-standing tensions between the Meitei and Kuki communities, resulting in over 250 deaths and the displacement of more than 50,000 people. The Meitei community predominantly resides in the Imphal Valley, while the Kuki community primarily inhabits the surrounding hill regions. Additionally, N. Biren Singh resigned as Chief Minister of Manipur on February 9, 2025, and the state is currently under President's Rule. Claim On April 2, an X (formerly Twitter) user named 'Jimmy' shared a video of a large group of protesters in Manipur who claimed to be demanding independence from India. The caption of the post, which garnered 26.1k views, read: "Manipur After being declared an autonomous state from India and no longer part of the country, #Manipur has become a majority #Christian area. In several places in Manipur, people are marching for independence from #India." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a Facebook post featuring a video similar to the viral video. The post was shared by a user, 'Siliguri Times Now,' on September 10, 2024. The caption of the post read: "People of #Manipur want change now. Women protesters took out a rally with torches against the Manipur Violence. Huge protest by Manipur women against Govt over 16 months long ongoing #violence | Rocket Attack" Here is the link , and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video's keyframes and the pictures in the Facebook post. The Desk came across an Instagram post by Manipuri filmmaker Romi Meitei, dated September 20, 2024, featuring the same visuals as seen in the viral video. The caption of the post read: "After DRONE BOMBING by Kuki Narco Terrorist 'MEIRA PAIBI' (women torch bearers) rally to protect the future of Manipur and stand for peace, unity, and progress." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports and came across a report by India Today NE dated September 9, 2024. The report consisted of an extended video version, as seen in the viral video. The headline of the report read: "Manipur: Meira Paibis hold torch rally demanding resolution to Manipur conflict" "In a powerful display of public frustration over the government's inaction to resolve the ongoing conflict in Manipur, a torch rally was organized today, September 9, by the Meira Paibis of Thangmeiband and neighboring areas. The protest marks yet another call for peace as the state continues to grapple with the crisis that has persisted for more than 16 months. Unlike the previous day's rally, which was marked by heightened tension, today's protest was notably peaceful," read the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. An X post by PTI also featured a video from the same torch march on September 9, 2024. The caption of the post read: "VIDEO | Manipur: Women hold a protest rally in Imphal's Thangmeiband over continued violence in the state." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to 2024, when a protest in Manipur's Imphal demanded a resolution to the Manipur conflict, not independence from India.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, PM Modi did not announce retirement, fake viral graphic shared as a false claim; details inside
content: New Delhi, April 7 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A graphic purportedly published by an English Daily claiming that Prime Minister Narendra Modi had announced his retirement is being shared by several social media users. However, an investigation by PTI Fact Check Desk found the viral graphic to be fake. The Desk reached out to the Times Network, and they denied creating any such post. Furthermore, no other reputable news item supports Modi's assertion that he announced his retirement from politics before the age of 75. Claim On April 2, an X (formerly Twitter) user shared a post of a leading English Daily claiming that PM Modi has announced his retirement from politics and September 16 would be his last day at work. The post allegedly quotes PM Modi: "September 16, 2025, will be my last day at work". The post also mentioned: "Announcement comes 2 days after meeting with RSS in Nagpur on Sunday". Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. To verify the claim, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find reports on PM Modi's Nagpur visit. However, the articles did not talk about his retirement from politics. A report by the Mint highlighted that Modi visited the memorial of RSS founder Keshav Baliram Hedgewar at the Sangh's headquarters in Reshim Bagh. He was accompanied by RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat and Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis at RSS headquarters. The title of the report read: "In first visit to RSS headquarters for an Indian PM, Modi calls Sangh 'banyan tree' of Indian culture" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk checked PMO and PM Modi's official social media accounts but did not find any such announcements. Notably, if he had made such a statement, it would have garnered national attention. Here is the link to PMO and PM Modi 's official X handle. The Desk also scanned Times Now's website but did not find any such report that cited his retirement. However, we did find a report dated April 1, 2025, whose headline read: "What Is Next For Yogi Adityanath? UP CM Answers Amid PM Modi 'Retirement' Buzz" "Speculations are rife after Sanjay Raut claimed that Prime Minister Narendra Modi will resign on September 17 this year. Weighing in on the claims, Yogi Adityanath maintained that his primary role is serving the people of Uttar Pradesh…Speaking to PTI in an exclusive interview, Yogi Adityanath asserted that he was a 'yogi' at heart, and politics was his responsibility, not a full-time job. The UP CM made it clear that his primary role is serving the people of Uttar Pradesh, and even this would come to an end one day," the report read. Here is the link to the report. The Desk conducted another set of customised keywords and came across a report by Hindustan Times, dated April 1, whose headline read: "'There is no retirement at 75 rule': Maharashtra BJP chief counters Sanjay Raut remark on PM Modi" A section of the report read: "Maharashtra BJP president Chandrashekhar Bawankule on Tuesday dismissed Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut's claim about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's retirement, saying that there is no rule in the party mandating retirement at 75. Calling Raut's remark a "political stunt," Bawankule rejected the claim that PM Modi visited the RSS headquarters in Nagpur to announce his retirement." Here is the link to the report. Continuing the investigation, PTI Fact Check reached out to the Times Network for its response to the social media post, and they vehemently denied reporting this news. "Times Now categorically denies creating any such post containing news that has not been reported or published by us on our channel, website, or any of our official social media handles. This is a clear case of abuse and misuse of our brand logo in a futile attempt to authenticate fake news. We have already flagged such accounts to X, and our legal team is looking into the matter," the Times Network replied. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral post was fake, and Times Now has not published any such article.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of attack on Nitish Kumar falsely linked to Waqf Amendment row; details inside
content: New Delhi, April 7 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media claims to show Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar being attacked in Patna. The footage shows a man approaching from behind and allegedly landing a blow on Kumar's face, with the claim that he was upset over the Chief Minister's support for the Waqf Amendment Bill, 2025. However, a PTI Fact Check investigation found that the viral video is unrelated to the current Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2025 row, which was recently passed by Parliament following its approval in the Rajya Sabha. The video actually dates back to March 2022 and shows a man, reportedly mentally unstable, attacking the Chief Minister in Bakhtiyarpur, Patna—Kumar's home turf. The old, unrelated video was falsely shared on social media as recent, with a misleading claim. Claim On April 4, an X user named '@HansRaj87366286' shared a video of an unidentified man attacking Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar. The video showed the assailant coming from behind and allegedly landing a blow on Nitish Kumar's face, reportedly over the Chief Minister's decision to support the Waqf Amendment Bill 2025 in Parliament. "A youth from Bihar slapped Bihar CM Nitish Kumar for supporting the Waqf Bill," the user shared the video with the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk used the InVid tool to extract keyframes from the viral video. One of these keyframes was reverse-searched on Google Lens, revealing multiple other posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts are found here and here , with their archived links available here and here . The search results via Google Lens also led the Desk to a video published on the official YouTube channel of the Economic Times. The channel posted the video (exactly the same as seen in the viral video) of an attack on Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar; however, its publishing date revealed the video to be from March 27, 2022, predating the political row which erupted amid the passage of the 'Waqf Board Amendment Bill 2025'. The video was then published with a description: "A man allegedly slapped Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar at his hometown of Bakhtiyarpur, media reports said. The man was immediately arrested by the securitymen. Kumar was in the town to pay homage to Shilbhadra Yaji, a freedom fighter from the state." Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image, highlighting that the content seen in the viral video exactly matched the video posted by the news portal. Next, taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk conducted a customized keyword search on Google and came across a report by News18 dated March 27, 2022. Like the details mentioned by the Economic Times in their video, the report by News18 also confirmed the incident of the attack on Nitish Kumar dated March 2022 and clarified that it does not hold any links to the present Waqf Bill row. "Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar was attacked on Sunday by a man during an event in his home turf Bakhtiyarpur in Patna, leading to a massive lapse in the CM's security system. Sources said that the assailant, believed to be a mentally unstable local resident, was immediately arrested," the report stated. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing an attack on Nitish Kumar was falsely linked to the present Waqf Amendment Bill row.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of elephant lifted by JCB falsely linked to Hyderabad's Kancha Gachibowli forest row; details inside
content: New Delhi, April 7 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported video showing an elephant being removed from its original habitat using a JCB excavator was recently shared on social media. Amid the recent row, users claimed that the footage depicted real scenes from Hyderabad's biodiversity-rich Kancha Gachibowli area. However, a PTI Fact Check investigation found that the video is unrelated to the current Kancha Gachibowli forest controversy. While the Desk could not independently verify the original location where the elephant was filmed being lifted by a JCB, it found that the same video has been circulating on social media since August 2018. An old, unrelated video was shared with a false claim. Claim On April 5, an X user named '@DeepsBDJ35' shared a purported video in which an old and injured elephant was allegedly being forcibly removed from Hyderabad's biodiversity-rich Kancha Gachibowli area by a JCB amid the ongoing controversy. The user claimed, "400 acres of forest are being cut down in Hyderabad, animals are being killed, deer have been seen crying at some places. Now look at this injured old elephant, how it is being forcibly removed by a JCB. This plight of animals will have an impact. Forests belong to animals only, but foolishly greedy humans are occupying them too. Humans are inviting their own destruction very fast. Such destruction has never been seen before," the user wrote while sharing the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk used the InVid tool to extract keyframes from the viral video. One of these keyframes was reverse-searched on Google Lens, revealing multiple other posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts were found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. The Google Lens search also led the Desk to multiple video links whose visuals exactly matched the content seen in the viral video. A key finding noticed by the Desk was that those videos had been published across different social media platforms, all predating the current controversy. A video published by a YouTube channel named 'cp wild Lanka', which also included the same visuals from the viral clip, showed that it was first published on social media on August 2, 2018. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image, highlighting the content seen in the viral video exactly matches with that of the video posted by the YouTube channel 'cp wild Lanka'. Additionally, as a part of the investigation, the Desk also conducted a customized keyword search on Google to gather more information about the incident—specifically where it was reported—however the search results could not independently verify the video's location or context. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video showing an elephant being removed by a JCB is not linked to the current Kancha Gachibowli forest controversy. The video had been posted on social media at least six years ago, making it unrelated to the recent events.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2022 video of Priyanka Gandhi Vadra protesting against inflation falsely shared claiming she protested over Waqf Amendment Bill recently
content: New Delhi, April 8 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video featuring Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra surrounded by a huge crowd and police officials. The video's sharers claimed that she was protesting against the Waqf Amendment Bill 2025. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral video dates back to 2022, when Priyanka Gandhi was protesting inflation, and is unrelated to the protest against the Waqf Amendment Bill. Notably, the Waqf Amendment Bill was passed in the Lok Sabha on April 2, 2025, and later cleared by the Rajya Sabha on April 4, 2025. Claim On April 4, an X (formerly Twitter) user named 'Sandeep Khasa' shared a video featuring Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra claiming that she was protesting against the Waqf Amendment Bill. The post's caption, originally in Hindi and garnering 192.8k views, read: "Congress is giving belt treatment to the BJP government on the Wakf Bill. Jairam Ramesh has said that we will go to the Supreme Court against the Waqf Bill. The Waqf Bill has been brought to loot the lands. Congress will protest against it from the streets to the Parliament." Here is the link and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk found the same video as seen in the viral one, uploaded on the official YouTube channel of Ten News National on August 5, 2022. The video's title read: "Priyanka Gandhi came out on the road wearing black clothes, police took her into custody. Watch the video" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the news report. Another report by NDTV, dated August 5, 2022, mentioned that Congress was staging a protest against inflation. The title of the report read: "Priyanka Gandhi Vadra Sits On Road In Protest, Cops Surround Her" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search of relevant media reports and came across a report by Hindustan Times dated April 5, 2022, whose headline read: "Watch | Amid Cong's Delhi protests, Priyanka Gandhi breaks barricades, arrested" According to the report: "Dramatic scenes emerged in the national capital as Congress intensified its protest against price rise and GST. Among other Congress leaders, Rahul Gandhi was detained by Delhi Police, while Priyanka Gandhi Vadra was arrested. The situation escalated as Priyanka refused to cooperate and tried to resist the detention by sitting on the road. She was finally dragged by police personnel, shoved into a car, and taken away." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to 2022, when Priyanka Gandhi was protesting inflation, and is unrelated to the protest against the Waqf Amendment Bill.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2024 video of people raising 'Israel tu barbaad hoga' slogans in Ujjain shared as recent claiming people shouted anti-Hindu slogans; details inside
content: New Delhi, April 8 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video depicting a huge crowd was recently shared on social media, claiming the people from the Muslim community raised anti-Hindu slogans in Ujjain on Eid in 2025. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral video dates back to 2024, and in the video, the people were raising 'Israel tu barbaad hoga' slogans in Ujjain. The viral video was shared with a false claim on social media. Claim On April 2, an X (formerly Twitter) user, going by the name Dr. Anita Vladivoski, shared a video of a huge crowd, claiming that they were Muslims raising anti-Hindu slogans in Ujjain, on Eid in 2025. The caption of the post, which garnered 198.9k views, originally in Hindi, read: "Unhel, Ujjain: Muslims pray for the destruction of Hindus on Eid. On the day of EID, they are praying - "Hindus will be destroyed, InshaAllah, InshaAllah. And all this is not being said secretly, but is being said while standing on the road near the temple." Here is the link , and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . To verify the claim, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find relevant media reports citing anti-Hindu slogans being raised this Eid, but we did not find any credible reports referring to the same. On further analysing the video carefully, the Desk found that the actual slogans raised were 'Israel tu barbaad hoga' (Israel, you will be destroyed). Taking a cue from this, the Desk again ran the keyframes of the viral video through Reverse Image Search and came across a report by Punjab Kesari dated April 12, 2024. The report featured the same video as seen in the viral video. The title of the report read: "Slogans of 'Israel, you will be destroyed' were raised..Video of sloganeering against Israel in Ujjain goes viral" Here is the link and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and news report. A report was also published by ETV Bharat dated April 12, 2024, whose headline read: "Anti-Israel slogans raised in Ujjain, video went viral on social media, police started investigation - Slogans against Israel in Ujjain - SLOGANS AGAINST ISRAEL IN UJJAIN" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to 2024, and in the video, the people were raising 'Israel tu barbaad hoga' slogans in Ujjain.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old South Africa video of elephant with facial deformity falsely shared linking it to Telangana's Kancha Gachibowli forest
content: New Delhi, April 8 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Days after the Telangana government's decision to auction 400 acres of land in Hyderabad's biodiversity-rich Kancha Gachibowli area for the construction of urban infrastructure and an IT park triggered a major political row, another video — allegedly showing animals disturbed by the development — began circulating on social media. This time, the video showed an elephant with a serious facial injury — a large hole below its forehead. Users claimed the injury was caused by a government-operated JCB (bulldozer) working in the area. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video was unrelated to the current Kancha Gachibowli forest controversy. It originally featured a female elephant named Rhandzekile from South Africa's Greater Kruger National Park, who was born with this rare deformity. An old and unrelated video was falsely shared on social media as recent. Claim On April 7, an X user named 'Umang Jain' shared a purported video of an elephant allegedly injured by a government JCB (bulldozer) in Telangana. A controversy surrounding land auctions from Hyderabad's biodiversity-rich Kancha Gachibowli area had triggered a massive political row. The video showed the elephant with a massive hole on its forehead, allegedly roaming in the forested area. "The Congress government in Telangana does not even have a good veterinarian who can treat this elephant that was injured by the government JCB. #SaveHCUBioDiversity," the user shared the video with the caption. Since being posted on social media, the video (at the time of posting the article) gained 264k views along with 9.9k likes. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk used the InVid tool to extract keyframes from the viral video. One of these keyframes was reverse-searched on Google Lens, revealing multiple other posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts were found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search result via Google Lens also led the Desk to a report published on a website named Animals Around The Globe on July 26, 2024. The report included several pictures of an elephant matching the one seen in the viral video, i.e., having a large hole below its forehead. The report, however, mentioned the elephant as a female named Rhandzekile. It stated that Rhandzekile was born with a congenital abnormality and is presently staying in South Africa's Greater Kruger National Park. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting the visual of the elephant seen in the viral video, matched with those from photos released by the report. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google. Several other reports covered developments surrounding the extraordinary survival of Rhandzekile, an exceptional elephant from South Africa. According to a report published by Africa Geographic on December 18, 2019, "Rhandzekile was first sighted in 2009 in the Umbabat Private Nature Reserve as a young sub-adult cow. Through the years since then, people who see her have expressed shock and awe that she has kept going." Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video showing an elephant with a large hole below its forehead originally featured a female mammal named Rhandzekile from South Africa's Greater Kruger National Park, who was born with this rare deformity.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old photo of Tej Pratap, Tejashwi Yadav with Rabri Devi misused to spread rumour of Lalu Yadav's death, details inside
content: New Delhi, April 8 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A photo featuring RJD leader and former Bihar Chief Minister Rabri Devi, along with sons and party leaders Tejashwi Yadav and Tej Pratap Yadav wearing white shirts and dhotis with their shaved heads was shared on social media with a claim that RJD supremo Lalu Prasad Yadav passed away at the age of 76. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found the viral claim to be baseless and fake. The Desk contacted Rashtriya Janata Dal Rajya Sabha MP Manoj Jha, who confirmed that Lalu Prasad Yadav is healthy and the news spreading about his death is completely false. The viral photo was shared with a false claim on social media. Claim On April 5, an X (formerly Twitter) user going by the name 'Digvijay Singh' shared a photo featuring Rabri Devi, Tejashwi Yadav, and Tej Pratap Yadav, wearing white shirts and dhotis with their heads shaved, claiming that Lalu Yadav passed away at the age of 76. The caption of the post read: "Lalu Prasad Yadav is no more, he breathed his last at the age of 76." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through Reverse Image Search and came across a similar post with the same caption. Here is the link to the post. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a web story published on 9 December 2023 on the website of Aaj Tak featuring the same photo as seen in the viral post. According to the report, Lalu Prasad Yadav visited Tirupati Balaji with his family. During the darshan, Tejashwi Yadav and Tej Pratap Yadav also got their heads shaved. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking the investigation forward, we scanned Lalu Prasad Yadav and Tejashwi Yadav's official social media accounts. Still, we found no information or confirmation about Lalu Yadav's death. Here is the link to his official X post, and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across a report in the Times of India dated April 2, 2025, whose headline read: "Lalu Prasad Yadav undergoes treatment at hospital for sores: What causes body sores and what is the line of treatment" Here is the link to the report. In the next part of the investigation, we contacted Dr. Rakesh Yadav, who is treating Lalu Prasad Yadav in AIIMS. He said: "Lalu Yadav is completely safe now, and his treatment is going on in the private ward of AIIMS." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Lalu Prasad Yadav is healthy and the news spreading about his death is completely false and baseless.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video shared on social media to falsely claim birds stole pieces of gold jewellery to make nest
content: New Delhi, April 9 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media claimed to show two birds sitting in a nest made of gold jewellery. The user alleged that the birds had stolen more than one kilogram of gold jewellery from three shops on Bangalore's High Court Road to build their nest. According to the claim, when the jewellers discovered the nest, they decided to recover the gold only after the baby birds hatched. It was also claimed that the shop owners increased security around the tree to prevent further losses. However, in its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was AI-generated and had been shared with a false claim to mislead viewers. Claim An X user named Pranav Anand Iyer shared a video on April 6 showing two birds sitting in a nest made of gold jewellery. The user claimed the birds had stolen more than one kilogram of gold from three jewellery shops on Bangalore's High Court Road. It was further claimed that the jewellers discovered the nest but decided to recover the gold only after the baby birds hatched. The shop owners allegedly also increased security around the tree. "These birds stole more than a kilogram of gold from three jewellery shops to build their nest on Bengaluru High Court Road. As they could recover this gold only after the birds hatched, the jewellery shop owners tightened security near this tree," the user wrote in the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the video, along with a screenshot: Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk used the InVid tool to extract keyframes from the viral video. One of the keyframes was reverse-searched on Google Lens, revealing multiple other social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts were found here and here , with archived versions here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a video posted on the Instagram handle Surendra Garhwal on April 1, 2025. The user, who described himself in his bio as a digital creator and an art and AI enthusiast, posted the exact same video as the one that went viral. Here is the link and archive link to the Instagram post, along with a screenshot: Below is a comparison image showing visuals from the viral video and those from the Instagram post, confirming they are the same. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the video to corroborate the claims circulated along with it. The analysis indicated that the video was AI-generated, as its visuals appeared overly smooth and uniform, resembling computer-generated effects rather than real-life footage. Next, to confirm this, the Desk ran the video through Hive Moderation, an AI detection tool. The result showed a 92% aggregate score, indicating that the video was highly likely to be AI-generated. The Desk also reviewed other posts on Surendra Garhwal's Instagram profile and contacted him to authenticate the above findings. While the Desk found several other highly realistic and well-crafted AI-generated videos posted on his handle, Garhwal also vehemently rejected the claim circulated along with the video. He stated, "No, this is all a lie. I created my video using AI. This is for entertainment purposes only." Here is a link to his Instagram handle. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing birds sitting on a nest built with gold jewellery was AI-generated.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video from Uttarakhand about action against illegally operated madrasas falsely shared in name of UP; details inside
content: New Delhi, April 9 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Following the President's assent to the Waqf Act, a purported video of an enquiry against a madrasa was recently shared on social media. Users claimed that the video showed an incident from Uttar Pradesh, where authorities allegedly began taking action against religious educational institutions days after the passage of the Waqf Amendment Bill. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was unrelated to Uttar Pradesh and bore no connection to the Waqf Amendment Bill. The video showed an incident from Uttarakhand, where authorities took action against an illegally operated madrasa per a government order. It is pertinent to note that back in March, over 100 illegally operated madrasas in the state were sealed by Uttarakhand authorities. The viral video depicted police action against one of these madrasas. Thus, an unrelated video was circulated on social media to mislead viewers. Claim An X user, 'Mohammed Naseeruddin', shared a video on April 6, allegedly showing authorities acting against a madrasa in Uttar Pradesh, merely days after the passage of the Waqf Amendment Bill. "Waqf trends started coming after the bill was passed. Madrasa action has started in UP. This video is a lesson for those who thought that nothing would happen with the Waqf Bill," the user wrote while sharing the video. At the time of writing this article, the video had gained 185.1k views and 2.1k likes. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk used the InVid tool to extract keyframes from the viral video. One keyframe was reverse-searched on Google Lens, revealing several other social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts were found here and here , with archived versions here and here , respectively. The reverse image search also led the Desk to a reel posted by a Facebook page named Roorkee-Haridwar Samachar. The page posted the video, identical to the viral one, on March 22, 2025 — well before the political row erupted over the 'Waqf Board Amendment Bill 2025'. The video was captioned, "An investigation was conducted by the Bhagwanpur Tehsil administration regarding the madrasas being run illegally." Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting that the content seen in the viral video matched the footage posted by the Facebook page. In the next part of the investigation, based on the above leads, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google regarding the Uttarakhand government's action against illegal madrasas in the state. The search led to a YouTube video published by DD News Uttarakhand on March 26, 2025. At the 1:23 timestamp, the same officials seen in the viral video can be identified taking action as part of the government's decision to shut down unregistered madrasas. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. The search result also led the Desk to a report published by Amar Ujala about the incident on March 25, 2025. The report stated: "Action against illegal madrasas is continuing in Uttarakhand. Today, action was taken against illegal madrasas on a large scale in Haridwar. More than 500 illegal madrasas are operating in the state. So far, 136 madrasas have been sealed in the entire state for not having complete documents." Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video is not from Uttar Pradesh but from Uttarakhand and showed state authorities acting against an illegally operated madrasa in Haridwar.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of lawyers protesting against Advocate Amendment Bill falsely shared linking it to Waqf Amendment Act
content: New Delhi, April 9 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video featuring many lawyers taking to the roads claiming they were protesting against the Waqf Board Bill. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral video is from February 2025, when the lawyers were protesting against the Advocate (Amendment) Bill, and is unrelated to the Waqf Board Bill. The video was shared with a false claim on social media. Claim On April 5, an X (formerly Twitter) user named Vinesh Phogat shared a video featuring a large group of lawyers taking to the roads, claiming that they were protesting against the Waqf Board Bill. The caption of the post, which garnered 14.5k views, originally in Hindi, read: "Lawyers have blocked the road against the Wakf Board Bill and are protesting in large numbers. Since 2014, Modi ji has not allowed anyone in the country to live peacefully. The farmers were brought on the road like this, the wrestlers have also been brought on the road. Do good to the country." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . To verify the claim, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find relevant media reports, but did not find any report that corroborated the details mentioned in the viral post. The Desk extracted the keyframes of the viral video, ran them through the Reverse Image Search, and came across a report by HNP News Hindi, dated February 22, 2025, whose headline read: "Lakhs of lawyers blocked the roads of Delhi? The government was shocked to see this! Watch it quickly." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the news report. The same banner appears at the 2:09 mark of the clip. It reads, "The Advocate (Amendment) Bill." Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across a report by India Today, February 23, 2025. According to the report, introducing the Advocates (Amendment) Bill in 2025 sparked massive protests, with lawyers claiming that the new law proposes massive changes to the Advocates Act, 1961, especially in redefining who is a legal practitioner and broadening the means of practising law. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Furthermore, an official press release by the Ministry of Law and Justice mentioned that the amended Advocates (Amendment) Bill, 2025 will be freshly tabled for public consultation. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video is from February 2025, when the lawyers were protesting against the Advocate (Amendment) Bill, and is unrelated to the Waqf Board Bill.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: This viral photo claiming Suhana Khan bought a luxury car is edited and shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, April 10 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported image of Bollywood actress and superstar Shah Rukh Khan's daughter, Suhana Khan, posing in front of a black luxurious car was recently shared on social media with a claim that she had bought it. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found the image to be digitally altered. The original image featured another Bollywood actress, Nora Fatehi, who reportedly bought the brand-new luxurious car worth Rs 60.90 lakh in December 2020. A digitally altered image was shared on social media as real with a false claim. Claim Bollywood actress Suhana Khan's fan page on Facebook shared a purported image of her buying a swanky, luxurious black car. "My new Car," the post shared by her fan account on April 7 reads. The image, when posting this article, garnered 17k likes and 1.1k comments. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and found another of Suhana Khan's fan page accounts had too shared the same purported image of her on Facebook with a similar claim. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Additionally, the search result via Google Lens also led the Desk to several social media posts that matched the background setting with that of the viral image. However, a closer analysis revealed it originally featured another Bollywood actress, Nora Fatehi, who bought a brand-new BMW 5-Series back in 2020. Here is the link to multiple images of Nora Fatehi shared by the car manufacturer congratulating her on her new purchase. A screenshot of the same has also been attached below: Here is a combination image highlighting that Suhana's photo has been superimposed on Nora Fatehi's image. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the inputs above, the Desk conducted a customized keyword search on Google and came across a report by News18, which reported about Nora Fatehi's new purchase — a brand-new luxurious car — back in December 2020. The title of the report reads, "Bollywood Actress Nora Fatehi Buys a Brand New BMW 5-Series Worth Rs 60.90 Lakh." Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the image of Suhana Khan with a brand-new luxurious car was digitally altered and shared with a false claim.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video falsely shared to claim protest held in Mumbai over imposition of speaking Marathi; details inside
content: New Delhi, April 10 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a large-scale protest near the Gateway of India in Mumbai was recently circulated on social media, with claims that it depicted a demonstration against the alleged imposition of speaking Marathi by non-Marathi-speaking communities in Maharashtra. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigation revealed that the video was AI-generated and shared on social media to mislead viewers. Additionally, it is worth noting that tensions have been rising in Maharashtra following several incidents of violence, where non-Marathi-speaking individuals were reportedly targeted for not speaking the local language. Claim An X user, Ninad Sawant, shared a video on April 9 allegedly showing a large group of people holding a protest in front of the Gateway of India in Mumbai. The video features individuals carrying placards with messages such as, "We don't speak Marathi; don't label us as traitors." The demonstration appeared to respond to everyone in the state's increasing pressure to speak Marathi. "Want to live in Maharashtra, earn money, and enjoy the facilities here, but openly oppose the local language. If these placard holders go abroad tomorrow, they will learn English, French, and German. But they are having trouble learning the language of their own country," the user captioned the video. When this article was published, the video had garnered over 74,000 views and 1,100 likes. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk used the InVid tool to extract keyframes from the viral video. One keyframe was reverse-searched on Google Lens, revealing several other social media users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts were found here and here , with archived versions here and here , respectively. The search result via Google Lens also led the Desk to a video published on an Instagram handle named 'Paribhraman'. The user first posted the video on April 9, 2025, and it is now being picked up by multiple users and shared with various claims. Here is the link and archive link to the post. In the next part of the investigation, as the Desk carefully analysed the video (of the protest) shared by the Instagram handle 'Paribhraman', it found a disclaimer mentioning that the entire content in this video was AI-generated. The user had created the video with a message that all languages should be respected. "India is a highly linguistically diverse country, with 22 officially recognised languages under the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, and a total of 121 languages and 270 mother tongues. Respect all languages," the user shared. Below is a screenshot highlighting the findings. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the visuals from the original post. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of people holding a protest against language imposition was AI-generated and was falsely shared on social media to mislead viewers.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Asaduddin Owaisi's video from JPC meeting falsely shared to claim he laughed after Waqf (Amendment) Bill passed in Parliament
content: New Delhi, April 10 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video featuring several political leaders, including AIMIM MP Asaduddin Owaisi, was recently shared on social media with the claim that he was seen laughing after the Waqf (Amendment) Bill was passed in Parliament. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video predates the passage of the Bill. It was actually recorded during a Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) meeting held on January 29, 2025. The social media post was shared with a false claim. Claim On April 5, an X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video featuring several political leaders, including Member of Parliament for Hyderabad Asaduddin Owaisi. The user claimed that Owaisi laughed after passing the Waqf (Amendment) Bill. The post's caption, which garnered 47.3k views, originally in Hindi, read: "The protectors of Muslims and democracy are having fun behind the scenes and laughing happily after the passing of the Wakf Amendment Bill. It is Owaisi who is laughing the most, but because of them, Abdul from Seelampur slum is ready to shed blood and get his house demolished by a bulldozer so that the objective of his community can be accomplished." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post by PTI dated January 29, 2025, featuring the same video as seen in the viral post. This clarifies that the video pre-dates the passage of the bill in Parliament. The post's caption read: "VIDEO | Members of the Joint Parliamentary Committee scrutinising the Waqf (Amendment) Bill, meet over tea after it adopted the draft report." Here is the link , and below is a screenshot of the same. Furthermore, the same video was uploaded on the official X handle of BJP Rajya Sabha MP Brijlal on January 29, 2025. The post's caption read: "Today, on 29-1-2025, after the adoption of the amendment by the 'JPC' on the 'Waqf Amendment Bill-2024, 'members of the ruling and opposition parties laughed and joked over tea. The atmosphere was happy; this is the beauty of parliamentary democracy." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across a PTI report from The Telegraph Online on January 29, 2025. The report mentioned that the members of the Joint Parliamentary Committee shared a light moment after a meeting on the Waqf Amendment Bill in New Delhi on Wednesday, Jan. 29, 2025. The headline of the report read: "Opposition members object to proposed omission of 'waqf by user' clause in Waqf Amendment Bill" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. The Waqf Amendment Bill was passed in the Lok Sabha on April 3, 2025, after a division of votes, with 288 MPs voting in favor and 232 against. An X post by PTI read: "VIDEO | The Lok Sabha has passed the Waqf (Amendment) Bill after a division of votes, with 288 MPs voting in favor and 232 against. The bill sparked intense debate and was later followed by voice votes on specific amendments." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. The Rajya Sabha further gave it a nod on April 4, 2025, with 128 MPs voting in favour of the Waqf (Amendment) Bill in the Rajya Sabha, 95 against. An X post by PTI read: "Parliament passes Waqf (Amendment) Bill with Rajya Sabha approving it. 128 MPs vote in favour of Waqf (Amendment) Bill in Rajya Sabha, 95 against" Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find relevant media reports and found a report by India Today on April 8, 2025. According to the report, the Waqf Amendment Act, 2025 officially came into effect on April 8, following its passage in both Houses of Parliament last week. "The Waqf (Amendment) Bill was passed in Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha following marathon over 12-hour debates in both Houses, and also received President Droupadi Murmu's nod," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video predates the passage of the Waqf (Amendment) Bill. It does not show that Owaisi and others are celebrating it.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2021 photo of CM Yogi Adityanath with Mukhtar Abbas Naqvi falsely shared linking it to recent Eid celebrations
content: New Delhi, April 10 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A photograph featuring Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath having a meal with BJP leader and former Union Minister Mukhtar Abbas Naqvi, along with Hema Malini, was circulated on social media, claiming CM Yogi visited Naqvi's residence to extend Eid wishes in 2025. However, PTI Fact Check investigated and found that the viral photo dates back to 2021, when Yogi Adityanath and Mukhtar Abbas Naqvi attended the Braj Raj Mahotsav in Vrindavan, Mathura. The photo is unrelated to any recent Eid celebrations at Naqvi's residence. It was misleadingly shared on social media with a false claim. Claim On April 2, an X (formerly Twitter) user named 'Prof.KS Bhardwaj shared a picture featuring UP CM Yogi Adityanath having a meal with BJP leader, former Union Minister Mukhtar Abbas Naqvi, and Hema Malini. The user claims that the CM visited Naqvi's residence to extend his wishes for Eid 2025. The overlying text on the photo, originally in Hindi, read: "Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath broke the myth of anti-Muslim sentiments, went to the house of former Union Minister Mukhtar Abbas Naqvi and wished him Eid Mubarak…" Here is the l ink to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through reverse image search and found that several other users had shared the same post, with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here . We first conducted a customised keyword search regarding the Eid celebration at Mukhtar Abbas Naqvi's residence to verify the claim. However, there were no reports of CM Yogi Adityanath attending the celebrations. We scanned the leader's official Facebook handle, and though he had uploaded many pictures of Eid, which was celebrated on March 31, and of him meeting several other leaders, there was no mention or photo of the CM. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Additionally, no information or post was available on CM Yogi Adityanath's official social media handles. This clarifies that the picture is not from the recent Eid celebrations at Naqvi's residence. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk reran the viral photo through Reverse Image Search and came across an X post by United News of India dated November 10, 2021. The post featured the same image as seen in the viral post. This clarifies that the photo has been on the internet since 2021. The post mentioned that the three enjoyed 'lithi-chokha' during Chhath Pooja celebrations at Hunar Haat in Mathura. The caption of the post read: "Union Minister Mukhtar Abbas Naqvi, Uttar Pradesh CM Yogi Adityanath, and Mathura MP and Bollywood veteran Hema Malini enjoy '#lithi-chokha' during #ChhathPooja celebrations at Hunar Haat in #Mathura." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral and X posts. Former Union Minister Mukhtar Abbas Naqvi also shared several images from the event on his official Facebook handle on November 10, 2021.
