The caption of the post read: "Shri Yogi Adityanath Ji said that the artisans and craftsmen of Hunar Haat are strengthening Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Ji's vision of #AatmanirbharBharat. Our India is rich in handicrafts and craftsmanship. Shri Yogi Adityanath Ji said that handicrafts & craftsmanship of India are centuries old. Artisans & craftsmen of #HunarHaat have presented this art, craft to us from generation to generation. This art should be respected; this art should be made more inclusive. Shri Yogi Adityanath Ji visited "Vishwakarma Vatika" in #HunarHaat . Shri Yogi Ji garlanded the statue of the great freedom fighter Raja Mahendra Pratap Singh. He also had different traditional foods while sitting on "Khatiya" in 'Mera Ganv Mera Desh" Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find relevant media reports and came across a report by The Times of India dated November 11, 2021. A section of the report read: "The Union and state governments are fully committed to ensuring the development of the Braj region and projects worth over Rs 425 crore are already in progress in the districts, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral photos date back to 2021, when Yogi Adityanath and Mukhtar Abbas Naqvi attended the Braj Raj Mahotsav, and are falsely linked to the Eid celebrations.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old and unrelated storm videos from different locations falsely shared claiming earthquake killed 98,000 people in Delhi
content: New Delhi, April 11 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a storm wreaking havoc across three different places was recently shared on social media with a claim that it depicted the horrific scenes from the time of the earthquake that struck Delhi on April 7, 2025. The user claimed that during the disaster that unfolded in the national capital, a total of 98,000 people lost their lives, while 87,000 others suffered injuries. In its investigation, however, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that no such disaster had struck the national capital on April 7, nor had such a heavy toll of lives been reported. The viral claim was false and shared on social media to mislead viewers. Claim An Instagram user '_father_sab' shared a video on April 7, allegedly showing how the massive earthquake that struck Delhi earlier this week created havoc in the region. The user claimed that a total of 98,000 people lost their lives, while 87,000 suffered injuries in the incident that struck the national capital on April 7. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk used the InVid tool to extract keyframes from the viral video. One keyframe was reverse-searched on Google Lens, revealing several other social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts were found here and here , with their archived versions here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google but could not find any authentic reports substantiating the viral claim that a massive earthquake struck the national capital on April 7 and claimed 98,000 lives. However, the search results led the Desk to several reports published by news outlets about a 5.0 magnitude earthquake in Nepal on April 4, whose tremors were also felt across the Delhi-NCR region. According to a report by Jagran on April 4, 2025, "A 5.0-magnitude earthquake hit Nepal on April 4, with light tremors felt across parts of Northern India, including Delhi NCR. The quake occurred at a depth of 20 km at 7:52 PM (local time)." The report, however, did not mention any damage to life or property in India as a result of these tremors. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot. Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the viral video and found it to be a compilation of three separate clips depicting storms, not an earthquake as claimed. To gather more details about where those three videos were first shot, the Desk once again conducted a Google reverse image search using keyframes from the footage. The reverse image search over the keyframe showing a roof collapsing onto parked cars during the storm led the Desk to a video posted by a user named '@Centinela35' on an X account on July 20, 2023. The channel's video exactly matched the viral one. However, the details attached to it mentioned that the video was from Zagreb, Croatia. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the visuals seen in the viral video, matched with those of the X video. Additionally, taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google about the massive storm that lashed Croatia back in 2023. The search results led the Desk to a report by Reuters on July 19, 2023, which mentioned that at least three people were killed in a severe thunderstorm that hit Slovenia and Croatia. "While in Croatia, two people were killed and several others were injured due to the incident; in neighboring Slovenia, a woman lost her life as a branch fell on her," the report said. Here is the link to the post. Moreover, as part of the investigation, the Desk also tried to ascertain the origin of the other two videos included in the viral compilation. However, the search results yielded no clear findings. Still, it is clear that no such earthquake occurred in Delhi on April 7, 2025, as claimed in the post. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video suggesting that over 98,000 people lost their lives in an earthquake that struck the national capital on April 7 was entirely false.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: These AI-generated photos of cricketer Shreyas Iyer and Bollywood actress Preity Zinta during IPL shared with false claim; details inside
content: New Delhi, April 11 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A collage depicting three purported images of Bollywood actress and Punjab Kings co-owner Preity Zinta along with the team's captain, Shreyas Iyer, from the IPL cricket ground, has recently been shared on social media. Users claimed that the duo shared a warm moment during the CSK vs PBKS IPL match, where Iyer purportedly kissed Preity Zinta after the team's victory. In its investigation, however, the PTI Fact Check Desk found all three images compiled in the collage to be AI-generated and shared on social media to mislead viewers. Claim A Facebook page, 'Titanium Army,' shared on April 9 a collage depicting three purported images of Punjab Kings co-owner Preity Zinta along with the team's captain, Shreyas Iyer. The photos showed the duo sharing a warm moment, as Iyer purportedly kissed Preity Zinta after Punjab Kings' victory against Chennai Super Kings in the IPL match held on April 8. "Shreyas Iyer kisses Preity Zinta in excitement of winning the CSK vs PBKS IPL match," the user shared in the post, which at the time of publishing the story had garnered 17k likes along with 62 shares. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation In the first part of the investigation, the Desk carefully cropped the three images (of Shreyas Iyer and Preity Zinta) attached in the collage. One by one, it then ran those through Google Lens and found several social media accounts that had also used the same images (though shared with different claims). Two such posts can be found here and here respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk analysed those images again and found several inconsistencies indicating that they might be AI-generated or digitally altered. For instance, subtle distortions in Shreyas Iyer's and Preity Zinta's facial features were noticeable. Additionally, the images in the collage had a glossy finish, a common characteristic of AI-generated visuals. Below is a screenshot highlighting these key findings: Next, taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk ran the images one by one through Hive Moderation (an AI detection tool). The tool detected a substantial presence of AI-generated elements in all the images. Below are the screenshots of the results: Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search about the match result pertaining to the Punjab Kings vs. Chennai Super Kings match held on April 8. The search result led the Desk to a report published by the official website of Punjab Kings regarding the team's smashing victory against CSK. In the match, Punjab Kings secured a clinical 18-run victory over Chennai Super Kings. Here is the link to the report: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the collage depicting images of Preity Zinta and Shreyas Iyer was AI-generated and not real.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of Akhilesh Yadav attending Iftar party shared with false claim that he skipped Kumbh Mela but attended Iftar party
content: New Delhi, April 11 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video featuring Samajwadi Party (SP) Chief Akhilesh Yadav offering prayers and sharing a meal with people belonging to the Muslim community was shared on social media with a claim that Yadav attended Iftar parties but did not visit the Maha Kumbh Mela this year. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that while it is true that Akhilesh Yadav took part in the Iftar party in Lucknow, he also visited the Maha Kumbh Mela. Yadav visited the Kumbh on 26 January 2025 and took a holy dip at the Triveni Sangam. The viral video was shared with a false claim on social media. Claim On March 29, an X (formerly Twitter) user going by the name Gems of Politics shared a video featuring SP Chief Akhilesh Yadav offering prayers and sharing a meal with people belonging to the Muslim community. The user claims that Yadav attended the Iftar party. However, he missed the Maha Kumbh Mela. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared it with similar claims. One such post can be found here . Upon further scanning the search results, we found an X post by News 24, dated March 29, 2025. According to the post, Akhilesh Yadav attended an Iftar party in Lucknow. The caption of the post read: "UP: SP chief Akhilesh Yadav attended Iftar party in Lucknow" Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk conducted a customised keyword search to verify whether Akhilesh Yadav attended the Maha Kumbh. It came across a report published by Live Hindustan on their YouTube channel on January 26, 2025. The title of the report read: "Akhilesh Yadav Maha Kumbh Dubki Video: Akhilesh took a dip in the Maha Kumbh | Yogi Adityanath | Prayagraj" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Deccan Herald published a report on 26 January 2025. According to the report, Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav took the holy dip at the Sangam (the confluence of Ganga, Yamun, and the mythical Saraswati rivers) at the Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj. "Speaking to reporters after taking the dip, Akhilesh took potshots at the Uttar Pradesh government over arrangements in the Mahakumbh and said that the arrangements could have been better." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk scanned Akhilesh Yadav's official Twitter handle and found a post dated January 27. The post's caption read: "The holy journey of Maha Kumbha! Maha Kumbh comes once in 144 years, that too on the banks of Sangam, meaning once in a lifetime and that too at the meeting point of rivers, that is why we should take a pledge from this that the life we have got can find its true meaning and significance only by the union of streams coming from different directions. Like Sangam, we should give a positive message of harmony throughout life. Whenever the confluence of the triveni of harmony, cordiality, and tolerance happens inside a person… then we will all experience Maha Kumbh." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Akhilesh Yadav attended the Iftar party and the Maha Kumbh Mela. He visited the Kumbh on 26 January 2025 and took a holy dip at the Triveni Sangam.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Social media post claiming govt has launched PM Kardata Kalyan Yojana to reward tax payer is fake: details inside
content: New Delhi, April 14 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): An old video of a person talking about the alleged PM Kardata Kalyan Yojana and its various provisions for taxpayers was recently shared on social media, claiming that the scheme will come into effect on April 1, 2025. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the Government of India has not launched any PM Kardata Kalyan Yojana scheme, and the viral video was uploaded as an April fools' prank. The video was misleadingly shared with a false claim. Claim On April 7, an X (formerly Twitter) user named 'Bhupy' shared a video of a person talking about PM Kardata Kalyan Yojana and its various provisions for taxpayers, claiming that it will come into effect on April 1, 2025. In the video, the person can be heard saying: "Taxpayers will receive different kinds of cards like silver, gold, and platinum based on the tax they pay in a financial year…Incentives like travel benefits could be availed under this scheme." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . After carefully analysing the entire video, the Desk found that the document shown in the viral video at the 1:19 timestamp features "Posted On: April Fools Day by LLA." Which indicates that it might be a prank. Below is a screenshot highlighting this. The Desk also noticed a watermark that read "Labour Law Advisor." On further scanning the social media accounts, we came across the same video uploaded on its X handle on April 1, 2025. A thread contained details of the scheme, but the last post mentioned 'Happy April Fools Day'. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot highlighting the same. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find if any such scheme was launched by the government, but it did not yield any such results. Further, we scanned the 2025-26 Budget document and the official Government of India website, but there was no announcement or detail regarding the scheme. Here is the link to the budget document, and here is the link to the official website. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that no such scheme was launched by the Government, and the video was uploaded on April 1 as an April fools' prank.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated photo of Virat Kohli, Anushka Sharma falsely shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, April 15 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A photograph featuring ace cricketer Virat Kohli and actress Anushka Sharma along with their children was shared with the claim that they were playing a video game. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the photo was AI-generated and falsely presented as real on social media. Claim On April 9, a Facebook user, Nikhil Bishnoi, shared a photo of Cricketer Virat Kohli and actress Anushka Sharma along with their children, claiming that they were playing a video game. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation To verify the claim, the Desk carefully analysed the photo and found several discrepancies in the photo indicating that it might be AI-generated or digitally altered. For instance, subtle distortions in Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma's facial features were noticeable. Additionally, the image had a glossy finish, a common characteristic of AI-generated visuals. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. In the subsequent part of the investigation, taking cues from the above findings, the Desk ran the image through Hive Moderation, an AI detection tool. The tool detected a substantial presence of AI-generated elements in the image. Below is a screenshot of the result: The Desk ran the viral photo through Sightengine, another AI detection tool, indicating a substantial presence of AI-generated content. Below is a screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral photo was AI-generated.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Viral video showing Muslim mob attacking woman from same community in UP falsely shared in name of religious hate crime; details inside
content: New Delhi, April 15 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it showed a group of Hindu men brutally assaulting a Muslim woman. It was alleged that the incident occurred in Muzaffarnagar, Uttar Pradesh, where the woman was reportedly targeted by Hindu men who were seen forcibly removing her hijab and even attempting to disrobe her. As the video progresses, a man can be seen trying to rescue the woman; however, he is also attacked by the mob. However, in its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was falsely shared as a religious hate crime in India. The Desk confirmed with a police official from the Khalapar region that all six individuals arrested in connection with the incident were, in fact, Muslim. The official further stated that the incident took place on April 12, when the victim, accompanied by a Hindu man, was returning after collecting loan repayments on behalf of a small finance bank. A group of youths allegedly stopped them in the Khalapar locality, hurled abuses, assaulted the woman, and stripped her of her burqa. The video was misleadingly circulated on social media, falsely linking it to a communal hate crime. Claim An X user going by the name '@Entidoto' shared, on April 13, a video showing a Muslim woman allegedly being thrashed by a group of Hindu men in Uttar Pradesh's Muzaffarnagar. The user claimed, "In Muzaffarnagar, a Hindu youth removed the burqa of a Muslim girl, pulled her braid, and even tried to take off her clothes. Six people have been arrested in this case. But who gave them the right to touch the girl?" Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. It is pertinent to note that at the time of publishing the article, the video had garnered 143k views and 3.1k likes. Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk used the InVid tool to extract keyframes from the viral video. One of the keyframes generated was then reverse-searched on Google Lens, revealing several other social accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts were found here and here , with archived versions available here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the details mentioned in the post above, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a PTI report carried by The Print on April 14. The report stated that the incident occurred on April 12, when the woman, who works for a finance company, was returning from Sujru village with her male colleague from a hindu community when a group of youths stopped them in the Khalapar locality, hurled abuses, beat her up, and stripped her of her burqa. "I tried to explain to them that we were on duty and were returning to the company after collecting money from clients, but they did not listen," the report quoted the victim as stating. Here is the link to the report. Meanwhile, the search result via Google Lens also led the Desk to an official statement posted by the Muzaffarnagar Police about the incident. The official stated, "On 12.04.25, some people misbehaved and assaulted the employees of Utkarsh Small Finance Bank in the Khalapar police station area. Khalapar police immediately registered a case under relevant sections and arrested 06 accused." Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot. Additionally, as a part of the investigation to ascertain the identity of the accused, the Desk contacted Mahavir Singh Chouhan, SHO Khalapar, who confirmed that all the accused belonged to the Muslim community and their names were: Shoaib, Shami, Sartaz, Shadab, Umar, and Arsh. Further investigation into the incident is presently underway. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video falsely claims to depict a religious hate crime incident in Muzaffarnagar.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Photo of victims in 6-year-old murder case falsely shared after Murshidabad violence with communal angle; truth inside
content: New Delhi, April 16 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media post featuring an image of a family of three —- apparently a mother, father, and child —- was recently shared with the claim that they were victims of a gruesome murder in West Bengal's Murshidabad district. The post alleged that the victims were a 35-year-old man named Gopal Pal (also referred to as Bandhu Prakash Pal), his 30-year-old pregnant wife, and their 8-year-old son, all supposedly murdered by a group of Rohingyas who had broken into their home. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the incident in question is not recent; it dates back to 2019. Furthermore, there is no communal angle to the case. The brutal murders were the result of a monetary dispute related to an insurance policy. A man named Utpal Behera, known to the family, was arrested, charged, and later sentenced to death for the crime. An old and unrelated post was thus shared on social media to mislead viewers. Claim An X post featuring an image of a family of three was recently shared by a user named '@ArunKosli', claiming that the image showed victims of a recent massacre in Murshidabad, West Bengal. According to the post, a 35-year-old man named Gopal Pal (Bandhu Prakash Pal), his 30-year-old pregnant wife, and their 8-year-old son were brutally murdered by Rohingyas who had allegedly broken into their home. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and found several other social media accounts sharing the same image with similar claims. Two such posts were found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search result via the Google Lens also led the Desk to a report published by 'The New Indian Express', on the development. As the Desk scanned through the report (whose feature image matched to that of the viral image) it found the incident dated back to October 2019, and involved the brutal killing of Murshidabad-based school teacher and RSS worker Bandhu Prakash Pal, his wife Beauty Pal (who was eight months pregnant at the time of incident), and their 5-year-old son Angan Pal. "The 40-year-old school teacher Bandhu Prakash Pal's body was found on a bed, and his five-year-old son Angan was lying on the floor. The body of Pal's wife, Beauty—reportedly eight months pregnant at the time—was found on another bed in an adjoining room," the report stated. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting that the viral image exactly matches that of the feature image of the report. Next, taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find details about the police investigation. This led to another report published by The Indian Express on October 16, 2019. According to this report, police arrested Pal's former neighbour, Utpal Behera, in connection with the crime. The investigation revealed that the murders were committed over a financial dispute related to an insurance policy. The report does not mention any involvement of Rohingyas or suggest a communal motive. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Additionally, the search result also led the Desk to find another report by The Indian Express dated August 25, 2023, stating that a fast-track court in Berhampur had found Behera guilty of the triple murder and sentenced him to death. Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the incident dated back to 2019 and did not have any communal angle. The offence occurred over a monetary dispute related to an insurance policy, and a person named Utpal Behera (known to the family) was arrested in connection with the incident.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video from Maharashtra falsely shared claiming Bajrang Dal members headed to violence-hit West Bengal
content: New Delhi, April 16 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid the recent violence reported in West Bengal's Murshidabad district during protests against the Waqf (Amendment) Act, a video showing a large group of bikers heading to an undisclosed location was widely shared on social media. Users claimed the bikers were members of the Bajrang Dal en route to the violence-hit state, which had recently witnessed communal unrest. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video is not recent and is unrelated to the protests in West Bengal. The footage was originally recorded in Sangli, Maharashtra, in February 2025, during a midnight procession of youths returning from an annual fair in Karnataka. The viral video was misleadingly linked to the ongoing unrest in West Bengal. Meanwhile, it is pertinent to note that violence erupted on April 11 and 12 in parts of Murshidabad—including Suti, Dhulian, and Jangipur—during protests against the Waqf (Amendment) Act. At least three people were killed, and several others were injured in the incident. Claim On April 15, an X user named '@Mahaveer_VJ' shared a video of a large group of bike-goers heading to an undisclosed location. The user claimed that these are members of Bajrang Dal who are on their way to the violence-stricken West Bengal amid the large-scale unrest reported there. "Bajrang Dal Rajasthan reached West Bengal," the user captioned the video. At the time of posting the article, the video garnered 490k views and 26k likes. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk used the InVid tool to extract keyframes from the viral video. One of the keyframes generated was then reverse-searched on Google Lens, revealing several other social accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts were found here and here , with archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search result via Google Lens also led the Desk to a video published on an Instagram handle with the name 'i.love.shrigonda'. The handle had posted the video that matched the visuals seen in the viral video. Here is the link and archive link to the video, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the content seen in the viral video, matched with that of the video posted by the Instagram handle in February 2025. In the next part of the investigation, as the Desk held a closer analysis of the video, it was revealed to have been first posted on February 19, 2025 (i.e., months before the violence struck Murshidabad), and that the video was from Sangli (as mentioned in the description). The video was shared with the caption, "Police beat up youths who were creating ruckus in Sangli at midnight." Next, taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by Maharashtra-based news outlet Saam TV, which described the incident as having occurred in the second week of February in Sangli, where hundreds of motorists were thrashed by the police for blaring their vehicle horns and cheering loudly at midnight. The motorists were returning to Sangli from an annual fair in Chinchali in neighbouring Karnataka. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Additionally, as a part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to check if Bajrang Dal had organised a rally or was heading to West Bengal. However, we couldn't find any authentic reports corroborating the claim. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video of a bike rally from Sangli was falsely shared in the name of a Bajrang Dal entourage to West Bengal.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2023 video of fans setting off firecrackers during Salman Khan's movie falsely shared linking it to American comedy film; details inside
content: New Delhi, April 17 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported video featuring a large group of people was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that they burst crackers during the screening of the American fantasy adventure comedy film A Minecraft Movie. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral video actually dates back to 2023, when a group of fans set off firecrackers during the screening of Salman Khan's Tiger 3 in Malegaon, Nashik district, Maharashtra — and not during A Minecraft Movie. The viral video was misleadingly shared with a false claim on social media. Claim On April 13, an X (formerly Twitter) user named DramaAlert shared a video featuring a large group of people claiming that they burst crackers during the screening of A Minecraft Movie in the theatre. The caption of the post, which garnered 1.3 million views, read: "FIREWORKS SET OFF IN 'MINECRAFT' MOVIE THEATRE. Should they be charged with Arson?" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across the same video uploaded on the official YouTube handle of The New India Express on November 13, 2023. According to the report, fans set off fireworks inside the movie theatre during the screening of Tiger 3. The title of the report read: "Tiger 3' screening: Salman Khan fans set off fireworks inside movie theatre" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a screenshot highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the news report. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across a report by the Times of India dated November 13, 2023. The report featured the same video as seen in the viral post. According to the report, the incident happened in Mohan Theatre in Malegaon, in the Nashik district of Maharashtra. The title of the report read: "Salman Khan's Tiger 3 fans burst firecrackers inside cinema hall in Malegaon" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. The report further mentioned: "The Malegaon Chhavani Police reported that people ignited large firecrackers, including 'rockets,' sparklers, multiple bursts, sutli bombs, and more, posing a risk to those inside the theatre at the time of the incident around 10.15 pm." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to 2023 when a group of fans set off firecrackers during the screening of Tiger 3 and not 'A Minecraft Movie'

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video capturing violence in Nepal falsely shared in name of recent West Bengal unrest; details inside
content: New Delhi, April 17 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of people hurling stones at police was recently shared on social media, claiming that the incident was linked to the violence reported in West Bengal's Murshidabad district during protests against the Waqf (Amendment) Act. The video showed police officials shielding themselves from stone pelters. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk, in its investigation, found that the video was unrelated to India and actually depicted violence during a pro-monarchy protest in Tinkune, Nepal, on March 28. Meanwhile, it is pertinent to note that violence erupted on April 11 and 12 in parts of Murshidabad — including Suti, Dhulian, and Jangipur — during protests against the Waqf (Amendment) Act. At least three people were killed, and several others were injured in the incidents. Claim An X user, Jitendra Pratap Singh, shared on April 13 a video showing a group of people hurling stones at police. The user claimed the incident is linked to recent violence reported in West Bengal's Murshidabad district during protests against the Waqf (Amendment) Act. "You can see the condition of the Bengal Police. How will the Bengal Police protect any Hindu? And I don't consider it the fault of the Bengal Police. There is no fault of these poor policemen; they are the people themselves who have been persecuted by the government. Now, in such a situation, you can understand what will happen to the Hindus in Bengal," the user shared the video with the caption. At the time of publishing this article, the video had garnered 4,083 views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk used the InVid tool to extract keyframes from the viral video. One of the keyframes generated was then reverse-searched on Google Lens, revealing several other social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts were found here and here , with archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search result via Google Lens also led the Desk to a video posted on a Facebook page named 'Explore Nepal'. Upon closer analysis, the Desk found the video to be exactly similar to the viral post and suggested it was originally from Nepal. The posting date of the video revealed it was uploaded on March 28—predating the violence in West Bengal. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting the content seen in the viral video, matched with that of the video posted by the Facebook page in March 2025. Additionally, the Google Lens search also led the Desk to another video published on the Facebook page of Nepal-based news portal Sunaulo Nepal on March 28, 2025. The video posted by the channel matched the background settings seen in the viral video, though it was shot from a different angle. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Moreover, as part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a detailed analysis of the video and it was revealed that the video was originally from Nepal and related to the violence that erupted in Tinkune during a pro-monarchy protest. Below is a combination image highlighting the background setting of the viral video matched to that of the video posted by the Nepal-based news portal. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by Kathmandu Post on March 28, elaborating on the details of the incident. According to the report by Kathmandu Post, "Several security personnel and protesters were injured in a clash at Tinkune during a protest calling for the restoration of the Hindu kingdom on Friday. Human rights organisations said that both Nepal Police and Armed Police Force personnel, as well as protesters, sustained injuries." Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Additionally, as a part of the investigation, the Desk also contacted Hikmat Acharya, a correspondent with Nepal-based TechPana Media outlet, who confirmed that the video was from Nepal and depicted violence that erupted during a pro-monarchy protest. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing protesters pelting stones at police was not from West Bengal but from Nepal.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of assault on women from Surat falsely shared in name of incident of caste violence in Uttar Pradesh
content: New Delhi, April 18 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported video showing a few men beating two women was widely shared on social media, with a claim that the men belonged to the upper-caste Hindu community and were attacking tribal-Dalit women in Uttar Pradesh. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral video is actually from Surat, Gujarat, not Uttar Pradesh. The two women were assaulted after allegedly being accused of stealing vegetables. Furthermore, the Surat Police arrested the two accused individuals. No communal angle has been reported in connection with the incident. The viral video was shared with a false claim on social media. Claim On April 13, a Facebook user named 'Sylhetian' shared a video of a few men beating two women, claiming that those men were upper-caste Hindus attacking tribal and Dalit women in Uttar Pradesh. The caption of the post, originally in Bengali, read: "In the BJP-ruled state Uttar Pradesh, the rule of law is going on over indigenous Dalit women !! In their country, Hindus are safe or are persecuted in the name of caste. Again, they think about Bangladesh's Hindus." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation To verify the claim, the Desk carefully analysed the video and found a watermark 'R Bharat Express-News' in the top right corner. Taking a cue from this, the Desk again ran the keyframes of the viral video through the InVid tool search and came across the same video on their Facebook page. According to the video, the incident happened in Puna, a suburb of Surat, not Uttar Pradesh. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the news report. The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports. It came across a report by New 18 dated April 12, 2025, which mentioned that the assault in the viral video occurred on April 6, when the woman, her husband, and daughter entered the market to steal vegetables. There was no mention of caste, and that they were attacked based on their caste. The title of the report read: "Watch: Woman, Daughter Beaten In Broad Daylight At Surat Market For Stealing Vegetables" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. "After a video of the incident spread online, a complaint was filed at the Puna Police Station. The two guards, named Anil Tiwari and Adityasingh Rajeshsingh, were later arrested," the report read. Furthermore, the Desk also scanned the official X (formerly Twitter) handle of Surat Police and came across a post dated April 10, 2025. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video is from Surat, not Uttar Pradesh, and the two women were assaulted after being allegedly accused of stealing vegetables.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Screenshot from scripted video falsely shared as real, claiming father 'married' daughter in Jharkhand
content: New Delhi, April 17 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A photo collage featuring two purported photos of a man and a woman dressed in wedding attire was recently shared on social media, with a claim that they were a father and daughter who had recently gotten married. The user alleged that the incident occurred in Jharkhand's Hazaribagh district, where the man married his 19-year-old daughter after "falling for her beauty." However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the images and found that they do not depict a man in Jharkhand marrying his daughter. Instead, the images were taken from a scripted video skit that portrays an elderly man marrying a young woman, who later runs away with his money. An old, scripted video was thus misleadingly shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user named Yogesh Baghel shared, on April 10, a collage containing two purported photos of a man and a woman in wedding attire. The user claimed they were a father and daughter who had recently gotten married and that the incident occurred in Hazaribagh, Jharkhand. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and found several other social media accounts sharing the same image with similar claims. Two such posts were found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. The Google Lens results also led the Desk to several social media accounts featuring a video where the same man and woman in similar wedding attire, were seen enacting as a newlywed couple. However, in none of these videos did their interaction or dialogue suggest they were father and daughter. Instead it depicted an incident where an elderly man marries an 18-year-old girl who later runs away with his money. Here is the link and archive link to one such post, along with a screenshot. Additionally, during the investigation, it was found that the same video had been posted across different timeframes, casting doubt on the origin and authenticity of the claim. Next, to corroborate the claim made in the viral post, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a video published by a YouTube channel called Monu Boora Vlogs on December 2, 2022. The video at the 6:20 timestamp featured the same individuals seen in the viral photos. However, a close analysis suggested that the duo was acting in a scripted skit titled "100-year-old man marries 18-year-old girl." The background conversation among the cast too confirmed that it was a fictional shoot and not a real wedding. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image highlighting that the couple in the viral post is the same as the one featured in the YouTube video. To further validate that the video was scripted, the Desk used the InVid tool to extract keyframes from the video posted by Monu Boora Vlogs. One such keyframe, featuring the same duo, was then run through Google Lens. This led the Desk to a Facebook page named Prince Verma. The user describes himself as an artist creating weekly entertainment content. As the Desk examined the user's profile, it was observed that the background settings in most of those videos closely resembled the keyframe used for investigation. This indicates a consistent shooting environment typically used for staged or scripted productions. Here is a link and archive link to one such video, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting that the background setting in most of the videos posted by the Facebook page Prince Verma closely resembles the one seen in the keyframe used by the Desk during its investigation. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral image does not depict a man in Jharkhand marrying his daughter. It is actually from a scripted video skit that portrays an elderly man marrying a young woman who later runs away with his money. The content was misrepresented on social media with a fabricated backstory.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video from Raigad's religious rally shared on social media to falsely claim Bajrang Dal members headed to violence-hit West Bengal
content: New Delhi, April 18 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Following recent clashes that erupted in West Bengal during protests against the Waqf (Amendment) Act, a video featuring a massive rally with people holding saffron flags and wooden sticks was widely circulated on social media. Those sharing the video claimed that the rally participants were heading to Kolkata's Raj Bhavan in connection with the recent violence in Murshidabad, West Bengal. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video is neither recent nor related to the protests in West Bengal. The footage was originally recorded in Raigad, Maharashtra, as part of the Dharatirth Gadkot campaign led by Sambhaji Bhide of Shri Shiv Pratishthan Hindustan. The event is also unrelated to the Bajrang Dal. The viral video was misleadingly shared with a false claim. Claim On April 17, a Facebook user named Raushan Singh shared a video showing a massive rally with saffron flags and wooden sticks, claiming that it was a Bajrang Dal rally heading to Kolkata in connection with the recent violence in West Bengal. The underlying text on the post, originally in Hindi, read: "Be a Hindu and Indian citizen by supporting Bajrang Dal, siege of West Bengal government" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . To verify the claim, the Desk first conducted a customised keyword search the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to check if Bajrang Dal had organised a rally or was heading to West Bengal. However, we couldn't find any authentic reports corroborating the claim. Taking a cue from this, the Desk again ran a few keyframes of the viral video through Google Lens and came across the extended version of the same video uploaded on ABP Manjha's official Facebook page, a Marathi news portal, on February 11, 2025. The title of the report read: "Raigad Sambhaji Bhide: Shiv Pratishthan Hindustan Gadkot campaign, Sambhaji Bhide's Dharkari at Raigad #abpmajha #abpMy #raigad #SambhajiBhide" This makes it clear that the video is from a Shiv Pratishthan Hindustan rally in Raigad, Maharashtra, and predates the unrest in West Bengal. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the news report. Next, taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by a Maharashtra-based news outlet 'Jai Maharashtra News' which described that Sambhaji Bhide Guruji, the head of the Shri Shiv Pratishthan Hindustan, led the final day of a four-day Dharatirth Gadkot campaign at Raigad Fort, where millions of saffron-clad supporters had assembled on February 11 (months before the violence struck Murshidabad) Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a religious rally in Maharashtra's Raigad was falsely shared in the name of a Bajrang Dal entourage to West Bengal.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of car seen atop a tree in China falsely shared as incident from India; details inside
content: New Delhi, April 18 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported video of a car mysteriously placed atop a tree was recently shared on social media with the claim that the incident took place in India. The video showed a crowd of onlookers standing beneath a tree, where a white car appeared to be perched around four to five meters above the ground. The car bore the words "xx Driving School" on its body. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was not from India but was filmed in China. It originally showed a promotional stunt by a driving school, which had deliberately hoisted the car onto the tree. Initially, the school claimed that a student had driven the vehicle up there, but later clarified that it was a marketing tactic aimed at attracting admissions. The video was shared online with a false claim. Claim On April16, an X user named 'Rare India Clip' shared the video showing a car dangling from a tree, claiming it depicted an incident from India. At the time of writing this article, the video had garnered over 39,000 views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk used the InVid tool to extract keyframes from the viral video. One of the keyframes was then reverse searched using Google Lens, which led to several other social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The reverse image search also led the Desk to a report published on Daum, a South Korean web portal, on April 18, 2025. The featured image in that report matched the keyframe extracted by the Desk. According to the article, the incident took place in China's Sichuan Province, where a local driving school hoisted the car onto a tree and falsely claimed that a student had driven it there. The driving school was later summoned and cautioned by several authorities, including the traffic police and the Cyber Administration Office. In their defence, the school stated that they took the step due to intense competition among nearby driving schools. "We planned an event to attract people's attention to recruit students," the report quoted an official as saying. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. A combination image below highlights that the background and content seen in the viral video match the feature image of the Daum report. Additionally, the Desk came across a report by cbgc.scol.com.cn, a Chinese news portal, which also confirmed that the video was from Sichuan province and was part of a stunt by a driving school. "On April 12, the reporter learned from the relevant departments of Changning County that the video was posted on a self-media video account named 'Boda Driving School Zihao' and was labelled 'the student drove the car up the tree', which attracted the attention of netizens. After investigating, the departments found that the car had been hoisted onto the tree. The claim that a student drove the car there was false. Moreover, people were seen climbing the tree during the process, which posed a safety hazard. Therefore, local authorities interviewed and warned the school," the report stated. Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a car mysteriously left atop a tree does not depict an incident from India, but from China.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Images showing pro-Palestinian protest in Bangladesh falsely shared as from Kolkata; Details Inside
content: New Delhi, April 21 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared four purported images, claiming they were from Suhrawardy Park in Kolkata, where thousands had allegedly gathered to express solidarity with the Palestinian people amid Israel's actions in the Gaza Strip. The images showed protesters waving Palestinian flags. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the images were not related to Kolkata or India. They originally depicted protests that took place on the streets of Dhaka, the capital of Bangladesh, condemning Israel's actions in the Gaza Strip. The social media post was shared with a false claim. Claim On April 12, an X user 'Quds News Network' shared four purported images, claiming they depicted scenes from protest sites in Suhrawardy Park in Kolkata, where thousands gathered to express their solidarity with the Palestinian people. "Thousands have rallied in Suhrawardy Park, Kolkata, India, in solidarity with the Palestinian people amid the ongoing Israeli genocide in Gaza," the user shared the images with the caption. At the time of posting, the story had garnered 107k views and 5.8k likes. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral images through Google Lens and found several other social media accounts sharing the same images with similar claims. Two such posts were found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search results via Google Lens also led the Desk to a post by Bangladesh-based television channel Somoy TV on April 12. The channel, on its official Facebook page, shared images matching those seen in the viral post. The images were shared with the caption: "March for Gaza. Millions of people are gathering at Suhrawardy Park in the procession." Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk also conducted a customised keyword search on Google to verify the actual location of Suhrawardy Park. The search results confirmed that it is located in Dhaka, Bangladesh, not in India. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a comparison image highlighting that the images in the viral post are the same as those featured in Somoy TV's post. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk this time conducted another customised keyword search on Google to gather more details about the protests that erupted on the streets of Dhaka. The search led the Desk to a news report by the Associated Press (AP), which stated that on April 12, tens of thousands of protesters rallied in Dhaka to condemn Israel's actions in the Gaza Strip. "The protesters, estimated at some 100,000, gathered at Suhrawardy Park in the Dhaka University area. They carried hundreds of Palestinian flags and chanted slogans such as 'Free, Free Palestine.' Symbolic coffins and effigies representing civilian casualties were carried during the rally," the report stated. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the images showing pro-Palestinian protests at Suhrawardy Park were from Bangladesh and not India.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Fake social media post shared to claim 150 accused in Murshidabad violence recorded statements in Hindi; details inside
content: New Delhi, April 21 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported screenshot bearing the watermark of News29 was widely shared on social media, with users claiming that the 150 accused in the Murshidabad violence recorded their statements in Hindi rather than Bengali. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral graphic was misleadingly shared as real. Upon further investigation, it was found that the viral post was fake, and the graphic was originally shared by a parody account named News29. The viral post was shared with a false claim on social media. Notably, the violence erupted on April 11 during protests against the Waqf (Amendment) Act, leaving three dead and hundreds displaced. Claim On April 17, an X (formerly Twitter) user named Bilal Ahmad shared a purported screenshot bearing the watermark of News29, claiming that 150 accused, in the Murshidabad violence, recorded their statements in Hindi rather than Bengali. The post's caption, which garnered 3,065 views, read: "You understood something,I did not understand." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Reverse Image Search and found several users shared the same viral screenshot with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived version can be viewed here and here . To verify the claim, the Desk found that there is no news portal by the name 'News29', indicating that it might be a dubious account of the news channel 'News 24'. Further search results revealed that the purported screenshot was originally shared on X by a user named 'TV 29'. The caption clarified that it is a parody post and should not be taken seriously. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. The bio section of the profile clearly mentions 'parody', which makes it clear that the post is fake. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Moreover, the Desk did not find any credible media reports stating that 150 accused in the Murshidabad violence recorded their statements in Hindi instead of Bengali. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across a PTI report carried by Hindustan Times on April 20, which stated that 100 FIRs have been lodged in the Murshidabad violence cases, and so far, 276 people have been arrested in these cases. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Another report by The Hindu, dated April 18, citing Director General of Police (South Bengal) Supratim Sarkar, mentioned that the police arrested the third accused, Inzamul Haque, in connection with the murder of Hargobind Das and his son Chandan Das during the recent violence in Murshidabad. The other accused arrested were Kalu Nawab and Dildar Nawab. None of the reports mentioned that the accused recorded the statements in Hindi. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral post was fake, and the graphic was originally shared by a parody account named News29.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of police thrashing intoxicated man falsely shared as recent incident linking it to Waqf protest in Madhya Pradesh
content: New Delhi, April 22 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video depicting a few police personnel thrashing a person on a street until he collapses was recently shared on social media. The user claimed that the accused seen in the video was a minority Muslim boy who was hit for protesting the Waqf Act in Madhya Pradesh. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral video dates back to 2020, and the two police personnel were beating an allegedly intoxicated man as he was creating a ruckus in Chhindwara District of Madhya Pradesh. Additionally, there have been no reports stating that a Muslim man was killed in Madhya Pradesh concerning the Waqf Bill protests. Notably, the violence erupted on April 11 during protests against the Waqf (Amendment) Act, leaving three dead and hundreds displaced. Claim On April 14, an X (formerly Twitter) user named Md Rafiqul Islam Hoby shared a video depicting a few police personnel thrashing a person on a street. The user claimed that the person was a minority Muslim boy who was hit for protesting the Waqf Bill in Madhya Pradesh. The post's caption, originally in Bangla, read: "Madhya Pradesh. This is the condition of Muslims in India (the neighbouring country is the New Israel in India). Police are beating up a minority Muslim boy for protesting the Waqf Bill. How can inhumans called humans beat a living person to death" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived version can be viewed here and here , respectively. To verify the claim, the Desk ran the keyframes of the viral video circulating on social media and found the same video uploaded on Facebook on May 25, 2020 (which pre-dates the passage of the Waqf Board Bill) by Th News Channel. As per the caption of the post accused man was drunk and creating a ruckus when the two policemen used force against him. The incident occurred in Madhya Pradesh's Chhindwara district. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. This clarifies that the video has been on the internet since 2020, while the Waqf Board Bill was passed on April 3, 2025. Furthermore, below is a screenshot highlighting the similarity between the viral video and the Facebook post. On further scanning the search results, the Desk also found a video report by the Punjab Kesari MP on May 24, 2020, in which the policemen were seen brutally beating a man, allegedly a drug addict named Vaman Sarai, until he fell unconscious. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking cue from the above-generated inputs, we then conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports citing the same incident. The Desk came across a report by NDTV dated May 24, 2020. As per the article, two policemen are seen raining blows on a man, apparently intoxicated, with their batons in a video that has been widely shared on social media, triggering huge criticism. "Two policemen are seen raining blows on a man, apparently intoxicated, with their batons in a video that has been widely shared on social media, triggering huge criticism. The video from Madhya Pradesh's Chhindwara, about 300 km from the state capital Bhopal, has now prompted a probe by the city police," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to 2020 and depicts two police personnel beating an allegedly drunk man in Madhya Pradesh. The incident is unrelated to the protest against the Waqf Bill.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Viral post claiming GST charge on UPI transactions over ₹2,000 is baseless, no such proposal in consideration by the government; details inside
content: New Delhi, April 22 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A post featuring Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman was recently circulated on social media, claiming that the finance ministry has considered the imposition of Goods and Services Tax (GST) on UPI transactions exceeding ₹2000. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found it to be completely false, misleading, and without any factual basis. Furthermore, the government is not currently considering a proposal regarding the imposition of GST on UPI transactions. The viral post was shared on social media with a baseless and misleading claim. Claim On April 18, an Instagram user named 'thenaughtytrolls' shared a post featuring Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman claiming that the finance ministry is considering imposing Goods and Services Tax (GST) on UPI transactions above ₹2000. The Indian government has reportedly considered imposing the Goods and Services Tax (GST) on UPI (Unified Payments Interface) transactions exceeding ₹2,000. This move has sparked widespread discussions among consumers and digital payment users nationwide. As UPI has become a primary mode of payment for millions, this change may impact daily spending, especially for small businesses, freelancers, and middle-class families," read the post's caption, which garnered 5,584 likes when uploading this article. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through Reverse Image Search and found several other users had shared a similar post with the same caption on social media. Two such posts can be viewed here and here . To verify the claim made in the viral post, the Desk first conducted a customised keyword search to find relevant media reports, but no such report was found. Also, the Desk scanned the Ministry of Finance's official website, but the search did not yield any official announcement regarding the same. However, if such a proposal had been under the government's consideration, it would have garnered the media's attention. Upon conducting another set of customised keyword searches, we found an article by India TV, dated April 21, which clarified that GST is levied on charges, such as the Merchant Discount Rate (MDR), relating to payments made using specific instruments. "Amid reports that the government is considering levying Goods and Services Tax (GST) on UPI (Unified Payments Interface) transactions over Rs 2,000, the Ministry of Finance has issued a clarification and stated that these claims are "completely false, misleading, and without any basis." The ministry also said that GST is levied on charges, such as the Merchant Discount Rate (MDR), relating to payments made using certain instruments," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk also looked for the official statement from the ministry. It came across a press release from the Ministry of Finance, dated April 18, which stated that the claims that the Government is considering levying Goods and Services Tax (GST) on UPI transactions over ₹2,000 are entirely false, misleading, and without any basis. "The claims that the Government is considering levying Goods and Services Tax (GST) on UPI transactions over ₹2,000 are false, misleading, and without any basis. Currently, there is no such proposal before the Government…The Government remains committed to promoting digital payments via UPI," it read. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim that the government will impose GST on UPI transactions is false, and the ministry or the government has made no such announcement.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of local Tripura politician arguing with cop falsely shared as incident from West Bengal; details inside
content: New Delhi, April 22 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing an altercation between a woman police personnel and an individual was recently shared on social media with a claim that the incident pertained to West Bengal. The user claimed the incident occurred in the state, where a local leader (associated with the ruling TMC) traded barbs with a woman DIG amid reports of violence there. In the video, the duo were engaged in a heated argument, with the woman official blaming the man for gathering a huge crowd and disturbing the law and order situation. However, in its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found the video was falsely shared under West Bengal. It originally depicted an altercation between a local Congress leader and a top police official from Tripura during a protest held in the state over the passing of the Waqf Amendment Act. An unrelated video was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim On April 17, an X user '@HiNdU05019434' shared a video showing an alleged altercation that broke out between a West Bengal woman DIG and a local TMC leader. Sharing the video, the user stated, "How a TMC person is talking to a DIG, threatening her. The officer is pretending to be helpless and listening to everything... Do you know why... Because the person in front is a Muslim. And in Bengal, the police are not allowed to talk loudly to Muslims." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk used the InVid tool to extract keyframes from the viral video. One keyframe was then reverse-searched using Google Lens, leading to several other social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search result via Google Lens also led the Desk to a video posted on a channel named Daily Post Tripura on April 14, 2025. The handle posted the video that matched the viral one; however, it was shared with the caption, "Badruzzaman exchanges words with the Superintendent of Police." The post also identified the location of the incident as "Kailashahar," a town in Tripura. Here is the link and archive link to the port, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image, highlighting that the content seen in the viral video matches that of the video posted by the YouTube channel. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk held a customised keyword search on Google to find the identity of the person seen involved in the altercation with the police personnel in Tripura, and other details surrounding the development. The search result using the keywords "Kailashahar," "SP," and "Badruzzaman" led the Desk to a report published by the Assam Tribune on April 12, 2025. The report's feature image matched the visuals of the people (the police personnel and the local leader) seen in the viral video, whereas the details revealed a scuffle broke out between agitating protesters and police personnel in Kailashahar, Tripura. "A violent scuffle broke out between protesters and police personnel on security duty in Kailashahar, the headquarters of Unakoti district, on Saturday. The clash followed a protest rally by Muslim community members against the Waqf Amendment Act. The rally was led by Congress leader Badruj Jaman (Badruzzaman), who also serves as the Chairperson of the local Panchayat Samiti," the report stated. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. The search result via Google Lens also led the Desk to a report on April 12 by The Times of India covering developments surrounding the incident. It also stated that "tensions prevailed in Kubjahar and a few neighbouring villages along the India-Bangladesh border in Kailashahar of Tripura's Unakoti district after a protest rally against the Waqf (Amendment) Act turned violent, leaving two policemen injured." Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video originally featured a Congress leader from Tripura arguing with the district's Superintendent of Police during a violent protest that broke out in the state.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video showing hidden sculpture of Goddess Kali falsely shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, April 22 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video featuring a massive sculpture of Goddess Kali was recently shared on social media. Users claimed it was carved into the earth, hidden for centuries, and now discovered in a forest. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found the claim false. Upon further investigation, it was revealed that the viral video showing a Goddess Kali temple in a forest was found to be AI-generated. Claim On April 18, an X (formerly Twitter) user named Ankita shared a video showing an ancient Goddess Kali sculpture, claiming it was carved into the earth and hidden for centuries. "Unearthed in Silence- The Jungle Temple of Maa Kaali Deep in the heart of a mist-laden forest, an awe-inspiring revelation- a colossal Maa Kaali sculpture carved into the earth itself, hidden for centuries, revealed by time," read the post's caption which garnered 1,387 views. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived version can be viewed here and here. The Desk first conducted a customised keyword search on Google to verify the claim and find relevant media reports. However, the search did not result in credible reports citing the information in the viral post. Further, on closer analysis of the video, the Desk also noticed that the sculpture featured in different idols of Goddess Kali in various locations in the viral video, indicating that it might be fake or AI-generated. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. The Desk ran a few keyframes of the viral video through Hive Moderation, an AI detection tool. The tool detected a substantial presence of AI-generated elements in the image. Below is a screenshot of the result: The Desk ran the viral photo through WasitAI, another AI detection tool, indicating a substantial presence of AI-generated content. Below is a screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was AI-generated.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Fake X handle in name of UPSC topper Shakti Dubey became active soon after results were declared; details inside
content: New Delhi, April 22 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Soon after the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) Examination 2024 final results were declared on Tuesday, and Shakti Dubey, a resident of Prayagraj, was announced as the topper, an X account (formerly Twitter) claiming to be her official handle began publishing multiple posts, including photos of Dubey and tweets attributed to her. The account quickly garnered thousands of followers, and its posts—allegedly offering personal insights into her examination journey and celebrating her success—reached a wide audience. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk closely analysed the handle and found it falsely linked to Shakti Dubey. Upon investigation, it was discovered that the account was initially created in January 2020 under the username @dhruvuncut. Following the announcement of the UPSC CSE 2024 results, the user changed the display name to "Shakti Dubey" in an apparent attempt to gain followers and social media traction. Claim On April 22, several social media posts began circulating online, claiming to be from the official X handle of UPSC CSE 2024 topper Shakti Dubey. The handle going with the username @ShaktiDubey01 was seen making posts allegedly sharing personal insights into Dubey's examination journey and celebrating her result. Here is the link and archive link to the social media handle in question, along with a screenshot of one of its posts. When this article was published, the post shared above had gained 892k views and 18k likes. Investigation To verify the authenticity of the profile, the PTI Fact Check Desk thoroughly examined the user's past posts. The search result led the Desk to an old post ( link provided here) made by the same user on February 16, 2024. Upon inspecting the comments under the post, the Desk noticed that replies were attributed to the username @dhruvUncut. Had the handle originally belonged to Shakti Dubey, the replies would have reflected the username @ShaktiDubey01 instead of @dhruvUncut. Below is a screenshot highlighting the findings. During the investigation, the Desk also found several comments from users who shared screenshots indicating that the handle currently operating under @ShaktiDubey01 was previously running as @dhruvUncut. Below is a screenshot highlighting the findings. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the X handle claiming to belong to Shakti Dubey, topper of the Civil Services Examination 2024, is false. After the UPSC results were announced, the handle was initially operated under the username @dhruvUncut and rebranded to impersonate Shakti Dubey.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: This social media post claiming FASTag will be replaced by a GPS-based toll system from May 1 is false
content: New Delhi, April 23 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a post claiming that, starting from May 1, 2025, the central government will roll out a GPS-based toll collection system, replacing the existing FASTag system. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found the viral post's claim to be false. Upon further investigation, it was revealed that no decision has been made regarding the nationwide implementation of satellite-based tolling from May 1, 2025. Claim On April 17, an X (formerly Twitter) user named 'Gems' shared a post claiming that FASTags will be replaced by the GPS-based toll system on May 1, 2025. "No More Stops In Toll Booths —India Launches GPS-based Tolling from May 1, 2025," read the post's caption, which garnered 20,1k views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral post through Reverse Image Search and found several other social media accounts sharing the same images with similar claims. One such post can be found here , with its archived version available here . To verify the claim, the Desk initially conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports. However, the search yielded no credible reports suggesting the GPS-based tolling system would be implemented from May 1, 2025. However, on further scanning, we did find a press release from the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways, dated April 18, which categorically mentioned that no such decision has been taken by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways or National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) regarding the nationwide implementation of satellite-based tolling from 1st May 2025. "To enable seamless, barrier-free movement of vehicles through toll plazas and reduce travel time, ' ANPR-FASTag-based Barrier-Less Tolling System' will be implemented at selected toll plazas," the release read. Here is the link to the release, and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk then conducted another set of customised keyword searches on Google and came across several reports that clarified that India was not launching a satellite toll system in May. One such report by NDTV, dated April 20, 2025, stated that a new hybrid tolling system will be tested on specific routes, with no nationwide rollout planned yet. The report headline read: "Will FASTag Be Replaced By GPS-Based Tolling From May 1? Here's What the Government Said" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that no decision has been made on nationwide satellite-based tolling since May 1, 2025.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Edited and fake screenshot of 2019 BBC Hindi report falsely shared linking it to recent Murshidabad violence
content: New Delhi, April 23 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A screenshot of a purported article from BBC Hindi website was circulated on social media, with users linking it to the recent violence in Murshidabad. The post alleged that individuals disguised as Muslims were involved in criminal activities during the unrest in Murshidabad, West Bengal. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk revealed that the claim is false. The news report in question dates back to 2019, and the two images being shared are from the protests in West Bengal against the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA) that year. Thus, both the article and the visuals are outdated and unrelated to the recent incidents in Murshidabad.
