Claim On April 19, an X (formerly Twitter) user named 'Kabeerthapar' shared a screengrab of an alleged news article published by BBC Hindi, claiming that people disguised themselves as Muslims to commit crimes during the violence in Murshidabad. The headline of the report, originally in Hindi, read: "Wearing caps and lungis, RSS men were pelting stones on the train: Press Review" "A group of frustrated hate-filled, disguised, paid, Sanghi criminals who have gone to Bengal's Murshidabad in the guise of Muslims to commit crimes, Sanghis have been caught many times earlier also while plotting such things, Mamata's police has arrested around 150 rioters, they can only speak Hindi," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral post through Reverse Image Search and found several other social media accounts sharing the same images with similar claims. Two such posts were found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. Further, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find the original BBC Hindi report, which was dated December 21, 2019. Though the report's headline was similar to one shared in the viral post, it did not carry the two images seen in the viral post. The report, citing the Telegraph newspaper, mentioned that six people were wearing caps and lungis. All of them are said to be associated with the Sangh Parivar. Two of these six people have been sent to police custody for five days. The remaining four boys are minors, three of whom have been booked under serious crimes and sent to jail for 14 days. According to The Telegraph newspaper, these six people were wearing caps and lungis, all said to be associated with the Sangh Parivar. Two of these six people have been sent to police custody for five days. The remaining four boys are minors, three of whom have been booked under serious crimes and sent to jail for 14 days. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk debunked the two images shared in the viral post. We ran the first image of the viral photo through Reverse Image Search. We came across reports mentioning that the picture shows an anti-CAA protest held in Satragachi, West Bengal's Howrah district, on December 14, 2019. The Free Press Journal carried a PTI photograph in its report dated December 15, 2019, mentioning that the West Bengal government had suspended internet services in some parts of the state following continuing violence by protesters railing against the new citizenship law (CAA). The headline of the report read: "Internet services suspended in parts of West Bengal, trains cancelled amid Citizenship Amendment Act protests" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between one of the images of the viral post and the news report. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk ran the second image seen in the viral post through Reverse Image Search and came across a report by The Statesman dated December 13, 2019. According to the article, the picture depicts Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA) protesters torching railway stations in Bengal. The headline of the report read: "Citizenship Act Protesters torch railway stations in Bengal" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral post and the news report. Also, the Desk contacted the Editor of BBC Hindi for an official statement, and the article will be updated once a response is received. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral actual report and the visuals are old and unrelated to the recent violence in Murshidabad

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video from Bangladesh falsely shared as 'Indian Army raids' in West Bengal; details inside
content: New Delhi, April 23 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing uniformed officials arresting people across different locations was recently shared on social media with the claim that it showed alleged perpetrators behind the violence that broke out in West Bengal's Murshidabad and South 24 Parganas districts following protests against the Waqf (Amendment) Act. The video appeared to depict Indian Army personnel arresting several individuals and raiding homes. However, upon investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was unrelated to West Bengal. It initially showed Bangladesh Army officials arresting drug traffickers in Mohammadpur. An unrelated video was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An X user, Nirmal Kumar Jha (@NirmalJ8881922), shared the video on April 21, claiming it showed Indian Army officials cracking down on the perpetrators of the violence that erupted in West Bengal. The footage showed uniformed officials arresting several individuals in different locations. "Indian soldiers are hunting down and arresting the Islamic invaders who committed atrocities in West Bengal—they must not be spared this time," the user posted alongside the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. When this article was published, the post had garnered 3.8k views. Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk used the InVid tool to extract keyframes from the viral video. One keyframe was reverse-searched using Google Lens, leading to several other social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here : The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a video published on the official YouTube channel of BanglaVision NEWS, a Bangladesh-based media outlet. The viral video's visuals matched those in a video uploaded by the channel, which documented a 100-minute operation conducted by the Bangladesh Army in Mohammadpur in October 2024. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image highlighting the visuals that match the viral clip and the original BanglaVision video. In the next step of the investigation, taking cues from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to learn more about the Bangladesh Army's operation in Mohammadpur. The search led to a report by the Bangladesh-based news portal Kalbela, published on October 28, 2024. The report described the Bangladesh Army's operation in Mohammadpur as a move to arrest drug dealer Bunia Sohel based on secret information. "Although the army was unable to arrest him, it was able to arrest his seven accomplices," the report stated. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing uniformed officials arresting several Muslim individuals and raiding homes was from Bangladesh and not from West Bengal. The claim shared on social media is false.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated photo showing bodies lying on ground falsely shared and linked to Pahalgam terror attack victims; details inside
content: New Delhi, April 23 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A day after the gruesome terror attack in Pahalgam, Jammu & Kashmir, multiple social media users shared a picture depicting several bodies lying on the ground, apparently injured or dead. Users claimed it showed the aftermath of the terror attack in Pahalgam. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the picture was AI-generated and was shared on social media with a false claim. According to reports, at least 26 civilians, mostly tourists, were shot dead by terrorists in Pahalgam, located in Jammu & Kashmir's Anantnag district, on Tuesday, marking one of the deadliest attacks in the Valley since the Pulwama strike in 2019. Claim On April 23, an X (formerly Twitter) user named 'Ayushi' shared a purported image showing the aftermath of the terror attack in Pahalgam, Jammu & Kashmir. "Show this picture to the people sitting in power, this should boil their blood enough to take the ugliest revenge ever known to mankind. #Pahalgam #PahalgamTerroristAttack," read the post's caption, which garnered 1,234 views so far. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through Reverse Image Search and found several users shared the same image with a similar claim on social media. One such post can be found here , with its archived version available here . After carefully scanning the post, the Desk came across a comment that mentioned the image was fake. Below is a screenshot highlighting this. The Desk also noticed several discrepancies, such as the overall glossy texture of the image and the lack of detail in the faces, which suggest that it may be AI-generated. Further, with the extensive media coverage of the terror attack, we couldn't find any such photograph. In the subsequent part of the investigation, taking cues from the above findings, the Desk ran the image through Hive Moderation, an AI detection tool. The tool detected a substantial presence of AI-generated elements in the image. Below is a screenshot of the result: The Desk ran the viral photo through WasitAI, another AI detection tool, indicating a substantial presence of AI-generated content. Below is a screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral photo is AI-generated

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2020 video of child sitting beside dead body falsely linked to recent Pahalgam terror attack; details inside
content: New Delhi, April 23 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A heart-wrenching video (which included an image of a child sitting next to a dead body, immediately followed by visuals of him crying) was recently shared on social media with the claim that it showed a Hindu boy sitting next to the body of his father, who was killed in the recent terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir's Pahalgam. However, in its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was unrelated to the Pahalgam terror attack. The video actually dates back to July 1, 2020, and shows a three-year-old Muslim boy sitting next to the body of his grandfather, who was killed during a terror attack in Jammu & Kashmir's Sopore. An old video was shared on social media with a false claim. Meanwhile, it is pertinent to note that terrorists opened fire at a famed meadow near Kashmir's Pahalgam town on April 22, killing 26 people, mostly tourists. The attack has been described as the deadliest in the Valley since the Pulwama strike in 2019. Claim An X user '@RealArnab_' shared, on April 23, a heart-wrenching video where a child was seen sitting next to a dead body. The video also included visuals of the child crying inconsolably. It was shared with the claim that it depicted the plight of a Hindu boy who lost his father in the Pahalgam terror attack the previous day. "#Muslims tell me what is the fault of this child? His father was shot in front of him. They checked the father's pants in front of an innocent child and shot him in the streets because he was #Hindu... #Pahalgam #PahalgamTerroristAttack," read the caption accompanying the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk used the InVid tool to extract keyframes from the viral video. One of the keyframes was then reverse-searched using Google Lens, leading to several other social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here : The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a video published by India Today on its official YouTube channel on July 1, 2020. The footage included visuals of the child sitting next to a dead body, as seen in the viral post. However, the description clarified that the incident occurred in 2020, when security forces in Jammu and Kashmir's Sopore rescued a three-year-old boy who was sitting beside his grandfather, who had been shot by terrorists. It is thus clear that the viral video has no connection to the Pahalgam terror attack. Here is the link to the post along with a screenshot. In the next step of the investigation, taking cues from the above, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by The Times of India on July 1, 2020. According to the report, the incident dated back to 2020 and showed heartbreaking images of a three-year-old boy sitting on the motionless body of his grandfather in J&K's Sopore. The 60-year-old grandfather, identified as Bashir Ahmad Khan, was killed in crossfire during an encounter between militants and security forces. The police later rescued the boy and took him to a shelter. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to July 2020. It shows a three-year-old child sitting near the motionless body of his grandfather, who was shot during the Sopore terror attack on July 1, 2020. The video is unrelated to the Pahalgam terror attack that occurred on April 22, 2025.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of Delhi couple who visited Pahalgam a week before terror attack falsely shared as Karnal victim Vinay Narwal's last moments; details inside
content: New Delhi, April 24 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid the tragic demise of 26 tourists in the horrific terror attack in Kashmir's Pahalgam on April 22, a video showing a man and woman dancing to a popular song was widely circulated on social media. Users claimed it showed one of the last moments of deceased Naval officer Vinay Narwal with his wife before the attack that took his life. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video does not show the final moments of Vinay Narwal along with his wife. It originally featured another couple, Yashika and Ashish Sehrawat, who later clarified on their social media accounts that the video was theirs, shot during a recent trip to Kashmir. It is now being falsely shared in the name of Vinay Narwal and his wife. Meanwhile, it is pertinent to note that the April 22 terror attack in Pahalgam killed 26 tourists, mostly Indians. The incident sparked nationwide outrage, with the Indian government vowing strict action against the perpetrators who, officials said, conspired to execute the heinous act from behind the scenes. Claim An X user '@RealBababanaras' shared a video on April 23, asserting that it depicted the last moments of Lieutenant Vinay Narwal, a Naval officer, with his wife, before he was killed in a terrorist attack in Pahalgam on April 22. The video allegedly showed both Narwal and his wife dancing on a popular song amid the scenic views of Kashmir. "Lt Vinay Narwal's last video from Kashmir. Pak will pay for this. #PahalgamTerroristAttack," the post stated. When this story was published, the video had garnered 36.2k views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk used the InVid tool to extract keyframes from the viral video. One keyframe was then reverse-searched using Google Lens, leading to several other social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. In the next step of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to learn more about the viral video. However, the search result led the Desk to a footage published from an Instagram account named Ashish Sehrawat on April 24, 2025. The user, who identified himself as a professional cricketer and Indian Railways Ranji Trophy player, stated in the video, shot along with his wife, that the couple dancing in Kashmir was him and his wife, Yashika Sehrawat, and not Vinay Narwal and his wife. "Hey guys, we are alive and wanted to address a recent video we posted that unfortunately sparked a lot of hatred, leading us to delete it. Sadly, the video was misused by multiple pages and news channels, falsely claiming it was the last video of late Vinay Sir and his wife. Our heartfelt condolences go out to their family. We kindly request that you report any pages misusing our video, as it's truly disheartening," the user stated. "It's shocking to see even reputable news channels and pages using unverified content for views, making it challenging to trust news sources," he added. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk also contacted Yashika Sehrawat, who clarified in her statement that the video belonged to her and her husband, Ashish Sehrawat. She said they had visited Pahalgam just a week before the terror attack struck the region. "As we were getting lots of calls from our well-wishers checking on our safety, we posted the video to let everyone know we were safe. Unfortunately, the video did not go down well and triggered a lot of hatred, forcing us to remove it. However, later we saw that the video was misused by multiple pages and news channels, falsely claiming it was the last video of the late Naval officer Vinay Narwal and his wife. We extend our heartfelt condolences to the victim's family," Yashika Sehrawat told the PTI Fact Check team. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video does not depict one of the last moments of Naval officer Vinay Narwal with his wife before the terrorist attack in Pahalgam killed him.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2020 video of shelling between India and Pakistan falsely shared as recent, linked to Pahalgam terror attack
content: New Delhi, April 24 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing artillery fire has been widely circulated on social media, with claims suggesting it depicts a recent exchange of shelling between India and Pakistan in the Tattapani sector along the Line of Control (LoC), following the terrorist attack in Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk reviewed the video and found the social media claims false. The investigation revealed that the video actually dates back to 2020 and is unrelated to the recent incident. It shows the Indian Army responding to a ceasefire violation by Pakistan in the Poonch area of Jammu and Kashmir. According to reports, terrorists opened fire on tourists in Pahalgam on Tuesday (April 22) afternoon, killing at least 26 men. Eyewitnesses stated that the attackers asked for the victims' identities and targeted those who were non-Muslims. Claim On April 23, an X (formerly Twitter) user named Amit Bhardwaj shared a video depicting artillery firing, claiming that it happened between Pakistan and India in Tattapani Sector at the LOC after the recent terrorist attack in Pahalgam. Heavy artillery shelling between Pakistan and India in the Tattapani Sector at the LOC. (Sources). More details soon," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk used the InVid tool to extract keyframes from the viral video. One keyframe was then reverse-searched using Google Lens, leading to several other social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here : On further scanning the search results, the Desk found that the same video was uploaded to several Facebook pages in 2020. A Facebook page named IAF Garud uploaded the same video on April 15, 2020. This clarifies that the video has no relation to the recent Pahalgam attack in Jammu and Kashmir. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the Facebook post of April 2020. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk ran another set of keyframes of the viral video through the InVid Tool search and came across a video report by Republic Bharat dated June 14, 2020. As per the report, the Indian army was giving a befitting reply to Pakistan, which violated the ceasefire in Poonch, Jammu & Kashmir. Though the report did not mention the source or the location of the video, it is evident that the incident is old. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Meanwhile, a day after the Pahalgam terror attack, the Indian Army and other security forces have been given a free hand to take retaliatory action. The Pakistani army violated the ceasefire along the Line of Control in the Tattapani area of Poonch, as per a report by News 18 dated April 23. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to 2020 when the Indian army was giving a befitting reply to Pakistan, after they violated the ceasefire in Poonch, Jammu & Kashmir. It is unrelated to the recent terrorist attack in Pahalgam.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old and unrelated video of Indian Army personnel falsely shared as recent, linking it to Pahalgam terror attack
content: New Delhi, April 24 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Days after the tragic incident in Pahalgam, where at least 26 tourists lost their lives in a hail of gunfire, a video began circulating on social media allegedly showing an Indian Army personnel seemingly shooting at two bodies. Social media users claimed the footage depicted an incident that occurred in the aftermath of the Pahalgam terror attack. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the matter and confirmed that the video was shared with a misleading and false claim. The viral footage has been available online since 2020 and resurfaced in 2022. It has no connection to the recent Pahalgam attack. Meanwhile, two days after the attack, India announced a series of diplomatic measures, including the closure of the main border crossing between the two countries, the suspension of a landmark water-sharing treaty, the expulsion of diplomats, and an order requiring some Pakistani visa holders to leave the country within 48 hours. Claim On April 23, a Facebook user shared a video featuring an Indian Army person shooting two bodies, claiming that the incident was from the recent terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir's Pahalgam. "A scene that calms the mind has arrived. The revenge of the new India has begun. We will enter every house and kill them. Jai Hind Sena," read the post's caption, originally in Hindi. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived version can be viewed here and here . On running the keyframes of the viral video through Reverse Image Search, the Desk found the same video shared on a website in 2022. In the video, a man can be heard speaking in Hindi, referring to the soldier as an "Indian Army commando." The title of the video read: "Indian army executes Kashmiri militants." Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a Facebook post dated December 18, 2020, which featured the same video along with several other clips, as seen in the viral video. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Though we could not independently verify the video's location, incident, or date, the investigation clearly shows that it has been on the internet since 2020 and was re-shared in 2022. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video pre-dates the recent terror attack in Pahalgam. It has been on the internet since 2020 and was re-shared in 2022.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Imran Khan's 2019 video of warning of retaliation against India falsely shared as recent, linking it to Pahalgam terror attack
content: New Delhi, April 25 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Following the terror attack in Pahalgam that claimed the lives of 26 tourists, a purported television address by former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan surfaced, in which he allegedly said that Pakistan would retaliate if India chose to attack. Social media users claimed that his statement came in response to the recent Pahalgam terror attack and Prime Minister Modi's warning to identify, track, and punish those responsible, along with their backers. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video was shared with a false claim on social media. Upon further investigation, it was revealed that the viral video actually dates back to 2019, when former Pakistan PM Imran Khan issued a statement following the Pulwama bombing that killed over 40 CRPF soldiers. The video is unrelated to the recent terror attack in Pahalgam. On February 14, 2019, the Pakistan-based terror group Jaish-e-Mohammed was behind the Pulwama attack. A 19-year-old school dropout who had joined the outfit the previous year was the suicide bomber who targeted a convoy of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), killing nearly 40 personnel. Claim On April 23, an X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video featuring former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan, claiming that they will retaliate if India chooses to attack after the terror attack in Pahalgam, J&K. In the video, former Pakistan PM Khan can be heard saying: "If you think that will launch any attack, then Pakistan will not just think about the retaliation. Pakistan will retaliate." Meanwhile, the post's caption, which garnered 4,029 views, read: "Pakistan will not just think about the retaliation; Pakistan will retaliate: Imran Khan. #PahalgamTerroristAttack #Pahalgam" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived version can be viewed here and here . To begin with, the 72-year-old Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder has been incarcerated since 2023, which hints that this television address of the former Pakistan PM might be old and not regarding the recent Pahalgam attack. His statements are shared by the visitors who meet him in Rawalpindi's Adiala Jail. Moreover, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search but found no credible reports citing former PM Khan stating retaliation. But we did come across a PTI report by The Print dated April 22, 2025, which mentioned that Khan has said that the country and its people need the establishment and his party to secure national unity and stability. The report headline read, "Imran Khan says Pak needs both the establishment and his party to secure national unity and stability." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. "The jailed PTI leader claimed that the country had been turned into a "banana republic" to crush the party and that institutions including the judiciary, Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) and police had been damaged in the process," read a section of the report. Further, we conducted another set of customised keyword searches and came across a video report from the Hindustan Times on February 19, 2019. As per the report, Imran Khan's reaction comes days after at least 40 CRPF jawans were killed in a terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir. Pakistan-backed terror outfit Jaish-e-Mohammad claimed responsibility for the attack. At 00:38 seconds timestamp, Imran Khan can be heard saying: "...If you think you will launch any attack on Pakistan. Pakistan will not think before retaliating. Pakistan will retaliate. There will be no other answer except retaliating…" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the report. Further searches also led us to several reports, one of which was published by NDTV on February 19, 2019. The report also carried the former Pakistan PM's video address. "This is Imran Khan's first statement on the Pulwama attack, the worst-ever terror strike on security forces in Jammu and Kashmir. Nearly 40 CRPF soldiers were killed in the attack," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to 2019 when former Pakistan PM Imran Khan issued a statement following the bombing in Pulwama that killed over 40 CRPF soldiers.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old mock-drill video from Anantnag falsely shared as footage from Pahalgam terror attack; details inside
content: New Delhi, April 25 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of two armed, masked men entering a building structure, followed by visuals showing security officials with guns cordoning off the area, was recently shared on social media with the claim that it depicted the original visuals of the Pahalgam terror attack that killed 26 innocent tourists on April 22. The video showed the masked men armed with guns hurriedly entering a building, followed by visuals of security officials pursuing them in an attempt to capture the duo. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it to be unrelated to the Pahalgam terror attack. The video originally showed a mock-drill conducted by Anantnag Police at Bijbehara Railway Station back in February 2025. The drill was part of the security preparations ahead of the Vande Bharat Express train flag-off event. An old and unrelated video was falsely linked to the Pahalgam terror attack on social media. Claim A YouTube channel named 'Dibya Assam' shared a video on April 24 with the claim that it depicted original visuals of the Pahalgam terror attack that killed 26 innocent tourists on April 22. The video showed two armed, masked men entering a building structure, followed by visuals of security officials with guns cordoning off the area. "Pahalgam Terror Attack LIVE Video: Pakistani Terrorist Attacked Indian Innocent People," the user shared the video with the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk used the InVid tool to extract keyframes from the viral video. One keyframe was then reverse-searched using Google Lens, leading to several other social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. One such post can be found here , with archive versions available respectively. The search result via Google Lens also led the Desk to a video posted on the official X handle of the Press Trust of India. The handle posted the video (matching the viral video) along with a caption stating that the footage depicted a mock drill conducted by Anantnag Police back in February 2025. "Anantnag Police conducted a mock drill at Bijbehara Railway Station earlier today, as part of security preparations ahead of the Vande Bharat Express train flag-off event," the caption read. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting how the content seen in the viral video matches the video posted by the news agency on its X handle. Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customized keyword search on Google to check if any videos linked to the Pahalgam terror attack were being circulated. The search result led the Desk to a report published by India Today on April 24, 2025. The report included chilling visuals where terrorists could be seen firing at unsuspecting tourists in Pahalgam. The sounds of gunshots and screams of tourists can also be heard in the background. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was not linked to the Pahalgam terror attack. It originally depicted a mock drill conducted by Anantnag Police at Bijbehara Railway Station in February 2025.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video pertaining to clashes at Nepal college falsely shared in name of attack on Kashmiri student post Pahalgam terror attack; details inside
content: New Delhi, April 26 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid the tragic demise of 26 tourists in the horrific terror attack in Pahalgam on April 22, a video recently circulated on social media claimed to show alleged harassment of Kashmiri students in Maharajgunj Medical Campus. The video showed a group of people attacking an individual with sticks. In its investigation, however, the PTI Fact Check Desk found the video to be unrelated to the alleged attack on Kashmiri students in the aftermath of the Pahalgam terror attack. The video was found to be available on social media since March 19, i.e., predating the tragic Pahalgam incident. Further, during the investigation, it was also found that the Maharajgunj Medical Campus is located in Kathmandu, Nepal. An unrelated video was shared on social media as recent with a false claim. Claim An Instagram user 'successunfolds_' shared, on April 25, a video allegedly showing Kashmiri students being attacked in Maharajgunj Medical Campus in the aftermath of the Pahalgam terror attack. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk used the InVid tool to extract keyframes from the viral video. One keyframe was then reverse-searched using Google Lens, leading to several other social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search result via Google Lens also led the Desk to a video published on an Instagram handle named 'creativemedicos2021'. The handle posted the same video as seen in the viral video. However, further investigation into its publishing date revealed the same was done on March 19, i.e., predating the Pahalgam terror attack. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the content seen in the viral video matched with that of the video posted by the Instagram handle. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised search on Google using the keywords Maharajgunj Medical Campus. The search result led the Desk to the official website of the Maharajgunj Medical Campus, where it was found that the campus is situated in Kathmandu, Nepal, and not in India. Below is a screenshot highlighting the finding. Additionally, the keyword search also led the Desk to a video posted on the Nepal-based Facebook page 'Routine of IOM Banda'. The handle, on March 19, posted two videos simultaneously—first about the violence among the students in Maharajgunj Medical Campus. This was the same video as seen in the viral post and was shared with the caption: "ANNFSU candidates...This is the scenario of Maharajgunj Medical Campus." Further, the second video pertained to police taking action against Rup Singh Sunar, All Nepal National Free Student Union (ANNFSU)'s secretary candidate for the Free Students' Union election process. Sunar was reportedly taken into custody for the recent incident of violence in the Maharajgunj Medical Campus boys' hostel. Thus, after closely investigating the two, it was clear that the viral video pertained to the violence that occurred in a college in Nepal. The links to the videos can be found here and here , along with the screenshots. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was falsely linked to the attack on Kashmiri students in the aftermath of the Pahalgam terror attack.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of 2024 Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon and Beirut's outskirts falsely shared as Indian Army action after Pahalgam terror attack
content: New Delhi, April 28 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing the demolition of a building was circulated on social media, with users claiming that the Indian Army fired a missile into Pakistan following the April 22, 2025, Pahalgam terror attack that claimed the lives of 26 tourists. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video was shared with a false claim. The viral footage dates back to November 2024, when Israeli strikes targeted southern Lebanon and the outskirts of Beirut, resulting in the death of a hospital director and six of his colleagues. The video is unrelated to the recent terror attack in Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir. Meanwhile, it is pertinent to note that terrorists opened fire at a famed meadow near Kashmir's Pahalgam town on April 22, killing 26 people, mostly tourists. The attack has been described as the deadliest in the Valley since the Pulwama strike in 2019. Claim On April 26, an Instagram user named viral_videedo shared a video of a building being demolished, claiming that the Indian Army shot a missile in Pakistan following the 22 April 2025 Pahalgam terror attack. The text on the video, which garnered 1,169 likes, read: "Pakistan's view after the attack on Jammu and Kashmir. Power Off Indian Army" Here is the link and archive link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived version can be viewed here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a video report by Arab News dated November 23, 2024, which makes it clear that the video is unrelated to the recent Pahalgam terror attack or the Indian Army's retaliation. The video of the report was shot from a different angle. The report showed the destruction in the southern Lebanese city of Tyre after an Israeli strike. The exact clip of the destruction of a building was after an Israeli strike hit a building in Beirut's southern suburbs following an Israeli army evacuation call. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the video. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the news report from 2024. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports and came across a Reuters report dated November 23, 2024. The report carried the same visuals as the viral video from a different angle. According to the report, Israeli forces pounded southern Lebanon and the outskirts of the capital Beirut, killing at least five medics, and ground troops clashed with Hezbollah fighters in the south. The title of the report read: "Israel pounds southern Lebanon and Beirut outskirts, killing five medics" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to November 2024, when Israeli strikes targeted southern Lebanon and the outskirts of Beirut.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old, unrelated video of armoured vehicles falsely shared in name of Pakistan's military movements at India border after Pahalgam terror attack
content: New Delhi, April 28 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid escalating tensions between India and Pakistan following the horrific Pahalgam terror attack, a video showing a convoy of armoured vehicles has surfaced on social media. The PTI Fact Check Desk recently received a fact-check query regarding one such post, where a user claimed that Pakistan had started moving many self-propelled howitzers to the Indian border. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found the viral claim to be completely fake and baseless. The video has been available online since at least March 2024. Although the Desk could not determine the exact origin or further details of the video, it confirmed that it is unrelated to the current border situation between the two countries. Meanwhile, on Saturday (April 26), Pakistan offered to join any "neutral and transparent" probe into the Pahalgam terrorist attack that killed 26 people. Claim A video showing a convoy of armoured vehicles is being shared with the claim that Pakistan has started sending a large number of self-propelled howitzers to the Indian border by an X user. "Pakistan Deploys Long-Range 203mm M110 Self-Propelled Howitzers Near Indian Border," read the post's caption, which clocked 96.6K views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. It then ran one of the keyframes through Google Lens and found that several users shared the same video with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions can be viewed here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X-post by Olga Robinson stating that this video has nothing to do with the current tensions between India and Pakistan. It was posted on TikTok in 2024. The post also had a screenshot of the TikTok video (barring the date March 3, 2024), which captured similar visuals as seen in the viral video. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a comparison of the viral video and the X post stating that the video dates back to 2024. Although TikTok is blocked in India, and we could not access the video, the PTI Fact Check Desk received another X post that carried a screenshot of the TikTok video dated 2024. Though we could not access the details and the origin of the video, it is clear that the viral video has been on the internet since March 2024 and is unrelated to the recent Pahalgam terror attack. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is another comparison of the viral video and the X post stating that the video dates back to 2024. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video has been available online since at least March 2024, and it is unrelated to the current escalating tensions between India and Pakistan.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video from Pakistan falsely shared claiming Indian Army attacked Pakistani posts in retaliation for Pahalgam attack
content: New Delhi, April 28 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Following the tragic Pahalgam terror attack that shook the nation, a video showing heavy smoke and people running amok was widely circulated on social media. Users claimed that the Indian Army was destroying multiple Pakistani posts across the Line of Control (LoC). However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral video was shared with a false claim. Upon further verification, it was revealed that the video actually dates back to 2023 and shows heavy shelling on a highway in Pakistan, as Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) supporters took to the streets to protest the arrest of former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan. Following the Pahalgam terror attack on April 22, India announced a raft of punitive measures, including the suspension of the 65-year-old Indus Waters Treaty, the closure of the Attari land-border crossing, and the expulsion of Pakistani military attachés. Claim On April 27, an X (formerly Twitter) user named Babu Rao shared a video depicting heavy smoke and people running amok, claiming that the Indian Army was destroying multiple Pakistani posts across the Line of Control (LoC). The post's caption that clocked 1,042 views read: "Indian Army shall not show any mercy to the Ter*rorist Republic of Pakistan. Multiple Paki posts being des*troyed in the Line of Control (LoC) last night." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. It then ran one of the keyframes through Google Lens and found that several users shared the same video with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions can be viewed here and here . On running the keyframes of the viral video through Reverse Image Search, and came across an X post by the official handle of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) dated March 11, 2023. As per the post, it reportedly showed heavy shelling during a protest at a highway in Pakistan. The post carried similar visuals as seen in the viral video. "Heavy shelling at Kashmir Highway as protesters number is increasing. It's time for people of Pakistan to come out and defend Pakistan. #ReleaseImranKhan," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the X post. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports citing the incident and came across a report by Dwan News dated May 10, 2023. "The Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) supporters in Islamabad and Rawalpindi took to the streets on Tuesday to protest the arrest of party chairman Imran Khan who was detained on the premises of the judicial complex in the federal capital by a contingent of Rangers," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to 2023, depicting heavy shelling on a Highway in Pakistan as Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf supporters took to the streets following the arrest of Imran Khan.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2022 video of massive explosion in Pakistan's Sialkot falsely linked to Indian Army's retaliation in PoK's Leepa Valley
content: New Delhi, April 28 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid escalating tensions between India and Pakistan following the Pahalgam terror attack, a video purportedly showing a massive explosion is being widely shared on social media. Users claim it depicts the Indian Army destroying a military ammunition depot in Pakistan-Occupied Kashmir's (Pok) Leepa Valley. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the matter and found that the viral video was misleadingly shared with a false claim. Further verification revealed that the footage actually dates back to 2022 and shows a massive explosion in the northern Pakistani city of Sialkot. On April 22, terrorists killed 25 tourists and a local pony rider in the resort town of Pahalgam. The attack has been described as the deadliest in the Valley since the Pulwama strike in 2019. Claim On April 27, an X (formerly Twitter) user named Shuvankar Biswas shared a video depicting a massive explosion, claiming that the Indian Army destroyed a military ammunition depot in POK's Leepa Valley. "Massive explosions in Leepa Valley military ammunition depot. Pakistan's Local media is silent, which explains a lot," read the post's caption, which garnered 408.7K views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. It then ran one of the keyframes through Google Lens and found several users shared the same video with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here . The Desk ran the keyframes of the viral video through Reverse Image Search and came across a report by NDTV dated March 20, 2020. This report clarifies that it is unrelated to the claim made in the viral post. It also carried an image similar to the clips seen in the viral video. "Media reports said a massive explosion occurred in the northern Pakistani city of Sialkot. The sound of the blast was reportedly heard near the cantonment area in the Punjab province," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video's visuals and the news report's cover image. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find relevant media reports and came across a report by Hindustan Times dated May 2022. "ARY News quoting ISPR said an accidental fire broke out at the Sialkot Garrison, but there was no loss of life. According to the ISPR, due to short-circuiting, an accidental fire broke out in an ammunition shed near Sialkot Garrison," read the report section. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to 2022 and shows a massive explosion in the northern Pakistani city of Sialkot.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old, unrelated video falsely shared, claiming Pak Army targeted Indian Army Post near LoC
content: New Delhi, April 29 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid rising tensions along the Line of Control (LoC), a video showing an explosion in the mountains has gone viral on social media, accompanied by claims that the Pakistan Army targeted and destroyed an Indian Army post on the Indian side of the border. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video was shared with the false claim on social media. Further investigation revealed that the viral video has been circulating on the internet since 2020 and is unrelated to any attack by the Pakistan Army at the LoC. Claim On April 28, an X (formerly Twitter) user named Anum Fatima shared a video of an explosion in the mountains, claiming that the Pakistan Army targeted an Indian Army post near the Line of Control (LoC) in Kashmir. The post's caption, which clocked 113.9K views, read: "The Pakistan Army successfully targeted an Indian Army post near the Line of Control (LoC) in Kashmir. Demonstrating strength and precision, the Pakistan Army responded firmly to provocations across the border." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. It then ran one of the keyframes through Google Lens and found that several users shared the same video with a similar claim. One such post can be found here ; its archived versions can be viewed here . During our fact-checking review of the viral video, we noticed that at approximately 13 seconds in, a voice over a radio can be heard saying, "Thank you so much, sir." Moments later, the radio broadcasts several lines of unintelligible speech, which did not resemble Urdu or the typical mix of Urdu, Hindi, and Punjabi commonly spoken in Pakistan. The language also appeared inconsistent with standard military communication among Pakistani forces. Toward the end of the clip, the same voice repeats the phrase, "Thank you so much, sir." The Desk once again ran the keyframes of the viral video through Reverse Image Search. I came across a YouTube video dated September 2020 with similar visuals but from a different angle. The location of the video, as mentioned, was Nepal. "All the activities were done safely by the Nepal Army. This video is just for information about how the Nepal army blasts the mountain to make the track for the expressway," as per the description of the video. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Toward the end of the viral video, a brief glimpse reveals writing on a tin wall. A closer look shows the text is in Devanagari script, which is commonly used for languages like Hindi and Nepali. While the inscription is not entirely legible, it offers another clue suggesting that the video may have been filmed in Nepal, where Nepali, written in Devanagari, is the national language. The Desk conducted a customised keyword search for news reports related to the incident but found no credible sources supporting the viral video's claim of a Pakistani attack on an Indian Army post. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video has been on the internet since 2020 and is unrelated to any attack by the Pakistan Army at the LoC.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: This video claiming Indian Army officials walked out of press conference when questioned is false
content: New Delhi, April 29 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported video from a press conference was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that Indian Army generals allegedly walked out of a meeting when questioned about their refusal to fight Pakistan. However, a PTI Fact Check investigation revealed that the viral video does not show any reaction by army officials to a journalist's question regarding the recent Pahalgam terror attack. Instead, the footage is from a press briefing held in March 2025 about the Patiala Colonel Assault case. The video has nothing to do with the recent Pahalgam terror attack and was shared online with a misleading claim. Claim On April 26, an X (formerly Twitter) user named Ragrey_shah shared a purported video from a press conference claiming that Indian Army generals allegedly walked out of a meeting when they were questioned for their refusal to fight Pakistan. Indian Army generals walked out of the meeting. They said We are not capable of fighting a war against Pakistan. Modi still wants war, but his army isn't capable of fighting. This is their reality," read the post's caption, which clocked 1,356 views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. It then ran one of the keyframes through Google Lens and found that several users shared the same video with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here . To verify the claim, the Desk ran the keyframes of the viral video through Reverse Image Search and came across an Instagram handle going by the name 'bikramsinghmajithia_'. The handle posted the video, which exactly resembles the visuals seen in the viral post on March 25. Further, the description stated that the video pertains to a press conference held regarding the Patiala Colonel Pushpinder Singh Bath assault case. In the description, the user also hailed a man identified as ManAman Singh Chinna (an independent journalist) for raising questions against the establishment to ensure justice for Col Pushpinder Singh Baath and his family. However, his question related to the army, what are they afraid of, which was in context to the Baath assault case, was presented as the Indian Army not responding to the journalist's question in response to their move against the Pahalgam terror attack. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the content seen in the viral video, matched with that of the video posted by the Instagram user. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk held a keyword search related to the Patiala Colonel Assault case. The search result led the Desk to a YouTube video published on the Government of Punjab's official handle on March 25. The video depicted the same press conference where Director General of Police (DGP), Punjab, Gaurav Yadav, jointly with Army officers, presented the details about the Baath assault case. Also, in the video at 3 minutes 25 seconds timestamp, the voice of a journalist raising the same question could be heard in the background. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. ​ Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video does not show the army's reaction to a journalist's question about the recent Pahalgam terror incident. It shows a press conference held regarding the Patiala Colonel Assault case in March 2025.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old, unrelated video falsely shared to claim Indian Army responded with artillery fire against Pakistani forces recently
content: New Delhi, April 29 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Following a ceasefire violation along the India-Pakistan border, with Pakistan resorting to unprovoked small arms fire at multiple locations along the Line of Control (LoC) in Jammu and Kashmir, a video showing artillery fire was shared on social media. The user claimed it depicted the Indian Army responding to a recent clash with Pakistani forces after the terrorist attack on tourists in Pahalgam. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral video was shared with a false claim. The footage has been available online since 2021 and is unrelated to any recent retaliation by the Indian Army against Pakistani forces. According to reports, since the Pahalgam terror attack, ceasefire violations by Pakistan have become increasingly frequent, following a systematic pattern of provocation. The Indian Army has responded swiftly and effectively, ensuring minimal civilian impact while maintaining high operational readiness along the sensitive frontier. Claim On April 25, an X (formerly Twitter) user named 'Chattam Tv' shared a video showing artillery fire, claiming that it depicted the Indian Army responding to a recent clash with Pakistani forces after the terrorist attack on tourists in Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir. The post's caption, originally in Telugu, translates to: "Pakistan opens fire along LOC. -War atmosphere between India and Pakistan. -Firing from Pakistani posts in all three areas. -The Indian Army gives a strong reply to the enemy army. -Information is being received that four Pakistani soldiers have been killed" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. It then ran one of the keyframes through Google Lens and found that several users shared the same video with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here . To verify the claim, the Desk ran the keyframes of the viral video through Reverse Image Search. It came across the same video uploaded on a YouTube channel in 2021, which clarifies that the viral video is not related to the Pahalgam terror attack. According to the description of the video, the Indian Army used locally made OFB 81mm mortars in retaliation for the Pakistani Army's ceasefire violation. The visuals in the viral video were similar to those on YouTube. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Our search also resulted in another video uploaded in 2021. At 00:38 seconds, the video had similar visuals to those in the viral social media post. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk, however, could not confirm the exact time or location of the video. However, our investigation shows that the video has been on the Internet since 2021 and is unrelated to the Pahalgam terror attack.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Pakistan shot down Rafale fighter jet near LoC? 2024 IAF Sukhoi fighter crash video from Maharashtra falsely shared as recent with fake claim
content: New Delhi, April 29 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): As the Pakistan Army violated the ceasefire along the Line of Control (LoC) for the fifth consecutive night on Monday (April 28), a video depicting the aftermath of an aircraft crash is being widely circulated on social media. The user claimed that Pakistan had shot down an Indian Rafale fighter jet near the LoC in the Poonch sector. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral video was shared with a false claim. Further investigation revealed that the footage dates back to 2024, when an IAF Sukhoi fighter crashed in Nashik, Maharashtra. The video is unrelated to the recent border tensions following the Pahalgam terror attack. Claim On April 29, an X (formerly Twitter) user named Anum Fatima shared a video depicting the aftermath of an aircraft crash, claiming that Pakistan shot down an Indian Rafale fighter jet near the LoC in the Poonch sector. "Breaking News: Pakistan Shot Down Indian Rafael Fighter Jet Near LOC Ponch Sector. Big Achievement for Pakistan Air Force," read the post's caption, which garnered 102.4k views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. It then ran one of the keyframes through Google Lens and found that several users shared the same video with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here . To verify the claim, the Desk again ran the keyframes of the viral video through the Reverse Image Search and came across the same video uploaded on Instagram by etnow news channel on June 4, 2024. This makes it clear that the video is not recent and unrelated to the Indian Rafael Fighter jet being shot down, as per the news channel, an Indian Air Force Sukhoi fighter jet crashed in Nashik, Maharashtra. "An Indian Air Force Sukhoi fighter jet crashed in Nashik, Maharashtra today, with both pilots safely ejected before the impact," read the caption of the post. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral and the Instagram post. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports. The search led us to a PTI report carried by the Indian Express on June 4, 2024. According to the report, the fighter jet was being flown by Wing Commander Bokil and his second in command, Biswas, when it crashed on a farm in Shirasgaon village in Nifad tehsil at 1:20 p.m. The headline of the report read: "IAF's Sukhoi fighter crashes in Nashik; pilot, co-pilot eject safely" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to 2024 when the IAF's Sukhoi fighter crashed in Nashik, Maharashtra. It is unrelated to the recent unrest due to the Pahalgam terror attack.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old photo of Northern Ireland fire falsely shared as 'Pakistan's attack' in PoK's Leepa Valley
content: New Delhi, April 29 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Several social media users shared an image claiming it depicted Pakistan's action against Indian checkpoints in the Leepa area of Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK), following the Pahalgam terror attack on April 22, 2025. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk revealed that the viral image was unrelated to the Pahalgam incident. In reality, it showed a fire that had broken out at the foothills of the Mourne Mountain range in Northern Ireland. The image was misleadingly shared online with a false claim. Claim An X user with the name '@from1pakis' shared on April 27 an image claiming it depicted Pakistan's action against Indian checkpoints in the Lipa area. "Urgent: Exclusive sources: The Pakistani army destroyed two Indian checkpoints in the Lipa area.," read the post's caption that clocked 53.1k views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with the screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. It then ran one of the keyframes through Google Lens and found several users shared the same video with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here . To corroborate the claim suggested in the social media post, the Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens. The search result then led the Desk to a report published by the BBC, whose feature image matched that of the viral post. According to their (BBC) report published on March 18, 2025, the image depicted a blaze that erupted at the foothills of the Mourne Mountain range in Northern Ireland. "The Northern Ireland Fire and Rescue Service (NIFRS) said it received a report at 18:42 GMT of about 200m of gorse on fire on the Attnadue Road outside of Castlewellan, Country Down. The fire is believed to have started deliberately," the report stated Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting that the image shared in the viral social media post was the same as the feature image of the BBC report, depicting a fire that started at the foothills of Mourne Mountain in Northern Ireland. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral image was unrelated to the recent Pahalgam terror incident. It showed fire starting at the foothills of the Mourne Mountain range in Northern Ireland.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Pak-based social handles falsely claim Indian Army officer was sacked after Pahalgam terror attack; details inside
content: New Delhi, April 30 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid escalating tensions between India and Pakistan following the Pahalgam terror attack, in which predominantly Hindu tourists were killed, several social media users shared a post featuring Lt Gen M. V. Sachindra Kumar. The users claimed that Lt Gen Kumar was removed from his position as head of the Northern Command by the Indian government in the aftermath of the Pahalgam incident. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the claim made in the viral post, shared primarily by a Pakistan-based news organisation and circulated by several Pakistani social media users, is fake and baseless. Lt Gen Kumar relinquished command of the Udhampur-based Northern Command upon his retirement, having attained the age of superannuation. Lt Gen Pratik Sharma is set to take charge as the new Commander-in-Chief of the Northern Army Command. Claim An Instagram post by Pakistan's news channel 92news_official, shared on April 29, featured Lt Gen M V Sachindra Kumar claiming that the Indian government has removed him as the head of the Northern Command following the controversial Pahalgam incident. The post's caption, which clocked 679 views, read: "Sources indicate Lt Gen Kumar's refusal to support retaliatory action against Pakistan frustrated political leaders, leading to his ouster. Lieutenant General Prateek Sharma will take over the post on May 1 as New Delhi seeks to contain the fallout. The incident has exposed major security lapses despite India's heavy military presence in the region." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens to verify the claim. The reverse image search shows several users sharing the post with a similar claim. A similar claim was shared by Times of Karachi an independent online news publishing platform from Karachi. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Another post was shared on social media, as well. Here is the link to the social media post. To commence our investigation, the Desk first conducted a customised keyword search to corroborate the viral claim that Lt Gen Kumar was removed from his post. However, the search did not yield any relevant or credible reports. However, our search did lead us to a Press Trust of India (PTI) report dated April 30, which, citing officials, categorically stated that Lt Gen M V Sachindra Kumar on Wednesday (April 30) relinquished the command of Udhampur-based Northern Command on his retirement after achieving the superannuation age. Quoting the Army in the report, it said: "Lt Gen M V Suchindra Kumar, Army Commander Northern Command laid wreath to honour the supreme sacrifice of the bravehearts at Dhruva War Memorial, Udhampur on superannuation and relinquishing command of the Northern Command." This clarifies that Lt Gen Kumar was not ousted from his post, but rather has assumed charge as the general officer commanding-in-chief of the Udhampur-based Northern Command, which is also known as Dhruva Command after achieving the superannuation age. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Furthermore, the Desk also found the Additional Directorate General of Public Information's (ADG PI) X post, which mentioned that Lt Gen MV Suchindra Kumar today relinquished Command of the Indian Army's Northern Command. Here is the link to the spot, and below is a screenshot of the same. Also, Lt Gen MV Suchindra Kumar assumed command as the General Officer Commanding-in-Chief of the Indian Army's Northern Command in February 2024, succeeding Gen Upendra Dwivedi, who now serves as the Chief of Army Staff. According to a report by India Today dated April 29, Lieutenant Gen Pratik Sharma, the Indian Army's Deputy Chief (Strategy), has been approved as the new commander-in-chief of the Udhampur-based Northern Army Command. "With an illustrious career spanning three decades, Lt Gen Sharma is an infantry officer who has served in varied operational environments. He was a part of key operations such as operations Pawan, Meghdoot, Rakshak, and Parakram," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Deks concluded that the viral claim shared by mostly a Pakistan-based news organisation and circulated by many Pakistani social media users stating that Lt Gen Kumar was ousted from his post following the recent Pahalgam terror attack is false and baseless. Rather, he relinquished the command of the Udhampur-based Northern Command upon his retirement after achieving the superannuation age.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: This photo falsely claiming Indian Army engaged in exchange of fire with its own unit is old and unrelated; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 1 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Several social media users shared a photo showing security personnel carrying an injured individual in uniform. The accompanying claim alleged that two Indian Army units exchanged fire along the Line of Control (LoC), resulting in the death of their own Sikh soldiers. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found the claim to be baseless. The photo used in the social media post has been available online since 2014, and there are no credible reports to support the claim shared with the photo in the post. Given the gravity of such an incident, especially if it had occurred along the LoC it would have received widespread coverage in mainstream media. The photo was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim On April 29, an X (formerly Twitter) user, Zulfiqar Ali Ch, shared a photo depicting a few security force people carrying a person (seen in the same security uniform), apparently injured. The user claimed that two Indian Army units exchanged fire along the Line of Control (LoC) and shot their own Sikh soldiers. "Indian Army Shoots Its Own Sikh Soldiers. On the night of April 25-26, two Indian Army units exchanged fire along the Line of Control in occupied Kashmir, resulting in the death of 5 Sikh soldiers. The incident occurred during a patrol near Japala Bridge, Baramulla," read the post's caption, which clocked 3,173 views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral social media post through Google Lens and found several other users who had similar posts and the same claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , and its archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk performed a Reverse Image Search of the picture posted alongside the claim in the social media post. The Desk came across another report by Al Jazeera, dated 2016, which featured the same image as seen in the social media post. The title of the report read: "Indian police claim killing Maoist fighters in Odisha" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. We came across an April 13, 2014, report by Anandabazar Patrika, an Indian Bengali-language daily newspaper, carrying the same image as seen in the viral post. According to the report, the picture shows soldiers removing the body of a colleague. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk carried out a customised keyword search on Google to look for any credible reports supporting the social media post alleging that the Indian Army had shot its own Sikh soldiers. However, the search did not yield any such reports. Given the seriousness of the alleged incident, especially if it had occurred along the Line of Control, it would have been widely covered by mainstream media. Therefore, in its investigation, the Desk found that the photo used in the social media post was first available on the internet in 2014 (used by Anandabazar) and then again featured in another report by Al Jazeera in 2016. The Desk could not verify the photo's source, but it clearly does not depict any recent incident. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim made in the post is baseless; there are no credible reports to corroborate it. The viral post has been available on the internet since 2014.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2018 video from Pakistan falsely shared claiming NIA thrashed Kashmiri zipline operator over Pahalgam attack; details inside
content: New Delhi, April 30 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a person being brutally beaten was recently circulated on social media, accompanied by the claim that it showed the Kashmiri zipline operator currently under investigation by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) in connection with the Pahalgam terror attack. The claim surfaced after a separate video of the operator chanting "Allahu Akbar" three times, allegedly at the time of the attack, went viral online. The post further alleged that the operator, identified as Arshad Nadeem, was taken into custody by the NIA and that the circulating video showed him being thrashed. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the viral video does not depict the Kashmiri zipline operator. The footage dates back to 2018 and originated in Pakistan. It has no connection to the Pahalgam terror attack that occurred on April 22, 2025. Claim An X user, Deepak Sharma (@SonOfBharat7), shared on April 29 a video allegedly showing the same zipline operator from Kashmir (whose video with a tourist went viral, where he was seen chanting 'Allahu Akbar' during the Pahalgam terror attack) being flogged by NIA officials. "Arshad Nadeem, the zipline operator who pushed a Hindu tourist to death, was welcomed at the NIA office. After the video went viral, this terrorist was arrested this evening and handed over to the NIA...What is your opinion...should he be killed or let go?" the user shared the video with the caption. When this story was published, the video had garnered 34.5k views and 2.8k likes. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool to extract multiple keyframes. Once generated, one of the keyframes was reverse-searched using Google, which led the Desk to numerous social media posts sharing the same image with similar captions. One such post can be found here , with its archived version available here respectively: The search result via Google Lens also led the Desk to a video published on the official X handle of Sher Mohammad Bugti, a central spokesman of the Baloch Republican Party. The user had shared the same video (as seen in the now-viral post) first on July 5, 2018, stating that it showed inhuman and degrading treatment inflicted by members of the Pakistani Army against a Baloch student. Tagging Human Rights Watch, the United Nations handle, and the United Nations Human Rights handle, the user had then captioned the video: "Please have a glance: inhuman and degrading treatment of cruel #PakArmy physical torture of innocent Baloch student. Plz, act through General Assembly resolution 39/46 of 10 December 1984 by Article 27 (1)." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting the content in the viral video, matched with that of the video posted by the X user in July 2018. The search result also led the Desk to a video published on a YouTube channel named Samba Khokhar, also back in 2018. While the video posted by the handle does not exactly resemble the viral video, the form of torture shown in the video is very similar to the former. According to the video, the procedure depicted—'Pak Army SSG Commando Training'—involves personnel being trained to resist torture and not reveal any confidential information in case of exigency. Here is the link to the video: It is pertinent to note that while the Desk could not independently verify the origin of the video, the investigation procedure clearly indicates that the video is not linked to the recent Pahalgam terror attack. Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk held a customized keyword search related to the NIA's investigation into the zipline operator's alleged role in the incident. The search result led the Desk to a report published by the Times of India on April 30, which stated that the NIA had picked up the zipline operator, identified as Muzamil, essentially to find out if he had prior knowledge of the impending carnage. "NIA sources said the purpose behind questioning Muzamil was to confirm the motive or thought process that led him to raise the 'Allahu Akbar' cry," the report stated. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video does not depict violent treatment inflicted on the zipline operator from Kashmir, who is being investigated for his alleged role in the Pahalgam terror attack.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Social media post claiming 15 out of 26 Pahalgam terror attack victims were Muslim is false; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 1 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Days after a deadly terror attack struck Kashmir's Pahalgam on April 22, a social media post was shared with a claim that 15 out of the 26 victims killed in the incident were from the Muslim community. The user shared a purported list of names—allegedly broadcast by Hindi news channel India TV—that included several Muslim-sounding names to support the claim.
