However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the post and found the list circulated in the name of Pahalgam terror attack victims to be false. Official records and credible media reports confirmed that only one victim, Syed Adil Hussain Shah, belonged to the Muslim community, while the remaining 25 victims were non-Muslims. Claim An X user, Sadia Abbasi (@SadiaAbbasii), shared a post on April 25 allegedly containing the names of the 26 people who died in the Pahalgam terror attack. The user claimed India TV shared the list and stated that 15 of the victims belonged to the Muslim community. The post read: "Out of 26 dead, 15 are Muslim names. This exposes Godi media, who have been shouting for the last day that names were asked before killing. The government should take note of these fake news channels and take action. The Godi media is the most influential means to spread hate and riots." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across several other social media posts sharing the same claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively: Next, referring to the claim that India TV had published this list, the Desk searched for relevant reports on their official website and found one published on April 23, 2025. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. However, upon scanning the report, the Desk found that none of the names listed in the viral post matched those in the India TV report. According to an India TV report, only one of the deceased, Syed Adil Hussain Shah, was a Muslim. The remaining 25 victims (including one Nepali citizen) belonged to the non-muslim community. Below is a combination image highlighting the stark differences between the names mentioned in the viral post and those reported by India TV. The search result also led the Desk to a report published by The Hindu on April 24, 2025. The report elaborately mentioned the names of the deceased, attached alongside their images. Additionally, the names mentioned in the report matched exactly with those published by India TV. "We stand in solidarity with the victims and their families, and with all those touched by this tragedy. In remembering them, we reaffirm our collective humanity and our resolve to uphold peace, even in the face of terror," the Hindu report stated. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim suggesting that a majority of those killed in the Pahalgam terror attack were Muslims is false.

title: PTI Fact Check: Grow By Growing Others | PTI Fact Check launches regional fact-checking and digital literacy drive across South Asia
content: New Delhi, May 1 (PTI): PTI Fact Check, the IFCN-signatory fact-checking unit of the Press Trust of India, has launched an ambitious regional initiative aimed at strengthening fact-checking and digital literacy across South Asia. Titled "Grow by Growing Others," the programme is being implemented in partnership with three leading media organisations in Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, and Nepal. PTI Fact Check, part of India's most credible news agency, was selected by the IFCN to spearhead the regional drive given its important role in countering misinformation and promoting digital literacy. Under the initiative, the PTI Fact Check team conducted a series of intensive two-day training sessions and workshops in three newsrooms between December 2024 and February 2025, equipping over 60 journalists with essential fact-checking skills. The initiative also aims to prepare participating newsrooms to apply for signatory status with the International Fact-Checking Network (IFCN), the global alliance that upholds standards for credible fact-checking organisations. Achieving IFCN signatory status is seen as a mark of commitment to transparency, non-partisanship, and rigorous methodology. Led by Pratyush Ranjan, Head of Fact Check and Digital Services at PTI, the training sessions covered a broad spectrum of critical topics, including the fundamentals of fact-checking, advanced internet verification tools, identification of misinformation, detection of AI-generated deepfakes, and techniques to improve digital security for journalists and newsrooms. The central objective of the Grow by Growing Others programme is to enable partner news organisations to establish their own fact-checking units. Additionally, the programme encourages these organisations to foster a culture of verification by further training their newsroom colleagues and contributing to a broader media literacy movement within their national ecosystems. The two-day training sessions began in Dhaka, Bangladesh, in December 2024 in collaboration with United News of Bangladesh (UNB). Dhaka, Bangladesh ( Dec, 19-20, 2024) (Photos of Pratyush Ranjan, Head of PTI Fact Check, conducting sessions in UNB newsroom in Dhaka (Bangladesh) on Dec 19 and Dec 20, 2024) In January 2025, the second leg took place in Colombo, Sri Lanka, with Wijeya Newspapers. Colombo, Sri Lanka (Jan 27-28, 2025) (Photos of Pratyush Ranjan conducting sessions in Wijeya Newspapers newsroom in Colombo (Sri Lanka) on Jan 27, 2025. PTI's CEO and Editor-in-Chief Vijay Joshi was also there on the second day of the sessions at Wijeya's head office in Colombo) The final sessions were held in February 2025 in Kathmandu, Nepal, in partnership with Techpana, a digital-first media platform. Kathmandu, Nepal ( Feb 5-6, 2025) (Photos of Pratyush Ranjan, Head of PTI Fact Check, and Ashisha Singh Rajput from PTI's Fact Check team conducting sessions in Techpana newsroom in Kathmandu (Nepal) on Feb 5 and 6, 2025) "This initiative is about building a strong and sustainable network of fact-checkers in the region," said Pratyush Ranjan. "By sharing what we've learned and mentoring others, we're creating a ripple effect of responsible journalism and digital awareness." The initiative began in November 2024 and is designed as a year-long capacity-building programme. Over the course of the year, PTI Fact Check will provide sustained, real-time mentorship and editorial guidance to the three participating news organisations. This ongoing support includes regular virtual check-ins, collaborative verification exercises, content review, and on-demand technical assistance to help each newsroom establish an independent and robust fact-checking desk. The long-term goal is to ensure that by the end of 2025, each newsroom is operationally ready to meet the stringent requirements for IFCN signatory status, which include transparency of methodology, independence, non-partisanship, and a public corrections policy. The PTI Fact Check team is also helping the partner organisations develop internal workflows, editorial guidelines, and verification protocols tailored to their specific news environments. The programme strongly emphasises building self-sufficient teams capable of producing high-quality fact checks, managing claims submissions, and tracking misinformation trends within their countries. PTI aims to establish a lasting framework for combating misinformation across the region by embedding structured fact-checking processes and providing end-to-end implementation support. During the workshops, PTI's team conducted hands-on sessions demonstrating real-time debunking methods for edited audios, videos, and images using freely available tools such as reverse image searches, metadata analysers, and advanced search operators. Participants were trained to verify viral photos, videos, deepfakes, and claims commonly circulated on social media platforms in their respective countries. The sessions also addressed the growing threat of deepfakes and AI-manipulated content. Journalists were taught to identify telltale signs of synthetic media and introduced to emerging tools for detecting manipulated visuals. A special module on cybersecurity awareness highlighted best practices for protecting sensitive data and communications in an increasingly hostile digital environment. Participants expressed strong enthusiasm for the initiative and emphasised the urgent need for such training in their newsrooms. "Misinformation is one of the biggest challenges facing journalism today. The training sessions we conducted gave the participating journalists the confidence to confront the issue of misinformation head-on," said Ashisha Singh Rajput of PTI Fact Check, who conducted training sessions at Techpana's newsroom in Kathmandu, Nepal. Bijay Timalsina, Co-founder and CEO at Techpana, also participated in the training sessions on both days in his newsroom. He said, "The two-day fact-checking training conducted by the PTI team was a transformative experience for our newsroom. It introduced us to modern fact-checking tools and verification techniques and laid the foundation for a more responsible and evidence-based approach to journalism. One of the most valuable outcomes of the session was how it empowered every member of our newsroom—from reporters to editors—with the fundamentals of fact-checking. We now approach every piece of information with a more critical lens, ensuring that accuracy and verification are at the core of our editorial process." "Following the training, our newsroom established a dedicated fact-checking unit. In just under two months, this team has produced over 30 fact-checking stories, many of which have gained significant traction on social media. In some cases, our reporting has even prompted established news outlets to revise or correct their own coverage. This speaks to the credibility and impact of our work, made possible by the skills we gained during the training." He further added, "Our connection with PTI's fact-checking unit didn't end with the training. Our team continues to stay in touch with PTI experts through online sessions, regularly seeking guidance when faced with complex verification challenges. This ongoing mentorship has strengthened our confidence and capability in navigating the evolving landscape of misinformation." "We believe fact-checking is no longer optional—it is an essential skill that every newsroom must adopt. Embedding fact-checking into daily editorial workflows should be a priority for all media organisations striving for credibility in the digital age. We're sincerely grateful to the PTI team for their support and commitment to strengthening journalism through this initiative. Their guidance has set us on a path toward more accountable and trustworthy reporting," the Techpana CEO said. (Group photo of Techpana journalists and the trainers of PTI Fact Check outside the Techpana office in Kathmandu, Nepal) PTI Fact Check's regional fact-checking and literacy drive comes at a time when South Asia faces a surge in misinformation campaigns, often fuelled by political polarisation, digital echo chambers, and the unchecked spread of content on social media platforms. With misinformation transcending borders and frequently targeting regional fault lines, the PTI-led programme promotes cross-border collaboration and knowledge-sharing among South Asian journalists. The Grow by Growing Others initiative marks a vital step toward building a more informed and resilient media landscape in the region by nurturing local capacity and promoting a network of trusted fact-checkers.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old protest video from India falsely shared claiming 'people demanded PM Modi's resignation after Pahalgam attack'
content: New Delhi, May 1 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid escalating tensions between India and Pakistan following the deadly Pahalgam terror attack that claimed 26 lives, a video depicting alleged clashes between police and civilians was widely circulated on social media. Users claimed the footage showed widespread protests erupting in India, demanding Prime Minister Narendra Modi's resignation in the wake of the attack. The video shows police officers apparently chasing groups of people with batons, while slogans can be heard in the background. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video is unrelated to the current tensions between India and Pakistan. A thorough analysis revealed that the footage has been available online since January 2020—well before the Pahalgam attack on April 22. Thus, an old and unrelated video was shared on social media with a false claim linking it to the ongoing India-Pakistan tensions. Claim An X user, Mian Amir Bashir (@Abdullah1176374), shared a video on April 30 claiming it showed protests erupting on the streets of India following the Pahalgam attack. The user wrote: "After the press conference by the Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister and the DG ISPR, chaos erupted in India. The Indian public took to the streets demanding Prime Minister Modi's resignation." When this report was published, the video had garnered 157.8k views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid verification tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was reverse-searched using Google Lens, which led to a match with a video published by a Facebook channel named Lie Lama. The handle posted the same video as the one seen in the viral post. However, a closer analysis revealed that the video was first published on January 10, 2020, clearly predating the current tensions between India and Pakistan that arose after the Pahalgam attack. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image, highlighting the identical frames from the viral video and the one posted on Facebook in January 2020. While the Desk could not independently verify when or where the video was originally shot, the investigation clearly shows that it does not show protests in India demanding PM Modi's resignation in the aftermath of the Pahalgam attack. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video does not depict protests which erupted in India demanding Prime Minister Modi's resignation after the Pahalgam terror attack. The video has been available online since January 2020, long before the recent tensions. An old and unrelated video was shared on social media, falsely linking to recent geopolitical tensions.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Pak-based social media handle falsely claimed Air Marshal SP Dharkar was dismissed after Pahalgam terror attack; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 1 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media post featuring a purported photo of Vice Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal SP Dharkar, was recently shared online. The post claimed that he was dismissed from his post following the Pahalgam terror attack. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false. Air Marshal SP Dharkar retired as Vice Chief of the Air Staff on April 30, 2025, upon superannuation from the Indian Air Force (IAF), after completing 40 years of distinguished service to the nation. The post circulating on social media was misleading and aimed at spreading disinformation. Claim An X user, '@PK_Matters', shared a purported image of Vice Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal SP Dharkar, on May 1, claiming that he was dismissed from his position in the aftermath of the Pahalgam terror attack. The user wrote: "After the Pahalgam incident, there was a shake-up in the Indian military leadership. Air Marshal SP Dharkar was dismissed." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found several other social media posts making the same claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here : In the next part of the investigation, taking a cue from the information mentioned in the social media post regarding Air Marshal SP Dharkar, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google. The search results led the Desk to a detailed press release issued by the Defence Ministry on May 1, 2025. The press release clearly stated that Air Marshal SP Dharkar retired as Vice Chief of the Air Staff on April 30, 2025, on superannuation from the Indian Air Force after completing 40 years of illustrious service to the nation, and was not dismissed from the post. "He held several important appointments in his career, including Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief at the Eastern Air Command (EAC) and Senior Air Staff Officer at the South Western Air Command. He also held the offices of Air Defence Commander at HQ EAC and Assistant Chief of the Air Staff (Training) at Air Headquarters. He was the first Director General of the Defence Space Agency," the press release added. Here is the link to the release, along with a screenshot: Additionally, the search results led the Desk to a social media post made by the Indian Air Force's official X handle. The post stated that Air Marshal SP Dharkar retired as VCAS on 30 April 2025, after 40 years of distinguished service. "A highly experienced fighter pilot, he held several appointments during his illustrious career, including AOC-in-C of EAC and the first Defence Space Agency Director General. Awarded with PVSM, UYSM & AVSM, he leaves behind a legacy of excellence," the post added. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Air Marshal SP Dharkar retired as Vice Chief of the Air Staff on April 30 and was not dismissed from his post in the aftermath of the Pahalgam attack.

title: PTI Fact Check: 10 more false and misleading social media posts debunked as misinformation wave continues after Pahalgam attack; details inside

Numerous accounts circulated false narratives, contributing to a digital storm of deceit. This coordinated effort appears to be more than mere rumour-mongering. By distorting facts and amplifying falsehoods, the campaign seems to undermine trust in official accounts and incite mistrust. PTI Fact Check identified and debunked ten such fake claims last week, all available here to read. Further investigation by PTI's Fact Check Desk has revealed the scale and intent behind this digital offensive. The team has uncovered and discredited ten additional instances of misinformation falsely linked to the Pahalgam attack. These findings serve as a stark reminder of the escalating threat posed by coordinated disinformation efforts, especially during moments of national crisis. Claim 1: A video depicting back-to-back explosions and people running amok was shared on X (formerly Twitter) by a user named 'The Squirrels' on April 30, claiming that the footage showed the Indian Army's retaliatory strike on Sialkot, Pakistan, after the Pahalgam terror attack. The post's caption, which clocked 11.9k views, read: "Breaking: Al Jazeera releases exclusive footage of the Indian Army's retaliatory strike on Sialkot, Pakistan — a strong response after the #PahalgamTerroristAttack.#Sialkot #IndianArmy #IndiaPakistan #PehalgamAttack #BreakingNews4o" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation: The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool to extract keyframes. One keyframe was reverse-searched using Google Lens, leading the Desk to a journalist, Baker Atyani's X post dated November 9, 2023 – this clarifies that the incident predates the Pahalgam terror attack and is unrelated to the Indian Army's retaliation. The post featured similar visuals to those seen in the social media post. The caption indicated that it was an Indonesian hospital in Gaza that was under Israeli attack, and several people were killed. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the content in the viral video that matches the video posted by the X handle. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports citing the incident. The search led us to a video report uploaded on Al Jazeera's official YouTube channel on November 9, 2024. The report, citing the Palestinian interior ministry, mentioned several injuries among thousands of displaced people sheltering in the yards of the Indonesian hospital in northern Gaza. The vicinity of the hospital was attacked by Israeli fighter jets, specifically the Tal al-Zaatar area. At 5 minutes 20 seconds, similar footage can be seen as shared by social media users. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to 2023 and showed an Indonesian hospital in Gaza that was under Israeli attack, killing several people. The video predates the Pahalgam terror attack and is unrelated to the Indian Army's retaliation. author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2023 video of Army truck accidentally catching fire falsely shared claiming 'Khalistani extremists attacked Army convoy in Punjab'
content: New Delhi, May 2 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid the ongoing standoff between India and Pakistan, which escalated following the Pahalgam terror attack, a video showing an army truck engulfed in flames was widely circulated on social media. The user claimed the incident took place in Punjab, alleging that Khalistani extremists had attacked an Indian Army convoy with Molotov cocktails, setting one of the trucks on fire. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found the video to be unrelated to any targeted attack on an Indian Army convoy. The footage actually dates back to May 2023 and shows an army truck that accidentally caught fire on the Ludhiana-Firozpur National Highway near Dakha. Initial reports suggest the fire may have been caused by friction between a cylinder in the truck and the road. Thus, an old and unrelated video was falsely shared on social media to mislead viewers. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user with the handle Bahar (@Queen_of_Herat) shared the video on May 2, claiming that Khalistani supporters had attacked an Indian Army convoy in Punjab. The user alleged that the extremists used Molotov cocktails to target the convoy, leading to a fire in one of the army trucks. "Sikhs of Khalistan threw a Molotov cocktail on an Indian Army convoy passing through Indian-occupied Punjab, setting an Indian Army truck on fire. Free Punjab Zindabad," read the caption accompanying the video. When this article was published, the video had garnered over 108k views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid verification tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was reverse-searched using Google Lens, which led the team to a report published by Amar Ujala on May 4, 2023. While the featured image of the report matched a keyframe from the viral video, a close analysis of the report's details revealed that the incident took place in Halwara, Punjab, in May 2023. It involved a truck part of a military exercise convoy that caught fire due to a mechanical fault. "The accident took place near Dakha on the Ludhiana-Ferozepur National Highway. There is no report of any soldier being injured in the incident. However, strong winds caused the fire to spread, damaging the goods inside the army truck," the Amar Ujala report stated. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. A combination image has been attached herewith, comparing the viral video to the Amar Ujala report's feature image. The image confirms that both show the same incident. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral claim was false. There was no attack by Khalistani extremists on an Indian Army convoy in Punjab.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated image falsely shared to claim Avtar Singh Mauni wore longest white turban; details inside
content: New Delhi, March 5 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported photograph of a man wearing a long white turban was circulated on social media. The user claimed that the man in the image was Avtar Singh Mauni from Punjab, who had set a world record for wearing the largest turban. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found that the viral image was shared with a false claim. The image is AI-generated. While Avtar Singh Mauni gained recognition in 2014 for wearing a turban weighing 100 pounds, considered the world's largest, this image is not authentic and has been digitally manipulated. Claim A picture featuring a man wearing a long white turban was shared on Instagram by a user named 'madhu_bogati' on May 1, 2025. The user claimed that it showed Avtar Singh Mauni, who hails from Punjab and will set a world record for wearing the highest turban. "The world's highest turban-wearing record is in the name of Punjab's Avatar Singh Moni. This turban weighs 45 kg and is 645 meters in length. It takes 5-6 hours to wear this turban," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through Reverse Image Search and found several other users shared the same photo with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here . To commence the investigation, the Desk first conducted a customised keyword search, according to the information written in the caption of the social media post, the search did not yield the Desk any credible reports or even articles that carried the same picture as seen in the post. If such a thing had happened, it would have garnered nationwide attention. After which the Desk then carefully analysed the photo, and the animals (two horses) visible in the background look distorted, hinting that the image might be manipulated or AI-generated. Below is a screenshot highlighting the mentioned findings. Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the viral image through SightEngine, an AI detection tool. The tool detected a substantial presence of AI-generated elements in the image. Below is a screenshot of the result: The Desk also ran the photo through WasitAI, another AI detection tool. This tool also detected a substantial presence of AI-generated elements in the image. Below is a screenshot of the result: Moreover, in 2014, Avtar Singh Mauni, then a 60-year-old resident of Patiala, was on the verge of a world record courtesy his 100-pound turban. According to a report by NDTV dated August 31, 2014, the turban stretches to 645 metres—almost the same length as 13 Olympic-sized swimming pools. A report section mentioned: "If validated, he will break the Guinness World record of Major Singh, a Nihang Sikh, whose 400 metre long turban weighs around 77 pounds." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral photo shared on social media is AI-generated, and though he did wear a 100-pound turban, it was back then in 2014 and not recent.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Viral video of Muslim woman hit by car in Kerala falsely shared as targeted attack against the community; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 3 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a burqa-clad woman being hit by a speeding car in India was recently circulated on social media with the claim that she was deliberately targeted due to her religious identity. The video shows the woman walking alongside a child on a busy road when a speeding car suddenly hits her from behind. While the child miraculously escapes unhurt, the woman sustains serious injuries. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found that the video was falsely shared as evidence of a targeted attack against Muslims in India. The Desk contacted an official from Kottakkal Police, who confirmed that both the accused and the victim belong to the same religion, and clarified that the incident was the result of negligence, not communal motives. The video was shared with a false claim intended to mislead viewers. Claim An X user, Syed Saleem (@syedsaleem__), shared a video on May 2 showing a burqa-clad woman accompanied by a child being hit by a speeding car in India. The user claimed that the incident was a targeted attack against Muslims in India. "Hello Human Rights Watch, UN Human Rights, this is a Hindu terrorist who ran over a Muslim woman with a car and drove away. This is a clear act of Hindu terrorists. India should be declared a Hindu terrorist state," the user posted along with the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was reverse-searched using Google Lens, which led the Desk to multiple social media posts that used the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here respectively. The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a report published by India Today on May 2, which featured the same keyframe used in the Desk's investigation. The report stated that the video showed a shocking incident that occurred in Kerala's Kottakkal area, where a woman pedestrian walking with a child was hit by a speeding car on April 26. While the child escaped unhurt, the woman, identified as a 33-year-old resident of Swagathamadu village, Badaria, suffered serious injuries. She was thrown several feet away onto the roadside after being hit. Nowhere did the report mention that the incident was a targeted attack. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting that the content in the viral video matches the feature image in the India Today report. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk closely examined the extended version of the CCTV footage included in the India Today report to verify the claim further. It showed that the car stopped immediately after hitting the woman, and two individuals got out to help her, indicating no intention to flee after the incident. Below is a screenshot highlighting the finding. Additionally, the Desk contacted an official from the Kottakkal Police regarding the viral claim. Speaking to PTI Fact Check, Vinod Valiyattoo, Inspector of Police, said the incident was a natural accident. The accused, Mohammad P.A., is in police custody, and the car involved is also in police possession. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video does not show a targeted attack against a Muslim woman in India.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2023 video of Israeli strike on Gaza hospital falsely shared as India's retaliatory action against Pakistan; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 2 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video allegedly showing India's retaliatory strike against Pakistan following the Pahalgam terror attack was recently circulated on social media, with claims that it depicted explosions in Sialkot. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video is unrelated to the current situation. It actually dates back to 2023 and shows an Israeli airstrike on an Indonesian hospital in Gaza that killed several people. The old video was falsely shared to mislead viewers about India's military response. Claim An X handle using the username The Squirrels (@thesquirrelsin) shared a video on April 30, allegedly showing India's retaliatory action against Pakistan following the Pahalgam terror attack. The video was claimed to show massive explosions rocking Pakistan's Sialkot, with people running in panic. "Breaking: Al Jazeera releases exclusive footage of the Indian Army's retaliatory strike on Sialkot, Pakistan — a strong response after the Pahalgam terrorist attack," the user wrote. When this report was published, the video had garnered 19.7k views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid verification tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was reverse-searched using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here : The reverse image search also led the Desk to a post by journalist Baker Atyani on X. He shared the same video, stating that it depicted a November 2023 incident in which an Indonesian hospital in Gaza came under Israeli attack. The video does not depict India's retaliatory strike against Pakistan. Here is the link and archive link to his post, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting the content in the viral video, which matches that of the video posted by the X user. To verify further, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports. This led to a video report uploaded by Al Jazeera on its official YouTube channel on November 9, 2023. Citing the Palestinian interior ministry, the report mentioned several injuries among thousands of displaced people sheltering in the yard of the Indonesian hospital in northern Gaza. The hospital's vicinity—specifically the Tal al-Zaatar area—was attacked by Israeli fighter jets. The exact footage seen in the viral video appears at the 5-minute 20-second mark in Al Jazeera's report. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to 2023 and showed an Indonesian hospital in Gaza that was under Israeli attack, killing several people. The video predates the Pahalgam terror attack and is unrelated to the Indian Army's retaliation.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Traffic dispute video from Dehradun falsely shared as communal attack incident; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 5 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A disturbing video showing a man bleeding profusely was recently circulated on social media, accompanied by the claim that it depicted yet another targeted attack against Muslims in India. The user alleged that the incident occurred in Dehradun, where a Muslim man, attending a wedding with his family, was attacked by a group of men after they discovered his religious identity. However, a PTI Fact Check Desk investigation found that the video was misleadingly shared with a communal narrative. It showed a fight between two groups over a traffic-related dispute in Dehradun, Uttarakhand. While police confirmed that members of different communities were involved in the altercation, there is no evidence to suggest the conflict was motivated by religious differences. Claim An X user, Mr. Haque (@faizulhaque95), shared a video on May 4, claiming it depicted another incident of a targeted attack against Muslims in India. The video showed a man bleeding profusely after he, along with his family, was allegedly attacked by a group over their religious identity in Dehradun, Uttarakhand. "Dehradun, Uttarakhand: A Muslim family came from Doiwala to Dehradun for a wedding. 5-6 people came and attacked them with iron rods and a knife at Banjarwala, asking their name and religion," the user captioned the video. When this story was published, the video had garnered 147k views and 3k likes. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other social media accounts that shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. In the subsequent investigation phase, taking cues from the information shared in the purported post, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google. The search result led to a report published by India Today covering the incident. According to the report, the incident occurred on May 1 in Dehradun, when Anish Ali, a resident of Bhogpur, was on his way to a wedding with his family. His car got stuck in a roadside drain outside a shop in the Monal Enclave area, causing a traffic jam. The road blockage led to a heated argument, which escalated into a physical altercation between Anish Ali and a resident, Sanjay Rawat. Members from both parties sustained injuries in the incident. "Dehradun Police said that while the altercation did involve members of different communities, there is no evidence to support the claim that the fight occurred due to religious differences," the report stated. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: The customised search also led the Desk to a statement released by Dehradun Police on their official Facebook handle. The police stated, "The incident led to controversy due to car damage and jamming, but through social media, some people are trying to communalise the incident. Police are keeping a constant watch on social media. Such individuals are being identified, and strict legal action will be taken against them." Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was falsely shared on social media with a communal angle

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, Singer Sonu Nigam didn't make any remark on BJP; fake social media card with Aaj Tak logo on it shared with the false claim
content: New Delhi, May 5 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid ongoing controversy around singer Sonu Nigam following a statement he made during a recent concert in Bengaluru, a purported graphic from leading Hindi news channel Aaj Tak, featuring his photo, was shared on social media. The claim accompanying the social media card alleged that Nigam called the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) "a bunch of fools" who would be unable to retaliate after the Pahalgam terror attack. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral post was shared with a false claim. The graphics card with the Aaj Tak Tak logo on it was fabricated. In the channel's actual post on X, Sonu Nigam said, "These people become an unpleasant ordeal," referring to an FIR filed against him. A video from the concert shows Nigam responding sharply to students who were aggressively shouting "Kannada, Kannada." In response, he noted that some of his most memorable work had been in Kannada. He also drew a metaphorical parallel to the Pahalgam incident, citing such hostility as a reflection of the intolerance that fuels unrest. Nowhere did he refer to the BJP in his remarks. Claim On May 3, an X (formerly Twitter) user shared a purported graphic from a leading Hindi news channel, Aaj Tak, featuring Sonu Nigam's picture with the claim that he called the BJP a bunch of fools who would not be able to retaliate after the Pahalgam terror attack. The post's caption that clocked 536.1k views read: "BJP is an army of idiots. These people will not be able to do anything at Pahalgam—Sonu Nigam's controversial statement." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral graphic through Reverse Image Search and found several other users had shared the same post with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across the original X post by Aaj Tak dated May 3, 2025, mentioning that the singer landed himself in trouble after he said something during a music concert held in Bangalore on 25-26 April that caused a ruckus. An FIR has been lodged against Sonu Nigam at Avalahalli Police Station in Bangalore. The singer has been accused of hurting the sentiments of the people of the Kannada community. Here is the link to the post, and below is the screenshot of the same. It all started after one of his recent concerts in Bengaluru when a student in the audience began shouting "Kannada, Kannada" in a harsh and demanding tone. A video of the incident quickly went viral on social media. Nigam responded: "Throughout my musical journey, I've sung in many languages, but some of my most memorable work has been in Kannada...However, I felt deeply hurt when that young man, who hadn't lived in this industry as long as I've been, tried to intimidate me into singing in Kannada. This is the reason behind the incident in Pahalgam. Please see who is standing before you. I love you guys." Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports and came across a report by The Economic Times dated May 1, 2025. According to the report, Sonu Nigam was in the middle of singing one of his popular Hindi tracks and abruptly paused his performance when a student in the audience began shouting "Kannada, Kannada" in a harsh and demanding tone. The singer, visibly displeased, addressed the situation directly on stage. "He went on to draw a parallel with a controversial incident in Pahalgam, using it as a metaphor for intolerance, and added, This kind of hostility fuels the kind of unrest we saw in Pahalgam. Please recognise who's standing in front of you. I genuinely care about you," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. We then scanned Sonu Nigam's social media handle and found a video on his official Instagram handle where the singer clarified his stance on the fiasco. He said, "There were only 4–5 goons shouting. Thousands of others were respectful. Please do not generalise the entire Kannadiga community. Kannadigas are very nice people." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk also conducted another set of customised keyword searches to find reports stating the details of the FIR that was lodged against Sonu Nigam following the entire controversy. A report by News 18 dated May 4, 2025, mentioned that an FIR was filed against him in Bengaluru over a controversial remark he made during a concert on April 27, 2025. "The FIR has been registered under Section 352, which pertains to intentional insults aimed at provoking a breach of peace," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Furthermore, concerning the viral Aaj Tak postcard that claimed that the singer called the BJP a bunch of fools and would not retaliate to the Pahalgam attack, Sonu Nigam took to his Instagram story to reject the claim, calling it fabricated. "It has come to my knowledge that some unknown people are attributing my name and image to ridicule and publicly abuse workers of a political party. They are using Aaj Tak's logo wrongfully. I therefore make it abundantly clear that I have no links or association whatsoever to any such doctored and fabricated posts," it read. Below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral Aaj Tak graphic is fake. In the original version, he said that these people became unpleasant after an FIR was filed against him.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Fact Check: Facor Global CEO's photo with Akhilesh Yadav shared to falsely claim 'SP chief was with Pakistani MP Saifullah Abro'
content: New Delhi, May 6 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid heightened tensions at the India-Pakistan border following the Pahalgam terror attack, a photo featuring Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav alongside another man was circulated on social media. Users falsely claimed that the man in the image was Pakistani MP Saifullah Abro. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found the claim false. The man in the photograph is not Saifullah Abro but Ashish Saraf, Chairman and CEO of Facor Global. The social media post was misleading and shared with a baseless claim. Claim On April 30, an X (formerly Twitter) user named 'Emon Mukherjee' shared a post featuring SP Chief Akhilesh Yadav along with a man, claiming that the man standing beside Yadav is Pakistani MP Saifullah Abro. "The traitor tap thief was celebrating in London with Pakistani Saifullah. In the Parliament of Pakistan, Member of Parliament Saifullah expressed happiness over his statement in favour of Pakistan yesterday, and there was a wave of happiness in Pakistan over Akhilesh Yadav's anti-India statement. It seems that the Samajwadi Party chief will contest the next election from Islamabad." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the photo through Reverse Image Search and found several users shared the same photo with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a website named 'Ashish Saraf', which featured the same person along with Akhilesh Yadav and several other images of Indian politicians, with the man seen in the social media post. Here is the link , and below is a screenshot of the same. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk checked the website's biography section and found that Ashish Saraf is the Chairman and CEO of Facor Global Pte Ltd., an international trading firm that provides financial advisory services for global investments. Below is a screenshot of the same. Upon further investigation of the photo, the Desk also came across an X post by BJP MP Nishikant Dubey dated April 30. The post featured the same image as seen in the social media post. The caption read: "Big good news for Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav ji who kept celebrating in London even during the budget session of Parliament, Pakistan Parliament MP Saifullah expressed happiness on his statement in favour of Pakistan yesterday, wave of happiness in Pakistan on Akhilesh Yadav ji's anti-India statement, it seems that Samajwadi Party chief will contest the next election from Islamabad?" Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. However, Dubey later issued a clarification, X post dated May 3, 2025, saying that Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, who was praised for his statements in the Parliament of Pakistan, was loitering in London even during the budget session of the Parliament. This is a picture of him loitering in London. "Some people do not know how to read Hindi? I wrote that Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, praised for his statements in the Parliament of Pakistan, was loitering in London even during the Parliament budget session. This is a picture of him loitering in London. I wish the English with Pakistani mentality understood Hindi?" read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking the investigation ahead, the Desk also scanned the official X handle of the Samaywadi Party Media Cell and came across an X post quoting Nishikant Dubey's post. SP Media Cell wrote that the person referred to as Saifullah is Ashish Sarraf, a decent, wonderful, and good person. Ashish Saraf's pictures are with many BJP leaders, and he has also made good investments in BJP-ruled states, and the proof of which is out there." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. The comparison image below shows the stark difference between Pakistani MP Saifullah Abro and Ashish Saraf. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the photo featuring Akhilesh Yadav with the Chairman & CEO of Facor Global, Ashish Saraf, was falsely shared as Yadav with Pakistani MP Saifullah Abro.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of banquet hall fire falsely shared as Bajrang Dal setting fire to a mosque; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 6 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a building engulfed in flames was recently circulated on social media with the claim that it depicted a mosque set on fire by members of the Bajrang Dal. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found it false. The video shows a fire that broke out at a banquet hall in Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh, due to a short circuit. It was not related to any targeted attack on a religious site. The social media post was shared with a false claim. Claim An Instagram user 'x___bipin___07' on April 27 shared a video claiming it showed a mosque set on fire by members of Bajrang Dal. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid verification tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was reverse-searched using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here : The reverse image search also led the Desk to a video on an Instagram page named 'apnaghaziabad' on April 4. The page shared the same video seen in the viral post, stating that it originally depicted fire that erupted at a banquet hall in Gaziabad's Raj Nagar Extension. "The banquet hall was on fire in Raj Nagar Extension on Thursday afternoon. Two vehicles were also gutted in the fire that is believed to have started from a short circuit," the user shared the video with the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the viral video's content, matched with the video posted by the Instagram page. In the subsequent part of the investigation, taking cues from the information shared in the purported post, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google. The search result led to a report covering the development published by the Hindustan Times on April 4. According to the report, two major fire incidents rocked Ghaziabad on April 3. The first incident occurred near the Raj Bagh Metro station, while the incident depicted in the video was a fire that erupted at a banquet hall in Raj Nagar Extension. The report mentioned, "The fire was suspected to have been triggered by an electrical short circuit. The front portion of the banquet hall was damaged, while a car and a small commercial vehicle were also destroyed." Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video does not depict a fire started by members of Bajrang Dal at a mosque.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old, unrelated video falsely shared claiming Indian fighter jet crashed during recent IAF night drill
content: New Delhi, May 6 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Several social media users shared a video showing an aircraft taking off, falsely claiming it depicted an Indian Air Force (IAF) fighter jet crashing during a recent night drill. They further alleged that it was the second such incident involving an IAF jet since a three-day military exercise started. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found that the video has been online since 2013 and has no connection to the recent IAF drill. It was misleadingly circulated as footage of a recent crash. Notably, although the exercise was initially planned for two days, IAF officials completed it in a single night. The viral video was shared with a false claim on social media. Claim On May 4, an X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video of an aircraft taking off, claiming that it was an Indian Air Force fighter jet that crashed during a takeoff drill, adding that it is the second crash of their fighter jet since the start of the 3-day exercise "An Indian Air Force fighter jet has crashed during a takeoff drill from a highway as part of a wartime exercise. This is the second crash of 1,410 views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid verification tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was reverse-searched using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a Facebook video with clips similar to those seen in the social media post. The post, dated October 22, 2017 (clearing that the video is not recent and unrelated to the three-day exercise), mentioned that an Indian Air Force Mig-27 crashed on takeoff. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities in the visuals of the Facebook post from 2017 and the viral social media post on X. The Desk also came across a YouTube post dated January 16, 2013, featuring the same video as seen in the social media post. Though no information was attached to the video, it is clear that the social media post is not recent. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Though the desk could not verify when and where the incident happened or provide any other details, it is clear that the video has been available on the internet since 2013. The Desk also conducted a customised keyword search to find relevant media reports citing the crash of an Indian jet, but the search did not yield any credible reports. If such an event had happened, it would have gained nationwide attention. However, the Desk came across a PTI report carried by NDTV dated May 2, 2025 which mentioned that the Indian Air Force (IAF) commenced its much-anticipated "land and go" drill on the 3.5-km stretch of the Ganga Expressway in Shahjahanpur district of Uttar Pradesh, marking a significant milestone in the country's defence preparedness. "Indian Air Force Begins 'Land And Go' Drills On Ganga Expressway In UP," read the headline of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. According to a report by Deccan Herald dated May 3, 2025, the drill, which took place between 7 pm and 10 pm on Friday, saw fighter jets Rafale, Sukhoi, Jaguar, and Mirage-2000 simulate touch-and-go landings and combat operations on the 3.5-kilometre airstrip near Piru village under the Jalalabad Police Station. "The drill was originally scheduled for two days, but IAF officials completed the entire exercise in one night," read a section of the report. The report, however, did not mention anything about the crash of a fighter jet. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video has been on the internet since 2013 and is unrelated to the night drill with fighter jets conducted by the IAF.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old photo of LeT terrorist arrested by BSF falsely shared with fake and fabricated confession involving RSS
content: New Delhi, May 6 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): An image showing a bearded man standing with two security personnel was recently circulated on social media, with the claim that he was a newly arrested Kashmiri terrorist who confessed during interrogation that the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) had supplied him with weapons and funds to incite violence against Hindus. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found that the image actually shows Abdul Qayoom, a terrorist arrested by the BSF in 2016 while attempting to infiltrate the Indian border through Akhnoor in Jammu and Kashmir. He is a resident of Sialkot, Pakistan. An old image was falsely shared with a fabricated narrative to mislead viewers. Claim On May 1, an Instagram user '__faiz_creation' shared a post featuring an image of a bearded man in the custody of two security personnel. The user claimed he was a recently captured Kashmiri terrorist who, during interrogation, confessed to receiving weapons and funding from the RSS. "A Kashmiri terrorist who was caught alive during interrogation said RSS provides us weapons and money and tells us to kill Hindus so that hatred can be filled in the minds of Hindus against Muslims," the user wrote in the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the photo through Google Reverse Image Search and found several social media accounts that had previously shared the same image with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The reverse image search also led to a news report published by DNA in September 2016. According to the report, the man in the image is 32-year-old Pakistani national Abdul Qayoom, who was arrested by BSF troops while attempting to infiltrate Indian territory across the border fence in Akhnoor, Jammu and Kashmir. The report also identified Qayoom as an activist of the Pakistan-based terror outfit Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT). "Qayoom was found to be well aware of various terrorist organisations based in Pakistan and their leaders, including Hafiz Saeed (Hizbul Mujahideen chief), Syed Salahuddin, and separatist leaders in Kashmir — Syed A. S. Geelani, Asiya Andrabi, Yasin Malik, etc.," the report stated. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image that highlights the fact that the image seen in the social media post matches the featured image in the news report. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search related to Qayoom's 2016 arrest to corroborate the details. This led to reports published by News18 India and The Quint, which confirmed the same facts — that Qayoom was arrested while trying to infiltrate the border and had links to LeT. However, none of the reports mentioned any confession regarding RSS providing weapons or funding. Here are the links to News 18 and The Quint's reports. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old image from 2016 has been falsely shared on social media with a fabricated claim linking a Pakistani terrorist to the RSS.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Road rage incident from Pune falsely shared as attack on Hindu family over anti-Pakistan post
content: New Delhi, May 5 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a violent brawl erupting between a group of people was recently circulated on social media, accompanied by a claim that it depicted an assault on a Hindu family in Pune after they allegedly posted against Pakistan on social media. The video gained widespread traction amid heightened tensions between India and Pakistan following the Pahalgam attack. However, upon investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found the video to be falsely shared with a misleading communal narrative. The incident was, in fact, a case of road rage. Shoaib Umar Saiyyad and his associates beat up Harsh Keshwani in Pune for honking. They later allegedly assaulted his family as well. Claim An X handle, using the username Prof Sudhanshu (@ProfSudhaanshu), shared a video on May 2 claiming it showed a targeted attack against a Hindu family in Pune. The user alleged the incident occurred after the family posted on social media against Pakistan. "What kind of secular India have you made? A Hindu family was attacked in Pune just because they posted against Pakistan! Is speaking against Pakistan in your own country now a crime?" the user wrote, sharing the video. When this report was published, the video had garnered 62.2k views and 3.7k likes. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of the keyframes was run through Google Lens, discovering several other social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , along with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a report published by Lokmat Times on April 29, covering the same incident. The feature image of the article matched the keyframe from the video, but the article revealed that the video depicted a brawl that broke out over a honking dispute, not a social media post against Pakistan. According to the report, the incident occurred around 2 p.m. on April 27 in Pune's Bhawani Peth area, when a man and his family were brutally attacked following a dispute over honking. "The incident started when a man named Harsh Keshwani, who was passing through a narrow lane, honked at Shoaib Umar Saiyyad, who was unloading goods from his auto-rickshaw parked on the road. Angered by the honking, Shoaib allegedly abused Harsh and started beating him. Later, Harsh returned with his family — including his sister Nikita and grandfather Bharat Keshwani — to confront Shoaib. However, Shoaib and his associates allegedly attacked Harsh and his family again," the report stated. "Shoaib reportedly hit Harsh on the head with a stone and threatened to kill him. Harsh sustained a serious head injury and was rushed to the hospital for treatment. Nikita and Karan were also injured in the attack. Stones were reportedly thrown at them, and Nikita suffered injuries to her hand and leg. Shoaib also abused their grandfather and allegedly threatened to burn their house," the report added. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Below is a comparison image highlighting that the viral video's content matches the report's feature image. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video does not depict an incident of assault on a Hindu family over any social media post.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Fake social media post shared claiming Pakistan captured IAF pilot after jet crash; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 5 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid heightened tensions between India and Pakistan following the Pahalgam terror attack that claimed 26 lives on April 22, a social media post allegedly linked to the ongoing hostilities between the two countries recently went viral. The post falsely claimed that the Pakistan Army had captured Indian Air Force pilot Wing Commander Dinesh Chandra after his aircraft crashed in Pakistani territory. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found it fabricated. The post was falsely shared on social media to mislead viewers. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user with the handle Cricket & Conflict (@Ahmedreal23) shared a post on May 4, alleging that the Pakistan Army had captured Indian Air Force pilot Wing Commander Dinesh Chandra after his aircraft crashed in Pakistani territory. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found several other social media accounts sharing similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here , respectively: Next, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search using the name "Wing Commander Dinesh Chandra" across all major social media platforms, including X and YouTube. It also searched for any credible media reports or official statements that could substantiate the viral claim. However, the search yielded no credible results to support the claim. Below is a screenshot showing that the search results yielded no credible evidence on social media to support the viral claim. The PTI Fact Check Desk does not rely solely on information provided by Grok and independently verifies all claims through thorough cross-checking before publication. In this case, we scanned other social media platforms and searched various news websites to check whether credible sources had reported on the claim shared in the social media post. However, we found no information to support the claim. To further verify, the Desk contacted a senior official from the Indian Air Force, who confirmed that the social media post was fake. Based on this, the Desk concluded that the claim suggesting the Pakistan Army had captured Wing Commander Dinesh Chandra after a jet crash is false.

title: PTI Fact Check: From airstrikes to algorithmic disaster - the real war is on our small screen
content: By Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check: In the wake of India's air strikes on nine terror facilities across Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir on the night of May 6–7, social media didn't just light up, it exploded with toxic misinformation. Even before official details could be confirmed, the digital space was hijacked by a barrage of false information, outdated and doctored videos, all masquerading as "breaking ground zero visuals" from the strikes. But this wasn't just the work of propaganda networks or bot armies. What's truly alarming is how common, unaware, misinformed, or already biased social media users became active players in this flood of falsehoods. Recycled videos from Syria, Gaza, Ukraine and other places and unverified footage were repackaged and shared as scenes from the India-Pakistan escalation. Video game footage even made its way into the mix, while dramatic music and captions turned misinformation into viral content. This is not just a platform problem; it's a people problem. Fueled by emotion, bias, prejudice, and hyperpatriotism, ordinary individuals have become unaware and misinformed foot soldiers in a digital war over social media platforms. The sheer volume of fake content being circulated, often without malicious intent, but with real consequences, shows how deeply vulnerable our digital society has become. And amid all this, social media platforms continue to prioritise reach and engagement over truth and responsibility. Their failure to moderate in real time, verify trending content, or label misleading visuals due to the enormous volume is enabling this digital disaster. However, regulation cannot come only from the top. It must start with us. Self-regulation is no longer optional. In a hyperconnected, high-stakes information ecosystem, every user has the power to calm or inflame a crisis. Before hitting "share," they must ask: Is this real? Is it verified? Is it necessary to post? The right to express oneself must come with the responsibility of ascertaining. Unchecked, this behaviour is more than irresponsible, it's dangerous. We are watching truth decay, public trust erode, and social divisions widen in real time. This is a wake-up call. The physical war may be confined to borders, but the information war is everywhere, and we are all combatants, whether we like it or not. If we do not draw the line and continue to let algorithms and anger lead the conversation, we are not only losing grip on the truth, we are actively sabotaging it. The battle for facts is now a fight for our collective sanity. Let's not become the enemy we're trying to defeat. (Author is the head of PTI Fact Check and Digital Services at the Press Trust of India)

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: After India's 'Operation Sindoor', old videos with misleading claims flood social media; PTI Fact Check debunks five such posts
content: New Delhi, May 8 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Following the Indian Armed Forces' 24 precision missile strikes under Operation Sindoor, targeting nine terror sites across Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, including key Lashkar-e-Taiba and Jaish-e-Mohammed strongholds in Muridke and Bahawalpur, social media platforms like X and Facebook were flooded with fake videos, misleading images, and unverified claims. Many of these originated from propaganda sources, including some based in Pakistan. The Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk thoroughly examined and debunked five false claims online. The investigation revealed a pattern of recycled content falsely attributed to Pakistan's supposed retaliation for Operation Sindoor. These misleading posts appear part of a coordinated attempt to exploit public sentiment and spread misinformation disguised as breaking news. Operation Sindoor was India's response to the April 22 terror attack in Pahalgam, located in Jammu and Kashmir's Anantnag district, which killed 26 people—25 Indian nationals and one Nepali citizen. Over 70 terrorists were killed and more than 60 were injured in the operation, significantly degrading the operational capability of these groups. Hours after the strike, Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri addressed the media, stating that it was essential to bring the perpetrators and planners of the Pahalgam attack to justice, especially in the absence of any demonstrable action from Islamabad against terror infrastructure on its territory or under its control. Claim 1: A video featuring a crashed aircraft engulfed in flames was shared by an X (formerly Twitter) user named South Asia Perspective on May 7, claiming that Pakistan recently shot down an Indian Rafale jet near Bahawalpur, linking it to Operation Sindoor carried out by the Indian armed forces. The post's caption that clocked 21.6k views read: " Big Breaking. Pakistan claims it has shot down an Indian Rafale jet near Bahawalpur." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Reverse Image Search and found several other users shared the same photo with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here , along with their archived versions, which can be viewed here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a news report by Lokmat Times, dated September 3, 2024, which clarifies that the picture in the viral social media post is not recent and unrelated to Operation Sindoor carried out by the Indian armed forces. The report highlighted that it was an Indian Air Force (IAF) MiG-29 fighter jet that crashed in Barmer. The pilot ejected safely, and there have been no reports of casualties. The article's feature image was similar to the one shared on social media platforms. "IAF Plane Crash in Rajasthan: Indian Air Force Mig-29 Fighter Jet Crashes Near Barmer, Pilot Safe (Watch Video)," read the report's headline. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the photo shared on social media and the cover image of the news report, which stated that the aircraft was a MiG-29 that crashed near Barmer. Based on the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across an X post by DD News Live dated September 2, 2024. The visuals shared closely resembled the photo seen in the viral post. The information shared in the post confirmed that an IAF MiG-29 encountered a critical technical snag in the Barmer sector, forcing the pilot to eject. "During a routine night training mission in the Barmer sector, an IAF Mig-29 encountered a critical technical snag, forcing the pilot to eject. The pilot is safe and no loss of life or property was reported. A Court of Inquiry has been ordered," read the caption. Here is the link to the X post, and below is a screenshot of the same. An X post dated September 2, 2024, by Press Trust of India (PTI) quoting the Indian Air Force also mentioned that during a routine night training mission in the Barmer sector, an IAF MiG-29 encountered a critical technical snag, forcing the pilot to eject. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral photograph dates back to 2024 and is unrelated to the Indian armed forces' Operation Sindoor. The incident occurred in the Barmer sector, Rajasthan, when a MiG-29 aircraft encountered a technical snag during a routine night training mission. Claim 2: A video showing a white plume of smoke which filled the sky, followed by a massive explosion, was shared on X by a user named '@QTHESTORMM' on May 7, claiming that Pakistan retaliated with a missile attack against India, after Operation Sindoor by the Indian armed forces. "MAJOR UPDATE: PAKISTAN RETALIATES AGAINST INDIA JUST NOW IN RECENT MISSILE ATTACK !!!," read the caption, which garnered 383.3k views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid verification tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was reverse-searched using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. One such post can be found here , and its archived version can be found here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk found an X post dated June 17, 2024, confirming that the video is old and unrelated to Operation Sindoor. The post featured the same video that has been circulating on social media recently. As per the caption, it showed the Beirut explosion. "Scary close-up of Beirut explosion. The Beirut explosion was a tragic event that occurred on 4 August 2020, when a large amount of ammonium nitrate stored at the Port of Beirut exploded, causing widespread damage and casualties," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. The 2024 X post mentioned the incident occurred in August 2020. Taking a cue from this, the Desk once again ran the keyframes of the viral video through Reverse Image Search and came across a 00:19-second video uploaded by a Facebook user on August 5, 2020. According to the user, it showed a bigger explosion at Beirut Port, Líbano. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Furthermore, considering all the above findings, the Desk conducted another set of customised keyword searches on Google to find relevant media reports. I came across a report by Mirror Now published on August 5, 2020. The report highlighted that the blast originated in the port warehouses, which have been described as the worst explosion in the Lebanese capital for years. At least 100 people have died, and more than 4,000 were injured during the catastrophic events. "Beirut explosion: Horrifying videos capture moment deadly blast smashes into cars and people," read the headline of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image that shows the similarities between the viral clip and those shared by the news report about the Beirut blast. Another report by Financial Express, published on August 7, 2020, shared the images of the aftermath of the blast, stating that three days after a massive explosion rocked Beirut, killing at least 149 people and causing widespread devastation, rescuers are still searching for survivors and the government is investigating what caused the disaster. "The chemicals that went up in flames in Beirut's deadliest peace-time explosion arrived in the Lebanese capital seven years ago on a leaky Russian-leased cargo ship that, according to its captain, should never have stopped there," read a section of the image. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Notably, Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk debunked the same video that circulated, claiming that the incident happened in Jaipur in 2024. On December 20, 2024, an LPG tanker collided with a truck while making a U-turn on the Jaipur-Ajmer highway. Here is the link to the story. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to 2024, which showed a massive explosion in Beirut and is unrelated to Pakistan's retaliation against India after Operation Sindoor. Claim 3: A purported Republic Bharat's footage alongside a picture showing a crashed aircraft was shared by an X user named 'SkyIsLimit' on May 7, claiming that the image showed the aftermath of the retaliation against the Indian armed forces by the Pakistan Army, while the Indian media confirmed the incident. In the 00:48-second video, it can be heard: "India's Jaguar fighter jet has been shot down. It was shot down during India's military attack on Pakistan…There is tension and anything can happen…" "Who says Pakistan hasn't done anything. See this video, Indian Media is also confirming. Pakistan Zindabad," read the post's caption, which clocked 882k views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid verification tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was reverse-searched using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. One such post can be found here , and its archived version can be found here . To debunk the video, the Desk first carefully scanned it and found several discrepancies, such as 'Breaking News HD' on the top right and bottom right corners of the video, along with the 'InShot' (a video editing software) logo. Further, 'Bharat' in Hindi is misspelled on the top right corner. Below is a screenshot highlighting the mentioned findings, which hint that the video is manipulated. Moreover, on carefully listening to the entire video report, at 00:31 seconds, the voice-over seems to be overlapped, hinting that it is edited and manipulated. Here is the link to the video from the same timestamp as mentioned. Considering the above findings, the Desk, after meticulously researching, found a news report from Republic Bharat, shared on 3 April 2025, about the crash in Jamnagar. The title of the report read: "Gujarat News: Jaguar Fighter Aircraft Crash...One Pilot Killed | R Bharat." This clarifies that an old video report was edited and manipulated using a fake voiceover and ticker text. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a Reverse Image Search on the picture of a crashed aircraft. The search resulted in a Press Trust of India (PTI) report carried by ABP Live on April 4, 2025. The report's cover image was similar to the one shared in the viral post. According to the report, the aircraft crash occurred near the Jamnagar IAF station. "Flight Lieutenant Siddharth Yadav, who was killed in the Jaguar fighter jet crash in Gujarat, was cremated with full military honours at his native Majra Bhalkhi village in Haryana's Rewari district," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the image shared in the viral post and the cover image of the news article. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video showing a news report by Republic Bharat is old, edited, and manipulated. The original report was regarding a Jaguar fighter aircraft crash in Gujarat's Jamnagar on April 2, 2025. Claim 4: A photo of what looks like an aircraft that is wrecked was shared by an X user named Dr. Syeda Abiha Fatimah Shah on May 7, claiming that the Pakistani PL-15 missile struck down an Indian Rafale jet near Bahawalpur, Pakistan.
