It could is an attempt to divert attention from the situation to weaken the Sharif Government. Fortunately, people are not falling for this as they are looking at the bigger goal - peace in the region. Imran Khan's party and leaders of PTI (Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaaf) have clearly announced that PTI stands with the government at this time with the Sharif Government. I am grateful professional journalists and fact-checkers for reaching out to me and other journalists in Pakistan to get the facts, which is difficult considering the situation between our countries." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the alleged Press Release by the Government of Pakistan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs is manipulated and digitally altered. Moreover, the injured picture of former Pakistan PM Imran Khan dates back to 2013 when he fell off a lift carrying him to a 10-14 feet high stage at a rally in Lahore.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated newspaper clip of The Daily Telegraph falsely shared to claim it praised Pak's Air Force
content: New Delhi, May 11 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Following the agreement between India and Pakistan to halt all military actions on land, air, and sea, effective from the evening of May 10, a purported front page of The Daily Telegraph, a UK newspaper, featuring a picture of a fighter jet with a Pakistani Air Force roundel on its tail fin, was shared on social media. The newspaper allegedly praised the Pakistani Air Force, calling it the "King of the Skies." However, the Press Trust of India (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that no such article was published by The Daily Telegraph on May 10. Further investigation revealed the newspaper clip to be fabricated and AI-generated, confirming that the viral post was shared with a false claim. Claim: An X user named Kamran Bashir shared a purported newspaper front page of The Daily Telegraph, a UK newspaper, claiming that it praised the Pakistani Air Force, calling it the "King of the Skies" "UK media about our Air Forces. Pakistan Zindabad," read the post's caption, which at the time of publishing this report garnered 663.9k views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the purported newspaper front page through Reverse Image Search and found several other users shared the same image with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived version can be viewed here and here , respectively. On carefully analysing the viral newspaper cover, and found several discrepancies hinting that it might be forged and fabricated. The date is listed as Saturday, 10 May, without a year. The web address is listed as "telegraph.cuk", which is a fake or mistyped domain — the real website is telegraph.co.uk. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. On further scanning the search results, the Desk also found the uncropped image of the doctored news front, uploaded by an X user on May 11, 2025. The Desk found the text in it riddled with errors and jumped sentences, again hinting that it is fabricated. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find reports of the Daily Telegraph writing about the Pakistan Air Force, but the search did not yield any reports. We also scanned through the website on May 10, 2025, the Daily Telegraph issue available online, and did not find any such page or report. Here is the link to the website; below is a screenshot of it. Considering the above findings, the Desk ran the cropped version of the viral newspaper clip through Decopy AI, an AI detection tool whose results confirmed that it was AI-generated. Below is a screenshot of the result. Using WasitAI, another AI-detection tool, the Desk ran the uncropped version of the newspaper clip, and the results confirmed that it was AI-generated. Below is a screenshot highlighting this. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that The Daily Telegraph's viral front page was AI-generated and shared as real, with a false claim.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Fake, parody X accounts impersonating Col Sofiya Qureshi and Wing Commander Vyomika Singh shared as real with false claims
content: New Delhi, May 12 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): As Operation Sindoor captures national attention, Colonel Sofiya Qureshi and Wing Commander Vyomika Singh -- the faces of the Indian Armed Forces' counterattack on terror camps across the border -- have emerged as proud symbols of courage and competence. However, several X accounts impersonating Col Qureshi and Wing Commander Singh, falsely claiming to be their official handles, began publishing multiple posts. One such account quickly garnered thousands of followers. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and confirmed that both accounts were fake, created as parody profiles and falsely attributed to the officers. These impersonator accounts were being circulated online as the official handles of Col Qureshi and Wing Commander Singh. Claim 1: X account by the name of Wing Commander Vyomika Singh An X post from the said account started circulating on social media, claiming it to be from Wing Commander Vyomika Singh's official X handle. The account, under the username "@WingVyomika," had 25.9K followers. Here is the link and archive link to the social media handle, along with a screenshot of one of its posts. Investigation When the Desk carefully scanned the bio section of the said account, it found 'Commentary Account' and 'Parody account' written. Hinting that it is a fake account that has been posted in the name of Wing Commander Vyomika Singh and has gained followers. "Proudly serving in the skies, defending the nation with unwavering courage. Indian Air Force | Duty, Honor ~ Commentary Account ~ protecting the motherland," read the bio section. Below is a screenshot highlighting the findings. Next, the profile also contained an official disclaimer from X saying "Parody Account," clicking on which led us to the platform's rules on fan, parody, and commentary accounts. It read: "We allow compliant Parody, Commentary, and Fan (PCF) accounts on X only if the purpose is to discuss, satirize or share information" Here is the link to the rules and policies for authenticity. Also, on further scanning the account, we found that the user had re-tweeted several posts from 'Indian Army Commentary', another dubious account. Making it clear that it was not the official account of the Wing Commander. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a parody account is being shared as a real account of Wing Commander Vyomika Singh Claim 2: X account by the name of Colonel Sofia Qureshi An X account impersonating Colonel Sofia Qureshii has also been viral, sharing multiple posts regarding Operation Sindoor. The account garnered 1,035 Followers. Here is the link to the account, and below is a screenshot of the posts by the user. Investigation To start our investigation, the Desk first noticed discrepancies in the user name, actually. For instance, military personnel do not write "col." in lowercase with a period. The correct designation is "Col" or "Colonel" with appropriate capitalisation and spacing. Also, the official name of the officer is misspelt as 'Sofia Qureshi'; the correct spelling is 'Colonel Sofiya Qureshi'. Below is a screenshot highlighting the above findings. Further analysis revealed' managed by @sariaqureshi_ _' in the bio. A serving officer would not declare a social media manager publicly, especially unofficially. The link to the Instagram handle of some other user is also very unprofessional. Moreover, the year of birth mentioned is 1989, highlighting that it is a fake account. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Moreover, the account had only 99 posts, most of which were made after the two officers' May 7 briefing. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a fake account in Colonel Sofia Qureshi's name was being used following the May 7 briefing of Operation Sindoor.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated videos of PM Modi & Amit Shah shared with false, fabricated, baseless claims; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 12 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Soon after India and Pakistan agreed to a full and immediate ceasefire, effective 5 PM Saturday (May 10), two purported videos of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah apologising to the world surfaced online. The video appeared to depict PM Modi and Amit Shah admitting that Pakistan defeated India in the war and therefore, the two leaders allegedly apologised to the global community. The PTI Fact Check Desk categorically debunked both videos, finding them to be doctored and falsely circulated on social media to mislead viewers. The social media post was shared with fake claims. Claim 1: An X user, Abubakar Qassam (@abubakarqassam), shared a video on May 10 claiming to show Prime Minister Narendra Modi apologising to the world. The video appeared to show the PM admitting that they "lost the battle" to Pakistan. "Modi's cries out over the effects of Operation Banyan Marsus. Should we accept Modi's apology?" read the post's caption, which clocked 39.7k views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation As part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the viral video and found multiple inconsistencies. For example, the PM's lip movements were distorted and not synchronised with the speech. Additionally, his facial expressions looked unnatural, and the overall glossy texture of the video raised suspicions that it was AI-generated. Below is a screenshot highlighting the key findings. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk ran the viral video through HiveModeration, an AI content detection tool. The results of which indicated that the video was AI-generated Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video shared on social media, showing PM Modi extending an apology, was AI-generated. Claim 2: An X user, Abubakar Qassam (@abubakarqassam), shared a video on May 10 claiming to show Union Home Minister Amit Shah apologising to Pakistan and its people. The video appeared to show Amit Shah admitting that they "lost the battle" to Pakistan. "Amit Shah also knelt down. Request for forgiveness from Pakistan and the Pakistani people, does it deserve forgiveness?????," read the caption. The post garnered 43.3k views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation As part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the viral video and found multiple inconsistencies. For example, the Union Home Minister's lip movements were distorted and not synchronised with the speech. Additionally, his facial expressions looked unnatural, and the overall glossy texture of the video raised suspicions that it was AI-generated. Below is a screenshot highlighting the key findings. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk ran the viral video through HiveModeration, an AI content detection tool. The results indicated that the video was AI-generated. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video shared on social media, showing Union Home Minister extending an apology, was AI-generated.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2011 Kashmir picture of suspected militants' bodies shared to falsely claim 'Indian soldiers killed by Pakistan
content: New Delhi, May 12 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): After India launched a massive strike deep inside Pakistan and Pakistan-Occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK) to avenge the killing of Indian civilians by Pakistan-linked terrorists. A few Pakistan-based social media accounts shared footage of bodies being covered with a green cloth. The user claimed that it shows 12 Indian soldiers who were killed due to Pakistan's attack on India. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the post was shared with the false claim on social media. Upon further investigation, the Desk found several reports published in 2011 and 2013 that carried a still from the footage, making it clear that it is not recent and unrelated to the recent tensions between India and Pakistan. According to reports, the image showed bodies of suspected militants in Kashmir. As India launched Operation Sindoor, it destroyed nine high-value terror launchpads across Pakistan and Pojk. The targets belonged to Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT), Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM), and Hizbul Mujahideen. The locations were identified as key training and operational centres for planning attacks against India. Claim: A video showing bodies lying on the ground and covered with a green cloth was shared by an Instagram user 'sabapti491' on May 7, claiming that it shows 12 Indian soldiers who were killed due to Pakistan's attack on India. "The video of 12 Indian soldiers killed in Pakistani counterattacks on Indian Dehramshala Check Post 1 and 2 in front of Rawalakot has surfaced," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation: The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid verification tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was reverse-searched using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , and its archived version can be viewed here and here . The Desk extracted the keyframes of the viral video, ran them through Reverse Image Search, and came across a report by a magazine called Foreign Policy, published on February 21, 2013. The cover image of the report was similar to a clip from the video. According to the report, in January, a series of attacks and counter-attacks by Indian and Pakistani soldiers were reportedly sparked by a grandmother who crossed the Line of Control to be near her children and their families, resulting in the deaths of soldiers on both sides. "What is striking about recent events and seems to be a particular throwback to earlier times, is the apparent brutality with which the two Indian soldiers involved were killed," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Though no details were mentioned regarding the photo, it is clear that the image is not recent and has been on the internet at least since 2013. On further scanning the search results, the Desk found another report by a French media organisation, Radio France Internationale, published in August 2011, which carried a similar photo. According to the report, the bodies were of suspected Kashmiri separatists. "According to official records, these unmarked graves contain the bodies of separatist fighters killed by the armed forces," read the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the featured image of the news report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the visuals shared on social media have been available online since 2011, making it clear that it is unrelated to the recent tensions between India and Pakistan.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: India-Pakistan 'stoppage of fire' agreement for UPSC exams? AI-generated meme of US President Trump shared with false claims; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 12 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported video featuring US President Donald Trump addressing a press briefing was recently shared on social media, with the claim that a ceasefire agreement between India and Pakistan was prompted by the upcoming UPSC Civil Services Prelims exam scheduled for May 25, 2025. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found it false. The video circulating online is AI-generated and was initially shared as a social media meme. Later, many other users shared the meme as real. Claim An X user, tweetsforupsc, shared a purported video featuring US President Donald Trump addressing a press briefing on May 11, 2025. The user claimed that a ceasefire between India and Pakistan was due to the upcoming UPSC Civil Services Prelims exam scheduled for May 25, 2025. "For Upsc Aspirants. Ur the real reason behind Ceasefire," read the post's caption, which clocked 231k views and 2.4k likes. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid verification tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was reverse-searched using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , and its archived version can be viewed here and here . As part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the viral video and found multiple inconsistencies. For example, President Trump's lip movements were distorted and not synchronised with the speech. Additionally, his facial expressions looked unnatural, raising suspicions that the video was AI-generated. Below is a screenshot highlighting the key findings. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk ran the viral video through HiveMorderation, an AI content detection tool. The results indicated that the video was AI-generated. Below is a screenshot of the result. Moreover, on May 10, 2025, President Trump posted on Truth Social that India and Pakistan had agreed to an immediate ceasefire. Nowhere in the post did he mention the UPSC exam as the reason. "After a long night of talks mediated by the United States, I am pleased to announce that India and Pakistan have agreed to a FULL AND IMMEDIATE CEASEFIRE. Congratulations to both countries for using Common Sense and Great Intelligence. Thank you for your attention to this matter!" the post read. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Meanwhile, India rejected any mediation related to the dispute on Jammu and Kashmir with Pakistan, reaffirming that Islamabad needs to return the territory occupied by it. According to a report by Hindustan Times dated May 11, 2025, the government's stance comes after US President Donald Trump offered to mediate the dispute between the nations. Citing Press Trust of India (PTI) in their report, it read: "The only matter related to Kashmir to discuss is Pakistan returning territory under its illegal occupation" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that President Trump's video is AI-generated and is being shared on social media with a false claim.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Social media posts falsely claimed Lt. Kiran Shekhawat martyred during recent India-Pakistan military conflict; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 12 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid the ongoing India-Pakistan military tensions, a purported image of a woman was recently shared on social media with the claim that she was an Indian security forces officer who lost her life while fighting against Pakistan during 'Operation Sindoor'. The user claimed the image depicted Lt. Kiran Shekhawat, a 27-year-old Indian officer who laid down her life for the country. However, in its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that while Lt. Kiran Shekhawat did indeed sacrifice her life for the nation, her death was not connected to the current India-Pakistan military tensions. Lt. Shekhawat lost her life in a 2015 naval aircraft crash off the coast of Goa. An old image was falsely shared on social media with a misleading claim. Claim An X user '@SureshK15152577' shared on May 10 an image purportedly depicting an Indian woman officer, Kiran Shekhawat, who died in the line of duty while fighting against Pakistan in the current India-Pak military conflict. The user stated, "Heartfelt tributes to 27-year-old Kiran Shekhawat who sacrificed her life for the country." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the social media image through Google Lens and found multiple users who had shared the same photo with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively: In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the information mentioned in the social media post regarding Kiran Shekhawat, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google. The search results led the Desk to a report published by NDTV, which confirmed that Lt. Kiran Shekhawat was the country's first woman officer who attained martyrdom in the line of duty. However, as the Desk delved further into the report, it found that Lt. Kiran Shekhawat, along with Lieutenant Abhinav Nagori, attained martyrdom back in March 2015 after the Dornier-228 maritime surveillance aircraft they were aboard crashed into the Arabian Sea near Goa. The incident is not connected in any way to the recent military conflict that has escalated between India and Pakistan. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Additionally, during the investigation, the Desk also came across a social media video purportedly claiming to depict the final moments of Lt. Kiran Shekhawat as she laid down her life for the country. The footage allegedly showed Lt. Shekhawat lying on the ground with serious injuries, while another teammate tried to rescue her. Here is the link and archive link to one such post, along with a screenshot: Although the investigation had already established that Lt. Kiran Shekhawat died in March 2015 and her death was unrelated to the ongoing India-Pakistan tensions, the Desk further tried to analyse the origin of the video. The result revealed that the video was probably a part of a shoot. For instance, at the 0:10 second timestamp, a camera was seen capturing the frames, thus clearly indicating that the footage depicted in the video was part of a staged shoot rather than a real situation. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the image and video circulated on social media in the name of Lt. Kiran Shekhawat were falsely linked to the ongoing India-Pakistan conflict. Lt Shekhawat lost her life in a 2015 naval aircraft crash unrelated to the present incident.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Fake, fabricated social media card with CNN logo shared to falsely claim India incurred greater losses than Pakistan during recent military conflict
content: New Delhi, May 13 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid heightened tensions between India and Pakistan following Operation Sindoor—under which India launched strikes on terrorist infrastructure at nine locations in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) on May 7—an infographic bearing CNN's logo and branding was circulated on various social media platforms. The graphic purportedly compares the reported losses of India and Pakistan and falsely claims that India suffered greater losses. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found it fabricated and false. CNN has neither reported such information nor published any comparison, as claimed in the social media card shared by users. The Desk also contacted a CNN spokesperson, who categorically denied reporting this information. The social media posts sharing the fake graphic appear to be part of a propaganda campaign against India. Claim An X user named 'Ihsan Khan' shared an infographic titled "India-Pakistan Conflict Statistics" on May 12, 2025. The graphic bears the logo of the multinational news organisation CNN and claims that India incurred greater losses than Pakistan after the launch of Operation Sindoor by the Indian Forces. The infographic claims Pakistan's strike inside India resulted in the destruction of 6 combat jets (including 2 Rafales) and a high-value S-400 air defence system. It also states that 26 Indian air bases were targeted, mentioning Jammu, Udhampur, Gujrat, and Pathankot as key examples. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral infographic through Reverse Image Search and found several other users shared the same post with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be found here and here , respectively. To commence the investigation, the Desk scanned CNN's official website to see if they had reported anything related to the statistics of the Indian-Pakistan conflict. But the search did not yield any credible results. Here is the link to the website, and below is a screenshot of the same. Meanwhile, during a press conference chaired by the DGMOs of all three services on May 11, it was reported that over 100 terrorists, including high-value targets such as Yusuf Azhar, Abdul Malik Rauf, and Mudasir Ahmed, were eliminated during Operation Sindoor on May 7. A report by Press Trust of India read: "Nine terror targets were identified after careful deliberations and they were hit using precision weapons, Director General of Military Operations Lt Gen Rajiv Ghai said at a media briefing." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk contacted a CNN spokesperson who categorically denied reporting this information. "This image is fabricated. CNN at no point reported this information," said a CNN spokesperson to PTI. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral infographic attributed to CNN is fabricated, and the multinational news organisation did not report such information.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated image of Rawalpindi Stadium falsely claims it sustained massive damage after Indian airstrike; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 13 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid heightened tensions between India and Pakistan, several social media users recently shared an image claiming it depicted massive damage to Rawalpindi Stadium in Pakistan following an Indian airstrike. The image allegedly showed the stadium completely destroyed due to India's strike under 'Operation Sindoor'. However, in its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the image was AI-generated and did not depict the actual state of the stadium. While news reports confirmed that areas near the stadium sustained some damage, the stadium itself did not suffer the extensive destruction shown in the viral image. The AI-generated picture was falsely circulated on social media to mislead viewers. Claim An X user, 'Jitendra Pratap Singh' (@jpsin1), on May 12 shared an image, claiming it depicted the damage caused to Pakistan's Rawalpindi Stadium after India's airstrike. The user wrote, "India destroyed Pakistan's Rawalpindi Stadium with a drone." When the story was published, the post had gained over 16k views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and found several social media handles that had shared the same photo with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find original images of Rawalpindi Stadium available online and determine whether those shared on social media matched the real one. The search results led the Desk to the ESPNcricinfo website, which shared multiple images of the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium. Upon reviewing those, the Desk compared them with the one shared on social media and found both to be completely different. Below is a comparison image indicating the result. Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the viral image and found multiple inconsistencies suggesting it to be AI-generated. For instance, the architectural structure of the stadium depicted in the picture appeared completely unreal, suggesting it was AI-generated. Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the image through 'WasItAI', an AI detection tool, and found that the image, or a significant part of it, was created by AI. Here is a screenshot highlighting the result: Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google for 'Rawalpindi Stadium being damaged during India's strike'. The search results led the Desk to multiple reports published around the development, confirming that the drone strike affected areas near the Rawalpindi Stadium. However, it did not cause the kind of major damage shown in the viral image. Below is a link to the report shared by Sports Today, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the image showing the damage caused to Rawalpindi Stadium was AI-generated and falsely shared to mislead viewers.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2022 mock drill video from Faridabad Metro Station falsely shared to claim terrorist was recently arrested there; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 13 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a man being detained by security personnel was recently shared on social media with the claim that it depicted a terrorist being arrested by CISF personnel at Faridabad Metro Station. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found it false. The video actually shows a mock drill conducted by the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) at NHPC Metro Station in Faridabad in June 2022. It is not related to any recent incident. An old video was falsely shared on social media with a misleading claim. Claim An Instagram user, 'shaily_kuntal_123', shared a video on May 7, claiming it depicted scenes from Faridabad Metro Station where CISF personnel had allegedly captured a terrorist. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One keyframe was then run through Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media users who had shared the same video with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively: The reverse image search also led the Desk to a video published on a YouTube channel named 'Faridabad News'. The channel posted the same video as the viral post. However, the details provided revealed that the incident originally depicted a mock drill conducted by the CISF at Faridabad Metro Station in June 2022. The video was shared with the caption: "Terrorist caught on Faridabad Metro Station is wrong, it's a part of the CISF mock drill." Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot: Below is a comparison image confirming that the content seen in the viral video matches the video posted on the YouTube channel: Next, taking a cue from these findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a social media post from the official handle of Faridabad Police. In June 2022, responding to a now-deleted post questioning the video's authenticity, Faridabad Police stated that the video was part of a mock drill conducted by CISF. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video shared on social media initially showed a mock drill conducted at Faridabad Metro Station and did not depict the arrest of a terrorist.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2023 Parliament video of Amit Shah's statement on 'Pakistan-occupied Kashmir' falsely shared after the recent India-Pakistan military conflict
content: New Delhi, May 14 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Soon after India and Pakistan agreed to ceasefire, effective 5 PM on Saturday (May 10) after the recent military conflict, a video of Union Home Minister Amit Shah was shared on social media, allegedly showing him saying that Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) would have been a part of India today if the ceasefire had been deferred by three days. The user claimed Shah made this statement following the recent ceasefire agreement between the two countries. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found the claim false. The video actually dates back to 2023, when Shah was speaking about former prime minister Jawaharlal Nehru during a parliamentary discussion on the Jammu and Kashmir Reservation (Amendment) Bill and the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation (Amendment) Bill. The claim in the social media post is absolutely false. Claim: A video featuring Union Home Minister Amit Shah allegedly saying that Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (Pok) would have been a part of India today if the ceasefire had been deferred by three days was shared by an X user, RedZoneReport, on May 12. In the 00:29-second video, he can be heard saying: "Biggest mistake when our Forces were winning…ceasefire was declared and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir was born. Had the ceasefire been deferred by three days, Pakistan-occupied Kashmir would have been a part of India today…" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation: The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid verification tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was reverse-searched using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived version can be viewed here and here . To commence the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the video and realised the speech was from the Parliament. Then, it noticed a date on the bottom right corner of the screen stating '06.12.23'. Hinting that it is old and unrelated to the recent tensions between India and Pakistan. Below is a screenshot highlighting the above findings. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on YouTube to find the original video of Amit Shah addressing the Parliament. The search led us to a YouTube video uploaded on the official channel of the Home Minister on December 6, 2023. Amit Shah spoke in the Lok Sabha about two bills related to J&K. On listening to the speech, at 53:27 minute timestamp, he could be heard saying: "Kashmir had to suffer because of the blunder that happened during Nehru's time…Kashmir had to suffer for years because of two big mistakes committed during Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru's tenure as the Prime Minister…First, when our Army was winning, a ceasefire was announced on reaching the Punjab area. And Pakistan-occupied Kashmir was born. Had the ceasefire been deferred by three days, Pakistan-occupied Kashmir would have been a part of India." Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk conducted another set of customised keyword searches to find relevant media reports. It came across a Press Trust of India (PTI) report from NDTV on December 7, 2023. According to the report, Amit Shah blamed Nehru's "two major blunders" -- declaring a ceasefire without winning the entire Kashmir and taking the issue to the United Nations -- for the sufferings of the people of Jammu and Kashmir. "Opposition, BJP At Loggerheads Over Amit Shah's Nehru Remark In Parliament," read the report's headline. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video featuring Union Home Minister Amit Shah dates back to 2023 and was speaking about Nehru during a Parliamentary discussion on the Jammu and Kashmir Reservation (Amendment) Bill and the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation (Amendment) Bill.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old, unrelated protest clip from Amritsar shared to falsely claim people protested against army, govt in Amritsar
content: New Delhi, May 15 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video featuring a crowd raising slogans was shared on social media, with the claim that it showed people protesting in Amritsar against the Indian Army and the Union government. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video was not recent but from April 2025. The protesters were villagers from Akhara village demonstrating against the state government over a biogas plant. It was a recent video, and the protest was not against the Indian Indian Army or the Central government. The video was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim: An X user named Iram Zahra shared a video of a crowd raising slogans on May 10, 2025. The user claimed that the crowd was protesting in Amritsar against the Indian army and the Union government. "Sikhs in Amritsar, India 🇮🇳 chanting against Modi Government and #IndianArmy. Modi Sarkar Murdabad | India Army Murdabad - Local Sikh people," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid verification tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was reverse-searched using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . As part of the investigation, the Desk extracted the keyframes of the viral video and ran them through reverse image search. It came across an Instagram post dated April 26, 2025. The video shared by the user matched the viral video. Though there were no details about the incident, it is clear that it is not recent. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk also came across another Instagram post dated April 26, 2025. The post carried a still resembling the viral video's visuals. According to the post, the villagers protested against a toxic biogas plant in Akhara near Jagraon in Ludhiana district. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking cue from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across a video by PTC News, from April 26, where the same demonstrations could be seen. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. We confirmed that the PTC News clips were from the same demonstration featured in the video shared by the X user. Below is a combination highlighting the similarities between the X post and the news report by PTC News. Additionally, the Desk conducted another set of customised keyword searches on Google to find relevant media reports; The Desk came across a report by Hindustan Times published on April 27, 2025. As per the report, the residents of Akhara village in Jagraon, who have been protesting for a long time against a biogas plant, clashed with police officers when the latter tried to remove them from the protest site, resulting in the detention of several of them. "The protesters, opposing the biogas factory, believe it would harm their environment, health, and farming land; to stop the factory, the villagers had set up a permanent protest camp in front of the site," read the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showed villagers from Akhara village protesting against the biogas plant, which was falsely linked to the protest against the government and the Indian Army.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old footage from a video game shared to support claim that Indian Air Defence downed Pakistani jet; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 12 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid ongoing tensions between India and Pakistan, a video showing a fighter jet being "intercepted by radar" was recently shared on social media with the claim that it depicted a Pakistani F-16 being shot down by the Indian defence system. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the viral video was falsely linked to the current India-Pakistan tensions. The footage has been available online since January 10, well before the recent developments between the two nations. Moreover, the video was from a video game and did not depict a real-world incident. Claim An X user, 'Ashok Danoda', shared a video on May 8, allegedly depicting a Pakistani F-16 fighter jet being shot down by the Indian air defence system. The user wrote: "Indian air defence system shot down Pakistan's F-16 fighter jet." When this story was published, the post had garnered 4.2 million views and 5,678 likes. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here . The reverse image search also led the Desk to a reel on a Facebook page named Fixture Gaming. The reel's visuals matched those in the viral video. However, upon further investigation, the Desk found that the video was originally posted on January 10—well before the recent rise in India-Pakistan tensions. Additionally, the Desk conducted a thorough analysis of the video, including cross-checking the footage. The findings clearly indicated that the video does not depict real footage but is instead a video game simulation. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image highlighting that the content seen in the viral video matches the video shared on the Facebook page. Next, as a part of the investigation, the Desk also conducted a customised keyword search on Google regarding any confirmed reports of Pakistani fighter jets being shot down by the Indian defence system. The search only yielded reports claiming by the Indian government that the Indian strikes had destroyed multiple Pakistani fighter jets, but no detailed statement on the development was released. Additionally, a keyword search for "Pakistani fighter jets intercepted by Indian air defence system" also led the Desk to a video where Pakistan's Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General, Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, was purportedly shown saying that India had shot down their two JF-17 Thunder fighter aircraft. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: To begin the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to verify whether Pakistan had officially acknowledged the loss of its two JF-17 Thunder aircraft. However, the search did not yield any credible or authentic reports confirming such a statement. Next, the Desk conducted a detailed video analysis that raised doubts about its authenticity. The Desk noticed several inconsistencies—for instance, the Pakistani official's lip movements did not align with the words being spoken, suggesting that the video may have been altered or AI-generated. Taking a cue, the Desk ran the video through Hive Moderation, an AI detection tool. The analysis revealed that the audio in the video had been generated using artificial intelligence. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video claiming to show a Pakistani F-16 fighter jet being shot down by India was false. It originated from a gaming simulation and was falsely presented as real footage. Furthermore, the video purportedly showing Pakistan acknowledging the downing of its two fighter jets was also found to be AI-generated.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2024 video of building destroyed by Israeli airstrike in Lebanon falsely shared as recent incident from Jodhpur; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 15 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a building reduced to rubble after being struck by an unidentified object was recently shared on social media with the claim that it depicted a recent incident occurred at AIIMS Jodhpur. However, upon investigation, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found the video unrelated to India. The footage actually shows an Israeli airstrike targeting Hezbollah-controlled areas in Beirut, Lebanon, in November 2024. An old, unrelated video was falsely circulated on social media to mislead viewers. Claim On May 10, an Instagram user, 'mukeshgurjar9417', shared a video showing a building turned to rubble after being hit by an unidentified object. The user claimed that the video depicted an incident that occurred at AIIMS Jodhpur. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation To corroborate the viral post's claim, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to verify whether such an incident occurred in Jodhpur. The search did not yield any credible reports confirming such an event. Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One keyframe was then analysed using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media posts that had shared the same video. However, the locations mentioned in these posts differed from the viral claim. While the viral post claimed the footage showed an incident in Jodhpur, two other posts claimed the incident occurred in Delhi and Hyderabad, respectively. The posts can be viewed here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively: The reverse image search also led the Desk to a video posted on the official YouTube channel of The Economic Times dated November 16, 2024. The video, shot from a different angle, matched the visuals of the viral post. Further details provided along with the video clarified that it showed an Israeli airstrike targeting a high-rise building in Beirut's southern suburb, causing widespread destruction. The video had no connection to any incident in India. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot: Below is a comparison image showing that the visuals in the viral video match the video posted by The Economic Times. The Google reverse search also led the Desk to a video shared by the US-based television broadcaster CBS News on its website. Like The Economic Times report, the CBS News video resembled the visuals from the viral clip. The accompanying details revealed that it depicted an Israeli military operation against Hezbollah, in which a building in the Lebanese capital, Beirut, was bombed. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video does not depict a building collapse incident in India.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video of Col Sofiya Qureshi shared with false claim that she spoke about her religion and terrorism; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 15 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Following the success of Operation Sindoor by the Indian Armed Forces during the recent India-Pakistan military conflict, Colonel Sofiya Qureshi and Wing Commander Vyomika Singh emerged as the leading faces of the Army's counteroffensive against terror camps across the border and the proud symbols of courage and competence in the country. Amid this, a purported video featuring Col Qureshi was circulated on social media, falsely claiming she spoke about her religion and terrorism. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video was manipulated using AI tools, with superimposed audio designed to mislead viewers into believing she made such statements. The video was fake and AI-generated, and it was shared with a false claim. Claim A purported video of Col Sofiya Qureshi allegedly saying that she is a Muslim but not a terrorist was shared by a Facebook user named 'Ripu Daman Kohli' on May 13, 2025. In the video, Col Qureshi can be heard saying: "I am a Muslim but not a Pakistani, I am a Muslim but not a terrorist. Terrorism has no religion." The post had 1.8 million views, 100k likes, and 5k followers when writing this article. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid verification tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was reverse-searched using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived version can be viewed here and here . To commence the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports to corroborate the details. However, the search did not yield any results that mentioned Sofiya Qureshi talking about being a Muslim. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk extracted the keyframes of the viral video and ran them through Reverse Image Search and came across the Press Briefing of Operation Sindoor on Sansad TV on May 7, 2025. We heard the entire press briefing, and nowhere in the video did the Colonel talk about her religion. Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri, Colonel Sofia Qureshi, and Wing Commander Vyomika Singh were also at the press briefing. Here is the link to the briefing, and below is a screenshot of the same. As part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the video and found several discrepancies. For instance, the lip movement was not synchronised with the voice. The unnatural and mechanical speaking styles and equally unnatural expressive movements indicated that the video might be AI-generated or manipulated. The Desk then ran the viral video through the Resemble.ai tool to analyse the video and its audio. The results indicated that it is fake and manipulated. Below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video featuring Colonel Sofiya Qureshi stating that she is a Muslim but not a terrorist and that terrorism has no religion is altered and a deepfake.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: This video of Amit Shah 'endorsing investment plan with huge return' is AI-generated and fake; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 15 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently shared on social media features Union Home Minister Amit Shah allegedly endorsing a new investment plan promising substantial monthly returns. In the video, he appears to claim that by investing Rs 21,500, one could earn monthly returns of Rs 3,50,000. Shah is also seen stating that the investment plan is not a scheme or advertisement, but his own 'personal' project. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video was manipulated using AI tools to mislead viewers into believing he made such statements. An AI-generated video was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim On May 14, a Facebook user named 'Mizpah Ministries Inc. New Jerusalem Chu' shared a purported video featuring Union Home Minister Amit Shah endorsing the new investment project. In the video, the Home Minister can be heard saying: "By investing Rs 21,500, you can earn Rs 3,50,000 per month. This is not a scheme but my personal project…If you are watching this video, it means that the project is open for you…" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation As part of the investigation, the Desk first conducted a customised keyword search to corroborate the details mentioned in the viral claim. However, the search did not yield any substantial and credible results. As part of the investigation, the Desk checked the link in the social media post. The link led the Desk to a dubious website, which suggests that the social media post might be fake or AI-generated. Below is a screenshot of the website. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk ran the video in the social media post through HiveModeration, an AI content detection tool. The results of which indicated that the video was AI-generated. Below is a screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Union Home Minister Amit Shah had not started any such investment project in his personal capacity, and the video shared was AI-generated.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated image falsely shared in name of wildfire in Israel; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 15 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): An image showing an urban area engulfed in massive flames and thick smoke, with fire spreading across multiple buildings and vehicles, was shared on social media. The user claimed that it depicted the recent wildfire in Israel. Moreover, wildfires broke out on the outskirts of Jerusalem on April 30, forcing evacuations of three communities and the closure of a main highway. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that a Facebook user who creates AI content circulated the same image, along with a similar video, during the Los Angeles fires in January this year. This made it clear that the photo did not depict the recent wildfires. Upon further investigation, the Desk found the image to be AI-generated using an AI detection tool and shared with a false claim on social media. Claim A photo showing a massive fire engulfing what appears to be an urban area was shared by an X user, 'Comrade Abiyos Roni,' on May 1. The user claims that the photo is from the recent wildfire in Israel. "This is not Gaza, this is Israel," read the post's caption, which garnered 2,868 views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the photo through Reverse Image Search and found several users shared the same post with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here . On running the viral photo through reverse image search, the desk found a video uploaded on Facebook by a user 'SoyLand.AI' on January 10, 2025. The hashtags mentioned 'aiart'. The Desk scanned through the 'about' section, which mentioned "Welcome To My AI World. Creating Viral Content with AI" - hinting that the video might be AI-generated. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Based on the above findings, the Desk ran the viral photo through Wasit AI, an AI-detection tool. The tool detected a substantial presence of AI-generated elements in the image. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the photo being shared on social media is AI-generated and was shared with a false claim on social media.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: This AI-generated image falsely showed Sara Tendulkar and Shubman Gill dressed in Army combat uniforms; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 16 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid the ongoing tensions between India and Pakistan, a purported image showing Indian cricketer Shubman Gill and daughter of former Indian cricketer Sachin Tendulkar, Sara Tendulkar—dressed in Army combat uniforms was recently shared on social media. The image was circulated with the claim that the duo had allegedly taken part in a strong offensive against Pakistan. However, a PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found that the image was AI-generated and falsely shared on social media to mislead viewers. Claim On May 8, a Facebook user named Rohit Lodhi shared a post featuring a purported image of Shubman Gill and Sara Tendulkar. The image showed them dressed in Army combat uniforms, standing with a military tank in the background. The post claimed the two had allegedly taken part in a strong offensive against Pakistan. At the time of publishing this story, the image had garnered 10k likes. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and came across multiple social media posts sharing the same photo with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. In the next step of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to check whether Sara Tendulkar and Shubman Gill had actually joined the Indian Army, as suggested by the image. However, the search yielded no credible news reports or social media posts from either individual that could confirm the claim. Next, the Desk then carefully analyzed the viral image depicting Shubman Gill and Sara Tendulkar in Army combat uniforms. The analysis revealed several inconsistencies, suggesting the image may be AI-generated or digitally altered. For instance, subtle distortions in the facial features of both individuals were noticeable. Additionally, the image had an overly glossy finish—a common characteristic of AI-generated visuals. Below is a screenshot highlighting these key findings: Next, taking cues from the above generated inputs, the Desk ran the viral image through 'Hive Moderation', an AI detection tool. The tool detected a substantial presence of AI-generated elements in the image. Below is the screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral image of Sara Tendulkar and Shubman Gill was AI-generated and falsely shared on social media to mislead viewers.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered video of Hollywood actor Sebastian Stan from movie promotional shoot shared to falsely link It to India's 'Operation Sindoor'
content: New Delhi, May 17 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported video of a man changing a display poster allegedly linked to the ongoing India-Pakistan tensions from a hoarding in a foreign country was recently shared on social media. The video showed the man walking past the hoarding, which purportedly depicted a scene from the Pahalgam terror attack, where terrorists were seen speaking to female eyewitnesses at the incident site and asking them to inform Prime Minister Narendra Modi about what had transpired. As the video progressed, the man paused and replaced the original poster with a new one bearing the message "I told Modi." This second poster was circulated to suggest a political or military statement made by India in the context of Operation Sindoor, a major counter-terrorism initiative. However, upon investigation, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found the video to be digitally altered. The original footage featured actor Sebastian Stan replacing a Thunderbolts movie poster with one that read The New Avengers. The video was manipulated and falsely shared on social media to link it with the ongoing India-Pakistan tensions. Claim Amid the ongoing India-Pakistan tension, an X user, Viक़as (@VlKAS_PR0NAM0), on May 13 shared a video of a man replacing a poster (both allegedly linked to the India-Pakistan tension) from a hoarding at an unknown location in a foreign country. While the first poster purportedly displayed a message showing a terrorist telling a woman, "Go tell Modi," the second one showed the woman asserting, "I told Modi." Both posters were circulated in an alleged reference linking them to India's launch of 'Operation Sindoor.' Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. When this story was published, the video had garnered 3.7 million views and 58k likes. Investigation The Desk used the InVid tool to extract multiple keyframes from the viral video. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk discovered several other users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The reverse image search also led the Desk to a video posted on the official X handle of Marvel Studios, the US-based television and film company. The handle had posted a video that matched the background settings from the viral clip. However, further details revealed that the video had been posted online on May 5 (predating the launch of Operation Sindoor on May 7). They indicated it was a promotional clip for the film Thunderbolts, which was released in US theatres on May 2. The original video showed the man replacing a Thunderbolts movie poster with one that read The New Avengers. Nowhere in the video was there any reference to the India-Pakistan tensions. Here is the link and archive link to the original post, along with a screenshot: Below is a comparison image highlighting that the viral video was digitally altered from the original version shared on social media: Additionally, the reverse image search led the Desk to a report published by the American news website Deadline Hollywood. In its May 5 article, Deadline Hollywood identified the man in the video as Hollywood actor Sebastian Stan. The report stated that Marvel Studios had tweeted a video of actor Sebastian Stan—who has long portrayed James "Bucky" Buchanan Barnes in the Marvel Cinematic Universe—replacing the Thunderbolts film poster with one for The New Avengers. "Stan, clad in black from head to toe like character Bucky often wears, and does so in his latest MCU film, can be spotted on a stroll with some rolled-up posters, and once he sees one at the bus stop, he stops to place a poster that reads The New Avengers over it," the report added. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing Hollywood actor Sebastian Stan putting up the "I told Modi" poster was digitally altered.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video from mock drill at Hyderabad Airport shared to falsely claim criminal was recently arrested there; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 19 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a man allegedly being detained by security personnel was recently shared on social media with the claim that it depicted a recent incident at the Rajiv Gandhi International Airport in Hyderabad, where security officials had reportedly apprehended a criminal. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found it false. The video actually shows a mock drill conducted by the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) at Hyderabad's Rajiv Gandhi International Airport as part of routine security preparedness. The video was falsely circulated on social media with a misleading claim. Claim An Instagram page named 'BNT NEWS TELANGANA' shared a video on May 10, claiming it showed scenes from Hyderabad International Airport where CISF personnel allegedly captured a criminal. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. At the time of publishing this story, the video garnered 67,618 likes. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of the keyframes was then analysed using Google Lens, which led the team to several social media users who had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively: Next, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to check whether any incident involving the arrest of a criminal had occurred at Hyderabad Airport. No official reports were found to corroborate the viral claim. However, the search led the Desk to an X (formerly Twitter) post by the Telangana State Cyber Security Bureau. In a post dated May 13, the Bureau clarified that a security mock drill had recently been conducted at Hyderabad Airport. However, the said footage from the drill (which was attached along the post) was falsely shared online with the claim that a terrorist had been arrested. Next, as the Desk investigated the footage, it found the visuals from the Bureau's video matched the viral video. This confirmed that the video shared on social media depicted a mock drill, not a real arrest. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image highlighting that the content in the viral video matched the footage shared by the Telangana State Cyber Security Bureau on its official X handle. The search also led the Desk to an official statement by Hyderabad Airport on its X handle on May 13. The statement confirmed that a mock drill was recently conducted at the airport. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video shared on social media initially showed a mock drill conducted at Hyderabad Airport and did not depict the arrest of a criminal.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video of senior Pakistani official shared after India's Operation Sindoor; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 19 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid India and Pakistan announcing a ceasefire following days of heavy military confrontation triggered by the Pahalgam terror attack, a video of a senior Pakistani official allegedly speaking about the destruction caused by the Indian strike began circulating on social media. The video purportedly showed Pakistan's Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General, Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, stating that India had shot down two of their JF-17 Thunder fighter aircraft. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found the video to be manipulated using AI tools, with superimposed audio designed to make it appear as though he had made the statement. Claim A Facebook page named 'IADN Centre' shared a video on May 8, allegedly showing ISPR Director General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry confirming that India had shot down two JF-17 Thunder fighter aircraft. When this story was published, the video had garnered 8.2k likes and 1.5k shares. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here . The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google to check for any official acknowledgement by Pakistan of the alleged downing of its two JF-17 Thunder aircraft. However, no credible or authentic reports confirmed such a statement. Continuing the investigation, the Desk next closely analysed the Pakistani official's video and observed several inconsistencies. Notably, the lip movements did not match the audio, suggesting that the footage had been altered or AI-generated. Based on these findings, the Desk ran the video through Hive Moderation, an AI detection tool. The analysis confirmed that the audio had been generated using artificial intelligence. Below is the screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a top Pakistani Army official confirming that the country had lost two of its fighter jets during its military confrontation with India was AI-generated.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2024 video of TMC's Kalyan Banerjee taking jibe at BJP shared to falsely claim he "mocked Rafale jets" during Operation Sindoor
content: New Delhi, May 20 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video featuring Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Kalyan Banerjee, apparently from Parliament, was recently shared on social media. The user claimed that the MP demonstrated an alleged failed attempt at using Rafale jets, linking it to Operation Sindoor launched by the Indian Armed Forces. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video actually shows Kalyan Banerjee mocking the Bharatiya Janata Party's poll slogan "Ab ki baar, 400 paar" in the Lok Sabha. The video dates back to 2024 and is unrelated to the recent border developments or Operation Sindoor. It was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim: An X user, Maria Zulfiqar Khan, shared a video showing TMC MP Kalyan Banerjee during a parliament session on May 12. The user claimed that the minister demonstrated an alleged failed attempt to use Rafale jets, linking it to Operation Sindoor launched by the Indian Forces. "Indian opposition leader "demonstrating" how the Rafales fell!!! Modi and Amit Shah's expressions are priceless! Dear Bollywood, please include this scene in your next propaganda movie!" read the post's caption, which clocked 355.3k views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation: The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid verification tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was reverse-searched using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived version can be viewed here and here . On analysing the video, the Desk noticed that the footage was from the Parliamentary proceedings, and at the moment, the Parliament session is not going on. Taking a cue from this, the Desk extracted the keyframes of the viral video and ran them through Reverse Image Search. It came across a YouTube short by NDTV Profit, dated July 2, 2024, which predates Operation Sindoor and clarifies that it is unrelated to the recent incident. The YouTube short featured the same video as the recent social media post. In the video, the opposition MP Kalyan Banerjee mocks the BJP's electoral performance in the 2024 General Election. The title of the video read: "TMC MP Kalyan Banerjee's Hilarious Swipe At NDA's '400 Paar Target'" Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image confirming the viral video's content matches the original footage shared on the Instagram handle. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search to find relevant media reports. We then came across a report by Hindustan Times published on July 2, 2024. As per the report, referring to the game, the MP from West Bengal's Srerampur constituency explained that the slogan '400' resonated loudly with 'chu' and ended with 'kit-kit'. "Viral video: TMC MP Kalyan Banerjee's 'chu-kit-kit' jibe at BJP's '400 paar' slogan," read the report's headline. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Meanwhile, Air Marshal Bharti, responding to international media reports about the Rafale fighter jet downed during Operation Sindoor, neither denied nor confirmed the claims. A report by Mint, dated May 11, 2025, stated that Air Marshal Bharti said that 'losses are a part of any combat scenario.' "Responding to a question about reports regarding Rafale jets, he said: I am happy you asked these questions. We are in a combat scenario, and losses are a part of it. The question is, have we achieved our objective? The answer is a thumping yes. As for details, I would not like to comment at this time as we are still in combat and giving advantage to adversaries. All our pilots are back home" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video featuring TMC's Kalyan Banerjee dates back to 2024, during the Parliament session, when he mocked the BJP's poll slogan 'ab ki baar 400 paar'.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: PM Modi's address to nation after India's Operation Sindoor shared out of context with false claim; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 20 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A short video clip of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's address to the nation, in which he detailed the success of India's military offensive under Operation Sindoor during the recent India-Pakistan conflict, was recently shared on social media. The user sharing the video falsely claimed that the Prime Minister "admitted Pakistan had shot down six Indian fighter jets and targeted the S-400 air defence system". However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that in the original speech, PM Modi said that instead of cooperating with India against terrorism, Pakistan chose to launch an attack. This move was met with a strong and decisive response. Upon further verification, the Desk concluded that the viral claim was false and fabricated. His statement was misrepresented and taken out of context. The video was shared on social media with a false claim to spread a misleading narrative. Claim: A video featuring Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressing the nation was shared by an X user named 'Kavita Yadav' on May 14, claiming that he admitted Pakistan shot down six Indian fighter jets and targeted the S-400 system. In the 00:13-second video, he says, "...started attacking India. Pakistan targeted our schools, colleges, Gurudwaras, temples, and the houses of the people…" "Modi himself admits that Pakistan attacked us, shot down 6 of our planes, attacked S400," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation: The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid verification tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was reverse-searched using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. One such post can be found here , and its archived version can be viewed here . The Desk extracted the keyframes and ran them through a reverse image search. It found the PM's Live address on the official YouTube channel 'Narendra Modi' on May 12, 2025. The attire in the Live address was similar to that shared on social media. Upon listening to the entire speech, we found that Modi did not make any such statement at any point during his speech. At 9 minutes 7 seconds, timestamp, he says, "Instead of cooperating with India against terrorism, Pakistan started attacking India. Pakistan targeted our schools, colleges, Gurudwaras, temples, and the houses of the people..But even in this, Pakistan was exposed. The world saw how Pakistan's drones and missiles scattered like straw in front of India…" Here is the link to the speech, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find relevant media reports and came across a report by The Economic Times dated May 13, 2025. The report mentioned that Pakistan launched a desperate assault targeting India's schools, colleges, temples, gurudwaras, and civilian homes. But India's air defence systems intercepted and destroyed every incoming missile and drone before they could cross the border. "PM Modi said, Pakistan targeted our schools, colleges, Gurudwara, temples, and residential areas. Pakistan targeted our sacred places. But in this, Pakistan itself was exposed. The world saw how Pakistan's drones and missiles scattered like stones in front of India. India's powerful air defence system destroyed them in the sky itself," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video featuring PM Modi admitting that Pakistan attacked India is false and fabricated. His statement was misinterpreted and taken out of context.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally morphed photo of Preity Zinta hugging IPL player Vaibhav Suryavanshi shared on social media with false claim; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 21 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A collage depicting two purported images of Bollywood actress and Punjab Kings co-owner Preity Zinta with 14-year-old Rajasthan Royals player Vaibhav Suryavanshi from an IPL cricket ground has recently been shared on social media. Users claimed that the collage showed the moment when Preity Zinta, after the Rajasthan Royals vs Punjab Kings match at the Sawai Mansingh Stadium in Jaipur, met the young Rajasthan Royals player and shared a warm hug. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that while the two did meet on May 19 after the scheduled match, the images allegedly showing them hugging were digitally morphed. In an official statement, Preity Zinta also clarified that the photos are fake. The morphed images were circulated on social media with a false claim intended to mislead viewers. Claim An X handle, 'Sports Today', shared on May 19 a collage depicting two purported images of Punjab Kings co-owner Preity Zinta along with 14-year-old Rajasthan Royals player Vaibhav Suryavanshi. The photos appeared to show the two sharing a warm hug after their meeting following the Rajasthan Royals vs Punjab Kings fixture in Jaipur on May 19. "Preity Zinta hugs Vaibhav Suryavanshi," the user captioned the photo collage. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk carefully cropped the two images from the collage shared on social media and then ran them separately through Google Lens. The reverse image search led the Desk to different social media handles that had shared the same collage with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customized keyword search on Google to verify whether Preity Zinta and Vaibhav Suryavanshi had actually met. The search led the Desk to a video published by Rajasthan Royals on its official Instagram account on May 19. The video showed PBKS co-owner Preity Zinta chatting with Vaibhav Suryavanshi post the Punjab Kings fixture against Rajasthan Royals at the Sawai Mansingh Stadium in Jaipur. However, the video did not show them sharing a hug as allegedly depicted in the social media post. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Additionally, the search about the alleged hug shared among the two after yesterday's IPL match led the Desk to an X post made by the Punjab Kings co-owner on her official handle. On May 20, reacting to a now-deleted news post shared by Republic Bharat—which featured the same images of the duo sharing a hug—Preity Zinta stated that the images were morphed. "This is a morphed image and fake news. Am so surprised now news channels are also using morphed images and featuring them as news items," she stated.
