Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the images claiming to show Preity Zinta and Vaibhav Suryavanshi sharing a warm hug after the May 19 IPL match were found to be morphed or AI-generated. Multiple AI tools are available on the internet that can manipulate normal photos to make it appear as if two people are kissing or hugging. Social media users should keep this in mind and avoid liking or sharing such images or videos unless they have been verified by authentic news sources.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old photo of padlocked grave in Hyderabad resurfaces with same false claim that it is from Pakistan; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 20 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported image showing a grave secured with an iron grill and padlock was once again shared on social media, accompanied by the claim that it was from Pakistan, where parents allegedly locked their daughter's grave to prevent post-burial sexual assault. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the same photo had been circulated on social media in 2023 with a similar false claim. Upon further investigation, it was revealed that the grave in question is not located in Pakistan, but in Hyderabad, India. The image was shared on social media with a misleading and false claim. The PTI Fact Check Desk had debunked the same claim, which was shared with the same photo two years back. Claim A purported photo of a grave locked with an iron grill was shared by a Facebook user named 'देश की बातें' on May 16, claiming that parents in Pakistan put up padlocks on the grave of their daughter to prevent rape. "Parents put up padlocks on daughter's grave to avoid rape in Pakistan," read the text on the picture. The post clocked 4.8k views, 1k comments, and 1k shares. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through reverse image search and found several other users shared the same picture with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived version can be viewed here and here . Notably, the same photo with a similar claim was also shared in 2023; one such post can be found here , along with its archived version, can be found here . Below is a screenshot of the same Upon further scanning the search results, the Desk found an X post dated April 30, 2023. The user shared that this grave is actually from Hyderabad, India. The post carried four pictures from the graveyard, one identical to the viral post. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting similarities between the viral photo (2025) and the X post (2023). Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on YouTube, and it came across a report published on May 1, 2023, by a local media outlet in Hyderabad, AS News Network. According to the report, the locked grave is located at the graveyard in the Madannapet Rein Bazar area in Hyderabad. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Based on the above findings, the Desk located the mosque on Google Maps and used Google Street View to get a front view of it. We found the same grave with the green metal grill right at the entrance in the viral image. Here is the link to the Google Street View, and below is a screenshot of the same. Moreover, AIMIM leader Waris Pathan also shared a video taken at the same grave on his X account on April 30, 2023, with a graveyard official explaining the reason behind the padlock on the metal grill. According to the official's comments, the padlock was put by family members of the dead to prevent others from further burying in the same grave. Here is the link to the X post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Upon further search, the Desk found a report by NDTV dated May 1, 2023, clarifying that the image is from the graveyard in the Madannapet area of Hyderabad. "Story On Pictures Of Padlock In Pakistan Incorrect, Grave From Hyderabad," read the report's headline. Here is the link to the report. The PTI Fact Check Desk had debunked the same claim two years back and had found in its investigation that the photo of the padlocked grave was located at a cemetery in front of Masjid E Salar Mulk in Darab Jung Colony in the Madannapet area of Hyderabad in India. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral photo of the locked grave shown is from a graveyard in the Madannapet area of Hyderabad in Telangana and was falsely shared in the name of Pakistan.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-Generated photo of YouTuber Jyoti Malhotra wearing 'BJP cap' shared with false claim; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 21 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): In the aftermath of the arrest of YouTuber Jyoti Malhotra for allegedly spying for Pakistan and leaking sensitive Indian military information, a photo began circulating on social media. The image showed her wearing a BJP cap and scarf, alongside what appeared to be a postcard from the leading Hindi news channel Aaj Tak. It was shared with the claim that the Haryana-based YouTuber, accused of espionage, is affiliated with the BJP. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the viral image and found it AI-generated and manipulated. The use of the Aaj Tak logo was also unauthorised and fake. The digitally morphed photo was shared on social media with a false claim. Jyoti is among 12 individuals who have been arrested from Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh over the past two weeks on charges of espionage, with investigators pointing to an alleged Pakistan-linked spy network operating in northern India. Claim A picture featuring YouTuber Jyoti Malhotra wearing a BJP cap and scarf was shared by a Facebook user named 'Kamlesh Singh' on May 18, claiming that the Haryana-based YouTuber accused of spying for Pakistan is affiliated with the BJP. The image was shared with an allegedly postcard from AajTak. A Haryana female YouTuber arrested on charges of treason, six people, including Jyoti Malhotra, were arrested. Jyoti Malhotra was accused of spying." Read the post's caption, which was initially in Hindi. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through Reverse Image Search and found that other users shared the same photo with an AajTak postcard and a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here . We scanned AajTak's official social media handles as part of the investigation. However, we found no matching image on any of the platforms. Here is the link to the X post by Aaj Tak on Malhotra's arrest. On analysing the photo carefully, the Desk found a discrepancy, like the extra glossy texture, hinting that it might be AI-generated. Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the photo through WasitAI, an AI-detection tool. The result indicated that the image was AI-generated. Below is a screenshot of the result. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk ran the photo through HiveModeration, another AI-detection tool. The results indicated that the image was AI-generated. Below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk also contacted the Head of India Today's Fact Check Desk regarding the social media post bearing the logo of Aaj Tak, who stated that it was fake. "It's fake," the Head responded to PTI. Meanwhile, according to a Press Trust of India (PTI) report published on May 20, Hisar-based Jyoti (33), who ran a YouTube channel titled 'Travel with JO', was arrested from the New Aggarsain Extension on May 16. "The National Investigation Agency, Intelligence Bureau and military intelligence officials are questioning Haryana YouTuber Jyoti Malhotra, who has been arrested on charges of spying for Pakistan, police said on Tuesday," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report. With all these findings and the response, the Desk concluded that the viral photo featuring YouTuber Jyoti Malhotra is AI-generated and was shared with a false claim on social media.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old, unrelated photo of Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant falsely shared as image of India's attack on Nur Khan Air Force base in Pakistan
content: New Delhi, May 21 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Following the launch of Operation Sindoor by the Indian Armed Forces during the recent India-Pakistan military conflict, an image showing a deserted control room began circulating on social media. The user sharing the image claimed it depicted the aftermath of India's strike on the Nur Khan Air Force Base located in Chaklala, Pakistan. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found the photo unrelated to the Nur Khan Air Force Base. Upon further verification, it was revealed that the image actually shows the control room of Reactor No. 4 at the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant (in present-day Ukraine), the site of a catastrophic explosion during a safety test on April 26, 1986. Additionally, a reverse image search showed that the photo has been available online since at least 2000. The viral post was shared on social media with a false claim intended to mislead viewers. Claim A purported photo of a destroyed control room was shared by an X user named 'Gopal Mishra Kaundilya' on May 18, claiming that it shows Pakistan's Nur Khan Airbase after India's attack. "Pakistan ke Noor Khan Airbus. Destroy Control room," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through Reverse Image Search and found several users shared the same photo with a similar claim on social media. One such post can be found here , and its archived version can be found here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk found a CNN report published on May 29, 2020, which carried the same photo as shared on social media—making it clear that the image was available on the internet even before India launched Operation Sindoor. According to the report, the photo was of an abandoned Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant in present-day Ukraine. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the social media post and the news report. Another report by the Telegraph, dated April 19, 2011, carried photos from the Chernobyl power plant. According to the report, the same picture was clicked on November 10, 2000, showing the damaged machinery in the Chernobyl nuclear power plant. "10 November 2000: The control room, with its damaged machinery, is seen inside reactor No. 4 in the Chernobyl nuclear power plant," read the photo's caption. Here is the link to the photo, and below is a screenshot of the same. Meanwhile, the Indian Air Force carried out precision strikes on nine terror-linked locations in Pakistan and Pakistan-Occupied Kashmir. According to a Times of India report published on May 20, the Indian Air Force hit radar installations, communication hubs, and air bases at 11 locations inside Pakistan. These included high-value targets like Nur Khan Airbase and Rahim Yar Khan Airbase. Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the old image from the Chernobyl nuclear plant is being falsely shared as Pakistan's Nur Khan Airbase after India's attack.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old Bangladesh video of man pleading to save his rickshaw shared as recent incident in Uttar Pradesh; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 21 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a man desperately pleading with authorities not to crush his rickshaw with a bulldozer was recently shared on social media, accompanied by the claim that it depicted an incident from Uttar Pradesh, India. However, upon investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video is not related to India but actually shows an incident from Bangladesh. As part of a drive to remove illegal battery-operated rickshaws from main roads, authorities in Dhaka seized several such rickshaws and destroyed a few on-site. The video was falsely circulated on social media with a misleading claim. Claim An X user '@tvkvijay_4tn' shared on May 18 a purported video in which a man is seen desperately pleading with authorities, allegedly from the Uttar Pradesh government, not to crush his battery-operated vehicle. The video shows him making emotional pleas to government officials, who do not relent and go ahead with crushing his battery-operated vehicle—allegedly as part of a rule banning battery-operated vehicles from main roads. "Officials in Uttar Pradesh smash battery cars, saying they are not allowed on main roads! What did you do with the BMW and AUDI car that caused the accident due to drunk driving, Mr. Modi?" the user posted with the video. When this story was published, the video had garnered 142k views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One keyframe was then run through Google Reverse Image Search, which led the Desk to several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The reverse image search also led the Desk to a video posted on the YouTube channel of the Bangladesh-based news portal Centrist Nation TV. On May 14, the portal posted the video featuring the same visuals (of a man crying as authorities crushed his rickshaw) seen in the viral post. The channel described the incident as having occurred in Bangladesh, not India. The description accompanying the video read: "In a dramatic crackdown, Dhaka authorities seized and crushed hundreds of illegal battery-powered rickshaws operating on the city's main road. Heartbreaking scenes unfolded as rickshaw pullers pleaded to save their only source of income." Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a comparison image showing that the visuals in the viral video match those in the video posted by the Bangladesh-based news channel. In the next part of the investigation, using cues from the information above, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google. It came across another news report from the Bangladesh-based portal The Business Standard. In its May 14 report, the portal elaborated on a key development following the incident. Of the three rickshaw pullers whose rickshaws were crushed during the crackdown, each received Tk 50,000 in financial assistance from the Dhaka authorities, the report stated. The report also featured an image of the same individual in the viral video pleading with officials. He was among the beneficiaries awarded compensation. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image confirming that the person seen in the viral video is the same individual captured in the news report as a beneficiary. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video shows authorities seizing and crushing illegal battery-run rickshaws in Bangladesh and not India.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Tiranga Yatra video from Surat after India's Operation Sindoor falsely shared in name of pro-India rally in Balochistan; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 22 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently shared on social media shows a large public procession with a music band playing 'Saare Jahan Se Achcha Hindustan Humara' and numerous Indian national flags waving in the air. The video is claimed to depict Baloch citizens in Pakistan's Balochistan region expressing solidarity with India by hoisting the Indian flag during a pro-liberation march. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found that the video was not from Balochistan. It was from Surat, Gujarat, where on May 14, 2025, a Tiranga Yatra was organised to celebrate the success of Operation Sindoor against Pakistan. The event featured a performance by the Saifee Scout Band of the Dawoodi Bohra community and had no connection to Balochistan or any pro-India rally there. Claim An X user, Praveen Kumar G.L., shared a video on May 20 depicting a large procession with a music band playing the 'Saare Jahan Se Achcha Hindustan Humara' song and featuring the Indian tricolour waving in the air. The user claimed that the video supported India at a pro-liberation march in Balochistan. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid verification tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was reverse-searched using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. One such post can be found here , and its archived version can be viewed here . Further, after carefully analysing the video, the desk found 'Saifee Scout Surat' branded on the band's instruments and a banner of 'Operation Sindoor' 'Tiranga Yatra' written. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Additionally, as part of the investigation, the desk ran the keyframes of the social media post through reverse image search. It came across an Instagram post from an account 'saifeescoutsurat' dated May 19, 2025. According to the post, a Tiranga Yatra was carried out in Surat, and the Surat Dawoodi Bohra Band made it even better with their music. "The Tiranga Yatra in Surat was exciting, and the Surat Dawoodi Bohra Band made it even better with their music. Their songs matched the proud feeling of the day. It was great to see and hear," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across a report by The Indian Express published on May 15, 2025. As per the report, a highlight of the event was the music bands of Saifee Scout Surat, which belongs to the Dawoodi Bohra community and is seen leading the yatra from Bhagal crossroads. "With Operation Sindoor, the Indian Army had sent out a message to the world: Whoever dares to harm an Indian will get a befitting reply, Union Jal Shakti Minister C R Paatil said as he led the Tiranga Yatra in Surat," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk also geo-located the spot seen in the social media clip in Gujarat's Surat. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the social media post and the Google Street View. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video in the social media post is from Surat, Gujarat, which depicts a Tiranga Yatra organised following the success of 'Operation Sindoor' against Pakistan. It has no connection to Balochistan in Pakistan.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Scripted child-lifting video shared as real on social media; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 22 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media claims to depict a real-life child-lifting incident, in which two men allegedly abduct a child outside his house. The footage shows the men luring the child with eatables before taking him away. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it was staged and scripted. The clip has no connection to real-life incidents and was misleadingly shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An Instagram page named bajrang_dal_official shared a video on May 20, allegedly capturing a real-life child-lifting incident. The footage showed two men kidnapping a child in front of his house after luring him with some food. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of the keyframes was then analysed using Google Lens, which led the team to several social media users who had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively: The Google Reverse Image Search also led the Desk to a video posted on a YouTube channel named 3RD EYE, which had over 2.96 million subscribers at the time of this story's publication. The channel had, on November 12, shared the same video (showing a child being lifted by two kidnappers in front of his house), as seen in the viral social media posts. However, upon thoroughly reading the disclaimer included with the video, the Desk found that it was scripted and not based on a real-life incident. The disclaimer clearly stated that all videos posted on the 3RD EYE YouTube channel feature scripted dramas and parodies. "Thank you for watching! Please be aware that this channel features scripted dramas and parodies of real people in different situations. This channel brings social awareness videos. These short films are for entertainment and educational purposes only!" the disclaimer reads. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting that the content in the viral video matches that of the video posted by the YouTube channel. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the social media video showing a child-lifting incident was scripted and bore no connection to any real-life event.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2023 video of Pakistan's former minister Fawad Chaudhry evading arrest falsely shared as recent clip with false claim
content: New Delhi, May 22 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): In the aftermath of the rumours that India had hit Pakistan's Nuclear facility located in Kirana Hills, a video featuring Pakistan's former Information Minister Fawad Chaudhry, exhausted and gasping for air, was shared on social media. The user sharing the video claimed that the minister had been admitted after suffering from radiation exposure. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video dates back to May 2023, not May 2025, during India's Operation Sindoor. The video showed him evading re-arrest by dashing into the building of a high court in Islamabad. An old and unrelated video was shared on social media with a false claim intended to mislead viewers. Meanwhile, India has firmly denied reports that it targeted Pakistan's sensitive Kirana Hills nuclear site during its recent air strikes, effectively countering growing social media claims of a radioactive leak and a potential atomic mishap. Claim A video allegedly featuring Pakistan's former Information Minister Fawad Chaudhury was shared by an X user named 'Abhi Athavale' on May 14, claiming that he had been admitted to the hospital after being exposed to nuclear radiation. "Former Information Minister Fawad Chaudhury was admitted to the hospital after being exposed to nuclear radiation! More catastrophes coming? Wait for 2/3 weeks, Pakistan will understand that they celebrated too early!" read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid verification tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was reverse-searched using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . Further, as part of the investigation, the Desk ran the keyframes through Reverse Image Search, which led us to a report by the Hindustan Times published on May 16, 2023. The report's cover image was identical to one of the clips of the social media post. According to the report, Fawad Chaudhry was seen running moments after the court ordered his release in connection with a case in which he was arrested for inciting violence. "Videos that went viral on social media showed Chaudhry running out of his vehicle towards the entrance of the court building. He was also seen hunching over and panting when a lawyer came for his help," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the clip from social media that matches the report's cover image. Taking a cue from the above finding, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on YouTube to find relevant media reports and came across a video report by First Post, published on May 17, 2023. In the video, Fawad Chaudhry could be seen trying to run away from cops to evade re-arrest by dashing into the building of a high court in Islamabad. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the court proceedings occurred in May 2023, not during the May 2025 Operation Sindoor. An old video with a false claim was shared on social media.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video from Myanmar falsely shared as Indian Army's arms seizure in Manipur; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 22 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): As the Indian Army achieved a major breakthrough in a joint counter-insurgency operation in Manipur leading to the seizure of 28 weapons, grenades, ammunition, and other war-like stores from armed cadres, a video showing a large cache of arms, ammunition, and cash spread on the ground was recently circulated on social media. Those sharing the clip claimed that the arms and ammunition were seized from militants by the Indian Army in Manipur. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found that the viral video is unrelated to the Indian Army's operation. The video actually shows a weapons seizure that occurred after the fall of Falam, a town in Chin State, Myanmar, which came under the control of the anti-junta Chin Brotherhood alliance on April 7. An old, unrelated video was falsely shared on social media to mislead viewers. Claim An X user, Jitendra Pratap Singh (@jpsin1), shared a video on May 17 showing a large cache of arms, ammunition, and cash, claiming the Indian Army had seized it from militants in Manipur. "Indian Army has recovered a huge cache of arms and cash from militants in Manipur," the user posted along with the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. When this story was published, the video had garnered 69,000 views and 4,000 likes. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , along with their archived versions available here and here , respectively: The reverse image search also led the Desk to a video posted on a Myanmar News Agency Facebook page. The page had posted the same video as what seen in the viral post on April 10. However, the accompanying details did not match those of the viral claim. The caption on the Facebook video stated that the footage depicted a stockpile of rare weapons obtained from the Battle of Falam. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image which confirms that the viral video and the Facebook post were identical. Since this evidence did not conclusively confirm the video's origin, the Desk next conducted a customised Google keyword search using "Battle for Falam" and its significance. This search led to a report by Myanmar-based news agency Myanmar Now, which provided more context. The report explained that the Chin Brotherhood Alliance—a coalition of armed insurgent groups active in Chin State of Myanmar—fought to take full control of the strategically important administrative town of Falam from the Myanmar military junta. The anti-junta alliance succeeded in its mission, seizing the junta's last remaining hilltop base on the night of April 7 after five months of conflict. "The alliance launched an offensive campaign on November 9 of last year to capture Falam and has taken over key locations in the township, such as a district-level police station, a township-level General Administration Office, and various junta outposts in the months since," the report added. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot. As it became clear that the Battle for Falam was linked to a military conflict in Myanmar, the Desk conducted another Google search using the keywords "large cache of arms and ammunition seized after the battle for Falam." This led to a video posted on April 10 by the official page of the Myanmar-based news portal Khit Thit Media. The footage—identical to the one seen in the viral posts—was captioned with details stating that after the final assault and the capture of the entire Falam township in Chin State, the Chin Nyinaung group had seized hundreds of thousands of weapons and ammunition from the Military Council. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video is unrelated to India and instead depicts events from Myanmar.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: February 2025 protest against canal construction falsely shared as recent demand for 'Sindhudesh' independence in Pakistan
content: New Delhi, May 23 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a public protest has gone viral on social media, with users claiming it depicts people in Pakistan demanding independence for "Sindhudesh." However, a fact-check by the Press Trust of India (PTI) reveals that the video is actually from a protest held in February 2025 in Sindh against the construction of six new canals on the Indus River. The claim linking the footage to a separatist movement is false and misleading. Claim A video depicting a protest was recently shared by a Facebook user, 'Media Prime,' on May 17. The user claimed that the people are now demanding "Sindhudesh's independence" in Pakistan. "After Baluchistan, the demand for the separation of Sindhudesh has arisen in Pakistan. Pakistan is bound to be divided into four parts," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid verification tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was reverse-searched using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. One such post can be found here , and its archived version can be viewed here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a Facebook post dated February 23, 2025, featuring the same video as seen in the social media post. Though no information was available along with the post, it is clear that the video is months old and not recent. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk ran the keyframes through reverse image search and found an X post dated February 23, 2025. The video in the X post resembled the visuals of the social media post. As per the X post, the protest was staged against constructing canals on the Indus River. "Pakistan is losing its identity! Stop constructing canals from the Indus and let the river flow freely. This is not just JSQM-A's demand, but also the demand of the entire Sindhi nation! #NoMoreCanalsOnIndus," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk also noticed a banner in the social media post that read 'Release Advocate Aamir Umrani'. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports and came across a report by The Tribune dated February 24, 2025. According to the report, the nationalist parties of Sindh organised protests against building six new canals on the Indus River. Meanwhile, Jeay Sindh Mahaz also blocked the National Highway in Shaheed Benazirabad district, demanding the safe recovery of the lawyer Aamir Ali Umrani, who has allegedly been subjected to enforced disappearance. "With vocal expressions of disapproval being reiterated time and again against building six new canals on the Indus River, the nationalist parties of Sindh organised protests and blocked highways in different parts of the province," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video in the social media post showing a protest is from February 2025 against the construction of six new canals on the Indus River in Sindh. It does not show any protest demanding Sindhudesh's independence.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally manipulated images of Rahul Gandhi falsely claim he was with arrested YouTuber Jyoti Malhotra; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 25 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Days after Haryana-based YouTuber Jyoti Malhotra was arrested for allegedly spying for Pakistan, two purported photos of her standing alongside the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha and senior Congress leader Rahul Gandhi were shared online. One image allegedly showed Malhotra in a blue saree standing next to Gandhi, while the other showed the two smiling at a rally. The Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated both images and found that neither featured Jyoti Malhotra with the Congress leader. The first image, originally from May 2018, showed Rahul Gandhi with then-Congress leader Aditi Singh. The second image showed him with a female supporter during the Bharat Jodo Yatra in Kerala in September 2022. In both cases, the women's faces were digitally replaced by Jyoti Malhotra using AI tools. The manipulated images were falsely circulated on social media to mislead viewers by linking the arrested YouTuber to the Congress party. Claim An X user, Vinod Kumar (@purneawala), shared two purported photos on May 22, allegedly showing Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi with Haryana-based YouTuber Jyoti Malhotra. Hisar Police arrested Malhotra on May 17 on charges of espionage. The first image shows Malhotra in a blue saree standing beside Rahul Gandhi; the second shows them smiling at what appears to be a rally. The user captioned the images, "Rahul Gandhi with Jyoti Malhotra. The picture says many things about the restlessness of Rahul Gandhi and Congress on Operation Sindoor. " Here is the link , archive link, and a post screenshot. Investigation The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found multiple social media posts sharing the same manipulated images of Rahul Gandhi with Jyoti Malhotra. Two such posts can be found here and here , along with their archived versions available here and here respectively: The Desk began its investigation with the first image, where Malhotra was allegedly seen wearing a blue saree beside Rahul Gandhi. A reverse image search on Google led to a May 7, 2018, India Today report featuring a visually similar image. Upon closer inspection, the Desk confirmed that the original image showed Rahul Gandhi with then-Congress leader Aditi Singh, not Jyoti Malhotra. Aditi Singh's face had been digitally swapped with Malhotra's to mislead viewers. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. A comparison image further confirmed the digital replacement of Aditi Singh's face with that of Malhotra. The Desk also used Google Lens to investigate the second image. The search led to a Facebook post by Rahul Gandhi dated September 18, 2022. The post included an image visually similar to the one shared in the viral post. Upon close examination, the woman in the original image was identified as a female supporter standing beside Rahul Gandhi during the Bharat Jodo Yatra in Kerala. Again, the woman's face had been digitally swapped with Jyoti Malhotra's using AI tools. Here is the link to the Facebook post, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image confirming the digital manipulation. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that neither of the images shared on social media featured Jyoti Malhotra with Rahul Gandhi. The original photos showed Gandhi with other individuals—Aditi Singh and a woman supporter—whose faces were digitally altered using AI tools to link Malhotra with the Congress party falsely.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old image of journalist Sheela Bhatt interviewing Dawood Ibrahim falsely shared as Supriya Shrinate; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 25 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): An image purportedly showing wanted terrorist Dawood Ibrahim seated beside a woman was recently shared on social media with the claim that the woman was Supriya Shrinate, Chairperson of Social Media and Digital Platforms for the Indian National Congress. The post further alleged that the image was from 1987, when Supriya Shrinate supposedly worked as a journalist. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the image does not feature Supriya Shrinate but rather journalist Sheela Bhatt. In 2023, Bhatt herself released the photo, stating it was from her interview with Dawood Ibrahim in 1987. The image was falsely shared on social media to mislead viewers. Claim An Instagram user '@mohapal_pal' shared, on May 16, a photo allegedly showing Supriya Shrinate, Chairperson of Social Media and Digital Platforms for the Indian National Congress, with wanted terrorist Dawood Ibrahim. The user claimed that the image was taken in 1987, when Congress leader Shrinate was working as a journalist. The caption read: "Pay attention and think. A woman journalist is sitting with Dawood Ibrahim. This photo is from 1987, and the woman journalist sitting there is today's Congress spokesperson Supriya Shrinate. Now do you understand how Congress is?" Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across social media handles that had shared the same photo with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively: In the next step of the investigation, the Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens. The search led the Desk to a post made by journalist Sheela Bhatt on X (formerly Twitter) on June 14, 2023. Bhatt shared the same image (seen in the social media post) and confirmed it was from her interview with Dawood Ibrahim at Pearl Building in Dubai in 1987. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image showing that the viral photo matches the one shared by Sheela Bhatt. Additionally, as the Desk continued its search, it found Bhatt's response to questions about the image's authenticity (one shared above) in the second part of her social media post. She posted the image shared above as genuine and featured her and Dawood Ibrahim only. "Flooded with queries about whether this is a fake pic or real. To put the record straight, I will post two cover pages: 1) Abhiyaan, the weekly by my late husband Kanti Bhatt and me, and 2) The Illustrated Weekly. Both carried out my interview with Dawood Ibrahim in 1987. Distinguished journalist Amrita Shah wrote the weekly's cover story. My interview ran alongside her cover story. I took all Dawood pics," Bhatt stated. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. The reverse image search also led the Desk to a report published by NDTV on July 13, 2023. The article confirmed that Sheela Bhatt had interviewed Dawood Ibrahim multiple times and featured the same image. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the image circulating on social media does not feature Congress leader Supriya Shrinate. It actually shows veteran journalist Sheela Bhatt interviewing wanted terrorist Dawood Ibrahim in Dubai in 1987.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Fact Check: 2024 photo misidentifies gamer Payal Dhare with PM Modi as arrested YouTuber Jyoti Malhotra
content: New Delhi, May 26 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a photo of a group of young individuals, claiming that the woman in the picture is YouTuber Jyoti Malhotra, who was recently arrested for allegedly spying for Pakistan, seen alongside Prime Minister Narendra Modi. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the woman in the photo is not Jyoti Malhotra, but Payal Dhare, a well-known Indian gamer. The image was taken during a meeting in April 2024 when Prime Minister Modi interacted with some of India's top gamers. Claim: An X user named Kanan Som shared a photo featuring PM Modi with a group of young people on May 19, claiming that the woman in the group was YouTuber Jyoti Malhotra. "Spy Jyoti Malhotra is an old player. Despite having such relations, she was framed on charges of spying, there is something fishy, something fishy," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link , and below is a screenshot. Investigation: The Desk ran the image in the social media post through reverse image search and found that other users had shared the same image with a similar claim on social media. One such post can be found here , and its archived version can be viewed here . Upon further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a video featuring similar visuals as seen in the social media post, on the official YouTube channel of PM Modi on April 13, 2024. According to the description of the video, PM Modi interacted with some of India's leading gamers—Tirth Mehta, Payal Dhare, Animesh Agarwal, Anshu Bisht, Naman Mathur, Mithilesh Patankar, and Ganesh Gangadhar—where he played PC and VR games with them. Nowhere in the description was it mentioned that the woman was Jyoti Malhotra. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. The description also mentioned the link to Payal Dhare's YouTube channel. Desk scanned her YouTube and came across the same video uploaded on April 13, 2024. The video featured similar visuals of her meeting PM Modi. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports. It came across a report by the Times of India on April 11, 2024. The article's cover image matched the picture in the social media post. According to the article, a select few Indian gamers got a chance to meet and interact with Prime Minister Narendra Modi. "These gamers include Animesh Agarwal, Mithilesh Patankar, Payal Dhare, Naman Mathur, and Anshu Bisht," the report read. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the social media post and the news report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the picture in the social media post does not feature Jyoti Malhotra. She is Payal Dhare. The photo was taken during a meeting in April 2024 when Prime Minister Modi interacted with India's top gamers.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of SP worker's self-immolation protest falsely shared as recent, linked to fake claim about PM Modi effigy burning
content: New Delhi, May 26 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video featuring a man on fire was recently shared by multiple social media users, along with the claim that he accidentally set himself ablaze while attempting to burn an effigy of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the man in the video was a Samajwadi Party (SP) worker who allegedly attempted self-immolation outside the BJP office in Kanpur in 2022. The incident occurred following the SP's defeat in the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, not while burning an effigy of PM Modi. The video was falsely shared on social media with a misleading claim. Claim A Facebook user, 'Kamlesh Pandey', on May 19, shared a video featuring a man claiming that he set himself on fire while trying to burn PM Modi's effigy. "In Kanpur, UP, the effigy of the red-capped SP brother would have been burnt by himself, he had gone to burn Modi ji's effigy. If I went to see something bad, I did not find anyone bad. When I searched my heart, I found no one worse than me. Today I am saved, now do not worry, my brother. If life is good, I will have another party. Jai Shri Ram, Jai Jai Shri Ram," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid verification tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was reverse-searched using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. As part of the investigation, the Desk ran the keyframes of the social media post through reverse image search and came across a report by India Today published on March 10, 2022. According to the report, the man in the social media post was a Samajwadi Party (SP) worker who allegedly attempted self-immolation outside the BJP party office in Kanpur, following the news of the party's defeat in the UP Assembly election. Though from a different angle, the report's cover image matched the visuals seen in the recent post. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Another report by The Indian Express made it clear that the SP worker set himself on fire on purpose and not while trying to burn an effigy of PM Modi. The report dated March 12, 2022, mentioned that A leader from Kanpur immolated himself in a bid to end his life outside the Vidhan Bhawan in Lucknow, police said. "The police added that Narendra Singh alias 'Pintu', who suffered 30% burns, is undergoing treatment at a civil hospital, and doctors said he was out of danger," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report. The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports. It came across a report by ETV Bharat in which Narendra alias Pintu Thakur said that the reason for their defeat was the BJP's tampering with EVMs. "At the same time, while talking to ETV Bharat, Narendra, crying, said that the BJP has tampered with the EVM, which is why Akhilesh Bhaiya is losing. Pawan Shrivastav, Advocate, Kanpur official, who was present in the hospital with the victim, said that the BJP government has committed fraud," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. ​ Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the man in the social post belongs to the Samajwadi Party (SP). He tried to set himself on fire after SP lost the 2022 UP Assembly elections, but not while trying to burn an effigy of PM Modi.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered video of FM Nirmala Sitharaman shared to falsely claim she 'announced investment scheme for stable daily income'
content: New Delhi, May 26 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported video featuring Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that she had announced an investment scheme guaranteeing a stable daily income. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found it fabricated and false. The minister did not announce any such investment scheme, and the video was digitally altered to promote a fraudulent offer. Claim A Facebook user shared a purported video of Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on May 13, claiming she announced an investment project that provides a stable daily income. In the two-minute, 13-second video, she says: "The people of India need support now, more than ever, and the government can no longer remain on the sidelines. I, Nirmala Sitharaman, Finance Minister, address every citizen of your great nation. That is why we are introducing a program that provides a stable daily income from day 1. Rs 65,000 a day is enough to cover all your expenses and improve your quality of life…" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to commence the investigation. However, the search yielded no relevant results or media reports citing the claim made in the social media post. Next, we also scanned the official handles and websites about Nirmala Sitharaman, but the search did not result in any substantial results. Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk ran the video through the InVid tool search to extract multiple keyframes of the video. One of these keyframes was reverse-searched using Google Lens, which led the Desk to a video uploaded on the official YouTube channel of the Finance Minister. The video was uploaded on April 8, 2025, and featured Sitharaman in the same attire, and the background also looked identical to the social media post. The title of the video read: "Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman's address during a chat on India becoming a developed economy by 2047." The Desk skimmed through the address but did not spot Sitharaman mentioning any such investment scheme. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the social media report and the YouTube video. Next, as part of the investigation, on clicking the link mentioned in the post, we were directed to the website of a South Africa-based jewellery store, 'Silvery', and not any investment platform. Hinting that the video may be fake and manipulated. Here is the link to the website. The desk carefully analysed the viral video and found inconsistencies. For example, the Finance Minister's lip movements were distorted and not synchronised with the speech. Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the viral video through HiveModeration, an AI content detection tool. The results indicated that the video was AI-generated. The Desk, the video through the AI audio detection tool Resemble.ai, termed the voice heard in the alleged clip of the Union Minister as "fake." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Union Minister Nirmala Sitharaman's video has been digitally altered as she has not announced any investment project.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video shared to falsely claim discovery of 5,000-year-old underwater Vishnu temple near Bali; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 26 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it showed visuals of a 5,000-year-old Vishnu temple discovered underwater near Bali, Indonesia. The footage depicted scuba divers exploring what appeared to be ancient temple ruins. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video was AI-generated and was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An X user, Sajjan Singh Chauhan (@DspSajjan), shared a video on May 20 showing a group of scuba divers exploring the ruins of a 5,000-year-old Vishnu temple that was recently found underwater near Bali, Indonesia. "Vishnu Temple is found underwater near Bali, Indonesia. It is said to be 5,000 years old. Locals call this new scuba diving spot at 'Pemuteran Beach' the 'Underwater Temple Garden, Bali'. Many sculptures were found under the sea water there," the user wrote. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk carefully scanned the video and found a watermark that said '@mbaiarts' at the bottom. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to determine what exactly '@mbaiarts' stands for. The search results led the Desk to an Instagram account bearing the same name as the watermark. Here is the link to the handle. Next, the Desk carefully scanned the videos posted on the handle. It found the footage, identical to the viral one, posted on the handle dated April 9, 2025, with details stating that all the visuals depicted in the video are AI-generated and do not hold any significance to a real expedition incident. "All visuals are AI-generated and created solely for artistic and educational wonder. With full respect to all faiths, this is a humble tribute to our shared spiritual heritage," the disclaimer mentioned alongside the video reads. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image confirming that the content seen in the viral video matches the video posted on the Instagram handle. Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk ran the social media video through Hive Moderation, an AI detection tool. The search result indicated that 99.9% of the footage contained deepfake or AI-generated content. Below is a screenshot highlighting the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the social media video was generated using AI and does not show real visuals of a Vishnu temple found underwater near Bali, Indonesia.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Reports claiming singer Sonu Nigam criticised BJP MP Tejasvi Surya over Kannada language row is false; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 27 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Several prominent media outlets recently cited an X post, allegedly made by singer Sonu Nigam, in which he purportedly criticised BJP MP Tejasvi Surya and commented that Kannada films should not be dubbed in Hindi or released nationwide. However, a fact check by the Press Trust of India (PTI) revealed that the post, though it appeared to bear Sonu Nigam's name, actually belonged to a Bihar-based lawyer, not the Bollywood singer. Upon further investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk reviewed Sonu Nigam's official Instagram account, where he clarified that he is not active on X (formerly Twitter) and had left the platform in 2017. The media outlets, therefore, reported incorrect information based on a misleading post. Claim Media outlets such as Financial Express, Indian Express, and The Economic Times, citing an alleged X post by Singer Sonu Nigam, claimed that he took a jab at BJP MP Tejasvi Surya and wrote that Kannada films should not be dubbed in Hindi and released across the country. Here is the link to the reports by Financial Express , Indian Express , and The Economic Times . In the X post, the singer allegedly called out Tejasvi Surya and his remarks on using Kannada in public sector banks by objecting to the nationwide releases of Kannada films and dubbing them in Hindi. "Don't dub Kannada movies in Hindi!. Don't release Kannada movies pan-India! Do you have the guts to say this to Kannada film stars, Mr.@Tejasvi_Surya, or you are just another language warrior?" read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation To commence the investigation, the Desk first skimmed through the X account of BJP MP Tejasvi Surya. It came across a post dated May 21, wherein he shared a video of a public sector bank employee arguing with a local customer over speaking in Kannada. Surya said that the employee's behaviour was 'not acceptable' and demanded that they know the local language to 'deal with local customers.' Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the X post bearing the name of Singer Sonu Nigam and found the user name as 'SonuNigamSingh'. Further, the bio section of the X account mentioned details that hinted it did not belong to Singer Sonu Nigam. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Additionally, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search as part of the investigation. It came across a report by NDTV dated May 24, 2017, which stated that Abhijeet Bhattacharya's colleague Sonu Nigam has announced that he's quitting Twitter because it's 'one-sided' and 'everyone is angry'. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. We then checked the singer's official Instagram account and found a post dated May 22 in which he called out media outlets, particularly The Times of India, for spreading misinformation. The singer wrote: "How many times have I declared I am not on Twitter? Spreading misinformation in my name is only going to poison the minds of people who have loved me so much all these years…" Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that media reports claiming singer Sonu Nigam slammed Tejasvi Surya over the Kannada language row are false.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of Syria combat operation falsely shared in name of 'Indian Army action in Kashmir'; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 27 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing two men running across hilly terrain was recently shared on social media with the claim that they were terrorists fleeing from Kashmir during an anti-terror operation launched by the Indian Army. The clip showed the duo sprinting through forest cover as bullets were fired at them by security forces. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found the video unrelated to India. It actually depicts a combat operation in Syria. The footage, dated March 2025, reportedly shows clashes between Syrian security forces and supporters of former President Bashar al-Assad. An old, unrelated video was falsely shared on social media to mislead viewers. Claim An X user, Ramesh Tiwari (@rameshofficial0), shared a video on May 15 claiming it depicted an Indian Army operation in Kashmir. The footage allegedly showed two terrorists running through forest cover in Kashmir amid heavy gunfire by the Army. When this story was published, the video had garnered 123k views and 1.3k likes. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple social media users who had shared the same video with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. The Google reverse image search also led the Desk to a video posted by the official X handle of a Türkiye-based news portal, TRHaber (@trhaber_com). On March 9, 2025, the handle posted the same video (showing two men running through forest cover), as seen in the viral social media posts. However, upon thoroughly reading the details of the video, the Desk found that the video was related to a combat operation in Syria, not India. "The video showed a clash between Syrian security forces and pro-government fighters in the Qardaha area of Latakia," a rough English translation of the post reads. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting that the content in the viral video matches that of the video posted by the Türkiye-based media portal. As the next step in the investigation, taking cues from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by CNN's Arabic channel. The report confirmed clashes between Syrian security forces and supporters of former President Bashar al-Assad around the same time the viral video was posted. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: While the Desk could not independently verify the exact origin of the video, the above findings made it clear that the viral footage is not linked to any anti-terror operation in Kashmir, as the post claimed.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered photo of Col. Sofiya Qureshi with cricketer Vaibhav Suryavanshi falsely shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 28 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Following an impressive innings by 14-year-old cricketer Vaibhav Suryavanshi in the Indian Premier League 2025, a photo showing the cricketer posing alongside Colonel Sofiya Qureshi was circulated on social media, claiming both of them posed together for a picture. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the image was digitally altered. The original photo featured Suryavanshi with former cricketer Wasim Jaffer, which the young player shared on his Instagram account in March 2024. The social media post was shared with a digitally edited photo and a false claim. Claim A photo featuring cricketer Vaibhav Suryavanshi posing alongside Col Sofiya Qureshi was shared by a Facebook user named 'MR Movie Review' on May 23, 2025. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through Reverse Image Search and found several other users shared a similar photo with the same claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here , along with their archived versions, which can be found here and here , respectively. After isolating Suryavanshi's face on the viral image, we performed a simple reverse image search that led us to his Instagram account post dated March 24, 2024. The post featured a similar photo with the same background, but it showed him with former Indian cricketer Wasim Jaffer, not Colonel Sofiya Qureshi. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the recent social media post and the 2024 Instagram post. Taking a cue from the above finding, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports and came across a report by The Indian Express published on November 26, 2024. One of the photos in the report's cover image showed Suryavanshi standing next to former cricketer Wasim Jaffer. "Vaibhav Surayvanshi was in an India U-19 team meeting ahead of their Asia Cup preparation when a member of the coaching staff broke the news to the 13-year-old that he had been picked by Rajasthan Royals in the IPL mega auction," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Moreover, we found no credible media reports of Colonel Sofiya Qureshi and cricketer Vaibhav Suryavanshi together. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the photo of Colonel Sofiya Qureshi with cricketer Vaibhav Suryavanshi is digitally altered.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2024 video of Shashi Tharoor from Jaipur Literature Festival falsely shared as his remark on Trump during recent US visit as leader of Indian delegation
content: New Delhi, May 28 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): The all-party delegation led by Congress MP Shashi Tharoor arrived in the US on Saturday (May 24) to project India's national consensus and firm stance against terrorism in all its forms. A video featuring Tharoor criticising US President Donald Trump was widely shared on social media, with users claiming the remarks were made by him during the delegation's current visit to the US. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video actually dates back to September 2024, during the Jaipur Literature Festival. In the video, Tharoor responded to a question about the American elections and shared his perspective as an Indian politician. Notably, Trump was not the President at the time. The video has no connection to the ongoing US visit and was falsely shared on social media to mislead viewers. The current delegation visit aims to brief international partners on India's response to the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack and reaffirm its commitment to combating cross-border terrorism. Claim An X user named 'Avinash Kadbe' shared a video on May 25 featuring Congress MP Shashi Tharoor criticising US President Donald Trump. The user claimed that the remarks were made during the Indian delegation's visit to the US. In the video, Tharoor says: "Look, it is really not our place, especially since I have been introduced as a member of the Indian parliament and so on. I should not comment on foreign countries' political leaders on their soil. But having said that, it is also true that people have political preferences. And mine is not a political preference. I do not pay taxes here, so I do not care if they are higher or lower. I am not seeking to be an immigrant here; even when I had the right to apply, I did not. And therefore, I am not worried about their stand on immigration. Those are other issues. On policy issues, everybody in this hall is entitled to their own preferences. But just the personal manner strikes me as not entirely as agreeable or pleasant as one would like to see in a distinguished American political figure. I had the great honour of meeting four or five American presidents during my time in the US and having detailed conversations with both the Bushes with Clinton. Much briefly with Obama. I mean, these are people of a certain class, a certain distinction, and it is not politics. Two Republicans on that list and two Democrats. But there was a certain political heft, statesman-like gravitas and intellectual quality that I find woefully lacking in this gentleman." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid verification tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was reverse-searched using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. One such post can be found here , and its archived versions can be viewed here . The Desk further ran the keyframes of the viral video through Reverse Image Search and came across an Instagram post dated September 24, 2024. The post featured the same video and Tharoor in identical attire. This makes it clear that the video is not recent, as seen in the social media post, during the delegation's visit to the US. Furthermore, the post's caption attributed the quote to Tharoor's appearance at the Jaipur Literature Festival (JLF) 2024. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarity of the attire worn by the Congress MP in the recent social media post and the 2024 Instagram post. Additionally, the Desk also came across the extended version of the video on the official YouTube channel of the Asia Society, dated September 12, 2024. The title of the report read: "Jaipur Literature Festival 2024 | Shashi Tharoor: A Man for All Seasons" Moreover, at that time, Donald Trump was not the President but was elected President on January 20, 2025. During the interview, Tharoor was asked about the elections in America and how he sees them from the Indian perspective. His response is being shared on social media as a recent incident during the delegation's US visit. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video featuring Congress MP Shashi Tharoor dates back to September 2024 during the Jaipur Literature Festival and not the recent visit of the Indian delegation to the US.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of child torture in Egypt's orphanage falsely circulated as incident from India; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 28 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A disturbing video showing a man mercilessly beating children with a stick was recently shared on social media, with claims that the incident took place in India. Users alleged that the video was from DPS in Rajbagh, Valsad, and that a teacher named Shakeel Ahmed Ansari was seen brutally thrashing a group of students. However, upon investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was unrelated to India. According to media reports, the footage actually shows an incident from Egypt, where the director of the Mecca Al-Mukarramah orphanage in the Giza governorate was caught on camera severely beating several resident children. The head of the orphanage was later jailed on charges of child abuse and endangering their lives. An old, unrelated video was falsely circulated on social media to mislead viewers. Claim An X user, Neelam Malhotra (@NeelamMalh11222), shared a video on May 27, allegedly showing Shakeel Ahmed Ansari, a teacher from DPS Rajbagh, mercilessly thrashing a group of school children with a stick. The video also appeared to show Ansari kicking the children. "Whatever number and group you have on WhatsApp, not even one should be left out, send this video to everyone. This is Shakeel Ahmed Ansari, a DPS School Rajbagh, Valsad teacher. Share it so much that the teacher and the school get shut down. Video going viral makes a lot of difference, and action is taken," the user wrote in the video's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (Important: The video contains sensitive visuals) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of the keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found that multiple social media accounts had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , along with their archived versions available here and here respectively: A Google Reverse Image Search also led the Desk to a news report published by the Arabic channel of France 24. The featured image of the report matched one of the keyframes used during the investigation. Dated August 2014, the article stated that the person in the video was the director of the Mecca Al-Mukarramah orphanage in the Giza governorate, Egypt, who brutally beat several children. The report further noted that the incident sparked widespread outrage in Egypt, prompting the Ministry of Social Solidarity to dissolve the board of directors of the orphanage and relocate the children to other facilities. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image showing that the visuals in the viral social media video matched the feature image of the news report. Additionally, the search result also led the Desk to a report by the BBC, published on September 10, 2014, confirming that the incident in the video took place in Egypt, not India. According to the report, the man in question—identified as Osama Mohammed Othman—was sentenced to three years in prison for assaulting seven children in his care and endangering their lives. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a man beating children with a stick was falsely linked to an incident that occurred in India. The video was originally from Egypt and was dated August 2014.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old, unrelated photo of theatre roof collapse falsely shared as ceiling collapse during 'Final Destination' screening in Argentina
content: New Delhi, May 28 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A photo showing a damaged room filled with debris appearing to be inside a movie theatre was recently shared on social media with the claim that the ceiling had collapsed during a screening of Final Destination: Bloodlines in Argentina. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the image does not show a theatre in Argentina or relate to the Final Destination screening. In reality, the photo dates back to February 2025 and was taken at a screening of Captain America: Brave New World in Washington. While a ceiling collapse did occur during a Final Destination screening in Argentina, this particular image is unrelated and was falsely shared online to mislead viewers. Claim A picture depicting a dilapidated condition with debris all around in a room, which looked like a movie theatre, was shared by a Facebook user named 'SK Mojammel Ali' on May 26. The user claimed the theatre ceiling collapsed during the "Final Destination Bloodlines" screening. "The ceiling collapsed in a theatre during the screening of the new 'Final Destination' movie," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the photo in the social media post through the Reverse Image Search and found several other social media users shared the same picture with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a report by NBC News published on February 27, 2025. The report carried a video depicting the aftermath of the ceiling collapse, and at 00:26 seconds, the visuals matched the picture shared on social media. Moreover, as per the report, a movie theatre ceiling collapsed during the 'Captain America: Brave New World' screening. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the social media post and the news report. Taking a cue from this, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports and came across a report by The New York Times published on April 27, 2025. The report said the theatre ceiling collapsed during the 'Captain America' screening in Washington State. "Two people watching 'Captain America: Brave New World' alone in a movie theatre in Wenatchee, Wash., on Tuesday night began hearing strange creaking and moaning. In a film where an absurd amount of furniture is smashed, dramatic final breaths abound, and fighters grunt through mortal combat, the sounds fit right in," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Notably, Argentine news outlet Infobae reported that a part of the ceiling broke off during a 'Final Destination' screening in Argentina on May 21, 2025. "The curious incident occurred this Monday, May 19, around 9:00 p.m. Fiamma Villaverde, 29, was walking through downtown La Plata with her 11-year-old daughter and a friend when they passed by the door of Cinema Ocho —located on 8th Street between 51st and 53rd, across from the Buenos Aires Legislature—and saw that they were about to screen Destino Final: Ties of Blood, the classic horror saga where death stalks those who manage to escape, by chance or by a vision, from a fatal accident. What they didn't imagine was that, minutes later, they would experience a traumatic episode that seemed to emulate the same logic as the film," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the photo in the social media post does not represent the collapse of a part of the roof in a theatre in Argentina during the screening of Final Destination. The image is from February 2025, during the screening of Captain America: Brave New World in Washington.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of woman assaulted in Bangladesh falsely shared as attack on YouTuber Jyoti Malhotra in India
content: New Delhi, May 28 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A disturbing video showing a woman being manhandled and brutally beaten by a crowd in broad daylight was recently circulated on social media with the claim that it showed Haryana-based YouTuber Jyoti Malhotra, who was allegedly arrested on charges of spying for Pakistan. Users claimed that an angry mob attacked Malhotra as she was being presented in court for a hearing. However, upon investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the woman in the video is not Jyoti Malhotra, and the incident did not occur in India. The video actually shows an agitated mob allegedly assaulting a woman who had spoken in support of Bangladesh's Awami League party near Dhanmondi 32—the residence of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman—in February 2025. Claim A Facebook user, Kashi Nath, shared a video on May 22 showing a woman being manhandled by an aggressive mob in broad daylight. The user claimed she was Haryana-based YouTuber Jyoti Malhotra, who had been arrested on charges of allegedly spying for Pakistan. "YouTuber Jyoti Malhotra, the traitor of the country, was beaten badly by the people as she was presented in court for the hearing," the user wrote in the caption accompanying the video. (Note: The video contains sensitive visuals. Viewer discretion is advised.) Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One keyframes was then run through Google Lens, leading to numerous social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively: Next, the Desk conducted a keyword-based Google search to verify whether any such incident involving Jyoti Malhotra being attacked by the public had been reported. The search did not yield any credible media reports confirming the claim. Had such an incident occurred, it would have received widespread media coverage. The Desk then ran the previously extracted keyframes through Google Reverse Image Search. The results led to a video posted on the official YouTube channel of Bangladesh-based news outlet Kalbela News. On February 6, 2025, the channel uploaded the full version of the same video circulating on social media. A closer analysis confirmed that the woman being manhandled in the video is not Jyoti Malhotra and that the incident did not occur in India.
