According to the video details, the incident occurred in Bangladesh, where a mob allegedly assaulted a woman for speaking in support of the Awami League near Dhanmondi 32, the residence of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. Additionally, the search result also led the Desk to a video posted on the official Facebook page of the Bangladesh Awami League, which, on February 6, had posted the same video of a woman supporter of the Awami League Party being manhandled by an agitated crowd in front of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's house at Dhanmondi 32. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing the woman being manhandled by the crowd was falsely linked to an incident in India.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old, unrelated video of Indian Army personnel's welcome falsely linked to Operation Sindoor
content: New Delhi, May 29 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing an Indian Army personnel receiving a warm welcome from his family was recently shared on social media. Users claimed that the soldier was returning from the recently launched Operation Sindoor. In the video, he walks on a red carpet, saluting and hugging his family members. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video is not recent and has no connection to Operation Sindoor. Further checks revealed that the video has been online since at least August 2023 and shows the soldier being welcomed after completing his initiation into military service. India launched Operation Sindoor, a coordinated military campaign on May 7, targeting nine terror launchpads in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK), following the April 22 terrorist attack in Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir, which claimed 26 lives. Claim An X user, Mahaveer_vj, shared a video on May 26 featuring an Indian Army personnel receiving a warm-hearted welcome from his family members. The user claimed that he received a welcome after his return from the recent Operation Sindoor. "Soldier coming back home after the Sindoor operation, What a lovely moment. Jai Hind," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One keyframe was then run through Google Lens, leading to numerous social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Desk then ran the extracted keyframes through Google Reverse Image Search and came across a Facebook post by Brut India dated August 17, 2023. The post clearly stated that the video was not related to Operation Sindoor. The video featured the same video as seen in the social media post. The video's title read: "This is how a soldier was welcomed by his family after returning to his village." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities of the content seen in the social media post and the video posted by Brut India. Taking a cue from the above finding, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find relevant media reports and came across a report by India Today published on August 15, 2023. The cover image of the report carried visuals from the video on social media; moreover, it was mentioned that a Sikh family recently rolled out the red carpet to welcome home their son, who had just completed his initiation into the military ranks. "In a heartwarming display of familial love and religious tradition, a Sikh family recently rolled out the red carpet to welcome home their son, who had just completed his initiation into the ranks of the military. The young soldier returned to his roots, greeted by the warmth of his family and the familiar customs of his faith," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Meanwhile, India launched Operation Sindoor, a coordinated military campaign that began on May 7, targeting nine terror launchpads in Pakistan and PoK, following the April 22 terrorist attack in Jammu and Kashmir's Pahalgam, which left 26 dead. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video dates back to August 2023 and is unrelated to the recent operation by the Indian Armed Forces

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video from PoK shared to falsely claim stones pelted at pilgrims travelling to Mata Vaishno Devi temple in J&K details inside
content: New Delhi, May 30 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it showed people pelting stones at pilgrims travelling to the Shri Mata Vaishno Devi temple in Jammu and Kashmir. The video depicted a group of individuals atop a hillside throwing stones at vehicles carrying pilgrims to the temple. However, upon investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was falsely linked to an incident in India. It actually showed protesters from Muzaffarabad in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) pelting stones at Pakistani Rangers during demonstrations against hikes in electricity and flour prices in May 2024. An old, unrelated video was falsely circulated on social media to mislead viewers. Claim A Facebook page named Uthishta Bharata shared a video on May 24 showing stones being pelted at pilgrims visiting the Mata Vaishno Devi shrine in Jammu and Kashmir. The video showed a group of people standing atop a hillside, hurling stones at vehicles carrying pilgrims to the shrine. "Jihadis attacked with stones on the convoy going to visit Vaishno Devi," the user shared the video with the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One keyframe was then run through Google Lens, leading to numerous social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here : In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to check whether any stone-pelting incident had occurred at the Mata Vaishno Devi shrine. The search did not yield any credible reports that could corroborate the claim. If such an incident had happened, it would have been widely covered by the media. As part of the investigation, the Desk also ran the keyframes extracted from the video through Google Lens. The reverse image search led to a video posted on an Instagram page named the_pahaari. On May 3, the Instagram user had posted the same video as seen in the social media claim. Still, the details inscribed on the video stated it was from Muzaffarabad in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK). The caption further mentioned that the incident dated back to May 2024 and involved Pakistani Rangers and residents. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a composite image highlighting that the content in the viral video matches the one posted on the Instagram page. Next, taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk conducted a keyword search on Google to verify whether any stone-pelting incident involving Pakistani Rangers and locals in Muzaffarabad, PoK, occurred in May 2024. The search led to a report published by India Today around the same time. The India Today report dated May 14, 2024, described a protest in Muzaffarabad, PoK, over rising food, fuel, and utilities prices, which escalated into violence. The report also described an incident that happened then, where protesters pelted stones at the convoy of Pakistani Rangers as it reached Muzaffarabad, near Shorran da Nakka village. Significantly, the incident described in the report matches the incident shown in the social media video. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Additionally, as a part of the investigation, the Desk used a VPN to search for Pakistani news reports related to the incident. This led to a video published on the official YouTube channel of Dawn News on May 18, 2024. The channel had posted the same video as seen in the viral post, confirming it depicted an incident in Muzaffarabad, PoK, where protesters had pelted stones at Pakistani Rangers' vehicles. The video was shared with the caption: "Stone Pelting on Rangers from Mountains in Azad Kashmir." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of pelting stones at pilgrims travelling to the Shri Mata Vaishno Devi shrine was falsely linked to India. The footage showed a stone-pelting incident that occurred in Muzaffarabad, Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK), during protests against price hikes in May 2024.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of Shashi Tharoor from Nagaland falsely shared as recent delegation visit abroad following Operation Sindoor
content: New Delhi, May 30 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of a woman complimenting Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on his looks and intelligence was shared on social media, with users claiming she was a foreign journalist who was "starstruck" by him during a recent visit by an Indian delegation abroad following Operation Sindoor. However, a fact check by the Press Trust of India (PTI) revealed that the video was from 2023, when Tharoor visited Nagaland to engage with the youth. The clip is unrelated to the recent diplomatic outreach and is being shared with a false claim. Claim A video featuring a woman complimenting Congress MP Shashi Tharoor for his good looks and intelligence was shared by an X user named 'Arohi Shukla' on May 29. The user sharing the video claimed that the woman was a foreign journalist who was 'starstruck' by the Congress MP, linking it to India's recent global outreach programme following Operation Sindoor. "Where foreign journalists are praising both the looks and intelligence of @ShashiTharoor. On the other hand, Congress people are bent on declaring him as Modi's "sycophant". What do you think, is @ShashiTharoor going to join BJP. #ShashiTharoor #IndiaPakistanWar #BJP," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One keyframe was then run through Google Lens, leading to numerous social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. Initially, the Desk, after careful analysis of the video, found 'The LS' watermark on the top left corner and then conducted a customised keyword search to find the video. The search led the Desk to the same video uploaded on YouTube by 'The Lungleng Show' on March 5, 2023, which clarifies that the video is old and not related to the recent global outreach program following operation Sindoor. The title of the video read: "Tharoor's Epic Reply to a Biggest Fan Girl in Nagaland | The Lungleng Show". Through the title, it is evident that the woman in the video was not a foreign journalist but a fan girl in Nagaland. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports citing the same. The search led the Desk to a report by the Hindustan Times, published on May 6, 2023. According to the report, Shashi Tharoor was in Nagaland interacting with Nagaland youth. "A video of senior Congress leader Shashi Tharoor interacting with Nagaland youth has been doing the rounds on the internet, in which he was asked to spill some secrets about this personality. In the video, a young woman, who describes herself as one of Tharoor's biggest fans, can be heard asking the Congress leader about the secret behind his looks and intelligence," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Moreover, we found the extended version of the video uploaded on the official YouTube channel of Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on February 28, 2023. The title of the report read: "Dr Shashi Tharoor Conversation with Nagaland Youth" Here is the link to the video. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to 2023 when Shashi Tharoor was in Nagaland to interact with the youth. The video is old and unrelated to the recent delegation visit following Operation Sindoor.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Railway travel concessions for senior citizens restored? No, this social media post is false and baseless; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 30 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A post circulating on social media claimed that Indian Railways has reintroduced travel concessions for senior citizens. According to the post, senior citizens would be eligible for discounted train fares in certain classes starting May 21, 2025. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found this claim false. The Union Budget 2025–26 does not mention the restoration of the senior citizen concession scheme. Further investigation confirmed that Indian Railways discontinued these concessions in March 2020 as part of its COVID-19 measures, and the government has since repeatedly clarified that there are no plans to reinstate them due to financial constraints. Claim A Facebook user going by the name 'Musannas Muthu' shared a post on May 28 claiming that Indian Railways has reintroduced travel concessions for senior citizens. The user further claimed that starting from 21 May 2025, senior citizens will be eligible for discounts on train fares across certain classes. "...To avail of the concession, senior citizens need to select the "Senior Citizen Concession" checkbox during online booking or inform the railway staff at the counter. The system will automatically calculate and apply the concession if eligible…," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation As part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a keyword search for the information mentioned in the social media post and found that other users and several dubious websites published similar details. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. To check the veracity of the claim made in the social media post, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find relevant media reports and did not find any such announcements. As part of the investigation, the Desk scanned the Union Budget 2025-26, and it does not mention any plan to reinstate concessions on train fares for senior citizens. Here is the link : Next, the Desk looked for official announcements from the Ministry of Railways and found a press release dated March 2020. The release mentioned that the central government withdrew several concessions in March 2020, including the senior citizen concession in trains, as part of measures to prevent the spread of COVID-19. "In order to contain the spread of the COVID-19 virus and to minimise the travel-related risks to elderly citizens, Indian Railways has taken steps to discourage senior citizens from undertaking non-essential journeys by removing special incentives which presently exist for their travel. Indian Railways has done this by withdrawing concessional booking of tickets to senior citizens for Unreserved & Reserved segments from 00:00 hrs of 20th March till further notice. This step has been taken to discourage them from making non-essential journeys," read the release. Here is the link to the release, and below is a screenshot of the same. As part of the investigation, the Desk scanned the IRCTC Portal and checked senior citizens' tickets. The results show that ticket prices for senior citizens remain the same as those for general-category passengers. Here is the link to the portal. Further investigation led the Desk to a Senior Citizen Concession notice, which stated that the senior citizen concession was withdrawn from March 20, 2020. Here is the link , and below is a screenshot of the same: In a report published on April 28, 2023, by Live Law, the Supreme Court rejected a plea seeking the restoration of concession in railway ticket prices for senior citizens. The report headline read: "Supreme Court Dismisses Plea To Restore Concession In Railway Tickets For Senior Citizens." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Furthermore, in December 2024, when the same issue was raised in the Lok Sabha, Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw responded that the total subsidy provided by the Government of India for all passengers travelling in Indian Railways is Rs. 56,993 crore. When the service cost is Rs. 100, the ticket is charged at Rs. 54, which amounts to a 46 per cent subsidy for every passenger travelling, including all the categories mentioned by the Hon. MP. Here is the link to the response, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim that the Indian government has restored concessions on train fares for senior citizens is false.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated images of Bollywood actor Sonakshi Sinha wearing a burqa shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 30 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A photo collage featuring multiple images of Bollywood actor Sonakshi Sinha dressed in a black burqa was recently shared on social media. Users circulated the photos to suggest that Sonakshi started following interfaith customs following her marriage to actor Zaheer Iqbal. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the images were AI-generated and falsely presented as real on social media. Claim On May 29, an X user going by the name Arun Yadav (@ArunKosli) shared a collage depicting multiple images of Bollywood actor Sonakshi Sinha dressed in a black burqa. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. When this story was published, the image had garnered 724.1k views. Investigation The Desk carefully cropped two purported images of Sonakshi Sinha from the collage and ran them through Google Lens. The search led the Desk to multiple social media posts that shared the same pictures with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk scanned Sonakshi Sinha's social media handles to check if she had ever shared the above purported images. However, it was found that no such photos had been posted from any of her social media accounts. Next, the Desk carefully examined the images to identify their origin. The analysis revealed several discrepancies, indicating that the images might be AI-generated or digitally altered. For instance, subtle distortions in facial features were clearly identifiable in both images, along with an excessive glossy finish, a common characteristic of AI-generated visuals. Below is a screenshot highlighting the visuals. Taking cues from the above inputs, the Desk separately ran the two purported images of Sonakshi Sinha through Wasitai (an AI detection tool). The tool detected a substantial presence of AI-generated elements in both images. Below are screenshots of the results. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the images of Sonakshi Sinha attached in the collage were AI-generated and falsely shared on social media to mislead viewers.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated photo of wrecked aircraft shared with false claim of Hajj pilgrims' death in Red Sea crash
content: New Delhi, June 2 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): An image allegedly showing a devastating aeroplane crash site at night, with bodies lying around covered in white cloth, was recently shared on social media. The user claimed that a Mauritanian flight carrying 220 Hajj pilgrims had crashed into the Red Sea. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the image was AI-generated. Upon further verification, Mauritania Airlines confirmed that the claim was false. An AI-generated image was used to support a fabricated narrative on social media. Claim A photo featuring a severely damaged aircraft, appearing to have crashed and caught fire, was shared by a Facebook user named 'Aryanboys An' on May 29, claiming that a Mauritanian flight carrying 220 Hajj pilgrims had crashed into the Red Sea. "The Hajj plane has crashed and 220 pilgrims have been martyred. The accident took place near the Red Sea. May Allah grant paradise to the pilgrims #Ameen," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the photo through Reverse Image Search and found several other users shared the same photo with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. As part of the investigation, the Desk carefully scanned the photo in the social media post and found several discrepancies that hinted it might be AI-generated or manipulated. For instance, the bodies lying on the ground did not appear real; the people near the plane, probably rescue workers, also did not appear real since they were structured differently, and the aircraft windows lacked realistic detail and structure. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the photo through WasitAI, an AI-detection tool. The tool detected a substantial presence of AI-generated elements. Below are screenshots of the results. Moreover, on conducting a customised keyword search, we found a report by The Saudi Times, published on May 29, 2025, which mentioned that Mauritania Airlines firmly denied circulating reports claiming that one of its aircraft carrying pilgrims had crashed in the Red Sea, describing them as completely unfounded. "The company confirmed that all Mauritanian pilgrims travelling abroad on its flights had safely arrived in the Kingdom, with no incidents reported on any of the scheduled trips," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report. Furthermore, Mauritania Airlines issued an official statement on its Facebook page, describing the news as fake. The post mentioned that Mauritania Aviation confirms that all the Mauritanian pilgrims have thankfully arrived in the Holy Lands safely, and no incident has been recorded regarding organised flights in this frame. "Some foreign social media pages have been circulating deliberate rumours about a plane carrying Mauritanian pilgrims off the Red Sea crash, which is baseless health news. Mauritania Aviation confirms that all the Mauritanian pilgrims have arrived in the Holy Lands safely, and no incident has been recorded regarding organised flights in this frame," read the post. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the photo showing a crashed aircraft was AI-generated, and Mauritius Airlines confirmed that the claim made in the post is fake.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2018 video of Kanpur builder's arrest falsely shared as BSF personnel suspected of espionage for Pakistan
content: New Delhi, June 2 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing two men in formal attire accompanied by police officers was recently shared on social media with the claim that they were BSF personnel suspected of spying for Pakistan. Users further alleged that the two were caught on a train carrying ₹96 lakh in cash. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video is not recent—it dates back to 2018. It actually shows Kanpur police seizing ₹96 crore in demonetised currency from builder Anand Khatri and several others. No BSF personnel were involved in the incident. The video was shared with a false claim intended to mislead viewers on social media. Claim A video featuring two men in professional suits accompanied by police officers was shared by a Thread user named 'Siddharth S Sinha', claiming that the two men were BSF personnel who were suspected of espionage for Pakistan. The users added that the two were caught in a train, carrying Rs 96 lakhs in cash. "2 BSF men - Pak Spies. These men were caught in a train, carrying 96 lakhs in cash. When homes were raided, one of the homes had 96 crores stashed in money. What should be the punishment for them?" read the post's caption. The post clocked 530 likes and 150 shares. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One keyframe was then run through Google Lens, leading to numerous social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a more extended version of the same video uploaded on a YouTube channel named 'taak jhaank' on January 27, 2018, which confirms that the video is not recent. The title of the video read: "Breaking News 96.40 crore Recovered from Anand Khatri, builder of Kanpur" Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting that the content in the viral video matches the one posted on YouTube. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports, and we came across a report by ABP Live published on January 17, 2018. According to 16 people, including a noted builder, were arrested by the Kanpur police in connection with the seizure of over Rs 96 crore in demonetised currency notes from the builder's ancestral house in Swaroop Nagar. "Senior Superintendent of Police Akhilesh Kumar Meena said today that Rs 95 crore belonged to Anand Khatri, the builder, and over a dozen others owned the remaining amount. They were arrested along with the builder and sent to jail after being booked under various sections," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Moreover, our search also led us to a report published on January 13, 2018, by NDTV mentioning that the CBI arrested Jibu D Mathew, a Commandant with the Border Security Force (BSF), at Alappuzha railway station in Kerala after seizing Rs 45.3 lakh in cash from his luggage. "Jibu D Mathew was a commandant with the BSF, the paramilitary force entrusted with guarding the borders with Pakistan and Bangladesh. He had been detained yesterday but was formally placed under arrest early this morning," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report. However, we did not find any reports of two BSF soldiers carrying Rs 96 lakh in cash or any of their houses being raided with ₹96 crore seized in 2025. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video dates back to 2018 and shows Kanpur police seizing Rs 96 crore in demonetised currency from builder Anand Khatri and others. No BSF personnel were involved in that incident.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Kangaroo waiting to board a plane? AI-generated video shared by social media users as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 2 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported video showing a kangaroo patiently waiting with a piece of paper in its hand, while two women nearby appear to be arguing, was recently shared on social media with the claim that it depicted a real incident. The user claimed the video captured a moment when airline staff denied the kangaroo entry to board a plane, as it patiently stood holding a boarding pass. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video was AI-generated and was falsely shared as real on social media. Claim An X user, Dr. Sheetal Yadav (@Sheetal2242), shared a video on May 27, allegedly showing a kangaroo patiently waiting to board a plane. The video showed him holding a boarding pass in his hand. "Airline staff is not allowing this cute kangaroo to board the plane. The way he is holding the boarding pass and waiting for it to be scanned looks very cute," the user captioned the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. When this story was published, the video had garnered 196.4k views and 5.1k likes. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One keyframe was then run through Google Lens, leading to several social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Reverse Image Search also led the Desk to a video published on an Instagram handle named infiniteunreality. The handle had posted the same video (showing a kangaroo allegedly waiting with a boarding pass in its hand) as seen in the viral post on May 26, 2025. However, upon closer inspection, the Desk found that the Instagram handle 'infinitereality' (through which the video was primarily shared) posted videos only created through visual effects and does not post real incidents. The bio of the handle reads, "Your Daily Dose of Unreality." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image showing that the content in the viral video matches the video posted by the Instagram handle. In the next step of the investigation, taking a cue from the above-generated input that the video was made using visual effects, the Desk ran the footage through Hive Moderation, an AI detection tool. The tool confirmed a substantial presence of AI-generated elements. Below is the screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a kangaroo waiting to board a plane was AI-generated and falsely shared on social media as real.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old shooting video from Brazil falsely shared as recent murder incident in India; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 2 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it depicted a horrific incident in India, where a person was allegedly shot dead on a busy road in broad daylight. The footage showed the victim, who was riding a two-wheeler, being intercepted by two bike-borne men—one of whom, seated on the passenger seat, allegedly shot him dead. The victim was then seen falling to the ground after the attack. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found the claim false. The incident actually took place in João Pessoa, Brazil, where a 22-year-old man was shot dead by two unidentified assailants in the Mandacaru neighbourhood in October 2024. The video captured the moment the attackers pulled up alongside the victim's motorcycle and fired multiple rounds, killing him on the spot. Claim An X user named Adv. Nazneen Akhtar (@NazneenAkhtar23) shared a video on May 29, claiming it showed a man being shot dead in broad daylight on a busy road in India. The footage showed the victim riding a two-wheeler on a busy road before being intercepted by two bike-borne men. One of them, seated on the passenger seat, allegedly shot him with a revolver. The victim was seen falling to the ground after the attack. "Watch live murder on road. There's goonda raj everywhere. Now the life of humans has become worse than that of insects. Think about how cheap human life has become — someone can come and steal it and go away. This is the pride of our country," the user captioned the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. When this story was published, the video had garnered 21k views. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with archived versions available here and here , respectively. A Google Reverse Image Search also led the Desk to a report published on the Brazil-based portal Nos Bastidores da Notícia, where the featured image matched the keyframe used in the investigation. The report described the shooting incident as having occurred in João Pessoa city, Brazil, on October 4, 2024. The report stated that the incident took place in the Mandacaru neighbourhood, where a 22-year-old man was shot dead while riding a motorcycle. "The criminals pulled up alongside the victim's motorcycle, and the passenger fired several shots, killing the motorcyclist on the spot," the report added. Here is the link to the report along with a screenshot. Below is a composite image highlighting that the content in the viral video matches the featured image from the Brazil-based portal. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video did not depict a shooting incident in India; it was originally from Brazil.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old image of Russian S-400 destroyed by Ukraine falsely linked to recent India-Pakistan military conflict
content: New Delhi, June 3 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A photo showing a charred, partially melted, and destroyed military vehicle was recently shared on social media with the claim that it depicted India's S-400 defence system, allegedly destroyed by Pakistan. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the image actually showed a Russian S-400 defence system destroyed by Ukraine in 2024. Further verification revealed that India has denied any such attack on its S-400 system, calling the claim "completely wrong." The photo was therefore shared on social media with a false narrative. Claim A photo showing a heavily damaged and likely destroyed military vehicle, specifically a radar or air defence system, was shared by an X user named 'Imran' on May 28. The user claimed that Pakistan destroyed India's S-400 defence system. "S-400 radar down. Indian tears at full blast. #IndiaPakistanWar," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the photo in the social media post through Reverse Image Search and found that other users shared the same picture with a similar claim. One such post can be found here , and its archived version can be viewed here . Upon further scanning the search results, the Desk came across the same image used in a May 24, 2024, YouTube video by Warthog Defence, a US-based, verified YouTube channel focusing on military news, analysis, and storytelling. The title of the video read: "A VIDEO OF THE US ATACMS MISSILES ATTACK ON RUSSIAN S-300/400 SYSTEM IN DONETSK || 2024" Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find relevant media reports. It came across a report by a Ukrainian-based news outlet, Defence Outlet, published on May 23, 2024. According to the report, the Ukrainian Armed Forces destroyed another S-400, but in this situation, the distance at which it was done says a lot. "The location of the events is declared as the Mospine district in the Donetsk region, or rather, a small field airfield from the DOSAAF era. And the photos and videos show the destruction of the SAM machines and the ATACMS missile engine," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Moreover, the Desk conducted another set of customised keyword searches, which led us to a report by India Today dated May 10, 2025, wherein Colonel Sofiya Qureshi clarified that Pakistan's claim that it damaged our S400 and Brahmos missile base with its JF 17 is entirely wrong. "Pakistan claimed that it damaged our S400 and Brahmos missile base with its JF 17, which is completely wrong, Colonel Sofiya Qureshi said during a Defence Ministry press briefing following India's announcement of a ceasefire with Pakistan," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the photo shared in the social media post shows a Russian S-400 defence system destroyed by Ukraine in 2024.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of damaged fire station in Myanmar after earthquake falsely shared as incident from West Bengal; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 3 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a portion of a collapsed fire station building damaging several vehicles was recently shared on social media, with claims that the incident occurred in West Bengal. Users also criticised the Trinamool Congress (TMC) government, alleging poor governance and corruption. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video actually shows the aftermath of an earthquake that struck Myanmar and is unrelated to West Bengal. It was shared on social media with a false claim. On March 28, 2025, a 7.7-magnitude earthquake hit central Myanmar, causing extensive damage to infrastructure, including religious monuments, buildings, and public facilities. The quake's epicentre was located in Sagaing, a city in central Myanmar. Claim A video showing a portion of a collapsed fire station building causing damage to vehicles was shared by a Facebook user named 'সন্দীপ হিন্দু' on May 24, 2025. The user claimed that the incident happened in West Bengal and further criticised the TMC government for the incident. "Great scene, Jay Bangla...When will you think again. See how much the #ChorTMC has eaten with your and my tax money. Contractor says, it's over to give everyone," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One keyframe was then run through Google Lens, leading to several social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with archived versions available here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a similar video uploaded on YouTube on May 24, 2024. The video's title read: "Damage To Sagaing Fire Station, Sagaing, Myanmar." Though no additional information was available in the description, the visuals matched those shared on Facebook as those of West Bengal. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a comparison image showing that the content in the social media post matches the video posted on YouTube. Taking a cue from this, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports and came across a report by the BBC published on March 29, 2025. The report mentioned the devastating earthquake in Myanmar in which 1600 people lost their lives, with locals in some areas telling the BBC they had been left to dig through rubble for survivors with their bare hands. The report included several pictures of the havoc caused by the earthquake, including a still from a video shared on social media in the name of West Bengal. The report depicted a fire station in Sagaing collapsing, crushing the fire engines. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Another report by the Deccan Herald, published on April 1, 2025, also cited the casualties caused by the devastating earthquake. Moreover, the feature image was similar to the clip shared on social media. As per the article, people stand by a collapsed fire station after a strong earthquake near its epicentre in Sagaing, Myanmar. "US aid response in Myanmar faces hurdles after staff cuts," read the report's headline. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video is from Myanmar and depicts the aftermath of the earthquake in Sagaing.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated images of train engines featuring Lord Ram's portrait falsely shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 3 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A photo collage recently shared on social media showed two purported images of train engines, one of the Vande Bharat and the other of an Express train, adorned with portraits of Lord Ram. Users sharing the collage claimed the images were real. However, upon investigation, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the collage was AI-generated and falsely shared on social media to mislead viewers. Claim On May 28, an Instagram handle with the username 'aapnorajasthan.official' shared a collage that included photos of train engines—one of the Vande Bharat and the other of an Express train. The images showed the engines covered with portraits of Lord Ram. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk carefully cropped the two purported images of the train engines (one of the Vande Bharat and the other of an Express train) from the collage and ran them through Google Lens. The search led the Desk to multiple social media posts that shared the same pictures with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk scanned the image and found a watermark that read @The Rail Pilot. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to determine what exactly @The Rail Pilot refers to. The search led to an Instagram account bearing the same name as the watermark. Here is the link to the handle, along with a screenshot: Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk scanned through all social media posts made from the handle and found the same image, identical to the one now circulating, posted on the handle on May 26, 2025. However, a disclaimer mentioned alongside the image read: "These pictures are made with Artificial Intelligence (AI)." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a comparison image confirming that the viral social media image matches the one posted on the Instagram handle: Additionally, taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk ran the social media image through Hive Moderation, an AI detection tool. The result indicated that 92.3% of the image content contained deepfake or AI-generated elements. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the social media image showing Lord Ram portraits on the train engines (of the Vande Bharat and Express trains) was not real and had been generated using AI.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of man killed in sickle attack in Brazil falsely shared as recent incident from India
content: New Delhi, June 3 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A disturbing video showing a man attacking another person with a sharp object was recently shared on social media with the claim that the incident occurred in India. The footage shows the attacker allegedly chasing another man while wielding a sharp weapon, ultimately assaulting him with it. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it unrelated to any incident in India. The video actually depicts a violent incident in Campo Alegre, Brazil, where a man was brutally murdered over a custody dispute involving a young girl. An old, unrelated video was falsely shared on social media to mislead viewers. Claim An X user, Adv. Nazneen Akhtar (@NazneenAkhtar23) shared a purported video on May 28 showing a man attacking another person with a sharp object. The user claimed that the incident had occurred in India. "After all, what was the fault of this boy that he was beaten so badly? Did 2025 come for this? Do the common people have no right to live?? @narendramodi @myogiadityanath Sir, will there be such massacres in the country now? Tell me, when will the bulldozer be run over by this murderer's house?" the user wrote in the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. When this story was published, the video had garnered 11.9k views. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of the keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found that multiple social media accounts had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Reverse Image Search also led the Desk to a report published on a UK-based portal, Need to Know, which elaborated on the same incident depicted in the viral video. The report included the same video of the attack in the viral post and clarified that the incident occurred in Brazil, not India. The report stated that the incident occurred in Campo Alegre, located northeast of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, on April 6, 2025. It identified the victim as 59-year-old Sebastião Fabiano da Silva, who was brutally murdered in broad daylight over a child custody row. "Sebastião Fabiano da Silva was riding his bike through town when two members of the opposing family allegedly attacked him. One of the suspects was armed with a plank of wood while the other had a long-handled sickle," the report added. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Below is a composite image highlighting that the content in the viral video matches that of the featured image in the news report. Additionally, the reverse image search led the Desk to multiple other news reports, confirming that the incident in the viral video pertained to Brazil and not India. Here is the link to one such media report covering the incident: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video does not depict an incident from India but from Brazil.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2023 video of pension reform protest in France falsely shared as recent incident in Paris after Champions League final
content: New Delhi, June 4 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Following Paris Saint-Germain's (PSG) historic win over Inter Milan in the UEFA Champions League final, a video surfaced on social media showing vehicles cautiously driving down a road flanked by blazing garbage bins. Users claimed the scene was from Paris in the aftermath of the final. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video actually dates back to 2023 and shows protests in France against pension reforms. It has no connection to the recent events in Paris. The footage was falsely shared on social media with a misleading claim. Notably, two people were killed and over 500 were taken into custody across France as PSG fans celebrated the club's Champions League victory. Claim A video showing a few vehicles driving cautiously down a road flanked by blazing garbage bins on both sides was shared by an X user named PressTV Extra on June 1, 2025. The user claimed that the incident happened in Paris following the UEFA Champions League final. "Apocalyptic scenes unfold in Paris as football fans set fire to garbage bins across the city following victory in the UEFA Champions League final," read the post's caption. The post clocked 2,456 views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One keyframe was then run through Google Lens, leading to several social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with archived versions available here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across the same video posted on X by a user named Clément Lanot on March 21, 2023. This makes it clear that the video is not recent and is unrelated to the current incidents happening in Paris. "Dozens of burning barricades, protesters advance in the 3rd arrondissement," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. When running the viral video's keyframes through Reverse Image Search, the desk came across a snippet of a March 2023 YouTube video report by Paris-based C dans l'air—France Télévisions. "After a social movement that has been held and organised for weeks, violence is making a comeback. Police methods are once again being criticised, and the Prime Minister is targeting La France Insoumise, whose "verbal violence is spilling over into the streets," in her words," read the translation in the description of the video. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Additionally, a similar clip was also featured in a news article by The Telegraph, published on March 21, 2023, mentioning that more than 100 people were arrested in Paris as protesters burned some of the stewing piles of rubbish left by striking bin workers. "It came as Emmanuel Macron prepared to break his silence on his move to ram through his pension reforms without a vote in parliament, which has further angered protesters," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video dates back to 2023 when a protest was carried out in France over pension reforms.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Scripted video of police arresting a Muslim man for 'trapping' Hindu girl falsely shared as real incident on social media; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 4 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media claimed to depict a real-life incident in which two police officers are seen arresting a Muslim man for allegedly trapping and marrying a Hindu girl, presenting it through a communal lens. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it scripted and staged. The clip has no connection to any real incident and was misleadingly shared on social media with a false narrative. Claim A video featuring two police officers arresting a man for allegedly trapping and marrying a girl was shared by an X user named 'Tathvam-asi', claiming that it shows the real incidents of 'Love Jihad'. "Love Jihaad caught red-handed by Police," read the post's caption. The post garnered 21.7k views and 1.5k likes. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One keyframe was then run through Google Lens, leading to several social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with archived versions available here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a similar video uploaded by a Facebook user named 'monty_deepak_sharma' on April 3, 2025. However, when we checked through the 'about' section of the page, we found 'Video creator' written in the bio. The link to the video and screenshots of the mentioned findings are below. The Desk also found the video uploaded by the same user on the YouTube Channel and other videos involving the same individuals seen in the viral video participating in similar incidents. Here is the link to the channel, and below is a screenshot of the same. The same user's Instagram also mentioned 'Video Creator' in the bio, and the handle featured several videos with the same individuals, indicating that it does not depict a real incident but is scripted and for educational and entertainment purposes only. Here is the link to the account, and below is a screenshot of the same. The PTI Fact Check debunked another video by Deepak Monty, which was falsely shared as police stopped MLA's car with black tinted windows. Here is the link to the report. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk contacted Deepak Monty, who told Press Trust of India that the video is scripted. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a scripted video was falsely shared as an actual incident of 'Love Jihad'.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old Tamil Nadu CPI(M) event video shared to falsely claim protest staged in Kerala over killing of Maoist leaders; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 5 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Days after two senior Maoist leaders, Nambala Keshav Rao, alias Basavaraju, and Pappu Lohara, were killed in separate major anti-Naxal operations in Chhattisgarh's Narayanpur and Jharkhand's Latehar districts, a video allegedly linked to a political protest following their deaths was shared on social media. Users claimed that members of the Communist Party staged a protest in Kerala after the Maoist leaders were killed. The video showed a group of people in red attire chanting slogans on the streets. However, upon investigation, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the video had no connection to any CPI(M) protest in Kerala. It actually showed the Red Volunteer March held in Madurai, Tamil Nadu, on April 6, 2025, during the CPI(M) Party Congress held from April 2 to 6, several days before the deaths of the Maoist leaders. An unrelated video was falsely shared on social media to mislead viewers. Claim A Facebook user '@ami.meghanatha' shared a video on May 28, purportedly showing a protest held by Communist Party members in Kerala over the killing of Maoist leaders Basavaraju and Pappu Lohara. The user wrote: "Communist rally in Kerala protests the killing of Maoist leaders Basavaraju and Pappu Lohara with slogans: 'No to capitalism, no to Hindi imposition.'" Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively: Next, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to check whether the CPI(M) had organised any such protest in Kerala. However, the search yielded no credible reports to corroborate the claim. If such an incident had occurred, it would have been widely covered by the media. As part of the investigation, the Desk then ran the keyframes extracted from the video through Google Lens, which led it to a social media post made from the official X handle of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) Tamil Nadu State Committee. The Desk found the social media post made on April 6 resembled the visuals seen in the viral video. The clothing pattern (red shirts) worn by the people in the viral video matched exactly those seen in the image posted on X. The X post described the video as a march taken out by the Red Volunteers of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) on the concluding day of the CPI(M)'s 24th Party Congress in Madurai, which began on April 2. These findings made it evident that the incident depicted in the video predates the killing of the Naxal commanders, which occurred in May. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the clothing pattern worn by the people in the viral video and those in the photo posted on X: Taking further cues, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search on Google. This time came across the full version of the video of the CPI(M) rally held in Tamil Nadu earlier in April 2025, posted on the party's official YouTube channel. Upon carefully scanning the video posted on April 9, the Desk found that the background setting seen in the YouTube video (flex boards, nearby buildings) matched that of the viral video. This confirmed that both videos are from the same event in Tamil Nadu and not Kerala. Additionally, it had already been established that the CPI(M) rally took place before the Naxalite killings in Chhattisgarh in May. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot: Below is a comparison image that clearly shows a match in the background settings of the viral video and the video posted on the official YouTube channel of CPI(M): Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video does not depict a protest held by Communist Party members in Kerala over the killing of Maoist leaders Basavaraju and Pappu Lohara.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Movie clip shared by social media user falsely claimed to show 26/11 Taj Hotel attack footage; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 5 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it showed real footage from inside Mumbai's iconic Taj Mahal Palace Hotel during the 26/11 terrorist attacks on November 26, 2008. The video, which appears to depict armed terrorists opening fire on guests and hotel staff, was presented as authentic visual evidence from the time of the attack. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found the claim false. The video circulating on social media is actually a scene from the Bollywood movie, 'The Attack of 26/11', which dramatises the terror attack on Mumbai's Taj Hotel. A movie scene was falsely shared as real footage from the 2008 tragedy. It is pertinent to note that on November 26, 2008, Mumbai witnessed one of the deadliest terrorist attacks in its history. At least 166 people were killed and over 300 injured when 10 heavily armed terrorists from the Pakistan-based group Lashkar-e-Taiba infiltrated the city via sea. They targeted multiple high-profile locations, including the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel, Oberoi Trident Hotel, Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus, and Leopold Café. The siege lasted nearly four days before Indian security forces neutralised nine of the ten terrorists and captured one alive. Claim A Facebook user named Narendra Shah shared a video on May 28, claiming it showed never-before-seen footage from inside the Taj Hotel in Mumbai during the 2008 terrorist attacks. The user wrote: "The terrorists had attacked the Taj Hotel in such a way that its video has come out now. You must not have seen it till now. How dangerous was the fear, whoever saw it with his own eyes at that time. Today, the Modi government has become a terror for these terror-creators, which is why Congress and all the Maulanas are upset?" Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. At the time of writing, the video had garnered over 820k views. Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of the keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found several social media accounts shared the same video with similar claims. One such post can be found here , with its archived version available here , respectively. Additionally, a Google Reverse Image search led the Desk to a YouTube video published by a channel named Grand Master Movies. The video uploaded to this channel on October 21, 2023, was identified as a full-length version of the Bollywood movie The Attack of 26/11. At the 29-minute and 43-second timestamp in the movie, the same visuals seen in the viral clip appeared, showing terrorists opening fire inside the Taj Hotel lobby. This confirmed that the viral video was not real footage from the 2008 attacks, but rather a dramatised scene from the film. While the attack on the Taj Hotel was a real and horrific event, no official or credible video footage from inside the hotel during the attack has ever been released publicly. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. Below is a composite image highlighting that the content in the social media video matched the visuals in the movie clip. Additionally, as a part of the investigation, the Desk also conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across details of the movie The Attack of 26/11. Directed by Ram Gopal Varma, the film is inspired by the real story behind Mumbai's 72-hour-long siege that shook the country to the core. Veteran Bollywood actor Nana Patekar plays the role of Mumbai's Joint Commissioner of Police, recounting the horrific scenes from the incident, including attacks at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, CAMA Hospital, Leopold Café, and the Taj Hotel. The visuals in the viral post were found to be from the exact dramatic depiction featured in the movie. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video claiming to show never-before-seen footage from inside the Taj Hotel in Mumbai during the 2008 terrorist attacks was a clip from a Bollywood movie.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: This video claiming to show Lord Ram's bow found in sea is AI-generated and shared with fake claim; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 5 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it depicted Lord Ram's bow being found in the sea. The video showed a giant bow being retrieved and later carefully placed on a ship. It also appeared to show the bow under police protection. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video was AI-generated and shared on social media with a fake claim. Claim An X user with the handle '@nair_nandu08' shared a video on May 31, claiming it showed Lord Ram's bow being found in the sea. The footage showed the bow being lifted out of the water and then carefully placed on a ship. "Lord Ramchand's bow was found in the sea," the user captioned the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of the keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , along with their archived versions available here and here , respectively: During a detailed video review, the Desk spotted a watermark reading "@mrmahadevshorts1" at the bottom. Based on this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and was led to an Instagram account with the same handle. Here is the link to the handle, along with a screenshot. The Desk then scanned the content posted on the page and found the duplicate footage, identical to the viral video, uploaded on May 30, 2025. The video caption clearly stated that the visuals were AI-generated and bore no connection to any real event. "This video is an AI-generated visualisation for educational and devotional purposes only. The visuals are reconstructed based on speculative archaeological hypotheses and artistic interpretations. It aims to inspire cultural curiosity and dharmic awareness, NOT to present verified historical evidence. Viewer discretion advised," the disclaimer on the video read. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image confirming that the visuals in the viral video match those in the video posted on the Instagram handle. Additionally, while scanning other videos posted by the user, the Desk observed that most of the content on the account is AI-generated and does not depict real events. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the social media video showing Lord Rama's bow being discovered in the sea was AI-generated.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Social media post claiming RBI has directed banks to stop disbursing ₹500 notes by September 30 is false; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 6 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A viral social media post claims that the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has directed all banks to stop disbursing Rs 500 notes through ATMs by September 30. It further states that only Rs 200 and Rs 100 notes will be available from ATMs thereafter. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the RBI has issued no such directive to stop disbursing Rs 500 notes. Instead, the RBI has instructed banks and White Label ATM Operators (WLAOs) to ensure that 75% of all ATMs dispense Rs 100 or Rs 200 denomination notes by September 30, 2025. The claim circulating on social media is false and misleading. Claim: An X user named 'CA Anupam Sharma' shared a post on June 2 claiming that the RBI has directed all banks to stop disbursing ₹ 500 notes by September 30 from ATM. The user further claimed that ATMs will only disburse ₹200 & ₹100 notes. "RBI has asked all banks to stop disbursing 500₹ notes by 30 Sep from ATM. Target is 75% of all banks BANKS ATM & then 90% ATM by 31Mar26. ATM going forward will only disburse 200₹ and 100₹ notes." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. The post clocked 635.9k views on social media. Investigation: The Desk conducted a keyword search of the given information in the post and found that several other users had shared the same post with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived version can be viewed here and here , respectively. To commence our investigation, the Desk first scanned the official website of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and checked its press release section, circulars, and publications. However, the search did not yield any information supporting the claim that the RBI has directed banks to stop dispensing ₹500 notes through ATMs. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports. This led us to a report by Financial Express published on April 29, 2025. As per the report, the RBI has asked banks to ensure that ATMs dispense ₹100 or ₹ 200 denomination notes to enhance the availability of these currency notes to the public. It did not mention any directives from the RBI to stop the disbursement of ₹500 notes. "In a circular released on Monday, the RBI said, As part of an endeavour towards enhancing public access to frequently used denominations of banknotes, it has been decided that all banks and White Label ATM Operators (WLAOs) shall ensure that their ATMs dispense ₹100 and ₹200 denomination banknotes regularly….," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk again looked through the RBI's website about this, shared on April 28, 2025. As per the notification, all banks and White Label ATM Operators (WLAOs) shall ensure that their ATMs dispense ₹100—and ₹ 200-denomination banknotes. "As part of an endeavour towards enhancing public access to frequently used denominations of banknotes, it has been decided that all banks and White Label ATM Operators (WLAOs) shall ensure that their ATMs dispense ₹100 and ₹200 denomination banknotes regularly as per following milestones: By September 30, 2025: 75% of all ATMs shall dispense either ₹100 or ₹200 denomination banknotes from at least one cassette. By March 31, 2026: 90% of all ATMs shall dispense either ₹100 or ₹200 denomination banknotes from at least one cassette," read the notification. Here is the link to the notification, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the RBI will not stop the disbursement of ₹500 notes from September 30. The RBI has instructed banks and WLAOs to ensure that 75% of all ATMs also dispense ₹100 or ₹200 denomination notes by September 30, 2025.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video showing clash in Indonesia falsely shared as incident from Tripura, claiming tribals attacked illegal Bangladeshi immigrants
content: New Delhi, June 7 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it showed tribals in Tripura launching a scathing attack on Bangladeshi immigrants who had entered India illegally. The footage allegedly showed the tribals using traditional bows and arrows to chase away the immigrants. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was falsely linked to India. It originally depicted a political clash in Indonesia's Intan Jaya Regency in December 2024. The old and unrelated video was misleadingly shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An Instagram user, 'freehu_890', shared a video on May 22, purportedly showing tribals in Tripura attacking illegal Bangladeshi infiltrators with bows and arrows. Users claimed the attackers launched the assault to prevent them from entering India. "Ancient Justice! Tripura tribals unleash their bows and arrows against the illegal Bangladeshi infiltrators," the caption along the video read. Here are the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of the keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found numerous social media accounts shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , along with their archived versions viewed here and here respectively: A Google Reverse Image search also led the Desk to a video published on the official YouTube channel of the Tribun Papua, an Indonesian newspaper distribution service. The Desk found that the video published by the news outlet matched the visuals seen in the social media post. However, the details indicated that the incident was unrelated to India and occurred in Indonesia. The title mentioned clashes in Intan Jaya Regency, one of the regencies in the Indonesian province of Central Papua. "TENSE! War between supporters of Intan Jaya Regency Pilkada Candidates," reads the loosely translated English version of the title. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. Below is a composite image highlighting that the content in the viral video matches the video posted on the YouTube channel. Using the above information in the next phase of the investigation, the Desk conducted a thorough keyword search on Google. This led to another video published by Indonesia-based news portal VIVA.CO.ID on its official YouTube channel. The news portal elaborated on the details of the incident, which was said to have occurred in Indonesia on December 7, 2024. The report mentioned that the video depicted political clashes that erupted in Indonesia's Intan Jaya Regency and lasted four hours. "The riot was triggered by suspicions from supporters of candidate pair number 3, Apolos Bagau, who accused candidate pair number 1, Aner Maiseni, of stealing their votes," reads the loosely translated version of the report. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot: The customised keyword search also led the Desk to multiple news reports (links to which can be found here and here ), which stated that the clash involved more than 1,000 people armed with arrows, machetes, stones, and other sharp weapons. The reports further stated that officials managed to calm the tension after intensive negotiations that lasted approximately four hours. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a political clash in Indonesia was falsely shared as an incident from Tripura.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2024 video of crowd dancing on street in Maharashtra falsely shared as recent celebrations after RCB's IPL victory
content: New Delhi, June 9 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a massive crowd dancing on the streets while waving Indian and saffron flags is being widely shared on social media, with users claiming it shows Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) fans celebrating the team's IPL victory in Bengaluru. However, a fact check by the Press Trust of India (PTI) reveals that the video has been online since at least 2024 and was filmed near Shivaji Chowk in Kavlapur, Kolhapur, Maharashtra, not in Bengaluru. It has no connection to RCB or their recent IPL win and was shared with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user named Vivek Shetty shared a video on June 4 depicting a huge crowd dancing on the streets while waving Indian and saffron flags, claiming that it showed RCB fans celebrating their victory in Bengaluru. "1st Celebration Scenes From Bengaluru On RCB's Win. #rcb," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of the keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. One such post can be found here , with its archived version available here Additionally, a Google Reverse Image search led the Desk to an Instagram video from June 30, 2024, uploaded by a user named 'aapal_kolhapur_mh09', featuring similar clips as seen on social media. This clarifies that the video is not recent and has been available online since 2024. The details in the video are mentioned to show people celebrating India's victory against South Africa in the T20 World Cup final held on 29 June 2024. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. After we carefully analysed the recent video in the social media post, we found 'Malkar Sweet Shop' in Marathi in the video, which clarified that the video is not from Bengaluru but Maharashtra. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk then geolocated the spot to Bhausingji Road near Shivaji Chowk, Kavlapur, Kolhapur. The location in the video matches the view on Google Maps Street View. Below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a screenshot highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the geolocation. Though the Desk could not independently verify the exact date when this video was recorded, it is clear that it predates RCB's IPL victory in June 2025. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video has been available on the internet at least since 2024 and was shot near Shivaji Chowk, Kavlapur, Kolhapur in Maharashtra, not in Bengaluru.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of motorcyclists falling into water-filled pit in Sri Lanka falsely linked to India; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 9 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing two people travelling on a motorcycle suddenly falling into a deep pit in the middle of the road was recently shared on social media with the claim that the incident occurred in India. The footage showed bystanders rescuing the individuals from the water-filled pit. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video was falsely linked to India. The incident actually took place in Sri Lanka in September 2023, where a man and his daughter fell into a 16-foot-deep, water-filled pit while riding a motorcycle. The old and unrelated video was misleadingly shared on social media as a recent incident, along with a false claim. Claim An X user, Davinder Pal Singh (@dpsingh1313), shared a video on May 31, allegedly showing an accident caused by poor road conditions in India. The video depicted two people on a motorcycle falling into a deep, water-filled pit in the middle of the road. "What is the point of charging so much tax from Indians? Free swimming and adventure with hospital bills. Thanks to Nitin Gadkari for providing roads better than US standards," the caption along the post read. When this story was published, the video had garnered 355.4k views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of the keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found that multiple social media accounts had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Reverse Image Search also led the Desk to a report published by the Sri Lanka-based news portal Daily Mirror. The report, whose featured image matched one of the keyframes the Desk used for investigation, confirmed that the incident took place near the Gothatuwa Drainage Board in Sri Lanka when a father and his daughter fell into a sinkhole while on their way to school in September 2023. "The incident occurred as they went to school on a motorcycle. The father, daughter, and their motorcycle plunged into the water-filled ditch. However, they were rescued by residents who sprang into action," the report mentioned. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image highlighting that the visuals from the viral video match the featured image of the news report, confirming that the incident occurred in Sri Lanka. Additionally, the reverse image search led the Desk to multiple other news reports, which confirmed the incident depicted in the video to have occurred in Sri Lanka in the Gothatuwa area, where the father-daughter duo fell into a 16-foot-deep pit. Here are links ( Link 1 , Link 2 ) to two such reports. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video showing motorcycle riders falling into a deep pit actually pertains to an incident in Sri Lanka, but was falsely shared as if it occurred in India.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video showing rafting mishap in Bosnia falsely shared as incident from India; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 9 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video purportedly showing a group of people being swept away into a river after their boat capsized during a rafting activity was recently shared on social media, with the claim that the incident occurred in Rishikesh, India. The footage showed a rafting boat with at least six passengers overturning in the river amid a strong current. However, upon investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was unrelated to India. The incident actually took place in Bosnia and Herzegovina in March 2025. The video shows a rafting boat with reportedly six people on board overturning in the Vrbas River amid strong currents. Fortunately, all of the rafters were reported to be safe.
