The old and unrelated video was falsely shared on social media with a misleading claim. Claim An Instagram page named 'theworldixe' shared a video on June 3 purportedly showing a rafting boat with passengers being swept into a river amid heavy streamflow. The user claimed that the incident occurred in Rishikesh, India, and that six passengers were swept away. "Six people were washed away during rafting in Rishikesh," read the text inscribed on the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One keyframe was then run through Google Lens, leading to numerous social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here : The Google Reverse Image search also led the Desk to a news report published by the Bosnia-based news magazine Slobodna Bosna. The report included a video whose visuals matched those of the viral social media video under investigation. However, the accompanying details revealed that the boat mishap occurred on the Vrbas River in the western part of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The report also mentioned that all the passengers were safe. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Below is a composite image highlighting that the content in the viral video matches the video included in the news report. Additionally, the search led the Desk to another report published by Nezavisne Novine, a Bosnian daily newspaper. This report included a detailed video of the incident and a statement by one of the rafters, who confirmed that no casualties occurred and all participants were safe. "There were six of us, and now there are five of us. We're joking, of course — we're all accounted for. We were just waiting for these conditions," one of the rafters mentioned. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a rafting mishap from Bosnia and Herzegovina was falsely shared in the name of India.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of Mumbai train passing through flooded tracks shared in name of Guwahati
content: New Delhi, June 9 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a train moving through heavily waterlogged railway tracks is being widely shared on social media with the claim that it depicts recent flooding in Guwahati. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found that the video is unrelated to Guwahati. The visuals are actually from Mumbai, which experienced severe waterlogging following heavy rainfall. On May 26, 2025, the city received over 250 mm of rain within 13 hours, leading to major disruptions across several areas, including the Masjid railway station. The video has been shared online with a false claim. Claim An Instagram user named Milan Orang shared a video on May 31 depicting severe waterlogging on the railway tracks, through which a train can be seen moving. The user claimed that it showed the flood incident in Guwahati. The post garnered 2,672 likes on social media. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of the keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived version available here and here , respectively. As part of the investigation, the Desk closely monitored the video and found 'CR' written on the train coaches, which stands for 'Central Railways' of which the Mumbai Suburban Railway system is part. Moreover, the train resembled the Mumbai Local. Through our search, we could also find a board that read 'Masjid', a station in Mumbai named 'Masjid Railway Station'. Below is a screenshot highlighting the mentioned findings. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk ran the extracted keyframes through reverse image search and came across a YouTube video uploaded by a user on May 27, 2025. The text reads 'Masjid Mumbai'. Although there was no additional information, it does hint that the video might be from Mumbai and not Guwahati. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports. The search led the Desk to a report by the Times of India published on May 27, 2025. It highlighted that the first monsoon showers of the season threw suburban rail services, especially the Harbour line, out of gear, with waterlogging reported at multiple locations, including Masjid station and CSMT. Over 50 Central Railway services were cancelled, 30 on the Harbour line, 20 on the Main line, and 18 Western Railway services. Several hundred services across CR and WR ran late, stranding thousands of commuters during peak hours," read the report section. Here is the link to the report. Another report by News18 Lokmat was published on their YouTube channel on May 26, 2025, which stated 'Mumbai Local Train Update: Local hit by rain, waterlogging at Masjid Bandar station, latest scenes' Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. However, the Desk could not independently verify the exact time the video was recorded. Based on the available evidence, the viral video is not related to the Assam floods of June 2025. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the waterlogging visuals were from Mumbai and unrelated to the recent floods in Guwahati.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Manipulated video of US President Donald Trump shared to falsely claim he 'announced ban on Elon Musk-owned Tesla Motors' in US
content: New Delhi, June 9 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Days after United States President Donald Trump and tech mogul Elon Musk were locked in a 'social media duel', a video featuring the President was shared on social media, falsely claiming that he had announced a ban on Musk-owned Tesla Motors in the US. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found the video to be AI-manipulated. Trump has made no such announcement. The video was shared on social media with a false claim. Notably, the spat began on Thursday (June 5), when their disagreement over a Republican mega-bill, which advances most of Trump's major domestic policy priorities, escalated into personal attacks. Claim An X user, @exsecular, shared a video on June 8 of US President Donald Trump claiming to announce a ban on the production of Elon Musk-owned Tesla Motors in the US, "effective immediately." In the video, Trump can be heard saying: "Elon stabbed me in the back a couple of days ago and went crazy on his platform X, lying about my involvement in the Epstein files, so I can't have that snake Elon making money in this country while I'm the president." The post clocked 560.4K views and 2.2 K likes. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of the keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived version available here and here , respectively. The Desk first conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports, but the search did not lead us to credible reports of Trump banning the production of Teslas in the country. We then ran the video's keyframes through reverse image search and found the same video on an Instagram post by a user named 'dangerousaireturns'. The post's bio read 'DangerousAi', hinting that the video might be AI-generated. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot highlighting the bio section. Based on the above findings, the Desk ran the video through Deepware, an AI-detection tool. The tool confirmed a substantial presence of AI-generated elements. Below is the screenshot of the result: The Desk then ran the video through Hive Moderation, an AI detection tool. The tool confirmed a substantial presence of AI-generated elements, giving the audio in the clip a higher score than the video element. Below is the screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was AI-generated. It was shared with the false claim that US President Donald Trump announced a ban on Tesla production in the US after an online spat with Elon Musk.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Movie still showing man abducted at gunpoint in Begusarai for forced marriage falsely shared as real incident; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 9 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video purportedly showing a man being abducted in broad daylight at gunpoint by a group of individuals was recently shared on social media, with claims that it depicted a real incident from Begusarai, Bihar. Users alleged that the footage showed a government school teacher being kidnapped at gunpoint for a forced marriage, a malpractice locally known as Pakadua Vivah in Bihar. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found the claim to be false. The footage was from a film shoot, not a real incident. Pakadua Vivah, a malpractice once prevalent in parts of northern India, where men were forcibly married at gunpoint, was only depicted for dramatic purposes. The clip was misleadingly shared on social media as a genuine incident. Claim An X handle with the username @thenewsbasket shared a video on June 6, purportedly showing a government school teacher in Bihar's Begusarai being abducted at gunpoint for a forced marriage, known locally as 'Pakadua Vivah'. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. The video had garnered 812K views and 7.5K likes at the time of publication. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One keyframe was then run through Google Lens, leading to numerous social media posts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. The reverse image search also led the Desk to a video posted on an Instagram handle named @rajanrddfilms. The page's bio describes the account as being managed by a filmmaker, actor, and dancer. Here is the link to the handle, along with a screenshot. Next, continuing the investigation, the Desk found that this handle had posted the same video (as that of viral one) on March 12, confirming in the caption that it was part of a film shoot based on the 'Pakadua Vivah' concept. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the visual match between the viral video and the one posted on the Instagram page: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video showing a man being abducted at gunpoint for a forced marriage in Bihar was staged and part of a film shoot.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of New Year festivities in China falsely shared as RCB fans celebrating IPL 2025 victory
content: New Delhi, June 10 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Following Royal Challengers Bengaluru's (RCB) historic win in IPL 2025, a video was recently shared on social media showing a large crowd releasing balloons into the sky. The user claimed it depicted RCB fans celebrating the team's victory. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video is actually from New Year celebrations in China and has been online since January 1, 2025. It is unrelated to RCB's IPL victory and was falsely shared on social media. Notably, RCB celebrated their maiden IPL title win after 18 years with a grand victory parade in Bengaluru. Tragically, the celebrations turned fatal when a stampede, reportedly due to overcrowding and poor crowd management, led to the deaths of eleven people. Claim An Instagram user named 'Royal Challengers Bengaluru' shared a video on June 4 featuring a large crowd releasing balloons into the sky. The user claimed it showed RCB fans celebrating the team's victory in IPL 2025. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through the InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. When we ran one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found that several other users shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archive versions can be found here and here , respectively. As part of the investigation, we examined the viral video closely and found text in Mandarin hinting that the video's location is not India. Below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk once again ran the keyframes of the video through reverse image search and came across a Facebook post by a user named 'China Marketing' that shared the same video on January 1, 2025, predating the IPL 2025 finals. The caption of the post read: "Happy New Year from China #China" Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk conducted customised keyword searches, which yielded several videos mentioning that the incident happened in China's Nanchang. Below is a screenshot of the same. Notably, Press Trust of India had debunked the uncropped version of the same video when it went viral with the false claim that a large crowd simultaneously released balloons into the sky during the 2025 Prayagraj Maha Kumbh. Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video in the social media post showed New Year celebrations, reportedly in China's Nanchang. It is unrelated to the RCB's victory in IPL 2025.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video of lion walking past man without harming him falsely shared as incident from India; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 11 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported video showing a lion approaching a man sleeping on a road was recently shared on social media. Users claimed the video depicted an incident in India, where a lion approached the sleeping man, sniffed him, and then walked away without causing harm. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video was AI-generated and falsely shared as a real incident. The social media post shared the AI-generated video with a false claim. Claim An Instagram handle with the username 'real_media_spot_official' shared on June 8, a video purportedly showing a lion approaching a man sleeping on the street. The user claimed that the incident occurred in India and that the lion walked away after sniffing the man. "A man sleeping on the street in India narrowly escaped being killed by a lion when the lion approached him, sniffed him, and then walked away," read the caption of the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of the keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found that multiple social media accounts had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. A Google Reverse Image Search also led the Desk to a video published on the YouTube channel, The World of Beasts. The channel shared the same video of a lion approaching a man on June 6. However, based on the details mentioned in the channel's bio, it was indicated that the video might be generated using AI and does not depict real incidents. It is pertinent to note that the channel's bio already mentioned that the content posted there was made using AI assistance. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a composite image highlighting that the content in the viral video matches the video posted by the YouTube channel. Next, taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk ran the video through Cantilux, an AI-detection tool. The results indicated that the content exhibited patterns and artefacts commonly associated with AI-generated media. Below is the screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concludes that the viral video does not depict a real incident. It is, in fact, AI-generated content falsely shared on social media with false claims.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated image falsely claims meeting between fugitive businessman Vijay Mallya and Congress leader Supriya Shrinate; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 11 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported image showing fugitive liquor baron Vijay Mallya sitting next to Congress leader Supriya Shrinate, allegedly taken during an event, was recently shared on social media, with claims suggesting the image was real. However, upon investigation, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the image was AI-generated and falsely circulated on social media to mislead viewers. Claim An X user, Urmila Singh (@Singh26Urmila), shared on June 7 an image purportedly featuring fugitive liquor baron Vijay Mallya sitting next to Congress leader Supriya Shrinate. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of the keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found that multiple social media accounts had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. Next, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to check if any credible news outlets had reported a meeting between the two individuals. However, the search did not yield any such reports that could corroborate the claim. Continuing with the investigation, further the Desk closely examined the image and observed several inconsistencies that strongly suggested it was AI-generated. author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Visa ban on Indians by Saudi Arabia? Temporary Hajj-season visa restriction falsely shared with misleading claim on social media
content: New Delhi, June 11 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A post circulating on social media claims that Saudi Arabia has imposed a visa ban specifically targeting Indian citizens. Many users portrayed it as a diplomatic failure of the Indian government. However, upon investigation, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found the claims to be false and lacking context. In reality, Saudi Arabia temporarily suspended specific categories of visas, not just for India, but for 14 countries, from April 13 to June 9, 2025. This temporary measure was implemented in light of the annual Hajj pilgrimage, a period when millions of people travel to Mecca, and was solely aimed at managing crowd control and preventing unauthorised entries. The social media posts misrepresented this seasonal administrative measure, twisting it into a false narrative to mislead the public and present it as a targeted diplomatic snub. Claim: On June 9, an X user named 'Ayesha' shared a post claiming that Saudi Arabia has banned work visas for Indian citizens. The user further stated that the Modi government has failed to manage foreign relations. India faces another diplomatic setback, as Saudi Arabia stops work visas for Indians. Another poor outcome of modi and jai shankar failed diplomacy.," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation On running the mentioned details in the post through Google search, we found several other users shared identical posts with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. The Desk also found an X post by Congress leader Pawan Khera, who wrote, "Saudi Arabia's visa suspension for 14 countries, including India, is just the latest blow in a steady collapse of India's foreign policy under Modi." His X post also questioned India's foreign policy on other fronts also. Here is the link to the X post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Additionally, as part of the investigation, we scanned the Saudi government's official websites but did not find any such notification or information. Moreover, we came across an X post by the newly launched Fact Check account by the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), which clarified that the Saudi government has not notified regarding a visa ban for Indians. It further stated that, as a matter of practice, Saudi Arabia imposes temporary restrictions on short-term visas during the Hajj season to avoid overcrowding. These restrictions are lifted once the pilgrimage concludes. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, we then conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports to corroborate the abovementioned details. The search led us to a report by Arab Times published on April 8, 2025, which highlighted that Saudi Arabia had announced new travel restrictions, suspending the issuance of certain visa categories to citizens of the same 14 countries. However, this restriction did not apply to Indian pilgrims travelling for Hajj, provided they had obtained the appropriate Hajj visa. Individuals holding valid Hajj permits or intending to get one were allowed to travel to Mecca and Medina for the pilgrimage. "The suspension was aimed specifically at curbing unauthorised entries by individuals attempting to perform Hajj without registration and to manage the large crowds during the pilgrimage season. The affected visa categories included Umrah, business, and family visit visas. The suspension was set to remain in place until mid-June 2025, coinciding with the end of the Hajj," read a report section. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Another report by Live Mint, published on June 10, 2025, noted that the 2025 Hajj pilgrimage had concluded with more than 1.6 million Muslims from over 150 countries participating. With the end of the Hajj, the temporary suspension of short-term visas for the 14 affected countries, including India, was lifted. "In April, to curb unauthorised Hajj pilgrimages and control inbound travel, Saudi Arabia suspended the issue of short-term visas for 14 countries: India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Egypt, Indonesia, Iraq, Nigeria, Jordan, Algeria, Sudan, Ethiopia, Tunisia, Yemen and Morocco," reiterates the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Also, the Desk emailed the Embassy of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in India about a statement they sent, and the article will be updated as soon as we get a response. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Saudi Arabia had temporarily suspended specific visa categories for India and 13 other countries from April 13 to June 9, 2025, coinciding with the Hajj season—the move aimed to prevent overcrowding and unauthorised participation in the pilgrimage.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated photos falsely shared to claim Aamir Khan tied the knot for a third time; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 12 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A photo collage featuring multiple images of Bollywood actor Aamir Khan, dressed as a groom and standing alongside his alleged partner Gauri Spratt, seen in bridal attire, was recently shared on social media. Users claimed that the images were from their recent wedding ceremony. However, upon investigation, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found that three of the four images in the collage were digitally altered using face-swapping technology. In contrast, the fourth image was generated using artificial intelligence (AI). The photos were falsely shared on social media to mislead viewers. Claim A Facebook page named 'Rakshita Talks' shared, on June 6, a collage depicting multiple images of Bollywood actor Aamir Khan and his partner Gauri Spratt, both dressed in bridesmaid and groomsmen's attire. The user claimed the photos were from Bollywood actor Aamir Khan's third wedding with his long-time partner, Gauri Spratt, which was recently held. The social media post also attached a link to a report, which further elaborated on the development. "OMG! 60yrs Aamir Khan Grand Entry at his 3rd wedding with Gauri Spratt after Kiran Rao Divorced," the user shared the collage with the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of the keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found that multiple social media accounts had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk held a customised keyword search on Google to find whether Aamir Khan had initially been tied the knot for a third time. The search result did not yield any credible reports that could corroborate the claim. Next, the Desk carefully cropped the four images depicted in the collage and ran them separately through Google Lens, the results of which can be found below, respectively: Image 1: The image shows Aamir Khan and Gauri Spratt sporting a Telugu wedding look, posing for a camera alongside an elderly couple. Below is a screenshot of the image. Investigation: The Desk ran the image through Google Lens, which led it to a news report published by Hyderabad-based news website SAKSHI.com. As the Desk scanned through the report, it found the image (visually similar to the one currently being investigated) published in the report on June 11, 2023. However, when the Desk inspected the image, it found that the original image showed Telugu actor Sharwanand and his wife posing for the camera during their wedding ceremonies, not Aamir Khan and Gauri Spratt. Sharwanand's face and that of his wife had been digitally swapped to circulate a false claim regarding Aamir Khan's marriage. Here is the link to the report: A comparison image further confirmed the digital replacement of Sharwanand and his wife's faces with those of Aamir Khan and Gauri Spratt. Image 2: The image claims to show South actor Ram Charan attending Aamir Khan's wedding. Below is a screenshot of the image. Investigation: The Desk also used Google Lens to investigate the second image. The search led to a report by the Indian Express, dated June 7, 2023. The post included an image visually similar to the one shared in the viral post. However, upon close examination, it was found that Ram Charan's picture from the wedding was originally from when he attended the wedding of actor Sharwanand to Rakshitha Shetty. Again, Sharwanand and his wife's faces had been digitally swapped with Aamir Khan and Gauri Spratt using AI tools to falsely claim that Aamir Khan had tied the knot for a third time. Here is the link to the report. Below is a comparison image confirming the digital manipulation. Image 3: The image depicts an entirely different wedding setting, where Aamir Khan is dressed in a white sherwani and headgear, while Gauri Spratt sports a heavy lehenga. Below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation: The Desk used Google Image Search to verify the image's authenticity. The search led to a report by India Today, which featured an image similar to the one being investigated. However, a closer analysis revealed that the image originally featured TV actress Shraddha Arya with her husband Rahul from her wedding. Shraddha Arya's and her husband's faces were digitally replaced with those of Aamir Khan and Gauri Spratt. Here is the link to the report: The comparison image shared here confirms the digital manipulation of Shraddha Arya and her husband's wedding image, which has been replaced with the faces of Aamir Khan and Gauri Spratt. Image 4: The image shows Aamir Khan and Gauri Spratt, dressed in traditional costume, posing for the camera. It also shows Aamir Khan holding flowers in his hand. Below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation: As part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the social media image and observed several inconsistencies that strongly suggested it was AI-generated. For instance, subtle distortions in facial features were identifiable in the image, along with an excessive glossy finish — a common characteristic of AI-generated visuals. Below is a screenshot of the same. Using the above inputs, the Desk ran the purported image through Hive Moderation (an AI detection tool). The tool detected a substantial presence of AI-generated elements in the image. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the collage depicting images of Aamir Khan and Gauri Spratt before their marriage is false. Also, the claim that the duo recently got married is untrue.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Passenger-recorded video of 2023 Nepal plane crash falsely shared as footage from recent Air India crash at Ahmedabad airport
content: New Delhi, June 12 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video circulating on social media shows a passenger recording from inside an aircraft, with claims that it is a Facebook Live video captured moments before the recent Air India flight crash in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. The latter part of the video appears to depict turbulence and disturbances inside the aircraft. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video is not recent. It dates back to 2023 and shows the final moments of a Nepal plane crash that was livestreamed on Facebook by a passenger. The video is unrelated to the recent Air India crash near Ahmedabad, which was falsely shared on social media. Notably, the London-bound Air India flight AI 171 crashed shortly after takeoff near Ahmedabad airport on Thursday afternoon. Thick plumes of smoke were seen rising from the crash site. The aircraft, carrying 242 passengers and crew members, was en route to London when the incident occurred. Claim An X user named 'Honest Cricket Lover' shared a video featuring a recording by a passenger onboard an aircraft on June 12. The user claimed it to be a Facebook live moments before the Air India flight that crashed in Gujarat's Ahmedabad a few hours ago. The video later depicted turbulence and disturbance of the aircraft. "Facebook live video before Ahmedabad ,Gujrat plane crash," read the post's caption. The post clocked 146.4k views on social media. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of the keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found numerous social media accounts shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. Notably, the same video was also shared by Bharat Samachar, a Hindi news channel, with the caption that it was a Facebook live video moments before the tragic plane crash near Ahmedabad, Gujarat. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. As part of the investigation, the Desk ran the keyframes of the viral video through Reverse Image Search and came across a report by Al Arabiya English published on January 16, 2023, featuring the same video as seen in the social media post. The report's publication date highlights that the video is not recent and is not associated with the Ahmedabad plane crash incident. Moreover, as per Al Arabiya English, it was a Facebook live of a passenger on a flight that crashed in Nepal. "Taken just minutes before the ill-fated Yeti Airlines aircraft crashed, the video, which was streamed on Facebook Live, showed the now-deceased passenger smiling as he captured scenes from the inside and outside of the plane. It showed the moment the plane crashed into a gorge and caught fire. As the camera continued to roll, it caught glimpses of the plane going up in flames for at least 30 seconds, when the screams of panicked passengers could be heard," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a set of combination images highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the one used by the news portal. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk then conducted a set of customised keyword searches, which led us to another report by El Paris published on January 17, 2023. This report featured the same visuals as seen in the social media post. The report highlighted that footage recorded by a passenger on board the aeroplane that crashed in Nepal shows how the aircraft tilted sharply in the air seconds before crashing to the ground. "The failed landing killed 69 of the 72 people on board, making it the country's deadliest aeroplane accident in three decades," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Another report by India Today, dated January 16, also carried the same video, which clarifies that it is not recent and unrelated to the Air India plane crash in Gujarat. The headline of the report read: "Nepal plane crash: Indian passenger captures final moments on FB Live" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Notably, London-bound Air India passenger flight AI 171 crashed shortly after takeoff near Ahmedabad airport on Thursday afternoon. Thick plumes of smoke were seen rising from the crash site. The aircraft, carrying 242 passengers and crew members, was en route to London when the incident occurred. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to at least 2023 when a Nepal plane crashed while an Indian passenger captured the final moments on Facebook Live. It is unrelated to the recent incident of the Air India plane crash in Gujarat.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video showing Hindu priest riding a crocodile falsely shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 13 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media claims to show a man dressed in orange robes calmly sitting on a crocodile's back in the middle of a water body. Users alleged that the man was a Hindu priest being taken by the crocodile to a temple. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the video and confirmed it was AI-generated. The investigation revealed that the video does not depict a real incident and was falsely shared online with a misleading narrative. Claim An X user, Disha Rajput (@DishaRajput24), shared a video on June 11 showing a man dressed in orange robes riding on a crocodile's back. The user claimed he was a Hindu priest being taken by the crocodile to a temple, while the former sits on his back. "See the power of Sanatan Dharma. The user wrote in the caption, " This crocodile takes the priest Maharaj to the temple on its back. " When this report was published, the video had garnered 601.7k views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of these keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found several social media accounts shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. A Google Reverse Image Search also led the Desk to a video published on the YouTube channel Dark Files. The same video of a priest riding on a crocodile's back was uploaded on June 9. However, according to the channel's bio, the content is created using AI tools and does not depict real events. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. A combination image was created to highlight that the viral video matches the one posted on the YouTube channel. Next, based on these findings, the Desk further analysed the viral video and observed several inconsistencies strongly suggesting that it was AI-generated. For instance, the background setting appeared highly unrealistic and unlikely to depict a real-life scenario. To verify this further, the Desk used Cantilux, an AI-detection tool, which confirmed that a substantial part of the video contained AI-generated content. Below is a screenshot of the result: Additionally, the video was tested using Hive Moderation, another AI-detection tool, which also concluded that a significant part of the video consists of AI-generated content. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a Hindu priest riding on a crocodile's back to reach a temple is not real and has been generated using AI.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Fabricated graphic claiming Kangana Ranaut criticised BJP falsely shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 13 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media graphic carrying an alleged quote from BJP's Mandi MP and Bollywood actor Kangana Ranaut was recently shared online. Users claimed that the post, which featured the logo of News 24, quoted the first-time MP Kangana Ranaut launching a scathing attack on the Bharatiya Janata Party. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found that the graphic attributed to News 24 was fabricated. Not only did the Mandi MP not make such a statement, but News 24 also issued a clarification confirming the post was fake and urged users to report it. Claim An X user, Nidhi Ambedkar (@nidhiambedkar), shared a social media post on June 12 that allegedly carried a quote from BJP's Mandi MP Kangana Ranaut. The graphic, which bore the News 24 logo, claimed that Ranaut had criticised the Bharatiya Janata Party for its supposed divide-and-rule stance. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the social media graphic through Google Lens, which led it to multiple social media posts sharing the same graphic with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. Next, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to verify whether Kangana Ranaut had ever made the alleged statement. If the quote had been genuine, it would likely have been widely reported by credible news outlets. However, the search yielded no credible reports or official statements attributing such remarks to Kangana Ranaut. Further, the Desk examined the official social media handle of News 24 Digital, under whose logo the graphic had been shared. While no such post carrying the alleged statement was found on the channel's official feed, the Desk did find a clarification post issued by News 24, stating that the viral graphic was fake. Sharing the same fabricated graphic bearing the false quote attributed to Kangana Ranaut, News 24 wrote: "This fake post is being circulated in the name of News 24. Please report it instead of spreading it." Here is the link and archive link to the clarification post, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral graphic allegedly quoting BJP's Mandi MP Kangana Ranaut and attributing it to News 24 is fake.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Unrelated video of building fire in Delhi falsely linked to Air India flight crash in Ahmedabad; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 13 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing thick smoke emerging from what appears to be a residential building was recently shared on social media, with a claim linking it to the June 12 Air India plane crash incident in Ahmedabad. The user claimed the video depicted visuals from the Air India plane (Flight AI171) crash site in Ahmedabad. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found that it was unrelated to the Ahmedabad plane tragedy. Instead, it depicted a fire incident that occurred on June 10 in Delhi's Dwarka Sector 13. The video showed a tragic moment when three members of a family jumped from their balcony as a fire engulfed their multi-storied building. An unrelated incident from Delhi was falsely shared on social media linking it to the Ahmedabad plane crash tragedy. Claim An X user, 'Unfiltered_Arjun' (@arjun_0022), shared a video on June 12, claiming it showed visuals from the site where an Air India flight (AI171) — carrying 242 passengers and crew — had crashed in Ahmedabad shortly after takeoff. The video showed thick smoke billowing from the top floor of a multi-storeyed residential building. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. When the story was published, the video had garnered 303K views. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of the keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found numerous social media accounts shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Reverse Image search also led the Desk to a video published on the official YouTube channel of The Indian Express dated June 10. The video depicted the same visuals (of the top floor of a multi-storied building erupting into fire) as seen in the viral video. However, the accompanying details revealed that the video showed a fire incident that occurred in Delhi. "A fire broke out in a flat on the 7th floor of Sabad Apartment, located in Dwarka Sector 13 near MRV School, on June 10," the details read. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting that the content in the viral video matched the video posted by the news portal on its YouTube channel. Next, taking cues from the above inputs, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to learn more about the fire tragedy that occurred in Dwarka Sector 13 on June 10. The search results led the Desk to a report published by Hindustan Times elaborating on the incident. The report stated that the video depicted a fire incident that occurred in Delhi's Dwarka Sector 13 area, where the top floor of a multi-storied residential building erupted into flames. Three people from a family also died in the incident after they jumped from their balcony in an attempt to escape the fire but were declared dead by doctors. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search on Google—this time to gather more information about the Ahmedabad plane tragedy and the visuals circulated after the incident. The search results led the Desk to an X post from the official account of Press Trust of India, which, while elaborating on the incident, shared images from the crash site. The post also included images showing how the passenger plane hit the medical college complex and reduced it to rubble. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video showing thick smoke from a residential building was not related to the Air India plane crash in Ahmedabad. It in fact showed a fire incident that occurred in Delhi's Dwarka Sector 13 on June 10.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, this video doesn't show bodies of Ahmedabad plane crash victims; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 16 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): In the aftermath of the tragic plane crash in Ahmedabad that claimed the lives of around 270 people, including several foreign nationals, on June 12, a video recently circulated on social media claimed to show visuals from inside a facility where the mortal remains of the victims were being kept. The footage showed bodies placed in caskets and covered with white cloth. However, upon investigation, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the video is unrelated to the Ahmedabad plane crash. The footage had been available online since May 2025, well before the tragedy occurred, and was reportedly from Pakistan. An unrelated video from Pakistan was falsely shared on social media in connection with the Ahmedabad incident. Meanwhile, it is pertinent to note that 270 people died in the crash of the London-bound flight from Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport. The aircraft went down shortly after takeoff, crashing into a nearby medical college campus in the Meghaninagar area. Authorities have confirmed that an investigation is currently underway to determine the cause of the accident. Claim An X user, Surendra Choudhary (@Surendr71280822), shared a video on June 14 purportedly showing visuals from inside a facility where the mortal remains of the victims of the Ahmedabad plane crash were being kept. The footage showed bodies placed in caskets and covered with white cloth. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of these keyframes in a Google Lens Search, the Desk found several social media accounts shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Reverse Image search also led the Desk to an Instagram handle named 'itz_army_jaat_01', where it found a video identical to the one circulating on social media had been posted. However, upon close analysis, the Desk found that the video had been published on May 13, 2025 — i.e., days before the Ahmedabad tragedy (which occurred on June 12). Furthermore, the details accompanying the video also suggested that it was from Pakistan, and not India. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Additionally, the Desk also came across several other videos during its search, all showing visuals similar to the viral clip and claiming to be from Pakistan. These videos had been posted on various dates throughout May, clearly indicating they were not related to the Ahmedabad plane crash tragedy. Here is the link and archive link to one such Instagram post. While the Desk could not independently verify whether the video was initially filmed in Pakistan, however, based on the publishing date of the video—May 2025—it was confirmed that the footage predates the June 12 tragedy. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the social media video claiming to show the mortal remains of the Ahmedabad plane crash victims was old and unrelated to the incident. It was falsely linked to the tragedy and had been available online since May 2025.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated photo showing Hyderabad's Charminar submerged in water falsely shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 17 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported photo showing the area near Charminar in Hyderabad submerged in water was recently shared on social media, with the claim that it depicted the Musi River flood that claimed 15,000 lives in September 1980. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the image and found that it was AI-generated and falsely shared on social media as a real photograph. Claim A purported photo showing the area near Charminar in Hyderabad inundated with water was shared by a Facebook user, 'Syed Saleem_Original,' on June 10. The user claimed that the picture was from the Musi River flood that killed 15,000 people. "#Devastating Musi River Floods 28 September 1908. A rare historical photograph showing the catastrophic floods that submerged parts of Hyderabad, claiming over 15,000 lives and reshaping the city's future," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through Reverse Image Search and found several other users shared the same photo with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. As part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the picture in the social media post and found a 'Meta AI' watermark at the bottom right corner. Images generated using Meta's AI tools include this watermark to indicate that artificial intelligence has created or altered them. This highlights that the image is not real. Furthermore, we also found several discrepancies like unclear signboards, blurry and indistinct faces of people, and a general lack of realistic detail and structure. Below is a screenshot highlighting the findings. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk ran the photo through 'Was It AI', an AI detection tool. The tool detected a substantial presence of AI-generated elements in both images. Below are the screenshots of the results. The Desk also ran the photo through Hive Moderation, another AI-detecting tool. The tool detected a substantial presence of AI-generated elements in both images. Below are the screenshots of the results. Moreover, Hyderabad experienced the tragic 1908 Musi river floods, which took place between 28-29 September that year. Hyderabad recorded rains of 12.8 inches in 24 hours and a staggering 18.90 inches in 48 hours, resulting in the city's worst floods in its recorded history. Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the photo in the social media post is AI-generated.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2020 video of smoke-filled aeroplane cabin falsely linked to Ahmedabad plane crash; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 17 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing smoke filling an aeroplane cabin as passengers scream in panic was recently shared on social media with the claim that it was linked to the tragic plane crash that occurred in Ahmedabad on June 12. Users alleged that the footage depicted scenes from inside the doomed AI-171 aircraft moments before it crashed after taking off from Ahmedabad's Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found it false. The footage actually shows an incident from 2020, involving a Ryanair flight in which smoke filled the cabin, causing panic among passengers. That flight made an emergency landing shortly after takeoff from Bucharest. An old, unrelated video was falsely shared on social media, misleadingly linking it to the Ahmedabad plane crash. Claim An X handle with the username @vdmempire shared a video on June 12, claiming it showed the last visuals from inside the London-bound Air India flight (AI171) moments before it crashed in Ahmedabad. The video showed thick smoke filling the aircraft's cabin, while passengers screamed in panic. "The last moment before the Air India crash," the caption shared with the video read. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. When this story was published, the video had garnered 712k views. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of the keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found numerous social media accounts shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. A Google Reverse Image search also led the Desk to a video posted by the X handle @TheWapplehouse on March 17, 2023. The video matched the viral clip and was shared well before the Ahmedabad plane crash. Additional context from the post confirmed that the footage was from inside a Ryanair aircraft during a 2020 incident when smoke filled the cabin shortly after takeoff, prompting fear and confusion among those on board. "Smoke fills the cabin of a Ryanair flight moments after takeoff (January 2020)," read the caption shared with the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting how the content in the viral video matches that of the video posted on X. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above inputs, the Desk held a customised keyword search on Google to gather more details about the Ryanair flight incident. The search led the Desk to a video published on the official Facebook page of the UK-based portal Daily Mail. On March 17, 2023, the page posted a video identical to the viral one and the X video that emerged during the investigation. Its details further confirmed that the footage depicted moments inside a Ryanair flight, where terrified passengers screamed and cried as thick smoke poured into the aeroplane cabin just moments after the Boeing 737-800 took off from the Romanian capital of Bucharest. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot. Additionally, the customised keyword search led the Desk to a news report published by the UK-based portal Metro. The report stated that the video being investigated was linked to the Ryanair plane incident, in which smoke filled the aeroplane cabin, causing panic among passengers. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video showing the final moments inside Air India Flight AI171 was, in fact, an old and unrelated video from 2020, which was now misleadingly linked to the Ahmedabad plane crash tragedy.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Satirical post about Apple firing lead designer falsely shared on social media as real news
content: New Delhi, June 17 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A widely circulated social media post claimed that Apple had fired digital entrepreneur Jon Yongfook and his team following the launch of the new 'Liquid Glass' design for iOS 26. The claim originated from Yongfook's own X account and was subsequently picked up by several news portals. However, a fact-check by the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false. Upon further examination, the Desk found a clarification from Jon Yongfook himself, stating that his earlier post about being sacked was intended as satire. The satirical content was misinterpreted and misleadingly shared as factual. Claim An X user, 'RVCJ Media,' shared a post on June 11 claiming that Jon Yongfook, who allegedly worked for Apple, was fired by the company following the unveiling of the new 'Liquid Glass' design for iOS 26. The text in the post read: "APPLE HAS FIRED JON YONGFOOK, THE LEAD DESIGNER BEHIND THE NEW LIQUID GLASS INTERFACE, JUST HOURS AFTER ITS WWDC 2025 LAUNCH. HE SAID THE TEAM SPENT 18 MONTHS PERFECTING THE GAUSSIAN BLUR EFFECT…" The post clocked 32k views, 1.8k likes. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral post through Reverse Image Search and found several other users shared information in their social media posts. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived version can be viewed here and here . Notably, our search also resulted in an X post by digital entrepreneur Jon Yongfook dated June 10, 2025. In the post, he wrote that he and his team spent the last 18 months tirelessly testing different levels of Gaussian blur on backgrounds when foreground elements are in focus, but Apple fired them. "I was fired by Apple today. My design team and I have spent the last 18 months tirelessly testing different levels of Gaussian blur on backgrounds when foreground elements are in focus. If you are looking for experts in the blur, glass liquid, grass or fur UI space, lmk," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Following his X post, multiple media outlets, such as Republic TV, News 24, and Gadgets 360 Hindi, based their articles on the above-mentioned post. Here are the links to Republic TV , News 24 , and Gadgets 360 Hindi posts, with archived versions available here , here , and here , respectively. The Desk scanned the official accounts like LinkedIn and X of Jon Yongfook, and there was no mention of him working at Apple or leading a design team. His bio states he is the founder of Bannerbear, a SaaS platform for automated image generation, and a former employee of Aviva. Here is the link to his LinkedIn and X account . On further scanning his X account, we found a clarification post in which he mentioned that his earlier post citing his being sacked was a 'satire'. "Bless all of you who recognised this as satire. I've been enjoying the puns. I've been an Apple user for 20+ years, and this is the worst UI I've seen. I hope they tweak it. To be perfectly transparent, this is overwhelming my notifications now, so I'm putting the thread on mute," read the post. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the social media post's claim was false and a 'satirical' post.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of Bharuch factory fire falsely shared linking it to recent Ahmedabad Air India plane crash
content: New Delhi, June 17 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a building engulfed in flames with thick black smoke billowing out was recently circulated on social media, falsely claiming to depict the aftermath of the June 12, 2025, Air India plane crash in Ahmedabad. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video predates the Ahmedabad crash. It actually shows a massive fire that broke out at a factory in Bharuch, Gujarat, on April 14, 2025. The footage is unrelated to the Air India Flight AI171 tragedy. Notably, the horrific crash of Air India Flight AI171 on Thursday, June 12, 2025, has left the nation in mourning. The confirmed death toll now stands at 279. The London-bound Boeing 787-8 Dreamliner, carrying 242 people, crashed into the BJ Medical College hostel complex shortly after takeoff, killing 241 passengers and crew on board, along with 38 people on the ground. Only one passenger, Vishwash Kumar Ramesh, miraculously survived and is currently recovering. According to officials, the grim task of identifying the victims relies heavily on DNA analysis, as many bodies were severely damaged or charred. As of Saturday night, 19 victims had been formally identified, with forensic teams working around the clock. Claim An Instagram user, 'so_mya3726', shared a video on June 14 showing a building engulfed in flames with thick black smoke emanating from it. The user claimed that the video shows the aftermath of the 12 June 2025 Ahmedabad plane crash. "242 people died in the crash and 20 doctors were killed in the hostel building," read the text on the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of the keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found numerous social media accounts shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. On closely analysing the video, the Desk found a logo of ABC News and then ran the extracted keyframes through reverse image search. It came across a Facebook post by ABC News 24×7, dated April 14, 2025, which predated the tragic Ahmedabad plane crash. As per the post, the fire broke out at a company in Bharuch, Gujarat. This confirms that the video is unrelated to the incident. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across several reports that covered the incident. One such report by ABP News dated April 14, 2025, stated that a massive fire broke out in a company in Bharuch, Gujarat. On receiving the information, the fire brigade vehicles reached the spot and started trying to control the fire. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Another report by TV9 Bharatvarsh, dated April 14, 2025, featured the same video as seen in the social media post but from a different angle. The report mentioned a fire in a factory in Bharuch, Gujarat. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video pre-dated the Air India plane crash in Ahmedabad and shows a massive fire that broke out in a factory in Bharuch, Gujarat.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Unrelated video from Bangladesh falsely shared as BSF constable beating man for selling Bangladeshi flag in West Bengal; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 17 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it showed a Border Security Force (BSF) constable brutally thrashing a man—allegedly a flag seller—in India. The users claimed that the incident occurred in West Bengal, where the BSF constable was seen beating the individual with a stick for selling the Bangladeshi flag. However, upon investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false. The video actually shows an incident that took place in Dhaka, where Bangladesh Army personnel resorted to a lathi charge to disperse a large crowd that had gathered outside the Bangabandhu National Stadium during a football match. The flag seller happened to be present at the scene and was hit during the crackdown. An unrelated video from Bangladesh was falsely shared on social media as one depicting an incident in India. Claim An X handle with the username '@desi_thug1' shared a video on June 15, claiming it showed a BSF constable brutally thrashing an individual in West Bengal for selling a Bangladesh flag. "Abdul selling the Bangladeshi flag in West Bengal... BSF constable gave him the best treatment," the user wrote in the caption. When this story was published, the video had garnered 709.2k views and 12k likes. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of the keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found numerous social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here respectively: The Google Reverse Image Search also led the Desk to a video posted on the official YouTube channel of the Bangladesh-based news portal Dhaka Post. The visuals in that video (showing an individual in military uniform thrashing a flag seller) matched those seen in the viral clip. However, the details confirmed that the video depicted an incident in Dhaka, not India. The video news report stated the incident occurred on June 10, when the Bangladesh Army resorted to a lathi charge to disperse a large crowd gathered outside the Bangabandhu National Stadium during a football match. The flag seller, who was happened to be present at the scene was hit during the crackdown. The report also mentioned that the Bangladesh Army had later expressed regret over the incident (of the flag vendor being beaten) and had also offered him compensation of 1 lakh Taka. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting that the content in the viral video matched the video posted by the news portal on its YouTube channel. Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find elaborate details about the incident. The search result led the Desk to several news reports (both video and text-based) confirming that the viral video showed an incident in Bangladesh, not India. Links to two such posts can be found here and here . Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video showing a uniformed individual attacking a flag seller is from Bangladesh, not India. It depicts a Bangladesh Army personnel dispersing a crowd (the flag seller was also part of it) outside a Dhaka stadium, not a BSF constable in West Bengal.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of Quran found in fire-damaged room falsely linked to recent Ahmedabad plane crash; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 17 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): In the aftermath of the tragic plane crash in Ahmedabad that claimed the lives of around 270 people, including several foreign nationals, on June 12, a video recently circulated on social media claimed to show a Quran, the holy Islamic scripture, mostly undamaged, found in the debris near the crash site. The user alleged that while everything else was destroyed or burned in the fire caused by the crash, the Quran miraculously remained intact. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it unrelated to the Ahmedabad plane crash. The investigation revealed that the video had been available online since March 2025, months before the tragedy occurred. An old and unrelated video was falsely circulated on social media, linking it to the Ahmedabad plane crash incident. Claim An X user, Sufiyaan._ (@Sufiyaan873), shared a video on June 15 claiming that a Quran, mostly undamaged, was recovered from the debris of the Air India flight that crashed in Ahmedabad. The user wrote that the holy book survived without damage while everything else was destroyed in the plane crash fire. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of these keyframes in a Google Lens Search, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, to corroborate the claim made in the social media post, the Desk carefully analysed the video and found a major discrepancy. The Desk found that the video depicted the interior of a fire-damaged room, not an aircraft crash site from where the Quran was recovered. Below is a screenshot from the video showing the surroundings (a fire-gutted room) where the Quran was recovered: Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk ran the keyframes generated earlier through Google Reverse Image Search. The search results led the Desk to an Instagram page named 'beautiful__islam_0', which had posted a video matching the visuals seen in the viral clip. On comparing the details, it was found that the video had been uploaded on March 9, 2025, months before the Boeing 787-8 aircraft crashed shortly after takeoff from Ahmedabad airport on June 12. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Additionally, the search result led the Desk to several other media accounts that shared the same video, though none identified the exact location of the incident. Notably, all these posts were made in March 2025, confirming that the footage predates the Ahmedabad plane crash. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. Although the Desk could not independently verify the location where the video was originally filmed, it conclusively established that the video had no connection to the recent Ahmedabad plane crash. The footage has been online since March 2025 and was falsely linked to the recent tragedy to mislead viewers.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2003 Baghdad bombing footage misrepresented as Iran's recent attack on Israel
content: New Delhi, June 18 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video showing several explosions occurring simultaneously in the same area, claiming it depicted Iran's largest assault on Israel to date — a strike allegedly powerful enough to shake the entire region. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video is not recent. It dates back to 2003 and shows Baghdad, Iraq, during the U.S.-led "Shock and Awe" bombing campaign. The footage has been misleadingly shared as if it were from a recent incident. The United States invaded Iraq in March 2003, launching a massive "shock and awe" campaign that lit up the skies, devastated large parts of the country, and paved the way for American ground troops to converge on Baghdad. The invasion was justified at the time by claims that Saddam Hussein possessed weapons of mass destruction — claims that were later proven false, as no such weapons were ever found. Claim An X user shared a video showing multiple explosions at different places in the same area, 'Savage Spit', on June 17, claiming that it depicted Iran's biggest assault on Israel to date, a seismic strike that's shaken the region. "🚨 BREAKING: This marks Iran's biggest assault on Israel to date, a seismic strike that's shaken the region. Iran has upped the ante, moving at a pace Israel is struggling to match. The ball is now in Israel's court… but will they rise to the occasion or be forced to bite the bullet? #IranIsraelWar #MiddleEast #Breaking #WarAlert #Tehran #IDF #IRGC #Iran #Pakistan #Israel #Palestine #Unity #İranisrail #طهران #اسریل #tahran #ایران #Netanyahu #NetanyahuWarCriminal #TelAviv #America #iranisraelwar #IsraelTerroristState #haifa #Gaza #OperationTruePromise3 #WW3," read the post's caption. The post clocked 1.6 million views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of the keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found numerous social media accounts shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . The Desk ran the keyframes of the video through reverse image search and came across an X post dated March 19, 2023, clarifying that the video is not recent and has been on the internet since 2023. Moreover, the video in the post was similar to the recent post shared on social media, Iran's attack on Israel. As per the 2023 post, the U.S and Allied Forces launched an all-out bombing on the city of Baghdad in the middle of the night. "Today, 19 March 2003: Operation 'Shock and Awe' over Iraq's Capital city. U.S and Allied Forces launched an all-out bombing on the city of Baghdad in the middle of the night." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. On further scanning the search results, the Desk found a report by The Atlantic, an American magazine, which carried a part of the video shared on social media. As per the caption on the picture, it showed government buildings in Baghdad on March 21, 2003, during a massive U.S.-led airstrike on the Iraqi capital. "Smoke covers government buildings in Baghdad on March 21, 2003, during a massive U.S.-led airstrike on the Iraqi capital, part of what was billed as a "shock and awe" campaign. Smoke billowed from a number of targeted sites, including one of President Saddam Hussein's palaces, an AFP correspondent said," read the caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports and came across a report by CNN published on their official YouTube channel, which mentioned that the visuals show the "Operation Shock and Awe: Iraq, 2003" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video dates back to 2003 and is from Baghdad, Iraq, during 'Shock and Awe' in 2003, which was shared as a recent incident.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old AIIMS heli-ambulance crash video shared in name of recent Kedarnath chopper tragedy; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 18 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Days after seven people lost their lives in a tragic helicopter crash while flying from the Kedarnath temple to Guptkashi in Uttarakhand, a video showing a damaged helicopter surfaced on social media. Users claimed the footage depicted the helicopter that crashed near Gaurikund on June 15, 2025. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found it to be false. The video in question is unrelated to the recent incident. It actually shows a heli-ambulance from AIIMS Rishikesh that crash-landed in May 2025. The footage was misleadingly shared as being from the June 2025 Gaurikund crash. Claim A Facebook user named 'Dataram Khinchi' shared a video on June 15 featuring the dilapidated condition of a helicopter, claiming it shows the helicopter that crashed in Gaurikund, Uttarakhand, on June 15, 2025. "Kedarnath Helicopter Crash: Helicopter coming from Kedarnath to Guptkashi crashes, seven dead; Heli service banned for two days. A major accident took place on Sunday during the Chardham Yatra in Uttarakhand. A helicopter coming from Kedarnath Dham to Guptkashi crashed in the Gaurikund area. Seven people, including a 23-month-old child, died in the tragic accident. After the accident, heli service has been banned for two days," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of the keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found numerous social media accounts shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here and its archived version can be found here and here As part of the investigation, the Desk ran the extracted keyframes through reverse image search and came across a Facebook post by ET Now News, dated May 17, 2025, featuring the same visuals, confirming that the video predates and is unrelated to the June 15, 2025, helicopter crash in Gaurikund, Uttarakhand. The post mentions that the video shows a separate incident involving a helicopter from AIIMS Rishikesh's heli ambulance service that crash-landed in Kedarnath after its rear section was damaged. A major tragedy was averted, and all three people on board, the captain, a doctor, and a medical staff member, escaped unharmed. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports and came across a PTI report from The Hindu on May 17, 2025. The report's display image was similar to the one shared on social media. As per the description, it was a damaged helicopter of AIIMS Rishikesh's heli ambulance service after it crashed while landing at Kedarnath, in Rudraprayag district, Uttarakhand, on May 17, 2025. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a May 2025 video of an AIIMS Rishikesh heli ambulance crash-landing was shared as a June 2025 Gaurikund helicopter crash incident.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Viral video of biker falling into waterlogged pothole during TV reporter's live coverage detected as AI-generated by Google's SynthID
content: New Delhi, June 18 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video circulating on social media shows a purported TV news reporter covering the impact of heavy rainfall in what is claimed to be a marginalised area of Mexico City. In the latter part of the clip, a man riding a motorcycle is seen being swept away by severe waterlogging. The dramatic footage shows the reporter, dressed in a yellow raincoat, reporting live in front of a large, water-filled pothole or road collapse caused by the flooding. As the camera rolls, the biker unknowingly drives straight into the hidden gorge, vanishing into the water. The incident appears to unfold in real time, with the reporter seemingly witnessing it live on air while discussing the dangers posed by poor drainage and road maintenance during heavy rains. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the video using SynthID—a tool developed by Google DeepMind that embeds digital watermarks into AI-generated content across images, audio, text, and video. The tool detected that both the visuals and the audio were created using Google AI. SynthID watermarks were identified throughout the video and audio content, confirming that the footage was artificially generated. The video was falsely shared as real on social media. Notably, PTI is among the early adopters of the SynthID Detector, which successfully identified hidden pixel-level watermarks in a screenshot extracted from the video under review. Claim: A video featuring a reporter allegedly reporting about excessive rain in Mexico City, claiming it to be from a marginalised area, was shared by an X user named 'Yamlikha_8' on June 16. Later in the video, a man riding a bike gets swept into the waterlogged portion. "Rain is very heavy here in Mexico City, and this marginalised area was oh. Another one is gone," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of the keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found numerous social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be found here and here As part of the investigation, the Desk found inconsistencies in the video. For instance, the man on the bike disappeared in a waterlogged portion, and the logo on the reporter's mic looked suspicious. Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the video through Google DeepMind's SynthID, a tool created by Google DeepMind that integrates digital watermarks into AI-generated content—such as images, audio, text, or video—within Google's generative AI products.
