Embedded watermarks are undetectable to the human eye but can be identified using Google's proprietary detection tools. Moreover, Press Trust of India is among the early users of the SynthID Detector, which successfully spotted hidden, pixel-level watermarks in a screenshot from the video under review. When the Desk uploaded the video to the SynthID detector to investigate it, the tool, which is made by Google AI, said, "SynthID detected in all or part of the uploaded content." Below is a screenshot of the result. The Desk uploaded an image to the SynthID detector to investigate it. The tool, which is made by Google AI, said, "SynthID detected in all or part of the uploaded content." Below is a screenshot of the result. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk took a screenshot of the video and uploaded it to the image section of the SynthID tool. The tool again said, "SynthID detected in all or parts of the content uploaded." The blue areas highlighted in the first photo from the Left say, "SynthID watermarks were detected in blue areas." We can see that it captures the maximum area of the screenshot taken from the video in question. The screenshot of the SynthID image detection results can be seen below: In the subsequent part of the investigation, the Desk extracted the audio from the viral video and uploaded the audio file in the audio section of the SynthID detection tool. When we searched for the results, the tool again said that SynthID was detected in all or parts of the content, as it said for the image and the video earlier. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video and the audio shared on social media are fabricated and AI-generated.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: This video of visibly distressed man seated inside an airplane not related to recent Ahmedabad plane crash; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 19 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a visibly distressed man seated inside an airplane cabin while the aircraft experiences severe turbulence was recently shared on social media, with claims that it captured the final moments of passengers aboard the ill-fated Air India flight AI 171 before it crashed in Ahmedabad on June 12, killing 270 people. The man was seen praying for his safety, while panicked screams from other passengers could be heard in the background. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the footage and found it to be unrelated to the Ahmedabad plane crash. The video has been available online since May 2025, nearly a month before the tragic incident occurred. An old and unrelated video was falsely circulated on social media, misleadingly linking it to the recent tragedy in Ahmedabad. Claim An X handle with the username @khaaan_0 shared a video on June 13, claiming it showed passengers' final moments aboard the ill-fated AI 171 before it crashed in Ahmedabad on June 12. The video showed a man seemingly distressed and worried for safety as the aircraft experienced major turbulence. The video also captured the screams of other passengers who appeared to be in panic. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of these keyframes in a Google Lens Search, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Reverse Image search also led the Desk to an Instagram handle named 'preetijain523'. The Desk found that the user had posted the same video seen in the viral post. However, further details revealed the video was posted on May 21, 2025, days before the Ahmedabad plane crash tragedy occurred. Here is the link and archive link to the video, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting that the content in the viral video matched the video posted by the Instagram handle. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the video and made a significant observation: the visuals of an aircraft cabin seen in the viral video did not match the interiors of any Air India aircraft. Instead, the cabin featured blue seat designs, which are standard in IndiGo flights. In contrast, Air India's aircraft interiors include deep red, aubergine, and gold tones, along with a chakra-inspired design. Below is a comparison image showing the blue-colored seats in the viral video, which match IndiGo's standard cabin interior. Additionally, as a part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search to check if any IndiGo flight had experienced turbulence around May 2025. The search led to a report by The First Post, which confirmed that an IndiGo flight from Delhi to Srinagar experienced severe turbulence on May 21. "Panic and screams broke out on an IndiGo flight from Delhi to Srinagar with over 220 passengers on board due to severe turbulence on May 21 amid a hailstorm in the region. Videos shared on social media showed distressed passengers, many offering prayers, as the aircraft shook mid-air," the report mentioned. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. While the Desk could not independently confirm whether the viral video was filmed on the exact Delhi–Srinagar IndiGo flight, it confirmed through a detailed investigation that the video was not related to the Ahmedabad Air India plane crash. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was falsely circulated on social media concerning the recent Ahmedabad plane crash tragedy.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Oct 2024 video of passenger ferry capsizing in Congo falsely shared as recent boat accident in Goa; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 19 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video purportedly showing a boat overcrowded with passengers capsizing in a water body was recently circulated on social media with claims that the incident occurred in India. The user alleged that the passenger boat had capsized in the sea off Goa, leaving 64 people missing. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found the claim false. The video actually depicts an incident that took place at Lake Kivu in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo in October 2024, where an overcrowded ferry capsized, resulting in the deaths of 78 people. An old and unrelated video was misleadingly shared on social media to misinform viewers. Claim An Instagram user, 'LK Gautam Mathura', shared on June 14 a purported video showing an overcrowded boat capsizing in a water body. The user claimed the video depicted an incident that occurred in Goa, where a passenger boat capsized in the sea, leaving 64 people missing. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. When this story was published, the video had garnered 92,449 likes. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of these keyframes in a Google Lens Search, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Reverse Image search also led the Desk to a video posted on the official YouTube channel of the news portal Firstpost on October 4, 2024. The Desk found that the video posted on the YouTube channel includes visuals of a boat capsizing in a water body, which exactly resemble the incident seen in the viral post. However, the video's accompanying details revealed the incident in DR Congo's Lake Kivu. The title of the video reads, "78 Dead After Boat Capsizes in DR Congo's Lake Kivu | Firstpost Africa." Here is the link to the video along with a screenshot. Below is a screenshot highlighting the content in the viral video, which is matched with the video posted by the news portal on its YouTube channel. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find more details related to the incident in DR Congo's Lake Kivu. The search result led the Desk to a report by Al Jazeera dated October 3, 2024, stating the boat, which had come from the town of Minova in South Kivu province, sank only 100 metres (328 feet) from its destination at the shore of Goma. "At least 78 people have died in the incident," the report added. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a video of a boat capsizing incident from DR Congo was falsely shared on social media in the name of an incident that allegedly occurred in Goa.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Social media post claiming arrest of lone survivor in recent Air India crash is false and baseless; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 20 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A week after the tragic Air India plane crash in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, which claimed 270 lives, a video surfaced on social media featuring a voice-over that claimed the lone survivor, Vishwas Ramesh Kumar, had been arrested at his home for allegedly lying about being on the ill-fated flight. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk contacted Jaipal Singh Rathore, Additional Commissioner of Police, Sector-2, Ahmedabad City, who confirmed that Kumar has not been arrested in any case. Further investigation revealed that Vishwas Ramesh Kumar was admitted to Ahmedabad Civil Hospital after surviving the crash. Following his discharge, he also attended the last rites of his brother, who was aboard the same flight. Therefore, the claims circulating on social media are entirely false and baseless. Notably, the Gatwick-bound Air India flight — a Boeing 787-8 Dreamliner — with 242 people on board, including crew members, took off at 1:38 pm on Thursday, June 12, and crashed within minutes, bursting into flames. Claim: An Instagram user, on June 18, shared a video with a voiceover that claimed that the lone survivor in the Air India plane crash was arrested at his home after he allegedly lied about being on the aircraft. "Truth revealed: Survivor of Air India crash arrested for falsely claiming to be on board #ahamedabad," read the post's caption The post garnered 32,934 likes. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation: Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of the keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found numerous social media accounts sharing the same claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be found here and here . As part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports of survivor Vishwash Kumar Ramesh's arrest, but the search did not result in any such report. However, we came across a report by Hindustan Times dated June 12, which carried a picture of the boarding pass that highlighted the passenger's name, Vishwash Kumar Ramesh, and his seat number 11A. This finding clarifies that Vishwash Kumar Ramesh did book a ticket. Moreover, the name of the flight mentioned on the pass was 'AI 171'. The report stated that Vishwash, a British national, was in India for a few days to visit his family and was going back to the UK along with his brother, Ajay Kumar Ramesh (45). Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the boarding pass. In the next part of the investigation, to verify whether he boarded the plane or not, we looked for the passenger list. A report by the Times of India dated June 12 carried the list of the passengers. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Furthermore, when Vishwas Ramesh Kumar was admitted to the City Hospital, Ahmedabad, Union Home Minister Amit Shah met him on June 12, 2025, as per an X post by the Press Trust of India. According to the above findings, it is clear that Kumar did board the plane, and he was admitted to the hospital after surviving the deadly crash. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. On conducting another set of customised keyword searches, and came across a report by India Today dated June 18, 2025, which mentioned that Air India crash survivor Viswashkumar Ramesh has been released from the hospital. He shared that he is heading home and will do the cremation of his younger brother on Wednesday. "Viswashkumar Ramesh, the sole survivor of the Air India plane crash in Ahmedabad, has been released from the Civil Hospital in Ahmedabad. In a telephonic conversation with India Today, Ramesh confirmed that he is heading home and will perform the last rites of his younger brother on Wednesday," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Press Trust of India (PTI) in its X post mentioned Vishwas Ramesh Kumar, the lone survivor of the tragic Air India AI-171 crash in Ahmedabad, performed the last rites of his brother, Ajay Ramesh, who was also onboard the ill-fated flight. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. To debunk the claim about the survivor's arrest, we skimmed through the official handles of DGP Gujarat , Gujarat Police , and Ahmedabad Police but did not find any news of Vishwas being arrested. Taking the investigation ahead, the Desk then contacted the Additional Commissioner of Police, Sector-2, Ahmedabad City, Jaipal Singh Rathore, who confirmed that the claim of Vishwash Kumar Ramesh's arrest is false and he has not been arrested in any case. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim made in the social media post of the lone survivor in the Air India plane crash, Vishwash Kumar Ramesh's arrest, is false. He did board the AI 171 plane and was admitted after he survived the deadly crash.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of hotel fire in Turkey falsely shared as recent library blaze in Delhi; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 20 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a multi-storey building engulfed in flames was recently shared on social media with the claim that it depicted a fire that broke out in a library in Delhi on June 14. The post also alleged that the incident resulted in thousands of deaths. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found the video to be unrelated to any incident in India. The footage shows a fire at an under-construction hotel in Antalya, Turkey, in January 2025. An old and unrelated video was misleadingly shared on social media as footage from a fire in Delhi. Claim An Instagram user 'official_rajkumar_ji_78' shared, on June 14, a video showing a multistoried building—allegedly housing a library in Delhi—engulfed in flames. The user claimed the incident occurred on June 14 and resulted in thousands of deaths. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of these keyframes in a Google Lens Search, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively: As the next step, the Desk conducted a customised Google keyword search to check for any recent fire incidents in a library in Delhi. The search led to a video news report by India Today, which covered a fire incident in May 2025 at the Guru Gobind Singh College of Commerce library in Pitampura. However, upon analysing visuals from that report and comparing them with the viral video, the Desk found them to be completely different. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Further, to corroborate the claim in the social media post, next, the Desk ran the keyframes (generated above from the video) through Google Reverse Image Search. The search led the Desk to a report by UK-based news portal Metro, which had included the same video as seen in the social media post. However, the details accompanying the video stated that it depicted a massive fire at a multistory under-construction hotel in Antalya, Turkey, on January 27, 2025. "A multi-storey blaze has broken out at a hotel construction site in a popular Turkish resort town, leaving workers trapped inside," the report mentioned. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Below is a comparison image showing that the visuals from the viral video match those shown in the video posted by the news portal: Additionally, the Google Reverse Image search also led the Desk to other news reports and videos that confirmed the incident depicted in the video was from Turkey. The report added that the fire reportedly began due to a welding machine, but all the workers were rescued, and the fire was eventually brought under control. Links to two such reports can be found here and here : Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a video showing a multistoried building engulfed in flames was falsely shared on social media, claiming it depicted a recent fire incident in Delhi that killed thousands. In reality, the video showed an under-construction hotel catching fire in Antalya, Turkey, in January 2025.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video from Florida mall falsely shared as chaos at Tel Aviv airport amid Iran-Israel conflict
content: New Delhi, June 23 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing people running frantically inside an indoor space, amid visible panic and chaos, has been shared on social media with the claim that it captures scenes from Tel Aviv airport as Israelis flee amid ongoing Iranian strikes. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the viral clip and found that it has no connection to the Iran-Israel conflict. The footage is actually from the Florida Mall in Orlando, United States, where panic erupted after a man accidentally shot himself. The video is unrelated to the recent events in the Middle East and has been falsely linked to the conflict on social media. Claim: A video featuring people running in an indoor space and chaos was shared by an X user named @Ayesha786Majid' on June 17, claiming that it showed the incident at Tel Aviv airport as Israelis run from Iranian strikes amid ongoing conflict "All this is the result of Netanyahu's actions, due to which Israeli citizens had to run barefoot. See how chaos has spread at Tel Aviv airport," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of these keyframes in a Google Lens Search, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. On running the keyframes through Reverse Image Search, we came across a similar video uploaded by an Instagram user 'realkingpolobeatz' on February 23. This clarifies that the video is old and is unrelated to the ongoing conflict. As per the caption, it showed people running in a mall in Florida, USA. Moreover, multiple users commented that people had started running after hearing a gunshot, with one saying that it happened because "someone shot themselves by accident." "PEOPLE RUNNING AT THE FLORIDA MALL IN ORLANDO FOR NO REASON #mall #orlandoflorida #florida #fyp #reels," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports and came across a report by 'WKMG News 6 ClickOrlando' uploaded on their official YouTube channel on February 17, 2025. As per the report, a man was injured after accidentally shooting himself at the Florida Mall. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Another report by Times Now, dated February 17, also reported the incident, mentioning that there were reports of a shooting at the Florida Mall on South Orange Blossom Trail in Orlando in Florida. Multiple eyewitnesses on social media reported that shots were fired at the mall. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. The report also carried an X post from the official account of the Orange County (FL) Sheriff's Office that cited that there was an accidental discharge of a firearm, and the only person injured was the person who was handling the firearm. "ALERT: Reports of a shooting at the Florida Mall are unfounded. There was an accidental discharge of a firearm, and the only person injured is the person who was handling the firearm," read the post. Here is the link , and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video actually shows people running in Orlando's Florida Mall after a man accidentally shot himself.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video showing train overturning into river falsely shared as real accident from Delhi; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 24 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported video of a passenger train overturning into a river and bursting into flames was recently shared on social media, with users claiming it depicted a major railway accident that had occurred in India. The post alleged that the incident took place in Delhi, where a passenger train supposedly derailed over the Yamuna River, resulting in multiple fatalities. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found it to be false. The investigation confirmed that no such incident involving a train derailing and plunging into the Yamuna River in Delhi had been reported. Additionally, the video in question was found to be AI-generated and was falsely shared on social media to mislead viewers. Claim An Instagram user, 'shakshishukla777', shared a video on June 17 allegedly showing a passenger train overturning into a river. The user claimed the incident occurred in Delhi and that the train had plunged into the Yamuna River, resulting in multiple deaths. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (As of the time of publication, the video had garnered 26,147 likes.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of these keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found that several other social media accounts had also shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively: In the next stage of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customized keyword search on Google to check if any credible news reports existed about a train derailing and falling into the Yamuna River in Delhi. The search yielded no reliable news reports confirming such an incident. Given the magnitude of the claim, any real incident of this nature would have been widely covered by the media. The Desk then carefully analyzed the video for visual inconsistencies that could help determine its authenticity. Upon examination, several indicators suggested the video was AI-generated. Notably, there were no clearly visible human faces, and the visuals had an overly glossy finish—a common characteristic of AI-generated content. To further validate these suspicions, the Desk ran the video through Cantilux, an AI detection tool, which confirmed that the video exhibited pattern distortions and artifacts typically associated with AI-generated media. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a passenger train being overturned into Yamuna river in Delhi was false.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of parking area fire in China falsely shared as aftermath of Iranian strike on Mossad HQ in Israel
content: New Delhi, June 24 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A dramatic video showing an area engulfed in flames, with thick black smoke rising into the sky, is being widely circulated on social media, with users claiming it captures the aftermath of an Iranian attack on a Mossad headquarters in Israel. However, an investigation by the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk reveals that the video is unrelated to the ongoing Israel-Iran conflict. It actually shows a massive fire that broke out at a motorcycle parking facility in Chongqing, China, and has been falsely shared on social media with a misleading claim. Claim: A video featuring an area engulfed in flames with thick black smoke in the air was shared by an X user '@WagnerAmb1W9' on June 17, claiming that it showed the aftermath of an Iranian attack on the Mossad headquarters in Israel. "Sputnik: Mossad headquarters is burning after Iran attack. IRGC Cyber Corps," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of these keyframes in a Google Lens Search, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively: As part of the investigation, the Desk ran the keyframes through reverse image search and came across a YouTube video by a media organisation, Shanghai Eye, resembling the social media post. The video was uploaded on June 12, 2025, and highlighted that a fire broke out at a motorcycle parking lot in China's Chongqing. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the social media post and the YouTube video. Taking a cue from this, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by Reuters that carried a similar video with the same information, adding that no casualties had been reported. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. In an X post dated June 12, CGTN Europe stated that a large fire broke out from a motorcycle parking facility in China's Chongqing. "A large fire broke out from a motorcycle parking facility in China's Chongqing. The fire was first reported by the public at 1:12pm local time and extinguished by rescue units 21 minutes later. Local fire services say no casualties were reported with the cause of the fire under investigation," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video shows a large fire broke out from a motorcycle parking facility in China's Chongqing, and is unrelated to the Israel-Iran conflict.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Unverified social media post claiming US used Indian airspace to carry out attacks on Iran falsely shared to mislead Internet users
content: New Delhi, June 24 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid reports that the United States had resorted to the use of force against Iran, striking three of its key nuclear facilities at Isfahan, Natanz, and Fordow, a purported social media post linked to the development was recently shared online. In the post, the user claimed that, for its first direct intervention in the Israel-Iran conflict, the US had used Indian airspace to launch attacks on the three nuclear facilities in Iran. The user further stated that the development had been confirmed by Pakistani media outlets. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found it to be false. The investigation revealed that the US military had not entered Indian airspace. Instead, it flew across the North Atlantic, passed through European and Middle Eastern airspace, and then proceeded to strike the designated targets in Iran. The claim shared on social media was false and appeared to be an attempt to mislead viewers and target India amid heightened diplomatic tensions. Claim An X user, Sahar Emami (@iamSaharEmami), shared a social media post on June 22 claiming that the US had used Indian airspace to launch an attack on Iran, targeting its three key nuclear installations. The user alleged that Pakistani media had confirmed the use of Indian airspace for the operation. "Pakistani media confirms that the US used Indian airspace to carry out attacks on Iran," the post read. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (As of publication, the post had garnered 722.4k views and 14k likes.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of these keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions listed here and here respectively: Next, the Desk conducted a custom keyword search on Google to find more information about the US precision strike carried out in the middle of the night against three Iranian nuclear facilities—Fordow, Natanz, and Esfahan. This search led to multiple news reports, an official US government release, and video reports of the development. While several details about the strike were available, specific information about the route taken by the US military was not clearly outlined in most public sources. What they (the US Department of Defence) had mention in its official release of the operation (also known as Midnight Hammer) was that a diversion tactic was employed before the actual strike on the nuclear facilities took place. "As part of a plan to maintain tactical surprise, a portion of the operation proceeded west into the Pacific as a decoy. This deception effort was known only to a small number of planners and senior leaders in Washington and Tampa. The main strike package, comprising seven B-2 Spirit bombers with two crew members each, proceeded quietly to the east with minimal communications. Over the 18-hour flight to the target area, the aircraft completed multiple in-flight refuelings. Once over land, the B-2s linked up with escort and support aircraft in a complex, tightly timed maneuver requiring precise coordination across multiple platforms in a narrow airspace—executed with minimal communication," the US Department of Defence in its release said. Here is the link to the release, along with a screenshot: In the subsequent part of the investigation, to further verify the route used by the US authorities, the Desk conducted an additional customised keyword search on Google and found a video released by the Associated Press of a press conference conducted by US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff General Dan Caine. This press conference followed the execution of Operation Midnight Hammer. Upon careful analysis of the video, the Desk noted that, at the 7-minute and 29-second mark, US authorities displayed a strategic map showing the flight path used for the operation. According to the map, B-2 bombers flew across the North Atlantic, passed through European and Middle Eastern airspace, and then proceeded to strike targets in Iran. Nowhere, it had been shown or stated by the US authorities that an Indian airspace was used by them for the attack. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim suggesting that the US had used Indian airspace to carry out attacks on Iran was false.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated image falsely shows Rahul Gandhi at Alexander Soros's wedding
content: New Delhi, June 25 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A photograph claiming to show Leader of Opposition and Congress MP Rahul Gandhi alongside American investor and philanthropist Alexander Soros at Soros's wedding was circulated on social media. Several users shared the image, alleging that Gandhi attended the ceremony. However, after conducting a thorough investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the image was created using artificial intelligence tools. While we could not independently verify whether Rahul Gandhi attended the wedding, there is no credible evidence to support this claim. Based on our analysis, the viral photo is not authentic, and the claim being made is false. Claim: A photo allegedly featuring Leader of Opposition (LoP) & Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and American investor and philanthropist Alexander Soros was shared by an X user, 'Raghunatha Prabhu, Modi ka Pariwar', claiming that Gandhi attended Soros's wedding ceremony. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the photo through Reverse Image Search and found that several other users had shared te same photo with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , and its archived version can be viewed here and here , respectively. As part of the investigation, the Desk first conducted a customised keyword search and we did not find any credible news reports stating that Rahul Gandhi attended the wedding of George Soros's son. We then carefully analysed the photo and found several discrepancies and inconsistencies that hinted towards it being manipulated, for instance, the bride, Huma Abedin, has a distorted hand, while Alex Soros's fingers appear to merge into Gandhi's outfit. Below is a screenshot highlighting the findings. Taking a cue from this we then ran the photo through Hive Moderation an AI-detection tool, which also concluded that the image was AI-generated. Additionally, the image was tested using another AI detection tool, SightEngine, which also concluded that the image was AI-generated. Although we could not independently verify Rahul Gandhi's presence at the wedding, available evidence confirms that the photo being circulated on social media was generated using artificial intelligence. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the photo claiming to show Rahul Gandhi at Alex Soros's wedding is AI-generated.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of Turkish leader being slapped in public falsely shared as attack on Israeli PM Netanyahu
content: New Delhi, June 25 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid heightened military tensions between Iran and Israel, which escalated after the latter launched blistering attacks on the heart of the former's nuclear and military infrastructure, a purported video showing an individual being attacked in public was recently shared on social media. The user claimed the video depicted Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu being attacked by a citizen amid the ongoing crisis in the Middle East. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found that it actually depicted Turkish opposition leader Özgür Özel being assaulted in Istanbul. The old and unrelated video was falsely shared on social media with a misleading claim. Claim An X handle with the username @putin_pandit shared a purported video on June 23, claiming that Israeli citizens had attacked Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu amid ongoing tensions in the Middle East. The video showed a man, allegedly PM Netanyahu, being thrashed by an individual before security personnel intervened and rescued him from the site. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (As of the time of publication, the video had garnered 59.4k views) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of these keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found that several other social media accounts had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. The Google Reverse Image Search also led the Desk to a video published on the YouTube channel of Turkey-based news portal Medyascope TV. The video featured the same visuals as those in the viral clip, where a man, allegedly to be Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu, is being assaulted in public. However, upon carefully reviewing the details of the video, published on May 4, 2025, the Desk found that it does not show the Israeli PM being attacked but rather Turkish opposition leader Özgür Özel being assaulted in Istanbul. "CHP Chairman Özgür Özel was slapped and attacked after the ceremony held for Sırrı Süreyya Önder at the AKM. Özel was removed from the area with his guards," the details stated along the video reads. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image showing that the visuals from the viral video match those shown in the video posted by the news portal: Additionally, the Google Reverse Image Search led the Desk to another Turkey-based news outlet, Daily Sabah. Its report, published on May 4, 2025, also covered the incident, confirming that Özel was slapped by an assailant. The featured image in the article matched the keyframe used by the Desk for analysis. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old and unrelated video from Turkey was falsely shared on social media as a recent incident involving Israeli PM Netanyahu.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, Israeli airport wasn't bombed by Iran; AI-generated video was shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, June 25 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid heightened military tensions between Israel and Iran, a purported video of an airport turned to ruins was recently shared on social media. Users claimed the video depicted the current situation at an international airport in Israel, which allegedly reduced to rubble following an Iranian strike. The video showed several aircraft at the airport compound appearing severely damaged. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it to be AI-generated. It does not depict a real incident involving an Israeli airport under attack. An AI-generated video was falsely shared on social media to mislead viewers. Claim An X user, Adv. Nazneen Akhtar (@NazneenAkhtar23), shared on June 19 a purported video showing an airport turned to ruins. The user claimed the video depicted the current condition of an international airport in Israel after it was hit by an Iranian strike. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of the keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found numerous social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. Next, the Desk conducted a customized keyword search on Google to verify whether any credible reports confirmed an Iranian missile strike destroying an airport in Israel. However, the search did not lead to any such credible news coverage supporting the claim. Further, as part of the investigation, the Desk then ran the keyframes (extracted above from the video) through Google Reverse Image Search. The search led it to a video posted on the Instagram handle '3amelyon' on June 6. The Desk found the handle had shared the same video (of aircraft reduced to rubble) as seen in the viral post. However, a closer review of the Instagram handle, through which the video was first shared, revealed that it is mostly known for sharing AI-generated content. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image showing that the video posted on Instagram handle matches to that of the viral video in circulation. Next, taking cues from the above generated inputs, the Desk ran the video through Cantilux (an AI detection tool). The results indicated that the video had been generated using artificial intelligence. "The content exhibits characteristic patterns and artifacts commonly associated with AI-generated media," the analysis noted. Below is a screenshot to the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was generated using AI.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old videos from China falsely shared as recent flash flood incident in Mumbai
content: New Delhi, June 26 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it depicted several parts of Mumbai being affected by flash floods. According to the claim, the video, purportedly captured on June 22, showed visuals from various locations across the city, highlighting the extent of damage caused by the floods. The first clip showed heavily waterlogged roads in front of a building, while the subsequent visuals—captured from different areas—depicted vehicles being swept away in floodwaters. However, in its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was not from India. In fact, three of the four clips were traced back to incidents in China, while the fourth was also found to be unrelated to India. An old and unrelated video compilation was falsely shared on social media, misleadingly linking it to Mumbai. Claim An Instagram handle with the username 'bittu_yaduvanshi_07' shared a video on June 23, claiming that it showed several parts of Mumbai severely affected by flash floods. The video featured multiple clips allegedly showing the scale of damage across the city. The first clip showed waterlogged areas in front of a building, while the following clips—shot in different locations—depicted vehicles being swept away by strong floodwaters. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk conducted a targeted keyword search on Google and found that several other social media users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. Next, the Desk extracted keyframes from each of the four clips in the video through InVid tool search and later ran it through Google Reverse Image Searches to identify the original sources of the same. Below is the result of the separate investigation for all the four visuals. Visual 1: Waterlogged Area in Front of a Building Below is a screenshot of the keyframe, the Desk used for investigation. Investigation (1): The Desk ran the keyframe extracted from the first visual through Google Reverse Image Search, which led to a video posted by the X (formerly Twitter) handle @Unstop_weather. The Desk found visuals seen in the social media video matched those in the clip shared by the X handle. However, according to the caption accompanying the original post, the footage was from Guangdong Province in China, where heavy rainfall had caused the Fengliang River in Meizhou City to rise sharply, resulting in severe waterlogging in low-lying areas. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image showing that the visuals from the social media video match those shown in the video posted by the X handle on Sept 7, 2023: Although the Desk could not independently verify the exact origin of the video, it reviewed the extended version of the clip shared in the original post. At the 15-second timestamp, the video shows a safety barrier marked with Mandarin text—a language not typically used in India. This detail further confirms that the video does not depict scenes from Mumbai. Below is a screenshot highlighting the finding. Video 2: The visuals show people seeking shelter on top of their vehicles as floodwaters begin to sweep the vehicles away Below is a screenshot of the keyframe, the Desk used for investigation. Investigation (2): The Desk ran the keyframe extracted from this visual through Google Reverse Image Search. The search led to a report published by ArabiaWeather Inc., a private weather company that provides services to consumers and businesses across the Arab world. The Desk found that the featured image in the report matched the keyframe used for investigation. According to the article, the footage was from Henan Province in southern China, recorded in July 2021, when a wave of historic floods caused widespread destruction in the region. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image further confirming that the visuals from the social media video match those with the feature image of the news report Video 3: The visuals show vehicles being swept away by floodwaters Below is a screenshot of the keyframe, the Desk used for investigation. The Desk ran the keyframe extracted from this visual through Google Reverse Image Search. The search led to a news report published by Excelsior, a Mexico-based news portal. The Desk found that the report included an image that matched the keyframe used for the investigation. According to the details provided in the article, the image showed the aftermath of Typhoon Yagi making landfall along the coast of Hainan, China, in September 2024. At no point did the article indicate the video holding any connection to India. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image further confirming that the visuals from the social media video match those with the feature image of the news report. Video 4: The visuals show vehicles being swept away by floodwaters Below is a screenshot of the keyframe, the Desk used for investigation. The Desk ran the keyframe extracted from this visual through Google Reverse Image Search. However, the search did not lead to any credible results that could corroborate the viral claim or confirm the location. As part of a deeper analysis, the Desk, next, examined the video closely and observed that the design and format of the vehicle number plates depicted in the video did not match the standard design used in India, indicating that the footage likely originated from a different country. Below is a screenshot highlighting the key findings. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old and unrelated set of videos, primarily from China, was falsely shared on social media with the false claim that it showed recent flash floods in Mumbai.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of paint factory fire in Malaysia falsely shared as Iranian missile strike in Israel; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 26 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported video showing a building engulfed in massive flames was recently shared on social media with the claim that it depicted a scene from Tel Aviv, where Iran had allegedly targeted Israel's defence system with missiles amid ongoing tensions. The video showed thick plumes of smoke emerging from a building while bystanders recorded the incident. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it to be unrelated to the conflict in the Middle East. The video actually showed a paint mixing factory fire in Senai, Malaysia, which occurred in April 2025, injuring three individuals. An old and unrelated video from Malaysia was falsely shared on social media by linking it to the ongoing conflict between Iran and Israel. Claim An X user, Sumon Kais (@sumonkais), shared a video on June 19, claiming it showed a missile strike by Iran on the Israeli Defence System in Tel Aviv. The video showed a building erupting into flames. "Iranian missiles accurately targeted the Israeli Defence System in Tel Aviv. You can see the multifold explosion during the fire eruption," the user shared the video with the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publication, the video had garnered 2.2M views and 13k likes) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of the keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found numerous social media accounts shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. The Google Reverse Image search also led the Desk to a video posted on an official YouTube channel of Malaysia based news portal 'The Sun' on April 25, 2025. The Google Reverse Image Search led the Desk to a YouTube video posted by Malaysian news outlet 'The Sun' on April 25, 2025. The background in this news clip matched the visuals from the viral video. The description confirmed the footage was from Senai's Desa Idaman Industrial Park, where a fire broke out at a paint mixing factory. "Three men, including a Bangladeshi national, suffered burns in a fire at a paint mixing factory in Senai's Desa Idaman Industrial Park," the description stated along the video reads. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image showing that the visuals from the viral video match those shown in the video posted by the news portal on its YouTube channel. Additionally, the search result also led the Desk to another video found on the official YouTube channel of Vanakkam Malaysia, a regional media company, on April 25, 2025. This video too matched the visuals in the viral clip and confirmed the same incident from Malaysia. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. Further, as a part of the investigation, the Desk also conducted a customised keyword search on Google about the present status of the conflict between Iran and Israel. The search result led the Desk to a news report by the Associated Press on June 25, which stated that a fragile ceasefire brokered by the US appeared to hold between Iran and Israel after days of heavy military exchange, which had killed over a hundred people so far. "A fragile ceasefire between Iran and Israel appeared to hold Tuesday (June 24) after initially faltering, and US President Donald Trump expressed frustration with both sides, saying they had fought 'for so long and so hard' that they do not know what they are doing," the report added. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video showing Iranian missiles accurately targeting the Israeli Defence System in Tel Aviv is false. The video is from Malaysia.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of restaurant fire from Tajikistan falsely shared as attack on Israel's Home Ministry
content: New Delhi, June 27 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid escalating military tensions between Iran and Israel—intensified by Israel's recent strikes on key Iranian nuclear and military sites—a video surfaced on social media showing a building engulfed in flames, with thick black smoke billowing into the sky. The video was shared with the claim that Iran had bombed Israel's Home Ministry building. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the social media clip and found that the footage is unrelated to the ongoing conflict. The video actually shows a fire that broke out at the Yakkasaroy (VIP) restaurant, formerly known as Temurmalik, located in Khujand, Tajikistan. The clip was misleadingly shared on social media with a false narrative, linking it to the conflict between Iran and Israel. Claim: A video featuring a building engulfed in flames with thick black smoke in the air was shared by a Facebook user, 'Mohit Chaudhary,' on June 23, claiming that Iran blew up Israel's Home Ministry building. "Iran blew up Israel's Home Ministry building this morning. Israel is suffering heavy losses in this war, which is why it is repeatedly asking America to join the war," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation: The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of these keyframes in a Google Lens Search, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively: As part of the investigation, the Desk ran the keyframes through reverse image search and came across a similar video uploaded on YouTube on June 22, 2025. As per the description, fire broke out at Suhtor dar restaurant "Temurmalik" in Tajikistan. "Fire Out of Control Suhtor dar restaurant "Temurmalik" and restaurant in Tajikistan #tajikistan," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports and came across a report by Sputnik published on June 20, 2025. As per the report, the Yakkasaroy (Temurmalik) restaurant in Khujand has completely burned down as a result of a fire. The ship-shaped establishment was reduced to black ash. The incident occurred on June 19, with a column of black smoke rising over Khujand. "Fire in Khujand completely destroyed a restaurant-ship: photo," read the headline of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Another report by Asia-Plus was published on June 20, 2025, which mentioned that on the evening of June 19, a major fire broke out in the Yakkasaroy (Family) restaurant, formerly known as Temurmalik, in Khujand. According to preliminary information, no one was hurt, but the building was almost completely destroyed by fire. "The three-story building with a total area of 631 square meters lost its top two floors - they burned down completely. The rest of the building may have also received serious damage, but the exact extent of the damage has not yet been determined," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk then looked up the restaurant's location on Google Maps. Although Google Maps Street View was not available, we reviewed the photos of the Sugdiyon Hotel uploaded on Google Maps. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between he social media post and the Google Maps image. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a fire broke out at the Yakkasaroy (VIP) restaurant, formerly known as Temurmalik, in Khujand, Tajikistan, and was falsely shared as Israel's Home Ministry building under fire.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video claiming Delhi Metro train accident falsely shared as real footage; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 27 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported video showing a metro train derailing after hitting large concrete blocks placed near the track was recently shared on social media. The user claimed the incident occurred in Delhi, where the metro allegedly struck the blocks while entering a station. The post further alleged that 5,000 people had died in the accident. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found it to be false. The investigation confirmed that no such incident involving a derailed metro train in Delhi had been reported. Moreover, the video in question was found to be AI-generated and was falsely shared on social media to mislead viewers. Claim On June 22, an Instagram user with the handle 'me_khusi_2026' shared a video allegedly showing a metro train derailing after striking large concrete blocks placed near the tracks. The user claimed the incident occurred in Delhi and further alleged that it resulted in the deaths of 5,000 people. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (As of the time of publication, the video had garnered 11,123 likes) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of these keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found that several other social media accounts had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. In the next stage of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to check if any credible news reports existed about a metro train derailing incident in Delhi. The search yielded no reliable news reports confirming such an incident. Given the magnitude of the claims, any real incident of this nature would have been widely covered by the media. The Desk then carefully analyzed the video for visual inconsistencies that could help determine its authenticity. Upon examination, several indicators suggested the video was AI-generated. Notably, the visuals had an overly glossy finish- a common characteristic of AI-generated content. To further validate these suspicions, the Desk ran the video through Cantilux, an AI detection tool, which confirmed that the video exhibited pattern distortions and artifacts typically associated with AI-generated media. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video was AI-generated and bore no connection to any real incident in Delhi.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2021 video of Diljit Dosanjh falsely linked to Sardaar Ji 3 film controversy
content: New Delhi, June 27 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid the ongoing controversy over actor-singer Diljit Dosanjh's latest film 'Sardaar Ji 3', a video featuring him has gone viral on social media. The film has sparked debate for casting Pakistani actress Hania Aamir at a time when diplomatic ties between New Delhi and Islamabad remain tense. Social media users sharing the clip claim that Dosanjh appears unfazed by industry pressure and insists he will continue to do what he believes is right—linking his comments to the 'Sardaar Ji 3' casting row. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the viral video and found that it is actually from 2021. In the original interview, Dosanjh was speaking about staying productive during the COVID-19 lockdown and reflecting on his journey as an artist. The video is unrelated to the current controversy and has been shared online with a false claim. Tensions between India and Pakistan have been particularly high since the Pahalgam attack in April. In the aftermath, Indian authorities banned the social media accounts of several Pakistani artists and prohibited their participation in Indian films and television projects. Claim: A purported video featuring singer and actor Diljit Dosanjh was shared on X by a user named 'Megh Update' on June 25, 2025, claiming that he is unfazed by the industry's pressure and will do what he feels is right. In the 00:39-second video, Dosanjh says: "I don't want to work in Bollywood, and I do not have any such wish of becoming a great Bollywood star. I love music…no one can stop me from making music…." The post clocked 1.1 million views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of these keyframes in a Google Lens Search, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively: As part of the investigation, the Desk ran the extracted keyframes through Reverse Image Search and came across an X post by Editor at The Hollywood Reporter India & Founder at Film Companion Studios, Anupama Chopra, dated September 12, 2021. The post featured a picture of Diljit Dosanjh in the same attire and background as seen in the viral post. The caption of the post mentioned a Sunday evening session with Diljit Dosanjh. The timeline of the post makes it clear that the video is old and not related to recent controversies surrounding the singer. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search and came across a video on the official YouTube channel of Film Companion Studios, dated September 20, 2021. "Diljit Dosanjh is a singular sensation. He is a multi-faceted artist who continues to innovate and entertain his legions of fans – even in the middle of a global pandemic. On FC Front Row, Diljit chats with Anupama Chopra about being productive in a lockdown and his evolution as an artist," reads the description. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Another report by The Hindustan Times published on September 20, 2021, mentioned that in an interview, Diljit Dosanjh said that he doesn't care about whether or not he cultivates a successful career in Bollywood, as he has absolute control when it comes to his music. He said that nobody can stop him from making the kind of music he wants to, and that he is proud of the fact that Punjabi singers are mostly independent. "He told Film Companion in Hindi, I have no desire of becoming a Bollywood star. I love music, and without anybody's say, I can make my music. No superstar can tell me that this music won't work, or that someone else's song would work better, none of this works on me. Punjabi artists are independent, and that's great freedom to have. Nobody can stop us, nobody can stop me from making music. I will keep making music for as long as I want to, and for as long as God allows me to. And I don't give a damn about getting work in Bollywood," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to 2021 during his interview, where he talked about being productive in a lockdown and his evolution as an artist.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Social media post falsely claims govt to levy toll on two-wheelers from July 15; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 27 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported social media post claiming that, effective July 15, two-wheeler vehicles would also be subject to toll charges was widely shared online. However, PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found that no such announcement had been made by the government. Both Union Minister Nitin Gadkari and the National Highways Authority of India issued official statements clarifying that the claim is false. A false post was shared on social media in an attempt to mislead viewers. Claim An X user named 'Saurabh' (@sauravyadav1133) shared a post on June 26 claiming that toll charges would be imposed on two-wheelers starting July 15, 2025. In the post, the user wrote, "Good news for two-wheeler riders… Now, from July 15, they too will have to pay toll tax." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (As of the time of publication, the post had garnered 4,696 views) Investigation The Desk ran the image attached to the social media post through Google Lens. The search results revealed that several other social media accounts had shared the same image with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. To verify the authenticity of the claim, the Desk conducted a customized keyword search on Google to check whether the government had announced any such decision. The search led to a clarification issued by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI), the nodal agency responsible for road network management under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. NHAI categorically denied the existence of any such proposal. "Fact Check: Some sections of the media have reported that the Government of India plans to levy user fees on two-wheelers. NHAI would like to clarify that no such proposal is under consideration. There are no plans to introduce toll charges for two-wheelers," the statement read. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Additionally, the Desk came across a social media post by Union Minister Nitin Gadkari on his official X handle, posted on June 26. In his statement, the minister strongly refuted the claim and criticized the spread of misinformation. "Some media houses are spreading misleading news about imposing a toll tax on two-wheeler vehicles. No such decision has been proposed. The exemption on toll for two-wheeler vehicles will continue fully. Spreading misleading news without verifying the truth to create a sensation is not a sign of healthy journalism. I condemn this," Gadkari stated. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim regarding the imposition of toll charges on two-wheeler vehicles from July 15, 2025, by the government is entirely false.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Deepfake Alert! Nirmala Sitharaman's Budget interview with PTI's CEO & Editor-in-Chief shared with superimposed audio to falsely claim FM endorsed trading platform
content: New Delhi, June 29 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported video of Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, appearing to endorse a trading platform during an exclusive conversation with Press Trust of India's CEO and Editor-in-Chief, Vijay Joshi, was recently circulated online. In the viral clip, the minister is allegedly seen responding to a question from PTI's EIC about the rising number of videos featuring her promoting money trading platforms. She purportedly states that all such videos are fake—except for the one in question, which includes a link to a so-called "authentic" platform. In the video, Sitharaman appears to endorse a platform called "Tickertape," claiming it is backed by the Government of India and the Union Council of Ministers. She further claims that citizens can invest as little as ₹21,000 and earn monthly returns of ₹10 lakh. The minister is shown stating that she is personally involved in the project and has earned the same amount in a single month. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found the video was created using generative AI to share false claim. The Finance Minister had indeed given an exclusive interview to PTI on the day of the Union Budget presentation, but at no point during the interview did she endorse any trading platform or investment scheme. The viral video was digitally manipulated with superimposed audio to promote fraudulent investments and was circulated on social media to mislead viewers. Claim A Facebook page named 'Vision Path' shared a video on June 26, allegedly showing Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in conversation with PTI CEO and Editor-in-Chief Vijay Joshi, promoting a trading platform called Tickertape. The video claims the platform is supported by the Government of India and the Union Council of Ministers. In the clip, the minister appears to urge citizens to avoid other fraudulent schemes and trust only the "official" trading platform (the one mentioned above), with a link embedded in the video. She claims that users can open an account by investing ₹21,000 and earn over ₹10 lakh per month. The minister also says that over 10,000 Indians are currently benefitting from this platform. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (As of the time of publication, the video had garnered over 269,000 views.) Investigation To verify the claim, the PTI Fact Check Desk conducted a customised keyword search on the official website of the Press Trust of India to check for any reports or video indicating that the Finance Minister had endorsed the investment platform. No such reports or videos were found on any platforms related to PTI. Next, the Desk used the InVid tool to extract keyframes from the video. One of these keyframes was reverse-searched using Google, which led to the original video published on PTI's official YouTube channel. The video features Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in an exclusive interview with PTI CEO and Editor-in-Chief Vijay Joshi, discussing key announcements of the Union Budget 2025–26. It was published on February 2, 2025. The Desk reviewed the full interview but found no mention of any trading or investment platform, indicating that the viral video had been digitally altered. Here is the link to the original video, along with a screenshot. Here is also a link to a comparison video shared by the official X handle of PTI Fact Check. The video clearly shows how the original interview clip was tampered with, using superimposed audio, to falsely claim that the duo discussed the benefits of investing in the trading platform during the interview. Below is a screenshot of the same. (https://rb.gy/0ouvqg) Further, based on insights gathered, the Desk used an AI-based tool, Resemble Detect, to analyze the authenticity of the minister's voice in the viral clip. The results confirmed that the audio had been edited. Here is the link to voice analysis result and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Union Minister Nirmala Sitharaman's video has been digitally manipulated with superimposed audio to promote fraudulent trading platform.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Viral image claiming to show Rudraprayag bus tragedy is AI-generated
content: New Delhi, June 30 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): In the aftermath of a tragic accident in Uttarakhand's Rudraprayag district, where a bus carrying 20 people veered off the highway and plunged into the Alaknanda river, a distressing image has been making the rounds on social media. The picture shows a bus stuck midstream in a gushing river, and several users have claimed that it captures the moment from the Rudraprayag tragedy that left multiple pilgrims dead. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the viral image and found it to be digitally manipulated and AI-generated. As per official recent reports, a 55-year-old man from Rajasthan was recovered on Friday as search operations continued to locate eight others still missing after a bus carrying 20 Char Dham pilgrims veered off the Badrinath National Highway and plunged into the Alaknanda River between Rudraprayag and Gauchar on Thursday morning (July 26). The 31-seater bus, headed to Badrinath, was carrying pilgrims from Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and Maharashtra when the accident took place at 7.50 am. Claim: An X user named '@me__himanshi' shared a purported image of a bus stuck in the middle of a fast-flowing river in a mountainous, rocky terrain on June 26. The user claimed that the image depicted a bus accident in Rudraprayag that killed several pilgrims. "Tragic bus accident in #Rudraprayag: Pilgrims' bus falls into Alaknanda river, several dead, many missing. Rescue operations are ongoing. Prayers for all," read the post's caption that garnered 909 views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the photo through Reverse Image Search and found that several other users had shared the same picture with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here . Notably, a similar image was shared by media outlets such as News18 Punjabi and Agniban . As part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the picture and found several discrepancies, for instance, the background and the water looked extra glossy. At the same time, the bus also did not seem to be a real one. All these observations hinted that the photo might be manipulated. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Taking a cue from this we then ran the photo through Hive Moderation an AI-detection tool, which also concluded that the image was AI-generated. Additionally, the image was tested using another AI detection tool, SightEngine, which also concluded that the image was AI-generated. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the image being shared as a bus accident that claimed the lives of several pilgrims is AI-generated.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old photo of Israeli airstrike on Gaza falsely linked to fresh Hamas attacks post Iran-Israel ceasefire
content: New Delhi, June 30 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A dramatic photograph showing a cityscape illuminated by massive flames and thick orange-red smoke billowing into the night sky has gone viral on social media. The image is being shared with the claim that, following a ceasefire between Iran and Israel, Hamas has resumed attacks on Israel. However, the Fact Check Desk of the Press Trust of India investigated the viral image and found the claim to be false. A reverse image search revealed that the photo is from October 10, 2023, and actually captures the aftermath of an Israeli airstrike on Gaza during the Israel-Hamas conflict. Claim: An X user named 'Adv.Nazneen Akhtar' on June 27, shared a photo featuring a cityscape at night with the sky filled with enormous, billowing flames and thick orange-red smoke, claiming that following a ceasefire between Iran and Israel, Hamas has started attacking Israel. "Here you go, the war with Iran is over, and now #Hamas has started hammering Israel, It seems like Hamas is trying to settle all past and future scores. The few cities Israel has left, Hamas will destroy them and only then be satisfied," read the post's caption. The post garnered 4662 views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation: As part of the investigation, the Desk ran the photo in the social media post through Reverse Image Search and came across a report by India Today dated October 23, 2023. The report's feature image was similar to the one shared on social media. As per the information mentioned below the picture it shows smoke and flames billow from targets hit in Israeli airstrikes in Gaza City. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the photo in the social media post and the news report. Another report by Business Today published on November November 14, 2023. The headline of the report read: "Israel-Hamas war: Here's how the ongoing geopolitical crisis in Middle East is impacting India's divestment plans". The cover image of the report was similar to the one shared on social media. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the picture dates back to October 10, 2023, showing an Israeli airstrike on Gaza.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video showing domestic violence incident involving Muslim couple in Uttar Pradesh falsely shared with communal narrative; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 30 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A visually disturbing video showing a man violently thrashing a woman was recently shared on social media with the claim that the two were an interfaith couple, where a Muslim man was beating his Hindu wife. The video purportedly depicted the Muslim husband attacking his Hindu wife in the presence of other family members. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found that the video was being circulated with a false communal narrative. Both the man and the woman belong to the Muslim community and are a married couple residing in Hapur, Uttar Pradesh. An old and unrelated video depicting a case of domestic violence was falsely shared on social media to incite communal disharmony. Claim An X user named 'Sanjay' (@Sanjay63399552) shared the video on June 25, alleging that it showed an interfaith couple, where a Muslim man was mercilessly beating his Hindu wife. The user captioned the video: "Hindus, look at the condition of marrying a Muslim." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (Disclaimer: The video contains sensitive visuals) (As of the time of publication, the video had garnered 84.2k views) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of these keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found that several social media accounts had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. The Google reverse image search also led the Desk to a video posted on the official X handle of India News, made to cover news from Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand. The Desk found that the handle had posted the same video (which includes visuals from the viral clip claiming a Muslim man was beating his Hindu wife) on June 19, 2025. However, the details shared alongside the post revealed that the video depicted a domestic violence incident that occurred in Hapur, Uttar Pradesh, and the man and woman shown are a married couple.. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image showing that the video shared by the news portal on its X handle matches that of the viral video in circulation. In the next part of the investigation, using the details obtained, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google for further verification. This led to a post made by the official X handle of Hapur Police on June 26, 2025, clarifying that the incident had no communal angle and was purely a case of domestic violence. In the post, the police stated: "The incident occurred about one and a half months ago. A case was registered under relevant sections at Hapur Nagar Police Station, and a chargesheet has already been filed in court. The couple is now living together by mutual consent." The police further added, "We are registering cases against those spreading misleading information and are taking legal action." Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was falsely shared with a communal narrative, whereas it actually depicted a domestic violence incident involving a Muslim couple from Hapur, Uttar Pradesh.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of building collapse in Bangkok falsely shared as recent incident from Mumbai; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 2 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it depicted a tragic incident that occurred recently in Mumbai, where a high-rise building collapsed within seconds. The footage showed a building, still under construction, collapsing as workers fled for safety.
