Users alleged that the incident occurred on June 18 and that thousands had lost their lives in the tragedy. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found the claim to be false. The video actually shows an incident from Bangkok's Chatuchak area, where a powerful earthquake originating in Myanmar, whose tremors were felt in Thailand, led to the collapse of a high-rise building in March 2025. Reportedly, over a dozen people were confirmed dead in the terrifying incident. An old and unrelated video from Bangkok is being falsely shared on social media and misattributed to a recent event in Mumbai. Claim An Instagram user, 'rajput_jyoti_singh_12', shared a video on June 23, claiming it depicted the collapse of a high-rise building in Mumbai. The user claimed that the incident occurred on June 18 and that thousands had died in the tragedy. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of the keyframes in a Google Lens Search, the Desk found numerous social media accounts shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The reverse image search also led the Desk to a video posted on the official YouTube channel of UK-based news platform Channel 4 News. The Desk found that the platform had, on March 28, shared the same video showing the building collapse, identical to the one circulating on social media. The video description reads: "A skyscraper under construction in Bangkok, Thailand, has collapsed following tremors from a 7.7 magnitude earthquake in neighbouring Myanmar." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image showing that the video shared by the news portal on its YouTube handle matches that of the social media video in circulation. Additionally, the search result also led the Desk to come across several other news reports that confirmed the video depicts an incident from Bangkok, not India. Links to two such reports can be found here and here . In the next phase of the investigation, using the details obtained, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to gather more information about the building collapse. The search led to a report published by Euronews on May 16, 2025, which revealed that the collapsed building was being constructed for Thailand's State Audit Office by a Chinese company and a Thai construction firm. The report also highlighted another major development in the incident, where a prominent Thai construction executive, along with engineers, designers, and builders, had surrendered to the police in May to face criminal negligence charges related to the fatal collapse. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. In the final part of the investigation, the Desk carried out another keyword search on Google to check if any recent high-rise building collapses had been reported in Mumbai. The search did not yield any credible media reports supporting the claim. Given the alleged scale of the incident (i.e., thousands dead), such a tragedy would have received widespread media coverage. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video showing the collapse of a high-rise building is not from Mumbai, as falsely claimed. The video is originally from Bangkok, Thailand.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Scripted video showing young man marrying elderly woman falsely shared as incident from Haryana; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 2 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported image showing a young man marrying an elderly woman was recently shared on social media, accompanied by the claim that it depicted a real-life incident from Haryana, India. The user alleged that the image showed a Muslim man named Mohammad Irfan marrying his grandmother, Sultana Khatoon. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the social media post and the image shared with it. The Desk found no credible evidence supporting the claim of a Muslim man marrying his grandmother. Instead, the photo was taken from a scripted video skit and does not depict a real-life event. Claim An X handle with the username @MeghUpdates shared a post on June 26, claiming that in a shocking incident from Haryana, a 21-year-old Muslim man married his grandmother. The user alleged that Mohammad Irfan married his grandmother, Sultana Khatoon, after they reportedly fell in love. An image of the two, allegedly from their wedding ceremony, was also shared. "In a shameful and shocking incident, a 21-year-old Mohammad Irfan from Haryana married his Grandmother, Sultana Khatoon, breaking all boundaries of familial relationships. Sultana had been living alone after the death of her husband, and Irfan had been staying with her to provide care and support. Over time, their bond reportedly grew, eventually leading to marriage," the user wrote in the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publication of the story, the post had garnered 726.4k views) Investigation The Desk ran the image of the duo shared in the viral post through Google Lens. The search result led the Desk to multiple social media accounts as well as news reports that shared the same image with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Reverse Image Search also led the Desk to a YouTube channel named 'Desi Chhora 2.0', which had posted the same video (showing a young man marrying an elderly woman), currently under investigation. The Desk found that the video was first uploaded to the channel in November 2022, with the caption: "Love between a 52-year-old woman and a 21-year-old boy." At no point was it mentioned that the video depicted an incident from Haryana. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image highlighting the content seen in the viral video, matched with that of the video posted by the YouTube channel. To further verify the authenticity of the claim, the Desk carefully analysed the video. At the 22-second timestamp, a disclaimer appeared stating that all characters, names, places, and events shown in the video are fictional and created solely for entertainment purposes. It mentioned that the content does not depict any real-life incident. Below is a screenshot highlighting the finding. Additionally, the Desk reviewed other videos posted by the same channel and found that 'Desi Chhora 2.0' is known for creating and sharing scripted video skits meant purely for entertainment. Several of these videos follow similar storylines, involving sensational themes, which suggests the channel's focus on producing fictional content. Links to two such videos can be found here and here . Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a 21-year-old Muslim man from Haryana marrying his grandmother is scripted.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of assault on retired medical officer in Bangladesh falsely shared with a communal angle; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 2 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A disturbing video showing an elderly man being garlanded with slippers is being widely shared on social media. The posts claim that the man is a Hindu teacher in Bangladesh who was publicly humiliated and assaulted by Muslims. However, a fact-check by the Press Trust of India (PTI) reveals that the claim is misleading. The man seen in the video is not a Hindu teacher, but a retired medical officer in Bangladesh who was reportedly attacked over alleged derogatory remarks made about Prophet Muhammad. The incident, though real, is being circulated online with a false communal narrative aimed at fuelling religious tensions. Claim: A video featuring an elderly man garlanded with slippers was shared by a Facebook user named 'Satyappa Khot' on June 29, claiming that a Hindu teacher in Bangladesh was being assaulted with a garland of shoes by Muslims. "A Hindu teacher who worked for 40 years was garlanded with slippers by radical Islamists in Bangladesh. This is the condition of Hindus in Bangladesh. THIS IS ISLSM????," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of these keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found that several social media accounts had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. Upon further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a report by Bangladesh's media outlet, published on June 15, 2025. The cover image of the report was similar to the visuals seen in the social media post. According to the report, the man, a retired community medical officer, was thrashed by an angry mob in Rajbari's Baliakandi for allegedly insulting the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH). The victim, Ahmed Ali, is a resident of Tekati village in Nawabpur union of the same upazila. This clarifies that there is no communal angle to the entire situation. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Another report by the Bangladeshi news outlet, published on June 15, 2025, mentioned that locals made a doctor walk around the market wearing a garland of shoes after he was beaten up by a mob for insulting the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH). "The incident took place on Sunday (June 15) in Beruli Bazar of Nababpur Union of the upazila. The accused is named Ahmed Ali. He works as a doctor at Nawabpur Union Health Complex," the report read. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a retired medical officer being assaulted in Bangladesh over alleged remarks on Prophet Muhammad was shared with a false communal angle.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video of aircraft accident falsely shared as real incident from Agra airport; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 2 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing an aircraft erupting into flames moments after landing was recently shared on social media, with the claim that it depicted a real incident that occurred at Agra Airport in India. The user alleged that the aircraft caught fire due to a spark in its wheels immediately after landing. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found that it was generated by AI and falsely shared on social media to mislead viewers. Claim An Instagram user, 'brahmn_vadi_karuna_shukla', shared a video on July 1 showing an aircraft bursting into flames just after landing on the runway. The user claimed that the incident took place at Agra Airport and that the fire was caused by a spark from the aircraft's wheels. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to verify whether any such aircraft accident had recently occurred in Agra. The search yielded no credible media reports to support the claim. Given the severity of the alleged incident, it would have received widespread media attention had it been real. During further analysis, the Desk noticed a watermark reading "@extremedrive" at the bottom of the video. Using this as a lead, the Desk conducted another keyword search and was directed to an Instagram account with the handle @extremedrive08. Here is the link to the handle, along with a screenshot. The Desk then scanned the content posted on the page and found duplicate footage, identical to the viral video, which was uploaded on May 1, 2025. The Desk found that several users had commented on the video, stating it to be AI-generated. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk ran the video through Cantilux (an AI detection tool), which revealed that the footage exhibited pattern distortions and artefacts typically associated with AI-generated media. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video was AI-generated and bore no connection to any real incident in Agra.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of woman driving car on railway track in Telangana shared with a false communal angle; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 2 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a woman driving a car along railway tracks is being widely shared on social media, with users falsely claiming that the driver is a Muslim woman. The posts also allege that the event took place in Telangana. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the woman involved in the incident is Vamika Soni, a 34-year-old from Lucknow. The Desk spoke to Shankarpally police inspector K. Srinivas Goud, who confirmed that the accused is not Muslim. Therefore, the video is being shared with a false communal narrative that misrepresents the facts of the case. Claim: A purported video of a car allegedly driven by a woman on the railway tracks was shared by an X user named 'RajeshSahu7994' on June 30, claiming that the incident happened in Telangana and the woman in the video was Muslim. "A new way of jihad. Leave Abdul aside, even Fatima is not forgetting her purpose. But how did she end up here. This video is from #Bharat's Telangana Ranga Reddy. This community and the Chinese secular gang will never let India progress," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of these keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found that several social media accounts had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by the Tribune dated June 27, 2025. As per the report, a drunk woman drove her car onto the railway tracks, ignoring staff warnings. The reckless act disrupted eight trains before she crashed into nearby trees. She was rescued and later arrested by the authorities. The incident has raised serious concerns over railway safety and public behaviour. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. According to a report by News 18, published on June 30, 2025, the Hyderabad police identified the woman during a preliminary investigation, confirming that she is from Lucknow and has been living in Hyderabad due to her professional commitments with an IT firm. She recently lost her job and had gone to the Narsingi police station with a grievance earlier that morning around 6:30 AM before suddenly leaving without taking her bag. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Further searches led us to a report by Hindustan Times dated June 27, 2025, which identified the accused as Vomika Sony from Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, thereby clarifying the woman's identity. "The incident happened at around 7 am between Nagulapalli and Shankarpalli stations when the woman, identified as Vomika Sony from Lucknow in Uttar Pradesh, suddenly entered the railway tracks at a level-crossing gate between Shankarpally-Nagulapally stations and continued driving her car, a Kia Sonet, despite attempts by railway staff to stop her, a railway official said," the report read. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. As part of the investigation, the Desk contacted Shankarpally police inspector K Srinivas Goud, who told Press Trust of India that the accused is not a Muslim. "She is not a Muslim," says Shankarpally police inspector K Srinivas Goud. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the accused woman who drove on railway tracks in Telangana is not a Muslim, and the video was shared with a false claim on social media.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2024 video from Rajasthan falsely shared as Yadav community protest over Etawah torturing incident
content: New Delhi, July 2 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Days after the alleged caste-based tonsuring of a Bhagwat Katha preacher and his aide in Etawah's Dandarpur village, a purported video featuring a large group of people was circulated on social media. The user who shared the video claimed it showed members of the Yadav community protesting on the streets of Etawah over the incident involving the katha vachak (narrator of holy texts). However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video dates back to 2024 and shows a nomination rally for Ravindra Singh Bhati, held on April 4, 2024, in Barmer, Rajasthan. The video is unrelated to the Etawah incident and was falsely shared on social media. A group of upper-caste men allegedly tonsured a religious preacher and his aide after discovering that they belonged to the Yadav community in Dandarpur village of Uttar Pradesh's Etawah district. The incident occurred on the intervening night of Sunday and Monday, and the accused were arrested on Monday. The four arrested individuals have been identified as Ashish Tiwari, Uttam Kumar Awasthi, Nikki Awasthi, and Manu Dubey — all residents of Dandarpur. Claim: An Instagram user named 'Yadav Anurag' shared a video on June 26 featuring a large group of people participating in a rally. The user claimed that the video shows members of the Yadav community protesting on the streets in Etawah over the incident involving the 'katha vachak' (narrator of holy texts). Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of these keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found that several social media accounts had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . The Desk then ran the extracted keyframes through a reverse image search and found the same video on the Instagram handle of MLA Sheo Constituency, Ravindra Singh Bhati, dated April 4, 2024, which clarifies that the video is a year old and unrelated to the Etawah incident. Here is the link , and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a set of combination images highlighting the similarities between the recent video and Ravindra Bhati's Instagram post. Taking a cue from this, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports and came across a report by Aaj Tak, uploaded on their official YouTube channel, which featured the same video as seen in the viral post, dated April 5, 2024. As per Aaj Tak, "Ravindra Singh Bhati's rally increased the tension of BJP-Congress in Lok Sabha Election! | Rajasthan". Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Another report by NDTV published on April 4, 2024, mentioned that a crowd of people had gathered at the nomination rally of Ravindra Bhati. It further highlighted that the crowd gathered at Ravindra Bhati's rally stunned opponents. The cover image of the report was similar to one of the clips seen in the video. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video dates back to 2024 from Ravindra Bhati's rally and is unrelated to the Etawah incident.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of behind-the-scenes film shoot of Kannada film falsely shared as real incident; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 3 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing police officials thrashing a group of people who were undressed was widely shared on social media. The users claimed that it captures police teaching a lesson to Ambedkar followers who were threatening 'Manuvadis. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video shows behind-the-scenes footage from the film Deadly Soma 2, shot in Karnataka. It does not depict any real incident. The video was shared with a false claim on social media. Claim: A video showing police officials thrashing a group of people who are undressed was shared by an X user 'bhimta_bsdk' on June 30, claiming that it captures police teaching a lesson to Ambedkar followers who were threatening 'Manuvadis. "The Bhimta gang, which was threatening Manuwadis on Instagram, got served today. Tochan Zindabad," read the post's caption. The post clocked 608.6k views on X. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of these keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found that several social media accounts had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived version can be viewed here and here , respectively. As part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the video and found the boards and shop name written in Kannada, which hinted that the incident happened in Karnataka. Following this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search, which did not yield any credible results or media reports covering the same. Moreover, we also noticed a logo at the top right corner of the video. We then ran the extracted keyframes through a reverse image search and came across a YouTube video uploaded by Kannada Pichhar—a page that uploads content related to movies. The 00:15-second video uploaded by the user was similar to the viral video being shared on social media. The caption of the video read: "deadlysoma movie shooting exclusive making". Moreover, the logo was the same as seen in the social media post. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. We also found the video on the Kannada Pichhar's Instagram handle, which shows a different angle of the same viral incident. The video begins with men running on the road, followed by police officials. The entire incident is captured by cinematographers and the filming crew, which is visible in the video. The caption, written in Kannada, translates to: "Policemen who stripped and beat a man in City Market | Deadly Soma 2 movie exclusive making video." The findings suggest that it is a staged scene from a movie, rather than a real incident. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video shows behind-the-scenes footage from the film Deadly Soma 2, shot in Karnataka. It does not depict any real incident.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Unrelated video of flash flood at Gujarat's Pavagadh temple falsely shared as scene from Mata Vaishno Devi temple; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 3 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it depicts the impact of heavy rains in Jammu and its surrounding areas, allegedly triggering flash floods near the Mata Vaishno Devi temple. The footage shows the stairway leading to the temple submerged in rainwater, making it appear like a cascading waterfall. Users claimed the video was from June 29, 2025. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found that it was falsely shared as being from the Mata Vaishno Devi temple. The footage actually shows a flood-like situation at Gujarat's Pavagadh Temple, where continuous heavy rainfall caused water to flow over the stairs, creating a waterfall-like effect. An unrelated video from Gujarat was thus falsely linked to a different temple location to mislead viewers. Claim An Instagram user, sandeep__yadav42, shared a video on June 30 claiming that heavy rainfall had triggered a flood-like situation near Mata Vaishno Devi temple in Katra, Jammu and Kashmir. The footage showed a heavy stream of rainwater gushing down the temple stairs, giving the appearance of a cascading waterfall. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of the keyframes in a Google Lens Search, the Desk found numerous social media accounts shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Reverse Image Search also led the Desk to a video published on the official YouTube channel of TV9 Gujarati on June 24, 2025. The visuals in this video matched those in circulation precisely. However, the title and description revealed that the footage was from Pavagadh Hills in Gujarat, not from Katra, Jammu and Kashmir. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot: A comparison image confirmed that the video shared by the news channel matched the one circulating on social media. Additionally, the Desk found another video published by News18 Gujarati, whose visuals also matched the viral video. The description clearly stated the location as Pavagadh Hills in Gujarat. "Amidst the heavy rains, a picturesque view was created on the Pavagadh hills of Panchmahal. The torrential rains activated the springs, with the view of the gushing waterfall of Khuniya Mahadev becoming a special attraction." Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that social media video has no connection with the Mata Vaishno Devi temple. The video was originally from Gujarat's Pavagadh Hills.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2022 Video of Colombian schoolgirl crossing river using pulley falsely shared as incident from India; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 3 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported video of a girl in a school uniform using a pulley to cross a river was recently shared on social media, accompanied by the claim that it depicted a crisis-like situation in India. The user alleged that, due to a lack of infrastructure, students from an unidentified location in India were forced to risk their lives by crossing rivers using ropes to attend school. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found that it was unrelated to India. The footage originated in Colombia, where students from the Puerto Mosquito area were seen crossing the Gaira River using a pulley system to reach their school. An old and unrelated video from Colombia was falsely shared on social media, misrepresenting it as an incident from India. Claim An X user, Aafrin (@Aafrin7866), shared a video on July 2, purportedly showing a school girl using a pulley to cross a river. The user alleged that the incident occurred in India and that students from an unidentified location were forced to take such life-threatening routes to attend school due to poor infrastructure. Sharing the video, the user wrote: "The most critical issue of the country, education, is being suppressed as Sanghi-BJP work together day and night to fuel Hindu-Muslim tensions." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (As of the time of publication of the story, the video garnered 73.6k views) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of the keyframes in a Google Lens Search, the Desk found numerous social media accounts shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Reverse Image search also led the Desk to a report published by NDTV on July 1, 2023. The Desk found that the feature image of the news report matched one of the keyframes it had used for the investigation. However, the subsequent details in the report stated that the video was from Colombia, a country in South America. The report mentioned that the girl could be seen using a precarious path to reach her school, where she crossed a river using a pulley or rope. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Below is a comparison image showing that the feature image from the news report matched the keyframe used by the Desk during the investigation. Next, taking cues from the above inputs, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find additional details related to the incident depicted in the video from Colombia. The search results led the Desk to a report published by a Colombia-based news portal, Zona Cero, in June 2022, which mentioned that the video of students crossing a river using a pulley system was indeed from Colombia. These were students from Colombia's Puerto Mosquito area, where they had to cross the Gaira River hanging from a pulley to attend school. "The viral videos prompted the Santa Marta mayor's office to visit the site to begin to structure initiatives to address student traffic in this area and ensure children don't have to risk their lives again by taking the pulley to cross the river," the report added. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of a schoolgirl crossing a river using a pulley was from Colombia, not India.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, Election Commission has not yet released poll dates for 2025 Bihar Elections; this social media post shares false details
content: New Delhi, July 4 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported social media post linked to the upcoming 2025 Bihar Assembly Elections was recently shared online. In the post, users claimed that the Election Commission had released the election schedule, stating that the first phase of voting would take place on October 21 and the final phase on November 20. The post further alleged that the vote counting would be held on November 24, 2025. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the claim was false. The Election Commission of India has not released the schedule for the 2025 Bihar Assembly Elections. The dates mentioned in the viral post originally pertain to the 2010 Bihar Assembly Elections. A fabricated post was thus shared on social media to mislead the public. Claim A Facebook user named Khan Habib shared a social media post on July 2, allegedly elaborating on the 2025 schedule for the Bihar Assembly Elections. In the post, the user claimed that the dates for the 2025 Bihar Assembly Elections had been announced, with the first phase of voting scheduled for October 21 and the last phase to conclude on November 20. The user also stated that the vote counting would be held on November 24. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google based on the details provided in the above-mentioned social media post. The search results led the Desk to multiple handles sharing the same claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively: In the next part of the investigation, to corroborate the claim about the 2025 Bihar Elections schedule mentioned in the social media post, the Desk scanned through the social media accounts and website of the Election Commission of India, which is responsible for administering elections in the country. The Desk could not find any official release or statement by the autonomous constitutional authority that corroborated the viral claim. However, the search led the Desk to a post shared by the Chief Electoral Officer of Bihar on his official Facebook page. In a post shared on July 3, the Chief Electoral Officer of Bihar clarified that the purported schedule for the Bihar Assembly Elections 2025, which mentioned the first phase of voting on October 21 and the last on November 20, was fake. The post also mentioned that the Election Commission of India had not yet announced any dates for the Bihar Assembly Elections. The claim being circulated on various social media platforms that the Bihar Assembly Elections will be held in six phases from October 21 to November 20, with the counting of votes taking place on November 24, is entirely untrue. The truth is that the dates of elections in India are fixed and announced only by the Election Commission of India. Publicising any kind of date or phase information without the official announcement of the Commission is illegal and misleading to voters," the post stated. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Additionally, in the subsequent part of the investigation, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search on Google to find details related to the election schedule mentioned in the social media post. The search result led the Desk to an official release by the Election Commission of India from September 2010. The Desk found that the election schedule mentioned in the viral post actually pertained to the 2010 Bihar Assembly elections. Upon scanning the release, the Desk confirmed that the 2010 Assembly Elections in Bihar were conducted in six phases, with the first phase of voting held on October 21, 2010, and the last phase on November 20, 2010. The release also stated that the vote counting took place on November 24, 2010. The dates for the elections mentioned in the official release matched those cited in the viral social media post. Here is the link to the official release by the Election Commission of India, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the Election Commission of India has not released the schedule for the 2025 Bihar Assembly Elections.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of Rahul Gandhi shared to falsely claim he attended Adani's birthday party
content: New Delhi, July 4 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video purportedly showing Congress leader and Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi was shared on social media, with users claiming that Gandhi attended the birthday celebration of industrialist Gautam Adani on June 24. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found that the video dates back to 2022. It shows Rahul Gandhi attending a private event in Kathmandu, Nepal. The timeline confirms that the video is old and unrelated to Adani's birthday. Claim: An Instagram user named 'sanjoyspeakth' on June 26 shared a video featuring Congress leader & LoP Rahul Gandhi, claiming that he was seen attending Gautam Adani's birthday celebration that was held on June 24. "On 24th June, Rahul Gandhi was seen at Gautam Adani's birthday party," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of these keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found that several social media accounts had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. The Desk then ran the extracted keyframes of the video through a reverse image search. It came across a YouTube video by India Today, dated May 5, 2022, which highlighted that Congress leader Rahul Gandhi was spotted at a nightclub in Kathmandu. The video clarified that it was old and not related to Adani's birthday. A video of the same was posted by BJP leaders Kapil Mishra and Amit Malviya, sparking controversy. "Telangana Congress Chief Revanth Reddy reveals that Rahul Gandhi was at the nightclub with the Chinese ambassador, sparking political reactions from BJP," read the description. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Another report by Times Now, published on their YouTube channel on May 3, 2022, stated that Congress claimed Rahul Gandhi was attending a private wedding function of a friend. "Congress leader and Wayanad MP Rahul Gandhi was seen grooving to music in a Kathmandu club, while his political party is in disarray. BJP attacked the Congress party and questioned its work ethics. Congress defended the former Congress president by saying that he was attending a private wedding function of his friend. People of Wayanad, the constituency of Rahul Gandhi, questioned the absence of Rahul Gandhi. At the same time, Union Women and Child Development Minister Smriti Irani was seen in Wayanad to review the progress of the Centre's schemes," read the post's description. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports. A report by India Today, published on May 3, 2022, highlighted that Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's visit to Nepal has become a topic of discussion on social media. While the BJP slammed the visit, Congress is defending it. Sources said that he went to Kathmandu to attend the wedding of one of his Nepali friends, Sumanima Udas. Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video dates back to 2022 and shows Rahul Gandhi at a party in Kathmandu, Nepal, not at Adani's birthday.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Deepfake Alert! UP CM Yogi Adityanath's PTI interview shared with superimposed audio to falsely claim he endorsed salt-cinnamon cure for ageing
content: New Delhi, July 4 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video featuring a video of Press Trust of India (PTI) CEO and Editor-in-Chief Vijay Joshi conducting interview of Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath was shared on a website, claiming they discussed about the various health issues and how home-made remedies eradicate the health problems fast and efficiently. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found that it was created using generative AI to disseminate false claims. The UP CM had indeed given an exclusive interview to PTI discussing a range of crucial issues from the Waqf Amendment Bill to the bulldozer actions, the controversial Namaz order in Meerut, etc. In a candid conversation, he also spoke on his vision for politics, prioritising the country, and the challenges faced while implementing reforms. During the interview, the PTI CEO and EIC did not ask any questions about health problems, and the UP CM did not provide any such answers, as claimed in the video shared on the website. The Desk also found the video to be shared by a malicious URL that often mimics legitimate platforms or uses deceptive tactics to spread misinformation or install malware. Claim: A video interview featuring PTI CEO and Editor-in-Chief Vijay Joshi and Uttar Pradesh CM Yogi Adityanath, claiming that they discussed the various health issues and methods to eradicate the root cause of ageing in seven days. The text over the video read: "97% of people suffering from joint pain don't know the simple and partially known salt water method that restores 100% joint health in 7 hours!" Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation To verify the claim, the PTI Fact Check Desk conducted a customised keyword search on the official website of the Press Trust of India to check for any reports or videos indicating that the Uttar Pradesh CM spoke about "mixing one spoon of salt and cinnamon and eradicate the root cause of ageing in seven days." No such reports or videos were found on any platforms related to PTI. Next, the Desk used the InVid tool to extract keyframes from the video. One of these keyframes was reverse-searched using Google, which led to the original video published on PTI's official YouTube channel. The video features Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath in an exclusive interview with PTI CEO and Editor-in-Chief Vijay Joshi, discussing a range of crucial issues, including the Waqf Amendment Bill, the use of bulldozers, and the controversial Namaz order in Meerut. The interview was live on PTI's YouTube channel on April 15, 2025. The Desk reviewed the full interview but found no mention of "eradicating the root cause of ageing in seven days", indicating that the viral video had been digitally altered. Here is the link to the original video, along with a screenshot. The video featured them in similar attire to that seen in the purported video, which claimed the two discussed "the root cause of ageing". Further, when we carefully analysed the link to the video, we found it to be a dubious website. Additionally, the lip movements of the PTI CEO and the UP CM did not match and looked out of sync, suggesting that the video might be fake or AI-generated. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk then ran the video through HiveModeration, an AI-detection tool, which resulted in a finding that the video is not AI-generated, while the audio is 68% AI-generated. The result clearly shows that the video has been taken from the original interview, while the audio has been superimposed on it. The Desk then ran the video through an AI-based tool, Resemble Detect, to analyse the authenticity of the CEO's and minister's voice in the viral clip. The results confirmed that the audio had been edited. Below is a screenshot of the same. Furthermore, the dubious link that uploaded the video has several comments at the bottom, and the PTI Fact Check Desk found the users commenting to be fake. When the Desk attempted to click on those comments to verify the authenticity of the users, we were unable to access them, confirming that they were fake. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Uttar Pradesh CM Yogi Adityanath's video has been digitally manipulated with superimposed audio to promote the eradication of the root cause of ageing in seven days.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of arrest in Rajasthan falsely shared as post-riot crackdown in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 7 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video circulating on social media claims to show Uttar Pradesh Police arresting supporters of Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad following the violence in Karchhana on June 29. The unrest reportedly erupted after Azad's supporters accused the police of preventing him from meeting the family of a Dalit man allegedly burnt to death in Karchhana, as well as the family of a rape survivor in the nearby Kaushambi district. The mob reportedly went on a rampage for over two hours. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found that the video is unrelated to the June 29 incident. It actually shows individuals apprehended on June 5, 2025, in Rajasthan for allegedly targeting a businessman. The clip was falsely linked to the Karchhana violence on social media. Claim A Facebook user 'Kanhaiya Singh' on July 2 shared a video featuring a few injured men being escorted by police officials, claiming that it showed Uttar Pradesh police arresting Chandrashekhar Azad's supporters who rioted during the Prayagraj riots. "Chandrashekhar Ravan supporters who RIOTED in Prayagraj are getting the TREATMENT they truly deserve from Yogi's UP Police," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of these keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found that several social media accounts had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. As part of the investigation, the Desk ran the keyframes of the video through reverse image search and found an X post by a user named 'Shankar Bansari Journalist' dated June 5, 2025. As per the caption, the extortion gang was caught red-handed, and four criminals were arrested from Sri Ganganagar, Rajasthan. "Sriganganagar Breaking News. Extortion gang caught red-handed, four criminals arrested! ₹5 lakh demanded from a businessman in the name of gangsters. Police captured criminals who arrived in a luxury Fortuner," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports and came across a report by Patrika.com published on June 5. The headline read: "4 miscreants arrested for extorting money in the name of gangsters". Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking the investigation further, the Desk then scanned the official social media handles of the Ganganagar Police and found that they shared news clippings of the arrest on their X , Facebook , and Instagram accounts. Below is a screenshot of the same. It confirms that the individuals seen in the viral video were apprehended on 5 June 2025 while targeting a businessman in Rajasthan. The incident is unrelated to the riots on 29 June 2025 in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video was unrelated to the riots on 29 June 2025 in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh. It shows individuals apprehended on 5 June 2025 while targeting a businessman in Rajasthan.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video of Amit Shah being attacked by a monkey outside a building shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 7 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported video of Union Home Minister Amit Shah "being attacked by a monkey while standing with government officials outside a building" was recently shared online. The video appeared to show a monkey jumping on the Union Home Minister as he greeted people with folded hands. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it to be AI-generated, falsely shared on social media, and intended to mislead viewers. Claim A Facebook user, Zulfi King, shared on July 1 a video that purportedly showed Union Home Minister Amit Shah being attacked by a monkey outside a building. The footage depicted Shah standing alongside government officials when a monkey suddenly jumped on him. "What did the monkey suddenly do to Amit ji amidst so much security?" the user wrote while sharing the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was reverse searched on Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media accounts that had posted the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , along with their archived versions viewed here and here respectively: The Google Reverse Image Search also led the Desk to a report published by The Financial Express on June 1, 2019. The report featured the same visuals of Amit Shah standing with officials outside the building, as seen in the viral video. However, nowhere in the report was there any mention of a monkey attack. The report originally stated that the image was from June 1, 2019, when Amit Shah officially took charge as Union Home Minister. "Amit Shah was received at the North Block office of the ministry by Union Home Secretary Rajiv Gauba and other senior officials," the report read. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Below is a comparison image showing that the visuals seen in the viral video match those in the original media coverage: The Desk also came across other news reports from reputable media outlets covering the same event. None of them mentioned any incident involving a monkey attack. Two such reports can be found here and here . In the next step of the investigation, the Desk closely analysed the video to determine whether it was real or fabricated. Several inconsistencies were found in the movements of individuals, particularly the personnel stepping aside during the alleged attack — their movements appeared unnatural and distorted, suggesting the video was AI-generated. Taking cues from these observations, the Desk ran the video through Cantilux (an AI detection tool), which revealed that the footage exhibited pattern distortions and artefacts commonly associated with AI-generated content. Below is a screenshot of the result. The Desk also analysed the video using Attestiv, another AI detection platform. The result flagged parts of the video as "suspicious." Below is a screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing Union Home Minister Amit Shah being attacked by a monkey was AI-generated and bore no connection to any real event.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Wimbledon 2024 photo of Sachin Tendulkar and his wife falsely shared as showing him giving standing ovation to Shubman Gill
content: New Delhi, July 7 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Following Shubman Gill's sensational performances of 269 and 161 runs at Edgbaston in the ongoing Test series against England, a collage featuring India's Test captain Shubman Gill and former cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar with his wife was circulated on social media. The user sharing the images claimed that Tendulkar and his wife gave a standing ovation to Gill. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the images are actually from Wimbledon 2024 and not related to the cricket match or Gill's performance. The photos were shared with a false claim on social media. According to reports, India stormed back into the series with a resounding 336-run win over England at Edgbaston, levelling the five-match contest 1-1. Leading from the front, skipper Shubman Gill was named Player of the Match for his record-breaking performance with the bat, scoring a monumental 269 in the first innings and a blazing 161 in the second, becoming the first player in Test history to post scores of 250 and 150 in the same match. Claim: A collage of a set of pictures featuring India's Test captain Shubman Gill and former cricketer Sachin Tendulkar with his wife was shared by an X user named '@mathewcbabraham' on July 6, claiming that Sachin Tendulkar and his wife Anjali gave a standing ovation to Shubman Gill. "Sachin Tendulkar and his wife Anjali gave a standing ovation to Shubman Gill winning the match in two straight sets," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the photo in the social media post through Reverse Image Search and found that several other users had also shared the same post, with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here ; their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. As part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a reverse image search on the second picture featuring Sachin Tendulkar and his wife and found the image to have been published on a stock image website, Getty Images. According to the information available from the image, Sachin Tendulkar and Anjali Tendulkar attended day six of the Wimbledon Tennis Championships at the All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club on July 6, 2024, in London, England. Here is the link to the website, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk scanned the official Wimbledon account and found a post welcoming the former cricketer. The caption of the post: "It's wonderful to have you with us again". The attire is similar to the one shared in a recent social media post. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Furthermore, the new captain, Shubman Gill, was hailed on Monday for leading from the front after India recorded their maiden Test win at Edgbaston, levelling the series against England at 1-1. After which, Tendulkar lauded the performance of the entire team and Gill. In an X post, he wrote: "A 𝘚𝘩𝘶𝘣lime innings from the 𝘮𝘢𝘯 of the moment! Congratulations, @ShubmanGill, on powering India to a brilliant Test victory! @RishabhPant17, @klrahul, and @imjadeja batted very well, especially in the 2nd innings. India's approach was to take England out of this game and force them to play differently, ensuring that there would only be one winner. What impressed me most about the bowlers was the length of their bowling. Needless to say, Akash Deep was the standout bowler, and in my opinion, he bowled the ball of the series to Joe Root. P.S.: Enjoyed the catch taken by Mohammad "Jonty" Siraj. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the images are actually from Wimbledon 2024 and not related to the cricket match or Gill's performance.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, Indian Railways not installing solar panels between train tracks; project details originally pertain to Switzerland
content: New Delhi, July 7 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported social media post suggesting a "path-breaking development" in Indian Railways recently surfaced online. In the post, the user claimed that removable solar panels would be installed between railway tracks in India. The user further alleged that the initiative was being undertaken by an Indian startup named Sun-Ways. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found it to be false. The Desk found that the project of installing removable solar panels on railway tracks is actually being implemented in Switzerland, not India. Additionally, the startup Sun-Ways, involved in the project, is based in Switzerland, not India. A false post was shared on social media to mislead viewers. Claim An X user, Rahul Kumar Das (@Rahul_Invest), shared a post on June 30 claiming that an Indian startup named Sun-Ways is deploying removable solar panels directly between railway tracks in the country. The user stated that once implemented, the move could generate over one terawatt-hour of electricity annually. India is turning train tracks into power plants. In a game-changing move for sustainable infrastructure, Indian startup Sun-Ways is deploying removable solar panels directly between railway tracks. No extra land needed. No disruption to rail services. Zero visual pollution. This approach could produce over one terawatt-hour of electricity annually, potentially powering over 200,000 homes — all by reimagining the space we already have," the user claimed. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (As of the time of publication, the post had garnered 7,132 views) Investigation The Desk ran the image shared along with the viral post through Google Reverse Image Search. The search led the Desk to several social media accounts that had posted the same picture along with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. In the next step of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to gather more information about the initiative. The search led to a report published by Swiss news portal swissinfo.ch on April 29, 2025. The Desk found that the feature image used in the report matched the image in the viral post. However, the report clearly stated that the project is being implemented in Switzerland, not India. The report also clarified that the startup Sun-Ways, which is deploying the solar panels, is based in Switzerland. It further noted that the image in question showed solar panels being installed between the railway tracks near Buttes, a town in western Switzerland. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Additionally, the Desk found a similar report published by the Indonesia Business Post in May 2025. The report used the same image as the viral post and reaffirmed that the initiative is being trialled in Switzerland, not India. "Swiss startup Sun-Ways has launched an innovative solar panel system that can be installed directly onto railway tracks without disrupting train operations. The removable solar panels are currently undergoing a trial phase along a 100-meter stretch of track in Buttes, Switzerland," the report stated. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: In a further step, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search to determine if Indian Railways is considering a similar project. However, the search did not yield any credible news reports confirming that such an initiative is being implemented or planned in India. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the project of installing removable solar panels between railway tracks is currently being implemented in Switzerland by the Swiss startup Sun-Ways, and not in India.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Deepfake video falsely claims Lt Gen Rahul R Singh "admitted" loss of S-400 system during Operation Sindoor; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 8 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported video featuring Lt Gen Rahul R Singh, Deputy Chief of Army Staff (CD&S), allegedly shows him "admitting" that India lost S-400 air defence systems during a recent military escalation with Pakistan in May 2025. The video was widely circulated on social media, sparking significant concern and speculation. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the viral clip and found it to be misleading. The video was edited, and at no point during his address did Lt Gen Rahul R Singh make any such statement. The clip was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim: A purported video featuring Deputy Chief of Army Staff Lt. Gen. Rahul R. Singh "admitting" to India allegedly losing S-400 defence systems during the military escalation with Pakistan in May 2025, was shared by an X user named 'The Geo Scope' on July 7. In the 1 minute 29 seconds video, the Deputy Chief of Army Staff said: "Few lessons that I thought I must flag as far as Operation Sindoor is concerned. Firstly, one border, two adversaries. So, we saw Pakistan on one side, but the adversaries were actually two, or perhaps three or four. We are currently in negotiations with Russia to get two S-400 systems by the end of August, which we lost to Chinese missiles on 10th May. But rest assured, our air defence will be fully operational soon. So Pakistan was the front face. We had China providing all possible support…" Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of these keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found that several social media accounts had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . As part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find relevant media reports that covered Deputy Chief of Army Staff Lt. Gen. Rahul R. Singh. But our search did not yield any relevant reports, and given the sensitivity of the matter, it would have received broad media coverage. Upon further scanning the search results, we found that Lieutenant General Rahul R. Singh, Deputy Chief of Army Staff (Capability Development and Sustenance), was delivering an inaugural address on New Age Military Technologies. He discussed the ceasefire between India and Pakistan. In an X post by Press Trust of India, in the 1 minute 18 seconds clip, Deputy Chief of Army Staff Lt. Gen. Rahul R. Singh says, "Few lessons that I thought I must flag as far as 'Operation Sindoor' is concerned. Firstly, one border, two adversaries. Pakistan was the front face. We had China providing all possible support, and it's no surprise because if you were to look at statistics, in the last five years, 81 per cent of the military hardware that Pakistan is getting is all Chinese. So, it's no surprise... China has perhaps seen that it's able to test its weapons against various other weapon systems that are available. It's like a live lab which is available to it." In the video, he did not mention any "negotiations with Russia to get two S-400 systems…which we lost to Chinese missiles" in the middle of his statements on Pakistan and China, contradicting the viral clip. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. In the video, Desk noticed the 'FICCI' logo in the backdrop of the now-viral footage, and taking a cue from this, Desk accessed the press release detailing his recent address, which did not contain any information about the alleged 'negotiations with Russia' to procure the device. Here is the link to the release, and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk also noticed a change in the viral audio froms 0:15 seconds to 0:31 seconds, where he purportedly spoke on the S-400s as compared to the rest of the clip. Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the video through Hive Moderation, an AI-detection tool, and it detected that the video likely contains AI-generated or deepfake content. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that in the original video, during the 0:15 seconds to 0:31 seconds timeline, Lt Gen Rahul R Singh said, 'Pakistan was the front face. We had China providing all possible support, and it's no surprise because if you were to look at statistics, in the last five years, 81 per cent of the military hardware that Pakistan is getting is all Chinese.' A manipulated video of him allegedly saying, 'We are currently in negotiations with Russia to get two S-400 systems by the end of August, which we lost to Chinese missiles on 10th May,' was shared as real on social media.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of miscreants with tonsured heads paraded in Rajasthan falsely shared as accused arrested in Prayagraj violence; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 8 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a group of men with tonsured heads being paraded on a road by police was recently shared online. The user claimed it depicted police action against supporters of the Chandra Shekhar Azad-led Bhim Army, allegedly involved in the violent protest held in Prayagraj late last month. The video showed the men, identified as the accused in the vandalism and stone-pelting incident in Prayagraj, apparently apologising with folded hands. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found that the video originated from Rajasthan. The video initially showed Rajasthan Police parading 12 miscreants arrested for planning to rob a petrol pump in two different police station areas in Baran district. The police first shaved the heads of the accused and then paraded them through the city. This unrelated footage from Rajasthan was falsely shared on social media to mislead viewers. Claim An X handle named Megh Updates (@MeghUpdates) shared on July 3 a video purportedly showing Uttar Pradesh Police punishing Bhim Army supporters involved in the violent protest in Prayagraj. The footage showed police parading the accused on the road, with the latter also seen allegedly apologising with folded hands. "Look what Baba's Police have done with the blue hooligans who went on a rampage after getting instigated to take law and order into their own hands in Uttar Pradesh's Prayagraj," the user captioned the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publication of the story, the video garnered 405.2k views) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts of those who have shared the same video with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Reverse Image Search also led the Desk to a news report published by NDTV Rajasthan on June 3, 2025. The individuals seen in the viral video matched those shown in the video featured in the news report. However, the accompanying details clarified that the incident occurred in Rajasthan, not Uttar Pradesh. The report stated that the video showed Rajasthan Police parading 12 miscreants who had been arrested for planning to rob petrol pumps in two different police station areas in Baran. "The police first shaved the heads of the 12 arrested accused and then paraded them across the city," the report read. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image that highlights the individuals seen in the viral video match those in the NDTV report. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find further details related to the incident. The search result led the Desk to a statement shared by Prayagraj Police on its official X handle, which clearly stated that the viral video originated from Rajasthan, not Uttar Pradesh. "This incident is related to the arrest of miscreants planning to loot petrol pumps in two different police station areas in Baran, Rajasthan. This post circulating on social media is false and misleading. This video is not related to the Prayagraj district. Prayagraj denies the said misleading/false post," the Prayagraj Police stated. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot. Additionally, to gather accurate information about police action in Prayagraj following the recent vandalism by Bhim Army supporters, the Desk conducted another keyword search. The search led to an India Today report dated June 30, which stated that Uttar Pradesh Police had arrested 50 supporters of Nagina MP and Bhim Army chief Chandrashekhar Azad in connection with the incident. "The incident took place on June 29 when authorities stopped the MP from entering a village where he intended to meet families of victims from recent incidents in Kaushambi and Karchana," the report stated. "Yamuna Nagar Deputy Commissioner of Police Vivek Chandra Yadav informed that around 50 people accused of stone-pelting and vandalism near Isota village have been arrested, while police are working to identify the rest of the mob," the report added. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an unrelated video from Rajasthan showing 12 accused in a robbery attempt being paraded by police was falsely shared on social media, linking it to the recent violence in Prayagraj.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2019 video of a woman being thrashed in Pakistan falsely shared with a communal spin; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 8 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of a woman being brutally thrashed by two individuals outside a building (seemingly a government office) was recently shared online. The user claimed the video depicted an incident from Pakistan, where a Hindu girl, who was trying to reach a local court to allegedly file a complaint following her elder sister's forced abduction and marriage, was obstructed by individuals present there. The video showed the men kicking and punching her outside the court premises. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found, through its investigation, that the woman was a Pakistani national, identified as Amrit Shahzadi. According to Pakistan's local daily, Dawn, she visited a court in Shakargarh in October 2019 in connection with a land dispute. A group of people, including lawyers, then assaulted her and her cousin, Abdul Qayyum, for pursuing the case. The claim made in the social media post was false. Claim An X user named Vini (@Vini__007) shared on June 24 a video purportedly showing a Hindu girl being brutally thrashed in Pakistan. The user claimed the video depicted an incident where a Hindu girl was trying to reach a court after her elder sister had been forcibly kidnapped and married off. However, as she was attempting to enter the court, Muslim lawyers allegedly punched and kicked her. "The girl is from the Hindu religion, her elder sister was forcibly taken and married off, and the younger sister reached the court... but they are not even letting her enter the court... see what a scene? Even there in the court, they are not allowing her to go in... they are punishing her, kicking her, and driving her away. There is no democracy for Hindus there. Now, do you understand why CAA/NRC is necessary? Yet the Hindu brotherhood here wants to maintain harmony," the user wrote in the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing, the video had garnered 7,864 views) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across multiple social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. The Google Reverse Image search also led the Desk to a report published by the Times of India on October 30, 2019. The report included the same video of a woman being thrashed by two individuals, as seen in the social media post. However, the accompanying details stated that the incident reportedly took place in 2019 at Shakargarh, Pakistan, where a woman identified as Amrit Shahzadi appeared in court for a hearing. She was attacked by a lawyer there. The lawyers, in their defence, alleged that the woman had attacked them first. Nowhere in the report was any communal angle mentioned. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image highlighting that the content seen in the social media video matches the video published by the news outlet. Next, taking cues from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find further details about the incident. The search led to a report published by Pakistan-based news outlet Dawn in 2019. The report identified the woman as Amrit Shahzadi, a resident of Shahpur Bhangu village in Pakistan. According to Dawn, Shahzadi and her cousin, Abdul Qayyum, had visited a court in Shakargarh concerning a land dispute case, but were assaulted there by a group of people, including lawyers, for pursuing it. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video from Pakistan's Shakargarh court, where lawyers thrashed a woman for reportedly pursuing a land dispute case, was falsely shared with a communal spin.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video of news anchor Sudhir Chaudhary falsely shared with claim that ration card holders will receive ₹5,000
content: New Delhi, July 9 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video was circulated on social media, allegedly showing news anchor Sudhir Chaudhary reading a news bulletin that claimed all ration card holders would receive ₹ 5,000 under new government rules effective from July 1, 2025. The video also urges viewers to apply for the scheme through a website called 'jharnanews.com'. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and confirmed it to be false. The video features AI-generated audio mimicking Sudhir Chaudhary's voice, and the entire post has been created to mislead users. The government has announced no such scheme, and Sudhir Chaudhary has not made any such statement. Claim: A purported video featuring journalist Sudhir Chaudhary reading a bulletin that claimed all ration card holders would receive ₹5,000 under new rules, effective from 1 July 2025, and that people should apply on a website called 'jharnanews.com'. In the video, Sudhir Chaudhary says, "From July 1, ration card holders will receive ₹5,000 under the new scheme of the government…" Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation: The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across multiple social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. One such post can be found here . To verify the claim, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports that cited the information mentioned in the viral post. However, the search did not yield any relevant reports or official announcements from the government. Given the seriousness of the issue, it would have received widespread media coverage. However, we did scan through the myScheme government website to check whether any such scheme exists. However, we found no mention of any scheme offering ₹5,000 to ration card holders, and no related information was available on the website. Here is the link to the website. We conducted another set of customised keyword searches to find the official press release on the Press Information Bureau, but we found no information about the scheme. Hinting that the information given in the viral video is fake. Here is the link to the PIB website. Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk ran the extracted keyframes through reverse image search and found the original video of Sudhir Chaudhary's news bulletin on DD News YouTube channel, titled DECODE with Sudhir Chaudhary LIVE: Iran Vs Israel War | Donald Trump | Ali Khamenei | Emergency, dated June 23, 2025. In that video, journalist Sudhir Chaudhary was presenting an episode of his DECODE series, discussing the Israel-Iran conflict in June 2025. We reviewed the entire video and found that at no point did he mention any scheme offering ₹5,000 to all ration card holders from July 1. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from the above findings, we realised that the audio in the viral post might be manipulated or AI-generated. We then ran the video through Hive Moderation, an AI-detection tool, which detected that the video is likely to contain AI-generated or deepfake content. Below is a screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim made in the video of the scheme offering ₹5,000 to all ration card holders from July 1 is fake. Additionally, Sudhir Chaudhary's audio is AI-generated, and the entire post was shared to mislead users.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Image of Bangladeshi woman attacked in family dispute falsely linked to communal violence; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 10 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A disturbing image of a woman covered in a plastic sheet and lying on the floor was recently shared online. The user claimed it showed a Hindu woman who had been brutally tortured to death in Bangladesh. It was alleged that the woman was raped and then murdered, with her body wrapped in polythene and discarded. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found it to be false and communally misleading. The image actually shows a Bangladeshi woman named Maria Begum, who was attacked due to a family dispute but survived. This unrelated incident from Bangladesh was falsely shared on social media to mislead viewers. Claim An X user named Deshbhakt (@Deshbhakt1392) shared, on June 30, a visually distressing image claiming it showed a Hindu woman who was purportedly tortured to death in Bangladesh. The picture showed the woman's body lying on the floor, wrapped in plastic. "After the horrific gang rape incident, another Bengali Hindu woman, legs and hands tied up, raped, murdered and thrown wrapped in polythene by Muslims in Bangladesh," the user posted along with the image. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the image shared in the social media post through Google Lens. The search result led the Desk to multiple social media accounts of those who have shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The reverse image search also led the Desk to a report published by a Bangladesh-based news daily, Khaborer Kagoj, on June 29, 2025. The report used the same image of a woman (blurred due to its disturbing nature) as seen in the social media post, stating that she was rescued by police near the Barisal-Bhola highway in Bangladesh in a critical condition. The report mentioned that the victim's hands and legs were tied and that she had been wrapped in polythene before being dumped by the roadside. However, she survived the attack. "She had been taken to the One Stop Crisis Centre (OCC) of Sher-e-Bangla Medical College Hospital in Bangladesh, where she is undergoing treatment," the report added. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. (Important: The feature image of the report is blurred due to its visually distressing appearance.) In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above inputs, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to identify the woman and gather further details related to the incident. The search result led the Desk to a report published by another Bangladesh-based news portal, Ajker Patrika, on June 29, 2025, which elaborated on the motive behind the attack as well as the identity of the victim. The report identified the woman as a 23-year-old Maria Begum from Bangladesh, and not a Hindu woman as claimed in the social media post. She alleged that her husband's ex-wife's relatives tortured her to force an abortion. She stated, "Her husband's ex-wife's brothers kidnapped her, took her to a forest, tortured her, tied her hands and feet, and left her wrapped in polythene." Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the image was falsely shared as part of a communal narrative. It showed Maria Begum, a Bangladeshi woman who survived a family-related assault.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Ritual of 'Agni Keli' at Karnataka temple falsely shared as 'fight over donations'
content: New Delhi, July 10 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a large crowd of men wearing dhotis and throwing burning torches at each other was widely circulated on social media. The user who shared the video claimed that pandits were attacking one another due to a dispute over donation money. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video actually depicts the 'Thootedhara' or 'Agni Keli' ritual, performed during the annual fair at the Kateel Durga Parameshwari Temple in Mangaluru.
