The video has no connection to any dispute over donations and was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim: A video featuring a large crowd wearing 'dhotis' and throwing burning torches at each other was shared by an X user named 'Surya Raj नागवंशी' on July 7, claiming that Pandits attacked each other due to a dispute over donation money. "When beggars didn't get a share from the donation box, they started fighting among themselves!!! If this isn't a business, then what is????!!!," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation: The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across multiple social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . As part of the investigation, the Desk ran the extracted keyframes through a reverse image search, which led to a YouTube report by April 21, 2025. The visuals seen in the report were similar to those seen in the social media post. The report highlighted that this is Thootedara, also known as Agni Keli, a centuries-old ritual held at the Sri Durgaparameshwari Temple. Villagers from Attoor and Kodettoor come together, united in faith. After prayers and receiving prasad, they step outside the temple, ready to participate in a brief but intense fire ritual. The title of the report read: ''Thootedara: A Ritual Where Devotees Play With Fire, Celebrated In Mangaluru's Kateel Temple" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the. Another report by Odisha TV was published on their YouTube channel on April 21, 2025, featuring the same video as seen in the social media post. The title of the report read "Kateel Temple 'Thootedara' Ritual Illuminates Celebrations in Mangaluru". Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find relevant media reports that cite the ritual. The search led us to a report by ETV, published on April 21, 2025, which mentioned that every year, in April, Thoutedara or Agni Keli, an age-old ritual, is held at the Sri Durgaparameshwari Temple. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video actually shows the 'Thootedhara' or 'Agni Keli' ritual held during the annual fair at Kateel Durga Parameshwari Temple in Mangaluru. The video is unrelated to any dispute over donation money.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old and unrelated images from Afghanistan falsely shared claiming Indian embassy was under terrorist attack recently; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 10 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media post accompanied by two images, allegedly showing the Indian Embassy in Kabul, has recently gone viral. The user claimed that the embassy had recently suffered a deadly terrorist attack and that the images depicted the aftermath. The first image showed a building engulfed in flames, while the second showed a heavily damaged structure with several people standing in front of it, presumably involved in rescue efforts. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found it to be false. Neither image is related to any recent incident involving the Indian Embassy in Kabul. The first image is from 2014 and shows a house on fire in Herat, Afghanistan, near the site of a clash between insurgents and security forces following an attack on the Indian Consulate on May 23, 2014. The second image shows the German Embassy in Kabul, which was severely damaged in a blast on May 31, 2017. An old and unrelated incident was falsely presented on social media to mislead viewers. Claim An X user, Shashank Patel (@ShaPatel09), shared on July 7 a post (with two images), claiming that the Indian Embassy in Kabul was the target of a brutal terrorist attack. The user alleged that the images were taken from the site of the attack, with the first showing a building in flames and the second showing a dilapidated structure, with several people standing outside, seemingly participating in rescue operations. "The Indian Embassy in Kabul, Afghanistan, was targeted in a brutal terrorist attack. Brave diplomats martyred in the line of duty. This barbaric act violates all diplomatic and human values. The global community must strongly condemn this cowardice," the user wrote in the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publication of the story, the post garnered 14.9k likes) Investigation The Desk ran the images attached to the viral post through Google Lens. The search led to multiple social media accounts sharing the same images with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here ; archive versions are available here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find details pertaining to the alleged attack. However, the search results did not lead the Desk to any credible news reports or official government statements regarding such an incident. Given the seriousness of the claim, had the event been real, the media would have widely covered it, and concerned government officials would have released official statements. To further verify the claim made in the viral post, the Desk also ran the attached images through Google Lens. The search results confirmed that neither of the images was related to any recent attack. Both were, in fact, old and unrelated to the Indian Embassy in Kabul. Below is a detailed investigation of both images: (a) Image 1 claimed to show the Indian Embassy building engulfed in flames Below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk ran this image through Google Reverse Image Search, which led to a report published by the US-based news portal USA Today on May 23, 2014. The Desk found that the image shared in the viral post matched the image included in the news report. However, the accompanying details revealed that the image actually showed a house burning in Herat, Afghanistan, near the site of a clash between insurgents and security forces after an attack on the Indian Consulate on May 23, 2014. "Gunmen armed with machine guns and rocket-propelled grenades attacked the Indian Consulate in western Afghanistan's Herat province, an assault that injured no diplomatic staff. Indian officials said there had been a threat against its diplomats in Afghanistan, but gave no other details," the report stated. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Below is a comparison image showing the match between the image in the social media post and the one used in the news report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the image did not pertain to any recent incident. It dated back to May 2014. (b) Image 2 purportedly shows the Indian embassy building in a dilapidated state Here is a screenshot of the same. The Desk ran the second image through Google Reverse Image Search and came across a report published by Sky News on May 31, 2017. The report included the same image of a heavily damaged building. However, the accompanying details identified the location as the German Embassy in Kabul, which was badly damaged in a suicide bombing on May 31, 2017. The report stated that over ninety people were killed and more than 400 injured when a suicide attacker drove into the capital's diplomatic quarter and detonated explosives. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Below is a comparison image showing that the image used in the viral post matches the one featured in the news report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the second image also did not pertain to any recent incident involving the Indian Embassy in Kabul. It dated back to May 2017 and depicted the German Embassy, which was severely damaged in a terrorist attack at that time.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old Jaguar fighter jet crash photos from Gujarat falsely shared as recent crash in Rajasthan's Churu
content: New Delhi, July 11 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A collage of two images showing the wreckage of a severely burnt aircraft was recently shared by several social media users, who claimed it depicted the plane that crashed in Rajasthan's Churu on July 9. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found that the two images actually show a Jaguar fighter jet that crashed in Gujarat on April 3, 2025. The crash claimed the life of one pilot, while another ejected safely from the ill-fated aircraft. The images are unrelated to the recent Churu crash and were shared with a false claim on social media. Claim: An X user on July 9 shared a collage of two pictures depicting a severely damaged aircraft, claiming that it showed the same aircraft that crashed in Rajasthan's Churu on July 9. "An Indian Air Force fighter jet crashed near Banoda village in Rajasthan's Churu at around 1.25 pm on Wednesday," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation: As part of the investigation, the Desk ran the photo from the social media post through a reverse image search, which led us to a report by India Today, published on April 3, 2025. The cover image of the report was similar to the collage shared on social media. This proves that the image does not depict the recent tragic crash in Churu, Rajasthan. According to the report, the Jaguar fighter jet, which was on a training mission, crashed at around 9.30 pm on Wednesday near Jamnagar city, and caught fire. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the image in the social media post and the news report. Another report by the Times of India was published on April 3, 2025, mentioning that a Jaguar fighter jet of the Indian Air Force (IAF) crashed during a training mission near Jamnagar Air Force Station, officials confirmed. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the two pictures in the social media post show a Jaguar fighter jet that crashed in Gujarat on April 3, 2025. The crash claimed the life of the pilot, while another pilot ejected safely from the ill-fated jet.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2015 image of jet crash in Odisha falsely shared in name of recent IAF Jaguar crash in Rajasthan
content: New Delhi, July 11 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): After a Jaguar trainer aircraft of the Indian Air Force crashed in Rajasthan's Churu district, several social media users shared a photo of a wrecked fighter jet, claiming it showed the same aircraft that crashed on Wednesday, July 9. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the image is from 2015 and shows a training jet crash in Baripada, Odisha. It does not depict the recent crash in Churu. The viral post is misleading and shares a false claim. Claim: A purported picture featuring a wretched fighter jet was shared by an X user named 'The Tatva' on July 9, 2025, claiming that the image depicts an IAF Jaguar jet that crashed in Churu, Rajasthan, on Wednesday (July 9). "IAF pilot dies as Jaguar Fighter crashes in Rajasthan's Churu," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation: The Desk ran the photo through reverse image search and found that several other users had shared the same picture with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived version can be found here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a report by Firstpost published June 4, 2015. The report carried the same image as seen in the social media post. According to the report, an advanced jet trainer aircraft of the Air Force crashed in a paddy field at Kudarsahi in Mayurbhanj district, leaving two pilots injured. The timeline and the information in the news article clarify that the image is not recent and does not depict the recent incident of a fighter jet crash. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Another report by the Telegraph published on June 4, 2025, featured a similar image to the one in the viral post. As per the Telegraph, an Indian Air Force trainer aircraft crashed near Kudursahi in Mayurbhanj. Two pilots have been injured in the incident. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Moreover, a Jaguar trainer aircraft of the Indian Air Force crashed during a routine training mission in Rajasthan's Churu district on Wednesday (June 9) afternoon, resulting in the death of both pilots on board. In an X post, the Indian Air Force said that a court of inquiry has been constituted to ascertain the cause of the accident. "An IAF Jaguar Trainer aircraft met with an accident during a routine training mission and crashed near Churu in Rajasthan today. Both pilots sustained fatal injuries in the accident. No damage to any civil property has been reported. IAF deeply regrets the loss of lives and stands firmly with the bereaved families in this time of grief. A court of inquiry has been constituted to ascertain the cause of the accident," read the X post. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the image in the viral social media post actually shows a photo from 2015 and shows a training jet crash in Baripada, Odisha, not the recent Churu incident.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: This video of woman lying near some bushes is actually a movie clip; footage shared as real incident from Jharkhand with false claim
content: New Delhi, July 11 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A distressing video showing a woman lying near some bushes was recently shared on social media, with claims that it depicted a horrific incident that had occurred in India. The user alleged that the video was from Jharkhand, where a woman had been brutally gang-raped by six individuals and then murdered. The footage purportedly showed police inspecting the victim's body at an unidentified location in the state. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found the claim to be false. The footage is actually from the shoot of a film titled Lujeg and is not related to any real-life incident. The clip was misleadingly shared on social media as a genuine crime scene. Claim An Instagram user named Suman Patel (@suman_patel_oficial_25) shared a video on July 3, claiming it depicted a horrific incident that recently took place in Jharkhand. The footage allegedly showed the body of a woman discovered at an unidentified location in Jharkhand after being brutally gang-raped by six men and murdered. The clip showed police inspecting the body. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here : The search also led the Desk to an Instagram handle named Mg Prodip Panging. The user had posted a video, seemingly to be an extended version of the clip seen in a social media video. It included visuals similar to those seen in the social media video (where police purportedly inspected the body of a woman being discovered). It also showed police taking the woman's body to a hospital. However, what caught the Desk's attention was that the entire process— from police inspecting the body near a dump yard to shifting it to a hospital — was being professionally recorded on camera, strongly indicating it was part of a film shoot rather than a real event. The caption also stated that the scene was part of a film shoot titled Lujeg. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image confirming that the visuals in the viral clip match the footage shared by the Instagram user. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the earlier findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find more details about the movie Lujeg. The search led to a video posted by Instagram user Chandan Doley (@chand_raj_music), who had been tagged earlier by Mg Prodip Panging in the behind-the-scenes (BTS) video from the Lujeg set only. While scanning Doley's Instagram account, the Desk found multiple videos reportedly being shared by the user from the Lujeg movie set. One such video, shared on May 14, showed the same scene of police inspecting the body of a woman, but shot from a different angle. The caption confirmed it as a scene from the film. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot. Additionally, the keyword search led the Desk to multiple other videos (links of which can be found here and here ) posted on YouTube, which also stated that they were shot from Lujeg's movie set. One such video showed the woman seen injured in the viral clip putting a mask on her face inside an ambulance — another clear sign that the footage was scripted and not from a real incident. Here is the link to the video. Moreover, in the subsequent part of the investigation, the Desk contacted Chandan Doley regarding the film shoot video being shared as real. This copy will be updated upon receiving a response. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a woman lying injured and inspected by police is not from a real incident in Jharkhand but part of a fictional movie scene from a film titled Lujeg, falsely circulated online as real.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Unrelated video of dog attacking child in Thailand falsely shared as incident from Delhi; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 11 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A horrifying video of a dog attacking a small child was recently shared online with the claim that the incident took place in India. The user alleged that the footage showed a child, accompanied by two individuals, being attacked by a ferocious dog while walking on a street in Delhi's Rohini area. The video showed bystanders rescuing the child from the clutches of the dog. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found that it was unrelated to Delhi. The footage actually shows a terrifying incident that occurred in June 2022 in Pattaya, Thailand, where a pet dog brutally attacked a two-year-old child who was out for a walk with his nanny and older brother. An old and unrelated video was falsely shared on social media to mislead viewers. Claim An X user, Dilip Kumar Singh (@DilipKu24388061), shared on July 8 a video purportedly showing a dog attacking a small child in Delhi's Rohini area. The video, originally captured by a CCTV camera installed near the incident site, showed the victim, accompanied by two individuals, walking down a street when the attack occurred. Later, bystanders were seen rescuing the child from the dog. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Reverse Image Search, the Desk came across several media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively: The search also led the Desk to a report published by Thailand-based news outlet Daily News on June 21, 2022. The report included the same video of a dog attacking a child as seen in the viral post. However, the details revealed that the incident occurred in Pattaya, Thailand, not in Delhi as claimed on social media. According to the report, the incident took place in a village in South Pattaya, where a two-year-old girl out for a walk with her nanny and older brother was brutally attacked by a large, unsecured house dog. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image that highlights the individuals seen in the viral video match those in the news report. Additionally, the Desk found more Thailand-based news reports covering the same incident of a dog mauling a two-year-old child. The accompanying details in those reports also confirmed the incident occurred in Pattaya, not Delhi. Links to two such media reports can be found here and here . Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a dog attacking a child occurred in Pattaya, Thailand and not Delhi.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of Kanwariyas involved in clash in Haridwar resurfaces as recent incident; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 11 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a group of people vandalising an e-rickshaw was shared on social media with the claim that it depicted a recent incident in India. The user alleged that the video showed Kanwariyas (participants in the annual Kanwar Yatra pilgrimage) attacking the vehicle, presumably in a fit of rage. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it to be old. It has now resurfaced on social media and is being falsely shared as a recent incident. Claim An X handle with the username '@Deshmukh_0' shared, on July 11, a purported video showing a group of Kanwariyas vandalising an e-rickshaw. The user claimed the incident had occurred recently and showed the group of Kanwariyas toppling the vehicle and hitting it with a stick-like object. "Look how these people have set out on the Kanwar Yatra with pure hearts. They are doing such great work that even the police, out of fear, cannot stop them," the user posted the video with the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of these keyframes in a Google Lens Search, the Desk found that several social media accounts had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The reverse image search also led the Desk to a video posted by the Press Trust of India on its official X handle. The Desk found the video posted on the news agency's handle was similar to the one seen in the social media post. However, the accompanying details shared along with the video revealed it to be at least one year old and not related to any recent incident. The video was shared by PTI on its official X handle on July 24, 2024, with details mentioning that an e-rickshaw was vandalised and its driver was beaten up by some 'kanwariyas' in Haridwar's Manglaur. "The incident occurred after the e-rickshaw accidentally hit one of the 'kanwariyas' along the road, in which no one was reported injured," the post added. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a comparison image highlighting that the content seen in the social media video matches the video shared by PTI. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above inputs, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find details related to the incident. The search result led the Desk to a report published by the Times of India, where again it was found that the video pertained to an incident that occurred in July 2024, and not a recent one. The report mentioned, "Sanjay Kumar, the e-rickshaw driver, reported to Haridwar SSP Paramendra Singh Dobhal that his vehicle had accidentally hit a kanwariya, although no one got injured in the incident, nor was their sacred kanwar damaged. However, the group of kanwariyas attacked Kumar, beating him with sticks and rods, and proceeded to vandalise his e-rickshaw," the report added. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of Kanwariyas vandalising the e-rickshaw was old and falsely shared as a recent incident.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered image falsely shows Sachin Tendulkar posing with Virat Kohli's portrait at Lord's; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 12 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported image of legendary Indian cricketer Sachin Tendulkar was recently shared on social media, claiming to show him posing in front of Virat Kohli's portrait displayed at the Lord's Museum in the United Kingdom. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the viral image and found it to be digitally manipulated and falsely shared on social media to mislead viewers. The original image actually shows Sachin Tendulkar posing with his own portrait, which was unveiled at the Lord's Museum on July 10. Claim An X user with the handle @ishi_178 shared on July 10 an image purportedly showing former Indian cricketer Sachin Tendulkar posing with a picture of Virat Kohli displayed at Lord's. "Sachin Tendulkar taking a picture with Virat Kohli's photo at Lord's," the caption read. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publication of the story, the post gained 51k views) Investigation The Desk ran the image shared in the social media post through Google Lens. The search result led the Desk to several social media accounts of those who shared the same photo with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The reverse image search also led the Desk to a post shared by Sachin Tendulkar on his official X handle. The image posted by him on July 10 matched the background seen in the viral photo. However, Tendulkar's original image showed him standing in front of his portrait, not Virat Kohli's. Further, the details shared along the image revealed that it was taken from the Lord's museum in the UK, where Tendulkar's portrait has been unveiled recently. "I first visited Lord's as a teenager in 1988, and returned in 1989 with the Star Cricket Club team. I remember standing near the pavilion, soaking in history and dreaming quietly. Today, to have my portrait unveiled at this very place is a feeling that's hard to put into words. Life has truly come full circle. I'm grateful and filled with wonderful memories," the former Indian cricketer, along with his post, shared. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below, a comparison image has been attached herewith highlighting the visual dissimilarities between the viral image and the original one, although both share the same background setting. Next, using cues from the findings above, the Desk conducted a customised Google keyword search to verify the details of Sachin Tendulkar's portrait unveiling and to check if a portrait of Virat Kohli was also unveiled at Lord's. The search led to multiple media reports and social media posts that elaborated on the unveiling of Sachin Tendulkar's portrait at the MCC Museum. None of the reports mentioned anything about Virat Kohli. According to a report by The Hindu, the portrait of Sachin Tendulkar was painted by Stuart Pearson Wright from a photograph taken by the artist at his home 18 years ago. The reports also mentioned that the picture will remain in the MCC Museum until later this year and will then be relocated to the Pavilion. Here's the link to the report published by The Hindu along with a screenshot. In the subsequent part of the investigation, to determine whether the viral image shared on social media was real or not, the Desk closely analysed it. It was noticed that the portrait frame in the viral photo was distorted, and there was an illogical word printed on the jersey in the portrait. Also, the background markings in both images (the viral one and Tendulkar's original post) were identical. This suggested the image to be AI-generated. Below is a screenshot highlighting the key findings Based on these observations, the Desk ran the image through Sight Engine, an AI detection tool. While the whole picture could not be definitively marked as AI-generated, when the Desk snipped and isolated the portion showing Virat Kohli's portrait from the viral photo, Sight Engine flagged it as AI-generated. Below is a screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral image showing Sachin Tendulkar posing with Virat Kohli's image was digitally manipulated and was falsely shared on social media to mislead viewers.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video of gorilla handing over child to mother falsely shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 12 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of a gorilla gently handing over a child to its mother, who is seen walking in the animal's enclosure, was recently shared on social media with the claim that it depicted a real incident. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found the video to be AI-generated. It was falsely shared on social media as real to mislead viewers. Claim An X user with the handle 'wholesome moments' shared on July 10 a video purportedly showing a gorilla handing back a child to its mother, who was seen walking in the animal's enclosure. Sharing the video, the user wrote, "A gorilla at the Bronx Zoo lifted a child and handed it back to their mother. The situation could have ended a lot worse." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publication of the story, the post garnered 5,842 views) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The reverse image search also led the Desk to a video posted on a YouTube channel named AI Videos (@AI-Videos-Arg), which has over 70.1K subscribers. The Desk found that the video posted by the YouTube channel matched the one shared on social media. However, as the Desk conducted a detailed search of the video, it found that it included altered or synthetic content. Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk scanned through other videos shared by the same YouTube channel. The search revealed that the content shared by it was generated mainly using AI. Here is the link and archive link to the video, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image confirming that the visuals in the viral clip match the footage shared by the YouTube handle. Taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk ran the video through Hive Moderation, an AI detection tool, which confirmed the video contained AI-generated or deepfake content. Below is a screenshot of the result. Additionally, the Desk also ran the video through Cantilux, another AI detection tool, which also mentioned the video included a moderate level of AI involvement. Below is a screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of a gorilla safely handing over a child to its mother from the animal's enclosure was AI-generated.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2020 video of Pappu Yadav falsely shared as his reaction after being stopped from boarding Bihar Bandh protest vehicle in Patna
content: New Delhi, July 14 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video from Wednesday's (July 9) Bihar Bandh protest appeared to show Congress leader Kanhaiya Kumar and Purnia MP Rajesh Ranjan, popularly known as Pappu Yadav, being stopped from boarding a protest vehicle carrying Rahul Gandhi, Tejashwi Yadav, and other senior INDIA bloc leaders in Patna. Soon after, a clip of Pappu Yadav speaking to the media began circulating widely on social media. The user sharing it claimed the MP had made remarks against Tejashwi Yadav following the incident at the rally. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found that the viral video is from the 2020 Bihar Assembly elections. It has no connection to the July 9 rally and was shared with a false claim on social media. Claim: A video featuring Purnia MP Rajesh Ranjan (Pappu Yadav) was shared by a Facebook user named Vivek Kaku Sirohi on July 10, claiming that he commented against Tejashwi Yadav after being stopped from boarding an open van during the July 9, 2025, Opposition rally in Bihar. "If Lalu's name is removed from Tejaswi's name, even a dog will not ask - Pappu Yadav. It seems Pappu Yadav has started to get some sense after getting shocked," read the post's caption. Here is the link , and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation: The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of these keyframes in a Google Lens Search, the Desk found that several social media accounts had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On carefully analysing the video, the Desk noticed 'Live City's' logo in the top right corner. Taking a cue, the Desk ran a custom keyword search and found the original video on their official YouTube channel. The video was uploaded on October 16, 2020, and the timeline clarifies that the video is not recent, unrelated to the July 9, 2025, incident. The title of the report read: "Bihar Chunav : Tejashwi पर खूब गरजे Pappu Yadav, बोले - Lalu Yadav के बेटा के अलावा वो क्या है जी?" At the 5:45 mark, the clip from the social media post begins to play. The original footage was shot in the lead-up to the 2020 Bihar Assembly elections. In it, a journalist interviews Pappu Yadav about his campaign and the public response to his Jan Adhikar Party. Over the course of the video, Yadav makes multiple critical comments about both Nitish Kumar and Tejashwi Yadav. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Moreover, the entire issue began when Congress leaders Kanhaiya Kumar and Pappu Yadav were stopped from boarding the truck carrying senior Mahagathbandhan leaders, including Congress MP Rahul Gandhi and RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav on July 9, during the 'Bihar Bandh' rally, organised to oppose the Election Commission of India's (ECI) decision to carry out a Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral rolls ahead of the state assembly elections. Here is the link to the X post by PTI, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video where Pappu Yadav is seen commenting on Tejashwi Yadav dates back to the 2020 Bihar Assembly elections. It is unrelated to the recent July 9 incident

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video of Gautam Adani falsely claims he promoted 'high-income investment scheme'
content: New Delhi, July 14 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video circulating on social media shows industrialist Gautam Adani allegedly promoting a high-return investment scheme. In the video, he appears to urge viewers to invest ₹21,000 with the promise of earning ₹15 lakh within a month. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the video is a deepfake, created using AI. The original footage is from a 2023 event in Israel—specifically, the Handover Ceremony at the Port of Haifa, where Adani gave a speech in the presence of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The viral video has been digitally altered and shared with a false narrative. Claim: A video featuring Indian Businessman Gautam Adani was shared by a Facebook user named 'Charly H. Fox' on June 30, claiming that he is promoting a high-income investment scheme and urging people to invest ₹21,000 to receive returns of ₹15 lakh within the first month. The post had clocked 11k likes. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation: As part of the investigation, the Desk, after carefully analysing the video, found several discrepancies. For instance, his introduction at the start seemed a little different, and his lip movements were not in sync. All this hinted that the video might be manipulated and AI-generated. Before running the video through an AI-detection tool, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google, which did not yield any credible reports/ releases by the Adani group on any such announcement by the industrialist. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk ran the video through Hive Moderation, an AI-detection tool, and the tool detected that the audio is likely to be AI-generated Taking the investigation ahead, the Desk extracted the keyframes and ran them through reverse image search, which led to the discovery of a video uploaded on the official YouTube channel of Adani Group. The video dated January 31, 2023, where Gautam Adani delivered a speech at the Handover Ceremony at the Port of Haifa, Israel, in the presence of the Prime Minister of Israel, Benjamin Netanyahu. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Upon listening to the entire 10-minute 21-second video, the Desk did not find any mention of the investment scheme. Also, the attire was similar to the one seen in the viral social media post. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the original YouTube video. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of Adani endorsing a highly profitable investment scheme is a deepfake and AI-generated. In the original video, he delivered a speech at the Handover Ceremony at the Port of Haifa, Israel, in the presence of the Prime Minister of Israel, Benjamin Netanyahu.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Viral video falsely claims 'Pakistan Zindabad' slogans were raised in Deoria; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 15 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video purportedly showing a group of individuals raising 'pro-Pakistan' slogans was recently shared on social media, with the claim that it depicted an incident that occurred in India. The video allegedly shows people chanting "Pakistan Zindabad" during a rally held in Deoria, Uttar Pradesh. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the footage and found the claim to be false. The video actually shows a Muharram procession held in Deoria on July 6, during which members of a local akhara named "Five Star Club" in the Thana Kotwali area chanted "Five Star Zindabad" slogans—referring to the name of their group. According to Deoria Police, at no point were "Pakistan Zindabad" slogans raised. An unrelated video was falsely shared on social media to push an anti-India narrative. Claim An X user, Deepak Sharma (@SonOfBharat7), shared a video on July 7, allegedly showing individuals chanting "Pakistan Zindabad" slogans while holding torches. The user claimed the footage was from a recent rally in Deoria, Uttar Pradesh. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publication of the story, the video garnered 49.5k views and 5.3k likes) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across multiple social media accounts of those who had shared the same video with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here . In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google based on the inputs shared in the purported social media post. The search result, however, did not lead the Desk to any credible news reports that could corroborate the details mentioned in the viral post. It is also pertinent to note that, given the seriousness of the claim, if it had been real, the media would have covered it extensively. Next, as part of the investigation to verify the authenticity of the claim, the Desk scanned through the social media handles of the Deoria Police, since it was being alleged that the incident occurred in that region. This search led the Desk to the official X handle of the Deoria Police (@DeoriaPolice), where they had released a statement declaring the video to be false. In the statement, the Deoria Police clarified that the crowd seen in the viral video had gathered for a Muharram procession on the night of July 6, during which they chanted "Five Star Zindabad" slogans about their club named "Five Star" located in the Thana Kotwali area. They did not raise slogans of "Pakistan Zindabad", the Deoria Police stated. "The slogan 'Five Star Zindabad' is being misleadingly circulated on social media as if it were 'Pakistan Zindabad', which is completely false, baseless, and misleading. The procession was completed peacefully under the supervision of the local police. Those spreading such misleading and baseless news will be identified and necessary legal action will be taken against them as per rules," the police added. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video shows "Five Star Zindabad" slogans, not "Pakistan Zindabad", chanted during a Muharram procession in Deoria.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old Tamil Nadu protest shared as rally against Udaipur Files after Delhi HC Stay
content: New Delhi, July 15 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A day before its scheduled theatrical release, the Delhi High Court put a hold on the film Udaipur Files, stalling its screening across the country. Soon after, a video showing a large crowd of men wearing skullcaps and staging a protest began circulating on social media. Users sharing the clip claimed it showed people protesting against the film, which is based on the 2022 killing of tailor Kanhaiya Lal in Udaipur. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found that the video is unrelated to the movie. It actually shows a protest held in April 2025 in Krishnagiri, a town in Tamil Nadu, against the Waqf Amendment Bill. The clip has been shared online with a false claim. Meanwhile, the Supreme Court on Monday said it would hear "in a day or two" a petition challenging the Delhi High Court's July 10 order staying the film's release. Senior advocate Gaurav Bhatia, representing the film's producers, mentioned the appeal before a bench of Justices Surya Kant and Joymalya Bagchi, seeking an urgent hearing. Claim: A video featuring a huge crowd with men wearing skull cap and staging a protesting was shared by a Facebook user named 'Akram Ali' on July 9, claiming that it shows a protest against the film 'Udaipur Files' based on the killing of Kanhaiya Lal. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation: The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an Instagram post dated April 14, 2025, which mentioned that a protest was held in Krishnagiri, Tamil Nadu, condemning the Waqf Amendment Bill. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. The contents seen in the above post were similar to the ones seen in the recent social media post. Below is a set of combination images highlighting the same. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports that covered the event. The search led us to a report by The Hindu, published on April 14, 2025. According to the report, Krishnagiri District All Jamaath and District Ulemas Federation organised a massive protest opposing the passing of the Waqf Amendment Act here in Krishnagiri. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking the investigation ahead and considering all the above findings, the Desk geolocated the Krishnagiri area on Google Maps and found the same visuals as the viral video. Below is a screenshot of the same. Moreover, the Supreme Court on Monday (July 14) agreed to hear "in a day or two," an appeal challenging the Delhi High Court order staying the release of the movie Udaipur Files: Kanhaiya Lal Tailor Murder based on the crime carried out by alleged Islamic fundamentalists in the city in Rajasthan. Senior Advocate Gaurav Bhatia, who appeared for the producers of the movie, mentioned the appeal against the Delhi High Court order before a bench of Justices Surya Kant and Joymalya Bagchi, seeking an urgent listing. The HC order came on July 10, a day ahead of its scheduled release on July 11. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the protest was held in Krishnagiri, a town in Tamil Nadu, in April 2025, against the Waqf Amendment Bill and is unrelated to the rally against the film Udaipur Files.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video of village submerged in water falsely shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 16 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported video showing a group of individuals taking shelter atop the roof of their homes as heavy rainwater continued to inundate streets and areas leading to their village was recently shared on social media with a claim that it depicted a real incident. The video allegedly showed visuals from a village where heavy rainwater gushed into the houses of people, forcing them to take shelter on the roof. The visuals also showed cattle getting trapped in the mayhem. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it was generated through AI to mislead people into believing it was a real incident. Claim An X user, Adv. Nazneen Akhtar (@NazneenAkhtar23), shared on July 11 a video purportedly showing a village submerged in water. The visuals allegedly showed heavy rainwater gushing into the houses of people, forcing them to take shelter on the roof. "Think… for some, this weather is pleasant, while for others, it's deadly. Some are enjoying this weather, while others are praying for their safety," the user shared the post with the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publication of the story, the video garnered 59k views) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across multiple social media accounts of those who had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. Next, the Desk examined the video to find clues about its origin. The search led to the comment sections, where several users pointed out that the video was AI-generated. Below are screenshots of two such comments: Taking cues from these inputs, the Desk carefully analyzed the video and noticed several inconsistencies. For instance, the rope beds in the visuals moved in an unnatural manner, and the overall footage had an overly glossy finish—both common characteristics of AI-generated videos. Based on these observations, the Desk ran the video through Cantilux, an AI detection tool, which confirmed that the footage exhibited pattern distortions and artifacts typically associated with AI-generated content. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a village submerged in water was AI-generated and did not depict a real incident.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered video of EAM Jaishankar falsely claimed he talked about 'India losing 3 Rafales to Pakistan'
content: New Delhi, July 16 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported video of External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar was recently shared on social media, in which he could be heard claiming that India lost multiple fighter jets to Pakistan, including three Rafales, during the recent clashes between the two nations in the aftermath of the Pahalgam terror attack. The video allegedly showed Jaishankar stating that India had already lost three Rafale jets to Pakistan during the conflict. "They did it anyway. We responded quickly, and the next morning, Mr. Rubio called me and said the Pakistanis were ready to talk," Dr. Jaishankar was heard saying. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found that the video was digitally manipulated, with superimposed audio falsely suggesting that EAM Dr. S. Jaishankar admitted Rafale jets were shot down during the recent India-Pakistan clash. Claim An X user named @iUdhoke shared on July 3 a video purportedly showing External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar admitting that India lost multiple fighter jets to Pakistan during the conflict between the two countries following the Pahalgam attack in Jammu and Kashmir. "India's EAM Jaishankar has finally admitted the loss of multiple fighter jets to Pakistan, including three Rafales. It was very unfair of Pakistan to target Indian jets," the user captioned the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video garnered 15.8k views) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across multiple social media accounts that had shared the same video with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here . In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find reports that could corroborate whether EAM Dr. Jaishankar had actually made such a statement. The search, however, did not yield any credible news reports to confirm this. Given the seriousness of the claim, if the EAM had made such statements, media platforms would have covered it extensively. However, this was not the case. Next, moving further, as part of the investigation, the Desk again ran the extracted keyframes through Google Lens. The search result led the Desk to a video published by Newsweek (an American magazine) on its official YouTube channel on July 1. The Desk found the background setting captured in the Newsweek video matched exactly with that of the viral video, leading the team to carefully analyze the extended version. The Desk found that at the 43:05-minute mark, Jaishankar said, "...the Pakistanis did attack us massively that night. We responded very quickly thereafter. And the next morning, Mr. Rubio (the US Secretary of State) called me up and said that the Pakistanis were ready to talk." Notably, he made no statement about India losing Rafale jets to Pakistan's offensive. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image confirming that the visuals in the viral clip match the footage shared by the YouTube handle. Furthermore, based on the insights gathered, the Desk utilised an AI-based tool, Resemble Detect, to analyse the authenticity of the minister's voice in the viral clip. The results confirmed that the audio had been edited. Here is the link to the voice analysis result, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that External Affairs Minister Dr. Jaishankar's video had been digitally manipulated with superimposed audio to falsely claim India lost 3 Rafale jets during a clash with Pakistan.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Smriti Irani's podcast clips on Rahul Gandhi taken out of context and falsely shared claiming she praised Gandhi; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 16 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video featuring former BJP MP and ex-Union minister Smriti Irani during a podcast with journalist Sushant Sinha was circulated on social media, with users claiming that she praised Congress leader and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, for "his change in politics," adding that Gandhi believes he has "tasted success." However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found that the claim was misleading. The podcast, which aired on August 28, 2024, did not show Irani praising Rahul Gandhi. In the original video, her remarks were a pointed critique, highlighting what she described as "Rahul Gandhi's divisive political tactics." The Desk also contacted journalist Sushant Sinha, the podcast host, who told PTI Fact Check that a portion of her statement had been taken out of context and shared with misleading claims. He clarified that Irani did not, at any point, praise Gandhi or his politics. Claim: A video featuring actress and former Minister of Education of India, Smriti Irani, at a podcast with Journalist Sushant Sinha was shared by a Facebook user 'I Support Rahul Gandhi' on July 14. The user sharing the clip from Sushant Sinha's 'Top Angle with Sushant Sinha' show claimed that Irani allegedly praised Congress leader and LoP in Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, for "his change in politics", adding that the leader believes he has "tasted success". In the 00:53-second video, Smriti Irani says, "I feel there is a change in Rahul Gandhi's politics. He thinks he has tasted success. Like I said, when he talks about caste, he is using it as an instrument. He wears white T-shirts in the Parliament, he's aware of what kind of message it sends to the youth…" Here is the link and the archive link ; below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation: The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. As part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search for the original podcast, which led the Desk to Sushant Sinha's podcast with Smriti Irani, dated August 28, 2024. Smriti Irani discussed the Kolkata Doctor case and the law and order situation in Bengal during the podcast. Has Mamata Banerjee lost the trust, and should the President's rule be imposed in Bengal? Here is the link with the exact timestamp featuring the contents similar to that of the viral video. In the conversation with Sinha, when asked whose politics is dangerous between Rahul Gandhi and Arvind Kejriwal, Irani replies: "...I feel that there is a change in Rahul Gandhi's politics. He thinks he has tasted success. If you have noticed, when he talks about caste, he uses it as an instrument; when he wears a white T-shirt in Parliament, he's aware of the kind of message it sends to the youth…Some politicians are effective when they stick to the script, while others write their script for history…Both (Rahul Gandhi & Arvind Kejriwal) are moving for personal ambition, and Modi is moving for national ambition…" Irani further criticised Gandhi's earlier temple politics, suggesting his recent focus on caste issues is a tactical move to gain media coverage after his previous efforts failed. Here is the link with the exact timestamp mentioning the said content. "When Rahul Gandhi was going from temple to temple, was he getting that traction? No, he was not. It had become a joke, and people had begun to think that it was all an illusion. Their strategist then thought that if there is no political gain to be had from all this, what can give us that political gain? Caste is, in part, about gaining political traction. If it had been his political thought, it would have been reflected in his political journey. It is part of his political strategy…," says Irani. Below is a screenshot from the podcast, where the attire worn by both Smriti Irani and Sushant Sinha is identical to the one seen in the viral video. The viral videos, shared by the Facebook users, showed a clipped portion of Smriti Irani's remarks, falsely suggesting she was praising Rahul Gandhi's political growth and recent success. However, in the full podcast with Sushant Sinha, Irani was actually found criticising what she called his shift to divisive caste-based politics and strategic image-building, like wearing white T-shirts in Parliament. When asked, during the interview, whether Rahul Gandhi or Arvind Kejriwal's politics was more dangerous, Irani responded with a sharp critique, contrasting their "personal ambition" with PM Narendra Modi's "national ambition." In the original podcast, she said Gandhi had adopted caste politics as a deliberate strategy after his earlier "temple politics" failed and became a joke. She further claimed the new shift in his focus was not a sincere ideological shift but a move to gain media attention and political relevance. After watching the full podcast, it was clear that her comments about Rahul Gandhi were clearly sarcastic and critical, and it can't be taken as praise for him. Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk contacted Journalist Sushant Sinha, who clarified that Smriti Irani had spoken extensively about Rahul Gandhi's politics in this podcast, and the viral video contains only a part of it. "Smriti Irani said a lot about Rahul Gandhi's politics in this podcast, and the viral video contains only a part of it. The entire conversation should be heard to understand the full context," Sinha told PTI Fact Check Desk. It is clear that her statement was completely misunderstood. What may sound like praise is, in fact, a sharp critique of Rahul Gandhi's divisive politics. Smriti Irani plainly laid out how his strategy has shifted in recent years—from temple visits to a focus on caste-based issues. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim that Smriti Irani praised Rahul Gandhi is misleading. Her remarks weren't praise, they were a pointed attack, aimed at calling out what she sees as his divisive political tactics.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: May 2024 speech video of AIMIM chief Owaisi falsely linked to recent controversy over 'Udaipur Files' movie
content: New Delhi, July 17 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video featuring All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) chief Asaduddin Owaisi speaking at a public rally has been widely circulated on social media. Users sharing the clip claimed that Owaisi urged Indian filmmakers to focus on social issues like unemployment instead of making films that allegedly target Muslims. Some also linked his remarks to the recently stalled film Udaipur Files. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the video was from May 2024, during the Lok Sabha elections, when Owaisi addressed a rally in Paliganj, Bihar. In the speech, he criticised Indian cinema for often portraying Muslims in a negative light and urged filmmakers to focus on real issues like unemployment. He also questioned films such as The Kerala Story and The Kashmir Files, claiming they vilified Muslims and promoted the Love Jihad conspiracy theory. The timeline makes it clear that the video predates recent developments and has no connection to the Udaipur Files controversy. It was shared online with a misleading claim. Claim: A Facebook user shared a video featuring AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi from a public rally, 'Hindi Quran Girl,' on July 9, 2025, claiming that he urged Indian filmmakers to make movies about social issues like unemployment rather than provocative films against Muslims. It is linked to the recent movie Udaipur Files. In the 00:40-second video, Owaisi said: "...Filmmakers, why don't make a film on issues like unemployment…" The post garnered 6.2k views on social media. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation: The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. As part of the investigation, the Desk ran the extracted keyframes through Reverse Image Search and came across a live video recording from Owaisi's personal Facebook page. The video, dated May 26, 2024, clarifies that the speech is not directed at the recent controversy surrounding the Udaipur Files. On reviewing the whole speech, the Desk found that at the 34:02 mark, Owaisi urged filmmakers to stop portraying Muslims negatively in Indian cinema and instead focus on issues like unemployment. Earlier, around the 33-minute mark, he also questioned films like The Kerala Story and The Kashmir Files, arguing that they were made to vilify Muslims and promote the Love Jihad conspiracy theory. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Jansatta reported the same video on their official YouTube channel on May 26, 2024. The video was titled: "Asaduddin Owaisi Rally: चांदोस-पालीगंज पटना में गरजे ओवैसी, PM Modi पर बोला हमला!" The description of the video read: "Lok Sabha Elections 2024: AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi also put all his strength in Bihar for the seventh and last phase of Lok Sabha elections 2024. During this, Owaisi targeted Prime Minister Modi in Paliganj." Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video dates back to May 2024 during the Lok Sabha Elections, and the speech was delivered from Paliganj, Bihar. The timeline clarifies that the video is not related to the recent incidents and is unrelated to the Udaipur Files controversy.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Clipped video of Rahul Gandhi falsely shared claiming he termed Lord Jagannath Rath Yatra a 'drama'
content: New Delhi, July 18 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video featuring Congress leader and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, addressing a public rally, has been widely shared on social media. Users sharing the video claimed that he referred to the Lord Jagannath Rath Yatra in Puri, Odisha, as a "drama." However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that in the original video, Rahul Gandhi was criticising the Rath being halted for the Adani family, not the festival itself or its followers. A clipped portion of the complete video was circulated on social media with a false claim. Claim: A video featuring Congress leader & Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, addressing a public rally, was shared by a Facebook user, 'Mani Mohantay', on July 11, claiming that he termed the Lord Jagannath Rath Yatra in Puri, Odisha, a 'drama'. In the 0:30-second video, Rahul Gandhi says, "When Jagannath Yatra takes place in Odisha, just think, just think, a rath comes out, a rath of Jagannath Yatra comes out, lakhs of people watch it and follow it, and then a drama happens, a drama happens." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation: The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. As part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find the original video of Rahul Gandhi's address. The search led us to the official YouTube channel of the Indian National Congress, where the entire program was broadcast live on July 11. The title of the video read: "LIVE: Shri Mallikarjun Kharge & Shri Rahul Gandhi | Samvidhan Bachao Samavesh | Bhubaneswar, Odisha." Skimming through the entire video, the Desk could identify the timestamp where Gandhi mentioned the Rath Yatra. However, it was not to demean the attendees of the Rath Yatra. At 26:16 minutes, he says, "When Jagannath Yatra takes place in Odisha, just think, a rath comes out, a rath of Jagannath Yatra comes out, lakhs of people watch it and follow it, and then a drama happens, a drama happens. The rath is stopped for Adani ji and his family. You can understand everything about Odisha's government. This is not your government, this is not Odisha's government. This is the government of Adani and five to six other such industrialists." He was criticising the Rath being stopped for Adani's family, not the festival or its followers. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the YouTube video published on the official account of Congress. Another set of customised keyword searches also led the Desk to a report by the Times of India, published on July 13, 2025, which mentioned that Gandhi's statement regarding the rath being stopped for Adani, and his claim that corporates like Adani were governing the state. The headline of the report read: "Rath deliberately stalled to help Adanis pull chariots, says Rahul; he has a habit of lying: BJP" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Additionally, a report by ET Now, published on June 28, highlighted that Gautam Adani, Chairman of the Adani Group, participated in the sacred procession of Mahaprabhu on Saturday, June 28. Adani, along with his family members, were seen attending the Ratha Yatra 2025. "Billionaire Gautam Adani, the Chairman of Adani Group, participated in the sacred procession of Mahaprabhu on Saturday, June 28. Adani, along with his family members, were seen attending the Ratha Yatra 2025. Accompanied by wife Priti, son Karan and other family members, Adani paid obeisance to Lord Balabhadra, Devi Subhadra and Lord Jagannath, standing in front of their chariots near Gundicha Temple. Gundicha Temple is considered the trio's aunt's house," reads a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Congress leader & Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi's remarks were criticising the Rath being stopped for Adani's family, not the festival or its followers.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old Kanhaiya Kumar clip misrepresented as comment on Rahul Gandhi after Bihar rally controversy
content: New Delhi, July 18 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video featuring Congress leader Kanhaiya Kumar addressing a gathering was widely shared on social media, claiming that he criticised Rahul Gandhi. The user sharing the video linked the clip to the July 9 incident in Bihar, where Kanhaiya Kumar and Pappu Yadav were stopped from boarding Gandhi's van during an Opposition rally. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that Kanhaiya Kumar's video dates back to 2023 and has no connection to the July 9 event. In the original clip, Kumar speaks about democracy and citizenship and does not criticise Rahul Gandhi. A clipped portion of the entire speech was shared with a false claim on social media. Claim: A user shared a video featuring Congress leader Kanhaiya Kumar addressing a gathering, 'Jitendra Pratap Singh', on July 14, claiming that Kumar took a jab at the Leader of the Opposition (LoP) in Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, recently. In the 00:13-second video, Kanhaiya Kumar says, "Son of a king will not become a king. In a democracy, voters decide who our ruler would be." The user shared the video with a caption that read: "After being kicked off the stage like a dog, Kanhaiya Kumar is on the attack against Rahul Gandhi and Tejashwi Yadav" The post clocked 31.1K views on social media. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. On further running the extracted keyframes of the viral video through reverse image search, the Desk was led to the live broadcast on the official Facebook handle of IYC and found the full version of Kumar's speech from the Youth Convention in Bengaluru. The video was published on July 27, 2023. The timeline proves that the video is not recent and is unrelated to the July 9 Opposition rally in Bihar. Moreover, the background and Kumar's attire were identical to those seen in the viral post. The caption of the post read:, "Live - Behtar Bharat Ki Buniyaad IYC Youth Convention, Bengaluru , Day 2 #BuniyaadIndiaKi." At around 13:25 timestamp in the video, Kanhaiya Kumar says, "Today, we should say this with pride that we are Mallikarjun Kharge's soldiers. We are Rahul Gandhi's soldiers". As we proceed in the video at around 15:00 timestamp, he says, "Our communication is clear. This country belongs to the people and will always belong to them. We resolve that everybody who is born in this country, regardless of their caste, sex, and religion, will be a citizen of this country. Being a citizen means that the son of a king will not become a king. In a democracy, voters decide who our ruler would be. This democracy is the foundation of India. And all workers of the Youth Congress should work towards protecting democracy" Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the social media post and the video uploaded on the official page of Congress. Moreover, during the recent July 9 Opposition rally in Bihar, there were reports that Kanhaiya Kumar and Pappu Yadav were stopped from boarding Rahul Gandhi's van during the rally. According to a report by NDTV, dated July 9, 2025, Kumar and Pappu Yadav were about to climb the stairs to the van when they were stopped by personnel in charge of ensuring the security of Mr Gandhi and the other leaders. "In a potential embarrassment for the Congress, its leader Kanhaiya Kumar and Purnia MP Pappu Yadav were stopped from boarding an open van which had Rahul Gandhi, RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav and some other senior politicians on it. During the INDIA bloc's 'Bihar Bandh' protests against the special intensive revision of electoral rolls on Wednesday, Kumar and Yadav were about to climb the stairs to the van when they were stopped by some personnel who were in charge of ensuring the security of Mr Gandhi and the other leaders. Videos of both leaders being stopped are now being widely shared," read the section of the report. Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of Congress leader Kanhaiya Kumar dates back to 2023 and was shared on social media with a specific context. Moreover, in the video, he did not take a dig at LoP Rahul Gandhi, but a clipped portion of the entire speech was shared with a false claim linking it to the recent incident of the July 9 Opposition rally in Bihar.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Viral post claiming Astronomer CEO Andy Byron issued apology is fake; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 21 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Several social media users shared a purported statement attributed to Astronomer CEO Andy Byron, claiming that he apologised to his family, wife, and the Astronomer team after being caught on camera sharing an intimate moment with a female co-worker at a Coldplay concert in Boston. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the viral statement attributed to Byron is fake. The company, Astronomer, clarified that Andy Byron has not issued any such statement. The post circulating on social media is false. The company has further confirmed that Byron has resigned from his position, and his resignation has been accepted. The now-former Astronomer CEO came under heavy criticism and faced allegations of 'cheating' after Coldplay's Kiss Cam segment caught him embracing Cabot. As the camera panned toward them, the two abruptly parted. While Byron ducked immediately, Cabot tried to hide her face — a move that made them appear supposedly guilty. Claim: A purported statement from Astronomer CEO Andy Byron was shared by an X user named '@SillySaltyAFVet' on July 18, claiming that the CEO allegedly apologised to his family, wife, and the Astronomer team, after he was caught on camera sharing an intimate moment with a female co-worker at Coldplay's concert in Boston. In the statement, CEO Andy Byron highlighted how "troubling" it was that a private moment became public without consent. The post clocked 42.1k views on social media. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Further, apart from social media users, several Indian media outlets had also shared the same story. Links to two such reports can be found here and here . Investigation As part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find news reports or any information available in the public domain, but did not find any evidence to support the viral claim. However, when we carefully analysed the viral post, we found several discrepancies that pointed us towards the possibility of it being fake. For instance, the spacing errors in the third paragraph and the penultimate paragraph contained a misspelt word, "spectacle.fi". Below is a screenshot that highlights the same issue. Taking the investigation further, the Desk scanned the official X handle of the Astronomer and came across a post stating that the Board of Directors has launched an investigation into the matter, adding that Andy Byron has not issued any statement; reports stating otherwise are incorrect. Astronomer is committed to the values and culture that have guided us since our founding. Our leaders are expected to set the standard in both conduct and accountability. The Board of Directors has started a formal investigation into this, and we will provide more details as soon as possible. Alyssa Stoddard was not at the event, and no other employees were in the video. Andy Byron has not put out any statement; reports saying otherwise are all incorrect," read the X post's caption, dated July 19. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Another post by the company highlighted that Andy Byron has tendered his resignation, which the Board of Directors has accepted. "As stated previously, Astronomer is committed to the values and culture that have guided us since our founding. Our leaders are expected to set the standard in both conduct and accountability, and recently, that standard was not met. Andy Byron has tendered his resignation, and the Board of Directors has accepted. The Board will begin a search for our next Chief Executive as Cofounder and Chief Product Officer Pete DeJoy continues to serve as interim CEO. Before this week, we were known as a pioneer in the DataOps space, helping data teams power everything from modern analytics to production AI. While our company's awareness may have changed overnight, our product and our work for our customers have not. We're continuing to do what we do best: helping our customers with their toughest data and AI problems," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral statement claiming to be shared by Byron is fake, and Astronomer has clarified that Andy Byron has not put out any statement.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated image falsely linked to recent Bangladesh Air Force jet crash in Dhaka
content: New Delhi, July 21 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A dramatic image of a burning aircraft, with thick black smoke and bright flames rising from the wreckage, is circulating on social media. The photo shows several people standing in the foreground, while a few others closer to the scene appear to be emergency responders or bystanders. The image is being shared with the claim that it shows the Bangladesh Air Force jet crash in Dhaka. However, a fact-check by the Press Trust of India (PTI) found that the viral image is AI-generated and has no connection to Monday's (July 21) incident in Dhaka. It is being circulated to mislead people into believing it depicts a real crash. A Bangladesh Air Force training aircraft crashed into Milestone School and College in Dhaka's Uttara area. According to police, firefighting units, ambulances, and Air Force helicopters rushed to the scene soon after the crash. The Dhaka Tribune reported that over 50 people have been taken to the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery following the incident. Claim: An X user named '@Alamgie59081717' shared a photo of a burning aircraft with thick, dark smoke and bright flames rising from the wreckage. The user sharing the post claims that it depicted the Bangladesh Air Force jet crash in Dhaka. "Bangladesh Milestone Many students killed in college plane crash Everyone please pray for them," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation: As part of the investigation, the Desk ran the photo through Google Search and found that several other social media users had shared a similar picture with an identical caption. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived version can be viewed here and here , respectively. Next, the Desk examined the picture to find clues about its origin. On careful analysis of the photo, we found inconsistencies indicating that it might be manipulated and not depict the actual incident. For instance, the glossy background, the flames, and smoke have an overly smooth appearance, and the people in the foreground, their faces and body proportions look vague or oddly shaped. Below is a screenshot that highlights the same issue. Based on these observations, the Desk ran the video through HiveModeration, an AI detection tool, which confirmed that the footage exhibited pattern distortions and artifacts typically associated with AI-generated content. Below is a screenshot of the same.
