The Desk then ran the picture in the social media post through another AI-detection tool called SightEngine, which also detected that a significant part of it was created by AI. Below is a screenshot of the same. Moreover, a Bangladesh Air Force training aircraft crashed into Milestone School and College in Dhaka. The incident took place in Dhaka's Uttara area. Here is a link to the X post by PTI, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the found the image shared by the user on social media is AI-generated and unrelated to Monday's incident in Dhaka.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video falsely shared as recent bridge collapse in Bihar; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 22 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a crumbling section of a bridge, allegedly collapsing in Bihar, has been widely shared on social media. Users circulating the clip claim it depicts a recent incident in the state. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found that the video is AI-generated and digitally manipulated. It is being falsely linked to Bihar to mislead viewers into believing it shows a real bridge collapse. Meanwhile, Bihar has indeed witnessed its 10th bridge collapse in just over two weeks, according to officials. The latest incident occurred in Saran on Thursday (July 3), where two other bridge collapses had been reported within the preceding 24 hours. No casualties were reported from the collapse of a 15-year-old bridge over the Gandaki River, which connected several villages in Saran with the Siwan district. Claim: A video featuring a portion of a bridge collapsing was shared by a Twitter user, '@ManishCEO2', on July 19, claiming that the incident occurred in Bihar. "The collapse of bridges in Bihar continues unabated; these days, it seems like the season for bridges and overpasses to fall in the state. On Wednesday, five bridges collapsed in a single day. Such news is coming from Bihar every day. In this sequence, Wednesday crossed all limits when five bridges collapsed in a single day in the two districts of Siwan and Chhapra. Is this not the corruption of the government?," read a post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. As part of the investigation, the Desk first conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports that cite the same incident. However, we could not find any credible reports of the bridge collapse. Given the seriousness of the matter, if such an incident had occurred in Bihar or any other state, it would have received broad media coverage. Next, the Desk carefully analysed the video and found several inconsistencies that hinted that the video might be manipulated or AI-generated. For instance, people and vehicles appear unnatural, and in some cases, individuals seem to merge into one another. Below is a screenshot that highlights the same issue. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk ran the video through HiveModeration. This AI detection tool confirmed that the footage exhibited pattern distortions and artefacts typically associated with AI-generated content. Below is a screenshot of the same. Meanwhile, according to a Press Trust of India report dated July 4, another bridge collapsed in Bihar on Thursday (July 3), the 10th such incident in the state in just over a fortnight, an official said. The latest incident was reported from Saran, which witnessed two more bridge collapses in the last 24 hours, District Magistrate Aman Samir said. Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video circulating on social media, purportedly showing a bridge collapse in Bihar, is AI-generated and manipulated.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Clipped video falsely claims JP Nadda insulted Jagdeep Dhankhar, leading to his resignation; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 23 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid the ongoing Monsoon Session of Parliament, a video featuring Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare, JP Nadda, addressing the House has been widely circulated on social media. In the viral clip, Nadda is heard stating, "Nothing will go on record. Whatever I say will go on record." Social media users sharing the video interpreted his statement as an insult directed at Vice President Jagdeep Dhankhar, leading to speculation that it prompted Dhankhar's resignation. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found that a clipped portion of the full video was shared with a false interpretation. In the original, unedited video, Nadda's remarks were directed at opposition members who were interrupting his speech, not at Vice President Dhankhar. Furthermore, parliamentary rules prohibit interruptions while a member is speaking, unless the Chair explicitly permits questions relevant to the discussion. Additionally, Jagdeep Dhankhar tendered his resignation on Monday (July 21), citing the need to "prioritise health care and abide by medical advice." The resignation is effective immediately and was submitted in accordance with Article 67(a) of the Constitution. Claim: A video featuring Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare JP Nadda addressing the House was shared by a user named 'Ankit Mayank' on July 21, claiming that he had insulted former Vice President Jagdeep Dhankhar, which led to the latter's resignation. In the 00:06-second video, Nadda says, "Nothing will go on record; whatever I say will go on record." The post's caption read: "12 PM — JP Nadda insulted Vice President #JagdeepDhankhar dictating "Nothing will go on record" 9 PM — Jagdeep Dhankhar resigned with immediate effect. His EGO got hurt or Modi-Shah showed him his AUKAT?" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available, here and here , respectively. Upon further review of the search results, the Desk found that the Indian Youth Congress and the Uttarakhand Youth Congress shared the same video. The link can be found here and here . Furthermore, as part of the investigation, the Desk reviewed the videos of the monsoon session from the Rajya Sabha and came across a full version of the video that had been shared on social media. The Desk found the complete video uploaded on the official YouTube page of Sansad TV on July 21, 2025. In the video, Dhankhar invited Mallikarjun Kharge, the Congress leader and Leader of the Opposition (LoP) in the Rajya Sabha, to address the House. Kharge initiated his remarks by focusing on the Pahalgam terror attack and Operation Sindoor. He critically highlighted that President Donald Trump had, on 24 separate occasions, asserted that the ceasefire between India and Pakistan was a direct result of his "interference," a statement he deemed insulting to the nation's sovereignty. Following this, when JP Nadda began his rebuttal to Kharge's statements, a disruption arose among the Members of Parliament. This prompted both Nadda and Dhankhar to appeal for decorum and to allow Nadda to continue his address without interruption. On skimming through the entire video, we found that at 11:30 minutes, he said: "I am not going into the details of it, but I would like to tell you," Nadda said, before being interrupted by members' shouting. At this point, he asked them to calm down, saying that none of their shouting or complaints would go on the records of the proceedings, "Whatever I say will go on record. You should know." Therefore, this makes it clear that Nadda addressed opposition interruptions, not Dhankhar. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a screenshot highlighting the similarities between the clip seen in the social media post and the video uploaded on Sansad TV's official YouTube channel. Next, as part of the investigation, they accessed the handbook of Rajya Sabha members, which states that they are not permitted to "a Member should not interrupt any Member who is speaking by making noises or in any other disorderly manner." "A statement made by a Minister from the records in his/her possession should be accepted as correct unless a specific point is raised to challenge it. A Member may, with the permission of the Chairman, make a personal explanation. However, there is no question before the House, but in such a case, no debatable matter may be brought forward, and no debate shall arise. Words containing insinuations, offensive and unparliamentary expressions should be scrupulously avoided. When the Chair holds that a particular word or expression is unparliamentary, it should be immediately withdrawn without any attempt to raise any debate over it. Words or expressions held to be unparliamentary and ordered to be expunged by the Chair are omitted from the printed debates," read the handbook. Here is the link to the handbook, and below is a screenshot of the same. Moreover, Jagdeep Dhankhar resigned as Vice President on July 21, creating a vacancy in the country's second-highest constitutional post and opening the way for an upcoming election. Until a new Vice President is elected, Deputy Chairperson Harivansh Narayan Singh will preside over the Rajya Sabha as acting Chairperson, in line with constitutional provisions. Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a clipped video from JP Nadda's speech at the parliament was shared with a false claim that he had insulted Jagdeep Dhankhar, which led to his resignation from the post of Vice President.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of cows killing elderly man falsely linked to Bihar's Banka district; incident originally happened in Maharashtra's Nashik
content: New Delhi, July 23 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing two cows attacking an elderly man as he got down from a bike and trampling him on the road was shared by several social media users, claiming that the tragic incident occurred in Bihar's Banka district. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the viral video is about a month old. The incident actually took place in Kalwan town, Nashik district, Maharashtra, where an elderly man, identified as Bhalchandra Raghunath Malpure, was attacked and killed by cows. The video is being falsely shared on social media with the claim that it occurred in Bihar. Claim: A video depicting two cows attacking an elderly man on the road was shared by a Facebook user, Bihar Say, on July 21, claiming that the incident occurred in Bihar's Banka district. "A cow suddenly attacked an elderly man on Sunday in Punisiya village of Banka district of Bihar. The injured person has been identified as a resident of Barahat, who had come to the village for some work," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . As part of the investigation, the Desk ran the extracted keyframes through a Reverse Image Search and came across the same video, which was uploaded on the official YouTube channel of 'Loksatta', a Marathi media channel, on June 24, 2025. The timeline of the video suggests that the video is not recent and is almost a month old. Moreover, the description of the video mentioned that an 85-year-old man died in a cow attack at Nashik. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the social media post and the YouTube video. Taking a cue from the above finding, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by The Free Press Journal dated June 24, 2025. As per the report, the man identified as Bhalchandra Raghunath Malpure (85), a resident of Chhatrapati Shivaji Nagar, Kalwan, was riding pillion on a two-wheeler. As he got down from the bike, the cows lifted Malpure with their horns and trampled him on the road. Bystanders attempted to help, but the cows continued to attack him. The headline of the report read: "VIDEO: 85-Year-Old Man Gored, Trampled To Death By Stray Cattle In Nashik's Kalwan". The cover image was similar to the clip seen in the social media post. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video is a month old, and the incident of an elderly man being attacked and killed by cows in Kalwan town, Nashik district, is being falsely shared as an incident from Bihar.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of man doused with water for urinating in public in Peru falsely shared as incident from Indore
content: New Delhi, July 23 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media video showing a man atop a water tanker splashing water on an individual caught urinating by the roadside was recently shared with the claim that the incident took place in Indore. The video allegedly shows a staffer from the Indore Municipal Corporation spraying water on a man urinating in public to discourage the act. However, upon investigation, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false. The video actually depicts an incident that occurred in Lima, the capital of Peru, in March 2025 and has no connection with Indore. An old and unrelated video was falsely shared on social media, misleading viewers by linking it to India. Claim An X user named Pankaj (@TPankaj001) shared on July 18 a purported video claiming that a person from the Indore Municipal Corporation showered water on an individual caught urinating in public. "In the video, a man is urinating by the roadside when the Indore Municipal Corporation's vehicle comes and sprays water on him," the user wrote while sharing the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered 47k views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. When one of these keyframes was checked using Google Lens, the Desk came across several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with archived versions available here and here . The search result also led the Desk to a report published by Peru-based news portal La República on March 15, 2025. The report featured the same video showing a man spraying water on an individual caught urinating in public. However, it clearly stated that the incident took place in Lima, Peru, not in Indore, as claimed on social media. According to the report, the incident occurred when a man approached a bridge in the middle of the street intending to urinate. A water tanker passed by, and a man riding in it decided to use the tanker's hose to soak the man as a lesson for his behaviour thoroughly. "The footage shows how the pedestrian, surprised by the incident, quickly tried to move away but ended up soaked even more. The video also captured the shocked expressions of passersby, who hadn't expected such a reaction," the report added. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: A comparison of visuals confirmed that the viral video matched the footage published in the Peruvian report. Additionally, a Google reverse image search also led the Desk to other reports and video posts by Peru-based local news handles, all confirming the incident took place in Lima. According to one local portal, Enfoco TV, the unusual incident occurred when a man was urinating outside the Lima electric train station. A nearby water truck then decided to drench him to stop him from littering the streets. "The scene has generated diverse reactions on social media, with many calling it a lesson for those who dirty public spaces," the report stated. Here is the link to the report along with a screenshot. Meanwhile, as part of the investigation, the Desk also conducted a customised Google search to verify whether any similar incidents had occurred in Indore. The search did not yield any credible news reports confirming such an event in the city. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video claiming to show Indore Municipal Corporation spraying water on a man urinating in public is misleading. The footage depicts an incident that occurred in Lima, Peru, in March 2025 and has no connection to Indore.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video of vehicles being swept away falsely shared as real incident in Delhi; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 23 ( Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing several vehicles being swept away by gushing water, reportedly under a flyover, is circulating widely on social media. Users sharing the clip claim it captures the aftermath of heavy rainfall in Delhi. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found no reports of any such incident in the national capital. Further investigation revealed that the video is AI-generated and has been shared online to mislead viewers. Claim: A video featuring several vehicles being washed away due to gushing water, apparently under a flyover, was shared by an X user named ' ammalalgurjar ' on July 4, claiming that the incident occurred in Delhi. The overlaying text in the video, originally in Hindi, read: "Water suddenly came on the road in Delhi" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation: The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived version can be found here and here , respectively. Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find relevant media reports; however, the search did not yield any credible media coverage. Moreover, such a drastic event in the national capital would have garnered widespread media coverage. Following this, the Desk carefully analysed the video being shared on social media and found several inconsistencies in it, which suggested that the video had been manipulated or fabricated —for instance, unnaturally smooth textures, erratic water flow, distorted reflections, and robotic vehicle movements. Below is a screenshot that highlights the same issue. Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the video through Cantilux , an AI-detection tool, which flagged the clip with a 73% probability of being generated by AI. Below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video being shared on social media, showing vehicles being washed away in water in Delhi, is AI-generated and fabricated.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of police station set on fire in Colombia falsely shared claiming Muslims burnt house of The Udaipur Files artist
content: New Delhi, July 23 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check): Amid the controversy surrounding the film The Udaipur Files, which depicts the gruesome murder of Rajasthan-based tailor Kanhaiya Lal, a video circulating on social media shows a mob setting a building on fire. Users claimed the house allegedly belonged to an artist involved in the film and that it was set ablaze by members of the Muslim community protesting its release. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it to be unrelated to the film. The footage actually shows an incident in Nazareth, La Guajira, Colombia, where locals set a police station on fire on July 4, 2025, after police mistakenly killed a man named Yulbert Barboza. An unrelated video from Colombia was falsely circulated online, linking it to protests against The Udaipur Files in India. Significantly, the Supreme Court is scheduled to hear on July 24 the matter regarding the stay on the release of the movie 'Udaipur Files: Kanhaiya Lal Tailor Murder'. The court has given the parties involved liberty to file their objections to the Centre's order, which cleared the movie with six cuts recommended by an expert committee. According to media reports, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta informed the bench led by Justice Surya Kant that the Centre ordered the cuts while considering applications seeking a revision of the certificate granted to the film by the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC). Claim An Instagram user named 'd_k_thakral_panchal' shared, on July 12, a purported video showing a mob setting ablaze the house of an artist involved in the movie Udaipur Files in India. The user claimed that Muslims set the artist's house on fire, stating they would not allow the film's release, which is already embroiled in controversies due to its alleged sensitive storyline depicting the gruesome killing of Udaipur-based tailor Kanhaiya Lal in 2022. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across multiple social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here . The Google Reverse Image search also led the Desk to a video published by the Instagram handle of the Colombia-based news portal Soy El Silencioso on July 5. The portal had shared the same video seen in the social media post; however, the details revealed that the video was from Colombia and not related to any protests in India. According to the news portal, the incident unfolded in the town of Nazareth, Uribia (La Guajira), where residents set a police station on fire after police mistakenly killed Yulbert Barboza, a young man returning to his hometown. Witnesses said the officers mistook the truck he was travelling in for another that had been used in a previous attack on police personnel. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. A comparison image confirmed that the visuals in the viral clip matched the footage shared by the Colombian news portal. Taking further cues, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find more details about the incident. This led to a report published by Colombia-based news portal Caracol Radio, which confirmed that the incident had taken place there, not in India. The report stated that the video depicted an incident in Nazareth, La Guajira, where a young man identified as Yulbert Fernández Barboza was shot and killed by police while travelling with others in a vehicle. "Apparently, hours before the incident, the police station had been attacked with gunfire by unknown assailants travelling in a pickup truck. The exchange of gunfire left no injuries. Hours later, young Yulbert Fernández, son of a well-known professor in the region, was driving a vehicle that apparently skidded near the police station, prompting officers to open fire, believing they were under attack again. The enraged community then set the police station on fire, causing severe damage. So far, there has been no official statement from the authorities," the report added. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral social media video actually depicts an incident in Nazareth, Colombia, where locals set fire to a police station on July 4, 2025, after police mistakenly killed a man named Yulbert Barboza. The video has no connection to any controversy or protests related to the release of the film Udaipur Files in India.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Protest video of Gujarat dairy farmers falsely shared as Kanwariyas spilling milk after altercation; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 24 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a group of people spilling milk onto a road from a truck has been widely shared on social media. Users claimed it shows Kanwariyas (participants in the annual Kanwar Yatra pilgrimage) spilling milk after an altercation with a milk vendor during the Yatra. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found that it actually depicts a protest by dairy farmers in Gujarat's Sabarkantha district, who were demanding a price hike for milk. The video is unrelated to any dispute involving Kanwariyas. Claim: A video featuring people throwing away milk on a road from a truck was shared on YouTube by a user named '@gameon2348' on July 21, claiming that Kanwariyas did it following a dispute with a milk vendor. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation: The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . As part of the investigation, the Desk ran the extracted keyframes through Reverse Image Search, which led us to a Facebook post from the official handle of Punjab Kesari Haryana dated July 20. According to the report, cattle farmers in Gujarat took to the streets to demand an increase in the milk price. The farmers expressed their anger by spilling milk on the roads. The clips shared on Facebook by Punjab Kesari matched the visuals shared on YouTube. "In Gujarat, cattle farmers have come out on the streets demanding an increase in milk prices. In Sabarkantha district, milk-producing farmers expressed their anger by spilling milk on the roads," read the caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the video published by Punjab Kesari Haryana. Upon further review of the search results, the Desk came across another post by the official X handle of Congress Kerala, dated July 21. According to the post, Dairy farmers staged a protest across Gujarat by dumping thousands of litres of milk. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search to find relevant media reports and came across a report by ABP published on July 22. As per the report, Dairy farmers and animal husbandry workers in Gujarat's Sabarkantha district staged a strong protest against Sabar Dairy, demanding an increase in the purchase price of milk. "The police have registered FIRs against 1000 people, including Sabar Dairy Director and former Congress MLA Jashubhai Patel, for violence, stone pelting and damage to public property. So far, 47 people have been arrested," read the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video shared on social media shows Dairy farmers staging a protest in Gujarat, demanding a rise in milk prices. The video is unrelated to any incident of dispute between Kanwariyas and a milk vendor.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: April 2025 video of Jagdeep Dhankhar falsely shared as from day before his resignation; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 25 ( Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video featuring former Vice President Jagdeep Dhankhar , allegedly from the ongoing Parliament Session on July 23, has been widely shared on social media. In the clip, Dhankhar was heard saying, "This part of the assertion will be deleted. Why? Because India's farmers and their sons are not afraid of anyone, not under any circumstances." The video was shared with the claim that the remarks were made a day before his resignation. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the video is not recent. It dates back to April 3, 2025, during a discussion in the Rajya Sabha as part of the Budget Session. The clip has been misrepresented online as being from the day before Dhankhar's resignation. Notably, the Monsoon Session of Parliament began on July 21, 2025, the same day Jagdeep Dhankhar stepped down. A clipped portion of the older video is now circulating with a false claim. Claim: An X user, ' Kapil_Jyani _', shared a video from the ongoing Parliament Session on July 23 featuring former Vice President Jagdeep Dhankhar . In the clip, Dhankhar says, "This part of the assertion will be deleted. Why? Because India's farmers and their sons are not afraid of anyone, not under any circumstances." The user claims the incident occurred a day before Dhankhar's resignation. In the 1 minute 26 seconds video, Congress President Millkarjun Kharge addresses Dhankhar , saying, "How will it work if you are so scared of the government?" To which Dhankhar replies, "This part of the assertion will be deleted. Why? Because India's farmers and their sons are not afraid of anyone, not under any circumstances." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. One such post can be found here , and its archived version is available here . Upon further review of the search results, the Desk came across an X post by the official NDTV handle, published on April 4, 2025. The timeline of the post clarifies that the video is not recent and does not pertain to the ongoing monsoon session that officially began on 21 July 2025. "'The farmer of India and his son fear no one...' - Chairman and Vice President Jagdeep Dhankhar ," read the caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Following this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across the original video, which was live-streamed on the YouTube channel of CNN News18 on April 3, 2025. The viral video clip appears at the timestamp 5:18:02. Both Kharge and Dhankhar are seen wearing the same attire as seen in the viral clip; this confirms that the footage is from the same day's proceedings. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a set of combined images highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the video shared by CNN-News18. Upon further review of the search results, the Desk found a report by Punjab Kesari , a Hindi-language media outlet, dated April 4, 2025. According to the report, Dhankhar commented on a discussion regarding the President's Rule in Manipur following the passage of the Waqf Amendment Bill. Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dates back to April 3, 2025, during a discussion in the Rajya Sabha budget session. It is not from a day before Jagdeep Dhankhar resigned. The Monsoon Session began on 21 July 2025, and Jagdeep Dhankhar resigned the same day.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of girl thrashing youth in Unnao falsely shared with communal twist; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 24 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it showed a recent incident from Unnao, Uttar Pradesh, where a Hindu girl publicly thrashed a Muslim youth with slippers for allegedly harassing her on her way to school. The users claimed the accused, identified as Aleem Sheikh, had been asking for the girl's phone number for the past 10 days. Eventually, the girl decided to teach him a lesson and beat him publicly, as depicted in the video. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it was falsely shared with a communal angle. While the individual was indeed publicly beaten for molesting a girl, he belonged to the same religion as the victim. An unrelated molestation incident was falsely shared on social media with a fabricated communal narrative. Claim An X user, Tufail Chaturvedi (@TufailChaturve), shared on July 20 a purported video of a girl thrashing a man on the street. The user claimed the video was linked to a molestation incident in Unnao, Uttar Pradesh, where a Hindu girl publicly beat a Muslim youth, identified as Aleem Sheikh, who had been harassing her for the past 10 days. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video garnered 19k views) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of these keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found that several social media accounts had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google reverse image search also led the Desk to a report published by TV9 Bharatvarsh on July 20. The report featured the same individuals seen in the viral video. It stated that the incident indeed occurred in Unnao, Uttar Pradesh, where a girl student beat a young man with slippers and slapped him publicly as he had been harassing her for a long time. "According to the information, the young man had been harassing the student for quite some time, which left her extremely upset. Tired of the harassment, the girl caught hold of him and showered slaps on him, also beating him with her shoes. During this, a crowd of passersby gathered and filmed the entire incident," the report stated. Moreover, the report also mentioned that the accused had been taken into police custody, but it did not specify his identity. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image showing that the feature image of the news report matches that of the viral video in circulation. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above-generated input, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find details about the accused's identity. The search led to a statement shared by the Unnao Police on its official X handle, in response to a post by a local media portal that interviewed the victim. In its statement, the Unnao Police confirmed that the accused had been taken into custody and clarified that he did not belong to the Muslim community. The accused was identified as Akash, son of Chandrashekhar, aged approximately 20 years, a resident of Brahmanagar, Pony Road, Police Station, Gangaghat, District Unnao. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was falsely shared with a communal narrative, claiming a Hindu girl thrashed a Muslim youth for harassment. In reality, the incident did occur in Unnao, Uttar Pradesh, but the accused, Akash, belongs to the same religion as the victim.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of Russian missile strike falsely linked to Thai airstrikes on Cambodia; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 25 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): As Thailand launched airstrikes on Cambodia amid the ongoing tensions between the two countries, a video showing a massive explosion with thick smoke billowing into the sky has been widely shared on social media. The posts claim that the Royal Thai Air Force carried out airstrikes, destroying at least two Cambodian military positions, including a brigade headquarters. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the video is not related to the ongoing Thailand-Cambodia conflict. The clip is from June and actually shows Russian missile strikes on Ukraine, falsely shared with a misleading claim. As per reports, Thailand and Cambodia have blamed each other for the clashes, alleging that civilians were being targeted. The escalation represents a rare instance of military conflict between member countries of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, though Thailand has tangled with Cambodia before over the border and has had sporadic skirmishes with its western neighbor, Myanmar. Claim: A video depicting a massive explosion with thick fumes emanating in the sky was shared by an X user named 'Baba Banaras' on July 24, claiming that at least two Cambodian military positions were destroyed, including Brigade HQ in Airstrikes by the Royal Thai Air Force. "After Russia-Ukraine, Israel-Palestine, Israel-Iran, India-Pakistan. Now Thailand -Cambodia. At least two Combodian military positions were destroyed including Brigade HQ in Airstrikes by Royal Thai Airforce," read the post's caption. The post clocked 687.6k views on social media. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived version is available here and here , respectively. Next, the Desk examined the video to find clues about its origin. The search led to the comment sections, where several users pointed out that the video shows a Russian attack on Ukraine Below are screenshots of two such comments: Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk ran the extracted keyframes through reverse image search, which led us to NBC News' official YouTube page, where the same video was shared on June 6, 2025. As per the report, Russian missiles hit the western Ukrainian city of Lutsk. The timeline and the information available in the video clarify that the video is not recent and depicts Russia's attack on Lutsk. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a set of combination images highlighting the similarities between the social media post and the video shared in the news report. On further scanning the search results, we also came across an X post by RT, a Russian state media, which featured the same video as seen in the social media post. The video published on June 6, mentioned that a massive Russian strike reportedly rained down on an aircraft repair complex in Ukraine's Lutsk. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. ​ Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk then conducted a cutomised keyword search to find relevant media reports that covered the incident. Our search led us to a report published by News18 on June 6, 2025. The cover image of the report was similar to the clips seen in the social media post. The report highlighted that Ukraine came under a massive aerial assault as the country's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that Russia targeted "almost all of Ukraine" in a coordinated missile and drone attack that killed at least three people and injured dozens more. "Air raid sirens rang out through the night across the country. While alerts in Kyiv have since been lifted, they remain in place in several other regions. In the northwestern city of Lutsk, officials said 15 drones and six missiles were used in an attack that injured at least five," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Notably, Thai and Cambodian soldiers have clashed along the border between their countries in a major escalation that left at least 15 people dead, mostly civilians, and one soldier. The two sides fired small arms, artillery, and rockets, and Thailand also launched airstrikes. The escalation represents a rare instance of military conflict between member countries of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, though Thailand has tangled with Cambodia before over the border and has had sporadic skirmishes with its western neighbor, Myanmar. Subsequently, the Desk concludes that the video claiming to show the destruction of the Cambodian military positions is false. This video is from June and shows Russian missile strikes on Ukraine.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of Maratha activist assault in Maharashtra shared with false political and caste angle; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 25 ( Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a group of men brutally thrashing another man inside a room has gone viral on social media. Users sharing the clip claim that the victim was a Dalit leader who was attacked by members of the Samajwadi Party's Yadav community for sitting on a sofa. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found it to be false. The video is from Latur, Maharashtra, and has no connection to the Samajwadi Party or the Yadav community. It actually shows Maratha activist Vijaykumar Ghadge being assaulted by local members of the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP). Vivekanand Chowk Police Inspector Santosh Ashok Patil confirmed to PTI that Ghadge does not belong to the Dalit community. There is no caste angle to the incident, and the video is being shared with a misleading political and communal narrative. Claim: A video of a group of people thrashing a man inside a room was shared by a Facebook user named ' Devit Aazad Rawan' on July 23, claiming that the victim was allegedly a Dalit leader and was hit by the Yadavs of the Samajwadi Party because he sat on the sofa. "When the Dalit leader sat on the sofa, the Yadavs beat him half to death. Is this the PDA alliance of Samajwadi Party? Imagine, when a Dalit leader has this status in the party, then how much injustice must be done to the common Dalit people? In the Samajwadi Party government," read the post's caption. The post garnered 759K views on social media. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived version are available here and here . As part of the investigation, the Desk ran the extracted keyframes through Reverse Image Search and came across a report by The Times of India published on July 21, 2025. As per the report, a Maratha outfit's protest at NCP state president Sunil Tatkare's press meet in Latur sparked chaos on Sunday evening. Chhava Sanghatna , led by Vijaykumar Ghadge, initially submitted a memorandum to Tatkare demanding Kokate's resignation. Chhava Sanghatna activists shouted slogans against Kokate and threw playing cards at Tatkare. Shortly after Tatkare left the venue, local NCP politicians approached Chhava Sanghatna activists in a nearby room and allegedly began assaulting them. One NCP worker allegedly struck a Chhava Sanghatna member on the head with a chair as police attempted to control the situation. The cover image of the report matches the clips seen in the viral social media post. This clarifies that the incident happened in Maharashtra's Latur, and a Maratha activist was beaten by NCP leaders. The video is unrelated to the Samajwadi Party. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. A set of customised keyword searches led the Desk to another report by Lokmat Times dated July 22, 2025, which reported that the Police from Vivekanand Chowk station arrested four more individuals in connection with the assault on Chhava Sanghatana state president Adv. Vijaykumar Ghadge Patil. With these arrests, the total number of accused held has reached six. Police are still searching for five more suspects. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Another report by India Today, published July 21, 2025, mentioned that activists of Chhava Sanghatna were protesting against Manikrao Kokate after a video showing him purportedly playing a game of rummy on his mobile phone during the monsoon session of the state legislature went viral. "A violent clash broke out on Sunday at a resthouse in Maharashtra's Latur after members of the Ajit Pawar-led Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) allegedly assaulted Vijaykumar Ghadge, the state president of All India Chhava Sanghatna, following a protest during a press conference. The incident occurred after a workers' dialogue meeting held by NCP's Maharashtra unit president Sunil Tatkare," read the mentioned post. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. As part of the investigation, the Desk contacted Vivekanand Chowk Police Inspector Santosh Ashok Patil, who told Press Trust of India that Vijaykumar Ghadge did not belong to the Dalit community "He is not a Dalit and belongs to the Maratha community," Vivekanand Chowk Police Inspector Santosh Ashok Patil told PTI. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video is from Maharashtra's Latur, where a Maratha activist was thrashed by local NCP members. There was no caste angle to the case and is completely unrelated to the Samajwadi Party.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2010 Brazilian murder case photo falsely shared, claiming Muslim partner killed Hindu woman recently in Assam
content: New Delhi, July 26 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A visually distressing image showing the corpse of a woman inside a refrigerator has recently gone viral on social media, accompanied by a claim that it shows a Hindu woman who was brutally killed by her Muslim partner and his friends in Assam. The user alleged that the victim, identified as Kajal, was murdered by her partner, Muhammad Sabir Miyan, and his seven friends. The post further claimed: "Kajal was killed by her partner Muhammad Sabir Miyan after he got bored of her. Sabir called seven of his friends, who gang-raped her and froze her alive. Even after her death, they raped her corpse for seven days." However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the image and found it to be unrelated to any incident in India. The photo actually pertains to a 2010 crime in Brazil. This unrelated and gruesome image has resurfaced on social media with a false communal narrative, misleadingly linking it to a fabricated incident in Assam. Claim An X user named Jignesh (@jignesh03011976) on July 24 shared a disturbing image of a woman allegedly killed by her Muslim partner, Muhammad Sabir Miyan, and his friends in Assam. The post claimed the woman, identified as Kajal, was killed after being tortured and gang-raped. "Kajal, a proud feminist, live-in supporter, and secularism icon, left her parents to live 'freely' with Muhammad Sabir Miyan. Initially, they enjoyed a lot, but then Sabir got bored of her. He called seven of his friends, who gang-raped her. She was torn apart, put alive in a freezer, killed by the cold. Even after death, they raped her corpse for seven days. Yes, this horror happened in Assam. But don't worry, our system will say 'no evidence'. Black coats will defend these monsters, the media will stay silent, and feminists will vanish," the user wrote. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across multiple social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. The Google reverse image search also led the Desk to a report published on a website named Documenting Reality, which included the same image of a woman's corpse found in a freezer. However, the accompanying details stated that it depicted an incident from Brazil, not India, and dated back to 2010. The report mentioned, "A 45-year-old man was arrested for the murder of his wife, whose body he hid in a freezer at their home in Osasco, Greater São Paulo. Police were led to the grisly discovery following an anonymous tip." Here is the link to the report: Additionally, the search results also led the Desk to a report published on a portal titled Noticias de Itabuna. The report published on the portal had featured the same viral image (showing the woman's corpse found in a refrigerator) back in March 2010, linking it to the aforementioned incident in Brazil. The report stated, "The victim's body was found frozen in a fetal position, and because it was still frozen, it could not be removed for identification. From the police station, the man was taken to an emergency room for medical attention, as he had injuries to his hands and arms, before being taken to the city's public jail." Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: In the subsequent part of the investigation, taking cues from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customized keyword search on Google to check if any similar incident had occurred in Assam. However, the search did not yield any credible news report that could verify the claim. The keyword search also led the Desk to a post shared by Assam Police on its official X handle in December 2022. In the post, Assam Police, while sharing the same viral image (in a blurred form), clarified that the image was being circulated in a false context and was likely linked to an incident in Brazil, not India. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the grisly image showing a woman's corpse in a freezer was falsely shared by linking it to an incident from Assam. No such incident had occurred there.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Free electricity scheme upto 150 units sparks wave of phone scams in Bihar; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 26 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Days after Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar announced the state government's decision to provide 125 units of free electricity to consumers ahead of the assembly elections, a suspicious message related to the scheme surfaced on the PTI Fact Check Desk's official WhatsApp number. The user, reportedly from Bihar, claimed that residents were receiving calls from unknown individuals who said that to avail the free electricity scheme (up to 150 units), people needed to register through a link sent to their phones. The callers allegedly guided them step by step on how to register. However, once done, the victims' phones could be compromised, allowing sensitive information—such as banking or biometric details—to be stolen. To verify the authenticity of this claim, PTI Fact Check contacted an official from the Bihar Electricity Department. The official clarified that no additional registration or procedure is required to receive the benefits of the scheme, as the adjustments will be directly reflected on consumers' electricity bills. The official further urged the public to lodge formal complaints if they receive such fraudulent calls. Claim On July 25, a message was forwarded to the PTI Fact Check Desk's WhatsApp handle by a user, reportedly from Bihar, claiming that several individuals in the state have been receiving repeated calls from unknown numbers. The callers allegedly inform people that, to avail the recently announced free electricity scheme (up to 150 units) by the state government, they must register through a link sent to their phones. The message further warned that if someone falls victim to this hoax, their personal data could be compromised, potentially exposing sensitive information—such as banking or biometric details—to theft. Below is a screenshot of the complaint received on the WhatsApp number. Investigation The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across multiple social media accounts where users claimed to have received such fraudulent calls and shared their experiences online. Links to two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. In the next phase of the investigation, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search on Google to gather further details related to the alleged call scam and verify whether any registration is actually required to avail the benefits of the scheme. The search led the Desk to the official Facebook page of the Electricity Department, Bikramganj. A post shared on the page clearly stated that no additional registration or procedure is required to avail the benefits of the free electricity scheme. It clarified that the adjustments would be directly reflected in consumers' electricity bills. The department further advised that if anyone receives such calls or messages, they should immediately lodge a complaint by dialing 1930. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Additionally, while scanning the department's Facebook page, the Desk found two more posts where the state government shared screenshots of news reports highlighting similar call frauds. These reports also mentioned that no additional registration is required to avail the benefits of the recently announced scheme. They urged the public to remain vigilant and avoid clicking on suspicious links, which are likely designed to steal individuals' personal data for financial fraud. Links to these posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. In the final part of the investigation, taking cues from the above inputs, the Desk contacted an official from Bihar's Electricity Department, who clarified that no additional registration is required to receive the scheme's benefits, as the adjustments will be automatically reflected on consumers' bills. The official further urged people to file formal complaints if they receive such fraudulent calls. He also mentioned that while no official complaints have been registered so far, the public should remain alert to such scams. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the calls asking people to register through a link to avail the state government's free electricity scheme are fraudulent. No additional registration is required, as the benefits will be automatically reflected on electricity bills. These calls are part of a scam designed to steal personal and banking information.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: BJP MP Arun Govil's remarks against Opposition taken out of context and shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, July 26 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid the ongoing Monsoon Session of Parliament, a purported video of BJP leader and Meerut MP Arun Govil allegedly targeting Prime Minister Narendra Modi recently surfaced online. The video appeared to show the BJP MP criticising PM Modi for leaving on a two-nation official visit just as the Parliament session had begun. In the clip, he was heard saying, "How are they going to face the people who elected them? Did they come here for this purpose? This is very shameful." However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found that Arun Govil's statement was taken out of context. While he did make the statement, it was in response to the Opposition's behavior in Parliament, not directed at PM Modi and his recent visit to UK and Maldives. The BJP MP's words were deliberately misattributed and falsely shared with the claim that he had criticised the Prime Minister. Meanwhile, it is pertinent to note that PM Modi was on the second leg of his two-nation official visit to the Maldives. Prior to his arrival there, he had visited the United Kingdom, where the two countries signed a series of agreements aimed at boosting trade and economic ties. Claim A Facebook page named 'Voice of Bihar Rahul Gandhi' shared, on July 25, a purported video of BJP leader and Meerut MP Arun Govil allegedly slamming PM Modi for leaving on a two-nation official visit while the Parliament session had just begun. The video claimed to show him saying, "How are they going to face the people who elected them? Did they come here for this purpose? This is very shameful." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing, the video had garnered 67,000 likes and 10,000 shares.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively: The search also led the Desk to a video published by the news portal CNBC Awaaz on July 23, 2025. In this original video, the BJP MP made the same remarks as those heard in the viral clip. However, upon careful analysis, it was clear that Arun Govil's statement was directed at the Opposition MPs for disrupting Parliament proceedings, not at PM Modi for his foreign visit. "This is a very bad attitude of the Opposition. They are not even aware of the cost of running Parliament. The government has said it is ready to discuss every issue, but the Opposition does not want a discussion; they only want to create noise," the Meerut MP had actually said. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot: In the final part of the investigation, taking cues from the above findings, the Desk also contacted BJP's Meerut MP for a statement on the matter. The story will be updated as and when a response is received. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Arun Govil's statement criticizing the Opposition's uproar in Parliament was taken out of context and falsely shared with the claim that he targeted PM Modi.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Clip from 2024 wrongly linked to former Vice President Dhankhar's resignation; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 28 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Speculation swirled in political circles after the resignation of former Vice President Jagdeep Dhankhar. Amid this, a video surfaced on social media, shared with the claim that it captured Dhankhar's final public speech. According to the posts, he allegedly questioned the Centre's stance on farmers' grievances and was forced to step down after the address, with health concerns cited as the official reason. The Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk, however, investigated and found the claims to be false. The video is neither recent nor linked to Dhankhar's resignation. It actually dates back to 2024, when he addressed the Centenary Foundation Day celebrations of the ICAR-Central Institute for Research on Cotton Technology (CIRCOT) in Mumbai, Maharashtra. Dhankhar is the third vice president of India to resign during his tenure. V V Giri and R Venkataraman had earlier stepped down from the post to contest the presidential election. Claim: A video featuring former Vice President Jagdeep Dhankhar delivering an address was shared by a Facebook user, 'Dreams160', on July 16, claiming that it was his last public speech, in which he purportedly questioned the Centre's stance on farmers' grievances. Adding that Dhankar was allegedly forced to resign after the address, while citing health concerns as the reason. In the 00:43-second video, he says, "Agriculture Minister, every moment of yours is precious. I earnestly request you to please tell me, Was a promise made to the farmers? Why was the promise made not fulfilled? What are we doing to fulfill the promise?" "Vice President Jagadish Dhankar's last speech, wasn't he forced to resign citing ill health after this speech? One day or another, this Dhankar himself will say" read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively: As part of the investigation, the Desk ran the extracted keyframes through a Reverse Image Search, which led to Dhankhar's original address being uploaded on the official YouTube channel of the Vice President of India, dated December 6, 2024. The attire seen in the social media clip is similar to the YouTube video. The timeline clarifies that the video is not recent and is not its last address before his resignation. On carefully analysing the entire video, from 18:38 to 19:19 timestamp the exact excerpts from the social media post can be heard. Dhankhar addressed the gathering as the chief guest at the Centenary Foundation Day celebrations of ICAR-Central Institute for Research on Cotton Technology (CIRCOT) in Mumbai, Maharashtra. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk also found a post on the official X handle dated December 3, 2024. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk also conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports and came across a report by India Today published on December 4, 2024. The report mentioned the Vice President also said that ignoring farmers' issues reflects flawed policymaking and urged the Centre to address their concerns on priority. "Speaking at an event in Mumbai, where he shared the stage with Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, Dhankar asked, "Agriculture Minister, did the Agriculture Minister who was there before you make any promise in writing? If a promise was made, then what happened to it?"," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report. Additionally, as per a report by The Times of India published on July 22, Jagdeep Dhankhar while speaking at an event at Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) on July 10 this year, said that he would retire at the right time, August 2027. "I will retire at the right time, August 2027, subject to divine intervention," he had said. Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video is not recent and does not depict the former Vice President Jagdeep Dhankhar's last address before his resignation. The video actually dates back to 2024.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video from Indonesia falsely surfaced as school children crossing river in Madhya Pradesh using thermocol box; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 28 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported video showing a group of children seated in a thermocol box and dangerously crossing a water body was recently shared on social media with the claim that the incident took place in India. The user claimed the video depicted the plight of schoolchildren in Madhya Pradesh, who allegedly cross a river in a thermocol box daily and then walk at least 2 kilometers to reach their school. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk scanned the video and found it to be unrelated to any incident in India. The video reportedly shows an incident from Indonesia, where a group of school-going children use a Styrofoam box to cross a river on their way home from school. An old and unrelated video from Indonesia was falsely shared on social media, linking it to an incident in India. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) handle with the username Ashok Bauddha (@AshokBuaddha) shared a purported video on July 23, claiming it showed children from Madhya Pradesh crossing a river while seated on a thermocol box. The user further alleged that, after crossing the river, the children walk two more kilometers to reach their school. "Children cross the river on thermocol and then walk 2 kilometres to go to school in Madhya Pradesh," the user captioned the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video garnered 20k views) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across multiple social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. The search also led the Desk to a report published by Indonesian news magazine Tempo on September 27, 2021. The report featured the same visuals of schoolchildren using a box to cross a river as seen in the viral video. However, the accompanying details revealed that the video depicted an incident from Kuala Sungai Dua Belas Village, Tulung Selapan District, Ogan Komering Ilir, South Sumatra, Indonesia. The report stated that three children in school uniforms and carrying large bags were seen crossing a large river using a Styrofoam box typically used for storing fish. "The head of Kuala Sungai Dua Belas Village, Hartoni, confirmed the video of children using Styrofoam to cross the river. However, he considered the activity normal, as it was commonplace for children in the area, who are familiar with rivers and the sea," the report added. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the content seen in the viral video, matched with that of the image used in the report. Additionally, the Desk found multiple other Indonesian news reports that covered the same incident. These reports confirmed that the video was indeed from Indonesia and not related to Madhya Pradesh or any location in India. Links to two such reports can be found here and here . Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing children seated in a thermocol box to cross a river is from Indonesia and not from Madhya Pradesh, India.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered image falsely claims that word 'surrender' was displayed above PM Modi's portrait in Maldives
content: New Delhi, July 29 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported image showing the word "surrender" displayed above Prime Minister Narendra Modi's portrait on a building was recently shared on social media, with a claim that the image depicted a real incident in the Maldives. Users alleged that during PM Modi's recent two-day state visit to the island nation on July 25–26—on the invitation of Maldivian President Dr Mohamed Muizzu—the Maldivian Defence Ministry displayed the portrait of the Indian Prime Minister on its building along with a derogatory message. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the image and found it to be digitally altered. While the image of PM Modi was indeed displayed on the Maldivian Defence Ministry's building, the word "surrender" was not mentioned above the portrait. A digitally manipulated image was falsely shared on social media with the intent to malign India's global image. Claim An X user, Manish Jaiky (@ManishJaiky), shared a purported image on July 25, claiming that the word "surrender" was displayed above Prime Minister Modi's portrait on a building belonging to the Maldives Defence Ministry. "This picture is not of a building, but of a mindset—surrender? A picture of India's Prime Minister is displayed on the wall of the Maldives' Defence Ministry, and it has the word 'surrender' written on it? So, is there still any doubt about how India's image has become a mockery on the international stage? Is this diplomacy or a new era of servitude? Is the Prime Minister's silence now in the national interest or an agreement to national humiliation? When a small island nation is humiliating India like this, words are not enough—action is needed. The dignity of a nation is built not by the propaganda of foreign policy, but by its prestige," the user captioned the post. built not by the propaganda of foreign policy, but by its prestige," the user shared the image with the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the image through Google Image Search and found multiple accounts those who shared the same image with similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. Meanwhile, the search also led the Desk to an image shared by the official Facebook page of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on July 26. This image matched the one under investigation. However, a side-by-side comparison revealed that there was no mention of the word "surrender" in the BJP's version, suggesting that the viral image had been digitally manipulated. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image, highlighting that the viral image was digitally altered, as the authentic version shared by official handles does not include the word "surrender". Additionally, the Google Reverse Image search also led the Desk to a social media post shared by the official X handle of the Maldives National Defence Force (MNDF). The post contained a similar image (shot from a different angle) showing PM Modi's portrait on the Maldivian Defence Ministry building. Once again, there was no mention of the word "surrender". The post suggested that the image was taken on July 25, when PM Modi and the Maldivian President jointly inaugurated the Ministry of Defence building in Maldives. At Republic Square, PM Modi was warmly received by Dr Mohamed Muizzu and was honored with a Guard of Honour by MNDF. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. In the next stage of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customized keyword search on Google to gather further details regarding the joint inauguration event. The search led to a press release by the Ministry of External Affairs on July 25. It confirmed that the state-of-the-art Ministry of Defence (MoD) building was constructed with India's financial assistance and is aimed at enhancing the operational capabilities of the Maldivian defence and law enforcement authorities. Here is the link to the release, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral image showing the word 'surrender' above Prime Minister Modi's portrait on the Maldivian Defence Ministry building was digitally altered.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Deepfake video falsely claims Chief of Army Staff General Upendra Dwivedi "admitted" loss of more than 250 soldiers during Operation Sindoor; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 30 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported video featuring the Chief of Army Staff, General Upendra Dwivedi, addressing a press briefing was widely circulated on social media. Those sharing the video claim that the General admitted that 'India lost more than 250 soldiers in Operation Sindoor'. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated and found that a manipulated and digitally altered portion from the original video was shared as real on social media. At no point during the address did he make any such statement. The video was shared with a false claim on social media. Claim: A purported video featuring the Chief of Army Staff, General Upendra Dwivedi, addressing a press briefing was shared by an X user 'The Whistle Blower' on July 28, claiming that he admitted India allegedly lost more than 250 soldiers in Operation Sindoor. In the 2-minute 11-second video, he says, "In the year 1989 India Army achieved victory on the heights of Kargil during Operation Vijay. In that war India Army expelled Pakistan's soldiers sitting on the high hills and drove them out of the borders and hoisted our flag on these snowy peaks…During Operation Sindoor, as well India Army, targeted the Pakistan-based terrorist infrastructure…The Indian Army suffered heavy losses, around 250 soldiers lost their lives, and at the same time, the complete movement of our assets was closely being monitored by Pakistan and Chinese satellites…" The caption of the post read: "Indian Army Chief Upendra Dwivedi admits to losing more than 250 soldiers in the war against Pakistan. Pakistan was aware of our every single movement due to Chinese satellites." The post clocked 120.9k views on social media. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation: The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of these keyframes in a Google Lens search, the Desk found that several social media accounts had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here and the archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. As part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find relevant media reports that covered Chief of Army Staff, General Upendra Dwivedi. But our search did not yield any relevant reports, and given the sensitivity of the matter, it would have received broad media coverage. On analysing the video closely, the Desk found The Indian Express' watermark on the top right corner, and found the original video upload on the official YouTube channel of The Indian Express on July 26, 2025. The excerpts from the viral video can be heard from 1 minute 11 seconds of the original video. At no point in the original video did he mention about the loss of lives of the soldiers. From 1-minute 11-second video, he says, "In the year 1989 India Army achieved victory on the heights of Kargil during Operation Vijay. In that war India Army expelled Pakistan's soldiers sitting on the high hills and drove them out of the borders and hoisted our flag on these snowy peaks…During Operation Sindoor, as well India Army, targeted the Pakistan-based terrorist infrastructure and effectively thwarted other aggressive actions of Pakistan and won a decisive victory. We gave an opportunity to peace, but they acted cowardly and we answered it with great might…" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. A report by Press Trust of India (PTI) also highlighted that the Army Chief said that Operation Sindoor was a message to Pakistan as well as a response to the Pahalgam terror attack, which was a deep wound for the entire nation. A section of the report quoting him read: "Operation Sindoor was a message to Pakistan as well as a response to the Pahalgam terror attack, which was a deep wound for the entire nation. This time India did not only mourn but showed that the response will be decisive,". The report did not contain any mention of the 'loss of 250 soldiers in Operation Sindoor' Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk then ran the portion from 00:56 seconds, where it noticed a change in the video, through Cantilux, an AI-detection tool, and it detected that the video has several indicators suggesting AI manipulation. Below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that in the original video from 1 minute 11 seconds, Chief of Army Staff, General Upendra Dwivedi, says that during Operation Sindoor, as well India Army, targeted the Pakistan-based terrorist infrastructure and effectively thwarted other aggressive actions of Pakistan and won a decisive victory. We gave them an opportunity to peace, but they acted cowardly and we answered it with great might. At no point in the video did he mention the 'loss of 250 soldiers'. A manipulated video of him was shared as real on social media.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of Kosi River bridge collapse in Bihar falsely shared as recent incident
content: New Delhi, July 30 ( Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a section of an under-construction bridge collapsing is being circulated on social media with claims that it shows a recent incident in Bihar's Supaul district, where a bridge over the Kosi River allegedly gave way. Users sharing the clip have linked it to the Nitish Kumar-led NDA government, criticizing its handling of infrastructure projects. The Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that while the video is indeed from Bihar's Supaul-Madhubani area and shows a bridge over the Kosi River collapsing, the incident took place in 2024 —not recently. The video is being shared online with a false claim. Claim: A video featuring a portion of an under-construction bridge collapse was shared by an X user '@dpsingh1313' on July 27, claiming that it is a recent incident from Bihar, criticising the Nitish Kumar-led NDA government in the state. "The double engine's rotten governance is a boundless saga of corruption. In Bihar, a bridge under construction between Supaul and Madhubani on the Kosi River, costing 1200 crores, collapsed. Reports indicate several workers were trapped, injured, and fatalities occurred," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively: As part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports that cite the incident. The Desk came across a report by The Hindu, published on March 22, 2024, mentioning that the country's largest Bakaur bridge, being constructed over the Kosi River, collapsed in Supaul district of Bihar on the same day, resulting in one death and nine injuries. The cover image of the report was similar to the clips in the viral social media post. The timeline of the report clarifies that the incident is not recent but dates back to 2024. "Country's largest under construction bridge collapses in Bihar; one killed, nine injured," read the Headline. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same.
