Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the content seen in the viral video and the news report. The Desk also found a video report published on the official YouTube Channel of News18 Bihar Jharkhand on March 22, 2024. As per the report, a bridge collapsed in Bihar's Supaul–Madhubani area. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Another set of customised keyword searches led us to an X post by former Deputy CM of Bihar Tejashwi Yadav dated March 22, 2024, where he criticised the government, suggesting that the collapse of bridges worth crores has become a recurring event. "In Bihar, a major accident occurred when a bridge under construction, costing 1200 crore, collapsed on the Kosi River between Bheja-Bakaur in Supaul-Madhubani , with reports of several workers being trapped, injured, and fatalities. In the double-engine government, the collapse of bridges worth crores has become a tradition. The government should ensure proper treatment for the injured, provide compensation, and take action against the responsible company and officials," read the caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an under-construction bridge over the Kosi River had collapsed in Supaul district in Bihar, but it is not a recent incident. The incident occurred in 2024.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Fake quote alert! This social media post claiming R Ashwin slammed BCCI for Asia Cup 2025 fixture is false and baseless
content: New Delhi, July 30 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Several social media users recently shared a viral graphic claiming that former Indian spinner Ravichandran Ashwin had criticised the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) for deciding to go ahead with the India vs Pakistan match during the Asia Cup 2025, scheduled for September. The graphic, which appeared to feature Ashwin's photo and a fabricated statement, quickly gained traction online, with many users believing it to be genuine. The Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the viral claim and found it to be entirely false. Ashwin has not made any such remarks against the BCCI. He took to his official X (formerly Twitter) handle to clarify that the statement attributed to him was fake. The viral graphic is misleading and has been circulated on social media with no basis Claim: A graphic attributed to former Indian spinner Ravichandran Ashwin was shared by an X user '@_Bruce__007' claiming that he criticised the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) for going ahead with the match between India Pakistan during the Asia Cup 2025 in September. The graphic quoting Ashwin read: "Small money is involved so World Championship of legends got cancelled. But India is still playing against Pakistan in Asia Cup and BCCI hasn't cancelled it because the amount of money decides the level of patriotism" The caption of the post read: "Ravichandran Ashwin spoke the most brutal truth about BCCI and Indian Cricket Team. You need guts to say such things" The post garnered 646.5K views on social media. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation When the Desk ran the viral claim through social media, we found that several others had shared a similar graphic with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived version can be viewed here and here , respectively. The Desk noticed that the graphic with a photo of Ashwin taken from his YouTube channel shows Ash Ki Baat, and then we scanned through the official YouTube page of the and found no recent videos or discussions where he spoke about the Asia Cup 2025 or criticised the BCCI regarding the match between India and Pakistan scheduled for September 14. Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports, but there were no credible reports citing the same. We then scanned through the official X handle of the former Indian spinner Ravichandran Ashwin and came across a quote-tweet dated July 28, where he clarified that the news is fake and he is not associated with any such statement. "Don't associate me with this fake news. Shame on those who trigger all this," he wrote in his X post. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. ​ Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral graphic quoting former Indian spinner Ravichandran Ashwin is completely false and baseless.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of family murder in Pakistan falsely shared as incident from Uttar Pradesh; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 30 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it depicted a horrific incident from Uttar Pradesh, where several members of a family were allegedly killed by thieves who had entered their house with the intention to steal. When they reportedly found nothing valuable, they allegedly murdered the family members. The video showed the bodies of several victims lying in a pool of blood. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found that it was not related to any incident in India. The video originally depicted an incident from Pakistan's Punjab province, where a man named Sajjad killed his wife and seven children, reportedly due to financial distress. According to reports, the accused confessed to committing the murders because he could no longer afford to feed his family. An old and unrelated video from Pakistan was falsely shared on social media, misleading viewers by linking it to an incident in India. Claim An Instagram user with the handle 'amin_ckt_' shared a video on July 13, purportedly depicting a recent horrific incident that allegedly occurred in Uttar Pradesh's Amroha district. The video claimed to show the gruesome murder of several members of a family by unidentified individuals who had entered their house with the intent to steal. When they reportedly found nothing valuable, they allegedly killed the family members. The video showed the body of a woman and several children lying in a pool of blood. "Thieves entered a house in a village in Amroha district of Uttar Pradesh with the intention of stealing, but when they could not find anything, they brutally murdered the entire family," the user captioned the video. Here are the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (Disclaimer: The video contains visually distressing content.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across multiple social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. A Google reverse image search also led the Desk to a video posted by a Facebook user named Shahid Blouch on April 11, 2024. The video shared by Shahid Blouch matched the viral clip shared on social media. However, the accompanying details stated that the incident occurred in Muzaffargarh district, Pakistan—not in India. Here is the link and archive link to the post. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above generated inputs, the Desk conducted a customized keyword search on Google to gather further details about the incident. This led to a news report published by Dawn, a Pakistan-based news outlet, on April 13, 2024. The report confirmed that the accused, Sajjad Hussain, a tailor, had used a hammer to murder his wife and seven children in Mudwala, Alipur tehsil of Muzaffargarh, allegedly due to financial stress. "Police preliminary investigation suggests that the suspect had been struggling with mental health issues for some time. A case was registered against him under relevant criminal sections," the report added. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Additionally, the Desk conducted another keyword search to check if any similar incident had occurred in Uttar Pradesh. The search, however, did not lead to any credible news reports supporting the claim that such an event had taken place in India. While scanning further, the Desk also came across a statement released by the Uttar Pradesh Police on its official X handle. The police noted that the same video was being falsely shared with a different claim — that Bajrang Dal members had entered Muslim homes in Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh, and committed the murders. The police clarified that the video was misleading and that the incident actually occurred in Muzaffargarh, Pakistan, in 2024. "Taking cognizance of this misleading video, MUZAFFARNAGAR POLICE immediately formed a team and arrested three individuals who were allegedly conspiring to incite communal tension and violence in western Uttar Pradesh by spreading rumors," the UP Police stated. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video falsely claimed to depict a horrific incident in Uttar Pradesh, when in fact, it originated from Muzaffargarh, Pakistan, in April 2024.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Viral video of baby Elephant using dustbin is AI-generated, not real; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 30 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported video showing a baby elephant (walking down a street, possibly with its mother) picking up a discarded can and placing it in a dustbin was recently shared on social media with the claim that it depicted a real incident. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the clip and found it to be AI-generated. The video was falsely circulated on social media to mislead viewers. Claim An Instagram handle with the username 'yourplanet.earth' shared, on July 23, a purported video showing a baby elephant walking down a street—possibly alongside its mother—picking up a used can lying on the ground and putting it into a dustbin. "If a baby elephant can use a dustbin, why can't we? This adorable act speaks volumes about civic sense—or the lack of it! Animals are setting examples humans ignore daily," the user wrote in the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively: In the next step of the investigation, the Desk closely analyzed the video to determine whether it was authentic or fabricated. Several inconsistencies were observed. Notably, the trash bin seen in the video initially displays the text "USE ME," however the text changes to "NBE ME" after the can is dropped inside by the baby elephant. Additionally, the walking style of the people in the background appears unnatural, and one person even seems to have a partially transparent body—clear indicators that the video was AI-generated. Taking cues from these anomalies, the Desk ran the video through Cantilux, an AI detection tool. The tool confirmed that the footage exhibited pattern distortions and artifacts commonly associated with AI-generated content. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video—showing a baby elephant picking up a discarded can and placing it in a dustbin—was AI-generated and bore no connection to any real-world incident.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video of PM Modi shared with false claim that he praised Jesus Christ during public address; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 30 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video circulating on social media shows Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressing a public gathering, with the claim that he praised Jesus Christ during his speech. However, a fact-check by the Press Trust of India (PTI) reveals that the video is both old and manipulated. The original footage is from 2022, when PM Modi spoke at a public event in Paraunkh village, Kanpur. At no point during the speech did he mention Jesus Christ. Further analysis shows that the video was digitally altered and AI-generated to spread misinformation. Claim: A video featuring PM Modi addressing a public gathering was shared by a Facebook user 'परमेश्वर का शुक्र है' on July 9, claiming that the Prime Minister praised Jesus in his speech. In the 00:37-second video, PM Modi says, "Yes, Yeshu forgave sins. In the Bible, Yeshu is considered the son of 'parmeshwar', and he has been given the rights to forgive the sins…" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively: Upon further review of the search results, the Desk came across the original video, uploaded on the official YouTube channel of Narendra Modi, on June 3, 2022. The attire worn by PM Modi in the original video matched the visuals seen in the social media post. According to the description, PM Modi was addressing a public gathering in Paraunkh, Kanpur. Upon listening to the entire address, we found that the visuals seen in the viral video can be viewed at 1:40 and 2:40 in the original video. However, PM Modi does not mention Jesus. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search to access the PIB release of PM Modi's address. On viewing the entire release, the Desk did not find any mention of Jesus. This hints that the original video might be manipulated and shared with false claims on social media. Here is the link to the release, and below is the screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk ran the audio on the social media post through Resemble AI, an AI-detection tool that detected that the audio is fake. Below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk also ran the video through Cantilux another AI-detection tool which detected 91% AI-probability. Below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video featuring PM Modi praising Jesus is manipulated and AI-generated.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated image of Shah Rukh Khan with Cristiano Ronaldo shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 30 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): An image recently circulated on social media claimed to show Bollywood superstar Shah Rukh Khan posing alongside legendary Portuguese footballer Cristiano Ronaldo at Haram Sharif in Mecca. The image showed the duo seemingly posing for a selfie. In its investigation, however, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found that the photo shared on social media was fake. An AI-generated photo was shared on social media as real with a false claim. Claim A Facebook page named SRK Community shared, on July 26, a purported image showing Bollywood superstar Shah Rukh Khan standing alongside legendary Portuguese footballer Cristiano Ronaldo at Haram Sharif in Mecca. "Wake up guys it's Saturday and here is a picture of Ronaldo and Shah Rukh Khan," the user shared the image with the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing the story, the image had garnered 42k likes.) Investigation The Desk ran the image shared in the social media post through Google Lens. The search result led the Desk to several social media accounts that had shared the same photo with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk scanned through the social media handles of the stalwarts to check whether the image depicting their visit to Mecca had been shared by them. However, the search result did not find any image that could corroborate their visit to Mecca. Additionally, the Desk also conducted a customised keyword search on Google to check if the duo had recently met; however, no details suggesting their meeting or visit to Mecca were found in the public domain. Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the social media image and observed several inconsistencies that strongly suggested it was AI-generated. For instance, subtle distortions in facial features were identifiable in the image, along with an excessively glossy finish — a common characteristic of AI-generated visuals. Below is a screenshot of the same. Using the above inputs, the Desk ran the purported image through Hive Moderation (an AI detection tool). The tool detected a substantial presence of AI-generated elements in the image. Below is a screenshot of the result. Additionally, the image was also tested using another AI detection tool, Sight Engine, which also concluded that the image was AI-generated and did not depict a real meeting between the two stalwarts. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the image showing Shah Rukh Khan posing alongside legendary Portuguese footballer Cristiano Ronaldo at Haram Sharif in Mecca was AI-generated.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Bangladeshi school harassment video falsely circulated as communal incident from India; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 31 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it showed a recent incident from West Bengal, in which a group of Muslim girls were seen harassing a Hindu girl—one of them repeatedly slapping her and pressuring her to build a relationship with former's brother. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found that the video has no connection to India. It actually originated from Shahid Muktijoddha Girls' High School in Bangladesh. A video from Bangladesh was falsely circulated on social media with misleading claims linking it to West Bengal. Claim An X user named VINI (@Vini__007) shared a video on July 27, purportedly showing a recent incident from West Bengal, where a group of Muslim girls heckled a Hindu girl, with one of them repeatedly slapping her and coercing her to show affection towards former's brother. "You will have to go with my brother and behave lovingly with him in private. A new form of Love Jihad," the user captioned the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered 544.3k views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analyzed the viral video to determine where it had originally been shot. One of the visible clue found was the logo on the school uniform worn by the girl being assaulted, which reads "Shaheed Muktijoddha Girls' High School." Based on this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to check whether a school by that name existed in India. The search revealed that a school with the same name exists—but it is located in Mirpur, Dhaka, in Bangladesh, not in India. Following this lead, the Desk compared the uniform worn by the girl in the viral video with a photograph of students from the same school found on its official Facebook page. A clear similarity was found between the uniforms. Below is a screenshot of the comparison: The Desk also separately compared the school logo on the girl's uniform with the original logo of the institution, and both matched. Below is a screenshot of the logo comparison: Additionally, the customised keyword search led the Desk to a post by West Bengal Police, which included an image of the same girl seen in the viral video. The statement clarified that the incident did not take place in West Bengal and was, in fact, from Bangladesh. "A viral video circulating on social media claims to show an incident from West Bengal, where a young girl is being coerced and tortured by some people. The video includes Hindi subtitles stating: 'You will have to go with my brother and behave lovingly with him in private. A new form of Love Jihad.' Additionally, the girl is seen being physically assaulted by a woman. Truth: The claim that this video is from West Bengal is false. The visual evidence, including the school uniform, the soldier's badge, and the background architecture, indicates that the video is from Bangladesh, specifically from Shaheed Muktijoddha Girls' High School, SECTION-12, BLOCK-D, ROAD-18, Pallabi, Mirpur, Dhaka-1216 in Bangladesh," the West Bengal Police said in a statement. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video claiming to show a group of Muslim girls from West Bengal coercing and assaulting a Hindu girl is false.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old, unrelated picture of Air India plane incident falsely shared as recent Air India Flight AI 315 fire
content: New Delhi, July 31 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A dramatic photo showing an aircraft engulfed in smoke on a runway is being widely shared on social media, with users claiming it shows Air India's flight AI 315 from Hong Kong to Delhi catching fire after landing in New Delhi. However, a fact-check by the Press Trust of India (PTI) reveals that the image is misleading. The photo is from a 2022 incident involving an Air India aircraft in Muscat, Oman. While flight AI 315 did experience a minor fire in its auxiliary power unit (APU) after parking at the gate in Delhi, the image in circulation is unrelated to the recent event. Claim: An X user named '@TheStdmScreen' on July 22 shared a picture of a wretched aircraft on the runway with smoke billowing from it, claiming that it shows Air India's flight AI 315 between Hong Kong and Delhi, which caught fire after landing in New Delhi. "Air India Flight AI 315 (Hong Kong → Delhi) experienced a brief APU fire shortly after landing and taxiing to the gate on July 22, 2025. The crew swiftly extinguished the flames, passengers and staff disembarked safely, and no injuries were reported. The aircraft is grounded pending investigation," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation: The Desk ran the picture through Reverse Image Search and found that several other users had shared the same picture with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived version can be viewed here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a report by Hindustan Times published on September 15, 2022. The cover image of the report matched the picture shared in the social media post. As per the report, over 140 passengers and the flight crew had to be evacuated from an Air India Express aircraft after smoke was spotted emanating from one of the engines while it was taxiing towards the runway at Muscat airport to depart for Cochin, the airline's spokesperson said. The timeline and the information in the report clarify that the incident is old and not recent. "Air India Express engine emits smoke in muscat; flyers evacuated," read the headline of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Another report by The Free Press Journal published on September 15, 2022, highlighted that an Air India Express plane caught fire in Oman, and all passengers were safe. "An Air India Express plane's engine caught fire on the tarmac of Muscat airport. The fire was reported by the pilot of another aircraft who saw the smoke. At least 14 passengers sustained 'minor injuries' while being evacuated from the Boeing 737," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the social media post and the cover image of the news report. Notably, on 22 July 2025, Air India flight AI 315 between Hong Kong and New Delhi caught fire after landing in India. As per an official X post by Air India dated July 22, Flight AI315, operating from Hong Kong to Delhi on 22 July 2025, experienced an auxiliary power unit (APU) fire shortly after it had landed and parked at the gate. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a 2022 picture of an Air India plane fire in Oman was falsely shared as a recent incident fire from a Hong Kong to Delhi flight.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: CCTV Footage from Myanmar Falsely Linked to Russia Earthquake; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 31 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): After a powerful magnitude 8.8 earthquake struck Russia's Far Eastern Kamchatka coast on July 30, triggering tsunami warnings for Hawaii, Alaska, and Japan, a CCTV video began circulating on social media. The footage shows furniture and shelves toppling over, with users claiming it captures the aftermath of the Russian quake. However, a fact-check by the Press Trust of India (PTI) found that the video is unrelated to the recent incident. It is actually from Myanmar, where a 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck the Sagaing region in March 2025. The clip is being shared out of context with a false claim. Claim: CCTV footage showing furniture and shelves falling allegedly due to tremors was shared on YouTube Shorts by a user named '@HavaiW7' on July 31, claiming that it depicted the tragic incidents of a strong earthquake of 8.8 magnitude on the Richter Scale in Russia. The footage also featured a woman taking cover under the table. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively: On further scanning the search results, the Desk found the same video on the official YouTube channel of 'Daily Mail News' published on March 31, 2025. As per the description of the report, it showed CCTV footage from an electronics store in Myanmar that captures the moment the 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck, as shelves fall while the entire building shakes. The timeline and the information clarify that the video does not depict a recent incident from Russia. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the contents seen in the social media post and the video uploaded by Daily Mail News. Taking a cue from the above finding, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports and came across a video report by The Times Now, dated March 31, 2025, uploaded on their official Instagram account. The caption mentions that it shows CCTV footage from an electronics store in Myanmar that captures the terrifying moment when the 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck on March 28, a powerful tremor that devastated both Myanmar and Thailand. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Notably, a massive magnitude of 8.8, the earthquake near Russia's Kamchatka Peninsula sent tsunami waves towards Japan, Hawaii, and the US west coast. In the following hours, more than two million people across the Pacific were ordered to evacuate, with alerts also issued in China, the Philippines, Indonesia, New Zealand, and as far as Peru, Chile, and Mexico. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing the furniture falling in a shop is an old video Myanmar, where a 7.7-magnitude earthquake hit the Sagaing region in March 2025.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2017 Rampur molestation video falsely shared as recent incident from West Bengal; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 31 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A visually distressing video showing a group of individuals harassing a girl, while another girl tries to save her from the assailants in broad daylight, was recently shared on social media with the claim that it depicted an incident from West Bengal. The user claimed the video showed a group of Muslim men teasing and kidnapping a Hindu girl walking with her mother. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found that the video is unrelated to West Bengal and actually depicts a horrific molestation incident that occurred in Uttar Pradesh in 2017. An old and unrelated video from Uttar Pradesh was falsely shared on social media linking it to an incident in West Bengal. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) handle with the username '@HiNdU05019434' shared on July 28 a video showing a group of Muslim men assaulting a Hindu girl in West Bengal. The user claimed the assailants teased and kidnapped the girl in broad daylight while she was walking with her mother. "Do you want to see this across the whole of India? This video is from West Bengal. It is heard that Jihadis harass a Hindu girl walking on the road in front of her mother, they abduct her—why? Because there is an anti-Hindu and Muslim-favoring government there," the user wrote while sharing the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. The search also led to a video news report published on the official YouTube channel of India TV. The report featured the same visuals of a woman being publicly molested as the viral video. However, a closer analysis revealed that the incident occurred in Uttar Pradesh in May 2017, not West Bengal. The report mentioned, the video depicted a case of public molestation in Rampur, Uttar Pradesh, where two girls were assaulted by a group of men in broad daylight. Here is the link and archive link to the video, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image comparing visuals from the viral video with those from the news channel report, confirming they are the same. In the next part of the investigation, using the clues from the video, the Desk conducted a keyword search on Google for additional context. This led to a detailed report by The Times of India dated May 29, 2017. The article reported that the incident occurred in a village under the Tanda police station in Rampur, Uttar Pradesh, where 14 youths were seen publicly molesting two girls. The assailants also recorded the act on mobile phones. "An FIR has been lodged against 14 persons. Main accused Shahnawaz has been arrested and the probe is on," the report said. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Additionally the customised keyword search held to know the development pertaining to the incident also led the Desk to a news report published by Hindustan Times on May 31, 2017, which stated 12 of the 14 people reportedly involved in the incident are arrested. "All the suspects have been remanded in judicial custody. One of them, a minor, was sent to a juvenile home," the report added. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of a molestation being circulated with a communal narrative in West Bengal is actually from a 2017 incident in Uttar Pradesh.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Scripted video showing a Muslim man marries a Hindu girl by hiding his identity shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 1 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of two policemen questioning an individual who allegedly hid his identity as a Muslim to marry a Hindu girl was recently shared on social media with the claim that it depicted a real incident. The user claimed that the man, identified as Salim, had hidden his original name and assumed the name Ravi to marry a Hindu girl. However, his deceit was exposed in front of the girl and her family, and he was being questioned by police. In its investigation, however, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the video was staged and scripted. The clip has no connection to any real-life incident and was misleadingly shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An Instagram handle with the username 'hinduranjitkumar' shared, on July 30, a purported video showing two policemen questioning a man identified as Salim, who had allegedly forged his name to Ravi in order to marry a Hindu woman. The video showed the man's real identity (as a Muslim) being revealed, and him being interrogated. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions here and here respectively. The search also led the Desk to a video published by a YouTube channel named Monty Deepak Sharma on July 23, 2025. The user, identifying himself as a digital creator, had uploaded the same video of police questioning a man for allegedly faking his religious identity, as seen in the viral video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting that the content in the viral video matches that of the video posted by the Facebook handle. However, as the Desk conducted a detailed review of Monty Deepak Sharma's YouTube channel, in the next part of the investigation, it was found that the user is known for uploading scripted content. The Desk found that the individuals playing the roles of the policemen, the married woman, and the man who allegedly faked his identity had appeared in several other scripted videos posted by Sharma. Links to two such videos can be found here and here : Additionally, as a part of the investigation, the Desk also examined Monty Deepak Sharma's other social media profiles, including his Facebook and Instagram handles. The bios on these platforms describe him as a digital content creator who regularly produces scripted videos. Below are screenshots of the two profiles. In the final part of the investigation, the Desk contacted Monty Deepak Sharma for a statement regarding the viral claim. The story will be updated as and when a response is received. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the social media video showing a Muslim man marrying a Hindu girl by hiding his identity was scripted and bore no connection to any real-life event.

title: PTI Fact Check: India's Digital Landscape Under Threat from Deepfakes and Scams
content: BY- Pratyush Ranjan NEW DELHI – In a new report titled "Contours of Cybercrime," New Delhi-based DataLEADS reveals that India is facing a rising wave of sophisticated online financial scams and deepfakes. This alarming trend is fuelled by the nation's rapidly expanding digital economy, with cybercriminals exploiting the system for financial gain. The report, launched on July 31 by the company's new vertical, GUARD (Global Unit for Analysis of Risk and Digital Threats), emphasises the urgent need for enhanced public awareness and stronger regulations to protect digital users. The findings were presented at a high-profile roundtable featuring dignitaries such as Mr. Surendra Nath Tripathi, Director General of the Indian Institute of Public Administration, and Mr. Abhishek Singh, Additional Secretary of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. Syed Nazakat, Founder and CEO of DataLEADS, stated that online fraud and deepfakes are now "part of a growing web of deception." He warned that as artificial intelligence becomes more integrated into daily life, deepfakes are emerging as a powerful new weapon for cybercriminals. GUARD was established by DataLEADS to actively monitor these threats, map fraud patterns, and advocate for better digital literacy and collaborative efforts to secure a "resilient digital India." The report's analysis of 100 social media scams and 600 financial fraud cases from the last year reveals a disturbing evolution in criminal tactics. Scammers are now using a combination of technologies, fake IDs, and psychological manipulation to defraud individuals across various digital platforms, from public social media to private messaging apps. A major concern highlighted is the rapid increase in AI-generated deepfakes, which pose a significant risk to individuals, businesses, and institutions by enabling convincing impersonations. Government data shows that India's digital economy lost over $2.66 billion (22,845 crore) to cybercriminals in 2024, a staggering 206% jump from the previous year. Despite efforts to combat this, such as blocking nearly a million fraud-linked SIM cards and over 260,000 IMEIs, cybercrime continues to thrive, often through sophisticated cross-border operations. The surge in online banking and e-commerce has been met with a corresponding rise in financial fraud. Scammers are adept at using multiple channels and emotional pressure to build trust with victims before stealing their money. Key findings from the report include: Focus on Financial Sectors: The fintech, stockbroking, and investment sectors are the most targeted, accounting for 500 of the 600 cases analysed by GUARD. Social Media as a Launchpad: Social media platforms are the initial point of contact, where victims are lured by public content and then moved to private chats with unverified advisors. Deepfakes of Public Figures: Deepfakes of celebrities and public figures are increasingly being used to promote fraudulent investment schemes and gaming applications. Sonia Bhaskar, Programme Head at DataLEADS, stressed the importance of early detection and widespread digital education. The report proposes several preventative measures for governments and online platforms, including tip-line-driven reporting, better cross-platform monitoring, and localised public awareness campaigns. It concludes with a warning that deepfakes, used for impersonating voices, faces, and brands, are one of the most urgent threats to public trust in the digital age.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: This social media post falsely claims multiple Indian paramilitary soldiers died in a bus accident in J&K details inside
content: New Delhi, August 1 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A collage containing multiple images of a bus seen falling into a river was recently shared on social media with a claim that it depicted a horrific accident involving Indian paramilitary soldiers in Jammu and Kashmir's Ganderbal district. The user alleged that the bus, carrying Indian paramilitary soldiers, fell into the Sindh river, claiming multiple lives and injuring others. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false. While the accident did originally occur—where a bus earmarked for ferrying troops of the ITBP slipped into the Sindh river—however, it was empty at the time of the incident. The bus driver sustained minor injuries but is in a stable condition. A false claim involving a real bus accident in Jammu and Kashmir was shared on social media to mislead viewers. Claim An X handle with the username 'The Journalist Eye' (@thjournalisteye) shared, on July 30, a collage depicting multiple images of a bus seen falling into a river. The user alleged that it was the same ill-fated bus carrying Indian paramilitary forces that fell into the Sindh river, resulting in multiple deaths. "Multiple Indian soldiers killed and injured after bus carrying Indian Paramilitary Forces fell into Sindh river at Ganderbal," the user claimed while sharing the collage. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the images shared in the viral post through Google Reverse Image Search. The search led to several social media accounts that had posted the same pictures with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customized keyword search on Google to find details about the accident, and whether ITBP personnel were involved in it and number of casualties reported. The search led the Desk to a video posted on the official Facebook page of the Press Trust of India. The video depicted the same incident—an ITBP bus falling into the Sindh river in the Kullan area—shot from a different angle. However, the caption did not clarify if there were any fatalities. "In Jammu and Kashmir's Ganderbal district, an ITBP bus fell into the Sindh river in the Kullan area, prompting the SDRF to launch a rescue operation. Efforts are underway to save those trapped as authorities work at the site," read the caption of the video. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: A side-by-side comparison of visuals from the PTI video and the viral image confirmed they depicted the same incident. Next, to verify whether any casualties were reported, the Desk conducted another keyword search on Google. This led to a video statement by SSP Ganderbal, published by local news portal Rising Kashmir. Speaking to them, the SSP confirmed that while the bus was earmarked for ITBP troops, it was empty at the time of the accident. "An empty ITBP bus skidded off a curve and plunged into the Sindh river near Resin Kullan, Ganderbal, during the early hours of July 30. The driver sustained minor injuries and is reported to be stable," the officer said. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Additionally, the Desk also found a statement issued by the Ganderbal Police, which also confirmed that the bus was empty at the time of the incident, and no lives were lost. The driver, who sustained minor injuries, is now stable. "During wee hours, at Resin Kullan, Ganderbal, one empty bus earmarked for ferrying troops of ITBP, while negotiating a curve, slipped into the river Sindh. The driver sustained minor injuries and is stable," the statement read. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the social media post falsely claimed multiple Indian paramilitary soldiers died in a bus accident in Ganderbal, Jammu and Kashmir. While the accident involving an ITBP bus did occur, no troops were on board, and no fatalities were reported.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Fake, fabricated Truth Social post claiming US President Trump criticised PM Modi's silence over tariff announcement shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 1 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A graphic circulating on social media claims that President Donald Trump expressed discontent on Truth Social over Prime Minister Narendra Modi's silence on his tweets, policy statements, and tariff concerns. The alleged post suggests Trump criticised India for benefiting from US deals while ignoring American interests. However, a fact-check by the Press Trust of India (PTI) reveals that the graphic is fabricated. Trump has made no such statement targeting PM Modi. The post features a satirical watermark and formatting inconsistencies that do not match authentic Truth Social posts, confirming that it is fake and fabricated. The graphic appears amid US President Donald Trump's recent imposition of 25% reciprocal tariffs on Indian goods and an unspecified penalty over purchases from Russia, which are scheduled to take effect on August 1. Claim: An X user named 'Advaita Kala' on August 1, shared an alleged 'Truth Social' post that claims US President Donald Trump expressed discontent over PM Modi's lack of response to his tweets, policy statements, and tariff-related concerns. The post clocked 178.8k views. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation To commence the investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk thoroughly scanned the official X (formerly Twitter) handle and Truth Social account of former US President Donald Trump. A detailed search through his recent and past posts yielded no trace of any statement resembling the one seen in the viral graphic. This absence of such content from Trump's verified accounts is an indication that the viral post is not authentic. As part of the investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk closely analysed the viral graphic and observed a watermark reading 'WOKEFLIX', further indicating that the graphic may not be genuine and was likely created for humour rather than factual reporting. Below is a screenshot highlighting the above finding. Additionally, the Desk noticed that the formatting, layout, and engagement metrics of the alleged post, which has a 'wokeflix' watermark, also differ significantly from an authentic Truth Social post. Below is a combination image highlighting the above-mentioned findings. Moreover, the PTI Fact Check Desk conducted a customised keyword search using multiple combinations related to the alleged statement. The search did not return any credible results or media coverage. Such a post would have been widely reported by major news organisations across the globe, given the seriousness and gravity of the matter. The complete absence of any coverage further confirms that the viral graphic is not based on any real statement made by Donald Trump. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the alleged 'Truth Social' post claiming US President Donald Trump expressed discontent over PM Modi's lack of response to his tweets, policy statements, and tariff-related concerns is completely fake and holds no truth.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of whale rescue in Russia falsely shared as recent incident after earthquake
content: New Delhi, August 4 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing five beluga whales stranded on a beach, surrounded by people attempting to rescue them, is being widely circulated on social media. Users sharing the clip claim the incident took place in Russia after the powerful 8.8 magnitude earthquake that struck the region on July 30. However, a fact-check by the Press Trust of India (PTI) reveals that the video is not recent. It dates back to August 2023, when a group of fishermen rescued five beluga whales in Russia's Kamchatka region. The video has no connection to the recent earthquake and is being shared online with a false narrative. A powerful magnitude 8.8 earthquake struck Russia's Far Eastern Kamchatka coast on July 30, triggering tsunami warnings for Hawaii, Alaska, Claim: A video showing a group of five beluga whales washed ashore was shared by an X user, 'Baba Banaras' on July 30, claiming that the incident happened in Russia following the massive 8.8 magnitude earthquake that struck the region on July 30. "Yesterday, five beluga whales washed ashore in Kamchatka, Russia, the exact epicenter of today's record-shattering magnitude 8.8 earthquake. Nature always knows first. This was the warning," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a report by Newsweek published on August 15, 2023. As per the report, five stranded beluga whales were rescued from where they were trapped on a beach. The belugas, four adults and a calf, were found stuck on a beach near the mouth of the Tigil River in Russia's Far East, local news outlet Kamchatka-Inform reported. The timeline of the report proves that the video is old and is unrelated to the recent earthquake in Russia. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google, which led us to a local report that mentioned that on August 10, during low tide, a family of beluga whales washed up on the coast in the Tigilsky district. Workers from the Sokol tribal community came to their aid, and the local fishermen successfully rescued them from the Sokol family artel. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. An X post by RT News, Russia's international news television network, published on August 21, 2023, featured the same visuals as seen in the viral post. It highlighted that five beached beluga whales were rescued after being beached on the shores of Tigilsky, on the Kamchatka peninsula in eastern Russia. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video dates back to 2023 when five beluga whales were rescued by fishermen in Russia's Kamchatka.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Report of army officials death in Ladakh road accident shared with false claim; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 4 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media post, purportedly featuring images of two soldiers—Lieutenant Colonel Bhanu Pratap Singh and Lance Dafadar Daljeet Singh—was recently shared online with the claim that they were ambushed in Ladakh. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found that while the two soldiers did tragically lose their lives, it was due to a boulder falling from a cliff onto their vehicle, which was part of a military convoy in Ladakh on July 30, 2025. In addition to the two fatalities, three other soldiers reportedly sustained injuries in the accident, as the vehicle was severely damaged by the impact of the falling boulder. The viral claim was therefore false and misrepresented the circumstances of the incident. Claim A Facebook page named 'South Asian Files' shared a post on July 30, featuring images of two soldiers—Lieutenant Colonel Bhanu Pratap Singh and Lance Dafadar Daljeet Singh. The user falsely claimed that the two were ambushed in Ladakh. "An Indian Army Colonel including a soldier got ambushed in Ladakh," the post's caption read. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk began the investigation by conducting a customised keyword search on Google using the names of the soldiers mentioned in the viral post. The objective was to verify whether the two had indeed lost their lives in an attack in Ladakh, as claimed. The search led the Desk to a PTI report carried by The Print, which detailed the actual incident. According to the report, the two soldiers did lose their lives, but it was due to a road accident that occurred at Charbagh near Durbuk in Galwan around 11:30 a.m. on July 30. A boulder from a cliff had fallen on one of the vehicles in an army convoy, which was carrying Lieutenant Colonel Bhanu Pratap Singh Mankotia and Lance Dafadar Daljeet Singh, along with three other soldiers. The report confirmed that Lt Col Bhanu Pratap Singh Mankotia and Lance Dafadar Daljeet Singh died in the accident, while the other three soldiers sustained injuries. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Additionally, the customised search also led the Desk to a post shared by the Fire and Fury Corps of the Indian Army on its official X handle. The post included the same photos of the two soldiers seen in the viral claim, but clarified that both had died in a road accident on July 30. "GOC, Fire and Fury Corps and All Ranks salute Lieutenant Colonel Bhanu Pratap Singh Mankotia and Lance Dafadar Daljeet Singh, who made the supreme sacrifice in the line of duty in #Ladakh on 30 Jul 2025 and offer deep condolences to the bereaved families in this hour of grief," the post read. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the social media post claiming that Lieutenant Colonel Bhanu Pratap Singh and Lance Dafadar Daljeet Singh were ambushed in Ladakh is misleading. While it is true that both soldiers tragically lost their lives in Ladakh, they died in a road accident after a boulder fell on their military vehicle.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of altercation inside IndiGo flight shared with false communal narrative; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 4 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it depicted a communal attack against a Muslim youth inside an IndiGo flight. Users alleged that the video showed a man (wearing a skull cap) being slapped by a co-passenger over his religious identity. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found that it was falsely shared with a communal narrative. While an altercation involving a man slapping a co-passenger did occur on a Kolkata-bound IndiGo flight, both the accused and the victim were found to belong to the same religion. An incident of in-flight unruliness was thus misrepresented online with a fabricated communal spin. Claim An X user, Tarique Anwar Champarni (@Champarni_Tariq), shared a video on August 1 purportedly showing an altercation inside an IndiGo flight, in which a man wearing a skull cap was allegedly attacked by a fellow passenger. The user claimed that the man was targeted for his religious identity. "This video is of an IndiGo Flight. A Muslim person with a beard and cap is being beaten with slaps. I demand that the Ministry of Civil Aviation, Government of India take action against this individual," the user wrote in the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing the story, the video garnered 25.4k views) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find detailed information related to the viral incident. The search result led the Desk to a video news report published by NDTV on its official YouTube channel. The Desk found that the visuals seen in the viral post were the same as those in the video shared by the news channel. The report stated that the video depicted the unruly behaviour of a passenger inside an IndiGo flight, where he slapped one of his co-passengers who was reportedly suffering a panic attack. Nowhere in the video was the identity of either the victim or the accused confirmed. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image comparing visuals from the viral video with those from the news channel report, confirming they are the same. Additionally, the customised keyword search also led the Desk to a statement issued by IndiGo regarding the matter on August 1, in which the airline strongly condemned the unruly behaviour of the individual, stating that he had been handed over to security and authorities upon arrival. "We are aware of an incident involving a physical altercation on board one of our flights. Such unruly behaviour is completely unacceptable, and we strongly condemn any actions that compromise the safety and dignity of our passengers and crew. Our crew acted in accordance with established Standard Operating Procedures. The individual involved was identified as unruly and handed over to the security and authorities upon arrival. All appropriate regulatory agencies have been duly informed, in line with protocol. We remain committed to maintaining a safe and respectful environment on all our flights," IndiGo said in a statement. Here is the link to the statement shared by IndiGo on its X handle, along with a screenshot: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search on Google to find information mentioning the identity of the accused. The search result led the Desk to a video news report published by India Today on August 2, 2025. The report included details of the incident and clarified that both individuals—the victim as well as the accused—belonged to the same community, thereby dispelling speculation about a hate angle. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Significantly, a report published by Dainik Bhaskar on August 2 also confirmed that both the victim (Hussain Ahmed Majumdar) and the accused (Hafizul Rahman) belonged to the same community. Here is the link to the report: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video showing an altercation inside an IndiGo flight was falsely shared with a communal narrative. In reality, the incident did occur, but both the accused and the victim belong to the same religion.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered video falsely claims PM Modi expressed panic after Pahalgam attack; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 5 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video circulating on social media, featuring Prime Minister Narendra Modi allegedly addressing the Parliament, claims that he expressed fear and helplessness following the recent Pahalgam terror attack. Users sharing the clip claim that the footage was "deliberately withheld by Indian news channels to avoid national embarrassment". However, a detailed investigation by the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk has found that the video was manipulated. The audio in the clip has been digitally altered to make it sound like Prime Minister Modi, but no such speech was made during the parliamentary session. The claim that media outlets suppressed the statement is also baseless. The video in question was shared with a false claim. Claim: A video featuring PM Modi addressing the Parliament was shared by an X user '@InsiderWB' on July 30, claiming that he expressed shock and fear after the Pahalgam attack, but news channels did not air the alleged clip to save national embarrassment. In the 2-minute 23-second video, he says, "Brothers and sisters, today I want to tell you a true story. When Pakistan suddenly attacked us, to be honest, I was in a terrible state. I did not expect that Pakistan would pounce on us like that. I completely lost my courage. I immediately called Amit Shah ji. I found out he was hiding under a quilt in the basement of his own house. He said, 'Prime Minister ji, I'm not feeling well. My blood pressure has shot up. I'm not in the right state of mind right now to respond to anything.' Then I thought, surely our National Security Advisor Ajit Doval ji would have a plan. I found out he was sitting in a boat, escaping to Sri Lanka. I asked, 'Doval ji, what are you doing?' He replied, 'Prime Minister ji, when it is a matter of life and death, even Chanakya's policies are forgotten. Right now, the only plan is to run and save ourselves.' Meanwhile, the army officers were asking me, 'Sir, what are your orders?' And my mind was not working. For a moment, I thought of returning to Gujarat. The next moment, I thought of going to the Himalayas and becoming a monk. Finally, I sought help from foreign countries, and Donald Trump called. He said, 'Modi ji, I thought you had become a Vishwaguru (world leader), but here you turned out to be a Panic Guru. This time for sure — Abki Baar, Panic Sarkar (This time, it's a Panic Government).' To tell you the truth, brothers and sisters, this time Pakistan has completely rattled me. Even in my next Mann Ki Baat episode, my mind will be filled only with tension. You people tell me what to do. Thank you." Meanwhile, the post's caption read: "Exclusive clips from PM Narendra Modi's Lok Sabha address, banned by nervous Indian channels fearing national embarrassment, have landed safely at Insider WB. I'm bravely sharing this exclusive, democracy saving footage with you first" The post clocked 17.8k views on social media. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation Upon analysing the video, the Desk found that it features the Sansad TV logo and includes a ticker at the bottom, claiming it's a special discussion on the "successful and decisive" Operation Sindoor, reportedly in response to the Pahalgam attack. The date visible in the footage is July 29, and the timestamp ranges from 6:15 to 6:17 PM IST. We then conducted a keyword search and came across PM Modi's speech published by Sansad TV on July 29, titled 'PM Modi Speaks in Lok Sabha on Special discussion on Operation Sindoor.' On scanning the video from 6:15 to 6:17 PM IST, as indicated in the viral clip, we did not find any statements matching the audio heard in the circulated version. In the clip, PM Modi is heard describing the parliamentary session as a celebration of Vijay Utsav and Gaurav Gaan, highlighting the destruction of terrorist bases. He goes on to commend the courage of Indian soldiers and declares that he is voicing the sentiments of the entire nation. We reviewed the complete speech but did not find any of the statements heard in the viral video. Hinting that the footage might be manipulated or altered. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. As part of the investigation, we found that while the audio in the video shared on a social media post sounds similar to Prime Minister Modi's, it lacks the natural rhythm, pauses, and delivery typical of his public speeches. The tone is smoother and more refined than his usual speaking style. Moreover, the lip-syncing doesn't align well with the audio, raising doubts about its authenticity and hinting at possible manipulation. Furthermore, based on the insights gathered, the Desk utilised an AI-based tool, Resemble Detect, to analyse the authenticity of the minister's voice in the viral clip. The results confirmed that the audio had been edited. Below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the audio is digitally altered and fake. PM Modi made no such statement during the Parliament session. The video was shared with a false claim on social media.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video showing a rope bridge collapse in Bali shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 5 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a large number of people falling into a ditch as a rope bridge they were walking on suddenly collapsed was recently shared on social media with the claim that it depicted a real incident that occurred in Indonesia's Bali province. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found the video to be AI-generated. It was falsely shared on social media as real to mislead viewers. Claim An Instagram user named 'maqthar_pasha' shared a video on July 29, purportedly depicting a horrific incident from Bali, Indonesia, where a rope bridge collapsed. The footage showed people falling into a ditch as the bridge gave way. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. The search result via Google Lens also led the Desk to a video posted on an Instagram handle named 'kolotov_ai'. The Desk found that the user, who has over 76k followers, had shared the same video on July 24. Upon checking the profile in detail, it was found that the user is known for sharing AI-generated content. The bio on the Instagram page identified the user as Kolotov Sergey, a neural networks specialist and AI creator. Here is the link and archive link to the video, along with a screenshot: Below is a comparison image confirming that the visuals in the viral clip match the footage shared by the Instagram handle. Taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk ran the video through Cantilux, an AI detection tool, which indicated that the video had a high level of AI involvement. Below is a screenshot of the result: Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find whether any similar incident had occurred in Indonesia. The search result yielded no credible news reports confirming such an event. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a video showing a rope bridge collapse incident in Indonesia is AI-generated and falsely shared as real.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video from Samajwadi Party's Bulandshahr meeting falsely shared claiming it showed attack on Maulana Sajid Rashidi
content: New Delhi, August 5 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A group of youths claiming affiliation with the Samajwadi Party allegedly slapped Maulana Sajid Rashidi in Noida after a TV news debate, accusing him of making derogatory remarks about party MP Dimple Yadav. Following this, a video showing an altercation in a closed room began circulating widely on social media, with users claiming it captured the moment SP workers attacked Rashidi. However, a fact-check by the Press Trust of India (PTI) reveals that the video is unrelated to the Noida incident. The footage actually shows a scuffle between two groups during a booth-level SP meeting held in Syana tehsil of Bulandshahr in May 2025—two months before the altercation involving Maulana Sajid Rashidi. The viral clip has been shared with a false narrative. Claim: A video showing an altercation between a group of people in a closed room was shared by an X '@yati_Official1' on July 30, claiming that the Samajwadi Party (SP) workers attacked Maulana Sajid Rashidi. "Akhilesh Yadav has maintained silence on the insult to Dimple Yadav, but Sapa supporters are not sparing the Maulana folks anymore, brother. Today, Sapa supporters beat up another Maulana," read the post's caption. The post garnered 9652 views on social media. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively: On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across several users who had shared the same video on social media. One such user named 'Royal Rajputs of Jammu' shared the video on May 30, well before the incident involving Maulana Sajid Rashidi. According to the caption of the original post, the video shows a clash during a Samajwadi Party meeting in Bulandshahr, UP, exposing internal conflicts and a lack of unity within the party. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports and came across a report by Dainik Bhaskar published on May 30, which states that there was a fierce fight between two groups in the booth-level meeting of the Samajwadi Party in Syana. The assembly in charge, Prempal Yadav, was present at the meeting held at the camp office of the SP leader located at Hanifgarhi. The cover image of the report had clips seen in the video shared on a social media post. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Another report by ABP News dated May 30 mentioned that a ruckus in an SP meeting in Bulandshahr occurred, and workers clashed with each other. "UP News: Two groups clashed with each other in the SP meeting held in Syana tehsil of Bulandshahr, and the situation reached the stage of fighting. The video of the scuffle is going viral on social media," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video is unrelated to Maulana Sajid Rashidi. It depicts a clash between two groups during a booth-level SP meeting in Syana tehsil of Bulandshahr in May 2025, two months before the incident where Maulana Sajid Rashidi was slapped in Noida.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated 'Saiyaara' title track falsely linked to legendary singer Kishore Kumar; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 5 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video clip, purportedly taken from a film song featuring Bollywood actors Amitabh Bachchan and Moushumi Chatterjee, has recently gone viral on social media. The clip is accompanied by a claim that the song heard in the background — "Saiyaara Tu Toh Badla Nahin Hai, Mausam Zara Sa Rootha Hua Hai" (which matches the title track of the recently released Bollywood film Saiyaara) — was originally sung by legendary playback singer and musician Kishore Kumar. Several social media users have claimed that the version heard in the viral video is the original, sung by Kishore Kumar, and that the track used in the recent film is a stolen version. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false. The investigation revealed that the Saiyaara song from the recently released film is a new creation. At the same time, the version heard in the viral video was recreated using AI to mimic Kishore Kumar's voice. Speaking to PTI Fact Check, musician and producer Anshuman Sharma — who repurposed the track — clarified that RJ Kisna originally sang the vocals and later transformed using AI technology to resemble Kishore Kumar's voice. Sharma also confirmed that he freshly produced the track used in his song. Additionally, the visuals in the viral clip — featuring actors Amitabh Bachchan and Moushumi Chatterjee — were taken from the original song "Rim Jhim Gire Sawan" from the 1979 Bollywood film Manzil. The AI-generated audio was superimposed onto these visuals, thereby misleading viewers. Claim An X user, Ravi Kumar, posted a video clip on July 31 that appears to be from an old movie scene featuring Bollywood actors Amitabh Bachchan and Moushumi Chatterjee. In the video, the background song — "Saiyaara Tu Toh Badla Nahin Hai, Mausam Zara Sa Rootha Hua Hai" — matches the title track of the recently released film Saiyaara and is heard in a voice resembling that of legendary singer Kishore Kumar. The user claimed that the version heard in the viral video was the original, sung by Kishore Kumar, and alleged that it was stolen and used in the recently released movie track. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims — that the playback song heard in the video was sung by the late Kishore Kumar, a veteran Indian playback singer and musician. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions also available here and here respectively. The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a video uploaded by the entertainment company Shemaroo Entertainment Limited on its official YouTube channel. The visuals in this video — featuring Amitabh Bachchan and Moushumi Chatterjee — were identical to those seen in the viral clip. However, the accompanying description clarified that the footage is originally from the popular Bollywood song "Rim Jhim Gire Sawan" from the 1979 film Manzil. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting that the content in the viral video matches that of the video posted by the entertainment company on its YouTube channel. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google keyword search using terms like "Kishore Kumar Saiyaara song." This led to a video posted by Instagram user @anshuman.sharma1 on July 26. The user had shared the same Saiyaara song rendered in Kishore Kumar's voice and explicitly stated in the caption that it was created using AI. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot. Additionally, the customised keyword search also led the Desk to a video posted by the same user, Anshuman Sharma, on his official YouTube channel, featuring an extended clip of the aforementioned song in Kishore Kumar's voice, generated using AI. In the description box, the user once again clarified that the vocals were generated using AI. "The full version is finally here! We converted the vocals sung amazingly by RJ Kisna into Kishore da's voice using AI, and I produced the retro background music. Let me know if you all want a breakdown of how I do these retro versions," the user mentioned. Moreover, the YouTube video also included the same visuals featuring Amitabh Bachchan and Moushumi Chatterjee as seen in the first-mentioned viral clip, further confirming that it had been taken from this AI-generated video. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting that the content in the viral video matches that of the visuals used in the YouTube video. Further, the Desk also contacted musician and producer Anshuman Sharma for clarification on the viral video. He stated, "We converted the vocals, beautifully sung by RJ Kisna, into Kishore da's voice using AI, and I produced the retro-style background music." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Kishore Kumar did not originally sing the Saiyaara song heard in the background of the viral video. The rendition in his voice was created using AI-based voice-cloning technology.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Scripted video of policeman being tricked and looted in broad daylight falsely shared as real incident
content: New Delhi, August 6 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video claiming to show a real incident of a policeman being looted in broad daylight has been widely shared on social media. The clip shows two individuals allegedly tricking a policeman and running away with his money without arousing his suspicion. In the video, the policeman was seen counting a bundle of notes taken from a bag when two pillion riders, a man and a woman, spot him and appear to devise a plan. The man hides behind some bushes while instructing the woman to ride past the officer and pretend to fall off the bike, which she does. The policeman rushes to help her, leaving his bag on a two-wheeler nearby. Meanwhile, the man emerges from the bushes, steals the bag, hides it under his shirt, and pretends to assist the woman. Together, they leave the scene. When the policeman returns, he finds his bag missing. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the video and confirmed that it is scripted and has been falsely shared as a real incident to mislead viewers. Claim An X handle with the username RAGHUWANSHI (@Ranjeetraghu_) shared a video on August 5, allegedly showing a policeman being tricked and looted in broad daylight. The footage purportedly depicted two individuals successfully executing a planned theft without raising the policeman's suspicion. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively: The search also led the Desk to a video posted on a YouTube channel named '3RD EYE', which has over 2.97 million subscribers. The Desk found that the same video, showing the alleged theft involving a policeman, was uploaded by the channel on September 28, 2024. However, a disclaimer by the channel clarified that the video was a scripted skit and does not depict a real incident. "Thank you for watching! Please be aware that this channel features scripted dramas and parodies to raise awareness about different situations. These short films are for entertainment purposes only." reads the disclaimer on the video. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot: A combination image comparing visuals from the viral social media video and the YouTube upload confirmed that they are the same. Additionally, the Desk also scanned other videos published on the 3RD EYE channel and found that all of them were scripted and produced for entertainment and awareness purposes. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video showing a policeman being tricked and looted in broad daylight was scripted and falsely shared as real to mislead viewers.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Clipped video of Amit Shah mentioning Sardar Patel during Parliament speech taken out of context and shared with false claim
