content: New Delhi, August 7 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of Union Home Minister Amit Shah addressing Parliament has gone viral, accompanied by claims that he made a factual error by suggesting Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel protested a political decision in 1960, ten years after Patel's death in December 1950. In the 13-second clip widely shared on social media, Shah appears to say that Patel went to All India Radio to stop an announcement. The posts accuse Shah of distorting history and point to the timeline discrepancy as evidence of a major slip-up in his speech. However, a closer review by the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the viral clip was misleading and taken out of context. Shah was responding to an interjection from another MP who mentioned Patel's name mid-speech. His brief reference to Patel was separate from his subsequent remarks about the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty, in which he directly criticised then Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru. The confusion appears to stem from the tight sequencing of these unrelated portions of the speech; Patel's name was mentioned in response to a heckle, not in the context of the treaty. Claim: A video featuring Union Home Minister Amit Shah addressing the Parliament was shared by an X user '@Aloksharmaaicc' on July 29, claiming that he allegedly said Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel opposed the 1960 Indus Water Treaty. In the 00:13-second video, Shah says, "Manyawar, in 1960, Sardar Patel had protested; he went to Air India Radio (AIR) in his car, and closed the doors, so that they wouldn't make the announcement." The post's caption read: "Sardar Patel ji had already passed away in 1950! So how could Sardar Patel ji have protested in 1960? Amit Shah ji's lie has been caught!" The post clocked 53.1k views on social media. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively: As part of the investigation, the Desk accessed the Lok Sabha address uploaded on the official YouTube channel of 'Sansad TV' dated Jul 29, 2025, where at 41 minutes 04 seconds, Amit Shah says, "Manyawar, I want to highlight some parts from the history of this country. In 1948, our forces held a decisive position in Jammu and Kashmir. Jawaharlal Nehru ji, despite the refusal from Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel ji ended the war…" The viral excerpts can be heard from 41:47 and 41:50, when he says, "Manyawar, in 1960". During his speech, an unexpected interruption comes from an unidentified opposition MP shouting something hard to catch at full speed, but when you slow down the clip to 0.75× playback, the interjection becomes clear: "Sardar Patel…" prompts Shah to pause. After gathering himself, Shah picks up where he left off. He says, "Sardar Patel protested. He drove to All India Radio, shut the car doors so that the announcement couldn't go through." Then, lowering his gaze to his notes, he resumes, "Manyavar, back in 1960, India held a position, geographically and strategically, of strength regarding the Indus waters. But what transpired? The Indus Waters Treaty was signed, resulting in the majority, 80% of our water being allocated to Pakistan." You can confirm this sequence by reducing the video speed and turning up the background audio; his words and the interruption emerge with clarity. This confirms that because these two segments came in quick succession, it created the misleading impression that Shah was claiming Patel had objected to the 1960 treaty. But in reality, the reference to Patel was a detour prompted by a heckle, not a historical assertion about the treaty itself, which Shah clearly pins on Nehru. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video being shared on social media was based on a completely false and baseless claim. In the original video, Shah never stated Sardar Patel had opposed the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty. His reference to Patel was actually a response to an interjection from another MP. After addressing that comment, Shah returned to his original line of argument, criticising Nehru over the treaty. The back-to-back nature of these remarks is what seems to have confused the users.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of Kenya protesters pelting stones on Army vehicle falsely linked to India; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 7 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a large group of people pelting stones at a vehicle on a highway was recently shared on social media with the claim that it depicted an incident in India, where locals allegedly attacked an Indian Army vehicle. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found that it actually showed a protest that took place in Kenya. The unrelated video was falsely shared on social media, misrepresenting it as an incident from India. Claim An Instagram user named jatshyolal shared a video on August 1 showing a group of locals pelting stones at a vehicle, claiming that it was an Indian Army vehicle passing through a highway. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search result also led the Desk to a video posted on a Facebook page named 'Nsem sisi Tv' on July 2. The visuals seen in the Facebook video matched those in the viral post. The caption, however, identified the incident as having occurred in Kenya and not India. Further, upon closer inspection, the Desk noted that the billboards visible in the background of the video included Kenyan city names, thus confirming the location. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. A combination image comparison confirmed that the visuals from the viral video matched those in the Facebook video. Additionally, the Google reverse image search also led the Desk to a video posted by the official YouTube channel of Mutembei TV, a Kenya-based news portal, on June 25, 2025. The footage showed a similar background and scene to that in the viral video. However, the caption and description stated that it is linked to the violent Gen Z protests that erupted in Kenya. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. In the subsequent part of the investigation, taking cues from the inputs generated above, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find significant details related to Kenya's Gen Z protests. The search led to a video news report published by DW News on July 10, 2025, which stated that the unrest began in Kenya in June last year, in response to government-proposed tax increases and incidents of police brutality. While the tax bill was later withdrawn, the protests reignited in June this year following the death of blogger Albert Ojwang while in police custody. "The protests resulted in 16 deaths, bringing the total number to 100 since June 2024. A significant number of protesters were also detained, while many others went missing," the report added. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a group of people pelting stones at a military vehicle was not from India, as claimed. The footage was, in fact, from Kenya and linked to the ongoing Gen Z protests there.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated image falsely shared as aftermath of recent Uttarkashi flash flood
content: New Delhi, August 7 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A striking image showing several collapsed houses along a riverbank, surrounded by rubble and debris, was widely circulated on social media platforms. The visuals suggested widespread destruction, with fast-moving floodwaters cutting through what appears to be a hilly town. Many users claimed that the photo captured the aftermath of a recent flashflood caused by a cloudburst in Uttarkashi, Uttarakhand — a region that has indeed witnessed extreme weather events during the monsoon. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the image being circulated on social media is manipulated and AI-generated. It was shared with a false claim. Notably, a cloudburst did trigger a flash flood in the high-altitude villages of Dharali, on the way to Gangotri, with the raging waters sweeping away several houses and leaving at least four people dead, officials said. Dharali is the main stopover en route to Gangotri and is home to many hotels, restaurants, and homestays. The devastating flash flood followed a cloudburst somewhere in the catchment area of the Kheer Ganga river, locals said. Claim: A photograph depicting the devastating aftermath of a severe flood or cloudburst in a mountainous region was shared by an X user, @Ashu31stDec, on August 5, claiming that the picture was from Uttarkashi's recent cloudburst. "The tragic incident of cloudburst in Uttarkashi has caused huge loss of life and property," read the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the photo through the Reverse Image Search and found that several other users had shared the same image with similar claims on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived version can be found here and here , respectively. On carefully analysing the picture, the Desk noticed a watermark at the bottom right corner of the picture that read 'ai'. Below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk ran the purported image through Hive Moderation (an AI detection tool). The tool detected a substantial presence of AI-generated elements in the image. Below is a screenshot of the result. Additionally, the image was also tested using another AI detection tool, WasitAI, which also concluded that the image was AI-generated. Below is a screenshot of the result: Notably, the Uttarakhand Police, in an X post dated August 5, 2025, shared the images showing actual damage in the Dharali market area due to the rising water level in Kheer Gadh. "In Dharali, Uttarkashi, due to the rising water level in Kheer Gadh, reports of damage have been received in the Dharali market area. Police/Fire/SDRF/Army, along with other disaster management teams, are engaged in relief and rescue operations at the site," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the picture allegedly depicting the aftermath of the cloudburst in Uttarkashi is manipulated and AI-generated.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: False claim and fraudulent link shared as government offering Rs 5,000 cash reward for Rakshabandhan and Independence Day; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 7 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video featuring the BJP's logo and an image of Prime Minister Narendra Modi has been widely circulated on social media, claiming that the central government is offering Rs 5,000 in cash rewards to all citizens on the occasion of Rakshabandhan and Independence Day. The post directs users to a website that promises the cash transfer via a virtual scratch card under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found it to be false. The website linked in the post does not belong to any official government domain and shows several red flags, including deceptive UPI prompts and URLs that mimic government schemes. A thorough check of the official Jan Dhan Yojana website revealed no such announcement or offer. Additionally, keyword searches and scans of news databases turned up no credible media reports confirming the existence of any such scheme. All evidence points to this being a coordinated attempt to mislead users, a fraudulent announcement falsely shared as real on social media. Claim: A purported video featuring the BJP's logo and PM Modi's picture was shared by a Facebook user 'BJP INDIA' on August 2, claiming that the government is offering Rs 5,000 cash rewards to citizens, on the occasion of Rakshabandhan and Independence Day. The post clocked 9.1k views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The post also carried a link which, when clicked, led the Desk to the a site which consisted to a virtual scratch card. The site mentioned: "Through Jan Dhan Yojana, everyone will get ₹5000 free in their account. Scratch the card to get money in your account…Every Indian citizen gets a gift of up to ₹5000 in their account under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana. Click here to transfer to your bank account," read the Hindi text on the website. Another link asked the user whether to "receive payment" using UPI apps PhonePe or PayTM. Below is a screenshot of the same. Next, the Desk noticed the hyperlink 'https://wh1463450.ispot.cc/', which does not resemble the original official government portal, further raising our doubts. The Desk also scanned the official website of the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), which did not have any announcement on such a giveaway. Here is the link to the official website. As part of the investigation, the Desk also conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports that covered the announcement. However, our search did not lead us to any credible news articles that cited the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the post and website claiming to offer Rs 5,000 cash rewards to citizens, on the occasion of Rakshabandhan and Independence Day is fraudulent and fake, as there has been no announcement from the government.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Violent clash between BNP factions in Bangladesh misrepresented as incident from India
content: New Delhi, August 7 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a group of angry people, particularly carrying long spears in their hands and marching in a line, was recently shared on social media with the claim that they were illegal Bangladeshi immigrants on their way to attack security personnel in Assam. The user alleged that the video depicted illegal Bangladeshi immigrants armed with homemade spears, preparing to launch a violent attack on officials and police personnel in Assam's Goalpara district. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found that the video was falsely shared in the name of India. The footage actually showed a violent clash between two factions of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) in Ashtagram, Kishoreganj. At least 40 people were injured in the incident, which also led to vandalism, looting, and arson. Claim An X handle with the username @KreatelyMedia shared a video on August 5 showing a large group of people marching in a line, carrying long spears. The user claimed that these were illegal Bangladeshi immigrants marching to attack officials and police officers in Assam's Goalpara district. "Illegal Bangladeshis have armed themselves with homemade spears to launch a violent attack on officials and police in Goalpara, Assam," the user posted alongside the video. At the time of publishing this report, the video had garnered 36,000 views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a video posted on the Facebook page of the Bangladesh-based news portal Daily Sun on July 1, 2025. The Desk found that the visuals seen in the viral video matched those in the video shared by the news portal. According to the accompanying details, the video showed clashes between two factions of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party, and at least 40 people were injured in the incident. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. A comparison of the images confirmed that the visuals from the viral video were identical to those in the Facebook post. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a keyword search on Google for more details. This led to a news report published by Bangladesh-based news portal Dhaka Mail on July 1, 2025. According to the report, the video showed a fierce clash that broke out between two BNP factions in Ashtagram, Kishoreganj, and not illegal Bangladeshi immigrants attacking security personnel in Assam. "The incident took place in Abdullahpur village of Khairpur-Abdullapur union of the upazila on Tuesday (July 1) morning," the report stated. "The violent clash occurred due to a long-standing family and political dispute between Union BNP President Kamal Pasha and Kishoreganj District Volunteer Party Joint Convener Farhad Ahmed," it added. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video allegedly showing illegal Bangladeshi immigrants on their way to attack security personnel in Assam is false. The video actually showed a violent political clash between two BNP factions in Kishoreganj district, Bangladesh.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2022 Himachal rescue video falsely shared as recent incident of flash floods in Uttarakhand's Uttarkashi district; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 8 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A dramatic rescue scene, where men are seen using ropes to save stranded youths from the middle of a swollen river, has been circulating widely on social media. Posts sharing the clip claim it shows the aftermath of the recent cloudburst and flash floods in Uttarakhand's Uttarkashi district. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video dates back to 2022 from Himachal Pradesh's Solan district and is unrelated to the recent cloudburst in Uttarkhand's Uttarkashi. The video was shared with a false claim on social media. Claim: A dramatic clip posted on X by user @anitaklab on August 6 shows several men using ropes to pull a few youths to safety from the middle of a fast-flowing river. The post claimed the footage was shot in Uttarkashi, Uttarakhand, in the aftermath of a recent cloudburst that triggered flash floods in the district. "Another video from Uttarkashi Dharali has surfaced; the situation is quite bad," read the post's caption. The post clocked 18.1k views on social media. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a video report uploaded on The Indian Express' official YouTube channel on July 29, 2022. According to the report, in Himachal Pradesh's Solan, locals rescued five youths after they were trapped in the river in Nalagarh. The clips from the social media post were similar to the video in the report. Therefore, the timeline and the visuals confirm that this incident is old and unrelated to the cloudburst in Uttarkashi. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Another report was published by Aaj Tak on their official YouTube channel on July 30, 2022. It mentioned that due to heavy rains, the rivers and rivulets are in full spate in Himachal Pradesh. 5 youths were trapped in the Chikli river in Nalagarh, Solan, during that time they had landed in the river to take a selfie. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video dates back to 2022 from Himachal Pradesh's Solan district and is unrelated to the recent cloudburst in Uttarkhand's Uttarkashi.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Image showing dead bodies of road accident victims in Gonda falsely linked to Uttarkashi tragedy; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 8 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Days after disaster swept through the Himalayan village of Dharali, where a massive cloudburst led to flash floods that barreled through homes, trees, and cars—leaving a significant number of people missing and a few dead—a purported social media photo showing several dead bodies lying on the ground is being shared online. Users claimed the image depicted the bodies of victims who died in the same Uttarakhand tragedy. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found the image to be unrelated to the Uttarakhand tragedy. The image actually showed the bodies of people who died in a road accident in Uttar Pradesh's Gonda district earlier, on August 3, 2025. An unrelated image of road accident victims was falsely linked to the Uttarakhand disaster. Claim An Instagram user named Laxman Lakshman Singh (@uk_01_laxman) shared, on August 6, a visually distressing image showing several dead bodies lying on the ground. The user claimed these were the bodies of people who lost their lives in the flash floods that hit Uttarakhand's Dharali village on August 5. "Many people died tragically due to cloudburst in Uttarakhand's Dharali village. May their souls rest in peace. Om Shanti Shanti," the user wrote in the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (Disclaimer: The image contains visually distressing content) Investigation The Desk ran the image through Google Lens and came across multiple social media accounts those who had shared the same image with similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a social media post shared by UP's Mahmoodabad MLA Asha Maurya on her official Instagram handle. The image shared by her matched the one seen in the viral posts. However, the caption revealed that the image depicted the bodies of people killed in a tragic road accident in Uttar Pradesh's Gonda district. The MLA expressed condolences for the victims' tragic demise. Here is the link and archive link to the post. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find more details about the accident. The search led to a news report published by Hindustan Times on August 3, 2025. The report stated: "Eleven people, including nine of a family, were killed and four others injured when a speeding SUV carrying them lost control and fell into the Saryu canal in Uttar Pradesh's Gonda district on Sunday morning." It added: "According to the Gonda SP, the vehicle was carrying 15 people who were on their way to offer prayers at Pirthvinath temple in Ayodhya from Sihagawan under Gonda's Motiganj police station. The mishap occurred near Rehra village under Itiyathok police station on the Seehgaon-Kharagoopur road." Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Additionally, to verify the actual death toll in the Dharali tragedy and gather information on the ongoing rescue efforts, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search. The search led to a New Indian Express report published on August 7. It stated that so far, three civilian fatalities had been confirmed, and over 100 people, including nine Army personnel, were feared missing after an Army post sustained extensive damage. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the image showing dead bodies of people who died in a road accident in Uttar Pradesh's Gonda district was falsely shared as being linked to the Uttarakhand flash flood tragedy.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of harassment of Muslim woman in UP's Moradabad shared with false communal narrative; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 8 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media post, attached with two purported images – the first showing a man allegedly groping a woman from behind and the second image showing the same man running away – was recently shared on social media with a claim that it depicted a harassment incident from Uttar Pradesh's Moradabad where a Muslim woman was harassed by a Hindu man. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it was falsely shared with a communal narrative. While an incident involving a man forcefully groping a burqa-clad woman did occur on a street in Uttar Pradesh's Moradabad, the investigation found that both the victim and the accused belong to the same religion. An incident of sexual harassment was misrepresented online with a fabricated communal spin. Claim A Facebook handle with the username 'Nazir Raees' shared, on August 4, a social media post attached with two purported images – the first showing a man allegedly groping a woman from behind and the second showing the same man running away from the location. The user claimed the images depicted a harassment incident from Uttar Pradesh's Moradabad where a Muslim woman was harassed by a Hindu man. "Disturbing & Shameful. Muradabad Muslim Woman Harassed By A Hindu Man On Road," the user shared the post with the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk began the investigation by running the image showing a man groping a woman from behind, shared in the social media post, through Google Lens. The search result led the Desk to a news report published by India Today on August 4, which had elaborated on the same incident mentioned in the social media post. However, nowhere was the identity of the accused reported to be Hindu. The report mentioned that a man was caught harassing a burqa-clad woman on CCTV camera in Uttar Pradesh's Moradabad. "The incident took place in the Gol Kothi Wali Gali area of Moradabad. In the CCTV footage, the woman is seen walking alone when the man comes from behind and suddenly gropes her. The woman tried hard to free herself from him and finally managed to make him run away from the spot," the report stated. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting the feature image of the news report matched with that of the image shared in the social media post, suggesting the two depicted the same incident of harassment. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find information mentioning the identity of the accused. The search result led the Desk to a news report published by Times of India on August 5, which mentioned that the Uttar Pradesh Police arrested a 28-year-old man, Mohd Aadil, on the charges of allegedly harassing a burqa-clad woman by touching her inappropriately after a brief chase. The report, mentioning the dramatic arrest of Mohd Adil, stated: "Due to the ongoing drone rumours, police were patrolling in a village when the cops saw a high-speed bike coming towards them. They gestured to the biker to stop, but he sped away, taking a U-turn. Police followed him. A considerable distance away, the accused slipped in mud and tried to flee on foot. However, when cops rushed towards him, he opened fire towards them. In retaliatory fire, the accused was shot in the leg and was arrested." It added, "During questioning, the accused Aadil told us that he thought the cops had come to arrest him due to his behaviour with the woman on Sunday." Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Additionally, the customised keyword search also led the Desk to an official statement shared by the Uttar Pradesh Police on the matter. In the statement, the Uttar Pradesh Police confirmed that the accused had been identified as Mohd Adil and that he had confessed to the crime. Moreover, the statement also elaborated on a similar incident (as described in the aforementioned article) which led to the arrest of the accused. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video showing an harassment incident in Uttar Pradesh's Moradabad was falsely shared with a communal narrative. In reality, the incident did occur, but both the accused and the victim belong to the same religion.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2017 video of UP cops drinking liquor in public shared as recent with false claim; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 11 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users have recently shared a video claiming it shows a recent incident in Uttar Pradesh, where two state police personnel were caught drinking liquor in public. The footage shows two policemen — one preparing a drink while sitting on the bonnet of a car, and the other visibly intoxicated, saying it was the "festival of police" and that they would drink and perform their duty simultaneously. However, a Press Trust of India (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigation found the claim to be false. The video is from 2017 and depicts two personnel of the Uttar Pradesh Police's Dial 100 service sitting on their official black SUV and drinking liquor on an open highway in Shamli. An old, unrelated video was thus falsely shared on social media with the claim that it showed a recent incident. Claim An Instagram handle with the username 'Khurshid Misthari' shared, on August 2, a video purportedly showing two personnel from the Uttar Pradesh police forces drinking in public. The video showed them consuming alcohol in broad daylight while on duty. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video had garnered 52,234 likes.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search results also led the Desk to a video posted on the official YouTube channel of One India Hindi. The Desk found that the same video, showing two police personnel consuming alcohol in public, had been uploaded by the channel. The details shared in the video indicated that the incident did indeed pertain to Uttar Pradesh and showed state police personnel drinking alcohol in broad daylight. However, the timeline mentioned in the news report indicated that the incident was at least eight years old and did not depict a recent event. The video news stated: "A video of Shamli district of UP has surfaced. Here, on the day of Holi, the policemen deployed at Dial 100 service drank alcohol in the middle of the road and created a ruckus. The surprising thing is that those policemen had converted the bonnet of the Dial 100 vehicle into a bar. It can be seen in the video that two bottles of liquor and a bottle of water are kept on the bonnet of the vehicle. One policeman is making a drink sitting on the bonnet of the vehicle, and the other is standing with the support of the bonnet." Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. A combination image comparing visuals from the viral social media video and the YouTube upload confirmed that they are the same. Additionally, taking cues from the findings above, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find further details related to the incident. The search led the Desk to a news report published by Financial Express on March 15, 2017, which stated that the video was first published by the Mayawati-led Bahujan Samaj Party, showing two drunk cops from the Dial 100 service of UP Police. "The Dial 100 service of UP Police has been started by the ruling party SP to reach people in need quickly and help them in the best possible way," the report added. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing two police personnel from the Uttar Pradesh Police drinking in public was falsely shared as a recent incident. The video dates back to March 2017.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video from Indonesia falsely linked to recent landslide in Chamba of Himachal Pradesh; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 11 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): The weather office sounded an orange alert of heavy to hefty rainfall on August 11 in Chamba, Kangra and Mandi districts, with a yellow alert in Una, Bilaspur, Hamirpur and Solan districts. Amid these alerts, a video has been widely circulated on social media showing a truck narrowly escaping a landslide. Several users sharing the clip claim that the incident took place in Chamba, Himachal Pradesh, in the wake of the current rain warnings.. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the viral video and found that the footage is not recent, nor is it from Himachal Pradesh. In reality, the video dates back to 2024 and shows a truck narrowly avoiding a landslide in Indonesia. The clip is unrelated to Chamba or the ongoing weather situation in Himachal Pradesh and has been shared online with a false claim. Claim: A video featuring a truck on a hilly location narrowly escaping a landslide was shared by a Facebook user, Pankaj Chandel, on August 2, claiming that the incident happened in Chamba, Himachal Pradesh. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the image through Google Lens and came across multiple social media accounts that had shared the same photo with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. Upon further review of the search results, the Desk came across a report by CNN Indonesia featuring similar clips to those seen in the social media post. The video was published on their official YouTube page on May 18, 2024. As per the report, a truck was nearly buried in a landslide in Sitinjau Lauik, Padang. The video also featured a man in a blue raincoat who is seen stepping onto the road, likely after sensing the landslide to warn approaching vehicles. The timeline and the information available clarify that the video is not from Himachal Pradesh. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the news report and the social media post. Another report by SindoNews.com dated May 17 highlighted that a landslide nearly buried a tanker truck on the Trans-Sumatra Highway in the Sitinjau Lauik area, Padang City, West Sumatra. Tree branches hit the rear of the tanker truck. Luckily, the tanker truck driver survived the incident. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video dates back to 2024, when a truck narrowly escaped a landslide in Indonesia and is unrelated to Chamba, Himachal Pradesh.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Manipulated, AI-generated video falsely shared to claim flood devastation in Prayagraj; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 12 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): As heavy rain lashes large parts of Uttar Pradesh, the number of flood-affected districts has risen to 24, intensifying concerns across both rural and urban regions. The situation remains grim, with reports of damage to homes, farmland, and infrastructure. Amid this, a video circulating widely on social media appears to show entire livelihoods being swept away by raging floodwaters. Many users claim the incident took place in Prayagraj. However, a Press Trust of India (PTI) Fact Check investigation found that the video is not genuine. Analysis revealed it to be manipulated and AI-generated, and it is being shared online with a false claim. Notably, as per reports, the water levels of the Ganga and Yamuna rivers in Prayagraj are continuously decreasing, now falling below the danger mark. The Prayagraj Municipal Corporation has launched cleaning operations in the flood-affected areas. Claim: A video depicting an entire area and entire livelihoods being swept away by the force of water was shared by an Instagram user '__india18__' on August 7, claiming that the incident happened in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh, following the flood situation. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation: The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports, but did not find any credible reports citing the tragic incident. Given the gravity of the matter and the potential loss, it would have received broad media coverage. On careful analysis of the video, the Desk found several discrepancies hinting that the footage might be manipulated or AI-generated. For instance, the movement of the vehicles and also the trees looks unnatural, and the extra glossy texture hints that it has been manipulated. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk then ran the video through Cantilux, an AI-detection tool, which indicated that the video had a high level of AI involvement. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video being shared on social media is manipulated and AI-generated and was shared with a false claim.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video shared to falsely claim bridge collapsed in Prayagraj; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 12 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it depicted a horrific incident from Uttar Pradesh's Prayagraj, where a bridge collapsed. The footage showed a large number of people standing and walking on the bridge, who, at the time of the incident, fell into a water body that was built upon. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found the video to be AI-generated. The video in the social media post was falsely shared as real to mislead viewers. Claim A Facebook handle with the username Alex Khan shared, on August 8, a video purportedly showing a horrific incident of a bridge collapse that occurred in Uttar Pradesh's Prayagraj. The footage showed a large number of people standing and walking on the bridge, who, at the time of the incident, fell into a water body that it was built upon. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video had garnered 16.5k likes and 1.4k shares) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find whether any similar incident had occurred in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh. The search results yielded no credible news reports confirming such an event. Had such an incident occurred, the media would have covered it extensively. Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the social media video and observed several inconsistencies that strongly suggested it was AI-generated. For instance, the fall of the bridge depicted in the video appeared too unreal, and the video seemed to have an excessively glossy finish — a common characteristic of AI-generated visuals. Taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk ran the video through Cantilux, an AI detection tool, which indicated that the video had a high level of AI involvement. Below is a screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a video showing a bridge collapse incident in Prayagraj, UP, is AI-generated and falsely shared as real.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-manipulated clip falsely claims journalist Rajat Sharma reported 50% cut in pharma exports to US
content: New Delhi, August 12 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): After US President Donald Trump announced a 25 per cent additional tariff, after announcing 25% tariff initially, on Indian imports, citing New Delhi's purchase of Russian crude, a video began circulating on social media featuring India TV anchor Rajat Sharma reading a news bulletin. Users sharing the clip claimed he said India had cut its pharmaceutical exports to the United States by 50 per cent in response to the tariff hike. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk reviewed the footage and found it had been digitally manipulated using AI. Moreover, there have been no reports indicating that India has reduced its pharmaceutical exports to the USA by 50%. The video was shared with a false claim on social media. Claim: A purported video featuring journalist Rajat Sharma reading a news bulletin was shared by an X user '@KailasSanatani' on August 11, claiming that India has cut off 50% of its pharmaceutical exports to the USA following the recent tariff hikes. "So the prediction turned out to be correct...! It is essential for every Indian citizen to seriously understand what is happening in our country and what our Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi ji is doing for the nation. This video is presented by senior journalist Rajat Sharma ji from India TV. Please watch and listen to it carefully in its entirety. Only then will you be able to properly understand how Modi ji is enhancing the country's pride and honour abroad and striving to take India to new heights on the global stage. We are proud that we have been blessed with such a great leader. It is our good fortune — perhaps the result of good deeds from past lives — that we have a dedicated, honest, and patriotic Prime Minister like Modi ji. He neither regards day nor night — constantly engaged in efforts to take the country forward. We must appreciate his efforts, honour him, and pray to God to grant Modi ji a long life and good health so that he can continue to serve the nation in this manner. It is a humble request to please watch this video in full and share it with as many fellow countrymen as possible," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. While reviewing search results, the Desk located the original and more extended version of the clip on 'India TV's' official YouTube channel, uploaded on July 15, 2025. In it, anchor Rajat Sharma, dressed identically to the viral footage, is seen presenting the day's top stories. At no point does he talk about India's pharmaceutical exports to the US or any tariff measures by Washington. Notably, the broadcast aired before US President Donald Trump announced a 50% tariff on Indian imports. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk carefully analysed the video shared on social media and found discrepancies in journalist Rajat Sharma's voice and lip movements while speaking. This suggests that the video may have been digitally altered or AI-generated. The Desk ran the footage through Hive Moderation, an AI-detection tool which detected 99% of the audio used in the video is AI-generated. Below is a screenshot of the same. Furthermore, the Desk utilised an AI-based tool, Resemble Detect, to analyse the authenticity of Sharma's voice in the clip. The results confirmed that the audio had been edited. Below is a screenshot of the same. To verify the claim in the post, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports stating that India has indeed reduced its pharmaceutical exports to the USA by 50% following the recent import tariff hikes by the USA. However, we found no credible reports indicating that India has reduced its pharmaceutical exports to the USA by 50% following the recent tariff hikes. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video featuring journalist Rajat Sharma, claiming that India has cut off 50% of its pharmaceutical exports to the USA, is manipulated and AI-generated.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally manipulated image of Chinook aircraft airlifting a JCB falsely linked to the recent Dharali tragedy; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 12 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): As relief and rescue operations continue in the Dharali area of Uttarkashi following a week of incessant rainfall and flash floods that wiped out almost an entire village, an image has been circulating on social media showing a JCB being airlifted by an IAF Chinook aircraft. Users claimed that, with roads blocked due to extreme weather, the JCB was flown in to continue relief work in the region. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found that the image is digitally altered. The composite was created by combining two separate photographs — one taken in 2020 and another from the recent Dharali tragedy. The manipulated image is thus being falsely linked to the ongoing disaster. Claim An X user, Saurabh Shrotriya (@MrShrotriya), shared on August 9 an image purportedly showing an Indian Air Force Chinook aircraft airlifting a JCB for relief work in Uttarakhand's Dharali, after roads there were blocked post-disaster. "When roads to Dharali were blocked, a Chinook helicopter airlifted a JCB for relief work. Had Congress been in power, we would've seen a repeat of the Kedarnath tragedy, where for 5 days no relief was sent, waiting to award contracts to Robert Vadra's aviation firm, and another week wasted so Sonia and Rahul could flag off trucks from Delhi. Disaster relief can't wait for politics," the user wrote in the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and found multiple social media accounts of those who shared the same image with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to check if the IAF's Chinook aircraft was being used in the rescue and relief efforts in Dharali, and whether it had recently airlifted a JCB to the region as claimed in the social media post. While the search results confirmed that the Chinook, along with Mi-17 V5 and ALH helicopters, was being used in disaster and relief operations in Uttarakhand, no reports related to a JCB being airlifted by a Chinook were found. Had the development been real, the media would have covered it extensively. Below is a link and archive link to the social media post shared by the IAF on August 9, showing the Chinook among other aircraft being used for the rescue operation. A screenshot has also been attached: Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the social media image in question. The analysis found the image to have been digitally edited, as the background of the helicopter in the upper half of the photo and the flood-affected area seen in the bottom half of the image appeared to be mismatched. Taking cues from the above findings, the Desk cropped the first half of the image and ran it through Google Reverse Image Search, which led to a Rediff report published on October 7, 2020. The report included a photo showing an Indian Air Force CH-47 Chinook helicopter carrying a howitzer. This closely matched the helicopter seen in the social media image, except that in the latter, a JCB was present in place of the howitzer in the original. The report further stated that the original image showed an IAF CH-47 Chinook helicopter carrying a howitzer during a dress rehearsal for the 88th Indian Air Force Day celebrations at the Hindon airbase. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting the similarity between the social media image and the image shared in the Rediff report. Furthermore, continuing with its investigation, the Desk also ran the bottom half of the social media image through Google Lens. The search results found that multiple media reports had used the image shared on August 5, 2025, stating that it showed the view of the Dharali market area after the flash floods. Here is the link to the report shared by Hindustan Times on August 5, which carried the same photo of Dharali as the one seen in the social media image: Below is a combination image highlighting that the visuals seen in the lower half of the social media post were the same as those in the image seen in the news report. Pertinently, based on the above findings, it was established that the image showing a Chinook airlifting a JCB in the aforementioned social media post is digitally altered. The image has been created using two different photos — one taken in 2020 and another from the recent Dharali tragedy. Additionally, to find details related to the viral claim, the Desk also conducted a customised keyword search on Google. The search results led to a statement issued by the Uttarkashi Police on its official X handle, which termed the image fake. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the image showing IAF's Chinook aircraft airlifting a JCB was digitally altered and shared on social media to mislead viewers.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2014 X post by Modi falsely linked to Rahul Gandhi's recent protest over alleged 'vote theft'; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 13 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi's allegation of over one lakh stolen votes in Karnataka's Mahadevapura assembly segment has triggered a political storm. Amid protests by opposition parties over alleged 'vote theft', a purported screenshot of an X post by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in which he allegedly criticised the Election Commission, was shared by several social media users. Those sharing the post claim that the Prime Minister announced his support for senior Congress MP Rahul Gandhi's protest against the ECI over alleged electoral malpractices. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found that the X post by Modi dates back to 2014, when he questioned the poll body's neutrality after being denied permission for a public meeting at a venue of his choice in Varanasi. He was not the prime minister when he posted the tweet shown in the recent social media post. An old post was misrepresented to mock the BJP's stance on the Opposition's ongoing 'vote theft' claims. Claim: An X user, @VoiceofRG, on August 8, shared a purported screenshot of an X post by PM Modi in which he criticised the Election Commission. The user sharing the screenshot claimed that the Prime Minister announced his support for senior Congress MP Rahul Gandhi's protest against the ECI over alleged electoral malpractices. The purported screenshot read, "It is unfortunate that EC is not concerned about the institution's neutrality, and that is why our Karyakarta have to embark on a Satyagraha" While the post's caption read: "Breaking: Narendra Modi announces support for Rahul Gandhi's campaign against ECI" The post clocked 15.3k views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral post through Reverse Image Search and found that several other users had also shared the same screenshot with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived version can be viewed here and here , respectively. On careful analysis of the X post by PM Modi, the Desk noticed that it was dated May 8, 2014. Following this, we ran a relevant keyword search on the social media platform that led us to the same post. Here is the link to the same, and below is a screenshot. As part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports that cited this X post. A PTI report carried by The Hindu dated December 4, 2021, highlighted that Narendra Modi questioned the poll body's neutrality over the denial of permission for a public meeting at a venue of his choice in Varanasi, even as he appealed to party workers to maintain peace while protesting the move. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the screenshot is being shared out of context and to mock the BJP's stance regarding the ongoing 'vote-theft' claims by the Opposition.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: PTI video clip of Rahul Gandhi, Rajiv Pratap Rudy from Parliament premises shared on social media with false claim; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 14 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing Congress leader and Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, shaking hands and conversing with BJP MP Rajiv Pratap Rudy in Parliament premises was shared on social media by several users. Those sharing the clip claimed that during their exchange, Gandhi allegedly asked Rudy if he was contesting the Constitution Club elections. Rudy allegedly replied, "Of course," after which Gandhi reportedly said, "Don't worry." However, a Press Trust of India (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigation found the claim to be completely false and baseless. In the original video, Gandhi and Rudy were simply exchanging pleasantries, with no mention of any elections. The viral version had background music added, which obscured the actual audio. The video was circulated on social media with a false claim. Notably, the "election" referred to in the social media posts was for a Secretary position at the Constitution Club of India, a social club for MPs and former MPs in Delhi. On August 12, 2025, Rajiv Pratap Rudy won the Secretary (Administration) post at the club, defeating fellow BJP leader Sanjeev Balyan by around 100 votes. Claim: An X user '@amitmishrainn' shared a video featuring Congress leader & LoP in Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, shaking hands and having a conversation with BJP MP Rajiv Pratap Rudy. The user sharing the clip claimed that during their discussion, Gandhi asked Rudy if he was contesting the internal club elections. When Rudy replied, "Of course," Gandhi responded with "Don't worry." "The election was won by ⁦@RajivPratapRudy⁩ on the very day when ⁦@RahulGandhi asked in Parliament, R u fighting club election? Rudy said, of course. Rahul then said, don't worry. This was revealed by a person present there before the results came out. As for the rest, @nishikant_dubey⁩ was there too," read the post's caption. The post garnered 151.6k views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. As part of the investigation, the Desk noticed PTI's watermark on the top right corner of the video. Based on this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find the original X post by the News Agency. The search led us to a post dated July 24, featuring the two leaders. In the 00:15-second video, though the audio is faintly audible, Rahul Gandhi can be heard asking about his flight, to which he replies, "...at 2 o'clock…". Nowhere in the video can it be heard that the two are discussing elections. Moreover, the video shared by the user on his social media platform consists of background music that overlaps the original conversation. "VIDEO | Parliament Monsoon Session: LoP Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi (@RahulGandhi) and BJP MP Rajiv Pratap Rudy (@RajivPratapRudy) were seen exchanging pleasantries inside Parliament complex," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Additionally, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find reports citing the claim mentioned in the social media post; however, the search did not lead us to any credible reports. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim made in the social media post is entirely false and baseless. In the original video, they were exchanging pleasantries and did not discuss elections.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2018 Unnao assault video resurfaces on social media with false claim of being recent; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 14 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it showed a recent incident from Uttar Pradesh's Unnao, in which a group of young men allegedly abducted and raped a woman. The footage showed the men forcefully dragging the woman into a forest as she pleaded for her release, and threatening to make the video go viral. However, a Press Trust of India Fact Check Desk investigation found the claim to be false. While the incident of molestation depicted in the video did occur in Uttar Pradesh's Unnao district, it took place in 2018, not recently. Reportedly, after the video went viral at the time, the Uttar Pradesh Police took action and filed a complaint against six people. An old incident from Uttar Pradesh has resurfaced on social media with a false claim that it happened recently. Claim An Instagram handle with the username Pushpendra Pal (@mahipat_pal_77) shared, on August 4, a visually distressing video showing a group of men harassing a woman. The user claimed the video depicted a recent incident from Uttar Pradesh's Unnao, in which the men dragged the woman into a forest and raped her while she pleaded for her release. "In Unnao, UP, four fearless criminals abducted this woman and raped her. When the woman screams and shouts, the criminals say that they will make the video viral. There are four criminals in total — one is making the video, and three are taking the woman towards the forest. Are women not safe in UP now? Honourable Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath Ji, you say that thieves, dacoits, mafia, urinate in their pants. Where did all these come from? Who will get justice for this woman now?" the user wrote in the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (Disclaimer: The video contains sensitive visuals) Investigation The Desk ran the video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search results via Google Lens also led the Desk to a video news report posted on The Quint's official YouTube channel. The same video, showing the group of men dragging a woman as she pleaded for her release, had been uploaded by the channel. However, the timeline mentioned in the report indicated that the incident was at least seven years old (reported in July 2018) and did not depict a recent event. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. A combination image comparing visuals from the viral social media video and the YouTube upload confirmed that they are the same. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find further details about the incident. The search led to a news report published by The Indian Express on July 7, 2018, which stated that the crime had occurred at least two months before the video originally went viral in 2018. The report noted that the victim had not filed a complaint initially, as she claimed she had been threatened by the accused. In the report, police stated: "The woman was with a neighbour, a man, when a group of youths came by and started misbehaving with them. While the neighbour fled after being assaulted, the woman was taken to the orchard. In the video, they dragged her to the thickets and raped her. After that, they allowed her to go, giving her Rs 50 to reach home." In the report, police also confirmed that a case had been registered against six people in the incident. Rahul (21) and Vimal (20) were arrested, while a third accused, Aakash (22), was already in jail in connection with a theft case. "Three others — Pawan, Ritik and Vipin — are absconding," they said. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Additionally, the customised keyword search also led the Desk to a video statement issued by the Uttar Pradesh Police on its official X handle, in which the timeline also confirmed that the video does not pertain to any recent incident but shows an old one. Here is the link to the video: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a woman being assaulted by a group of men in broad daylight in Uttar Pradesh's Unnao was not from a recent incident. It dates back to 2018, and most of the perpetrators were arrested at the time.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video showing a Filipina nurse caught stealing from US store falsely shared with claiming she was Indian; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 14 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it depicted an Indian Hindu nurse caught stealing from a store in the USA. The footage showed the security officials of the store allegedly intercepting the woman as she was about to leave the premises with stolen goods. In its investigation, however, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false. According to multiple news reports, the woman held in the store in the USA on charges of theft was not Indian but a Filipina nurse, also, the incident dated back to January 2025. An old and unrelated video showing a Filipina nurse stealing from a store in the USA was falsely shared with the claim that she was an Indian national. Claim An X handle with the username Sunny (@19Maradona_) shared, on August 12, a video claiming it depicted an Indian Hindu nurse caught stealing from a store in the USA. The footage showed the security staff allegedly intercepting the woman as she was about to leave the store with goods and merchandise she had not paid for. As the video continues, it later also shows the woman being strictly questioned by the security staff over the reported theft. "Indian Hindu nurse got caught stealing from a store in USA," the user captioned the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing the story, the video had garnered 2.6 lakh views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search result via Google Lens also led the Desk to a report published on a website named The Daily Netizen on August 10, 2025. The Desk found that the video seen in the viral post — showing a woman being intercepted by police officials on charges of shoplifting from a store — was the same as the one included in the news report. However, the details mentioned in the report stated that the woman depicted in the video was originally a Filipina nurse caught on camera allegedly shoplifting more than $300 worth of merchandise from a store in the United States. "Store staff, who had been monitoring her movements, were reportedly aware of exactly what she took and the total cost of the stolen goods. As she attempts to leave, staff and responding police officers intercept her at the store's exit," the report stated. "The woman later discloses her identity as Marie Sumaya, an immigrant from the Philippines," the report added. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image comparing visuals from the viral video with those from the video shared in the report, confirming they are the same. In the next part of the investigation, to thoroughly re-check the identity of the woman held in the video, allegedly on charges of shoplifting, the Desk carefully watched the extended version of the incident shared in the report. The Desk found that at the 3:15 timestamp, the woman identified herself as being from the Philippines, directly disproving the claim that she was Indian. Further, at the 3:23 timestamp, she also admitted she was a professional nurse and was ready to pay for all the items seized from her custody. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the woman depicted in the video is not Indian but a Filipina nurse. She was apprehended for theft at a store in the USA in January 2025.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Rajan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered Amul ad mocking Trump's tariff hike circulates on social media with false claim; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 14 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Rajan, PTI Fact Check ): After US President Donald Trump announced a 25 per cent additional tariff, after announcing 25% tariff initially, on Indian imports, citing New Delhi's purchase of Russian crude, a purported Amul advertisement, making a satirical comment about US President Donald Trump was shared by several social media users. Those sharing the advertisement claimed that it was in response to his decision to double tariffs on India's exports to 50%. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the advertisement in question is fake. While Amul did put up an ad of a cartoon on Trump's controversial tariff chart, the one being circulated on social media is computer-generated and not original. The post was shared with a false claim on social media. Claim: A purported Amul advertisement, making a satirical comment about US President Donald Trump, was shared by an X user, '@ravianantapuri', on August 11, claiming that the ad was in response to his decision to double tariffs on India's exports to 50%. "Amul highlights US tariff hike in an innovative way!" read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral post through Reverse Image Search and found that several other users had also shared the same screenshot with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here . As part of the investigation, the Desk scanned Amul's official Instagram account, which led us to a post dated April 4, 2025, featuring a cartoon on Trump's controversial tariff chart, a couple of days after the US president had announced so-called reciprocal tariffs on imports from about 90 nations. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk did not find the ad shared on social media on Amul's official Instagram. We then noticed the difference in font sizes and styles in the viral advertisement, indicating that it was digitally altered. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the picture through a fake Image Detector, which flagged the image as "computer-generated or modified". Below is a screenshot of the same. As part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports, but we could not find any credible reports citing the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the alleged billboard Amul ad was modified and was shared with a false claim on social media.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Viral posts claiming Johny Lever's death are false and baseless; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 14 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A collage of photographs featuring veteran comedian and actor Johny Lever with his family has been widely circulated on social media, accompanied by claims that he "passed away a while ago" and that his last rites would be held today. However, a Press Trust of India Fact Check Desk investigation found no truth to the claim. Johny Lever is alive, and there is no credible report or official confirmation of his death. Meanwhile, Johny Lever celebrates his 67th birthday today, on August 14, 2024. Johny Lever, a celebrated figure in Indian cinema, is renowned for his exceptional comic timing and unforgettable performances. With a career spanning over three decades, he has brought joy to audiences through iconic roles in film Claim: A Facebook user, 'Gaurav Rinshu Kumari' on August 14, shared a collage of pictures of Indian Actor Johny Lever along with his family, claiming that Johny Lever passed away a while ago. "Johny Lever passed away a while ago. Will his last rites be held today? Last journey of Johny Lever, Sir," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through Reverse Image Search and found that several other users had shared the same picture with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived version can be viewed here and here , respectively. To commence the investigation, the Desk first scanned the official X and Instagram handles of the actor, but we did not find any posts stating his health issues or demise. Moreover, the Instagram stories that Lever had shared showcased people congratulating him on his birthday on August 14, 2025. Here is the link to his X and Instagram accounts , and below is a screenshot of his stories. As part of the investigation, the Desk also skimmed through the official Instagram handle of the comedian and his daughter Jamie Lever's account to see whether she had posted about Johnny Lever's health or demise, but did not find any relevant posts or information. Here is the link to the official Instagram handle of Jamie Lever, and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk also conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports that cite his demise, but we did not find any relevant reports; given the gravity of the matter, this particular news would have been reported by leading media outlets. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim about Johny Lever's death is entirely baseless and misleading.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Assam clash video falsely shared as Bihar Sarpanch assault over votes; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 18 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A disturbing video showing a group of people brutally assaulting a man has been widely shared on social media. Those posting it claimed that the incident took place in Bihar, where residents allegedly thrashed a sarpanch for seeking votes in favour of a former AIMIM MLA. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found it to be false. The viral video is not from Bihar at all, but from Assam. It actually shows a violent clash between two groups during a gram panchayat meeting in the state. The footage has been misrepresented online and shared with a false claim to create a false political narrative. Claim: A video showing a group of people brutally assaulting a man was shared by an X '@wahab_abdhul' user on August 8, claiming that a sarpanch was thrashed by residents in Bihar for seeking votes for an ex-AIMIM MLA. "In Bihar, Sarpanch ji came to campaign for votes for a fugitive AIMIM MLA, and people thrashed him. The people clearly said – no alliance with AIMIM in the future, no votes," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post by the official handle of India Today NE (Northeast) dated August 4, 2025. The post featured a similar video to the one seen in the social media post; moreover, the available information indicates that the incident occurred in Assam. This clarifies that the incident is unrealted to Bihar. "A village-level meeting convened at the Jamuna #GaonPanchayat in #Doboka, #Assam turned #violent following a heated altercation between the relatives of an elected #panchayat representative and a group of local residents," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports that covered the incident. Our search led us to another report by India Today NE published on August 4, 2025. As per the report, a village-level meeting convened at the Jamuna Gaon Panchayat in Doboka, Assam turned violent following a heated altercation between the relatives of an elected panchayat representative and a group of local residents. The clash reportedly stemmed from disputes related to past allegations of corruption and administrative irregularities. Here is the link , and below is a screenshot of the same. Our searches also led us to a report by a media outlet 'North East Live', reporting that they were from the Jamunamukh Gram Panchayat office in Doboka, Hojai district, Assam. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video is from Jamuna (Jamunamukh) Gram Panchayat office in Doboka, Hojai district, Assam.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: This video in social media post falsely claims Indian tourist thrashed for assaulting minor in Turkey; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 18 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it depicted an incident from Istanbul, where a group of locals thrashed an Indian tourist for allegedly sexually harassing a 14-year-old Turkish girl. The video purportedly showed a group of men beating the same Indian tourist in what appears to be a mall. In its investigation, however, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found the man accused of harassing a minor Turkish girl was not Indian, and the claim is false. According to a local media report, the man being thrashed in the video was a Yemeni-origin US national who was accused of filming a woman in a shopping mall in Turkey back in May 2022. An old and unrelated video from Turkey was falsely shared on social media, linking the accused's identity to that of an Indian. Claim An X user named Rizwan Shah (@rizwan_media) shared on August 14 a video, purportedly from Istanbul, where a group of local citizens thrashed an Indian tourist accused of sexually harassing a 14-year-old Turkish girl. "Turks Deliver Street Justice in Istanbul. An Indian tourist accused of sexually harassing a 14-year-old Turkish girl was beaten by locals in Istanbul, as enraged citizens took matters into their own hands," the user shared the video with the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video had garnered 1.5k views) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search result via Google Lens also led the Desk to a report published by a Turkey-based news portal, 'Haber 3,' on May 10, 2022. The Desk found the keyframe used for investigation exactly matched that of the image included in the news report. However, the accompanying details suggested the incident depicted in the video occurred on May 10, 2022, in the Bakırköy district of Istanbul. A Yemeni-descent American citizen, AAM, was beaten by bystanders as he was allegedly spotted in a shopping mall in Istanbul, filming videos of women with his phone camera.
