"According to ODA TV, the refugee, who was stuck in the middle of the crowd that was growing by the second, was saved from being lynched by the intervention of shopping mall security," the report added. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image comparing visuals from the viral video with that from the image shared in the news report, confirming they are the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a man being beaten up by the public at a mall in Turkey was falsely identified as an Indian citizen. The man was originally identified as a Yemeni-descent American citizen, who was beaten by bystanders as he was allegedly spotted in a shopping mall in Istanbul, filming videos of women with his phone camera.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video from Italy falsely shared in name of Guptkashi floods; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 18 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): As Uttarakhand continues to reel from the catastrophic tragedy in Dharali village on August 5 — where massive flash floods triggered by heavy rains left a trail of destruction — a video, allegedly shot around the same time in Guptkashi, has recently been shared on social media. The clip appears to show a river flowing at a dangerously high level, close to several residential buildings. Users claimed the video depicted the scale of the ongoing disaster in the state, triggered by heavy rains. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it to be unrelated to the recent rain-induced disaster in Uttarakhand. The visuals are from July 2025 and show flood-like conditions in Bardonecchia, Italy, caused by heavy rains. Claim An Instagram user named vikashkumar4104 shared a video on August 5, purportedly showing a river flowing at an extremely dangerous level, close to several residential buildings. The user claimed the visuals were from Guptkashi in Uttarakhand's Rudraprayag district and depicted the scale of the ongoing disaster in the state triggered by heavy rains. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a video posted on the X handle of the Jordan-based news channel Roya News English on July 1, 2025. The Desk found that the visuals in the social media video were the same as those in the video shared by the news portal. However, the accompanying details revealed that the footage depicted an incident from Italy, not Uttarakhand. The news portal stated that the video showed powerful floods hitting the Italian town of Bardonecchia after heavy rainfall. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a comparison image showing visuals from the viral video alongside those from the video shared by the news portal, confirming they are identical. Additionally, the search led the Desk to a video posted on the official YouTube channel of the UK-based news outlet The Sun on July 1, 2025. This video also confirmed that the incident took place in Italy, not India. The video was shared with the description: "Dramatic footage captures the moment a devastating flash flood hits Bardonecchia, Italy. At least one person has been killed in the fierce floods caused by heavy rains, the authorities announced, as extreme weather events become more frequent. The 70-year-old man was hit by a torrent of water and mud after he got out of his van in the alpine town, authorities say." Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video in question is not from Guptkashi or any recent flood incident in Uttarakhand. Instead, it shows flash floods that struck Bardonecchia, Italy, in July 2025 after heavy rainfall.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Mohammed Siraj's 2024 T20 World Cup welcome picture falsely shared as recent Test series celebrations
content: New Delhi, August 18 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A photo showing Indian cricketer Mohammed Siraj holding the national flag while being surrounded by a cheering crowd has gone viral on social media. Users sharing the image claimed it captured his grand welcome after the recently concluded India vs England Test series. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the picture actually dates back to 2024, when Siraj had received a grand welcome in Hyderabad after India's victory at the 2024 T20 World Cup. The image is unrelated to the recently concluded India vs England test series. The post was shared with a false claim on social media. Claim: A picture featuring cricketer Mohammed Siraj carrying the national flag, surrounded by people surrounding his vehicle, was shared by a Facebook user 'Indian Cricket Badshah' on August 7, claiming that it shows him receiving a grand welcome after the India vs England test series. "Mohammad Siraj was given a warm welcome when he returned to his home in Hyderabad after the Test series against England was tied 2-2," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the picture through Reverse Image Search and found that several other users had shared the same post with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a post by Dainik Jagran, uploaded on their official Instagram account, featuring the same picture as seen in the recent post. The post dated July 6, 2024, highlighted that fast bowler Mohammad Siraj reached his hometown Hyderabad for the first time after winning the World Cup. The timeline and the details mentioned in the post clarify that the picture is not recent. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports, which led the Desk to a report by NDTV streamed on their official YouTube page on July 6, 2024. "India pacer Mohammed Siraj arrived in Hyderabad after being a part of the victory parade and felicitation ceremony in Mumbai. Siraj arrived at the Rajiv Gandhi International Airport on Friday, and fans turned up in numbers to shower their love and support." read the description. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the picture featuring cricketer Mohammed Siraj dated back to 2024 and is unrelated to the recently concluded India vs England test series.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old Coimbatore airport feud video falsely linked to cab driver harassment; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 18 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a visibly enraged woman engaged in an altercation with a man and another woman at a public place was recently shared on social media with the claim that it depicted an incident in Tamil Nadu. Users alleged that the clip showed scenes outside an airport where a cab driver was misbehaving with a woman passenger, dragging her to a car, and forcing her to take the ride. They further claimed the incident occurred in front of police, who allegedly sided with the "cab drivers" instead of helping the passenger. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found the claim to be false. Multiple news reports confirmed that the video shows a personal feud at Coimbatore airport. In reality, the woman had accused a man—who was arriving with his newlywed wife—of cheating on her. The video has no connection to cab drivers or passengers being forced to take rides. Claim An X user with the handle @bradybr2001 shared the video on August 16, claiming it showed a cab driver outside an airport in Tamil Nadu misbehaving with a woman passenger and dragging her into a car to take the ride forcefully. The user alleged that the horrific incident unfolded in front of state police officials, who instead of protecting the woman, sided with "cab mafias." The post read: "This is Tamil Nadu ruled by Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam. Look at how cab mafias are misbehaving with women passengers and physically dragging them into their cars, that too right in the presence of policemen. Instead of discharging his duties, the policeman acts as an agent at the airport. This is a Periyar Model." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search result via Google Lens also led the Desk to a video shared by the official X handle of the Indian Express's Tamil edition. The Desk found the video shared by the news portal on March 27, 2025, was the same as the one seen in the social media post; however, the accompanying details revealed that it showed a personal feud, where a woman confronted her alleged lover and his newlywed wife at Coimbatore airport. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image comparing visuals from the social media video with those from the video shared by the news portal, confirming they are the same. Additionally, based on these findings, in the next part of the investigation, the Desk also conducted a customised keyword search on Google to gather more details related to the incident. The search led the Desk to multiple reports, including those by The Indian Express and Asianet News Tamil on March 27, 2025. These reports confirmed that the incident was a personal dispute involving a woman confronting a man, whom she accused of cheating, at the airport. Reportedly, the man had arrived at Coimbatore airport with his newlywed wife when the altercation broke out. The reports also mentioned that a relative of the man, present at the spot, attempted to pacify the situation by holding the woman's hand. However, she slapped him and continued arguing. Links to the report by the Indian Express and Asianet News Tamil covering the incident can be found here and here . Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video in question does not show cab drivers in Tamil Nadu harassing passengers or police siding with them. Instead, it depicts a personal feud at Coimbatore airport, where a woman confronted a man and his newlywed wife, accusing him of cheating.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old 2022 Nitish Kumar video questioning BJP, RSS falsely shared as recent
content: New Delhi, August 18 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar angrily questioning the BJP and the RSS over their role in the freedom struggle is being circulated on social media with the false claim that it is recent. Users sharing the clip cited tensions despite his party's current alliance with the BJP-led NDA. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found the claim to be false. The video is not recent but from 2022, when Kumar's JD(U) had exited the NDA and formed a new government in Bihar under the Mahagathbandhan banner. An old video is being shared with a misleading context. Claim: A purported video featuring Bihar CM Nitish Kumar addressing a session was shared by a X user named '@bole_bharat' on August 16, claiming that he questioned the BJP and the RSS over their contributions to the Indian freedom struggle. Moreover, Kumar's party is currently allied with the BJP-led NDA. In the 00:27-second clip, he says, "How are they linked to Independence? In the 75th year (of Independence), they were saying 'will do this, and will do that.' Where were you during the Independence struggle? Who fought the battle for Independence?…" Moreover, the text on the video, originally in Hindi, read: "Why Nitish Kumar flare up at RSS and PM Modi?" The post clocked 25.9k views on social media. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. To commence the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports, but the search did not lead us to any report that cited the information mentioned in the social media post. Next, the Desk ran the extracted keyframes through Reverse Image Search and came across a report streamed on Live Hindustan's official YouTube page on August 24, 2024. Accusing the BJP-led centre of being solely focused on "publicity," Kumar can be heard speaking around 19 minutes, "…Now they (centre) are giving different names. How are they linked to Independence? In the 75th year (of Independence), they were saying 'will do this, and will do that.' Where were you during the Independence struggle? Who fought the battle for Independence? …" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. The same video was also streamed on the official YouTube channel of Bihar Vidhan Sabha TV on August 24, 2022. From the 2:47:01 timestamp in the recording of the Bihar Assembly proceedings, the excerpts from the viral video can be found. Here is the link , and below is a screenshot of the same. Notably, Nitish Kumar's JD(U) quit the NDA in 2022 and formed a new government in Bihar under the Mahagathbandhan alliance. The coalition secured a trust vote on August 24, 2022, with 160 votes in its favour, as BJP members staged a walkout. In 2024, ahead of the Lok Sabha elections, the Bihar CM returned to the BJP-led NDA. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of Nitish Kumar flaring up at RSS and PM Modi is not recent and dates back to 2022, during which Kumar's JDU had walked out of the NDA to form the new government in Bihar under the Mahagathbandhan banner. An old video was shared as recent.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Punjab neighbour attack video falsely shared as communal clash incident in West Bengal
content: New Delhi, August 18 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media claimed to depict an incident in West Bengal, where a Muslim man allegedly attacked a Hindu man with a sword-like object. The footage shows the victim riding a two-wheeler when a man armed with a sword (identified by users as Muslim) assaults him. As the video continues, several bystanders rush to the victim's aid. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found the claim to be false. The incident did not occur in West Bengal but in Samrala, Punjab. Reports confirmed that the visuals show Surinder Singh attacking his neighbour, Kultar Singh, with a kirpan. The video was misleadingly shared with a communal narrative. Claim A Facebook user named Chandan Shandilya shared a video on August 13, purportedly from West Bengal, showing a Muslim man attacking a Hindu man with a sword. The video, which appears to be CCTV footage of the incident, showed a man with a sword (claimed to be Muslim) attacking another man on a bike, identified as Hindu. The video was shared with the caption: "Hindus, watch this video, it shows the condition of Hindus in West Bengal, how our Hindus are living there. Where Hindus decrease and Muslims increase, Hindus will be killed in the same way. Wake up Hindus, don't let your numbers decrease." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video garnered 41k views) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. Further, a Google Lens search led the Desk to a news report published by the Punjabi edition of News18 on August 12, 2025. The keyframe extracted for the investigation exactly matched an image included in the report. However, the accompanying details confirmed that the video depicted an incident from Punjab's Samrala and not West Bengal. According to the report, the incident involved a brutal attack on a lawyer named Kultar Singh and his family by his neighbour, Billu, in Punjab's Samrala. Nowhere did the report identify the accused as Muslim. The report mentioned: "The victim, Kultar Singh, said that he practices in Khamano. As soon as he left home on a motorcycle in the morning, his neighbour Billu attacked him with a kirpan. To escape the attack, Kultar Singh tried to flee by throwing down his motorcycle, but the accused threw him to the ground and began attacking him with a kirpan." Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image comparing visuals from the viral video with those from the image shared in the news report, confirming they are the same. In the next stage of investigation, to reconfirm the identity of the accused, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search on Google, based on the above findings. This search led to a report by Hindustan Times published on August 13, 2025, which confirmed that both the victim and the accused belong to the same religion. The report identified the accused as Surinder Singh alias Billu and the victim as Kultar Singh. The report added: "Kultar Singh alleged that the accused has been a drug addict, creating a nuisance and hurling abuses outside their house for the past few days. ASI Davinder Singh, who is investigating the case, said that an FIR under Sections 118(1) (voluntarily causing hurt by dangerous weapons or means), 127(1) (wrongful confinement), and 109 (attempt to murder) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita has been registered and the accused arrested." Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a video showing a man attacking his neighbour in Punjab's Samrala was falsely shared with a communal narrative, linking it to an incident from West Bengal. The investigation found that both the victim and the accused belong to the same religion and that the incident pertained to Punjab.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Scripted video of woman jumping into canal with child falsely shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 20 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it depicted a real-life incident where a woman jumped into a canal or river with a child after fighting with her husband. The video showed the duo engaged in a heated altercation when suddenly the woman leapt into the water, holding the child in her arms, allegedly in a fit of rage. In its investigation, however, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the video was staged and scripted. The clip had no connection to any real-life incident and was misleadingly shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An X user, Divya Kumaari (@divyakumaari), on August 16 shared a video claiming it depicted a real-life incident where a woman jumped into a canal or river with a child after fighting with her husband. The video showed the duo visibly engaged in a heated altercation before the woman jumped into the water with the child in her arms, allegedly in a fit of rage. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered 989k views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a video uploaded on a YouTube channel named Prabhat Kumar, which has over 228k subscribers. The Desk found that the channel user, who identifies himself as a "Digital Content Creator," shared the same video of a man and woman fighting—where the latter jumps into a canal or river with a child, as seen in the viral clip—on August 14. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting that the content in the viral video matches that of the video posted by the YouTube channel. In the next part of the investigation, to analyse the credibility of the video and determine where it was originally shot, the Desk conducted a detailed review of Prabhat Kumar's YouTube channel. It was found that the user is known for uploading scripted content. The Desk also found that the individuals featured in the viral video had appeared in several other scripted videos posted by Kumar. Links to two such videos can be found here and here : Further, the Desk reviewed Kumar's YouTube channel bio, which clearly stated that the user creates scripted videos made solely for entertainment purposes. Below is a screenshot of the user's profile. In the final part of the investigation, the Desk contacted Prabhat Kumar for a statement regarding the viral claim. The story will be updated as and when a response is received. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video claiming to show a woman jumping into a canal or river with a child after fighting with her husband was scripted and had no connection to any real-life event.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of IAF Chief consoling family of Sgt Surendra Kumar shared with false claim linked to Pilot Shivangi Singh
content: New Delhi, August 20 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of Indian Air Force (IAF) Chief, Air Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singh, standing beside a grieving woman as she interacted with another woman, was recently shared on social media with a false claim. Users alleged that it showed the IAF Chief meeting the mother of IAF pilot Shivangi Singh, who they claimed went missing during India's recently concluded Operation Sindoor, launched to avenge the killing of Indian civilians by Pakistan-linked terrorists. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false. The video actually shows Air Chief Marshal A P Singh, accompanied by his wife Sarita Singh, visiting the family of late Sgt Surendra Kumar, who laid down his life in the line of duty during Operation Sindoor in Rajasthan's Jhunjhunu. At his home, they met his mother Nanu Devi, wife Seema, and children Vritika and Daksh. Moreover, the claim about Squadron Leader Shivangi Singh going missing is also false. She is presently a serving member of the IAF and continues to remain deployed operationally. Claim A Pakistan-based X handle, operating under the username Azhar Naseem Khan (@p_naseemkhan), shared on August 18 a video showing India Air Force (IAF) Chief Air Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singh visiting the home of allegedly missing IAF pilot Shivangi Singh. The post purportedly claimed that the IAF Chief, along with his wife, met Shivangi Singh's mother, who was seen crying due to the absence of any news about her daughter. "Indian Air Force Chief visits the home of missing Indian pilot Shivangi Singh during the war. Trying to console Shivangi Singh's mother, who is in a terrible state from crying, as there is no news about where Shivangi Singh is. Note: We absolutely do not have Shivangi Singh," the user shared the video with the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here respectively. The search via Google Lens also led the Desk to a video posted on a YouTube channel named Bharat Raftar News on August 14, 2025. The Desk found that the video posted by the channel exactly matched the video shared in the social media post. However, the details mentioned along with it revealed that it depicted the Air Force Chief's visit to Sgt Surendra Kumar's house, who laid down his life in the line of duty during Operation Sindoor, and not at IAF pilot Shivangi Singh's home. Here is the link and archive link to the video, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting that the content in the viral video matches that of the video posted by the YouTube channel. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find details related to the Air Force Chief's visit. The search result led the Desk to a post shared by the Indian Air Force on its official X handle, wherein it was identifiable that the woman seen wailing in the video was the same as the woman captured in a photo shared by the IAF. The IAF had mentioned that the woman was the mother of late Sgt Surendra Kumar, who laid down his life in the line of duty during Operation Sindoor. "Air Chief Marshal AP Singh, along with Mrs Sarita Singh, paid a visit to village Mehradasi in Jhunjhunu district, Rajasthan, the hometown of late Sgt Surendra Kumar, who laid down his life in the line of duty during Operation Sindoor. At his home, they met his mother, Mrs Nanu Devi, wife, Mrs Seema, and children, Vritika and Daksh. It is worthwhile to mention that Jhunjhunu has a proud legacy of service to the nation, with 21,700 Ex-Servicemen hailing from the district and 3,552 serving Air Warriors in the Indian Air Force," the post mentioned. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Additionally, as part of the investigation to find details related to Air Force pilot Shivangi Singh and whether she had gone missing, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search on Google. However, the search result yielded no credible news reports that could corroborate the claim. Had the incident been real, the media would have covered it extensively. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the social media video was misrepresented. It depicted the IAF Chief and his wife visiting the family of late Sgt Surendra Kumar in Jhunjhunu, Rajasthan, and not the home of pilot Shivangi Singh, who is also not missing as claimed in the post.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Viral Vietnam dog theft video falsely linked to Supreme Court's order on stray dogs in Delhi-NCR
content: New Delhi, August 20 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid outrage over the Supreme Court's August 11 order directing the Delhi government, the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD), and other NCR authorities to relocate stray dogs to shelters and pounds within eight weeks of the directive, a disturbing video showing dead dogs being pulled out of black plastic bags has gone viral on social media. The video shows a man removing dog carcasses from bags while another person places them on the ground. Social media users claimed the incident took place in Delhi following the apex court's order. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found the video to be unrelated to Delhi or any part of India. The clip is from Vietnam's Ca Mau province, where two men were arrested on suspicion of stealing dogs. Authorities recovered the bodies of 12 dead dogs from their possession. Thus, a video from Vietnam has been falsely shared in connection with the Supreme Court's directive on stray dogs in Delhi-NCR. Claim In the aftermath of the Supreme Court's directive on stray dogs in Delhi and the NCR region, a video showing a man removing dog carcasses from multiple black plastic bags was recently shared on social media by an Instagram user named 'hii_soni_d91' on August 15. While sharing the video, the user claimed the incident had taken place in Delhi, merely days after the Supreme Court's order directing the relocation of stray dogs to shelter homes. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video garnered 1,743 likes) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a video shared by a Facebook user named Thiên Kim on August 5, 2025. The Desk found that the video shared by this user was identical to the one circulating in viral social media posts. However, the accompanying details indicated that the video originated from Vietnam, not India. The video was shared with a caption (translated from Vietnamese to English) that reads: "Professional group of dog thieves in Gia Rai Ward, Ca Mau." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image comparing visuals from the viral video with those from the video shared by the Facebook user, confirming they are the same. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the findings above, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find details related to the incident reported in Vietnam. The search led the Desk to a Vietnamese news portal, the Voice of Vietnam, on August 5. The Desk verified that the image included in the news report matched the keyframe used during the investigation. The report revealed that the incident occurred in Ca Mau province, Vietnam, where police arrested a group of dog thieves. Authorities also seized 12 dead dogs along with other materials from their possession, the report added. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing multiple dead dogs being taken out of plastic bags does not originate from India, but from Vietnam.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of Bangladeshi man torturing his wife falsely shared as incident from Karnataka
content: New Delhi, August 20 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it showed a horrifying incident from Karnataka, where a 65-year-old Muslim man brutally beat his 62-year-old ailing wife and tried to bury her alive. The video shows the man forcefully dragging his wife out of their house to a pit he had dug. He then attempts to place her inside and cover her with soil. The woman can be heard crying out for help before being struck again by her husband. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found the video to be unrelated to India. It actually shows an incident that occurred in Bangladesh on August 8, 2025. The man, identified as Khalilur Rahman, was seen trying to bury his sick wife, Khosheda Begum, alive at their home. Reports said the situation was brought under control with the help of local residents before the police arrived. Thus, an unrelated video from Bangladesh was falsely circulated on social media as an incident from Karnataka." Claim A Facebook user named Brijendra Mishra shared on August 13 a disturbing video, claiming it was from Karnataka, where a 65-year-old Muslim man brutally beat his 62-year-old ailing wife and tried to bury her alive. Sharing the video, the user wrote: "This incident is from Congress-ruled Karnataka. A 65-year-old mullah married his 42-year-old middle-aged sister. Then he tried to bury his 62-year-old first wife, who was an old, sick woman, by beating her alive. The woman was crying and screaming, but everyone was busy making videos. No one went to save her." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (Disclaimer: The video contains sensitive visuals) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens revealed several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here . The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a news report published by Prothom Alo, a Bengali-language daily newspaper in Bangladesh. The Desk found that an image in the news report (showing an elderly man striking a woman) matched a keyframe from the viral video. The details in the report confirmed the incident took place in Sreebardi Upazila, Sherpur District, Bangladesh—not India. The report stated that on August 8, Md. Khalilur Rahman (80) tried to bury his paralysed, bedridden wife, Khosheda Begum (70), alive after becoming frustrated with her illness. "In the video, Khalilur Rahman can be seen dragging his wife out of the house and into the yard. He dug a small hole with a spade on one side of the yard. He then laid his wife in the hole and tried to bury her with soil. The video was posted by the accused's grandson, which quickly went viral," the report noted. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image comparing visuals from the viral video with those in the news report, confirming they are the same. Additionally, the search results via Google Lens also led the Desk to multiple other news reports by Bangladesh-based news portals covering the same incident. These reports mentioned that the incident occurred in Bangladesh, where a man identified as Khalilur Rahman tried to 'bury his paralysed wife alive' out of growing frustration over her ill health. "Khalilur is not known as a bad man. He is usually cheerful, but his wife's illness made him gloomy. I don't understand why he did this," one of Rahman's neighbours was quoted as saying. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing an old man torturing his wife in Bangladesh was falsely shared as an incident from India.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video showing bullock cart race from Maharashtra falsely linked to Rahul Gandhi's Voter Adhikar Yatra in Bihar; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 22 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it depicted visuals from Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi's recently launched 'Voter Adhikar Yatra' in Bihar, where thousands of people had thronged the streets to witness it. The video showed a massive crowd gathered in an open space, allegedly recording visuals of the yatra. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found that the video is unrelated to Rahul Gandhi's programme. It actually shows people attending the annual bullock cart race held at Pedgaon's Hind Kesari ground in Maharashtra in June 2025, months before the Vote Adhikari Yatra began. An unrelated video from Maharashtra was thus falsely shared on social media linking it to Rahul Gandhi's Bihar yatra. Claim An X user, Ravinder Kapur (@RavinderKapur2), shared on August 19 a purported video from Rahul Gandhi's 'Voter Adhikar Yatra' in Bihar, claiming thousands had gathered on the streets to witness it. The caption read: "A Tsunami of people have gathered in Bihar for the rally of INDIA alliance leader and LoP Rahul Gandhi. You couldn't find an inch of empty space at the venue of the rally." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered 128.7k views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens revealed several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here . The search also led the Desk to a video posted on an Instagram handle named 'maharashtra_king_mathur___ 1001'. The Desk found that this video matched the one circulating in viral posts. However, the accompanying details showed it was shot at Hind Kesari Ground in Pedgaon, Satara, Maharashtra, back in June 2025 — weeks before Rahul Gandhi's yatra began on August 17, 2025. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image comparing visuals from the viral video with those with the video shared in the Instagram post, confirming they are the same. In the next stage of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find more details about the event at Hind Kesari Ground. This led to another video shared by an Instagram handle named 'love_bailgada_sharyat' on August 18, 2025. The video exactly matched the viral clip, and the details confirmed it showed the bullock cart race at Pedgaon, where thousands had gathered to watch the event. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Additionally, to confirm the origin of the video — that it was shot during a bullock cart race at Hind Kesari Ground in Pedgaon, Satara, Maharashtra — the Desk geolocated the place. The search led the Desk to a photo uploaded in June 2025 on Google Street View imagery of Hind Kesari Maidan, which matched the background settings seen in the viral video. Here is the link to the same image: Below is a combination image comparing visuals from the viral video with the photo uploaded in June 2025 to Google Street View imagery of Hind Kesari Maidan. In the subsequent part of the investigation, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search on Google regarding the bullock cart race held at Pedgaon's Hind Kesari Ground. The search led to multiple videos of the race available on YouTube. Two such examples can be found here and here : Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing thousands of people gathered was not related to Rahul Gandhi's 'Voter Adhikar Yatra' in Bihar.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Image of RSS workers engaged in relief operation in Uttarakhand shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, August 23 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): An image purportedly showing members of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) carrying supplies on their shoulders was recently shared on social media with the claim that they were stealing belongings from abandoned houses in Uttarakhand after the recent cloudburst incident. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated and found the claim to be false. The image actually shows 70-year-old Gulab Singh Negi leading a group of RSS Swayamsevaks in delivering food, rations, and shelter to families affected by the Uttarkashi cloudburst tragedy. Thus, an image of RSS workers engaged in a relief operation in Uttarakhand was falsely shared with a misleading claim. Claim An X user, Nidhi Singh Rathore (@NehaSinghratho), shared on August 19 an image allegedly depicting RSS members stealing belongings from abandoned houses in Uttarakhand following the recent cloudburst. "In Uttarakhand, recent cloudbursts caused massive destruction. People fled their homes to save their lives, leaving them behind. RSS members were seen stealing belongings from those abandoned homes," the user wrote while sharing the image. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing the story, the image had garnered 1.8k views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and found multiple accounts which shared the same image with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search also led the Desk to an Instagram account, jammukashmirnow, which had posted the same image of RSS workers as that seen in the social media post on August 11. The caption clarified that it showed RSS volunteers engaged in relief work in disaster-hit Uttarkashi, not stealing belongings from abandoned homes. The Instagram post elaborated that the image depicted RSS volunteers providing relief in Uttarkashi. It also highlighted the dedication of 70-year-old RSS worker Gulab Singh Negi, who is also tirelessly working on the ground despite the hardship. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. A comparison confirmed that the image shared on social media was the same as that in the Instagram post. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from these findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google for more details on RSS relief efforts in Uttarakhand. This search led to a report published by Organiser on August 11, 2025, which included the same image. The report stated that it showed 70-year-old Gulab Singh Negi leading a group of RSS Swayamsevaks in delivering food, rations, and shelter to families devastated by the Uttarkashi cloudburst. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Additionally, the customised keyword search led the Desk to an X post by Assam Cabinet Minister Ashok Singhal on August 11. He too confirmed that the image showed RSS volunteers led by 70-year-old Sanghchalak Gulab Singh Negi delivering aid to people in flood-hit Uttarkashi. "In flood-hit Uttarkashi, 70-year-old RSS Sanghchalak Gulab Singh Negi Ji wades through devastation, leading an army of swayamsevaks bringing food, aid, and hope to victims. This is RSS; always ready to answer the Nation's call, always ready for duty," the Assam Minister shared the post, along with a caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the image showing RSS members carrying supplies on their shoulders was falsely shared with the claim that they were stealing belongings from abandoned houses in Uttarakhand after the recent cloudburst. In reality, the image depicted 70-year-old Gulab Singh Negi leading RSS volunteers in delivering aid to affected families in disaster-hit Uttarkashi.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Clipped video of Suvendu Adhikari falsely shared claiming he criticised BJP in his speech
content: New Delhi, August 23 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video purportedly showing senior West Bengal BJP leader and Nandigram MLA Suvendu Adhikari making a controversial statement against his own party at a recent public meeting has gone viral on social media. The clip appeared to show Adhikari criticising the BJP, suggesting the party might face extinction if it did not change its course. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated and found that his remarks were taken out of context. In reality, Adhikari was criticising the ruling All India Trinamool Congress (AITC) while defending the BJP's stance against illegal infiltration in the state. A clipped portion of his statement was selectively circulated on social media to mislead viewers. Claim An X user, Nilanjan Das (@NilanjanDasAITC), shared on August 17 a purported video of West Bengal's senior BJP leader Suvendu Adhikari criticising his own party. The footage allegedly showed the Nandigram MLA stating that if the party did not change its course, it might soon face extinction. "West Bengal Leader of Opposition warns that @BJP4Bengal will face extinction if it doesn't change course — 'BJP is pushing everyone back by branding them Bangladeshi.' Very uncharacteristic of Suvendu Adhikari. Why this sudden change of heart?" the user shared the video with caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered 97,000 views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens led to several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here : The Google Lens search also led the Desk to the extended version of Suvendu Adhikari's address (from which the viral clip was taken), which was live-streamed on his official Facebook page on August 17, 2025. The details mentioned that the video was shot during his address at Kolkata's Taratala, where BJP workers held a protest against "language terrorism" and "violent political culture" in the state. Here is the link to the original video, along with a screenshot: A comparison of screenshots confirmed that the people standing alongside Suvendu Adhikari in the viral video were the same as those seen in the live-streamed video on his official page. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk verified whether Suvendu Adhikari had indeed criticised the BJP in that public address. At the 13:48 mark of the original video, the exact statement heard in the viral clip was found. However, upon careful review, it became clear that his remarks were directed against the AITC, while defending the BJP's position on "illegal infiltrators." At no point in the complete video did Adhikari criticise the BJP. The investigation revealed that the senior BJP leader was targeting the Mamata Banerjee-led AITC leaders over alleged corruption cases and women's safety issues in the state during his address. He later also raised the issue of illegal infiltration, defending the BJP's stance and criticising the AITC. It was in this context that Adhikari made the statement heard in the viral video. However, the version circulated online was not the complete statement but a clipped portion shared to mislead viewers. The original statement made by Adhikari during the address was as follows: "What did they (AITC) say here? They said, We will remove the BJP entirely. BJP will not remain here. Leave this attitude, this BJP attitude. Come to the streets, what is the BJP doing? BJP is driving everyone out, calling everyone Bangladeshi. Oh no, listen clearly. On August 15, Independence Day, our Prime Minister said from the Red Fort that no country in the world has infiltrators, and our country will not have infiltrators. What are you scared of?" He further added: "Let me state this very clearly — Indians, whether Hindu, Muslim, Sikh, Christian, or Buddhist, are not included in this. During the Summary Intensive Revision of the voter list, Indians do not have to worry about anything. Not only Indians, but even the Hindus who came from Bangladesh to West Bengal to protect their religious identity will not be considered as infiltrators. They are our friends, our relatives, and refugees who deserve protection." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video claiming to show West Bengal BJP leader Suvendu Adhikari criticising his own party was clipped and shared out of context. In the original version of the video, it was clear that his criticism was directed at the AITC. However, only a clipped portion was posted to mislead viewers.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated image falsely showed AAP leader Gopal Italia pictured with the Delhi CM assault case accused; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 23 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Days after 41-year-old Rajkot resident Sakriya Rajeshbhai Khimjibhai was arrested in connection with the attack on Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta during a Jan Sunwai programme at her camp office in Civil Lines on August 20, a purported image of him standing alongside Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leader Gopal Italia surfaced online. Social media users claimed that the accused was known to the AAP leader and alleged that the latter's party had links to the attack on the Delhi CM. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found that the viral image was digitally manipulated and falsely shared to mislead viewers. The original picture showed Italia standing alongside another individual, whose image was digitally replaced with that of the accused in the Delhi CM assault case. Claim On August 20, senior Delhi BJP leader Harish Khurana shared an image purportedly showing Sakriya Rajeshbhai Khimjibhai — the accused in the Delhi CM assault case — standing with AAP leader Gopal Italia. Khurana alleged that the accused was known to the AAP leader and that the attack on the Delhi CM was linked to the party. He wrote: "What was suspected has happened. This photo of Arvind Kejriwal's close associate Gopal Italia says a lot. That is, it is clearly visible that the attack on Rekha Gupta ji today is connected to the Aam Aadmi Party. Kejriwal ji should tell the truth of this photo? Kejriwal ji please explain Yeh Rishta Kya Kehlata Hai." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the post garnered 362k views) Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and found multiple accounts sharing the same image with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with archived versions available here and here . To verify the authenticity of the image, the Desk checked the social media accounts of AAP leader Gopal Italia. The search led to his official X handle, where the AAP leader had clarified that the image was digitally manipulated. In a post, Italia shared a link to a video on his Facebook account, stating that the doctored image had been taken from the same video. In the original footage, he was seen with another individual whose part was later digitally replaced with that of the accused in the viral photo. In his X post, Italia wrote: "Harish Khurana ji, you yourself don't have more respect than a troll, but before indulging in such cheap antics, didn't you think about the honour of your father, Madanlal ji? Seeing your deeds, which are even lower than those of a small-time BJP worker paid two rupees per tweet, would the late Madanlal Khurana ji be very pleased? What would he think, seeing his son become a petty troll? After becoming an MLA, it's unfortunate for me to have to explain things to cheap trolls like you, but still, take a look at this." He further added:"You took some screenshots from this old video of mine, edited them, and posted fake photos. Being the son of a CM, didn't you feel even a bit of shame doing such disgusting things? My appeal to all media is not to run news based on this petty troll Harish ji's tweet without verifying it. I will be forced to take legal action. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. A combination image confirms that the original video showed Italia with another individual, who was digitally replaced with the accused arrested in the Delhi CM assault case. To strengthen verification, the Desk also ran the viral image through Hive Moderation, an AI detection tool, which flagged substantial AI-generated elements in the image. Below is a screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the image showing AAP leader Gopal Italia with the accused arrested in connection with the Delhi CM assault case was digitally manipulated and shared on social media to mislead viewers.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Viral ICC rankings screenshot claiming Kohli, Rohit's retirement shared with false claim; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 25 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported screenshot of the ICC ODI rankings was shared by several social media users, which did not feature cricketers Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma. Those sharing the post claim that this hinted at the duo's retirement from the format. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the claim that Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli were removed from ODI rankings, indicating their retirements, was found to be false. A technical glitch had caused the brief disappearance of the two from the list on the ICC website. The two have not yet announced their retirement from the format. Notably, just weeks ago, Rohit was ranked No.2 and Kohli No.4 in the world. No formal retirement or inactivity clause applies to either player. Claim: An X user, @Ajayahire_cric, on August 20, shared a purported screenshot of the ICC ODI rankings, which does not feature Virat Kohli & Rohit Sharma, claiming that this could hint at the duo's retirement from the format. "No Rohit Sharma & Virat Kohli in the Updated ICC ODI Rankings. Looks like Retirement announcement is on the cards," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation: The Desk ran the viral screenshot through Reverse Image Search and found that several other users had shared the same post with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. As part of the investigation, the Desk first scanned the official ICC website and then looked up the ICC ODI batting rankings, where we found Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli ranked at number two and four, respectively. Here is the link to the website, and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports citing Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli's retirement. We found a report by The Times of India published on August 21, which mentioned that the two cricketers were briefly removed from the ICC ODI batting rankings on Wednesday due to a technical glitch, despite both continuing to be active in the format. "The ICC's swift clarification and fix helped settle the confusion around the temporary omission of two of India's biggest names from the ODI batting rankings," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. In another report by Hindustan Times published on August 21, an ICC spokesperson clarified that there was an error in our rankings tables, but it has been rectified. "Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli Retiring From ODIs Too? Here's The Truth Behind Viral 'ICC Rankings' Excluding The Duo," read the report's headline. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim that Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli have been removed from ODI rankings, indicating their retirements, was found to be misleading. A technical glitch had caused the brief disappearance of the two from the list on the ICC website. The two have not yet announced their retirement from the format.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Viral video of metro bridge collapse in Mumbai is AI-Generated and shared with false claim; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 25 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a metro bridge collapsing, with a train crashing onto the road, was shared on social media with the claim that the incident took place in Mumbai, Maharashtra recently. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video depicting the metro bridge collapse was digitally manipulated, powered by AI tools, and was shared with a false claim on social media. Claim: A video depicting a metro bridge collapsing, with the metro falling, was shared by an Instagram user 'noori_khan_7867' on August 18, claiming that the incident occurred in Mumbai, Maharashtra. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. As part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find relevant media reports that cite the incident. However, the Desk did not find any report, and given the seriousness of the issue, if such an incident had occurred, it would have been reported by several media outlets. Next, the Desk carefully scanned the post and found that several users in the comment section mentioned that the video is AI-generated. Below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk ran the video through HiveModeration, an AI-detection tool, which indicated that the video had a high level of AI involvement. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of a metro bridge collapse shared on social media is manipulated and AI-generated and was shared with a false claim.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Image showing cash worth crores seized from Congress MLA falsely linked to BJP MP; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 25 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): An image showing a large pile of cash on a table, with several individuals standing nearby, was recently shared on social media. Users claimed the image depicted money seized from a Member of Parliament belonging to the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) during a raid conducted by the Enforcement Directorate (ED). However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk, in its investigation, found that the image was unrelated to any raid involving a BJP MP. The photo actually showed cash recovered from a property linked to Karnataka Congress MLA K C Virendra. Thus, an unrelated image of recovery from a Congress MLA was falsely shared on social media, linking it to a BJP MP. Claim On August 23, an X user, Ravinder Kapur, shared an image purportedly showing a huge pile of cash stashed on a table. The user claimed it was allegedly recovered from the BJP MP. "Enormous cash recovered from one BJP MP. What will happen to the BJP MP? Your guess is as good as mine," the user wrote while sharing the image. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing this story, the post had garnered 49k views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and found multiple accounts which shared the same image with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search via Google Lens also led the Desk to a news report published by the English edition of Dainik Bhaskar on August 23, 2025. The report included the same image (a pile of cash on a table) as seen in the viral social media posts. However, details in the report confirmed the money was recovered from the property of Karnataka Congress MLA K.C. Virendra and not from any BJP MP. The report stated, "Karnataka Congress MLA KC Virendra was arrested by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) on Saturday. The arrest is in connection with a money laundering case. On Friday, the ED conducted raids at Virendra's properties. During the raids, the agency recovered Rs 12 crore in cash, jewellery worth Rs 6 crore, and foreign currency worth Rs 1 crore. Four vehicles were also seized." Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. A comparison confirmed that the image shared on social media was the same as that carried in the news report. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find further details related to the development. The search led to a post by the official X handle of the Enforcement Directorate, sharing details of the raid at the properties of Karnataka Congress MLA K.C. Virendra. The post also included the exact image of the seized cash, confirming that it amounted to about ₹12 crore (approx). The report stated, "ED Bengaluru has conducted search operations on 22-08-2025 and 23.08.2025 at 31 locations across India including Gangtok, Chitradurga District, Bangalore City, Hubli, Jodhpur, Mumbai and Goa (including five casinos viz. Puppy's Casino Gold, Ocean Rivers Casino, Puppy's Casino Pride, Ocean 7 Casino, Big Daddy Casino) in the case against Sh. K C Veerendra, MLA, Chitradurga District, and others, in the matter of illegal online and offline betting. During the search operations, various incriminating documents, a cash amount of Rs. 12 Crore (approx.), including (approx.) 1 Crore in foreign currency, Gold Jewellery worth Rs. 6 Crore (approx.), Silver articles around 10 kgs, properties related documents, along with four vehicles were seized. Further, 17 bank accounts and two bank lockers were also frozen." "K C Veerendra was arrested from Gangtok on 23.08.2025 and produced before Judicial Magistrate, Gangtok, Sikkim and transit remand was obtained for producing him before the jurisdictional Court in Bangalore," it added. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral social media image actually depicted cash seized from the properties linked to Karnataka Congress MLA K.C. Virendra and not any BJP MP.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2025 video showing Puri's Jagannath Yatra falsely linked to Rahul Gandhi's 'Voter Adhikar Yatra' in Bihar; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 25 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): As Congress' 'Voter Adhikar Yatra' led by Rahul Gandhi continues to traverse multiple locations in Bihar, which is set to go to polls by the end of the year, a video showing an aerial view of a street packed with thousands of people was recently shared on social media. Users claimed the video depicted the crowd gathered for Rahul Gandhi's 'Voter Adhikar Yatra' in Bihar. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found the video unrelated to Rahul Gandhi's political movement in Bihar. In reality, the video showed devotees thronging the streets of Puri, Odisha, during the annual Jagannath Rath Yatra. An unrelated video from the Jagannath Yatra in Puri was falsely linked to Rahul Gandhi's political campaign in Bihar. Claim An X handle with the username @DhruvRatheFc shared on August 20 a video purportedly showing a massive crowd gathered for Leader of the Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi's recently launched 'Voter Adhikar Yatra' in Bihar. Sharing the video, the user wrote: "Rahul Gandhi has written history. Rubika Liyaquat will never say that Rahul Gandhi has broken all records. This flood of people in Bihar will break the arrogance of the 2 great men." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens led to several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here . The search result via Google Lens also led the Desk to a video posted on a YouTube channel named @AarambhtvAtd. The video included the same aerial visual showing thousands of people thronging on the street (as seen in the social media post). However, the details mentioned along with it stated the visual to be from Jagannath Yatra in Puri. Also, the date of publication of the video, i.e., June 26, 2025, by the YouTube channel predated the Voter Adhikar Yatra kickstarted in Bihar on August 20, 2025. The title of the video reads, "The Grand Rath Yatra of Lord Jagannath Begins." Here is the link and archive link to the video, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image comparing visuals from the viral video with those in the YouTube video, confirming they are the same. In the next part of the investigation, to strengthen the inquiry that the visuals depicted in the above shared video do not pertain to Bihar and showed visuals during the annual Jagannath Rath Yatra, the Desk carefully analysed the footage. The analysis found that the video does contain visuals of the Shree Jagannath Temple in Puri, thus proving that the video is unrelated to Rahul Gandhi's ongoing political movement in Bihar. An image is attached below, highlighting a side-by-side comparison of the viral footage with a photo of the temple from the PTI gallery, confirming that the video is indeed from Puri, Odisha. Additionally, as part of the investigation to find details related to the commencement of this year's annual Rath Yatra, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google. This led to a report published by The Indian Express on June 26, which confirmed that the main Rath Yatra was held on June 26–27, notably coinciding with the release date of the above-mentioned YouTube video. While the Desk could not independently verify whether the footage was filmed during this year's procession, it was able to establish that the video indeed originated from Puri. Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a large gathering during the annual Jagannath Rath Yatra in Puri was falsely linked to Rahul Gandhi's Voter Adhikar Yatra in Bihar.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2024 Ecuador kidnapping video falsely shared as incident from India
content: New Delhi, August 27 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it showed a horrific incident in India where two men allegedly abducted a woman. The video shows a man and a woman conversing when a car pulls up near them. As the woman tries to walk away, the man she was speaking with forcefully pushes her toward the car. Another individual inside the vehicle then drags her in. Several bystanders rush to help, but the car speeds away before they can intervene. Users circulated the video to target the law-and-order situation under the BJP-led government. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found that the video is unrelated to India. It actually depicts a kidnapping that took place on September 26, 2024, in the Las Casas area of northwestern Quito, Ecuador. According to local media reports, the woman was later released. Claim A Facebook user, Rakesh Kumar, shared on August 21 a video purportedly from India, showing two men abducting a woman. In the video, one man pushed her toward the car while another, waiting inside, dragged her in. Sharing the video, the user criticised the BJP government's law-and-order situation, captioning it: "See, BJP's good governance, a girl is kidnapped in just 49 seconds — in the blink of an eye." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these through Google Lens, the Desk came across several social media accounts sharing the same clip with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here . The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a video posted by Ecuadorian news outlet Radio Pichincha on its official X handle. The clip was identical to the one circulating on social media, but the details confirmed it originated from Ecuador, not India. The news outlet reported (translated from Spanish to English) that the kidnapping took place in the Las Casas area of northwestern Quito, Ecuador. "A woman was kidnapped by individuals travelling in a black sedan without license plates. It happened at 19:56 on September 26, 2024, at the intersection of Ruiz de Castilla and Aldana streets, in the La América–Las Casas sector, north of Quito," the report stated. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image comparing visuals from the viral video with those in the X video, confirming they are the same. To find further details related to the incident, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search using the above inputs. The search led to multiple Ecuadorian news reports that confirmed the kidnapping occurred in the Las Casas area in 2024, not in India. Reports also mentioned that the victim was later released in Chillogallo, south of Quito. Links to two such reports can be found here and here . Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a woman being kidnapped in Ecuador was falsely shared on social media, linking it to an incident from India.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2023 video of individuals pushing detached coach of Falaknuma Express after an accident recently shared with false claim; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 27 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing locals, army personnel, police officials, and railway staff jointly pushing a train coach was recently shared on social media, accompanied by the claim that it reflected the deteriorating standards of railway infrastructure in India. Users alleged that under the Bharatiya Janata Party-led government, railway infrastructure had declined to such an extent that people were forced to push a train to start it physically. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false. While the visuals of a train coach being pushed are genuine, they date back to July 2023, when a portion of the Howrah–Secunderabad Falaknuma Express caught fire, damaging a few coaches. At the time, army jawans, police officials, and passengers manually detached the adjacent coaches to prevent the fire from spreading further. Hence, the claim circulated along with the video is false. Claim An X user, Devesh Vishwakarma (@devesh_aap), shared a video on August 24, purportedly showing locals, army officials, police personnel, and railway staff jointly pushing a train coach to get it started. Sharing the video, the user criticised the government, claiming: "In Modi's rule, not just trains but people's lives are also running with a push. In history so far, you wouldn't have seen pushing in trains, see it in Modi's rule." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video had garnered 1,100 views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across multiple social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a news report published by NDTV on July 10, 2023. The report included the same visuals showing individuals pushing a train coach, as seen in the viral social media posts. However, the details in the report clarified that while the visuals were genuine, they dated back to July 2023, when a portion of the Howrah–Secunderabad Falaknuma Express caught fire, damaging a few coaches (S2 to S6). The report added: "However, to restrict the spread of fire to other coaches, the rear portion consisting of three coaches — S1 and two General Coaches — was detached and manually moved away by dedicated railway staff and local police." It further noted that the action was taken "to minimise the damage and safeguard the belongings of passengers." Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image showing visuals from the viral video alongside the NDTV video, confirming they are the same. Additionally, the search also led the Desk to several other news reports covering the incident. The reports also stated that officials carried out the move to prevent the blaze from spreading to other coaches. Links to two such posts can be found here and here . In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to check if the Railway Ministry had issued any statement regarding the incident. The search led the Desk to a social media post published by the Official Spokesperson of the Railway Ministry on July 10, 2023, on its official X handle. The post confirmed that railway personnel and local police joined forces to detach the rear coaches and prevent the fire from spreading further. "After the fire incident, prompt response was given & an engine was on its way to help detach the coaches to stop further spread of fire, but instead of just waiting for the engine to come, our alert Railway & Local police personnel took immediate action," the Railway Ministry Spokesperson wrote. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the 2023 visuals showing individuals pushing a detached coach of the Falaknuma Express after a fire accident are being shared with a misleading claim.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Edited video falsely shows Kangana Ranaut criticising Election Commission over 'vote chori'
content: New Delhi, August 27 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video featuring BJP MP Kangana Ranaut talking to the mediapersons in the Parliament premises was shared by several social media users. Those sharing the video claim that the MP criticised the Election Commission over the 'vote chori' allegation by the opposition parties. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video was digitally altered. In the original video, BJP MP Kangana Ranaut criticised Rahul Gandhi, alleging that he had insulted voters and created a spectacle in Parliament. The viral clip was selectively edited to suggest she was targeting the Election Commission. Claim: A video featuring BJP MP Kangana Ranaut talking to the media in the Parliament premises was shared by a Facebook user 'Moni Singh' on August 25, claiming that she criticised the Election Commission over the 'vote chori' allegation. In the 00:27-second video, she says, "As you can see, the way the Election Commission has insulted people and voters, many of them are expressing grief over this. They have been deeply humiliated in their communities, and in a way, their respect has been completely shattered by Rahul Gandhi ji." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens led to several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here . The search result via Google Lens also led the Desk to an Instagram post by 'live mint' dated August 18, wherein Kangana Ranaut could be seen in the same attire. However, in the video Ranaut says, "EC has reprimanded Rahul Gandhi, that he insulted people and voters. Rahul Gandhi has dishonoured the voters he named. Despite such reprimanding, they (the INDIA bloc MPs) did drama here today. So, you can understand that if they don't get power, they would not let any work be done" Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Additionally, the search result also led the Desk to a video shared by Times Now, on their official YouTube channel on August 18. As the Desk analysed the video, it found the same to be selectively edited, and a line, "How much reprimand has been given to Rahul Gandhi," was removed. Following this, the video creates the false impression that Kangana Ranaut was criticising the Election Commission, whereas in the original video, she was targeting Rahul Gandhi. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. As part of the investigation, the Desk also conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports related to Kangana Ranaut's statement. The search led the Desk to a report by ABP published on August 18. The title of the report read: "'We will spread chaos everywhere...', why did Kangana Ranaut get angry at Rahul Gandhi outside Parliament?" "Kangana Ranaut Slams Rahul Gandhi: Kangana Ranaut further said that today, when the country is progressing, the opposition parties are unhappy. She said that the public is watching everything, and because of this, the opposition will not be able to win any election," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video is digitally altered. In the original video, BJP MP Kangana Ranaut criticised Rahul Gandhi, alleging that he had insulted voters and created a spectacle in Parliament. The viral clip was selectively edited to suggest she was targeting the Election Commission.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video showing cattle swept away by floodwaters shared as real in name of Rajasthan's Sawai Madhopur; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 27 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing dozens of cattle being swept away by raging muddy waters was recently shared on social media with the claim that it depicted an incident from Rajasthan's Sawai Madhopur. The user alleged that relentless rainfall had triggered widespread flooding, causing the region to come to a standstill, with severe loss to livestock also reported, as depicted in the video. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found that it was generated using AI and falsely shared to mislead people into believing it was a real incident. Meanwhile, it is pertinent to note that at least six people, including four minors and a government school teacher, died in separate rain-related incidents in Rajasthan. The state continues to be battered by heavy rains, leading to flood-like situations in several areas. Claim An X handle with the username @dayalg343 shared, on August 24, a video showing dozens of cattle being swept away by raging muddy waters.
