The user claimed the footage was from Rajasthan's Sawai Madhopur, where incessant rainfall had triggered flooding, causing severe livestock losses. "Friends, the water has washed away so much... But if we stand together, no wave can drown our hope. Let's come together to help the brothers and sisters of Sawai Madhopur overcome the crisis," the user wrote while sharing the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across multiple social media accounts of those who had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the video to corroborate the claim that it was from Sawai Madhopur. The visuals, however, revealed several inconsistencies. For instance, the cattle floating in floodwaters appeared unnatural, and the overall footage had an overly glossy finish — both typical characteristics of AI-generated videos. To confirm, the Desk ran the footage through Cantilux, an AI detection tool, which identified distortions and artefacts typically associated with AI-generated content. Below is a screenshot of the result. In the subsequent part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google keyword search to find details about rain-induced floods in Rajasthan. The search led to an NDTV report published on August 24, showing how incessant rainfall over three days triggered severe soil erosion in Jhadawata village. The erosion created an 80-foot-wide and 50-foot-deep crater in farmland, displacing hundreds of families, many of whom were left dependent on external aid for food and other essentials. Additionally, the report also noted that rainfall wreaked havoc in Dausa district, causing widespread waterlogging and severe disruptions to daily life. Low-lying areas were inundated, roads turned into rivers, and residents faced significant hardships. Here is a link to the video, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing dozens of cattle being carried away by raging muddy waters was AI-generated and did not depict a real incident from Sawai Madhopur, Rajasthan.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 20-minute Noida–IGI Airport commute possible? Misleading claim debunked as no direct corridor exists
content: New Delhi, August 27 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A viral social media post claimed that with the inauguration of the Dwarka Expressway and the Delhi section of the Urban Extension Road-II (UER-II), commuters could reach Indira Gandhi International Airport from Noida in just 20 minutes. The claim was amplified by headlines in several media outlets after Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Delhi section of the Dwarka Expressway and UER-II Phase 1 on August 16. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found the claim to be misleading. While PM Modi inaugurated the Delhi section of the Dwarka Expressway and UER-II Phase 1 on August 16, neither project provides a direct corridor from Noida to Delhi's IGI Airport. Even after full completion, Noida will remain outside their alignment, making a 20-minute commute to IGI Airport unrealistic. Social media users shared the false claim without verifying its accuracy. Claim: A post claiming that commuters could now travel from Noida to Indira Gandhi International Airport in just 20 minutes with the opening of the Dwarka Expressway and the UER-II Delhi stretch was shared by a user on X, @IndianTechGuide, on August 16. "Noida to Delhi Airport in 20 minutes! Dwarka Expressway, UER-II Delhi stretch opens tomorrow," read the post's caption. The post clocked 738.8k views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran a keyword search and found that several media outlets had also covered the story with a similar headline of 'Noida to IGI in 20 minutes'. Two such links can be found here and here ; their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. Media outlets like Outlook Traveller and Zee News ran headlines suggesting that Noida commuters could now reach IGI in 20 minutes. These headlines did not quote the PM directly. They were putting their own interpretative spin on it, likely misreading "airport connectivity" as applying to Noida. Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Delhi section of the Dwarka Expressway (NH-248BB) and Phase 1 of the Urban Extension Road-II (UER-II, NH-344M) on August 16, according to the government's official release. Here is the link to the official press release: Dwarka Expressway (NH-248BB): Connects Shiv Murti (near IGI) to Kherki Daula Toll Plaza (Gurugram). Helps Delhi–Gurugram commuters. UER-II (NH-344M): Semi-ring road project along Delhi's western and northern edges. Phase 1 connects NH-1 (on the north Delhi side, near Bawana) to Dwarka (Sector 24). When complete, it will connect NH-1, NH-10, NH-8, and NH-2, easing movement between Sonipat, Rohini, Mundka, Najafgarh, Dwarka, IGI, and Gurugram. Neither Dwarka Expressway nor UER-II provides a direct corridor from Noida to the airport. Even after completion, Noida will remain on the eastern edge of NCR, while IGI lies on the western side. The projects aim to decongest Delhi and improve cross-city and interstate traffic, rather than reducing Noida–IGI travel time to 20 minutes. Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to study the route of the Delhi Urban Extension Road (UER) II and came across a report by The Metro Rail Guy. According to the information, the 74.98 km Delhi Urban Extension Road (UER) II project is an under-construction expressway (NH-344M) by NHAI, which, in Phase 1, will form a 38.111 km 3rd semi Ring Road within Delhi along its western boundary. Elaborating with the help of the map, it highlighted that the UER 2's alignment in the north starts from NH 1 (Km. 23.800) near the village Bankoli and terminates near the junction of Sector 24 in Dwarka. Its route will connect old NH-1, NH-10, NH-8, and NH-2 via Bawana Industrial Area, Rohini, Mundka, Najafgarh, and Dwarka, providing seamless access between north, northwest Delhi, IGI Airport, and Gurugram. Below is a screenshot of the map used by the website. (Note: the map below doesn't show the full alignment/extent of the spur to Sonipat:) (Source: URS Scott Wilson India – AECOM India's DPR) The UER 2 is expected to be fully completed and opened in December 2024 (current deadline). The Delhi Government will take up phase 2 of UER 2. It includes constructing the Rangpuri Bypass to Vasant Kunj, upgrading Nelson Mandela Marg to Andheria Mor, building an interchange at the intersection of Anuvrat Marg, Mehrauli-Badarpur Road, and NH-236, and widening Mehrauli-Badarpur Road. It also includes building an elevated corridor at critical locations along NH-2. Below is a screenshot depicting Phase 1 and Phase 2 on the Map. (Source: URS Scott Wilson India – AECOM India's DPR) Dwarka Expressway (NH-248BB): Connects Shiv Murti (NH-48, near Mahipalpur/IGI T3) to Kherki Daula Toll (Gurugram). Primarily eases Delhi–Gurugram traffic. UER-II (NH-344M): Semi-ring road project around Delhi's western/northern side. Will eventually connect NH-1 (Sonipat side) to Dwarka/IGI/Gurugram, still under construction and not fully open. These expressways don't provide a straight shot from Noida to IGI Airport. They help traffic coming from Sonipat, Gurugram, and Dwarka, not from Noida. Even after the completion of Phase 2, the alignment remains on Delhi's western and southern edges. Commuters from Noida would still need to cross central or southern Delhi roads to reach these expressways, so a direct high-speed corridor from Noida to IGI does not exist. Here is the link to the report. The visual shows how Noida and IGI sit on opposite ends of Delhi. Even with new highways, you'd still have to cross almost the entire city's width, making the 20-minute distance unrealistic. Below is a screenshot of the same. Additionally, the Desk checked the route from Noida Sector 62 to Indira Gandhi International Airport Terminal 3 at 1 PM on August 24, which showed a total distance of 35 km and a travel time of 54 minutes. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. The Desk checked the route from Noida Sector 18 to Indira Gandhi International Airport Terminal 3 simultaneously, which showed a total distance of 30 km and a travel time of 1 hour and 2 minutes at 11:00 am. Below is a screenshot of the same. Travel times on Google Maps vary by traffic, but even during late-night or non-peak hours, the journey from Noida to IGI Airport rarely takes less than 45–50 minutes, which is still more than double the viral claim. According to Google Maps, the driving distance from Noida (Sector 62) to IGI Terminal 3 is approximately 42 km, with typical travel times ranging from 50 to 65 minutes, depending on traffic conditions. From Sector 18, the distance is slightly shorter at about 40 km, but it still takes close to an hour during normal conditions. (These are road distances, not straight-line measurements.) While Prime Minister Modi inaugurated the Dwarka Expressway (Delhi section) and Phase 1 of UER-II on August 16, neither of these projects currently provides or will provide a direct Noida–IGI corridor. Even after the full completion of UER-II Phase 2, Noida remains outside its alignment. The highways primarily benefit traffic from Gurugram, Sonipat, Rohini, Najafgarh, and Dwarka. The 'Noida to IGI in 20 minutes' line appears to be a media exaggeration that misinterpreted the government's claim of improved airport connectivity for western NCR commuters. Below is a map illustrating the following: Blue: Dwarka Expressway (Shiv Murti ↔ Dwarka ↔ Gurugram) Red dashed: UER-II Phase 1 (Bawana ↔ Dwarka) Green dotted: Noida → IGI Airport route. It can be seen that Noida (far east) and IGI (far west) sit on opposite ends of Delhi, while the new highways run along the west/northwest corridor, explaining why the "20 minutes from Noida" claim doesn't hold. Even after the full completion of UER-II (with a December 2024 deadline) and future Delhi government upgrades (Phase 2), Noida will not have a direct corridor onto these expressways. Travel from Noida to IGI will still require crossing central/south Delhi roads (like Ring Road, Barapullah, or NH-48).

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of motorcycles spinning after collision in Indonesia falsely linked to India; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 28 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it depicted a bizarre incident from Jaipur, Rajasthan, where two motorcycles collided in an accident and got stuck together. The motorcycles then began spinning in circles on the road, disrupting traffic. The video showed onlookers rushing with a stick to separate the motorcycles, eventually managing to stop them. The Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it to be unrelated to India. The video actually showed an unusual incident that occurred earlier in Indonesia's Pekanbaru city. An unrelated incident from Indonesia was falsely shared on social media as one from India. Claim An Instagram page named Wirally shared on August 22 a video purportedly showing an incident from Jaipur, Rajasthan, where two motorcycles collided in an accident and got stuck together. The video then showed the vehicles spinning in circles on the road, disrupting traffic. "A road accident in Jaipur turned unusual when two motorcycles collided and spun in circles, disrupting traffic. Onlookers rushed in with a lathi to separate the bikes, and the video quickly went viral," the user shared with the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered 15,096 likes.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across social media accounts sharing the same clip with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here . The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a video posted by Indonesia-based portal PT PSNEWS Merakyat Indonesia on its Instagram handle on August 18, 2025. The post carried the exact same video of motorcycles spinning on a road, as seen in the viral clip. However, the details stated alongside it confirmed the video originated from Indonesia, not India. The post mentioned the incident took place on Jalan Arifin Ahmad in Pekanbaru, where two motorcycles "stuck" together after a crash. As a result, they spun in the middle of the road, attracting the attention of locals. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image comparing visuals from the viral video with those in the Instagram video, confirming they are the same. Additionally, the search result via Google Lens also found reports from multiple Indonesia-based portals confirming the video originated from Pekanbaru city, Indonesia, and not India. Links to two such posts can be found here and here . In the next part of the investigation, to reconfirm the origin of the video that it originated from India, the Desk carefully analyzed it. A significant clue was spotted in the form of a license plate number — "BM 3675 FC" — visible in the video. The two-letter state code BM depicted on the license plate does not belong to any Indian state or union territory. Taking cues from this input, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found on the MPM Rent website that BM is the vehicle registration code for Indonesia's Riau Province. Importantly, Pekanbaru city, where the incident occurred, is the capital of Riau Province. This confirmed that the video originated from Indonesia and not India. Here is the link to the website. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video showing spinning motorcycles from Indonesia, falsely linked to India.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Viral 'IIMT topper is ice cream seller' video is fabricated; institute confirms false claim in social media posts
content: New Delhi, August 28 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video purportedly showing an ice cream seller claiming to be the same person featured on a hoarding of the Delhi-NCR-based IIMT Group of Colleges was recently shared on social media. Users mocked the college, alleging that the advertisement was fake and that an ice cream seller was falsely portrayed as alumnus Puneet Gautam, who had secured a campus placement with an annual package of Rs 1.8 crore. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false. In a statement, the IIMT Group of Colleges confirmed the video was fabricated and circulated to spread misleading and defamatory content against the institute. The college also stated that it had lodged an official complaint with local and cyber authorities, seeking strict action against those responsible for the conspiracy. Hence, the claim made in the viral video is FALSE. Claim An X user, Neetu Khandelwal (@T_Investor_), shared on August 21 a video capturing an ice cream seller who claimed to be the same individual pictured in a hoarding of the 'IIMT Group of Colleges'. After posting the video, the user mocked the college authorities for sharing a fake advertisement, in which an individual, initially an ice cream seller, was falsely portrayed as an alumnus of the institute who had secured a campus placement with an annual package of ₹1.8 crore. "The Education System is a Joke. According to IIMT's Advertisement, Puneet Gautam received a Rs 1.80 cr annual package. Puneet Gautam is selling ice cream under this fake advertisement," the user shared the post with a caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video garnered 600k views) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across social media accounts sharing the same clip with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here . In the next part of the investigation, to corroborate the claim in the viral video, the Desk scanned through the social media handles of the institute to check if it had posted anything related to the same. The search result led the Desk to a post shared from the official Facebook handle of the 'IIMT Group of Colleges' on August 21, wherein the institute clarified the viral allegations as fake. In a detailed statement, the Director General (Academics) of IIMT Group of Colleges stated that the circulation of the video was a deliberate attempt to malign the institute's reputation. He stated, "It is shameful and unfortunate that some mischievous elements are spreading false and insulting content against the IIMT Group of Colleges. They have tried to compare our proud alums with an unknown ice cream vendor and labelled it as fraud. We strongly condemn this act — it is fake, baseless, and a deliberate attempt to defame IIMT's reputation." The DG (Academics) further added that the institute has filed a formal complaint with local and cyber authorities to take strict action against those behind the conspiracy. Here is the link and archive link to the detailed version of the post, along with a screenshot. In the subsequent part of the investigation, to gather more details about alumnus Puneet Gautam — the individual featured on the hoarding — the Desk contacted the DG (Academics) of IIMT Group of Colleges. In his response, he confirmed that Puneet Gautam had completed a B.Tech in Computer Science Engineering from IIMT College of Engineering in 2011. He further stated: "He is working in a reputed company in London on an annual salary package of ₹1.80 crore. However, he was wrongly introduced as an ice-cream seller in a fake video, calling IIMT's promotion a fraud. This is an extremely condemnable incident." The institute also shared a statement from alumnus Puneet Gautam himself, which read: "I am disheartened to see a video going around on Instagram that uses a boy who resembles me and also mentions IIMT. I am not in that video, and I request that necessary steps be taken to remove it." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video claiming that an ice cream vendor was the same person shown on an IIMT Group of Colleges hoarding as alumnus Puneet Gautam, who secured a ₹1.8 crore placement, is false.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video of artisans making giant Ganesha idol falsely shared as real statue in Chennai
content: New Delhi, August 29 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid the ongoing 10-day Ganesh Chaturthi celebrations across the country, a video showing hundreds of people creating a massive Lord Ganesha idol was widely shared on social media. Users claimed it depicted the creation of the world's largest Ganpati statue in Chennai, involving several artisans. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated and found the video to be AI-generated. The footage was falsely shared as real to mislead viewers. Claim An X user, Abhisar G. Mehta (@5258c79d2d73491), shared on August 27 a purported video depicting the making of the world's largest Ganpati statue in Chennai. The footage showed hundreds of people participating in the creation of the massive idol. "The world's largest Ganpati statue in Chennai," the user captioned the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here . In the next stage of the investigation, to determine whether the video was real or AI-generated, the Desk conducted a detailed review of the viral footage and spotted a watermark reading 'hoohoocreations80' throughout the clip. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised Google search, which led to an Instagram account with the same name, 'hoohoocreations80'. On scanning the Instagram handle, the Desk found the same video uploaded on August 23, 2025. It showed the creation of massive Ganesh idols, involving hundreds of artisans. However, the account's bio clearly stated that it is known for sharing AI-generated content. Here is the link and archive link to the Instagram post, along with a screenshot: Below is a comparison image confirming that the visuals in the viral video match those posted on the Instagram handle. In the subsequent part of the investigation, based on the above findings that suggested the video was AI-generated, the Desk also ran the footage through Hive Moderation, an AI-detection tool. The result indicated that 99% of the footage contained deepfake or AI-generated content. Below is a screenshot highlighting the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an AI-generated video showing artisans involved in the creation of a humongous Ganesha idol was falsely shared as real.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: This viral video of people saving car from river is AI-generated, not real
content: New Delhi, September 1 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video purportedly showing several individuals preventing a car from slipping into a stream was recently shared on social media, with claims that it depicted a real incident. The footage appeared to show people rescuing a car after a section of road caved in, while another SUV was seen stuck in the flowing water. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found that the video was AI-generated and falsely shared as real to mislead viewers. Claim A Facebook handle with the username Flop and Lazy shared, on August 24, a video purportedly showing a group of individuals trying to rescue a car from being swept away in a water stream. The video appeared to show people preventing the vehicle from falling into a waterbody due to the road caving in. It also showed another car stuck in the flowing water. "Deadly flash floods start without warning," the user captioned the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered 9.3k views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here : To verify the authenticity of the video, the Desk examined the Facebook account from which it was originally shared. The analysis found that the account regularly shares AI-generated videos, rather than real incidents. Two such AI-generated videos from the same user can be found here and here : On closer examination of the viral video itself, the Desk also found several discrepancies suggesting it was AI-generated. For instance, the visuals displayed unusual distortions and an overly glossy finish — both typical signs of AI-generated content. Taking cues from these findings, the Desk ran the video through Hive Moderation, an AI-detection tool. The results confirmed that 99% of the footage contained deepfake or AI-generated elements. Additionally, the Desk conducted a customised Google keyword search to check if any real incident resembling the viral claim had recently occurred. The search led to an NDTV video report, published on August 26, which confirmed a similar real incident in Jammu & Kashmir. The report showed a section of the Tawi River bridge in Jammu collapsing, leaving several vehicles stranded. The video showed a portion of the bridge caving in, trapping an SUV and other cars on it. Here is the link and archive link to the report, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video showing people saving a car from falling into a river was AI-generated and falsely shared as a real incident to mislead viewers.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video showing bridge collapse incident falsely shared as real to mislead viewers; details inside
content: New Delhi, September 1 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): As heavy rains continue to cause widespread damage to property and crops across different parts of India, a video purportedly showing a newly constructed bridge collapsing within seconds was recently shared on social media. Users claimed that the incident had led to the loss of crores of rupees spent on building the bridge. author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: False claim about US President Donald Trump being in coma circulates online; details inside
content: New Delhi, September 1 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media post recently claimed that US President Donald Trump was in critical condition and had slipped into a coma, citing a statement allegedly from his medical team. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found it to be false. No official statement from the White House or any US authority suggested that President Trump's health was a concern. Moreover, on September 1, Trump himself posted multiple updates on his Truth Social handle, debunking the claim. The viral post was false and shared online to mislead viewers. Claim An X handle with the username News platform shared on August 30 a post claiming that US President Donald Trump had slipped into a coma. Sharing an alleged statement attributed to President Trump's medical team, the user said: "President Trump's medical team says he is in critical condition and is now in a coma." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the post had garnered 76.7k views and 2,241 likes.) Investigation The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found multiple social media accounts that shared similar claims. Additionally, claims suggesting that the US President has died have also been widely shared. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted another keyword search on Google to find credible reports mentioning President Donald Trump's health. The search results did not lead to any reliable reports confirming his deteriorating condition. However, the Desk found a report by the Economic Times on August 30, 2025, which stated that the US President had been diagnosed with chronic venous insufficiency (CVI). The report also mentioned growing speculation about Trump's health after he was spotted with visible swelling in his legs and bruises on his hands. "Trump, the oldest person to serve a second term, has faced intensifying scrutiny over his age and cognitive fitness. Though his physician recently declared him 'fully fit' after a comprehensive physical that included a perfect score on the Montreal Cognitive Assessment, public concern about his health has remained," the report added. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. In the subsequent part of the investigation, the Desk conducted another keyword search on Google, seeking further details on concerns about Trump's health and the recent claims. The search led to a September 1 NDTV report quoting a post by President Trump on his official Truth Social account, in which he wrote that he had "never felt better" in his life—indirectly debunking claims of ill health. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk scanned Trump's Truth Social handle, where a series of recent posts by him were found, further refuting the claim of his deteriorating health. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the post suggesting President Donald Trump was in critical condition and had slipped into a coma was false.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered Trump video 'blaming India for Pakistan floods' shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, September 2 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Several provinces of Pakistan, including Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab, Sindh, and Balochistan, are reeling from devastating floods. Amid this crisis, a video surfaced on social media showing US President Donald Trump addressing a public gathering. Those sharing the clip claimed he said that India's opening of dams in Kashmir had caused the floods in Pakistan. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the video was generated using AI and was a deepfake. Trump never made such a statement. In the original video, he was speaking about trade issues with China. The viral clip was shared with a false claim. Claim: A video featuring US President Donald Trump addressing a public gathering was shared by an X user, @Ltcolonelvikas, on August 30, claiming that Trump said India's opening of dams in Kashmir caused the floods in Pakistan. In the 1 minute 14 seconds video, he says, "Flood news Pakistan…let me tell you the truth and no one tells the truth like I do—the horrible floods in Pakistan, the destruction, the tragedy. It's not just climate, it's not just rain, it's India. India opened their dams in Kashmir, which was very unfair and very dangerous. They opened the gates, and millions of tons of water came rushing into Pakistan through Ravi…" Here is the link and the archive link ; below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here : The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find if Trump made such a statement, but found no such report. The Desk then investigated the causes of the recent floods in Pakistan. It came across a report by Al Jazeera dated August 28, which mentioned that Deforestation and glacial melting are the two leading causes compounding the climate crisis in northern Pakistan. The report did not mention one of the reasons connected to India or dams in Kashmir. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. As part of the investigation, the Desk ran the video through a Reverse Image Search. It came across a video streamed on the official YouTube Forbes Breaking News channel, dated May 31, 2025, which predates the floods in Pakistan. Trump was seen in the same attire and in the same background. Upon analysing the entire video, we found that he does not mention anything about the floods in Pakistan or India. He was speaking to reporters in the Oval Office about China, specifically responding to a question regarding China's alleged violation of a trade agreement on tariffs. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk ran the video through HiveModeration, an AI-detection tool which indicated an 88.7% likelihood of being AI-generated, confirming that the viral video is a deepfake. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim that Trump said India caused floods in Pakistan is AI-generated and a deepfake.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Did Kejriwal praise PM Modi? Old, edited video shared with false claim; details inside
content: New Delhi, September 2 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of former Delhi Chief Minister and AAP supremo Arvind Kejriwal was recently shared online, allegedly showing him praising Prime Minister Narendra Modi. In the video clip, Kejriwal appeared to say that he was not just a fan of PM Modi but his true devotee, adding that the PM's life story inspired him. The Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found the claim to be false. The Desk reviewed the full version of Kejriwal's public statement, as shown in the viral clip, and at no point in the original footage did he make such a remark, confirming that the claim is misleading. Claim A Facebook handle with the username DK Gupta shared on August 30, a video purportedly showing former Delhi Chief Minister and AAP supremo Arvind Kejriwal praising PM Modi. In the video, the AAP leader allegedly stated that he is not just a fan of Prime Minister Modi, but is his true devotee. The former Delhi Chief Minister added that PM Modi's life story is very inspiring. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video garnered 35k likes and 12k shares) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. To verify the authenticity of the alleged statement, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google. However, the search did not yield any credible news reports. Had Kejriwal made such remarks, they would have been widely covered by the media. Next, to corroborate the source of the visuals, the Desk ran a keyframe from the viral video through Google Lens. This led to a news report published by India Today on December 21, 2024. The featured image of the report exactly matched the keyframe used in the investigation. The report covered Kejriwal's address during the run-up to the Delhi Assembly elections in December 2024, where he criticised Union Home Minister Amit Shah for his remarks on Dr. B.R. Ambedkar in the Rajya Sabha. The report also mentioned that Kejriwal launched the Dr. Ambedkar Samman Scholarship at the same event. Nowhere did it mention Kejriwal praising PM Modi. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. A comparison of visuals confirmed that Kejriwal's appearance in the viral video matched that of the event reported by India Today. Furthermore, the Desk found the extended version of the video on the Aam Aadmi Party's official YouTube channel, which was uploaded on December 19, 2024. The clip clearly showed the same event, identifiable by Kejriwal's clothes and the background. However, nowhere in the original video did Kejriwal praise PM Modi. The Desk concluded that the viral video was false, with Kejriwal's voice might be superimposed using AI. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video, which claimed to show former Delhi Chief Minister and AAP supremo Arvind Kejriwal praising Prime Minister Narendra Modi, is doctored. The original footage, available on AAP's official channel and reported by credible media, shows no such remarks.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated image of drone show 'welcoming PM Modi to China' falsely shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, September 3 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): An image circulating on social media, purportedly linked to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's recent visit to China, claimed that a drone show was organised in Tianjin on August 30 — his first visit in seven years to attend the 25th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit. The image suggested that the show displayed PM Modi's face along with the message, "Modi Welcome to China." However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the image had been digitally altered. PM Modi's face and the accompanying message were AI-generated and falsely shared on social media to mislead viewers. Claim An X user named Mr Sinha shared on August 30 a social media image purportedly showing a drone show organised to welcome PM Modi during his recent visit to China. The image appeared to show a drone display projecting Modi's face and the message "Modi Welcome to China." The drone formation also depicted a dancing lady. "Unbelievable times we are living in," the user wrote in his caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the post garnered 1.7 million views and 56.2k likes) Investigation The Desk ran the viral social media image through Google Lens and found multiple social media accounts that shared the same image with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. Next, the Desk conducted a customised Google keyword search to verify whether any drone show was organised during PM Modi's visit to the 25th SCO Summit in Tianjin. The search, however, did not lead to any credible news reports corroborating the claim. Had such an event occurred, both national and international media would have widely covered it. To further verify the source of the image, the Desk performed a Google Reverse Image Search. The results led to a report published by China's state-run Xinhua News Agency on April 20, 2025. The report included a similar image to the one circulating on social media. However, it only showed a drone display of a dancing girl, without PM Modi's face or the message "Modi Welcome to China." According to the Xinhua report, the photo captured a drone light show held in Nan'an District of Chongqing Municipality on April 19, 2025 — months before PM Modi's visit to China on August 30, 2025. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. A comparison of the viral photo with the original image shows that Modi's face and the words "Modi Welcome To China" were digitally inserted. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral image claiming a drone show was organised in honour of PM Modi in China was AI-generated to mislead viewers.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old Dubai Airport flooding video falsely shared as Delhi Airport
content: New Delhi, September 3 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Heavy monsoon showers have lashed NCR, prompting the India Meteorological Department (IMD) to issue rainfall alerts for Delhi, Noida, Gurugram, and Ghaziabad. Amid this, a video showing a waterlogged airport with aircraft stranded on the tarmac went viral on social media, with claims that it depicted flooding at Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport. The PTI Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false. The video is not from Delhi but from Dubai International Airport, which was inundated in April 2024 after record rainfall. No credible reports suggest that there was any flooding at Delhi Airport in September 2025, as shown in the social media post.. Claim: A video showing an airport inundated with water, with planes stuck in floodwater, was shared by a Facebook user, 'Sukhraj brar', on September 1, 2025, claiming that the incident happened at Delhi airport. The post garnered 12,000 likes and 1,700 shares on social media. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here : As part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports, but the search did not lead us to any credible reports citing floods at Delhi airport. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk ran the extracted keyframes through a Reverse Image Search and came across the same video shared by various handles, many of which claimed that the incident occurred at Dubai Airport on 16 April 2024. "The #UAE is hit by rare heavy #rainstorms this morning: vehicles are submerged & planes struggle to navigate through water in #Dubai Airport. Heavy rainfall creates massive ponds on streets and airport runways across the UAE," read an X post caption by iChongqing. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Additionally, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by MorungExpress dated April 18, 2024, featuring key frames from the viral video. According to the report, over 30 flights, including those operated by Air India Express, Air India, IndiGo, Emirates, and SpiceJet airlines, to and from India have been cancelled due to severe flooding in Dubai, triggered by the heaviest rainfall witnessed in decades. Here is the link , and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video of a flooded airport in Dubai was falsely shared as that of Delhi Airport.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No. Govt has not declared Sept 3-6 as nationwide public holidays; false messages shared on social media
content: New Delhi, September 3 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A viral social media post claimed that the government has declared September 3, 4, 5, and 6, 2025, as nationwide public holidays, leading to the closure of schools and colleges. The PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found it to be false. According to the official holiday calendar on the National Portal of India, only September 5 has been declared as a gazetted holiday for Milad-un-Nabi or Id-e-Milad (the Birthday of Prophet Muhammad). While a few states, including Kerala, have local holidays on September 4 and 5 for Onam, no state has announced continuous holidays from September 3 to 6. Claim: A Facebook user, Priya Jamatia, shared a post on September 1, claiming that the Central government had recently declared September 3, 4, 5, and 6 as public holidays. "Schools and colleges closed! Government declares September 3, 4, 5, 6 as public holidays - Government holiday," read the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the post through Reverse Image Search and found that several other users had shared the same post with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. To verify the claim, we first checked whether the Government of India had announced any such decision, but found no official notice or press release on the matter. The Desk then visited the National Portal of India. According to the Indian government's national portal, only 5 September 2025 (Friday) has been declared as a gazetted holiday for Milad-un-Nabi or Id-e-Milad (the Birthday of Prophet Muhammad). Here is the link to the website, and below is a screenshot of the same. Further, the Desk checked the holiday list for September available on the official website of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). Only Ranchi has a holiday on 3 September, while banks in Kochi and Thiruvananthapuram will be closed on 4 September. The list showed that banks in the majority of cities will get holidays on 5 September. Here is the link to the website, and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk conducted a customised keyword search but did not find any news reports or any information available in the public domain to support the claim that the government has announced continuous holidays. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the Indian government has not declared 3, 4, 5, and 6 September 2025 as nationwide public holidays.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Scripted video showing a woman food delivery executive being assaulted shared on social media as real incident; details inside
content: New Delhi, September 3 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it depicted a purported assault on a woman food delivery executive by two male customers. The footage allegedly showed the female delivery executive dropping off a food package at a customer's home. The customer, seemingly in an inebriated state, refused to pay for the package. When the woman intervened, the man started misbehaving with her. Moments later, another man emerged from the house, and the duo forcibly took her inside. She was later seen coming out of the house visibly injured and distressed, suggesting an assault may have occurred. In its investigation, however, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the video was staged and scripted. The clip had no connection to any real-life incident and was misleadingly shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An X user, @divyakumaari, shared, on September 1, a video purportedly showing a female food delivery executive being assaulted by two male customers. The footage showed the delivery executive handing over food at a customer's home, where the man refused to pay. When the woman asked for the payment, the customer started misbehaving with her. Later, another man came out of the house and forcibly took her inside. She was later seen coming out of the house visibly injured and distressed, suggesting an assault may have occurred. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the post had garnered 157.6k views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here , respectively. The Google Reverse Image Search also led the Desk to a video posted on a Facebook page named 3RD EYE, which had over 1.1 million subscribers at the time of this story's publication. The channel had shared the same video (showing a food delivery executive being assaulted) on June 21, as seen in the viral social media posts. However, upon thoroughly reading the disclaimer included with the video, the Desk found that it was scripted and not based on a real-life incident. The disclaimer clearly stated that the video was intended to raise awareness, entertain, and educate its viewers. "Thank you for watching! Please note that this page features scripted dramas, parodies, and awareness videos. These short films are created for entertainment and educational purposes only. All characters and situations depicted in the videos are fictional and intended to raise awareness, entertain and educate," the page caption read. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a combined image that highlights the content in the viral video matches the video posted by the Facebook channel. Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk also scanned through other videos posted on the Facebook page. It was found that the channel is known for posting only scripted content. Links to two such videos can be found here and here . Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video claiming to show a woman food delivery executive being assaulted by two men is scripted. The footage was produced for awareness and entertainment purposes and has no link to any real-life incident.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Edited 2023 video of PM Modi with school children falsely linked to 'vote theft' row
content: New Delhi, September 3 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Following Congress leader and Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi's allegation of 'vote theft' against the Election Commission and the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party, a video featuring Prime Minister Narendra Modi interacting with school children was shared widely on social media. Those sharing the video claimed that during the interaction, a child allegedly accused the PM of committing 'vote chori'. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found the claim to be false. The footage is not recent and does not include such a remark by the child. It is from 2023, when PM Modi attended the Akhil Bharatiya Shiksha Samagam in Delhi. The original version has been edited and shared on social media with the false claim. Claim: A video featuring PM Modi interacting with school children was shared by a Facebook user, 'humoursguy', on September 1, claiming that the children allegedly said during a conversation with the PM that he did 'vote chori'. PM Modi asks the children if they know Modi. In response, a child says, "I have seen you on TV". On this, Modi ji asks, "What did I do on TV?" After this, the child answers, "Vote theft". Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Desk ran the extracted keyframes through Reverse Image Search and came across a video streamed on the official YouTube channel of DD News on July 29, 2023. According to the video's description, PM Modi inaugurated the Akhil Bharatiya Shiksha Samagam 2023 at Pragati Maidan. That is, one thing is clear: this video is quite old, and the matter of alleged vote theft was not in discussion at that time. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. The search led us to an X post by the official handle of the Prime Minister dated July 29, which featured the same video as seen in the social media post. On watching the original video in its entirety, there is no mention of "vote theft" anywhere. In the video, PM Modi asks the children, "What do I do on TV?" The children do not respond clearly to this. After this, one of these children says that he had seen PM Modi in a photo. After saying this, this child hugs PM Modi. Here is the link , and below is a screenshot of the same. Further in the video, Modi looks at the children's paintings, and the children also ask him to take a photo with them. That is, the child's answer about "vote theft" has been edited and added to the video. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of the conversation between PM Modi and children about "vote theft" is edited.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of priest 'miraculously surviving heart attack' during Ganesh puja is scripted; details inside
content: New Delhi, September 4 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently shared by multiple social media users claimed to show a priest miraculously surviving a heart attack while performing a Ganesh puja. In its investigation, however, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found the video to be staged and scripted. The clip had no connection to any real-life incident and was misleadingly circulated on social media with a false claim. Claim An Instagram user, Deepak Maholi, shared on August 31 a video purportedly showing a priest miraculously surviving a heart attack while performing a Ganesh puja. The footage showed the priest suddenly collapsing mid-ritual, appearing to suffer a near-fatal attack. Later, a religious flag from the Ganesh idol falls on him, after which he miraculously wakes up and prays to the deity for saving him. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered 32,665 likes.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here , respectively. A Google reverse image search also led the Desk to a video posted on a YouTube channel named 3RD EYE, which had over 2.98 million subscribers at the time of this story's publication. The channel had shared the same video (showing a priest miraculously surviving while performing a Ganesh puja) on July 11, 2025. However, upon thoroughly reviewing the disclaimer attached to the video, the Desk found that it was scripted and not based on a real-life incident. The disclaimer clearly stated that the video was intended to raise awareness, entertain, and educate viewers. "Thank you for watching! Please note that this page features scripted dramas, parodies, and awareness videos. These short films are created for entertainment and educational purposes only. All characters and situations depicted in the videos are fictional and intended to raise awareness, entertain and educate," the page caption read. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a combined image showing that the content in the viral video matches the video posted by the YouTube channel. Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk also scanned other videos posted on the same channel. It was found that the channel is known for uploading only scripted content. Two such examples can be found here and here . Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video, which claims to show a priest miraculously surviving a heart attack while performing a Ganesh puja, is scripted. The footage was created for awareness and entertainment purposes and has no link to any real-life incident.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video falsely shared as mass funeral after earthquake in Afghanistan's Kunar
content: New Delhi, September 4 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing what appears to be a mass funeral procession, with hundreds of bodies wrapped in white cloth being carried for burial, is circulating widely on social media. Users sharing the clip claimed it showed scenes from Afghanistan's Kunar province, alleging that more than 800 people were killed and thousands were injured overnight in a powerful earthquake. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the footage and found that the video is not real. It is AI-generated and is being shared online with a false claim. Claim: A video depicting a mass funeral, in which hundreds of bodies shrouded in white cloth are being carried to their final resting place was shared by an X user '@WakeelMubariz' on September 2, claiming that it was Afghanistan's Kunar province, where more than 800 people have lost their lives and thousands have been injured just in one night due to a devastating earthquake. "This is not Gaza — this is Afghanistan's Kunar province, where more than 800 people have lost their lives and thousands have been injured just in one night due to a devastating earthquake. Yaa Allah, help us and protect us. Anyone who wishes to help or donate can reach out to the following Afghan numbers, shared by the spokesperson of the Islamic Emirate, which are valid and active," read the post's caption. The post garnered 76.7k views on social media. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. As part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the video and found several discrepancies that suggested it had been manipulated. For instance, there are no identifiable faces in the video. A few figures appear to be moving in the eight-second-long clip, but their movements appear unnatural, almost robotic. It also appears that each body was being carried by two people, without the aid of a cot or coffin. Several individuals seem to be walking away from the procession, or in the opposite direction of the crowd. Below is a screenshot that highlights the same issue. Moreover, several other users also highlighted in the comment section that the video appears to be AI-generated. Below is a screenshot of two such users. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk ran the keyframe through Hive Moderation, an AI-detection tool that identified the content as 70.6% AI-generated. Below is a screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video being shared on social media is AI-generated and was accompanied by a false claim.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of family swept away in Pakistan floods falsely linked to Punjab floods; details inside
content: New Delhi, September 5 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): As torrential rains continue to trigger devastating floods in parts of Punjab — leaving 37 people dead and causing widespread damage — a social media video allegedly showing a family being swept away by floodwaters has gone viral. The clip shows several people stranded on a rocky platform amid surging waters before being washed away. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found that the video is unrelated to the current floods in Punjab. It actually depicts a tragic incident that occurred in June 2025 in Pakistan. The old footage was falsely circulated online in the context of Punjab's flood crisis. It is pertinent to note that a fresh spell of heavy rains has worsened the situation in Punjab, with the death toll climbing to 37 on Wednesday. Crops spread across 1.75 lakh hectares in 23 districts have been damaged in what is being described as the state's worst deluge since 1988. Claim On September 2, X user Indrajeet Gurjar (@IndrajitGurjar) shared a video showing a group of people, purportedly from the same family, being swept away during the recent floods in Punjab. The footage showed people standing on a rocky platform in the middle of rising floodwaters before being carried away. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a video posted on the official YouTube channel of Al Jazeera English on June 27, 2025. The video depicted the same visuals of a group of people trapped in the middle of heavy floodwaters. However, the details in the post stated that it was from Pakistan, not India. The description reads, "Several people believed to be part of the same family were filmed being swept downstream after flash flooding trapped them in the middle of the Swat River. Rescuers said 18 members from the same family were either dead or missing." Here is the link and archive link to the video, along with a screenshot: Below is a combined image that highlights the visual similarities between the viral video and the video posted by the YouTube channel. Additionally, taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google, which led it to a news report published by The Guardian on its YouTube channel on June 27, 2025. The report detailed further updates on the incident, mentioning that of the 17 members of a family caught in the floodwaters in Pakistan, nine had died while four were successfully rescued. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: In the next step of the investigation, the Desk also conducted a customised Google search to find the latest details related to the flood situation in Punjab. The search led to a news report published by PTI on September 3, which stated that the death toll from the floods in the state had reached 37. The report also mentioned that rescue efforts are being carried out on a large scale to provide aid to the victims. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a group of people being swept away in floodwaters is not related to the floods in Punjab. It is an old video from Pakistan, misleadingly shared as a recent tragedy from Punjab.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old 2021 video from Ukraine falsely shared as storm clouds over Gurugram
content: New Delhi, September 5 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A dramatic video showing thick, dark clouds rolling across the sky, resembling billowing smoke, is circulating on social media. Many users shared the clip, claiming it captured unusual weather conditions over Gurugram, Haryana. The Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found it to be misleading. The footage is not from Gurugram. It actually depicts a rare weather phenomenon known as a "thunder collar" or shelf cloud that appeared over Lviv, Ukraine, in August 2021. The same video, which has been online for over three years, is now being reshared with a false geographic context. Claim: An Instagram user shared a video showing thick smoke billowing in the sky, captioned 'watch.this.alone,' on September 2, claiming that it depicted the weather conditions in Gurugram, Haryana. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. One such post can be found here , with its archived versions available here . Upon further review of the search results, the Desk found that the video was uploaded to YouTube on August 18, 2021, by 'Meteored', who posted the video with the title 'Terrifying shelf cloud in Lviv, Ukraine'. "This spectacular cloud formation surprised many people in the city yesterday, where the storm discharged intensely," read the post's description. Here is the link , and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the YouTube post. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by UA News on August 18, 2021. The headline of the report read: "Rare phenomenon: Lviv covered by a unique 'thunder collar' cloud (Video)" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. ​ Another X post by BBC Weather, dated August 21, 2021, mentioned the dramatic skies over Kyiv, Ukraine, as a massive shelf cloud moved in. The visuals of the X post matched the clips of the viral video. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video shows the 'thunder collar' cloud phenomenon over Lviv in Ukraine in August 2021.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered video falsely claims Congress President Kharge blamed Rahul Gandhi for 'ruining the country'
content: New Delhi, September 5 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video featuring Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge addressing a public gathering is circulating widely on social media with the claim that he accused Rahul Gandhi of being responsible for the country's destruction. In the clip, Kharge appears to say that Gandhi is "busy ruining the nation". However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found that the video was digitally altered. The original footage, from March 2024, shows Kharge criticising Prime Minister Narendra Modi, not Rahul Gandhi. Claim: A video featuring Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge addressing a public gathering was shared by a Facebook user, Pankaj Sinha, claiming that he made a statement that Rahul Gandhi is responsible for the country's destruction. In the video, Kharge says, "Brothers, before everything, I would like to say Rahul Ji is busy ruining the country." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . Upon further review of the search results, the Desk came across an original speech on the Congress party's official YouTube channel, dated March 3, 2024. It was part of the "Jan Vishwas Rally" of the INDIA alliance held in Patna. In the full-length video, around the 29-second mark, Kharge can be clearly heard saying that it's Prime Minister Modi who is responsible for harming the country, not Rahul Gandhi. The edited version replaces this, making it appear as though Kharge attributed blame to Gandhi instead. There is no reference to Rahul Gandhi in the original speech. "तेजस्वी के चाचा गए हैं मामू के यहां चाय पीने..| Mallikarjun Kharge ने मोदी-नीतीश को मंच से जमकर धोया," read the description. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. As part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find reports that mentioned Kharge blaming Rahul Gandhi, but there were no credible news reports citing the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the original video dates back to March 2024, and Kharge was blaming the Prime Minister, not Rahul Gandhi.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old Bangladesh mosque donation video shared with false claim of Muslim donations for Punjab flood relief
content: New Delhi, September 5 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing members of the Muslim community emptying a sack filled with cash has recently gone viral on social media, with claims that it depicts donations made for flood relief in Punjab, which is currently battling flash floods. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false. The footage is unrelated to India and actually shows donations being counted at the Pagla Mosque in Kishoreganj, Bangladesh, on August 30, 2025. While several Muslim organisations in India have indeed extended support for Punjab's flood relief efforts, the viral clip is unrelated to these contributions. It was misleadingly linked to the ongoing crisis. Claim A Facebook page with the username Ravish Kumar Journalist shared a video on September 2, showing a group of individuals from the Muslim community emptying a sack containing a large sum of cash. The user alleged it was the amount donated by the latter to support flood relief work in Punjab, which is currently affected by flash floods. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered 7k likes and 1.4k shares.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here , respectively. The search results via Google Lens also led the Desk to a video posted on the Facebook page of the Bangladesh-based news portal Somoyer Konthosor on August 30, 2025. The video depicted the same visuals of individuals from the Muslim community emptying a sack of cash, as seen in the viral video. However, the details mentioned alongside it stated that the video was from Bangladesh, not India. The caption clarified that it showed a donation collection at Pagla Masjid in Bangladesh. Here is the link and archive link to the video, along with a screenshot. Below is a combined image that highlights the visual similarities between the viral video and the video posted by the Facebook handle. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find further details related to the development. The search result led the Desk to a news report published by Dhaka Tribune on August 30, 2025. The report stated that the Pagla Mosque, located in Bangladesh's Kishoreganj region, collected Tk 12.09 crore in donations after opening its 13 donation boxes, surpassing its previous record of Tk 9.17 crore collected in April. "The counting, conducted on the mosque's second floor, took 13 hours and involved over 450 people, including mosque staff, madrasa students, bank officials, and volunteers," the report noted. It further added that the funds collected would support the construction of a multistorey Islamic complex costing nearly Tk100 crore, as well as social welfare activities and a madrasa. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk also conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find out if there were any reports of the Muslim community in India assisting with flood relief aid or support in Punjab, ravaged by flash floods. The search led to reports published by Punjab Kesari and Zee News, which confirmed that Muslim communities in India have indeed provided aid. For example, people in several villages in Yamunanagar district collected food items and lakhs of rupees in cash to support flood victims in Punjab. However, it is important to note that the viral video is unrelated to these genuine efforts. Links to the reports published by two media news outlets can be found here and here . Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing the counting of donations at a mosque in Bangladesh is shared as Muslims donating for the Punjab flood relief operations.

title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video of bridge collapse falsely linked to Punjab floods
content: New Delhi, September 8 (Kaushiki Goel, Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a bridge collapsing and people running in panic is being widely shared on social media, with users claiming it shows a recent incident in flood-hit Punjab. The PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video is not real. It is AI-generated and has been falsely linked to the flood situation in Punjab. Claim: A video depicting a bridge collapse with people running amok was shared by a Facebook user, 'Gujarat Media star', on September 7, claiming that the incident happened in Punjab due to the flood situation in the state. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here , respectively. As part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find this particular video; however, there were incidents of bridge collapse in Punjab due to floods, but the video being shared on social media was not reported. Given the sensitivity of the matter and the damage caused by the collapse, it would have been covered by several news portals. Taking a cue from this, the Desk carefully analysed the video and found several discrepancies that suggested the video had been manipulated or was AI-generated. For instance, people appeared unnatural, almost robotic, and the area behind them looked unaffected. Below is a screenshot that highlights the same issue. The Desk then ran the frames of the video through WasitAi, an AI-detection tool, which detected that the video was AI-generated. Below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk found that the visuals are AI-generated, not from Punjab. The video was shared with a false claim.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of Priyanka Gandhi mocking PM Modi falsely linked to row over remarks on his mother; details inside
content: New Delhi, September 8 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra addressing a public rally is being circulated on social media with the claim that she mocked Prime Minister Narendra Modi, accusing him of playing the "victim card" after a youth allegedly made derogatory remarks about his late mother during the Rahul Gandhi-led Voter Adhikar Yatra in Darbhanga, Bihar. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found that the video is old. It dates back to November 2023, when Priyanka Gandhi Vadra made remarks about PM Modi in Datia, Madhya Pradesh. The video has no connection to the recent controversy over derogatory remarks against the PM's mother during the Voter Adhikar Yatra in Bihar. It was falsely shared on social media with a misleading context. Claim: A video featuring Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra addressing a public rally was shared by a Facebook user, Ajith Gadiya, on September 3, 2025, claiming that she mocked PM Modi, accusing him of playing the "victim card," after a youth allegedly made derogatory remarks about his late mother during the Rahul Gandhi-led Voter Adhikar Yatra in Darbhanga, Bihar. In the 00:38-second video, she says, "...and don't ask about Modi ji…he is the first PM who is permanently suffering from his own pain. He went to Karnataka with a long list, claiming that the has been abused. He is always crying…" "Priyanka Vadra mocks PM Narendra Modi for speaking about abuses hurled at his mother…She even smirked while calling him a "victim"! What else to expect from the daughter of an Italian lady?" read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. Upon further review of the search results, the Desk came across a report by The Economic Times, dated November 15, 2023, which featured the same video, confirming that it predates the current controversy. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search and found the video on the official YouTube channel of Congress on November 15, 2023. The timeline of the video makes it clear that it predates the ongoing controversy. The title of the video read: "LIVE: Smt. Priyanka Gandhi ji addresses the public in Datia, Madhya Pradesh." Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video dates back to November 2023 when Priyanka Gandhi Vadra made remarks about PM Modi in Datia, Madhya Pradesh. It has no connection to the derogatory remarks against his mother during the Voter Adhikar Yatra in Bihar.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of women fighting in Telangana bus falsely linked to Andhra Pradesh's 'Stree Shakti' scheme
content: New Delhi, September 9 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing women fighting inside a crowded bus has gone viral on social media, with users claiming it was shot in Andhra Pradesh after the launch of the state government's 'Stree Shakti' free bus travel scheme. The footage was widely shared as a recent incident linked to the policy. However, a PTI Fact Check investigation found that the video is neither recent nor from Andhra Pradesh. It dates back to at least January 2024 and was filmed in Telangana, months before the Andhra Pradesh government rolled out the 'Stree Shakti' scheme in August 2025. Claim: A video depicting women fighting in a bus was shared by a Facebook user 'Deccan Times' on August 20, claiming that the incident occurred in Andhra Pradesh after the state government introduced the 'Stree Shakti' scheme in August aiming to allow free bus travel for all girls, women, and transgender individuals in the AP State Road Transport Corporation-run (APSRTC) buses. "A fight among women passengers for seats in the bus. Incident in a bus travelling from Vizianagaram to Kothavalasa. Recently launched free bus scheme in AP," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. Upon further review of the search results, the Desk came across the same video, uploaded on YouTube by 'Alo TV Channel' on January 1, 2024. The timeline of the report clarifies that the video is not recent and predates the recent scheme that was introduced in Andhra Pradesh. Its description mentioned the location as Sangareddy, which is located in the state of Telangana. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. A local TV channel shared the same video on YouTube on January 1, 2024. The title of the report mentioned: "Ladies Fight in Free Bus at SangaReddy To Zaheerabad". The description and the timeline of the report make it clear that the video is not recent. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Meanwhile, the government introduced the 'Stree Shakti Scheme', which will offer free bus travel on five categories of buses operated by APSRTC, as per an order dated August 11, 2025. The scheme will be available to all girls, women, and transgender individuals residing in the state.
