Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video being shared on social media dates back to at least January 2024, predating the AP scheme, which was introduced in August. The video is not from Andhra Pradesh but Telangana.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2017 Bihar flood photo falsely shared as recent floods in Punjab; details inside
content: New Delhi, September 9 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A photo showing a man wading through floodwaters while pulling a makeshift raft made of banana tree trunks is circulating widely on social media. The raft, loaded with grain sacks and other belongings, is being shared with the claim that the image depicts the recent flood situation in Punjab. The PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found it to be misleading. The photo is not from Punjab. It is an old image from Bihar's Araria district, taken during the devastating floods of 2017. The image is now being reshared with a false context. Notably, Punjab is experiencing massive floods, caused by the swollen Sutlej, Beas, and Ravi rivers, as well as seasonal rivulets, due to heavy rainfall in their catchment areas in Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir. Claim: A picture depicting a man swimming through floodwaters, pulling along a makeshift raft and working to save his belongings, was shared by an X user, @NeeleshGaurav, on September 3, claiming to be from Punjab. "From the satellite, only smoke is visible. The crops of Haryana are being destroyed, and the sinking Punjab is not seen..!," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the picture through Reverse Image Search and found that several other users had shared the same photo with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here ; their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. Upon further scanning of the search results, the Desk came across a PTI report carried by The Hindu, featuring the same image as seen in the X post. The article, published on August 19, 2017, clarifies that the incident is not recent and is unrelated to Punjab. The report mentioned that the toll in the Bihar floods rose to 153 while the number of those marooned in 17 districts of the state crossed the one-crore mark. "Bihar flood toll mounts to 153, 17 districts affected," read the report's headline. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the feature image of the news report and the picture shared in the X post. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across another report by Financial Express published on August 17, 2017, featuring the same picture as seen in the social media post. The report, citing PTI, highlighted that in the picture, a villager is seen carrying grains on a banana raft as he navigates a flooded village in the Araria district of Bihar. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the picture of a man carrying grains on a banana raft is from Bihar, originally taken during the 2017 floods in Araria district.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Udaipur saree shop video falsely shared as looting incident in Muzaffarpur during Bihar Bandh protest
content: New Delhi, September 9 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing chaos inside a saree shop was recently shared on social media, accompanied by the claim that it depicted an alleged looting incident by members of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in Bihar. Users alleged that the video showed BJP Mahila Morcha leaders looting a saree shop in Muzaffarpur during the Bihar Bandh protest on September 4, organised by the ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA) against the alleged abusive remarks made about Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his late mother during Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's recently concluded 'Voter Adhikar Yatra.' However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video was unrelated to Bihar. It featured visuals from a saree shop in Udaipur, Rajasthan, where women were seen crowding to take advantage of sale offers. An unrelated video from Rajasthan was falsely shared online, linking it to Bihar. Claim An X user, Davinder Pal Singh (@dpsingh1313), shared a video on September 5, allegedly depicting BJP Mahila Morcha leaders looting a saree shop in Muzaffarpur, Bihar, during the 'Bihar Bandh' protest on September 4, 2025. Sharing the video, the user wrote: "During yesterday's Bihar Bandh, BJP Mahila Morcha leaders raised the slogan 'I am also a mother'..!!. In Muzaffarpur, a saree shop was looted." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the post had garnered 1.6k views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here , respectively. The search also led the Desk to a video posted on the Instagram page 'Agarwal Sarees' on August 20, 2025. The video exactly matched the one shared in the viral post. However, the details revealed that it was shot inside a saree shop in Udaipur, Rajasthan, where customers were crowding to take advantage of sale offers, and the video did not belong to Bihar. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a combined image highlighting the visual similarities between the viral video and the video posted by the Instagram page. In the next part of the investigation, to corroborate the finding that the video belonged to Udaipur, Rajasthan, the Desk contacted the number mentioned on the Instagram page of Agarwal Sarees. The person who responded confirmed that the video (seen in the viral post) was shot at their shop in Udaipur and showed customers crowding during a sale. The person also stated that the shop is located in Maldas Street, Udaipur, and they regularly witness such a large crowd during their sale offers. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing chaos inside a saree shop in Udaipur during a sale was falsely shared on social media as a looting incident in Muzaffarpur during the Bihar Bandh protest.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally edited graphic falsely shows PM Modi using thumb impression as his official signature; details inside
content: New Delhi, September 9 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A graphic depicting the official signatures of 14 global leaders, including Russian President Vladimir Putin, US President Donald Trump, French President Emmanuel Macron, and Prime Minister Narendra Modi, was recently shared on social media. The post claimed to show their official signatures, but in PM Modi's column, it falsely depicted him using a thumb impression instead of a signature. In its investigation, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the graphic had been digitally edited. Verified sources confirm that PM Modi signs in both Hindi and English, debunking the false claim that he uses a thumb impression as his official signature. Claim An X handle with the username Anjana (@Tinyhunterme), in a post dated September 4, shared a graphic depicting the official signatures of fourteen global leaders, including Vladimir Putin, Donald Trump, Emmanuel Macron, and Narendra Modi. The post, however, falsely showed PM Modi using his thumb impression as his official signature instead of signing his name. Additionally, in a veiled dig at PM Modi, the user wrote: "The signature of the man who has an MA in Entire Political Science." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the graphic shared in the social media post through Google Lens. This led to several social media accounts sharing the same graphic, which falsely depicted PM Modi using his thumb impression as a signature. Links to two such posts can be found here and here ; their archived versions are available here and here . In the next stage of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find any official documents, reports, or images bearing PM Modi's authentic signature. The search led to a report published by the news portal India.com on December 9, 2023. The report detailed the Prime Minister's visit to the Press Trust of India (PTI) headquarters, during which he penned a poem in immaculate Hindi. Notably, the report included an image of the poem with PM Modi's signature clearly visible underneath. The signature confirmed that he signs in Hindi and does not use a thumb impression. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Below is an image highlighting authentic examples of PM Modi's signature. Additionally, the search led the Desk to a letter signed by PM Modi and uploaded on the official PM India website. It was clearly found that PM Modi officially signs in Hindi (writing his full name) and does not use a thumb impression. Here is the link to the letter published on the official PM India website, along with a screenshot: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to check if PM Modi has used any other signature. The search led to a letter written and signed by PM Modi, published in the Bengali language on the Ministry of External Affairs website in September 2015. In this document, PM Modi signed in English, once again confirming that he does not use a thumb impression as his official signature. Here is the link to the letter by PM Modi in Bengali, published by the Ministry of External Affairs in September 2015, along with a screenshot: In the subsequent part of the investigation, to check the origin of the graphic (showing PM Modi using a thumb impression as his official signature) shared on social media, the Desk ran it through Google Lens. The search led to several social media accounts sharing the exact image of the signatures of world leaders. However, in those images, PM Modi's column showed his actual Hindi signature, not a thumb impression. This proved that the graphic circulating on social media was digitally altered by replacing PM Modi's real signature with a thumb impression. Links to two such posts can be found here and here , along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral social media post claiming PM Modi uses a thumb impression among world leaders' signatures was digitally edited. The investigation found that PM Modi signs in both Hindi and English.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of attacks on police personnel from Indonesia falsely shared as recent Nepal protest footage
content: New Delhi, September 10 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a mob attacking police personnel seated on the ground and using riot shields was recently shared by several social media users, with the claim that it depicted the ongoing protests in Nepal. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated and found the claim to be false. While protests in Nepal have indeed turned violent, culminating in Prime Minister K P Sharma Oli's resignation, the viral video is from Indonesia, not Nepal. It dates back at least 10 days. The riot shields visible in the clip match those used by Indonesian police, not Nepal Police. On Monday (September 8), protests in Kathmandu, led by youth angered by the blocking of several social media sites, turned violent, forcing police to open fire, which resulted in the deaths of 19 people. The unrest escalated further on Tuesday (September 9), with demonstrators setting fire to government buildings and politicians' homes and attacking leaders, despite Prime Minister Oli's resignation. Claim: A video showing a mob attacking police personnel sitting on the road and using riot shields was shared by an Instagram user 'bistagorkha600' on September 9, claiming that it is from the ongoing protests in Nepal. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation As part of the investigation, the Desk ran the keyframes of the video through a Reverse Image Search, which led us to a video uploaded on YouTube by a user named 'RAKYAT BERSATU' on August 30, 2025. The description, originally in Indonesian, loosely translates to, "The PANDEMO caused a huge commotion against the police. The people unite". The title of the video read: "POLICE VS MASSES, HUGE DEMONSTRATION" Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. The timeline of the video and the details mentioned clarify that the video is at least 10 days old, and the riot shields seen in the video match those used by Indonesian police, not Nepal Police. Below is a screenshot that highlights the same issue. Below is a combined image highlighting the similarities between the content seen in the Instagram post and the YouTube video. As part of the investigation, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search and came across a report by Associated Press, streamed on their official YouTube channel on August 29, 2025. The report highlighted that Indonesian riot police violently dispersed hundreds of students enraged by the lavish allowances of parliament members. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. While protests in Nepal have indeed turned violent, leading to Prime Minister K P Sharma Oli's resignation, and President Ram Chandra Poudel was at an undisclosed location under the protection of the Army. This particular video is unrelated to the situation there.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Viral 'child dragging mother's body' video not from Punjab floods, but scripted in UP
content: New Delhi, September 10 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): As social media fills with distressing visuals linked to the recent flash floods in Punjab, one particularly shocking video has gone viral. It shows a child wading through floodwaters while allegedly dragging the body of his dead mother, with users claiming it depicts the aftermath of the devastating floods in Punjab. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found that the video is staged and scripted. It has no connection to the Punjab floods or any real-life tragedy. The clip was created by a social media influencer from Uttar Pradesh, who later confirmed that she is alive and clarified that the video was produced purely for entertainment purposes. Despite this, the video is being misleadingly circulated online with a false claim. Claim An X user, Amrita Mishra (@Amrita_2121), shared the video on September 9, presenting it as another heart-wrenching incident from flood-hit Punjab. She claimed it showed a child in Punjab wading through flood water while pulling the body of his dead mother. The user wrote: "The most painful picture of humanity. The bodies floating in the floods are not just counting deaths, but also showing where our sensitivities have died. An innocent child kept pulling his dead mother's body out of the... perhaps he still had hopes that his mother would get up. But the biggest question is why the people standing around, instead of helping, kept making videos on their phones. This was not just the death of that child's mother... It was the death of humanity. Let us think... If we were in that place, what would we do?" Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered 3.2k views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here , respectively. The search via Google Lens also led the Desk to an X post made by a user named Ashish Patel (@patel_ashish01) on September 7, 2025. The user had shared the same image of a child pulling the body of a woman out of water, as seen in the viral video. However, he clarified that the video was merely a staged social media reel shot in Pilibhit, Uttar Pradesh, by a content creator named Aarti Gangwar. He added that the creator was making such videos by putting her own life at risk to generate content for social media, thereby spreading false rumours. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a combined image highlighting the visual similarities between the viral video and the image included in the social media post. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above inputs, the Desk conducted a Google search using the keyword "Aarti Gangwar." The search led to an Instagram account under the same name, where the user described herself as a digital creator. While scanning through the account, the Desk found that she had been tagged in a video shared by another Instagram user, 'swati_gangwar_pilibhit.' In that video, they described the viral clip of the child pulling a woman's body in water as a mere social media reel, clarifying that she was perfectly fine. She also mentioned that her entire family was present when the video was recorded. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a child pulling a woman's body in floodwater was staged and scripted. It was created by a social media influencer from Pilibhit, Uttar Pradesh, and had no connection to the recent floods in Punjab.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2022 video of Balen Shah taking oath as Kathmandu Mayor resurfaced with false claim; details inside
content: New Delhi, September 12 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid the ongoing Gen-Z protests in Nepal since September 8, a video showing Kathmandu Metropolitan City Mayor Balendra Shah, popularly known as Balen, taking an oath has gone viral on social media. Several users claimed the clip shows him being sworn in as the new Prime Minister of Nepal. The Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk examined the viral video and found the claim to be false. The footage is from May 2022, when Balen Shah took the oath of office after being elected as the mayor of Kathmandu Metropolitan City. There is no official report or credible media coverage of him being appointed as Nepal's Prime Minister. Claim: A video featuring Kathmandu Metropolitan City Mayor Balendra Shah (Balen) taking the oath was shared by a Facebook user 'शंखर क्षेत्री' on September 11, claiming that he has been appointed as the Prime Minister. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here , respectively. Upon further review of the search results, the Desk came across the same video, which was streamed on the official channel of AP1 HD TV on May 30, 2022. The title of the report read: "Kathmandu's newly elected Mayor Balen takes oath, what will be his first decision? | AP1HD". Balen is seen taking the oath at 1 hour, 6 minutes, 37 seconds into the video. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combined image that highlights the similarities between the content in the Facebook post and the video streamed on YouTube. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports covering the event and came across a report by a local media outlet, myRepublica, published on May 30, 2022. The cover image of the report matched the visuals seen in the recent Facebook post. At the same time, the report highlighted that the newly elected mayor of Kathmandu Metropolitan City (KMC), Balendra Shah (also known as Balen Shah), took the oath of office and secrecy. Shah took the oath of office and the oath of secrecy at a swearing-in ceremony held at City Hall. Chief Election Officer Raju Kumar Khatiwada administered the oath of office and distributed certificates to Mayor Balen. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk also conducted a customised keyword search to find reports that mention Mayor Balen Shah taking the oath as the Prime Minister of the country. Although there are speculations and questions surrounding the Prime Ministerial position, there has been no confirmation, and we did not find any reports that highlight it. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video featuring Mayor Balen Shah taking the oath dates back to 2022. This video shows him taking the oath after being elected mayor of Kathmandu Metropolitan City. There is no mention of Balen Shah being appointed or taking the oath as Prime Minister in any official media outlet.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2022 Republic Bharat news report of Nitish Kumar quitting BJP resurfaced with false claim
content: New Delhi, September 12 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid the ongoing political rumblings in Bihar ahead of the upcoming assembly polls (scheduled to be held this year), a video news clipping purportedly by the Republic Media Network, allegedly showing that Nitish Kumar had resigned as the Bihar Chief Minister, was recently shared on social media. The clipping purportedly stated that Kumar-led Janata Dal (United), which was in alliance with the Bharatiya Janata Party, had broken ties with the latter and switched allegiance to the Mahagathbandhan alliance in the state. The report also claimed that Kumar had submitted his resignation to Governor Phagu Chauhan and that a new government under the Mahagathbandhan alliance would be formed in Bihar, with Nitish Kumar as Chief Minister and RJD's Tejashwi Yadav as Deputy Chief Minister. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video dates back to August 2022 and is being shared on social media with a false claim, making it appear recent. The video is from the time when Kumar moved out of the alliance with the BJP in 2022 to forge ties with the opposition Mahagathbandhan. However, the coalition did not last long, and just months ahead of the 2024 Lok Sabha polls — in January 2024 — Kumar once again resigned as Chief Minister, breaking ties with the Mahagathbandhan and rejoining the BJP. Thus, an old and unrelated video depicting the 2022 political crisis in Bihar is being shared on social media as recent, accompanied by a false claim. Claim An Instagram handle with the username 'rajasthan__king_7773' shared a video news clipping, purportedly by the Republic Media Network, on September 7, highlighting a major political crisis in Bihar ahead of the 2025 assembly polls. The report stated that, in a significant political shuffle, Nitish Kumar-led JD(U) had broken its alliance with the BJP and that Kumar had resigned as Chief Minister of Bihar. It also claimed that the JD(U) would now switch sides to join the opposition Mahagathbandhan camp. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here , respectively. In the next step of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find reports elaborating on Nitish Kumar resigning as the Bihar Chief Minister ahead of the 2025 assembly elections. However, the search did not yield any credible news reports on such a development. Had the political change actually occurred in Bihar, it would have been extensively covered by the media. Next, as a part of the investigation, the Desk closely analysed the social media video clipping. The Desk found that it mentioned that Nitish Kumar had tendered his resignation to Bihar Governor Phagu Chauhan. Currently, news reports indicate that Arif Mohammed Khan is the current Governor of Bihar, having succeeded Phagu Chauhan, the former Governor. This confirmed that the development shown in the viral video is not recent but from the period when Chauhan was Governor. Taking cues from this, the Desk conducted another keyword search. I came across a report by The New Indian Express, which elaborated on Nitish Kumar's resignation as Bihar CM and submission of his resignation to Governor Phagu Chauhan. The report confirmed that this development dates back to August 2022, when Kumar broke ties with the BJP to form an alliance with the opposition Mahagathbandhan. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Additionally, the customised keyword search on Google also led the Desk to a video published by the official YouTube channel of Republic Bharat on August 9, 2022. Upon review, it was evident that the viral social media clip was taken from this 3-minute video. Here is the link and a screenshot of the video news report that has been published. Below is a combined image that shows the content in the viral video is the same as that of the YouTube channel. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the news clipping claiming Nitish Kumar had resigned as Bihar CM and quit the NDA ahead of the 2025 assembly polls was false. The video actually dates back to August 2022, when Nitish Kumar broke ties with the BJP to join the Mahagathbandhan.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old Sikkim video falsely shared as demonstration in Nepal in support of PM Modi; details inside
content: New Delhi, September 12 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan ): A video recently shared by multiple social media users claims to show a demonstration in violence-hit Nepal in support of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The footage allegedly depicts a large group of Nepali citizens marching with a banner of PM Modi and waving the Indian flag during a rally. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the video is unrelated to Nepal. It actually shows a procession organised by Sikkim's Limboo Tribe in May 2025 to welcome Prime Minister Modi as part of the 50th-anniversary celebrations of Sikkim's statehood. Although Modi's visit was cancelled due to inclement weather, he virtually addressed the celebrations from Bagdogra. The old video from Sikkim is now being falsely shared on social media, linking it to Nepal's ongoing unrest. Claim An X user named Kajal Kushwaha (@_KajalKushwaha) shared a video on September 10 allegedly depicting a rally held in support of Prime Minister Narendra Modi in violence-hit Nepal. The video purportedly showed a large group of Nepali citizens carrying a banner of PM Modi and waving the Indian flag. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing, the video had garnered 227.4k views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, to corroborate the claim made in the viral video, the Desk closely analysed it. The search results highlighted that the banner displayed by the crowd during the rally suggested the footage was from Sikkim, India, and not Nepal. The banner in the video carried a message stating that the Limboo Tribe of Sikkim organised the rally to welcome Prime Minister Narendra Modi to the state. "SIKKIMESE LIMBOO TRIBES WARMLY WELCOME PRIME MINISTER OF INDIA SHRI NARENDRA MODI JI TO THE STATE OF SIKKIM. SUKHIM YAKTHUNG SAPSOK SONGCHUMBHO," the message on the banner reads. Here is a screenshot highlighting this finding. Next, taking cues from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google. It came across a video posted on a Facebook page named Sukhim Yakthung Sapsok Songchumbho on May 30. The Desk found that the video posted on the Facebook page included visuals identical to those seen in the viral post. The caption confirmed that the video originated from the Indian state of Sikkim, not Nepal, which is currently marred by deadly unrest. The caption stated: "We, the Sikkimese Limboo Tribe, under the banner of Sukhim Yakthung Sapsok Songchumbho, were eagerly prepared to extend a warm welcome to the Hon'ble Prime Minister of India, Shri Narendra Modi, on his scheduled visit to Sikkim on 29th May 2025, to commemorate the 50th Anniversary of Sikkim's Statehood. Unfortunately, due to adverse weather conditions and low visibility, the Hon'ble Prime Minister could not land in Sikkim. However, he graciously addressed the people of Sikkim virtually from Bagdogra. On this significant occasion, we extend our heartfelt gratitude to the Hon'ble Prime Minister for his kind words and warm wishes for Sikkim and its people. Under his visionary leadership, we sincerely hope and pray that our beloved nation continues to grow and prosper." It further added: "We also take this opportunity to express our deep appreciation and thanks to our dynamic leader and the people's Chief Minister, Shri P.S. Tamang, for his unwavering support and continuous guidance." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a combined image highlighting the visual similarities between the viral video and the Facebook video posted by the page Sukhim Yakthung Sapsok Songchumbho. To further verify details about Prime Minister Modi's address on the 50th Anniversary of Sikkim's Statehood, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search on Google. This search led to a press release posted on the official website of the Government of Sikkim, which corroborated the details mentioned in the above social media post. It confirmed that Prime Minister Narendra Modi virtually greeted the people of Sikkim on the historic occasion of the state's golden jubilee of statehood, marking five decades since its integration into the Indian Union in 1975, in Nepali, one of the official languages and the lingua franca of the state. "Due to inclement weather conditions, the Prime Minister could not attend the grand celebration at Paljor Stadium in person. However, he conveyed his heartfelt greetings and assured the people of Sikkim that he would visit the State within the year," the press release stated. Here is the link to the official press release by the Government of Sikkim: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a video showing a procession organised by Sikkim's Limboo Tribe to welcome Prime Minister Narendra Modi to the state in May 2025 was falsely shared as a recent demonstration held in violence-stricken Nepal in support of PM Modi.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated image of BSP chief Mayawati's statue being constructed in Delhi falsely shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, September 12 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users have recently shared an image claiming it depicts a gigantic statue of Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) leader Mayawati under construction in Delhi. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found the image to be AI-generated and falsely shared as real to mislead viewers. Claim An X handle with the username BSP Voice (@BspVoice) shared, on September 11, a purported image showing a gigantic statue of BSP chief Mayawati being constructed in Delhi. Sharing the image, the user wrote: "A statue of Behenji (the BSP chief, popularly referred to as) is being constructed in Delhi." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing the story, the post had garnered 40k views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral social media image through Google Lens and found multiple social media accounts that shared the same image with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. Next, to verify whether such a statue was indeed being built in Delhi, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google. However, no credible news reports confirmed the development. Had such a massive project been real, mainstream media would have covered it extensively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk tried to find the authenticity of the image by closely analysing it. The Desk observed the image to consist of several inconsistencies. The entire image appeared unrealistic — for instance, it depicted a statue of Mayawati being constructed right in front of India Gate, which is implausible. Taking cues from these findings, the Desk ran the image through Hive Moderation, an AI-detection tool. The result indicated that 99% of the pictures contained AI-generated or deepfake content. Here is a screenshot highlighting the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the image showing a gigantic statue of BSP chief Mayawati being constructed in Delhi is AI-generated.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old protest video from Pakistan falsely shared as recent scenes from Nepal protests
content: New Delhi, September 15 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of a protester catching a tear gas canister mid-air and hurling it away is being widely circulated on social media, with users claiming it shows scenes from the ongoing unrest in Nepal. The Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated and found the claim to be false. The clip has been online since May 2022 and actually shows an incident in Pakistan, not Nepal. Claim: A video featuring a protester catching a tear gas canister mid-air and throwing it away was shared by a Facebook user, 'Revolutio Hail', on September 10, claiming that the incident happened in Nepal. "The boy caught the tear gas shell like a cricket ball and threw it away. This video is viral in Nepal. #Nepalprotest," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across the video uploaded by a Facebook user in May 2022. The post claimed that the visuals were from Pakistan. The timeline and the details mentioned in the video clarify that it predates the recent unrest in Nepal. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the recent video shared on social media and the visuals seen in the old Facebook post. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across another Facebook post by 'Gulf Today' published on May 26, 2022. The caption of the post mentioned that a Pakistani protester caught a teargas canister and threw it back at the police. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Moreover, in the videos, the name 'Total PARCO' is visible on a fuel station on the left side of the road. Total PARCO in Pakistan refers to Total PARCO Pakistan Limited (TPPL), a joint venture between TotalEnergies and Pak-Arab Refinery Limited (PARCO), which operates fuel stations across Pakistan. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video dates back to at least May 2022, and is from Pakistan and not Nepal.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video from Bangladesh shared as Punjab flood relief effort
content: New Delhi, September 15 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing Muslim men, identifiable by their skullcaps, wading through floodwaters with food, was shared by several social media users. Those sharing the claim that it depicts relief efforts during the recent floods in Punjab. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video is not from Punjab. It is an old video from Bangladesh showing madrassa students helping local flood-hit communities in August 2024. The post was shared with a false claim on social media. Claim A video showing Muslim men, identifiable by their skullcaps, wading through floodwaters with food was shared by a YouTube user, 'QurHub,' on September 8, claiming that it depicts relief efforts during the recent Punjab floods. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here , respectively. Upon further review of the search results, the Desk came across the same video, which was uploaded to a YouTube channel called 'Protidiner Bangladesh' on August 25, 2024. The timeline of the video clarifies that it is not recent and does not depict the current flood situation in Punjab. The title of the video read: "Madrasah students came forward to meet the needs of the country | Madrasah Student | Flood Food | PBNews" Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the social media post and the YouTube video. Another video was uploaded to the YouTube page of a user, 'Ahlehadeeth Andolon Bangladesh,' on August 26, 2024, identifying it as relief work in the country amid floods in Feni. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk found that the video does not show Muslim men helping victims of the Punjab floods. It is from Bangladesh that madrasa students provided food aid to their local community.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Social media post falsely claims Karnataka road tragedy was deliberate attack by Muslim man; details inside
content: New Delhi, September 15 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media post, shared along with visuals of the recent tragic road accident in Karnataka's Hassan district that claimed at least 10 lives, alleged that the accused arrested in connection with the case belonged to the Muslim community. The post further contended that the truck driver, purportedly identified as Mohammed Firoz, had deliberately rammed into people participating in a Ganesh idol immersion procession on September 12 in Hassan district. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found this communal claim to be false. The Desk confirmed that the prime accused booked in the case is a truck driver named Bhuvanesh, and not someone named Mohammed Firoz. Media reports also stated that an FIR has been registered against the accused, and further investigation into the incident is underway. A video of the Hassan accident is thus being falsely shared online with a communal spin. Claim On September 13, an X user with the handle @rssbihar9mm shared a social media post alleging that the accused booked by Hassan Police in connection with the September 12 accident belonged to the Muslim faith. The user claimed that the truck driver who rammed into a group of people participating in a Ganesh idol immersion procession in Hassan district was identified as Mohammed Firoz and that the act may have been deliberate. The post read: "Once again, an Islamic terrorist attack! In Hassan district of Karnataka, India, a truck driver named Mohammad Firoz ran over a crowd of Hindus heading for Ganpati immersion with his truck, resulting in the deaths of at least 8 Hindus and injuring more than 18 others." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, to verify the details of the incident and the identity of the accused, the Desk conducted a customised Google keyword search related to the Hassan road tragedy. The search led to a report published by Deccan Herald on September 14, which identified the accused as Bhuvanesh, not Mohammed Firoz. The report stated that an FIR had been filed at Gorur police station against truck driver Bhuvanesh, who rammed into a Ganesh immersion procession around 8:30 pm on September 12. "The truck, moving from Hassan to Holenarsipur, hit a motorbike and swerved to the right, hitting the median before ploughing into the procession moving from Holenarsipur towards Hassan. Nine of the deceased were in the procession. Bike rider Prabhakar also died. Bhuvanesh, a native of Hassan district, who was beaten up by the public, is also being treated at the hospital under police custody," the report added. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. In the subsequent part of the investigation, to further re-verify that the truck driver arrested in connection with the Hassan tragedy does not belong to the Muslim community and has been identified as Bhuvanesh only, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search on Google to check whether Karnataka Police had issued any statement or video byte regarding the case. The search led the Desk to a video byte given by Hassan Superintendent of Police Mohammad Sujeetha, who, speaking to IANS, reiterated that the prime accused in the tragic road incident is driver Bhuvanesh. She said: "The entire scene of the accident is being subjected to forensic examination to determine whether there were any mechanical failures or other factors involved." Here is the link and archive link to the video, along with a screenshot: Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk carried out further searches using the information gathered above, which led it to the FIR copy filed by Karnataka Police in connection with the incident. The FIR also identified the accused as Bhuvanesh, and not as Mohammed Firoz. Here is the link to the FIR copy. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim giving the Hassan road tragedy a communal colour by identifying the accused as a Muslim man named Mohammed Firoz is false. The driver has been confirmed as Bhuvanesh, a resident of Hassan district.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old Nevada shooting video falsely linked to Charlie Kirk's assassination
content: New Delhi, September 16 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a man being carried by a group of people was shared on social media, with users claiming it depicts the suspect involved in the assassination of Charlie Kirk fleeing the scene. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the footage and found it to be old and unrelated. The video actually shows a man suspected of shooting six people at Reno's Grand Sierra Resort in Nevada. It is being falsely circulated on social media in connection with Kirk's killing. Charlie Kirk was shot dead while speaking at an open-air event organised by Turning Point USA, the organisation he co-founded, at Utah Valley University. Claim: A video showing a man being carried by a group of people was shared by an X user, '@JackStr42679640', on September 12, claiming that he was the suspect in Charlie Kirk's murder who was running from the scene. "New video surfaces showing Charlie Kirk's real killer escaping after the shooting…," read the post's caption. The post garnered 152.7k views on social media. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post by '@atensnut' on July 29, 2025, which clarifies that the video predates the killing of Charlie Kirk. The post's caption highlighted that it shows the shooting at the Casino in Reno, Nevada. "Shooting at Casino in Reno, Nevada. Several people were shot, and some fatally. Video of the suspect running away. He is now in custody," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combined image highlighting the similarities between the content seen in the recent social media post and the above X post. Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across an Instagram post dated July 30, 2025. The caption of the post highlighted that the Sparks Police Department has confirmed that the viral video circulating on social media is of the man suspected of shooting six people at Reno's Grand Sierra Resort. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video pre-dates Kirk's assassination. The video shows a man suspected of shooting six people at Reno's Grand Sierra Resort. The video was shared with a false claim on social media.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Viral video of Anurag Thakur, Jay Shah and Pakistan's Shahid Afridi is not from Asia Cup 2025; details inside
content: New Delhi, September 16 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): As calls to boycott the India-Pakistan clash grew louder following the Pahalgam terror attack and Operation Sindoor, the two sides still faced each other in the Asia Cup on September 14, 2025, where India secured a seven-wicket victory. Amid this backdrop, a video surfaced on social media showing BJP leader Anurag Thakur, ICC chairman Jay Shah, and former Pakistani cricketer Shahid Afridi seated together during an India-Pakistan match. Users sharing the clip claimed it was from the Asia Cup 2025 encounter. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found that the video was not from the ongoing Asia Cup. It is an old clip from the Champions Trophy match held in February 2025. The video is now being circulated with a false claim on social media. Claim A video from a stadium featuring BJP leader Anurag Thakur, ICC chairman Jay Shah, and former Pakistani cricketer Shahid Afridi was shared by an X user '@RealWahidaAFG' on September 14, claiming that they were watching the India-Pakistan Asia Cup 2025 match. "Anurag Thakur, Jay Shah, and Shahid Afridi are in the stadium watching the India-Pakistan match like high school friends. But some Twitter patriots want to boycott the game against Pakistan. #INDvPAK #AsiaCup," read the post's caption. The post clocked 173.1k views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here Upon careful analysis of the video, the Desk found "Champions Trophy" banners in the background, which do not belong to the Asia Cup match on September 14, 2025. Below is a screenshot that illustrates this point. Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk ran the keyframes through Reverse Image Search and found the same video uploaded by a user on YouTube Shorts on February 26, 2025. The timeline of the video clarifies that it is not recent and has been on the internet at least since February. "Shahid Afridi and Jay Shah watched the Pakistan vs India match together at the Dubai Stadium," read the description of the video. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the contents seen in the recent social media post and YouTube Shorts. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find reports that highlighted the incident, and came across a report by Asianet News published on February 24, 2025. The report mentioned that Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MP and Union Minister Anurag Thakur was spotted sitting with former Pakistan captain Shahid Afridi during the Champions Trophy 2025 clash between the two arch-rivals at the Dubai International Stadium "IND vs PAK, Champions Trophy: Anurag Thakur spotted with Shahid Afridi, Netizens react after pic goes viral," read the Headline of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video featuring BJP leader Anurag Thakur, ICC chairman Jay Shah, and former Pakistani cricketer Shahid Afridi watching the cricket match is an old clip from the Champions Trophy in February 2025.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video showing escalator collapse at mall falsely shared as real incident from Mysuru; details inside
content: New Delhi, September 16 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently shared on social media claims to show several people dying after an escalator collapsed at BM Habitat Mall in Mysuru, Karnataka. The video showed multiple escalators inside the mall suddenly collapsing, causing people travelling on them to fall and die. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated and found the video to be AI-generated and falsely shared as real to mislead viewers. Claim An X user, Preeti Mishra (@learning45378), shared a video on September 11 that purportedly showed a tragic accident at Mysuru's BM Habitat Mall. The footage depicted multiple escalators inside the mall suddenly collapsing, leading to people falling to their deaths. "Escalators collapsed and many people died at the BM Habitat Mall, Mysore," the user captioned the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered more than 3,000 views) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here , respectively. The search result via Google Lens also led the Desk to a video posted on the YouTube channel Disaster Strucks on June 10. The Desk found that the video posted by the channel was identical to the one circulating on social media. However, the details shared by the YouTube creator clearly stated that it was AI-generated. "This is AI art, generated by me," the channel owner, known for sharing AI-generated content, mentioned in the video description. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a combined image highlighting the visual similarities between the viral video and the YouTube video. In the next step, taking cues from the findings above, the Desk ran the viral video through Hive Moderation, an AI-detection tool. The results indicated that 99% of the footage contained AI-generated or deepfake content. Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to check if any such incident had occurred at Mysuru's BM Habitat Mall. The search led the Desk to a report published by The Indian Express on September 9, 2025, which described a tragic but unrelated accident at the same mall. According to the report, two men died after falling from a height inside the shopping mall. One technician, identified as Sunil (30), slipped while trying to remove an advertisement board from the top floor. Another man, Chandru, a visitor, also died while attempting to save him. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing multiple escalators collapsing at Mysuru's BM Habitat Mall, resulting in multiple casualties, was AI-generated.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old Maldives video falsely shared as Nepal protesters chanting for PM Modi
content: New Delhi, September 16 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): As social media buzzed with multiple videos capturing the gruesome visuals of vandalism reported across various parts of Nepal during one of the deadliest episodes of unrest the country has witnessed in years, a video depicting a large group of people chanting slogans in support of Prime Minister Narendra Modi recently surfaced online. Users claimed the footage was from Nepal, where protesters were allegedly shouting "Narendra Modi Zindabad" slogans. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found the video to be unrelated to Nepal. It was originally recorded during PM Modi's visit to the Dhoshimeyna Building in Malé, Maldives, in July 2025, alongside Maldivian President Mohammed Muizzu. During the visit, citizens welcomed PM Modi and chanted "Modi Zindabad" slogans as he arrived. An old and unrelated video from the Maldives was thus misleadingly shared on social media, linking it to the ongoing unrest in Nepal. Claim A Facebook user named Modibhakt Heeralal Singh shared a video on September 11, purportedly showing a demonstration in violence-hit Nepal. The video depicted a large group of people chanting slogans in support of Prime Minister Narendra Modi in violence-stricken Nepal. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video garnered 50k likes and 7.5k shares) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here , respectively. The search results also led the Desk to a video shared by the official X handle of TV9 Marathi on July 25, 2025. The footage matched the viral video but was reported as being from the Maldives during PM Modi's visit, not Nepal. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. A combined image highlighted the visual similarities between the social media video and the footage posted by TV9 Marathi. Additionally, the Desk also found the same visuals uploaded by The Indian Express' YouTube channel, which confirmed that the video was from the Maldives. The portal shared it with the caption: "Narendra Modi Zindabad echoes in Malé as PM Modi receives warm welcome." Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a Jansatta report published on July 25, 2025, which confirmed that the video was taken when PM Modi arrived to inaugurate the Dhoshimeyna Building, the newly built Maldivian Ministry of Defence headquarters in Malé. Citizens welcomed him with chants of "Narendra Modi Zindabad." Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing people chanting "Narendra Modi Zindabad" is from the Maldives, not Nepal.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Fake circular claims ITR deadline extended to Sept 30; Sept 16 was the official last date
content: New Delhi, September 17 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A circular allegedly issued by the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT), claiming that the deadline for filing income tax returns (ITRs) for the assessment year 2024–25 had been extended to September 30, 2025, was shared widely on social media, with many users believing it to be genuine. The Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found the circular to be fake and fabricated. No such extension has been announced. According to an official CBDT press release dated May 27, 2025, the ITR filing deadline was initially extended from July 31 to September 15, 2025. Later, on September 15, the CBDT granted a one-day extension, setting the final deadline as September 16, 2025. Claim: On September 14, X user 'Rohit Agarwal' shared a circular allegedly attributed to the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT), claiming an extension of the ITR filing deadline for the assessment year 2024–25 to September 30, 2025. The post clocked 10k views on social media. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation As part of the investigation, the Desk first checked the website and social media handles of the Income Tax Department but found no notification or circular. Here is the link to the website, and here is the link to the social media handle. However, the Income Tax Department on its official X handle posted a circular stating that on September 15, 2025, the CBDT extended the deadline only until September 16, 2025. At the time of writing this article, nothing was mentioned regarding a further extension until September 30. Here is the link to the X post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk then carefully analysed the circular being shared on social media and found several discrepancies in it that highlighted it might be fabricated and fake. For instance, the subject line reads "15th" instead of "15th." The body mentions "14th September" as the current deadline. Below is a screenshot that highlights the same issue. The Desk then accessed the official Press Release by the CBDT, published on May 27, 2025, which extended the filing deadline from July 31 to September 15, 2025. Here is the link to the release. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the circular claiming that the ITR filing deadline has been extended to September 30, 2025, is fake. The official extension is only until September 16, 2025.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old Sri Lanka video falsely shared to claim Hindu man rescued girl from Muslim kidnappers; details inside
content: New Delhi, September 17 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a man forcefully dragging a girl into a car, while another individual rushed forward to stop him in an attempt to save the girl, was recently shared on social media. Users claimed the video showed the girl being kidnapped by two Muslim youths named Afroz and Imran, but that she was rescued by a Hindu man named Harshvardhan, who risked his life despite not knowing her. In its investigation, however, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false. The incident captured in the video took place in Sri Lanka in January, where a teenage girl was abducted over a personal dispute but was later rescued by the Sri Lankan police. The man who intervened to help the girl was not a Hindu named Harshvardhan, as claimed. According to media reports, he was identified as 25-year-old Mohamed Isadeen Arshad Ahmed, who was later commended for his bravery in attempting to rescue the schoolgirl from being abducted in Davulagala. An old and unrelated video from Sri Lanka was falsely shared on social media with a communal and misleading claim. Claim An X handle with the username Baba Banaras (@RealBababanaras) shared on September 11 a video allegedly showing a Hindu man named Harshvardhan saving a girl named Ayesha from being kidnapped by two Muslim youths, identified as Afroz and Imran. The video showed a man in a T-shirt pushing the girl into a car, only to be interrupted by another man, said to be Harshvardhan, who ran towards the car to save her. "He is a real hero. Afroz and Imran were kidnapping a girl named Ayesha. A boy named Harshvardhan was passing by. To save her, he risked his life and saved the girl whom he did not even know. This is the eternal Hindu tradition. Harshvardhan is injured but out of danger. Salute," the user wrote while sharing the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing, the video had garnered 1.8 million views and 33,000 likes) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here , respectively. The search also led the Desk to a video posted on the YouTube channel of the Sri Lanka–based news portal Colombo Gazette on January 12, 2025, where the visuals of a girl being abducted in broad daylight matched exactly with those in the viral video. However, the portal did not report any communal links to the incident. It stated that the abduction took place in Gelioya, Sri Lanka, where a teenage girl was abducted over a personal dispute. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Below is a combined image highlighting the visual similarities between the viral video and the video included in the news report. While the report elaborated on the incident of a girl being forcefully dragged into a van, it did not mention the identity of the other individual seen in the video running towards the van in an attempt to save her. Taking cues from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a post shared by the Facebook page of Colombo Gazette on January 13. The post stated that the teenage girl abducted in Gelioya had been found by police in Ampara two days after the incident. "A teenage girl who was abducted in broad daylight on the street in Gelioya, Kandy, on Saturday has been found in Ampara, and the main suspect has been arrested. The police stated that the girl was found with the main suspect while they were preparing to board a bus from Ampara to Kandy. The suspect, a relative of the girl, admitted to committing the crime," the report added. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Additionally, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search on Google to find reports or posts that elaborated on the identity of the individual seen in the video running towards the van in an attempt to save the girl. The search led the Desk to a post shared by the official account of the Sri Lanka–based news portal NewswireLK on January 13, 2025. The post identified the man as 25-year-old Mohamed Isadeen Arshad Ahmed, not a Hindu man named Harshvardhan as claimed in the social media post. "Sri Lanka Police has commended 25-year-old Mohamed Isadeen Arshad Ahmed for his bravery in attempting to rescue a schoolgirl from being abducted in Davulagala," the post read. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video, which was falsely shared as an incident involving two Muslim youths and a Hindu man named Harshvardhan, is actually from Sri Lanka. The video depicts the abduction of a teenage girl over a personal dispute in Gelioya earlier in January 2025, and the man attempting to rescue her has been identified as 25-year-old Mohamed Isadeen Arshad Ahmed, not Harshvardhan.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Fake post claims Ricky Ponting called India 'big loser' after Asia Cup 2025; details inside
content: New Delhi, September 17 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media post allegedly quoting former Australian cricketer Ricky Ponting claimed that he called India the "big loser" for refusing to shake hands with Pakistan players after their Asia Cup 2025 match. The purported statement, attributed to an interview on Sky Sports, went viral on several social media platforms. The Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found it to be fake. Ponting did not make any such remarks. On his official Instagram account, the cricketer clarified that the comments being circulated online were entirely false and that he had made no public statement about the Asia Cup 2025. The post was shared to mislead the viewers Claim: An X user's 'Pro Cricket' on September 15, shared a purported statement allegedly attributed to former Australian cricketer Ricky Ponting about India's behaviour in the recent Asia Cup, claiming that he called Indian players the "big losers" for refusing to shake hands with Pakistan players after their Asia Cup 2025 match. "Ponting On SkySports: This match will be remembered forever with India as the big loser. The way the Pakistani team wanted to shake hands at the end has immortalised them as champions of the gentleman's game with India as the perpetual sore loser," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation As part of the investigation, the Desk first conducted a customised keyword search to determine if Ponting had made any such remarks. However, our search did not reveal any reports that carried his statement. To verify the claim, we then scanned through Sky Sports Cricket's official YouTube and social media handles to find the interview, but they did not post or carry any such interview. Given the gravity of the statement and the popularity of Ricky Ponting, such a statement would have been widely covered. Here is the link to YouTube, and here is the link to their X handle. Next, the Desk then looked through the social media handles and came across a post on his official Instagram account, where he clarified that he had not made any statements and indeed had made no public comments about the Asia Cup at all. "I am aware of certain comments being attributed to me on social media. Please know that I categorically did not make those statements and indeed have made no public comment about the Asia Cup at all," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim that Ricky Ponting called India a "big loser" over the Asia Cup handshake is false. Ponting clarified that he never made any such remarks.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video from Ahmedabad falsely shared as BJP flags being raised in China during PM Modi's visit
content: New Delhi, September 17 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users have recently shared a video claiming it shows Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) flags being raised in China to welcome Prime Minister Narendra Modi during his recent visit to the country. The video allegedly showed PM Modi waving at a crowd during a roadshow in China, with BJP flags visible in the background. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found the video to be unrelated to PM Modi's visit to China. The footage was originally from his roadshow in Ahmedabad in August 2025. An old and unrelated video from Ahmedabad was thus falsely shared as footage from PM Modi's China visit. Claim An Instagram handle with the username __modi__jee__143 shared a video on September 4, allegedly showing BJP flags being raised in China to welcome Prime Minister Narendra Modi during his recent visit to the country. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here , respectively. The search also led the Desk to a video shared on the official YouTube channel of Prime Minister Narendra Modi on August 25. The video exactly matched the one circulating on social media. However, the description clarified that it was from Ahmedabad during his official visit to the city earlier in August 2025. "Prime Minister Narendra Modi held a vibrant roadshow in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. The PM was welcomed by the citizens in large numbers," the description stated. Here is the link and archive link to the video, along with a screenshot: Below is a combined image highlighting the visual similarities between the viral video and the one shared on PM Modi's official YouTube channel. Additionally, the Google Lens search also led the Desk to the same video, which was posted by several media portals and political figures from Gujarat, where it was clearly described as being from Ahmedabad, not China. Two such examples can be seen here and here , with their archived versions available here and here . In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find details related to PM Modi's visit to Gujarat earlier in August 2025. The search result led the Desk to a press release issued by the Prime Minister's office on August 24, whereby it elaborately described PM Modi's two-day visit to Gujarat on 25th-26th August, 2025. The report mentioned that, during the visit, the Prime Minister also inaugurated and laid the foundation stone for multiple development projects worth Rs 5,400 crores, dedicating them to the nation. Here is the link to the press release issued by the Prime Minister's office. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video claiming to show BJP flags being raised in China to welcome Prime Minister Narendra Modi is misleading. The video is not from China but from Ahmedabad, Gujarat, during PM Modi's roadshow in August 2025. An unrelated video was falsely shared in the name of his recent visit to China.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Hisar statue removal misshared as 'man's body in pillar' claim; details inside
content: New Delhi, September 18 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video seemingly showing the torso of a man cemented inside a pillar after it was broken open was recently shared on social media. Users claimed it depicted a real incident where a man's body was discovered inside a cemented pillar. In its investigation, however, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false. The video actually showed a statue of an individual named Kumbharam, who his family described as a soldier of the Azad Hind Fauj. The statue was removed in Hisar's Arya Nagar following protests from villagers, who argued that Kumbharam was not part of the Azad Hind Fauj. The clip has no connection to any real incident of a man being cemented inside a pillar. An unrelated video from Hisar was misleadingly shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An X handle with the username @Ansari5k shared a video on September 16, purportedly showing the dead body of a man cemented inside a pillar. The footage allegedly showed the upper body of the deceased visible after the pillar was broken using construction machines. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing the story, the video had garnered 566k views and 3.2k likes.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here , respectively. The search also led the Desk to a video posted on the Instagram handle Ajit Singh (@ajit9823singh) on September 11, 2025. The visuals (showing the torso of an individual visible after the pillar was broken) matched those in the viral video. However, details accompanying the footage revealed that it depicted an incident from Arya Nagar in Hisar, where the statue of a freedom fighter had been removed. And not that it showed a body of a man cemented inside a pillar was found. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a combined image highlighting the visual similarities between the viral video and the video shared by the Instagram handle. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above inputs, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google. The search led to a report published by Amar Ujala on September 11, 2025, which carried visuals similar to those seen in the viral video. The report clarified that the footage showed the statue of an individual named Kumbharam—described by his family as a soldier of the Azad Hind Fauj—being removed following protests by villagers. It did not show a man's body cemented in a pillar. The report added that while Kumbharam's family described him as a soldier of the Azad Hind Fauj, villagers disputed this claim. At their request, the district administration, along with police, removed the statue earlier last week. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Below is a combined image highlighting the visual similarities between the viral video and the video included in the news report. Additionally, a customised keyword search also led the Desk to a report published by Dainik Jagran, which confirmed that the video depicted the removal of Kumbharam's statue in Arya Nagar. It did not show any incident of a man found cemented inside a pillar. Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video claiming to show a man's body cemented inside a pillar is misleading. The footage actually shows the removal of a statue of Kumbharam in Hisar's Arya Nagar following protests by villagers.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old Kolkata protest video falsely linked to PM Modi's Manipur visit
content: New Delhi, September 18 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Following Prime Minister Narendra Modi's recent visit to Manipur, a video featuring a large group of people walking under a foot-over-bridge with slogans of 'Vote Chor, Gaddi chod' was shared by several social media users. Those sharing the video claim that it shows people of Manipur protesting against the PM for alleged 'Vote Chori' However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video is not recent but from April, when a protest was held in Kolkata against the Waqf (Amendment) Act. It is not related to Manipur or PM Modi's visit. Moreover, a day after Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Manipur, in a first after ethnic clashes broke out in the state, a mob clashed with security forces in Churachandpur over the arrest of two persons for allegedly vandalising the banners and cutouts of the prime minister. Claim: A video featuring a large group of people walking under a foot-over-bridge with slogans of 'Vote Chor, Gaddi chod', was shared by a Facebook user 'अंसारी मनुवर' on September 14, claiming that the video shows people of Manipur protesting against PM Modi for 'Vote Chori'. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here Upon further review of the search results, the Desk came across the same video, uploaded by an Instagram user named 'trisharooy' on April 14. The description of the post highlighted that the location was Kolkata and the protest was against the Waqf Amendment Bill. The available information and timeline clarify that the video is not recent and was not recorded in Manipur, but rather in Kolkata, and pertains to the Waqf Amendment Bill. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the contents seen in the recent social media post and the Instagram post. Taking a cue from the above finding, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search to find relevant media reports and came across a report by the Times of India published on April 16. The report mentioned that while Bhangar turned into a battlefield as police stopped protesters from heading to Kolkata for the rally against the new Waqf law, around 5,000-odd ISF supporters still managed to dodge cops and reach. It also contained visuals similar to those seen in the social media post. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk carefully analysed the video and found that the audio seems to be overlaid or edited to make it sound like a vote chori protest. Next, another search on Google did not lead the Desk to any credible report indicating that a protest with the said slogans took place during PM Modi's visit to Manipur in September 2025. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video is not recent, but from April, when a protest was held in Kolkata against the Waqf (Amendment) Act.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video clip from Bihar rally shared to falsely claim 'PM Modi promised free electricity to all'
content: New Delhi, September 18 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressing a public rally is being shared on social media with the claim that he announced free electricity for the people. The Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found the claim to be misleading. Modi did not announce free electricity. The viral clip is from a rally he addressed in May 2024, where he spoke about the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana. Under the scheme, households installing rooftop solar panels can reduce their electricity bills to zero, with the government also purchasing surplus power.
