Claim: A video featuring PM Modi addressing a public rally was shared by an Instagram user 'sindhusaab' on September 10, claiming that during his speech, he announced free electricity for the people. "We have decided that your electricity bill will be zero. Till now, you were paying the electricity bill; now the government will give that money," says PM Modi in the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here As part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports that cite PM Modi's announcement; however, there were no credible reports covering his statements. Given the seriousness of the matter, such a remark would have been covered by leading news portals. To verify the claim, the Desk then ran the keyframes of the video through a Reverse Image Search and came across the full version of the video, which was uploaded on PM Modi's official YouTube channel on May 25, 2024. According to the video description, PM Modi was addressing a rally in Patna, Bihar. The timeline of the video clarifies that the video is not recent. At 44:48 in the same video, the Prime Minister can be heard saying, "This is a scheme that will ensure you have no problems throughout your life. Modi has decided that your electricity bill should be zero. Zero electricity bill. We have launched the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana. Solar panels will be installed on the rooftops. This will generate electricity. You will use that electricity for free as needed, and the government will purchase any excess electricity and compensate you for it. To achieve this, Modi will provide Rs 75,000 to every family for the installation of solar panels. You can register yourself online right now." Here is the link , and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Prime Minister Narendra Modi has not announced free electricity. At his rally, he had promised zero electricity bills if solar panels were installed under the "PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana."

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: This video claiming Punjabi youths were "sold" by Indian govt to Russia is false; details inside
content: New Delhi, September 19 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a group of young men in military fatigues claiming they were stranded in Russia and forced to join the frontline in the war against Ukraine was recently shared on social media. Users alleged that these men, reportedly from Punjab, had been "sold" by the Indian government to the Russian Army. In its investigation, however, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false. The video actually shows a group of Indians who were duped by job agents on the pretext of studying or working in Russia and later coerced into fighting in the war. The Indian government has been actively working to secure the safe return of all stranded Indian nationals from Russia. Claim An X handle with the username Pak warrior (@pak_warrior12) shared on September 15 a video showing a group of individuals from Punjab describing their plight of being stranded in Russia and coerced into joining the Russian Army. Users claimed these youths were from Punjab and had allegedly been sold to the Russian Army by the Indian government to fight in the war against Ukraine. "India's government and military deceived innocent Punjabi youth with job offers in Russia, only to sell them into the Russian Army and send them to the frontlines against Ukraine. A shameless betrayal by the Indian state and its forces," the user shared the video with caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens results also led the Desk to a video published by news portal Mojo Story on its official X handle on September 11. The video showed the same visuals of youths stranded in Russia as seen in the viral clip. However, the accompanying details revealed that the men were Indians who had moved to Russia for study or work but were deceived and coerced into joining the Russian Army. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a combined image highlighting the visual similarities between the viral video and the one shared by the news portal: Additionally, the Google Lens search led the Desk to a Hindustan Times report published on September 17, 2025. The keyframe from the viral video matched the feature image of the report, which covered the plight of Indians stranded in Russia. The report identified two of the individuals in the video as Samarjeet Singh from Ludhiana and Bhuta Singh from Moga. It also carried statements from their families. Samarjeet Singh's father, Charanjeet Singh, said his son had left for Russia in July with the help of a local agent, expecting to study and work part-time in construction, but "we never thought he would be forced into a war." Similarly, Bhuta Singh's sister, Karamjit Kaur, stated that he had travelled to Russia in October 2024 to pursue a language course and take on part-time jobs. Still, the family only became aware of his plight after his videos went viral. The report further detailed how these individuals had travelled on student visas, were promised other jobs later, but were eventually trapped and "recruited" into the Russian Army. At no point did the report state that they were "sold" by the Indian government. Instead, it confirmed that they had been duped by job agents who facilitated their travel to Russia. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: The Desk also conducted a customised keyword search to check whether the Indian government had taken any action regarding the plight of these youths. The search led to a statement by Ministry of External Affairs Spokesperson Randheer Jaiswal, who strongly urged Indians to stay away from offers to join the Russian Army. He said: "We have seen reports about Indian nationals having been recruited recently into the Russian army. The government has, on several occasions over the past year, underlined the risks and dangers inherent in this course of action and cautioned Indian citizens accordingly. We have also taken up the matter with Russian authorities, both in Delhi and Moscow, asking that this practice be ended and that our nationals be released. We are also in touch with the families of the affected Indian citizens." Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video does not show Punjabi youths being "sold" to the Russian Army by the Indian government. Instead, it shows Indians who were duped by job agents with promises of study or work opportunities in Russia but were later coerced into joining the war. The Indian government has clarified its stance, warned citizens against such risks, and is actively working to bring back those stranded in Russia.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of PM Modi's roadshow in Bihar falsely shared claiming he visited Nepal amid unrest
content: New Delhi, September 19 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a large group of people showering flower petals at Prime Minister Narendra Modi's convoy was recently shared on social media with the claim that it depicted the welcome he received on his arrival in Nepal's Pokhara after the recent unrest. The video allegedly showed PM Modi waving at the crowd gathered to welcome him. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found that the video was unrelated to Nepal. It originally showed a roadshow held by PM Modi in Bihar in May 2025. An old and unrelated video of PM Modi holding a roadshow in Bihar was falsely shared as showing him being welcomed in Nepal amid the recent unrest. Claim An Instagram user, Rohit Rof, shared a video on September 13, purportedly showing Prime Minister Narendra Modi's arrival in Nepal's Pokhara amid the unrest. The footage allegedly showed PM Modi waving at the crowd gathered to welcome him. "PM Modi arrives in Pokhara, Nepal," the overlay text on the video reads. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing, the video had garnered 14,750 likes) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes. The Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search result via Google Lens also led the Desk to a video posted on an Instagram handle named rtrracinghorse. The video shared by this handle exactly matched the one seen in the viral post. However, the details provided alongside it revealed that the footage dated back to May 30, during PM Modi's visit to Patna. The video was not linked to any visit by PM Modi to Nepal after the unrest. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a combined image highlighting the visual similarities between the viral video and the one shared by the Instagram handle. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to check if the Prime Minister had undertaken any visits to Bihar around the end of May, during which he held a roadshow. The search led to a video posted on the official YouTube channel of Narendra Modi, which confirmed that the Prime Minister had a roadshow in Bihar in May 2025. Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the video shared on PM Modi's official YouTube channel. The analysis found multiple similarities between the visuals in the YouTube video and those in the viral post. For example, visuals showing a group of officials in white attire walking near the Prime Minister's car were present in both the viral video and the YouTube video, confirming that the footage was from Bihar and not Nepal. Here is the link and archive link to the video, along with a screenshot: Below is a combined image highlighting the visual similarities found in the viral video and the one shared by PM Modi's official YouTube channel. In the subsequent part of the investigation, the Desk also conducted a customised keyword search on Google to check whether PM Modi had visited, or would be visiting, Nepal in the coming days after the formation of the new government led by interim Prime Minister Sushila Karki. The search did not lead to any credible news reports confirming such a visit. Had such a development occurred, it would have been widely reported by the media. The search, however, led the Desk to a report published by NDTV on September 17, which stated that in her first foreign outreach, Nepal's interim Prime Minister Sushila Karki would hold a telephonic conversation with PM Modi that day. "This will be Ms Karki's first official diplomatic engagement with any head of government since assuming office on September 12, signalling that India remains Kathmandu's foremost foreign policy priority," the report noted. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing PM Modi's roadshow in Patna, Bihar, was falsely shared as evidence of him making an official visit to Nepal amid the recent unrest.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of man dancing to Bollywood song falsely linked to CJI BR Gavai; details inside
content: New Delhi, September 19 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing an elderly man wearing spectacles and dancing to a Bollywood number, apparently at a club, was recently shared on social media. Users claimed that the man in the video was Chief Justice of India BR Gavai. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found it to be false. A visual comparison of photographs of the Chief Justice with those of the man seen dancing confirmed that they are two different individuals. An unrelated video of a man dancing at a club was thus falsely linked to the Chief Justice of India. Claim An X handle with the username @Crazy_Sambha shared a video on September 18, claiming that the individual dancing in the clip to a Bollywood number was the sitting Chief Justice of India, BR Gavai. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video garnered 143.4k views and 3.5k likes) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here , respectively. In the next stage of the investigation, to verify whether the individual in the viral video was indeed BR Gavai, the Desk carefully analysed the visuals. A comparison of the images of Chief Justice of India BR Gavai with that of the man seen dancing clearly showed they are two different individuals. Below is a combined image highlighting the differences between the two. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of an elderly individual dancing to a Bollywood number was falsely linked to the Chief Justice of India.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old photo of former PM Manmohan Singh with Pakistan cricket team falsely linked to 26/11 aftermath
content: New Delhi, September 19 (Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): As calls to boycott the India-Pakistan clash grew louder following the Pahalgam terror attack and Operation Sindoor, the two sides still faced each other in the Asia Cup on September 14, 2025, where India secured a seven-wicket victory. Amid this backdrop, a picture of former Prime Minister Dr Manmohan Singh with the Pakistan cricket team began circulating on social media, with the claim that he had invited the team to India soon after the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks. The Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false. The image is from March 30, 2011, when Dr Manmohan Singh and then Pakistan PM Yousuf Raza Gilani met the Pakistani cricket team before the India-Pakistan World Cup semi-final in Mohali. In reality, following the 26/11 attacks in 2008, India cancelled a planned cricket tour to Pakistan, a clear indication of frozen ties in the aftermath of the tragedy. Claim: A picture featuring former PM Dr Manmohan Singh, along with Pakistan's cricket team, was shared by a Facebook user 'Anil Pandya' on September 17, claiming that Dr Manmohan Singh invited the cricket team to India shortly after the 26/11 terrorist attacks in Mumbai. "The Pakistan cricket team arrived in India shortly after the 26/11 terrorist attacks in Mumbai. The then Prime Minister Manmohan Singh was present to welcome the Pakistan cricket team. Sharad Pawar is also seen with him. And they opposed the Ind-Pak match at Dubai," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the picture through Reverse Image Search and found that several other users had shared the same picture with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. On closely analysing the picture, the Desk found 'ICC Cricket World Cup 2011' written on Pakistan cricket team captain Shahid Afridi's jersey, indicating that the image is from the India vs Pakistan match during the 2011 World Cup, which India, Bangladesh, and Sri Lanka co-hosted. Below is a screenshot that highlights the same issue. Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found the same picture archived on the PMO website. The text highlighted that the then PM Dr Manmohan Singh and the then Prime Minister of Pakistan, Yousuf Raza Gilani, were interacting with the Pakistani Cricket Team at the Indo-Pak World Cup semi-final, at the Punjab Cricket Association stadium, in Mohali on March 30, 2011. "The Prime Minister, Dr Manmohan Singh and the Prime Minister of Pakistan, Mr Yousuf Raza Gilani, interacting with the Pakistani Cricket Team at the Indo-Pak World Cup semi-final, at the Punjab Cricket Association stadium, in Mohali on March 30, 2011," read the post's caption. Here is the link , and below is a screenshot of the same. Upon scanning the search results, the Desk came across a report by Times Now, published on March 31, 2011, stating that then-PM Dr Manmohan Singh arrived at the cricket stadium in Mohali to witness the Indo-Pak World Cup semi-final match and for talks with his Pakistani counterpart, Yousuf Raza Gilani. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports and came across a report by NBC News on December 19, 2008. The report mentioned that India cancelled a cricket tour to Pakistan, a clear sign of a freeze in relations in the aftermath of the terrorist attacks on Mumbai. "Cricket is one of the few things India and Pakistan agree on. But with New Delhi accusing Islamabad of not curbing Pakistani-based terrorists blamed for the Mumbai attack, India on Thursday cancelled a cricket tour to Pakistan, a clear sign of a freeze in relations," read the description of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the picture featuring former PM Dr Manmohan Singh is from March 30, 2011, when PM Manmohan Singh and Pakistani PM Yousuf Raza Gilani met the Pakistan team before the India-Pakistan World Cup semi-final in Mohali.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video falsely shared as Punjab flood footage; details inside
content: New Delhi, September 19 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing devastating flood waters sweeping through streets and homes is circulating on social media with the claim that it depicts the recent flood situation in Punjab. Several users are sharing it with captions implying that entire neighbourhoods and livelihoods are being lost in that state. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video is not genuine. Analysis revealed it to be manipulated and AI-generated, and it is being shared online with a false claim. Claim: A video shared by a Facebook user, 'Raj Kumar', on September 5, claims to show the devastation caused by floods in Punjab. The posts suggest that heavy rains and river overflow in Punjab have caused this disaster. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. By running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media accounts had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports, but did not find any credible reports that covered the same video. Given the gravity of the matter and the potential loss, it would have received broad media coverage. Upon careful analysis of the video, the Desk found several discrepancies that hint the footage might be manipulated or AI-generated. For instance, the movement of the vehicles and also the trees looks unnatural, and the extra glossy texture hints that it has been manipulated. Below is a screenshot that highlights the same issue. Next, taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk ran the video's keyframes through Sight Engine, an AI-detection tool. The result indicated that 94% of the content is AI-generated. Below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing flood devastation in Punjab is actually AI-generated and was shared with a false claim on social media.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered photo of Rahul Gandhi with controversial preacher Zakir Naik shared as real
content: New Delhi, September 19 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): An image purportedly showing Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi sitting beside controversial Islamic preacher Zakir Naik was recently shared on social media, accompanied by the claim that it depicted a recent meeting between the two in Malaysia. Users alleged that during this meeting, Rahul Gandhi discussed matters related to India with Naik. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the image and found it to be digitally manipulated. A reverse image search traced the original photo, shared in 2023, which showed Zakir Naik and his son meeting the Grand Mufti of Oman. In the viral image, the Grand Mufti had been replaced with Rahul Gandhi. An AI-generated, digitally altered photo of Rahul Gandhi with Zakir Naik was therefore falsely shared on social media as real. Claim On September 13, X user Ashok Pandey (@ashokpa61296551) shared a photo purportedly showing Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, sitting beside fugitive Islamic preacher Zakir Naik in Malaysia, claiming they had held discussions on India-related matters. "In Malaysia, a patriot is discussing with other patriots about making India strong. This patriot has been engaged in such patriotism since 2014. Their ancestors have also been dedicated to patriotism since 1946-47," the user wrote. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral social media image through Google Lens and found multiple social media accounts that shared the same image with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search via Google Lens also led the Desk to a Facebook post shared by a news portal named Arabian News on March 23, 2023. The Desk found that the image included in the Facebook post was the original one, as it held multiple similarities with the viral image. The original photo shows Zakir Naik and his son, Farik, meeting the Grand Mufti of Oman, Shaikh Ahmad bin Hamad Al Khalili. However, in the viral image, the Grand Mufti's face was digitally altered and replaced with that of Rahul Gandhi. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a comparison image highlighting how the original photo was digitally altered and then shared on social media to mislead viewers. In the next part of the investigation, taking cues from the above findings, the Desk ran the viral image through two AI-detection tools — Hive Moderation and Was It AI. The results from both platforms clearly stated that the image of Rahul Gandhi and Zakir Naik sitting together was AI-generated and did not depict a real incident. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the image of Rahul Gandhi sitting beside fugitive Islamic preacher Zakir Naik was digitally manipulated and falsely shared as real.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally manipulated video of Tejashwi Yadav falling from a horse during a roadshow shared as real
content: New Delhi, September 22 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it showed Leader of Opposition in the Bihar Legislative Assembly, Tejashwi Yadav, falling from a horse moments after mounting it during a roadshow in Mokama. The video purportedly depicted the horse, on which the RJD leader sat to begin the roadshow ahead of the upcoming 2025 assembly elections, suddenly performing multiple tricks, causing him to fall. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found that it had been digitally manipulated using AI. The original footage shows Tejashwi Yadav riding the horse without falling, but it was altered to depict him losing balance falsely. Claim An X user, Namami Bharatam (@Namami_Bharatam), shared a video on September 20 allegedly showing the Leader of Opposition in the Bihar Legislative Assembly, Tejashwi Yadav, falling from a horse as he tried to mount it during a roadshow in Mokama, ahead of the 2025 assembly elections. The video purportedly showed the horse on which the RJD leader sat to begin the roadshow suddenly performing multiple tricks, causing him to fall. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered 369.5k views and 5.6k likes.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available, here and here respectively: To verify the details about the roadshow conducted by Tejashwi Yadav, and whether he indeed fell from a horse during the event, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google. The search led to a report published by Patna-based daily Patna Express on September 17. The report confirmed that the visuals of Tejashwi Yadav riding a horse in Mokama were from a recent roadshow ahead of the 2025 elections. However, the report made no mention of him falling off the horse. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Below is a combined image highlighting the visual similarities between the viral video and the featured image in the news report, confirming that both depict the same incident. Next, to check the authenticity of the viral video, the Desk ran the extracted keyframes through Google Lens again. This search led to a video posted on the official X handle of Tejashwi Yadav's office on September 18, showing an extended clip of the same incident. Careful analysis of this official clip revealed that it did not show Tejashwi Yadav falling from the horse, as depicted in the viral version. On the contrary, it showed him mounting the horse and beginning his roadshow in Mokama without incident. This confirmed that the viral video was digitally manipulated to mislead viewers. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video, which claims to show RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav falling from a horse during a roadshow in Mokama, is digitally manipulated. The original video shows him riding the horse without falling.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video claiming Burj Khalifa lit up with singer Zubeen Garg's photo is digitally generated
content: New Delhi, September 22 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently shared by multiple social media users claimed to show the world's tallest building in Dubai, the Burj Khalifa, illuminated with the image of singer Zubeen Garg as a tribute following his sudden passing in Singapore on September 19. The Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found that no such tribute was paid to the Indian singer in Dubai. The investigation revealed that the video circulating online was created using an online template that mimics Burj Khalifa light shows. The claim in the viral post is false. Meanwhile, it is pertinent to note that the popular Indian singer died on September 19 in Singapore while swimming in the sea without a life jacket. He had arrived in Singapore to participate in the North East India Festival (NEIF), but there he met with a tragic accident, which claimed his life. Claim An Instagram page named signonews shared a video on September 21, purportedly showing the Burj Khalifa, the world's tallest building in Dubai, lit up with a picture of popular Indian musician Zubeen Garg to pay tribute after his sudden death in Singapore. Sharing the video, the user wrote: "Mourning the death of Zubeen Garg in Dubai. Tribute to such a great artist." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing the story, the video had garnered 88,547 likes.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to check if the Burj Khalifa had actually been illuminated with images of Zubeen Garg as a tribute. The search results, however, did not lead to any credible news reports or videos confirming the same. Had such a development taken place, Indian media outlets would have widely covered it. Additionally, the Desk also scanned through the official Instagram page of Burj Khalifa since the time the Indian singer passed away in Singapore on September 19. The search, however, could not find any social media posts related to Zubeen Garg shared by the handle. Next, to check the authenticity of the video, the Desk ran the extracted keyframes through Google Lens. The results led to multiple videos where the background patterns displayed were precisely similar to those seen in the viral video. The light shows and patterns in those clips closely matched the viral video, indicating that a regular video template was used to create it. Links to two such posts showing similar background patterns can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively: Below are two comparison images highlighting the similarity between the background patterns in the viral video and those in other template-based videos. This confirms that the viral clip was generated using a pre-existing video template available online. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video claiming the Burj Khalifa was lit up with the image of singer Zubeen Garg as a tribute after his death is false. The viral clip was created using an online video template that mimics Burj Khalifa light shows. No credible reports or evidence confirm that such a tribute took place in Dubai.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video of Buddha statue at Hyderabad's Hussain Sagar Lake falsely shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, September 23 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a massive Buddha statue being transported and installed is circulating on social media with the claim that it captures the installation of the iconic Buddha statue at Hussain Sagar Lake in Hyderabad in 1992. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the clip and found it to be AI-generated. The viral video does not depict the 1992 installation of the Hussain Sagar Buddha statue and is being shared with a false claim. Claim: A video showing a grand statue of the Buddha was shared by a Facebook user, 'Sharma Nvrk,' on September 19, claiming that the Buddha statue was being installed at Hussain Sagar Lake in Hyderabad. "Just roll back to 1992 and recollect the olden days when *Buddha Statue* was being installed at *Hussain Sagar* in *Tank Bund, Hyderabad*.Many of us would have witnessed this and once again get *thrilled* watching this," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. Upon careful analysis of the video, the Desk found several inconsistencies, including an extra glossy texture, missing body parts of the people, and irregular movements, which suggested that the video might have been generated using AI. Below is a screenshot that highlights the same issue. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk then ran the video through Hive-Moderation, an AI-detection tool that highlighted that the video is 99.9% AI-generated. Below is a screenshot of the same. Upon further scanning of the search results, the Desk came across the same video, uploaded by an Instagram user named 'bharathfx1'. The description of the video mentioned that the images/videos in the reel are AI-generated. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing the installation of the Buddha statue at Hussain Sagar, Hyderabad, in 1992, is AI-generated.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally-altered video of CDS Anil Chauhan falsely shared to claim 'he admitted India lost Rafale jets in Operation Sindoor'
content: New Delhi, September 23 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video featuring Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) General Anil Chauhan speaking at a briefing has gone viral on social media with the claim that he allegedly admitted "India lost four Rafale jets during Operation Sindoor" due to miscalculating the strength of the Pakistan military. The video shows General Chauhan allegedly acknowledging that the Indian side underestimated Pakistan's response capability, leading to the loss of the Rafale fighter aircraft. It is being circulated as a major admission by India's top military officer. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the footage and found it to be digitally manipulated. General Anil Chauhan did not make any such remarks. The viral clip has been altered and was shared with a false claim. Claim: A video featuring Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) General Anil Chauhan addressing a briefing was shared by an X user, 'The Whistle Blower,' on September 18, claiming that the Chief had again admitted to losing four Rafale Jets due to miscalculating the Pakistan military's capability. In the video, he can be heard saying, "On the 7th, we attacked nine terrorist targets between 1 am and 1.30 am. You know, there were operations in Balakot before this. We kept saying that we had killed them; they were successful, but there was no evidence, satellite imagery or photographs. But what we were doing now, why did we do it at 1:30 am? We thought that the Pakistani Air Force would be sleeping, and no one would know what we had attacked in Pakistan. But they all found out. Our four Rafales fell, but we have learned a lot…" "Indian Army Chief once again admits to losing 4 Rafale Jets due to miscalculating Pakistan military's capability. Underestimating Pakistan was the biggest mistake of Indian politicians," read the now-deleted post's caption. Here is the link , and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation As part of the investigation, the Desk first conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports. Still, we did not find credible media reports confirming such a statement or incident. Taking the investigation further, the Desk conducted another set of customised keyword searches to locate the original video on PTI's X handle, as the watermark appears in the top right corner of the video. In the 1 minute 22 seconds video, he says, "On the 7th (of May), the terrorist targets we had chosen, we struck them between 1:00 and 1:30 at night… Why did we strike at 1:30 at night? That is the darkest time; it would be the most difficult to get satellite images, photographs, and collect evidence. Yet, we struck at one or 1:30 in the morning. Why was that? It was for two reasons. First, we had confidence in our capabilities, knowing that, even at night, we would be able to obtain imagery. And the second important reason was that we wanted to avoid civilian casualties. The best time would have been 5:30–6:00 AM, when daylight starts, but at that time, the first Azaan or the first prayer takes place, and in Bahawalpur and Muridke, there might be a lot of movement at that time, so that many civilians could have been killed… We wanted to avoid that, which is why we chose the time between 1:00 and 1:30". Here is the link to the X post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Next, on carefully analysing the viral video, the Desk noticed a missing microphone and blurry mouth movements. At the 0:30–0:48 second mark, where the contentious line is heard, there is a noticeable audio shift. Below is a screenshot that highlights the same issue. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk ran the audio through Resembe AI, an AI-detection tool that detected that the audio had been edited. Below is a screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video featuring CDS Anil Chauhan admitting to the loss of 4 Rafale jets due to miscalculating Pakistan military's capability is altered and fake. He never said such a statement.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: This social media post misleads users with false claim about PM Modi's death
content: New Delhi, September 23 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media post featuring an image of a flower-decorated ambulance (typically used during cremation ceremonies) alongside a portrait of Prime Minister Narendra Modi adorned with a garland was recently shared online, claiming that the PM had died. This claim is absolutely false. The investigation further revealed that the image of the flower-decked ambulance was actually from the last rites of Bollywood actor Anil Kapoor's mother, Nirmal Kapoor, held on May 3. The claim made in the social media post is absolutely nonsensical and not truthful. Claim An Instagram user, 'miss_cutipie_8800,' shared a post on September 11 claiming that Prime Minister Narendra Modi had passed away. The post featured an image of a flower-decorated ambulance (typically used during cremation ceremonies) along with PM Modi's portrait adorned with a garland, suggesting his death. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation According to a report by the Press Trust of India on Monday (September 22), Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Itanagar, the capital of Arunachal Pradesh, where he unveiled infrastructure projects worth Rs 5,125.37 crore. The report mentioned that, during a function at Indira Gandhi Park in Itanagar, the PM virtually laid the foundation stones for two major hydropower projects in Shi Yomi district and a convention center in Tawang. "He also launched multiple key infrastructure projects worth over Rs 1,290 crore, catering to various sectors including connectivity, health, fire safety, and working women's hostels, among others," the report added. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: The Desk also reviewed the official X handle of PM Modi, which contained several posts detailing his visit to Itanagar. In these posts, PM Modi shared snippets from his speech at Itanagar during the foundation stone-laying ceremony of multiple development projects. The information thus suggested that the claim that PM Modi had passed away was nonsensical and not truthful. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Next, to verify the authenticity of image of the ambulance, the Desk ran it through Google Lens, which led to the official Instagram page of Zoom TV. The page shared a video on May 3 showing the same flower-decorated ambulance as seen in the social media post. The video confirmed that the ambulance was used during the cremation ceremony of Bollywood actor Anil Kapoor's mother, Nirmal Kapoor. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting that the ambulance seen in the Instagram video shared by the news portal matches the one in the social media post. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the social media post claiming the death of Prime Minister Narendra Modi is false.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of scuba diver losing consciousness underwater falsely linked to death of veteran singer Zubeen Garg; details inside
content: New Delhi, September 23 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): As a teary-eyed Assam bid its final goodbye to beloved singer Zubeen Garg who was laid to rest today (Tuesday) in Kamarkuchi in the presence of thousands of well-wishers and family members, days after he passed away in Singapore reportedly due to drowning, a purported video of him losing consciousness during a scuba diving activity was widely shared on social media. Users claimed the clip captured the final moments of the late singer in Singapore, allegedly during a scuba diving session that led to his death. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found the video to be unrelated to Zubeen Garg's death. The clip originally showed a diver sharing his experience of blacking out and losing consciousness underwater in May 2025, which clearly predates the singer's death on September 19. It is also pertinent to note that while it was initially reported that Garg died while scuba diving, Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma later clarified that the singer drowned while swimming without a life jacket. Thus, an old and unrelated video of a diver facing a health emergency underwater was falsely linked to the death of popular Assamese singer Zubeen Garg. Claim An X user, MD RIZWAN HOSSAIN (@rizwan_hossain), shared on September 19 a video purportedly showing the last moments of famous Assamese singer Zubeen Garg, who died in Singapore the same day. The video allegedly showed him losing consciousness during a scuba diving activity, which he later allegedly succumbed to. "Famous Indian Singer from Assam Zubin Garg died in Singapore while Scuba diving. Here is the last moment video," the user captioned the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered 25.9k views) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such videos can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search also led the Desk to a video posted on an Instagram handle named 'saltymammals', which exactly matched the viral clip. However, the accompanying details revealed that it was published on June 13, 2025, well before the singer's death on September 19. Further details stated that the video showed a freediver (going with the Instagram handle @stop.the.sun) ascending from a deep dive in the ocean. "As the diver approaches the surface, he blacks out and loses consciousness. The safety divers quickly respond and pull the diver to the surface. After a few seconds at the surface, the diver regains consciousness and starts breathing on his own," the post reads. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a combined image highlighting the visual similarities between the viral video and the one shared by the Instagram account. Next, taking cues from the above-generated inputs, the Desk scanned through the Instagram handle @stop.the.sun, which had shared the same video on May 14, along with a caption describing the diver's personal experience of blacking out underwater. Nowhere was the video linked to Zubeen Garg's death. The diver's post read: "Lost consciousness for the first time. Ascent from 78 meters. Safety @gkreivenas Camera @freelookaround. The low speed of descent and the desire to squeeze 2 meters to reach 78 meters played a cruel joke on me. Total dive time 3:13. Some people ask me why I'm with no fins on training? I dive with no fins #FIM all the time to train in the same conditions as for competitions. You think that's one of the most dangerous sports? No, it's the safest sport. Ask me why." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: In the subsequent part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find details about the cause of Zubeen Garg's death. The search led to a September 20 report by The Indian Express, which confirmed drowning as the cause of death. The report stated: "The popular Indian singer was swimming without a life jacket during his accidental death. While it was initially reported that Garg died while scuba diving, Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma later stated the singer drowned while swimming without a life jacket, despite repeated warnings from lifeguards." Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a video showing a scuba diver losing consciousness underwater was falsely linked to the death of Assamese singer Zubeen Garg. The video was initially shared months before Garg's death and had no connection to the tragic incident in Singapore.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Clipped video falsely claims Rahul Gandhi said Modi and Shah win elections because people support them
content: New Delhi, September 23 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of Congress leader and Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha (LoP) Rahul Gandhi addressing a rally has gone viral on social media with the claim that he admitted Prime Minister Narendra Modi wins elections because the people of India support him and Union Home Minister Amit Shah. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it to be clipped and shared out of context. In the original footage, Gandhi accused Modi and Amit Shah of winning elections by manipulating votes with the help of the Election Commission, rather than due to public support. Therefore, the video was shared with a false claim. Claim: A video featuring Congress leader Rahul Gandhi addressing a public rally was shared by an Instagram user, 'bura_aadmi_but_not_villain,' on September 21, claiming that he said Narendra Modi wins elections because India supports him and Amit Shah. "And listen carefully, Narendra Modi wins elections, and India supports Narendra Modi and Amit Shah," says Rahul Gandhi in the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. Upon further review of the search results, the Desk came across a video featuring the same clips that were uploaded to the official YouTube channel of Congress on August 27, 2025. Upon analysing the entire video, we found duplicate content at the 12:40 mark. "And listen carefully, Narendra Modi wins elections by stealing votes. Narendra Modi wins elections by allegedly stealing votes, manipulating vote counts, and inflating the number of votes. And Narendra Modi and Amit Shah are helped by India's Election Commission," says Rahul Gandhi. This makes it clear that a part of the original video was clipped and shared out of context on social media. He was addressing the 'Voter Adhikar Yatra' at Gaighat, Muzaffarpur, Bihar, on 27 August 2025, where he focused on alleged voter-list manipulation or "vote chori," accused the BJP, PM Narendra Modi, Amit Shah, and the Election Commission of enabling electoral fraud, highlighted marginalised groups' votes being cut, criticised media and corporate influence. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video featuring Rahul Gandhi saying that Modi won the elections because India supports Modi and Amit Shah was shared with a false claim.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Viral clip showing Amit Shah blaming Ajit Doval, calling for PM Modi's resignation, is AI-generated
content: New Delhi, September 24 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of Union Home Minister Amit Shah, purportedly from an exclusive interview with a news portal, was shared with a claim that he allegedly criticised National Security Adviser (NSA) Ajit Doval and Prime Minister Narendra Modi over Operation Sindoor. The clip shows Shah allegedly blaming Doval for a failed plan and calling for Modi's resignation. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the video is manipulated using AI. Shah did not make any such remarks, and the viral clip was circulated with a false claim. Claim: A video featuring Union Home Minister Amit Shah in an exclusive interview with a news portal was shared by an X user, 'The Whistle Blower', on September 22, claiming that he criticised NSA Ajit Doval and Prime Minister Narendra Modi over Operation Sindoor. In the 1 minute 30 seconds video, he says, "I have seen very difficult times for Modi ji, but there hasn't been such a time. We made a huge mistake with the plan that was given by Doval ji during Operation Sindoor. We assumed Pakistan would not do anything once we attacked them with our Rafale. But, with Col Sofiya Qureshi's press conference, it was clear that Pakistan attacked us with their missiles at 26 places…Where is Modi ji's 'vikas'? PM Modi should resign…" The post garnered 2586 views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation As part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the video and found several discrepancies in it, which suggested that it might have been manipulated. For instance, the irregular lip movement and the voice did not match Amit Shah's original voice. Below is a screenshot that highlights the same issue. The Desk noticed FirstPost's logo in the top left corner of the video, and taking a cue from this, we conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find the original video. We found the original 30-minute interview shared by Firstpost's X handle on September 19. In the interview, Shah discusses his association with PM Modi, characterising him as a leader who exemplifies meticulous planning, grassroots connectivity, and unwavering discipline. Shah recalled their initial meeting at a Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) gathering in Ahmedabad, noting that the leadership qualities he observed then continue to shape PM Modi's approach today. He further elaborated on PM Modi's contributions to strengthening the BJP's organisational foundation in Gujarat, his disciplined leadership methodology, and pivotal decisions made during his tenure as Prime Minister. In the video, he did not blame NSA Doval or PM Modi regarding Operation Sindoor or calling for the PM's resignation. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the contents seen in the social media post and the X post by First Post. Another set of customised keyword searches led us to a transcript of the interview published by Storyboard18 on September 21. Nowhere in the transcript does Shah point fingers at PM Modi or Doval or ask for their resignation. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk then ran the audio of the video through Resemble AI, an AI-detection tool, which highlighted that it is fake. Below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video has been manipulated using AI. Amit Shah never made such a remark.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Viral clip misrepresents Modi's 2011 remarks on GST; he spoke on IT infrastructure, not opposition in original footage
content: New Delhi, September 24 (Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, purportedly showing him declaring that the Goods and Services Tax (GST) "will never succeed," was shared on social media. The clip was circulated with the claim that Modi, as the then Chief Minister of Gujarat, opposed the implementation of GST. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found the video to be misleading. The footage was a clipped portion of his 2011 remarks, in which he said GST would not succeed without a proper IT network, not that he opposed the tax reform itself. The truncated clip was shared online with a false claim. Claim: A video featuring PM Modi addressing the public through a video conference was shared by an X user, '@INCKerala', on September 22, claiming that he allegedly said GST 'will never succeed'. In the 00:15-second video, he says, "As far as GST is concerned, BJP and Gujarat's stand has been the same that GST can never be successful…" "Dear @PiyushGoyal, You need a memory jog. Here is Narendra Modi, the erstwhile CM of Gujarat, categorically declaring that he will never allow GST to be implemented in India," read the post's caption. The post clocked 328.3k views. Here is a link and an archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. Upon further review of the search results, the Desk came across the extended version of the video uploaded to the official YouTube channel of Narendra Modi on March 22, 2011. Narendra Modi was replying to the then PM Manmohan Singh on his remarks on Goods and Services Tax (GST). In the full video, PM Modi clearly states from the 00:39 mark, "As far as economic reform, GST are concerned, the BJP and Gujarat's take is clear from the beginning itself. One year ago, I had a meeting with Mr Pranab Mukherjee, the Foreign Minister of India, in Gujarat. At that time, I had told him that unless he established an IT network, GST would never succeed. And he accepted my words. And in my presence, he had informed my principal secretary that a task force should be formed and an IT backup system should be set up immediately. Only then can GST succeed. He also agreed…." Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the recent X post and the YouTube post. As part of the investigation, the Desk also conducted a customised keyword search to determine if any media outlet had carried the statement made by him in the viral post; however, we did not find any credible reports. Meanwhile, during the 2010-2011 fiscal year, early discussions on GST faced challenges regarding IT infrastructure, with states expressing concerns about data integration and tax administration. In March 2011, PM Modi (then Chief Minister of Gujarat) emphasised the critical need for a strong IT network for the success of GST. In 2013, the Goods and Services Tax Network (GSTN) was established as a not-for-profit, non-governmental company to provide the IT infrastructure for GST. Finally, in 2017, GST was rolled out nationwide, supported by the advanced GSTN system that had been developed over several years. The viral claim gained traction around the rollout of GST 2.0 on September 22, which lowers taxes on essential and mass-market goods while increasing rates on luxury items and sin products. The GST regime, which replaced a patchwork of indirect taxes with a unified system, marked its eighth anniversary on July 1, 2025. According to official data, gross GST collections for 2024–25 hit a record ₹22.08 lakh crore, reflecting a 9.4 per cent growth over the previous year. Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video featuring PM Modi saying that the GST system will never be implemented is a clipped portion of the complete and original video. In the original video, he said that GST would not succeed without a proper IT network.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video claiming desecration of Lord Ganesha idol in Karnataka by 'conversion mafia' shared with false information; details inside
content: New Delhi, September 24 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a Lord Ganesha idol being desecrated after a pair of slippers was placed on it was recently shared on social media, along with a claim that the incident was carried out at the behest of people attempting to instigate communal hatred. Some users alleged that the so-called "conversion mafia" was behind the act. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false. The incident did occur in Belur, Hassan district, but police confirmed that the accused was a local woman with unstable mental health. No communal angle was established in the case. Claim An X handle with the username Treeni (@TheTreeni) shared a video on September 21 claiming that a Lord Ganesha idol was desecrated at a temple in Hassan, Karnataka, by people attempting to incite communal hatred. The user further alleged that a "conversion mafia" was responsible for the act. The post read: "Hinduphobia is real! Lord Ganesha was desecrated with a slipper garland in Hassan, Karnataka. Conversion mafia suspected behind this vile act." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered 8.7k views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these frames, the Desk found several other social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. Next, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to verify details of the incident and check for any communal angle. The search led to a PTI report dated September 21, which provided detailed information about the incident and confirmed that an arrest had been made. According to the report, the incident took place earlier in the week at a temple in Belur town, Hassan district, Karnataka, where outrage erupted after slippers were found placed on a Lord Ganesha idol. Quoting Superintendent of Police Mohammad Sujitha, the report stated that, prima facie, a woman was responsible for the act. Her mental condition was described as "a bit unstable." "She is said to have indulged in similar acts at home too, according to her family, and this will be inquired into. She used to sell flowers and lived in Hassan's Vijayanagar with her mother and two sons, one of whom is differently abled. She lost her husband six years after marriage," the SP told the media. The PTI report made no mention of the incident being linked to communal hatred. Here is the link to the report. To cross-check further, the Desk conducted another search to identify the arrested woman and ascertain her background. This led to a Deccan Herald report dated September 22, which identified the accused as Leelamma, a resident of Vijayanagar Layout in Hassan. The report also confirmed that her mental health condition was unstable. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. In the subsequent part of the investigation, the Desk also contacted a Karnataka Police official, who confirmed that the incident was not motivated by any communal considerations. Furthermore, the Desk attempted to contact Hassan SP, MS Mohammed Sujitha, for a statement on the matter. The story will be updated once a response is received. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral claim suggesting a Lord Ganesha idol was desecrated in Karnataka by a "conversion mafia" to incite communal hatred is false.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old Guwahati water pipeline burst video falsely shared, claiming it captured cloudburst aftermath in Kolkata
content: New Delhi, September 25 (Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing water gushing near a railway line has gone viral on social media with the claim that it captures the aftermath of a cloudburst in Kolkata. The clip, widely shared on Facebook and other platforms, was circulated against the backdrop of the city reeling under its heaviest rainfall in nearly four decades, which left several areas waterlogged and caused multiple deaths. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the footage and found that it didn't show a cloudburst in Kolkata. The video was filmed in Guwahati, Assam, and depicted water surging out of a burst water supply pipe in the Chandmari area. Claim: A video showing water gushing down near a railway line was shared by a Facebook user, Deblina Das, on September 23, claiming that it was a cloud burst incident from Kolkata. "Cloud burst at Kolkata," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. Upon further review of the search results, the Desk came across an X post by 'Hindusthan Samachar News Agency' on September 20, clarifying that the video has no connection to Kolkata's disaster, as it predates the disaster. The post carried the same visuals as seen in the recent social media post. It was reported that the incident occurred in the Chandmari area of Guwahati and involved an explosion in a drinking water supply pipe. "A scene of water gushing over 20 feet high after an explosion in the drinking water supply pipe in the Chandmari area of Guwahati," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combined image highlighting the similarity between the content seen in the Facebook post and the X post. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports. It came across a report by a local media outlet, Pratidin Times, published on September 20. According to the report, the pipe rupture has disrupted the supply of potable water to several neighbourhoods, affecting hundreds of households. Traffic congestion and flooding have been reported in low-lying areas near the site of the break. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Meanwhile, according to reports, at least 10 people have died after Kolkata city in the eastern Indian state of West Bengal saw its heaviest rainfall in 39 years. Nine of the deaths were caused by electrocution in stagnant water. Residential areas and businesses in the city and its suburbs have been grappling with severe waterlogging since Monday night. Several key roads remain flooded, and train services are disrupted, forcing commuters to wade through knee-deep waters. Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video shows water gushing out from a burst pipe in Guwahati's Chandmari area in Assam, and not Kolkata.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of Raveena Tandon with Tejashwi Yadav resurfaced to falsely claim she will campaign for RJD leader in Bihar polls
content: New Delhi, September 25 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of Bollywood actress Raveena Tandon and Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) leader Tejashwi Yadav seemingly posing for the camera was recently shared on social media with the claim that the two are set to join hands for the upcoming Bihar Assembly Elections 2025. Several users alleged that the actress would campaign for Tejashwi Yadav during the polls. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found that it was falsely linked to the Bihar elections. The footage is at least 10 months old, and no official reports suggest that Raveena Tandon will campaign for Tejashwi Yadav. The clip actually shows Tejashwi Yadav meeting Raveena Tandon at Deoghar Airport in Jharkhand in November 2024. Claim An X user, Arun Yadav (@ArunKosli7), shared a video on September 23 purportedly showing RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav meeting Bollywood actress Raveena Tandon. The user claimed that the two are set to join hands for the upcoming Bihar Assembly Elections 2025, with Raveena Tandon campaigning for the RJD leader. "Hey Raveena Tandon. You're a woman with strong religious inclinations, and you have respect in society too, so why are you promoting these anti-Hindu? Don't compromise your religion for a few bucks, otherwise your films and your daughter's films will flop. Otherwise, you are sensible," the user captioned the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video garnered 206k views and 4.3k likes) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such videos can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search also led the Desk to a video shared on the official Instagram handle of RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav. He had posted the same video of him meeting Bollywood actress Raveena Tandon, dated November 17, 2024, when the duo met at Deoghar Airport in Jharkhand. This confirmed that the footage was at least 10 months old and unrelated to the upcoming Bihar Assembly Elections. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a combined image highlighting the visual similarities between the viral video and the one shared by the Instagram account. Next, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to check if any credible news reports or official social media statements confirmed that Raveena Tandon would campaign for Tejashwi Yadav in the upcoming Bihar Assembly Elections. The search, however, yielded no reliable results. Given the stature of both individuals, such a development would likely have been covered by mainstream media. The Desk also reviewed the recent posts on the social media handles of both Raveena Tandon and Tejashwi Yadav. No content related to any election collaboration was found. While the Desk could not independently verify whether Raveena Tandon will be campaigning for Tejashwi Yadav in the upcoming Bihar Assembly Elections, it found no credible evidence to support the claim. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video of Tejashwi Yadav meeting Raveena Tandon at Deoghar Airport was falsely shared on social media as evidence of their alleged partnership for the Bihar Assembly Elections 2025.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old BBC interview of ex-CJI Chandrachud shared with false claim linking it to CJI Gavai's remark
content: New Delhi, September 26 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of former Chief Justice of India (CJI) D.Y. Chandrachud, purportedly from a BBC interview, has gone viral with the claim that he was responding to current CJI B.R. Gavai's recent "ask Lord Vishnu" remark. The viral clip shows Chandrachud allegedly saying that the Constitution does not require judges to be atheists in order to be impartial, and that his faith teaches him the universality of religion while ensuring equal justice for all. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the claim is misleading. The remarks attributed to Chandrachud were indeed made in a BBC interview earlier this year. Still, they were in response to a question about the Ayodhya verdict, not CJI Gavai's controversial observation in the temple idol case. Chandrachud has made no public comments so far on CJI Gavai's remarks. Claim: A video featuring former CJI DY Chandrachud in an interview with BBC was shared by an X user '@anubhavgupta_ji' on September 19, claiming that he responded to CJI Gavai's 'ask lord Vishnu' remark, saying that the Constitution does not demand judges to be atheists to be impartial. "I do pray. I make no bones of the fact that I'm a man of faith. Our Constitution does not require you to be an atheist to be an independent judge. And I value my faith. But what my faith teaches me is the universality of religion. And irrespective of who comes to my court, and I dare say that it applies to the other judges in the Supreme Court as well, Irrespective of who comes to you as a litigant, you dispense equal and even-handed justice," says former CJI DY Chandrachud. "D.Y. Chandrachud to BBC on Gawai Remark: "I'm a man of Faith. Our constitution does not require you to be an Atheist to be a Judge. My Faith teaches me the Universality of Religion. I dispensed equal justice irrespective of Religion. Diff. b/w a Merit & Reserved B.R Gawai," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation As part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across a report by The Mint published on February 14, 2025, way before CJI Gavai's remark. The report highlighted that former CJI DY Chandrachud stated that claims of him praying before God before delivering the Ayodhya Ram Mandir judgment were false. In a recent interview, he said that his faith teaches him to be evenhanded with every religious group. "Appearing on BBC's HARDtalk earlier this week, Chandrachud told journalist Stephen Sackur that claims of him praying to god before passing the judgment were 'incorrect'," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking the investigation forward, the Desk conducted another set of customised keywords to find the original BBC interview on YouTube, and came across the interview published on February 12. Chandrachud spoke about the landmark cases during his tenure, like the abrogation of Article 370 and the Ayodhya verdict. At the 16-minute-30-second mark, the interviewer, Stephen Sackur, says, "One more key judgment that you were involved in that I need to discuss. That is your decision to give a green light to the building of a Hindu temple in Ayodhya on what was the rubble, the remains of a mosque that was destroyed in 1992. Now the decision you took again resonated throughout the country. You said at that time that you had asked God for a solution to this mosque dispute." Responding to this, Chandrachud stated that although this was being said on social media, it was incorrect. "Stephen, if you look at social media and try to derive what was said by a judge from social media, you'll get the wrong answers. What I said was this. I was asked specifically. I make no bones of the fact that I'm a man of faith. Our Constitution does not require you to be an atheist to be an independent judge. And I value my faith. But what my faith teaches me is the universality of religion. And irrespective of who comes to my court — and I dare say that it applies to the other judges in the Supreme Court as well — Irrespective of who comes to you as a litigant, you dispense equal and even-handed justice." Here is the link to the interview, and below is a screenshot of the same. In his recent interview with India Today on September 22, former CJI DY Chandrachud tells Rajdeep Sardesai, "Why The Constitution Matters", he did not mention anything about CJI Gavai's remark. Here is the link to the interview, and below is a screenshot of the same. Upon listening to another interview on Lallantop published on their YouTube channel on September 21, 2025, former CJI DY Chandrachud did not talk or mention CJI Gavai's remarks. Clarifying that, as recent Chandrachud had not made any comments about the CJI Gavai controversy. Here is the link to the interview, and below is a screenshot of the same. Chief Justice B.R. Gavai and Justice K. Vinod Chandran, on September 16, refused to entertain the plea filed by Rakesh Dalal, who sought the replacement and consecration of the damaged idol at the Javari Temple in Chhatarpur district. "This is purely publicity interest litigation... Go and ask the deity himself to do something. If you are saying you are a strong devotee of Lord Vishnu, then you pray and do some meditation," the CJI said. Here is the link to the Times of India report. Furthermore, Chief Justice of India B R Gavai, following his remarks during a recent hearing of a plea seeking restoration of a Lord Vishnu idol in Madhya Pradesh's Khajuraho, set off a furore on social media, said that he "respects all religions". CJI Gavai clarified that his comments were made in the context of the fact that the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) has jurisdiction over its upkeep. "I believe in all the religions, I respect all the (religions)," CJI Gavai said. Here is the link to The Indian Express report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video featuring former CJI DY Chandrachud in an interview, responding to CJI Gavai's 'ask lord Vishnu' remark, was shared with a false claim. He was responding to a question about his judgment on the Ayodhya case. He has made no comments so far about the CJI Gavai controversy.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video of a cat stuck on aircraft's wing falsely shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, September 26 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a cat stuck on the wing of an aircraft during takeoff was recently shared on social media with the claim that it captured a real-life incident. The video allegedly shows a passenger filming the cat clinging to the wing while the plane is in mid-air. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it to be AI-generated, but falsely shared on social media as real to mislead viewers. Claim An X user, Adv. Nazneen Akhtar (@NazneenAkhtar23) shared a video on September 23, purportedly showing a real incident of a cat stuck on the wing of an aircraft during takeoff. Users shared the post stating: "This clip was taken while the aircraft was taking off. If it had been known before, perhaps this cat would have been taken off the aircraft's wing… I don't know what must have happened to the poor cat." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered 425k views and 1.2k likes.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. Upon closer inspection, the Desk noticed a watermark reading "Veo" at the bottom-left corner of the video. This suggested that the clip was likely generated using Veo, Google's advanced text-to-video generative AI model. Veo is capable of producing high-quality, realistic videos from text or image prompts and includes features such as native audio generation, style transfer, and editing controls, including background and lighting adjustments. Below is a screenshot from the viral video, where the Veo logo is clearly visible, indicating that the video was likely generated using AI. To further verify this, the Desk used Google's Veo tool with a relevant prompt to create a similar video of a woman filming a cat stuck on the wing of an aircraft during take-off. The tool generated a near-identical video, also displaying the Veo watermark in the same position. This confirmed that the viral video had been generated using AI and was not a recording of a real incident. Below is a screenshot of the AI-generated output created during the verification process. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an AI-generated video of a cat stuck on an aircraft's wing was falsely shared on social media as real.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Movie clip of woman 'prisoner' dancing in front of cops falsely shared as real incident in UP; details inside
content: New Delhi, September 26 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users have recently shared a video claiming it shows a recent incident in Uttar Pradesh where a woman prisoner danced in front of the police after being released on bail. The posts alleged that the woman performed the act to mock the police. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found the claim to be misleading. The video was actually a behind-the-scenes (BTS) moment from the shooting of a film titled Ek Chatur Naar, and not a real incident. Claim On September 22, an Instagram user named Gulbahar Choudhary shared a video allegedly showing a woman prisoner in Uttar Pradesh dancing in front of the police after securing bail. The video was shared with the claim that the woman danced to berate the police. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such videos can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search also led the Desk to the same video posted from the official Instagram account of actor Sushant Singh, who has worked in several Bollywood films and television serials.
