His account has over 41.6k followers. On September 12, Singh shared the same clip of a woman dancing in front of the police, but clarified in the description that it was not a real incident. Instead, it was a behind-the-scenes (BTS) moment from the set of a film titled Ek Chatur Naar. He also mentioned that the video was reposted from the Instagram page of MGR Studios. Singh captioned the video: "Reposted from MGR Studios! When Chhaya Ma'am slips into Mamta ki Saas mode and suddenly...her inner Naagin comes out! The drama is real, the sass is unreal, and the character? Fully possessed! BTS moments like these make Ek Chatur Naar truly unforgettable." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. A combined image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral video and the one shared from Singh's account. To cross-verify, the Desk also scanned the official Instagram handle of MGR Studios (Merry Go Round Studios). The page had shared the same video in collaboration with actress Chhaya Kadam, the woman seen dancing in the clip. This confirmed that the video was part of a film shoot and not a real-life incident. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Moreover, the Desk also conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find details related to the movie 'Ek Chatur Naar'. According to the information available on Google, the film prominently features Divya Khosla and Neil Nitin Mukesh, and was released on September 12. 2025. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was a behind-the-scenes moment from the movie Ek Chatur Naar, misrepresented on social media as a real incident of a woman prisoner dancing after getting bail.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Social media flooded with AI-generated videos, carrying phishing and fake links, falsely claim govt announced direct cash benefit schemes
content: New Delhi, September 27 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple videos recently circulated on social media claimed to promote lucrative "schemes" allegedly announced either by the government or private entities to provide monetary benefits to citizens. The clips followed a similar pattern, featuring images of Prime Minister Narendra Modi or other officials announcing the so-called schemes, followed by visuals of prominent TV news anchors seemingly explaining how people could register on certain websites to avail the benefits. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated five such posts and found that all of them were fake. The videos were generated using artificial intelligence (AI) and manipulated visuals of the Prime Minister and TV anchors to mislead viewers into believing the schemes were authentic. These deceptive videos were created to dupe people and could potentially result in financial loss if users fell for the fraudulent claims. Below is a detailed investigation into the four false posts. Claim 1: A Facebook page with the username Coin Prize shared a video on September 21, allegedly claiming that under the government's 'Kanya Uthan Yojana', a family with two daughters can now receive at least ₹1 lakh. The video began with a woman announcing the alleged decision, followed by visuals of a TV anchor—purportedly from the news channel IBC 24—explaining the procedure to avail the benefit. The anchor claimed that users could register by submitting their details on a website called My Tahuko. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation: The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to verify details about the government's Kanya Utthan Yojana. The search led to a report published by Hindi news portal Hindustan on August 31. The report clarified that under the Bihar government-led scheme, aimed at promoting women's literacy, female students graduating from Bihar would receive ₹50,000 per individual. It further highlighted that registrations for the scheme are accepted only through the official Bihar government portal, MedhaSoft. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. As a part of the investigation, the Desk also scanned through the MedhaSoft portal and confirmed that it is the only authentic source for students registering for this scheme. Thus, the website promoted in the viral video, My Tahuko, is dubious and potentially harmful, as submitting personal details there could result in financial fraud. Below is a screenshot of the result. Next, to test the authenticity of the video itself, the Desk examined it closely and noted multiple lip-sync discrepancies, indicating manipulation. The audio track was extracted from the video and analysed using the AI-detection tool Resemble AI, which confirmed the voice was AI-generated. Below is a screenshot of the result, which confirms the video was generated using AI. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video was artificially generated using AI to promote a fake scheme. It was shared online to mislead viewers and potentially trick them into providing personal information on a fraudulent website. Claim 2: A Facebook page named Coin Prize shared another video on September 23, allegedly claiming that the government would provide ₹1 lakh financial assistance to all women across the country. The video began with a woman at a podium announcing the supposed decision, followed by a news anchor—purportedly from Rastriya Jagat Vision News—explaining how beneficiaries could avail the benefits by submitting their details on a website called Sarkar Ji. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation: The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to check whether any such announcement (of financial assistance of Rs 1 lakh to be provided to all women across the country) had been made by the Centre or any state government. However, no credible news reports were found. Such a massive policy decision would have been widely covered in mainstream media if it were genuine. Next, the Desk examined the website Sarkar Ji. The link was found to be dubious, as genuine government portals always carry the ".gov.in" domain, which was absent. The website also hosted several suspicious "offers" that are never promoted on official portals—further confirming its fraudulent nature. Below are two screenshots, with the first highlighting the anomaly spotted in the dubious link shared above. While the other shows a homepage of a government website. In the next part of the investigation, the video was again checked for authenticity. However, in the video, lip-sync mismatches were spotted. Taking a cue from this, the Desk extracted audio from the video and ran it through Resemble AI, which confirmed it was AI-generated. Below is a screenshot of the result, which confirms the video was generated using AI. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video was AI-generated and falsely promoted a fraudulent scheme. The link provided (Sarkar Ji) is fake and could be used to scam users. Claim 3: On September 24, the same Coin Prize page shared another video, this time claiming that the government had announced ₹12,000 financial assistance for all women. The video allegedly included a snippet of Prime Minister Narendra Modi announcing the amount, followed by a news anchor explaining that beneficiaries could apply through the Sarkar Ji website. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation: Since the Desk had already identified Sarkar Ji as a fraudulent website in the previous claim, it was established that this video too was misleading. Additionally, the Desk also conducted a customised Google search to determine if any government scheme offering ₹12,000 assistance to women had been recently announced. No credible reports or official announcements were found. Such a scheme, if genuine, would have been extensively covered by national and state-level media. Next, to verify how the video promoting the dubious scheme was generated, the Desk ran it through the AI detection tool Hive Moderation. The results confirmed that the video contained AI-generated or deepfake content. Below is a screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video was AI-generated and used to promote a dubious scheme via the same fraudulent website (Sarkar Ji). It was designed to deceive viewers into providing personal details for potential financial fraud. Claim 4: An Instagram handle named free_guruji_25 shared a video on August 22 that purportedly showed PM Modi announcing benefits linked to ration cards. The video claimed that all ration card holders would now receive ₹15,000 in three instalments by registering through a website named sspedite.site. The latter part of the video showed senior journalist Sudhir Chaudhary allegedly explaining the registration steps and endorsing the website. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation: The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to check if the government had announced any financial assistance linked to ration card holders in the country. However, the search did not lead to any credible news reports or government statements that could confirm the same. Next, the Desk scanned through the website sspedite.site mentioned in the claim. The assessment confirmed the link to be dubious, as it remained non-functional. As established in the earlier claim, any authentic government portal for scheme registration always carries the ".gov.in" domain. Since this was missing, the link (sspedite.site) was confirmed to be fraudulent. Additionally, to verify the authenticity of the snippet showing PM Modi in the video, the Desk ran it through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of the keyframes (depicting PM Modi) was analysed through Google Lens, which led to a video shared on the official YouTube channel of the PMO India on March 7, 2025. The background setting in the viral video matched the one seen in this official video, which was filmed during PM Modi's visit to Surat. The Desk carefully reviewed the speech at the 57-minute timestamp, where the same clip of PM Modi—used in the viral video—appeared. However, it became clear that his remarks were not related to ration card holders or any such scheme. He was speaking in a completely different context. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video was AI-generated and misrepresented. A clip from PM Modi's visit to Surat was falsely portrayed as an announcement of a financial scheme. The misleading video was shared on social media to deceive viewers.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video claiming Air Marshal 'admitted Pakistani drones infiltrated Delhi, Gujarat' is false and fabricated
content: New Delhi, September 29 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of Air Marshal Rakesh Sinha, purportedly from an exclusive interview with Press Trust of India (PTI), has gone viral on social media with the claim that he admitted "Pakistani drones had infiltrated Delhi and Gujarat, and that India lost two S-400 air defence systems due to their surveillance". The clip shows him allegedly stating that Prime Minister Narendra Modi directed the forces to prevent further infiltrations and that the losses were linked to Operation Sindoor. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the viral video has been digitally manipulated. In the original interview, Air Marshal Sinha only spoke about the upcoming 'Cold Start' exercise in October to test drones and counter-drones, with the participation of all three services, industry, R&D, and academia. He did not make any remarks about Pakistani drones reaching Delhi or Gujarat, or about the destruction of S-400 systems. Claim: A video featuring Air Marshal Rakesh Sinha in an exclusive interview with PTI was shared by an X user, 'The Whistle Blower', claiming that he admitted that Pakistani drones reached Delhi and Gujarat, and that S-400 systems were destroyed because of their surveillance. "We are conducting an exercise, Cold Start, which will be conducted in the first week of October, since Pakistani drones infiltrated Delhi & Gujarat. PM Modi told us that there should be no more infiltration from Pakistani drones. We have already lost two S-400 systems because of them…," says Air Marshal Rakesh Sinha. The post clocked 118.8k views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on X to find the post by Press Trust of India and found a post uploaded on September 23, 2025. In the 00:24-second video, the Air Marshal did not mention anything about Pakistani drones or the loss of S-400 systems. He said, "We are conducting an exercise, Cold Start, which will be conducted in the first week of October. In the central sector, where we will test the drones and counter-drones. All three services, industry partners, and R&D, academia, everyone will be participating." Upon listening to the entire interview, the Desk noticed the change in the voice of the viral video, which hinted that it might be manipulated. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Next, the Desk also came across a report by PTI published on September 23, but it did not mention anything about Pakistani drones. Given the seriousness of the matter, such a statement by the Air Marshal would have been carried by several media outlets. However, the report highlighted that in his address at a conference on air defence systems here, Air Marshal Rakesh Sinha, Deputy Chief of Integrated Defence Staff (OPS) at HQ IDS, also spoke of the lessons drawn from Operation Sindoor and the need to "stay ahead" of the adversary in military thinking and planning. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking the investigation ahead, the Desk then ran the audio from the viral video through Resemble AI, an AI-detection tool, which also highlighted that the audio is Fake. Below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim is entirely fake and fabricated. The video has been digitally manipulated. In the original recording, Air Marshal Rakesh Sinha made no such remarks.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: This doctored video of Ladakh DGP falsely shows him admitting that Sonam Wangchuk was arrested without evidence; details inside
content: New Delhi, September 30 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Days after climate activist Sonam Wangchuk was arrested and charged under the stringent National Security Act (NSA) for allegedly being one of the prime accused in the violence that erupted in Leh, a video of Ladakh ADGP Dr. S. D. Singh purportedly stating that Wangchuk had been arrested without any proof was recently shared on social media. The video allegedly showed the Ladakh ADGP admitting to the media that they had arrested Wangchuk on the directions of the Indian Defence Minister, and that too without any evidence against him. In its investigation, however, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found the video to be doctored. The original video actually showed Ladakh Director General of Police (DGP) S. D. Singh Jamwal explaining the reasons for Wangchuk's arrest and defending the police action of firing at protestors. The viral clip had been manipulated to insert a false statement, misleading viewers. Claim An X user, Shalini Shukla (@shalini_sh1), shared a video on September 29 that purportedly showed ADGP Ladakh Dr S. D. Singh provided details about the arrest of environmental activist Sonam Wangchuk following the recent violence in Leh. The video allegedly showed the ADGP confirming to the media that the police had not found any evidence against Wangchuk but arrested him on the directions of Indian Defence Minister Rajnath Singh. "Breaking News: ADGP Ladakh Dr S. D. Singh admits that he arrested Sonam Wangchuk on the directions of the Indian Defence Minister without any evidence," the user wrote in the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing the story, the video garnered 304.1k views and 3.6k likes) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such videos can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. Next, to verify the authenticity of the video, the Desk analysed it closely. The viral clip included a logo of The New Indian Express, suggesting it might have been taken from a video originally published by the news portal. A customised keyword search led the Desk to the same video, posted by The New Indian Express on its official YouTube channel on September 27, 2025. The video identified the official as Ladakh Director General of Police S. D. Singh Jamwal—not ADGP. Upon careful review, the Desk found that nowhere in the original video did the DGP say that Wangchuk had been arrested without evidence or at the behest of the Defence Minister. This suggested the viral video had been doctored. In fact, the original video showed the Ladakh DGP describing Wangchuk as a prime accused in the Leh violence, stating that he was being investigated for alleged links with Pakistan. He also defended the police action against protesters, calling it an act of "self-defence." Here is the original video link and a screenshot: A comparison image highlights the visual similarities between the viral clip and the video from The New Indian Express. The Desk also found other news reports carrying the same video clip of the Ladakh DGP speaking to the media about Wangchuk's arrest and the Leh violence. In none of them did he make the purported remarks heard in the viral version. Links to two such reports can be found here and here . In the final step, the Desk extracted the audio from the viral video and ran it through Resemble AI, an AI detection tool. The tool indicated that while the voice seemed real, it may have been an impersonation. Here is the screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was edited with fake audio and wrongly showed Ladakh DGP S D Singh Jamwal admitting to arresting Sonam Wangchuk without evidence, which is false.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, Sonam Wangchuk did not say 'Ladakh won't stop China in case of attack'; old video clip shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, September 30 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of Ladakh activist Sonam Wangchuk, purportedly shot during his hunger strike, was shared on social media with the claim that he allegedly said if China were to attack India through Ladakh, "we wouldn't stop them." The clip was circulated as supposed evidence that Wangchuk questioned Ladakh's role in defending the country. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false. The viral footage is not recent but clipped from a longer video Wangchuk posted on his official X account in March 2024. In the original speech, delivered on the seventh day of his fast, Wangchuk was quoting a local comedian to highlight Ladakhis' frustration with the Centre. He went on to clarify that the people of Ladakh have always stood, and will continue to stand, as protectors of India's borders. The selective edit strips away this context and falsely suggests that Wangchuk himself made the controversial remark. Earlier this week, Ladakh witnessed violent protests during a shutdown call. At least four people died and dozens were injured as demonstrators clashed with the police. Climate activist Wangchuk, who spearheaded the agitation, ended his 15-day hunger strike in the wake of the violence, appealing for calm. The Centre, however, blamed him for the unrest, alleging that his fiery speeches, including references to "Gen Z protests in Nepal", provoked demonstrators. Wangchuk has since been arrested. Claim: A video featuring Ladakh activist Sonam Wangchuk, apparently during his hunger strike, was shared by a Facebook user 'സംഘശക്തി - തലായി തലശ്ശേരി' on September 27, claiming that he allegedly said that if China were to attack India through Ladakh, we wouldn't stop them. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a similar video uploaded on Sonam Wangchuk's official X account on March 12, 2024. Making it clear that the video is not recent. Wangchuk can be seen in the same attire in the video posted on the X account as visible in the recent social media post. Upon reviewing the entire 3-minute 16-second video, it was discovered that a portion of the original footage had been clipped and shared with a false claim on social media. Sonam Wangchuk was explaining the hunger strike on the evening of the seventh day. He explains that despite the heavy snowfall in the morning, a large number of people, including students, young people, monks, and ex-servicemen, joined the protest. Speaking as an ex-serviceman, Wangchuk also explained the importance of the role played by volunteers and scouts in Ladakh during the Indo-Pak war. He then repeated the words of a comedian. "There is a famous comedian here, and his words are as follows: 'If China enters here, the people of Ladakh will sacrifice their lives to stop them. But if the Indian government does nothing for us, then next time the Chinese come, we will pave the way for them, that is, we will not stop them. Why should we sacrifice our lives when we are not protected?' After saying this, the police questioned the comedian," Wangchuk quoted the comedian as saying. At the end of the video, Wangchuk expresses hope that the government will keep its promises and that the people of Ladakh will continue to protect India, just as they have always done. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. As part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find reports from 2024 that covered his hunger strike. We came across an article by The Hindu published on October 21, 2024, which highlighted that climate activist Sonam Wangchuk and others from Ladakh ended their hunger strike after 16 days on Monday (October 21, 2024) following an invitation from the Union Ministry of Home Affairs to resume dialogue with civil society leaders from the region. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. He staged a hunger strike in October 2024, which was called off after the Home Ministry assured him that talks on Ladakh's demands would resume. "Join Secretary, Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, Prashant Lokhande met the activists, who have been sitting on an indefinite fast at Delhi's Ladakh Bhawan since October 6, and handed them a letter from the home ministry. The letter said the high-powered committee of the ministry, which was holding talks with representatives from Ladakh, will hold the next meeting on December 3," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Meanwhile, Sonam Wangchuk has been charged under the stringent National Security Act (NSA) that provides for extended preventive detention without any scope for bail. A curfew has been imposed in Leh, and internet services have been snapped to stop the spread of misinformation. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video featuring Sonam Wangchuk, allegedly stating that he would not stop China from attacking India through Ladakh, is a clipped portion of the original video. Wangchuk was actually quoting a comedian during his hunger strike in March 2024.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-manipulated video falsely claims Dharmendra Pradhan announced removal of numbers 6 and 0 from math syllabus
content: New Delhi, September 30 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, purportedly from a recent public interaction, was shared on social media with the claim that he announced the BJP government's decision to remove the numbers 6 and 0 from the mathematics syllabus to "avoid embarrassment for the Indian Air Force." The clip further shows him allegedly linking the move to Pakistan downing six Indian jets, and presenting it as part of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's effort to reshape history. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the video is digitally manipulated using AI. In the original event, an hour-long conversation at The Hindu MIND- Pradhan spoke about the National Education Policy (NEP), dropout rates, and the need for multimodal strategies to boost enrolment. He made no reference whatsoever to altering the math syllabus or to Pakistan's military claims. The viral video has been circulated with a false claim. Claim: A user shared a video featuring Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan addressing a gathering, 'The Whistle Blower', on September 26, claiming that he announced the BJP government had decided to remove the numbers 6 and 0 from the math syllabus to avoid embarrassment for the Indian Air Force. He also alleges that Pakistan downed six Indian jets. "We have created a huge paradigm shift for the Indian students. We have completely changed the curriculum, especially in Maths. We have observed that ever since Pakistan has downed our six jets, we have decided to remove 0 and 6 from our Math syllabus. This speaks a lot about PM Modi's effort to glorify our culture and remove the painful parts that can't be processed, as they can't be made part of our history," says Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation As part of the investigation, the Desk ran a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant reports that covered such a remark. However, we could not find any such report, and given the seriousness of the statement, it would have been carried by several media outlets. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted another set of customised searches to find the original video. The search led us to the extended video on the official YouTube Channel of The Hindu, published on September 22, 2025. Pradhan was interacting at The Hindu MIND, and upon analysing 1-hour 20-minute video, we did not find him making any such remark or statement. This suggested that the viral video might have been manipulated. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. According to The Hindu article dated September 22, Pradhan lauded the National Education Policy (NEP) and stated that it was rooted in the Indian ethos and also futuristic. "Responding to a question on the dropout rate of students in schools across India, Pradhan advocated for a multimodal strategy for the enrolment percentage to remain 100% even in Standard 12," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report. Taking the investigation further, the Desk carefully analysed the video and found several discrepancies. It then extracted the audio from the video and ran it through Resemble AI, an AI-detection tool. It detected that the audio is fake. Below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video has been manipulated using AI. Dharmendra Pradhan never made such a remark.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Viral video of Bangkok road collapse falsely linked to Delhi; details inside
content: New Delhi, September 30 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a busy road suddenly caving in has gone viral on social media with claims that it was filmed in Delhi, where ongoing metro construction allegedly caused the collapse. The clip, shared by several users on Instagram and Facebook, suggests that tunnelling work under the city triggered a massive sinkhole. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the claim is false. The video is not from Delhi at all but from Bangkok, Thailand, where a large sinkhole opened in front of Vajira Hospital on September 24, 2025, after soil seeped into an underground metro tunnel. Claim: A video showing a road caving in was shared by an Instagram user, 'vipan_mahadev_2055,' on September 26, claiming that the incident occurred in Delhi due to ongoing metro construction work underground. "Result of walking the metro underground," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. Upon further scanning the search results, the Desk came across the same video uploaded to YouTube Shorts by a user stating that the road had collapsed in Bangkok, Thailand. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combined image highlighting the similarities between the content seen in the social media post, which claims it is from Delhi, and the YouTube short. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search. The video was uploaded on an Instagram page by the user 'thenowindia' on September 24, 2025, from a different angle. It mentioned that a giant 50-meter-deep sinkhole opened near Vajira Hospital in Bangkok. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking the investigation forward, the Desk searched for relevant reports that covered the incident and found a report by Nation Thailand, published on September 24, which highlighted that Bangkok Governor Chadchart Sittipunt had inspected the road subsidence in front of Vajira Hospital on Samsen Road, Dusit District. He explained that the collapse was caused by soil entering the underground metro tunnel at the junction between the tunnel and the station. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Using Google Street View, we located Vajira Hospital on Samsen Road, Dusit District. We created a combination image, which confirmed that the incident occurred in Bangkok, not in Delhi. As part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find reports that cited incidents of road caving in due to the under-construction metro. Our search led us to a report by Dainik Jagran published on August 9, 2025, which mentioned that a portion of the under-construction metro line near the Masoodpur flyover in Vasant Kunj caved in. According to the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC), approximately 10-15 meters of pavement in the excavation area caved in. Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of a road collapsing and forming a large sinkhole in Bangkok is being falsely shared, implying it occurred in Delhi.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of cable car crashed in Chhattisgarh falsely shared claiming ropeway accident occurred in Varanasi; details inside
content: New Delhi, September 30 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it depicted a ropeway accident in Varanasi, alleging that the ropeway project collapsed immediately after inauguration. The user shared the video, claiming it showed a ropeway cabin car coming crashing down in Varanasi, thus injuring a BJP worker sitting inside it. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video was unrelated to Varanasi. It actually showed a ropeway accident in Chhattisgarh, where a cable car crashed from a small height at a hilltop temple in Rajnandgaon, injuring a BJP leader. The video was falsely shared on social media, misrepresenting it as a Varanasi ropeway accident. Claim On September 27, X user Abu Khan (@AbuKhanoo1) shared a post claiming that the Varanasi ropeway project, built at a cost of ₹800 crore, collapsed immediately after inauguration. The post stated that a ropeway cabin crashed, injuring a BJP worker inside. "Modi ji had a 4-kilometre-long ropeway built in Banaras, costing about ₹800 crore. But as soon as it was inaugurated, the ropeway met with an accident, and the cabin came crashing down. The most interesting part— a BJP leader also tumbled down with it," the user captioned the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Desk's Google Lens search also led to a video shared on NDTV Chhattisgarh's official YouTube channel on April 25, 2025. The video showed the same visuals as the social media post—a man appearing distressed near an overturned ropeway cabin. Upon careful analysis, it was found that the video depicted an accident at a hilltop temple in Rajnandgaon, Chhattisgarh, where a BJP leader was injured after the cable car he was travelling in crashed from a small height. The video had no connection to the Varanasi ropeway project. The report stated that BJP state general secretary Bharat Lal Verma sustained injuries in the accident. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the visual similarities between the social media video and the one shared by NDTV Chhattisgarh. The search also led the Desk to a PTI report shared by The Print, which provided further details on how the accident occurred. The report, quoting an official, mentioned, "As per preliminary information, when the gear of the trolley was changed to slow it down for its arrival at the base station, the cable car got detached and crashed on the ground from a small height. "While other occupants were reported to be safe, Verma sustained injuries on his back and shoulder," the official added. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to check if any similar accident occurred in Varanasi. The search results, however, did not yield any credible news reports to confirm this. Had the incident occurred, the media would have covered it extensively. The search did, however, lead the Desk to a Times of India report published on August 26, which stated, "Varanasi's ambitious ropeway project is now being fast-tracked with Divisional Commissioner S. Rajalingam fixing Dec 12 as the deadline to complete all works at the last station near Godowlia Crossing (GC)." Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video depicting a ropeway accident in Chhattisgarh was falsely shared as a ropeway accident from Varanasi.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2021 statement by PM Modi targeting Mamata Banerjee over corruption charges shared out of context to falsely claim he called himself a thief
content: New Delhi, September 30 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, seemingly from a public event where he stated, "If my mother had stopped me when I used to commit petty thefts, I would not have become such a big dacoit," was recently shared on social media. The clip was circulated in a way that purported to present the Prime Minister as calling himself a thief. In its investigation, however, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found that the video had been shared out of context. The clip was from Prime Minister Modi's address in Siliguri, West Bengal, in 2021, where he made the statement while targeting Mamata Banerjee and the TMC over corruption charges. In his speech, he narrated a story about a thief to illustrate how wrongdoing must be curbed at an early stage before it escalates into bigger crimes. Thus, the viral claim is false. An old and unrelated statement of Prime Minister Modi, aimed at Mamata Banerjee, was falsely circulated on social media as if he had called himself a thief. Claim An X handle with the username @NetaFlixIndia shared on September 26 a video allegedly showing Prime Minister Narendra Modi stating that "if my mother had stopped me when I used to commit petty thefts, I would not have become such a big dacoit." The video was shared in a way that depicted PM Modi calling himself a thief. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing the story, the video had garnered 14k views) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a video shared on the official YouTube channel of PMO India on April 10, 2021. It was found that the clip of PM Modi speaking about stealing, as seen in the viral post, was also present in the official video at the 40:39 timestamp. The video dated back to 2021 and was from Siliguri, where PM Modi delivered a public address. Upon careful analysis, the Desk found that the statement made by Prime Minister Modi was in reference to his attack on West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee, rather than an admission about himself. In the speech, PM Modi accused Mamata Banerjee and the TMC of corruption, narrating a story about a thief to emphasise the importance of stopping wrongdoing at an early stage before it escalates into bigger crimes. During his address, PM Modi said: "Tolabazi in every scheme...cut money in every scheme... A few days ago, Didi said in Siliguri that her tolabaz takes only 100, 200, and 500 rupees. What's the big deal with that? Didi said calmly that the tolabaz take 100, 200, and 500 rupees with ease... why does Modi shout so much about this? Brothers and sisters, when we were young, we heard a story. In that story, a very big bandit was sentenced to death. When he was asked about his last wish, he said he wanted to meet his mother. The government made arrangements, and when he met her, he pounced on her and bit off her nose. When people asked why he did this, he said: 'If my mother had stopped me when I was committing petty thefts, I wouldn't have become such a big robber. I wouldn't have had to go to the gallows." Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a 2021 statement by PM Modi targeting Mamata Banerjee over corruption charges was shared out of context to mislead viewers.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally manipulated video falsely claims 'Vote Chor' Slogans raised at Bihar Deputy CM Samrat Choudhary's rally
content: New Delhi, September 30 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): As political fervour ahead of the upcoming assembly elections continues to swirl across Bihar, with leaders from both ruling and opposition parties engaging in public outreach programmes, a purported social media video showing chants of "Vote Chor, Gaddi Chhod" being raised at a rally of Bihar Deputy Chief Minister is being widely shared. The footage allegedly showed the Bihar Deputy Chief Minister standing atop a bus and waving to the crowd when slogans of "Vote Chor" were raised against him. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found that it had been digitally manipulated. While the visuals showing Samrat Choudhary waving at the crowd are real, the voice with the slogans in the background was found to have been superimposed. A digitally manipulated video was falsely shared on social media to mislead viewers. It is also pertinent to note that Congress leader Rahul Gandhi had earlier alleged in a news conference that systemic "vote chori" (vote theft) was being orchestrated by the Bharatiya Janata Party. Since then, opposition leaders have been using this slogan to target the government. Claim An X user, Priyanka Bharti (@priyanka2bharti), shared a video on September 24, purportedly showing "Vote Chor" slogans being raised at a rally of Bihar Deputy Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary. The footage showed the Deputy Chief Minister standing atop a bus and waving to the crowd while the slogans were allegedly being raised. "Look at this! We don't just say that every child in the country is chanting the slogan 'Vote Chor, Gaddi Chhod!' Up on the bus, Samrat Choudhary is standing, and from below, slogans are being shouted: 'Vote Chor, Gaddi Chhod!'" the user captioned the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video garnered 157.6k views) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such videos can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search also led the Desk to a YouTube video posted by the channel "jhahuri madhubni bihar1" on July 26, 2025. The Desk found that the video included the same visuals as the viral video, showing Bihar Deputy Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary standing atop a bus and waving at the crowd. The video also showed Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar present on the occasion, sitting inside the bus and acknowledging the waves of people with folded hands. However, nowhere in the video were the "Vote Chori" slogans heard. The video was shared with the caption, "Nitish Kumar's arrival at Laukahi block in Bihar's Madhubani district." The video was shared with the caption, 'Nitish Kumar's arrival at Laukahi block in Bihar's Madhubani district'. Here is the link and archive link to the video, along with a screenshot. Below is a combined image showcasing the visuals depicted in the viral video and the YouTube video from the same event. Next, the Desk conducted a customised Google search to find details regarding Nitish Kumar's roadshow in Madhubani district. The search led to a Jagran report published on July 26, which confirmed that Chief Minister Nitish Kumar had visited Madhubani on July 26. The report mentioned: "Chief Minister Nitish Kumar held a road show and unveiled a statue in Madhubani. He also laid the foundation stone for five projects worth ₹649 crore. He then departed for Sitamarhi. He was accompanied in the roadshow by Deputy Chief Ministers Samrat Choudhary and Sanjay Jha." Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. In the subsequent part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to determine when the opposition first raised the 'Vote Chori' allegations. The search led the Desk to a press release published on the official website of the Congress, which elaborated on the claims of vote chori that Rahul Gandhi raised against the ruling party on August 7, 2025. During the press conference, Rahul Gandhi targeted the BJP over vote chori, which later also garnered strong support from hundreds of opposition lawmakers. It is thus clear that the video of Samrat Choudhary conducting a roadshow in Madhubani had no connection to the vote chori slogans, as the roadshow took place in July, while the allegations were first raised in August. Here is the link to the press release published on the Congress Party's website. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video claiming 'Vote Chor, Gaddi Chhod' slogans were raised at Bihar Deputy Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary's rally was digitally manipulated. While the visuals of Choudhary waving to the crowd are real, the audio of the slogans was artificially added and does not correspond to the actual event.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video of a diver given CPR falsely shared as late singer Zubeen Garg's final moments; details inside
content: New Delhi, September 30 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media video showing a group of divers allegedly helping a fellow diver who was lying unconscious on a boat while receiving CPR treatment was recently shared online. Users claimed the video depicted the last moments of legendary singer Zubeen Garg, who was allegedly administered primary medical intervention before he died in Singapore on September 19. The clip was circulated in the context of earlier reports suggesting that the Assamese singer was killed while scuba diving in Singapore. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it to be unrelated to Garg's death. The video was initially created using AI and was falsely shared on social media to mislead viewers. Claim An Instagram user, Rajkumar Raj, shared a video on September 22, purportedly depicting the last moments of legendary singer Zubeen Garg before he died in Singapore on September 19. The footage allegedly showed Garg (in a diver's costume) lying unconscious on a boat, while fellow divers were seen giving him CPR and urging him to respond. The clip circulated alongside reports that had earlier claimed Garg died while scuba diving. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search via Google Lens also led the Desk to the same video shared by Instagram user raja_faizan_vlog on September 20, 2025. The user, who describes himself as a digital creator with over 31k followers, posted the same video along with a caption that featured one of Zubeen Garg's viral videos from Singapore. However, in the additional part of the caption, he also clearly stated that the video was a creative AI-generated story made as a tribute to Zubeen Garg. He further clarified: "It is not real footage and does not represent actual events. All visuals and voices are AI creations following Instagram's policy. Made with love and respect for Zubeen Da." Thus, it was established that the video was not linked to the death of Zubeen Garg but was created using AI as a tribute to him. However, it has since been picked up by other social media users without verifying its authenticity. Here is the link and archive link to the video, along with a screenshot. In the subsequent part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find details about the cause of Zubeen Garg's death. The search led to a September 20 report by The Indian Express, which confirmed drowning as the cause of death. The report stated: "The popular Indian singer was swimming without a life jacket during his accidental death. While it was initially reported that Garg died while scuba diving, Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma later stated the singer drowned while swimming without a life jacket, despite repeated warnings from lifeguards." Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an AI-generated video showing a scuba diver being given CPR was falsely linked to the death of Assamese singer Zubeen Garg.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI generated image of Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi holding 'I love Muhammad' poster shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, October 2 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): As Uttar Pradesh's Bareilly reels from violent clashes linked to the ongoing 'I love Muhammad' poster controversy late last week, a purported social media image showing Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi along with his sister and Wayanad MP Priyanka Gandhi was widely shared. The image allegedly showed the two leaders extending support to the protest by themselves holding a 'I love Muhammad' poster. The same image also depicted several other individuals in the background carrying similar posters. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found the image to be AI-generated and falsely shared to mislead viewers. Claim A Facebook user, Mukhtar Ahmad Munna, shared on September 27 an image purportedly showing Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi holding 'I love Muhammad' poster. The same image also depicted several other individuals in the background carrying similar posters. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing, the post had received 2.8k likes.) Investigation The Desk ran the image shared in the social media post through Google Lens. This led to several social media accounts sharing the same image, falsely depicting Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi standing with 'I love Muhammad' posters. Links to two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here , respectively. Next, the Desk thoroughly examined the image to verify its authenticity, i.e., whether it was real or AI-generated. The analysis revealed multiple inconsistencies, suggesting the image was AI-generated. For instance, the text on the placard was missing and an extra hand appeared between Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi while holding the poster. Also, a person in the background had a visibly warped face. Below is a screenshot highlighting the findings: Taking cues from these observations, the Desk ran the viral image through two AI-detection tools — Hive Moderation and Was It AI. Results from both platforms confirmed that the image of Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi holding the 'I love Muhammad' poster was AI-generated and did not depict a real incident. Below are the screenshots of the results: In the subsequent part of the investigation, the Desk also conducted a customised keyword search on Google to determine whether Rahul Gandhi or Priyanka Gandhi had issued any statements regarding the protest, which had recently caused widespread attention across India. The search found no credible news reports or statements from the leaders themselves. Instead, the search led to a PTI report published on September 28, in which Congress' media and publicity department head Pawan Khera, highlighted India's syncretic cultural traditions while addressing the controversy on the matter. In his statement targeting the BJP, Khera stated, "In a harmonious country that has seen the tradition of mystic saint Meerabai and Sufism, such 'dwarfs' have come who see an enemy of our rich cultural tradition in a seven-year-old boy. They killed and then hung the body of a seven-year-old because he was from another religion. What harm could that child cause to our cultural heritage?" He further added, "You say in a market in Indore that Muslims should be pushed out. Our culture is so vast, and you find these working-class Muslims a danger. If someone says I love Muhammad, you have a problem with it. If that person loves his or her prophet, you should love that person." Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the social media image showing Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi holding "I love Muhammad" poster was AI-generated and falsely shared to mislead viewers, with no connection to any real-life event.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Scripted video of roadside loot falsely shared as real incident; details inside
content: New Delhi, October 3 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing two individuals allegedly being robbed by a duo they had stopped to help was recently shared on social media, accompanied by the claim that it depicted a real incident. The clip appeared to show two people riding through a lane on a two-wheeler. They stopped to assist a duo lying on the road, seemingly unconscious after falling from their vehicle, which was also seen nearby. However, as the video progressed, it revealed that the duo had staged the situation. They attacked and looted the unsuspecting individuals and fled on their two-wheeler. The Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk, however, found that the video was scripted and staged for entertainment and informational purposes. It bore no connection to any real-life incident and was misleadingly shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An Instagram user, Sneha Sharma (@sharma_sneha1001), shared on September 23 a video that purportedly showed two individuals being tricked before being attacked and looted by two men. The video showed the victims riding through a lane on their two-wheeler when they stopped to help a duo lying unconscious on the road next to their own vehicle. As the individuals tried to help them stand, the duo suddenly attacked them, seemingly knocking them unconscious, and fled on their two-wheeler. The user sharing the video claimed it depicted a real incident. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively: The search results also led the Desk to a video posted on a Facebook page named K94 Studio Space on September 15, 2025. The Desk found that the social media video was similar to the one shared on the Facebook page, but shot from a different angle. However, additional details shared by the Facebook page in the comments section clarified that the video was not factual but scripted and created to raise awareness. The user wrote: "This is a fictional scenario, not real. The content is made to spread awareness, educate, and encourage caution. Please keep this in mind while watching." Here is the link and archive link to the Facebook post, along with a screenshot: A combined image below highlights that the content in the viral video matches the video posted by the Facebook page. Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk also reviewed other videos posted by the Facebook page and found that it is known for posting scripted content. Links to two such videos can be found here and here . Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video, which claims to show two individuals being looted by a duo whom they stopped to help, is scripted. The footage was created for awareness and entertainment purposes and has no link to any real-life incident.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Varanasi's old Ramleela–Namaz tradition video falsely shared with communal twist
content: New Delhi, October 3 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported video shared on social media showed members of the Muslim community offering namaz at a venue where a traditional Ramleela performance by the Hindu community was being held. Users claimed that the namaz was deliberately provided at the exact location to instigate communal tensions and provoke riots. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it had been shared with a false communal claim to mislead viewers. In reality, the footage depicts a 500-year-old tradition from Varanasi, specifically from the Lat Bhairav Ramleela. As part of this practice, members of the Muslim community offer namaz on one side of the Lat Bhairav temple platform. At the same time, verses from the Ramcharitmanas are recited on the other. This centuries-old example of communal harmony in Varanasi was thus misleadingly circulated on social media with a false narrative. Claim An X handle with the username Paise Wala (@AmirLadka) shared a video on September 30, purportedly showing members of the Muslim community offering namaz at a place where a Ramleela play was already ongoing. The user claimed the act was meant to incite communal tensions and provoke riots. The post read: "The Ramleela was going on. But the jihadis deliberately decided to offer namaz on the road in a way meant to provoke, so that people would get triggered and riots would break out." Here are the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered 64.6k views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search via Google Lens also led the Desk to a video shared on the official Instagram page of Dalimss News Banaras, a leading local news portal from Varanasi, on September 27, 2025. The Desk found the video posted by the local news portal was identical to the viral clip. However, the accompanying details revealed that the video actually depicted a centuries-old tradition from Varanasi's Lat Bhairav Ramleela, where members of the Muslim community offer namaz alongside recitations from the Ramcharitmanas. "This practice has been continuing for about 574 years," the post mentioned. The post also quoted Dayashankar Tripathi, the chief narrator of the Ramleela Committee, stating: "The Jayant Netra Bhang Leela of Shri Lat Bhairav Ramleela Committee is always extraordinary. On this day, while the chants of Ramcharitmanas verses continue and dialogues of the play move forward, Muslim brothers complete their namaz alongside the azaan." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: A comparison of screenshots highlighted the visual similarities between the viral video and the one shared by the news portal. Additionally, the Desk found a detailed news report published by Amar Ujala on September 25, 2025, elaborating on the tradition. The report stated that the tradition of Lat Bhairav's Ramleela has continued since the time of Tulsidas and is now considered a living example of Kashi's Ganga-Jamuni culture. The report also carried images matching the keyframes extracted from the viral video, further confirming that the video originally depicted this centuries-old tradition from Varanasi but was being shared with false claims. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was misrepresented. The footage, originally depicting a centuries-old tradition from Varanasi's Lat Bhairav Ramleela, where Muslim community members offer namaz alongside the chanting of Ramcharitmanas, was falsely shared with a communal claim to mislead viewers.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Doctored video falsely claims 'ADC Leh said Home Ministry ordered Wangchuk's arrest'; details inside
content: New Delhi, October 3 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Days after climate activist Sonam Wangchuk was arrested under the stringent National Security Act (NSA) for allegedly being one of the prime accused in the violence that erupted in Leh last month, a social media video purportedly showing Additional Deputy Commissioner (ADC) Leh, Ghulam Mohd, was shared online. The clip appeared to show him addressing a press conference with Additional Superintendent of Police, Leh, Regzin Sangdup, and claiming that Wangchuk had been arrested on the orders of the Union Home Ministry, even alleging that he was a Pakistani spy. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it had been digitally altered. The original clip showed the ADC Leh briefing the media on the unfolding situation in Leh after the violent clashes. He was also seen urging residents to maintain law and order following the unrest that left four dead and 90 injured. The doctored video of the Leh official was misleadingly circulated on social media to create a false impression. Claim An X user, Rakesh Mohan Chaturvedi (@_Rakesh_RC), shared a video on October 3, purportedly showing ADC Leh, Ghulam Muhammad, stating that they had arrested climate activist Sonam Wangchuk at the direction of the Union Home Ministry. The video allegedly showed the ADC Leh stating that they had received an order from Amit Shah's office to charge Wangchuk as a Pakistani spy. In a post, the user wrote: "The officer is categorically saying the orders to charge Sonam Wangchuk as a Pakistani agent and to arrest him came from the Union Home Ministry headed by Amit Shah." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here : The search via Google Lens also led the Desk to a video shared on the official Facebook page of the Department of Information and Public Relations, Leh, UT Ladakh. The video, posted on September 25, was of a press briefing conducted by the ADC Leh along with ASP Leh, Regzin Sangdup. The background settings in this official video matched those seen in the viral clip. After careful analysis, nowhere in the original press briefing did the ADC Leh state that they had arrested Wangchuk on the direction of the Union Home Ministry, nor did he mention charging Wangchuk as a Pakistani spy under instructions from the Home Ministry. The original clip showed the ADC Leh briefing on the unfolding situation in Leh after the violent clashes and urging the public to maintain law and order following the unrest that killed four and injured 90. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot. A comparison image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral clip and the official video from the Department of Information & Public Relations, Leh, Ladakh. Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google search on the charges under which Sonam Wangchuk was being detained. The search led to a Press Trust of India report published on September 26, which stated that the climate activist was being detained under the NSA. The report mentioned: "The climate activist had been arrested from his village Ulyaktopo by a strong team of Ladakh Police, led by Director General S D Singh Jamwal, and was immediately shifted to the Jodhpur Central Jail in Rajasthan." Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was digitally altered with fake audio and falsely showed ADC Leh stating that Wangchuk had been arrested and charged with spying for Pakistan at the direction of the Union Home Ministry, which is untrue.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video clip shared on social media to falsely claim actor Rani Mukerji scolded Rajdeep Sardesai over her weight remark; details inside
content: New Delhi, October 6 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A short video clip from the India Today Conclave Mumbai 2025 featuring journalist Rajdeep Sardesai and actor Rani Mukerji has gone viral on social media, with claims that Sardesai asked the actress if she had "become very fat after marriage." Several users alleged that Mukerji scolded him in response and that this portion of the event was edited out of the official coverage. The claim gained traction online, sparking criticism against Sardesai. In the clip, Mukerji can be heard saying, "Chup chap baith jaa idhar, baith jaa idhar," which many users misinterpreted as an angry retort to the alleged weight-related remark. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false. The viral video is clipped out of context from a longer segment of the conclave, where Sardesai had asked Mukerji to recreate a scene from her film Mardaani. The exchange was a scripted act from the movie, not a personal comment on her appearance. Claim: A video from India Today's conclave was shared by an X user, Amitabh Chaudhary, on October 3, claiming that journalist Rajdeep Sardesai, during an interaction with actor Rani Mukerji, asked her if she had "become obese after marriage," to which she scolded him on the spot. "It is being heard that Rajdeep Sardesai asked Rani Mukerji a question that, after marriage, you have become obese. So Rani Mukerji scolded him right there, and the video was immediately edited, and this part was not shown," read the post's caption. In the 00:07-second video, Mukherji can be heard shouting, "'Chup chap baith jaa idhar, baith jaa idhar'" The post clocked 64.6k views on social media. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the video through Reverse Image Search and found that several other users had also shared the same video with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. As part of the investigation, the Desk first conducted a customised keyword search to find the original video of the conclave. We found the video uploaded on the official YouTube channel of India Today, dated September 26, 2025. Watching the 48-minute-long video, we found that in one segment, journalist Rajdeep Sardesai interviewed National Award-winning actress Rani Mukerji, discussing her roles in films like "Mardaani" and "Mrs Chatterjee vs. Norway." The next part of the conversation also featured former IPS officer Meera Chaddha Borwankar, whose life inspired the film Mardaani. During the discussion, Mardaani was mentioned several times, and Rajdeep requested Rani Mukerji to recreate a scene from Mardaani for the audience. At 31 minutes into the video, former IPS officer Meera Chadha Borwankar, referring to a scene from Mardaani, said, "Look, there was a scene in Mardaani where she (Rani Mukerji) was standing in the police station. She was very short, about 5 feet tall, and there were very tall and broad policemen standing in front of her. In her own way, she asks them to look into a case, and they regard her the way the director has portrayed them: all the masculine police officers, probably from the crime branch, look at her, accept her leadership, and do what they are asked to do. That one scene was compelling, showing that gender doesn't matter here, but work efficiency and perhaps rank matter. I find that scene truly extraordinary." Rajdeep then requests her to reprise her role from Mardaani. During this, Rajdeep acts like a thug. Rani Mukerji, like her character from that film, scolds him and tells him to sit down. After this act, the audience applauds and praises him. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. The clipped version, which was shared in a viral post, was uploaded on the official Facebook page of India Today on September 26, 2025. The post's caption read: "#IndiaTodayConclaveMumbai2025 | Rani Mukherjee throws some playful tough looks at @SardesaiRajdeep—definitely a moment you don't want to miss!" Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Furthermore, we also found a video containing the above portion, which was uploaded to Aaj Tak's Facebook page on September 27, 2025. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. During our investigation, we also contacted journalist Rajdeep Sardesai for clarification. The story will be updated as and when we receive a statement from him. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a clipped portion of the original video was shared with a false claim on social media. The two were actually recreating a scene from the film Mardaani on stage.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Scripted video showing a Muslim man arguing with a female police official in UP falsely shared as real
content: New Delhi, October 6 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users have recently shared a video claiming it shows a recent incident in Uttar Pradesh, where a man wearing a skull cap is seen engaged in a heated altercation with a female police official. Users alleged that the man, accompanied by another individual, misbehaved with the policewoman as she confronted them. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video was scripted. It had no connection to any real-life incident and was misleadingly circulated on social media with a false claim. Claim An X user, Arun Yadav (@ArunKalkiArmy), shared a video on October 1, purportedly showing an incident from Uttar Pradesh, where a man wearing a skull cap, accompanied by another individual, was seen misbehaving with a woman police official. The video also appeared to show the policewoman slapping the man as he attempted to bribe her by placing a bundle of currency notes in her hand. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered over 444k views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search results from Google Lens also led the Desk to a video posted on a YouTube channel named Amit Dixit Social Message on September 21, 2025. The Desk found that the video, uploaded by it, included the same visuals as the viral clip, showing an altercation that erupted between an individual wearing a skull cap and a uniform-clad woman. However, a careful analysis of the video showed that at the 00:03 timestamp, a disclaimer appeared stating that the video was scripted and bore no connection to any real incident. "The names, characters, occupations, places, and events depicted in this video are fictitious. It bears no resemblance to any person, living or dead. Any connection to any real-life event or character is purely coincidental," the disclaimer read. The video was shared with the caption, "Watch the teacher being beaten in front of the police." Here is the link and archive link to the video, along with a screenshot: A combined image below highlights that the visuals in the viral clip match those in the video posted by the YouTube channel. Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk also reviewed other videos uploaded by the same YouTube channel and found that it is known for posting scripted content. Links to two such videos can be found here and here : Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video — claiming to show a Muslim man engaged in a heated altercation with a woman police official in Uttar Pradesh — was scripted and unrelated to any real-life incident.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Edited video falsely claims Prashant Kishor 'threatened' Kushwaha community ahead of Bihar polls
content: New Delhi, October 7 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A short video of Jan Suraj leader Prashant Kishor addressing a public gathering has gone viral on social media, with claims that he allegedly threatened members of the Kushwaha community ahead of the Bihar elections. Several users alleged that Kishor warned the community of "trouble" if his party came to power. The video has drawn sharp reactions online, with many users accusing him of making caste-based threats. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the video has been edited and misrepresented. The viral clip stitches together two separate portions of an interview, altering the context of Kishor's remarks. The original video shows that his comments were aimed at corrupt politicians and officials, not at the Kushwaha community. The Election Commission of India has announced that the Bihar Assembly elections will be conducted in two phases on November 6 and 11. The count will take place on November 14. Claim: A video featuring Jan Suraj leader Prashant Kishore addressing a gathering was shared by an X user 'Narad Singh' on October 3, claiming that he threatened the Kushwaha community ahead of the Bihar elections. "Man of the Kushwaha community, ensure that Jan Suraj does not win under any circumstances. If it does, then you will be in trouble," says Prashant Kishore in the 00:13-second video. The post's caption read: "Those who showed the dream of changing Bihar..We will rise above caste and religion, and pursue the politics of development! Even before becoming Chief Minister, he had threatened that...If I become Chief Minister, the Kushwaha community will not be spared..Far from changing Bihar, the mindset hasn't changed." Here is the link , and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here : Upon closer examination of the viral video, we noticed a jump cut between Prashant Kishor's "Kushwaha Samaj ka aadmi" and "Praise that Jan Suraj doesn't win in any way, if it wins, you're in trouble." This happens when a video combines two separate clips or parts of a statement. We noticed the microphone in Kishor's hand with the City Post Live logo. Taking a cue from this, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search, which led us to its YouTube channel, where the video was uploaded on September 30, 2025. We reviewed the entire interview, and at no point did he threaten the Kushwaha community or suggest any action would be taken after Jan Suraj's victory in the Bihar elections. Between 26:00 and 26:03, Prashant Kishor uses the phrase "Kushwaha Samaj ka Admi ." His facial and neck movements during this interview are identical to those seen in the initial portion of the viral video. The journalist had asked him, "If anyone launches a movement against any leader, the people of that community take to the streets. But this is the first time we've seen that, whether the allegations are true or false, no one has come out against you." Prashant Kishor replied, "Because we're not saying anything wrong, why would a member of the Kushwaha community take to the streets? Is the allegation false? Weren't the people who were murdered from the Kushwaha community?" After this, when asked about the Jan Suraj CM face if the government is formed, Prashant Kishor says, "…You should understand the situation, what will happen to Samrat Chaudhary if Jan Suraj becomes the CM? You are threatening us; you should understand this. We are telling people right now that these corrupt leaders and officers should start doing as much puja and paath as they know. Do puja, paath, aarti, vinnat, whatever you want to do, celebrate Navratri well. Ensure that Jan Suraj does not win; if he does, you will be in trouble. Whatever you have looted, known or unknown, everything will be recovered from you". Prashant Kishor had allegedly commented on corrupt politicians and officers, stating that if Jan Suraj wins, then they will be in trouble, and not for the benefit of the Kushwaha community, as is being claimed in the viral message. This part occurs between 26:55 and 27:35 in the original video, while the second part of the viral video can be seen from 27:20 to 27:28. Here is the link to the original video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Prashant Kishor's statements were made in response to two different questions, which have been edited and combined to make it appear as if he had threatened the Kushwaha community. The video was shared with a false claim on social media.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Viral ambulance dance video wrongly shared claiming DMK supporters danced after Karur incident
content: New Delhi, October 7 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of people dancing inside an ambulance is being shared on social media with the claim that it shows DMK supporters celebrating after the Karur stampede. Several users circulated the clip linking it to the incident that occurred during actor-politician Vijay's roadshow on September 27. However, Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found the claim to be false. The video predates the Karur tragedy and has been available on the internet since September 21, 2025. Claim: A video showing people apparently dancing inside an ambulance was shared by an Instagram user, 'ecrpvijay', on September 29, claiming that DMK supporters had danced inside the ambulance after the Karur incident. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here : Upon further review of the search results, the Desk came across the same video, uploaded by VNews27 on September 21, 2025. The timeline of the video clarifies that it predates the Karur tragedy that occurred on September 27.
