"Staff dancing in a mobile hospital vehicle.. - Viral video | Ambulance | Dance," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the contents seen in the recent social media post and the video uploaded on VNNews27. Taking a cue from the above finding, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports. It came across a video report by Sun News, uploaded to their YouTube page on September 21. "Mobile hospital | Workers | Dancing | Viral Video | Ambulance | Sun News," read the description of the video. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Our search did not reveal any credible reports linking the incident to DMK workers and the Karur stampede, which occurred on September 27. Moreover, as of October 2, the death toll at the stampede, which occurred at an overcrowded roadshow held by Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) founder and actor Vijay, has climbed to 41. The stampede occurred soon after Vijay began his speech in Karur. According to multiple sources, the entire incident unfolded within 10 minutes. Over a dozen people who sat on a tree branch collapsed on a crowd, worsening the situation further. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video predates the stampede in Karur, which happened on September 27. The video has been available on the internet since September 21, 2025.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old photo of Sonam Wangchuk with Muhammad Yunus falsely shared to claim they recently met amid Ladakh unrest
content: New Delhi, October 7 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A picture of Ladakh activist Sonam Wangchuk with Bangladesh's interim Chief Advisor and Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus has gone viral on social media, with claims that the two met recently amid the ongoing unrest in Ladakh. The post alleges that the meeting is part of a larger "international conspiracy" against India involving foreign actors and domestic "broker gangs." The claim has surfaced at a time when tensions in Ladakh remain high following violent clashes between protesters and police that left several dead and dozens injured. Against this backdrop, the image is being circulated as supposed proof of international involvement in the agitation. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the claim is false. The picture is not recent; it dates back to February 2020, when Wangchuk met Yunus at the British High Commission in Dhaka. At that time, Yunus had no political role and was known globally only as an economist and Nobel laureate. He assumed the role of interim Chief Advisor in Bangladesh much later, in August 2024. The image has been falsely linked to the current Ladakh violence. Claim: A Facebook user, 'Prem Kumar Mahur', on September 25, shared a picture featuring Sonam Wangchuk and Bangladesh's interim Chief Advisor, Muhammad Yunus, claiming that the two met recently amid the recent violence in Ladakh. "Sonam Wangchuk of Ladakh with Mohammad Yunus of Bangladesh. This is the game of international conspirators against India and the conspiracy of their agents, the International Broker Gang and the International Broker Family," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the picture through Reverse Image Search and found that several other users had also shared the same image with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. Upon further review of the search results, the Desk came across a Facebook post by Sonam Wangchuk, dated February 2020, featuring the same picture as seen in the recent social media post. The timeline of the picture clarifies that it is not recent and is unrelated to the violent clashes in Ladakh. The caption of the post read: "WONDERFUL MEETING Dr YUNUS AT BRITISH HIGH COMMISSION, DHAKA Nobel laureate, one of the biggest social entrepreneurs in the world yet so humble n loving." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Notably, in 2020, Muhammad Yunus had no political role. He was just an economist and a Nobel Laureate. Yunus became the chief advisor of Bangladesh's interim government in August 2024 following the fall of the Sheikh Hasina government. "Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus took the oath of office as head of Bangladesh's interim government after protests forced out former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina this week. The key tasks for Yunus now are restoring peace in Bangladesh and preparing for new elections following the ouster of Hasina, who fled to India after weeks of student protests over job quotas grew into an uprising against her increasingly autocratic 15-year rule," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Indian security forces have imposed a curfew in Leh, the capital of the Himalayan region of Ladakh, after at least four people were killed in violent clashes between police and protesters demanding statehood for the federal territory. Dozens were also injured, and an office of India's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) was set on fire in the unrest. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the picture dates back to 2020 and at that time Muhammad Yunus had no political role. He was just an economist and a Nobel Laureate.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of Bokaro Police mock drill falsely shared to claim Uttar Pradesh Police fired tear gas on protesters
content: New Delhi, October 7 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it showed Uttar Pradesh Police firing tear gas at a group of people protesting against the state administration. The clip showed a group of individuals raising slogans, while several police officials standing at a distance fired tear gas shells to disperse them. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found it to be false. The video actually depicts a mock drill conducted by the Bokaro Police in Jharkhand to train personnel in handling riot-like situations. It had no connection to any real incident involving Uttar Pradesh Police or protesters. Claim An X user, Kavya Gupta, shared a video on October 2, claiming it showed the Uttar Pradesh Police taking action against people who, "falling for the opposition's deception," had begun protesting against the state administration. The clip appeared to show protesters shouting slogans while police officers fired tear gas shells to disperse them. "They thought India was Nepal. Here, Baba Ji rules... UP Police will leave them in a cloud of smoke," the user captioned the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here respectively: A Google Lens search also led the Desk to a video posted on the official X handle of Bokaro Police (@bokaropolice) on September 27, 2025. The visuals in this post were identical to those seen in the viral clip. Upon reviewing the accompanying text, the Desk found that the video did not show any real altercation between protesters and police. Instead, it documented a mock drill conducted by the Bokaro Police ahead of the Dussehra festival to train officers in managing riots and emergency situations. In the post, Bokaro Police stated that the exercise was aimed at preparing personnel to handle emergencies and maintain law and order during festive gatherings. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: A comparative image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral clip and the official video shared by Bokaro Police. To further verify, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to locate media reports about the mock drill. The search led to reports published by Hindi news outlets such as Prabhat Khabar and Hindustan, which confirmed that Bokaro Police had carried out a mock drill to train officials in crowd control, riot management, and emergency response during the festive season. The reports also noted that the exercise included route marches, siren alerts, and cordon drills as part of the preparedness efforts. Links to the reports by Prabhat Khabar and Hindustan can be found here and here . Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video claiming to show Uttar Pradesh Police firing tear gas on protesters was actually footage of a mock drill conducted by Bokaro Police in Jharkhand and bore no connection to any real incident.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Fake X handle impersonates suspended lawyer in Supreme Court shoe-throwing row; details inside
content: New Delhi, October 7 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Hours after the Delhi Police released now-suspended Supreme Court advocate Rakesh Kishore, who allegedly attempted to hurl a shoe at Chief Justice of India B R Gavai during court proceedings, an X account purportedly belonging to the lawyer began gaining traction online. The account, claiming to represent Kishore, has been actively posting since the night of October 6, openly criticising the Supreme Court and Chief Justice Gavai. However, a Fact Check by the Press Trust of India revealed that the handle was falsely linked to Kishore. Records showed that the account had been operating under the username @IndianArmy_LG since early 2025. Following the October 6 shoe-throwing incident, it changed its username to @RakeshKishore_l in an apparent attempt to impersonate the lawyer and exploit the controversy. Claim On October 6, several social media posts began circulating online, claiming to be from the official X handle of now-suspended Supreme Court advocate Rakesh Kishore, who was booked for allegedly attempting to hurl a shoe at Chief Justice of India B.R. Gavai during court proceedings. The handle, using the username @RakeshKishore_l, was seen making multiple posts allegedly targeting the Supreme Court and the Chief Justice of India. In several posts shared since October 6, the account—purportedly linked to the suspended lawyer—was also seen defending his actions. Here is the link and archive link to the social media handle in question, along with a screenshot of one of its posts. When this article was published, the post shared above had gained 1.1 million views and 45 thousand likes. Investigation The Desk began the investigation by directly entering the username of the suspected account under investigation into Grok, the X AI chatbot, with a prompt to help identify whether the handle had previously operated under a different username. The Grok website-based search revealed that the X account @RakeshKishore_l was impersonating the 71-year-old now-suspended Supreme Court advocate Rakesh Kishore, who was involved in the recent shoe-throwing incident targeting CJI B.R. Gavai also indicated that the suspected handle had recently changed its username from @IndianArmy_LG to @RakeshKishore_l sometime between October 1–6, 2025, likely to capitalize on the publicity surrounding the incident. Below is a screenshot of the result generated by the Grok. Meanwhile, as part of the investigation, the Desk also posted the same query in the comment section of one of the posts from the suspected handle, tagging Grok. However, the response generated there stated that the @RakeshKishore_l account was created in February 2025 and showed no record of username changes since its creation. This statement stood in stark contrast to Grok's earlier website-based response. Below is a screenshot of the query posted, and the result generated by the Grok. However, when the Desk confronted Grok about the conflicting responses to the same query — regarding whether the handle @RakeshKishore_l had previously operated under a different username — it replied that it found no record of any username change. Grok stated, "Upon verification using current profile data and public tools, RakeshKishore_l was created in February 2025 with no recorded username changes. The app's info (Jan 2018 creation and recent change) seems incorrect or based on outdated data. It likely impersonates the advocate, as no news links him to this handle." Below is a screenshot of the result generated by Grok. The Desk again questioned Grok regarding the inconsistency in its responses—one version suggesting no username change, and another (via its website) indicating that the account was previously operated as @IndianArmy_LG. Grok responded, "Based on verified profile data, RakeshKishore_l joined in February 2025 with no recorded username changes. I cannot confirm a previous handle as IndianArmy_LG or impersonation of Lt. Gen. Rajiv Ghai, though recent posts include military topics. The app's info may differ due to varying data sources — I'm uncertain on that detail." Below is a screenshot of the result generated by Grok. Next, the Desk provided Grok with two screenshots—one showing an old post made by the same user @RakeshKishore_l on September 29, 2025. The replies under the post were attributed to the username @IndianArmy_LG. Had the handle originally belonged to Rakesh Kishore, the replies would have reflected @RakeshKishore_l instead. This screenshot demonstrated that the handle was previously active under the @IndianArmy_LG username. Providing the screenshots, the Desk asked Grok: "The same account was active with the username @IndianArmy_LG. Now it's active with @RakeshKishore_l. What's your take and response to this?" Grok responded, "Thanks for the screenshots—they show the account posting under IndianArmy_LG in late September with the name Rakesh Kishore. However, current profile data indicates creation in February 2025 with no public record of changes. This suggests a possible username switch, though I can't confirm it definitively from available sources. The app's differing details might be from cached data; I'll note it for review." Below is a screenshot of the result. The Desk again raised a query with Grok, pointing out that receiving two different responses to the same question from the same platform raises serious concerns about the verification consistency of its database. Grok replied, "I understand the frustration with differing responses across platforms. The app may rely on aggregated or cached data that conflicts with direct X API verification, which confirms RakeshKishore_l's creation in February 2025 without prior handles or activity. We're investigating to synchronize sources and ensure consistency — your report helps refine this. Thanks for highlighting it." Below is a screenshot of the result. The Desk further questioned Grok after observing that a Community Note had been added to the X handle, stating that the account did not belong to Rakesh Kishore. Grok responded, "The proposed community note correctly flags that RakeshKishore_l does not belong to the actual Supreme Court advocate Rakesh Kishore, who has no verified X account based on my searches. This suggests potential impersonation, aligning with the account's prior handle change to IndianArmy_LG in 2025. X's rules prohibit this; thanks for pointing it out — I've noted it for review." Below is a screenshot of the result. Thus, it was confirmed that the account @RakeshKishore_l does not belong to the same Supreme Court lawyer Rakesh Kishore (the man behind the attack on the CJI). Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk also contacted Rakesh Kishore to verify whether he operated any X handle. In his response, he denied owning any such account. This confirmed that the X handle @RakeshKishore_l, operating under his name, is fake. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the X handle claimed to belong to Rakesh Kishore, the now-suspended Supreme Court lawyer who attempted to attack CJI B.R. Gavai, is false. After the events of October 6, the handle previously operating under the username @IndianArmy_LG was rebranded to impersonate Rakesh Kishore.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Edited video shared to claim 'vote chor' slogan was raised during Nitish-Samrat Chaudary's rally in Rohtas; details inside
content: New Delhi, October 8 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video claiming that people shouted "Vote chor, gaddi chhod" (vote thief, leave the throne) slogans in front of Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar and Deputy CM Samrat Chaudhary has gone viral on social media. The clip allegedly shows the two leaders sitting on stage while the crowd heckles them during a public event. The claim surfaced amid heightened political activity in Bihar, where the Assembly elections will be held in two phases on November 6 and 11, with counting scheduled for November 14. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false. The slogans heard in the viral clip were added later, and no such chants were raised during the actual event. The original video, shot during Nitish Kumar's public programme in Rohtas on September 25, contains routine background noise and applause but no chants of "Vote chor, gaddi chhod." Claim: A video featuring Bihar CM Nitish Kumar and Deputy CM Samrat Chaudhary sitting on a dias was shared by an X user 'Akram Premiar' on October 5, claiming that slogans of 'Vote Chor, Gaddi Chhod' were raised by the people. In the 00:08-second video, "'Vote Chor, Gaddi Chhod'" slogans can be heard in the background. The post clocked 40.4k views on social media. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here : Upon further review of the search results, the Desk came across a similar video uploaded to the YouTube channel of The India Club Live on September 25. CM Nitish Kumar and Deputy Chief Minister Samrat Chaudhary can be seen disembarking from a helicopter, climbing onto the stage, and then felicitating the Chief Minister. Following this, from the 1:20-minute mark, both leaders are seen sitting on the stage, mirroring the scene in the viral video. However, we don't hear slogans like "Vote Chor, Gaddi Chhod" anywhere during this video. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Additionally, we also found the same video uploaded on the YouTube page of 'Up24 news' on September 25, 2025. No slogans related to "vote theft" were heard in either of these. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google. It came across a report by The Times of India published on September 25, which mentioned that CM Nitish Kumar launched a total of 302 development projects worth over Rs 1,901.15 crore in Rohtas and its neighbouring Kaimur district. While 124 projects worth Rs 921 crore were launched in Rohtas district, the remaining 178 projects worth over Rs 980.15 crore were launched in Kaimur district, which was carved out of Rohtas in 1991. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Our investigation reveals that slogans related to "vote theft" were not raised at the Sasaram public interaction event where the video is circulating. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the slogan "Vote thief, leave the throne" heard in the viral video was added separately. No such slogan is heard in the original video.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated amusement park accident video falsely shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, October 8 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it showed an accident at an amusement park, where a joy ride had collapsed. The clip allegedly depicted authorities clearing the site of the incident, with claims that at least 536 people had died. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it to be AI-generated. It was misleadingly shared on social media as real footage to misinform viewers. Claim An Instagram user named Munnakumar shared a video on October 2 claiming it depicted an accident at an amusement park, where a joy ride had collapsed. The footage allegedly showed authorities clearing the site of the accident and removing debris from the collapsed structure, which reportedly killed at least 536 people. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here , respectively. Next, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to check if any real accident of a similar nature — where a joy ride collapsed at an amusement park killing 536 people — had actually occurred. However, the search did not yield any credible news reports of such an incident. Given the gravity of the claim, if such a tragedy had indeed taken place, it would have received widespread media coverage. As part of the investigation, the Desk ran the extracted keyframes through Google Lens once again. The search led to a video posted on an Instagram page named Disaster Strucks, which has over 154k followers. The Desk found that the video posted by this handle on June 30 matched precisely with the one circulating on social media. However, a careful analysis of the video revealed multiple anomalies suggesting that it was AI-generated. For instance, several individuals in the clip appear to pass through barricades, indicating digital distortion — a common trait in AI-generated visuals. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: A comparison image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral social media clip and the video posted by the Instagram handle. Next, taking cues from the above findings, the Desk ran the viral video through Hive Moderation, an AI detection tool. The results indicated that 89.7% of the footage contained AI-generated or deepfake elements. Below is a screenshot highlighting the result: Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk also reviewed the profile of the user Disaster Strucks. In the profile bio, the user clearly mentioned that all content posted on the Instagram channel is AI-generated. Below is a screenshot of the user's profile: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video, which purportedly showed an accident at an amusement park where a joy ride collapsed, resulting in multiple casualties, was AI-generated and falsely shared as real.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Cropped video falsely claims Rahul Gandhi admitted his social media presence is 'fluff'
content: New Delhi, October 8 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A short video of Congress leader and Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi speaking at a university event in Colombia has gone viral on social media, with users claiming he admitted that his social media presence is "fluff" and that he does not rely on it. The clip was shared with captions suggesting Gandhi's remarks were an acknowledgement that his online following and views were not genuine or organic. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the video has been selectively cropped and shared out of context. In the full version of his address, Gandhi cautioned students and young professionals against relying solely on social media fame for career growth, calling it a temporary phenomenon. The video was shared with a false claim on social media. Claim: A video featuring Congress leader Rahul Gandhi was shared by an X user, 'BhikuMhatre', on October 2, claiming that he said his social media presence is a "fluff" and that he does not rely on it. In the 00:10-second video, Gandhi can be heard saying, "I have a big Social Media Presence, but I would not rely on it. That thing is all Fluff" The post garnered 32.4k views on social media. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here : Upon further review of the search results, the Desk came across an extended video uploaded to the official YouTube page of The Hindu on October 2, 2025. Rahul Gandhi addressed a seminar on "The Future Is Today" at EIA University in Columbia. In his address, Rahul Gandhi discussed innovation, youth empowerment, and the challenges India faces in adapting to rapidly changing technological changes. He urged greater focus on education, skill development, and visionary policies to ensure India's next generation is prepared to seize future opportunities. Upon listening to his entire 2-hour 36-minute interview, the Desk found that between 1:00:00 and 1:03:46. At 1:00:01, a person asks Rahul Gandhi questions about the role of AI or electric engines in production, the future of youth in a digital world, and becoming a social media influencer and creating jobs. At the end of the question, the person asks Rahul Gandhi for a final message for the youth that could be crucial to job creation. Rahul Gandhi responds to this question at 01:01:33, says, "Yesterday someone asked me why did you come to Colombia? In the 21st century, it's essential to understand and appreciate diverse cultures. Because you never know how you can connect, or how and where you will connect with someone, until you actually go there. Because for me to say that I will connect with Colombia from India, or that way, I will know that this type of relationship with Colombia will not work. So, being open to other cultures, no matter how big or small, is very important." Then at 01:02:30 in the video, Rahul Gandhi addresses the influencer issue, saying, "My personal view for those who are pursuing the role of influencer is that you should enjoy it, but please don't depend on it, because these things will disappear. It is temporary, it is a temporary phenomenon, make sure you have some strong skills that you can depend on and that are useful, and the more specific and unique your skills are, the easier it will be for you, I think." Further, at 01:03:03, Rahul Gandhi gives an example, saying, "If you're a doctor, make sure you have expertise that no one else has, because you're probably the first generation who can sell that skill anywhere in the world. You don't just need to sell it in Colombia; you can sell it anywhere. So, you have the tools for mass marketing, mass projection, but you need one or two or three skills that make you unique. For example, I have a huge social media presence, but I wouldn't rely on that. That's largely a gimmick. Be careful." Rahul Gandhi then said to the person who asked the question and the people present at the event, "So I would say that if you are producing here in Medellin, then it is excellent and I wish you all the best." Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Moreover, Rahul Gandhi was cautioning young people against relying on social media fame. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Rahul Gandhi's statement was cropped and shared without any context on social media.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Edited graphic falsely shared to claim 'ABP News poll showed Om Prakash Rajbhar as 23% choice for Bihar CM'
content: New Delhi, October 9 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A graphic claiming to show the results of an ABP News opinion poll for the upcoming Bihar Assembly elections was shared on social media claiming Om Prakash Rajbhar, a minister in the Uttar Pradesh government, was the choice of 23 per cent of respondents for the post of Bihar's Chief Minister. The same graphic also shows Nitish Kumar leading the poll with 42 per cent votes, followed by Tejashwi Yadav, Prashant Kishor, Chirag Paswan, and Samrat Chaudhary. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk examined the viral graphic and found that it had been digitally altered. The original ABP News poll listed the last category as "Other," not Om Prakash Rajbhar, confirming that the viral version is doctored. The picture was shared with a false claim on social media. Claim: A Facebook user shared a graphic of an opinion poll, 'Digital Ramsewak', on October 7, claiming that in an opinion poll conducted by ABP News regarding the Bihar Assembly elections, Om Prakash Rajbhar was declared the choice of 23 per cent of people for the post of Chief Minister. The graphic indicates that 42 per cent of people prefer Nitish Kumar for the post of Chief Minister in Bihar. This is followed by 15 per cent for Tejashwi Yadav, 9 per cent for Prashant Kishor, 8 per cent for Chirag Paswan, 3 per cent for Samrat Chaudhary, and 23 per cent for Om Prakash Rajbhar, a minister in the Uttar Pradesh government and a BSP leader. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the picture through reverse image search and came across an Instagram post dated October 6, 2025, by ABP News. The information in the image in the Instagram post closely matched the information in the viral photo. However, the original image did not show Om Prakash Rajbhar as the 23 per cent choice for the post of Chief Minister of Bihar, but instead listed "Other." The image depicted the MATRIZE-IANS opinion poll for the post of Chief Minister of Bihar, conducted by ABP News' Election Centre. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. The same graphic was also uploaded on the official Facebook page of ABP on October 6, 2025. It also did not mention Om Prakash Rajbhar, instead listing "Other" as the 23 per cent choice for Bihar's Chief Minister. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find a relevant report. It came across a report by ABP published on October 6, which mentioned that Chief Minister Nitish Kumar's name remains the top choice for the post of Chief Minister in Bihar. Forty-two per cent voted for CM Nitish Kumar, followed by Tejashwi Yadav at 15 per cent, Prashant Kishor at 0.9 per cent, Chirag Paswan at 0.8 per cent, Samrat Chaudhary at 0.3 per cent, and others at 23 per cent. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the graphic claiming to depict an ABP News opinion poll, showing Om Prakash Rajbhar as the 23 per cent choice for Bihar's Chief Minister, is doctored. The original image of the opinion poll did not mention Om Prakash Rajbhar.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video from Nepal falsely shared to claim youths vandalised BJP leader's car in Bihar; details inside
content: New Delhi, October 10 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it showed youths in Bihar vandalising the car of a BJP leader ahead of the state assembly elections. The footage allegedly showed several individuals throwing stones and kicking the bonnet of the vehicle. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found that the video is linked initially to violence that erupted in Nepal during the Gen Z protests. According to news reports, the video shows protesters damaging the car of a Nepalese government official in Pokhara. An old and unrelated video from Nepal was falsely shared on social media, linking it to an incident in Bihar. Claim An Instagram user named Qazi Syed Mohiullah Hussaini shared on October 1 a video purportedly showing a mob vandalising the car of a BJP leader in Bihar. The footage allegedly showed several individuals throwing stones and kicking the bonnet of the vehicle. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here , respectively. Next, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to verify whether any such incident of stones being thrown at a BJP leader's car had occurred in Bihar. However, the search did not yield any credible news reports confirming the claim. Given the nature of the alleged incident, it would have been widely reported by the media had it actually occurred. As part of the investigation, the Desk then ran the extracted keyframes through Google Lens again. The search results led the Desk to a video posted on an Instagram page named 'timesg.ind', which introduces itself as a media news company. The Desk found that the video posted by the page on September 9 exactly matched the one circulating on social media. However, the caption accompanying the post confirmed that the incident took place in Nepal. The handle mentioned that the video depicted an incident from Nepal during the Gen Z protest, where demonstrators torched and overturned a Nepal government official's car in Pokhara. "The anti-corruption and anti-censorship protests that have gripped Kathmandu have now spilled into Pokhara, where demonstrators torched and overturned a government official's car on Tuesday afternoon," the user wrote in the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. A comparative image below highlights the visual similarities between the social media video and the one shared by the Instagram handle. In the subsequent part of the investigation, taking cues from the above findings, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search on Google to find details related to the incident in Nepal. The search led the Desk to a report published by Republic Bharat, which, while reporting on the violence during the GenZ protests in Nepal, also included the same visuals of the car being torched — confirming that the video originated in Nepal and had no connection to Bihar. Here is the link to the report: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the social media video linked to the violence in Nepal during the GenZ protest was falsely shared on social media, claiming it showed protesters vandalising a BJP leader's car in Bihar ahead of the state assembly polls.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Edited video with superimposed audio falsely shared to claim UP CM Yogi walked off after singer's objectionable lyrics about govt
content: New Delhi, October 10 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video featuring Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath sitting on a stage alongside Gorakhpur MP Ravi Kishan has gone viral on social media, with claims that the CM walked off after a singer performed objectionable lyrics about the government. The clip has been circulated with captions suggesting Adityanath left the event in protest. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the viral video was doctored. The original footage, recorded during a Janmashtami event at Gorakhnath Temple in August 2025, shows a bhajan performance in which Ravi Kishan is seen dancing while Yogi Adityanath smiles and later exits the stage. The viral version was manipulated with superimposed audio containing objectionable lyrics, creating a misleading impression. Claim: A video featuring UP CM Yogi Adityanath sitting on a stage with Gorakhpur MP Ravi Kishan was shared by an X user '@BhavnaJJoshi' on October 8, claiming that the CM left the stage due to a singer's objectionable lyrics about the government. The post clocked 203.8k views on social media. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot below. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . Upon further review of the search results, the Desk discovered the same video, which was uploaded to Facebook by a user named Ravi Kishan on August 17, 2025. However, the audio in this video differed from that in the viral video; instead, the singer was singing a hymn dedicated to Shri Ram and Radheshyam. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Furthermore, we also found another video of the same event uploaded on a Facebook page called UP Khabar on August 17, 2025. The video was shot from a different angle. The video shows the singers singing the Shri Ram-Radheshyam bhajan, to which Ravi Kishan dances. Yogi Adityanath smiles at the sight of Ravi Kishan dancing. Yogi Adityanath then gets up and leaves. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports. This search led to a report by Dainik Bhaskar, published on August 17, 2025, which contained footage from the viral video. The report stated that Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath celebrated Shri Krishna Janmashtami with great pomp at the Gorakhnath Temple in Gorakhpur. During the bhajan evening, MP Ravi Kishan sang bhajans and danced, prompting a smile and encouragement from Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking the investigation ahead, the Desk found the audio in the viral video was uploaded to a YouTube account on August 21, 2024. In this video, a singer is seen singing an obscene song from another platform while criticising the government. Here is the link to the video. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video, which claims Yogi Adityanath left the stage after making objectionable comments about the government, is doctored. The original video showed a bhajan being sung.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI video of monkey drawing Lord Hanuman's sketch on wall in India shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, September 12 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video purportedly showing a monkey drawing a sketch of Lord Hanuman on a wall was recently shared on social media, accompanied by a claim that it depicted a real incident. The video showed the monkey allegedly drawing the sketch of Lord Hanuman on a temple wall in India, while people standing nearby recorded the act on their phones. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it to be AI-generated. It was misleadingly shared on social media as real footage to misinform viewers. Claim An X handle with the username Voice Of Sanatan (@Ritik_Sanatani) shared on September 10 a video that purportedly showed a monkey drawing a sketch of Lord Hanuman on a temple wall in a village in India. "Monkey draws a picture of Lord Hanuman. In a village in India, a monkey drew the figure of Lord Hanuman on the temple wall using coal. People considered it a miracle and described it as a divine sign. This unique sight went viral on social media," the user captioned the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered 1,000 views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here , respectively. The search results via Google Lens also led the Desk to a video posted on an Instagram handle named 'multiversematrix' on October 9, 2025. The Desk found the video posted by the Instagram handle was identical to the one circulating on social media. However, the details included in the Instagram post suggested that the video was created using AI and did not depict a real incident. The description revealed that the video had been generated using Higgsfield AI software. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: A comparative image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral social media clip and the video posted by the Instagram handle. Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk carefully reviewed the Instagram profile of 'multiversematrix'. In the profile bio, the user clearly mentioned that all content posted on the channel is AI-generated. Below is a screenshot of the user's profile: In the subsequent part of the investigation, the Desk ran the video through an AI detection tool — Zhuque AI Detector — which confirmed that 84% of the footage contained AI-generated or deepfake elements. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a monkey drawing a sketch of Lord Hanuman on a temple wall in a village in India was AI-generated and falsely shared on social media to mislead viewers.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Viral post falsely claims PMO launched hotline for citizens to report corruption in India; details inside
content: New Delhi, October 13 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media post recently went viral, claiming that the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) of India has introduced a major initiative to promote a citizen-centric governance model. The post alleged that a dedicated hotline number — 9851145045 — has been launched by the PMO, where citizens can report instances of corruption or bribery, unnecessary delays, and misconduct in government offices. In its investigation, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false. The hotline number shared in the viral post actually belongs to the Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers (OPMCM) of Nepal, not India. Nepali citizens use the number to report grievances related to government service delivery and have no connection with the Indian Prime Minister's Office. Claim A Facebook user named Neha Shah on October 10 shared a post claiming that the Indian government had introduced a hotline to report issues such as corruption, bribery, and misconduct in government offices. The post read, "A major move towards transparent governance! The PMO has introduced a dedicated hotline (9851145045) where citizens can report Corruption or bribery, unnecessary delays, and misconduct in government offices. Every call matters—your action can help build a corruption-free India." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found several similar posts circulating the same claim about a "PMO hotline" number, 9851145045, being introduced. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find any government releases or media reports that could have elaborated on the alleged initiative by the Prime Minister's Office. However, the search did not lead to any credible news reports confirming the same. Had the development been real, either media outlets or official government portals would have released a press statement about it. Next, the Desk entered the hotline number into the Truecaller application to identify its owner. The search result suggested that the number belongs to the office of Nepal's Interim Prime Minister Sushila Karki, as indicated by the name displayed on the application. Below is a screenshot of the result, which shows the number is being displayed in the name of Nepal's interim Prime Minister: Taking cues from the above findings, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search on Google to verify if the Nepal government had issued any hotline number matching the one mentioned in the social media post. The search led to a report published by the Nepal-based outlet Republica on September 20, 2025, which stated that a dedicated hotline number — 9851145045 —(exactly matching one from the social media post), had been announced by the Nepal government to report grievances related to government service delivery. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Additionally, the search to trace the origin of the number also led the Desk to the official website of Nepal's Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers (OPMCM). Under its "Hello Government" section, the same number is mentioned for citizens who wish to share complaints or suggestions to improve governance. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the hotline number (9851145045) claimed to have been introduced by the Indian Prime Minister's Office for reporting corruption and misconduct is not linked to India. The number actually belongs to Nepal's Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers (OPMCM).

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Viral video claiming to show light show in Rajasthan's Jaisalmer actually from China's Dunhuang city; details inside
content: New Delhi, October 13 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a spectacular light show on a sandy terrain is being widely shared on social media with the claim that it depicts a scene from Jaisalmer, Rajasthan. The video purportedly shows colourful beams of light projected into the night sky in Jaisalmer, with several spectators seen sitting and capturing the scenic view. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found that it is unrelated to Jaisalmer. The original footage shows visuals from a light show held in Dunhuang city, Gansu province, China, but was falsely shared on social media as a light show from Rajasthan's Jaisalmer to mislead viewers. Claim An Instagram handle with the username 'jaisalmer_tour_official' shared a video on October 11, purportedly showing a spectacular light show being organised in Jaisalmer's sandy terrain. The footage showed colourful beams of light projected into the night sky, with several spectators seen sitting and capturing the scenic view. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here , respectively. The search result via Google Lens also led the Desk to a video posted on an Instagram page named 'dunhuang_plus' on August 8, 2025. The Desk found that the location settings in the video posted by this Instagram page matched the visuals seen in the viral post. The caption of the video stated that it was shot at the scenic Dunhuang Desert in northwest China's Gansu Province. The video from the Instagram page was filmed during a live performance by Chinese singer Zhou Shen in Dunhuang. Although the viral video circulating on social media was from a different event, the location in both videos was the same — Dunhuang city in Gansu Province, China. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: A comparison image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral social media clip and the video posted by the Instagram page. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to verify additional details related to the video's location. The search led the Desk to a news report published by the Chinese media portal Xinhuanet in 2023. The report included multiple images resembling the location seen in the viral video. It stated that they were taken in Dunhuang, Gansu Province, at the Mingsha Mountain and Crescent Spring — a scenic spot known for its unique landscape where desert dunes and a pristine water spring coexist side by side. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video being shared as showing a light show in Jaisalmer, Rajasthan, is actually from Dunhuang city in Gansu Province, China, and was falsely circulated on social media to mislead viewers.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of IAF MiG-21 crash in Rajasthan falsely shared claiming it showed how Taliban shot down Pakistani jet on Durand Line
content: New Delhi, October 13 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): In the aftermath of the reported October 11 clashes along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border, a video showing the burning wreckage of an aircraft has gone viral on social media, with users claiming that it showed how the Taliban shot down a Pakistani jet along the Durand Line. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found the claim to be false. The footage is not from Pakistan or Afghanistan but from India, and shows a MiG-21 trainer aircraft of the Indian Air Force that crashed near Rajasthan's Barmer district in July 2022. A three-year-old video is being circulated on social media with a misleading claim. According to reports, Pakistan's military said on Sunday (October 12) that 23 of its troops and more than 200 Taliban and affiliated fighters on the Afghan side were killed in the overnight border clashes. Claim: A video showing the wreckage and burning of what looked like an aircraft was shared by an X user 'Nehra Ji' on October 12, claiming that the Taliban shot down Pakistan's jet on the Durand Line. "The Taliban has shot down Pakistan's jet on the Durand Line. Pakistan's fighter jet is also being shot down in Afghanistan. And Congress is saying that Pakistan has shot down India's Rafales," read the post's caption. The post garnered 250.4k views on social media. Here is the link to the post, along with an archive link . Below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here : Upon running the extracted keyframes through Reverse Image Search, the Desk came across the extended version of the same video, which was uploaded on the official YouTube page of 'The Economic Times' on July 28, 2022. The timeline of the video clarifies that the video is not recent and is unrelated to the Pakistan-Afghanistan tension. Moreover, the accompanying caption with the video stated that A MiG-21 fighter aircraft of the Indian Air Force crashed near the Barmer district of Rajasthan. Both pilots have lost their lives in the unfortunate incident, officials confirmed. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports and came across a report by The Indian Express published on July 29, 2022. The report highlighted that two pilots were killed after an Indian Air Force fighter aircraft crashed in Barmer. Moreover, the cover image of the report was similar to the clip shared recently on social media. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking the investigation ahead, the Desk came across an X post by the Indian Air Force on July 28, 2022. Expressing condolences, the post mentioned that an IAF MiG-21 trainer aircraft was involved in an accident in the western sector during a training sortie. Both pilots sustained fatal injuries. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a three-year-old MiG-21 trainer aircraft crash in the Barmer district of Rajasthan was shared as a recent incident of the Taliban shooting down a Pakistani jet on the Durand Line.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old, unrelated video falsely shared claiming Nepal's Gen-Z youth torched mosque after Durga idol attack
content: New Delhi, October 13 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a burning building and scattered items on the ground has been widely shared on social media with the claim that it shows members of Nepal's Gen-Z community setting a mosque on fire in retaliation for an alleged attack during a Durga idol immersion. The post, shared by several users on X, linked the visuals to recent religious tensions in the country and alleged that "furious Gen-Z youth" carried out the act. However, PTI Fact Check found the claim to be misleading. The video is not recent and has no connection with any incident related to Durga idol immersion. The footage is actually from September 2025, when massive demonstrations broke out across Nepal during the Gen-Z protests against the government's move to ban several social media platforms. Meanwhile, Durga Puja idol immersion processions in Janakpurdham of Madhesh Province and Banke district of Lumbini turned violent on October 3, prompting police intervention and prohibitory orders across several areas. The clashes mirrored a similar outbreak in Janakpur barely a month earlier during Ganesh idol immersion, highlighting recurring communal flashpoints in Nepal's southern plains. Claim: A video showing a burning structure and scattered items on the ground after an apparent vandalism incident was shared by an X user 'Ocean Jain' on October 9, claiming that Gen-Zs of Nepal were angered by the attack on Durga idol immersion and set a mosque on fire. "Baba's bulldozer has now reached Nepal as well. After the attack during Durga immersion, the Nepalese government has begun demolishing illegal Islamic properties. Meanwhile, furious Generation Z youth have set a mosque on fire in retaliatory action!" read the post's caption. The post clocked 22.2k views on social media. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot below. Investigation The Desk ran the picture through Reverse Image Search and found that several other users had shared the same post with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived version can be viewed here and here , respectively. Upon careful analysis of the video, we found three distinct scenes within it. Scene 1: Investigating the first scene, we performed a reverse image search using keyframes and found a video uploaded to the Facebook account of a media portal in Birgunj, Nepal, on September 9, 2025. It contained scenes similar to the viral video. The caption accompanying the video stated that protesters had set fire to the house of Birgunj Mayor Rajesh Man Singh. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Our investigation led us to the same video uploaded on YouTube by a user 'gopyakhabarp' on September 19, clarifying that the video is not recent. The caption accompanying the video stated that Birgunj Mayor Rajeshman Singh's house was also set on fire. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking the investigation ahead, we investigated the second scene seen in the viral video, in which some items are seen scattered at one place. Scene 2: During our investigation, we found a video uploaded to Birgunj Sanjal's (a local media outlet of Nepal) Facebook account on September 10, 2025, which contained scenes similar to the viral video. The caption of the post described the footage as taking place after the vandalism and arson that occurred during a protest at the Birgunj Municipality office. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Scene 3: During our investigation, we found a video (from a different angle) uploaded to the Facebook account of Nepali media outlet Agnipath on September 9, 2025. The caption accompanying the video stated that the scene was from a fire at the home of Birgunj Mayor Rajeshman Singh during a Zen-Z protest. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Moreover, in September this year, the Nepal government moved to ban 26 social media platforms, including Facebook and YouTube, and protests erupted with thousands of young people storming parliament in the capital Kathmandu. Several districts are now under a curfew.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Fake claim of Bhojpuri singer Khesarilal Yadav's death circulates on social media
content: New Delhi, October 10 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A post shared by several social media users claimed that popular Bhojpuri singer and actor Khesarilal Yadav has passed away. The post included a picture of the singer with condolence messages. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk examined the claim and found it to be false. The singer himself refuted the rumours through a post on his verified X account, confirming that he is alive. Moreover, we did not find any credible reports that carried the news. No statement or confirmation about Yadav's death has been issued by his family, representatives, or the Bhojpuri film industry. Claim: A Facebook post by a user 'Balwant Singh' on October 5, shared a picture, claiming that Bhojpuri singer Khesarilal Yadav has passed away. Here is the link to the post, along with an archive link . Below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the picture through Reverse Image Search and found that several other users had shared the same post with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived version can be viewed here and here , respectively. As part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find reports that covered the news of his demise. However, we did not find any news articles that carried such information. Given the seriousness of the situation, such news would have been reported by all the news outlets. PTI Fact Check also found that no statement or confirmation about Yadav's death has been issued by his family, representatives, or the Bhojpuri film industry. No credible media outlet reported any such incident. Taking a cue from this, we then scanned the social media handle of the singer, and on viewing his X account, we came across a post dated September 4, 2025. He clarified that tweeting a post confirmed he was alive. "I am alive," read a rough translation of the text, originally written in Bhojpuri. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Moreover, he paid a tribute to late Mulayam Singh Yadav on his death anniversary today, on his X handle on October 10. This clarifies that he is alive and the reports of his death are false. Here is the link to his post. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral claim that Bhojpuri singer Khesarilal Yadav has died is baseless. He is alive, as confirmed through his verified X account on September 4, 2025.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old Gurugram video of people entering metro without tickets falsely linked to Patna; details inside
content: New Delhi, October 14 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Days after Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar inaugurated the first phase of the Patna Metro priority corridor, a video showing several people slipping under turnstiles and entering a metro station without tickets has been widely shared on social media, with users claiming it depicts scenes from the newly inaugurated Patna Metro. However, a PTI Fact Check investigation found that the video was not from Patna but from a Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) station in Gurugram, identifiable by signage for Oyster's Water Park and the DMRC logo visible in the footage. The clip was misleadingly shared on social media with a false claim. The opening of the first short section of the Patna Metro comes ahead of state elections, with limited services being operated using a three-car Titagarh trainset leased from the Pune Metro. Claim: A video showing people sneaking into a metro station without tickets was shared by an X user, @sarviind' on October 12, claiming that the incident happened at the newly inaugurated Patna Metro. "We are Bihari and we can do anything," read the overlying text, originally in Hindi, on the video. Here is the link , and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here : Upon closely examining the video, the Desk found a logo on the card-swapping machine that resembled the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC). This hints that the video is not from the Bihar metro. Below is a screenshot highlighting the logo. Below is a comparison between the Delhi Metro logo and the Patna Metro logo. Next, we also noticed "Oyster's Water Park" written on a signboard in the background. The water park is now closed, though it indicates that the metro station in the video is likely the Millennium City Centre or HUDA City Centre in Gurugram, the two closest stations to the water park. Below is a screenshot of the same. We searched HUDA City Centre on Google Maps, which matches the frame from the video being circulated on social media. Here is the link to the Google Maps image. Moreover, the turnstile in the video appears old and worn out, which is unlikely to be the case for the recently inaugurated Patna Metro. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video is not from Patna metro. It is from a Gurugram metro station.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated image falsely shared to claim 'Bangladeshi women cricketers played ICC Women's World Cup 2025 match wearing burqas'
content: New Delhi, October 14 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Days after New Zealand clinched its first victory against Bangladesh with a massive 100-run lead in the ICC Women's World Cup 2025 match, an image purportedly from the match day went viral on social media. The picture showed two burqa-clad women standing on a cricket pitch, with one of them also wearing full cricket gear. Users claimed these were Bangladeshi women cricket players who played the match wearing burqas. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found the image to be AI-generated and shared to mislead viewers. It was not discovered that the Bangladeshi women players wore burqas during the match. Instead, the highlights uploaded by the ICC showed the Bangladeshi players wearing their regular jerseys for the game. Claim An X user, Imtiaz Mahmood (@ImtiazMadmood), shared a purported image from the Bangladesh vs New Zealand ICC Women's World Cup 2025 match on October 13, which was held on October 10. The image allegedly showed two Bangladeshi women players who played the game wearing burqas. Here is the link and an archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the image had garnered 1 million views) Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and found multiple handles that shared the same photo with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. In the next step of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to verify whether Bangladeshi women cricketers actually played their recent ICC Women's World Cup 2025 match against New Zealand wearing burqas. However, the search results did not lead to any credible news reports confirming the claim. Had it been true, media outlets would have covered it extensively. Additionally, the search led the Desk to a detailed report published by the ICC on its website elaborating on the key highlights of the match between Bangladesh and New Zealand. While the report described New Zealand's massive 100-run victory against Bangladesh, it also included multiple images and short videos capturing moments from the match. In none of the pictures or videos examined by the Desk were the Bangladeshi players seen wearing burqas. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: In the subsequent part of the investigation, the Desk also carefully analysed the image and found that it contains the Gemini logo (Google's AI tool) placed in the bottom-right corner of the picture. This suggested that the image was likely generated or manipulated using this tool. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the image showing two burqa-clad women standing on a cricket pitch is AI-generated and does not depict any instance of Bangladeshi women cricketers playing a cricket match in burqas.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Fake letter shared on social media to falsely claim 'PM Modi urged citizens to use only Swadeshi products during Diwali festival'
content: New Delhi, October 14 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported letter allegedly attributed to the Prime Minister, in which he appealed to citizens to buy only Made-in-India products during the approaching festive season, recently went viral on social media. In the letter, the Prime Minister reportedly urged citizens to use only Swadeshi products at home during the upcoming Diwali festival. He stated that if this initiative were supported, it would help India reach the forefront of the world. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the letter and found it to be fake. While PM Modi did appeal to citizens last month during his 'Mann Ki Baat' address to use Swadeshi products during the festive season, the viral letter shared in his name is not authentic or verified, and there are no such reports available on news websites. Claim A Facebook user, Anand Sinha, shared a post on October 3, featuring a purported letter written by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. In the letter, the PM allegedly urged citizens to buy only Swadeshi (Made-in-India) products during the approaching festive season. He reportedly stated that if citizens agreed, this small step would help India reach the forefront of the world. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk used Google Lens to analyse the image of the letter being shared on social media, which led to multiple other accounts sharing the same letter. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively: Additionally, the Google Lens search also led the Desk to a few social media posts from 2016, which showed that the same letter had circulated at that time. This confirmed that the viral letter is not recent and is at least nine years old. Here is the link and archive link to the post: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk again ran the viral letter image through Google Lens. The search results led to an X post shared in August 2016 by the Prime Minister's Office. The post attached a letter similar to the one in circulation. Although the text in the PMO letter was blurred, the pattern and placement of text matched the viral letter. Likewise, the formatting of "Vande Mataram" and Narendra Modi's signature in both the viral social media post and the PMO document was identical. However, the caption shared by the PMO for its post identified the letter to be fake. It stated, "Few appeals with PM's 'signature' are circulated on social media. Such documents are not authentic." Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot. Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk also conducted a customised Google search to check whether PM Modi had recently spoken about buying Made-in-India products. The search led to the transcription of PM Modi's last month's 'Mann Ki Baat' address, in which he appealed to citizens to make a special resolution this festive season by buying Swadeshi products. During the address, PM Modi stated, "If we decide to celebrate this festival only with Swadeshi products, you will see the joy of our celebrations rise manifold. Make 'Vocal for Local' your shopping mantra. Resolve that, for all times, you will buy only what is produced in the country. You will take home only what is made by the people of the country. You will use only those goods which bear the toil of a citizen of the country. When we do that, we don't just buy goods; we bring home hope to a family, honour the hard work of an artisan, and give wings to the dreams of a young entrepreneur." Here is the link to the post. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral letter attributed to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, urging citizens to buy only Made-in-India products during Diwali, is fake. While PM Modi did promote Swadeshi products during his recent 'Mann Ki Baat' address, the letter circulating on social media is not authentic.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Viral video claiming UP citizens covered drains is fake. It's old Ghaziabad theft clip played in reverse
content: New Delhi, October 14 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing two men unloading what appears to be an iron cover from an e-rickshaw and placing it on a roadside drain has gone viral on social media with the claim that citizens in Uttar Pradesh are voluntarily helping the government by covering open drains with solid steel gates. The clip was shared with a caption suggesting that people had taken it upon themselves to fix civic infrastructure. However, the video raised doubts due to visible inconsistencies in movement and direction, prompting PTI Fact Check to verify its authenticity. The investigation revealed that the viral clip is not genuine but a reversed version of an older video showing two men stealing, not installing, an iron drain cover in Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh. The footage was misleadingly shared on social media with a false claim. Claim: A video showing two men unloading an iron cover from an e-rickshaw and placing it on a drain was shared by an X user '@1vinci6le' on October 7, claiming that the citizens of UP are helping the government by covering the drains with solid steel gates. "In UP, citizens are taking charge. They are helping the government by covering the drains with Solid steel gates," read the post's caption. The post clocked 1,139 views on social media. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot below. Investigation As part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the video and found several discrepancies. After the installation, both men walked backwards, and the e-rickshaw moved in reverse without a driver. These anomalies indicated that the video had been reversed. A reverse image search led us to a video published by Times Now on August 3. The original footage shows the two men removing the cover from the drain, loading it onto the e-rickshaw, and fleeing the scene with one of them driving the three-wheeler. According to the news channel, thieves stole an iron drain cover in Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh. They had also concealed the e-rickshaw's number plate by blacking it out. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarity between the contents seen in the social media post and the video uploaded by Times Now. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports, and our search led us to a video uploaded by NDTV on their YouTube shorts, dated August 3, 2025. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video has been reversed. The unedited version shows the burglary of the iron drain cover.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered video of Taliban leader falsely shared to claim 'he offered to build Hindu temples in Afghanistan in exchange for money'
content: New Delhi, October 15 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently shared on social media claimed to show senior Taliban official and Afghanistan Foreign Minister Mawlawi Amir Khan Muttaqi, who is on a six-day visit to India, stating that he had spoken to Prime Minister Narendra Modi regarding the opening of Hindu temples in Afghanistan in exchange for money. The video allegedly showed the Afghan Foreign Minister saying, "I have told Modi ji that if they would give a few dollars to the Taliban, then we will also build temples of Lord Shiva and Vishnu Devi in Kabul, Kandahar and Helmand so that devotees from India can visit Afghanistan on religious pilgrimages. We have chanted 'Jai Shri Ram' slogans here. We are grateful and extremely indebted to Modi ji for the love he has shown us." However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it to be digitally manipulated. The video originally came from a press conference addressed by the Afghanistan Foreign Minister on October 12 during his visit to India. Nowhere in the media reports or the videos of the press conference published by credible outlets did the Minister make any statement about building Hindu temples in Afghanistan. This confirmed that the audio was superimposed to mislead viewers. Claim An X user, Raza Ijaz (@mehmoo89300), shared on October 12 a purported video of senior Taliban official and Afghanistan Foreign Minister Mawlawi Amir Khan Muttaqi, in which he was allegedly seen stating that he had spoken to Prime Minister Narendra Modi regarding the opening of Hindu temples in Afghanistan in exchange for money. The video included the following statement: "I have told Modi ji that if they would give a few dollars to the Taliban, then we will also build temples of Lord Shiva and Vishnu Devi in Kabul, Kandahar and Helmand so that devotees from India can visit Afghanistan on religious pilgrimages. We have chanted 'Jai Shri Ram' slogans here. We are grateful and extremely indebted to Modi ji for the love he has shown us." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across several social media posts made through the official X handle of the Press Trust of India (PTI). The posts included video snippets from the Afghanistan Foreign Minister's interaction with the media from the same press conference shown in the viral video. The background settings in both videos — the one shared on social media and the official PTI clips — were found to be similar. However, upon examining each of these PTI posts, none contained any statement by the Afghan Foreign Minister referring to the building of Hindu temples in Afghanistan in exchange for money. Instead, the topics he covered included women's rights under the Taliban-led government, the ongoing conflict between Afghanistan and Pakistan, the presence of the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) in Afghanistan, Pakistan's reaction to India-Afghanistan relations, and calls for Indian investment in Afghanistan. Links to the original PTI posts can be found here , here , here , here , here and here . A combination image has been attached, confirming that the visuals in the viral social media video and the PTI videos are the same. Additionally, the Desk found multiple news reports covering the same press conference addressed by the Afghanistan Foreign Minister. None of these reports mentioned any statement about building Hindu temples in Afghanistan. Had such a remark been made, it would have been widely reported by credible media outlets. Link to one such report can be found here , along with a screenshot: The search results also led the Desk to a video posted by The Hindu on October 12, which is the extended version of the Afghanistan Foreign Minister's press conference. However, in that video as well, the Minister did not make any statement regarding the construction of Hindu temples in Afghanistan in exchange for money. This confirmed that the social media video is digitally manipulated and does not depict a real instance. Here is the link to the video. Moreover, in the subsequent part of the investigation, to verify the authenticity of the video, the Desk examined it closely and noted multiple lip-sync discrepancies, indicating manipulation. The audio track was extracted from the video and analysed using the AI detection tool Resemble AI. The tool showed that while the voice appeared realistic, it may have been an impersonation. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was edited with fake audio and falsely showed senior Taliban official and Afghanistan Foreign Minister Mawlawi Amir Khan Muttaqi as saying that he had spoken to Prime Minister Narendra Modi regarding the opening of Hindu temples in Afghanistan in exchange for money.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video falsely shared to claim 'PM Nehru had warned an illiterate man would divide India on religious lines'
content: New Delhi, October 15 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it showed former Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru allegedly delivering a speech at least 75 years ago, in which he was purportedly seen warning citizens to "take care of this country; otherwise, after a few years, an illiterate man would divide it on the basis of religion." However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it to be AI-generated. The clip was falsely shared on social media to mislead viewers.
