Claim An Instagram user named Baba Shaikh (@shaikhbaba730) shared on October 12 a purported video that showed former Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru allegedly stating that 75 years later, an illiterate man would divide the country on the basis of religion. Here is the link and an archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered 76,201 likes.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here , respectively. In the next stage of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find media reports or video links that might contain an extended version of the former Prime Minister's speech. However, the search did not lead to any credible news reports or verified video sources confirming the claim. Had such a speech been genuinely delivered, multiple news outlets or archives would have covered it. Next, the Desk proceeded to check the authenticity of the viral video. On close examination, multiple lip-sync discrepancies were noted, indicating manipulation. Based on these observations, the Desk ran the video through Hive Moderation, an AI detection tool. The analysis showed that 88% of the video is likely to contain AI-generated or deepfake content. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing former Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru allegedly warning that an illiterate man would divide the country on the basis of religion is AI-generated and was falsely shared on social media to mislead viewers.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2023 image of Bihar CM Nitish Kumar meeting Lalu Yadav falsely shared as recent; details inside
content: New Delhi, October 16 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Days after the Election Commission of India announced the dates for the upcoming Bihar Assembly elections — scheduled to be conducted in two phases on November 6 and November 11, with counting on November 14 — a purported image showing JD(U) leader and Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar meeting Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) chief Lalu Prasad Yadav was widely shared on social media. Users claimed that the image was recent and that the two leaders met just ahead of the state elections. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the image and found that it dates back to April 2023, when the JD(U) was in alliance with the RJD, and Nitish Kumar had visited Lalu Prasad Yadav in New Delhi. An old and unrelated image of the two leaders was falsely shared on social media, linking it to the upcoming polls in Bihar. Claim An Instagram user, Sunil Kumar Yadaw (@sunilkumaryadaw.yadaw), on October 14 shared an image of Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar seemingly greeting RJD supremo Lalu Prasad Yadav. The user claimed the image was recent and that the two leaders had met ahead of the Bihar Assembly elections. "In Bihar, electoral politics seems to be heating up, and in the meantime, you can see Nitish Kumar has met Lalu Prasad Yadav," the user captioned the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and found multiple handles that shared the same photo with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. A Google Lens search also led the Desk to multiple news reports featuring the same image of Nitish Kumar and Lalu Yadav as seen in the social media post. However, upon careful analysis of the reports, it was found that the image dates back to April 2023, when JD(U) chief Nitish Kumar met his then ally, RJD supremo Lalu Prasad Yadav, in New Delhi. It is pertinent to note that Nitish Kumar has aligned with the RJD twice in the last decade, most recently as part of the Mahagathbandhan. However, he again switched allegiance to the BJP-led NDA in January 2024, ahead of the Lok Sabha elections. The social media image dates back to the same time (April 2023) when the two were working in alliance. Here is a link to the PTI report carried by India Today, elaborating on the meeting between the two leaders and the image captured on that occasion: A comparison image below confirms that the feature image from the news report matches the one in the social media post. Additionally, links to other media reports elaborating on the same meeting held between Nitish Kumar and Lalu Prasad Yadav in April 2023 can be found here , here and here . Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the image of Nitish Kumar meeting Lalu Prasad Yadav is old and unrelated to the current political developments in Bihar.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Rajan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of Tejashwi Yadav meeting injured man in Bihar falsely linked to recent Bareilly violence
content: New Delhi, October 16 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Rajan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav consoling a man who appears to be injured has gone viral on social media with the claim that the man was a Maulana from Bihar who the Uttar Pradesh Police allegedly beat for taking part in the recent communal violence in Bareilly. The post further suggests that Yadav met the man after the incident to hear his grievances. However, a fact check by PTI found the claim to be false. The video is not from Bareilly, Uttar Pradesh, but from Madhubani district in Bihar and dates back to February 2025. The clip shows Yadav meeting Mohammad Firoz, an Imam who was allegedly assaulted by the local police in Madhubani. This incident drew wide political and media attention in Bihar earlier this year. Claim: A video showing a man lamenting his plight before RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav was shared by an X user '@KESRIYAA' on October 10, claiming that the man in the footage is a Maulana from Bihar who was involved in the violence in Bareilly, Uttar Pradesh, who was severely beaten by the UP police and later met Tejashwi Yadav to share his grief. "A Maulana from Bihar praises the services provided by Yogi police in the Bareilly violence. The poor guy's only fault was that he had gone from Bihar to Bareilly to participate in the violence," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, along with an archive link . Below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here : On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across the same video uploaded on a YouTube channel named 'Runcut' on February 4, 2025. The description accompanying it mentioned that Tejashwi Yadav visits the Bihar Imam, who was brutally beaten by police. The video begins with a portion of the viral clip, in which the man recounts the police brutality he suffered. The video narrates the incident, which details Tejashwi Yadav meeting an Imam in Bihar who was brutally beaten by the police. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from the above finding, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports and came across a report by ABP News, dated February 5, 2025. The report mentioned that Police in Madhubani, Bihar, were accused of beating a man named Mohammad Firoz during a vehicle check. He was beaten so severely that Leader of the Opposition Tejashwi Yadav himself travelled to Benipatti in Madhubani to inspect his injuries. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Another report by The Hindu, published on February 4, 2025, also highlighted that an RJD leader levelled the charges after an Imam was allegedly beaten up in police custody in Madhubani district of Bihar. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Moreover, protests against alleged "administrative action" over 'I Love Muhammad' posters turned violent in UP's Bareilly after Friday (September 26) prayers, as a crowd of over 1,000 people carrying banners and placards with religious slogans gathered near the Islamia Ground and pelted stones at police and vandalised several vehicles. Police resorted to a lathi charge and lobbed tear gas shells to disperse the crowd, creating a stampede-like situation. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video is related to an incident in Madhubani, Bihar. It has no connection to any incident in Uttar Pradesh.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2011 video of lawyer Prashant Bhushan being thrashed falsely shared as recent, linked to assault on CJI's shoe-thrower
content: New Delhi, October 16 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a man being thrashed by another person has gone viral on social media with the claim that it shows the individual who allegedly threw a shoe at Chief Justice of India (CJI) B.R. Gavai being attacked in retaliation. However, a fact check by PTI Fact Check Desk found the claim to be misleading. The video is not related to the recent incident involving lawyer Rakesh Kishore. It dates back to October 2011 and shows lawyer and activist Prashant Bhushan being assaulted inside his Supreme Court chamber over his comments on the Kashmir issue. The old video is being falsely linked to the shoe-throwing episode to spread misinformation on social media. Claim A Facebook user shared a video showing a man being thrashed by another man, 'Prabhakarrao Gummapu', on October 14, claiming that the person attacked was the same person who threw a shoe at Chief Justice of India (CJI) BR Gavai. "Our people slapped the person who attacked Gavai garu. Isn't this what we need? React is awesome," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot below. Investigation Upon running the keyframes through Reverse Image Search, we found a video uploaded to the official YouTube channel of Times Now in October 2011. The timeline with the video clarifies that the video is not recent and is unrelated to the recent incident. The accompanying text with the video mentioned that Lawyer and activist Prashant Bhushan was roughed up and beaten up by three youths suspected to belong to a right-wing group, in his Supreme Court chamber, for his advocacy of a plebiscite in Jammu and Kashmir. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find media reports and came across a report by NDTV published on October 12, 2011. The report featured the same video as the recent social media post. It mentioned that Prashant Bhushan, a core member of Team Anna, was assaulted today in his chamber in the Supreme Court. Three people reportedly stormed into Mr Bhushan's chamber and began beating him while he was in the midst of a TV interview. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video dates back to 2011 and shows lawyer Prashant Bhushan being attacked in his SC chamber for his comments on the Kashmir issue. It has nothing to do with lawyer Rakesh Kishore or the recent incident.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video of dog helping a child cross railway track shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, October 17 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported video showing a dog helping a child cross a railway track while a train can be seen approaching from behind was recently shared on social media with the claim that it depicted a real incident. The video allegedly showed the dog jumping onto the railway track, where the child was seemingly playing, picking him up from behind, and placing him safely on the platform while a train was arriving. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found that the video was AI-generated and falsely shared as a real incident said to have occurred at Mumbai Central Station, misleading viewers. Claim An X user named Mohini (@MohiniWealth) shared a purported video on October 15, claiming it showed a dog helping a child cross a railway track safely while a train was coming from behind. The user claimed that the video depicted a real incident that occurred at Mumbai Central Station. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video garnered 542k views) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. using Google Lens on one of these keyframes, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a video posted on a YouTube channel named Multiverse Matrix on October 8, 2025. The Desk found that the video posted by the user was identical to the one from the viral post. However, upon careful analysis of the description, it was found that the video had been generated using an AI video platform, Higgsfield.ai. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. A comparison image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral social media clip and the video posted by the YouTube channel. Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk also reviewed the bio section of the YouTube channel Multiverse Matrix, where the user stated that the content shared on the channel was generated through AI. Below is a screenshot of the user's profile. In the subsequent part of the investigation, the Desk ran the video through an AI detection tool- Hive Moderation- which confirmed that 91% of the footage contained AI-generated or deepfake elements. Below is a screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an AI-generated video of a dog helping a child cross a railway track was falsely shared as a real incident said to have occurred at Mumbai Central Station.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Clipped video falsely shared to claim Tejashwi Yadav said 'he only wants power, and public can go to hell'
content: New Delhi, October 17 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) leader Tejashwi Yadav addressing the media has gone viral on social media with claims that he said he only wants power and that the public can "go to hell." The clip, shared by several users, allegedly shows Yadav making the remark while speaking to reporters, sparking criticism and debate online. However, a fact-check by PTI found the claim to be misleading. The viral video is clipped and taken out of context. In the original version, Yadav was criticising Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) leader Chirag Paswan and Hindustani Awam Morcha (Secular) leader Jitan Ram Manjhi, accusing them of being power-hungry. The truncated version circulating online omits this context, giving the false impression that Yadav made a dismissive comment about the public. Claim: An X user shared a video of RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav speaking to the media, 'Nehra ji', on October 14, claiming that he said he just wants the chair (power) and that the people can go to hell. In the 00:06-second video, he can be heard saying, "I just want the chair, the public can go to hell." Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot below. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. Upon further scanning the search results, the Desk came across the extended version of the same video, which was uploaded on a YouTube page in the name of '@darshnews01' on September 7, 2025. The description of the video reads, "Tejashwi said, 'Chirag-Manjhi only want the chair, the rest can go to hell, the public." In the video, a journalist asks Tejashwi Yadav, "Chirag and Manjhi are fighting among themselves, there's no coordination regarding seats." In response, Tejashwi Yadav says, "Both are ministers at the Centre. Tell me about the work they've done for Bihar. These people are power-hungry; they just want the chair, the public can be damned. This is their mindset." Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by News18 Hindi on September 7, 2025. The headline of the report read: "These people are just hungry for power, the public can go to hell... Tejashwi Yadav targets Chirag and Manjhi's war of words." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an incomplete video of Tejashwi Yadav attacking leaders of his rival parties is being shared with a false claim

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of Nitish Kumar's remarks about Lalu Yadav shared as recent amid ongoing political developments
content: New Delhi, October 17 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar speaking to the media about RJD chief Lalu Prasad Yadav has gone viral on social media with the claim that he recently targeted the BJP, accusing it of falsely implicating Yadav in an ongoing case. Several users shared the clip to suggest that Kumar had come out in support of Lalu Yadav during the current political situation in Bihar. However, a fact check by PTI found that the video is not recent but dates back to 2022. The clip initially shows Nitish Kumar responding to media questions about a separate case at that time. The video has resurfaced online with a misleading claim linking it to the current political context. The Delhi Rouse Avenue court has framed various criminal charges against Rashtriya Janata Dal, RJD President Lalu Prasad, his wife Rabri Devi, son Tejashwi Yadav and several others in the alleged IRCTC Scam case. Special Judge-PC Act Vishal Gogne passed the order. The court has framed charges of corruption, criminal conspiracy and cheating against the three. The case will proceed to trial since all the accused have pleaded not guilty. Claim: A video showing Nitish Kumar apparently answering a question about the CBI's move to challenge Lalu Yadav's bail application in the Supreme Court was shared by an X user, 'Nehra Ji', on October 15, claiming that he responded to the question saying that they are targeting Lalu Yadav. In the 00:17-second video, he says, "They're just harassing the poor guy. They're deliberately harassing him. Don't you see that those in the centre are harassing everyone these days? They're sparing some and harassing everyone else" "Nitish Kumar is exposing the BJP's true colours. A storm is coming in Bihar's politics. Regarding the case against Lalu Yadav ji, Nitish Kumar ji stated that the BJP is misleading him with lies. I think Chacha will flip sides. What do you all think?" read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, along with an archive link . Below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one keyframe, the Desk came across the extended version of the video uploaded on the YouTube channel named 'Live Cities Media Private Limited' on August 25, 2023. The timeline of the report clarifies that the video is not recent, but a two-year-old video shared as recent. The same portion is available from the 2:00 minute mark in the video. Then-Deputy Chief Minister Tejashwi Yadav accompanied Chief Minister Nitish Kumar during that time. He gave this answer when asked about Lalu Yadav. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by Dianik Jagran dated August 25, 2023. The headline read: "What did Nitish Kumar say on Lalu's statement that 'there will be many coordinators in the India alliance'?" The report highlighted that while returning from garlanding the statue of BP Mandal, Nitish Kumar had reacted to the CBI's move to the Supreme Court to cancel the RJD supremo's bail. He had said that he was being deliberately harassed. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Moreover, CBI filed a petition in the Supreme Court challenging the Jharkhand High Court's decision to grant bail to Lalu Prasad Yadav on medical grounds in the fodder scam case. The Supreme Court heard the petition on August 25, 2023. In January 2024, a few months before the Lok Sabha elections last year, Nitish Kumar left the Grand Alliance and returned to the NDA. Before this, in August 2022, he broke ties with the BJP and formed a Grand Alliance government with the RJD, Congress, and the Left parties. Tejashwi Yadav was appointed Deputy Chief Minister. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video claiming to show Nitish Kumar targeting the BJP over Lalu Yadav is a two-year-old video. Nitish Kumar was part of the Grand Alliance at that time.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2023 video of Samrat Choudhary criticising Nitish Kumar falsely shared as recent; details inside
content: New Delhi, October 17 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Days after the Election Commission of India announced the dates for the upcoming Bihar Assembly elections — scheduled to be conducted in two phases on November 6 and November 11, with counting on November 14 — a purported video of BJP leader and Bihar Deputy Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary criticising Chief Minister Nitish Kumar was widely shared online. Users claimed the video was recent, showing Choudhary calling Nitish Kumar "scrap material" ahead of the polls. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found that it dates back to July 2023, when the BJP and JD(U) were not in alliance in the state. At that time, the JD(U) was in alliance with Lalu Prasad Yadav-led Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD), a partnership that ended when Nitish Kumar switched back to the BJP-led NDA in January 2024. An old and unrelated video of Samrat Choudhary criticising Nitish Kumar was falsely linked to the upcoming Bihar Assembly elections. Claim An X user named Parmanand Azamgarhi (@parmanandyadavv) shared on October 15 an alleged video of BJP leader and Bihar Deputy Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary criticising Chief Minister Nitish Kumar. The user claimed the footage showed a recent statement by Choudhary, in which he called Nitish Kumar "scrap material" ahead of the Bihar polls. "A new twist has come in the politics of Bihar. Nitish Kumar has now become scrap material," the user captioned the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video garnered 18.3k views) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple handles, those who shared the same video making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search results via Google Lens also led the Desk to a video posted by Bihar Tak on its official X handle on July 17, 2023. The video did show Samrat Choudhary criticising Bihar CM Nitish Kumar, similar to the one seen in the viral social media video. However, upon careful analysis, it was found that the footage dated back to July 17, 2023 — a time when Nitish Kumar-led JD(U) was not in alliance with the BJP in the state. The JD(U) had then formed the government in partnership with the RJD before breaking its ties and switching allegiance to the BJP again in January 2024. Here is the link and archive link to the video: Additionally, the search results also led the Desk to the YouTube channel Zee Bihar Jharkhand. The channel shared the same video of Samrat Choudhary, in which he was seen criticising the Bihar Chief Minister. However, the details mentioned in the description revealed that the footage dated back to July 2023 and was not recent. Here is the link and archive link to the video, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of Samrat Choudhary criticising Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar was not recent and dated back to July 2023.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Edited photo of Virat Kohli 'giving autograph on Pakistani flag' shared with false claim; details inside
content: New Delhi, October 21 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared an image of Virat Kohli, claiming it showed him giving an autograph to a Pakistani fan on the latter's national flag. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found that the image was digitally altered. The original photo reportedly showed Kohli signing a Pakistani fan's Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) jersey, not the country's flag. A digitally edited image of Virat Kohli was falsely shared on social media to mislead viewers. Claim An X user named Zeeshan Nadeem (@Shani_7800) shared an image of Indian cricketer Virat Kohli on October 16, claiming he was giving an autograph on a Pakistani flag. "Virat Kohli spotted giving autographs to a Pakistani fan in Perth, Australia," the user captioned the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the image garnered 789.8k views) Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and found multiple handles that shared the same photo with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and came across an Instagram post from the sports news website InsideSport Cricket, dated October 16, 2025. The post featured a similar picture to the viral one but clearly showed Virat Kohli signing a fan's RCB jersey — not a Pakistani flag. This confirmed that the viral image had been digitally altered. Here is the link and archive link to the Instagram post, along with a screenshot: Below is a combined image highlighting how the original photo of Virat Kohli signing a fan's RCB jersey was digitally altered to make it appear as though he was signing a Pakistani flag. Additionally, the search result via Google Lens also led the Desk to a video posted by the X handle of a multi-sports platform named RevSportz Global (@RevSportzGlobalM) on October 16, 2025. It too featured the same visuals of Virat Kohli signing a fan's RCB jersey, as depicted. The platform further revealed that the fan captured with Kohli was indeed from Pakistan, but he had asked the cricketer to sign his RCB jersey — not the Pakistani flag. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a digitally altered image of Virat Kohli signing a Pakistani flag was shared online as genuine.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered video shared to falsely claim Defence Minister Rajnath Singh 'stated India funded Afghan Taliban to fight Pakistan'; details inside
content: New Delhi, October 21 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Days after India and Afghanistan held a series of bilateral talks during the Taliban-appointed Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi's week-long visit to India, a purported video of Defence Minister Rajnath Singh was recently shared on social media in which he was allegedly heard admitting that India is funding the Afghan Taliban to fight against Pakistan. The video allegedly showed the Defence Minister stating at the RSS centenary celebrations that India is trying to give Pakistan the harshest punishment with the support of the Afghan Taliban — a punishment that had not been given even after the 1971 war. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found the video to be digitally altered. The visuals depicted in the viral clip were originally from the flagging-off ceremony of the first batch of BrahMos missiles manufactured at the BrahMos Integration and Testing Facility Centre in Lucknow. A short segment from Defence Minister Rajnath Singh's address at the Lucknow event was taken and digitally altered by superimposing a fake audio track to mislead viewers. Claim An X user, Mansoor Ahmed Dhillon (@MansoorDhillon_), on October 19 shared a purported video of Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, claiming it was from the RSS's centenary celebrations, where he allegedly stated that India is funding the Afghan Taliban to fight against Pakistan. "Breaking: At RSS's 100-year celebrations, Rajnath Singh admits India is funding the Taliban to fight Pakistan for dollars. This exposes Hindutva's dark ambition to destabilize Pakistan and Afghanistan in pursuit of Akhand Bharat," the user captioned the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple handles, those who shared the same video making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a video posted on Defence Minister Rajnath Singh's official YouTube channel on October 18, 2025. It was found that the background visuals depicted in the viral social media video matched those in the video posted on Rajnath Singh's official channel, which captured him attending an event in Lucknow. The YouTube video showed the Defence Minister delivering an address at the flagging-off ceremony of the first batch of BrahMos missiles manufactured at the BrahMos Integration and Testing Facility Centre in Lucknow — not at the RSS's centenary celebrations, as claimed. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting the visual similarities between the viral social media clip and the video posted on the Defence Minister's YouTube channel. Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the complete video of the event shared on Rajnath Singh's YouTube channel to check whether he made any such statement as depicted in the viral video. However, nowhere in the extended clip did the Desk find the Defence Minister making any statement about India supporting the Afghan Taliban. In the original video, Rajnath Singh was heard praising India's defence capabilities. "Operation Sindoor is proof that victory has become a habit for us, and now we must further enhance our capabilities. The operation was just a trailer. It has made Pakistan realise what might follow," he said. In the subsequent part of the investigation, taking cues from the above findings, the Desk extracted the audio segment from the viral video and ran it through the AI audio detection tool Resemble AI. The tool indicated that while the voice appeared realistic, it may have been an impersonation. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video claiming to show Defence Minister Rajnath Singh admitting that India is backing the Afghan Taliban to fight against Pakistan was digitally manipulated.

author: Kaushki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Altered video falsely claims actor Manoj Bajpayee campaigned for Tejashwi Yadav
content: New Delhi, October 21 (Kaushki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video featuring actor Manoj Bajpayee has gone viral on social media with the claim that he is campaigning for Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) leader Tejashwi Yadav ahead of the upcoming Bihar assembly elections. In the clip, Bajpayee can be seen speaking with several people who remind him that "Tejashwi Yadav will take charge of the next government in Bihar on November 14," implying his political support for Yadav. However, a fact check by PTI found the claim to be false. The viral video is an altered version of an old advertisement Bajpayee featured in for an OTT platform in 2023. The original clip shows the actor engaging with people about movie recommendations, not politics. The doctored version uses AI-generated audio to create the impression that Bajpayee was endorsing Tejashwi Yadav. Bajpayee has also publicly clarified that he has no political affiliations and described the circulating video as "fake" and "patched-up," urging people not to share such misleading content. Claim: A video featuring actor Manoj Bajpayee having a conversation with several individuals in the video who remind him that "Tejashwi Yadav will take charge of the next government in Bihar on 14 November," was shared by an X user 'Dhanraj Yadav'. The user sharing the video claimed that Bajpayee was campaigning for Rashtiya Janata Dal (RJD) leader Tejashwi Yadav. "On November 14, the Tejashwi government is coming to Bihar," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here , respectively. On careful analysis of the video, the Desk noticed discrepancies in the video, such as the lip synchronization being off and a watermark of 'Spoof' at the lower right corner of the video. Below is a screenshot of the same. To first locate the original video, the Desk ran the extracted keyframes through Reverse Image Search and on further scanning the search results, we came across the same video uploaded on Amazon Prime Video's YouTube channel on 1 November 2023. In the video, Bajpayee can be seen taking film recommendations from people and not campaigning for the RJD for the upcoming assembly elections in Bihar. The timeline of the report clarifies that it is a one-year-old video, unrelated to the Bihar elections to be held this year in November. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search to find reports that stated Manoj Bajpayee's support for RJD. Our search, however, did not lead us to any such report. However, we did come across an X post by Bajpayee dated October 16 in which he explicitly stated that he has no association or allegiance with any political party, and the video in question is a fake and patched-up edit of an ad he did for Prime Video. "I would like to publicly state that I have no association or allegiance with any political party. The video being circulated is a fake, patched-up edit of an ad I did for Prime Video. I sincerely appeal to everyone sharing it to stop spreading such distorted content and urge people not to engage with or encourage such misleading content," he read. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking the investigation ahead, the Desk extracted the audio from the video and ran it through an AI-detection tool, extracted the audio from the viral video and ran it on an AI-detection tool, Hive Moderation, which concluded that the audio was 99.4 percent 'likely' AI-generated. Below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the audio used in the video is AI-generated and not real. The original video dates back to 2023, of an ad that Bajpayee featured in from Prime Video.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, MTV India is not closing down by the end of 2025; viral claim misinterprets UK media report
content: New Delhi, October 21 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media post claiming that MTV India will cease operations by the end of 2025 has gone viral, sparking speculation about the channel's future. The post claimed that MTV India, once a defining force in youth and pop culture, would "shut down by December 31, 2025." The claim quickly spread across multiple social platforms, drawing nostalgic reactions from users. However, PTI Fact Check found the claim to be false. The report referenced in the viral post pertains to MTV's operations in the United Kingdom, not India. MTV India, which is licensed by JioStar, has not issued any such announcement. The channel's official Instagram handle also clarified that they are "not going anywhere" and urged users to verify information before sharing it further. Claim: A post claiming that the iconic musical channel MTV India is set to shut down its operations in the country by December 2025 was shared by an Instagram user,'thebharatpost' on October 14, 2025. "MTV India, a cornerstone of youth culture and music television in the country, is set to cease operations by December 31, 2025…," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation As part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find an article published by Exchange4media, said that the decision was announced for five channels in the UK and that the move would not affect India. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Moreover, MTV is licensed by JioStar in India, which did not share any information regarding the channel's shutdown by the end of 2025 in India. Here is the link to their press release section. Taking the investigation ahead, the Desk scanned the official X, Facebook, and Instagram accounts of MTV India, but did not find any announcement on the official social media handles. However, in their October 18 post, they clarified that MTV India is not shutting down their services. "Hum kahin nahi ja rahe; and honestly without us your feed would be boring. MTV India yahin hai, with main character energy.Check your sources, fam. Kill that false alarm!," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the post claiming that MTV to shut down its services in India is fake.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, Delhi CM Rekha Gupta did not criticise PM Modi in Bihar rally speech; clipped video shared online with false claim
content: New Delhi, October 21 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta addressing a public rally in Bihar has gone viral on social media, with users claiming that she mocked Prime Minister Narendra Modi, saying he "could not manage his family, so how would he manage Bihar." The video appears to show Gupta taking a dig at the PM while speaking on stage. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the viral video and found that the claim is false. The clip is from Gupta's campaign speech in Bihar Sharif on October 15, 2025, where she was canvassing for BJP candidate Sunil Kumar as part of the NDA's election campaign for the Bihar Assembly polls. A review of the full video shows that Gupta's remarks were aimed at the Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) and its leadership, not at the Prime Minister. In the extended version of the speech, Gupta can be heard praising the Nitish–Modi duo and the NDA alliance, while criticising the RJD for corruption and dynastic politics. Claim: A video featuring Delhi CM Rekha Gupta addressing a public rally was shared by an Instagram user, 'sasikantsingh1', on October 16, claiming that she took a dig at PM Modi, saying that he could not manage his family, how would he cater to Bihar. In the video, Gupta can be heard saying, "Those who could not take care of their family, how would they handle Bihar?...Bihar needs to have strong leadership, not those who cannot handle their family." The text on the video, originally in Hindi, read: "Rekha Gupta's comment on PM Modi" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across the extended version of the social media post, uploaded on the official YouTube Channel of Navbharat Times on October 15, 2025. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta was addressing a rally in Bihar Sharif while campaigning for BJP candidate Sunil Kumar as part of the NDA's election campaign for the 2025 Bihar Assembly polls. Upon analysing the entire video, the Desk found the excerpts from the social media post at 48 minutes 05 seconds, she says, "This is a party (BJP) that is not corrupt…they worry about the citizens of the country. Those who cannot manage their own family, how will they manage Bihar? That is why we need to give Bihar's reins into strong hands…" This clearly implies that her comments were not for PM Modi but were directed towards the RJD. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking the investigation ahead, the Desk conducted a customied keyword search to find relevant media reports that cited Gupta taking a swipe at PM Modi. But we did not find any relevant report; however, given the seriousness of the matter, it would have been carried by all major news outlets. Moreover, the Bihar Assembly Elections are slated to take place in two phases on November 6 and November 11. The BJP has released a list of 40 star campaigners, featuring top leaders, including the PM, Home Minister Amit Shah, party chief JP Nadda, and top leaders like Rajnath Singh, ahead of the Bihar Assembly elections. The list features a mix of prominent leaders and celebrities. It includes five Chief Ministers, including Assam's Himanta Biswa Sarma, Delhi's Rekha Gupta, and Maharashtra's Devendra Fadnavis. Bhojpuri film actors Manoj Tiwari, Ravi Kishan, both MPs, and Pawan Singh were also named. According to a report, the PM will start his campaign from Karpurigram in Bihar's Samastipur on October 24 after paying obeisance to the state's political stalwart and former CM Karpoori Thakur, BJP Bihar president Dilip Jaiswal said on Sunday. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Rekha Gupta was actually criticising RJD and not PM Modi.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video from UAE's National Day celebrations falsely shared as Diwali festivities in Saudi Arabia
content: New Delhi, October 22 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A picturesque video of firecrackers illuminating the night sky was recently shared on social media, claiming it showed Diwali celebrations organised by the Muslim community in Saudi Arabia. The clip shows people enjoying the vibrant display as fireworks light up the sky. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the video was falsely linked to Diwali celebrations in Saudi Arabia. The footage actually showed the UAE's 52nd National Day celebrations, during which fireworks lit up the sky to mark the grand occasion. At no point did the video depict Diwali festivities in Saudi Arabia. An old and unrelated video from the UAE's National Day was misrepresented online as Diwali celebrations in the Kingdom. Claim An X user, Vaishali Mishra (@1VaishaliMishra), shared a purported video on October 20, claiming it showed Diwali celebrations being held in Saudi Arabia by the Muslim community. She wrote, "Diwali in Saudi Arabia. Real Muslims are bursting firecrackers with great enthusiasm, while the illegitimate offspring born from their own seeds are whining about Diwali firecrackers in India." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered 274k views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple handles, those who shared the same video making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a video shared on the YouTube channel '@kalyan.entertainment' on December 3, 2023. The Desk found that the video posted on this channel exactly matched the one in the viral post. The description stated that it showed the UAE's 52nd Union Day celebrations. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. A comparison image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral social media clip and the video posted on the YouTube channel. Additionally, the Desk found another matching video posted on December 3, 2023, by a YouTube channel named Alih Aradani Vlog. The video matched the background visuals seen in the viral post and also described the event as the UAE's 52nd Union Day celebrations. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. In the next stage of the investigation, to re-verify the video's location, the Desk closely analysed it and identified several elements confirming that it was filmed during the UAE's 52nd Union Day celebration. For instance, the Emblem of the United Arab Emirates was visible at multiple places, along with the 52nd-year celebration logo. Additionally, the video was shared on December 3, 2023, which coincides with the UAE's National Day celebrations held on December 2, 2023, marking the unification of the seven emirates in 1971. Below is a screenshot highlighting the findings. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video claiming to show Diwali celebrations organised by the Muslim community in Saudi Arabia is false. The video is, in fact, from the 52nd National Day celebrations held in the United Arab Emirates in December 2023 and has been falsely linked to Diwali festivities.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2018 photos from Micronesia falsely shared as recent plane crash in Mumbai; details inside
content: New Delhi, October 22 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A set of photos showing an aircraft floating in the sea has gone viral on social media, with users claiming that a passenger plane crashed near Mumbai and that two people were injured. The user alleged that the incident took place in the Arabian Sea off Mumbai's coast, adding that all passengers were rescued and a few were hospitalised. The PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the viral photos and found that the claim is false. The images are not from Mumbai but from Chuuk Island in the Federated States of Micronesia, where an Air Niugini Boeing 737-800 crash-landed in a lagoon on September 28, 2018, after missing the runway. The viral photos are thus being shared out of context to claim a recent plane crash in Mumbai falsely. Claim: A collage of two pictures of an Air Niugini plane in the water was shared by a Facebook user 'Royal Kisan' on October 14, claiming that the aircraft crashed in Mumbai and that two people were injured. "A very tragic incident occurred at sea in Mumbai. A plane crash occurred. All passengers were rescued safely. One or two were injured and were sent to the hospital," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot below. Investigation The Desk ran the picture through Reverse Image Search and found several other users who had shared the same photo with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a report by Financial Express published on September 28, 2018. The report presented a similar image to the one seen in the social media post. The time also clarifies that the incident is not recent and is unrelated to any crash in Mumbai. "Air Niugini Boeing 737-800 flight crash-lands into Micronesia sea: Pics of freak mishap and rescue. All 47 passengers and crew aboard an Air Niugini Boeing 737-800 flight were rescued safely after the aircraft crash-landed in a Pacific lagoon. The plane hit the water short of the runway while trying to land at Chuuk Island in the Federated States of Micronesia," read the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the social media post and the news report. Another report by the BBC, published on September 28, 2018, mentioned that a passenger aircraft had come down in a lagoon off Chuuk International Airport in Micronesia after it missed the runway, according to airport officials. The Air Niugini plane from Papua New Guinea was seen sitting in shallow water just off the coast. Locals responded by approaching the aircraft in small vessels to help rescue the 36 passengers and 11 crew. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. The report also carried several pictures from the incident site. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the social media post and the news report. This makes it clear that, according to the reports, the viral photo is not from Mumbai. It shows an Air Niugini Boeing 737-800 that came down in a lagoon off Chuuk International Airport in Micronesia after missing the runway on 28 September 2018. However, the Desk also conducted a set of customised keyword searches on Google to find if such an incident had happened in Mumbai, but the search did not lead us to any credible reports. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that 2018 photos of a plane that crash-landed in a Pacific lagoon in Micronesia are being falsely shared from Mumbai.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered video shared to falsely claim PM Modi 'admitted India funded Afghan Taliban to fight Pakistan'; details inside
content: New Delhi, October 22 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video claiming that Prime Minister Narendra Modi allegedly admitted India was funding and supporting the Afghan Taliban to fight against Pakistan has gone viral on social media. The clip allegedly shows Modi making the controversial statement while addressing armed forces personnel aboard INS Vikrant during Diwali celebrations. The post also claimed that an Indian journalist had released a "censored" portion of his speech that was not broadcast by Indian media. The PTI Fact Check Desk examined the viral clip and found that it is digitally altered. The original footage shows the Prime Minister addressing Navy personnel aboard INS Vikrant and praising the armed forces for their unity and coordination during Operation Sindoor. A review of the full video confirms that Modi did not refer to Afghanistan, the Taliban, or Pakistan. Claim: A video featuring PM Modi addressing a gathering, aboard INS Vikrant, was shared by an X user 'Hawk's eye' on October 21, claiming that he admitted India is funding and supporting the Afghan Taliban to fight against Pakistan. "None of India's soldiers will lay down their lives because we have made Afghanistan our slaves. These people lick my shoes for a few dollars…," says PM Modi in the video. The post's caption read: "Breaking News: Indian journalist Geeta Biswas releases censored portion of Narendra Modi's speech, which was not allowed to air on any Indian media. Modi explains the next strategic advances in full detail." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot below. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on one keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. One such post can be found here , with its archived versions viewed here . Upon analysing the video, we found a watermark of 'The Tribune', taking a cue from which we conducted a customised keyword search to access the original and complete video. The search led us to the official YouTube channel of The Tribune, where the video was uploaded on October 20. The description, along with the video, mentioned that PM Modi was on board the INS Vikrant with the armed forces, delivering a speech during the Diwali celebrations. Upon listening to the entire 1 hour 47 minute 16 seconds video, the Desk found that he did not make any such statements of funding and supporting the Afghan Taliban to fight against Pakistan. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. A PTI report carried by The Hindu on October 20 mentioned that the extraordinary coordination among the three services together compelled Pakistan to surrender during Operation Sindoor. He also lauded the valour and determination of security forces, stating that it was due to this that the nation has achieved a significant milestone by "eliminating Maoist terrorism". The headline of the report read: "PM Modi celebrates Deepavali aboard INS Vikrant, hails armed forces' unity in Operation Sindoor" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. To verify the claim, the Desk carefully watched the video and found several discrepancies, including mismatched lip-sync. We then extracted the audio from the video and ran it through Resemble AI, an AI-detection tool. The tool indicated that while the voice appeared realistic, it may have been an impersonation. Below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video has been digitally manipulated. In the original footage, Prime Minister Narendra Modi made no such statement.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2011 photo from Pakistan shared to falsely claim 'Indian aircraft destroyed amid May 2025 tensions'
content: New Delhi, October 22 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A photo showing a wrecked aircraft in a hilly region is being shared online with claims that it shows an Indian jet shot down during India-Pakistan tensions in May 2025. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the claim is false. The image has been online for over a decade and shows a Pakistan Air Force jet that crashed during a training mission near Sargodha in 2011, not a recent incident involving India. The picture is unrelated to Operation Sindoor. Claim: A picture showing a wrecked aircraft in a mountainous area was shared by an X user 'idrw' on October 21, claiming that it was an Indian aircraft linking it to the India-Pakistan tensions in May 2025. "First Kill of Indian S-400 was JF-17 on the First night. Confirmed by IAF," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot below. Investigation The Desk ran the picture through Reverse Image Search and found that several other users had shared the same photo with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a report by Dawn News published on August 17, 2017. The report carried the same image as seen in the recent social media post, clarifying that the picture is not recent. The text, along with the picture, mentioned that it showed the wreckage of the PAF jet, which had crashed. "PAF jet crashes while on training mission near Sargodha, pilot survives," read the headline of the report. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot below. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the social media post and the news report. The Desk also came across another report, by Hindustan Times, published on December 12, 2012, highlighting that a Pakistani air force jet crashed in Attock near Islamabad, Pakistan. "File-photo-Villagers-stand-near-wreckage-of-a-Pakistani-air-force-fighter-jet-that-crashed-in-Attock-near-Islamabad-Pakistan-AP-Photo-Ghulam-Shabbir," read the caption alongside the picture. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot below. Our search further led us to another report by The Tribune published on November 15, 2011. The report again carried the exact image of the wrecked aircraft, mentioning that the jet crashed near Mansar Town after taking off from Kamra Airbase. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk could not find when the picture was first shared, but our investigation proves that the photo has been available online at least since 2011. This clarifies that it is unrelated to India-Pakistan tensions of May 2025.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered video falsely shared to claim 'Mallikarjun Kharge criticising Rahul Gandhi, Tejashwi Yadav'; details inside
content: New Delhi, October 23 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it depicted Congress party chief Mallikarjun Kharge criticising party leader and Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav. The footage allegedly showed Kharge addressing a gathering and stating, "One must be vigilant. If you are not vigilant, Rahul Gandhi and Tejashwi Yadav will land you in trouble." However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it to be digitally altered. The original video showed Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge criticising Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah over "vote chori" (vote stealing) allegations. Their names were digitally replaced with those of Rahul Gandhi and Tejashwi Yadav. A digitally manipulated video of Kharge was falsely shared on social media to mislead viewers. Claim An X user, Ms. Bhumi (@ibmindia20), on October 19 shared a purported video of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, allegedly criticising Rahul Gandhi and Tejashwi Yadav. In the video, Kharge appeared to say, "One must be vigilant. If you are not vigilant, Rahul Gandhi and Tejashwi Yadav will land you in trouble." The user captioned the video: "Sometimes Congressis tell the truth... Heartfelt thanks to Kharge ji for speaking the truth." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered 79.7k views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple handles, those who shared the same video making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The search also led the Desk to a video posted on the official YouTube channel of the Congress Party on September 1, 2025, showing Kharge addressing the public during the 'Voter Adhikar Yatra' in Patna. The visuals matched those from the viral post. Upon careful analysis, the Desk found that the viral clip was taken from the 1:37 timestamp of the original video. In that segment, Kharge could be heard saying: "Through vote stealing, Modi ji is trying to win in Bihar. You must be vigilant. If you are not vigilant, Modi ji and Shah will land you in trouble." This confirmed that the viral video was digitally altered — with the names of "PM Modi and Amit Shah" replaced by "Rahul Gandhi and Tejashwi Yadav." Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the visual similarities between the viral social media clip and the video posted from the official YouTube channel of the Congress party. Additionally, the Desk found the full transcript of Kharge's speech uploaded on the Congress Party's official website. The transcript confirmed that Kharge was criticising PM Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah over "vote chori" allegations — not Rahul Gandhi or Tejashwi Yadav. Here is the link to the transcription uploaded on the party's website. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video of Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge allegedly criticising Rahul Gandhi and Tejashwi Yadav is digitally altered. The original video shows him criticising Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah over "vote chori" allegations.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated image falsely shared in name of Ayodhya's Diwali 2025 celebrations
content: New Delhi, October 23 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): The grand Diwali celebrations in Ayodhya this year once again made global headlines, with over 26 lakh diyas illuminating the ghats of the Saryu River and more than 2,000 people performing aarti together, setting two new world records. Amid this, a stunning aerial image showing an illuminated cityscape went viral on social media, with users claiming it captured the breathtaking view of Ayodhya during the Deepotsav 2025 celebrations. However, a PTI Fact Check investigation found that the viral picture was not real but AI-generated. Tools used by the Desk confirmed with over 90 per cent probability that the image was artificially created. Further, the image was traced back to an AI artist's profile on X, confirming it originated as digital artwork and not a real photograph from the festivities. Claim: A picture showing an aerial view of an area being illuminated, apparently by diyas, was shared by an X user 'Ocean Jain' on October 20, claiming that it was from Ayodhya during this year's Diwali celebration. The post clocked 14.3k views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot below. Investigation The Desk ran the picture through Reverse Image Search and found that several other users had shared the same photo with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post by a user named '@Bhaveshlivelife' on October 21, the caption along with the picture mentioned that it is an AI-generated Diwali image that went viral. "Check out this stunning AI-generated Diwali image that went viral! It beautifully symbolises Hindu cultural endurance, sparking conversations around tradition, pollution critiques, and the incredible 2.6 million diyas lit in Ayodhya!" read the post's caption. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. However, the Desk also conducted a customised keyword search to find reports that extensively covered the pictures from Ayodhya being illuminated. But our investigation did not lead to this particular picture being used by media outlets. Here is the link to a report by Hindustan Times, and below is a screenshot showing a few snippets of Ayodhya. On careful analysis of the picture in the viral post, the Desk found several discrepancies that hinted it might be manipulated or AI-generated, for instance, the extra glossy texture and irregularities. Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the picture through SightEngine, an AI-detection tool which found it 95% likely to be AI-generated. Below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk ran the picture through WasIt AI, another AI-detection tool, which also detected that it is AI-generated. Below is a screenshot of the same. Moreover, while accessing the source of the picture, we found the earliest instance of this photograph being uploaded online was on October 20, 2025, by @WallzByAI, an AI artist, who, in another post, confirmed it to be their work. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an AI-generated picture was falsely shared as real in the name of Ayodhya being illuminated on Diwali.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video falsely shared to claim elephant held Lord Shiva's statue stuck in flood waters; details inside
content: New Delhi, October 23 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check): A video showing an elephant holding a statue of Lord Shiva was recently shared on social media, accompanied by a claim that it depicted a real incident. Users claimed the video showed the elephant holding the giant statue to save itself from being swept away in floodwaters after getting stuck. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the video was AI-generated and falsely shared as a real incident, misleading viewers. Claim An X user, Prarthana Singh (@PrarthaSingh83), shared a video on October 21 of an elephant allegedly holding a statue of Lord Shiva to save itself from being swept away in floodwaters. The footage showed the elephant holding the statue as it became stuck in the water. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple handles, those who shared the same video making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a video posted by an Instagram user named Pranav Vijayan on October 18, 2025. The video he shared was identical to the one in the viral post. However, a careful review of Vijayan's profile revealed that his handle is known for sharing AI-generated clips. This was also mentioned in his bio, where he identified himself as an AI video creator. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: A comparison image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral social media clip and the video shared by the Instagram user. Next, taking cues from the above findings, the Desk ran the video through the AI detection tool- Zhuque AI Detector, which confirmed that 99% of the footage contained AI-generated or deepfake elements. Below is a screenshot of the result: Additionally, in the subsequent part of the investigation, the Desk also reached out to Pranav Vijayan, who confirmed that the video had been created using AI-generated elements and does not depict a real instance. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing an elephant holding a giant statue of Lord Shiva while stuck in floodwaters was AI-generated and falsely shared as a real incident to mislead viewers.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered video falsely shows PM Modi watching Pawan Kalyan's Telugu film
content: New Delhi, October 24 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, claiming it showed him watching the newly released Telugu-language film They Call Him OG in his office. The clip purportedly depicted the Prime Minister intently viewing the movie. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it had been digitally altered. The original footage was from 2019, when PM Modi was watching the live telecast of the Chandrayaan-2 launch. In the viral version, those visuals were replaced with a still from the Telugu movie, misleading viewers about the context. Claim On October 21, Instagram user Hitesh Sankhala shared a purported video of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, allegedly showing him watching the newly released Telugu-language film They Call Him OG at his office. The video appeared to depict the Prime Minister intently watching the movie. The user wrote: "Prime Minister Modi Sir watching an OG movie." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple handles sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search results also led the Desk to a video shared by India Today on its official YouTube channel on July 22, 2019. The Desk found that the background, clothing, and gestures of PM Modi in the India Today video matched precisely those in the viral video. The only difference observed was that, in the original India Today footage, PM Modi was watching the live telecast of the Chandrayaan-2 launch at his office. In the viral version, those visuals were digitally replaced with a scene from They Call Him OG. Here is the link and archive link to the video, along with a screenshot. A comparison image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral social media clip and the video shared by India Today on YouTube. Additionally, the Google Lens search led the Desk to several news reports featuring the same footage of PM Modi as in the viral video. These reports also confirmed that the original video showed PM Modi watching the live telecast of the Chandrayaan-2 launch in 2019. The visuals were digitally altered to depict him watching a scene from the Telugu movie 'They Call Him OG'. Links to three such reports published by multiple media outlets can be found here , here , and here . Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video showing Prime Minister Narendra Modi watching a still from the Telugu movie 'They Call Him OG' was digitally altered. The original footage, from 2019, actually showed the Prime Minister watching the live telecast of the Chandrayaan-2 launch.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2024 Punjab stubble burning video falsely shared as recent to claim it caused Delhi's post-Diwali pollution; details inside
content: New Delhi, October 24 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): As Delhi's air quality plummeted to 'severe' levels following Diwali celebrations, a video showing fields engulfed in flames went viral on social media, with users claiming it captured large-scale stubble burning in Punjab that caused the capital's toxic smog. However, a PTI Fact Check investigation found that the video is not recent. The footage dates back to November 2024, when it was reported as an incident from Dagru village in Punjab's Moga district. The video is now being circulated out of context amid the ongoing debate over Delhi's pollution crisis. Claim A video showing grasslands on fire was shared by an X user '@vsvadivelfca' on October 22, claiming that it shows stubble burning in Punjab resulting in massive air pollution. "This is the level of Stubble Burning going on in Punjab. This is a perennial cause of air pollution in Delhi and its suburbs," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here , respectively. When the Desk ran the extracted keyframes through Reverse Image Search, it found the extended version of the same video uploaded by News9 Live on November 1, 2024. The report's timeline clarified that the video is not recent but is a year old. The accompanying text mentioned that it depicted the incident of stubble burning in a field in Dagru village, Moga district, Punjab. This practice, while common among farmers, poses significant environmental challenges, including air pollution and health risks. "We take a closer look at an incident of stubble burning in a field in Dagru village, Moga district, Punjab. This practice, while common among farmers, poses significant environmental challenges, including air pollution and health risks. We discuss the implications of stubble burning, its impact on air quality, and the ongoing efforts to find sustainable alternatives. Join us as we raise awareness about this pressing issue facing Punjab's agricultural landscape," read the description of the video. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combined image highlighting the similarities between the content in the social media post and the News9 Live. Meanwhile, according to a report, Delhi's sky turned grey and hazy a day after Diwali fireworks lit up the city. The air is toxic, making the national capital the "most polluted major global city". The pollution levels, or the Air Quality Index (AQI), soared to severe levels, resulting in difficulty breathing, itchy eyes, and discomfort for even healthy people. Here is the link to the report. While another report by The Indian Express mentioned that Punjab has recorded 484 farm fires till Wednesday (October 22) this year, a sharp 69% drop from last year's figure of 1,581 and a 73% drop from 1,794 fires recorded in 2023 during the same period. Here is the link to the report. On further scanning the news report, we also came across a report by The Times of India, which cites a study by the consultancy Climate Trends, highlighting that while stubble burning contributes to Delhi's PM2.5 levels, it is not the only factor affecting air quality. With a 77.5% reduction in stubble burning in 2025, Delhi's PM2.5 remained high due to emissions from firecrackers, traffic, industries, and dust. Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of stubble burning is not recent but dates back to 2024.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Unrelated videos from Maharashtra, Haryana falsely shared to claim 'Chhattisgarh MLA slapped cop over cow vigilantes'
content: New Delhi, October 24 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video circulating on social media claims to show a Chhattisgarh MLA slapping a police officer in anger over the arrest of cow vigilantes. The video shared on social media combines two separate clips- one showing a man slapping another seated on a chair, and another showing a police officer dragging a man by his hair. However, a PTI Fact Check investigation found that the viral video is false. The first clip is from Maharashtra, where a farmers' union leader assaulted a bank manager in August 2024, while the second is from Haryana, showing police action during a clash with cow vigilantes in April 2025. The two unrelated incidents are falsely linked to create a misleading narrative. Claim: A video shared by Instagram user 'premsingh3307' on October 22 shows two clips- in the first, a man slaps another man seated on a chair; in the second, a police officer is seen dragging a man by his hair and forcing him into a police vehicle. The post claims that a Chhattisgarh MLA slapped a police officer in anger over the arrest of cow vigilantes. "This is the lion MLA of Chhattisgarh who entered the police station and slapped the police? Actually, a truck full of cows let the cops go, then caught the cow protectors coming from behind and put them in the police station. Then MLA came as Sunny Paji," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here , respectively. On the running keyframes of the first part of the video, the Desk conducted a Reverse Image Search and found a report by The Times of India published on 14 August 2024 that featured the same clip seen in the social media post. The report highlighted that the video actually shows Swabhimani Shetkari Sangathan youth wing president Mayur Borde slapping a bank manager. The incident occurred on 13 August 2024 at a Bank of Maharashtra branch in Varud Budruk village, Jaffrabad tehsil, Jalna district, Maharashtra. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. The Desk also conducted a customised Google search to identify other reports covering the same news. Our search led us to a report by The Indian Express published on August 14, 2024. The report also carried the same image as seen in the video. It mentioned that Swabhimani Shetkari Sanghatana's youth wing president, Mayur Borde, was caught on camera slapping a bank branch manager in Maharashtra's Jalna district multiple times, alleging harassment of farmers. "Swabhimani Shetkari Sanghatana youth wing leader slaps bank manager for 'harassing farmers', video goes viral," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Taking the investigation ahead, the Desk ran the second part of the video, showing a police officer dragging a man by his hair, through Reverse Image Search, and came across a report by Dainik Bhaskar carrying the same video, published in April 2025. It highlighted that the Panipat police in Haryana dragged a cow vigilante by his hair in the middle of the road and even beat him. The vigilante alleges that he helped the police seize two cattle smugglers' vehicles. However, instead of taking action, the police released him. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. As part of the investigation, we also conducted a customised keyword search to find other reports and came across the same video uploaded on the official YouTube channel of Haryana Tak on April 17, 2025. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. This shows the first part, which shows Swabhimani Shetkari Sangathan youth wing president Mayur Borde slapping a bank manager in Jalna, Maharashtra, in August 2024. The second part shows a police officer dragging a man named Karan in Panipat, Haryana, during a clash with cow vigilantes in April 2025. Moreover, we also searched for reports of any such incident in Chhattisgarh. Still, our search did not lead to any article stating that an MLA in Chhattisgarh slapped a police officer after the arrest of a cow protector. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the two unrelated incidents are shared with a false claim of a Chhattisgarh MLA slapping a police officer over cow vigilantes.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: This burglary video falsely linked to India is actually from Paraguay
