content: New Delhi, October 24 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it showed a burglary in India, where a Bangladeshi immigrant allegedly entered the house of a Hindu businessman and stole a bicycle. The clip purportedly showed the infiltrator, identified as Mohammad Zubair, sneaking into the house at midnight and crossing a barbed-wire fence with the stolen item. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found that it was falsely attributed to India. The footage shows a burglary that occurred in Asunción, Paraguay's capital. An unrelated video of a theft in Paraguay was misleadingly shared on social media, linking it to an incident in India. Claim An X handle with the username Baba Banaras (@RealBababanaras) shared a video on October 23, claiming it showed a burglary incident from India. The video allegedly captured a Bangladeshi immigrant trespassing into a Hindu businessman's house, crossing a barbed wire fence around midnight, and stealing a bicycle from the premises. The user wrote: "Illegal Bangladeshi infiltrator Mohammad Zubair was caught on CCTV stealing from a Hindu businessman's house. Police later arrested him. Such illegal Rohingya & Bangladeshi elements are a growing threat to India's internal security, from theft to terror. Deport them all." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered 20.1k views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple handles sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search results also led the Desk to a video published on the Instagram handle of Radio Cáritas UC, a Paraguay-based news portal, on April 30, 2025. The news portal had shared the same video as the one seen in the viral post. However, the detailed description accompanying the video revealed that it depicted an incident from Paraguay — not India. The description stated that the video showed an incident in Paraguay's Asunción city, where an individual entered a home to rob it by crossing razor-sharp wire attached to the fencing wall. The individual then stole a bicycle from the premises. Here is the link and archive link to the original post, along with a screenshot: A comparison image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral social media clip and the video shared by the Instagram handle. Additionally, the Google Lens search results led the Desk to a video published on the YouTube channel of another Paraguay-based news portal, SNT Paraguay. The channel shared a report featuring a journalist speaking with a resident of the same area where the burglary shown in the viral video occurred. It was reported that the incident happened in Bella Vista, Barrio Jara, Asunción, Paraguay — not in India. "A man stole two bicycles from the yard of a house in Asunción and was caught on security cameras. Neighbours are reporting the growing insecurity in the area and calling for increased police presence," read the English translation of the description accompanying the video. Here is the link to the YouTube video, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an unrelated video showing a burglary incident in Paraguay was falsely shared on social media, linking it to an incident in India.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2023 video of Samrat Choudhary criticising Nitish Kumar falsely shared as recent; details inside
content: New Delhi, October 27 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Ahead of the Bihar Assembly Elections slated to be held in two phases - November 6 and November 11, with counting on November 14, a purported video featuring BJP leader and Bihar Deputy Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary criticising Chief Minister Nitish Kumar was shared by several social media users. Those sharing the video claim that it showed a recent statement by Choudhary, in which he said that it is imperative to remove Nitish Kumar from power. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video actually dates back to 2023, a time when Nitish Kumar-led JD(U) was not in alliance with the BJP in the state. The JD(U) had then formed the government in partnership with the RJD before breaking its ties and switching allegiance to the BJP again in January 2024. The video was recorded during Choudhary's speech at the Ambedkar Samagam event in Patna, held on the death anniversary of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar. The video was shared with a false claim on social media as recent. Claim: A video featuring BJP leader and Bihar Deputy Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary criticising Chief Minister Nitish Kumar was shared by an X user, 'Sameer Lohiya', on October 23. The user claimed the footage showed a recent statement by Choudhary, in which he said that it is imperative to remove Nitish Kumar from power. "In 2025, Nitish Kumar's repeated flip-flops must end, and a BJP government must be formed in Bihar. When he sees his female colleagues, they say they have banned liquor. But friends, when Nitish Kumar first became Chief Minister of Bihar in 2005, there were 987 liquor shops in Bihar. And when Nitish Kumar ruled for 11 years, he increased the number of liquor shops to 11,000. He made the people of Bihar 11 times more alcoholic," says Choudhary in the 1-minute 12-second video. Furthermore, the text in the video also identifies Samrat Choudhary as the state president of the Bihar BJP. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a Facebook post by the BJP Bihar featuring the same video as seen in the social media post. The video was uploaded on Facebook on December 7, 2023. The timeline clarifies that the video is not recent, but a two-year-old video which was falsely shared as recent. A time when Nitish Kumar-led JD(U) was not in alliance with the BJP in the state. The JD(U) had then formed the government in partnership with the RJD before breaking its ties and switching allegiance to the BJP again in January 2024. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google led to the extended version of the video uploaded on the YouTube channel by the 'Rad News' on December 7, 2023. Samrat Choudhary was delivering a speech at the Ambedkar Samagam event held in Patna on December 7, 2023, on the death anniversary of Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar. During his speech, Samrat Choudhary attacked the RJD and Nitish Kumar. Attacking Nitish Kumar, he says, "Nitish Kumar ji, his party is behind him, the Janata Dal United. We believe that he is holding a program next to them, which is why it's raining, and this has become inauspicious for us. Therefore, friends, we must do auspicious work. In 2025, we must put an end to Nitish Kumar's repeated flip-flops and form a BJP government in Bihar. Friends, Nitish Kumar constantly says, when he sees his female colleagues, that he has banned liquor. But friends, when Nitish Kumar first became Chief Minister of Bihar in 2005, there were 987 liquor shops in Bihar. During his 11 years in power, Nitish Kumar increased the number of liquor shops to 11,000. He has made the people of Bihar 11 times more alcoholic." Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Moreover, in March 2023, the BJP appointed Samrat Choudhary as the president of the Bihar unit. However, when Nitish Kumar left the Grand Alliance and returned to the NDA in January 2024, Samrat Choudhary was appointed Deputy Chief Minister in the new NDA government. Subsequently, in July 2024, Samrat Choudhary was removed from the post of state president and Dilip Jaiswal was appointed as his replacement. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video featuring Samrat Choudhary taking a dig at Nitish Kumar dates back to 2023, a time when Nitish Kumar-led JD(U) was not in alliance with the BJP in the state. The JD(U) had then formed the government in partnership with the RJD before breaking its ties and switching allegiance to the BJP again in January 2024.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of woman assaulted by police falsely linked to Uttar Pradesh; incident from Rajasthan
content: New Delhi, October 27 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A disturbing video showing a woman being assaulted by police officers in an open field is being widely shared on social media with the claim that the incident took place in Uttar Pradesh. The video shows a uniformed officer hitting a woman and trying to choke her while others stand by. Several users reshared the footage, tagging Uttar Pradesh Police and demanding action. However, a PTI Fact Check investigation found that the video is being circulated with a false claim. The incident did not take place in Uttar Pradesh but in Rajasthan's Didwana-Kuchaman district, where a police officer was booked and suspended for assaulting a woman during a dispute in early September 2025. Claim: A video showing a woman being assaulted by police officers in an open field was shared by an Instagram user named 'skyeakubali45' on October 11, claiming that the incident happened in Uttar Pradesh. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here , respectively. Upon further reviewing the search results, the Desk came across a few snippets of the video in a report by Dainik Bhaskar, published in September 2025. As per the report, a serious case of police misconduct has come to light in Didwana-Kuchaman. An Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) was caught on video beating a woman, abusing her, and choking her throat during a dispute. The incident occurred when police tried to take her husband into custody. Following complaints, the Superintendent of Police (SP) has taken disciplinary action against the ASI. This clarifies that the incident happened in Rajasthan and not in Uttar Pradesh. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from the above finding, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find the video report said that the affected family was Dalit. The whole incident started on September 7 when four police personnel, including ASI Vinod Kumar, reached the house of a person named Champalal Meghwal. Champalal had alleged that the police had targeted his family in a land case. He had also filed a complaint in this regard at the Markana police station on August 17. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of an assault on a woman by police officers is actually from Rajasthan and not Uttar Pradesh.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video of monkey serving food at restaurant in India shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, October 27 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a monkey serving a plate of steaming idlis to a customer was recently shared on social media with a claim that it depicted an incident from a restaurant in India. Users claimed that the video showed a monkey, allegedly recruited as a waiter, serving food to a customer. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found that it was AI-generated and falsely shared as a real incident, misleading viewers. Claim A Facebook user named Mrityunjay Jha on October 21 shared a video allegedly showing a monkey serving food to a customer at a restaurant in India. The user claimed the video depicted a monkey, seemingly hired as a waiter, serving a plate of idlis to a customer. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple social media handles sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here : The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a video posted on an Instagram handle named multiversematrix on October 19, 2025. The video shared by the handle was identical to the one circulating on social media. However, upon analyzing the details provided in the post, it was found that the video was created using artificial intelligence (AI). The Instagram user mentioned in the caption that the video was fully generated using Higgsfield, an advanced AI-driven video generation tool. Here is the link and archive link to the original post, along with a screenshot: A comparison image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral social media clip and the video shared by the Instagram user. Next, taking cues from the above findings, the Desk ran the video through an AI detection tool, Zhuque AI Detector, which confirmed that 99% of the footage contained AI-generated or deepfake elements. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video showing a monkey serving food to a customer at a restaurant was AI-generated and falsely shared as a real incident to mislead viewers.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Scripted video shared to falsely claim police officials thrashed woman in India; details inside
content: New Delhi, October 27 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it depicted a recent incident from India, where two police officials brutally thrashed a woman. The video, which did not show the victim's face, allegedly captured her in a distressed state with her clothes torn, while the officials continued to assault her. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found that it was scripted and showed two police officials interrogating a male tantrik, not assaulting a woman. The video had no connection to any real-life incident and was misleadingly shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An Instagram user, Reena Rajput, on October 4, shared a video purportedly showing two Indian police officials brutally thrashing a woman. The video allegedly showed the woman in a distressed state, with her clothes torn, while the officials continued to beat her. The user wrote, "I have never seen such atrocities on women in any other government. Is this the law, Modi ji?" Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several social media handles sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here : The Google Lens search results also led the Desk to a video posted on a YouTube channel named Haunted Guru Ji on September 6, 2025. The Desk found that the visuals seen in the viral video appeared at the 7-minute, 45-second mark of this YouTube video. However, the description clearly stated that the content was scripted, showing a scene where police officials interrogate a male tantrik after he was caught committing a crime. It did not depict a real instance of two police officials brutally thrashing a woman. "The material and information contained in this video are strictly for information related to paranormal activities and are for entertainment purposes only," the description reads. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot: A comparison image below highlights that the content in the viral video matches the video posted by the YouTube channel. Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk reviewed other videos posted by the same channel and found that it is known for producing scripted and dramatized content. Two such examples can be found here and here : Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video claiming to show two police officials brutally thrashing a woman is fake. The original footage was a scripted video showing two police officials interrogating a male tantrik and was created purely for entertainment purposes. It has no link to any real-life incident.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Clipped video falsely claims Rahul Gandhi blamed PM Modi, RSS, and BJP for eagles flying during speech
content: New Delhi, October 28 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video circulating on social media claims that Congress leader and Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha (LoP_ Rahul Gandhi blamed Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the RSS, and the BJP for eagles flying overhead during one of his speeches. A PTI Fact Check investigation found that the viral clip is misleading. The video is a doctored combination of two separate parts of his 2020 speech in Kondli, Delhi, edited to misrepresent his remarks. Gandhi did not make any such statement blaming PM Modi or the BJP for eagles flying above. Claim: A video featuring Congress leader Rahul Gandhi addressing a public gathering was shared by an Instagram user 'Np_official' on October 18, claiming that he allegedly blamed PM Modi, RSS, and BJP for eagles flying above during a speech. In the video, he can be heard saying, "Please tell me one thing, why is this eagle flying here? What is the reason for this? The reason for this is Narendra Modi. The reason for this is RSS. The reason for this is BJP." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across the extended version of the same speech uploaded on the official YouTube channel of Rahul Gandhi on February 5, 2020. He was addressing a public meeting in Kondli, Delhi. Upon analysing the video, we found that at 3:15 minutes, Gandhi can be heard saying, "What is the reason behind this. A lot of people will say that the reason is Narendra Modi. The reason is RSS and the reason is BJP. But I will want to look at it differently. The biggest reason is that the youth of the country don't have any aim. They are afraid of unemployment." At 10:12 minutes, Gandhi spoke about the eagles, as can be heard in the social media post. He compared how the common people faced poor living conditions, while the government gave tax benefits to the country's upper strata. He says, "Brother, tell me what the eagles are doing here? Why are they flying here? Can anybody say why the eagles are flying here? The dirt in this area tell me how many crores of rupees you think will be needed to remove it? How many? Five crore, ten crore? A 10-year-old girl is saying it'll cost five crore. Okay, it might take 50 crores. Narendra Modi ji had waived off Rs 1,30,000 crores of taxes for the richest people of India a few days ago. You people stay in dirt all the time, and the rich live in peace in castles and airplanes." Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video is a combination of two different elements of his speech that have been altered.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, this video does not show Indian cricketer Ravindra Jadeja performing a fire stunt
content: New Delhi, October 28 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it depicted Indian cricketer Ravindra Jadeja performing risky fire stunts on a road. Users claimed the video was from Diwali celebrations. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the video does not feature Ravindra Jadeja performing the stunt. The video originally shows a content creator who regularly posts similar videos. An unrelated video of a content creator performing a fire stunt was falsely shared on social media, identifying him as Indian cricketer Ravindra Jadeja. Claim An Instagram page with the username g18news_com on October 23 shared a video allegedly showing Indian cricketer Ravindra Jadeja performing a risky firecracker stunt on the occasion of Diwali. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the social media video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple handles sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Desk also conducted a customised keyword search on Google to check whether any credible news outlets had reported on the alleged fire stunt performed by Ravindra Jadeja. However, the search did not lead to any reports confirming that the video featured the cricketer. Next, the Desk ran the extracted keyframes through Google Lens again. The search led to a video shared by an Instagram user named Rahul Bharwad (@rahul_chosla_0561) on October 21, 2025. The video shared by this user matched exactly with the viral clip. Upon analysing the details, however, it was found the video captures the same user Rahul Bharwad, who regularly posts videos performing fire stunts on his account. The video does not capture Indian cricketer Ravindra Jadeja. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. A comparison image below highlights the visual similarities between the social media clip and the video shared by the Instagram handle. Additionally, the Desk compared the image of the individual from the viral clip with verified images of Ravindra Jadeja. It was found that both are two different individuals. Below is a screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video depicting a content creator performing a fire stunt was falsely shared on social media, claiming it showed Indian cricketer Ravindra Jadeja.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old image from PM Vishwakarma launch in Dwarka falsely shared as PM Modi's staged home visit
content: New Delhi, October 28 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A photograph showing Prime Minister Narendra Modi interacting with a woman, seemingly inside a house, has been widely shared on social media with the claim that the visit was staged. Several users alleged that the setting was artificially created with newly installed household items such as a sewing machine, carpet, pillow covers, and a high-mast light to project a humble background for the Prime Minister. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the image is not from a residential visit but from an exhibition held at Yashobhoomi in Dwarka, New Delhi, on September 17, 2023. The event marked the launch of the PM Vishwakarma Scheme, where the Prime Minister interacted with artisans and beneficiaries as part of the exhibition showcasing traditional crafts. The image was shared with a false claim on social media. Claim: A picture showing PM Modi interacting with a woman, apparently inside a house, was shared by an X user, @AG_knocks' on October 26, claiming that the visit was staged and the house was refurbished and furnished with new household items like a sewing machine, an expensive carpet, pillow covers, and a high-mast light. The user further highlighted that the woman in the picture was wearing an ID card. "After fake classroom, fake Yamuna, now a fake hut -Plastic paint -new sewing machine -expensive carpet -new pillow covers -high-mast light installed. The woman is wearing ID card even at home. Is this a hut or a studio? Btw, who goes inside someone's house wearing shoes?," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the picture through Reverse Image Search and found that several other social media users had also shared the same picture with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be found here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search, the Desk came across a report by News18 published on September 17, 2023. The report carried the same image as seen in the social media post. According to the report, the image was taken on the PM's 73rd birthday, when he visited a three-day exhibition in Yashobhoomi, Dwarka, at the launch of the PM Vishwakarma Scheme on the occasion of Vishwakarma Jayanti. "Prime Minister Narendra Modi interacted with Vishwakarma partners at the India International Convention and Expo Center in Dwarka to launch the "PM Vishwakarma" scheme. He spent time with several artisans and learned about their skills from women artisans," read the caption along with the picture. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from the above finding, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and found the same picture in MSME Insider, a monthly bulletin published by the Ministry of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises. The October 2023 edition highlighted the launch of the PM Vishwakarma Scheme. It included several images showing Prime Minister Modi interacting with artisans at the exhibition, with the viral image appearing on page 6. He also distributed Vishwakarma certificates to 18 beneficiaries. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the picture of PM Modi inside the house is from an exhibition held in September 2023 at Yashobhoomi, Dwarka, New Delhi, during the launch of the PM Vishwakarma Scheme

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered video shared to falsely claim 'PM Modi announced free bike scheme for citizens'
content: New Delhi, October 28 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported video of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in which he was seen briefing the public about a newly introduced government scheme offering free bikes to every citizen, was recently shared on social media. The video allegedly showed the Prime Minister at a public rally announcing a "bonanza scheme" to distribute free Splendor bikes to all citizens on the occasion of the four-day Chhath festival. The clip further included visuals of a news anchor confirming the scheme, claiming that to avail of its benefits, users must like and share the video and submit their details through links mentioned on the Instagram profile shown. It also stated that the bikes would be given only to those who followed the handle. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it to be digitally manipulated. The video falsely shows PM Modi announcing a free bike scheme for citizens during Chhath Puja. The original footage was from February 2019, when PM Modi delivered a speech at the launch of the PM-KISAN scheme in Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh. His original speech was digitally altered, with superimposed audio falsely suggesting he announced a free bike scheme. Claim An Instagram page with the username 'trending_jobs24' shared a video on October 27, purportedly showing Prime Minister Narendra Modi announcing a government scheme to distribute free Splendor bikes to every citizen on the occasion of the Chhath festival. The video showed PM Modi at a public rally announcing the alleged "bonanza scheme" and was followed by a clip of a news anchor claiming that citizens could avail of the offer by liking, sharing, and entering their details through links on the Instagram profile. "Chhath Puja special offers free Splendor bike," read the caption of the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video garnered 8326 likes) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple handles, those who shared the same video making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. Next, the Desk conducted a customized keyword search on Google to check if any credible media outlets or government sources had reported on such a scheme. However, the search did not lead to any credible reports confirming the existence of a free bike scheme. Given the scale of the claim, such an announcement would have received extensive media coverage if it were real. Continuing the investigation, the Desk ran the keyframes extracted above through Google Lens. The search result led the Desk to a YouTube video shared by the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) that matched the visuals from the viral clip. Upon analysis, it was found that the footage was from PM Modi's speech at the launch of the PM-Kisan Samman Nidhi Yojana in Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh, in February 2019. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the visual similarities between the viral social media clip and the video shared by the Prime Minister's Office. Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the complete video of the event shared on the PMO India's YouTube channel to verify whether the Prime Minister made any such statement as depicted in the viral clip. However, nowhere in the extended footage did the Desk find PM Modi mentioning a free bike scheme. In the original video, the Prime Minister spoke about farmers' welfare, the PM-KISAN scheme, and other agriculture-related initiatives. In the subsequent part of the investigation, taking cues from the above findings, the Desk extracted the audio segment from the viral video and ran it through the AI audio detection tool Resemble AI. The tool indicated that the voice heard in the video was fake. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video of PM Modi was digitally altered to falsely claim that he announced a free bike scheme for citizens on the occasion of the Chhath festival.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video from Guatemala falsely shared to link it to plastic pollution in India; details inside
content: New Delhi, October 29 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing large heaps of plastic waste floating in a polluted water body has been widely shared on social media with the claim that the visuals are from India. Several users used the clip to criticise environmental policies, arguing that India imposes bans and taxes on plastic use while failing to curb mass pollution in its own rivers. However, the PTI Fact Check found the claim to be misleading. The video is not from India but from Guatemala. The footage dates back to 2022 and shows plastic waste washed up along the shores of the Motagua River, a waterway known for carrying garbage from Guatemala City into the Caribbean Sea. The visuals were earlier reported by multiple international outlets, including CBS News and Reuters, and have no connection to India. Claim: A video showing mounds of plastic waste polluting a water body was shared by X user @GlobalDiss on October 18, claiming the footage was from India. "You pay carbon taxes, sky-high energy bills, banned plastic straws, and carry useless paper bags that tear instantly. All to "save the environment." Meanwhile in India…," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On running the extracted keyframes through Reverse Image Search, the Desk came across an X post by CBS News on July 22, 2022, that mentioned mounds of plastic waste lapping onto the Caribbean shores of Guatemala. This makes it clear that the incident is not recent, definitely not from India. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot. Taking a cue from the above finding, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google. It came across a Reuters report published on June 9, 2022, featuring several other visuals of the Rio Motagua, including photographs of heaps of plastic waste. It mentioned that plastic bottles and mounds of trash lap onto the shores of a once pristine beach in a Honduran fishing village. It comes from neighbouring Guatemala, carried down from a heavily polluted river. Guatemala's Rio Motagua runs from the edge of the country's capital, Guatemala City, out to the Caribbean Sea. What once was a roaring river slows to a trickle in some areas, choked by trash. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Taking the investigation forward, the Desk found that a video was published by the verified YouTube channel 4Ocean on June 9, 2022. The channel stated that the video depicts Guatemala's coastlines. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showed plastic waste washing up on the shores of the Motagua River in Guatemala in 2022

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Temple ritual from Udupi falsely shared online as 'caste-based bias' incident in India; details inside
content: New Delhi, October 29 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it depicted an alleged caste-based discrimination incident in India. The footage allegedly showed two instances — the first visual purportedly showed poor, low-caste Hindu people being served food on the bare floor instead of on plates. In contrast, the second visual showed a group of Muslim people seemingly enjoying a feast, sitting side by side. The user compared the two visuals, claiming Muslims treat everyone equally, whereas Hindus divide people based on caste. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false. The video actually captured a unique temple tradition at Karnataka's Udupi Krishna Temple, where devotees receive prasad on the floor and eat it there as an act of devotion. The video has no connection to any caste-based discrimination incident in India and was misleadingly shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An X user, Aqsa Aleena (@MuslimahAqsa), on October 28 shared a video claiming it depicted an alleged caste-based discrimination incident in India. The footage allegedly showed poor, low-caste Hindu people being served food on the floor, while Muslim people were shown sitting together and eating a feast. The user captioned the post: "This is the beauty of Hinduism, where poor, low-caste people are served food on the ground, while high-caste people are served in plates. That's why I say there is no religion better than Islam." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video garnered 3,000 views) Investigation The Desk ran the social media video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple handles sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a video shared by content creator 'gujju__guide' on his Instagram page on February 19, 2025. The video bore striking similarities to the viral visuals, such as people being served food on the floor and willingly partaking in the ritual. Upon reviewing the video's caption and context, the Desk found that it did not depict any caste-based discrimination. Instead, it showed a traditional ritual at Udupi Krishna Temple in Karnataka, where devotees are served prasad on the floor and consume it there as a mark of devotion. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image highlighting visual similarities between the viral and Instagram videos, confirming that both were filmed at the exact location. Additionally, the Desk found several other videos by content creators showcasing the same tradition at the Udupi Krishna Temple. Links to three such videos can be found here , here and here . Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing devotees being served food on the floor at the Udupi Krishna Temple was falsely shared on social media with the claim that it depicted a caste-based discrimination incident in India.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered video falsely claims actor Sonu Sood extended support for Khesari Lal Yadav's candidacy in Bihar elections
content: New Delhi, October 30 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): With the Bihar Assembly elections around the corner — scheduled to be held in two phases on November 6 and November 11, and the counting of votes on November 14 — a purported video of Bollywood actor Sonu Sood extending support to Bhojpuri singer and actor Khesari Lal Yadav, who is contesting in the upcoming state polls, was shared on social media. The video allegedly showed the actor backing Khesari Lal Yadav's decision to contest from Chhapra on a Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) ticket and wishing him success in the elections. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it to be digitally manipulated. In the original video, Sonu Sood was seen sharing a motivational message. The viral clip had been doctored with superimposed audio that falsely suggested he had extended support to Khesari Lal Yadav for the upcoming Bihar Assembly Elections 2025. Claim An X user, Surendra Yadav (@Surendr0032083), on October 29, shared a video purportedly showing Bollywood actor Sonu Sood extending his support to Bhojpuri singer and actor Khesari Lal Yadav, who is contesting on an RJD ticket from Chhapra in the Bihar Assembly elections. The video allegedly showed the actor backing Khesari Lal Yadav's decision to contest from Chhapra and wishing him success amid criticism. "Film actor Sonu Sood speaks in support of Khesari Lal Yadav, slams opponent," the user wrote while sharing the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered 24.2k views and 2.5k likes.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple handles sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. Next, the Desk conducted a customised Google search to verify whether Sonu Sood had indeed extended his support to Khesari Lal Yadav. The search, however, did not lead to any credible news report confirming the same. Continuing the investigation, the Desk ran the extracted keyframes (depicting visuals of Sonu Sood) through Google Lens. The search led to a video posted by the actor on their official X account, which matched the visuals from the viral clip. The actor shared the original video on his official handle on October 25, 2025. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. A comparison image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral video and the one shared by Sonu Sood on his official account. Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the complete video shared from the actor's handle. However, nowhere in the extended footage did the Desk find the actor extended support to Khesari Lal Yadav. In the original video, Sonu Sood was delivering a motivational message. In the subsequent part of the investigation, drawing on the above findings, the Desk extracted the audio segment from the viral video and ran it through the AI audio-detection tool Resemble AI. The tool indicated that the voice heard in the video was fake. Below is a screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a digitally manipulated video of Sonu Sood was falsely shared on social media, showing him extending support to Khesari Lal Yadav in the upcoming elections.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Maharashtra coaching clip falsely shared as Kerala's 'Muslim classroom'
content: New Delhi, October 30 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it showed a classroom arrangement specifically for Muslim students at a college in Kerala. The clip allegedly showed a makeshift partition separating the seating of Muslim boys and girls. The video drew mixed reactions online — some users praised what they called the Kerala government's "initiative." In contrast, others alleged it was an appeasement tactic by the state's Left-leaning government to woo Muslim voters. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found that the video was unrelated to Kerala. The visuals were actually from a private coaching institute in Maharashtra's Nanded district. An unrelated video from Maharashtra was thus misleadingly circulated on social media, falsely linked to claims about classroom segregation in Kerala. Claim An X user, Zahra Noor (@zahra_malik3), on October 22, shared a purported video claiming it showed a classroom in Kerala where separate seating arrangements were made for Muslim boys and girls. "For Muslims, co-education should be stopped, and this kind of education system should be implemented throughout India. Salute to Kerala for taking this bold step for Muslim boys and girls," the user wrote while sharing the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered over 553,000 views.) Investigation The Desk ran the social media video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple handles sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. Further, the Google Lens search results led the Desk to an Instagram handle linked to a private educational institute named M.O.S. Academy. The video shared there matched the visuals from the viral post. The description accompanying the video clarified that it was filmed at the MOS Academy, a private educational institute, not at any college in Kerala. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a comparison image highlighting visual similarities between the viral video and the Instagram reel, confirming that both were filmed at the exact location. Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk examined the Instagram account that shared the original video; the account's bio stated that MOS Academy is located in Nanded, Maharashtra, not Kerala. Moreover, several other videos posted on the same handle depicted the same classroom setup, showing the same partition dividing male and female students. Additionally, to reconfirm the institute's location, the Desk searched for MOS Academy on Google Maps. The result confirmed that the institute is situated in Nanded, Maharashtra. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video claiming to show a classroom arrangement for Muslim students in a Kerala college was false. The footage actually originated from MOS Academy, a private coaching institute in Nanded, Maharashtra, and had no connection to Kerala.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Year-old video falsely shared to claim 'Nitish Kumar urged Modi to return as Chief Minister'
content: New Delhi, October 30 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A short video of Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar speaking at a public gathering is circulating on social media with the claim that he said Prime Minister Narendra Modi should become the Chief Minister again. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found the claim to be misleading. The clip is not recent; it dates back to May 2024 during a Lok Sabha election rally in Patna Sahib, Bihar. Reports from the time confirm that Kumar misspoke, referring to Modi as Chief Minister before correcting himself to say he meant Prime Minister. Claim: A video featuring Bihar CM Nitish Kumar addressing a public gathering was shared by an X user 'mukeshbudharwi' on October 28, claiming that he said that Modi should become the Chief Minister again. In the 00:13-second video, he says, "Respected Narendra Modi should become Chief Minister again, the country should develop, Bihar should develop, everything should happen." Then, when interrupted by leaders on the stage, he says, "Narendra Modi is already the Prime Minister." The post clocked 12.6k views on social media. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further review of the search results, the Desk came across an Instagram post by AajTak dated May 26, 2024, featuring the same video seen in the recent social media post. The timeline clarifies that the video is not recent but a year old. The caption of the post read, "Chief Minister Nitish Kumar's tongue slipped while addressing a public rally in Daniyawan, Patna Sahib Lok Sabha constituency, Bihar. He said, "We want to win all 40 seats in Bihar and more than 400 seats across the country. And Narendra Modi should become the Chief Minister again." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Taking a cue from the above finding, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google to identify relevant media reports. It came across a Hindustan Times report published on May 26, 2024. The report highlighted that Nitish Kumar inadvertently wished Narendra Modi to become 'Chief Minister' once again instead of 'Prime Minister'. As the other leaders present on the stage realised the gaffe, they swiftly reacted. One of them attempted to correct his flub, showing the immediate impact of the slip. Correcting himself, Kumar said that he meant that Modi would become the Prime Minister again and keep moving ahead. "Narendra Modi is already a Prime Minister...That's why I am saying that he may keep moving," he said. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Our searches also led us to the official YouTube page of Janta Dal (United), livestreamed on May 26, 2024. Within this 44-minute video, we found the viral video segment starting around minute 42. Chief Minister Nitish Kumar held this public meeting in support of Patna Sahib Lok Sabha candidate Ravi Shankar Prasad. He said, "We have come to request you, brother, that our candidate, Ravi Shankar Prasad, please make him victorious with a huge majority. Now, what is my wish? We want to win all 40 seats in Bihar. Today, we want to win more than 400 seats across the country and that respected Narendra Modi should become the Chief Minister again. The country should develop, Bihar should develop, everything should happen." After this, when leaders Ravi Shankar Prasad and Sanjay Jha, who were present on the stage, interrupted him, he said, "Narendra Modi is the Prime Minister, and he will remain Prime Minister. So, after that, we are saying that he will lead the way, so that is what we want, this is what we have to do." Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video featuring Bihar CM Nitish Kumar, saying that PM Modi should become the CM again, was recorded during the 2024 Lok Sabha election rally.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old photo of cricketer Shreyas Iyer from hospital shared as recent after his latest injury from India–Australia ODI
content: New Delhi, October 30 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A photo of Indian cricketer Shreyas Iyer smiling while seated on a hospital bed is being widely shared on social media with the claim that he was recently hospitalised after sustaining an injury during the India–Australia ODI in Sydney on October 25, 2025. The post claims that Iyer was moved out of the ICU and is now in stable condition. However, a PTI Fact Check investigation found the image is being shared with a false context. The photo is not from the recent injury sustained during the Sydney match. It dates back to April 2021, when Iyer underwent shoulder surgery following the India–England ODI series. While the BCCI has confirmed that Iyer is currently undergoing treatment for a spleen injury sustained during the Australia match, the viral photo is unrelated to the present incident. Claim: A photo of Indian cricketer Shreyas Iyer smiling while sitting on a hospital bed was shared by an X user, @RAJESHKCWIN0333, on October 28, claiming that Iyer had been hospitalised following an injury during the India–Australia match in Sydney. "OOD NEWS FOR FANS - SHREYAS IYER OUT OF ICU. Shreyas Iyer is safe now. Shreyas Iyer has been moved out of the ICU, now in a stable condition," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation : The Desk ran the picture through Reverse Image Search and found that several other users had shared the same photo with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a Hindustan Times report that carried the same picture of Shreyas Iyer as seen in the social media post. The article, published on April 8, 2021, noted that Iyer had sustained a shoulder injury during last month's India-England ODI series. He had injured his shoulder in the first ODI and subsequently missed the next two matches. The report's timeline clarifies that the picture is not recent but from his injury back then. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. We also came across an X post by Sreyas Iyer featuring the same picture of him in the hospital, shared on April 8, 2021, mentioning that Surgery was a success and that, with lion-hearted determination, he'd be back in no time. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Meanwhile, according to a statement issued by the BCCI, Iyer sustained an impact injury to his left lower rib cage while fielding during the third ODI against Australia in Sydney on October 25, 2025. He was subsequently taken to the hospital for further medical evaluation. The board confirmed that scans revealed a laceration injury to his spleen. Iyer is currently under treatment, medically stable, and recovering well. Here is the link to the statement. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the picture showing Shreyas Iyer posing in a hospital bed is not recent but dates back to 2021.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of gunfire exchange in Lebanon falsely shared as incident from Jaipur; details inside
content: New Delhi, October 31 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it depicted a deadly shooting incident near Jaipur's Jagatpura Airport. The footage allegedly showed three cars stopped at a crossroad on an empty road, when an individual from the first car stepped out, seemingly carrying a loaded gun, and began firing incessantly at the occupants of the other two vehicles. While one person managed to escape safely, another individual, apparently injured, was seen writhing in pain and rolling on the road. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it to be unrelated to Jaipur or any part of India. The video actually showed an exchange of gunfire that broke out between security officials and a wanted criminal in Lebanon. An unrelated video from Lebanon was falsely shared on social media, linking it to a shooting incident in India. Claim An Instagram page with the username 'Jaipur Post' shared a video on October 19, purportedly showing a deadly shooting incident near Jaipur's Jagatpura Airport. The footage allegedly depicted three cars stopped at a crossroad on an empty road, when an individual from the first car stepped out, seemingly carrying a loaded gun, and began firing incessantly at the occupants of the other two vehicles. While one person managed to escape safely, another individual, apparently injured, was seen writhing in pain and rolling on the road. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing the story, the video had garnered 9,307 likes.) Investigation The Desk ran the social media video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple handles sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search result also led the Desk to a video shared by an Instagram page named 'Uncensored Press' on October 13. The video matched the visuals from the viral post. However, the video's description revealed that the incident occurred in Lebanon and was not related to Jaipur. "An ambush along the Damour-Saadiyat road injured an officer and a member of the Mount Lebanon Investigations Unit," the caption of the post read. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a comparison image highlighting the visual similarities between the viral video and the original footage shared by the Instagram page. In the subsequent part of the investigation, drawing on the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google regarding the incident. The search led to multiple video news reports published by Lebanon-based outlets, confirming that the gunfire exchange indeed took place in Lebanon. The reports stated that the incident showed a wanted individual being chased by security officials on the Damour–Saadiyat road. Links to two such posts can be found here and here . Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an unrelated video of gun fire exchange in Lebanon was falsely shared on social media linking it to an incident from India.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Clipped video falsely claims Rahul Gandhi talked about himself when he said 'he has direct connection with God'
content: New Delhi, November 3 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video featuring Congress leader Rahul Gandhi addressing a public rally has gone viral on social media with the claim that he said he does not suffer from any illness because he has a direct connection with God. In the 15-second clip, Gandhi can be heard saying, "I do not get any illness; I have a direct connection with God, I talk to Him directly," which users shared to suggest he was referring to himself. However, a PTI fact check found the claim to be misleading. The viral video is a clipped portion of a longer speech delivered in Darbhanga, Bihar, where Gandhi was actually taking a jibe at Prime Minister Narendra Modi. In the full context, Gandhi mimics Modi while criticising him for staging a dip in the polluted Yamuna river, sarcastically suggesting that Modi would claim he doesn't fall sick because he talks directly to God. The viral clip removes this context, falsely implying that Gandhi made the claim about himself. Claim: A video featuring Congress leader Rahul Gandhi addressing a rally was shared by an X user 'Jitendra pratap singh' on October 30, claiming that he doesn't have any disease as he has a direct connection with God. In the 00:15-second video, he says, "I do not get any illness; I have a direct connection with God, I talk to Him directly." The post clocked 52.3k views on social media. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . Upon further review of the search results, the Desk came across a video of Rahul Gandhi's speech from a joint public meeting, livestreamed on the YouTube channel of the Congress leader from Darbhanga, Bihar, on October 29. The video shows the public meeting addressed by several Mahagathbandhan leaders, including Rahul Gandhi, Tejaswi Yadav, and Mukesh Sahani. Upon listening to the entire speech, we found that at the 34-minute timestamp, he says, "In the last meeting, I said before the elections, you can make Modi ji do anything you want. At the next meeting, if anyone says, 'Modi ji, please dance on stage and we will vote for you,' he will start dancing and perform Bharatanatyam. He performed a drama, and through that drama, the truth of India was revealed. What was the drama? On one side, there is the Yamuna, a river with dirty water; if anyone drinks it, they will fall ill or even die. No one can go into it; it is so filthy that if you step into it, you'll get an infection immediately. But Modi ji staged a drama. He made a small pond there, did you see it? This is India for you. For elections, they will show you anything. 'Look, brothers, I have a 56-inch chest, I'm taking a dip in the Yamuna…'" Furthermore, at the 35:30-minute timestamp, the viral clip shows Rahul Gandhi, mimicking what PM Modi would say, stating, 'I do not get any illness; I have a direct connection with God. I talk to him directly.' He added, "And then, from behind, a pipe is installed, clean water is poured into it; and then our media friends show it: 'Look, look! Narendra Modi ji is bathing in the Yamuna.' However, there was a problem; someone had taken a picture of the pipe. Then Modi ji said, 'Now I am not going there anymore…'" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Rahul Gandhi was talking about Prime Minister Modi, sarcastically suggesting that PM Modi would claim to have a direct connection with God. A clipped portion was shared with a false claim on social media.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video claiming monkey rode bike falsely shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, November 3 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media video purportedly showing a monkey riding a bike was recently shared online, accompanied by claims that it depicted a real incident. The clip appears to show a monkey walking through a vegetable market when it spots a parked bike with the keys still in the ignition. The monkey then jumps onto the bike, starts it, and begins to ride before eventually crashing into a person standing nearby. The Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it to be AI-generated, falsely shared as a real incident to mislead viewers. Claim On November 2, an X user named Surendra Yadav (@Surendr0032083) shared a video allegedly depicting a real incident of a monkey riding a bike. The footage showed a monkey walking through a vegetable lane when it spotted a parked bike with its keys still in the ignition. The monkey then jumped onto the bike, started it, and began riding before eventually crashing into an individual standing nearby. The user captioned the post, "Monkeys keep doing all sorts of ridiculous things, look, it crashed the bike. Whenever you park your bike, don't forget to take out the key." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video garnered 150k views) Investigation The Desk ran the social media video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple handles sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search results also led the Desk to a video shared by an Instagram user named Joe Ulaeto on October 29, 2025. The visuals from the viral video matched those of the video shared from this Instagram handle, which likely uploaded it first before it was picked up and circulated widely on social media. However, upon careful analysis, the Desk observed several discrepancies — including a sudden burst of fire at one of the vegetable stalls depicted in the video. Moreover, it is highly unlikely that a monkey could ride a bike as shown in the clip. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. A comparison image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral social media clip and the video shared by the Instagram handle. In the subsequent part of the investigation, drawing on the above findings, the Desk ran the viral video through the AI detection tool Hive Moderation, which confirmed that 99.9% of the footage contained AI-generated or deepfake elements. Below is a screenshot of the analysis result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an AI-generated video of a monkey riding a bike was falsely shared on social media as a real incident.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video falsely shared to claim cow saved child from bull's attack; details inside
content: New Delhi, November 3 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video depicting a cow saving a child from a bull's attack, seemingly in a farm field, was recently shared on social media with the claim that it showed a real incident. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found that the video was AI-generated and falsely shared as real to mislead viewers. Claim An X handle with the username @albadi_jhindiyo, on October 31, shared a video allegedly showing a real incident in which a cow saved a child from a bull's attack in a field. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered 216.8K views.) Investigation The Desk ran the social media video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple handles sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a video posted on a YouTube channel named Aloísio na Roça on October 28, 2025. The footage shared there matched the visuals from the viral post. However, the description accompanying the YouTube video revealed that it had been created using the AI app "Sora," which converts text prompts and images into hyperrealistic videos with sound using OpenAI's latest technology. "The cow protected the boy from the bull #soravideos," the video was titled. Here is the link and archive link to the video, along with a screenshot: Below is a comparison image highlighting the visual similarities between the viral video and the YouTube short. Next, taking cues from the above findings, the Desk ran the viral video through the AI detection tool Hive Moderation, which confirmed that 97.6% of the footage contained AI-generated or deepfake elements. Below is a screenshot of the analysis result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an AI-generated video of a cow saving a child from a bull's attack was falsely shared on social media as real.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2020 Bihar rally photo falsely shared as recent chair-breaking at BJP event
content: New Delhi, November 3 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A photograph of broken chairs scattered across a rally ground was shared by several social media users with claims that it shows angry attendees vandalising furniture at a recent BJP event in Bihar. The picture was framed as evidence of growing public resentment ahead of the state elections. The accompanying caption alleged that people, frustrated with the BJP, hurled chairs after the rally ended, and suggested that only the Election Commission's intervention could secure a BJP victory in the state. However, a PTI Fact Check investigation found that the photo is several years old and is being misrepresented online to push a misleading narrative. Reverse image searches and archived posts show that it first surfaced in 2020 during the previous Bihar assembly elections, when it was linked to a public meeting addressed by Bhojpuri actor-turned-politician Dinesh Lal Yadav 'Nirahua' in Banka district. The 2025 Bihar Assembly Elections will be held in two phases for 243 seats. Voting will take place in the first phase on November 6 for 121 seats, and in the second phase on November 11 for 122 seats. Vote counting will take place on November 14. Claim: A picture featuring broken chairs at a rally was shared by an X user '@INDStoryS' on October 30, claiming that angry people broke the chairs at a BJP rally in Bihar. The image shows several broken chairs near a stage. A poster on the stage also features photos of Prime Minister Modi, Chief Minister Nitish Kumar, and several other leaders. "After the BJP rally in Bihar ended! Why did the people vent their anger by throwing chairs!? But in this situation, you can see what appears and watch. There is so much outrage among the people of Bihar that if they still win the election, the Election Commission will have a very big contribution to the BJP," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the picture through Reverse Image Search and found that several other users had shared the same photo with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here . Upon further review of the search results, the Desk came across a Facebook post dated October 26, 2020. The caption read, "This is how Nirahua, who came to campaign for Nitish Kumar, was welcomed in Bihar. This is a photo from a public meeting held today in Belhar, Banka district, by Nirahua, who came to campaign for JDU candidate Manoj Yadav." The report's timeline clarifies that the picture is not recent, dating back to 2020. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Our search further led us to another Facebook post dated October 26, 2020, claiming that it was from a public meeting held by Dinesh Lal Yadav Nirahua in support of NDA candidate Manoj Yadav in the Belhar Assembly constituency of Banka district. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised Google search for relevant media reports and came across a report by ETV Bharat published on October 26, 2020. The report stated that Bhojpuri superstar Dinesh Lal Yadav Nirahua campaigned for NDA candidate Manoj Yadav in Belhar Assembly constituency on the final day of campaigning for the first phase of the Bihar Assembly elections. The then-BJP MP Ramkripal Yadav accompanied Nirahua to the event, held at Jhama Maidan, the block headquarters. However, the report did not mention the chair breaking. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. However, the news report did not mention any chairs being broken at this public meeting. The Desk cannot confirm who broke these chairs or why. However, it is clear that the photo is more than five years old and is being misrepresented as recent. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the image being shared on social media dates back to the 2020 assembly elections in Bihar.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Viral video falsely claims 'Amit Shah called Indian Army an Army of Hindutva'
content: New Delhi, November 3 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of Union Home Minister Amit Shah speaking at a public event is circulating on social media with dramatic claims about his remarks on the Indian Army. Several users allege he described the Army as belonging to Hindutva, the RSS, and a Hindu nation. The clip appears to show him urging those who disagree to leave for Pakistan, framing the forces as exclusive to one community. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated and found the claim to be false. The viral clip is a deepfake. The original footage is from Shah's address in Munger, Bihar, and does not contain any of the statements attributed to him. Claim: A video featuring Union Home Minister Amit Shah addressing a public gathering was shared by a Facebook user, Annu Malik, on October 28, claiming that he said that the Indian Army is an army of Hindutva, the RSS, and a Hindu nation. In the video, he can be heard saying, "I have been listening to the nonsense of the Congress and the AAP on social media, in which they repeatedly say that the Indian Army is being saffronised and our Army is now becoming a Party Army. I am saying this in front of the whole world with my 56-inch chest that the Indian Army is an Army of Hindutva. This is the Army of the RSS, not the Army of a Muslim, not the Army of a Dalit, not the Army of a Christian. Whoever has a problem with this Army should leave Pakistan. We consider our Army to be the Army of the Hindu Rajya…" "Home Minister Amit Shah offers a scathing rebuttal to Lt. Gen. Vinay Ghai. Amit Shah has openly expressed his desire to saffronize the Indian Army in his recent statement. He said that everyone who disagrees with the politicisation of the Indian Army should be sent back to Pakistan because this is essentially a Hindutva Army and it will stay like this," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . Upon running the extracted keyframes through Reverse Image, we found the same video in an extended version on the official YouTube channel of Amit Shah, live-streamed on October 25, 2025. He was addressing a rally in Munger, Bihar. We noticed that Shah's outfit and background matched those seen in the social media post. Upon watching the entire video, we did not find any remarks he made about the Indian Army. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot. Further, the Desk noticed several anomalies, such as Lip movements that appear unnatural and out of sync with the audio, and a smudged overall jawline. Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the video through an AI-detection tool, Deepfake-O-Meter, which identified it as a deepfake. Below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video is manipulated and that the original footage is from Amit Shah's address in Bihar's Munger district, in which he did not make any such remarks about the Armed Forces.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: White couples shocked to see their babies' skin colour? AI-generated videos falsely shared as real on social media; details inside
content: New Delhi, November 4 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Three videos allegedly showing white couples expressing disappointment over the birth of their babies, whose skin colour appeared different from theirs, were recently shared on social media with the claim that they depicted real incidents. The clips, showing three separate instances, featured mothers lying on hospital beds holding their newborns, while the fathers appeared to question the babies' skin colour. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the visuals and found that they were AI-generated and not related to any real-life events. Claim An X user named Mariyam_MBD (@Mariyam_MBD) on November 2 shared a video allegedly capturing two separate instances of white couples giving birth to dark-skinned babies. The clips, seemingly recorded in hospital rooms, showed the parents appearing visibly shocked. In both instances, the mothers were seen holding the babies, while the fathers appeared to be questioning the babies' skin colour. While further investigating the claim, the Desk also came across another similar video of a white couple giving birth to a dark-skinned baby, shared by a Facebook page named RNT Communication on November 2. A YouTube channel named Aaj Ki Khabar News also published a video allegedly covering the same incident; however, it did not use visuals from the viral post. Links to these posts can be found here , here and here along with their archived versions viewed here , here and here . Investigation The Desk began the investigation by carefully separating the two instances in the video using an online tool called Online Video Cutter. Visual 1: With the first extracted clip, the Desk ran it through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Using one of these keyframes in Google Lens, the Desk came across a video shared on the YouTube channel Braided Entertainment. The Desk found that the video on the YouTube channel matched the visuals from the viral post exactly. However, after careful analysis, it was found that the video contained multiple lip-sync discrepancies, indicating manipulation. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image confirming that the visuals from the viral social media post and the YouTube channel's video are identical. Next, based on the observations above, the Desk ran the video through Hive Moderation, an AI detection tool. The analysis showed that 99% of the video is likely to contain AI-generated or deepfake content. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the visuals depicting the first instance of a white couple seemingly expressing disappointment over the birth of their baby with dark skin were AI-generated. Visual 2: Next, the Desk began investigating the second visual. The Desk ran the video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across a video shared by the same YouTube channel, Braided Entertainment. The video, shared on October 31, matched the visuals from the viral post. However, a detailed review of the footage found multiple discrepancies, including unnatural lip-syncing by the individual who appears to be the father. Here is the link and archive link to the video, along with a screenshot. The image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral social media clip and the YouTube channel's video. In the subsequent part of the investigation, to verify whether the said video was AI-generated as suspected, the Desk ran it through Hive Moderation, an AI detection tool. The analysis showed that 99% of the video is likely to contain AI-generated or deepfake content. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the visuals depicting the second instance of a white couple seemingly expressing disappointment over the birth of their baby with dark skin were AI-generated. Visual 3: The Desk began investigating the video shared by a Facebook page named RNT Communication. It ran the video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk once again came across the aforementioned YouTube channel, Braided Entertainment, which had shared the same video on October 30. The visuals from the YouTube video were identical to those seen in the viral post. However, a detailed analysis of the video revealed multiple discrepancies, including unnatural lip-syncing by the individual appearing to be the father, suggesting manipulation. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a comparison image highlighting the visual similarities between the viral social media clip and the video shared by the YouTube channel. As part of the investigation, to verify whether the said video was AI-generated as suspected, the Desk ran it through Hive Moderation, an AI detection tool. The analysis showed that 99% of the video is likely to contain AI-generated or deepfake content. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the visuals depicting the third instance of a white couple seemingly expressing disappointment over the birth of their baby with dark skin were AI-generated and not from a real incident.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: This photo of Harmanpreet Kaur with World Cup trophy is AI-generated; details inside
content: New Delhi, November 4 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A picture showing Indian women's cricket captain Harmanpreet Kaur asleep while holding the World Cup trophy is circulating on social media, claiming that it captures her celebration after India's 2025 World Cup win. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk reviewed the claim and found that the photo is not real. It appears to be AI-generated and does not match any verified visuals from the tournament or the captain's official posts. Claim: A photo featuring the Indian Women's Team Cricket captain Harmanpreet Kaur holding the trophy while asleep, was shared by an X user 'Aryan' on November 3, claiming that it depicted the celebration post the 2025 World win.
