"𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗗𝗥𝗘𝗔𝗠 𝗛𝗔𝗦 𝗖𝗢𝗠𝗘 𝗔𝗟𝗜𝗩𝗘! From dreams to reality — India are World Champions!" read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the picture through Reverse Image Search and found that several other users had shared the same photo with a similar claim on social media. One such post can be found here . Further, the Desk also conducted a customised keyword search to find reports that extensively covered the pictures from the World Finals. But our investigation did not lead to this particular picture being used by media outlets. Moreover, the Indian Women's Team skipper did share a picture of the trophy on her official Instagram account, but it was different from the one being shared on social media. Here is the link to the image, and below is a screenshot. On close analysis of the picture in the X post, we found several inconsistencies; for instance, the face appears smooth yet very textured. Moreover, the trophy differs from the real one. All this suggested that the picture might be manipulated. Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the picture through Hive-Moderation, an AI-detection tool, which flagged it as AI-generated. Below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the picture showing Harmanpreet Kaur with the trophy is AI-generated.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered video shared to falsely claim 'President Murmu stated PM Modi forced her to sit in Rafale jet'; details inside
content: New Delhi, November 4 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of President Droupadi Murmu delivering a speech is being widely shared on social media with the claim that she accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the Union government of pressuring her to board a Rafale aircraft for publicity. The clip circulating online carries text alleging that if anything happened to her during the Rafale sortie, PM Modi and his "Hindutva government" would be responsible. However, the PTI Fact Check reviewed the video and found the claim to be false. The footage is from the President's address at the 10th International Women's Conference in February 2025, months before her Rafale flight in October 2025. She made no such remarks during the event. The viral clip is digitally manipulated. President Droupadi Murmu, on October 29, flew in the two-seater Rafale fighter jet of the Indian Air Force (IAF) and called the experience "unforgettable". She is the first President of India to fly in two different fighter jets of the IAF. In 2023, she flew in another twin-seater, Sukhoi-30MKI. Claim: A Facebook user shared a video featuring President Droupadi Murmu delivering a speech titled 'Raj Kumar' on November 1, claiming that she blamed PM Modi for using her as a prop to elevate Rafale PR. "Draupadi Murmu makes a major revelation about the BJP. Draupadi went to board the Rafale plane, threatened by the Hindutva government today. If anything happens to me in the Rafale plane, Modi and his Hindutva government will be responsible," read the text on the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across the extended version of the social media video shared on the official YouTube channel of India Today on February 14, 2025. She was addressing the 10th International Women's Conference: President Droupadi Murmu Inaugurates The Conference. This clarifies that the event took place in February 2025, while President Murmu's Rafale sortie occurred in October 2025, months apart, making it unlikely that her remarks were related to the flight. Upon analysing the entire video, we found no such statement made by the President, confirming that the viral clip has been digitally manipulated. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot. The background and the attire that the President was wearing were similar to those seen in the social media post. Below is a combination image highlighting the same. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk ran the video through Resemble AI, an AI-detection tool, which found that the audio is real but might be an impersonation. Below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video claiming that Prime Minister Modi and the government blackmailed President Murmu to sit in the Rafale jet is manipulated and AI-generated.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video of car made of bricks falsely shared as real footage from India
content: New Delhi, November 4 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently shared on social media claimed to show a car whose entire body was made of bricks. The clip allegedly showed a man waiting inside the brick structure of a vehicle at a traffic signal in India, while several passersby stopped to record the unusual sight. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it to be AI-generated and falsely shared as a real incident. Claim On November 3, an X user named Arzoo Alam (@ArzooAl34714966) shared a purported video of a car whose entire body was made of bricks. The footage allegedly showed a car halting at a traffic signal in India, with a man inside. It also appeared to show several passersby recording the unusual sight of the vehicle. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video garnered 6,923 views) Investigation The Desk ran the social media video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple handles sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here ; their archived versions are available here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analyzed the video and noticed a watermark reading "Atrang Vision" displayed on it. Using this as a lead, the Desk conducted a customised Google search and found an Instagram page with the same name, 'Atrang Vision.' Upon scanning the handle, the Desk found the same video of the brick-structured car (similar to that of the viral post) shared on October 26, 2025. However, the post's description mentioned that the video was AI-generated. Here is the link and archive link to the video, along with a screenshot: A comparison image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral social media clip and the video shared by the Instagram page. In the subsequent part of the investigation, drawing on the above findings, the Desk ran the viral video through the AI detection tool Hive Moderation, which confirmed that 99.8% of the footage contained AI-generated or deepfake elements. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a car whose body was made of bricks was AI-generated and falsely shared on social media as a real incident to mislead viewers.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Scripted crime drama falsely shared claiming it showed 'shooting of woman cop in Raebareli'; details inside
content: New Delhi, November 6 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently shared on social media claimed to show a horrific incident from Uttar Pradesh's Raebareli, where a woman police official was allegedly shot dead in broad daylight. The video appeared to show gunshots being fired at the officer, while panicked passersby were seen running for safety. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it to be unrelated to any real incident—it was part of a serial shoot and was falsely shared on social media to mislead viewers. Claim An X user named Manendra Kumar Yadav (@ManendraKumarY9) on November 2 shared a video purportedly showing a woman police official from Raebareli, Uttar Pradesh, being shot dead in broad daylight. The footage allegedly showed gunshots being fired at the officer while passersby ran helter-skelter to save their lives. "A woman police official was shot dead in Raebareli," the user wrote. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing, the video had garnered 6,923 views.) Investigation The Desk ran the social media video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found multiple handles sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a video shared by an Instagram user named Ajay Gupta, who identified himself as a reel creator. On October 30, he had shared the same video of a woman police officer being shot, identical to the one circulating on social media. However, upon careful analysis of the post's caption, the Desk found that the user clarified it was not real footage but a scene from a serial shoot. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. A comparison image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral social media clip and the video shared by the Instagram user. Additionally, the search result led the Desk to a video uploaded by the popular YouTube channel Nova Crime Thrillers, known for sharing dramatised crime stories. The video, posted on September 23, 2025, featured the same scene of the woman police officer being shot, visible at the 4:09 timestamp. This confirmed that the viral clip was taken from a scripted crime show and not a real incident. Here is the link to the video. In the subsequent part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google search to determine whether Raebareli Police had issued any clarification regarding the viral video. The search led to a post shared by the official X handle of Raebareli Police on November 2, where it refuted the claim and confirmed that the video was not related to any real incident. The police further clarified that the visuals were from a film or TV series shoot. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video claiming to show a woman police officer being shot dead in Uttar Pradesh's Raebareli was not real. The visuals were taken from a scripted crime show and falsely shared on social media as an actual incident to mislead viewers.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Amid rising pollution in Delhi-NCR, old Beijing smog photos falsely shared as images from India
content: New Delhi, November 6 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A set of four hazy skyline photos is circulating on social media, with users claiming the images show worsening air pollution across Noida and Faridabad. One widely shared post alleges that friends sent the pictures in Delhi-NCR and suggests that authorities are manipulating AQI data to downplay the crisis. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk reviewed all four images and traced them to news reports published between 2013 and 2021 documenting severe smog in Beijing, China. None of the photographs shows the current pollution situation in Delhi-NCR. They have been repurposed online and shared with a misleading claim. Claim: A set of four pictures depicting thick smog was shared by an X user '@Tyagi__Ishan' on November 4, claiming that it showed the current pollution situation in Noida and Faridabad, part of Delhi-NCR. "Pollution is getting worse every day in the NCR region. My friends from Noida and Faridabad sent me these images from their homes and offices today. Look at air pollution, and the government is manipulating the data of AQI," read the post's caption. The post clocked 280k views on social media. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation To commence the investigation, the Desk categorically checked the four pictures and debunked the claim. Picture 1: The Desk ran this picture through Reverse Image Search and found a Guardian report published on September 15, 2015, that carried the same picture as seen in the social media post. The report mentioned that buildings in Beijing were blanketed in heavy smog in January 2014, when the municipal government issued a yellow smog alert, with air quality readings reaching the most polluted level. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. The Desk also came across a National Geographic report published on January 24, 2014, featuring the same picture as seen in the social media post. It is mentioned that China has some of the dirtiest air in the world. Still, a large share of the country's pollutants is generated during the manufacture of goods destined for countries like the United States, according to a new study. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Picture 2: The Desk ran this picture through Reverse Image Search and found a Hindustan Times report published on November 5, 2021, whose cover image is similar to the one in the social media post. The report mentioned that a cold wave arriving from Siberia over the weekend is expected to disperse the pollution. In the picture, Buildings are seen in Beijing's central business district on a polluted day, November 5, 2021. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Picture 3: On running the picture through Reverse Image Search, the Desk found the picture carried by The Guardian in its report published on December 10, 2013, highlighting that China's noxious air pollution has made people smarter, funnier and impervious to missile attacks, the country's official media reported this week, as a toxic cloud covering half of the government began to lift. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Picture 4: As part of the investigation, the Desk ran the picture through a reverse image search and found that it had been used in a BBC report published on May 4, 2017. The text, along with the picture, mentioned Beijing's skyline could barely be made out amid the dust. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the information was taken in China between 2013 and 2021, and was falsely shared as current pollution concerns in Delhi-NCR.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Claim in social media post that Smriti Mandhana took fewer ODI innings than Virat Kohli to score 5,000 runs in international cricket is TRUE
content: New Delhi, November 6 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media post claims that India batter A social media post claims that Indian woman cricketer Smriti Mandhana has become the youngest and fastest player to reach 5,000 runs in Women's ODIs, surpassing men's cricket star Virat Kohli's record in terms of speed to the milestone. The claim followed India's ICC Women's Champions Trophy match against South Africa, after which several users shared congratulatory posts along with comparative graphics highlighting Mandhana's achievement. The posts state that Mandhana reached 5,000 ODI runs in 112 innings, while Kohli took 114 innings to get the 5,000-run mark in men's ODIs. PTI Fact Check verified the claim by reviewing official match data published by the International Cricket Council (ICC), the players' past ODI career summaries, and recent BCCI acknowledgements. The records confirm that Mandhana indeed completed 5,000 ODI runs in 112 innings, becoming the fastest to do so in women's cricket and, in terms of innings taken, faster than Virat Kohli's 114-innings milestone in men's ODIs. Claim: An Instagram user 'iasworldofficial' on October 13, claiming that Mandhana has become the youngest and fastest to 5,000 ODI runs, and in doing so has overtaken Kohli's Indian record for speed to that mark. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the picture through Reverse Image Search and found that several other users had shared the same picture with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here . To verify the claim, the Desk first conducted a customised keyword search and found a report by The Economic Express dated October 12, 2025, which mentioned that Mandhana reached the 5,000 runs mark in Women's ODIs during a match against Australia. The 29-year-old batter achieved the feat in just her 112th match during India's World Cup 2025 encounter against Australia in Visakhapatnam, surpassing legends of the game with her trademark elegance and consistency at the crease. Here is the link to the report. Furthermore, we also came across an X post by BCCI dated October 12, 2025, highlighting that Smriti Mandhana is the youngest and fastest to reach 5,000 runs in Women's ODIs. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Moreover, match write-ups and video highlights note Mandhana brought up 5,000 and called it the youngest/fastest to the mark in women's ODIs. Here is the link to the ICC tournament highlighting Mandhana's 5000 ODI runs, and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk, as part of the investigation, accessed the ESPN report records pages list, which lists Mandhana at 5,022 (after the innings), and confirmed she reached the milestone in 112 innings. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. To verify whether she surpassed Virat Kohli's mark, we conducted another set of customised keyword searches on Google and came across a Money Control report published on October 13, 2025. It stated that Mandhana achieved the milestone in 112 innings, which is the fastest by any Indian. She overtook Virat Kohli in the process, who had completed the same in 114 innings. In the overall list comprising both men and women, Mandhana is only behind Pakistan's premier batter Babar Azam, who took 97 innings, and South Africa great Hashim Amla, who took 101 innings to reach the milestone. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Moreover, another report by NTDV Sports was published on November 21, 2013, stating that Virat Kohli reached 5,000 ODI runs in 114 innings (he equalled Viv Richards' pace at the time). "Virat Kohli, with his feat of reaching 5,000 runs in 114 innings, has equalled Vivian Richards' record. Both now share a record for managing 5000 runs in the least number of innings," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Below is a comparison table with the key numbers for both players and their records. ( Smriti Mandhana Notes ; Virat Kohli Notes ) However, it is important to note that the comparison is speed to milestone, not total career runs. Mandhana has not scored more total ODI runs than Kohli. The "youngest" label applies in the women's category. Some headlines said "fastest in ODIs" (any gender)- technically, the fastest to 5,000 ODI runs among men is Babar Azam (97 innings) in the men's list. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Mandhana's achievement of reaching 5,000 WODI runs in 112 innings is true. She has therefore become the fastest Indian (men's or women's) to get the 5,000-run milestone in ODI innings, overtaking Kohli's 114 innings.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Social media post claiming Brazilian hairstylist mocked Rahul Gandhi as 'failed politician' is false; details inside
content: New Delhi, November 10 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media post featuring a video of a foreign woman recording herself has gone viral with the claim that she is Brazilian hairstylist Larissa Nery, who allegedly mocked senior Congress leader Rahul Gandhi by calling him a "failed politician." Users who shared the video suggested that Nery had criticised Gandhi after he purportedly used her old photograph in his recent press conference on his alleged 'vote-theft' claims. However, the PTI Fact Check examined the viral video using digital verification tools and found that Larissa Nery acknowledged that her photograph was used in India but made no remarks about Rahul Gandhi or Indian politics in her video. The findings confirm that the viral claim attributing the "failed politician" remark to Nery is based on a false translation of her original Portuguese video. Notably, a day before the first phase of polling in Bihar, Rahul Gandhi, in a press conference, alleged mass rigging in the 2024 Haryana elections. From 25 lakh fake votes to a Brazilian model's photo on 22 voter ID cards – the Congress MP made huge allegations against the Election Commission in the press conference. Claim: A video featuring a foreign woman recording a video was shared by an X user 'Citizen MattersX' on November 6, claiming that she was Brazilian hairstylist Larissa Nery, who mocked senior Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, calling him a "failed politician". "There's this failed politician who lost nearly 100 elections in India, using my old pics to amplify his lies and propaganda against the ruling party. His party members are so obsessed with me and proposing to me in DMs. Yuckk." ~Brazilian model whose pic RaGa used for #FakeNarrative," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . To verify the claim, the Desk conducted a customised Google search for relevant media reports. It came across a report by The Print published on November 6, which mentioned that Nery had posted an Instagram story for her, with around 5,400 followers, expressing shock that her image was being used for voting in India. "They had used my picture as if I were Indian to scam voters. Can you believe it? What kind of madness are we living in?" Nery says in Portuguese in one of several clips she has since posted about the controversy. In another story, she shared a clip from Gandhi's press conference with the caption in Portuguese: "Guys, how crazy — I'm famous in India as the 'mysterious Brazilian model'," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Our search also led us to another report published by NTDV on November 6, which stated that Larissa Nery clarified that the photograph Gandhi shared during a press conference yesterday was taken years ago, when she was about 20 years old. "In her latest Instagram status, she has posed, "Wow, that's crazy! I'm Famous in India as the 'mysterious Brazilian Model'!"," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Another report by India Today, published on November 6, stated that Larissa revealed that Indian journalists had been trying to reach her for comments on the use of her image. "A bunch of Indian journalists are looking for me, wanting interviews. I've responded, saying that I'm the so-called 'mysterious Brazilian model' — but I'm not even a model," she emphasised," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report. Taking the investigation forward, the Desk carefully analysed the video shared on social media, in which she spoke Portuguese, and ran it through a transcription tool (Turboscribe). Below is a transcription of the video along with the screenshot. "(0:09) It's an old picture, okay? (0:10) I was young in the picture; I was about 18 or 20. (0:13) I'm using a picture of me to do... (0:16) I don't know if it's an election, (0:18) something you have to vote for. (0:21) And... (0:22) In India! (0:24) They're putting me as an Indian (0:26) to hit others, everyone, look how crazy! (0:28) How crazy is this? What world am I living in? (0:31) Then a reporter called me (0:33) wanting to know about this train, (0:35) called my office, my job, (0:37) wanting to talk to me for an interview, (0:39) then I didn't answer, (0:40) I told Tata not to give me my number and such, (0:42) the guy found my Instagram, called me on Instagram, (0:45) now another person who has nothing to do with the subject, (0:47) a friend of mine from another city, (0:50) sends me a picture, (0:51) I'll put it here for you, (0:52) down here for you to see, here. (0:54) You won't believe it. (0:56) Guys…," read the transcription. Therefore, it is clear that neither the reports nor the transcriptions include any insult to Rahul Gandhi. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video featuring the 'Brazilian Model' calling Rahul Gandhi a "failed politician" is a false translation. The original Portuguese video posted by Larissa Nery contains no such remarks about Rahul Gandhi or Indian politics.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Clipped video falsely claims gangster-turned-politician Surajbhan Singh called Bhumihars 'mad'; details inside
content: New Delhi, November 10 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A fierce political contest is unfolding in Bihar's Mokama, where two heavyweight families from the Bhumihar community are pulling the region in opposite directions. On one side is Anant Kumar Singh, better known locally as Chhote Sarkar- the JDU's star contender. On the other hand is RJD nominee Veena Devi, backed by her husband and influential leader Surajbhan Singh. Amidst this, a video interview of RJD leader Surajbhan Singh circulated on social media platforms, claiming he called members of the Bhumihar community "mad." However, the PTI Fact Check Desk reviewed the full interview on Ajit Anjum's YouTube channel and found a very different picture. Anjum asks a pointed question about tensions in Mokama and whether Bhumihars were involved. Singh replies by repeating the question in an interrogative way-"Bhumihars are mad?", and then goes on to explain the incident, criticise the way a small group's actions were portrayed as community-wide, and explicitly calls Bhumihars an "intelligent caste." Therefore, it is clear that he used the word 'mad' in an interrogative tone while responding to a question, not as a derogatory remark on the community. Claim: A video of an interview featuring Surajbhan Singh with journalist Ajit Anjum was shared by an X user '@iAnkurSingh' on November 4, claiming that he called the people of the Bhumihar community "mad". The RJD leader says, "Bhumihar pagal hai" "Bhumihar Pagal Hai -Surajbhan Singh. Just because Surajbhan went to RJD, now he has started abusing Bhumihars," read the post's caption. The post clocked 73.3k views on social media. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across the original interview on Ajit Anjum's official YouTube Channel, streamed on November 4. "46'Even if 100 Lalan Singhs come...', Surajbhan Singh's challenge to Lalan Singh || Ajit Anjum," read the title of the video. On listening to the entire interview, at the 30:30-minute mark, Ajit Anjum questions What is happening with Bhumihars? People are saying Bhumihars are going there (towards Anant Singh). To which the RJD leader, indirectly referring to the alleged clash between Anant Singh's convoy and Jan Suraaj's Piyush Priyadarshi group during the election campaign that led to the death of Dularchand Yadav, said: "Bhumihars are mad? 2-5 boys threw stones and came there as if to create casteism. An atmosphere was created to spoil the environment. This is something to note: why did the Election Commission take such significant action? Why were shots fired? Why was a vehicle run over? You keep saying 'Bhumihar' over small matters. Bhumihar is an intelligent caste." Ajit Anjum further questions, "How many Bhumihars are there in Mokama Vidhan Sabha? Surajbhan Singh says, "Whatever Bhumihars are there in Mokama Vidhan Sabha, this is an intelligent caste." Here is the link to the interview, and below is a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video clip and Surajbhan Singh repeatedly called the Bhumihar community 'intelligent'. The word 'mad' was used in an interrogative tone, not as a derogatory remark against the community.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2022 video of Chirag Paswan's protest reshared to falsely claim he was arrested recently; details inside
content: New Delhi, November 10 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Following the conclusion of the first phase of the Bihar Assembly Elections, a video showing Union Minister and Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) chief Chirag Paswan sitting inside a police jeep is being shared online with the claim that he was recently arrested for vote theft ahead of the Bihar Assembly elections. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk examined the video and found it to be old and unrelated to the ongoing Bihar elections. It shows Chirag Paswan's 2022 protest detention, not a recent arrest over "vote theft." It is irrelevant to the recent Bihar Assembly Elections. The 2025 Bihar Assembly Elections will be held in two phases for 243 seats. Voting took place in the first phase on November 6 for 121 seats, and in the second phase on November 11 for 122 seats. Vote counting will take place on November 14. Claim: A video featuring Union Minister and Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) President Chirag Paswan sitting in a police jeep was shared by an Instagram user 'ahiran_santu_1k' on November 6, claiming that he was arrested for 'vote theft'. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . To verify the claim, the Desk conducted a customised Google search for reports on Paswan's arrest, but the search did not yield any credible news articles. However, given Chirag Paswan's prominence, such news would have been covered by several media outlets. Taking the investigation forward, the Desk then ran the extracted keyframes through a Reverse Image Search and found a video report by Bihar Tak dated February 15, 2022, showing Chirag Paswan being taken away in a police vehicle as a crowd followed the jeep. According to the report, he was detained during a protest march against the policies of Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar. The report's timeline clarifies that it is not recent and is unrelated to the 2025 Bihar Assembly Elections. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. The same video was covered by Prabhat Khabar, which uploaded it to its official YouTube channel on February 15, 2025. According to the report, Paswan, along with hundreds of his supporters, was marching to the Raj Bhavan to demand the dismissal of the government led by Chief Minister Nitish Kumar. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. The Desk also conducted another set of customised keyword searches. It came across a report by India Today published on February 15, 2022, highlighting that the Lok Janshakti Party leader Chirag Paswan was arrested after police lathi-charged party workers who were holding a protest march in Patna to highlight the issue of unemployment in Bihar. The protest march began from the JP roundabout near Gandhi Maidan and was headed towards Raj Bhavan in Patna. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video is old and unrelated to the ongoing Bihar elections. It shows Chirag Paswan's 2022 protest detention, not a recent arrest over "vote theft."

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Fake notice shared to falsely claim 'Uttarakhand University asked students to join PM event for 50 marks'; details inside
content: New Delhi, November 10 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media post claiming that Dev Bhoomi Uttarakhand University directed select students to attend Prime Minister Narendra Modi's November 9 event at the Forest Research Institute in Dehradun, allegedly offering 50 internal marks in return, was shared by several social media users. The users asserted that the university had made participation mandatory for second-year BTech CSE specialisation and BCA students in the Indian Knowledge System course. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk examined the viral circular, checked the university's official communication channels, and reviewed similar posts shared by social media users to verify whether the notice was genuine. Our search also revealed that this notice is doctored; the university issued no such circular. Claim: A user shared a circular allegedly issued by Dev Bhoomi Uttarakhand University, 'Prashant Bhushan', on November 8, claiming that the university had directed a section of its students to participate in the Prime Minister's rally, promising them 50 internal marks in return. "All B. Tech CSE and Specialisation (2nd Year) and BCA (2nd Year) students are hereby informed that they must attend the upcoming event at FRI on Sunday, 9th November 2025, where they will interact with the Hon'ble Prime Minister of India.Attendance at this event will be counted toward the Bharatiya Gyan Parampara (Indian Knowledge System) course, and 50 internal marks will be awarded to each participant. Hence, participation in this event is mandatory for all programs having the Indian Knowledge System course," read the circular. The post clocked 607k views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral post through a Reverse Image Search and found that several other users had also shared it with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here . On close analysis of the circular, the Desk found several discrepancies; for instance, it did not include a date of issue, a common practice for university circulars. Further, the absence of an official signature, stamp, or seal firmly suggests it is fake. As part of the investigation, the Desk accessed the circulars on the official website of Dev Bhoomi Uttarakhand University and found a Diwali Holiday notice issued on September 22, which, unlike the viral circular, included all the necessary official seals and dates. Below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combined image highlighting the differences between the Diwali Holiday circular and the notice recently shared on social media platforms. Further, we checked the university's social media accounts and found that the official Facebook page of Dev Bhoomi Uttarakhand University publicly denounced the notice on November 8. "It has come to our attention that a fake notice has been circulated in the name of DBUU regarding marks for the upcoming visit to FRI on 09 November 2025. We would like to clarify that the notice is completely false and was neither issued nor approved by the University. It does not bear any official signature, reference number, or authorisation. Please rely only on official DBUU communication channels for accurate information." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. The Desk also reached out to the university for an official statement, and the story will be updated as and when we receive a response. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the notice in question is doctored; the university issued no such circular.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old Beirut smoke photo falsely shared as image of recent blast near Delhi's Red Fort
content: New Delhi, November 11 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A dramatic image showing thick black smoke rising into the sky was shared by several social media users, claiming that it captures the aftermath of an explosion near Gate No. 1 of the Red Fort (Lal Qila) Metro Station in Delhi. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the image in question is actually related to the Israel-Lebanon tensions and has been available on the internet since 2024. It is unrelated to the Delhi or the recent blast in the national capital. Meanwhile, Union Home Minister Amit Shah will chair a high-level security review meeting on Tuesday following the blast near the Red Fort here that left nine people dead, sources said. Claim: An X user, '@Laraib_Fatiima' on November 10, shared a picture depicting thick black smoke billowing in the sky, claiming it to be from the recent explosion in Delhi. "BREAKING NEWS. There are reports of a powerful explosion in New Delhi, India. The blast occurred near Gate No. 1 of the Red Fort (Lal Qila) Metro Station, in the crowded and high-security Chandni Chowk area. Investigations are ongoing. Initial reports suggest the cause might have been a gas cylinder leak or a vehicle battery malfunction, but authorities are not ruling out a terrorism angle — especially since a few days ago, an interstate terror module was busted in Haryana with 2,900 kg of explosives. No group has claimed responsibility so far," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the picture through Reverse Image Search and found that another user had also shared the same picture with a similar claim on social media. One such post can be found here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a report by the Australian Broadcasting Corporation published on September 27, 2024, carrying the same picture as seen in the social media post. According to the report, it is actually related to Israel-Lebanon tensions. "Massive explosions could be heard across Lebanon's capital about 6:20pm local time (1:20am Saturday AEST). Large plumes of smoke were also visible. Previous IDF strikes in Beirut have been attempts to kill the leadership of the Hezbollah militant group," read a section of the report. Moreover, the caption accompanying the picture mentioned, "Smoke billows over Beirut's southern suburbs. (Reuters: /Mohamed Azakir)". The timeline and the caption clarify that the picture is not recent and definitely not from Delhi. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find other relevant report, and came across a report by Daily Mail published on September 28, 2024. The report carrying the picture mentioned that smoke billows over Beirut's southern suburbs overnight. The headline of the report read: "Iran may hit back at British and US targets in Middle East after Israel killing of Hezbollah chief - as region risks being plunged into wider war, experts warn" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Moreover, a blast occurred in a car near Red Fort here on Monday (November 10) evening, prompting authorities to rush five fire tenders to the spot, an official said. At least nine people lost their lives, while several were reported injured and gutting several vehicles. Here is the link to an X post by PTI and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the picture being shared on social media is actually related to Israel-Lebanon tensions and has been available since 2024.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video shared to falsely claim 'UP CM threatened Bihar voters after Delhi blast'; details inside
content: New Delhi, November 11 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Following the blast near Delhi Red Fort, a video of Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath delivering a fiery speech is circulating widely on social media, with claims that he 'warned Bihar voters that what happened in Delhi would happen in Bihar if they did not support the BJP in the upcoming Assembly elections'. The clip also appears to show him invoking the recent explosion near the Red Fort on November 10, which left several injured and triggered a high-level security response in the capital. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated and found the claim to be false. The viral footage is an older speech from Siwan, Bihar, and has been digitally manipulated. At no point did the Chief Minister reference the Red Fort blast or issue such threats. A powerful explosion ripped through a slow-moving car at a traffic signal near the Red Fort Metro station around 6.52 pm on Monday, killing 12 people and injuring several others. Police and paramilitary personnel have been deployed across key public areas as investigations continue. Claim: A Facebook user, 'Mohammed Ahsan,' on November 11, shared a video featuring UP CM Yogi Adityanath addressing a gathering, claiming that he threatened the people of Bihar that 'what happened in Delhi would happen in Bihar', as a consequence of voting against the BJP in the elections. "I warn the people of Bihar. What happened in Delhi could happen in Bihar. We didn't launch the Trishul so our soldiers could show off their skills. We want to build a Hindu nation. For this Hindu nation, whether it is 8 or 800 lives that must be sacrificed, we will do it," says Yogi Adityanath in the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation To verify the claim, the Desk first conducted a customised Google search for relevant media reports that mentioned Yogi Adityanath threatening the people of Bihar. However, the Desk did not find any such report, and given the seriousness of the matter, such a statement would have been reported by leading media outlets. Next, the Desk also noticed that his speech was delivered during the day, while the blast near Delhi's Red Fort occurred at around 6:52 pm. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk ran the video through the Invid tool to extract keyframes, then ran them through Reverse Image Search and found the extended version of the same video uploaded to The Print's official YouTube channel on October 31, 2025. He was addressing a public meeting in Siwan, Bihar. Upon listening to the entire speech, we found that he did not mention the Delhi blast at any point. Moreover, the video's timeline clarifies that it is not recent and is unrelated to the Delhi blast. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Upon analysing the video, we found several discrepancies, suggesting it might be manipulated —for instance, unnatural speech patterns and speech and lip movements that were not in sync. Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the video through Hive-Moderation, an AI-detection tool. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video is AI-manipulated and is being shared with a false claim on social media.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Doctored video shared to falsely claim CDS Anil Chauhan 'criticised PM for politicising army'; details inside
content: New Delhi, November 11 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of Chief of Defence Staff General Anil Chauhan was circulated by several social media users, alleging he attacked Prime Minister Narendra Modi and accused the government of treating the Indian Army as a partisan tool. Adding that the remarks were made in connection with the Bihar elections. PTI Fact Check reviewed the footage and traced it to General Chauhan's address at the Military Literature Festival in Chandigarh on November 9. The full speech carries no such comments. The viral version shows tell-tale signs of manipulation, including mismatched lip movement and irregular audio. A voice analysis tool also flagged the audio as potentially impersonated. The claim that the CDS made political remarks targeting the Prime Minister and the Army is fabricated. Claim A video featuring Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) General Anil Chauhan addressing a gathering was shared by an X user 'Zaryyabali' on November 10, claiming that he allegedly said that since PM Modi came into power, he always considered the Indian army as the concubine of his political party. "Indian CDS Anil Chohan slams central government, "A professional army always fights for their country, but ever since PM Modi came into power, he has always considered the Indian army as the concubine of his political party, this is exactly why we opposed the saffronization of the Indian army," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . As part of the investigation, the Desk first conducted a customised keyword search to find reports that carried CDS Anil Chauhan's statement. Still, we did not find any credible reports that mentioned such a remark by the CDS. Given the seriousness of the statement, it would have been carried by all leading news portals. Taking a cue from this, the Desk then ran the extracted keyframes through Reverse Image Search and found the original video live-streamed on the official YouTube channel of The Indian Express on November 9, 2025. He was addressing the 9th edition of the Military Literature Festival in Chandigarh. The event highlights India's defence heritage, strategic insights, and the role of the armed forces in shaping national security. Upon listening to the entire speech, we found that he did not make any such statement at any point. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. On careful analysis of the video, the Desk found several discrepancies suggesting it might be manipulated, for instance, unnatural speech patterns and speech and lip movements that were not in sync. Taking a cue from this, the Desk extracted the audio and ran it through Resemble AI, which detected that 'although the voice is real, it may be an impersonation' Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video featuring Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) General Anil Chauhan making political remarks about the Prime Minister of India and the Indian Army, linking it to the Bihar elections, is manipulated.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyus Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video shared to falsely claim 'Khesari Lal Yadav's house was demolished in Mumbai'; details inside
content: New Delhi, November 12 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyus Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of a bulldozer tearing down a building is circulating on social media, with users alleging that Bhojpuri actor and RJD candidate Khesari Lal Yadav's house was demolished for illegal construction after he joined the party. The clip has been shared by multiple accounts, framing the supposed action as political targeting. However, the PTI Fact Check reviewed the footage and found key visual inconsistencies. No credible news report indicates that Yadav's home was razed. Instead, a recent NDTV report shows that the Mira Road Municipal Corporation issued only a notice regarding alleged illegal construction. An AI-detection analysis flagged the viral clip as AI-generated. The video was shared with a false claim on social media. Claim: A video showing a bulldozer running down a building was shared by a Facebook user 'यदुवंशी लालू' on November 10, claiming that Bhojpuri actor Khesari Lal Yadav's house was demolished. "Khesari Lal Yadav's house has been demolished. Wasn't it illegal until Khesari was in the RJD? It became illegal as soon as he joined the RJD. All Yadavs still need to understand that being a Yadav is the biggest crime in the BJP government," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . To verify the claim, the Desk first conducted a customised keyword search on Google to relevant media reports stating Khesari Lal Yadav's house was being bulldozed. The Desk did not find any such report stating such an occurrence. However, during our search, we found a report by NDTV that the Municipal Corporation had issued a notice to Khesari Lal Yadav for illegal construction at his Mira Road bungalow. The Municipal Corporation had asked Khesari Lal Yadav to remove the unlawful structure from his home in Mira Road. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the notice. Upon careful analysis of the video, the Desk found several inconsistencies that suggested it might be AI-generated. Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the footage through HiveModeration, an AI-detection tool, which flagged it as AI-generated. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing Khesari Lal Yadav's house being demolished is AI-generated and that no such incident occurred.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video falsely linked to Tamil Nadu claims patient falling from moving ambulance
content: New Delhi, November 14 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing an ambulance speeding down a road as a stretcher carrying a patient rolls out onto the street has gone viral on social media, with claims that the incident took place in Coonoor, Tamil Nadu. The clip was widely shared, with users describing it as an example of medical negligence and alleging that the driver continued driving unaware of the mishap. However, a fact check by PTI found the claim to be false. The video is neither from Tamil Nadu nor real. It is an AI-generated creation originating from Puerto Rico, first shared by a digital creator known for posting AI-powered parody videos. Further analysis using AI-detection tools, including Hive Moderation and WasItAi, confirmed that the visuals were generated using artificial intelligence. Claim: A video showing an ambulance door opening mid-way was shared by an X user, @TheAsifReyaz, on November 11, claiming that a patient fell onto the road along with the stretcher in Coonoor, Tamil Nadu. "A shocking incident emerged from Coonoor, Tamil Nadu, an ambulance door opened in motion, and a patient fell onto the road along with the stretcher. The driver had no idea and kept driving ahead. A vehicle meant to save lives ended up becoming a stark symbol of negligence!" read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On reviewing the video carefully, the Desk found a signboard displaying names of places such as "Toa Baja", which is located in Puerto Rico, not India. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Moreover, the Desk noticed a watermark 'AI Criolla' on the video. A search led to an Instagram post from digital creator Nebulo Ivan Vélez, dated November 3, 2025. The caption, written in Spanish, humorously described the scene as an ambulance incident in Puerto Rico. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot. The user's bio also mentioned that the page produces "AI-powered parodies". Below is a screenshot of the same. Taking the investigation forward, the Desk ran the video through Hive Moderation, an AI-detection tool. Below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk also ran the screengrab through WasItAi, an AI-detection tool, which stated that the image is AI-generated. Below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video being shared on social media in the name of Tamil Nadu is an AI-generated video from Puerto Rico.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old photo of car fire from Ambedkar Nagar falsely shared as scene from Nov 10 Delhi blast
content: New Delhi, November 14 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A collage of two images showing a burning car was widely circulated on social media, with users claiming it depicted visuals from the November 10 explosion near Red Fort in Delhi. However, a PTI fact-check found that the images are unrelated to the November 10 event. The pictures are from an older incident in Ambedkar Nagar, Delhi, that took place on April 3, when a moving car caught fire on the Khanpur–Chirag Delhi road. No connection exists between the viral photo and the recent blast near the Red Fort. The picture was shared with a false claim on social media. Claim: A collage of two pictures featuring a car engulfed in fire was shared by an X user '@ABHISTRONG' on November 10, claiming that they are images of the recent November 10 blast near Red Fort. "Extremely saddened and shocked by the tragic car explosion near Delhi's Red Fort, which has taken several innocent lives. My heartfelt condolences to the victims and their families," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the picture through a reverse image search using Google Lens and found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further review of the search results, the Desk came across the second image shared in a report published by Agniban on April 3. The report states that on April 2, a moving car suddenly burst into flames in Ambedkar Nagar of Delhi. The vehicle was reportedly on the Khanpur-Chirag Delhi road when the incident occurred. The headline of the report read, 'A moving car suddenly burst into flames in Delhi, with a blast.' Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised Google search for relevant media reports. It came across a video featuring the same images live-streamed on the official YouTube channel of NDTV India on April 3, 2025. A white car is also seen beside the burning car. A few seconds into the video, a small explosion occurs on top of the vehicle, followed by sparks flying. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Another set of customised keyword searches led us to a report by ETV Bharat published on April 3, 2025. The report's cover image was similar to the picture in the social media post. "Giving details of the incident, South Delhi District DCP Ankit Chauhan said that around 9 pm on Wednesday, the PCR of the Ambedkar Nagar police station area received a report of a car fire. Considering the seriousness of the situation, police immediately arrived at the scene, where a car was engulfed in flames on the route from Khanpur to Chirag Delhi," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the image is old and shows a car that caught fire in Ambedkar Nagar on April 3. It is not connected to the Delhi car blast.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Edited clip shared to falsely claim DCP North Delhi Raja Banthia ruled out terror link in Nov 10 Delhi blast
content: New Delhi, November 14 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of DCP North Delhi Raja Banthia speaking to reporters has been widely shared on social media, with claims that he ruled out any terror link to the November 10 blast near Red Fort and blamed it on a CNG or electric fault. The clip, circulated with captions alleging that police had rejected the possibility of terrorism, quickly gained traction. However, the PTI Fact Check reviewed the footage, traced it to the source, and compared it with the unedited byte issued by the Press Trust of India. The investigation found that the viral version carries manipulated audio. In the authentic video, Banthia confirms that UAPA, the Explosives Act, and relevant sections of the BNS have been invoked, and makes no reference to a CNG blast or dismissing a terror angle. Claim: A video featuring DCP North Delhi Raja Banthia speaking to the media was shared by a Facebook user, Mubeen Ahmad, on November 12, claiming that he allegedly said that the blast was caused by a CNG or electric fault and dismissed any terror angle. "As per the investigation, this does not look like a terrorist attack. We haven't found any bomb parts. It seems that it is a CNG blast…," says DCP North Delhi Raja Banthia. The post's caption read: "Modi government's Red Fort false flag plan is certain to fail, NCR police have surprised Amit Shah gang by rejecting the possibility of terrorism…," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Investigation As part of the investigation, the Desk noticed the PTI logo in the top-right corner of the video and ran a Reverse Image Search on a portion of the video, which led us to the original X post by Press Trust of India, dated November 11, 2025. The caption highlighted that A case has been registered at Kotwali police station, and UAPA, Explosives Act, and relevant sections of the BNS have been invoked. "VIDEO | Delhi blast: DCP North Raja Banthia says, "A case has been registered at Kotwali police station, and UAPA, Explosives Act, and relevant sections of the BNS have been invoked. FSL teams, forensic experts, and other specialised units are investigating the crime scene. We are collecting all evidence. We cannot say anything conclusively yet. Information will be made public once we have facts," read the post's caption. Upon listening to the entire 00:56-second byte, we at no point find any mention of a CNG blast or the DCP negating the terrorist attack claim. Here is the link to the X post, and below is a screenshot of the same. As part of the investigation, the Desk extracted the audio from the video. It ran it through Resemble AI, an AI-detection tool, which indicated that the voice is authentic but might be an impersonation. Below is a screenshot of the same. In an official statement dated November 12, 2025, the Union Cabinet described the car explosion near the Red Fort as a "heinous terror incident perpetrated by anti-national forces." The Cabinet expressed grief over the loss of lives. It directed authorities to conduct a swift and thorough investigation to ensure that the perpetrators, collaborators, and their sponsors are brought to justice without delay. Here is the link to the official release. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an AI-manipulated video was shared with a false claim that DCP North Delhi Raja Banthia called the November 10 Delhi blast a CNG blast.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video of crocodile hunting a tiger falsely shared as real wildlife footage
content: New Delhi, November 14 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media video depicting a crocodile hunting a tiger was recently shared online with the claim that it showed a real incident. The video allegedly captured a dramatic encounter in which a tiger standing near a waterbody was suddenly attacked by a crocodile, dragged into the water, and killed. In its investigation, however, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found the video to be AI-generated and shared as real to mislead viewers. Claim On November 13, X user Shagufta Khan (@Digital_khan01) shared a video purportedly showing a real incident of a tiger being killed by a crocodile. The video allegedly captured a fierce battle between the tiger and the crocodile, with the reptile overpowering the mammal. The user wrote: *"Witness the true law of the jungle where a stunning battle between a tiger and a crocodile left everyone stunned. See how even nature's true champions sometimes find themselves on the brink of defeat."* Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video had garnered 118.6k views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was checked using Google Lens, which led the Desk to numerous social media handles sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here ; their archived versions are available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a video shared by a Facebook user named Isabel Giraldo on November 10, 2025. The video shared on the Facebook handle was identical to the viral clip. However, a careful review of the user's caption revealed that the footage was generated by AI using Sora. The Desk also checked the Facebook user's bio, which clearly stated that all videos shared from the account are digitally created for entertainment purposes. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. A comparison image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral social media clip and the video shared by the Facebook user. In the subsequent part of the investigation, drawing on the above findings, the Desk ran the viral video through the AI detection tool Hive Moderation. The analysis confirmed that 99.9% of the footage contained AI-generated or deepfake elements. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video depicting a crocodile hunting a tiger was AI-generated and falsely shared as real to mislead viewers.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old, unrelated video shared to falsely claim Dharmendra shared video message after his discharge from Hospital
content: New Delhi, November 14 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of Bollywood veteran Dharmendra has been circulating on social media with claims that he shared it after being discharged from the hospital earlier this month. The clip shows him seated at home, speaking to fans about life and staying positive. The post, amplified by several users, also accuses media outlets and political leaders of spreading false news about the actor's health. However, the PTI Fact Check reviewed the video, traced its digital footprint, and compared it with earlier uploads. The investigation revealed that the footage is not recent. It was originally posted in August 2025, months before his hospitalisation, and has no connection to his recovery. Claim: A video featuring Bollywood veteran Dharmendra was shared by an X user, @BHEEM_BAUDH, on November 11, claiming that the user had shared it after being discharged from the hospital. The video shows Dharmendra sitting in a chair, wearing a black hat, a brown kurta, and checkered pyjamas, speaking to fans about life and positivity. "Look at @aajtak people and @anjanaomkashyap and @yadavakhilesh, you all together spread the false news of Dharmendra Pa ji's death. Now look, Dharmendra Pa ji is sitting right in front of you; you all should feel ashamed and apologise for spreading false news. #DharmendraDeol #Dharmendra," read the post's caption. The post clocked 241.7k views on social media. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation As part of the investigation, the Desk ran the video through the InVid tool search, extracted keyframes, and ran them through Reverse Image Search, which led us to a report by Network 18 published on August 11, 2025. The image used was similar to the one seen in the social media post. It also mentioned that Veteran actor Dharmendra has long been an inspiration to younger generations and remains a beloved figure among his loyal fans. Embracing the digital age, he stays active on social media, sharing glimpses of his life with admirers. In his latest post, Dharmendra emphasised the importance of prioritising health to enjoy life to the fullest. "Dharmendra Has A Special Message For Fans: 'Doston, Zindagi Bahut Khoobsurat Hai…'," read the headline. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. The report also carried an Instagram post by the Veteran actor featuring the original video on August 11, with a caption expressing gratitude and positivity. Here is the link to the report, and below is the screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video featuring actor Dharmendra, claiming he recorded it after his hospital discharge, is false. The video is from August 2025, months before being admitted to the hospital.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Month-old candidature announcement video of Jan Suraaj Party's Ritesh Pandey resurfaced with false claim of election victory
content: New Delhi, November 14 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing Bhojpuri singer and Jan Suraaj Party candidate from Kargahar, Ritesh Pandey, celebrating with supporters is being widely circulated on Instagram with the claim that it captures the moment after his alleged victory in the Bihar Assembly elections. However, PTI Fact Check reviewed the visuals, traced the earliest available uploads, and compared them with election-day developments. The investigation found that the clip is neither recent nor related to the ongoing Bihar poll results. Instead, it dates back to early October, when Pandey was announced as the Jan Suraaj Party's candidate from the Kargahar constituency. Claim: A video featuring Bhojpuri singer & Jan Suraaj Party candidate from Kargahar, Ritesh Pandey, celebrating with his supporters in a room was shared by Instagram user 'awaazind' on November 14, claiming it depicted the celebration after clinching victory. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Investigation As part of the investigation, the Desk first ran the video through the InVid tool to extract keyframes. Those frames were then put through a Reverse Image Search, which led us to clips matching the viral footage on the official YouTube channel of Bihar Tak, dated October 9, 2025. The timeline makes it clear that the video is not recent and has no connection to his win or the Bihar Assembly election results. Moreover, the video description mentioned that Ritesh Pandey News: Jansurja has made Bhojpuri singer Ritesh Pandey its candidate for the Kargahar assembly seat. As soon as Ritesh Pandey's name was announced, Jansurja workers celebrated. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. On further scanning the search results, the Desk also came across the same video uploaded on YouTube Shorts by a user '@Desinewsbihar' on October 9, 2025. The visuals were precisely similar to the video shared on social media. Additionally, the title mentioned that Bhojpuri singer Ritesh Pandey (to contest from) Kargahar. "Karagahar से Bhojpuri के Ritesh pandey," read the title. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the recent social media post and a month-old YouTube short video. Taking the investigation ahead, the Desk also conducted a customised keyword search and came across a Facebook post by a user 'Prashant Kishor Ki Sena' who uploaded the same video on October 9, stating that famous Bhojpuri singer and actor Ritesh Pandey is the Jan Suraj Party candidate from the Kargahar seat in Rohtas district. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. As far as the results of the Bihar Assembly elections are concerned, Ritesh Pandey — contesting for the debutant Jan Suraaj Party of strategist-turned-politician Prashant Kishor — appeared the least likely to win. As of 5 p.m. on November 14 (counting day), he was placed fourth with 16,203 votes. The vote count is expected to change as counting continues, but his victory is improbable given the latest trends, which show him trailing by more than 75,000 votes. Voting took place in two phases, on November 6 and 11, with 121 constituencies going to the polls in the first phase and 122 in the second. Counting began on Friday and is still underway. The ruling NDA is heading toward a landslide victory, with its candidates leading in over 200 out of 243 seats, delivering a significant blow to the opposition Mahagathbandhan coalition. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video featuring Bhojpuri singer & Jan Suraaj Party candidate from Kargahar, Ritesh Pandey, celebrating with his supporters is a month-old video, recorded when he was announced as a candidate from the Kargahar constituency.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Scripted video depicting argument between passenger and flight attendant shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, November 14 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it showed a real altercation that broke out between a passenger and a flight attendant in the aircraft cabin. The footage allegedly showed the passenger engaged in a heated verbal altercation with a flight attendant and another elderly individual inside the cabin. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found the video to be scripted and not depicting any real incident. The video was initially uploaded to YouTube by a Nagpur-based aviation training centre, Fly High Institute, which is known for regularly sharing scripted videos on its social media platforms for awareness. Claim On November 12, an X handle with the username Sangeetha (@Sangeeta_cbe) shared a video, alleging it depicted a real argument between a passenger and a flight attendant in the aircraft cabin. The video allegedly showed the passenger engaged in a heated verbal altercation with a flight attendant and another elderly individual inside the cabin. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video had garnered 677k views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was checked using Google Lens, which led the Desk to numerous social media handles sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here ; their archived versions are available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search result also led the Desk to a video on the official YouTube channel of a Nagpur-based aviation training centre, Fly High Institute. The video shared by the channel on November 12 was precisely similar to the one seen in the viral post. It is well known that the training institute regularly shares scripted videos on its social media platforms for awareness. The institute often posts videos showing how its students are trained to handle aviation-related exigencies professionally. The footage seen in the viral post is one such example. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. The image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral social media clip and the YouTube channel's video. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video, which purported to show a real altercation between a passenger and a flight attendant in an aircraft cabin, was scripted and did not depict any real incident.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of MS Dhoni mobbed by fans resurfaced with false claims that 'he was arrested in UK'
content: New Delhi, November 14 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media video showing an individual wearing a mask being escorted by two people, while several passersby ran behind them recording the scene, was recently shared online. Users alleged that the masked individual in the video was former Indian cricketer Mahendra Singh Dhoni and that it showed him being arrested by the UK Police. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false. The video originally showed the veteran cricketer being escorted by security staff in London in 2022, after he was surrounded by enthusiastic fans trying to take selfies with him, but the UK Police did not arrest him. Claim An Instagram page with the username Cricket Adda 18 45 (cricket_adda_18_45) shared a video on November 9, alleging that it depicted former Indian cricket team captain Mahendra Singh Dhoni being arrested by the UK Police. The footage allegedly showed the veteran cricketer, wearing a mask, being escorted by two individuals. In the clip, several passersby were also seen recording the visuals of the former Indian captain being taken away. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video garnered 23,908 likes) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was checked using Google Lens, which led the Desk to numerous social media handles sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here ; their archived versions are available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search results also led the Desk to a news report published by Wion on July 17, 2022. The report included the same video of MS Dhoni being escorted by two individuals, as shown in the viral clip. However, upon reviewing the details, it was found that the video showed Mahendra Singh Dhoni being escorted in London after he was mobbed by fans cheering his name and trying to click selfies with him. The footage showed him being guided to his car by security staff and did not depict an arrest by the UK Police. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: A comparison image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral social media clip and the video included in the Wion report. Additionally, the search results led the Desk to several other news reports confirming that the video did not show the former Indian captain being arrested. Instead, it captured Dhoni being escorted through a crowd of enthusiastic fans eager to take selfies with him in England back in July 2022. Links to three such reports can be found here , here and here . Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral claim was false and the video did not show MS Dhoni being arrested by UK Police, but captured him being escorted by security personnel as fans surrounded him in London in 2022.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered video shared to falsely claim 'Rajnath Singh linked blasts in Islamabad, Dhaka to PM Modi'
content: New Delhi, November 14 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media video showing Defence Minister Rajnath Singh allegedly stating that the recent suicide attacks outside a court in Islamabad and the series of bomb blasts in Dhaka ahead of a crucial verdict against the deposed Bangladesh Prime Minister were carried out at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, has gone viral online. The video appeared to show the Defence Minister speaking at an event, purportedly saying: "Did you see what happened in Delhi yesterday? These terrorists thought that if there were a bomb blast in India before the Bihar elections, the votes of the Bharatiya Janata Party would decrease. But in a single day, on the orders of Prime Minister Narendra Modi ji, we have carried out bomb blasts in Islamabad and Dhaka and told them that Modi will only win the Bihar elections. These bomb blasts will be the reason for the Congress's defeat in the Bihar elections." However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the audio in the viral video had been digitally manipulated and overlaid on visuals from Rajnath Singh's address at the Delhi Defence Dialogue, held on November 11. The footage was falsely shared on social media to mislead viewers. Claim An X user, Shakir Juggan (@Letme_145), on November 11, shared a video that allegedly showed Defence Minister Rajnath Singh claiming that the recent suicide attack outside an Islamabad court and a series of bomb blasts in Bangladesh were orchestrated at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The video purportedly captured Singh saying, "Did you see what happened in Delhi yesterday? These terrorists thought that if there were a bomb blast in India before the Bihar elections, the votes of the Bharatiya Janata Party would decrease. But in a single day, on the orders of Prime Minister Narendra Modi ji, we carried out bomb blasts in Islamabad and Dhaka and told them that Modi will only win the Bihar elections. These bomb blasts will be the reason for the Congress's defeat in the Bihar elections." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found a video posted on Defence Minister Rajnath Singh's official YouTube channel on November 11, 2025. The background in the viral video matched that of the official channel's video, which showed Rajnath Singh's address at the Delhi Defence Dialogue. However, upon careful examination, the Desk found no such remarks as heard in the viral video. This confirmed that the audio had been digitally altered. In the original speech, the Defence Minister extended condolences to those who lost their lives in the Delhi accident on November 10, 2025, and assured that those responsible would be brought to justice. Here is the link to the original video, along with a screenshot: The image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral and YouTube videos, confirming that both depict Rajnath Singh's address at the same event. In the next stage of the investigation, the Desk examined the viral video closely and noticed multiple lip-sync inconsistencies, indicating manipulation. The audio track was extracted and analysed using the AI detection tool Resemble AI, which revealed that while the voice sounded realistic, it was likely an impersonation. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video had been edited with fabricated audio and falsely claimed to show Defence Minister Rajnath Singh making statements about the recent attacks in Islamabad and Dhaka.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of Zubeen Garg's funeral crowd shared to falsely claim 'anti-BJP protest erupted after Bihar results'; details inside
