content: New Delhi, November 16 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a massive crowd moving along a roadway is being widely circulated on social media with the claim that it captures a protest against the BJP in Bihar, allegedly held a day after the party's victory in the state elections. The clip, shared by several Instagram accounts, is being promoted as evidence of public unrest following the poll outcome. However, PTI Fact Check examined the footage, analysed keyframes using digital verification tools, and traced the earliest online instances of the video. The investigation found that the visuals are neither recent nor connected to the Bihar elections. Instead, the crowd seen in the clip had gathered in Guwahati in September 2025, when thousands of people assembled to pay their last respects to Assam's iconic singer Zubeen Garg. Claim: A video featuring a large crowd on a road was shared by Instagram user 'loktantravoice1' on November 10, claiming that a protest was held against the BJP in Bihar, a day after the party's win in the elections. "Protest after Bihar Election #truth #biharelection2025 #protestaganistbjp," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. ​Investigation As part of the investigation, the Desk ran the video through the InVid tool search and extracted the keyframes. Running the extracted keyframes through Reverse Image Search led us to an Instagram post dated September 22, by a user 'mkbhai_official', featuring the same visuals as seen in the recent social media post. The video's caption mentioned that it was from the late singer Zubeen Garg. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combined image highlighting the similarities between the recent and September social media posts. ​Our search also led us to another post by an Instagram user named 'mahariaprahlad', dated September 21, 2025. As per the caption, the people of Assam arrived to pay their last respects to the late singer Zubeen Garg. "People of Assam arrived to pay last respects to the singer, late Zubin Garg! Millions of people in Guwahati paid tribute to their beloved singer with slogans of Zubin Zubin Zubin," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised Google search for relevant media reports. I came across a YouTube short video by Indian Times, published on September 22, 2025. The caption mentioned that thousands in Guwahati bid an emotional farewell to singer Zubeen Garg. "An ocean of grief filled Guwahati as thousands gathered to pay their last respects to legendary singer Zubeen Garg. Known as the voice of Assam and beyond, his melodies will forever echo in the hearts of his fans," read the description. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the September 2025 video shows Garg's funeral and does not depict an anti-BJP protest.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old, unrelated bus-fire video and photo resurface, falsely linking them to recent Indian Umrah pilgrims' accident in Saudi Arabia
content: New Delhi, November 17 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): In a tragic accident that claimed the lives of forty-five pilgrims, one survivor remains hospitalised after a bus carrying Indian Umrah pilgrims met with an accident in Madinah, Saudi Arabia. Amid this, several users shared dramatic visuals online, falsely claiming they showed scenes from the Saudi Arabia bus–tanker collision involving Indian pilgrims. One claim circulated a video of a bridge engulfed in flames with a massive plume of black smoke, asserting that it showed the incident in which at least 45 pilgrims were feared dead. Another post used a photograph of a firefighter near a burning bus, alleging that it depicted rescue efforts from the same tragedy. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk reviewed both visuals, and the investigation confirmed that neither is linked to the recent Madinah accident. The bridge-fire clip is from a 2017 fuel tanker accident on Aqabat Sha'ar Road, while the bus-fire image has been online since at least 2022 and is associated with unrelated incidents reported from the United States and Turkey. The Desk has categorically debunked both claims. Claim 1: A video featuring a thick black smoke billowing into the sky as massive flames engulf a section of a bridge built over a rocky valley was shared by an X user 'Baba Banaras' on November 17, claiming that it captures the aftermath of a deadly accident in Saudi Arabia, in which several Indian Umrah pilgrims were reportedly killed after their bus collided with a tanker. "BREAKING: At least 42 Indian Umrah pilgrims are feared dead after their bus crashed into a tanker in Saudi Arabia. This is really heartbreaking 💔 Prayers for departed souls," read the post's caption. The post clocked 64.6k views on social media. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . Upon further review of the search results, the Desk also found that India Today had carried the video in its report on November 17, 2025. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. After running the keyframes through Reverse Image Search again, we found that a YouTube user uploaded the same video on June 24, 2017, with an Arabic caption. The timeline of the report clarifies that the video is not recent and is not related to the death of the Indian Umrah pilgrims after a bus carrying pilgrims collided with a diesel tanker near Madinah, in which at least 45 pilgrims were feared dead. The English translation of the caption read: "Fuel tanker overturns and its driver is burned to death in Aqabat Sha'ar" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combined image highlighting the contents of the recent social media post and the 2017 YouTube video. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google, which led us to a report on alarabiya.net regarding the June 24, 2017 incident. According to the report, a 32-ton oil tanker met with an accident on Aqaba Shabar Road, in which the driver was burnt to death. This makes it clear that the viral video is not of a recent incident from Saudi-Arabia in which at least 45 pilgrims were feared dead Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. This makes it absolutely clear that the video is 8 years old and is not related to the death of the Indian Umrah pilgrims after a bus carrying pilgrims collided with a diesel tanker near Madinah, in which at least 45 pilgrims were feared dead Claim 2: Another X user, going by the name 'Milagro Movies', shared a picture of an emergency scene involving a bus fire, claiming that a firefighter was actively working at the rear of the bus carrying Indian pilgrims in Saudi Arabia, which had collided with a diesel tanker. "Breaking News: 42 Indian Umrah pilgrims died in a bus accident in Saudi Arabia. Om Shanti," read a post's caption. The post clocked 15k views on social media. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the picture through Reverse Image Search and found that several other users had shared the same image with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here . Upon further review of the search results, the Desk came across a report published by NDTV on June 4, 2023, featuring the same image as seen in the social media post. The report highlighted that a pregnant school bus driver in Wisconsin, US, is being hailed for her bravery after she saved dozens of children from a fire, the New York Post reported. The report's timeline, along with the information provided, clarifies that the picture is not recent and is not related to the bus collision in Saudi Arabia, in which at least 45 pilgrims were feared dead. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Further searches led us to another report by a website named 'petel.bg' that carried the same image in its report dated November 7, 2022. The report mentioned that at least seven people were killed in a collision between a truck and a bus in eastern Turkey. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Though the PTI Fact Check Desk could not independently verify the source of the picture, our investigation shows that the photo is old and has been available on the internet at least since 2022. It is not related to the recent tragedy in Saudi-Arabia, in which at least 45 pilgrims were feared dead Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing heavy smoke, claiming to be from the bus-tanker collision in Saudi-Arabia, carrying Indian Umrah pilgrims, dates back to 2017. Similarly, the picture depicting a firefighting operation near a charred bus has been available on the internet at least since 2022.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of Rahul Gandhi's Bhagalpur rally resurfaced to falsely claim 'youth protest erupted after Bihar election results'
content: New Delhi, November 17 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a packed nighttime crowd waving flags and surrounding a moving car has been shared online with claims that it captures Bihar's youth protesting against alleged vote theft after the recent assembly election results. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk examined the footage and found that the video is neither recent nor related to any protest. It dates back to August 2025 and was recorded during Rahul Gandhi's Vote Adhikar Yatra in Bhagalpur, Bihar. The footage was widely circulated at the time by Congress leaders and regional pages, and carries no connection to the current election cycle or claims of unrest in the state. Claim: A video showing a crowded nighttime scene showing people waving flags was shared by an Instagram user 'desi_bhokal_bhai' on November 15, claiming that Bihar's youth took to the streets in a powerful protest against alleged vote theft by the BJP and the Election Commission after the recent election results. "Look at the power of Bihar's youth, as Nepal will be in a similar situation! The BJP and EC will be afraid of vote theft," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On analysing the video carefully, the Desk found Congress's flags throughout the crowd and a car moving through the gathering with people standing out of its sunroof. A closer look at the people confirmed that it was Rahul Gandhi's rally. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Taking the investigation forward, the Desk then ran the extracted keyframes through Reverse Image Search and came across a Facebook post dated August 22, by a user named 'Jignesh Mevani', featuring the same video as seen in the recent social media post. The post's timeline clarifies that the video is not recent and does not show any protest in Bihar. "From the skies above Bihar, you can see it clearly—this is no rally, this is a revolution against #VoteChori," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. On further review of the search results, the Desk found the same video uploaded to the official Facebook channel of the Indian National Congress - Bihar on August 22. The caption accompanying the video mentioned that it was a Vote Adhikar Yatra in Bhagalpur, Bihar. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Taking a cue from the above post, the Desk conducted a customised Google search and found the video uploaded by Rahul Gandhi to his official Facebook page on August 22, 2025. "From the skies above Bihar, you can see it clearly—this is no rally, this is a revolution against #VoteChori!," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video claiming to show a protest by Bihar's youth is false. The video is months old from Rahul Gandhi's Voti Adhikar Yatra held in Bhagalpur, Bihar, in August 2022.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old, July 2025 SFI protests video from Rajasthan resurfaced falsely as 'post-election results protests from Bihar'
content: New Delhi, November 17 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a crowd pushing against a metal gate and waving banners has been shared online with claims that it captures a fresh protest from Bihar's Muzaffarpur district in the wake of the assembly elections. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk reviewed the footage, analysed it using visual verification tools, and traced it back to older uploads. The investigation found that the clip is neither recent nor from Bihar. It dates back to July 2025 and shows members of the Students' Federation of India (SFI) protesting at Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay Shekhawati University in Sikar, Rajasthan, demanding the restoration of student union elections. Multiple reports from regional media outlets at the time had covered the demonstration and confirmed that students had broken a channel gate during the agitation. Claim A video featuring a group of people carrying banners and vandalising a gate was shared by an Instagram user 'araria_ka_star_' on November 15, claiming that a protest was staged in Bihar. "Just like Nepal, our Bihar Muzaffarpur has started. Let's go Biharians, get ready to fight," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post dated July 28, 2025, by a user '@vijendra_dhaka_', carrying the same video as seen in the recent social media post. The caption accompanying the video stated that, in response to the demand for the restoration of student union elections, SFI Rajasthan staged a protest at Shekhawati University in Sikar. "Demanding the restoration of student union elections, SFI Rajasthan staged a protest at Shekhawati University in Sikar. The channel gate was broken during the demonstration due to the university administration's high-handedness," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports and came across a report by Patrika News, a Hindi-Rajasthani-language daily newspaper, published on July 29, 2025. The report's cover image was similar to a clip seen in the social media post, just from a different angle. The report highlighted that the Students Federation of India (SFI) broke the channel gate of the administrative building, expressing their anger at Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay Shekhawati University, Sikar, demanding the resumption of student union elections. "SFI officials and workers sat on the stairs outside the administrative building. The students protested for more than three hours, and Registrar Seta Yadav approached them and accepted the memorandum. It is noteworthy that earlier, also during the tenure of former Vice Chancellor Bhagirath Singh Bijarnia, the SFI had broken the channel gate," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. As part of the investigation, the Desk conducted another set of customised keyword searches on Google, which led us to another report by Dainik Bhaskar published in July, highlighting that the Students' Federation of India (SFI) continues its vigorous protests at Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Shekhawati University (Sikar), demanding the reinstatement of student union elections. Hundreds of students surrounded the Vice Chancellor's office, raising slogans on the university campus. "SFI protest at Shekhawati University, broke the gate and entered: Protest outside the VC's office, SFI state president said - will not allow the VC to enter the university," read the headline of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video is not recent and dates back to July 2025, showing the Students Federation of India (SFI) expressing its anger at Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay Shekhawati University, Sikar, and demanding the resumption of student union elections.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video depicting 'fight' between Indian and Pakistani players in Sharjah shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, November 17 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing individuals wearing what appear to be Indian and Pakistani cricket team jerseys engaged in a physical altercation on a pitch was recently shared on social media, with claims that it depicted a real fight between players of the two teams in Sharjah. The video allegedly captured individuals involved in a heated argument, with others attempting to pacify them. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the video was AI-generated and falsely shared as real to mislead viewers. Claim An X handle with the username 'update man' (@Vijayma70555375) shared a video on November 16, alleging that it showed a fight between an Indian and a Pakistani cricket player inside a stadium in Sharjah. The video allegedly captured the players engaged in a heated argument while their teammates attempted to pacify them. The user wrote, "Fight between Pakistani and Indian players in Sharjah." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video garnered 1.4 million views and 4.6k likes) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was checked using Google Lens, which led the Desk to numerous social media handles sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here ; their archived versions are available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a video posted by the Instagram handle Jhatka AI, whose bio states that it primarily shares AI-generated content. The Desk found that the video—identical to the viral clip—was posted by the Instagram handle on November 14, 2025. Upon careful analysis, the visuals clearly indicated AI generation due to multiple inconsistencies. For instance, the word "Pakistan" was misspelt on the player's jersey, and another player's disproportionately long and unnatural hand was visible in the footage. Here is the link and archive link to the video, along with a screenshot. A comparison image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral social media clip and the Instagram video. Next, drawing on the above findings, the Desk ran the viral video through the AI detection tool Hive Moderation. The analysis confirmed that 96.3% of the footage contained AI-generated or deepfake elements. Below is a screenshot of the result. In the subsequent part of the investigation, the Desk also conducted a customised keyword search on Google to verify whether any real incident of an argument between Indian and Pakistani players had been reported. The search did not yield any credible news reports confirming a fight or even a match between the two national teams taking place in Sharjah at the time. However, the search led to a report published by The Times of India on November 17, 2025, which mentioned a recent controversial moment during the India A vs Pakistan Shaheens match in the Asia Cup Rising Stars tournament. The report stated, "The incident involved a relay catch between Nehal Wadhera and Naman Dhir that was ultimately ruled not out by the third umpire." The report, however, made no mention of any physical altercation between players. Here is a link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video claiming to show a physical altercation between an Indian and a Pakistani cricket team player was AI-generated and does not depict a real incident.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Months-old video of Tejashwi Yadav greeting Chirag Paswan passed off as recent, connecting to recent Bihar poll results; details inside
content: New Delhi, November 18 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Days after the Election Commission of India announced the results of the much-awaited Bihar Assembly polls, where the National Democratic Alliance (NDA), led by the BJP, secured a striking victory by winning 202 seats in the 243-member Assembly, a purported social media video showing senior RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav seemingly greeting NDA ally and Lok Janshakti Party–Ram Vilas (LJP-RV) chief Chirag Paswan began circulating widely online. Users sharing the video claimed that the leaders had recently met after the results, hinting that their meeting could signal a major political shift in the state ahead of the new government formation. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the video of the two leaders meeting is at least five months old, dating back to May 2025. The exchange took place in Nawada, where the two leaders had a brief interaction and exchanged pleasantries. It was not related to the 2025 Bihar Assembly elections. An old, unrelated video of Opposition leaders Tejashwi Yadav and Chirag Paswan greeting each other was falsely shared on social media as if it were recent and linked to the latest polling in the state. Claim An Instagram user, Shailender Kumar (@shailenderkumar0888), shared a video on November 14 showing senior RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav greeting LJP-RV chief Chirag Paswan. The user claimed that the two leaders had recently met after the election results and that the meeting could signal a major political shift before the formation of the new government. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video garnered 14,045 likes) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was checked using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media handles sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here ; their archived versions are available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search result also led the Desk to a video posted by a YouTube channel named 'NBC24 Media'. The Desk found that the channel's video matched the visuals in the viral post. However, upon careful analysis of the video, it was found that it did not pertain to a recent event. Instead, it was five months old, published on May 20, 2025. The video shows the two leaders exchanging brief pleasantries in Nawada. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: The image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral social media clip and the YouTube channel's video. In the next part of the investigation, drawing on the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised Google keyword search to gather more information about the meeting. The search result led the Desk to a video posted by a YouTube channel named News Tak on May 21, 2025. It stated that the two leaders had visited Pandey Gangaut village in Nawada district to pay tribute to martyr Manish Kumar. The video made no mention of the Bihar polls or any political shift. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video circulating on social media was old and unrelated to the ongoing political developments in Bihar. The clip showing Tejashwi Yadav and Chirag Paswan exchanging pleasantries dates back to May 2025 and has no connection to the recent Bihar Assembly election results.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2022 Argentina World Cup celebration video falsely shared as massive RJD protest against EC in Patna
content: New Delhi, November 18 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a massive crowd spilling over highways and city streets was shared widely on social media with the claim that more than 20 million RJD supporters had assembled in Patna to protest against the Election Commission. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and revealed that the viral visuals have no connection to Patna or to any political demonstration in India. Instead, the footage dates back to December 2022, when millions of people in Buenos Aires poured onto the streets to celebrate Argentina's FIFA World Cup victory. The evidence makes it clear that the viral video was misrepresented online and has no link to Bihar or the Election Commission. Claim: A video showing an enormous crowd filling the streets was shared by an X user, @BefittingFacts, on November 18, claiming that over 20 million RJD supporters gathered to protest the Election Commission. "Patna: Over 20 million RJD supporters gathered to protest against the Election Commission," read the post's caption. The post clocked 48.6k views on social media. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation As part of the investigation, the Desk ran the video through the InVid tool search to extract the keyframes. Running a single frame through Reverse Image Search, the Desk found that the video snippets, shot from a different angle, appeared in a CBS News report published on December 21, 2022. The report mentioned that huge crowds celebrate Argentina's World Cup win. "An estimated crowd of four million jubilant soccer fans flooded the streets, and even highways, of Buenos Aires, as Argentina tried to hold a victory parade for its World Cup champions," read the description. The report's timeline and the description accompanying the video clarify that the incident dates back to 2022 and is not related to Patna, Bihar at all. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combined image highlighting the similarities between the social media post and the news report, though from a different angle. Taking a cue from this, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports. Our search led us to a report by India.com published on December 21, 2022. The report's cover image was similar to the clip shown in the social media post. The caption accompanying the picture mentioned that Argentina fans flooded onto the streets of Buenos Aires to celebrate Messi and Co.'s FIFA World Cup Triumph. "Lionel Messi and Argentina have done it again at last as they went on to clinch their 3rd FIFA World Cup triumph, beating France 4-2 on penalties after 3-3 of 120 minutes of play on Sunday at Lusail Iconic Stadium," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Moreover, on careful analysis of the viral video, we saw a few people standing in a terrace-like area wearing Argentina's football kit. Below is a screenshot of the same. Taking the investigation forward, the Desk also conducted a customised keyword search to determine whether a protest was held in Patna, Bihar, against the EC. However, we did not find any such reports. Given the gravity of the matter, such news would have been covered by the leading news channels. Moreover, in recent days, PTI Fact Check has debunked several other protest visuals claiming to be from Bihar. Two such stories can be viewed here and here . Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video, which showed a sea of people claiming to be RJD supporters gathered to protest against the Election Commission, was false. The video dates back to 2022, when an estimated crowd of 4 million soccer fans flooded the streets as Argentina tried to hold a victory parade for its World Cup champions.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video of monkey snatching gun from soldier shared as real; claim is false
content: New Delhi, November 18 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it showed an incident at an Indian checkpoint, where a soldier is seen sleeping. In the clip, a monkey allegedly jumps near the dozing soldier, grabs his rifle, and fires it—forcing the soldier to run away from the post. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk reviewed the footage and found that the video is AI-generated. It does not depict any real incident involving Indian security personnel. Claim A Pakistan-based X user, Ch Mudasir (@ij422), on November 16, shared a purported video of an Indian security personnel at a border checkpoint. The video allegedly shows the soldier dozing at the post when a monkey suddenly jumps near him, grabs his rifle, and fires it—causing the startled soldier to run away. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video had garnered 177.9k views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was examined using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here ; their archived versions are available here and here , respectively. As part of the investigation, the Desk carefully analysed the viral video and identified multiple inconsistencies indicating that it was AI-generated. For instance, the manner in which the soldier jumps from the checkpoint appears unnatural, and the monkey handling a heavy service rifle is highly improbable. The visuals also show the chair missing legs—another anomaly. Below is a screenshot highlighting these findings. Next, using cues from the above observations, the Desk ran the video through the AI-detection tool Hive Moderation. The tool determined that 98% of the video likely contains AI-generated or deepfake content. Below is a screenshot highlighting the result. Additionally, the Desk conducted a customised Google search to determine whether any similar real-life incident had been reported. However, the search yielded no credible news reports confirming such an event. Had such an unusual incident taken place, media outlets would have covered it. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing an Indian soldier running from a checkpoint after a monkey allegedly fired his rifle was AI-generated and was falsely shared as a real incident to mislead viewers.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of Faridabad firing incident falsely shared with communal twist; details inside
content: New Delhi, November 18 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video seemingly capturing visuals from inside a narrow lane, where an individual opened fire at a girl who was engaged on her mobile phone, was recently shared on social media. Users claimed the video showed a horrific recent incident from Haryana's Faridabad, where a 19-year-old Hindu girl returning from her coaching centre was shot by a Muslim man for rejecting his advances. The video allegedly captured the accused, identified as belonging to the Muslim community, patiently waiting for the victim to pass through the lane before suddenly opening fire at her. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it to be falsely linked with a communal angle. The video, in fact, depicted an incident that took place in Faridabad's Shyam Colony on November 3, 2025, where a man named Jitendra, alias Jatin Mangla, shot a 17-year-old girl for rejecting his advances. Importantly, it was confirmed that both the victim and the accused are Hindu, and there is no communal angle to the incident. Claim An Instagram handle with the username 'sanataniboycg' shared a video on November 8, allegedly showing a recent incident from Haryana's Faridabad, where a Muslim man opened fire on a 19-year-old Hindu girl for rejecting his advances. The claim further states that the girl was returning from her coaching when the incident occurred. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. One of the keyframes was checked using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media accounts sharing the same clip with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here ; with their archived versions viewed here and here respectively. Next, the Desk conducted a customised Google keyword search based on the details mentioned in the viral posts. This search led to a PTI news report published by The Hindu, which stated that the accused who shot a 17-year-old JEE aspirant in Faridabad had been arrested. Notably, the report identified the accused as 30-year-old Jitendra alias Jatin Mangla, confirming that he belonged to the same religion as the victim, Kanishka. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. The image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral social media clip and the news report's feature image. The search also led the Desk to a News18 report dated November 6, 2025, which similarly confirmed the identity of the accused as Jatin Mangla, again establishing that both individuals belonged to the same community. Here is the link to the report. Additionally, the Desk found a video statement issued by the Faridabad Police on their official X handle on November 6. In the statement, the police confirmed that the accused, 30-year-old Hindu man Jatin Mangla, had been arrested for firing at a 17-year-old girl in Faridabad. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that while the video depicts a real incident from Faridabad, the claim linking it to a communal angle is false. Both the accused and the victim are Hindu.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old, unrelated protest videos resurfaced falsely claiming 'BJP office torched after Bihar election results'
content: New Delhi, November 19 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video stitched from two unrelated clips is circulating on social media with the claim that anti-govt protestors set a BJP office on fire after the 2025 Bihar Assembly elections. The first clip shows crowds gathered before a locked gate, while the second shows a building engulfed in flames. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated and found that neither of the footage has any link to Bihar or the recent elections. The first clip has been available on the internet since September 2025, and the second video is a month old from Ladakh. Claim: A video consisting of two clips, with one depicting people gathered in front of a closed gate and the other showing a burning structure, was shared by an Instagram user 'rjd_ravi_official' on November 15, claiming that anti-Modi protestors torched a BJP office building after the 2025 Bihar Elections. "The BJP office was burnt by the public! #bjp #rjd #jdu #jalaya #birodh #vote #chori #evm," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . The Desk categorically debunked both the video. Video 1: Showing people gathered outside a closed gate- as part of the investigation, the Desk ran the footage through the InVid tool search to extract the keyframes. Running one of the keyframes through Reverse Image Search, the Desk found an Instagram post by a user named 'yogitabhayana' on October 4. The video clips matched the ones seen in the recent social media post. The text accompanying the video mentioned that a protest was held in Pithoragarh, Uttarakhand. "Justice for Kashish – Pithoragarh, Uttarakhand. Kashish, a young 7-year-old girl from Pithoragarh, was brutally raped and murdered. Her dreams were silenced, her life stolen. This is not just Kashish's fight—this is a fight for every daughter, every sister, every woman who deserves safety and dignity. We demand justice. We demand change. No more silence. No more excuses," read the caption of the post. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Our search also led us to a report streamed on Facebook by 'News Pth TV' on September 6. The caption read, "Pithoragarh: Hundreds of lives at risk, what next in the Nanhi Pari case?". The report's timeline clarifies that it is not recent and is unrelated to the Bihar elections. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised Google search for relevant media reports. It came across a report by The Times of India, published on September 14, mentioning that hundreds of residents held a demonstration at Ramlila Ground in Pithoragarh to protest the Supreme Court's recent decision to acquit a 'convict on death penalty' in the rape-murder of a seven-year-old girl in Haldwani in 2014. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. This makes it clear that the video has been available on the internet since September 2025 and has no connection to the Bihar elections. Video 2: After running the second video through the InVid tool to extract the keyframes, then running the keyframes through Reverse Image Search, the Desk found a YouTube video titled 'NewsX Live' uploaded on September 24. The video mentioned that violent protests erupted in Ladakh, with demonstrators demanding statehood and inclusion in the Sixth Schedule. "At least four people were killed and over 70 were injured. Protesters set the local BJP office and vehicles on fire. Police responded with teargas and baton charges to control the unrest. Stay updated for the latest developments," read the description of the same. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised Google search and came across a report by the Indian Express published on September 24, 2025. The description with the image mentioned that smoke billows out from the BJP office in Leh as it is set on fire during a massive protest over the statehood demand and the inclusion of Ladakh under the Sixth Schedule. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the two video clips are unrelated and were falsely shared as a protest following the Bihar elections.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: This social media post claiming govt has announced free electric cycle scheme for students is absolutely false; edited video shared as real
content: New Delhi, November 20 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video has recently been circulating on social media, allegedly describing a new government scheme offering free electric cycles to all school students under 18. Some of these videos also feature Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in which he is allegedly seen stating that the policy was announced following his party's landslide victory in the recently concluded Bihar Assembly Elections 2025. The videos follow a similar pattern: a female voice urges viewers to share the video with at least five people to avail themselves of the scheme's benefits. Viewers are then instructed to follow specific social media handles and enter their details via a link in the Instagram page's description. It is pertinent to note that, while the videos follow a similar format, the specific social media handles mentioned vary depending on the channel that circulates the content. The links for data entry differ as well. The Press Trust of India (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated these videos and found the claims to be false. The government has not announced any scheme to provide free electric cycles to schoolchildren. Furthermore, the visuals of Prime Minister Narendra Modi used to enhance the credibility of the videos have been digitally manipulated. The footage was taken from his past address, where he made no such claims; the audio was digitally altered to mislead viewers. Claim Social media has been flooded with videos elaborating on an alleged government scheme that guarantees free electric cycles to all schoolchildren under 18. Some of these videos also feature Prime Minister Narendra Modi purportedly confirming the scheme's implementation in celebration of the BJP's massive victory in the upcoming Bihar Assembly Elections 2025. The video is accompanied by a female voice urging viewers to send the purported clip to at least five people and follow the mentioned Instagram page. It further states that to avail of the benefit, one must fill in their details by clicking the website link in the description of the respective social media handles. Links to these posts can be found here , here , here , and here ; their archived versions are available here , here , here , and here , respectively. A screenshot of these posts is attached below. Investigation The Desk began the investigation by conducting a customised Google search to determine whether any credible media outlets had reported on such a scheme. The search results did not yield any credible reports confirming the existence of a free electric cycle scheme. Given the scale of the alleged claim, such an announcement would have received extensive media coverage if it were authentic. Significantly, as part of the investigation, the Desk also scanned multiple government channels, including the 'My Scheme' portal, where details regarding the scheme would be accessible if it had been implemented. No evidence was found regarding the implementation of such a scheme. This confirmed that the claim of distributing free electric cycles to all schoolchildren under 18 is false. In the subsequent part of the investigation, the Desk examined the viral video showing Prime Minister Narendra Modi allegedly announcing free electric cycles in the wake of the 2025 Bihar Assembly Elections. The Desk ran the footage through the InVid tool to extract multiple keyframes. Running one of these keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk located a video shared by the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) that matched the visuals from the viral clip. Upon analysis, it was found that the footage was from PM Modi's speech at the launch of the PM-Kisan Samman Nidhi Yojana in Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh, in February 2019. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting the visual similarities between the viral social media clip and the video shared by the Prime Minister's Office. Next, the Desk carefully analysed the complete video of the event shared on the PMO India YouTube channel to verify whether the Prime Minister made any such statement as depicted in the viral clip. Nowhere in the extended footage did PM Modi mention a free bicycle scheme. In the original video, the Prime Minister spoke about farmers' welfare, the PM-KISAN scheme, and other agriculture-related initiatives. Taking cues from the findings above, the Desk extracted the audio segment from the viral video and ran it through the AI audio detection tool, Resemble AI. The tool indicated that the voice in the video was fake. Below is a screenshot of the result: Moreover, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search on Google to find details about similar schemes being implemented in other states. The search results led to several links indicating that several states—including Assam, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, Rajasthan, West Bengal, and Tamil Nadu—provide free regular bicycles to students, particularly school-going girls in government schools. Links to the same can be found here , here , here , here , here , and here . Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video claiming the government is distributing free electric cycles to school students is fake. The investigation confirmed that no such scheme has been announced, and the video featuring Prime Minister Narendra Modi was digitally manipulated using footage from a 2019 event, with the audio altered using AI technology to mislead viewers.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old Nepal protest video falsely shared as 'youths vandalising BJP leader's car in Bihar'
content: New Delhi, November 20 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Days after the Election Commission of India announced the results of the 2025 Bihar Assembly Elections—where the BJP-led NDA coalition registered a massive victory over the opposition's Mahagathbandhan alliance—a video surfaced on social media with the claim that youths in Bihar had vandalised the car of a BJP leader. The footage appeared to show several individuals throwing stones at the vehicle and kicking its bonnet. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk examined the visuals and found that the video had been falsely attributed to post-election violence in Bihar. The clip actually shows a scene from Nepal, where protests by Gen Z demonstrators had turned violent. Reports confirm that the vehicle being attacked belonged to a Nepalese government official in Pokhara. Despite this, the old video was misleadingly circulated on social media, claiming it depicted violence in Bihar following the election results. Claim An Instagram page with the username 'rocky_pigeon_00' shared a video on November 16, purportedly showing a mob vandalising the car of a BJP leader in Bihar. According to the claim, the footage depicted individuals throwing stones and kicking the bonnet of the BJP leader's vehicle, days after the party's victory in the state assembly polls. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered 17,340 likes.) Investigation The Desk began its investigation by conducting a customised Google keyword search to verify whether any such incident of a BJP leader's car being attacked had occurred in Bihar. However, the search did not return any credible news reports confirming the claim. Given the seriousness of the alleged incident, it would likely have been widely reported by the media if it had actually taken place. Next, the Desk extracted multiple keyframes from the viral video using the InVid tool. These keyframes were then run through Google Lens, which led to a video posted on an Instagram page named 'timesg.ind', which describes itself as a media news platform. The Desk found that the video posted by this page on September 9 matched the viral clip exactly. The post's caption clarified that the incident occurred in Nepal. It stated that the footage depicted violence during Nepal's Gen Z protest, where demonstrators torched and overturned the car of a Nepalese government official in Pokhara. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the social media video—linked initially to violence during the Gen Z protests in Nepal—was falsely shared to claim that youths vandalised a BJP leader's car in Bihar. It is pertinent to note that the PTI Fact Check Desk had earlier debunked the same claim. For the detailed investigation, refer to the link below.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video falsely shared to claim 'train accident happened in Uttar Pradesh's Bareilly'; details inside
content: New Delhi, November 21 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it depicted a massive train accident in Uttar Pradesh's Bareilly, where three coaches of a passenger train allegedly plunged into the Ramganga river. The video appeared to show a train derailing while crossing a bridge over the river, leading to three coaches falling into the water. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the video was AI-generated and falsely shared on social media to mislead viewers. Claim An Instagram page named First Post Now (firstpostnow_official) shared a video on November 17, purportedly showing a tragic railway accident in Bareilly. The footage claimed to depict a passenger train crossing a bridge over the Ramganga river before derailing, causing three coaches to fall into the river. "Heartbreaking accident in Bareilly! The balance of the moving train got worsened and within seconds it left the track and entered the Ramganga river," the user wrote in the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing the story, the video had garnered 3,411 likes.) Investigation The Desk first ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. One of the keyframes was analysed using Google Lens, which led to several social media accounts sharing the same clip with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions viewed here and here respectively. The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a video posted on November 16 by Instagram user Anmol Bohraa, who shared the same footage. Upon analysing the content of his profile and the caption of the post, it was found that the video was AI-generated. In the caption, the creator explicitly wrote: "Learn How to Make Viral AI Reels Like This — Join My Patreon Course 👉 From the Link in My Bio!" The caption clearly indicated the video to be AI generated. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: A comparison image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral clip and the reel posted by the creator. As part of the investigation, the Desk also reviewed the Instagram profile of the user, where it was noted that he regularly shares AI-generated content. Based on the above findings, the Desk concluded that the video depicting a train accident in Bareilly was AI-generated.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video tweaked to falsely show Khan Sir attacks BJP on vote tampering in recently concluded Bihar Polls; details inside
content: New Delhi, November 22 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media video allegedly showing popular educator and YouTuber Khan Sir levelling allegations against the BJP of vote tampering in the recently concluded Bihar Assembly Elections was recently shared online. The video purportedly showed the educator accusing the NDA of vote theft in Bihar, claiming that although he voted for the RJD and had earlier dismissed Rahul Gandhi's allegations of vote chori, he now believes votes were indeed stolen. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it to be digitally manipulated. In the original clip—shared by Zee Jharkhand-Bihar on its YouTube channel on July 31, 2024—the popular educator was speaking about the infrastructure of educational institutions, and not making allegations against the BJP regarding vote tampering in the Bihar Assembly Elections. A digitally altered video of Khan Sir was falsely circulated on social media by linking it to the elections. Claim On November 17, an Instagram page with the username 'samajwadi___fans1' shared a video of popular educator and YouTuber Khan Sir, in which he was allegedly seen questioning the Bharatiya Janata Party-led NDA's victory in the recently concluded Bihar Assembly polls. In the video, the educator appeared to accuse the NDA of vote theft in Bihar, stating that although he voted for the RJD and had earlier dismissed Rahul Gandhi's allegations of vote chori, he now believes votes were indeed stolen. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk first ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. One of the keyframes was analysed using Google Lens, which led several social media accounts to share the same clip with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here ; their archived versions are available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search result also led the Desk to a video published by a YouTube channel affiliated with Zee News, which covers developments from Bihar and Jharkhand. The video was posted on July 31, 2024 — months before the assembly elections were held in Bihar. The video featured a byte of the popular educator, with the background and his attire matching those in the viral clip. However, nowhere in the original video did the educator raise any suspicion regarding the BJP's victory in the state. In the original clip shared by Zee News, he spoke solely about the infrastructure of educational institutions. This confirmed that the viral video had been altered with superimposed audio. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot: The image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral social media clip and the video shared by the Zee News YouTube channel covering Bihar and Jharkhand. In the next stage of the investigation, drawing on the above findings, the Desk examined the viral video closely and identified multiple lip-sync inconsistencies, indicating manipulation. The audio track was extracted and analysed using the AI detection tool Resemble AI, which confirmed it to be fake. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video had been edited with fabricated audio and was falsely shared to claim that Khan Sir questioned the Bharatiya Janata Party-led NDA's victory in the recently concluded Bihar Assembly polls.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of mock drill conducted by security officials falsely shared as terrorists being arrested from Mumbai; details inside
content: New Delhi, November 22 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media video purportedly showing two individuals being held at gunpoint by a group of security officials at a busy location was recently shared online. Users claimed the visuals depicted two terrorists being apprehended by Mumbai Police from Andheri West's Kamdhenu Shopping Complex on November 15. The video also showed several bystanders recording the incident as the police escorted the alleged terrorists away. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found that it actually showed a mock drill conducted by the Mumbai Police, and not a real terror-related arrest. An unrelated video of a routine security exercise was falsely shared as a genuine incident to mislead viewers. Claim An X user, Divya Singh Sharma, on November 16, shared the video along with the claim that it showed Mumbai Police arresting two terrorists from Andheri West's Kamdhenu Shopping Complex. "Terrorist arrested from Andheri West Lokhandwala. This is the Kamdhenu Shopping complex, a few metres away from my home. Some Islamic apologists say that terrorism has no religion. I say, but why do all the terrorists have the same religion?" the user wrote while sharing the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered 1.2k views.) Investigation The Desk first ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. One of the frames was analysed using Google Lens, leading to several social media posts sharing the same clip with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. Next, to verify the video's authenticity, the Desk carefully analysed it, examining both the visuals and the audio. In the background, several bystanders could be heard stating that the incident unfolding before them was not real, but a staged exercise. Drawing on these preliminary cues, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to check whether any credible media outlet had reported the alleged arrest of two terrorists in Mumbai. No such news reports were found. Given the heightened security environment in the country—particularly after the recent terrorist attack near Delhi's Red Fort—an event involving the arrest of two terrorists would have been widely covered by mainstream media. While no news reports confirmed the claim of an actual terrorist arrest, the search led the Desk to a report published by the Free Press Journal on November 16. The report included screenshots matching those in the viral video and clarified that the visuals were from a mock drill conducted by the Mumbai Police, not a real arrest. The report also quoted a statement from the Oshiwara Police, confirming that the video indeed depicted a mock drill. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. The image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral clip and the photo shared in the news report. Additionally, a customised keyword search led the Desk to another report published by UNI on November 16. This report also carried a statement from the Oshiwara Police, reiterating that the video was from a mock drill and not an arrest of terrorists in Mumbai. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video does not show Mumbai Police arresting terrorists, but footage from a mock drill that was falsely shared online with a misleading narrative.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Deepfake video of Aishwarya Rai Bachchan shared with false claim that she questioned PM Modi on 'Op Sindoor'; details inside
content: New Delhi, November 22 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media video purportedly depicting Bollywood actress Aishwarya Rai Bachchan confronting Prime Minister Narendra Modi over India's loss of military assets to Pakistan during Operation Sindoor was recently circulated online. The video, which was shot in Andhra Pradesh's Puttaparthi—where Aishwarya Rai Bachchan arrived to participate in the centenary celebrations of Shri Sathya Sai Baba—allegedly showed her questioning PM Modi at a public podium about why India lost four Rafales, several fighter jets, two S-400 systems, and 300 soldiers to Pakistan. She was purportedly heard saying: "I want to ask Prime Minister Narendra Modi why we lost six jets to Pakistan. Why did we lose four Rafales to Pakistan? Why did we lose two S-400 systems to Pakistan? Why did we lose 300 soldiers to Pakistan? Why did we lose a significant part of our boundary in Kashmir and Rajasthan to Pakistan? Prime Minister Narendra Modi, we know that the film fraternity does not get involved in politics, but this is something that the nation demands to know." However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found that it had been digitally altered. In the original clip—covering Aishwarya Rai Bachchan's address at the event—she made no reference to India losing military assets. Instead, she spoke only about the teachings of Sri Sathya Sai Baba. A digitally manipulated video of the Bollywood actress was falsely shared on social media, claiming she confronted the Prime Minister over developments related to Operation Sindoor. Claim An X handle, Ramesh Speaks (@Rameshspeech), on November 20, shared a purported video of Bollywood actress Aishwarya Rai Bachchan in which she was allegedly heard questioning Prime Minister Narendra Modi over India losing defence jets to Pakistan during Operation Sindoor. The viral clip captured her purportedly saying: "I want to ask Prime Minister Narendra Modi why we lost six jets to Pakistan… why we lost four Rafales… two S-400 systems… 300 soldiers… and part of our boundary in Kashmir and Rajasthan to Pakistan." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered 2,204 views.) Investigation The Desk first ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. One of the keyframes was analysed using Google Lens, which led to several social media posts sharing the same clip with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. To verify the authenticity of the video, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found the extended clip of Aishwarya Rai Bachchan's address from the centenary celebrations of Shri Sathya Sai Baba. The search result led to a video published by a YouTube channel associated with the revered late spiritual figure. The channel shared a full livestream of the centenary programme on November 19, attended by several dignitaries, including Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Aishwarya Rai Bachchan. The entire programme lasted approximately 3 hours and 25 minutes. However, upon reviewing the video, the Desk found that Aishwarya Rai Bachchan did not question the Prime Minister at any point. Instead, she spoke about the teachings of Sri Sathya Sai Baba, highlighting the principles of Discipline, Dedication, Devotion, Determination, and Discrimination. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot. In the next stage of the investigation, the Desk extracted the audio track and analysed it using Google's AI detection tool Resemble AI. The tool indicated that the voice heard in the viral video was artificially generated. Below is a screenshot of the results: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a digitally manipulated video of Aishwarya Rai Bachchan was falsely circulated on social media, claiming she confronted Prime Minister Narendra Modi about India losing military assets to Pakistan.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video of people looting cash from highway falsely shared as incident from Uttar Pradesh
content: New Delhi, November 24 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video circulating on social media purportedly shows dozens of people rushing to collect currency notes scattered across a road, with an overturned vehicle visible in the background. The user claimed that the mishap caused the money inside the vehicle to spill onto the road, following which around 500 people allegedly rushed to the spot and looted the cash. The user posted: "On a highway in Uttar Pradesh, a truck loaded with cash overturned, and notes began flying across the road. In no time, around 500 people gathered at the scene and looted the notes." author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, IAF Chief did not criticise Tejas induction after Dubai air tragedy; digitally edited video shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, November 24 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): In the aftermath of the tragic accident at the Dubai Air Show, where the Indian Air Force's (IAF) Tejas fighter aircraft crashed during an aerial manoeuvre at Al Maktoum International Airport, a video circulating on social media falsely claims that Air Chief Marshal A P Singh blamed the incident on the induction of Tejas into the IAF. In the viral clip, the Air Chief is purportedly heard saying that he had warned the Indian government against inducting the indigenous fighter jet, adding, "This is not a plane, this is a samosa. And samosas are not meant to fly." However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk reviewed the circulating footage and found that the video had been digitally altered. The audio was manipulated and superimposed onto an older clip from the Air Chief Marshal's address during the 93rd Indian Air Force Day celebrations — long before the Dubai Air Show tragedy. Therefore, the claim circulating on social media is false. The IAF Chief did not make any such remarks on Tejas following the accident. Claim On November 23, X user Satish Sain shared a purported video of Air Chief Marshal A.P. Singh, in which he was heard criticising the Indian government for inducting the multi-role fighter aircraft Tejas into the Indian Air Force. In the purported statement—claimed to have been made in the aftermath of the Dubai Air Show tragedy, where a Tejas fighter jet crashed in a ball of fire, killing the lone pilot—the IAF chief was allegedly heard questioning the aircraft's operational capability and comparing it to a "samosa." "I already told the Indian Government not to fly this and not to induct this in the Air Force. They did not listen to us, and see what happened today. This is not a plane, this is a samosa. And samosas are not meant to fly," the IAF chief was purportedly heard saying. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk first ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. One of the keyframes was analysed using Google Lens, which led to several social media posts sharing the same clip with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here ; their archived versions are available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a video shared by a YouTube channel named India Today Global, which featured the same visuals of the IAF chief seen in the viral clip. The description stated that the footage was from a press briefing held by Air Chief Marshal A.P. Singh on the occasion of the 93rd Indian Air Force Day celebrations. However, upon reviewing the extended clip of the IAF chief's address from the event, the Desk found no trace of the alleged statement. Instead, the briefing focused on the IAF's operational readiness, modernisation plans, and key initiatives to strengthen India's aerial defence capabilities. Below is the link to the video, along with a screenshot: A comparison image below highlights the background similarities between the viral video and the footage shared in the news report, confirming they originate from the same event. In the next stage of the investigation, the Desk extracted the audio track from the viral video and analysed it using Google's AI detection tool Resemble AI. The tool indicated that the voice heard in the clip was artificially generated. Below is a screenshot of the result: Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google search for any official statement by the IAF chief regarding the Dubai Air Show crash. The search led to a post shared by the Indian Air Force on its X handle on November 22, mourning the death of Wg Cdr Namansh Syal in the incident. "A dedicated fighter pilot and thorough professional, he served the nation with unwavering commitment, exceptional skill and an unyielding sense of duty. His dignified persona earned him immense respect through a life devoted to service, as seen in the send-off attended by UAE officials, colleagues, friends, and officials of the Indian Embassy. The IAF stands in solidarity with his family in this hour of profound grief and honours his legacy of courage, devotion and honour. May his service be remembered with gratitude," the post stated. Here is the link to the post. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a digitally manipulated video of the IAF chief was shared on social media to falsely claim that he criticised the induction of the Tejas aircraft into the Indian Air Force following the recent Dubai Air Show tragedy.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: This social media post claiming Gautam Gambhir retired as Indian cricket team head coach is absolutely false; details inside
content: New Delhi, November 25 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media post featuring a purported statement by Indian cricket team head coach Gautam Gambhir recently went viral, claiming that he had announced his retirement from the cricket world, both as a coach and from any future involvement. The alleged statement suggested that Gambhir was stepping down due to the "constant stream of criticism" directed at him despite his contributions to the game. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found it to be false. No official announcement regarding such a decision was found from either Gambhir or the BCCI, confirming that the claim is FAKE. Claim An X user (@imRavY_) on November 24 shared a purported statement attributed to Indian cricket team head coach Gautam Gambhir, claiming he had announced his retirement from the cricket world "as a coach and from any future involvement." In the alleged statement, he reportedly said: "Honestly, the constant stream of criticism and trolling has simply become exhausting. I gave everything I had to this game, but the atmosphere around it, particularly online, makes it clear that my time is up. I leave with my records intact and my head high. Wishing Indian Cricket all the very best for its future endeavours." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the post had garnered 1.2 million views.) Investigation To verify the claim, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to check for any credible reports about Gambhir announcing his retirement. The search did not return any reliable news confirming such a development. Given the significance of such an announcement, it would have been widely covered by the media if it were real. Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk reviewed the social media handles and official websites associated with Gautam Gambhir and the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI). However, no announcement or statement related to the alleged retirement was found on any of these platforms. If the claim were true, both Gambhir and the BCCI would have issued official statements. Significantly, the Desk also contacted senior PTI sports journalist Mona Parthsarthy, who categorically dismissed the claim. She stated that Gambhir has a strong professional presence and is expected to continue in his coaching role for a long time. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim regarding Gautam Gambhir announcing his retirement from all cricket-related roles is false.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video falsely shared as 'Haryana youth trapped in Russia seeking help from Indian authorities'
content: New Delhi, November 25 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video circulating on social media shows a man, seemingly on a battlefield, pleading for help. Users claimed that the clip features a youth from Haryana who was allegedly forced to fight in Russia and was now appealing to the Indian government to ensure his safe return. In the emotional message, the man urges viewers to share the video widely so it reaches the authorities, claiming that an intense battle is underway and that his fellow soldiers have died, leaving him as the only survivor. Several users also alleged that the youth had been duped into travelling to Russia and was forced to join the ongoing conflict. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it to be AI-generated . It does not show any Indian national in distress, and the clip has been falsely shared as real to mislead viewers. It is essential to clarify, however, that there are credible reports of Indian citizens being coerced into joining the Russian military to aid the country in its war against Ukraine. At least 44 Indian nationals are currently serving in the Russian Army. Many of them were reportedly taken to Russia under the pretext of studying in universities or securing jobs, but were later compelled to participate in the conflict. Recently, the Ministry of External Affairs reiterated that the issue has been raised with the Russian authorities and urged an end to such recruitment practices while working to secure the release of the Indians concerned. Claim On November 24, an X user named Ashok Danoda (@ashokdanoda) shared a video showing a youth from Haryana (allegedly fighting in the Russia–Ukraine war) pleading with the Indian government for his safe return to the country. The video purportedly showed the individual recording himself from the battlefield, urging viewers to circulate his message so that it reaches the authorities and help can be extended to him. In his emotional plea, he allegedly stated, "An intensive fight is going on here. All of my 10 fellow soldiers have died, and only I have been left alive." Moreover, the user, in his claim, also allegedly stated that the victim had arrived in Russia after being duped. He said, "Studying in India is very expensive, so the children of Haryana have gone to Russia. A war is going on there, so after giving the kids 10 days of training, they were sent to the battlefield. So far, the bodies of some of these youths have reached home, some are missing, and one surviving youth is seeking help from the Indian government. We will have to see if help reaches him or if his body will reach." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video garnered 277.1k views) Investigation The Desk first ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. One of the keyframes was analysed using Google Lens, which led to several social media posts sharing the same clip with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here respectively. Moreover, the Google Lens search result also led the Desk to a video shared by an Instagram handle named 'vsdipak576'. The Desk found that the user had shared the same video of the purported soldier depicted in the viral visuals on November 21, 2025. However, upon careful analysis of the video description, it was found that the user had already stated it was AI-generated and not a depiction of a real incident. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. A comparison image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral clip and the video posted by the Instagram user. Next, based on the findings above, the Desk ran the video through the AI detection tool Hive Moderation. The result indicated that 99.9% of the overall video is likely to contain AI-generated or deepfake content. Below is a screenshot of the result. Additionally, as part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find reports regarding Indian citizens being duped into fighting a war in Russia. The search led the Desk to a recent report published by The Times of India, which confirmed that at least 44 Indian nationals are currently serving in the Russian Army amid the Ukraine conflict. The report mentioned that these individuals were lured to Russia under the pretext of education or lucrative job opportunities but were later forced to fight in the war. Further, the report also included a statement by the Ministry of External Affairs, which said it has once again taken up the matter with Russian authorities to secure the release of the Indian citizens and to end the practice of such recruitment. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Significantly, the customised keyword search also led the Desk to another recent report published by The Hindu on November 3, 2025, which stated that a protest was held at Jantar Mantar by at least two dozen families of individuals who had been lured to Russia and were seeking the safe return of their kin. "The protesting family members said that agents 'lured' young men with lucrative job offers and promises of citizenship, and they were sent to the war zone," the report stated. Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that while reports of Indian citizens being coerced into joining the Russian Army and fighting in the war are true, the particular viral video under investigation was found to be AI-generated and falsely shared as real to mislead viewers.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Social media flooded with fake, misleading videos falsely claiming protests erupted in Bihar after election results; details inside
content: New Delhi, November 27 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Quickly after the recent Bihar assembly election results, social media was swamped with dramatic videos claiming to show violence, arson and clashes erupting after the NDA's victory. What followed wasn't just noise, it was a full-blown wave of misinformation, with dozens of posts stitching together unrelated, months-old or foreign footage to falsely link them to the Bihar verdict. From torch-lit marches to burning vehicles and chaotic street scenes, these clips flooded platforms, often accompanied by captions warning of statewide unrest. Many of them garnered thousands of views within hours. The Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk examined 10 of the most widely shared visuals. Every single one turned out to be misattributed, unrelated to the post-result scenario, or sourced from incidents that took place weeks or months earlier in different states, and in several cases, different countries. The pattern highlights how rapidly high-stakes political moments become fertile ground for recycled content and false narratives. Below is a detailed breakdown of the 10 viral posts that dominated timelines after the Bihar results and how each one unraveled under verification. Claim 1: A video showing a large crowd gathered at a location was shared by Instagram user '' the recently concluded Assembly election results, specifically in the Kaimur district. "As of today, November 15, 2025, there are reports of protests and political clashes in Bihar related to the recently concluded Assembly election results, specifically in the Kaimur district…," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation 1: When the Desk ran the video's keyframes through Reverse Image Search, it found the video uploaded to YouTube Shorts by 'warrior003' on June 23, 2025. The post's caption suggested the video is from a bullock cart race held in Maharashtra. The timeline and caption clarify that the video is not recent and is unrelated to the Bihar elections. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combined image highlighting the similarities in the content seen in the recent social media post and YouTube Shorts.
