Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised Google search and came across an Instagram post dated June 28, 2025. The caption along with the video mentions that a bullock cart race was organised at the Hindkesari Ground in Pedgaon, Satara, Maharashtra. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. The PTI Fact Check Desk had earlier debunked this same claim. The report can be read here . Subsequently, the Desk concludes that the video is not recent but dates back to June 2025 from a bullock cart race held in Maharashtra. It is not related to the Bihar or the recently held assembly elections. Claim 2: A video showing several vehicles charred and others on fire was shared by an Instagram user, 'mr_abhishek_yadav_302_', on November 18, claiming it was an incident from Bihar following the state's election results. "The youth of Muzaffarpur district, Bihar, are seen in a different environment. Bihar is going to be more dangerous than Nepal," read the overlaying text on the video. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation 2: On running the keyframes of the video through Reverse Image Search, the Desk found the same video shared by a Facebook user 'Ashish Sharma' on September 12, 2025. The caption mentioned that the video showed a protest in Nepal. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combined image highlighting the similarities between the content in the recent social media post and the old Instagram post. On further scanning the search results, the Desk also found an Instagram page named SA News Sikkim featuring the same video on September 10, 2025, claiming it was from the violence in Nepal. According to the caption, the video is from protests in Nepal where vehicles were set on fire near Singha Durbar due to anger over the social media ban. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Though the Desk could not independently verify the source of the video, it is, however, clear that the footage has been available on the internet at least since September. Claim 3: A video featuring a house-like structure engulfed in flames was shared by Instagram user 'deepakbbu312' on November 17, claiming it was the aftermath of a protest held in Bihar and linking it to the recent election results. "E Bihar ha modi ji. Galat state chun liya modi ne chori karne k liye," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation 3: Upon running the video's keyframes through Reverse Image Search, the Desk found the same video uploaded to Instagram by a user 'amu__4ever', which claimed that Birgunj mayor Rajesh Man Singh's house was set on fire by Gen X during the Nepal protest. "House of Rajesh Man Singh set into the fire by Gen-Z during the Protest in Birgunj, Nepal. He was the mayor of Birgunj," read a post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Taking a cue from the above finding, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports that cited the incident. The search led us to an X post by Press Trust of India on September 10, 2025. The caption accompanying the video also highlighted that the footage was from Birgunj Mayor Rajesh Man Singh's residence. "VIDEO | Nepal: Visuals from outside Birgunj Mayor Rajesh Man Singh's residence, which was vandalised and set afire during yesterday's protests," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a vandalised residence is not related to Bihar or any protest in the state following the elections. The footage dates back to September during the Gen Z protest in Nepal. Claim 4: A video showing a massive gathering of people was shared by an X user 'Parmanand Azamgarhi' on November 17, claiming that the entire state of Bihar had descended upon the Election Commission's house. "This video is said to be from Bihar. The entire state of Bihar has descended upon the Election Commission's house," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation 4: The Desk ran the video through the InVid tool search to extract the keyframes, and running the keyframes through Reverse Image Search, the Desk found that the same video was uploaded by a Facebook user 'Rahul YaduVanshi' on November 9, 2025. It predates the Bihar Assembly election results on 14 November 2025. This confirms that it cannot be from any protests in Bihar after the NDA's victory. The social media posts allege that it is from an RJD candidate's rally, as an RJD party flag can also be seen in the viral clip. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Though the Desk could not independently verify the video's source, it is clear that the footage predates the Bihar Assembly election results on 14 November 2025. This confirms that it cannot be from any protests in Bihar after the NDA's victory. Claim 5: A video of people apparently protesting, holding torches and banners and raising slogans, was shared by Instagram user 'gulbahar_choudhary8' on November 15, claiming the protest was held following the BJP's victory in the Bihar Assembly elections. "Protest held in Bihar following BJP's victory in Bihar," read the overlying text on the video. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot. Investigation 5: The Desk ran the video through the InVid tool search and extracted the keyframes. Upon running one of the keyframes through Reverse Image Search, the Desk found the same video uploaded to the official Instagram post of the Chhattisgarh Youth Congress on August 14. The post stated that the visuals are from the Youth Congress's Mashal rally in Raipur in August 2025, held in protest against the BJP and alleged vote theft. The timeline predates the Bihar Assembly election results by months. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combined image highlighting the similarities between the content in the recent social media post and the months-old post. The Desk also traced photos from the rally uploaded on the Facebook page of Chhattisgarh Bhilai Nagar MLA Devendra Yadav, on August 13, 2025. The rally was taken to the State Election Commission office in Raipur. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video is of the Youth Congress's Mashal rally in Raipur in August 2025, held in protest against the BJP and alleged vote theft. Claim 6: A video showing people with torches gathered in a market-like area was shared on Instagram on November 15, 2025, by an Instagram user, who claimed it was a protest rally against the BJP and JDU in Bihar, linking it to the aftermath of the results of the Bihar Assembly Elections 2025. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation 6: As part of the investigation, the Desk found that, though the caption stated it was a protest following the election result, the text on the video read '2 lakh teachers are protesting against BJP-JDU in Bihar'. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised Google search and found the same video uploaded to Instagram by the user 'mahuamoitrafans' on February 11, 2025. The text, along with the video, mentioned that teachers staged a protest in Bihar's Jehanabad earlier today against the competency test. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Our search also led us to a Facebook post by a user dated February 10, 2024. The text, along with the video, mentioned that 2 lakh teachers and students protested against the BJP-JDU Government in Bihar. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. In the above video, we also found a board with Begusarai written in Hindi. Below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video is not recent. Although we couldn't confirm the exact location of the video, it's clear that the footage predates the recent Bihar Assembly Elections. Claim 7: A video of a large crowd carrying torches in a procession was shared by a Facebook user, Sanjeev Kumar, on November 19, claiming to show protests against the Election Commission of India (ECI) and the BJP in Bihar after the election results. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot. Investigation 7: Upon running the keyframes of the video through Reverse Image Search, the Desk came across the same video uploaded on Instagram by a user 'deolichannel' on September 25, mentioning that a youth demonstration in Jaipur, organised to seek justice for the families of children killed in the Jhalawar school tragedy. The caption of the post below reads, "Naresh Meena is on a hunger strike at SMS Hospital. A massive torchlight procession was led by his son, Anirudh, to pay tribute to the children who died in the Jhalawar-Piplodi accident". Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combined image highlighting the similarities in the content of the social media post. The Desk also conducted a customised Google search for relevant media reports and found a NDTV report published on September 25, 2025. It highlighted that supporters of Naresh Meena held a torch procession in the streets of Jaipur on Thursday (September 25) night. Naresh Meena has been on a hunger strike for the last 14 days. He demands justice for the families of the children who died in the Piplodi school accident in Jhalawar. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concludes that the video is from a march organised in Jhalawar, Rajasthan, demanding justice for the children who died in a school accident. It has no link to the Bihar and Assembly elections. Claim 8: A video showing people pelting stones and vandalising vehicles was shared by an X user 'SHAAN SUNDAR' on November 17, claiming that it is post-result violence in Bihar. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot. Investigation 8: As part of the investigation, the Desk ran the keyframes through Reverse Image Search and found the same video uploaded to the Instagram post of 'citynewsrajkot' on October 12, which mentioned that police and farmers clashed at the AAP Kisan Mahapanchayat in Botad, Gujarat. "Police and farmers clash at AAP Kisan Mahapanchayat in Botad: Police fire tear gas after stone-pelting, three policemen injured, 20 detained; combing operation begins," read the caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Taking the investigation forward, the Desk also conducted a customised keyword search on Google to identify relevant media reports and came across a report published by the Times of India on October 12. The report highlighted that at least three cops were injured and 20 people detained after tension flared in Haddad village of Botad district after police moved in to disperse a gathering organised by the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) for a 'kisan mahapanchayat', which had been denied permission by the local administration. The report's cover image was similar to the content seen in the social media post. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video is months old, from October 12, 2025, and shows a farmer protest in Rajkot, Gujarat, organised by AAP in October 2025, during which violence occurred. Claim 9: A video depicting people vandalising public property and occupying a government building was shared by a Facebook user, Manirul Islam, on November 17, 2025, claiming that it showed the protest against the alleged vote theft in Bihar. "Protest tandav started in Bihar against theft of vote, it may slowly spread all over India. Once upon a time, maybe in Delhi too. Waiting to see what's happening now," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation 9: The Desk ran the video's keyframes through Reverse Image Search and found that a Facebook user uploaded the video on September 13, 2025. The post claimed that the video originated from Nepal. The timeline and the post's caption clarify that the video is not recent and is unrelated to the recent Bihar polls. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combined image highlighting the similarities in the content of the social media posts. The Desk then traced the building in the viral video to the District Administration Office in Chitwan, Nepal, and found that its architecture matched exactly, as shown in the comparison below. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the protest did not occur in Bihar on September 24, 2025. It depicts violence in Chitwan, Nepal, during Gen-Z protests in September 2025, when government offices, including the District Administration Office, were vandalised. Claim 10: A video of protesters holding a torchlight procession and shouting slogans was shared by a Facebook user, 'Political insight local', on November 17, claiming that it was a demonstration against the Election Commission after the Bihar elections. "Following the Bihar elections, people are protesting against the Election Commission. They allege vote theft; otherwise, how did the BJP win so many seats despite having a lower vote share than the RJD? #BiharElections #BiharPolitics," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation 10: The Desk ran the video through the InVid tool's search and extracted its keyframes. Upon running the keyframes of the footage through Reverse Image Search, the Desk found the same clip shared on the official X handle of NSUI Rajasthan on August 19, 2025. The post read, "NSUI Balotra organised a huge torchlight procession under the leadership of State President Vinod Jhakhar against the vote theft by the ECI BJP and pledged to protect democracy and wage a decisive struggle against vote theft." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Our search also led us to another Instagram post by NSUI Rajasthan President Vinod Jhakand, uploaded on August 19, 2025. The caption of the post read: "We all pledged to defend democracy and wage a decisive struggle against vote theft. The BJP and the Election Commission are jointly attacking democratic rights by stealing people's votes, but student power will not allow this conspiracy to succeed." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video is unrelated to the Bihar Elections and dates back to August.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2023 video of West Bengal railway station fire falsely shared as recent incident from New Delhi
content: New Delhi, November 27 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): As Delhi reels under the distressing memories of the massive blast near the Red Fort, which killed over 15 people and injured several others, another purported social media video showing a massive fire at a railway station was shared online with the claim that the incident also pertained to the national capital. The video allegedly showed a large fire erupting on a railway platform, with people at the scene immediately throwing objects onto the tracks. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found the video to be unrelated to Delhi. It was originally recorded in West Bengal and captured a fire that broke out at the Santoshpur railway station in Kolkata in April 2023. While the cause of the fire at the time remained unknown, it had reportedly taken firefighters several hours to extinguish the blaze. An old, unrelated video from West Bengal was falsely shared on social media as an incident in New Delhi. Claim On November 19, Instagram user Abhishek Verma (a74467906) shared a video purportedly depicting a massive fire at a railway station. The user claimed the incident had occurred at a railway station in New Delhi, just days after the massive blast near the Red Fort that killed over 15 people and injured several others. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was examined using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens results also led the Desk to a video shared on the ETV Bharat Facebook page. The handle had shared the same video of a fire on a railway platform, but the details confirmed the incident occurred in 2023 at the Santoshpur railway station in South 24 Parganas, West Bengal. At no point did the video depict any incident from New Delhi. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot: The image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral clip and the video shared on the news portal's Facebook page. Additionally, the Google Lens search results led the Desk to a news report published by the Times of India on April 6, 2023. The report also confirmed that the incident occurred in West Bengal, where a fire broke out at the Santoshpur railway station. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Further, the Desk conducted a customised Google search to determine whether any such incident, similar to the one depicted in the viral video, had occurred recently in New Delhi. However, the search yielded no credible news reports confirming such an event. Given the severity of the claim, any such real incident would have received widespread media coverage. Subsequently, based on the above findings, the Desk concluded that the video claiming to show a fire at a station in New Delhi is false. The footage originally depicted a 2023 fire incident at a railway station in West Bengal, not Delhi.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated image of a girl falsely linked to rescue of missing 4-year-old Aarohi in Varanasi
content: New Delhi, November 27 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared an image of a girl, claiming she was 4-year-old Aarohi, who had gone missing for six months but was recently traced at an orphanage in Varanasi by the Mumbai Police. The purported image, shared along with an emotional rescue story, showed the child standing with Mumbai Police officials after being found. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found that the image purportedly depicting 4-year-old Aarohi is AI-generated. While the story of the rescue of the missing child from a Varanasi orphanage is real, the photo circulating on social media has no connection to the incident. An AI-generated image was falsely shared on social media and linked to the genuine rescue of a 4-year-old girl from an orphanage in Varanasi. Claim An X user, Suresh (@isureshofficial), on November 26 shared a social media post accompanied by a heartwarming story about 4-year-old Aarohi from Mumbai, who had gone missing for 6 months and was recently traced at an orphanage in Varanasi by the Mumbai Police. The post also included a purported image of Aarohi with Mumbai Police officials after her rescue. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation To begin with the investigation, the Desk ran the viral image of a girl using Google Lens. The search led the Desk to multiple social media accounts that shared the same photo with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. To verify the image's authenticity, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google using the details from the viral post. The search led to a Times of India report published on November 25, 2025, covering the same rescue story of the 4-year-old. However, upon closer examination of the newspaper's image, it was found to differ from the photo circulating on social media. The image in the news report shows Aarohi (with her face blurred) standing alongside her parents and other individuals. In contrast, the image shared in the viral post shows the girl surrounded by uniformed people. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: A comparison image (below) clearly shows that the girl in the social media post does not match the real image of Aarohi shared in the news report. Continuing the investigation, the Desk ran the original image from the news report through Google Lens. This led to a post shared by the Mumbai Police on their official X handle on November 15, 2025. The Mumbai Police post detailed the investigation that led to Aarohi's rescue and included an image of the child (matching the one used in the Times of India report) from the Varanasi orphanage where she was found. This confirmed that the image used in the news report was authentic. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk examined the viral image for visual inconsistencies and found several elements indicating the image was AI-generated. For instance, the child's fingers appear distorted, and the face of an individual standing in the background is visibly warped. Below is a screenshot highlighting these findings. Following this, the Desk ran the viral image through the AI-detection tool SightEngine. The result indicated that the image is 99% AI-generated. Below is a screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the image circulating on social media was AI-generated and bore no connection to the real rescue of the 4-year-old girl.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Unrelated, old video clips shared in name of recent Tejas crash at Dubai Airshow; details inside
content: New Delhi, November 28 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A viral video showing an aircraft performing sharp aerobatic manoeuvres before spiralling down and crashing was shared widely on social media with the claim that it captured the moment the Indian Air Force's Tejas jet went down during its display at the Dubai Airshow on November 21. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk examined the footage using video verification tools, keyframe analysis, and reverse image search and found that it is not a single continuous recording of the crash. Instead, it is a stitched-together compilation of two unrelated videos: the opening segment shows a manoeuvre by an aircraft uploaded online days before the Tejas crash, while the final crash sequence matches footage of a Polish Air Force F-16 that went down during an airshow rehearsal in Radom, Poland, in August 2025. Claim: A video showing an aircraft performing aerobatics and, in the latter part of the footage, losing control and crashing on the ground was shared by Instagram user 'thefactthreads_' on November 22, claiming it depicted the Dubai Airshow incident. "At 2.08 pm (local time) on Friday, the Indian Air Force's Tejas jet was performing an aerial manoeuvre, enthralling the audience gathered at the Dubai Airshow. The next minute, it appeared to lose balance before nosediving and crashing, sending thick black smoke billowing from the crash site. The pilot of the aircraft, which has a near-perfect safety record, died in the incident, the IAF confirmed," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further review of the search results, the Desk found the same video, streamed on the NBC News YouTube channel on August 29, 2025. We found that the footage was similar to the one seen in the social media post. The report mentioned that a Polish Air Force F-16 that crashed during an airshow rehearsal, resulting in the pilot's death. The timeline and details make it clear that the video is unrelated to the Dubai Airshow. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the social media post and the news report. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised Google search for relevant media reports and came across a Reuters report dated August 29, 2025. The report highlighted that a Polish Air Force F-16 fighter jet crashed during a rehearsal for an airshow in Radom, central Poland, and the pilot died. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking the investigation forward, the Desk once again ran the extracted keyframes through Reverse Image Search to identify the initial portion of the footage and came across the same video uploaded to the YouTube channel AIRFORCE.IAF8 on November 18, 2025. The crash segment seen in the viral video does not appear in this clip. This upload predates the crash of the Tejas fighter jet on November 21, 2025. The caption read, "Tejas performs sharp turn manoeuvres at Dubai Airshow #DubaiAirshow #DAS2025 #DubaiAirshow2025 #IAF." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Notably, on November 21, 2025, an Indian Air Force (IAF) Tejas fighter jet crashed during its aerobatic display at the Dubai Airshow 2025. The pilot, Wing Commander Namansh Syal from Kangra, lost his life in the accident. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video is a compilation of two videos; in the first clip, an aircraft was performing manoeuvres predating the crash, and the video has been online since at least November 18, 2025. The second clip shows an aircraft crashing, which is from a Polish Air Force F-16 accident during an airshow rehearsal in Poland in August 2025, in which the pilot died.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2012 Syria explosion falsely shared as 'Israel blowing up a terrorist's body in Palestine'
content: New Delhi, November 28 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A dramatic video showing a blast tearing through a funeral procession was shared by several social media users. The video shows a large crowd carrying flags and chanting religious slogans during a funeral procession. Those sharing the footage claim that Israel placed a time bomb in the body of a terrorist and returned it to the Palestinians. However, the PTI's Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video of the explosion during the funeral procession is not from Palestine, but from an incident that took place in Syria in 2012. The video was shared with a false claim on social media. Claim: An X user shared a video of an explosion during a funeral procession for 'Dilip Kumar Singh' on November 23, claiming that Israel placed a time bomb in the body of a terrorist and returned it to the Palestinians. "Israel put a time bomb in a terrorist's corpse and returned it to the Palestinians. The result is in front of you; we, too, should learn something from Israel. The Indian Army should also do the same with terrorists," read the post's caption. The post clocked 366.8k views on social media. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation: The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further review of the search results, the Desk found the same video used by NBC News in a report published on July 2, 2012. The text alongside the video mentioned that it shows an attack on a funeral procession in Syria. The timeline and the details mentioned clarify that the video is not recent. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from the above finding, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search and came across a report by Al-Jazeera published on July 1, 2012. It stated that a massive explosion occurred during a funeral procession near Damascus, killing 133 people. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of the explosion during the funeral procession is not from Palestine, but from an incident that took place in Syria in 2012.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered video of Chief of Army Staff shared to falsely claim 'he confirmed Sonam Wangchuk's custodial death'; details inside
content: New Delhi, November 28 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of Chief of Army Staff General Upendra Dwivedi, in which he was purportedly seen offering condolences on the alleged death of Ladakh activist Sonam Wangchuk while in state custody, was recently shared online. The video appears to show the Army Chief expressing concern over the activist's alleged custodial death, claiming he had requested the central government to conduct a thorough and transparent inquiry into the matter. "All facts must be verified so that confidence in our institutions remains intact," the audio in the viral clip states. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk reviewed the circulating footage and found the video to be digitally manipulated. The audio had been altered and superimposed onto a genuine clip from General Dwivedi's address at the Chanakya Defence Dialogue 2025, held on November 27. At no point during his address did he make any such remark. Therefore, the claim circulating on social media is false. Claim An X user, @Mushk_0, on November 27 shared a video claiming that Indian Army Chief General Upendra Dwivedi offered condolences on the alleged custodial death of Ladakh activist Sonam Wangchuk. The video appears to show the Army Chief stating that he had asked the central government to initiate a thorough and transparent investigation into Wangchuk's supposed death. The user captioned the video: "Following the custodial death of Sonam Wangchuk, Indian Army chief Gen. Upendra Dwivedi offered condolences, now being suppressed by the media. Even the Army seems exhausted by Hindutva fascists forcing their own agenda." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video garnered 135.1k views) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was examined using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here ; their archived versions are available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search result also led the Desk to a PTI news report published on November 27, 2025, whose feature image exactly matched the keyframe used in the investigation. Upon reviewing the report, the Desk identified that the video of the Indian Army Chief was from the first day of the Chanakya Dialogue 2025, held on November 27, which he attended. However, nowhere in his speech at the event (as covered in the news report) did he make the alleged statement heard in the viral video. The report originally highlighted that, in his address at the inaugural session of the Chanakya Defence Dialogue, the Indian Army Chief "outlined a set of springboards that will drive the years of transformation ahead for the force, to remain decisive and future-ready in this rapidly evolving global landscape." Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Next, building on the findings above, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google about the event. This led to the creation of a YouTube channel named Strategic Frontlines, which uploaded the whole proceedings from Day 1 of the defence dialogue, including the same address by the Army Chief, from which the viral clip was purportedly taken. However, after carefully reviewing his entire address, the Desk found no instance where the Army Chief made the alleged statement about the Ladakh activist. The findings indicated that the audio heard in the viral clip was digitally generated and superimposed onto the original video to mislead viewers. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. A comparison image below highlights the background similarities between the viral video and the footage shared in the YouTube video, confirming they originate from the same event. In the next stage of the investigation, the Desk extracted the audio track from the viral video and analysed it using Google's AI detection tool, Resemble AI. The tool indicated that the voice in the clip was artificially generated. Below is a screenshot of the result: Additionally, the Desk carried out a customised keyword search to find any credible reports or official statements confirming the custodial death of Ladakh activist Sonam Wangchuk, who is reportedly booked under the NSA. However, no credible news reports supported this claim. Given the seriousness of the allegation, such an incident would have received widespread media coverage had it been true. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a digitally manipulated video of Indian Army Chief General Upendra Dwivedi was falsely shared online with a fabricated audio track to claim that he confirmed the custodial death of Ladakh activist Sonam Wangchuk.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of man assaulting a burqa-clad woman in Bangladesh falsely shared as incident from India
content: New Delhi, December 1 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A disturbing video of a man assaulting a woman in broad daylight was recently shared on social media with the claim that the attacker is a Hindu man assaulting a burqa-clad Muslim woman in India. The visuals show the woman collapsing to the ground after being struck on the head, allegedly by the enraged youth. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the claim and found that the video is not from India but depicts an incident in Bangladesh. Claim An X user, Parmanand Azamgarhi (@parmanandyadavv), on November 26 shared a video claiming it showed a Muslim woman in India being assaulted by a Hindu man. The video shows the woman collapsing to the ground after being struck on the head, allegedly by an enraged Hindu youth in broad daylight. The user captioned the post: "Sanatani people are mistreating women of other religions, especially Muslim women, and no action is being taken against these people. The Constitution grants equality to everyone." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing the story, the video garnered 384k views) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was examined using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. Next, to verify the video's authenticity—particularly the location where it was filmed—the Desk carefully analysed its visuals. During the review, the Desk noticed a poster or pamphlet pinned to a tree, which could help identify the location. The text on the poster, written in Bengali script, was zoomed in and translated into English. The translation revealed words such as "Madrasatul Ehsan Al-Islamia" and "in the academic year 2024." Below are two images: the first showing a zoomed-in view of the poster, and the second showing the Bengali-to-English translation. Next, using these clues, the Desk conducted a Google search with the extracted keywords. The search led to the Facebook page of an educational institution with the same name—Madrasatul Ehsan Al-Islamia—located in Dhaka, Bangladesh. Below is a screenshot of the institution's Facebook page. Additionally, the Desk carried out another customised keyword search to determine whether any institution with a similar name—Madrasatul Ihsan—exists in India. No notable institution by this name was found in India. The only well-known institution bearing this name was located in Bangladesh. In the next phase of the investigation, the Desk examined further clues to verify the claim. A vehicle passing by in the video displayed the words "JAC Motors" and "Energypac" on its front. Using this information, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search on Google and found a report published by the Industry Insider portal that highlighted a key link connecting Energypac and JAC Motors to Bangladesh. The report stated that Energypac, a leading electrical engineering company in Bangladesh, is the sole distributor of JAC Motors, a state-owned Chinese automobile and commercial vehicle manufacturer, in the country. The two companies had partnered back in 2006 to introduce advanced technologies and innovative automotive products to the Bangladeshi market. Significantly, this confirmed that the incident depicted in the video originated in Bangladesh and had no connection to India. Moreover, it was also found that JAC Motor's vehicles are not available in India. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a video of a Muslim woman being assaulted by a man in Bangladesh was falsely shared on social media as an incident from India.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video of man locating container full of iPhones floating in water falsely shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 1 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of a person standing on a boat, purportedly claiming that he had found a container filled with iPhones floating in the water, was recently shared on social media as a real incident. In the visuals, the individual, along with others on the boat, can be seen retrieving iPhones from the container. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the video does not depict a real incident, but is an AI-generated clip shared online to mislead viewers. Claim On December 1, an X account named Cleverly (@Cleverlydey4u) shared a video of a person standing on a boat, purportedly claiming that he had found a container filled with iPhones floating in the water. In the visuals, the individual, along with others on the boat, can be seen retrieving iPhones from the container. "They found a container leaking in the river, omo! Just look at the phones," the user captioned the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing, the video had garnered 1.9 million views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was examined using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search results also led the Desk to a video shared by Instagram user @oye_sanki_1 on November 29, 2025. It was found that this video matched the viral clip exactly. However, a closer examination revealed that the Instagram user had already clarified in the caption that the video depicting a supposed container full of iPhones was AI-generated and not a real incident. "The primary purpose of this video is purely educational and creative. It has been created to demonstrate how advanced modern Artificial Intelligence technology has become. All scenes, visuals, events, characters, reactions, and environments shown in the video are AI-generated. Nothing depicted here is real, and it should not be interpreted as a real incident, real discovery, or real footage," the user wrote in the description. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. A comparison image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral clip and the video posted by the Instagram content creator. As part of the investigation, the Desk also reviewed the user's Instagram profile and noted that the handle regularly shares AI-generated content. In the subsequent phase of the investigation, based on the inputs generated above, the Desk analysed the viral clip using the AI-detection tool Hive Moderation, which confirmed that 99 per cent of the footage contained AI-generated or deepfake elements. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video claiming to show a container full of iPhones floating in water is not real. It is an AI-generated clip that has been falsely shared on social media as an actual incident.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video of Indian soldiers calling Pakistan Army dangerous falsely shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 2 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported social media video containing testimonials of two Indian Army soldiers, in which they were allegedly seen calling the Pakistani Army dangerous, was recently shared online. The first visual showed a soldier named Mukesh allegedly criticising Prime Minister Narendra Modi while stating that India should not mess with Pakistan, as its army is very dangerous. The second visual depicted another soldier, named Prakash, continuously weeping and allegedly stating that the Pakistani Army would not spare their lives. "The Pakistani Army is very dangerous. I request the Indian government to please arrange for our safe return," the soldier is heard saying. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the video does not depict any real incident but is an AI-generated clip falsely shared as real to mislead viewers. Claim A Facebook user, Muhammad Arshad, on November 27 shared a video attached with two purported testimonials of Indian Army soldiers, in which they allegedly called the Pakistani Army dangerous. The first visual showed a soldier named Mukesh allegedly criticising Prime Minister Narendra Modi while stating that India should not mess with Pakistan, as its army is very dangerous. The second visual depicted another soldier, Prakash, continuously weeping and allegedly saying that the Pakistani Army would not spare their lives. "The Pakistani Army is very dangerous. I request the Indian government to please arrange for our safe return," the soldier stated. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video garnered 2.2k views) Investigation The Desk first ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. One of the keyframes was analysed using Google Lens, which led several social media accounts to share the same clip with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a video shared by an Instagram handle named 'green_travel_graphy', as its visuals matched those of the viral clip. It was found that the handle 'green_travel_graphy' was the first to share the purported video depicting the testimonials of two soldiers on November 17, long before other accounts picked it up. However, upon carefully analysing the video to check its authenticity, the Desk found multiple anomalies suggesting that it was AI-generated. For instance, the soldiers' lip movements in the video appeared unnatural. Here is the link and archive link to the video, along with a screenshot of the findings suggesting that the footage is AI-generated. Next, using cues from the findings above, the Desk ran the video through the AI-detection tool Hive Moderation. The result showed that 99.9% of the footage was likely AI-generated or deepfake content. Below is a screenshot of the result. In the subsequent part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google keyword search to check whether any such videos of soldiers had been shared initially. The search did not lead to any credible news reports confirming such an incident. Given the intensity of the claim, had it been authentic, media outlets would have widely covered it. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an AI-generated video of Indian soldiers calling the Pakistani Army dangerous was falsely shared online as a real incident to mislead viewers.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old, unrelated video falsely shared as final rites of Bollywood actor Dharmendra; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 2 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a large crowd surrounding a flower-adorned vehicle was circulated on social media with the claim that it captured the final rites of veteran Bollywood actor Dharmendra, who passed away on November 24. The clip prompted emotional responses online, with users believing they were watching the actor's funeral procession. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk reviewed the visuals using keyframe analysis and reverse image searches and found that the clip has no connection to Dharmendra's funeral. The footage has been online since September 2025. Additional searches confirmed that Dharmendra's funeral was held at the Pawan Hans Crematorium in Mumbai. The evidence makes it clear that the viral video was misrepresented and has no link to the actor's last rites. Claim: A video featuring a large crowd gathered around a vehicle decorated with flowers, resembling a funeral procession, was shared by an Instagram user 'sayman_bhagve_09' on November 24, claiming that it was the final rites procession of veteran Bollywood actor Dharmendra. "Dharmendra, the superstar, passed away. How much love is there for the people who love him?" read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further review of the search results, the Desk came across another Instagram post dated September 21 featuring the same video. The caption alongside the footage mentioned it was Zubeen Garg's funeral procession. The post's timeline clarifies that the footage is not recent and is unrelated to actor Dharmendra's funeral. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Taking a cue from the above finding, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant media reports. The search led us to a YouTube video report by India Times on September 22, 2025. The description mentioned that thousands in Guwahati bid an emotional farewell to singer Zubeen Garg. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. The search also led us to another report published by The New Indian Express on September 21, 2025, highlighting that people gather as the mortal remains of singer Zubeen Garg are being taken to his residence from the Guwahati airport. "The mortal remains of singer Zubeen Garg were brought to Guwahati from New Delhi in a special flight. Tens of thousands of people had been waiting outside the airport and along a road in the city since Saturday night in anticipation of the arrival of the legend – a composer, lyricist, music director, music producer, actor, film director, film producer, screenwriter, and above all, philanthropist and young generation's heartthrob," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. As part of the investigation, the Desk conducted another set of customised keyword searches regarding actor Dharmendra's death and came across a video report published by NDTV. It highlighted that the film industry mourns the loss of the legendary Dharmendra (89), Bollywood's original 'He-Man', who passed away in Mumbai. His funeral was held at the Pawan Hans Crematorium. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video predated Dharmendra's death and had been available on the internet since at least September 2025.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Fabricated letter falsely claims 'IAF Chief praised Pakistan's defence capabilities'; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 2 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A letter circulating on social media attributed to Indian Air Force Chief Air Chief Marshal AP Singh claims he praised Pakistan's defence capabilities and acknowledged the loss of a Rafale jet in a supposed clash with Pakistan. The document shared appears to carry the IAF insignia and the Air Chief's photograph, giving it the impression of an official communication. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk gave a closer look and found that the letter has been digitally altered. The original message released by the Indian Air Force on November 30 contains none of the claims being circulated. Instead, it offers a formal greeting for Defence Partnership Days 2025, with no reference to Pakistan, Rafale jets or any defence comparison. An examination of the viral version shows inconsistencies in formatting, font, bullet points and distorted insignia, indicating manipulation. The post was shared with a false claim on social media. Claim: A purported letter attributed to Indian Air Force Chief Air Chief Marshal AP Singh, allegedly signed by him, was shared by an X user 'PakistanPulse' on November 30, claiming that he allegedly praised Pakistan's capabilities and talked about the loss of a Rafale jet in a clash with Pakistan. "Indian Air Force Chief praises Pakistan Air Force in the greetings message of Defence Partnership Day 2025. Despite fewer resources & older equipment, Pakistan continues to surprise us. Their creativity and enthusiasm remain impressive, a reminder that innovation isn't just about tech," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation As part of the investigation, the Desk first checked the official X handle of the Indian Air Force and came across the original letter uploaded on November 30. After analysing the letters, the Desk found that both contained the picture of Air Force Chief Air Chief Marshal AP Singh and the IAF insignia, but upon closer inspection, there were many differences. "The Chief of the Air Staff, Air Chief Marshal AP Singh, conveys his best wishes for the success of Defence Partnership Days 2025 being organised by the Centre for Aerospace Power & Strategic Studies (CAPSS) and Indian Military Review (IMR) on 1-2 Dec 2025 at Manekshaw Centre, New Delhi. The event will foster closer cooperation between the Armed Forces and the defence industry to identify sources of indigenous supply, import substitution and resilient supply chains towards a more Atmanirbhar Bharat," read the post's caption. The letter does not talk of Rafale fighter jets or praise Pakistan's defence capabilities. Here is the link to the X post, and below is a screenshot of the same. On reviewing the letter circulating on social media, the Desk found discrepancies, including a mismatched font: the original had four bullet points, while the circulating version had five. Moreover, there were spacing issues; the IAF insignia in the viral letter revealed distortion, suggesting possible digital tampering. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the letter is fabricated. The original letter does not contain praise for Pakistan.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: A digitally altered video of Shah Rukh Khan explaining meaning of 'jihad' in front of PM Modi shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 3 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of Bollywood actor Shah Rukh Khan, in which he was allegedly heard explaining the meaning of "jihad" in front of Prime Minister Narendra Modi at an event, was recently shared online. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found the video to be digitally altered. While the visuals are from a 2019 event where Shah Rukh Khan met PM Modi, the audio segment mentioning "jihad" was taken from a 2011 event in Pune, where the actor attended a book launch. An old, unrelated statement made by Shah Rukh Khan in 2011 was superimposed over his visuals from the 2019 event, which also featured PM Modi. Claim On November 24, an X handle with the username @MR_COOL77777 shared a video of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Bollywood actor Shah Rukh Khan attending an event. The video allegedly showed the latter explaining the meaning of "jihad" to the audience, to which the Prime Minister was seen nodding in agreement. The user shared the video with the caption: "Shahrukh Khan, the world's richest man and Bollywood's biggest superstar, is explaining the true meaning of jihad to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, and he is nodding in agreement." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing, the video had garnered 58.8K views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVID tool, extracting multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was examined using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here ; their archived versions are available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search result also led the Desk to a video posted by the YouTube channel OneIndia Hindi on October 22, 2019. The Desk found that the visuals in this video matched those in the viral clip exactly. However, upon analysing the extended footage, it was found that Shah Rukh Khan did not explain the meaning of "jihad" at the event in front of PM Modi. This indicated that the viral video had been digitally altered. Initially, the video was from a 2019 meeting in which Prime Minister Modi met Bollywood actors and filmmakers, including Shah Rukh Khan, to discuss initiatives marking the 150th birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi. During his speech at the event, while PM Modi stood beside him, Shah Rukh Khan stated, "I truly believe that Gandhiji needs to be reloaded. Gandhiji 2.0 is what we need, because the world is changing. You have digitalised everything." Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot: The image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral clip and the original YouTube video. Next, based on the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised Google search and found a report published by The Hindu that extensively covered the 2019 meeting between PM Modi and members of the film fraternity. However, the report did not mention Shah Rukh Khan speaking about "jihad". Here is the link to the news story published by The Hindu, along with a screenshot: In the subsequent part of the investigation, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search to determine whether Shah Rukh Khan had ever made the statement heard in the viral video. This led the Desk to a video uploaded by a YouTube channel named "tejgyan" on November 17, 2011. The video showed Shah Rukh Khan attending a book release event in Pune in November 2011, where he made the statement heard in the viral video. At around the 09:30 mark, Shah Rukh Khan was heard saying: "I belong to Islam, I am a Muslim. We have a word that is often misused: Jihad. The thought process behind jihad is the same: fighting and conquering the evil thoughts within us is called jihad. Killing people on the streets is not jihad." Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. This confirmed that while the audio used in the viral video was authentic, it had been taken out of context and digitally overlaid onto unrelated footage from the 2019 event. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a digitally altered video of Shah Rukh Khan was falsely shared as though he spoke about "jihad" in front of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video of an elephant rescuing a dog from floodwaters falsely shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 3 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of an elephant rescuing a dog stuck in floodwaters was recently shared on social media, claiming it was a real incident. The video allegedly shows an elephant wading through a strong current of floodwater to rescue a dog that had taken shelter on the roof of a house. The visuals show the elephant eventually lifting the dog with its trunk to safety. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found that the video is AI-generated and was falsely shared as a real incident to mislead viewers. Claim An X user named Unmai Kasakkum, on November 29, shared a video depicting an elephant purportedly saving the life of a dog stuck amid heavy flooding. The video allegedly shows an elephant walking through a strong stream of floodwater to reach a dog that had taken shelter on the roof of a house. The visuals show the elephant finally rescuing the dog, holding it with its trunk. The user captioned the post: "This elephant is a true hero, helping the dog escape the floodwaters. Love the nature." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing, the video had garnered 627,000 views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was then examined with Google Lens, which led several social media accounts to share the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here ; their archived versions are available here and here , respectively. To verify the authenticity of the video, the Desk carefully analysed it and identified multiple anomalies indicative of AI generation. For instance, the elephant's tusk suddenly appears, then disappears, and then reappears in the video. Additionally, the background audio also seems unnatural and inconsistent. These inconsistencies clearly suggest that the video is AI-generated. A screenshot highlighting these anomalies is provided below. Next, based on the above findings, the Desk ran the video through the AI detection tool Hive Moderation. The results indicated that 99.9% of the overall video is likely to contain AI-generated or deepfake content. A screenshot of the result is provided below. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an AI-generated video of an elephant rescuing a dog from floodwaters was falsely shared on social media as a real incident to mislead viewers.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of PM Modi pausing his speech during Delhi rally shared with false claim of teleprompter malfunction; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 3 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of Prime Minister Narendra Modi pausing during a public address has been circulating online with the claim that he stopped mid-speech because the teleprompter malfunctioned. The clip, widely shared on social media, prompted quick jabs and commentary, with users insisting the pause revealed a technical glitch during the rally. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk reviewed the footage and traced it back to an earlier rally from January 2025, not the recent event it is being misrepresented as. A closer examination of the full speech shows that Modi paused only because the crowd broke into loud chants, not due to any teleprompter issue. Claim: A video featuring PM Modi addressing a public rally was shared by an X user, Manish Rj' on November 30, claiming that he stopped mid-speech due to a malfunction in the teleprompter. PM Modi can be seen pausing his speech during the public address. "Phir se Teleprompter band ho gaya. Har jagah beizzati ho jaati hai bechare ki…," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . As part of the investigation, the Desk ran the extracted keyframes through a reverse image search and found the same video uploaded to the official YouTube channel of Narendra Modi. The video was aired on January 5, 2025, and he was addressing a rally in Rohini, Delhi. The timeline thus clarifies that the video is not recent. Upon further analysis of the video, the Desk found that at 13 minutes 8 seconds, PM Modi, while speaking about laying the foundation stone for several development projects, briefly paused as the crowd began chanting slogans. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot. Moreover, the Desk also conducted a customised Google search for relevant media reports citing a teleprompter malfunction during PM Modi's speech. The search did not yield any reports, and given the issue, such a report would have been covered by all media outlets. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video is not recent and dates back to January 5, 2025. Moreover, PM Modi did not pause mid-speech because of a teleprompter glitch, but because people were chanting slogans.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old Kolkata flood video falsely linked to Chennai rains amid Cyclone Ditwah
content: New Delhi, December 4 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): As the weakened cyclonic storm Ditwah brought incessant and widespread rain across Chennai, a video showing waterlogged roads and cars half-submerged in floodwater circulated widely on social media this week, with users claiming it captured the impact of the ongoing rains in Chennai. The clip spread quickly, fuelling worry online as Tamil Nadu continued to grapple with heavy showers triggered by Cyclone Ditwah. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the footage has nothing to do with Chennai. The same video has been online since September 2025, when it was shared from Kolkata after intense rainfall flooded parts of the city. The evidence shows the viral clip predates the current weather events and misrepresents the situation in Tamil Nadu. Claim: A video showing severe flooding on the roads, with several cars partially submerged, was shared by X user Anveshka Das on December 2, claiming it depicted the current situation in Chennai. "Chennai in Rain," read the post's caption. The post clocked 15.8k views on social media. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a Facebook post by a user named 'Kais Kalim' on September 25, featuring the same video of the floods as seen in the recent social media post. The caption, along with the video, mentions that it shows the situation in Kolkata. "Park Circus 7-point Kolkata on 23rd September..," read the post's caption. The timeline and the post's text clarify that the video is not recent and is unrelated to the floods in Chennai, Tamil Nadu. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combined image highlighting the similarities between the content in the recent social media post and a month-old post. Furthermore, on closer analysis of the video, the Desk found a vehicle with a yellow licence plate bearing the WB registration, indicating West Bengal. Below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk noticed the hoardings with "Royal Indian Restaurant", " Golden Meat Shop," "Reliance Optician" written on them. Taking clues from the same, the Desk using geo-location located the site seen in the footage in Kolkata. This confirms that this road is not in Chennai, but in Kolkata. Below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised Google search for relevant media reports on the floods in Kolkata and came across a Reuters report published on September 25, 2025. The report highlighted that at least 12 people died as heavy rain lashed the eastern Indian city of Kolkata and surrounding areas ahead of a major festival, flooding streets, disrupting transport, and leaving residents stranded for hours. Here is the link to the report. However, the Desk could not independently verify when the video was initially recorded, but the video has been available on the internet at least since September 2025. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the location is not Chennai and predates the current bout of incessant rainfall in Tamil Nadu. The video claiming to show extensive flooding in Chennai amid incessant rain following Cyclone Ditwah is false.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered video shared to falsely claim 'BSF IG Ashok Yadav admitted failure in para-troops counter-terror efforts'
content: New Delhi, December 5 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video of IG, BSF Kashmir Frontier Ashok Yadav, in which he was allegedly seen highlighting his force's recent failure in counter-terrorism operations. In the purported video, the senior BSF official was allegedly heard claiming that zero terrorists had been eliminated this year, while the intelligence branch had spent most of the year misidentifying cows, shadows and, occasionally, their own patrols as high-value threats. "As for the 100–120 terrorists allegedly waiting to infiltrate across the LoC, our latest assessment suggests they might already be inside, perhaps running small businesses by now," the official was claimed to have said. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found the video to be digitally manipulated during its investigation. While the visuals were taken from a genuine press briefing, a fabricated audio track was overlaid to attribute statements to the senior official falsely. Claim An X handle with the username Hawk's Eye (@Hawkss_eye), on December 1, shared a video on IG featuring BSF Kashmir Frontier Ashok Yadav, in which he was allegedly seen highlighting his force's recent failure in counter-terrorism operations. In the purported statement given to the media, the senior BSF official reportedly claimed that zero terrorists had been neutralised in 2025, while also stating that 100–120 terrorists had infiltrated across the Line of Control (LoC) and might already be inside Indian territory. The official was also allegedly heard stating that the force had achieved "zero" success in counter-terrorism operations because the Centre had refused to provide procurement budgets and funds. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing, the video had garnered 125.3K views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was then examined using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here ; their archived versions are available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens results also led the Desk to a video shared by Kashmir-based news portal Daily Excelsior on December 1, 2025. The footage was found to be an extended version of the clip shared in the viral post, with identical background visuals in both versions. However, when the Desk analysed the video to verify whether Yadav originally made the purported statement heard in the viral clip, it found no such mention. In the original clip, IG, BSF Kashmir Frontier Ashok Yadav is heard stating that the G Unit of the BSF is monitoring all 69 launching pads along the LoC, where around 100 to 120 terrorists are currently waiting to infiltrate, and not that they had already entered Indian territory. In the same video, the senior BSF official is also heard stating that, in close coordination with the Indian Army and other sister agencies, the BSF Kashmir Frontier achieved significant operational success during 2025–26. He did not state that zero terrorists had been neutralised. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. A comparison image below highlights the background similarities between the viral video and the original footage, confirming that they originate from the same event. Additionally, drawing on the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised Google search for keywords related to the press briefing held by the senior BSF official on December 1, 2025. The search led to a Hindustan Times news report that included statements similar to those in the original video, not the claims made in the viral clip. This further indicated that the viral video had been digitally manipulated. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. In the next stage of the investigation, using the findings above, the Desk extracted the audio track from the viral video. It analysed it with the AI audio detection tool Resemble AI. The tool indicated that the voice in the clip was artificially generated. Below is a screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a digitally manipulated video of IG, BSF Kashmir Frontier Ashok Yadav, was falsely shared online, with a fabricated audio track, to claim that he had highlighted the force's failure in counter-terrorism operations.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Fake, fabricated document shared to falsely claim 'India requested former Pak PM Imran Khan's custody'; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 5 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A screenshot of a document marked "Top Secret" and attributed to India's Ministry of External Affairs is circulating on social media with the claim that the Indian government formally requested Pakistan to transfer former Prime Minister Imran Khan to India for his personal security as a "political prisoner". However, the PTI Fact Check Desk examined the viral document, cross-checked official sources, and found that the letter is fabricated. The Desk noticed several formatting inconsistencies that hinted it was fake and showed that India made no such request to Pakistan regarding Imran Khan. Claim: An X user shared a document purportedly issued by the Ministry of External Affairs, 'Abubakar Qassam', on December 1, with "Top Secret" written on the document, claiming that the Indian government formally requested Pakistan to transfer former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan, currently in jail, to India for his "personal security" as a political prisoner. "Breaking News: Top secret letter of the Indian Ministry of External Affairs gets leaked on Social Media. Indian Government has requested Pakistan to send Imran Khan as a political prisoner to India just like Haseena Wajid," read the post's caption. The post clocked 15.4k views on social media. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the alleged document through Reverse Image Search and found that several other users had also shared the same post with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here . On careful analysis of the alleged document, the Desk found several inconsistencies that suggested it might be a fabricated or fake document. For instance, the "Top Secret" stamp in the top-right corner appears visually inconsistent with official government markings, and there are inconsistencies in the text and spacing. Normally, an official document uses the same font, style, and correct punctuation marks that were missing for the document in question. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same. Moreover, in the purported document, the Desk noticed that it refers to the former Pakistan PM as "Imran Ahmed Khan Niazi." But the official Indian communications addressed him as "Imran Khan". The viral document uses phrases such as "political prisoner," terminology that is unlikely to appear in formal diplomatic correspondence between India and Pakistan. Here is the link to the report carrying the official document As part of the investigation, the Desk checked the Ministry of External Affairs' official website, press releases, and public statements, and found no reference to such communication. Here is the link to the official website. Taking the investigation forward, the Desk checked MEA's PAI (Pakistan, Afghanistan & Iran) Division, which also yielded no record of any such letter. The PTI Fact Check Desk had debunked another fake document attributed to Air Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singh. Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the alleged document is fake and is being shared with an incorrect claim.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, IAF did not escort Russian President Vladimir Putin's plane into Indian airspace during his recent India visit; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 7 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): On the margins of Russian President Vladimir Putin's recently concluded state visit to India, a social media video was circulated online claiming to show IAF fighter jets escorting President Putin's aircraft as it entered Indian airspace. The visuals showed President Putin watching the military jets' manoeuvres from aboard his plane as it was escorted through Indian airspace. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk, upon investigation, found the video to be unrelated to President Putin's recent visit to India. The viral footage actually consists of visuals from two separate visits in 2017 and 2019. The first shows Su-35 fighter jets escorting President Vladimir Putin to land at the Khmeimim air base in western Syria during an unannounced visit in 2017. The second shows Putin's 2019 visit to the Chkalov Flight Test Centre in Akhtubinsk. Old and unrelated footage from two different events was falsely circulated and linked to his recent visit to India. Claim On the margins of President Vladimir Putin's state visit to India, an X user named @RealWahidaAFG shared a video claiming that the leader's aircraft was escorted by Indian Air Force fighter jets as it entered Indian airspace. The visuals showed President Putin looking at the manoeuvres of military jets from aboard his plane. The user wrote, "IAF fighter jets guiding President Putin's aircraft as it enters Indian airspace. A moment that captures trust, respect, and a partnership built over decades. Long live the friendship between India and Russia." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video had garnered 232.6k views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was then examined using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here ; their archived versions are available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search results also led the Desk to a video posted by the YouTube channel US Plus. The Desk found that the visuals in that video matched those from the viral clip. However, a closer analysis revealed that the footage was not recent, but dated back to 2017, when Su-35 fighter jets escorted President Vladimir Putin to the Khmeimim air base in western Syria during an unannounced visit. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. | The image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral clip and the YouTube channel's video. Next, taking cues from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search regarding Su-35 fighter jets escorting President Vladimir Putin to Syria. The search result led the Desk to a news report published by Russia's state-controlled international network, RT International, on December 16, 2017, that elaborated on the mission's details. The report quoted one of the pilots who covered President Putin's plane, who said the jets were "heat traps" ready to take possible enemy missiles upon themselves. The report also included a statement from President Putin, in which he thanked the airmen, saying: "The pilots — those guys — I watched them. They were not just flying nearby. During landing, they descended to fly below our plane. I am thankful to them and want them to hear and know that." Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Moreover, during the investigation, the Desk found that the final five seconds of the 30-second viral clip — particularly the visuals showing jets in the sky — did not match the footage from President Putin's 2017 visit to Syria. To verify these visuals, the Desk ran those keyframes through Google Lens. The search results led to a video posted on the official website of the President of Russia on May 14, 2019, which confirmed that the visuals were from President Putin's visit to the Chkalov Flight Test Centre in Akhtubinsk. Here is the link to the report. A comparison image below highlights the visual similarities between the final visuals of the viral clip and the footage shared on the official website. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old and unrelated video, comprising footage from President Vladimir Putin's visits in 2017 (Syria) and 2019 (Akhtubinsk), was falsely circulated on social media and misleadingly linked to his recent state visit to India.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Edited video shared to falsely claim 'PM Modi announced gold giveaway scheme for Aadhaar card holders'
content: New Delhi, December 8 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of PM Modi addressing a public gathering is circulating on social media with the claim that he promised one tola of gold to every Aadhaar card holder, provided no member of the family was employed in a government job. The clip, shared thousands of times, includes audio purportedly of the Prime Minister making the announcement, leading many users to believe it is a newly launched welfare scheme. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the footage and found it to be from a 2019 event in Gorakhpur, and there is no record or official announcement of any such scheme. The audio in the video has been manipulated to create a false impression, making the viral claim entirely fabricated. The footage was digitally altered and falsely shared on social media. Claim: A video featuring PM Modi addressing a gathering was shared by a Facebook user, 'Fryder01', on December 4, claiming that the Prime Minister announced that one tola of sona would be free for Aadhaar cardholders, provided no family member is in a government job.
