In the video, PM can be heard saying, "Even though the price of gold is skyrocketing, one tola sona will be given free to all Aadhaar card holders, but no one in the family should have a government job" The post clocked 45.7k likes and 2.3k shares on social media. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation: The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . As part of the investigation, the Desk first conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find relevant reports that cite PM Modi announced such a scheme. However, we found no credible media reports or official announcements supporting these claims. If such schemes had been announced, they would have been widely covered by multiple media outlets. Taking the investigation forward, the Desk also scanned the MyScheme portal of the Government of India and PIB press releases to determine whether any of the schemes mentioned in the viral claims had been recently announced or launched. The search, however, did not lead to any release or statement. Here is the link to the MyScheme portal and PIB The Desk once again ran the extracted keyframes through Reverse Image Search and found the original video of PM Modi, streamed on the official YouTube channel of PMO India on February 24, 2019. He was addressing the launch of the PM Kisan Samman Nidhi Yojana in Gorakhpur, UP. The timeline and the description mentioned clarify that the video is not recent. Upon listening to the entire 56 minutes and 34 seconds speech, the Desk found that he did not mention giving free gold to the people anywhere in the address. Here is the link to the address, and below is a screenshot. The attire in the YouTube video matched the viral clip being circulated on social media. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities. Furthermore, the Desk extracted the audio from the video and ran it through Resemble AI, an AI-detection tool, which found the voice was authentic but may be an impersonation. Below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video featuring PM Modi announcing free gold to Aadhaar cardholders is manipulated and fake.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old Goa Airport Garba video shared to link it to recent IndiGo flight cancellations falsely
content: New Delhi, December 8 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): After IndiGo cancelled hundreds of flights across India this week, failing to make sufficient changes to its roster planning to accommodate new government norms, a video of people dancing in a closed premises was shared by several social media users. Those sharing the video claim that passengers performed Garba at Goa Airport after a flight delay, linking to the recent widespread flight cancellations However, the PTI Fact Check investigated and found that the video in question is neither recent nor related to the current cancellations. The footage dates back to September 2025, when a Surat-bound flight scheduled to depart from Goa was delayed due to a technical issue. According to reports, the passengers were looking forward to going to Surat and participating in the Navratri festivities. The video was shared with a false claim on social media. Claim: A video showing a group of people dancing inside a closed premises was shared by an X user 'Dr MJ Augustine Vinod' on December 5, claiming that passengers performed Garba at Goa Airport after a flight delay, linking to the recent widespread IndiGo flight cancellations. "WANT TO MAKE A LEMONADE FROM A LEMON 🍋? Learn from Gujjus PS Okay ! I get it, it was Goa!! Gujjus going back to a dry state may have been HAPPY !! Notwithstanding," read the post's caption. The post clocked 13.9k views on social media. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found that an Instagram post by the user 'heraldo_goa' featured the same video as seen in the social media post. The Instagram post dated September 30 mentioned that after a five-hour delay of a flight from Goa to Surat, passengers and airline staff at Goa airport turned the wait into a festive celebration by performing Garba together. "After a five-hour delay of a flight from Goa to Surat, passengers and airline staff at Goa airport turned the wait into a festive celebration by performing Garba together. A flight attendant arranged speakers, bringing everyone into the dance, and a video of the lively event quickly went viral on social media," read the post's caption. The post's timeline therefore clarifies that the video is not recent and is unrelated to the recent IndiGo flight cancellations. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk then conducted a set of customised keyword searches on Google to find relevant media reports. The search led us to a report by NDTV published on September 30, 2025, mentioning that passengers performed Garba at Goa Airport due to a flight delay. The report also included snippets from the recent viral video circulating on social media. "The flight attendant arranged for speakers, bringing everyone together for Garba. The video of passengers and airline staff dancing has gone viral," read the report. "Surat-bound flight was scheduled to depart from Goa at 5 pm on Sunday. Passengers were looking forward to going to Surat and participating in Navratri festivities, particularly Garba. But the flight was delayed due to a technical issue," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Our search also led us to the same video uploaded to Times Now's Facebook page, which mentioned that a flight delay at Goa airport turned into a joyous celebration as passengers spontaneously broke into Garba. "A flight delay at Goa airport turned into a joyous celebration as passengers spontaneously broke into Garba, filling the terminal with dance, music, and festive cheer," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of Garba, which was recently circulated, linking it to the IndiGo flight cancellation, is false. The video dates back to September 2025 and is unrelated to the recent happenings.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2018 image of passengers stranded on Delhi airport tarmac falsely linked to ongoing IndiGo crisis
content: New Delhi, December 8 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): As IndiGo continues to struggle with widespread cancellations and delays, social media has been flooded with posts claiming to show the scale of the disruption. One such post features passengers sitting on the airport tarmac beside an IndiGo aircraft, presented as a scene from the ongoing crisis. However, the PTI Fact Check examined the image and found that the photo is not recent at all, and has no link to the current wave of cancellations. The picture actually dates back to 2018, when a thunderstorm disrupted flight operations at IGI Airport. The prolonged wait for passengers on IndiGo's Delhi–Bengaluru flight 6E 2977 was primarily due to the non-availability of crew. This clarifies that the photograph was shared with a false claim on social media. Claim: A picture depicting a few passengers sitting on the airport tarmac near an IndiGo aircraft was shared by an X user 'Fundamental Investor' on December 4, claiming that it reflected the recent crises of IndiGo flight cancellations. "Modiji had promised that he would make railway stations as Classy as Airports. Now, Airports & Lounges have become like Railway stations," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the picture through Reverse Image Search and found that several other users had shared the same post with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further review of the search results, the Desk came across a report by The Economic Times that featured the same image seen in the recent social media post. The report published on May 14, 2018, stated that an IndiGo Delhi-Bengaluru flight was parked on the Delhi airport tarmac for more than 7 hours until early morning due to crew unavailability, with passengers kept waiting in the shuttle, inside the plane, or on the tarmac. The report's timeline clarifies that the image is not recent and is unrelated to recent flight cancellations. "IndiGo passengers stranded on tarmac for 7 hours for non-availability of crew," read the headline of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised Google search and found a Times of India report published on May 15, 2018, that highlighted a thunderstorm disrupting flight operations at IGI Airport. The prolonged wait for passengers on IndiGo's Delhi–Bengaluru flight 6E 2977 was primarily due to the non-availability of crew. The aircraft finally departed nearly seven hours late, after passengers spent considerable time waiting in the shuttle, inside the plane and on the tarmac. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. More than 450 IndiGo flights were cancelled across various airports on Monday (December 8) as operations at the country's largest airline were yet to return to normal, with disruptions continuing for the seventh straight day in an air travel crisis of a scale India has never witnessed. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the image circulating on social media linking to the recent flight cancellations actually dates back to 2018 and is unrelated to the recent events.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated image of Putin reading Bhagavad Gita falsely shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 8 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A picture claiming to show Russian President Vladimir Putin reading the Russian edition of the Bhagavad Gita aboard his aircraft went viral on social media, shortly after Prime Minister Narendra Modi gifted him a copy during their recent meeting in New Delhi. The image spread quickly, amplified by several accounts that framed it as a candid moment from Putin's return journey. However, the PTI Fact Check investigated and reviewed the claim through reverse image search, official social media scans, media reports, and AI-detection checks. The investigation found no authentic photograph of Putin reading the book on his flight, and Hive Moderation flagged the viral image as 99.9 per cent AI-generated. A manipulated and AI-generated image was shared with a false claim on social media. Claim: A picture showing Russian President Vladimir Putin reading the Russian edition of the Bhagavad Gita inside the aircraft was shared by an X user 'Russian Army' on December 7, claiming that it was the exact copy Prime Minister Narendra Modi gifted him during his visit to India. "The lovely gift given by India, the Shrimad Bhagavad Gita. President Putin reading the Shrimad Bhagavad Gita," read the post's caption. The post clocked 1 million views on social media. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the image through Reverse Image Search and found that several other users had shared the same post with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here . As part of the investigation, the Desk first scanned the official X handle of PM Modi and found that the Prime Minister had indeed gifted him the Russian edition of the Bhagavad Gita. The post, dated December 5, carried a picture of PM Modi giving the copy to Putin. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Taking the investigation forward, the Desk then scanned the official X handle of the President of Russia to find a picture of him reading the Gita on the aircraft. However, our search did not yield any such picture as shown in the viral social media post. Here is the link to the X post of the President of Russia. Next, the Desk conducted a set of customised keyword searches on Google and found that while media outlets did report that PM Modi gave the Bhagavad Gita to Putin. However, none of the reports actually shared a photograph of Putin reading the book on his flight back. The Desk then carefully examined the image in question and found several inconsistencies, including an extra-glossy background and mismatched detailing on the book's cover. Following this, the Desk ran the image through Hive Moderation, an AI-detection tool. The tool detected that the image is 99.9% AI-generated. Below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the image showing Putin reading the Gita is AI-generated.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video of elephant falling on truck falsely shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 8 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media video showing an elephant falling from a cliff onto a truck full of passengers, before tumbling down a mountainside, was recently shared online with the claim that it was a real incident. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the video was AI-generated and was being circulated as real to mislead viewers. Claim An X handle with the username News 24 (@News_2028) shared a video on December 6, claiming it showed an elephant falling from a cliff onto a truck full of passengers before tumbling down a mountainside. The user wrote, "A massive elephant falls onto a truck full of passengers." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing, the video had garnered 1.2 million views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was then examined with Google Lens, which led several social media accounts to share the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here ; their archived versions are available here and here , respectively. To verify the authenticity of the video, the Desk carefully analysed it and identified multiple anomalies indicative of AI generation. For instance, one of the elephant's legs suddenly appears after it tumbles down the mountainside. In addition, the background audio seems unnatural and inconsistent. These irregularities strongly indicate that the video is AI-generated. Based on these findings, the Desk also ran the video through the AI detection tool Hive Moderation. The results showed that 97.7% of the video is likely to contain AI-generated or deepfake content. A screenshot of the result is provided below. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of an elephant falling from a cliff was AI-generated and was falsely shared on social media as a real incident to mislead viewers.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old, unrelated movie shoot video of Bollywood actor Sunny Deol shared with false claim after his father Dharmendra's death; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 8 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of Bollywood actor Sunny Deol, seemingly intoxicated and roaming the streets, was recently shared on social media. Users claimed the actor was found wandering in Juhu after the sad demise of his father, veteran actor Dharmendra, earlier on November 24. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found the claim circulated along with the video to be misleading. The footage originally shows Sunny Deol shooting a scene for a movie and does not depict any real event. An unrelated video of the actor during a movie shoot was shared with a false claim to mislead viewers. Claim An X user, Aman (@DonajCR7), on December 6, shared a purported video of Bollywood actor Sunny Deol seemingly in a drunken state, roaming the streets of Juhu after the sad demise of his father, veteran actor Dharmendra, on November 24. The user shared: "Sunny Deol found drunk on the streets of Juhu after the sad demise of Dharmendra Ji. He could at least care about his late father's name and fame. Such a shameful act." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing, the video had garnered 759.5k views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVID tool, extracting multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was then examined using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here ; their archived versions are available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a video shared by the media portal Mojo Story on its YouTube channel, whose logo is also visible in frames of the viral video. The Desk found that this was the same video of Sunny Deol as seen in the viral footage. However, after analysing the details, it was determined that the visuals were from a movie shoot and did not show a real event. Moreover, the video dates back to December 2023 and is not recent. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. A comparison image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral clip and the video posted by the media portal on its YouTube channel. Next, taking cues from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised Google search and found a report published by News18 on December 6, 2023. In the report, the popular actor was quoted as stating that the visuals of him wobbling around and being unable to hold himself in the middle of the road were from a movie shoot, not a real incident. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. Additionally, the customised keyword search also led the Desk to a video shared by Sunny Deol on his official X handle on December 6, 2023. In the video, the actor, sharing the extended version, confirmed that the visuals were from a movie shoot and not a real incident. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an unrelated clip of Bollywood actor Sunny Deol from a movie shoot was shared with a false claim to mislead viewers.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Did Russian President visit Ayodhya's Ram Temple with PM Modi, UP CM? AI-generated photo shared as real, accompanied by a false claim
content: New Delhi, December 8 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared an image claiming that Russian President Vladimir Putin visited the Ram Temple in Ayodhya along with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath during his recently concluded two-day state visit to India. The image shows the leaders standing in the temple's sanctum sanctorum. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found, in its investigation, that AI generated the image. No credible media reports or government releases confirmed the Russian President's visit to the Ram Temple in Ayodhya during his official trip to India. An AI-generated image of Russian President Putin visiting the Ram Temple in Ayodhya was shared as real to mislead viewers. Claim In the wake of Russian President Vladimir Putin's recently concluded two-day state visit to India, an X user, @nityaa78, on December 7, shared a purported image of the leader showing him visiting the Ram Temple in Ayodhya alongside PM Modi and Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. The photo shows the leaders standing in the temple's sanctum sanctorum. The user shared the caption, "At the feet of the Lord stand the world's top three most powerful personalities." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and found multiple social media accounts that had shared it with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to identify credible media reports covering President Putin's visit to the Ram Temple in Ayodhya, along with PM Modi and UP CM Yogi Adityanath, during his recently concluded visit to India. However, the search did not yield any credible news reports confirming the same. Had the development been real, media reports would have extensively covered it. Next, the Desk scanned the Ministry of External Affairs' social media handles, which had been regularly posting updates on the Russian President's visit to India, including the locations he visited and the people he met. However, no information related to his visit to the Ram Temple in Ayodhya was found. Had this been real, the Ministry would have surely updated the details of such a visit. In the subsequent part of the investigation, to verify the image's authenticity, the Desk carefully analysed it and found multiple anomalies, suggesting it was AI-generated. In the photo, the Russian President is also seen dressed in Indian attire, which is highly unlikely. Taking further cues from the above, the Desk ran the viral image through the AI detection tool Hive Moderation. The results asserted that there is a 99.9% likelihood that the image contains AI-generated or deepfake content. Below is a screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an AI-generated image of President Putin visiting the Ram Temple in Ayodhya was shared as real to mislead viewers.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-manipulated image of MS Dhoni presenting the 'Player of the Series' trophy to Virat Kohli shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 8 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A picture showing MS Dhoni handing over the Player of the Series trophy to Virat Kohli after the India–South Africa ODI series spread widely on social media, quickly gathering traction among cricket fans. The image was shared as a moment of Dhoni personally stepping in to present the award to Kohli, adding an emotional layer to the claim. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk reviewed the visual using reverse image search, official cricket records, news reports, and AI-detection tools. The investigation revealed that no such moment took place and that the viral picture is digitally manipulated. Virat Kohli scored the most runs in the three-match ODI series against South Africa, with 302, including two centuries in the first two matches and an unbeaten half-century in the third. Claim: An image showing former captain MS Dhoni presenting a trophy to Virat Kohli was shared by an X user 'Cricnow' on December 7, claiming that Dhoni presented the 'Player of the Series' trophy to Virat Kohli at the conclusion of the India vs South Africa ODI series. "Dhoni himself came to give the player of the series to Kohli," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation As part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find credible media reports that cited that Dhoni presented the award to Kohli. However, the search did not lead to any such reports. Moreover, the Desk also scanned the BCCI website, but unfortunately, there was no mention on it. The Desk ran the image through Reverse Image Search and found a report by Jansatta, published on December 7, featuring an original photo of Kohli receiving the Player of the Series award after the final ODI. The original image, however, does not show Dhoni. "Virat Kohli batted brilliantly during the three-match ODI series against South Africa. Kohli's performance didn't give the impression of being out of touch. He batted with complete freedom, thoroughly enjoying the game, scoring a lot of runs for his country, and played a major role in India's series win," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combination image of the social media post and the news report. Taking a cue from the above finding, the Desk carefully analysed the picture being circulated on social media and found 'Gemini's' watermark at the bottom right corner. This clarifies that the image is AI-manipulated. Below is a screenshot of the same. As part of the investigation, the Desk ran the image through Synth ID, a digital watermarking technology developed by Google DeepMind that enables users to identify content generated by Google AI. It detected 'Very High' AI-generated content. Below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the image featuring Dhoni and Virat Kohli is AI-manipulated.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video of man performing skating stunt on top of moving train falsely shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 8 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video being shared on social media claimed to show a man meeting with a horrific accident while performing a skating stunt on top of a moving train. The visuals showed the man performing a dangerous manoeuvre on the moving train while riding a skateboard; however, he appeared to lose his balance and fall from the top. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the video does not depict any real incident. Instead, it is an AI-generated clip that was falsely shared online to mislead viewers. Claim An X user named Shaikh (@TalibShaikh143) shared a purported video on December 6 of a man performing skating stunts on a moving train and later falling from it. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video had garnered 340k views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVID tool, extracting multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was then examined using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a video posted by the Instagram account named sphereofai on December 5, 2025. The Desk found that the video posted on the Instagram account matched the viral footage of the man's supposed accident. However, upon analysing the details, the Desk noted that the user had already stated that the video was AI-generated and did not depict a real incident. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. A comparison image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral clip and the video posted by the Instagram content creator. As part of the investigation, the Desk also reviewed the Instagram profile and noted that the handle regularly shares AI-generated content. In the subsequent phase of the investigation, based on the inputs generated above, the Desk analysed the viral clip using the AI detection tool Hive Moderation, which confirmed that 99 per cent of the footage contained AI-generated or deepfake elements. Below is a screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an AI-generated video of a man performing a skating stunt on a moving train was falsely presented as real to mislead viewers.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Fake audio clip of PM Modi claiming BJP would give ₹2,000 to citizens shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 9 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media post carrying a purported audio message of Prime Minister Narendra Modi — in which he allegedly claimed that the Bharatiya Janata Party is set to give every citizen a sum of ₹2,000 — was recently shared online. In the alleged appeal, the Prime Minister was heard requesting that people click the link in the post to receive the amount directly in their bank accounts. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false and the audio to be inauthentic. Moreover, the link promoted in the post was also identified as dubious and potentially part of an online scam designed to mislead citizens and extract their personal or financial information. Claim A Facebook page named 'IND 4999' shared a purported social media post on December 2, attached with an audio message allegedly featuring PM Modi claiming that the Bharatiya Janata Party is set to give every citizen a sum of ₹2,000. In the purported appeal, the Prime Minister is heard urging people to click the link in the post to receive the amount directly in their bank accounts. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video garnered 19.1k views) Investigation The Desk began the investigation by scanning the social media handles of PM Modi to verify whether he had shared any audio clip suggesting that the BJP would give every citizen a sum of ₹2,000. However, the search did not yield any such post on any of the Prime Minister's official social media accounts. Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk also reviewed the Bharatiya Janata Party's social media handles and official website to identify credible information regarding the purported scheme mentioned in the viral post. No official release, announcement, or credible information about such a scheme was found. Given the significance of the claim, if such a scheme were real, the BJP would have issued an official statement, and the media would have widely reported on it. In the subsequent part of the investigation, to verify the authenticity of the post, the Desk clicked the link in the viral audio post. The link was identified as dubious. If the BJP had truly announced the scheme, the URL should have been connected to one of the party's official domains. However, the URL shared — 'https://inaam.pardhaanoffers.info/d/' — appeared suspicious, and sharing personal information on such a site may lead to financial fraud. Below is a screenshot highlighting the dubious link. In the next step, the Desk extracted the audio clip and ran it through Google's AI-based audio detection platform, Resemble AI. The analysis suggested that the audio might be an impersonation. Below is a screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the audio was AI-generated and the link promoted in the post was fraudulent, making the viral claim entirely baseless.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Edited photo of menu card from Putin's state banquet with typographical errors shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 9 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): An image purportedly showing a menu card from the state banquet hosted for Russian President Vladimir Putin during his recent official visit to India was widely shared on social media, with claims that it contained multiple typographical errors. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found the image to be digitally altered. Several official news reports that included the actual menu card did not show any of the typographical errors seen in the viral image, confirming that it was AI-generated. Thus, the claim is FALSE. Claim On December 7, X user Jawhar Sircar (@jawharsircar) shared an image claiming to show the official menu card from the state banquet held for Russian President Vladimir Putin, alleging that it contained multiple typographical mistakes. The user wrote: "After Modi has said English is for Macaulay's slaves, the PR guys of Rashtrapati Bhavan went about murdering English, with so many typos and spelling mistakes in the menu card of the President's state dinner for Mr Putin. Why not print in Hindi or Gujarati?" Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the post had garnered 298.1k views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and found multiple social media accounts that had shared it with a similar claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. To verify the image's authenticity, the Desk conducted a customised Google search for the dinner menu presented at the state banquet hosted for Russian President Vladimir Putin. The search results led the Desk to a post shared by PTI on its official X account on December 5, 2025, which included a similar image of the menu card as seen in the viral post. However, upon careful analysis of the menu card image shared on the news agency's handle, no such typographical mistakes were found, contrary to what was claimed in the viral post. This finding led to the conclusion that the image shared in the viral post had been digitally altered. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a combination image highlighting how the original photo was digitally altered to allegedly show typographical mistakes. Additionally, the customised keyword search for the state dinner hosted for the Russian President led the Desk to multiple news reports that also featured the menu card. No typographical mistakes were found in these either, further confirming that the viral image was digitally altered and not authentic. Links to two such reports can be found here and here . Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral image had been digitally altered and was falsely circulated as the original menu card used at the state banquet hosted for President Putin.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video shared to falsely claim python spotted inside crowded train; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 9 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently shared on social media claimed to depict a horrifying incident inside a crowded train in Madhya Pradesh, where a massive python supposedly appeared from the luggage rack right above a sleeping child, triggering fear and panic among passengers. The visuals showed people screaming in fear and rushing away from their seats. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found during its investigation that the video does not depict any real incident. Instead, it is an AI-generated clip that was falsely shared online to mislead viewers. Claim An X user named Talib Shaikh X (@TalibShaikh143) shared a video on December 8, purportedly capturing a terrifying incident inside a crowded train coach. The video appeared to show a massive python hanging from the luggage rack directly above a sleeping child, causing chaos among passengers. Describing the alleged incident, the user wrote: "Unbelievable terror captured! A massive python was spotted hanging from the luggage rack right above a sleeping child on a crowded train coach, reportedly near a small village in Madhya Pradesh! The video shows the terrifying moment the reptile dangled inches from the unsuspecting boy's face. The instant passengers noticed the danger, chaos erupted! Screams, panic, and desperate scrambles as people fled their seats to escape the terrifying sight. Can you imagine waking up to this?" Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered 22.1k views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was examined using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. To verify the video's authenticity, the Desk carefully analysed the visuals and noticed a watermark reading "@shawnnarranhanft." A customised keyword search using this watermark led the Desk to an active Instagram account with the same name. Further examination of the account revealed that it had shared the same video seen in the viral post on November 12, 2025. Importantly, the user had clearly mentioned in the details that the video was created using the AI content generation platform Sora. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: A comparison image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral clip and the video posted by the Instagram content creator. In the next stage of the investigation, based on the findings above, the Desk analysed the viral clip using the AI-detection tool Hive Moderation, which confirmed that 95.8% of the footage contained AI-generated or deepfake elements. Below is a screenshot of the results: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of a massive python emerging from an overhead luggage rack inside a crowded train was AI-generated and was falsely presented as real to mislead viewers.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Social media posts falsely allege India blocked Pakistan's aid flight to Sri Lanka
content: New Delhi, December 10 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media accounts shared a post claiming that India refused to grant airspace to a Pakistani aircraft carrying humanitarian aid to cyclone-hit Sri Lanka, forcing Islamabad to send the relief shipment by sea. The posts, amplified by several accounts, framed the alleged denial as proof of India's hostility. However, the PTI Fact Check, after a closer look at official statements and credible reporting, found that the claim has no basis. India did receive Pakistan's request for overflight clearance and approved it the same day. Given the urgency of humanitarian assistance, the Government of India processed the request expeditiously that same day and granted overflight permission as per the proposed itinerary. Sri Lanka has suffered from massive floods caused by Cyclone Ditwah. Over 350 people have been confirmed dead across Sri Lanka as authorities continue to battle rising floodwaters in parts of the capital, Colombo. India has sent 53 tons of relief material to Sri Lanka under Operation Sagar Bandhu as part of its emergency response to Cyclone Ditwah. Claim: A post circulated on X by a user 'Ch Mudasir' on December 1 claimed that India refused to grant airspace to Pakistan for humanitarian aid flights headed to Sri Lanka. The post further claimed that owing to the refusal, Pakistan will now send aid to Sri Lanka via sea. "INDIA'S FACE EXPOSED AGAIN!! India has refused to grant Pakistan airspace for humanitarian aid flights bound for Sri Lanka to help people affected by the ongoing flood disaster. Pakistan will now send the aid by ship," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Investigation When Desk ran the claim through a search, we found that several other social media users had shared it. Two such posts can be found here and here . As part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google search for relevant media reports that cite the same incident. However, our search did not lead us to any such report; moreover, a report published by The Hindu on December 3, 2025, mentioned that India on Tuesday (December 2, 2025) trashed as "ridiculous" Pakistan's claim that its request for using Indian airspace to send humanitarian aid to cyclone-hit Sri Lanka was denied by New Delhi. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted another set of customised keyword searches on Google, which led us to a report by a Sri Lankan daily, The Daily Mirror, stating that India granted rapid clearance for Pakistan's humanitarian aid flight to cyclone-hit Sri Lanka. "India has granted rapid clearance for Pakistan's aid flight carrying relief material to cyclone-hit Sri Lanka, foreign media reported today. Indian media quoting officials confirmed that Pakistan submitted a request for overflight at approximately 1300 hrs (IST) on Monday, seeking same-day permission to fly over Indian airspace. Given the purpose of the request--to provide humanitarian assistance to Sri Lanka--India processed the request," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Taking the investigation forward, the Desk then scanned the official X handle of MEA Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal for a statement on the situation. The search led us to an X post dated December 2, in response to media queries regarding Pakistan's statement on overflight clearance. The statement read: "We reject the ridiculous statement made by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Pakistan, which is yet another attempt to spread anti-India misinformation. The request for overflight clearance for Pakistani aircraft carrying humanitarian assistance to Sri Lanka was received by the High Commission of India in Islamabad at around 1300 hrs on December 01, 2025. Given the urgency of humanitarian assistance, the Government of India processed the request expeditiously the same day. It granted permission for overflight as per the proposed itinerary at 1730 hrs on December 01, 2025. India remains committed to assisting the people of Sri Lanka in these challenging times through all available means" Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim that India refused to grant Pakistan access to its airspace for humanitarian aid flights to Sri Lanka is false and baseless. India indeed granted the permission.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, Lok Sabha has not yet passed Right to Disconnect Bill 2025; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 10 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid a wave of social media posts celebrating what many users described as a major "win for Indian employees," a video of NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar) MP Supriya Sule speaking in the Lok Sabha went viral this week. The clip was widely circulated with the claim that the Right to Disconnect Bill 2025 had been cleared by the lower house, giving workers the legal right to switch off from work-related calls, messages and emails after office hours. The posts quickly gained traction, with many users treating the supposed passage of the bill as official and immediately enforceable. However, the PTI Fact Check reviewed the claim and found that the excitement was built on a false premise. While Sule did introduce the Right to Disconnect Bill as a Private Member's Bill, it has neither been debated nor passed in Parliament. The bill remains pending (at the time of writing this article), and no such legal right has been approved. Claim: A video featuring Lok Sabha member Supriya Sule in the Parliament was shared by an Instagram user 'the_corporate_counsel' on December 8, claiming that the Lok Sabha passed the Right to Disconnect Bill 2025, granting employees a legal right to ignore work-related calls and messages after office hours. "HUGE NEWS! Say goodbye to after-hours emails and weekend calls! India's Lok Sabha has reportedly passed the "Right to Disconnect Bill 2025," giving employees the legal power to ignore work calls, texts, and emails once their shift ends," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . As part of the investigation, the Desk first conducted a customised Google search for relevant media reports citing the passage of the bill in the Lok Sabha. Our search, however, led us to multiple reports, one such article by Hindustan Times dated December 7, mentioned that Supriya Sule, Lok Sabha MP from the Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar), introduced a private member's bill in the lower house on Friday (December 5) seeking legal right for employees to ignore work-related calls and emails beyond office hours. "What is the Right to Disconnect Bill introduced in Lok Sabha, and can it clear Parliament?" read the headline of the report. This clarifies that it is a private member's bill and not a government bill. Also, the article nowhere highlights the bill being passed. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Another NDTV report published on December 7 highlighted that the bill states employees should not be compelled to respond to official communication after work hours or on holidays. It grants every worker the right to refuse calls and emails, without fear of disciplinary action. "'No Work Calls After Office Hours': Right To Disconnect Bill Explained," read the headline of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. The Desk therefore found that, at the time of writing this article, the bill had not been passed by parliament. Taking the investigation ahead, the Desk checked the status of the Right to Disconnect Bill 2025 on the Sansad website and found that the private bill introduced by NCP MP Supriya Sule on December 5, 2025, is still pending. Discussions on this bill have not yet taken place in Parliament. This clarifies that the bill has not yet been passed. Here is the link to the Sansad website, and below is a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the Right to Disconnect Bill 2025 is a private bill that is still pending and has not been passed in the Lok Sabha.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-manipulated video shared to falsely claim Gambhir confirmed 'Virat Kohli & Rohit Sharma will play for 2027 World Cup'
content: New Delhi, December 10 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Virat Kohli's 302-run haul, including two centuries, and Rohit Sharma's crucial half-centuries in India's 2–1 ODI series win over South Africa have sparked renewed debate about the future of India's senior batting core. Amidst this, a video featuring coach Guatam Gambhir addressing a press briefing was shared by several social media users. Those sharing the video claim he said that Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma will play in the 2027 ODI World Cup. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the footage and found that though Gambhir did say that Kohli and Rohit are class players. However, when he was asked whether the two players would be considered for India's ODI World Cup squad in 2027, head coach Gautam Gambhir replied that the ODI World Cup is two years away and that it is most important to stay in the present. The Desk further ran the video through an AI-generation tool, which revealed that the audio had been AI-generated. Claim: A video featuring coach Gautam Gambhir addressing a press briefing was shared by Instagram user 'legendsrevolution' on December 7, claiming that he said that Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma will be playing in the 2027 ODI World Cup. "Virat and Rohit have played this series…especially Virat, who scored two 100s and one 50. Surely, he is the best batsman on the planet right now. I am confirming that these two will be playing the 2027 World Cup," says Gmabhir in the video. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation As part of the investigation, the Desk first conducted a customised keyword search on Google, which led us to a report by The Indian Express, December 7, highlighting that Gambhir said there was no need to read too much into the performances of Kohli and Rohit about the next 50-over World Cup, still two years away. "They are world-class players and their experience is important in the dressing room. They've been doing it for a long time. Hopefully, they can continue doing the same, which is going to be important in the 50-over format," Gambhir said after India's nine-wicket win over South Africa in the series decider, cited the report. Here is the link to the report. The search also led us to another report published by NDTV on December 7, featuring a collage of images as seen in the recent social media post of Gautam Gambhir's press briefing. The report also noted that when asked whether the two players would be considered for India's ODI World Cup squad in 2027, head coach Gautam Gambhir gave a blunt reply. "Look, first we have got to realise that the ODI World Cup is two years away from now. The most important thing is to stay in the present," he said at the press conference after India's nine-wicket win over South Africa in the deciding ODI in Visakhapatnam, cited the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk conducted another set of customised keyword searches to access the original press briefing. Our search led us to the press conference published by BCCI on December 6. Upon reviewing the entire conference, we found that he did not make any statement confirming the two players to be part of the 2027 ODI World Cup. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot. Taking the investigation ahead, the Desk noticed that the voice in the viral social media post differs from that of the original press briefing. Following this, the Desk extracted the audio from the video and ran it through Resemble AI, an AI-detection tool. The tool detected that the audio is fake. This confirms that the viral video was generated using AI-manipulated audio. Below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video featuring coach Guatam Gambhir confirming that Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma will be playing for the 2027 ODI World Cup is fake and generated using AI-manipulated audio.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu dancing at family wedding falsely linked to recent IndiGo crisis
content: New Delhi, December 10 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): As the IndiGo airline crisis riggered by severe pilot shortages and new crew rest regulations has led to over 4,500 flight cancellations in the past week, leaving thousands of passengers stranded at major airports across the country, a video of Civil Aviation Minister K. Ram Mohan Naidu dancing on a stage at what appears to be a function has gone viral. Users sharing the clip claim the minister was enjoying himself instead of addressing the aviation crisis. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk reviewed the footage and found it to be several months old. The video was recorded during a family wedding in Andhra Pradesh in July 2025, long before the ongoing IndiGo disruption. It has no connection to the recent wave of IndiGo flight cancellations. Claim A video showing Civil Aviation Minister K Ram Mohan Naidu dancing on a stage was shared by an X user 'Suraj G Naik' on December 7, claiming that the minister was enjoying himself instead of addressing the aviation crisis. "Flights delayed, terminals overcrowded, passengers helpless… and the Aviation Minister is dancing. This government has mastered one thing: entertainment over governance. Stop dancing and start managing the mess you created," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . As part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a set of customised keyword searches on Google and found that the same video was streamed on the official YouTube page of ETV Andhra Pradesh on July 29, 2025. The text mentioned that Ram Mohan Naidu was seen dancing at the wedding reception. The video's timeline and the text clarify that it is not recent and has no connection to the IndiGo flight cancellations. The description noted that the minister attended the wedding celebrations of his uncle Prabhakar's son at a resort in Bhogapuram, Vizianagaram district. During the Sangeet ceremony, Naidu performed a group dance with his brothers. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combined image highlighting the similarities between the content in the recent social media post and the YouTube video. The same video was also streamed on a YouTube channel 'Tone News' on July 29, 2025. The text mentioned, "Ram Mohan Naidu Dance at Sangeet Function | Srikakulam". This makes it clear that the video has no connection with the recent flight cancellations. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Moreover, according to reports dated December 9, Civil Aviation Minister K Ram Mohan Naidu said the Centre will cut IndiGo's winter flight schedule and reallocate those slots to other airlines in the wake of the country's largest carrier's massive operational meltdown. IndiGo cancelled more than 1,000 flights in a single day after failing to comply with the DGCA's revised pilot duty and rest rules, despite having ample time to prepare. There is still no clarity on why the airline was unprepared or whether the board provided adequate oversight, said IiAS. Calling the mass cancellations a move to "reboot the network, systems, and roster" appears opportunistic, as a planned exercise would have involved advance communication to passengers and staff. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video featuring Civil Aviation Minister K Ram Mohan Naidu dancing on the stage at an event dates back to July 2025 and is unrelated to the IndiGo flight cancellation.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Bengaluru airport chaos video shared in name of Hyderabad airport during recent IndiGo flight cancellations
content: New Delhi, December 10 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): As IndiGo's ongoing operational crisis continues to disrupt air travel across the country, more than 4,500 flights have been cancelled over the past week due to pilot shortages and revised crew rest rules. Major airports have been grappling with long queues, delayed baggage, and stranded passengers. In the middle of this chaos, a video showing a massive crowd around baggage counters began circulating online, with claims that it was from Hyderabad airport and reflected the impact of the cancellations. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video has been shared in a false context. The footage does not show Hyderabad airport at all, but Kempegowda International Airport in Bengaluru. The video was shared with an untrue claim on social media. Claim: A video showing a sea of people with their luggage at the baggage counter was shared by a Facebook user, 'EM News Hyd', on December 6, claiming the incident of utter chaos occurred at the Hyderabad airport due to IndiGo flight cancellations. "Indigo Flight Cancellations: Airport Chaos. This is the situation at Hyderabad Airport. Terrible conditions at airports nationwide due to Indigo flight cancellations," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a report by Deccan Herald published on December 5, 2025. The report carried the same image as seen in one of the clips of the social media post. However, it highlighted that stranded passengers were searching for their luggage near a counter after IndiGo cancelled more than 400 flights at Kempegowda International Airport in Bengaluru. "In Pics | Indigo crisis: Weary passengers stranded across airports," read the headline of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combined image highlighting the similarities in the content of the social media post and the news report. Taking a cue from this, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google, which led us to a PTI report carried by The Hindu published on December 5, 2025, mentioning that IndiGo's On-Time Performance (OTP) plummeted to 8.5% on Thursday (December 4, 2025), with worsening operational disruptions impacting flight schedules. "Stranded passengers search for their luggage near a counter after IndiGo cancelled more than 400 flights, at the Kempegowda International Airport, in Bengaluru," read the caption of the cover image. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Taking the investigation forward, the Desk, using Google Maps, located the Kempegowda International Airport and found many similarities with the contents seen in the social media post, such as escalators, pillars, signboards, and counters. Below is a screenshot of the same. As for the news of a heavy crowd at Hyderabad airport, the Desk conducted another set of customised keyword searches on Google and found reports of chaos at the airport following the flight cancellations. A YouTube Shorts video posted by ET Digital mentioned that passengers are facing chaos as Indigo Airlines' flight delay complaints have risen at Hyderabad Airport. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. However, the viral video being shared on social media is not from Hyderabad. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing people with their luggage at the Hyderabad airport is actually from Kempegowda International Airport in Bengaluru.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-manipulated video of Sudha Murty shared to falsely claim she promoted investment platform; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 10 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video featuring Author and Rajya Sabha member Sudha Murty addressing the people with what looks like a video conference. Those sharing the video claim that she promoted an AI-based investment opportunity and allegedly assured viewers they could earn a large sum of money by investing in the scheme. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video is actually from a podcast in which Murty appeared, and there was no mention of any investment platform. Therefore, the Desk ran the audio through an AI-detection tool, which revealed that the video had been digitally altered by adding fake audio and flagged the audio as counterfeit. Claim: A Facebook user shared a video featuring Author and Rajya Sabha member Sudha Murty, claiming that she promoted an AI-based investment opportunity and allegedly assured viewers they could earn a large sum of money by investing in the scheme. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation As part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google search for reports that cite Murty promoting an investment platform. But the search did not yield any credible reports. Moreover, any such investment platform (if any) promoted by Sudha Murty would have been widely reported. Next, the Desk ran the video through the InVid tool's search and extracted the keyframes. When it ran one of the keyframes through Reverse Image Search, the Desk found a podcast video uploaded to the YouTube channel of BeerBiceps (Ranveer Allahbadia) on February 26, 2021. In the podcast, Sudha Murty can be seen wearing the same outfit and seated against the same background as in the viral clip. Upon analysing the entire podcast, the Desk found no mention of any investment platform. The title read: "Sudha Murthy - So What If I Lost The Battle, I Lived The War | The Ranveer Show 96" Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combined image highlighting the similarities between the content in the social media post and the YouTube podcast. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk then extracted the audio from the video and ran it through Resemble AI, an AI voice-detection tool, which found the audio to be entirely fake. Below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video has been digitally manipulated. The audio in the viral video is fake and digitally edited to match visuals from the original podcast.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Bangladesh religious gathering video shared to falsely claim Assam's Muslims prayed for removal of CM Himanta Biswa Sarma; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 11 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it depicted a Muslim gathering in Assam where people allegedly prayed for the removal of Himanta Biswa Sarma from the Chief Ministerial position. The visuals showed hundreds of people wearing skull caps and reciting prayers. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the video is unrelated to Assam or any part of India. The video was initially filmed in Bangladesh and shows a religious gathering held at the Charmonai Darbar Sharif in Barisal. An unrelated video from Bangladesh was falsely shared on social media, accompanied by a misleading claim linking it to India. Claim On December 8, an X handle named Mama Meme Sena (@mamamemesena) shared a video claiming to show a Muslim gathering in Assam where people allegedly prayed to Allah for the removal of Himanta Biswa Sarma from the Chief Minister's post. The user wrote: "Muslims in Assam are praying to Allah to remove Himanta Biswa Sarma from the Chief Minister post." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing the story, the video had garnered 41.2k views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was then examined using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens results also led the Desk to a video posted by a Bangladesh-based Facebook user named NouMuslim Muhammad Raj on November 27, 2025. The user shared the same video seen in the viral clip but did not specify when or where it was filmed. In the description, he only mentioned that it was from a religious congregation he attended. Here is the link and archive link to the video, along with a screenshot: A comparison image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral clip and the video posted by the Facebook user. To further determine when and where the video was captured, the Desk analysed the user's Facebook profile and found another video shared on November 29. The background visuals in this video matched those seen in the viral clip. Here, the user mentioned that the video was from "Charmonai Mahfil", which he had attended. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: In the next phase of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google keyword search about "Charmonai Mahfil." The search led the Desk to multiple news reports, which revealed that Charmonai Mahfil is a massive traditional Islamic religious gathering held at the Charmonai Darbar Sharif in Barisal, Bangladesh. According to the Bengali calendar, it is held twice a year — in Agrahayan (mid-November to mid-December) and Falgun (mid-February to mid-March) — and attracts thousands of participants from across the country. Links to two such reports can be found here and here . Moreover, the customised keyword search also led the Desk to images posted by Jamia Talimia Madrasa Dhaka on its Facebook page on the same day. The photos, labelled as being from the Charmonai Mahfil 2025, matched the keyframes used in the Desk's investigation. This confirmed that the visuals in the viral video were from a religious congregation in Bangladesh, not from Assam or India, and unrelated to any prayer for the removal of Himanta Biswa Sarma. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a combined image highlighting the match between the Facebook post and the keyframe used in the investigation. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video depicting a religious congregation in Bangladesh was falsely shared as a gathering in Assam, along with the false claim that Muslims were praying for the removal of Himanta Biswa Sarma from the Chief Minister's post.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video shared to falsely claim 'Bangladeshis living in Kolkata declared they will rule West Bengal'; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 11 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): As political content continues to flood social media in the run-up to the Bengal elections, an alarming video began circulating widely on social media. The 14-second clip shows a man introducing himself as a Bangladeshi living in Kolkata and claiming that "Bangladeshis will rule West Bengal soon," while expressing support for Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found a watermark from an AI-video generator, subtle rendering inconsistencies, and discrepancies in facial movement. Further analysis using AI-detection tools confirmed that both the visuals and the audio were artificially generated. An AI-generated video was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim: A video showing a man claiming to be a Bangladeshi residing in Kolkata was shared by an X user, 'Mahaveer_VJ', on December 3, in which the man allegedly said Bangladeshis would soon rule West Bengal and expressed support for Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee. In the 0:14-second video, the man can be heard saying, "I am from superpower Bangladesh, I live in Kolkata, and I fully support Mamata Banerjee. We Bangladeshi will rule in West Bengal soon". The post clocked 116.7k views on social media. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . As part of the investigation, on careful analysis of the viral video, the Desk noticed a watermark of an AI-video generator 'Sora' at the top right corner of the video. Hinting that this video might be AI-generated. Below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk then ran the video through Hive Moderation, an AI-detection tool, which flagged it as AI-generated. Below is a screenshot of the same. Next, the Desk extracted the audio from the video and ran it through Resemble AI, another AI voice-detection tool, which flagged the audio as 'fake'. Below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a Bangladeshi man allegedly saying that Bangladeshi will rule West Bengal is fake and AI-generated.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video shared to falsely claim Indian Yogi lifted 130-kg weight in gym with his mind; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 11 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently shared on social media claimed to show a real incident in which an Indian Yogi was seen lifting 130 kg of weight in the gym using only his mind. The visuals showed Yogi sitting on a gym platform while a weight of over 130 kilograms appeared to rise into the air, allegedly under his mind's control. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found during its investigation that the video does not depict any real incident. Instead, it is an AI-generated clip falsely shared online to mislead viewers. Claim On December 11, an X handle with the username 'Vaidya Parampara' (@vaidyaparampara) shared a purported video of an Indian Yogi allegedly seen moving 130 kg in the gym with his mind. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered 16k views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was examined using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here ; their archived versions are available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search results also led the Desk to a video posted on the Facebook page Desi Kalakaari on December 2, 2025. The footage posted by the page matched the video seen in the viral post. Upon reviewing the Facebook account, it was found that the page is known for sharing AI-generated content, which the account owner has also mentioned in his bio. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: A comparison image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral clip and the video posted by the Facebook content creator. Next, based on the findings above, the Desk analysed the viral clip using the AI-detection tool Hive Moderation, which confirmed that 95% of the footage contained AI-generated or deepfake content. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an AI-generated video depicting an Indian Yogi lifting 130 kg of weight in the gym with his mind was falsely shared as real.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of police action on protesting teachers in Dhaka falsely shared in name of West Bengal lathi-charge over Babri Masjid demand
content: New Delhi, December 12 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A tense video showing police officers charging at a packed crowd has been circulating widely on social media. The clip, posted with claims that West Bengal Police had lathi-charged Muslims demanding the Babri Masjid. A large crowd can be seen moving through a congested intersection as police push forward, striking demonstrators and firing what appear to be stun grenades. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated and found that this clip has nothing to do with West Bengal, the Babri Masjid issue, or events in India. The video was traced back to November 2025, when thousands of primary school teachers in Dhaka were protesting to demand better pay and service benefits. The demonstration escalated at Shahbagh, prompting police to use lathis and stun grenades to disperse the crowd. Claim: A video showing a large crowd of people gathered in an area. At the same time, the Police lathi-charged to disperse them was shared by an Instagram user 'bhaajpaaankitpandit' on December 8, claiming that the Police lathi-charged Muslims demanding Babri Masjid in West Bengal. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a Facebook post by Bangladesh Bulletin dated November 8, featuring images that match the footage. As per the post caption, the incident was reported to have occurred at Shahbagh, Dhaka. "120 teachers injured in a huge lathi charge of police in Shahbagh!" read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combined image highlighting the similarities between the content in the viral social media post and that of the Bangladeshi news outlet. Taking a cue from the above finding, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by a Bangladeshi daily published on November 8, 2025. The report highlighted that the Police lathi-charged protesting primary school teachers in the capital's Shahbagh, injuring 120 teachers. "The Inspector-in-charge of the police camp at DMCH Hospital, MD, confirmed the matter. Faruk. He said that 120 primary school teachers were injured and came to the emergency department of Dhaka Medical College. Many are undergoing treatment in the emergency department. Some teachers have left after receiving treatment," read a section of the same. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video is actually from Bangladesh, where primary school teachers were protesting for their demands near Shahid Minar in Dhaka and then began marching towards Shahbag. Police then lathi-charged them and threw stun grenades.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated image of Putin taking dip in the river Ganges, along with PM Modi, UP CM Yogi Adityanath, shared as real
content: New Delhi, December 11 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported image of Russian President Vladimir Putin, in which he was allegedly seen taking a dip in the river Ganges along with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, was recently shared on social media. Users claimed the image was real and showed the Russian President taking a dip in the holy river during his recently concluded visit to India. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the image is AI-generated. No credible media reports or government releases confirmed that the Russian President took a dip in the holy river during his official trip to India. An AI-generated image was falsely shared as real to mislead viewers. Claim A Facebook user named Devi Prakash shared a purported image on December 8 of Russian President Vladimir Putin allegedly taking a dip in the Ganges during his recent visit to India. The image also showed him accompanied by PM Modi and UP CM Yogi Adityanath. The user wrote: "Wow! Modi ji has allowed Putin to take a dip in the Ganges River; this is a wonderful initiative that strengthens cultural ties between the two countries." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing the story, the image had garnered 83k likes.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and found multiple social media accounts that had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to identify credible media reports that might have covered an instance of President Putin taking a dip in the Ganges along with PM Modi and UP CM Yogi Adityanath during his official visit to India. However, the search did not yield any credible results. Had such an event occurred, mainstream media would have extensively covered it. The Desk then reviewed the Ministry of External Affairs' social media handles, which had been regularly posting updates on President Putin's visit, including details about the places he visited and the leaders he met. Yet, there was no information indicating that he had taken a dip in the Ganges with PM Modi or CM Yogi Adityanath. If such a development had taken place, the Ministry would have officially documented it. In the subsequent stage of the investigation, the Desk closely analysed the image and found multiple visual anomalies suggesting it was AI-generated. In the photo, President Putin is also seen dressed in Indian attire, which is highly unlikely. Following these observations, the Desk ran the image through the AI-detection tool Hive Moderation, which reported a 99.9% likelihood that the image contains AI-generated or deepfake content. A screenshot of the result is provided below: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the image depicting Russian President Putin taking a dip in the river Ganges during his visit to India is AI-generated and was falsely shared as real.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2024 Mumbai airport tarmac video falsely linked to recent IndiGo flight cancellations
content: New Delhi, December 12 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A short clip showing a group of air travellers sitting on the tarmac and eating out of food trays has been circulating widely on social media. Those sharing the video claim these were IndiGo passengers forced to eat on the airport runway due to the airline's recent flight cancellations. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video dates back to January 2024, when passengers on an IndiGo flight from Goa to Delhi were diverted to Mumbai due to poor visibility. The unscheduled stopover dragged on for hours, leaving passengers stranded inside the aircraft. Several of them eventually stepped out, collected their meal packets, and sat on the tarmac beside the parked plane. The footage was shared with a false claim on social media. Claim: A Facebook user shared a video on December 6 showing people sitting on the tarmac and eating, 'Sahib Rajput', claiming that the passengers had to eat there due to the inconvenience caused by recent IndiGo flight cancellations. "Indigo passengers seen eating food while sitting on the airport's 'runway'. Due to problems in flight operations, passengers are facing a lot of trouble," read the post's caption. The post clocked 8.1k likes on social media. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across the same video used by NDTV in its report dated January 16, 2024. As per the report, the exhausted passengers are seen sitting on the tarmac just a few steps away from an IndiGo plane, and having their meals. The report's timeline clarifies that it is not recent and is unrelated to the recent IndiGo flight cancellations. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the social media post and the News Report. Our search also led us to the same video, streamed on the official YouTube channel of Mint on January 16, claiming that passengers on a Goa-Delhi Indigo flight, which was delayed by over 10 hours, were seen eating their dinner on the Mumbai airport tarmac. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Another report by Hindustan Times, published on January 16, 2024, stated that the crew on board a Goa-Delhi IndiGo flight that was diverted to Mumbai due to poor visibility had the most harrowing 12 hours of their lives.
