"Upset by the unexpected stopover, with many of them demanding that the flight be immediately taken to Delhi, passengers instead collected their food packets and sat down to have their dinner on the tarmac, next to the parked aircraft," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video, featuring passengers sitting on the tarmac and having their meal, is a year old and unrelated to the recent IndiGo flight cancellations.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-manipulated video falsely claims DG NCC warned of Pakistani drones reaching Delhi and Gujarat in May
content: New Delhi, December 13 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video featuring NCC Director General Lt General Virendra Vats has been making the rounds on social media, with claims that he admitted Pakistani drones had reached Delhi and Gujarat earlier this year and retreated before causing major damage because India supposedly lacks matching technology. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the audio used in the footage is AI-generated and fake. In the original video, he was speaking about the future of drone technology and cyber training for NCC cadets and not cross-border drone intrusions. The video was shared with a false claim. Claim: A video featuring DG NCC Lt General Virendra Vats addressing the media was shared by an X user, 'Nawaz Khan', on December 11, claiming that he allegedly revealed that Pakistani drones reached Delhi and Gujarat as per intelligence reports in May this year. "Pakistani drones reached Delhi and even Gujarat as per our intelligence reports in May this year. Had they actually struck and not gone back, we would have suffered huge losses. Sadly, we don't have the same advanced technology which Pakitan has…," says DG NCC Lt General Virendra Vats in the purported video. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation As part of the investigation, the Desk first conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find reports that cite the said claim. However, our search did not lead us to any relevant media coverage or report. The Desk noticed 'IANS' watermark on the top right corner of the video being shared on social media, taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across the original X post dated December 11. Mumbai, Maharashtra: NCC DG Lt. General Virendra Vats says, "Drones will play a major part in our economy. So, besides opening greater opportunities for our cadets, also ability to reinforce our defence forces in terms of drone and also cyber issues. So, in the coming time, you will see that NCCC, you can say NCCCC, National Cyber Cadet Corps, some selected cadets will be given a first-class cyber training..." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk ran the video through Hive Moderation, an AI-detection tool that detected that 55.6% of the audio was AI-generated. Below is a screenshot the same. Next, the Desk extracted the audio from the video and ran it through Resemble, another audio AI-detection tool, which detected that the audio is fake. Below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video featuring DG NCC Lt General allegedly revealing that Pakistani drones reached Delhi and Gujarat as per intelligence reports in May this year is a fake and manipulated video.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated clip falsely passed off as Indira Gandhi's interview on Emergency
content: New Delhi, December 13 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A short video purportedly showing former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi sitting across from an interviewer and remaining silent when questioned about the 1975 Emergency has been circulating widely on social media. The users sharing the video claim that it is rare archival footage to suggest that Indira Gandhi avoided or refused to respond when confronted about one of the most controversial episodes of her tenure. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the viral video and found that the claim is false. A detailed examination revealed that the footage is not part of any documented or archived interview of Indira Gandhi. No credible historical records, news archives, or verified interviews match the visuals seen in the clip. Further technical analysis confirmed that both the video and the audio were artificially generated using AI-based manipulation tools. The viral clip has no basis in historical reality and is being falsely circulated as authentic archival material. Claim: A video featuring former Prime Minister of India Indira Gandhi sitting across from an interviewer was shared by a Facebook user, 'Arun Yadav', on December 3, claiming that the former PM kept silent when she was questioned about the 1975 emergency. The post clocked 5.2k likes on social media. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . The Desk conducted a thorough, customised keyword search on Google to find archival interviews of Indira Gandhi. Still, the search did not yield any trustworthy reports, historical archives, or documented interviews matching the viral clip. As part of the investigation, the Desk also ran the extracted keyframes through Reverse Image Search, but it did not yield any matches, indicating the clip is not sourced from genuine historical footage. The Desk noticed that the video was very smooth, suggesting that it might be manipulated or fake. Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the video through Hive Moderation, an AI-detection tool that flagged it as fake and AI-generated. Below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk then extracted the audio from the video and ran it through Resemble AI, an AI voice detection tool which also flagged the audio as fake. Below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video claiming to show former PM Indira Gandhi staying silent when asked about the 1975 emergency is fake and created using AI-manipulation techniques.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated images falsely show Akhilesh Yadav, Dimple Yadav praying at Kaaba
content: New Delhi, December 14 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Two photographs purportedly showing Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and party MP Dimple Yadav dressed in ihram, the white garment worn by Muslim pilgrims during Hajj or Umrah, have been widely circulated on social media. Those sharing the images claim that the couple visited Mecca and offered prayers at the Kaaba, Islam's holiest shrine in Saudi Arabia. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the images and found the claim to be false. The photographs do not depict Akhilesh Yadav and Dimple Yadav praying at the Kaaba. Instead, the images were generated using artificial intelligence tools and have no basis in reality. Claim: A set of two pictures featuring SP chief Akhilesh Yadav and part MP Dimple Yadav wearing the ihram (the special robe worn by Muslim pilgrims during the Hajj or Umrah) was shared by an X user '@Akash8996' on December 11, claiming that the two were praying at the Kaaba, the holiest shrine in Islam in Mecca, Saudi Arabia. "These two photos are going viral on the internet !! Has Akhilesh become a mullah or is there still some Yadav left #VandeMataram," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation As part of the investigation, the Desk first conducted a set of customised keyword searches on Google to find if Akhilesh Yadav and Dimple Yadav had actually visited Mecca. However, the search did not yield any credible results, and news of a prominent political figure visiting a religious site in India typically receives extensive media coverage. The Desk also scanned the official X handle of both the leaders, but found no mention or pictures of them visiting the Kaaba. Here is the link to their X handles. Next, on careful analysis of one of the pictures, the Desk found the Google Gemini mark on the bottom right corner. This hinted that the images might be AI-generated or fake. Below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the image through Hive-moderation, an AI-detection tool, which detected that it was 99.9% AI-generated. The Desk ran the other image through Hive-Moderation, which detected it to be 99.9% AI-generated. Below is a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the set of pictures is AI-generated and not real.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, Russian President Putin did not write anything against Indian government in Rajghat Visitors' Book; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 15 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A purported social media post recently went viral, with users claiming that Russian President Vladimir Putin had criticised the Narendra Modi government in a message written in the official visitors' book at Rajghat during his recent visit. The claim further alleged that Putin indirectly appealed to the people of India to overthrow the present government, which he allegedly described as running on a "Godsewadi hatred ideology." However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found the claim to be misleading in its investigation. In his original message, as verified by credible news reports and the Russian Foreign Ministry's official release, the Russian President praises Mahatma Gandhi and speaks of shared values between India and Russia. Claim A Facebook user, Munish Kumar Verma, on December 8 shared a post claiming that Russian President Vladimir Putin criticised the Narendra Modi government in the message he wrote in the Rajghat visitors' book. The user claimed that the Hindi translation of Putin's message read: "Not only I, but my ancestors, the people of Russia, and the entire world believe that India is a secular, democratic country based on the principles of non-violence and brotherhood shared by Mahatma Gandhi and Nehru. I would like to appeal to the people of India that the future of this country lies in overthrowing the government running on the 'Godsewadi' hatred ideology as soon as possible." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the post had garnered 4.1k likes.) Investigation The Desk began its investigation by conducting a customised Google keyword search to check whether any credible media outlet had reported that President Vladimir Putin had called for the removal of the Narendra Modi government in his Rajghat message. The search yielded no such credible reports. Considering the gravity of the alleged statement, any such remark by the Russian President would have received extensive media coverage. Instead, the search led the Desk to a WION report published on December 5, which detailed what Putin actually wrote. According to the report, the Russian President described Mahatma Gandhi as "one of the founders of modern India" and wrote that Gandhi's ideas about freedom, virtue and compassion remain relevant today. Putin wrote: "In many respects, Mahatma Gandhi anticipated the new, more just multipolar world order that is now taking shape." Nowhere in the report was there any mention—direct or indirect—of Putin criticising the Indian government or calling for its removal. Here is the WION report link , along with a screenshot: The WION report also included a post from the official X account of the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, dated December 5, which shared the original image of Putin's handwritten note in the visitors' book. As part of the investigation, the Desk extracted the Russian text and translated it using Google Translate. The translation showed that Putin praised Mahatma Gandhi as a philosopher and visionary who made a significant contribution to peace. At no point did he mention or criticise the current Indian government. The English translation reads: "One of the founders of the modern Indian state, the great philosopher Mahatma Gandhi, made an invaluable contribution to the cause of peace. His ideas about freedom, virtue, and humanity remain relevant to this day. In many respects, he anticipated the new, more just world order that is currently taking shape. In his letters to Leo Tolstoy, he reflected on a future world free from domination and hegemony, founded on equality, mutual respect, and cooperation between nations. These are the very principles and values that Russia and India jointly defend on the international stage today." Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: A screenshot showing the English translation of Putin's message was also attached. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim circulating on social media is false. In his original message, as verified by credible news reports and the Russian Foreign Ministry's official release, the Russian President praises Mahatma Gandhi and speaks of shared values between India and Russia.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Was Indian Army official pushed during Lionel Messi's India visit? Video shared with false claim by social media users
content: New Delhi, December 15 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing Argentine football superstar Lionel Messi walking inside a packed stadium, surrounded by a tight security cordon, has been circulating widely on social media. The clip was shared with claims that Messi's security guards pushed aside an Indian Army personnel during his GOAT India Tour 2025. Social media users alleged that the incident reflected a slight against the Indian Army, with some posts using derogatory language while amplifying the claim. The video appears to show a uniformed official attempting to move past the security ring around Messi, only to be stopped and pushed back by personnel guarding the footballer. The visuals were projected as evidence that an Army officer was manhandled by Messi's private security team, triggering sharp reactions and nationalistic outrage online. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the viral claim and found it to be misleading. The individual seen in the video is not an Indian Army soldier but a West Bengal Police officer. Further, the personnel who stopped and pushed him are not Messi's private guards but Indian security forces deployed as part of the Z-plus security cover accorded to the football star during his India visit. Claim: A video featuring Argentina's FIFA World Cup-winning icon Lionel Messi in a stadium surrounded by his guards was shared by an X user, 'Zardan Sangzi', on December 14, claiming that Lionel Messi's security guards pushed an Indian Army personnel during his GOAT India Tour 2025. The video featured an official trying to break through Lionel Messi's security cordon at the stadium, but was stopped. "Aukaat of Indian Army in front of Messi security guards….," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further review of the search results, the Desk came across a Hindustan Times report published on December 13 that stated Lionel Messi's GOAT India Tour 2025 got off to a controversial start. The Argentine visited Salt Lake Stadium in Kolkata on Saturday. "A video of a police official has gone viral, as he tried to break through Lionel Messi's security cordon in the stadium, and wasn't allowed to do so," read a section of the report. This clarifies that the official in the video is not an Army officer but a West Bengal Police official. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google search on Messi's security and came across a report by UNI published on December 13. The report highlighted that the Argentine superstar was accorded Z-plus security, a category typically reserved for visiting heads of state, with more than 5,000 personnel expected to be on the ground to ensure an incident-free visit. This makes it clear that the personnel who pushed the West Bengal police official are Indian security officers. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. The Desk, on careful analysis of the video, found West Bengal Police's emblem on the officer's uniform, which makes it clear that no Indian Army official was involved. Below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the man seen in the video is a West Bengal Police officer. At the same time, those pushing him are CRPF personnel assigned to Messi's security detail.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 5-year-old IAF document on pilots who left service digitally manipulated with wrong data to share false claim; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 15 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media post featuring a document, appearing to be an official RTI reply, was recently shared online, alleging that the Indian Air Force (IAF) had confirmed that 163 pilots resigned in the wake of India–Pakistan tensions in May 2025. The post further claimed that 780 IAF pilots had quit the force over the last five years. However, in its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the document had been digitally manipulated by inserting data from a 2020 RTI response stating that 798 pilots resigned between 2010 and 2019, not in the last five years. The viral post altered this five-year-old document, changing dates and figures to create a misleading narrative. Claim An X user, Annushi Tiwari (@Kussikhuelafn), on December 11 shared a social media post attached to a purported official RTI document, claiming that 163 IAF pilots resigned in 2025 following the India-Pakistan conflict in May. The document further claimed that the total number of pilots who quit the IAF in the last five years stood at 780. The user wrote: "Documents of IAF show that 780 pilots resigned in 5 years, and after the Pakistan-India war, 163 pilots resigned. Many families whose pilots were martyred in the war are still facing oppression to keep them silent. Rahul Gandhi has been proven right once again today." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing the story, the post had garnered 107.1k views.) Investigation The Desk ran the image of the purported document through Google Lens and found several social media accounts that had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. In the next stage of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google search to determine whether any credible media outlet had reported that 780 IAF pilots had resigned in the last five years, including 163 after the May 2025 conflict. The search did not yield any such credible news report. Given the seriousness of the claim, it would likely have been widely covered had it been true. Instead, the search led the Desk to a report published by Aaj Tak on August 18, 2020, which stated that 798 IAF pilots resigned between 2010 and 2019—not in the last five years, and not due to any recent events. The 2020 Aaj Tak story was based on an IAF document released in response to an RTI filed by India Today. When the Desk compared the 2020 document with the one shared in the viral post, it found that the latter had been digitally manipulated. While most of the content in the two documents appeared identical, except for the following changes in the manipulated version: the date was altered from 7 August 2020 to 7 December 2025, the timeline of pilot resignations was changed from 2010–2019 to 2017–2025, and a new claim of 163 resignations in 2025 was inserted. Here is the link to the Aaj Tak report, along with a screenshot: A comparison image below highlights how the original document was digitally altered to falsely claim that 163 IAF pilots resigned after the India–Pakistan conflict in May 2025. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk then examined India Today's original RTI-based report from August 18, 2020. The report clearly states that the RTI document recorded 798 resignations from 2010 to 2019, contradicting the viral claim. The report reads: "In the last 10 years, 798 pilots of the Indian Air Force (IAF) have resigned, and of them, 289 pilots were given no-objection certificates to fly private airlines. The IAF revealed this in response to a Right to Information (RTI) application filed by India Today." Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a five-year-old RTI document from the IAF was digitally manipulated using incorrect data to claim mass resignations of 163 pilots falsely occurred after the India–Pakistan conflict in 2025.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video of people 'looting cash from highway' falsely shared as real incident
content: New Delhi, December 15 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video circulating on social media purportedly shows dozens of people rushing to collect currency notes scattered across a road, with an overturned vehicle visible in the background. It was shared with the claim that the visuals were from a highway where people allegedly looted cash spilt on the ground after a truck overturned. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk has found that the video is AI-generated and has no connection to any real incident. The clip has been digitally created and is being shared online with a false narrative to mislead viewers. Claim: A video purportedly depicting an unusual incident on a highway, in which a truck loaded with cash overturned, was shared by an X user on December 13. The user claimed that the mishap caused the money inside the vehicle to spill onto the road, following which people allegedly rushed to the spot and looted the cash. "If notes are flying on the highway, then suddenly everything comes to a halt. Brakes, noise, rushing people— Money in the air, sense on the ground," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation To verify the authenticity of the viral video, the Desk carefully analysed it and noticed a watermark displaying the name "Shaanzo." Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised Google search and came across an Instagram handle with a similar name. Upon reviewing the Instagram account, the Desk found a video posted by the user on November 13 that matched the visuals in the viral clip exactly. A closer examination revealed that the user had clarified in the caption that the video depicting a supposed loot was AI-generated and not a real incident. "Thankyou for 3.2Million views. AI Generated / Creative Video) — This is fictional content."For entertainment only — Not a real incident," read the post's caption. Below is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: A comparison image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral clip and the video posted by the Instagram content creator. Next, using the above findings as context, the Desk analysed the viral clip using the AI-detection tool Hive Moderation, which confirmed that 67.4% of the footage contained AI-generated or deepfake elements. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an AI-generated video of people looting cash from a highway was falsely shared on social media as a real incident.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Scripted video of woman in bridal attire shared with false claim that she met her former partner hours before wedding; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 15 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently shared on social media claimed to show a real incident in which a woman dressed in bridal attire went to meet her former partner for the last time, just hours before her wedding. The visuals showed the two, seemingly engaged in a conversation on a road, while another individual, who had driven the woman to the meeting, recorded the moment. In the clip, the person recording claimed that the woman was unable to marry her former partner due to family pressure. The video also showed the woman crying inconsolably after returning to the car. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false. The video was originally shared by a content creator named Aarav Mavi on December 13 from his Instagram handle, who later confirmed to PTI that it was scripted and does not depict a real-life incident. The scripted video was falsely presented on social media as a real event to mislead viewers. Claim On December 13, an X handle with the username @venom1s shared a purported social media video claiming to show a woman dressed in bridal attire meeting her former partner for the last time, hours before her wedding. The visuals showed the two engaged in a conversation on a road. At the same time, another individual, who escorted the woman in a car, recorded the video and claimed that she could not marry her former partner due to family pressure. The user wrote: "She is getting married, but still went to meet her ex-boyfriend. There are many such cases in society where girls meet their ex before marriage, and some even after marriage." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing the story, the video had garnered 1.8 million views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was examined using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search results also led the Desk to several media reports, including Navbharat Live and TV9 Punjabi, which covered the viral video while presenting it as a real incident. Links to these reports can be found here and here : Additionally, the Google Lens search led the Desk to an Instagram account run by Aarav Mavi (@chalte_phirte098). The user identified himself as a content creator and had shared the same video on December 13, 2025. At the time this story was published, the video had garnered 2.1 million likes and 53.1k comments on Instagram. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: A comparison image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral clip and the video posted by the Instagram content creator. In the next phase of the investigation, to verify the video's authenticity, the Desk contacted the content creator. Speaking to the PTI Fact Check Desk, he confirmed that the video was scripted and did not depict a real-life incident. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a scripted video showing a woman meeting her former partner hours before her wedding was falsely shared on social media as a real incident to mislead viewers.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old Pushpa 2 premiere crowd falsely linked to Lionel Messi's recent Hyderabad visit; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 15 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a massive crowd gathered at night, cheering loudly and waving mobile phone flashlights, has been circulating widely on social media. Several users sharing the footage claim it captures scenes from Hyderabad, where fans supposedly turned out in large numbers to welcome Argentina's FIFA World Cup–winning footballer Lionel Messi during his GOAT India Tour 2025. The visuals show what appears to be an overwhelming public response, with people packed closely together, raising their phones and reacting enthusiastically—giving the impression of a historic reception for the football star. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk investigated the viral claim and found that the video has no connection to Lionel Messi or his visit to India. A detailed examination revealed that the footage predates Messi's GOAT India Tour 2025 and actually shows crowds gathered in Hyderabad for an entirely different event. The visuals are from December 2024 and capture the massive public turnout at Sandhya Theatre during the premiere of the Telugu film Pushpa 2: The Rule, when fans assembled to catch a glimpse of actor Allu Arjun. Claim: A video featuring a sea of people cheering loudly and flashing their phones was shared by an X user, 'mamtesh manohar', on December 13, claiming to show the frenzy of fans welcoming Argentina's FIFA World Cup-winning icon, Lionel Messi, in Hyderabad. "BREAKING | HYDERABAD. Messi has arrived in Hyderabad! The GOAT touches down in Hyderabad, fans go wild! Historic moment for Indian football," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across the same video uploaded by an X user, '@lokeshreddy_000', on August 15. The caption of the post read: "Still can't get over it -#Pushpa2". The text and timeline of the post clarify that the video is not recent and is unrelated to Messi's GOAT India Tour 2025. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combination post highlighting the similarities between the recent social media post and months-old post. Taking a cue from the above finding, the Desk conducted a set of customised keyword searches on Google. It came across a video uploaded on the YouTube channel 'News Buzz' on December 5, 2024. The title mentioned 'Allu Arjun Exclusive Visuals @ Sandhya Theatre Hyderabad | Pushpa 2 | Rashmika Mandanna | Sukumar' Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot. Below is a composite image highlighting Allu Arjun's attire and his waving gesture from atop a vehicle, seen in the recent social media post and YouTube video. Moreover, Sandhya Theatre was not in the list of places associated with Messi's Hyderabad visit. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video claiming to show fans welcoming Lionel Messi in Hyderabad actually shows massive crowds at Sandhya Theatre during the Pushpa 2: The Rule premiere in 2024, who came to see Allu Arjun.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Fake driving licence image misidentifies Bondi Beach attacker as Indian national Santosh Narain; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 15 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media post featuring an image of a driving licence purportedly belonging to one of the two gunmen involved in Australia's Bondi Beach attack was recently shared online. The post claimed that one of the attackers had been identified as an Indian national named Santosh Narain. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false. The original image of the driving licence belonging to one of the two alleged gunmen showed his name as Naveed Akram, which was digitally altered to misrepresent the attacker's name as Santosh Narain. Furthermore, as part of its investigation, the Desk accessed credible media reports confirming that the attackers were Sajid Akram and his son Naveed Akram. The manipulated social media post was circulated online to mislead viewers. Claim An X user, Imran Dawarr (@Imrandawarr), on December 14 shared a social media post attached with an image of a driving licence, claiming it belonged to one of the gunmen involved in the Bondi Beach attack in Australia. The name highlighted on the licence was alleged to confirm that the attacker was an Indian national named Santosh Narain. The user wrote, "Bondi Beach shooter identified as Santosh Narain, who is wearing an Indian cricket jersey." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the post had garnered 2.5k views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral image of the purported driving licence through Google Lens. The search results led to multiple social media accounts that had shared the same image with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a report published by India Today on December 14, 2025, which detailed the Bondi Beach shooting incident. The report included the exact image of the driving licence seen in the viral posts. However, upon close examination, it was found that the original name mentioned on the driving licence was Naveed Akram, not Santosh Narain. This confirmed that the name had been digitally altered in the viral image to identify the attacker as an Indian national falsely. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Below is a comparison image showing how the attacker's name on the driving licence was digitally manipulated to falsely claim the identity of Santosh Narain. In the next stage of the investigation, taking cues from the original name found on the authentic driving licence—Naveed Akram—the Desk conducted a customised Google keyword search to verify the identities of the attackers involved in the Bondi Beach shooting on December 14, 2025. The search led to a report published by Australia-based news outlet Nine News on December 15, 2025. The report identified the two gunmen as 50-year-old Sajid Akram and his 24-year-old son Naveed Akram. The report stated: "Naveed was born in Australia in 2001, while his father arrived in Australia in 1998 on a student visa and transferred to a partner visa in 2001. Sajid was believed to be on a resident return visa (RRV) at the time of the shooting." The report also quoted NSW Police Commissioner Mal Lanyon, who stated that a detailed background investigation of both individuals was underway. At no point did the report identify either of the gunmen's name was Santosh Narain. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Additionally, the keyword search led the Desk to a report published by Australia-based news outlet The Sydney Morning Herald on December 15, 2025. The report also identified the attackers as father-and-son duo Sajid Akram and Naveed Akram. The report stated that Sajid Akram was killed during police action, while Naveed Akram sustained serious injuries and was hospitalised. The report further quoted Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke stating: "Sajid arrived in 1998 on a student visa, transferred to a partner visa in 2001, and later held resident return visas. Naveed was born in Australia." Here is the link to the report: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a digitally altered image of a driving licence was falsely circulated online to misidentify one of the Bondi Beach attackers as an Indian national, with his name as Santosh Narain. (The story has been updated removing some unnecessary information)

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video depicting a horrific accident on a highway shared as real incident; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 16 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently shared on social media claimed to depict a horrific accident that allegedly occurred on a highway in India. The visuals showed a car moving in the wrong direction, crashing into another vehicle, which, upon impact, toppled into the air before falling to the ground. Another car was also visibly hit by the vehicle travelling on the wrong side. However, upon investigation, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the video was AI-generated and falsely shared as real to mislead viewers. Claim On December 15, an X handle with the username Shagufta Khan (@Digital_khan01) shared a purported video claiming to show a major accident that occurred on a highway in India. The visuals showed a car moving in the wrong direction, crashing into another vehicle, which toppled into the air due to the force of the impact before falling to the ground. Another car was also visibly hit by the vehicle travelling in the wrong direction. The user captioned the video: "Why do people drive in the wrong direction on the highway...?" Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered 10.4k views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was examined using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. One such post can be found here , along with its archived version. In the next step of the investigation, to verify the authenticity of the video, the Desk closely analysed the footage and found multiple anomalies suggesting that it was AI-generated. For instance, the visuals of the accident appear highly unrealistic, as the car that topples into the air seems to split in two. Additionally, the other vehicle involved in the collision continues moving as if unaffected. Below is a screenshot highlighting these observations. Based on these findings, the Desk further analysed the viral clip using the AI-detection tool Hive Moderation. The results indicated that 81 per cent of the footage contained AI-generated or deepfake content. Below is a screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video depicting a horrific accident that seemingly occurred on a highway in India, allegedly caused by a car moving on the wrong side, was AI-generated and falsely shared as real.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: This photo of Lionel Messi holding copy of Indian Constitution is not real but digitally altered; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 16 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): An image depicting Argentine football superstar Lionel Messi allegedly holding a red-and-black pocket edition of the Indian Constitution was recently shared online. Users claimed that Messi displayed the Constitution during his visit to India. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found the image to be digitally altered. The original photo shows the Argentine football star waving to the crowd during his visit to Hyderabad, but it was manipulated to give the false impression that he was holding the Constitution, misleading viewers. Claim An X handle with the username Parinda (@Parthian_1), on December 14, shared an image of Argentine football superstar Lionel Messi from his recently concluded India tour, in which he was allegedly seen holding a red-and-black coat-pocket edition of the Indian Constitution. Sharing the image, the user wrote, "Jai Sanvidhan". Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the post had garnered 38.8k views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and found multiple social media accounts that had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search results also led the Desk to a post shared by Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy on his official X handle. The post included an image of the Argentine football player that was visibly similar to the viral social media post; however, it did not show him holding a copy of the Indian Constitution. Upon a close read of the details shared by the Telangana Chief Minister on his X account, it was found that the image was from Messi's visit to Hyderabad on December 13, 2025. The picture showed him waving to fans at the Rajiv Gandhi International Stadium, but was digitally altered to show him holding a copy of the Indian Constitution. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. Below is a comparison image showing how the original picture of the Argentine football superstar waving to fans during his visit to Hyderabad, Telangana, was digitally altered to depict him holding a red-and-black, pocket-sized copy of the Indian Constitution. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the image of Argentine football superstar Lionel Messi waving to fans during his visit to Hyderabad had been digitally altered to depict him holding a copy of the Indian Constitution.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video falsely shared as construction worker's miraculous escape while hugging daughter; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 17 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video circulating on social media claims to show a construction worker narrowly escaping death at a construction site as he rushed forward to hug his daughter. The clip, widely shared with an emotional backstory, suggests that the man survived a potentially fatal incident due to a moment of divine intervention. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk has found that the video is not real. The investigation reveals that the visuals are AI-generated and do not depict any actual incident. The clip has been digitally created and is being shared online with a false narrative to mislead viewers. Claim: A video purportedly showing a construction worker at a construction site was shared by an Instagram user, 'shayro_ke_alfaz', on December 9, claiming that he narrowly escaped death while going to hug his daughter. "ek Hug Ne Baap Ki Zindagi Wapas De Di | Emotional Story. Kabhi kabhi Khuda ki Rahmat ek pal mein zindagi badal deti hai…A father saved by a single hug," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . Upon careful analysis of the video, the Desk found several inconsistencies. For instance, the girl's face appeared distorted, the iron rods in the concrete column repeatedly changed shape, from straight lines in one frame to a mesh in another, and the shovel also looked distorted. Below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the video through HiveModeration, an AI-detection tool, which flagged it as AI-generated. Below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an AI-generated video of a man narrowly escaping his death was falsely shared on social media as a real incident.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-manipulated video shared to falsely claim 'Australian PM cancelled all Pakistani visas after Bondi Beach attack'
content: New Delhi, December 17 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check): A video purportedly showing Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese addressing the media has gone viral on social media, with claims that Australia has cancelled visas of all Pakistani nationals following the recent terror attack at Bondi Beach. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk has found the claim to be false. An investigation reveals that the viral video is neither recent nor connected to the Bondi Beach attack. The clip has been digitally altered using AI-generated audio, falsely superimposed onto unrelated footage of the Australian Prime Minister from a 2022 parliamentary briefing. The Australian government has made no official announcement regarding the cancellation of Pakistani visas following the attack. Meanwhile, fifteen people were killed when the two gunmen targeted Jewish attendees at a Hanukkah event, including a 10-year-old girl, a British-born rabbi, a retired police officer, and a Holocaust survivor. Claim: A video featuring Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese addressing the media was shared by a Facebook user, Kanchan Gaikwad, on December 17, claiming that Australia has cancelled visas of all Pakistani nationals following a terror attack at Bondi Beach. "The Pakistani-origin terrorist Naveed Akram has been arrested in today's terror attack. Australia is suspending all visa services for Pakistani(s), effective immediately," says Australian PM in the video. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . As part of the investigation, the Desk first conducted a customised Google search to determine whether Anthony Albanese had made such an announcement following the Bondi Beach attack. This search did not yield any credible news reports. However, after the attack, we came across his press conference dated December 14, which was aired on the official YouTube channel of 9 News Australia. At no point in the address did the speaker talk about cancelling all Pakistani visas. "Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has condemned the shooting as a "targeted" and "evil" act of antisemitism. An attack on Jewish Australians is an attack on every Australian. Every Australian tonight will be, like me, devastated over this attack on our way of life. The PM said the National Security Committee convened today shortly following the shooting," read the description. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Our search also led us to a report by The Times of India published on December 15, highlighting that Sajid Akram was shot dead in a gunfight with police at the scene, while Naveed was arrested and taken to the hospital, where he remains in a critical but stable condition under police guard. "Sajid Akram was shot dead in a gunfight with police at the scene, while Naveed was arrested and taken to hospital, where he remains in a critical but stable condition under police guard. Social media footage showed moments of bravery amid the terror, including a bystander who confronted one of the gunmen and wrestled a weapon away. By the time the area was secured, the beachfront was littered with discarded shoes, blankets and picnic items, stark reminders of the sudden violence that shattered across a grassy hill overlooking Bondi Beach," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report. Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk extracted the keyframes of the social media post and ran them through Reverse Image Search to access that particular briefing. The search led the Desk to a report by the Brisbane Times published on August 4, 2022. The cover image used in the report matched the clip seen in the social media post. The report highlighted a parliamentary discussion on the proposed Indigenous Voice to Parliament. The report's timeline and details indicate that the clip is not recent and is unrelated to the Bondi Beach attack. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the social media post and the news report. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk noticed that in the social media post, the Australian PM's lip movements appeared slightly distorted and out of sync. Following this, the Desk extracted the audio from the video and ran it through Resemble AI, a voice AI-detection tool, which flagged the audio as fake. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video featuring Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese saying that Australia has cancelled all Pakistani visas after the Bondi Beach attack is fake and AI-manipulated.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Edited video shared to falsely claim Owaisi named Bondi Beach attackers as Indian NRIs; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 17 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video circulating widely on social media claims to show journalist Palki Sharma Upadhyay hosting AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi in what is being described as a sensational interview on the Bondi Beach attack. The clip is being pushed with the assertion that Owaisi, speaking on Sharma's show, "exposed" the attackers as Indian NRIs from Uttar Pradesh. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and examined the video in detail to verify its authenticity. The investigation reveals that the viral clip is not a genuine interview. Instead, it is a digitally manipulated montage stitched from two unrelated videos of Palki Sharma Upadhyay and Asaduddin Owaisi from different occasions, accompanied by fabricated audio. The content has been deliberately edited to create a false narrative that neither occurred nor was ever reported by any credible outlet. Claim: A video showing journalist Palki Sharma Upadhyay and AIMIM Chief Asaduddin Owaisi, apparently, during Sharma's show, was shared by an X user, 'Rizwan Shah', on December 16, claiming that in an explosive interview, Owaisi exposes the identity of the Bondi Beach attackers as Indian NRIs from Uttar Pradesh. "BREAKING. Owaisi drops a bomb with Palki Sharma, claiming Bondi attackers were Indian NRIs from UP. Narrative cracks, facts emerge, fake anti-Pakistan propaganda falls apart again," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. One such post can be found here . As part of the investigation, the Desk divided the video into two parts - one featuring Palki Sharma Upadhyay and the other featuring Asaduddin Owaisi and extracted the keyframes of the clip depicting Sharma and ran them through Reverse Image Search. This led us to the original video, aired on the official YouTube channel of First Post, from her Vantage show, dated November 26, 2025. She reported on China's tough stance on Taiwan and its rare call with Trump. The report's timeline and description clarify that it is neither recent nor related to the Bondi Beach attack. Moreover, nowhere in the entire report did she talk about Owaisi or the attack. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Palki Sharma is seen wearing the same attire in the report as in the recent X post. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the two. Next, the Desk extracted the keyframes of the other part of the viral video featuring Owaisi. It ran it through a Reverse Image Search, which led us to an ANI interview dated October 12, 2025, in which he said no decision had yet been taken on an alliance with the Congress for the Jubilee Hills by-election and emphasised his good relationship with Revanth Reddy. This clarifies that the video is totally unrelated. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Two separate clips of Palki Sharma and Owaisi have been edited together to falsely claim that Owaisi identified the Bondi Beach attackers as Indian NRIs from Uttar Pradesh. Furthermore, the Desk extracted the audio from the viral post and ran it through Resemble AI, an AI-detection tool, which found it to be fake and manipulated. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the clip showing Owaisi identifying the Bondi Beach attackers as Indians on Palki Sharma's show is digitally manipulated. The original clip of Palki Sharma is from her Vantage show, and Owaisi's footage is taken from an unrelated interview to set a false narrative.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2023 pro-Palestinian video falsely shared as Bondi Beach attack celebration; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 17 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A disturbing video showing a Muslim cleric addressing a crowd, with people gathered around him at night, has been widely circulated on social media in recent days. Those sharing the clip have claimed that Muslims in Sydney were celebrating the recent terror attack at Bondi Beach, alleging that the gathering reflected approval of the violence. Given the sensitive nature of the claim and the potential for the video to incite hatred and misinformation, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk examined the footage's authenticity and context. A detailed investigation found that the viral video has no connection to the Bondi Beach attack and is being falsely linked to a recent tragedy. In reality, the clip dates back to October 2023 and shows a speech delivered during a pro-Palestinian rally in Sydney following the October 7 Hamas attack on Israel. Fifteen people were killed when the two gunmen targeted Jewish attendees at a Hanukkah event, including a 10-year-old girl, a British-born rabbi, a retired police officer, and a Holocaust survivor. Claim: A video showing a group of people gathered in an area. At the same time, a Muslim cleric could be seen delivering a speech, which a Facebook user shared, 'IIT Madras Junta Against Leftist APSC' on December 15, claiming that Muslims in Sydney were celebrating the Bondi Beach terror attack. "The Muslims in Australia are smiling and happy about the Bondi massacre; they even lit fireworks to celebrate. They need to all be deported from every country to Arab pig countries," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post by a user 'David Atherton' on October 9, 2023, featuring the same video as seen in the recent post. The report's timeline makes it clear that the clip is not recent and is not related to the Bondi Beach attack. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the recent social media post and the 2023 X post. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk once again extracted the keyframes and ran them through a reverse image search, which led us to a Daily Mail report published on October 9, 2023. The headline of the report read: "Sheikh Ibrahim Dadoun: Muslim preacher who praised Palestinian terrorists who massacred hundreds of innocent Israelis recently held prayers next to Anthony Albanese - as he breaks his silence on the backlash" The report also carried the same video as seen in the recent social media post. The title read: "Muslim preacher praises Palestinian terrorists in western Sydney" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Further searches led us to a report by Sky News Australia aired on their official YouTube channel on October 9, 2023, which mentioned that a controversial Islamic cleric who celebrated Hamas' attack on Israel at a rally in Sydney also spoke at a Muslim community event alongside Prime Minister Anthony Albanese. "Muslim preacher who celebrated Hamas invasion spoke at community event alongside Albanese," read the title of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search, which led us to a report by ABC News published on October 9, mentioning that the prime minister has criticised comments made at a pro-Palestinian rally at which speakers described attacks on Israel as an act of "courage" and "resistance". "Pro-Palestinian rally at Lakemba in Sydney criticised for 'celebration' of attacks on Israel," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a Muslim cleric giving a speech dates back to October 2023, and they were celebrating the October 7 Hamas attack on Israel.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Fabricated document falsely attributed to Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri on Bondi Beach shooting shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 18 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A day after the Telangana Director General of Police confirmed that one of the two alleged assailants in the Bondi Beach firing incident, Sajid Akram, holds an Indian passport, a purported social media post featuring a document allegedly issued by Indian Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri was shared online. The document claimed to show directions from the Foreign Secretary to the Indian High Commissioner in Canberra, instructing them to extend full cooperation to the Australian government in the ongoing investigation into the mass shooting incident at Sydney's Bondi Beach on December 14. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found the document to be fake. In an official statement, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) confirmed that the document was fabricated. No such communication, nor any document signed by Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri, has been issued in connection with the Bondi Beach shooting. A false document attributed to the Indian Foreign Secretary was shared online to mislead viewers. Claim On December 16, an X handle named Romi (@RomiAlerts) shared a purported social media post containing a document attributed to Indian Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri. The document claimed that he had directed the Indian High Commissioner in Canberra, Australia, to extend full cooperation to Australian authorities in the investigation into the mass shooting that occurred at Sydney's Bondi Beach on December 14. It is pertinent to note that the purported document surfaced online shortly after the Telangana Director General of Police confirmed that one of the two alleged assailants, Sajid Akram, holds an Indian passport. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the post had garnered 102.9k views.) Investigation The Desk ran the image of the purported document through Google Lens and found several social media accounts that had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. Next, to verify the claim's authenticity, the Desk conducted a customised Google search for credible media reports or official government releases confirming the issuance of such a document. The search did not yield any news reports or official statements, indicating that the Indian government had issued no such document. Had the document been genuine, credible media outlets would likely have reported on it, or the communication would have been published on the official website or social media handles of the Ministry of External Affairs. Instead, the search led the Desk to an official post by the Ministry of External Affairs' Fact Check handle, which shared the same document and categorically termed it as fake. "The letter used in this post is fake," the MEA Fact Check handle stated. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the document circulated on social media, allegedly issued by Indian Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri in connection with the Bondi Beach firing incident, is fake. The document was falsely linked to the recent mass shooting in Australia and shared online to mislead viewers.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Fabricated video of Sanjay Dutt shared to falsely claim he criticised Nitish Kumar over hijab controversy; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 18 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): As Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar continues to face criticism for pulling down the veil of a Muslim woman at a public event, a social media video purportedly showing Bollywood actor Sanjay Dutt criticising the JD(U) chief over the incident was recently shared online. The visuals showed the actor in a self-recorded message urging Nitish Kumar to apologise for his actions. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found the video to be digitally manipulated. The original video, shared on Sanjay Dutt's official Instagram account in 2019, shows the actor speaking about the Marathi film 'Baba', produced under Sanjay Dutt Productions, and urging viewers to watch it. A fabricated audio track, falsely portraying him as criticising Nitish Kumar over the hijab controversy, was later overlaid on the clip to mislead viewers. Claim An X handle with the username Mehreen Mehmood Mufti (@MMufti786) on December 17 shared a video of Sanjay Dutt in which he was allegedly heard criticising Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar for pulling down the veil of a Muslim woman at a public event. The visuals showed the actor in a self-recorded message urging Nitish Kumar to apologise for his actions. Here is the link and archived link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the post had garnered 9,000 views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was examined using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a video shared by Bollywood actor Sanjay Dutt on his official Instagram account on August 8, 2019. The self-recorded video shared from his handle had a background setting similar to that seen in the viral clip. However, upon analysing the original video, the Desk found that Dutt was speaking about the Marathi film 'Baba', the first Marathi movie produced under his banner, and not criticising Nitish Kumar over any controversy. In the original video, Dutt stated: "Hello, everybody. Namaskar to you all. 'Baba' is the first Marathi film I have produced. I want to thank the media for the wonderful reviews and the audience for all their love and affection." He added: "This movie is about family, love and relationships. I would request everyone to go and enjoy the movie, live the dream of a father and a mother, and let me know about it." Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. The image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral clip and the original video the actor shared on his Instagram account. In the next stage of the investigation, based on these findings, the Desk extracted the audio track from the viral video. It analysed it using the AI audio detection tool Resemble AI. The tool indicated that the voice in the clip was artificially generated. Below is a screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a digitally manipulated video of Sanjay Dutt was falsely shared online to mislead viewers.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video falsely shared to claim leopard jumped out of cage at a zoo in India; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 19 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video recently shared on social media claimed to depict a real incident in which a leopard jumped out of a cage at a zoo and reached a spot where visitors were standing. The video showed people screaming in fear after the leopard suddenly leapt from the cage and emerged into an open area near the visitors. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the video does not depict any real incident. Instead, it is an AI-generated clip that was falsely shared online to mislead viewers. Claim On December 18, an X handle with the username Roshni P (@roshnipar0786) shared a video depicting a horrific incident allegedly occurring at a zoo, presumably in India. The video purported to show a real incident in which a leopard jumped out of a cage and reached a spot where visitors were standing, causing panic among them. Here is the link and archived link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video had garnered 531.2k views.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was examined using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. To verify the authenticity of the video, the Desk carefully analysed it and identified multiple anomalies indicative of AI generation. For instance, the leopard appears standing in one place in one frame but changes position in a fraction of a second in another. Similarly, a woman clad in a yellow saree appears at one spot in the video, then suddenly at a different location in the next frame. These inconsistencies strongly indicate that the video is AI-generated. Based on these observations, the Desk also analysed the clip using the AI-detection tool Hive Moderation. The results showed that 99.9 per cent of the video is likely to contain AI-generated or deepfake content. A screenshot of the result is provided below. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to verify whether any incident similar to the one depicted in the video had occurred anywhere in India. However, the search did not yield any credible news reports confirming such an incident. Had it been real, the incident would likely have been widely reported by the media. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a leopard jumping out of a cage near visitors at a zoo is AI-generated and was falsely shared online as a real incident to mislead viewers.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: '4 Indians arrested in Bondi Beach attack case? No, digitally manipulated video and false claim shared by Pak-based social handles, websites to mislead Internet audience
content: New Delhi, December 20 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Days after the Telangana Director General of Police confirmed that one of the two alleged assailants in the Bondi Beach firing incident, Sajid Akram, holds an Indian passport, a purported social media video surfaced online claiming that Australian Federal Police Commissioner Krissy Barrett had allegedly stated that four more Indian nationals were arrested in connection with the incident. In the purported video, the Australian federal commissioner was quoted as saying: "During an intelligence-led operation, authorities confirmed the arrest of four individuals of Indian nationality following the Bondi incident as part of the ongoing investigative efforts. These arrests represent a significant development in uncovering a wider network under scrutiny. We acknowledge and appreciate the cooperation provided by the Indian authorities and intelligence partners." However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it to be digitally manipulated. The original video shows Barrett outlining key developments in the ongoing investigation, including that the surviving alleged Bondi Beach shooter has been charged with 59 offences. A fabricated audio track, falsely portraying her as confirming the arrest of four Indian nationals, was later overlaid on the clip to mislead viewers, mainly by Pak-based social media handles and websites. Claim An X handle with the username The_Nexus (@Nexus_Again) on December 20 shared a video allegedly showing Australian Federal Police Commissioner Krissy Barrett stating that authorities had arrested four Indian nationals in connection with the Bondi Beach terror attack case. Sharing the video, the user wrote: "Australian authorities have arrested five individuals, including four Indian nationals, in connection with the Bondi Beach terror attack that killed 15 people and wounded dozens. The attack, carried out by a father-son duo—Sajid Akram, an Indian, and his son Naveed—is linked to ISIS." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (It is pertinent to note that upon checking the "About" section of the X handle, the Desk found that the account is operated from Pakistan.) Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was analysed using Google Lens, which led the Desk to several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. Importantly, checking through the "About" section of the X handles, the Desk found these accounts were operated from Pakistan. Screenshot of the same has been attached below. The search also led the Desk to reports published by Pakistan-based news portals The Pakistan Connect and Azaad Digital, which similarly claimed that the arrest of four Indian nationals in connection with the Bondi Beach terror attack had been confirmed by India's Ministry of External Affairs. Links to these reports can be found here and here . Screenshots of the "About" sections of these news portals have been included to confirm that they are based in Pakistan. In the next stage of the investigation, to verify the authenticity of the video, the Desk closely analysed the footage and observed that it carried the logo of international news outlet The Guardian. Taking this cue, the Desk conducted a customised Google search to locate the original Guardian report featuring the Australian federal commissioner's statement regarding the Bondi Beach attack. The search led the Desk to a report published by The Guardian on December 18, 2025, which included a video visually identical to the viral clip. However, upon careful review of the original video, the Desk found that Barrett did not mention any arrests of Indian nationals in connection with the incident. In the original footage, Barrett confirmed that the surviving alleged Bondi Beach shooter had been charged with 59 offences and stated that the New South Wales Joint Counter-Terrorism Team would execute further search warrants in the coming days to support the investigation. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot. The image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral clip and the original video published by The Guardian. In the next stage of the investigation, based on these findings, the Desk extracted the audio track from the viral video and analysed it using the AI audio-detection tool Resemble AI. The tool indicated that the voice in the clip was artificially generated. Below is a screenshot of the result. In the subsequent part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find any credible news reports or official government releases by the Ministry of External Affairs confirming the arrest of Indian nationals in connection with the Bondi Beach attack. However, the search did not yield any credible information supporting the claim. Had such arrests occurred, they would have been widely reported by the media. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a digitally manipulated video of Australian Federal Police Commissioner Krissy Barrett, falsely claiming that four Indian nationals were arrested in connection with the Bondi Beach terror attack case, was shared online as real to mislead viewers.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video of Hindu monk meditating on snow-covered cliff shared as real

One of these keyframes was analysed using Google Lens, which led several social media accounts to share the same video with similar claims.
