author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered 2024 image of Bangladeshi students falsely shared as 'killers of Sharif Osman Hadi' crossing India-Bangladesh border
content: New Delhi, December 22 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A photograph showing two young men pulling suitcases at what appears to be a border checkpoint has been widely circulated on social media with a claim linked to the killing of Bangladeshi activist Sharif Osman Hadi. The image, shared by multiple social media users, claimed to show the alleged shooters involved in Hadi's killing fleeing Bangladesh and crossing into India through the Petrapole–Benapole border. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false. The photograph in question is neither recent nor connected to the killing of Sharif Osman Hadi. In reality, the image dates back to 2024 and was originally published by a mainstream Indian news outlet in an unrelated context. It shows Bangladeshi students entering India through a border check post to pursue higher education, not accused criminals attempting to flee the country. The Desk also found that the viral version of the image has been digitally manipulated, with facial alterations used to misrepresent the individuals as suspects in the high-profile killing. Claim: A purported photograph showing two individuals carrying their luggage was shared by an X user, 'Kashmir Digital', on December 19, claiming that they were killers of Sharif Osman Hadi crossing the border between India and Bangladesh. "The suspected shooters involved in the killing of Usman Hadi have surfaced, showcasing the two crossing the India-Bangladesh border," read the text accompanying the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the image through Reverse Image Search and found that several other users had also shared the same picture with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here . Our search also revealed that a report published by Pakistan-based new portal 'Kashmir Digital' claimed that the suspected shooters involved in the killing of Osman Hadi have surfaced, showcasing the two crossing the India-Bangladesh border, complicating the investigation of the high-profile case. Screenshot of the "About" sections of the news portals has been included to confirm that they are based in Pakistan. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a report by The Indian Express published on August 7, 2024. We found a similar image and background in the report, featuring Bangladeshi students studying at a university in Meghalaya who are crossing the India-Bangladesh border at a check post. However, the Desk noticed that the faces in the recent social media post have been digitally altered. "Russel Mondol (21), a resident of Jhenaidah who studies engineering at a college in Meghalaya, enters India through the border check-post. (Express Photo by Partha Paul)," read the photo caption. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combined image highlighting the similarities between the background in the social media post and the news report's cover image. Meanwhile, Bangladesh has intensified its crackdown on the killing of young leader and activist Sharif Osman Hadi, with authorities identifying the alleged shooter, issuing a nationwide lookout notice, and imposing a travel ban on the prime accused as violent protests spread across the country. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the picture has been digitally altered & dates back to 2024. It shows Bangladeshi students entering India through a border check post, not the Hadi killers.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-manipulated video falsely claims Indian journalist questioned Jordan's protocol during PM Modi's visit
content: New Delhi, December 22 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video clip featuring journalist Palki Sharma presenting a news bulletin has gone viral on social media, with claims that she questioned Jordan's diplomatic protocol during Prime Minister Narendra Modi's recent visit to the Middle East. The clip, widely circulated online, purportedly shows Sharma asking why King Abdullah II of Jordan did not personally receive the Indian Prime Minister at the airport, suggesting a downgrade in the level of welcome compared to previous visits. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk found the claim to be misleading and the video digitally manipulated. While the visuals in the viral clip do originate from a genuine episode of Vantage with Palki Sharma, aired on December 17, the audio has been altered using artificial intelligence tools to insert remarks that were never made during the original broadcast. Further verification — including AI voice analysis and a cross-check with official reports on the visit — confirmed that the viral clip uses fabricated audio layered over authentic footage to push a false narrative. PTI Fact Check also noted that official coverage of the visit highlighted gestures reflecting close bilateral ties, including the Jordanian Crown Prince personally accompanying Prime Minister Modi during his engagements. Claim: A video featuring journalist Palki Sharma presenting a news bulletin was shared by an X user, 'Ammar Solangi', on December 18, claiming that she questioned Jordan's protocol during Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit, asking why King Abdullah II did not receive Modi at the airport on his arrival. "PM Modi's recent visit to Jordon has raised serious diplomatic questions. In the past, PM Modi received a warm and high-level welcome during his visit to Jordon. However, this time, reports indicate low protocol compliance. With King Abdullah II not receiving him at the airport. This has drawn attention to The post clocked 140.1k views on social media. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation As part of the investigation, the Desk noticed the First Posts logo in the top-left corner of the video. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised Google search and found the original news report. The original video was from her "Vantage with Palki Sharma" episode, which aired on December 17. Upon analysing the video, the Desk found that at the 33:30-minute timestamp, the visuals in the original report match those seen in the viral video. However, in the original broadcast, Sharma does not question Jordan's protocol or raise concerns about King Abdullah II not receiving PM Modi at the airport. "Modi was on a diplomatic tour to Jordan, Ethiopia, and Oman, and mentions that he was welcomed at the airport in Jordan by the country's Prime Minister…," says Palki Sharma. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Below is a combined image highlighting the similarities between the social media post and the news report. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk extracted the audio from the video and ran it through Resemble AI, an AI voice detection tool. It detected that the audio is fake. Below is a screenshot of the same. According to a PTI report carried by The Hindu, Jordanian Crown Prince Al Hussein bin Abdullah II personally drove Prime Minister Narendra Modi to the Jordan Museum on Tuesday (December 16, 2025), in a special gesture reflecting the warmth of ties between India and the Arab nation. PM Modi arrived in Jordan's capital, Amman, on Monday (December 15) on a two-day visit at the invitation of King Abdullah II. Jordan is the first leg of the Prime Minister's four-day, three-nation tour, which will also take him to Ethiopia and Oman. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of journalist Palki Sharma questioning Jordan's protocol during Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit, asking why King Abdullah II did not receive Modi at the airport on his arrival, is manipulated and created using fake audio.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old, edited France 24 video clip shared to falsely link Bangladeshi activist Osman Hadi's killing to India; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 22 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Days after Sharif Osman Hadi, a youth leader from Bangladesh and an outspoken critic of both India and former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, was shot dead by bike-borne assailants in central Dhaka on December 12, a purported news clipping was shared on social media claiming that France 24 journalist Genie Godula had reported on his killing and linked it to India. The video allegedly shows the France 24 journalist stating that sources had claimed India was responsible for the killing of the Bangladeshi Gen-Z figure. "Reports citing local sources from Bangladesh say activist Osman Hadi was shot in the head and killed under disputed circumstances. Some sources claim that links connected to India's intelligence agency, the RAW, are being examined. Investigations are currently ongoing. Following the incident, protests have erupted on the streets, with demonstrators demanding justice. Protesters have also called for action against India-linked political groups, while others are demanding a transparent probe into the alleged Indian involvement," she is heard saying in the viral clip. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the purported France 24 clip was digitally manipulated. The original video, from August 2024, shows Genie Godula reporting on American athlete Noah Lyles, who had clinched a gold medal at the Paris Games. A fabricated audio track falsely portraying her as linking India to Osman Hadi's killing was later overlaid on the clip to mislead viewers, primarily by Pakistan-based social media handles. Claim A Pakistan-based X account, Zardan Sangzi (@ZardanSi), on December 21 shared a purported France 24 news clip in which journalist Genie Godula allegedly cited sources claiming that India's intelligence agency was behind the killing of Bangladeshi Gen-Z figure Osman Hadi. "India is responsible for the killing of Bangladeshi Gen-Z figure Osman Hadi. France 24 reports that India's intelligence agency, RAW, hired agents to assassinate him. India continues to sponsor terrorism globally," the user claimed. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered 43,700 views.) Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk ran the viral video through the InVID tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was analysed using Google Lens, which led several social media accounts to share the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. Notably, upon reviewing the "About" sections of these X accounts, the Desk found that they were operated from Pakistan. Screenshots confirming the same have been attached below. The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a video shared by France 24 on its official X handle on August 5, 2024. The visuals in the original clip matched those seen in the viral video and showed journalist Genie Godula reporting on a news development. However, upon listening to the original audio, it was found that she was reporting on American sprinter Noah Lyles' gold medal win at the 2024 Paris Games. At no point did she mention Osman Hadi's death or link it to India. The finding thus suggested that the video was digitally manipulated. Here is the link to the X post, along with a screenshot: The image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral clip and the original France 24 video. In the next stage of the investigation, the Desk extracted the audio track from the viral video and analysed it using the AI audio-detection tool Resemble AI. The tool indicated that the voice in the clip was artificially generated. Below is a screenshot of the result: Moreover, as a part of the investigation, the Desk also conducted a customised keyword search related to Osman Hadi's death and the allegations linking it to India. This led to a report published by Firstpost on December 19, which stated that accusations were being made against India for allegedly sheltering the attackers and demanding their extradition. "Political offshoots such as the National Citizen Party claimed that the assailants had already fled to India after committing the shooting. They called on the interim government to take drastic steps, including shutting down the Indian High Commission in Dhaka until the suspects were returned," the report stated. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a digitally manipulated video falsely showing France 24 journalist Genie Godula linking the killing of Bangladeshi activist Osman Hadi to India was circulated on social media as real to mislead viewers.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered video falsely shared to claim 'PM Modi demanded Nitish Kumar's resignation' after hijab row
content: New Delhi, December 24 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): As Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar continues to face criticism over an incident in which he was seen pulling down the veil of a Muslim woman at a public event, a video shared on social media claims to show Prime Minister Narendra Modi allegedly demanding Kumar's resignation. The video purportedly shows PM Modi, in a recorded message, alleging that Nitish Kumar's mental state was not stable and calling for him to step down. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the video was digitally manipulated. PM Modi did not demand Nitish Kumar's resignation. A fabricated audio track was falsely overlaid on an old video clip of the Prime Minister to mislead viewers. Claim A Facebook handle named 'Sahilalam Aimim' on December 21 shared a video claiming that Prime Minister Narendra Modi had demanded the resignation of Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar following the hijab controversy. The visuals allegedly show PM Modi stating that Nitish Kumar's mental state was not good. "Modi ji demanded Nitish Kumar's resignation over the hijab issue," the user captioned the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk ran the viral video through the InVID tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was analysed using Google Lens, which led the Desk to a video published on the official YouTube channel of the Prime Minister's Office (PMO). The visuals in the PMO video matched the background and attire worn by PM Modi seen in the viral clip. However, upon further examination, the Desk found that the original video dates back to June 2025, while the controversy involving Nitish Kumar occurred in December 2025. The original footage features PM Modi's remarks at the International Conference on Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (ICDRI) 2025, and has no connection to the hijab-related incident. These findings indicate that the video was digitally manipulated and does not depict a real event. Here is the link to the original video, along with a screenshot: Next, the Desk extracted the audio track from the viral video and analysed it using the AI audio-detection tool Resemble AI. The tool indicated that the voice in the clip was artificially generated. Below is a screenshot of the result: As part of the investigation, the Desk also conducted a keyword search to verify whether PM Modi had ever demanded Nitish Kumar's resignation. The search did not yield any credible media reports supporting such a claim. Had such a statement been made, it would have been widely reported. The search, however, led to a news report published by The Indian Express on December 22 detailing a recent meeting between PM Modi and Nitish Kumar in New Delhi. The report makes no mention of the Prime Minister demanding the Bihar Chief Minister's resignation. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video purportedly showing Prime Minister Narendra Modi demanding the resignation of Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar was digitally manipulated and falsely circulated as real.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video falsely shows PM Modi statue made from coconut leaves; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 24 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it showed an individual creating a statue of Prime Minister Narendra Modi using coconut leaves. The visuals allegedly depicted the individual meticulously giving the statue a fine finish. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the video was digitally generated and falsely circulated online as real to mislead viewers. Claim An X handle named Dr Jasraj Prajapati (@Its_Me_Jasraj) on December 22 shared a video claiming to show a man creating a statue of Prime Minister Narendra Modi using coconut leaves. Sharing the video, the user wrote: "Narendra Modi ji statue made from coconut leaves." Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered 190,200 views.) Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk ran the viral video through the InVID tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was analysed using Google Lens, which led to several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively: The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a video shared by a Facebook page named Funny Entertainment TV. The Desk found that the video shared by the page on December 20, 2025, was identical to the viral clip and appeared to be the original source. However, upon reviewing the Facebook page, the Desk observed that it is known for sharing AI-generated content. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the Facebook post had garnered over 20 million views and more than 1 million likes.) A comparison image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral video and the clip posted by the Facebook page. In the next stage of the investigation, the Desk further analysed the viral clip using the AI-detection tool Hive Moderation. The results indicated a 99% likelihood that the video contains AI-generated or deepfake content. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing an individual creating a statue of PM Modi using coconut leaves was AI-generated and falsely circulated as real.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old wrestling tournament video falsely linked to Save Aravalli movement; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 24 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid heightened public attention around environmental issues and ongoing concerns over mining and development in Rajasthan's Aravalli range, a video showing a massive crowd assembled in a hilly landscape began circulating widely on social media. The visuals were shared with claims that they depicted people participating in the Save Aravalli movement, a campaign aimed at protecting one of India's oldest mountain ranges from ecological degradation. However, the authenticity of the claim raised questions, particularly as no major reports or official confirmations corroborated such a massive protest at the time. The PTI Fact Check Desk examined the viral video and found that it dates back to August 2025 and actually is from a wrestling tournament held in Kariri Khanpur, Mahwa, in Dausa district, Claim: A video featuring a sea of people gathered in a hilly area was shared by an Instagram user 'momaji_ka_ladla' on December 19, 2025, claiming that the people were gathered as part of the Save Aravalli movement in Rajasthan. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the image through Reverse Image Search and found that several other users had also shared the same picture with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an Instagram post featuring the same visuals, uploaded on August 31, 2025. The timeline of the post clarifies that it predates the Aravalli Hills controversy that began in November 2025. The post's description mentioned that the video is from Rajasthan's biggest wrestling tournament, held at Kariri Khanpur, Mahwa. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from the above findings, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google, which led the Desk to the video uploaded on Jagat Tak News' YouTube channel on August 31, 2025. The title of the video read: "Todabhim: Kariri Ghazipur wrestling match | These two fought well till the very last moment". Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the recent social media post and the YouTube video. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video claiming to depict the Save Aravali protest is actually months old and from a wrestling tournament held in Kariri Khanpur, Mahwa, in Dausa district.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Viral clip misrepresents Javed Akhtar's stand on Nitish Kumar hijab issue
content: New Delhi, December 24 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video clip showing filmmaker and lyricist Javed Akhtar responding to a question on face covering has gone viral on social media, with claims that he supported Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar amid the recent hijab controversy. The clip shared widely on social media is being presented as Akhtar's endorsement of Nitish Kumar's conduct after the CM pulled the veil of a woman doctor during a government event in Patna on December 15, triggering widespread criticism. However, a detailed investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk revealed that the claim is misleading. The viral video is not related to the hijab controversy and predates the incident by several weeks. The footage is from a literary event held on November 29, 2025, where Akhtar was responding to a general question on the concept of face covering, long before the Bihar CM's remarks sparked public outrage. Further verification shows that Akhtar has, in fact, publicly condemned Nitish Kumar's action in a separate social media post, calling for an unconditional apology to the woman involved. Claim: A video featuring filmmaker and lyricist Javed Akhtar addressing questions at a gathering was shared by an X user 'Arvind Mohan Singh' on December 17, claiming that he supported Bihar CM Nitish Kumar on the hijab controversy. "Nitish Kumar did what was right, what was the need to cover his face - Javed Akhtar (lyricist and screenwriter)," read the caption of the post. Responding to a question about how covering face makes a woman less strong, Javed Akhtar can be heard saying, "...Why should you be ashamed of your face? I agree that revealing clothes, whether worn by men or women, do not look dignified…But what makes her cover her face? What is so vulgar, obscene, and undignified about her face?... She's been brainwashed, even if she says she's doing it willingly..." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the image through Reverse Image Search and found that several other users had also shared the same picture with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here, and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across the original and extended version streamed on the official YouTube channel of SOA Literary Festival on November 29, 2025. The visuals match those seen in the recent social media post. Moreover, the timeline of the video clarifies that it is unrelated to the Hijab controversy that happened in December 2025. Upon scanning the entire video, at 46 minutes in, we found the clip similar to the social media post. Here is the link of the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. As part of the investigation, the Desk also found pictures of the same event uploaded by author Vani Tripathi Tikoo on her X account on November 29, 2025. The text accompanying the photos read, "The creative odyssey of #JavedAkhtar saab! #SOALiteraryFestival," Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Taking the investigation ahead, the Desk also scanned the X handle of filmmaker Javed Akhtar and came across a post dated December 18, 2025, about Nitish Kumar calling for an apology regarding the hijab controversy. "Every one who knows me even in the most cursory manner knows how much I am against the traditional concept of Parda but it doesn't mean that by any stretch of imagination I can accept what Mr Nitish Kumar has done to a Muslim lady doctor . I condemn it in very strong words . Mr Nitish Kumar owes an unconditional apology to the lady," read his X post. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. The controversy that erupted after Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar pulled the veil of a doctor at a government event. It all began on December 15, when she was handed her appointment letter by the CM. Video footage of the appointment ceremony went viral when the CM, noticing her hijab, remarked, "What is this?" and pulled down the veil. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video featuring filmmaker and lyricist Javed Akhtar talking about covering the face is actually from an event in November 2025, whereas the hijab controversy took place on Dec 15 at an event held in Patna.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old Chhattisgarh protest video misrepresented as resistance to Aravalli hill cutting; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 25 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A dramatic video showing chaotic scenes of a violent clash between two groups in a hilly region has been widely circulated on social media, with users claiming that it captures residents of Rajasthan forcefully resisting government officials who allegedly arrived to cut the Aravalli hills. The clip, which shows stone pelting, baton charges, and panic amid rugged terrain, was shared with emotive captions urging people to rise in defence of the Aravalli range and warning of its imminent destruction. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that while protests related to the Aravalli issue did take place in Rajasthan, the viral video in question does not depict those events. Instead, the footage is from an unrelated incident in Chhattisgarh, where villagers clashed with police over the proposed expansion of a coal mine. The video was shared with a false claim on social media. Claim: A video showing a clash between two groups, apparently police and protesters, in a hilly area, was shared by an Instagram user 'jodhpurichora_rj19' on December 21, claiming that government officials had come to cut the Aravalli hills and were met with strong resistance from residents. "A crowd of millions to save the Aravalli range. Every person in Rajasthan will have to take to the streets and save their Aravalli mountains," read the post's caption. The post clocked 18,132 likes on social media. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation: The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across the same video streamed on the official YouTube channel of ABP News on December 3, 2025. The title of the report read: "Chhattisgarh Breaking: Villagers clash with police in Ambikapur, 40 policemen injured in stone pelting." The description of the video clarifies that the video is unrelated to the Aravali protest. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities between the social media post and the news report. Taking a cue from the above finding, the Desk then conducted a set of customised keyword searches on Google and came across a report by India Today published on December 3, 2025. The cover image of the report was similar to that of the clips seen in the social media post. "Around 40 cops injured as villagers clash over mine land expansion in Chhattisgarh," read the headline of the report. As per the report, tension flared in Chhattisgarh's Surguja district after residents of a nearby village launched a violent protest against the proposed expansion of the Amera coal extension mine in Lakhanpur block. Villagers alleged that the mine operator was attempting to extend the project area without formal land acquisition and without their consent, endangering their farmland, water sources, and homes. "According to eyewitnesses, the situation escalated when villagers tried to stop workers and officials heading towards the mine gate. The crowd, armed with sticks, axes and slingshots, reportedly began pelting stones at police personnel deployed at the site, triggering chaos. Around 40 police personnel were said to be injured, while some villagers also sustained injuries in the clashes," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. Meanwhile, according to reports, on Monday (December 22), protests broke out in several cities, including Jodhpur, Udaipur, and Sikar, leading to clashes between protesters and the police. While the police resorted to a baton charge and detained several people in Jodhpur, in Sikar, protesters scaled Harsh Mountain, a 945 m peak that is part of the Aravalli range, to agitate. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video actually shows people protesting against land acquisition for a coal mine in Chhattisgarh and is unrelated to the Aravali issue.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of Dhaka college student falsely linked to death of Bangladeshi Hindu worker Dipu Chandra Das
content: New Delhi, December 25 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A disturbing video showing a man being carried by policemen while crying and pleading for mercy has been widely shared on social media, with users claiming that it depicts Bangladeshi police allegedly handing over a Hindu garment worker, Dipu Chandra Das, to extremists moments before his death. The visuals, coupled with emotive captions alleging police complicity and religious targeting, quickly gained traction online, triggering outrage and renewed debate over the safety of minorities in Bangladesh. Given the serious nature of the allegations and the communal sensitivity surrounding the claim, the PTI Fact Check Desk examined the video to verify its authenticity, timeline, and context. The investigation revealed that the video being shared with the claim is not recent and predates the alleged lynching of Dipu Chandra Das. Further checks revealed that the visuals have no connection to the incident involving Das and do not show Bangladeshi police handing him over to extremists. Instead, the video shows a Dhaka College student who was briefly detained by police in Dhaka in November 2025 and later released. According to reports, Hindu factory worker Dipu Chandra Das was set on fire after being lynched in Bangladesh's Mymensingh. His family has claimed that the 27-year-old was killed over workplace rivalry rather than any alleged "blasphemous" remark. Das was killed by a mob last week amid a fresh wave of unrest following the death of student leader Sharif Osman Hadi, a prominent face in the anti-government protests that led to the ouster of former premier Sheikh Hasina. Claim: A video featuring a man being carried by a group of policemen, while he cries and pleads for mercy was shared by an Instagram user 'Jammugrove' on December 22, claiming that it shows Bangladeshi police handing over Dipu Chandra Das to extremists before his death. "25-year-old Hindu garment worker Dipu Chandra Das is seen desperately pleading for his life in Mymensingh, Bangladesh. Surrounded by police officers who appear indifferent, Das explains his innocence amid unsubstantiated blasphemy accusations stemming from a workplace dispute," read the text accompanying the post. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation: The Desk ran the image through Reverse Image Search and found that several other users had also shared the same picture with a similar claim on social media. Two such posts can be found here and here, and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across the same visuals uploaded by Bangladeshi news outlet Bhorer Kagoj on November 18, 2025. The caption read: "What happened to this Dhaka College student?" The timeline of the report and description mentioned clarify that the video is not recent and is unrelated to the lynching of Dipu Chandra Das Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. As part of the investigation, further searching the search results led us to an extended version of the video uploaded on YouTube by a user 'Dhaka Today News'. The description of the video read: 'Dhaka College student starts crying after being beaten by police || Dhaka Today' Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same. Though the Desk could not independently verify the source of the video, however, it is clear that the video predates the violence and is completely unrelated to the alleged lynching of Das.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Scripted video showing a woman being harassed over a dowry demand shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 25 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media video purportedly showing a woman being harassed by her husband and father-in-law over a dowry demand was recently shared online, claiming it to depict a real incident. The video allegedly shows the two men physically assaulting the woman while she weeps and pleads for mercy. The visuals later show another man intervening, freeing the woman, and reprimanding her husband and father-in-law for their actions. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the video was scripted and falsely circulated as real to mislead viewers. Claim An X user named PARVEEN (@parwiinshaikh) on December 22 shared a video claiming to show a woman being harassed by her husband and father-in-law over a dowry demand. The clip allegedly shows the duo physically assaulting the woman while she cries and pleads for mercy, followed by another man intervening and reprimanding the accused. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered 69,300 views.) Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk ran the viral video through the InVID tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was analysed using Google Lens, which led to several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively: During further analysis, the Desk found that at the 40-second mark, a disclaimer appears in the video stating that the content is created for entertainment purposes. The clip does not depict a real-life incident. Below is a screenshot highlighting the disclaimer: The Desk then ran the extracted keyframes through Google Lens again, which led to a video uploaded on November 29, 2025, on a YouTube channel operated by a content creator named Ankur Jatuskaran. Upon analysing the YouTube video, the Desk found multiple indicators that the clip was staged. For instance, the disclaimer in the YouTube video states that the content is scripted and created for entertainment purposes. Additionally, individuals appearing in the viral video—particularly the man portrayed as the woman's husband—are the same as those seen in the YouTube video. The background setting and storyline in both videos are also identical. This indicates that the viral video was created by Ankur Jatuskaran as part of a scripted drama. Furthermore, as the video progresses, another individual—portrayed as the woman's father-in-law—can be seen appearing as a bystander, further indicating staged content. Here is the link to the YouTube video, along with a screenshot: Below are comparison images highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the YouTube clip: The Desk also reviewed the YouTube channel in question and found that most of the videos uploaded on it depict scripted dramas and are not based on real incidents. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a woman being harassed over a dowry demand by her husband and father-in-law was scripted and falsely shared on social media as a real incident to mislead viewers.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of women assaulted with chairs in Bangladesh falsely linked to India
content: New Delhi, December 25 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media video purportedly showing an individual assaulting two women with plastic chairs while a large crowd looks on was recently shared online. Users claimed that the incident occurred in India and that two Muslim women were beaten with chairs after removing their hijab. The visuals show a man repeatedly thrashing two women with a plastic chair, continuing the assault even after one of them falls to the ground. However, in its investigation, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the video was falsely linked to India. The incident shown in the clip actually took place in Chittagong city, Bangladesh, and was wrongly associated with India by propaganda accounts to mislead viewers. Claim An X handle named S Surinder (@KhalsaVision_) on December 19 shared a video showing an individual hitting two women with plastic chairs while a large crowd watched. The user claimed that the incident occurred in India and that two Muslim women were beaten after removing their hijab. "Nitish Kumar's legacy. Two more Muslim women were beaten with chairs after removing their hijab," the user wrote. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the video had garnered 395,800 views.) Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk ran the viral video through the InVID tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was analysed using Google Lens, which led to several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively: The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a news report published by Bangladesh-based newspaper Prothom Alo on December 18, 2025. The feature image of the report matched the keyframe used in the investigation. Upon analysing the report, the Desk found that it stated the incident had occurred in Chittagong city, Bangladesh, earlier last week. While the exact motive behind the incident was still being ascertained, the report quoted a Bangladeshi police official saying that the incident took place at Bijoy Mela in the CRB area of Chittagong. "After the incident, two women came to the outpost and gave a verbal complaint. Later, no one was found there. That day, there was a fight at several shops where there was a crowd of people," the official was quoted as saying. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: A comparison image below highlights the similarity between the viral video and the feature image used in the Prothom Alo report. Additionally, the search results led the Desk to another Bangladesh-based news outlet, Bangladesh Pratidin, which also published a detailed report on the incident. The outlet stated that the assault took place during a fair held in the CRB area of Chittagong city. The report does not link the incident to India. Here is the link to the report, along with a screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing two women being assaulted with plastic chairs was falsely linked to India. The incident occurred in Chittagong city, Bangladesh, and was misleadingly shared on social media as an incident from India.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally manipulated clip of Sanjay Dutt shared to falsely claim he 'justified lynching of Hindu man' in Bangladesh; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 25 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid escalating outrage across India following the lynching of a 27-year-old Hindu garment worker from Bangladesh, Deepu Chandra Das, over alleged charges of blasphemy, a social media video of Bollywood actor Sanjay Dutt was widely shared online, falsely claiming that he supported the incident. In the purported video, Dutt was allegedly heard stating that the lynching was bound to happen as Deepu Chandra Das had insulted the religious sentiments of Muslims. "What happened to Deepu Chandra in Bangladesh was absolutely justified. Look, I am a true Hindu, and I never support what is wrong. The way Deepu Chandra insulted the beloved Prophet of the Muslims, this was bound to happen to him. Just think for a moment how you would feel if someone made derogatory remarks about our Lord Rama. Deepu Chandra has received the punishment he deserved. As for the rest of you, the comment section is open; feel free to express your opinions," he was allegedly heard saying in the video clip However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the video was digitally manipulated. The original footage dates back to 2017 and shows Sanjay Dutt promoting his film Bhumi. A fabricated audio track was later superimposed on the clip to mislead viewers. The edited video clip was shared online with false claim to mislead people. Claim An Instagram user named ayubeditz on December 21 shared a video of Bollywood actor Sanjay Dutt in which he was purportedly heard stating that the lynching of Dipu Chandra Das — a 27-year-old Hindu garment worker from Bangladesh who was beaten to death and whose body was set on fire in Mymensingh by an unruly mob over charges of blasphemy — was justified. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing the story, the video had garnered 74.7k views.) Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk ran the viral video through the InVID tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was analysed using Google Lens, which led to several social media accounts sharing the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively: Next, as part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find credible news reports or videos corroborating claims that the Bollywood actor supported the gruesome incident in Bangladesh. However, the search did not yield any credible news reports confirming such statements. Had this development been true, it would have been widely reported by the media. Further, the Desk ran the extracted keyframes through Google Lens once again. This search led to a video uploaded on the official YouTube channel of the entertainment portal FilmiBeat. The Desk found that the video of Sanjay Dutt speaking at a public event was exactly the same as the visuals seen in the viral clip and was first published in 2017. Notably, the lynching incident occurred on December 18, 2025. Further analysis revealed that the original video was from the promotional event of the Bollywood film Bhumi, starring Sanjay Dutt and Aditi Rao Hydari. The video had no connection to the recent lynching incident in Bangladesh. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot: In the next stage of the investigation, the Desk extracted the audio track from the viral video and analysed it using the AI detection tool Resemble AI. The tool indicated that the voice in the clip was artificially generated. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a digitally manipulated video of Sanjay Dutt, in which he was purportedly heard supporting the lynching of Deepu Chandra Das in Bangladesh, was falsely shared as real.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered video of Yogi Adityanath shared to falsely claim 'he urged PM Modi to carry out full-blown attack on Bangladesh'
content: New Delhi, December 26 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): As outrage continues against the Bangladesh government over the brutal lynching of a Hindu youth, Deepu Chandra Das, on alleged charges of blasphemy, a purported social media video of Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath was recently shared online. In the video, Adityanath was allegedly heard directing remarks at Prime Minister Narendra Modi in connection with the incident, stating that if India could not take action against Bangladesh, the Prime Minister should resign from his post. He was also purportedly heard making remarks about Pakistan Army Chief Asim Munir, claiming that as long as Munir remains in Pakistan, India would continue to face trouble. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found the video to be digitally manipulated. While the original clip does show Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath addressing the lynching of a Hindu youth in Bangladesh and targeting the opposition over what he described as appeasement politics, he was nowhere heard urging Prime Minister Modi to launch an attack on Bangladesh or resign from office. Claim An Instagram handle with the username 'flashfeedindia01' on December 26 shared a purported video of Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, in which he was allegedly heard directing remarks at Prime Minister Narendra Modi over the lynching of a Hindu individual in Bangladesh. In the video, the UP Chief Minister, while addressing the state assembly, was purportedly heard stating that if India could not take action against Bangladesh, the Prime Minister should resign from his post. He was also allegedly heard making remarks about Pakistan Army Chief Asim Munir, claiming that as long as Munir remains in Pakistan, India would stay in trouble. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video had garnered 6,736 views.) Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk ran the viral video through the InVID tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was analysed using Google Lens, which led several social media accounts to share the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively: Next, the Desk conducted a customised Google search for credible news reports or videos that could substantiate the claim. However, the search did not yield any credible reports confirming the claim. Given the seriousness of the allegation, had it been true, the media would have widely reported it. The search instead led the Desk to a video shared on December 24, 2025, by the official X account of Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. The video shows the Chief Minister addressing the Uttar Pradesh Assembly and speaking about the lynching of a Hindu youth in Bangladesh. The Desk carefully analysed the clip to verify whether Adityanath had urged Prime Minister Modi to either attack Bangladesh or resign from office. No such statement was found, indicating that the viral clip had been digitally manipulated. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. In the original video, Adityanath was heard stating, "You view Dalits merely as a vote bank, which is why you remain silent. Look at what happened in Bangladesh—how a Dalit youth was brutally burned to death. You shed tears for Gaza, but not a single word comes out of your mouth when a Dalit youth is killed in Bangladesh. Your silence speaks volumes because you see him only as a vote bank to be exploited. This is not politics; this is the truth." Further targeting the opposition, he said: "You organise candle marches over the Gaza issue, but when a Hindu—especially a Dalit—is killed in Pakistan or Bangladesh, you fall silent. A condemnation resolution should be passed, and a statement from the Leader of the Opposition must be issued. We condemn this incident and warn the Bangladesh government." Nowhere in the speech did he call upon Prime Minister Modi to attack Bangladesh or resign. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a digitally altered video of Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath was falsely shared on social media, claiming that he directed Prime Minister Modi to either attack Bangladesh or resign from his post.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Scripted video of woman putting toddler in refrigerator while absorbed in phone conversation shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 26 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media video depicting a woman mistakenly putting her toddler in a refrigerator while seemingly engrossed in a phone call was recently shared online, claiming it to be a real incident. The visuals allegedly showed the woman, absorbed in a phone conversation, placing her baby inside a refrigerator. Later, when her husband demanded food, she handed him an empty plate. The video further showed the couple searching for the baby but failing to locate it. However, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk investigated the video and found it to be scripted. A disclaimer mentioned in the video confirmed that it was created for educational and entertainment purposes. Claim An X user, Sweta Srivastava (@swetasamadhiya), on December 24 shared a video claiming to depict a real-life incident in which a woman, seemingly engrossed in a phone call, mistakenly puts her toddler in a refrigerator. The visuals allegedly showed the woman placing the baby in the refrigerator and later handing her husband an empty plate when he asked for food. The video further showed the couple searching for the baby but being unable to find it. "Women, after carrying a child in the womb for nine months and giving birth, take care of them. You can talk on the mobile anytime," the English translation of the text shared along with the video reads. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video had garnered 70.3k views.) Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was analysed using Google Lens, which led several social media accounts to share the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively: The Google Lens search results also led the Desk to a video posted on the Facebook page Ideas Factory on April 6, 2024. It was found that the video shared by the page was an extended version of the viral clip. In the longer video, the child was later shown being safely removed from the refrigerator by an individual purported to be the father. However, upon analysing the disclaimer accompanying the video, it was found that the content was created for educational and entertainment purposes and does not depict a real-life incident. "Thank you for watching! Please be aware that this page features scripted dramas and parodies. These short films are for entertainment and educational purposes only. Characters in the video are fictional," the disclaimer stated. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. Below are comparison images highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the Facebook clip: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk also reviewed the Facebook page in question and found that most of the videos uploaded on it depict scripted dramas and are not based on real incidents. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a woman mistakenly putting her child in a refrigerator while being engrossed in a mobile phone call was scripted and falsely shared on social media as a real incident to mislead viewers.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of Christmas tree fire falsely linked to 'Islamic Radicals' in UK
content: New Delhi, December 29 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a large Christmas tree engulfed in flames inside what appears to be a shopping mall has gone viral on social media, with users claiming that the incident took place in the United Kingdom and was the result of an attack carried out by Islamic radicals. The clip, which captures a rapidly spreading fire and panicked reactions from people nearby, has been shared with provocative captions framing it as an act of religious violence during the Christmas season. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found that the video has been shared with a false and misleading narrative. While the video shows a Christmas tree catching fire in a mall, it is unrelated to the United Kingdom and does not depict an act of religious vandalism. The footage originates from China and dates back to December 2024, when it was reported as an accidental fire incident at a shopping complex. Claim: A video featuring a Christmas tree placed inside what looked like a mall, engulfed in fire, was shared by an X user, 'Sweta Srivastava', on December 26, claiming that it was set on fire by Islamic radicals in the United Kingdom. "Islamist Jihadist Burned Christmas Tree in UK," read the caption of the post. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across the same video uploaded on YouTube by a user named 'Cultura Colectiva Plus', with the description, 'Christmas Tree Catches Fire in a Mall of China CLIP'. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot. Taking a cue from the above finding, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found a report by the Mirror published on December 31, 2024. It mentioned that shoppers can be heard screaming as an intense fire rips through the Christmas tree put on display in an outdoor area of a shopping centre. "The 10-meter-tall Christmas tree ablaze in a shopping mall in Chengdu in China, was shared on Douyin - the Chinese version of TikTok on Dec. 25, 2024," read the description of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. Another report by the New York Post, published on December 31, 2024, also featured the same video, shot from a different angle, and stated that a Christmas tree became a towering inferno at a shopping centre in Chengdu, China. "Christmas is cooked. In the same week that Bryant Park's iconic holiday market caught fire in Midtown Manhattan, a Christmas tree became a towering inferno at a shopping centre in Chengdu, China. No injuries were reported, and mall staff quickly extinguished the terrifying blaze," read the description of the post. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Taking the investigation forward, the Desk conducted another set of customised keyword searches on Google to determine whether such an incident had occurred in the UK. But the search did not lead to any credible report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video, which claims to be from the UK, is actually from China and is a year old.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video shared to falsely claim 'Hindu man pleaded for safety of his life in Bangladesh
content: New Delhi, December 30 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Days after a Hindu man, Deepu Chandra Das, was brutally lynched in Bangladesh on the alleged charge of blasphemy, followed by another similar incident in which an individual named Amrit Mondal was beaten to death by an angry mob on allegations of involvement in criminal activities, a social media video purportedly linked to a Hindu man pleading for his safety in the country has been circulating online. The video allegedly shows the individual walking through an arson-hit area, pleading for safety, dignity, and protection amid fear and uncertainty rose after the brutal lynching of the Hindu youth. He is purportedly heard stating that, like Deepu Chandra Das, other people from the Hindu community will also be killed. However, during its investigation, the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found that the video was AI-generated and falsely shared as real to mislead viewers. Claim An Instagram handle with the username 'The India Times' shared a video on December 26 that purportedly shows a Hindu man pleading for the safety of his life and that of the entire community in Bangladesh. In the self-recorded video, the individual speaks about the deteriorating situation in the country while citing the recent lynching of a Hindu man. He allegedly states that other people from the Hindu community will be killed in a similar manner. "This is Bangladesh. It's nighttime here. They will also kill us like 'Deepu Chadar'. You can see for yourself what is happening here. Share this video as much as possible so that someone can save us. Everything has deteriorated here so suddenly, I am not able to understand," the individual is purportedly heard saying. Here is the link and archived link to the post, along with a screenshot: Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk ran the viral video through the InVID tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was analysed using Google Lens, which led several social media accounts to share the same video with similar claims. Two such posts were found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively: The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a video shared by an Instagram handle named Kuldeep Meena on December 24, 2025. The Desk found that the video shared by this account matched the visuals from the viral clip. However, upon analysing the handle, the Desk observed that the account primarily shares AI-generated content in which the user places himself in digitally created background scenarios. Additionally, several visual inconsistencies were also spotted in the video, indicating that it is AI-generated. For instance, the man mispronounces Deepu Chandra Das's name as "Dipu Chadar". Further, the electric pole shown in the video appears to be emitting light without any visible source. Here is the link to the post, along with a screenshot: Below is a comparison image highlighting similarities between the viral clip and the Instagram video: In the next stage of the investigation, the Desk analysed the video using the AI-detection tool Hive Moderation. The results indicated a 99 per cent likelihood that the content was AI-generated or a deepfake. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video purportedly showing a Hindu man pleading for his safety and that of the Hindu community in Bangladesh is AI-generated and has been falsely circulated as a real incident to mislead viewers.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: This AI-generated photo of Kohli, Rohit Sharma, Jasprit Bumrah at Jagannath Temple falsely shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 30 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared an image claiming it showed Indian cricket team players Virat Kohli, Rohit Sharma, and Jasprit Bumrah visiting the Lord Jagannath Temple in Odisha along with their respective wives—Bollywood actress Anushka Sharma, sports manager Ritika Sajdeh, and sports presenter Sanjana Ganesan. However, during its investigation, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found that the image was AI-generated and falsely shared as real to mislead viewers. Claim An X handle with the username darshan (@18kohliso) on December 27 shared a purported image claiming to show Indian cricketers Virat Kohli, Rohit Sharma, and Jasprit Bumrah visiting the Lord Jagannath Temple in Odisha, along with their wives- Bollywood actress Anushka Sharma, sports manager Ritika Sajdeh, and sports presenter Sanjana Ganesan. The user captioned the post: "Rohit, Kohli and Bumrah's family visited the Lord Jagannath Temple." Here is the link and archived link to the post, along with a screenshot: (At the time of publishing this story, the image had garnered over 1.2 million views.) Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and found that multiple social media users had shared it with similar claims. Two such posts were found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. In the next stage of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google search to determine whether any credible media reports had covered the visit of the Indian cricketers and their families to the Jagannath Temple in Odisha. However, the search yielded no credible results. Had such a visit taken place, it would have been widely reported by mainstream media outlets. The Desk also reviewed the official social media accounts of all six individuals featured in the image. None of them had shared or posted the viral image on their handles. If the image were genuine, it would likely have been shared or acknowledged by at least one of them. In the subsequent stage of the investigation, the Desk ran the image through the AI-detection tool Hive Moderation, which indicated a 99.9 per cent likelihood that the image contains AI-generated or deepfake content. A screenshot of the result is provided below: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the image purportedly showing Virat Kohli, Rohit Sharma, and Jasprit Bumrah visiting the Lord Jagannath Temple in Odisha along with their families is AI-generated and has been falsely circulated as a real photograph to mislead social media users.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Rajan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video claiming Yogi Adityanath left stage after Rajnath Singh's arrival at public event is misleading; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 30 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Rajan, PTI Fact Check ): A video from a public event in Lucknow was recently shared on social media claiming that Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath left the stage soon after Defence Minister Rajnath Singh arrived, with users suggesting it reflected a rift between the two leaders. However, an investigation by the Press Trust of India's (PTI) Fact Check Desk found the claim to be misleading. While Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath did leave the event before its conclusion, he did not exit the stage immediately after Defence Minister Rajnath Singh arrived. The full videos from the event show both leaders attending the programme together. Claim An Instagram handle with the username 'Neha Singh Rathore Supporter' on December 25 shared a purported video of Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath from a public event in Lucknow. The footage allegedly showed the UP Chief Minister leaving the stage as soon as the Defence Minister arrived to participate in the event. Moreover, users in the comment section suggested that the video depicted a rift between the two leaders. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video had garnered 602,000 views.) Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk ran the viral video through the InVID tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was analysed using Google Lens, which led to several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts were found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively: To verify the authenticity of the video, the Desk carefully analysed it and found, from the background poster visible in the clip, that the event attended by the two leaders was 'Ekal Kavya Path', held on the eve of former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee's birth anniversary in Lucknow on December 24, 2025. Below is a screenshot highlighting the finding. Next, taking cues from the above finding, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found a complete video recording of the event shared on the official YouTube channel of Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on December 24, 2025. Upon reviewing the 53-minute-and-50-second footage, the Desk found that Rajnath Singh and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath were seated next to each other for most of the programme and were seen interacting with one another. Both leaders also addressed the gathering. It was only around the 45:54 timestamp that Yogi Adityanath disappeared from the footage, suggesting he left the event at that point—and not immediately after Rajnath Singh arrived on stage. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. The search also led the Desk to a video of the same event shared on the official YouTube channel of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. In this video as well, both leaders were seen attending the event together, with the Chief Minister leaving only after some time, while Rajnath Singh remained present throughout. The video also showed the two leaders sharing cordial interactions. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. Further, the Desk searched for videos shared by poet Kumar Vishwas, who had also attended the event. This led to a short clip uploaded on his official YouTube channel on December 26, 2025. In the video, at the 8:35 timestamp, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath can be clearly seen leaving the stage courteously after a brief interaction with Defence Minister Rajnath Singh. Here is the link to the video, along with a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video was misleadingly shared. While Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath did leave the event before its conclusion, he did not exit the stage immediately after Defence Minister Rajnath Singh arrived. The full videos from the event show both leaders attending the programme together.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Suvendu Adhikari's Gaza reference video clip linked to Bangladesh issue; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 30 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video clip of BJP leader and Leader of the Opposition in the West Bengal Assembly, Suvendu Adhikari, addressing reporters has been widely shared on social media with the claim that he instigated violence against Indian Muslims by allegedly invoking Israel's military actions in Gaza. Several social media users circulated the post, alleging that Adhikari openly called for a massacre of Muslims in India and compared his remarks to Israel's actions against Gazans. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk examined the viral video to verify the claim and found that it was shared with a misleading narrative. A review of the whole clip, along with contemporaneous media reports and footage, shows that Adhikari's remarks were made in the context of alleged lynchings of Hindus in Bangladesh and a protest march to the Bangladesh Deputy High Commission in Kolkata. While his statement drew comparisons to Israel's actions in Gaza, it did not include any reference to Indian Muslims, nor did it call for violence against them. The video was selectively framed on social media to falsely suggest communal incitement within India. Claim: A video featuring BJP leader and Leader of Opposition in the West Bengal Assembly, Suvendu Adhikari, addressing the media, was shared by an X user '@s_afreen7' on December 27, claiming that he allegedly instigated people against Indian Muslims, similar to the actions of Israel against Gazans. In the video, he can be heard saying, "Just like Israel taught Gaza…Our sacred Hindu values and the government are working in the interest of Hindus and the country. A lesson must be given, similar to how we taught Pakistan a lesson in Operation Sindoor." The post's caption read: "Just as Israel has carried out the massacre of Gaza's innocents, this BJP leader wants to orchestrate exactly the same kind of massacre against India's Muslims! This is BJP leader Shuvendu Adhikari from West Bengal! What's astonishing is, despite this call for massacre, neither has an FIR been filed yet, nor has there been any arrest!" Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through the InVid tool, extracting multiple keyframes. Using Google Lens on a single keyframe, the Desk found several social media accounts sharing the same video and making similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post by IANS dated December 26, 2025, featuring Adhikari addressing the media. In the video, he can be heard saying, "These people must be taught a lesson, just like Israel taught Gaza. Our sacred Hindu values and the government are working in the interest of Hindus and the country. A lesson must be given, similar to how we taught Pakistan a lesson in Operation Sindoor…" He did not mention calling for the massacre of Indian Muslims. Moreover, the post also noted that Adhikari made the statement on the lynching of Hindus in Bangladesh. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Taking a cue from the above finding, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by the Indian Express published on December 28, mentioning that BJP's Suvendu Adhikari, the Leader of Opposition in West Bengal, said Bangladesh ought to be taught a lesson akin to what Israel taught Gaza. Suvendu marched to the Bangladesh Deputy High Commission in Kolkata alongside party leaders and several seers, in protest against the killings of two Hindu men, Dipu Das and Amrit Mondal, in the neighbouring country. "Sabak sikhaana chahiye. Jaise Israel sikhaaya Gaza mein. Uss tareeke se. Hamaare Bharat ke 100 crore Hindu; desh ka Hindu hitt mein chal raha hai sarkar. Sabak sikhaana chahiye. Jaise Operation Sindoor mein Pakistan ko hum logon ne sabak sikhaaya (A lesson should be taught. Like Israel taught in Gaza. Our country's 100 crore Hindus; the government is being run in the interest of Hindus. A lesson should be taught. Like we taught Pakistan during Operation Sindoor," he said, reading a section of the report. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot. The search also led us to the same video, aired on the official YouTube channel of NDTV, with the title, "'India Should Teach Lesson To Bangladesh as Israel Did In Gaza': BJP's Suvendu Adhikari". "Bengal BJP leader Suvendu Adhikari demands India teach Bangladesh a "lesson" akin to Israel's Gaza strikes, citing "one billion Hindus" and Operation Sindoor against Pakistan. This follows rising attacks on Hindus in Bangladesh," read the description. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of Suvendu Adhikari instigating people against Indian Muslims is false. The actual video Adhikari demanded India teach Bangladesh a 'lesson' akin to Israel's Gaza strikes over the alleged lynchings of Hindus in Bangladesh.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video of peacock garlanding lord Ram idol falsely shared as real; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 31 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video claiming it showed a real incident of a peacock offering a garland to the idol of Lord Ram at the Ayodhya temple. However, the Press Trust of India's Fact Check Desk found that the video was AI-generated and falsely circulated as real to mislead viewers. Claim On December 30, an X handle with the username @Atulya_Bharat__ shared a video claiming to show a real incident in which a peacock offered a garland to the idol of Lord Ram at the Ayodhya temple. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing the story, the video garnered 59k views) Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk ran the viral video through the InVID tool and extracted multiple keyframes. One of these keyframes was analysed using Google Lens, which led to several social media accounts that had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts were found here and here , with their archived versions available here and here , respectively. The Google Lens search also led the Desk to a video shared by an Instagram handle named Ashish Saxena (ash_saxena). The Desk found that the video shared by the handle on December 29, 2025, was identical to the viral clip and appeared to be the original source. Moreover, the user who shared the video indicated that it was created using an AI text-to-video model, Sora. At no point did the video depict a real incident of a peacock offering a garland to the idol of Lord Ram at the Ayodhya temple. The Desk also analysed other posts shared by the handle and found that it frequently shares AI-generated content. Here is the link and archive link to the post, along with a screenshot. (At the time of publishing this story, the Instagram post had garnered over 1.3 million views and more than 124,000 likes.) A comparison image below highlights the visual similarities between the viral video and the video shared by the Instagram handle. In the next stage of the investigation, the Desk further analysed the viral clip using the AI-detection tool Hive Moderation. The results indicated a 90 per cent likelihood that the video contains AI-generated or deepfake content. Below is a screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a peacock offering a garland to the idol of Lord Rama at the Ayodhya temple was AI-generated and falsely circulated as real.
